`BACKUP-AND-RESTORE.md`:

```md
# Preserve terminal work without replacing it

Keep the exact matching course package and all original attempts. Course-specific
export commands take precedence: Tiny Browser TERMINAL.md, Storage README and Agent
League README describe their own formats. Preserve source, notes and first failures;
an exported result is evidence, not authenticated authorship or a transferable grade.

For portable Sandbox, Blockchain and Onion process work, ordinary file backup is a
supported terminal route, not an invented CLI export function. On the documented
macOS/POSIX profile, leave the course directory, choose a new sibling backup path and
copy the entire matching directory (including dotfiles and attempts):

```sh
test ! -e COURSE-BACKUP && cp -Rp COURSE-DIRECTORY COURSE-BACKUP
```

Replace both names with actual paths. The test must succeed before copying. Stop
course commands while taking the copy so source and history are a consistent set.
Keep the original. To restore, use a new destination, not an existing working folder:

```sh
test ! -e RESTORED-COURSE && cp -Rp COURSE-BACKUP RESTORED-COURSE
```

Enter RESTORED-COURSE, verify your source/notes and previous attempts remain, then run
its documented checks and a new experiment. New receipts must be additive. This copy
does not restore running relay processes, IPC circuits or ephemeral keys; start fresh
processes and circuits using the Onion instructions. A file copy is not a hardware
power-loss or synchronization guarantee. A failed copy is not a completed backup.

```

`CI.md`:

```md
# Public learner contract CI

Pushes to main, pull requests and manual dispatch select changed courses. Course
source or its matching ZIP selects that course; .ci/workflow/common setup changes
run the full configured matrix. A newly added course without a contract fails
selection. Changes to a generated source manifest alone do not hide course diffs.

Checks bind every source file to its ZIP member and executable bit, then use the
existing validation runner for syntax, exact documented setup, named initial
TODO outcomes and configured export/recovery. A stale archive, import crash,
missing dependency, wrong diagnostic or unexpected exit fails. An expected
unfinished starter is not a completed exercise.

The public profile is intentionally separate from full private qualification:
green means these configured public interface regressions pass. It does not mean
that all exercise/capstone implementations succeeded, a blind learner finished,
or human learning occurred. Complete learner implementations are not legitimate
public fixtures here, and are not published merely to make CI green. The retained
source-aware complete runs and new independent blind trials stay private.

The ordinary verify_courses.py CLI still exits2 for incomplete coverage. The
public_contracts.py adapter reports full_exercise_capstone_completion:false and
only passes when all explicitly configured public checks succeed. It never
suppresses a failed or blocked check. Reports uploaded by Actions contain only
summary outcomes, never workspaces, code submissions or blind-trial histories.

All jobs use standard public-repository runners, immutable official Action pins,
contents:read, no persistent checkout credentials, no custom secrets, no release
permissions and no pull_request_target trigger. macos-26 is the standard arm64
profile for supplied native targets; no larger/paid runner is requested. Node and
Python are provisioned only in the disposable hosted CI environment, not on the
operator's Mac. No npm dependencies are installed. No site deployment, visibility,
repository protection, billing or credential settings are changed by CI.

Run locally with already installed tools from the repository root:

    python3 -B -m unittest discover -s .ci -p test_pipeline.py -v
    python3 -B .ci/public_contracts.py --course time-travel-debugger --output NEW_DIR

The JSON-formatted .yml workflow is valid YAML and locally parsed as JSON. Public
course/source licenses and third-party terms apply unchanged. CI is regression
evidence; current qualification is described in QUALIFICATION.md.

The configured matrix now includes the five original terminal releases, Inside
the Shot and Compiler. Inside the Shot checks its exact packet, supplied native
ARM64 target launch and initial public Python model diagnostic. Compiler reads
all nine lessons and checks setup/starter/export/restore. These remain public
interface regressions, not complete learner solutions. Full-path/private-fixture
CI was explicitly deferred; no credential infrastructure is being added for it.

## Targeted recovery and feedback regressions

Adaptive runs generated lossless session-capacity controls (formats 1/2/3,
continued saving, malformed references and existing bounds) without private learner
work. Adaptive also runs checks.test.mjs: one-line wrong edits of the already-public
support layers (a pooled row rate used as p, `now > deadline`) must fail with messages
naming the rule and lesson, the unedited layers must pass, `play --help` must print
usage, and progress wording must not shrink after an edit. Firmware starts with the parser-only checker; its separate staged-checker
regression verifies that later feedback remains gated until the documented stage.
These deterministic regressions do not establish full learner completion.

Small LLM Runtime runs .ci/test_small_llm_runtime_feedback.mjs: plain-word practice
answers, short failure messages, explicit input-cache mutation reports and the
module 07 and trained stop/tokenizer rules. Its runtimes are test doubles that
replay public goldens or fixed logits; no learner solution is included.

Anti-cheat's contract checks exact packaging, JavaScript syntax, five public
offline runtime/control suites, sealed M1/order/seven-core workspace preparation
and blank-prediction refusal. It never starts HTTP/browser listeners and does
not establish complete learner exercises or capstone success.

## Sightline and two part-two courses

The configured matrix now also includes Sightline, Time-travel Debugger part two
and Anti-cheat Engineering part two. Each contract checks exact packaging,
JavaScript syntax, the documented setup command and the untouched starter's first
check, which must fail with a named "not written yet" message. None of the three
documents an export command, so no export stage is configured. Sightline's serve
command and its optional live model aren't run. These remain public interface
regressions, not complete learner solutions.

```

# License scope

Free to Learn makes its original course material available for learning, teaching, reuse and remixing, including commercial reuse. This grant covers only rights held by the project; it does not assert ownership of third-party material or create rights in uncopyrightable facts or public test values.

- **Original code: MIT.** Executable code, code examples, styling, configuration, schemas, and original technical fixture data accompanying the software use [MIT](LICENSES/MIT.txt). Retain the copyright and permission notice in copies or substantial portions of that software. This includes supplied code carried into a redistributed learner project.
- **Original lesson content: CC BY 4.0.** Lesson prose, instructions, questions, feedback, rubrics and original illustrations use [CC BY 4.0](LICENSES/CC-BY-4.0.txt). Credit Free to Learn, link to the license and identify modifications. Preserve applicable attribution/disclaimer notices, and do not imply endorsement. Commercial sharing and adaptations are permitted under those terms.
- **Mixed files have distinct parts, not a choice of licenses.** In Markdown/HTML/JSON/JavaScript containing both lessons and software, the original narrative lesson content is CC BY 4.0 and the executable code or code examples are MIT. A file extension does not relicense its other parts. Ordinary implementation comments belong to the code; embedded lesson explanations belong to the content.
- **Third-party exceptions take precedence.** Fonts, named pretrained assets, publisher material, public test-vector material and their notices retain their own terms and attribution. See [THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md](THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md) and the file-level [LICENSE-SCOPE.json](LICENSE-SCOPE.json). Our MIT/CC BY grant does not replace those terms.

The complete standard license texts control; this summary adds no restrictions. CC BY does not grant trademark/endorsement rights. Choosing these licenses is not a certification of every possible third-party right. Public-source delivery and course qualification are separate from licensing; consult QUALIFICATION.md for the current release status.

## Sightline and two part-two courses

Each of these courses was tested in four ways before release. Three fresh AI
learner runs per course worked from a learner copy, each with a different
starting instruction. A separate AI cold reader graded the lessons for
assumed context, and a writing pass edited the lessons and README. Then a bare
clone ran under an empty environment with Node 26.5.1 on macOS arm64. The
learners and readers were AI agents, not people.

Sightline's three runs each passed all eight modules and all ten levels. Its bare
clone ran 66 commands, with the starter and with the course's worked engine. One
lesson claim didn't reproduce and was fixed, and the 66 commands then ran without
a failure. Debugger part two's three runs each passed all 44 checks. Its bare
clone ran 48 commands after setup, and 3 piped debug.mjs sessions failed until
the input loop was fixed. Anti-cheat part two's three runs each passed all 34
checks and all 9 scoreboard budgets. Its bare clone ran init, the six starter
checks, the worked solution's check all and 47 lesson commands, all as the
lessons say. The worked solutions aren't published. In every course the
untouched starter failed each unit cleanly with a "not written yet" message.

The runs took 13 to 54 minutes, far below the courses' estimates in hours.
Passing checks shows working code, not that the lessons teach. In each course
the run that went straight to the exercises passed every check without opening
a lesson. Fixes from these runs are in the published text.

One more AI learner then took each fixed course in order from its download. Each
passed every check, and Sightline's climbed all ten levels. They found no garbled
text and no command that failed. They did find unclear sentences, which are
listed for the next update. Sightline's lesson page was opened once in a browser
and its first practice questions were answered there. Nothing else was tried in
a browser, and these runs didn't use Node 22.

`courses/adaptive-decision-engine/API.md`:

```md
# Function and evidence contracts

All work files are ordinary ES modules. Use named exports and relative imports to other work modules. `../shared.mjs` supplies immutable constants, targetAt, distance and hash. The independent-episode bound is supplied by ../uncertainty.mjs. `../game.mjs` supplies the authoritative engine. You may also import supplied `../control.mjs` (createController), `../fixtures.mjs` (fixtureTransport), `../resample.mjs` (pairedInterval), and `../data.mjs` (async loadData for dev/calibration/evaluation). These helpers use the same offline files in Node and the browser. Browser and terminal evaluate the same files. contracts.d.ts describes editor types without requiring a compiler.

## 01 · observe.mjs

`observe(state)` returns exactly public fields: episodeId, revision, round, health, supplies, charge, budget, lastKind (null initially), recentDamage (last three), recentMoves (last three), pressure, target and flags `{historyComplete, available}`. Pressure is null with fewer than three events or observationMissing. Otherwise use 0.6*(12-health)/12 + 0.4*min(1,sum(recentDamage)/6). Target comes from targetAt(profile, round). Do not leak seed, future hazards or bot plans. Do not mutate the state.

## 02 · constraints.mjs

`allowedActions(observation)` returns unique strings. At round 12 or health zero, return []. Otherwise include rest. Scout needs health >=4 and budget >=1; swarm health >=6 and budget >=2; brute health >=8 and budget >=3. Neither swarm nor brute may follow either high card. Return the complete set in any order.

## 03 · rules.mjs

`chooseRules(observation, memory={})` returns `{action:{kind}, memory:{recovering}, reason, origin:'rules'}`. The action must be legal, deterministic and meaningful for the beacon objective. Use target limits from the observation and explicit handling for unknown pressure. Public minimum: complete at least one of twelve seeded development episodes and expose encounters on at least 30% of the possible rounds. Other lawful heuristics are accepted.

## 04 · adapter.mjs

`buildRequest(observation, allowed, config={model:'fixture-v1',host:'offline'})` returns `{body,binding}`. Body includes model, canonical observation string as state, and questions.encounter with type choice, instructions and criteria keyed by allowed actions. Binding includes stateHash, questionHash, episodeId, revision, allowed, model, host, adapterVersion and requestId covering body plus the other binding fields.

`parseResponse(raw,request,current,origin='synthetic-fixture')` returns `{ok:true,action,distribution,score,binding,origin}` or `{ok:false,error}`. Read raw.answers.encounter, an object `{type, choice, probabilities, confidence}`, and require raw.model to equal the bound model. Require `type: 'choice'`; `choice`, the selected label, must be one of the legal actions; `probabilities` must have exactly the legal actions as keys, with finite values in [0,1] summing to one within 1e-9; and `confidence` must be a finite number in [0,1]. On success, `action` is `{kind: choice}`, `distribution` is `probabilities` and `score` is `confidence`. Example: `{type:'choice', choice:'scout', probabilities:{rest:0.3, scout:0.7}, confidence:0.68}`. Reject changed request body, question or current context. Distinguish stale, invalid-binding and invalid-response. Do not normalize malformed data.

## 05 · confidence.mjs

`fitCalibration(rows)` accepts only calibration rows with a nonempty episodeId/domain, unique `(episodeId, revision)`, integer revision, score in [0,1] and label 0/1. An episode must belong to one domain. Return version 2, the event/estimand description, a sorted domain list and `domains[domain] = {episodes, rows, bins}`. The three bins have edges 0,.5,.8,1.0000001. Each bin returns lo,hi,n,yes,episodes,p,rowRate,interval. Here n/yes count rows/events; p averages each participating episode's event fraction equally, while rowRate is yes/n. Empty bins have p:null.

Use supplied `episodeInterval(rates)` from `../uncertainty.mjs`. It applies a two-sided Hoeffding bound to independent episode summaries in [0,1], with alpha=.05: radius = sqrt(log(2/alpha)/(2*m)). This conditional claim requires independent, comparable episodes within the declared domain. The fixed synthetic corpus does not establish population coverage, and rows within one episode are not independent samples.

`brier(rows,predict)` returns mean squared forecast error. `select(proposal,table,domain,threshold=.65)` uses only the requested domain's bin. Require a valid score, at least ten distinct episodes, and lower interval endpoint >= threshold. Return use/reason plus domain, probability, interval and episode count when supported. Unknown domains, duplicate rows and scarce episode evidence cannot borrow strength from other domains. No universal threshold or model performance is implied.

## 06 · evaluate.mjs

Call supplied `auditEpisode(ep)` from `../audit.mjs` before measuring. A complete episode contains id,seed,profile,bot,events,decisions,final and termination='completed' or 'defeated'. Optional targetSchedule/requestLimit must match its initial environment. The auditor reconstructs every transition from the seed, checks before/after values, hazards, target, decision revision/action, independently derived violation arrays and final state/history. A healthy prefix, missing tail, altered final state or extra post-terminal transition is rejected. Recorded authority violations may be audited as deliberately faulty complete traces; they remain nonzero safety metrics and block adoption.

`metrics(ep)` computes survival,completion,distance,playedDistance,challenge,proposalViolations,executedViolations,fallbacks,calls,latencyMs,duplicateEffects,staleEffects. The fixed denominator is 12; unplayed rounds after an actual defeat contribute distance 1. Count rounds with nonempty violation arrays, sum reservations/latency/effects, and preserve zero versus missing evidence. The honest engine emits no executed violations; the fault controls prove that the metric does not erase them.

`compare(pairs)` validates unique matched IDs,seeds,bots,profiles,target schedules and request limits, and returns n, per-pair rows, mean differences and each bot/profile slice. Differences are candidate minus baseline. `recommend(report,gates)` returns rules,selective or collect-more-evidence using frozen maxCalls,completionLoss,survivalLoss,minDistanceGain. Any executed violation, duplicate effect, stale effect or exceeded request allowance blocks adoption. The supplied runner independently recomputes the report and rejects false counts or inconsistent recommendations. The fixture controller uses the frozen allowance, including zero.

### Comparison report shape

`compare(pairs)` takes a nonempty array of `{base, candidate}` episode pairs. Use these field names so the runner can consume your report:

- `n` is the number of pairs.
- `rows` contains one record per pair, in input order. Each record has `id` equal to `base.id`, `slice` equal to the bot name, a slash, and the profile name (for example, `cautious/pulse`), and the fields `base`, `candidate` and `difference`.
- `base` and `candidate` contain the corresponding complete `metrics(ep)` objects, with all twelve metric names listed above. Use `base` as the field name, even when your explanation calls it the baseline.
- `difference` contains candidate-minus-base values for every listed metric except `playedDistance`. Keep `playedDistance` in both episode metric objects; it is not included in the paired difference or aggregate means.
- `mean` averages each difference field across all pairs. `slices` maps each distinct `slice` string to `{n, mean}`, where `n` counts that slice's pairs and `mean` averages only their differences. The report retains both overall and per-slice evidence.

For example, the same `cautious/pulse` identity appears in a row's `slice` and in the matching `slices` entry; a row called only `profile: 'pulse'` cannot identify the bot/profile group. Report rows remain paired records, not individual rounds. The supplied runner adds `distanceInterval` afterward; your `compare` return does not need to compute it.

### Fallback counting

For this course, count one fallback for each recorded decision whose `reason` is **not** exactly one of `rules`, `challenge`, `recovery` or `supported`. Those four reasons contribute zero; every other reason contributes one. The comparison is case-sensitive. For example, `supported` contributes zero while `unavailable` or `invalid-response` contributes one, even when the executed action is legal. Read the recorded `reason`; neither `origin: 'rules'` nor an executed rest action alone determines this count. These are the existing course accounting labels, not a universal classification of fallback behavior.

## 07 · schedule.mjs

`reserve(state,context,now)` returns `{state,ticket}` or `{state,error}`. State fields: used,maxRequests,timeoutMs,serial,pending,armed. Refuse a second in-flight request and exhausted allowance. Increment used before dispatch. Ticket includes token, episodeId, revision and deadline. `settle(state,ticket,current,now,result)` clears matching pending and returns accepted plus proposal, or an error. Reject mismatched token/context and results at or after deadline. `expire(state,now)` clears an expired pending request without refunding used.

## 08 · scenarios.json and REPORT.md

Create `{version:1,cases:[...]}` with at least two distinct constructed interventions. Each case has id,hypothesis,health,budget,damageA,damageB. Damage arrays contain exactly three integers from 0 through 4. Health is 4..12 and budget 0..18. IDs and tested conditions must be unique; reversing the same history pair does not create a new case. The check builds equal-current-state snapshots and changes only past damage, then executes your observer and rules. Both cases must change the chosen encounter. Display-only changes must not. These are explicitly constructed counterfactuals, not claims of naturally observed episodes.

REPORT.md contains original failure, alternatives, intervention, negative control, source identities, results and remaining limits. Prose reasoning is reviewed by the rubric, not a keyword checker.

## 09 · director.mjs

`policy(state,memory={})` composes observation and your rules. `checkpoint(state,memory,scheduler,identities)` returns version 'beacon-keep/1', copies of state/memory, identities and scheduler with pending:null, armed:false; record invalidatedPending. `restore(record,identities)` rejects version/source/calibration mismatches and invalid game or budget state, returns fresh copies, and remains disarmed. Browser Save/Resume captures the already-selected encounter, its advanced policy memory and its episode/revision/source/mode binding. Resume restores that selected result without calling the policy again; resolving it then selects the next round once. This stored selection is completed data, not a pending network operation. Saving is disabled while a decision computation or game transition is in progress. CLI resume returns the selected result when present and never reevaluates it implicitly. A legacy checkpoint without a saved selection restores state/memory only; the browser offers an explicit Choose a new encounter action. The original unsaved encounter cannot be reconstructed reliably. Mode inference from session.game requires matching state and memory; an explicit mode choice takes precedence. Terminal writes update both checkpoint.json and the session ledger, and checkpoint.json is authoritative when both exist.

### Terminal checkpoint writer and identities

```sh
node lab.mjs checkpoint ./work --mode project --seed saved-expedition
node lab.mjs resume ./work
```

The writer runs one complete episode and saves its terminal state and final policy memory. `--mode rules` selects chooseRules; `--mode project` selects the learner-created policy. The default is rules. It records playMode as learner or project and writes checkpoint.json plus the session ledger. Resume uses the saved mode; an explicit `--mode rules` or `--mode project` overrides it. A legacy checkpoint lacking a bound mode requires an explicit choice unless a matching saved game state and memory establish the association. A terminal checkpoint has no next encounter. Browser Save checkpoint can instead retain the completed selection at the current game revision; export that session to carry it into the terminal.

For CLI compatibility, identities.source is SHA-256 of the UTF-8 JSON string produced from all current named work .mjs source entries, sorted by filename with localeCompare (the supplied bundle.mjs identity helper). identities.calibration is SHA-256 of the UTF-8 text of evaluation/calibration-data.json, including its exact whitespace (the supplied sha256 helper). The checkpoint writer computes both. Use those same values when constructing a record through the pure API for later CLI use. A changed source or calibration identity is refused; do not rewrite an old identity merely to suppress the refusal.

The project-plan.json sourceHash printed by `fingerprint` is a short project fingerprint for the capstone contract. It has a different purpose and encoding from the SHA-256 checkpoint identities. A pure API round trip with caller-supplied identity strings proves equality for those strings; CLI resume also checks compatibility with its independently computed values.

## 10 · project.mjs and project-plan.json

Create project.mjs yourself and export `policy(state,memory)`. Read the current target through your observation, including a supplied twelve-interval `state.targetSchedule`, and respect optional `state.requestLimit`. Outages set observationMissing on the current call. Return a legal rules fallback with reason='unavailable', origin='rules', and zero new calls when observation is unavailable. The reason must not be used on a normal measured state.

In the published final-round control, charge 12 is already secured and every candidate action survives both hazard values. There is no remaining-round tradeoff. Select an action minimizing the worst possible distance from the announced band under the documented fixed player. Tied optimal actions are all accepted. The low and high bands have different optima, so a target-blind health heuristic cannot pass. This is a bounded semantic check, not a general optimality requirement during the rest of the episode.

Create project-plan.json with version:1, sourceHash covering all current work/*.mjs (print it with `node lab.mjs fingerprint ./work`), adoption (rules/selective/collect-more-evidence), your nonempty rationale and limits, and at least two scenarios. Each scenario has unique id/seed, profile:'pulse', bot, a twelve-entry targetSchedule of valid [lo,hi] intervals, nonempty unique missingRounds in 0..11, and integer requestLimit in 0..2. The two contracts must differ in schedule, outage or allowance, not only names. Replace the REPORT.md starter with your own evidence account. The checker binds and executes the artifacts; it does not grade whether the written argument is persuasive. Use the separate rubric for that judgment.

The public check also retains the original meaningful-game minimum: at least one completion and 30% encounter exposure across twelve supplied cases. No model win is required. No complete project solution is supplied by support packs.

## Portable evidence files

Named exports include every listed work module plus REPORT.md, scenarios.json, project-plan.json, evaluation-plan.json, results.json and checkpoint.json. The browser creates plan/results/checkpoint from its controls. CLI freeze records source and gates; evaluate saves all event results. Freeze again only as a new experiment after a code change. Never copy credentials or arbitrary local files into these fields. Actual provider captures remain local and are not exported automatically.

Session storage restores the learner schema `{schema:1,sources,attempts,...}`. On disk, format 2 is `{schema:2,encoding:"source-text-table/1",texts,session}`. Format 3 uses `schema:3`, `encoding:"source-text-table/2"` and an additional `resultRefs` array of strictly increasing attempt indices. Each listed attempt stores a text-table index in its `result` field. That text must also be referenced as a current or historical `results.json` source and must contain a JSON `result` value. Parsing restores that value; all other attempt fields and every exact source string are unchanged. The writer uses a reference only when the original result has the exact same JSON serialization as the retained value. Unmatched results stay inline. Both stored and fully restored evidence count toward the existing limits; malformed, dangling or mixed-format references are rejected.

The scripted transport intentionally ignores question instruction semantics. `node generate-data.mjs WORKDIR NEWDIR` reproduces all 180 synthetic episodes using your adapter and observer. Changing prompt prose cannot turn this fixture into a model experiment.

`courses/adaptive-decision-engine/BRIDGE.md`:

```md
# Optional prerequisite bridge · 60–90 minutes estimated

This course assumes JavaScript functions, arrays, objects, ES modules, async/await, JSON and elementary averages. These tasks recommend practice; they do not lock navigation.

## Preserve the original

Explain why `{...state, health:state.health-2}` preserves the original object, while assigning state.health changes it. Create an object with a nested history array, copy it, append one event without changing the original, and test both lengths. A shallow object spread does not copy the nested array.

Worked reasoning: copy the outer object and create a new history array with the old elements plus the new event. Completion task: replace the event's damage without altering either original object or array. Independent task: keep two alternate next states from the same prefix.

## Wait and fail explicitly

An async function returns a promise. Await pauses that function until resolution or rejection. Make a promise that resolves to a number, then one that rejects with an Error. Use try/catch to preserve the failure reason. Independent task: race a result against a timeout and verify that a late result does not execute a second state change.

## Validate JSON shape

Parsing JSON establishes syntax, not correctness. Parse a record with probability 2; require a finite number between zero and one and reject it. Completion task: validate every entry and sum a two-choice distribution. Independent task: reject missing and extra action keys without depending on their order.

## Compute a weighted measure

For health 6 of 12, missing fraction is 0.5. Weight it by 0.6 to obtain 0.3. If recent damage is 3 of a normalizing 6, its weighted term is 0.2. Together they make 0.5. Independent task: compute the same formula at health 8 with damage sum 6. Expected relation: the health term is smaller while the damage term reaches its cap. Explain why missing history must remain unknown.

If any task needed help, use the matching support route and record that assistance. These prerequisites support the course; they are not graded as independent mastery of its later director.

# Beacon Keep · Adaptive Decision Engine

Build a director for a twelve-round expedition. The beacon is lit, and the expedition succeeds, when it survives all twelve rounds with a charge of 12 or more. Observe recent play, choose legal encounters, calibrate evidence, evaluate whole episodes and recover after interruption. A well-supported decision to keep rules is a successful outcome.

## Start

Extract the ZIP, open a terminal in this folder, then run:

```
node lab.mjs serve
```

Open the printed http://127.0.0.1 address. Stop with Ctrl-C. The server selects an available port by default; use --port 4317 to keep a stable browser origin. Browser drafts are stored by origin, including port. Export before changing origins.

Qualified terminal environment: Node 26.5.1 on macOS arm64. Browser checks are reported separately; physical-device and screen-reader support are not inferred from terminal checks. No package install, account, GPU, provider or network access is required for the core course. Node 22 and other operating systems have not been qualified. Reading and the supplied game need a browser; sustained implementation benefits from a desktop editor.

## Terminal workspace

```
node lab.mjs start ./work
node lab.mjs check 01 ./work --help-used none --prediction 'Pressure is unknown initially'
node lab.mjs play ./work --mode rules --seed demo-01 --bot fixed
node lab.mjs play --help
node lab.mjs status ./work
node lab.mjs support 04 ./work ./assisted-04
node lab.mjs fingerprint ./work
node lab.mjs freeze ./work
node lab.mjs evaluate ./work --manifest evaluation/dev.json --mode fixture
node lab.mjs evaluate ./work --manifest ./work/project-plan.json --mode project
node lab.mjs evaluate ./work --manifest evaluation/evaluation.json --mode project
node lab.mjs checkpoint ./work --mode project --seed saved-expedition
node lab.mjs resume ./work
node lab.mjs export ./work ./my-beacon.zip
node generate-data.mjs ./work ./new-synthetic-data
```

Start refuses an existing directory. Check 01 initially fails with an intentional TODO. Edit the named files, then rerun. Each failed case says what was checked, what your code produced, what was expected and which lesson section to reread; the full JSON record is printed first. `play` accepts `--bot fixed|cautious|aggressive` and `--profile steady|pulse`; `node lab.mjs play --help` lists its options. Use --variant 1 for a repeatable fresh public case. Work runs in a bounded worker with a ten-second deadline. Node code has ordinary local permissions; this is not a hostile-code sandbox.

`checkpoint` runs one complete episode with the selected rules or project policy and saves its terminal state, final policy memory, spent allowance, source/calibration identities and director mode. Use `--mode rules` for your rules policy or `--mode project` for your capstone; the default is rules. `resume` restores the saved result without another policy call. A browser checkpoint retains its selected encounter when exported. For a legacy checkpoint with no associated mode, choose explicitly with `node lab.mjs resume ./work --mode project` or `--mode rules`.

The short value from `fingerprint` belongs in project-plan.json. CLI checkpoints use separate SHA-256 source and calibration identities. Use the checkpoint writer above to create those bindings; a hand-built API record must use the same identities to be compatible with CLI resume. API.md §09 defines them.

Support creates a separate assisted directory, retains the original work and history, and supplies only earlier modules. Module 10 support never supplies project.mjs. The browser records support before replacing earlier layers in its current draft. Neither route counts supplied code as unaided work.

## Carry work between browser and terminal

Export my project ZIP includes current source, immutable attempt snapshots, result logs, optional checkpoint and session.json. Extract elsewhere and run the included lab.mjs with ./work. The exported work/.beacon/session.json preserves the same attempt trail as root session.json. The CLI also discovers root session.json when opening a legacy export at ./work. To make a separate named copy, import explicitly:

```
node lab.mjs import session.json ./imported-work
node lab.mjs check 03 ./imported-work --help-used imported
```

Import never merges histories heuristically. The browser keeps a backup before importing; the terminal requires a new target. A failed save refuses a new committed check. Results remain historical when source, question or course identity changes. A pending record after interruption is evidence of an incomplete run, not a pass. Checkpoints preserve the selected encounter as well as policy memory, so resume does not call the policy twice. A legacy checkpoint without that selection restores state only; choose a new encounter explicitly in the browser. The current checkpoint.json is authoritative over an older imported session copy.

## What is supplied

Game engine, authority, renderer, public checks, helpers, synthetic transport, event corpus, local HTTP transport and archive plumbing are supplied. You implement the director layers. Author controls, private review evidence and held-out assessments are excluded from the learner archive. Prior-layer support is explicitly labeled assistance.

See API.md for exact function and file contracts, RUBRIC.md for reasoning evidence, BRIDGE.md for prerequisites, and SOURCES.md for provenance. The course estimates 24–34.5 active hours plus an optional 60–90-minute bridge. Those are planning estimates; no human timing or learning gain is claimed.

## Optional provider status

The optional Node HTTP transport is mock-tested only. No live request was run during production. Use provider-config.example.json only after reviewing current documentation and costs. `node live.mjs provider-config.example.json ./work` is a dry run. Adding --arm explicitly enables a one-request smoke using LIQUID_API_KEY. The browser never reads it. A smoke is not a comparison, and strict monetary caps are refused without a verified billing bound. The required course is fully offline.

## Session storage and recovery

A saved or exported session keeps the exact text of every file you checked and every attempt's question, prediction, help, status and result. To keep the file small, it stores each distinct file text once and lets attempts point to it (format 2). Format 3 does the same for check results: when an attempt's result is identical to one already stored in a saved results.json, the attempt points to that copy instead of repeating it. Nothing is dropped; restoring gives back every attempt exactly. These tools read formats 1, 2 and 3. Older copies of the course tools cannot read format 3, so keep your original export before changing tools. Use `node lab.mjs import session.json NEWDIR` to restore an exported session, then the usual check commands.

The limits remain bounded: at most 1,000 attempts and 20 MB of stored UTF-8 JSON evidence, with a 128 MB expanded-evidence bound. Legacy pretty-printed format-1 input is limited to 40 MB. Existing per-work-file limits still apply. Distinct large evaluations can still reach the stored limit. Export before reaching it; after a capacity refusal, preserve the complete existing workspace before starting another session. Export also applies these limits and is not a capacity bypass. No attempts are removed automatically. Browser local-storage quotas may be smaller; a browser save failure does not establish that an export or later check was saved.

`courses/adaptive-decision-engine/RUBRIC.md`:

```md
# Evidence rubric

Code and reasoning are separate judgments. Public checks exercise stated behavioral contracts. They do not prove learning, independent transfer or production readiness.

For each claim, score 0 (absent or contradicted), 1 (partially supported), or 2 (supported by reproducible evidence):

1. Observation and constraints: distinguish public history from hidden future; explain a boundary case and preserve executor rejection.
2. Baseline and tradeoff: show meaningful completion and exposure, and a case where recovery helps one metric at a cost to another.
3. Uncertainty: name the calibrated event, split by episode, report per-domain row and distinct-episode counts, intervals and risk/coverage; handle domain shift without pooling it away.
4. Comparison: retain complete paired episodes, adverse slices, failures, interval and frozen adoption limits.
5. Diagnosis: preserve a controlled failure, a single-cause intervention, negative control and remaining alternative.
6. Release decision: choose rules, selective use or more evidence consistently with the frozen policy; reproduce export and recovery.

Every claim used to adopt a candidate needs level 2. A total cannot compensate for false provenance or a violated hard gate. A supported decision to retain rules passes the reasoning goal.

Strong example: “Our synthetic controller abstained on all eligible bins because their lower bounds missed the frozen threshold. Candidate outcomes matched rules while consuming four reservations per episode. We retain rules for this environment; this says nothing about a real provider.”

Weak example: “The model is safer because no player died.” This omits charge, exposure, pairing, origin and uncertainty. If the evidence is synthetic, calling it a model result is false.

Self-review is immediately available. Another assessor can review the same artifact without a service gate. Independent held-out transfer and human timing/learning remain unverified until corresponding trials occur.

# Sources and provenance

Beacon Keep mechanics, prose, exercises, diagrams, checks and synthetic events were authored for this course. Original SVG/CSS assets are included. The reference-to-render direction is restrained warm/cool contrast and clearly separated causal components; no reference images are distributed.

The local workflow adapts the accepted Tensor/Autograd course's preserved attempts, explicit earlier-layer support and positive export inventory. Its dependency-free stored ZIP writer and Markdown renderer were reused and extended within the same Ivy project. This is infrastructure reuse, not learner work or a new independent assessment.

Technical reading, checked 1 November 2026:

- Liquid d1 documentation: https://docs.liquid.ai/lfm/models/d1 — named typed request/response and optional raw HTTP boundary. Documentation support is not live qualification.
- Liquid decision models: https://docs.liquid.ai/lfm/models/decision-models — typed decisions. Vendor performance claims are not adopted as game evidence.
- Guo et al., On Calibration of Modern Neural Networks (2017): https://proceedings.mlr.press/v70/guo17a.html — calibration concept. Our event, bins and fallback policy are original teaching choices.
- Agarwal et al., Deep Reinforcement Learning at the Edge of the Statistical Precipice (2021): https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper/2021/hash/f514cec81cb148559cf475e7426eed5e-Abstract.html — uncertainty in evaluation. Applying whole-episode pairing here is a design choice, not a validated sample-size guarantee.

Synthetic corpus: 60 development, 60 calibration and 60 evaluation episodes. Scores are explicitly authored and labels are computed from actual subsequent game transitions. Full source request/response/event records are in evaluation/corpus.json. Seeds are disjoint by split. No provider, credential or real user behavior is represented in this corpus.

Public minimums and timing estimates are course design choices. Human engagement, retention, learning gain, real-provider performance, a physical phone and screen-reader behavior remain unmeasured. Author qualification is source-aware; it is not independent learner assessment.

The repaired uncertainty method uses Hoeffding, W. (1963), “Probability Inequalities for Sums of Bounded Random Variables,” Theorem 2: https://www.cs.rpi.edu/academics/courses/spring06/random/hoefding.pdf . The two-sided bound is applied to independent episode summaries within a named domain; it is not a pooled row-level Wilson claim. Its assumptions and synthetic-data limitations are taught explicitly.

`courses/adaptive-decision-engine/assessment-fixtures.mjs`:

```mjs
import {episode,initial,violations} from './game.mjs';
import {replayRecordedStep} from './audit.mjs';
export function makeDefeatFixture(seed='audit-defeat'){
 let state=initial(seed,'steady',seed);const decisions=[];
 while(!state.terminal){
  const why=violations(state,'brute');const next=replayRecordedStep(state,'brute','press');
  decisions.push({proposed:'brute',executed:'brute',proposalViolations:why,executedViolations:why,reason:'supported',calls:1,latencyMs:2,origin:'constructed-authority-fault',revision:state.revision});state=next.state;
 }
 return {id:seed,seed,profile:'steady',bot:'constructed-fault',termination:'defeated',events:state.history,decisions,final:state};
}
export function makeCountFixture(seed='audit-counts'){
 return episode(state=>({action:{kind:'brute'},memory:{},reason:state.round%2?'timeout':'unavailable',calls:state.round%3,latencyMs:state.round+.25,origin:'synthetic-fixture'}),{seed});
}

`courses/adaptive-decision-engine/assessment.mjs`:

```mjs
// Supplied independent assessment oracle; learner metrics are checked against raw transitions.
import {auditEpisode} from './audit.mjs';
const keys=['survival','completion','distance','playedDistance','challenge','proposalViolations','executedViolations','fallbacks','calls','latencyMs','duplicateEffects','staleEffects'];
export function expectedMetrics(ep){
 auditEpisode(ep);let loss=12-ep.events.length,challenge=0,proposalViolations=0,executedViolations=0,fallbacks=0,calls=0,latencyMs=0,duplicateEffects=0,staleEffects=0;
 for(let i=0;i<ep.events.length;i++){
  const e=ep.events[i],d=ep.decisions[i];loss+=Math.max(e.target[0]-e.pressure,0,e.pressure-e.target[1]);challenge+=Number(e.kind!=='rest');proposalViolations+=Number(d.proposalViolations.length>0);executedViolations+=Number(d.executedViolations.length>0);fallbacks+=Number(!['rules','challenge','recovery','supported'].includes(d.reason));calls+=d.calls;latencyMs+=d.latencyMs;duplicateEffects+=d.duplicateEffects||0;staleEffects+=d.staleEffects||0;
 }
 const alive=Number(ep.final.health>0),n=ep.events.length;
 return {survival:alive,completion:Number(alive&&n===12&&ep.final.charge>=12),distance:loss/12,playedDistance:(loss-(12-n))/n,challenge:challenge/12,proposalViolations,executedViolations,fallbacks,calls,latencyMs,duplicateEffects,staleEffects};
}
export function expectedComparison(pairs){
 if(!pairs.length||new Set(pairs.map(p=>p.base.id)).size!==pairs.length)throw Error('nonempty unique pairs required');
 const rows=pairs.map(({base,candidate})=>{
  for(const key of ['id','seed','bot','profile','targetSchedule','requestLimit'])if(JSON.stringify(base[key])!==JSON.stringify(candidate[key]))throw Error('unpaired '+key);
  const a=expectedMetrics(base),b=expectedMetrics(candidate);
  return {id:base.id,slice:base.bot+'/'+base.profile,base:a,candidate:b,difference:Object.fromEntries(keys.filter(k=>k!=='playedDistance').map(k=>[k,b[k]-a[k]]))};
 });
 const average=xs=>Object.fromEntries(Object.keys(xs[0].difference).map(k=>[k,xs.reduce((s,x)=>s+x.difference[k],0)/xs.length]));
 return {n:rows.length,rows,mean:average(rows),slices:Object.fromEntries([...new Set(rows.map(r=>r.slice))].sort().map(slice=>{const xs=rows.filter(r=>r.slice===slice);return [slice,{n:xs.length,mean:average(xs)}];}))};
}
function matches(actual,expected,path){
 if(typeof expected==='number'){if(!Number.isFinite(actual)||Math.abs(actual-expected)>1e-9)throw Error('incorrect metric: '+path);return;}
 if(expected===null){if(actual!==null)throw Error('incorrect null metric: '+path);return;}
 if(typeof expected!=='object'){if(actual!==expected)throw Error('incorrect report identity: '+path);return;}
 if(!actual||Array.isArray(actual)!==Array.isArray(expected))throw Error('missing report field: '+path);
 if(Array.isArray(expected)&&actual.length!==expected.length)throw Error('missing report rows: '+path);
 for(const [key,value]of Object.entries(expected))matches(actual[key],value,path+'.'+key);
}
export function verifyMetrics(actual,ep){matches(actual,expectedMetrics(ep),'metrics');return true;}
export function verifyComparison(report,pairs){matches(report,expectedComparison(pairs),'report');return true;}
export function expectedRecommendation(report,gates){
 if(report.rows.some(r=>r.candidate.executedViolations||r.candidate.duplicateEffects||r.candidate.staleEffects||r.candidate.calls>gates.maxCalls))return 'rules';
 if(Object.values(report.slices).some(s=>s.mean.completion< -gates.completionLoss||s.mean.survival< -gates.survivalLoss))return 'rules';
 return report.mean.distance<=-gates.minDistanceGain?'selective':'collect-more-evidence';
}

```mjs
import {CARDS,copy,canonical,targetAt} from './shared.mjs';
import {initial,hazard,violations} from './game.mjs';
const fail=message=>{throw Error('invalid episode: '+message);};
const equal=(a,b)=>canonical(a)===canonical(b);
// Audit physics can reconstruct a recorded authority violation. It never commits a game action.
export function replayRecordedStep(state,kind,move){
 const card=CARDS[kind];if(!card)fail('unknown executed action');
 if(state.terminal)fail('transition after termination');
 const s=copy(state),before={health:s.health,supplies:s.supplies,charge:s.charge,budget:s.budget};
 let damage=0,charge=0,h=null;
 if(kind==='rest'){if(move!=='rest')fail('rest move mismatch');s.health=Math.min(12,s.health+2);s.supplies=Math.min(4,s.supplies+1);}
 if(kind!=='rest'){
  if(!['press','brace','repair'].includes(move))fail('unknown player move');
  h=hazard(s.seed,s.round);damage=card.threat+h;charge=card.reward;
  if(move==='brace'){damage=Math.max(0,damage-2);charge=Math.max(0,charge-1);}
  if(move==='repair'){if(!s.supplies)fail('repair without supply');s.supplies--;s.health=Math.min(12,s.health+3);damage=Math.max(0,damage-1);charge=0;}
  s.health=Math.max(0,s.health-damage);s.charge+=charge;
 }
 s.budget-=card.cost;
 if(s.budget<0)fail('negative recorded budget');
 const pressure=.6*(12-s.health)/12+.4*Math.min(1,[...s.history.slice(-2).map(e=>e.damage),damage].reduce((a,b)=>a+b,0)/6);
 const event={round:s.round,revision:s.revision,kind,move,hazard:h,damage,charge,before,after:{health:s.health,supplies:s.supplies,charge:s.charge,budget:s.budget},pressure,target:targetAt(s.profile,s.round,s.targetSchedule)};
 s.round++;s.revision++;s.terminal=s.health===0||s.round===12;s.history.push(event);
 return {state:s,event};
}
export function auditEpisode(ep){
 if(!ep||typeof ep.id!=='string'||!ep.id||typeof ep.seed!=='string'||!Array.isArray(ep.events)||!Array.isArray(ep.decisions)||ep.events.length!==ep.decisions.length||!ep.events.length||ep.events.length>12)fail('identity or event/decision count');
 if(!['steady','pulse'].includes(ep.profile)||typeof ep.bot!=='string'||!ep.bot)fail('unknown episode environment');
 let state=initial(ep.seed,ep.profile,ep.id,{targetSchedule:ep.targetSchedule,requestLimit:ep.requestLimit});
 for(let i=0;i<ep.events.length;i++){
  const event=ep.events[i],d=ep.decisions[i];
  if(d.revision!==state.revision||d.executed!==event.kind)fail('decision/revision mismatch at '+i);
  if(!Number.isInteger(d.calls)||d.calls<0||!Number.isFinite(d.latencyMs)||d.latencyMs<0)fail('invalid request accounting at '+i);
  for(const key of ['duplicateEffects','staleEffects'])if(d[key]!==undefined&&(!Number.isInteger(d[key])||d[key]<0))fail('invalid effect counter');
  const proposed=violations(state,d.proposed),executed=violations(state,event.kind);
  if(!equal(d.proposalViolations,proposed)||!equal(d.executedViolations,executed))fail('inconsistent violation accounting at '+i);
  const next=replayRecordedStep(state,event.kind,event.move);
  if(!equal(event,next.event))fail('transition discontinuity or altered event at '+i);
  state=next.state;
 }
 if(!state.terminal)fail('nonterminal prefix is not a complete episode');
 const termination=state.health===0?'defeated':'completed';
 if(ep.termination!==termination)fail('terminal reason mismatch');
 if(!ep.final||!equal(ep.final,state))fail('final state/history mismatch');
 return true;
}

import {zipFiles} from './zip.mjs';
import {canonical} from './shared.mjs';

export async function sha256(text){const buffer=await crypto.subtle.digest('SHA-256',new TextEncoder().encode(text));return [...new Uint8Array(buffer)].map(b=>b.toString(16).padStart(2,'0')).join('');}
export async function identity(sources){return sha256(JSON.stringify(Object.entries(sources).sort(([a],[b])=>a.localeCompare(b))));}
// Formats 2/3 intern exact source strings; format 3 also references matching
// attempt results inside retained results.json texts. The learner schema stays 1.
// Limits are bytes of UTF-8 JSON, including escaping. No history is discarded.
export const SESSION_INPUT_LIMIT=40000000; // Legacy pretty-printed exports may exceed 20 MB on disk.
const STORED_LIMIT=20000000, EXPANDED_LIMIT=128000000, MAX_ATTEMPTS=1000;
const encoding='source-text-table/1', resultEncoding='source-text-table/2', encoder=new TextEncoder();
function resultFromText(text){
 try{const value=JSON.parse(text);if(record(value)&&Object.hasOwn(value,'result'))return {value:value.result,key:JSON.stringify(value.result)};}catch{}
 return null;
}
const jsonBytes=value=>encoder.encode(JSON.stringify(value)).length;
const record=value=>value!==null&&typeof value==='object'&&!Array.isArray(value);
function sourceEntries(sources){
 if(!record(sources))throw Error('Invalid source snapshot');
 const entries=Object.entries(sources);
 for(const [name,text] of entries){
  if(!WORK_FILES.includes(name)||typeof text!=='string'||text.length>(name==='results.json'?8000000:200000))throw Error('Unexpected or oversized work file');
 }
 return entries;
}
function packedSession(session){
 if(session?.schema!==1||!Array.isArray(session.attempts)||session.attempts.length>MAX_ATTEMPTS)throw Error('Invalid session schema');
 const texts=[],indices=new Map(),lengths=[],resultTexts=new Map();
 let expansion=0;
 const refs=sources=>Object.fromEntries(sourceEntries(sources).map(([name,text])=>{
  let index=indices.get(text);
  if(index===undefined){index=texts.length;indices.set(text,index);texts.push(text);lengths.push(jsonBytes(text));}
  if(name==='results.json'&&!resultTexts.has(index)){const result=resultFromText(text);if(result)resultTexts.set(index,result);}
  expansion+=lengths[index]-String(index).length;
  if(expansion>EXPANDED_LIMIT)throw Error('Session exceeds 128 MB expanded evidence limit');
  return [name,index];
 }));
 const sources=refs(session.sources);
 const attempts=session.attempts.map(a=>{
  if(!record(a)||!a.id||!a.sourceHash||!a.question||!a.help)throw Error('Invalid attempt history');
  return {...a,sources:refs(a.sources)};
 });
 // Match exact JSON values, never heuristically merge results or rewrite source text.
 const byResult=new Map([...resultTexts].map(([index,result])=>[result.key,index])),resultRefs=[];
 for(let i=0;i<attempts.length;i++){
  const a=attempts[i],key=Object.hasOwn(a,'result')?JSON.stringify(a.result):undefined,index=byResult.get(key);
  if(index!==undefined){resultRefs.push(i);expansion+=jsonBytes(a.result)-String(index).length;a.result=index;}
 }
 const saved={...session,sources,attempts};
 if(jsonBytes(saved)+expansion>EXPANDED_LIMIT)throw Error('Session exceeds 128 MB expanded evidence limit');
 const packed=resultRefs.length?{schema:3,encoding:resultEncoding,texts,resultRefs,session:saved}:{schema:2,encoding,texts,session:saved};
 const text=JSON.stringify(packed);
 if(encoder.encode(text).length>STORED_LIMIT)throw Error('Session exceeds 20 MB stored evidence limit; preserve the existing workspace before starting a new session');
 return text;
}
export function validateSession(session){packedSession(session);return session;}
export function serializeSession(session){return packedSession(session);}
export function parseSession(text){
 if(typeof text!=='string'||encoder.encode(text).length>SESSION_INPUT_LIMIT)throw Error('Session input exceeds 40 MB');
 const input=JSON.parse(text);
 if(input?.schema===1)return validateSession(input);
 const resultFormat=input?.schema===3&&input.encoding===resultEncoding;
 if((!(input?.schema===2&&input.encoding===encoding)&&!resultFormat)||!Array.isArray(input.texts)||!record(input.session)||input.session.schema!==1)throw Error('Invalid session storage format');
 if(encoder.encode(text).length>STORED_LIMIT)throw Error('Session exceeds 20 MB stored evidence limit');
 if(!Array.isArray(input.session.attempts)||input.session.attempts.length>MAX_ATTEMPTS||input.texts.length>(MAX_ATTEMPTS+1)*WORK_FILES.length)throw Error('Invalid session schema');
 if(!resultFormat&&Object.hasOwn(input,'resultRefs'))throw Error('Invalid result references');
 const resultRefs=resultFormat?input.resultRefs:[];
 if(!Array.isArray(resultRefs)||resultRefs.some((index,i)=>!Number.isInteger(index)||index<0||index>=input.session.attempts.length||(i>0&&index<=resultRefs[i-1])))throw Error('Invalid result references');
 const used=new Set(),unique=new Set(),lengths=[],resultTexts=new Map();
 for(const value of input.texts){
  if(typeof value!=='string'||value.length>8000000||unique.has(value))throw Error('Invalid source text table');
  unique.add(value);lengths.push(jsonBytes(value));
 }
 let expanded=jsonBytes(input.session);
 const restore=refs=>{
  if(!record(refs))throw Error('Invalid source references');
  return Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(refs).map(([name,index])=>{
   if(!WORK_FILES.includes(name)||!Number.isInteger(index)||index<0||index>=input.texts.length)throw Error('Invalid source reference');
   expanded+=lengths[index]-String(index).length;
   if(expanded>EXPANDED_LIMIT)throw Error('Session exceeds 128 MB expanded evidence limit');
   if(name==='results.json'&&!resultTexts.has(index)){const result=resultFromText(input.texts[index]);if(result)resultTexts.set(index,result);}
   used.add(index);return [name,input.texts[index]];
  }));
 };
 const sources=restore(input.session.sources);
 const attempts=input.session.attempts.map(a=>{
  if(!record(a))throw Error('Invalid attempt history');
  return {...a,sources:restore(a.sources)};
 });
 for(const i of resultRefs){
  const a=attempts[i],index=a.result,result=resultTexts.get(index);
  if(!Number.isInteger(index)||!result)throw Error('Invalid result reference');
  expanded+=jsonBytes(result.value)-String(index).length;
  if(expanded>EXPANDED_LIMIT)throw Error('Session exceeds 128 MB expanded evidence limit');
  a.result=structuredClone(result.value);
 }
 if(used.size!==input.texts.length)throw Error('Unreferenced source text');
 return validateSession({...input.session,sources,attempts});
}

export async function exportZip(publicFiles,session){validateSession(session);const current=currentCheckpoint(session);if(current)session={...session,checkpoint:current,sources:{...session.sources,'checkpoint.json':JSON.stringify(current,null,2)}};const files=Object.entries(publicFiles);for(const [name,content]of Object.entries(session.sources)){const saved=session.lastEvaluation&&name==='results.json'?session.attempts.find(a=>a.id===session.lastEvaluation):null;files.push(['work/'+name,saved?JSON.stringify({plan:session.plan,result:saved.result},null,2):content]);}const saved=serializeSession(session);files.push(['session.json',saved],['work/.beacon/session.json',saved]);if(session.checkpoint&&!('checkpoint.json' in session.sources))files.push(['work/checkpoint.json',JSON.stringify(session.checkpoint,null,2)]);const inventory=await Promise.all(files.map(async([name,content])=>({name,sha256:await sha256(content),bytes:new TextEncoder().encode(content).length})));files.push(['export-manifest.json',JSON.stringify({schema:1,sourceHash:await identity(session.sources),files:inventory},null,2)]);return zipFiles(files);}

export function checkpointMode(record,{explicitMode,game}={}){
 const allowed=['demo','learner','project'];
 if(record.playMode!==undefined&&!allowed.includes(record.playMode))throw Error('Checkpoint has an invalid director mode');
 if(explicitMode!==undefined&&explicitMode!==null){if(!allowed.includes(explicitMode))throw Error('Invalid explicit director mode');return explicitMode;}

 const sameState=game?.state&&canonical(game.state)===canonical(record.state);
 const sameMemory=game&&canonical(game.memory)===canonical(record.memory);
 if(sameState&&sameMemory&&allowed.includes(game.mode))return game.mode;

}

 }

export function calibrationReport(c,calibration,evaluation,threshold=.65){
 const table=c.fitCalibration(calibration),reports=[];
 for(const domain of [...new Set(evaluation.map(r=>r.domain))].sort()){
  const rows=evaluation.filter(r=>r.domain===domain),training=calibration.filter(r=>r.domain===domain),slice=table.domains[domain];
  const mapped=rows.filter(r=>slice?.bins.some(b=>r.score>=b.lo&&r.score<b.hi&&b.p!==null));
  const chosen=rows.filter(r=>c.select({ok:true,score:r.score},table,domain,threshold).use);
  const prevalence=training.length?training.reduce((n,r)=>n+r.label,0)/training.length:null;
  reports.push({domain,rows:rows.length,episodes:new Set(rows.map(r=>r.episodeId)).size,events:rows.reduce((n,r)=>n+r.label,0),rawBrier:c.brier(rows,r=>r.score),mappedRows:mapped.length,mappedBrier:mapped.length?c.brier(mapped,r=>slice.bins.find(b=>r.score>=b.lo&&r.score<b.hi).p):null,prevalenceBrier:prevalence===null?null:c.brier(rows,()=>prevalence),selected:chosen.length,coverage:chosen.length/rows.length,risk:chosen.length?chosen.reduce((n,r)=>n+1-r.label,0)/chosen.length:null});
 }
 return {table,rows:calibration.length,evaluationRows:evaluation.length,threshold,domains:reports};
}

```ts
export type Kind='rest'|'scout'|'swarm'|'brute';
export type Action={kind:Kind};
export interface Observation {episodeId:string;revision:number;round:number;health:number;supplies:number;charge:number;budget:number;lastKind:Kind|null;recentDamage:number[];recentMoves:string[];pressure:number|null;target:[number,number];flags:{historyComplete:boolean;available:boolean}}
export interface Choice {action:Action;memory:{recovering:boolean};reason?:string;origin?:'rules'|'synthetic-fixture'|'recorded'|'live'}
export interface Request {body:{model:string;state:string;questions:Record<string,unknown>};binding:{requestId:string;stateHash:string;questionHash:string;episodeId:string;revision:number;allowed:Kind[];model:string;host:string;adapterVersion:string}}
export type Proposal={ok:true;action:Action;distribution:Record<Kind,number>;binding:Request['binding'];origin:string}|{ok:false;error:string};
export interface Reservation {token:number;episodeId:string;revision:number;deadline:number}
export interface Scheduler {used:number;maxRequests:number;timeoutMs:number;serial:number;pending:Reservation|null;armed:boolean}

// Runtime recovery metadata is supplied; it does not serialize network promises.
export type PlayMode='demo'|'learner'|'project';
export interface SavedSelection {version:1;episodeId:string;revision:number;stateHash:string;memoryHash:string;source:string;playMode:PlayMode;decisionHash:string;decision:Choice & {proposed?:Kind;executed:Kind;violation:boolean}}
export interface RuntimeRecovery {version:1;phase:'selected'|'unselected'|'terminal';selection:SavedSelection|null}

`courses/adaptive-decision-engine/control.mjs`:

```mjs
// Supplied orchestration; the course-owned policies are injected.
export function createController(modules,{transport,table,domain='fixed/steady',maxRequests=4,timeoutMs=25,now=()=>performance.now(),setTimer=setTimeout,clearTimer=clearTimeout,onEvent=()=>{}}) {
 let scheduler={used:0,maxRequests,timeoutMs,serial:0,pending:null,armed:false},latest=null;
 const sch=modules['schedule.mjs'],ad=modules['adapter.mjs'],cf=modules['confidence.mjs'];
 function fallback(obs,memory,reason,calls=0,latencyMs=0){return {...modules['rules.mjs'].chooseRules(obs,memory),reason,origin:'synthetic-fixture',calls,latencyMs};}
 async function decide(state,memory={}) {
  const obs=modules['observe.mjs'].observe(state);latest={episodeId:obs.episodeId,revision:obs.revision};const allowed=modules['constraints.mjs'].allowedActions(obs);
  if(!obs.flags.available)return fallback(obs,memory,'unavailable');
  const started=now(),reservation=sch.reserve(scheduler,latest,started);scheduler=reservation.state;if(!reservation.ticket)return fallback(obs,memory,reservation.error);
  const request=ad.buildRequest(obs,allowed,{model:'fixture-v1',host:'offline'}),ticket=reservation.ticket;
  let timer,finished=false;
  const wait=new Promise(resolve=>{timer=setTimer(()=>resolve({timeout:true}),timeoutMs);});
  const response=Promise.resolve().then(()=>transport(request)).then(raw=>({raw}),()=>({error:'unavailable'}));
  response.then(()=>{if(finished)onEvent({kind:'late-response-discarded',token:ticket.token});});
  const arrived=await Promise.race([response,wait]);finished=true;clearTimer(timer);
  if(arrived.timeout){scheduler=sch.expire(scheduler,ticket.deadline);onEvent({kind:'timeout',token:ticket.token});return fallback(obs,memory,'timeout',1,timeoutMs);}
  const parsed=arrived.error?{ok:false,error:arrived.error}:ad.parseResponse(arrived.raw,request,obs,'synthetic-fixture');
  const settled=sch.settle(scheduler,ticket,latest,now(),parsed);scheduler=settled.state;
  if(!settled.accepted)return fallback(obs,memory,settled.error,1,now()-started);
  const selection=cf.select(parsed,table,domain);
  if(!selection.use)return fallback(obs,memory,selection.reason,1,now()-started);
  return {action:parsed.action,memory,reason:'supported',origin:'synthetic-fixture',calls:1,latencyMs:now()-started};
 }
 return {decide,getState:()=>structuredClone(scheduler),restore:s=>{scheduler={...structuredClone(s),pending:null,armed:false};latest=null;}};
}

import {fixtureTransport} from './fixtures.mjs';
import {pairedInterval} from './resample.mjs';
export async function runEvaluation(modules,manifest,mode='rules',gates={maxCalls:2,completionLoss:0,survivalLoss:0,minDistanceGain:.02}) {
 if(!['rules','fixture','project'].includes(mode))throw Error('evaluation mode must be rules, fixture or project');
 if(!manifest?.episodes?.length||new Set(manifest.episodes.map(e=>e.id)).size!==manifest.episodes.length)throw Error('frozen unique episode manifest required');
 if(!Number.isInteger(gates.maxCalls)||gates.maxCalls<0||gates.maxCalls>20||['completionLoss','survivalLoss','minDistanceGain'].some(k=>!Number.isFinite(gates[k])||gates[k]<0))throw Error('invalid frozen evaluation gates');
 const baseline=(s,m)=>modules['rules.mjs'].chooseRules(modules['observe.mjs'].observe(s),m);
 const data=await (typeof process==='undefined'?fetch(new URL('./evaluation/calibration-data.json',import.meta.url)).then(r=>r.json()):import('node:fs/promises').then(fs=>fs.readFile(new URL('./evaluation/calibration-data.json',import.meta.url),'utf8')).then(JSON.parse));
 const table=modules['confidence.mjs'].fitCalibration(data),pairs=[];
 for(const spec of manifest.episodes){const environment={...spec,requestLimit:Math.min(spec.requestLimit??gates.maxCalls,gates.maxCalls)},base=await episode(baseline,environment),controller=createController(modules,{transport:fixtureTransport,table,domain:spec.bot+'/'+spec.profile,maxRequests:environment.requestLimit,now:()=>0});const candidate=mode==='project'?modules['project.mjs'].policy:mode==='fixture'?controller.decide:baseline;const result=await episode(candidate,environment);pairs.push({base,candidate:result});}
 const report=modules['evaluate.mjs'].compare(pairs);verifyComparison(report,pairs);const recommendation=modules['evaluate.mjs'].recommend(report,gates);if(recommendation!==expectedRecommendation(report,gates))throw Error('recommendation contradicts validated report and frozen gates');return {recommendation,gates,origin:mode==='fixture'?'synthetic-fixture':mode==='project'?'learner-project':'rules',warning:'No real model was called. Synthetic comparisons do not qualify a provider.',manifest,report:{...report,distanceInterval:pairedInterval(report.rows)},pairs};
}

`courses/adaptive-decision-engine/feedback.mjs`:

```mjs
// Learner-facing summaries of check results and progress. Pure functions shared by the browser and terminal.
import {escape} from './render.mjs';

const UNITS = Array.from({length: 10}, (_, i) => String(i + 1).padStart(2, '0'));
const list = ids => ids.join(', ');

// attempts: saved session attempts; currentHash: identity of the current work files; build: current course build.
export function progressSummary(attempts, currentHash, build) {
  const passes = attempts.filter(a => a.result?.passed === true && UNITS.includes(a.result?.unit));
  const ever = UNITS.filter(u => passes.some(a => a.result.unit === u));
  const current = ever.filter(u => passes.some(a => a.result.unit === u && a.sourceHash === currentHash && a.build === build));
  const recheck = ever.filter(u => !current.includes(u));
  if (!ever.length) return {ever, current, recheck, text: 'No unit check has passed yet. Each passing check is saved with the files it ran on.'};
  const parts = ['Units passed at least once: ' + ever.length + ' of 10 (' + list(ever) + ').'];
  if (!recheck.length) parts.push('All of them pass with your current files.');
  else {
    parts.push(current.length ? 'Passing with your current files: ' + list(current) + '.' : 'None has been checked since your latest edit.');
    parts.push('Recheck after your latest edit: ' + list(recheck) + '. Earlier passes stay in your history.');
  }
  return {ever, current, recheck, text: parts.join(' ')};
}

function caseLines(r) {
  const verdict = r.pass ? 'Pass' : 'Fail';
  const why = r.pass ? '' : '<p class="case-message">' + escape(r.message || ('Observed ' + JSON.stringify(r.actual) + ', expected ' + JSON.stringify(r.expected) + '.')) + '</p>';
  // Current messages end with their own "Reread ..." pointer; older saved results only carry repair.
  const where = r.pass || /Reread /.test(r.message || '') ? '' : '<p class="case-reread">Reread: ' + escape(r.section || r.repair || '') + '</p>';
  return '<li class="case ' + (r.pass ? 'pass' : 'fail') + '"><p class="case-head"><span class="case-verdict">' + verdict + '</span> ' + escape(r.label) + '</p>' + why + where + '</li>';
}

// Returns HTML for a check result: a heading with the count and one item per case.
export function resultHtml(result, error) {
  if (error) return '<p class="result-summary fail">The check could not run: ' + escape(error) + '</p>';
  if (!result || !Array.isArray(result.results)) return '';
  const passed = result.results.filter(r => r.pass).length, total = result.results.length;
  const head = '<p class="result-summary ' + (result.passed ? 'pass' : 'fail') + '">Unit ' + escape(result.unit) + ', variant ' + escape(result.variant) + ': ' + passed + ' of ' + total + ' cases passed.</p>';
  return head + '<ol class="cases">' + result.results.map(caseLines).join('') + '</ol>';
}

// Plain-text lines for the terminal, printed after the JSON record.
export function resultText(result) {
  if (!result || !Array.isArray(result.results)) return '';
  const passed = result.results.filter(r => r.pass).length;
  const lines = ['Unit ' + result.unit + ', variant ' + result.variant + ': ' + passed + ' of ' + result.results.length + ' cases passed.'];
  for (const r of result.results) {
    lines.push((r.pass ? 'PASS ' : 'FAIL ') + r.label);
    if (!r.pass) lines.push('     ' + (r.message || ('observed ' + JSON.stringify(r.actual) + ', expected ' + JSON.stringify(r.expected))));
  }
  return lines.join('\n');
}

```

`courses/adaptive-decision-engine/fixtures.mjs`:

```mjs
import {hash} from './shared.mjs';
export function fixtureResponse(request,kind='valid') {
 const obs=JSON.parse(request.body.state),allowed=request.binding.allowed;
 const pick=allowed.includes('scout')?'scout':'rest',index=parseInt(hash([obs.episodeId,obs.revision,'synthetic-score']),16)%3,score=[.35,.68,.92][index];
 const probabilities=Object.fromEntries(allowed.map(k=>[k,k===pick?(allowed.length===1?1:.7):(allowed.length===1?0:.3/(allowed.length-1))]));
 const response={model:request.binding.model,answers:{encounter:{type:'choice',choice:pick,probabilities,confidence:score}},usage:{input_tokens:null,output_tokens:null}};
 if(kind==='wrong-question')response.answers={recovery:response.answers.encounter};if(kind==='wrong-model')response.model='unrequested-model';if(kind==='invalid-sum')response.answers.encounter.probabilities[pick]=1.2;
 return response;
}
export const fixtureTransport=async request=>fixtureResponse(request);

```

`courses/adaptive-decision-engine/game.mjs`:

```mjs
import {ACTIONS,CARDS,copy,hash,targetAt} from './shared.mjs';
export function initial(seed='demo-01',profile='steady',episodeId=seed,options={}){const extra={};if(options.targetSchedule!==undefined)extra.targetSchedule=copy(options.targetSchedule);if(options.requestLimit!==undefined)extra.requestLimit=options.requestLimit;return {...extra,episodeId,seed,profile,round:0,revision:0,health:12,supplies:2,charge:0,budget:18,history:[],terminal:false};}
export function validate(s){for(const [k,max] of [['health',12],['supplies',4],['charge',100],['budget',18],['round',12],['revision',12]])if(!Number.isInteger(s[k])||s[k]<0||s[k]>max)throw Error('invalid state: '+k);if(s.round!==s.revision||s.history.length!==s.round)throw Error('invalid state: history/revision');if(s.targetSchedule!==undefined&&(!Array.isArray(s.targetSchedule)||s.targetSchedule.length!==12||s.targetSchedule.some(p=>!Array.isArray(p)||p.length!==2||!p.every(Number.isFinite)||p[0]<0||p[1]>1||p[0]>p[1])))throw Error('invalid target schedule');if(s.requestLimit!==undefined&&(!Number.isInteger(s.requestLimit)||s.requestLimit<0||s.requestLimit>20))throw Error('invalid request limit');}
export function violations(s,kind){const why=[];if(!ACTIONS.includes(kind))return ['unknown-action'];if(s.terminal||s.round>=12||s.health<=0)return ['terminal'];if(kind==='rest')return why;if(CARDS[kind].cost>s.budget)why.push('budget');if(s.health<=3)why.push('recovery-only');if(kind==='swarm'&&s.health<6)why.push('swarm-health');if(kind==='brute'&&s.health<8)why.push('brute-health');if(['swarm','brute'].includes(kind)&&['swarm','brute'].includes(s.history.at(-1)?.kind))why.push('high-cooldown');return why;}
export const legal=s=>ACTIONS.filter(k=>violations(s,k).length===0);
export const hazard=(seed,round)=>parseInt(hash([seed,round,'hazard']),16)%2;
export function resolve(s,action,move='press',expectedRevision=s.revision){validate(s);if(expectedRevision!==s.revision)throw Error('stale revision');const kind=action?.kind,why=violations(s,kind);if(why.length)throw Error('illegal action: '+why.join(','));if(kind!=='rest'&&!['press','brace','repair'].includes(move))throw Error('invalid player move');if(kind!=='rest'&&move==='repair'&&s.supplies===0)throw Error('repair needs a supply');const n=copy(s),card=CARDS[kind],before={health:s.health,supplies:s.supplies,charge:s.charge,budget:s.budget};let damage=0,charge=0,h=null;
 if(kind==='rest'){n.health=Math.min(12,n.health+2);n.supplies=Math.min(4,n.supplies+1);move='rest';}
 if(kind!=='rest'){h=hazard(s.seed,s.round);damage=card.threat+h;charge=card.reward;if(move==='brace'){damage=Math.max(0,damage-2);charge=Math.max(0,charge-1);}if(move==='repair'){n.supplies--;n.health=Math.min(12,n.health+3);damage=Math.max(0,damage-1);charge=0;}n.health=Math.max(0,n.health-damage);n.charge+=charge;}
 n.budget-=card.cost;n.round++;n.revision++;n.terminal=n.health===0||n.round===12;const pressure=.6*(12-n.health)/12+.4*Math.min(1,[...s.history.slice(-2).map(e=>e.damage),damage].reduce((a,b)=>a+b,0)/6);
 const event={round:s.round,revision:s.revision,kind,move,hazard:h,damage,charge,before,after:{health:n.health,supplies:n.supplies,charge:n.charge,budget:n.budget},pressure,target:targetAt(s.profile,s.round,s.targetSchedule)};n.history.push(event);validate(n);return {state:n,event};}
export function botMove(bot,s,kind){if(kind==='rest')return 'rest';const t=CARDS[kind].threat;if(bot==='aggressive')return s.health<=4&&s.supplies?'repair':'press';if(bot==='cautious')return s.health<=5&&s.supplies?'repair':'brace';return t>=2?'brace':'press';}
export async function episode(policy,{seed='demo-01',profile='steady',bot='fixed',id=seed,missingRound=-1,missingRounds=[],targetSchedule,requestLimit}={}){let s=initial(seed,profile,id,{targetSchedule,requestLimit}),memory={},decisions=[];while(!s.terminal){const input=copy(s);if(s.round===missingRound||missingRounds.includes(s.round))input.observationMissing=true;const d=await policy(input,memory);memory=d.memory??memory;const proposal=d.action?.kind,why=violations(s,proposal);const kind=why.length?'rest':proposal;const result=resolve(s,{kind},botMove(bot,s,kind));decisions.push({proposed:proposal??null,executed:kind,proposalViolations:why,executedViolations:[],reason:d.reason??'rules',calls:d.calls??0,latencyMs:d.latencyMs??0,origin:d.origin??'rules',revision:s.revision});s=result.state;}return {id,seed,profile,bot,...(targetSchedule===undefined?{}:{targetSchedule:copy(targetSchedule)}),...(requestLimit===undefined?{}:{requestLimit}),termination:s.health===0?'defeated':'completed',events:s.history,decisions,final:s};}

```

`courses/adaptive-decision-engine/generate-data.mjs`:

```mjs
// Reproduce the original synthetic corpus using your current adapter and observer.
import {readFile,writeFile,mkdir} from 'node:fs/promises';
import {join} from 'node:path';
import {loadModules} from './loader.mjs';
import {initial,resolve,botMove,legal} from './game.mjs';
import {fixtureResponse} from './fixtures.mjs';
import {distance} from './shared.mjs';
import {identity} from './bundle.mjs';
const [work,output]=process.argv.slice(2);
if(!work||!output)throw Error('Usage: node generate-data.mjs WORKDIR NEW-OUTPUT-DIR');
const sources={};for(const n of ['observe.mjs','constraints.mjs','adapter.mjs'])sources[n]=await readFile(join(work,n),'utf8');
const m=await loadModules(sources),corpus={origin:'synthetic-fixture',sourceHash:await identity(sources),generation:'The scripted transport ignores instruction semantics. It chooses scout when legal, else rest; a keyed hash selects score 0.35, 0.68 or 0.92 before the transition.',episodes:[]};
await mkdir(output);
for(const split of ['dev','calibration','evaluation']){const manifest=JSON.parse(await readFile(new URL('./evaluation/'+split+'.json',import.meta.url),'utf8')),rows=[];for(const spec of manifest.episodes){let state=initial(spec.seed,spec.profile,spec.id);const events=[];while(!state.terminal){const obs=m['observe.mjs'].observe(state),request=m['adapter.mjs'].buildRequest(obs,legal(state)),raw=fixtureResponse(request),proposal=m['adapter.mjs'].parseResponse(raw,request,obs);if(!proposal.ok)throw Error('Your adapter rejected the generated response: '+proposal.error);const next=resolve(state,proposal.action,botMove(spec.bot,state,proposal.action.kind)),label=Number(next.state.health>0&&distance(next.event.pressure,next.event.target)===0);rows.push({episodeId:spec.id,split,domain:spec.bot+'/'+spec.profile,revision:state.revision,score:proposal.score,label});events.push({observation:obs,request,raw,event:next.event,label});state=next.state;}corpus.episodes.push({...spec,split,events});}await writeFile(join(output,split+'-data.json'),JSON.stringify(rows,null,2),{flag:'wx'});}
await writeFile(join(output,'corpus.json'),JSON.stringify(corpus),{flag:'wx'});console.log('Wrote 180 synthetic episodes to '+output+'. No provider was called.');

```
