`courses/adaptive-decision-engine/lessons/01.md`:

```md
# 01 · Read the game before choosing

Your expedition has health 6 after three rounds, but that number does not tell you whether damage is accelerating. Build an observation that describes what the director knows now, without exposing the future.

## State becomes an observation

The **state** is the game's complete record. The **observation** is the subset available to a decision policy. A **policy** maps an observation to an action. A **transition** applies an action and the player's move to produce the next state. The supplied engine owns transitions. You own observations and, later, the policy.

Start the demonstration below. Choose Press for one encounter and Brace for the next. Watch the health and charge columns in the round log. Press earns the card's full charge and takes its threat plus a hidden hazard of zero or one. Brace earns one less charge and prevents up to two damage. Repair consumes a supply, heals three before damage, and earns no charge. Rest has no player move: it restores two health and one supply. The beacon is lit when the expedition survives all twelve rounds with a charge of 12 or more. Only encounters earn charge, so avoiding every encounter cannot light the beacon before the twelve-round deadline.

Before your next move, predict whether Brace will produce at least as much health as Press on the same card and hazard. Then try it with Replay same seed. Replay resets both the game and the director's memory, so the comparison begins from the same situation. The hazard is indexed by seed and round, so changing how many random numbers a policy requests cannot change the round's hazard.

![Diagram: Observation boundary](figures/boundary.svg)

{{practice:01a}}

## Measure recent pressure

**Pressure** is a designed pacing signal, not a measurement of fun. It combines missing health with damage in the last three resolved rounds. Divide missing health by twelve and weight it by 0.6. Divide recent damage by six, cap that fraction at one, and weight it by 0.4. Add the terms. The target is an interval: a steady expedition requests pressure between 0.25 and 0.55.

For health 6 and damage [2, 1, 0], the missing-health term is 0.6 × 6/12 = 0.3. The history term is 0.4 × 3/6 = 0.2. Pressure is 0.5. At the same health with [0, 0, 0], pressure is 0.3. A policy can distinguish recovering from recent damage from staying at the same health for several quiet rounds.

At round zero, three observations do not exist. Return pressure as null until there are three actual events. Null means unavailable; zero means measured and calm. Preserve the actual short recentDamage array and set historyComplete false. Also return null whenever observationMissing is true. A later policy may still use known health, but it must not invent a measurement.

{{practice:01b}}

## Implement the public boundary

The API reference defines the exact fields. Read the current state without modifying it. Select the last three resolved events, extract damage and player moves, compute pressure only when available, and copy the episode identity and revision. A **revision** identifies which state a later answer belongs to. It advances once per resolved round. Do not copy the complete state with object spread: that would also copy the seed and any future-only test metadata.

In the editor, complete observe.mjs. Start by returning the health and recentDamage fields. Below the editor, choose **Assistance used** and type what you expect in **Prediction or assistance detail**, then press **Commit & check** to see the remaining contract failures. Those two fields are saved with that attempt only, so fill them in again before each check. Then add the explicit field list from API.md. The first incomplete run is saved; repairing it appends another attempt.

For a completion problem, use the worked calculation above but leave out the last division: health 9 and recent damage [1, 2, 0] contribute 0.15 from health. Compute the history term and finish pressure. Then solve a fresh case with health 8 and damage [0, 0, 0], without using the worked numbers.

## Debug a leak and transfer

Imagine an observation includes nextHazard. Two games have identical public histories but different next hazards. Their observations must remain identical. A difference would let the director use information unavailable when the player acts. This is a causal boundary, not merely a naming convention. The checker supplies extra hidden fields and changes them while holding the public prefix fixed.

After your first repair, use Fresh public variant. It checks a different deterministic prefix while keeping the requirement unchanged. These cases are visible and repeatable; they are practice, not protected assessment. Add your own pair of same-prefix states with different hidden fields and describe what should remain equal. Keep that example for module 08.

Before continuing, you should be able to explain why pressure can be null at health 12, why the seed is excluded, and why two health-6 states can carry different pressure. A passing checker supports the observation contract. It does not establish that pressure captures a human player's experience.

```

```md
# 02 · Make illegal choices impossible

A proposal can spell “brute” correctly and still be forbidden in the current state. Build the complete legal action set before choosing any encounter.

## Intersect the constraints

An **action** is the director's choice of rest, scout, swarm or brute. The player chooses Press, Brace or Repair only after an encounter appears. Keep these two decisions separate. The legal-action function accepts your observation and returns an array of allowed action names, with no duplicates.

Each encounter spends director budget: scout costs one, swarm two and brute three. The expedition starts with eighteen budget points. Rest costs zero and remains available in every nonterminal state. At health three or below, rest is the only action. Swarm also needs health at least six; brute needs at least eight. Swarm and brute are high encounters. A high encounter cannot immediately follow either high encounter. That one-round restriction is a **cooldown**.

An action must satisfy every applicable rule. Budget permission does not override low health. Health permission does not override cooldown. First handle terminal states: health zero or round twelve has no legal action, including rest. Then consider each action using the conjunction of its constraints. Conjunction means all conditions hold; disjunction means at least one holds.

For health 7, budget 2 and previous swarm, scout and rest remain legal. Brute fails its cost and health tests as well as cooldown. Swarm passes cost and health but fails cooldown. Checking only the first reason can be enough for control flow, but retain all reasons when explaining a rejected proposal.

![Diagram: Every condition must hold](figures/constraints.svg)

{{practice:02a}}

## Complete a filter

Work through one candidate at a time before writing a compact filter. Start with scout at health 4 and budget 1. The state is not terminal, health is above three, and budget covers one. Scout has no additional health threshold and is not high, so the previous card does not affect it. Scout is legal.

Now keep health and budget fixed and replace scout with swarm. Fill the missing final check yourself: cost two cannot be covered by budget one. Do not keep swarm merely because health exceeds three. Next test health 8, budget 3 and previous scout. List the legal set without copying the worked answer; this case combines both high-action thresholds with a clear cooldown.

Implement allowedActions in constraints.mjs. A table of costs and minimum health is a reasonable approach. Separate predicates are also valid. The checker accepts either order of the returned set. It rejects duplicates, extra actions, missing actions and mutation of the observation. Returning only rest is safe in some states but incomplete whenever scout is also legal.

{{practice:02b}}

## The executor remains authoritative

Your policy will eventually propose an action. The supplied engine checks the original state again immediately before commitment. This catches a stale or defective policy, but a rejected proposal still counts as a proposal violation. The trace records both proposed and executed actions. It does not award your policy correctness because the engine recovered with rest.

This separation matters when a delayed response arrives. A brute proposal may have been legal at revision 4, then become illegal after another choice advances the game. Module 07 will bind the response to a revision. For now, distinguish choosing within a set from verifying that the set still belongs to the current state.

## Debug the tempting OR

A broken filter says “enough budget OR enough health.” At health 2 with budget 18 it admits a brute. That counterexample isolates the Boolean error: abundant budget cannot buy permission to ignore the recovery rule. Construct a second counterexample where health is abundant but budget is exhausted. Changing both inputs in one test without predicting each constraint makes diagnosis harder.

Your public check enumerates health 0 through 12, budget 0 through 18 and each possible previous card. Its oracle uses a separately written table of thresholds. The table and your implementation can still share a misunderstood specification, so keep your hand-worked boundary cases. Enumeration verifies this finite domain; it does not prove arbitrary extensions correct.

For transfer, use a terminal state with healthy health and unused budget. The temptation is to return rest because it is free. Explain why round twelve ends permission for every action. Then create a near-boundary pair at health five and six with budget two and previous rest. Only one condition changed. Predict exactly which action becomes legal, run your function, and preserve the result in your report.

Move on when the complete set passes and you can distinguish malformed action, illegal action and stale action. These are different failure reasons, even if all eventually lead to the same fallback.

```

```md
# 03 · Build the director you must beat

You now know what the director can observe and what it may choose. Build a deterministic rules director that lights the beacon while leaving room to recover.

## Choose a useful comparison

A **baseline** is the policy you compare another policy against. A weak baseline can make an expensive system look useful without improving the product. Always resting survives twelve rounds with full health, but earns no charge. That policy cannot satisfy the beacon goal. Your baseline must expose the player to encounters and complete at least one of the twelve published development cases.

The public check also requires encounters on at least thirty percent of the 144 possible rounds across those cases. This is a declared minimum for a meaningful demonstration, not a claim about enjoyable pacing. No policy must match the author's exact actions. Stronger rules and different lawful tie-breaking are welcome.

Begin with an ordered decision table. When health is very low, recover. When pressure is above the target band, enter recovery. When recovered sufficiently, resume challenge. During challenge, prefer an affordable encounter that respects the legal set. One reasonable starting point chooses brute at health ten or above, swarm at eight or above, then scout. Those thresholds are design choices to evaluate, not discovered truths.

{{practice:03a}}

## Keep a small memory

If you switch to recovery above 0.55 and immediately switch back below 0.55, small changes can alternate rest and challenge every round. **Hysteresis** uses different enter and leave boundaries. Enter recovery above the upper target; leave only below the lower target and with enough health. While pressure sits between those boundaries, preserve the previous recovery flag.

Consider pressure 0.50 with recovering true. The state has not crossed the leave boundary, so continue recovery. At pressure 0.20 and health 8, the leave condition holds, so resume challenge. The same pressure 0.50 with recovering false stays in challenge. Memory therefore changes the decision even when the current observation is identical.

The function returns an action and new memory. Do not mutate the old memory. Reusing an old object should reproduce the old decision, which is essential for replay and later checkpoint tests. Missing pressure needs a deliberate fallback: known health can trigger recovery, but null must not silently act like measured zero.

For a completion problem, start in recovery at pressure 0.30 and health 7. Fill the decision-table row: does either exit condition hold? Then independently solve the same pressure with recovering false. Preserve both predictions before calling your function.

{{practice:03b}}

## Play your implementation

Complete chooseRules in rules.mjs. Return {action: {kind}, memory: {recovering}}; a reason string is useful in the trace. Read the allowed set before choosing. When no action exists, stop with a terminal error instead of inventing a last rest. If your observe.mjs or constraints.mjs still fails, the **Use earlier-layer support** button (or `node lab.mjs support 03 ./work`) fills in the course's versions of modules 01 and 02 so you can work on this one. It keeps your original files in the attempt history, records that support was used, and never writes rules.mjs for you.

Select My rules director below, then New expedition. Play at least one seed with mostly Press and another with mostly Brace. Watch charge, health and remaining rounds together. Repair can save health but costs both a supply and a charge opportunity. A policy that produces a smooth pressure curve may still miss the charge deadline.

Run the terminal play command from README to exercise the same source against the fixed, cautious and aggressive bots. These bots are explicit fixtures. Their names describe their programmed rules, not measured human populations. Save a baseline manifest before tuning later candidates so that a comparison cannot secretly weaken the rules side.

## Debug and transfer

Use all-rest as a negative control. It should pass legality and fail meaningful completion. If your evaluator later declares all-rest superior based only on survival, the evaluator has changed the product goal. Retain survival and completion as separate outcomes.

For a fresh problem, switch the target from steady to the supplied pulse schedule. The target band changes every three rounds. Read target from the observation instead of hard-coding the steady limits. The public check does not require one particular response to pulse; evaluate the consequence and explain your tradeoff.

Before moving on, export the ZIP, extract it in a fresh directory, and run a check on the included work. A demonstration using supplied rules is not your implementation. The export must contain the code you edited, failed and revised attempts, and enough instructions to run without this browser. Passing this module gives you a playable baseline, which is the control for every later model experiment.

# 04 · Worked notebook

This output was executed with the author demonstration. It is not your submission.

```json

# 04 · Connect a typed decision source

A response about the wrong question can look perfectly valid. Build an adapter that accepts only an encounter answer bound to the current request.

## A finite question

An **adapter** converts between your application's contract and an external interface. It contains question construction and interpretation; the supplied transport owns network mechanics. Your buildRequest function takes the observation and allowed action names. It produces a named encounter question with a description for each permitted choice. Do not offer brute when brute is illegal and hope the model remembers to avoid it.

A typed response selects one label from a finite set and supplies a distribution over that set. A **distribution** assigns a nonnegative number to every permitted label, with a total of one. Different key order is harmless. An unexpected label, missing label, negative number or nonfinite value invalidates the response. Do not repair malformed probabilities by silently dividing by their sum: that changes the evidence you received.

For comparison, imagine a weather-card selector with choices clear and rain. A valid distribution might put 0.7 on clear and 0.3 on rain. A second answer named temperature cannot stand in for weather even if it also contains two numbers. Our encounter answer uses the same principle: read answers.encounter by name, never the first object entry.

{{practice:04a}}

## Bind context before dispatch

A **binding** records which request an answer belongs to. Construct it before sending: episode ID, revision, hash of the observation, hash of the question, allowed action set, requested model, provider host and adapter version. The locally assigned request ID also covers the outbound body. A **hash** here is a deterministic change detector. The course's short internal hash is not a cryptographic signature; export manifests use SHA-256 for artifact identity.

When the response arrives, compare the binding with the current observation. At episode camp-2 revision 8, an answer for camp-2 revision 7 is stale. An answer for another episode at revision 8 is also stale. If the provider returns a different model from the one requested, reject it. A provider need not echo every local binding field: your transport must retain the actual request/response association instead of guessing from content.

The supplied fixtureResponse creates synthetic answers and explicit faults. It is not a language model and never contacts a service. Use its valid response for the first adapter run, then substitute wrong-question, wrong-model and invalid-sum fixtures. Keep these labels in reports. A replayed real capture would also need an exact matching request; changing a question while reusing an old answer creates a different experiment.

{{practice:04b}}

## Implement and repair

Complete buildRequest and parseResponse in adapter.mjs using API.md. Return either an explicit successful proposal or {ok:false,error:...}. A failure must not become a fake rest proposal from the model. The controller may execute a rules fallback afterward, but its trace must preserve the difference.

Work in stages. First construct the question with an allowed subset of rest and scout. Then complete the missing normalization checks for the selected action. Finally validate the complete distribution and every binding field. In the fresh public variant, object ordering changes. Your adapter must treat mappings by name rather than by insertion position.

Try a deliberately wrong implementation that reads Object.values(answers)[0]. Give it both a recovery answer and an encounter answer, with recovery first. Record the wrong selection, repair the named lookup, and rerun with the order reversed. That control distinguishes a repaired binding from code that merely happens to work on one fixture.

## The optional HTTP boundary

The package includes a Node-only HTTP transport for the documented Liquid endpoint. It is mock-tested, not live-qualified. Reading the course and running public checks never reads credentials. The browser does not ask for an API key. The optional terminal smoke defaults to a dry run and requires explicit arming, a named model, one-request cap, byte limit and deadline before it can dispatch.

A request cap limits count, not an invoice. The transport refuses a strict monetary cap because the package has no verified upper bound on token billing. Unknown usage remains unknown. Do not enable a provider merely to finish this lesson; the offline adapter is sufficient for every required exercise.

Before continuing, explain why a well-formed answer can still be invalid, and save one wrong-question rejection. This proves an interpretation boundary, not model quality or a useful choice.

# 05 · Decide when to abstain

A confident choice can still lead outside the target band. Build a calibration table for a named event and use it to decide when rules should take over.

## Name the event before measuring

A Choice distribution describes preference among action labels. Its confidence value is not automatically the probability of survival, completion or good pacing. **Calibration** compares a forecast with the frequency of a defined event. Our event is: the next resolved round ends alive and inside the announced pressure interval.

Every dataset row records an episode ID, revision, domain, synthetic choice score and event label. A label of one means the event occurred; zero means it did not. The label is computed after applying the player move and hazard. The score is generated before that transition. The corpus generator's rule is explicit: the fixture chooses scout when legal and emits one of three hash-selected scores. This deliberately makes a score that may carry little useful information about our event.

The event concerns one round under a particular action and player policy. It does not describe the probability of finishing the expedition. If you change the policy, player behavior or target schedule, the states you visit may change too. Calibration from one distribution of states does not automatically transfer to another.

![Diagram: Map a score to an event](figures/calibration.svg)

{{practice:05a}}

## Fit a domain table on separate episodes

A **split** reserves whole episodes for a purpose: development explores a policy, calibration fits a mapping, and evaluation measures the frozen result. Adjacent rounds share history. Splitting by episode prevents related rounds appearing on both sides; it does not make rounds within an episode independent.

A **domain** here is the declared bot/profile combination. Keep a separate table for each domain. Ninety easy-domain successes and ten hard-domain failures at score 0.9 do not make the hard domain's event probability 0.9. That would transfer evidence across populations without support. In our supplied corpus, some cautious-player domains have no events at all. Inspect those rows in the table below rather than averaging them away.

Within each score bin, first group rows by episode. Compute each episode's event fraction, then average those fractions equally. The result answers this question: if you pick one of the bin's episodes at random, each equally likely, and then pick one of that episode's rows in the bin at random, how likely is that row to be an event? For example, take the ninety easy-domain successes above, one row per episode, and add one more easy episode that contributes ten failed rows to the same bin. The episode fractions are ninety ones and one zero, so the equal-episode mean is 90/91 ≈ 0.989. Pooling rows instead gives 90/100 = 0.9, because the single long episode counts ten times. The table reports both: p is the equal-episode mean and rowRate is the pooled row rate. Display both row counts and distinct episode counts; they answer different questions.

The supplied episodeInterval helper treats those bounded fractions as independent episode observations. Its conservative radius is sqrt(log(2/0.05)/(2*m)), where m is the number of episodes. Clip mean minus/plus the radius to [0,1]. This is a Hoeffding bound under independent, comparable episodes from the stated domain. It is not a claim that these deterministic fixture seeds establish a population interval, and it does not establish transfer to a changed policy or domain.

For ninety independent all-success episodes, the mean is 1 and the lower bound is about 0.857. For ten all-failure episodes in another domain, the mean is 0 and the upper bound is about 0.429. Repeating twelve successful rounds from one episode still gives m=1, and the selector abstains. The minimum of ten episodes is a declared teaching policy; the interval, not the count alone, must also support the threshold.

For completion practice, put six successes and four failures in one episode and compute its fraction. Then add a second episode with one failure. Compare the equal-episode mean with the pooled row mean. Explain why duplicating the first episode's rows under the same identities must be rejected rather than treated as more evidence.

![Diagram: Map a score to an event](figures/calibration.svg)

{{practice:05b}}

## Score forecasts and choose coverage

The **Brier score** is the average squared error between forecast and binary label. Lower is better for this event. For forecasts [0.9, 0.9, 0.6, 0.6] and labels [1, 0, 1, 0], the squared errors sum to 1.34, giving 0.335. A constant forecast of 0.5 scores 0.25 on those labels. A confident forecast can therefore lose to a simple constant.

A constant prevalence forecast has a limitation: it does not distinguish easy from difficult cases. Report its score without calling it a universally useful selector. Compare mapped forecasts with both raw scores and the calibration prevalence baseline on the separate evaluation data. The generated corpus includes six bot/profile domains; report counts for each instead of hiding a weak slice in an overall average.

**Abstention** means declining to use a proposal and executing the rules fallback. The selector abstains for unknown domains, insufficient bins, invalid proposals and intervals below threshold. **Coverage** is the fraction of proposals used. A high threshold can yield zero coverage. That is an honest result if the evidence is weak; do not lower the threshold after viewing final evaluation just to produce an impressive chart.

## Implement and transfer

Complete fitCalibration, brier and select in confidence.mjs. Start with counts, then add probabilities and intervals, then the abstention reasons. The check rejects evaluation rows, duplicate episode/revision identities and cross-domain borrowing. It also gives episodes different numbers of rows, so a pooled row rate used as p, or a minimum counted in rows instead of episodes, fails. A positive control also requires accepting a genuinely supported bin, so always abstaining is not a complete selector. Inspect episode families yourself; a field called calibration cannot establish independence.

For a fresh case, reverse the relationship: high scores now accompany failures. Keep the original threshold frozen and predict what happens. Refit only on a new calibration split, assign it a new identity, and compare separately. In module 08 you will distinguish a faulty formula from a changed domain. No result in this lesson establishes how any real provider behaves.

```

# 06 · Compare complete expeditions

A director changes the states it will see next. Compare complete episodes under matched conditions before deciding whether to adopt a candidate.

## Pair the experiment, allow paths to diverge

An **episode** is one expedition, from initial state to defeat or the twelve-round finish. A snapshot test asks what a policy would choose in one saved state. It cannot reveal the later consequences of changing that choice. Run both policies from the same initial seed, bot and target profile, then let each trajectory evolve.

A **pair** contains one baseline episode and one candidate episode with the same case identity. The supplied engine indexes hazards by seed and round. Both policies therefore face the same hazard for round five even if their earlier choices consumed different numbers of random draws. Their health and legal actions may still differ because earlier choices differed.

The manifest freezes the list of episode IDs, seeds, player bots and profiles. Do not remove a case after a timeout or defeat. Those outcomes are part of the experiment. Development, calibration and evaluation each contain sixty episodes with disjoint seed families. These counts are bounded teaching datasets, not a statistical guarantee.

![Diagram: Compare the same starting cases](figures/pairs.svg)

{{practice:06a}}

## Recompute the product outcomes

Your metrics function first audits the complete transition trail, then reads events and decision records. The auditor reconstructs the seed-driven world and compares the final state, including its terminal reason. A healthy prefix is missing evidence and must be rejected, even if its event and decision arrays have equal lengths. Report survival and completion separately. Survival means health remains above zero when the run ends. Completion additionally requires twelve resolved rounds and at least twelve charge. Challenge exposure is the number of encounter rounds divided by twelve. All-rest has survival one, completion zero and challenge zero.

For each resolved round, distance from the target interval is max(lower − pressure, 0, pressure − upper). Values inside the band have zero distance. Average over the fixed twelve-round denominator. If a defeat ends after four rounds, the eight unplayed rounds each contribute distance one. Also report actual-played-round distance separately. Otherwise a quick defeat could look excellent because it avoided difficult later rounds.

Keep proposal violations separate from executed violations. A rejected brute proposal that falls back to rest is still a proposal violation. Count fallback reasons, request reservations, latency and duplicate/stale effects. Nonzero fault controls check every count; an all-zero summary cannot pass. Fixture timing is simulated; do not call it measured network latency. The event record includes origin so a fixture is never silently merged with a live capture.

For completion practice, imagine two played rounds with distances 0.1 and 0.2 followed by defeat. The fixed-denominator distance is (0.1 + 0.2 + 10)/12. Compute it before running your metric. Then compare it with the played-only average and explain which denominator could hide failure.

{{practice:06b}}

## Summarize paired differences

For each pair, subtract baseline from candidate. Negative target-distance differences favor the candidate; positive completion differences favor the candidate. Keep the direction explicit rather than declaring every positive number good. Report every bot/profile slice with its sample count. An improved overall mean can coexist with unacceptable degradation in one slice.

The supplied resampler draws complete pairs with replacement and recomputes the mean. It does not draw individual rounds. An interval that crosses zero is compatible with either direction under the resampling procedure; it does not prove equality. The deterministic resampling seed makes the report reproducible, not more certain.

Implement compare in evaluate.mjs. Open Function contracts (API.md), section 06, for the required comparison report shape and exact fallback-counting labels. The runner needs per-pair slice identities and both complete metric objects to check your arithmetic. Test it first by pairing a policy with an identical copy: every difference should be zero. Then reorder the input pairs and check that the conclusion is unchanged. Reject mismatched seed, bot, profile and episode identity. An average over unrelated cases loses the benefit of pairing.

## Freeze an adoption rule

Before final evaluation, record hard gates: no executed violations, no duplicate or stale effects, no request allowance exceeded, and complete event accounting. Then state acceptable completion and survival degradation and the minimum target-distance improvement worth adopting. Use development results to choose these limits. Changing them after seeing final results requires a new experiment identity.

The CLI's fixture evaluation runs the complete selective controller, including calibration and fallback, with the same request limit you froze. A zero allowance makes zero requests. The runner independently recomputes every report field before applying your recommendation. In the shipped synthetic corpus, weak confidence evidence may make rules the defensible choice. A rule-based release is a valid outcome. Keep the raw episodes and a report explaining the decision.

Your fresh problem is a candidate that improves the mean but harms the cautious/pulse slice. Use the published degradation limit, not enthusiasm for the overall chart. Automated checks validate arithmetic and consistency. Your explanation of why those limits fit the product remains a reasoning task for the rubric and later review.

```md
# 07 · Spend time and calls deliberately

A late correct answer can still be wrong for the current game. Build a scheduler that reserves budget before dispatch and discards results after their deadline or revision.

## One pending request

A **scheduler** records whether a request is pending, how many reservations have been spent, and when a pending request expires. It has a small state machine: idle, pending, then accepted, timed out or rejected. The deadline uses an injected monotonic clock, a clock that only moves forward during a run. Wall-clock date changes should not extend a request's allowance.

reserve takes scheduler state, episode/revision and current time. If another request is pending, return in-flight without dispatching another one. If the request limit is exhausted, return budget-exhausted. Otherwise increment used immediately, create a fresh token and store the deadline. A failed request still consumed a reservation. Counting only successful responses would permit an unlimited failure loop.

A request token distinguishes separate dispatches even at the same revision. Episode and revision distinguish game state. You need both: a later request at revision eight must not accept an earlier token that also happened to use revision eight.

![Diagram: A late result has no effect](figures/deadline.svg)

{{practice:07a}}

## Let fallback win exactly once

Work through this timeline. Revision 8 dispatches at time 10 with timeout 5, so its deadline is 15. At time 15 the scheduler expires it and the controller chooses rules. The game commits that fallback and advances to revision 9. At time 18 the old response arrives. Its JSON is valid, but its state is old. Discard it and record a late-response event; do not resolve another round.

settle checks the current pending token and episode/revision before accepting a proposal. It also checks the deadline. At the deadline itself, the result is timed out, so compare with now >= deadline. The tie is deliberately defined so behavior does not depend on callback ordering. The public check settles one response exactly at its deadline and another one tick earlier. Clearing pending state does not refund used reservations.

Complete the missing transition for an unavailable response before implementing the full scheduler: pending becomes idle with used unchanged. For token 3 at time 12 with deadline 15, write used, pending and accepted after the failure. Then use the same state with a valid response: it must be accepted exactly once. Rejecting every response is not a correct scheduler. Then independently solve a timeout followed by a reset to another episode that also starts at revision zero. An episode ID check must reject the original answer even though revisions match.

{{practice:07b}}

## Integrate without hiding failure

The supplied createController composes your observation, constraints, adapter, calibration and scheduler functions. It owns Promise racing and transport injection. Your scheduler owns reservation and acceptance policy. The controller returns a decision; the authoritative engine commits it once after validating the revision and action.

Read control.mjs alongside your implementation. A fallback records the real reason: unavailable, uncertain, timeout, stale or budget-exhausted. It also records one call for a dispatched failure. A request never begins just because a frame rendered. Decisions occur once per round, and only the controller can request evidence.

The public check runs a delayed synthetic transport, allows timeout fallback, then releases the old response. It expects one returned decision and one late-discard log. This is stronger than testing settle in isolation: it exercises the composition that could accidentally apply both answers. It is still a local deterministic failure experiment, not observed provider latency.

## Cost and cache limits

A call cap is straightforward to enforce; a monetary cap requires a verified upper bound on billing units and rates. The optional transport refuses a strict cost claim it cannot establish. A deadline controls how long the game waits, not whether a remote server has billed work already sent. Preserve unknown usage as unknown.

A cached proposal is valid only for the exact bound request. A matching action name is insufficient. If observation, question, model, host or allowed set changes, the binding changes. The default implementation performs no approximate cache reuse and no retries. If you add retries, every retry spends another reservation.

For transfer, combine a timeout with a new episode and a late response. Record the token, old and new episode/revision, used count and total committed rounds. Predict these values before running. Your successful scheduler must preserve game responsiveness and evidence of the failure at the same time.

# 08 · Break your own explanation

A plausible story about a bad decision is not yet a diagnosis. Construct a case that changes the suspected cause while holding other inputs fixed.

## Compare explanations with an intervention

An **intervention** deliberately changes one suspected cause. A **negative control** changes something that should not affect the outcome. Consider a faulty observer that uses only health. Two states have equal health but different recent damage. If the observer returns the same pressure, the defect is in the observation. If the observer distinguishes them but the policy ignores that distinction, the defect is in policy use.

These are different explanations with different repairs. Changing a threshold while leaving the faulty observer untouched may improve one recorded run without addressing the lost information. Preserve the failing source before editing so you can distinguish a real repair from a changed test case.

The supplied exercise format uses controlled snapshots rather than pretending the counterfactual history happened naturally. Label these as constructed interventions. Replace recent damage while holding health, budget, round and last action fixed. Then change only display color as a negative control. Display color is outside the observation contract and should not change a decision.

{{practice:08a}}

## Create two original cases

In scenarios.json, create two cases using the schema in API.md. Each needs an ID, hypothesis, health, budget, damageA and damageB. Use three nonnegative integer damage values from zero through four. The two histories should make your rules policy choose different encounters. Choose different health or budget conditions so the second case tests a distinct boundary. Duplicate IDs, cloned conditions and reversed copies of the same history pair are rejected.

The public checker constructs the states, runs your actual observe and chooseRules functions on each intervention, and also changes display color. It requires changed decisions for the history interventions and unchanged decisions for the display control. It does not award correctness for an asserted passed flag in your JSON.

For the completion problem, take a previously recorded decision where your policy entered recovery. Hold health and budget fixed, remove only recent damage, and predict whether the policy should leave recovery. You supply the numbers. Then create the second case without copying the first case's values. If your policy legitimately ignores damage by design, revise the experiment to test the observation boundary first and explain the limitation; the current public exercise specifically asks you to implement a history-sensitive baseline.

{{practice:08b}}

## Preserve the reasoning record

Your REPORT.md should state the original failure, at least two possible explanations, the intervention, the negative control, actual before/after decisions and the remaining alternatives. An intervention supports a narrow claim: in this constructed case, the changed input affected the result. It does not show that the same input explains every poor episode.

Record source hashes for the original and repaired policy. The attempt store retains full code and questions before execution. Attach the original case identity to both results. A repair run against a different case is useful development but cannot by itself show that the original defect was removed.

Automated checks verify the controlled relation and execute your cases. They cannot judge whether your prose gives a sensible causal account. Use the reasoning rubric for that judgment. A complete project includes both the behavioral evidence and the explanation; a keyword-filled report with no actual intervention is insufficient.

## Distinguish a defect from missing evidence

Now change the target profile and remove the observation for one round. This is a different kind of change. A calibration table fitted on steady states does not automatically describe pulse states, and an unavailable pressure reading cannot support a precise pressure claim. The correct outcome may be abstention rather than a more elaborate threshold.

Use a fresh domain label and predict whether select will accept it. Keep the calibration table fixed for the first run. Then collect an explicitly separate calibration set if you want to support that domain. Reusing evaluation labels to fill the missing bin would hide uncertainty instead of resolving it.

For transfer, show a case where a repair helps the original intervention but the new missing-observation case still needs fallback. Explain the remaining limit. The goal is a defensible explanation with a counterexample, not a story that makes every result look like success. Keep planted faults labeled as planted; none of these cases establishes a real model's failure frequency.

`courses/adaptive-decision-engine/lessons/09.md`:

```md
# 09 · Resume without changing the decision

Closing a page must not erase recovery memory or replenish a spent request budget. Build a checkpoint that reproduces the next decision after a restart.

## Decide what must survive

A **checkpoint** is a serialized record of the information needed to continue. The game state alone is insufficient when the policy has memory. A policy can also update memory when it selects an encounter, before the player resolves the round. Save that completed selection with its state and memory binding; calling the policy again during resume could select a different encounter and advance memory twice. At pressure 0.30, recovery may continue or remain off depending on the previous recovery flag. Save that flag. Also save used request reservations, maximum allowance, serial token and the identities of policy source and calibration data.

The checkpoint has a version because its meaning can change. Restore must refuse an unknown version or mismatched source/calibration identity. A JSON object with similar-looking fields is not proof of compatibility. The source identity says which policy produced the memory; the calibration identity says which evidence supports selective use.

Do not restore a pending network operation. Its process and callbacks no longer exist, and restarting it silently could spend again. The saved checkpoint clears pending, records that a pending request was invalidated, and preserves the spent reservation. Restore also forces armed false. A new process requires a new explicit decision before any real provider operation.

![Diagram: Enough state to continue](figures/checkpoint.svg)

{{practice:09a}}

## Prove next-step equivalence

Begin with a state and nonempty policy memory. Compute the next deterministic decision without changing the original objects. Create a checkpoint, serialize it to JSON, parse into fresh objects, restore, and compute the next decision again. Compare the full pending action and memory result. In the runtime, resume must not call the policy again when this selected result was saved. Use a counter that changes on every decision to expose double evaluation; an idempotent recovery flag alone can hide the defect.

For a worked field example, a scheduler used three of four reservations and had request token three pending. After restore, used remains three, maxRequests remains four, pending is null and armed is false. Exactly one reservation remains. The old request is not retried. The checkpoint's invalidatedPending flag records why the pending slot disappeared.

Complete that field table for a checkpoint taken after a timed-out request, where pending is already null. Then independently test a checkpoint with no history and another midway through recovery. A serialization test using empty default memory can pass while hiding the real bug.

{{practice:09b}}

## Export the actual work

The browser and terminal keep separate stores. Browser edits live under the local origin, including its port. Terminal work lives in the directory you created. Export is the explicit bridge: the ZIP contains the local reader, engine, public checks, your current source, attempts and session.json. Extract it before running Node commands.

Use node lab.mjs import session.json NEWDIR to restore exported browser work into a fresh terminal directory. Import refuses to overwrite an existing directory. The browser import preview asks before replacing the current workspace and retains its previous data as a local backup. Current checkpoint.json takes precedence over an older checkpoint copied into the session ledger. An older export without a saved encounter restores state and memory only, then requires you to explicitly choose a new encounter; it does not claim to reproduce an encounter that was never recorded. The exported archive includes file hashes so you can identify changes after transfer.

A historical pass belongs to the saved source and question. If you edit constraints.mjs, an earlier result remains visible but is historical. Never reinterpret the old answer under new code. A failed save prevents a new committed check from executing, leaving the existing attempt history available for export.

## Repair a broken restore

Plant a defect that resets used to zero. Demonstrate that next action equality alone fails to catch the extra allowance. Add an assertion about budget continuity. Then plant a memory reset and show that budget equality alone misses the changed decision. The two controls measure different parts of recovery.

Finally, alter only a display preference and restore into fresh objects. The next decision should remain equal because display state is outside the policy contract. Alter the source or calibration identity and expect an explicit refusal. A refused incompatible checkpoint is safer evidence than a superficially successful resume with unknown meaning.

Your transfer artifact is a ZIP reopened outside the original folder, with a successful next-step equivalence check and the original failed attempts intact. Do not claim live-request recovery: the course deliberately disarms it. Human accessibility and other operating systems still need their own observed evidence.

# 10 · A new pacing contract

The target now pulses, one round loses its pressure observation, and only two request reservations remain. Create your own director and defend which version should ship.

## Build without a finished project

Create project.mjs with an exported policy(state, memory) function. There is no completed capstone starter. You may compose your earlier modules, replace a heuristic, or keep an entirely rule-based policy. Return an action and serializable memory. Each returned decision must preserve origin and request count where applicable.

The public changed contract uses a pulse target: rounds alternate between lower and higher requested pressure bands in groups of three. One observation interval is unavailable. The action meanings, health limits and cooldown remain unchanged. Read the announced target rather than assuming steady values. A supplied targetSchedule gives twelve explicit intervals, while requestLimit gives the scenario allowance. On missing evidence, return a labelled rules fallback with no new request. The normal-state result must not pretend an outage occurred.

Prior-layer support is available as an explicit assisted route. It supplies the earlier modules, never project.mjs or your adoption conclusion. If you use it, retain your original draft and record the assistance. An assisted capstone can demonstrate integration, but it does not establish unaided mastery of the supplied layers.

{{practice:10a}}

## Freeze your experiment

Before evaluating the final version, save the baseline and candidate source identities, episode manifest, calibration identity, metric definitions and adoption limits in REPORT.md. State the hard gates: lawful execution, no duplicate or stale effects, complete event accounting and no more than two request reservations per episode. Choose allowed completion and survival losses and a target-distance improvement requirement using development data.

Run complete paired episodes. Report every bot/profile slice, including failures. Include an interval over paired episode differences. If the evidence remains ambiguous, choose rules or collect more evidence. You do not need a model win, a provider account or an optimistic conclusion to complete this project.

The public code check includes two final-round states with the same health and history but different announced targets. Charge 12 is already secured, every candidate survives both hazards, and there is no future round. Choose an action with the smallest worst-case band distance under the fixed player; every tied optimum is accepted. A health-only heuristic cannot satisfy both cases. This bounded final-step proof complements complete pulse/outage episodes; it does not require a greedy policy on earlier rounds. It also asks for meaningful game engagement: at least one completion and thirty percent challenge exposure across its twelve cases. Those are minimum artifact requirements, not proof of useful pacing. Your own frozen evaluation should be stronger and aligned with the product outcome you defend.

## Add an original scenario family

Create project-plan.json with your source fingerprint, adoption decision, rationale, limits, and two original scenario contracts. Each contract supplies its target schedule, outage rounds and request allowance. The checker executes the contracts and rejects two copies that differ only in name or seed. Run the same authored family from the evaluation panel or with node lab.mjs evaluate ./work --manifest ./work/project-plan.json --mode project to retain its full paired event log. Replace the REPORT.md starter with an evidence account; the code check establishes artifact completeness and consistency, while the separate rubric judges your reasoning. Create new seeds and a scenario family that exposes an assumption in your director. It may concentrate pressure near a target boundary, delay recovery until supplies are scarce, or change when observation is unavailable. Explain what stays inside the published game rules and what is a deliberate extension.

Preserve a controlled failure and repair using the method from module 08. Hold the original case fixed for the repair test, then test a different case that was not used to tune the repair. Label this public transfer practice honestly. Protected independent assessment requires another assessor to choose unseen cases after your submission is frozen; it is not included in the self-paced package.

{{practice:10b}}

## Deliver something another learner can run

Your final ZIP must include project.mjs, the earlier learner modules, scenarios, report, evaluation events, checkpoint and attempt history. The ordinary export includes your source and histories; place named result/checkpoint files through the supported commands described in API.md so they join the allowlist. Do not smuggle arbitrary local folders, environment files or API keys into the archive.

Extract into a fresh directory. Start the local reader, import session.json if needed, run the project game, run the public checks, reproduce the report and prove next-decision equality after restore. Ask another person to follow README without this conversation. Record any instruction they had to guess and repair it before calling the artifact portable.

## Review the claim you are making

Use the six-part rubric: observation and constraints, baseline tradeoffs, uncertainty scope, paired evaluation, causal counterexample and bounded release decision. Each claim used to justify adoption needs supporting evidence. A high total cannot compensate for a false claim that a fixture was a real model run or that an illegal choice became valid because the executor repaired it.

State what remains untested. The supplied fixture comparison does not qualify Liquid or any other provider. Automated public checks do not prove independent transfer. If someone tries your director after reading your code, their result does not show how a newcomer who never saw the code would do. Human learning, motivation and full accessibility require corresponding human observations.

A successful outcome is a working director with a defensible choice about its operating policy. If your evidence says the rules baseline should ship, deliver that decision with the same care as a selective model policy. The course is about controlling and measuring decisions, including the decision not to delegate one.

`courses/adaptive-decision-engine/loader.mjs`:

```mjs
// Compiles the same ES module source graph in browser and Node workers.
export async function loadModules(sources) {
 const urls=new Map(),visiting=new Set();
 function build(name){if(urls.has(name))return urls.get(name);if(visiting.has(name))throw Error('circular learner imports');if(!(name in sources))throw Error('missing learner file: '+name);visiting.add(name);
 const source=sources[name].replace(/(from\s*|import\s*)(['"])([^'"]+)\2/g,(all,p,q,path)=>{if(['../shared.mjs','../game.mjs','../control.mjs','../fixtures.mjs','../resample.mjs','../data.mjs','../uncertainty.mjs','../audit.mjs'].includes(path))return p+q+new URL(path.replace('../','./'),import.meta.url).href+q;if(!/^\.\/[a-z-]+\.mjs$/.test(path))throw Error('Use local named course modules only: '+path);return p+q+build(path.slice(2))+q;});
 const url=typeof process==='undefined'?URL.createObjectURL(new Blob([source],{type:'text/javascript'})):'data:text/javascript;base64,'+Buffer.from(source).toString('base64');urls.set(name,url);visiting.delete(name);return url;}
 const modules={};for(const name of Object.keys(sources).filter(n=>n.endsWith('.mjs')))modules[name]=await import(build(name));return modules;
}

`courses/adaptive-decision-engine/node-run.mjs`:

```mjs
import {Worker} from 'node:worker_threads';
export function run(message,timeoutMs=10000){return new Promise((resolve,reject)=>{const worker=new Worker(new URL('./node-worker.mjs',import.meta.url),{workerData:message,execArgv:[]});const timer=setTimeout(()=>{worker.terminate();reject(Error('Execution timed out; your saved attempt remains available.'));},timeoutMs);worker.once('message',r=>{clearTimeout(timer);worker.terminate();r.ok?resolve(r.value):reject(Error(r.error));});worker.once('error',e=>{clearTimeout(timer);worker.terminate();reject(e);});});}

```

```mjs
import {initial,resolve,legal,botMove,hazard} from './game.mjs';
import {copy,distance,canonical,hash} from './shared.mjs';
export function terminalCase(target){
 let s=initial('terminal-control','pulse','terminal-control');for(let i=0;i<11;i++)s=resolve(s,{kind:'rest'},'rest').state;
 s.health=8;s.charge=12;s.budget=3;s.history.slice(-3).forEach((e,i)=>e.damage=[2,1,0][i]);
 s.targetSchedule=Array.from({length:12},()=>[...target]);s.requestLimit=2;return s;
}
export function terminalChoices(state){
 const score={};
 for(const kind of legal(state)){
  const losses=[];
  for(const bit of [0,1]){
   let seed='terminal-'+bit;while(hazard(seed,state.round)!==bit)seed+='x';
   const next=resolve({...copy(state),seed},{kind},botMove('fixed',state,kind));
   if(next.state.health<=0||next.state.charge<12)throw Error('terminal control is not viability-neutral');
   losses.push(distance(next.event.pressure,state.targetSchedule[state.round]));
  }
  score[kind]=Math.max(...losses);
 }
 const best=Math.min(...Object.values(score));return {scores:score,allowed:Object.keys(score).filter(k=>Math.abs(score[k]-best)<1e-9)};
}
export function projectFingerprint(sources){return hash(Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(sources).filter(([name])=>name.endsWith('.mjs'))));}
export function readProjectPlan(sources){
 let plan;try{plan=JSON.parse(sources['project-plan.json']);}catch{throw Error('Create project-plan.json using API.md; include your source fingerprint and original scenarios.');}
 if(plan.version!==1||plan.sourceHash!==projectFingerprint(sources))throw Error('project plan source fingerprint is missing or stale; current: '+projectFingerprint(sources));
 if(!['rules','selective','collect-more-evidence'].includes(plan.adoption)||typeof plan.rationale!=='string'||!plan.rationale.trim()||typeof plan.limits!=='string'||!plan.limits.trim())throw Error('Record adoption, rationale and limits; argument quality remains a separate rubric judgment.');
 const report=sources['REPORT.md']||'';if(!report.trim()||report.includes('Record your prediction, threshold choices, counterexamples, frozen adoption gates, evidence and remaining alternatives.'))throw Error('Replace the REPORT.md starter with your own evidence account.');
 if(!Array.isArray(plan.scenarios)||plan.scenarios.length<2)throw Error('Create two original scenario contracts.');
 const ids=new Set(),seeds=new Set(),contracts=new Set();
 for(const item of plan.scenarios){
  if(typeof item.id!=='string'||!item.id||ids.has(item.id)||typeof item.seed!=='string'||!item.seed||seeds.has(item.seed))throw Error('Scenario identities and seeds must be unique.');ids.add(item.id);seeds.add(item.seed);
  if(item.profile!=='pulse'||!Array.isArray(item.targetSchedule)||item.targetSchedule.length!==12||item.targetSchedule.some(p=>!Array.isArray(p)||p.length!==2||!p.every(Number.isFinite)||p[0]<0||p[1]>1||p[0]>p[1]))throw Error('Provide twelve valid target intervals.');
  if(!Array.isArray(item.missingRounds)||!item.missingRounds.length||new Set(item.missingRounds).size!==item.missingRounds.length||item.missingRounds.some(n=>!Number.isInteger(n)||n<0||n>11)||!Number.isInteger(item.requestLimit)||item.requestLimit<0||item.requestLimit>2)throw Error('Invalid outage schedule or request allowance.');
  const key=canonical({targetSchedule:item.targetSchedule,missingRounds:item.missingRounds,requestLimit:item.requestLimit});if(contracts.has(key))throw Error('Scenario contracts must differ beyond names/seeds.');contracts.add(key);
 }
 return plan;
}

// Optional Node transport. Importing this module neither reads credentials nor calls a provider.
const ENDPOINT='https://api.liquid.ai/decisions/v1/systemone';
export function createHttpTransport(config,{fetchFn=fetch,getKey=()=>process.env.LIQUID_API_KEY}={}) {
 if(config?.endpoint!==ENDPOINT||!config.model||!Number.isInteger(config.maxRequests)||config.maxRequests<1||config.maxRequests>20||!Number.isInteger(config.maxInputBytes)||config.maxInputBytes<1||config.maxInputBytes>32000||!Number.isInteger(config.timeoutMs)||config.timeoutMs<1||config.timeoutMs>30000)throw Error('invalid-config');
 if(config.strictCost!==undefined)throw Error('strict cost cannot be bounded: no verified token/rate upper bound');
 let used=0;
 return {status:()=>({used,maxRequests:config.maxRequests,armed:config.arm===true,qualification:'mock-tested; no live qualification'}),async send(request){
  if(config.arm!==true)throw Error('disabled: explicitly arm each terminal session');
  if(used>=config.maxRequests)throw Error('budget-exhausted');
  if(request.binding?.host!=='api.liquid.ai'||request.body?.model!==config.model)throw Error('invalid-binding');
  const body=JSON.stringify(request.body);if(Buffer.byteLength(body)>config.maxInputBytes)throw Error('input-too-large');
  const key=getKey();if(!key)throw Error('missing-credential');used++;
  const controller=new AbortController(),timer=setTimeout(()=>controller.abort(),config.timeoutMs);
  try{const response=await fetchFn(ENDPOINT,{method:'POST',redirect:'error',signal:controller.signal,headers:{Authorization:'Bearer '+key,'Content-Type':'application/json'},body});if(!response.ok)throw Error('provider-http-error');const reader=response.body.getReader();let size=0,parts=[];while(true){const {done,value}=await reader.read();if(done)break;size+=value.length;if(size>65536){await reader.cancel();throw Error('response-too-large');}parts.push(value);}return JSON.parse(Buffer.concat(parts).toString('utf8'));}catch(e){throw Error(e.name==='AbortError'?'timeout':'provider-request-failed');}finally{clearTimeout(timer);}
 }};
}

`courses/adaptive-decision-engine/recovery.mjs`:

```mjs
// Supplied runtime state machine. A selected encounter is data, not a live request.
import {copy,hash,canonical} from './shared.mjs';
import {legal,validate} from './game.mjs';
const same=(a,b)=>canonical(a)===canonical(b);
export function bindSelection(state,memory,decision,source,playMode){
 validate(state);
 if(state.terminal)throw Error('Cannot bind a selection to a terminal state');
 if(decision.memory!==undefined&&!same(decision.memory,memory))throw Error('Selection memory does not match checkpoint memory');
 const permitted=legal(state),proposed=decision.proposed??decision.action?.kind;
 const executed=permitted.includes(proposed)?proposed:'rest';
 if(decision.executed!==executed||!permitted.includes(executed))throw Error('Selection does not match authoritative action filtering');
 return {version:1,episodeId:state.episodeId,revision:state.revision,stateHash:hash(state),memoryHash:hash(memory),source,playMode,decisionHash:hash(decision),decision:copy(decision)};
}
export function snapshotRecovery(record,selection,source,playMode){
 if(record.state.terminal)return {version:1,phase:'terminal',selection:null};
 if(!selection)return {version:1,phase:'unselected',selection:null};
 const result=restoreSelection({...record,playMode,recovery:{version:1,phase:'selected',selection}},{source},playMode);
 if(!result.choice)throw Error('Selected checkpoint could not retain its encounter');
 return {version:1,phase:'selected',selection:copy(selection)};
}
export function restoreSelection(record,identities,playMode){
 const saved=record.recovery;
 if(record.state.terminal){if(saved&&saved.phase!=='terminal')throw Error('Checkpoint phase disagrees with terminal state');return {phase:'terminal',choice:null,selection:null};}
 if(!saved)return {phase:'legacy-unselected',choice:null,selection:null,notice:'Legacy checkpoint has no saved encounter. State and memory were restored without running the policy. Choose a new encounter explicitly to continue.'};
 if(saved.version!==1||!['selected','unselected','terminal'].includes(saved.phase))throw Error('Unknown checkpoint recovery state');
 if(saved.phase==='terminal')throw Error('Nonterminal checkpoint cannot have terminal phase');
 if(saved.phase!=='selected')return {phase:'unselected',choice:null,selection:null,notice:'State and memory restored. Choose an encounter to continue.'};
 const item=saved.selection;
 if(!item||item.version!==1||item.episodeId!==record.state.episodeId||item.revision!==record.state.revision||item.stateHash!==hash(record.state)||item.memoryHash!==hash(record.memory)||item.source!==identities.source)throw Error('Saved encounter binding does not match checkpoint state, memory or source');
 if(item.playMode!==playMode)return {phase:'unselected',choice:null,selection:null,notice:'Director mode changed explicitly. The old encounter was not rerun; choose a new encounter to continue.'};
 const checked=bindSelection(record.state,record.memory,item.decision,item.source,item.playMode);
 if(!same(checked,item))throw Error('Saved encounter is inconsistent');
 return {phase:'selected',choice:copy(item.decision),selection:copy(item)};
}
export function selectionScheduler(memory){
 const source=memory?.scheduler;
 if(source)return {...copy(source),pending:null,armed:false};
 return {used:0,maxRequests:2,serial:0,timeoutMs:25,pending:null,armed:false};
}

`courses/adaptive-decision-engine/render.mjs`:

```mjs
export const escape=s=>String(s).replace(/[&<>"']/g,c=>({'&':'&amp;','<':'&lt;','>':'&gt;','"':'&quot;',"'":'&#39;'}[c]));
const inline=s=>escape(s).replace(/`([^`]+)`/g,'<code>$1</code>').replace(/\*\*([^*]+)\*\*/g,'<strong>$1</strong>');
export function renderMarkdown(md){
 let code=false,list=false,parts=[];
 for(const line of md.split('\n')){
   if(line.startsWith('```')){if(list){parts.push('</ul>');list=false;}parts.push(code?'</code></pre>':'<pre><code>');code=!code;continue;}
   if(code){parts.push(escape(line)+'\n');continue;}
   if(/^[-*] /.test(line)){if(!list){parts.push('<ul>');list=true;}parts.push('<li>'+inline(line.slice(2))+'</li>');continue;}
   if(list){parts.push('</ul>');list=false;}
   if(!line.trim())continue;
   const fig=line.match(/^!\[([^\]]+)\]\((figures\/[a-z-]+\.svg)\)$/);if(fig){parts.push('<figure><img src="'+fig[2]+'" alt="'+escape(fig[1])+'"></figure>');continue;}
   if(/^#{1,3} /.test(line)){const n=line.indexOf(' ');parts.push(`<h${n}>${inline(line.slice(n+1))}</h${n}>`);continue;}
   const m=line.match(/^\{\{practice:([a-z0-9-]+)\}\}$/);if(m){parts.push(`<div class="practice" data-practice="${m[1]}"></div>`);continue;}
   parts.push('<p>'+inline(line)+'</p>');
 }
 if(list)parts.push('</ul>');if(code)throw new Error('unclosed code fence');return parts.join('\n');
}

```mjs
import {hash} from './shared.mjs';
// Resample complete paired episodes, never individual correlated rounds.
export function pairedInterval(rows,key='distance',count=1000){if(!rows.length)return null;const means=[];for(let b=0;b<count;b++){let sum=0;for(let i=0;i<rows.length;i++){const n=parseInt(hash(['bootstrap',b,i]),16)%rows.length;sum+=rows[n].difference[key];}means.push(sum/rows.length);}means.sort((a,b)=>a-b);return [means[Math.floor(count*.025)],means[Math.min(count-1,Math.floor(count*.975))]];}

`courses/adaptive-decision-engine/shared.mjs`:

```mjs
export const VERSION='beacon-keep/1';
export const ACTIONS=['rest','scout','swarm','brute'];
export const CARDS={rest:{threat:0,reward:0,cost:0},scout:{threat:1,reward:2,cost:1},swarm:{threat:2,reward:3,cost:2},brute:{threat:3,reward:4,cost:3}};
export const canonical=x=>JSON.stringify(x,(_,v)=>v&&typeof v==='object'&&!Array.isArray(v)?Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(v).sort(([a],[b])=>a.localeCompare(b))):v);
export function hash(x){let h=2166136261;for(const c of typeof x==='string'?x:canonical(x)){h^=c.charCodeAt(0);h=Math.imul(h,16777619);}h^=h>>>16;h=Math.imul(h,0x85ebca6b);h^=h>>>13;h=Math.imul(h,0xc2b2ae35);h^=h>>>16;return (h>>>0).toString(16).padStart(8,'0');}
export const copy=x=>JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(x));
export const distance=(p,[lo,hi])=>Math.max(lo-p,0,p-hi);
export const targetAt=(profile,round,schedule)=>schedule?schedule[round]:profile==='pulse'?(round%6<3?[.15,.35]:[.4,.65]):[.25,.55];
export function distributionOK(d,allowed){return !!d&&typeof d==='object'&&!Array.isArray(d)&&Object.keys(d).sort().join()===allowed.slice().sort().join()&&Object.values(d).every(x=>Number.isFinite(x)&&x>=0&&x<=1)&&Math.abs(Object.values(d).reduce((a,b)=>a+b,0)-1)<1e-9;}
export function wilson(y,n){if(!n)return [0,1];const z=1.96,den=1+z*z/n,c=(y/n+z*z/(2*n))/den,d=z*Math.sqrt(y/n*(1-y/n)/n+z*z/(4*n*n))/den;return [Math.max(0,c-d),Math.min(1,c+d)];}

`courses/adaptive-decision-engine/uncertainty.mjs`:

```mjs
// Supplied bound for independent episode summaries in [0,1].
// Hoeffding (1963), Theorem 2; two-sided union bound, fixed alpha.
export function episodeInterval(rates,alpha=.05){
 if(!Array.isArray(rates)||rates.some(x=>!Number.isFinite(x)||x<0||x>1)||!Number.isFinite(alpha)||alpha<=0||alpha>=1)throw Error('invalid episode summaries');
 if(!rates.length)return [0,1];
 const mean=rates.reduce((a,b)=>a+b,0)/rates.length;
 const radius=Math.sqrt(Math.log(2/alpha)/(2*rates.length));
 return [Math.max(0,mean-radius),Math.min(1,mean+radius)];
}

```

async function choose(){
 const epoch=++decisionEpoch,mode=$('#mode').value,state=structuredClone(game),inputMemory=structuredClone(memory),allSources=structuredClone(session.sources);
 selecting=true;choice=null;selection=null;renderGame();
 try{
  const source=await identity(Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(allSources).filter(([n])=>n.endsWith('.mjs'))));
  const sources=mode==='demo'?await fetch('./support/04.json').then(r=>r.json()):allSources;
  const d=await worker({task:'decision',sources,mode:mode==='project'?'project':'rules',state,memory:inputMemory});
  if(epoch!==decisionEpoch||game.episodeId!==state.episodeId||game.revision!==state.revision||$('#mode').value!==mode)return;
  const proposed=d.action?.kind,allowed=legal(state);memory=structuredClone(d.memory??inputMemory);
  choice={...d,memory:structuredClone(memory),proposed,executed:allowed.includes(proposed)?proposed:'rest',violation:!allowed.includes(proposed)};
  selection=bindSelection(state,memory,choice,source,mode);
 }finally{if(epoch===decisionEpoch){selecting=false;renderGame();}}
}

async function move(which){
 if(!choice||selecting||resolving)return;
 resolving=true;renderGame();
 try{
  const epoch=decisionEpoch,currentChoice=choice,source=await identity(Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(session.sources).filter(([n])=>n.endsWith('.mjs'))));
  if(epoch!==decisionEpoch||choice!==currentChoice)return;
  restoreSelection({state:game,memory,recovery:{version:1,phase:'selected',selection}},{source},$('#mode').value);
  game=resolve(game,{kind:choice.executed},which,game.revision).state;choice=null;selection=null;++decisionEpoch;
  session.game={state:structuredClone(game),memory:structuredClone(memory),mode:$('#mode').value};save();
  if(!game.terminal)await choose();
 }catch(e){notice('Game stopped: '+e.message);}finally{resolving=false;renderGame();}
}

`courses/adaptive-decision-engine/worker.mjs`:

```mjs
import {loadModules} from './loader.mjs';
import {runChecks} from './checks.mjs';
import {episode} from './game.mjs';
import {runEvaluation} from './evaluation.mjs';
import {calibrationReport} from './calibration-report.mjs';
async function rows(split){const url=new URL('./evaluation/'+split+'-data.json',import.meta.url);return typeof process==='undefined'?fetch(url).then(r=>r.json()):import('node:fs/promises').then(fs=>fs.readFile(url,'utf8')).then(JSON.parse);}
export async function execute(message){const modules=await loadModules(message.sources);if(message.task==='calibrate')return calibrationReport(modules['confidence.mjs'],await rows('calibration'),await rows('evaluation'));if(message.task==='checkpoint')return modules['director.mjs'].checkpoint(message.state,message.memory,message.scheduler,message.identities);if(message.task==='restore')return modules['director.mjs'].restore(message.record,message.identities);if(message.task==='decision')return message.mode==='project'?modules['project.mjs'].policy(message.state,message.memory):modules['rules.mjs'].chooseRules(modules['observe.mjs'].observe(message.state),message.memory);if(message.task==='check')return runChecks(message.unit,modules,message.sources,message.variant);if(message.task==='play'){let policyMemory={};const policy=message.mode==='project'?modules['project.mjs'].policy:(s,m)=>modules['rules.mjs'].chooseRules(modules['observe.mjs'].observe(s),m);const result=await episode(async(s,m)=>{const decision=await policy(s,m);policyMemory=structuredClone(decision.memory??m);return decision;},message.options);return {...result,policyMemory};}if(message.task==='evaluate')return runEvaluation(modules,message.manifest,message.mode,message.gates);throw Error('unknown worker task');}
if(typeof process==='undefined')self.onmessage=async({data})=>{try{self.postMessage({ok:true,value:await execute(data)});}catch(e){self.postMessage({ok:false,error:e.message});}};

```

`courses/adaptive-decision-engine/zip.mjs`:

```mjs
// Original dependency-free stored ZIP writer, used in Node and the browser.
const enc=new TextEncoder(),table=Array.from({length:256},(_,n)=>{let c=n;for(let k=0;k<8;k++)c=c&1?0xedb88320^(c>>>1):c>>>1;return c>>>0;});
const crc=bytes=>{let c=0xffffffff;for(const b of bytes)c=table[(c^b)&255]^(c>>>8);return (c^0xffffffff)>>>0;};
const bytes=x=>typeof x==='string'?enc.encode(x):new Uint8Array(x);
function header(size){const b=new Uint8Array(size);return {b,v:new DataView(b.buffer)};}
function concat(parts){const out=new Uint8Array(parts.reduce((s,p)=>s+p.length,0));let i=0;for(const p of parts){out.set(p,i);i+=p.length;}return out;}
export function zipFiles(files){
 const local=[],central=[],seen=new Set();let cursor=0;
 for(const [name,input] of files){
   if(seen.has(name))throw new Error('duplicate archive path '+name);seen.add(name);
   if(!name || name.startsWith('/') || name.includes('\\') || name.split('/').some(x=>x==='..'||!x))throw new Error(`invalid archive path ${name}`);
   const n=enc.encode(name),data=bytes(input),sum=crc(data),h=header(30),c=header(46);
   h.v.setUint32(0,0x04034b50,true);h.v.setUint16(4,20,true);h.v.setUint16(6,0x800,true);h.v.setUint16(12,33,true);h.v.setUint32(14,sum,true);h.v.setUint32(18,data.length,true);h.v.setUint32(22,data.length,true);h.v.setUint16(26,n.length,true);
   c.v.setUint32(0,0x02014b50,true);c.v.setUint16(4,20,true);c.v.setUint16(6,20,true);c.v.setUint16(8,0x800,true);c.v.setUint16(14,33,true);c.v.setUint32(16,sum,true);c.v.setUint32(20,data.length,true);c.v.setUint32(24,data.length,true);c.v.setUint16(28,n.length,true);c.v.setUint32(42,cursor,true);
