`courses/advanced-storage/CONTRACTS.md`:

```md
# Learner contract, prototype v2

This is the executable slice's contract. The wider design contains additional planned interfaces; this document names the executable scope. The current database has one process, fixed schemas, logical concurrent clients and a synchronous atomic publication boundary.

`buildEngine(BaseEngine)` returns your subclass. The supplied shell owns handles, the private write map, typed predicates, durable string encoding, disk I/O and traces. Your methods decide the eight policies below. Histories are arrays in ascending commit-sequence order. A version is `{table,key,csn,row}`; `row:null` is a tombstone. Rows are detached at client boundaries. CSNs are logical numbers, not times or disk batch IDs.

## 01 — visibleVersion(history, snapshot, examine)

Return the committed version with greatest `csn <= snapshot`, including a tombstone, or `null` when no version qualifies. Call `examine(version)` when examining a version so the trace records work. Do not mutate history. The shell overlays the transaction's own private writes before consulting this method. Requirements: R02, R03.

## 02 — commitTransaction(tx)

The shell verifies an active owned handle and refuses commit while a query is open. Your method must check `this.conflicts(tx)` before persistence. A nonempty conflict list finishes the transaction aborted. A read-only successful transaction finishes committed without generating a write CSN. Otherwise call `this.prepare(tx)`, then durably persist its result, publish its complete logical root, and finish committed. A failure during persistence/publication must poison the coordinator and return indeterminate through the supplied helper. Do not promise definite failure after losing an acknowledgement. Requirements: R04, R05.

Helpers:

| Helper | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `conflicts(tx)` | Calls your later validation policies when the current stage enables them. Unit 02 uses a declared validation-free stage and independent writes; it is not SI yet. |
| `prepare(tx)` | Returns `{csn,versions,changes,operations}` without writing; checks the version limit. |
| `persist(prepared)` | Sends one atomic batch to the accepted store. May fail after bytes became durable. |
| `publish(prepared)` | Installs the complete new logical history and CSN; no other client runs inside this synchronous call. |
| `finish(tx,state,details)` | Makes the handle terminal, closes queries, clears private writes and returns `{status:state,...details}`. |
| `indeterminate(tx,error)` | Poisons the engine, makes this handle indeterminate and returns a diagnostic. |

Successful write commits return `{status:'committed',csn}`. Validation aborts return `{status:'aborted',conflicts}`. State/input/resource errors throw with a named category. A pre-persistence resource refusal leaves the active transaction available to abort. An indeterminate coordinator must be reopened before any further use.

## 03 — writeConflicts(tx)

Return a list with one description for every conflicting key, in any order and any clear description format. Each key in `tx.writes` conflicts when its latest committed history version has `csn > tx.snapshot`. The history map uses `JSON.stringify([table,key])` keys. A tombstone counts as a committed write. Value equality does not erase a write occurrence. Conflict-free independent writers both commit. Requirements: R06, R09.

## 04 — readConflicts(tx)

Used in database-wide `serializable` mode. Return conflicts between the transaction's logical reads and committed changes after its snapshot. The shell records point reads, including missing keys, as `{kind:'point',table,key}`. Scans record `{kind:'predicate',table,predicate}` even when empty. `this.changes` contains `{table,key,csn,before,row}` entries. A predicate depends on either a matching before-image or matching after-image. `BaseEngine.matches(row,predicate)` handles typed evaluation and null rows.

The mode validates ordinary transactions even if they happen to perform no writes. An explicit `begin({readOnly:true})` prohibits writes and may serialize at its pinned snapshot; the supplied dispatcher skips conflict validation only for that declared read-only case. It guarantees the declared commit-order serial interpretation for accepted histories; it is not PostgreSQL SSI and may abort more often. All writers in a run use the same mode. An SI anomaly demonstration belongs in `snapshot` mode, where read dependencies are intentionally not validated. Requirements: R07, R08.

At scan admission, the supplied shell takes one deep copy of the complete predicate, including nested `and.args`. That owned value is used for predicate validation, index candidate selection, every iterator pull and the recorded logical dependency. Later caller mutations cannot retarget an open scan. Create a new scan to ask a different query. Capturing the query is a supplied-runtime responsibility; your `readConflicts` policy must validate the recorded dependency, not guess what a caller might have changed elsewhere.

## 05 — indexMemberships(history, field)

Return the distinct typed values appearing in any retained non-tombstone version at that field. The shell builds a materialized candidate map from these memberships and rebuilds enabled maps before publication. It derives candidate keys, then applies your visibility policy and rechecks the predicate. Use `BaseEngine.valueKey` if you need a typed map key. Private writes are merged separately. Old membership cannot disappear merely because the latest row moved. Map rebuilding is deliberately simple; an incrementally maintained tree is not implemented. Requirements: R10 and plan-independent R07.

## 06 — retainedVersions(history, watermark)

Return a nonempty safe subsequence of history. Preserve every version newer than the watermark and the newest version at or below it, when one exists. A more conservative safe list is allowed, but cleanup after all readers finish must make progress and retain only the latest version in the no-reader checks. A tombstone may be the needed boundary. The shell computes the watermark from all active transaction snapshots, including idle ones, and protects query handles until close/exhaustion/abort/error. It retains the latest tombstone even when no readers remain. Requirements: R11–R13.

The shell persists deletion records using the accepted batch store. Logical removal does not imply physical log shrinkage. No compaction speed or memory-RSS claim follows from the returned `removed` count.

## Operations available to your schedule

`begin`, `get(tx,table,key)`, `put(tx,table,key,row)`, `delete`, `scan(tx,table,predicate,{access})`, `commit`, `abort`, `vacuum`, `close`. Scan returns a closeable iterator. `access` is `scan` or `index`; index currently supports equality and `isNull`. An open query prohibits private writes and commit in that transaction. Abort closes its queries. Terminal handles cannot read, write or commit again.

Default table `items` has `label:text`, `group:text`, `active:boolean`, `value:integer`. Keys are unsigned 31-bit integers. Values can be null, or their declared type; text is valid Unicode up to 128 UTF-8 bytes, integers are signed 32-bit. Predicates support `true`, `eq`, `lt`, `ge`, `isNull`, `and`. `lt` and `ge` form a half-open range. Text comparison is bytewise UTF-8. Equality with null is false; use `isNull`. At most three tables, eight fields per table, two indexes per table, 8 active transactions, 128 distinct staged writes and 12,000 retained versions are enforced. Other larger resource targets in the design are not yet enforced by this slice.

## Scenario file

A scenario object has `mode`, `initial` and `actions`. `initial` is an array of version records conforming to the fixture format. An action names `op` and, when needed, transaction alias `tx`, `table`, `key`, `row`, `predicate` and `access`. Start each alias with `{ "op":"begin", "tx":"reader" }`. Scans are drained within one action; the lower-level API supports paused iterator tests. The scenario runner exposes `open-scan`, `pull`, `close-query`, `analyze`, `compare-plans` and `inspect`; it does not expose restart or fault injection. Those are checked directly by the public/instructor API tests and remain runner work.

Public criteria name exact requirements and can be read in `checks.mjs`. The checker records failures rather than treating code-import errors as bad database semantics. Passing these finite checks is not a proof for all client programs, independent acceptance, or a completed course.

## 07 — summarizeSnapshot and planEqualityJoin

`summarizeSnapshot(rows, field, metadata)` receives visible `{key,row}` entries and dated physical metadata. Return that metadata unchanged with `rowCount` and `frequencies:[{value,count}]`. Include null as its own value. The metadata supplies table, field, snapshot, physicalCSN, physicalRevision, physicalKeys, total versionProbes from analysis, and historical indexCandidates by value. The prototype uses exact bounded frequencies rather than sampling. The persisted physicalRevision advances on write publication and on cleanup that removes versions. Cleanup can make statistics stale even when the snapshot and physicalCSN are unchanged.

`planEqualityJoin(left,right,value,weights)` estimates three fixed candidates for a query selecting `left.field = value` and joining equal fields. Let m and n be the corresponding non-null visible frequencies; equality to null gives both zero. Let a and b be historical index candidate counts for the value. The candidate visits are: scan-loop `(left.physicalKeys, m * right.physicalKeys)`; scan-hash `(left.physicalKeys, right.physicalKeys)`; index-loop `(a, m * b)`. Estimate each side's version examinations as the ceiling of its visits times its analysis versionProbes divided by physicalKeys (zero for an empty side). Predicate evaluations equal total candidate visits. Every candidate estimates m*n output rows. Hash build adds right.rowCount, and hash probe adds m, only for scan-hash. Other hash costs are zero.

Return `{candidates,selected}`. Every candidate is `{id,estimatedRows,work,cost}` with IDs scan-loop, scan-hash, index-loop. Work fields are candidateVisits, versionExaminations, predicateEvaluations, hashBuild, hashProbe, outputRows. Cost is their weighted sum. Choose any minimum-cost candidate; numeric verification uses absolute tolerance 1e-9. Default weights are respectively 1, 2, 1, 2, 1, 1. These teaching work units are not milliseconds. The statistics may be stale and the estimates may be wrong; correctness still requires the same query result.

Planning must not execute candidates. The supplied operators and comparator own actual execution. They build needed indexes before measured comparisons and expose index-build events separately. This planning prototype rejects staged private writes; use a read-only transaction. It supports two distinct tables and one same-type equality field, not general SQL, three-way joins, correlated predicates or optimizer search.

## 08–09 — learner-authored investigations

The executable evidence interfaces and criteria are in PROJECTS.md. You author the scenarios, preserved defect/repair, observations and explanations. Source-aware author calibration is kept outside the learner packet. `engineeringPassed` is a bounded check result, not independent acceptance, a learning-effectiveness claim or course completion.

```

`courses/advanced-storage/PROJECTS.md`:

```md
# Investigation and transfer contracts

Keep your authored scenarios, run folders and descriptors inside your project (`work/`) so the supplied export copies the whole investigation. Run source is self-contained policy code exporting `buildEngine`; importing private instructor files is not a valid submission.

## Scenario operations

`begin` takes a transaction alias `tx` and optional Boolean `readOnly`. `get`, `put`, `delete`, `scan`, `commit`, `abort` use that alias. Reads/writes name `table` and where appropriate `key`, `row`, `predicate`, `access`. `open-scan` names a query alias `as`; later `pull` and `close-query` use `query`. `inspect` returns pins/version count/CSN; `vacuum` attempts logical reclamation.

`analyze` names `tx`, `table`, `field`, and a saved statistics alias `as`. `compare-plans` names `tx`, a query `{left,right,field,value}`, and `leftStats`/`rightStats` aliases. It executes all three supplied physical candidates over one snapshot. Queries in this slice require read-only transaction state (no staged writes); explicit read-only declaration is recommended. An alias cannot replace a still-active transaction or an existing query.

The scenario root is `{mode, schema, initial, actions}`. `mode` is `snapshot` or `serializable`. `schema` maps table names to column/type objects; types are `integer`, `text`, `boolean`, each nullable. `initial` contains version records `{table,key,csn,row}`. Initial rows and schemas are supplied input; your authored actions are the client program. Use a single initial CSN unless history itself is the intended test. At most 500 actions are accepted.

Execute a scenario with `node lab.mjs run work work/scenario.json work/runs/NAME --help-used none --prediction "your expected result and reason"`. The output directory must not exist. The prediction and exact source are recorded before execution. A run returns observations, not an automatic pass. Reads before a regular Serializable transaction commits are provisional; a declared read-only transaction has a stable serialization point at its snapshot and cannot write.

## Unit 08 descriptor

Author `work/investigation.json` with these fields:

| Field | Required value |
| --- | --- |
| `format` | `advanced-storage-investigation-v1` |
| `runs` | Object with `broken`, `repaired`, `variant` paths relative to the descriptor |
| `diagnosis` | Your causal explanation; nonempty presence is checked, quality uses the rubric |
| `claims` | At least two objects described below, covering predicted and observed cost |

A cost claim contains `run` (`broken`, `repaired`, `variant`), zero-based `action` index, physical `plan` ID, `measure` (`observedCost` or `estimatedCost`), and numeric `value`. The referenced action must be `compare-plans`. Absolute numeric tolerance is 1e-9; costs are work units, not time. Unsupported, conflicting or invented claims fail.

Broken and repaired runs use exactly the same scenario bytes and different source bytes. The variant uses the same repaired source but changes the transaction/read/write/cleanup operation structure. Changing labels, values, or adding only inspection/statistics bookkeeping is insufficient. All three runs replay from their saved sources and must match recorded results and runtime identity.

The broken run must exhibit a snapshot mismatch against the independent copied-map oracle. Repaired and variant runs must have none. The repaired scenario must include an overlapping commit, a read after another commit, indexed access, vacuum with and without pins, and a plan comparison. The repaired engine must pass all seven component milestones.

Run `node lab.mjs assess work work/investigation.json --help-used none`. An engineering pass is evidence for those criteria only. The explanation rubric asks for the violated invariant, discriminating schedule, causal repair, preservation of valid alternatives, and accurate distinction between estimates and measurements.

## Optional supplied witness minimization

Use `node lab.mjs minimize work/runs/broken work/witnesses/first --seed 7 --budget 80 --help-used none` to reduce a recorded snapshot defect without overwriting its original source or evidence. `show-witness` explains removed operations and the preserved failure; `replay-witness` verifies both original and reduced runs. See [WITNESSES.md](WITNESSES.md) for exact signature, budgets and export/import rules. This is supplied investigation tooling, not another learner policy. Keep the full original scenario for the required repair comparison and the independent schedule variation.

## Unit 09 supplied schema and invariant

Use tables named `items`, `collections`, and `holds`. Suggested supplied schema: items has `collection:integer`, `location:text`, `eligible:boolean`; collections has `collection:integer`, `name:text`; holds has `collection:integer`. Choose a small initial catalog with at least two items and two collections. All rows have separate integer primary keys. Use three distinct aliases for the exporter, purger and holder, with one transaction for each role in a run. Other clients may perform additional transactions.

The purge transaction reads an empty holds predicate for its target collection, then stages deletion of one or more existing items in that collection. A different transaction commits a matching hold before the purge finishes. Its change must be a holds read dependency, without a same-key write conflict masking that dependency. The SI run exposes the purge succeeding despite its outdated premise; the Serializable run aborts the purge with a holds read-conflict witness. Deleting a missing key does not demonstrate this invariant.

An exporter declared read-only starts early, retains its old item view through at least one concurrent change of collection/location, and commits successfully. After the move commits, retrieve the moved item through an indexed predicate that matches its old membership but not its new one. A drained scan or an explicitly consumed iterator is accepted. Observe cleanup while the exporter is pinned, then demonstrate actual version removal after all pins close. Make a within-snapshot plan comparison in the export view and another in a later snapshot. A current observer is allowed—and expected—to see different data from the exporter.

Author `work/transfer.json`:

| Field | Required value |
| --- | --- |
| `format` | `advanced-storage-transfer-v1` |
| `runs` | Paths named `snapshot` and `serializable`, relative to this descriptor |
| `roles` | Your transaction aliases named `exporter`, `purger`, `holder` |
| `explanation` | Your invariant/retention/plan-cost argument |

The two scenario files must differ only in database-wide mode, and both use the same current engine source. The checker verifies all snapshot observations with the copied-map oracle, the specific purge/hold pattern, the read-only exporter, index/lifetime work, separate view comparisons and component regressions. It does not grade prose quality or claim an independently authored unseen assessment.

Run `node lab.mjs transfer work work/transfer.json --help-used none`. Then export outside the source tree and repeat the component checks, `assess`, and `transfer` using the copied project. Local engineering flags are not a learning certificate or a live-course completion claim.

## Workshop preparation

The [schedule experiment workshop](WORKSHOP.md) can supply learner-authored schedules and ordinary run directories for these projects. Each deterministic trial is stored at `EXPERIMENT/trials/TRIAL`; actual snapshot failures can enter the existing minimizer unchanged. Compare predicted and observed behavior, preserve your failing policy, repair it on the same schedule, then add a structurally different challenge. Workshop completion alone does not satisfy the investigation or transfer criteria in this document.

`courses/advanced-storage/README.md`:

```md
# Advanced Storage: concurrent snapshots

Build eight database policies on a supplied durable store: version visibility, atomic commit ordering, write conflicts, predicate conflicts, historical index membership, safe version retention, snapshot statistics and costed plan selection.

**This public source course contains nine units.** Seven cumulative code milestones lead to an adversarial investigation and an unfamiliar archive-export transfer. The reference and controls have source-aware engineering evidence. Local terminal and reader journeys have bounded checks; a blind learner trial, human learning and comprehensive accessibility remain unverified. The source is available in the public Free to Learn repository; this does not claim a hosted course service or independent learning validation.

## Start

Clone the public source once, record the revision, and enter this course directory:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/itsHabib/free-to-learn.git
cd free-to-learn
git rev-parse HEAD
cd courses/advanced-storage
```

Keep the printed revision with your notes so another learner can reproduce your source. For an assigned revision, run `git checkout --detach FULL_COMMIT_SHA` from the repository root before entering the course directory, replacing `FULL_COMMIT_SHA` with that revision. If you already have a local checkout, enter its `courses/advanced-storage` directory directly. All commands below run there. A ZIP download and access to a private Ivy repository are not required.

Use Node **26.5.1**. That is the tested runtime; other versions/platforms are unqualified. After obtaining the public source, the course runs offline: no npm install, account or paid service is needed.

```sh
node lab.mjs doctor
node lab.mjs start work
node lab.mjs question 01a
node lab.mjs check work 01 --help-used none
```

The last command should report unfinished visibility code in the untouched starter. To commit a question response, run `node lab.mjs answer work 01a RESPONSE_JSON --help-used none`, replacing `RESPONSE_JSON` with your JSON answer; quote strings and arrays for your shell. Read [the contract](CONTRACTS.md) and [unit 01](lessons/01.md), edit `work/engine.mjs`, then check again. Continue through [02](lessons/02.md), [03](lessons/03.md), [04](lessons/04.md), [05](lessons/05.md), [06](lessons/06.md), [07](lessons/07.md), [08](lessons/08.md) and [09](lessons/09.md). Checks are cumulative. You can read every lesson without passing a check.

Unit 01 includes a [bounded visibility scaffold and snapshot experiment](lessons/01.md#014-run-a-snapshot-experiment). Run `node verify-opening.mjs` to verify its displayed code and the supplied probe independently of your solution. This is a teaching-material check, not a learner pass.

Each check and snapshot probe saves your exact source, assistance declaration and result in a new attempt directory. Each answer is committed before its feedback is printed. Prior attempts remain intact. Public questions/checks are readable; these local records are neither secret tests nor authenticated authorship certificates. If you use hints, a model, another person or supplied code, describe that in `--help-used`.

You need JavaScript ES modules, arrays/Map, exceptions, basic concurrency traces and the previous recoverable-storage course or equivalent. The supplied foundation owns framing, WAL, short writes, recovery and compaction. You do not rebuild those. The shell also supplies schema checking, disk transport, private-write storage, query handles and trace recording; your eight policy methods make the database decisions.

## Preserve and replay your work

```sh
node lab.mjs export work ../advanced-storage-export
```

The destination must be new and outside this course/project. In that exported directory, run `node lab.mjs check work 07 --help-used "export replay"`. This creates a fresh result without rewriting historical passes. Exports include the learner source and attempts, never the separate instructor directory.

Use `node lab.mjs run work SCENARIO.json NEW_RUN_DIRECTORY --help-used none --prediction "your expected outcome"` to run your own transaction schedule after implementing the necessary policies. The scenario format is in the contract. The runner records actual events and a hash-bound manifest. A successful scenario execution is an observation, not a capstone pass.

For an actual wrong snapshot result, the supplied [witness minimizer](WITNESSES.md) removes irrelevant actions and initial versions while preserving the exact failure. Use `minimize`, `show-witness` and `replay-witness`; keep its output inside your project for export. Budget-limited results are explicitly best-so-far.

The [schedule experiment workshop](WORKSHOP.md) adds a prediction-and-observation loop after units 04–06. Create an editable retention or predicate workbook with `node lab.mjs workshop-init work retention work/retention`, compare copies of your own policies, and inspect snapshots, dependencies and deterministic events action by action. Genuine wrong reads feed directly into the existing witness commands. The workshop supplies no completed engine and awards no course pass.

## Limits

The core models concurrent logical clients in one process, with serialized commit publication. It does not establish thread safety, multiple-process writers, remote transactions or power-loss durability. Indexes store historical candidate memberships and rebuild their maps before publication; they are not B-trees. Queries include single-table scans and the bounded two-table equality join described in the contract. Open `index.html` directly in your installed browser for practice and pure-policy checks in units 01, 05, 06 and 07. The reader restores committed responses and policy source when reopened and exports its history. Browser work is separate from `work/engine.mjs`; use the Node route for the complete engine, persistence and final projects. Your JavaScript runs with your ordinary local permissions, not in a security sandbox. The checker subprocess has a 15-second limit; custom scenario execution is trusted local code.

The supplied `runtime/foundation.mjs` and `runtime/disk.mjs` retain verified existing MIT coverage and Free to Learn attribution; see [their notice](runtime/FOUNDATION-NOTICE.md) and complete accompanying license. Original course code uses MIT and original lesson material uses CC BY 4.0; see [License and reuse](LICENSE.md). Existing component notices remain in force.

The final two projects use [PROJECTS.md](PROJECTS.md), `node lab.mjs assess`, and `node lab.mjs transfer`. Keep their run folders inside your project for portable export. Technical references are in [SOURCES.md](SOURCES.md).

# Sources and limits

This local course prototype uses original prose, schemas, exercises, policy code and fixtures. It includes the accepted recoverable-store public support component as supplied prerequisite code; exact provenance and verified existing MIT coverage for `runtime/foundation.mjs` and `runtime/disk.mjs` are in [FOUNDATION-NOTICE.md](runtime/FOUNDATION-NOTICE.md). The complete Free to Learn copyright and permission notice accompanies those files. Original course code uses MIT and original lesson material uses CC BY 4.0 under LICENSE.md; existing supplied-component notices remain in force. The original source and accepted learner archives were left unchanged.

Primary conceptual references:

- [Berenson et al., A Critique of ANSI SQL Isolation Levels](https://arxiv.org/abs/cs/0701157): isolation definitions and Snapshot Isolation.
- [PostgreSQL 18 transaction isolation](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/18/transaction-iso.html): snapshots, anomalies and transaction retries. Our declared read-only route and conservative validation are a smaller original contract, not PostgreSQL compatibility.
- [PostgreSQL 18 index consistency](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/18/index-locking.html) and [vacuuming](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/18/routine-vacuuming.html): historical visibility, lifetime and reclamation distinctions.
- [PostgreSQL 18 planner statistics](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/18/planner-stats.html) and [EXPLAIN](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/18/using-explain.html): estimates versus observations and alternative access/join plans. This prototype's work units are its own defined model.
- [Selinger et al., Access Path Selection](https://research.ibm.com/publications/access-path-selection-in-a-relational-database-management-system): original cost-based access/join-planning reference; abstract/metadata consulted.

These sources ground technical distinctions. No university project source, purchased book material, third-party data or copied exercise is bundled. MVCC and database-building courses already exist; no novelty claim is made.

The local engineering evidence is source-aware. It does not establish human learning, difficulty, duration, complete accessibility, browser behavior, power-loss durability or production suitability. The full Node route uses only the installed runtime and local files. No API account, inference service or network call is part of normal execution. Browser checks cover a smaller set of pure policies. Direct-file practice journeys have bounded checks; complete engine and project checks use Node, and broad browser/accessibility coverage is not established.

The separate instructor reference, defective controls and calibration scenarios are excluded from the learner export. Public practice answers and checker requirements are intentionally readable; they are learning aids, not held-out learning measures. External rights, publication authorization, review and live-delivery acceptance remain separate from the licenses for project-owned material and the verified MIT coverage of the two supplied foundation files.

`courses/advanced-storage/WITNESSES.md`:

```md
# Reduce a failing schedule without changing the failure

The supplied minimizer helps you explain a wrong snapshot result. It uses the exact learner policy saved in a recorded run, even if you have since repaired `work/engine.mjs`. It never edits the original run or your current policy. A failure of the learner policy is not evidence that the supplied repaired engine is broken.

After recording a genuine failing run with `lab.mjs run`, use a new sibling directory inside your project:

```sh
node lab.mjs minimize work/runs/broken work/witnesses/first --seed 7 --budget 80 --help-used none
node lab.mjs show-witness work/witnesses/first
node lab.mjs replay-witness work/witnesses/first --help-used none
```

`show-witness` prints the expected and observed result, the reduced action trace with original indices, and removed action/data indices. The same explanation is saved as `witness.md`. The execution traces are `original/results.json` and `reduced/results.json`. This is a terminal/Markdown feature; no browser execution or phone preview is claimed.

## What counts as the same failure

The input must be a complete recorded run with `engine.mjs`, `scenario.json`, `results.json` and `manifest.json`. Source, scenario, result and runtime identities are checked before the search. Two fresh, seeded processes must reproduce the recorded execution and a mismatch against the existing copied-map snapshot oracle. A passing run, syntax error, invalid transaction schedule, stale result, timeout or resource refusal is not a semantic witness.

The target is the **first snapshot mismatch**: its original action index, mismatch kind, exact expected value and exact observed value. Every accepted candidate must preserve all four, under the same source, seed and isolation mode, and reproduce identically twice. A new earlier mismatch is a different failure and is rejected. This deliberately conservative signature can retain more data than a looser, domain-specific equivalence would.

The current oracle covers point reads, scans, iterator pulls and supplied join results. It does not prove general serializability, minimize arbitrary exceptions, or recognize every application invariant. Use it for the observation defect that unit 08 already asks you to preserve.

## Search and limits

The search removes whole transaction groups, chunks and individual actions, and initial version records. It retains the target action, preserves execution order, and does not shorten strings, rename aliases, change predicates or rewrite row values. Progress is measured as fewer actions and/or fewer initial versions, never fewer JSON bytes. Invalid candidates are discarded without becoming the new witness.

The default budget is 80 fresh-process replays and 10 seconds. `--budget` accepts 2–200; `--max-ms` accepts 100–30000. Each replay has a 750 ms limit. The seed is an unsigned 32-bit integer. It chooses deletion order and fixes `Math.random` inside replay; the original run must still match. Source using clocks, external state or other nondeterminism may be rejected. No network or external service is needed, and learner code still runs with your local permissions.

This tool accepts at most 96 actions, 128 initial versions, 64 KiB of self-contained policy source and 128 KiB of scenario JSON. Relative source imports are unsupported, consistent with the recorded-run contract. A replay result is limited to 1 MiB; a completed witness bundle to 3 MiB. Larger course schedules remain runnable but must be narrowed explicitly before this bounded tool can process them.

`best-so-far` means a replay/time budget ended. Its preserved failure is verified, but the witness is not claimed irreducible. `locally-irreducible` means the search reached a fixed point for the tested single-action, single-version and transaction-group deletions. It is never a claim of global shortest length or a proof that every remaining operation causes the defect. Read `search.json` for attempted removals, rejection categories and budget use.

## Export, import and repair

Keep the witness under `work/`. The existing `export` command copies the original run, both witness traces, exact saved policy, seed, mappings, signature and tool/runtime identities. Import by extracting/copying that exported course to a new directory, then run `replay-witness work/witnesses/first --help-used "import replay"`. Replay checks content hashes and the deletion mapping before running both cases. A stale tool/runtime or edited file requires an explicit new run; old evidence is never silently relabeled current.

Use the smaller trace to formulate your causal explanation, then repair your policy and replay the **full original scenario**. The reduced witness does not replace unit 08's composed-mechanism checks, same-scenario repair or genuinely different schedule variation. Keep the failing source and witness as evidence rather than overwriting them with a passing implementation.

`courses/advanced-storage/WORKSHOP.md`:

```md
# Schedule experiment workshop

Turn a concurrency claim into a schedule you can change, predict and inspect. You use **your own policy implementation** on the supplied course engine. There is no completed engine hidden in this workshop.

Start after unit 04 for the predicate experiment with scans. Implement unit 05 before running its index trials. Start the retention experiment after unit 06. An untouched starter still reports its unimplemented methods; creating a workbook does not complete them.

## First experiment

From the course directory, using Node 26.5.1:

```sh
node lab.mjs workshop-init work retention work/retention
```

This creates `work/retention/workbook.json` and two copies of your current policy, `baseline.mjs` and `candidate.mjs`. Your project engine and previous attempts stay intact. Keep the baseline as your control; edit the candidate to explore a different collection policy. Both initially contain the same code, so their results should agree until you change something.

Open the workbook in your text editor. It contains a real, editable transaction schedule, named observation checkpoints and separate predictions for each trial. The retention schedule pauses a query, commits a writer, collects versions, closes just the query, collects again, then ends the reader and collects once more.

1. Trace the starting versions by hand. Which version is each reader entitled to use?
2. For every trial/checkpoint, add an `expected` JSON value and write `because`. Predict the actual behavior of that policy, including suspected defects. Do not write only what you wish a correct database would do.
3. Run the experiment after committing those predictions:

```sh
node lab.mjs workshop-run work work/retention/workbook.json work/retention-run-1 --help-used none
node lab.mjs workshop-show work/retention-run-1
node lab.mjs workshop-show work/retention-run-1 candidate clean-paused
node lab.mjs workshop-show work/retention-run-1 candidate old-pull
```

The command refuses missing predictions or reasons **before** executing policy code or creating the experiment directory. It snapshots the workbook, schedules and policy files before any trial runs. Reusing an output directory is refused. Each run leaves the original predictions visible beside the observations, even when they were wrong.

Here is the format for one prediction in the initial retention workbook:

```json
"old-snapshot": {
  "expected": 2,
  "because": "The reader begins after the initial versions at CSN 2 and before the writer publishes."
}
```

Fill the other predictions yourself. A row prediction needs the complete row object (or `null` for absence). A `pull` prediction needs the complete iterator result: either `{"done":true}` or `{"done":false,"value":{"key":1,"row":{...}}}`. The ellipsis is explanatory, not valid JSON. Pin predictions use the runtime form `[{"tx":1,"snapshot":2,"openQueries":0}]`; transaction IDs start at 1 in begin order.

## Experiment A: how much history is enough?

Compare your current retention method with a candidate of your choice. One deliberately risky hypothesis is that keeping only each key's latest version is enough. Another is that keeping all history forever is safest. A third preserves the watermark boundary. Implement the alternative yourself in `candidate.mjs`, then predict its different removal counts **and** old-reader results.

Inspect `clean-paused`, `idle`, `clean-idle`, `old-get` and `clean-free`. The trace exposes active transaction snapshots, open query counts, retained-version count, logical read dependencies and the exact events emitted. A closed iterator does not end its transaction. Explain a remaining pin using the actual transaction state, not a rule about whether someone recently read a row.

Now change the experiment, not only the algorithm:

- Move `old-start` and `open` after `publish`. Update your predictions before rerunning. Does the latest-only candidate still lose a needed version for this schedule?
- Add a second reader beginning after `publish`, release the original reader before `clean-idle`, and predict the new watermark. Give every new action and transaction a new ID/alias.
- Replace the writer's update with a delete. Predict the tombstone case, including what the old and new readers see. Keep the other rows as controls.

Save each revision in a new output directory. Find a schedule that distinguishes your two policies, then a schedule on which they agree. Agreement on one schedule is not general safety. Keeping everything may preserve every observed read while failing the cleanup progress contract; the snapshot oracle does not grade that progress.

## Experiment B: two bookings, one empty predicate

```sh
node lab.mjs workshop-init work predicate work/bookings
```

Both ordinary transactions read the same empty `group = reserved` predicate and then reserve different keys. The workbook compares your baseline in Snapshot mode, Serializable mode with a scan, and Serializable mode with an index. A fourth trial uses your candidate policy with Serializable/index access. If unit 05 is unfinished, remove both index trials for now; add them back after implementing index membership.

Predict each commit status and the fresh reader's final keys. The application rule is **at most one reservation**. Decide from the final keys whether it holds. No canned "invariant passed" result is supplied.

Inspect `b-empty` in the scan and index trials. Read the captured predicate in the transaction state. An empty result still records a dependency. Then inspect `b-commit`: which committed change intersects that dependency? Index candidate counts may differ while the logical question stays the same.

Make at least one further experiment and predict all affected checkpoints:

- Reverse `a-commit` and `b-commit`. Which writer survives the conservative Serializable rule?
- Change b's predicate and staged row to a different group. Should unrelated bookings both be admitted?
- Stage the same key in both transactions. Separate a write/write rejection from predicate validation.
- In `candidate.mjs`, change only your predicate conflict policy. Can it miss an insertion into an empty result? Can it reject unrelated activity? Explain both an accepted and a rejected outcome.

The writes in this workbook are explicit schedule actions, not conditional application code. If you move a read so it becomes nonempty, you must also reconsider whether the application would still issue that write. This workshop does not invent application branches.

`snapshot` and `serializable` are the course modes, not selectable isolation levels on a real database. The latter is the course's conservative commit-order validation, not PostgreSQL SSI. Declaring these booking transactions `readOnly:true` is not a way to avoid conflicts: their writes would be invalid.

## Author a different schedule

The JSON remains yours to edit. Keep `format` as `advanced-storage-workshop-v1` and supply a title, an experimental question and an integer seed. `scenario.initial` and `scenario.actions` use [the existing course contract](CONTRACTS.md). Every action also needs a unique lowercase `id`, such as `reader-before-cleanup`. It remains attached to the action in exported runs and reduced witnesses.

A trial selects a policy source relative to the workbook, an explicit `mode`, and optionally `access:"scan"` or `access:"index"`. The access override applies to **every** scan/open-scan in that trial. Omit it to use each action's access selection. Use an index-compatible equality or `isNull` predicate for an index trial; a range with index access is an invalid experiment, not a database anomaly. All selected policy files must live inside your project and fit the course's portable self-contained `buildEngine(BaseEngine)` interface.

A checkpoint names an action and a projection of its result, after-action state or measured work:

```json
{
  "id": "visible-values",
  "after": "my-scan",
  "path": ["result", "*", "row", "value"],
  "question": "Which values does this reader see, in key order?"
}
```

`*` maps over an array. Use `['state','versions']` for retained-version count, `['state','pins']` for pins, or `['work','versionExaminations']` for this action's measured version probes (write these as double-quoted JSON strings). Results are compared as JSON values; object key order is ignored and array order is preserved. Missing fields are reported as unavailable, never silently equated with `null`. Comparison is exact; there is no numeric tolerance.

Limits are 96 actions, 128 initial versions, four trials, 48 checkpoints, 128 KiB per workbook, 64 KiB per policy, 750 ms per execution and one MiB of worker output. The workshop uses the basic transaction/query/cleanup actions; plan analysis and fault injection remain with the existing course interfaces. It stops writing if internal free space is below 5,000,000,000 bytes or the destination lacks room for the planned output. Output on an internal path must also preserve that internal floor. These are bounded experiments on trusted local code, not a JavaScript security sandbox.

## Read a disagreement honestly

The report separates three questions:

| Evidence | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Prediction matched/different | Whether your prior JSON claim equals the observed projection. Predicting broken behavior correctly still matches. |
| Snapshot mismatches | Whether the existing copied-map oracle found a wrong read against the observed commit history. It does not grade which commits should have been admitted. |
| Execution status | Whether the trial completed and repeated identically. Invalid operations, missing implementations, resource limits, timeouts and differing repeats are not semantic witnesses. |

A Snapshot-mode two-booking anomaly can have **zero snapshot mismatches**: each client read a valid old view. A bad Serializable validator can also admit both without producing a wrong snapshot value. Use the commit statuses, final keys and dependencies to explain that failure; the existing minimizer does not minimize application invariants or commit-admission errors.

Every completed trial runs twice in fresh processes using the same seeded `Math.random`. This detects variation in those two observations; it does not control clocks, filesystem state or arbitrary code effects. A differing repeat retains both outputs and receives no ordinary run manifest. Inspect `observation.json` and `repeat.json`. If a worker throws, available partial events remain visible; a forcibly timed-out process may provide no partial trace.

## Take a real wrong read into the existing minimizer

When the report identifies an actual snapshot mismatch for a deterministic trial, its `trials/TRIAL` directory already has the existing run format. For example, after your retention candidate demonstrably loses an old view:

```sh
node lab.mjs minimize work/retention-run-1/trials/candidate work/retention-witness --seed 17 --budget 80 --help-used none
node lab.mjs show-witness work/retention-witness
node lab.mjs replay-witness work/retention-witness --help-used none
```

Use the seed saved in your workbook if you changed it. The minimizer independently checks exact source/runtime/results and fresh reproducibility. It can refuse a candidate; the workshop does not manufacture a failing result for it. [Its original limitations](WITNESSES.md) still apply.

Read which actions survived, explain the first wrong read, repair your candidate, and rerun the **same** workbook into a new experiment directory. Keep your earlier prediction and failure. Then construct a structurally different schedule to challenge the repair. This is preparation for [unit 08's investigation](PROJECTS.md), not a replacement for its requirements or a course completion verdict.

## Preserve the experiment

The project export includes workbooks, policy snapshots, predictions, event traces, run manifests and witnesses:

```sh
node lab.mjs export work ../advanced-storage-with-workshop
```

From the exported directory, `node lab.mjs workshop-show work/retention-run-1` verifies saved file hashes and displays the recorded comparison. It does not rerun policy code. Use `workshop-run` with a new destination for new evidence, or `replay-witness` to verify a reduced failure. Hashes detect accidental changes; editable local receipts are not authenticated authorship certificates.

These schedules use the real supplied **course implementation** and its in-memory disk model. A `durable` event means that model acknowledged a batch. It is not an experiment on hardware durability, real filesystem recovery, physical disk shrinkage, OS threads or distributed transactions. Measured work counters are not elapsed-time benchmarks. The original local-use and publication-rights restrictions remain in force.

`courses/advanced-storage/browser-policy-checks.mjs`:

```mjs
// Bounded pure-policy checks only. Full engine/persistence checks require Node.
export function runPolicyChecks(module, unit) {
  class Shell { static valueKey(v) { return JSON.stringify([typeof v,v]); } }
  const Engine=module.buildEngine(Shell), engine=new Engine(), results=[];
  const equal=(a,b)=>{if(JSON.stringify(a)!==JSON.stringify(b))throw Error(`Expected ${JSON.stringify(b)}, observed ${JSON.stringify(a)}`);};
  const check=(id,fn)=>{try{fn();results.push({id,passed:true});}catch(e){results.push({id,passed:false,message:e.message});}};
  const h=[{csn:2,row:{group:'A',value:4}},{csn:5,row:null},{csn:9,row:{group:'B',value:7}}];
  if(unit==='01') {
    check('R03 boundary',()=>equal(engine.visibleVersion(h,2)?.row.value,4));
    check('R03 future exclusion',()=>equal(engine.visibleVersion(h,4)?.row.value,4));
    check('R03 deletion',()=>equal(engine.visibleVersion(h,8)?.row,null));
    check('R03 absence',()=>equal(engine.visibleVersion(h,1),null));
    check('R03 examine',()=>{const one=[h[0]], seen=[];equal(engine.visibleVersion(one,2,v=>seen.push(v))?.row.value,4);equal(seen.length>0&&seen.every(v=>one.includes(v)),true);});
  } else if(unit==='05') {
    check('R10 historical membership',()=>equal(engine.indexMemberships(h,'group').slice().sort(),['A','B']));
    check('R10 unique membership',()=>equal(engine.indexMemberships([...h,{csn:10,row:{group:'B'}}],'group').slice().sort(),['A','B']));
  } else if(unit==='06') {
    check('R11 boundary retention',()=>{const kept=engine.retainedVersions(h,8).map(v=>v.csn);equal(kept.includes(5)&&kept.includes(9),true);});
    check('R11 no-reader progress',()=>equal(engine.retainedVersions(h,9).map(v=>v.csn),[9]));
  } else if(unit==='07') {
    const weights={candidateVisits:1,versionExaminations:2,predicateEvaluations:1,hashBuild:2,hashProbe:1,outputRows:1};
    const stats=n=>({rowCount:n,physicalKeys:n,versionProbes:n,frequencies:[{value:'A',count:n}],indexCandidates:[{value:'A',count:n}]});
    check('R16 many-match crossover',()=>equal(engine.planEqualityJoin(stats(8),stats(12),'A',weights).selected,'scan-hash'));
    check('R15 visible frequencies',()=>equal(engine.summarizeSnapshot([{key:1,row:{group:'A'}}],'group',{snapshot:4}).frequencies,[{value:'A',count:1}]));
  } else throw Error('Choose a supported pure-policy unit.');
  return results;
}

`courses/advanced-storage/checks.mjs`:

```mjs
import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
import { MemoryDisk } from './runtime/disk.mjs';
import { openStore } from './runtime/foundation.mjs';
import { DEFAULT_SCHEMA } from './runtime/base.mjs';
import { analyze, comparePlans, explain, executePlan, COST_WEIGHTS } from './runtime/plans.mjs';

export const row = (value, group = 'A', active = true) => ({ label: `item-${value}`, group, active, value });
export function fixture(Engine, versions = [{ table: 'items', key: 1, csn: 1, row: row(10) }], options = {}) {
  const disk = options.disk ?? new MemoryDisk(), store = openStore(disk);
  const csn = Math.max(0, ...versions.map(v => v.csn));
  store.batch([...versions.map(v => ({ type: 'put', key: `v:${v.table}:${v.key}:${v.csn}`, value: JSON.stringify(v) })),
    { type: 'put', key: 'meta', value: JSON.stringify({ format: 1, csn, schema: options.schema ?? DEFAULT_SCHEMA }) }]);
  store.close(); return new Engine({ ...options, disk });
}
const ver = (key, csn, value, group = 'A') => ({ table: 'items', key, csn, row: value === null ? null : row(value, group) });
const commitPut = (db, key, value, group = 'A') => { const t = db.begin(); db.put(t, 'items', key, row(value, group)); assert.equal(db.commit(t).status, 'committed'); };
const rows = (db, tx, p = { op: 'true' }, access = 'scan') => [...db.scan(tx, 'items', p, { access })];
const eq = (field, value) => ({ op: 'eq', field, value });
const range = (lo, hi) => ({ op: 'and', args: [{ op: 'ge', field: 'value', value: lo }, { op: 'lt', field: 'value', value: hi }] });
const tests = [];
function test(unit, id, name, run) { tests.push({ unit, id, name, run }); }

test(1, 'R03-boundary', 'A commit exactly at the snapshot is visible; future commits are not.', E => {
  const db = fixture(E), h = [ver(1, 1, 10), ver(1, 4, 40), ver(1, 9, 90)];
  assert.equal(db.visibleVersion(h, 4)?.row.value, 40); assert.equal(db.visibleVersion(h, 8)?.row.value, 40);
  assert.equal(db.visibleVersion(h, 0), null); assert.equal(db.visibleVersion([], 9), null);
});
test(1, 'R03-examine', 'Visibility reports examined versions so measured work is not silently omitted.', E => {
  const db = fixture(E), h = [ver(1, 2, 20)], seen = [];
  assert.equal(db.visibleVersion(h, 2, v => seen.push(v))?.row.value, 20);
  assert.ok(seen.length > 0, 'Call examine(version) when inspecting a version.');
  assert.ok(seen.every(v => h.includes(v)), 'Report the actual examined history version.');
});
test(1, 'R03-delete', 'A visible tombstone stays absent even when an older value exists.', E => {
  const db = fixture(E), h = [ver(1, 1, 10), ver(1, 2, null), ver(1, 5, 50)];
  assert.equal(db.visibleVersion(h, 3)?.row, null); assert.equal(db.visibleVersion(h, 5)?.row.value, 50);
});
test(1, 'R03-own-write', 'Private writes and deletion affect only their owner.', E => {
  const db = fixture(E), a = db.begin(), b = db.begin(); db.put(a, 'items', 1, row(11));
  assert.equal(db.get(a, 'items', 1).value, 11); assert.equal(db.get(b, 'items', 1).value, 10);
  db.delete(a, 'items', 1); assert.equal(db.get(a, 'items', 1), null); assert.equal(db.get(b, 'items', 1).value, 10);
});
test(1, 'R02-detached', 'Mutating a returned object cannot alter stored history.', E => {
  const db = fixture(E), t = db.begin(), result = db.get(t, 'items', 1); result.value = 999;
  assert.equal(db.get(t, 'items', 1).value, 10);
});
test(1, 'R03-overlay-scan', 'Scan merges private inserts and removes private deletions once.', E => {
  const db = fixture(E), t = db.begin(); db.put(t, 'items', 2, row(20)); db.delete(t, 'items', 1);
  assert.deepEqual(rows(db, t).map(x => x.key), [2]);
});
test(1, 'R03-examine-work', 'A reader several versions behind reports more than the one version it returns.', E => {
  const db = fixture(E), h = [ver(1, 1, 10), ver(1, 4, 40), ver(1, 7, 70), ver(1, 9, 90)], seen = [];
  assert.equal(db.visibleVersion(h, 5, v => seen.push(v))?.row.value, 40);
  assert.ok(new Set(seen).size >= 2, 'With the snapshot between two commits, any search must look at a version on each side of it; report each version you examine.');
});

test(2, 'R05-two-row', 'A multi-row commit leaves an old reader on its entire old snapshot.', E => {
  const db = fixture(E, [ver(1, 1, 10), ver(2, 1, 20)], { stage: 2 }), old = db.begin(), w = db.begin();
  db.put(w, 'items', 1, row(11)); db.put(w, 'items', 2, row(21)); assert.equal(db.commit(w).status, 'committed');
  assert.deepEqual(rows(db, old).map(x => x.row.value), [10, 20]); assert.deepEqual(rows(db, db.begin()).map(x => x.row.value), [11, 21]);
  const phases = db.events.filter(e => ['persist-start', 'durable', 'published', 'committed'].includes(e.type)).map(e => e.type);
  assert.deepEqual(phases, ['persist-start', 'durable', 'published', 'committed']);
});
test(2, 'R05-reopen', 'Both rows survive a fresh engine reopening the same accepted store.', E => {
  const db = fixture(E, [], { stage: 2 }), t = db.begin(); db.put(t, 'items', 7, row(70)); db.put(t, 'items', 8, row(80));
  assert.equal(db.commit(t).status, 'committed'); const restored = new E({ disk: db.disk, stage: 2 });
  assert.deepEqual(rows(restored, restored.begin()).map(x => x.row.value), [70, 80]);
});
test(2, 'R05-uncertain', 'Failure after durable acknowledgement poisons the engine; reopen finds the whole commit.', E => {
  const db = fixture(E, [], { stage: 2, fault: phase => { if (phase === 'after-durable') throw Error('injected stop'); } }), t = db.begin();
  db.put(t, 'items', 1, row(1)); db.put(t, 'items', 2, row(2)); assert.equal(db.commit(t).status, 'indeterminate');
  assert.throws(() => db.begin(), /reopen/); const restored = new E({ disk: db.disk }); assert.equal(rows(restored, restored.begin()).length, 2);
});
test(2, 'R05-uncertain-before-durable', 'A failure inside persistence, even before the durable acknowledgement, is indeterminate, never a definite abort.', E => {
  // CONTRACTS 02: "A failure during persistence/publication must poison the coordinator and return indeterminate through the supplied helper."
  const db = fixture(E, [], { stage: 2, fault: phase => { if (phase === 'before-persist') throw Error('injected stop'); } }), t = db.begin();
  db.put(t, 'items', 1, row(1)); assert.equal(db.commit(t).status, 'indeterminate');
  assert.throws(() => db.begin(), /reopen/);
});
test(2, 'R05-read-only-csn', 'A successful transaction without writes does not allocate or persist a write CSN.', E => {
  for (const declared of [false, true]) {
    const db = fixture(E, undefined, { stage: 2 }), before = db.csn;
    const t = db.begin({ readOnly: declared }); db.get(t, 'items', 1);
    const events = db.events.length;
    assert.equal(db.commit(t).status, 'committed');
    assert.equal(db.csn, before, 'A read-only commit must not consume a write CSN.');
    assert.equal(db.pins().length, 0);
    assert.ok(!db.events.slice(events).some(e => ['persist-start', 'durable', 'published'].includes(e.type)), 'No write persistence for a read-only commit.');
    const reopened = new E({ disk: db.disk, stage: 2 }); assert.equal(reopened.csn, before);
    const w = reopened.begin(); reopened.put(w, 'items', 2, row(20));
    assert.equal(reopened.commit(w).csn, before + 1);
  }
});
test(2, 'R04-terminal', 'A terminal handle cannot commit twice, write or read again.', E => {
  const db = fixture(E, [], { stage: 2 }), t = db.begin(); db.put(t, 'items', 1, row(1)); db.commit(t);
  assert.throws(() => db.commit(t), /active/); assert.throws(() => db.get(t, 'items', 1), /active/); assert.throws(() => db.put(t, 'items', 2, row(2)), /active/);
});
test(2, 'R04-open-query', 'Open queries block commit and private writes until closed.', E => {
  const db = fixture(E, undefined, { stage: 2 }), t = db.begin(), q = db.scan(t, 'items');
  assert.throws(() => db.commit(t), /Close queries/); assert.throws(() => db.put(t, 'items', 2, row(2)), /Close queries/);
  q.close(); assert.equal(db.commit(t).status, 'committed'); assert.equal(db.pins().length, 0);
});

test(3, 'R06-same-key', 'The second writer of a shared key aborts after the first commits.', E => {
  const db = fixture(E), a = db.begin(), b = db.begin(); db.put(a, 'items', 1, row(11)); db.put(b, 'items', 1, row(12));
  assert.equal(db.commit(a).status, 'committed'); assert.equal(db.commit(b).status, 'aborted'); assert.equal(db.get(db.begin(), 'items', 1).value, 11);
});
test(3, 'R06-abort-not-durable', 'A validation abort reaches no storage: after reopening the store the aborted write is absent.', E => {
  // CONTRACTS 02: "Your method must check this.conflicts(tx) before persistence. A nonempty conflict list finishes the transaction aborted."
  const db = fixture(E), a = db.begin(), b = db.begin(); db.put(a, 'items', 1, row(11)); db.put(b, 'items', 1, row(12));
  assert.equal(db.commit(a).status, 'committed'); const csn = db.csn, events = db.events.length;
  assert.equal(db.commit(b).status, 'aborted');
  assert.ok(!db.events.slice(events).some(e => ['persist-start', 'durable', 'published'].includes(e.type)), 'Check conflicts before persistence: an aborted commit must not persist or publish anything.');
  const restored = new E({ disk: db.disk });
  assert.equal(restored.csn, csn, 'Reopening must not find a commit that was reported aborted.');
  assert.equal(restored.get(restored.begin(), 'items', 1)?.value, 11, 'Reopening must show the committed writer, not the aborted one.');
});
test(3, 'R09-independent', 'Independent active writers both commit and do not move an old reader.', E => {
  const db = fixture(E), r = db.begin(), a = db.begin(), b = db.begin(); db.put(a, 'items', 2, row(2)); db.put(b, 'items', 3, row(3));
  assert.equal(db.commit(a).status, 'committed'); assert.equal(db.commit(b).status, 'committed'); assert.equal(db.get(r, 'items', 2), null);

test(3, 'R06-absent-insert', 'Two writers inserting the same previously absent key still conflict.', E => {

test(3, 'R06-ABA', 'Changing a value and restoring it does not erase a write conflict.', E => {

test(3, 'R06-all-conflicts', 'Write validation reports every conflicting key, not only the first one.', E => {

test(3, 'R06-delete-reinsert', 'A stale reinsertion conflicts with a committed deletion.', E => {

test(3, 'R04-abort-terminal', 'A validation abort finishes the handle: no pin remains and it cannot be used again.', E => {

test(4, 'R07-read-then-deleted', 'A committed deletion of a row that was read is a conflict, for a point read and for a predicate read.', E => {

test(5, 'R10-null-and-typed', 'Null is an indexed value of its own, distinct from the text "null"; index and full scan agree.', E => {
  // CONTRACTS 05: "distinct typed values"; operations: index access "supports equality and isNull".
  const nullRow = { label: 'item-1', group: null, active: true, value: 1 };
  const db = fixture(E, [{ table: 'items', key: 1, csn: 1, row: nullRow }, ver(2, 1, 2, 'B')]), old = db.begin();

const twoTables = { items: DEFAULT_SCHEMA.items, bookings: DEFAULT_SCHEMA.items };
function joinFixture(E, selective = true) {
  const versions = [];
  for (let key = 1; key <= 8; key++) versions.push({ table: 'items', key, csn: 1, row: row(key, !selective || key === 1 ? 'A' : 'B') });
  for (let key = 1; key <= 12; key++) versions.push({ table: 'bookings', key, csn: 1, row: row(key, !selective || key === 1 ? 'A' : 'C') });
  return fixture(E, versions, { schema: twoTables });
}
const query = { left: 'items', right: 'bookings', field: 'group', value: 'A' };
test(7, 'R15-summary', 'Snapshot statistics preserve snapshot identity and visible value frequencies.', E => {
  const db = joinFixture(E), t = db.begin(), stats = analyze(db, t, 'items', 'group');
  assert.equal(stats.snapshot, t.snapshot); assert.equal(stats.rowCount, 8); assert.equal(stats.physicalKeys, 8);
  assert.equal(stats.frequencies.find(x => x.value === 'A')?.count, 1); assert.equal(stats.frequencies.find(x => x.value === 'B')?.count, 7);
  assert.ok(stats.versionProbes >= 8, 'Visibility work must be recorded, not silently omitted.');
});
test(7, 'R14-plan-equivalence', 'All supplied physical plans return the same bag of joined rows.', E => {
  const db = joinFixture(E), t = db.begin(), stats = { left: analyze(db, t, 'items', 'group'), right: analyze(db, t, 'bookings', 'group') };
  const result = comparePlans(db, t, query, stats); assert.ok(result.runs.every(r => r.rows.length === 1));
  assert.equal(result.explanation.selected, 'index-loop');
});
test(7, 'R16-plan-crossover', 'Many matching rows make hash preferable to repeated index probes under this profile.', E => {
  const db = joinFixture(E, false), t = db.begin(), stats = { left: analyze(db, t, 'items', 'group'), right: analyze(db, t, 'bookings', 'group') };
  const result = comparePlans(db, t, query, stats); assert.ok(result.runs.every(r => r.rows.length === 96));
  assert.equal(result.explanation.selected, 'scan-hash');
  assert.ok(result.runs.find(r => r.id === 'scan-hash').cost < result.runs.find(r => r.id === 'index-loop').cost);
});
test(7, 'R16-cost-estimates', 'Estimated work includes version examinations and weighted component costs.', E => {
  const db = joinFixture(E), t = db.begin(), left = analyze(db, t, 'items', 'group'), right = analyze(db, t, 'bookings', 'group');
  const result = explain(db, t, query, left, right), index = result.candidates.find(c => c.id === 'index-loop');
  assert.equal(index.work.candidateVisits, 2); assert.ok(index.work.versionExaminations >= 2); assert.equal(index.estimatedRows, 1);
});
test(7, 'R15-stale', 'New physical history marks older statistics stale without changing an old query result.', E => {
  const db = joinFixture(E), t = db.begin(), left = analyze(db, t, 'items', 'group'), right = analyze(db, t, 'bookings', 'group');
  commitPut(db, 1, 100, 'B'); const result = comparePlans(db, t, query, { left, right });
  assert.equal(result.explanation.stale, true); assert.ok(result.runs.every(r => r.rows.length === 1));
});
test(7, 'R15-vacuum-generation', 'Cleanup dates physical statistics even when the logical snapshot does not change.', E => {
  const db = joinFixture(E); commitPut(db,1,100); commitPut(db,1,101);
  const t = db.begin({readOnly:true}), left=analyze(db,t,'items','group'), right=analyze(db,t,'bookings','group');
  const before=comparePlans(db,t,query,{left,right}); assert.equal(before.explanation.stale,false);

test(7, 'R15-summary-contract', 'A summary returns its metadata unchanged, counts every visible row and keeps null as its own value.', E => {
  // CONTRACTS 07: "Return that metadata unchanged with rowCount and frequencies:[{value,count}]. Include null as its own value."
  const db = fixture(E), metadata = { table: 'items', field: 'group', snapshot: 3, physicalCSN: 7, physicalRevision: 9, physicalKeys: 4, versionProbes: 6, indexCandidates: [{ value: 'A', count: 2 }, { value: null, count: 1 }] };
  const visible = [{ key: 1, row: row(1, 'A') }, { key: 2, row: { ...row(2), group: null } }, { key: 3, row: row(3, 'B') }];
  const result = db.summarizeSnapshot(visible, 'group', structuredClone(metadata)), { rowCount, frequencies } = result;
  for (const key of Object.keys(metadata)) assert.deepEqual(result[key], metadata[key], 'Metadata field ' + key + ' must come back unchanged.');
  assert.equal(rowCount, 3);
  assert.deepEqual(frequencies.map(f => [typeof f.value, f.value, f.count]).sort(), [['object', null, 1], ['string', 'A', 1], ['string', 'B', 1]]);
});
test(7, 'R16-estimate-formulas', 'Each candidate follows the published estimate formulas with the supplied weights.', E => {
  // CONTRACTS 07: visits scan-loop (left.physicalKeys, m * right.physicalKeys); scan-hash (left.physicalKeys, right.physicalKeys);
  // index-loop (a, m * b). Version examinations per side: ceiling of visits * versionProbes / physicalKeys. Predicate
  // evaluations equal total visits. Every candidate estimates m*n rows. Hash build adds right.rowCount and hash probe adds m,
  // only for scan-hash. Cost is the weighted sum. Equality to null gives m = n = 0.
  const db = fixture(E), base = { snapshot: 5, physicalCSN: 5, physicalRevision: 5, field: 'group' };
  const left = { ...base, table: 'items', physicalKeys: 10, versionProbes: 25, rowCount: 9, indexCandidates: [{ value: 'A', count: 4 }, { value: null, count: 2 }], frequencies: [{ value: 'A', count: 3 }, { value: 'B', count: 5 }, { value: null, count: 1 }] };
  const right = { ...base, table: 'bookings', physicalKeys: 6, versionProbes: 9, rowCount: 5, indexCandidates: [{ value: 'A', count: 5 }], frequencies: [{ value: 'A', count: 2 }, { value: 'C', count: 3 }] };
  const weights = { candidateVisits: 1, versionExaminations: 3, predicateEvaluations: 2, hashBuild: 5, hashProbe: 7, outputRows: 11 };
  const shape = plan => Object.fromEntries(plan.candidates.map(c => [c.id, [c.work.candidateVisits, c.work.versionExaminations, c.work.predicateEvaluations, c.work.hashBuild, c.work.hashProbe, c.work.outputRows, c.estimatedRows, c.cost]]));
  const plan = db.planEqualityJoin(structuredClone(left), structuredClone(right), 'A', { ...weights });
  assert.deepEqual(shape(plan), { 'scan-loop': [28, 52, 28, 0, 0, 6, 6, 306], 'scan-hash': [16, 34, 16, 5, 3, 6, 6, 262], 'index-loop': [19, 33, 19, 0, 0, 6, 6, 222] });
  assert.equal(plan.selected, 'index-loop');
  const none = db.planEqualityJoin(structuredClone(left), structuredClone(right), null, { ...weights });
  assert.ok(none.candidates.every(c => c.estimatedRows === 0 && c.work.outputRows === 0));
  assert.equal(none.candidates.find(c => c.id === 'scan-loop').work.candidateVisits, 10, 'With m = 0 the scan-loop visits only the left side.');
});

export function runChecks(Engine, through = 7) {
  const results = [];
  for (const t of tests.filter(t => t.unit <= through)) {
    try { t.run(Engine); results.push({ unit: t.unit, id: t.id, name: t.name, passed: true }); }
    catch (error) { results.push({ unit: t.unit, id: t.id, name: t.name, passed: false, message: error.message, code: error.code ?? 'CHECK' }); }
  }
  return { through, passed: results.every(r => r.passed), total: results.length, failures: results.filter(r => !r.passed).length, results };
}

Then compare query plans without changing the question they answer.</p><p class="note">Use Node 26.5.1 for the complete engine, disk and project checks. This reader saves committed practice responses and bounded policy checks in this browser. Reopen the same file to continue; export your history to keep a separate copy.
