`courses/anti-cheat-engineering-part-two/labcmds/14.mjs`:

```mjs
// Lab commands for unit 14: your detector on the corpus, its threshold, the freeze and the
// held-out split. lab.mjs lists them with its own commands (node lab.mjs help).
//
//   features PROJECT [--split dev|heldout]   your features by kind, and robust scales over the legal sessions
//                                            (held-out only after your first held-out result)
//   tune PROJECT [--write]                   your score and chooseThreshold on the dev split
//   freeze PROJECT                           record the sha256 of your detector's three files
//   restore-frozen PROJECT                   put back the three files as your latest freeze copied them
//   heldout PROJECT                         your frozen detector on the held-out split
//   recordings PROJECT                       your detector on the recorded adapted searchers (with no
//                                            threshold stored, at the one tune would choose on dev)
//
// Freezes and held-out results are kept the way lab.mjs keeps check attempts and predictions:
// one new folder per record in PROJECT/attempts/, named by the time, holding freeze.json or
// heldout.json. A folder is never overwritten, so your first held-out result stays where it
// was written and every later one is added after it.
import { existsSync, mkdirSync, readFileSync, writeFileSync, readdirSync, copyFileSync, realpathSync } from 'node:fs';
import { createHash, randomUUID } from 'node:crypto';
import { dirname, join, resolve, relative } from 'node:path';
import { fileURLToPath, pathToFileURL } from 'node:url';
import { makeCorpus, KINDS } from '../public/corpus.mjs';
import { median, quantile } from '../public/stats.mjs';
import { makeLoader, NOT_WRITTEN } from '../checks/harness.mjs';

const root = join(dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), '..');
const say = (s = '') => console.log(s);
// A path as you would type it from the folder you run commands in: project/attempts/...
const shown = (path) => relative(process.cwd(), path) || '.';
const COURSE = JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(root, 'course.json'), 'utf8')).id;
const BUDGET = 0.002;
const FROZEN = ['detect/settings.json', 'detect/features.mjs', 'detect/detector.mjs'];
const FEATURES = ['shots', 'hitRate', 'missMedian', 'fireMedian', 'fireSpread', 'inputsMedian', 'cadenceCV', 'missLag1'];
const RECORDINGS = ['delay', 'delay-misses'];
const COUNT_FIELDS = ['total', 'tp', 'fp', 'tn', 'fn', 'recall', 'falsePositiveRate', 'precision'];

const f3 = (x) => (x === null || x === undefined ? '-' : typeof x === 'number' && Number.isFinite(x) ? x.toFixed(3) : String(x));
const pct = (k, n) => (n ? `${((100 * k) / n).toFixed(1)}%` : '-');
const pad = (s, n) => String(s).padEnd(n);
const lpad = (s, n) => String(s).padStart(n);
const ratio = (k, n) => (n ? k / n : null);

function project(dir) {
  if (!dir) throw Error('Name your project folder: node lab.mjs COMMAND PROJECT ...');
  const p = resolve(dir);
  if (!existsSync(join(p, 'PROJECT.json'))) throw Error(`${dir} is not a project folder: make it with a starting route from lesson 12 (node examples/start-chapter.mjs ${dir} write, or supplied)`);
  return p;
}

// "detect/features.mjs line 12" for the first line of an error's stack inside the project.
function where(error, p) {
  const roots = [p, pathToFileURL(p).href];
  try { const real = realpathSync(p); roots.push(real, pathToFileURL(real).href); } catch { /* keep the given path */ }
  for (const line of String(error?.stack ?? '').split('\n')) {
    for (const r of roots) {
      const i = line.indexOf(r);
      const m = i < 0 ? null : line.slice(i + r.length).match(/^\/?([^:]+):(\d+)/);
      if (m) return ` (${decodeURIComponent(m[1])} line ${m[2]})`;
    }
  }
  return '';
}

// Calls your function; an error it throws comes back saying what it was given and where.
function caller(p) {
  return (what, f) => {
    try {
      return f();
    } catch (error) {
      const message = String(error?.message ?? error).split('\n')[0];
      if (message.includes(NOT_WRITTEN)) throw Error(message);
      throw Error(`${what}: ${error?.name ?? 'Error'}: ${message}${where(error, p)}`);
    }
  };
}

const sha256 = (path) => createHash('sha256').update(readFileSync(path)).digest('hex');
const hashes = (p) => Object.fromEntries(FROZEN.map((f) => [f, existsSync(join(p, f)) ? sha256(join(p, f)) : null]));

// Your freezes and held-out results, oldest first.
function records(p) {
  const folder = join(p, 'attempts');
  const out = [];
  for (const name of existsSync(folder) ? readdirSync(folder).sort() : []) {
    for (const file of ['freeze.json', 'heldout.json']) {
      const path = join(folder, name, file);
      if (!existsSync(path)) continue;
      try { out.push({ ...JSON.parse(readFileSync(path, 'utf8')), folder: name }); } catch (e) { throw Error(`${shown(path)} is not valid JSON (${e.message}): restore it before you go on`); }
    }
  }
  return out.sort((a, b) => (a.at < b.at ? -1 : a.at > b.at ? 1 : 0));
}

// A new folder in attempts/ named by the record's own time; never an existing one.
function save(p, kind, record, copies = []) {
  const name = `${record.at.replaceAll(':', '-')}-${kind}-${randomUUID().slice(0, 8)}`;
  const folder = join(p, 'attempts', name);
  mkdirSync(folder, { recursive: true });
  for (const f of copies) { mkdirSync(dirname(join(folder, f)), { recursive: true }); copyFileSync(join(p, f), join(folder, f)); }
  writeFileSync(join(folder, `${kind}.json`), JSON.stringify(record, null, 2) + '\n', { flag: 'wx' });
  return `attempts/${name}`;
}

// The latest freeze, provided your three files still hash to it; otherwise a refusal.
function requireFrozen(p, dir, what) {
  const all = records(p);
  const freeze = all.filter((r) => r.kind === 'freeze').at(-1);
  if (!freeze) throw Error(`Freeze first: node lab.mjs freeze ${dir}. ${what} looks at the held-out split, so it runs only on a frozen detector.`);
  const now = hashes(p);
  const changed = FROZEN.filter((f) => now[f] !== freeze.files?.[f]);
  if (changed.length) {
    const seen = all.some((r) => r.kind === 'heldout');
    throw Error(`${changed.join(' and ')} changed since you froze at ${freeze.at} (the frozen copies are in ${freeze.folder ? shown(join(p, 'attempts', freeze.folder)) : 'your attempts folder'}). Freeze again (node lab.mjs freeze ${dir}) before ${what}.${seen ? ' Your first held-out result stays first; the next one is saved as a later run.' : ''}`);
  }
  return { freeze, runs: all.filter((r) => r.kind === 'heldout') };
}

function count(decisions) {
  let tp = 0, fp = 0, tn = 0, fn = 0;
  for (const d of decisions) {
    if (d.label === 'cheat') { if (d.flagged) tp++; else fn++; } else if (d.flagged) fp++; else tn++;
  }
  return { total: decisions.length, tp, fp, tn, fn, recall: ratio(tp, tp + fn), falsePositiveRate: ratio(fp, fp + tn), precision: ratio(tp, tp + fp) };
}
const precisionAt = (b, r, f) => { const d = b * r + (1 - b) * f; return d === 0 ? null : (b * r) / d; };

async function detector(p, need = []) {
  const loader = makeLoader(p);
  const settings = loader.json('detect/settings.json');
  if (!settings || typeof settings !== 'object' || Array.isArray(settings)) throw Error('detect/settings.json must hold a JSON object: your score\'s settings, "budget" and "threshold"');
  const fns = {};
  for (const [file, name] of [['detect/features.mjs', 'features'], ['detect/detector.mjs', 'score'], ...need]) fns[name] = await loader.fn(file, name);
  return { settings, loader, ...fns };
}

// What your features are given, here as in the checks and the scoreboard: a session's play,
// its record.inputs and rounds, and nothing else (no id, label, kind or seed).
const playOf = (c) => ({ record: { inputs: c.record.inputs }, rounds: c.rounds });

function scored(cases, d, settings, call) {
  return cases.map((c) => {
    const f = call(`your features threw on case ${c.id}, given { record: { inputs }, rounds } only`, () => d.features(playOf(c)));
    return { c, s: call(`your score threw on case ${c.id}`, () => d.score(f, settings)) };
  });
}

const finiteThreshold = (settings) => typeof settings.threshold === 'number' && Number.isFinite(settings.threshold);
const listed = (rows, k = 5) => rows.slice(0, k).map((x) => `${x.c.id} ${f3(x.s)}`).join(', ');

// ------------------------------------------------------------------ features

async function features({ plain, o }) {
  const dir = plain[0];
  const p = project(dir);
  const split = o.split === undefined ? 'dev' : String(o.split);
  if (!['dev', 'heldout'].includes(split)) throw Error('--split takes dev or heldout');
  // The held-out split's features only once your first held-out result is saved, so that
  // looking at them can shape only later runs.
  const first = records(p).find((r) => r.kind === 'heldout');
  if (split === 'heldout' && !first) throw Error(`The held-out split's features are shown only after your first held-out result is saved (node lab.mjs freeze ${dir}, then node lab.mjs heldout ${dir}), so that looking at them cannot shape that result.`);
  const call = caller(p);
  const feature = await makeLoader(p).fn('detect/features.mjs', 'features');
  const cases = makeCorpus({ split });
  const rows = cases.map((c) => ({ c, f: call(`your features threw on case ${c.id}, given { record: { inputs }, rounds } only`, () => feature(playOf(c))) }));
  say(`Your features on the ${split} split: ${cases.length} sessions (makeCorpus({ split: '${split}' }) in public/corpus.mjs).`);
  if (split === 'heldout') say(`Your first held-out result was saved at ${first.at}; what you see here can shape only later runs.`);
  say();
  say('Pooled hit rate by kind: all hits over all shots of the kind\'s sessions.');
  say(`  ${pad('kind', 12)} ${lpad('sessions', 8)} ${lpad('shots', 7)} ${lpad('hits', 6)} ${lpad('hit rate', 9)}`);
  for (const kind of KINDS) {
    const of = cases.filter((c) => c.kind === kind);
    let shots = 0, hits = 0;
    for (const c of of) for (const r of c.rounds) if (r.shot) { shots++; if (r.result === 'hit') hits++; }
    say(`  ${pad(kind, 12)} ${lpad(of.length, 8)} ${lpad(shots, 7)} ${lpad(hits, 6)} ${lpad(pct(hits, shots), 9)}`);
  }
  say();
  const legal = rows.filter((x) => x.c.label === 'legal');
  say('Each feature by kind: the median, lower quartile and upper quartile of your features over');
  say('the kind\'s sessions (a session where the feature is null is left out and counted).');
  say(`Under each, all ${legal.length} legal sessions together: the median and 1.4826 × the median`);
  say('absolute deviation (MAD), a robust scale: z = (value - median) / scale; and the same for');
  say('Math.log1p(value), for a feature you compare on a log scale.');
  for (const name of FEATURES) {
    say();
    say(`${pad(name, 14)} ${lpad('sessions', 14)} ${lpad('median', 9)} ${lpad('lower q', 9)} ${lpad('upper q', 9)}`);
    for (const kind of KINDS) {
      const all = rows.filter((x) => x.c.kind === kind).map((x) => x.f?.[name]);
      const values = all.filter((v) => typeof v === 'number' && Number.isFinite(v));
      const missing = all.length - values.length;
      const n = `${values.length}${missing ? ` (${missing} null)` : ''}`;
      say(`  ${pad(kind, 12)} ${lpad(n, 14)} ${lpad(f3(median(values)), 9)} ${lpad(f3(quantile(values, 0.25)), 9)} ${lpad(f3(quantile(values, 0.75)), 9)}`);
    }
    const values = legal.map((x) => x.f?.[name]).filter((v) => typeof v === 'number' && Number.isFinite(v));
    const m = median(values);
    const scale = m === null ? null : 1.4826 * median(values.map((v) => Math.abs(v - m)));
    const missing = legal.length - values.length;
    say(`  ${pad('all legal', 12)} ${lpad(`${values.length}${missing ? ` (${missing} null)` : ''}`, 14)}   median ${f3(m)}, 1.4826 × MAD ${f3(scale)}`);
    if (values.length && values.every((v) => v >= 0)) {
      const logs = values.map((v) => Math.log1p(v));
      const lm = median(logs);
      say(`  ${pad('', 12)} ${lpad('', 14)}   of log1p: median ${f3(lm)}, 1.4826 × MAD ${f3(1.4826 * median(logs.map((v) => Math.abs(v - lm))))}`);
    }
  }
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------------ tune

async function tune({ plain, o }) {
  const dir = plain[0];
  const p = project(dir);
  const write = o.write === true || o.write === 'true';
  const call = caller(p);
  const d = await detector(p, [['detect/detector.mjs', 'chooseThreshold']]);
  const { settings } = d;
  const budget = settings.budget;
  if (typeof budget !== 'number' || !(budget >= 0 && budget <= 1)) throw Error(`detect/settings.json needs "budget": 0.002 (one false flag in 500 legal sessions); it holds ${JSON.stringify(budget)}`);
  if (budget !== BUDGET) say(`Note: detect/settings.json holds budget ${budget}. The course's budget is 0.002, and freeze takes no other.`);
  const dev = scored(makeCorpus({ split: 'dev' }), d, settings, call);
  const legal = dev.filter((x) => x.c.label === 'legal');
  const cheats = dev.filter((x) => x.c.label === 'cheat');
  const t = call('your chooseThreshold threw on the dev legal scores', () => d.chooseThreshold(legal.map((x) => x.s), budget));
  say(`Your score on the dev split (makeCorpus({ split: 'dev' })): ${legal.length} legal sessions, ${cheats.length} searcher sessions.`);
  say(`Your chooseThreshold on the ${legal.length} legal scores at budget ${budget} (at most ${budget * legal.length} of them at or above it):`);
  say(`  threshold ${t}${typeof t === 'number' && Number.isFinite(t) ? ` (${f3(t)})` : ''}`);
  if (typeof t !== 'number' || Number.isNaN(t)) throw Error(`chooseThreshold returned ${JSON.stringify(t)}, not a number: nothing ${write ? 'written' : 'to store'}`);
  const r = count(dev.map((x) => ({ label: x.c.label, flagged: x.s >= t })));
  const flaggedLegal = legal.filter((x) => x.s >= t).sort((a, b) => b.s - a.s);
  say(`At that threshold, on dev (counted by the lab from your scores):`);
  say(`  legal sessions flagged     ${r.fp} of ${legal.length}${flaggedLegal.length ? `: ${listed(flaggedLegal)}${flaggedLegal.length > 5 ? ', ...' : ''}` : ''}`);
  say(`  searcher sessions flagged  ${r.tp} of ${cheats.length} (recall ${f3(r.recall)})`);
  say(`  tp ${r.tp}  fn ${r.fn}  fp ${r.fp}  tn ${r.tn}`);
  say(`  highest legal scores:   ${listed([...legal].sort((a, b) => b.s - a.s))}`);
  say(`  lowest searcher scores: ${listed([...cheats].sort((a, b) => a.s - b.s))}`);
  if (!Number.isFinite(t)) {
    say(`No score meets the budget, so no threshold can be stored (JSON has no ${t}).`);
    return;
  }
  const held = settings.threshold;
  if (Object.is(held, t)) { say(`detect/settings.json already holds threshold ${t}.`); return; }
  if (!write) { say(`detect/settings.json holds threshold ${JSON.stringify(held)}. Run node lab.mjs tune ${dir} --write to store ${t}.`); return; }
  const file = join(p, 'detect/settings.json');
  const fresh = JSON.parse(readFileSync(file, 'utf8')); // re-read, so only threshold changes
  fresh.threshold = t;
  writeFileSync(file, JSON.stringify(fresh, null, 2) + '\n');
  say(`Stored threshold ${t} in detect/settings.json (it held ${JSON.stringify(held)}); its other fields are unchanged.`);
  const freeze = records(p).filter((x) => x.kind === 'freeze').at(-1);
  const now = hashes(p);
  if (freeze && FROZEN.some((f) => now[f] !== freeze.files?.[f])) say(`This differs from what you froze at ${freeze.at}, so heldout refuses until you freeze again (node lab.mjs freeze ${dir}).`);
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------------ freeze

async function freeze({ plain }) {
  const dir = plain[0];
  const p = project(dir);
  for (const f of FROZEN) if (!existsSync(join(p, f))) throw Error(`${f} is missing from your project: nothing frozen`);
  const call = caller(p);
  const d = await detector(p, [['detect/detector.mjs', 'chooseThreshold']]);
  const { settings } = d;
  if (settings.budget !== BUDGET) throw Error(`detect/settings.json holds budget ${JSON.stringify(settings.budget)}; the course's budget is 0.002 (API.md). Nothing frozen.`);
  if (!finiteThreshold(settings)) throw Error(`detect/settings.json holds threshold ${JSON.stringify(settings.threshold)}, not a finite number. Run node lab.mjs tune ${dir} --write first. Nothing frozen.`);
  const now = hashes(p);
  const all = records(p);
  const last = all.filter((r) => r.kind === 'freeze').at(-1);
  if (last && FROZEN.every((f) => last.files?.[f] === now[f])) {
    say(`Already frozen at ${last.at} with these exact files (${shown(join(p, 'attempts', last.folder))}). Nothing new recorded.`);
    return;
  }
  // The dev split first: a freeze that fails the budget there would waste your first held-out look.
  const dev = scored(makeCorpus({ split: 'dev' }), d, settings, call);
  const legal = dev.filter((x) => x.c.label === 'legal');
  const flagged = legal.filter((x) => x.s >= settings.threshold).length;
  const allowed = BUDGET * legal.length;
  const cheats = dev.filter((x) => x.c.label === 'cheat');
  const caught = cheats.filter((x) => x.s >= settings.threshold).length;
  if (flagged > allowed) throw Error(`At your threshold ${settings.threshold}, your score flags ${flagged} of the ${legal.length} dev legal sessions; the budget allows ${allowed}. Run node lab.mjs tune ${dir} --write, then freeze. Nothing frozen.`);
  let chosen;
  try { chosen = d.chooseThreshold(legal.map((x) => x.s), BUDGET); } catch (e) { chosen = `an error (${String(e?.message ?? e).split('\n')[0]})`; }
  say(`On the dev split, at your threshold ${settings.threshold}: ${flagged} of ${legal.length} legal sessions flagged (the budget allows ${allowed}); ${caught} of ${cheats.length} searcher sessions flagged.`);
  if (!Object.is(chosen, settings.threshold)) say(`Note: your chooseThreshold gives ${chosen} on these scores, not ${settings.threshold}. The checks accept any threshold within the budget on dev; node lab.mjs tune ${dir} --write stores chooseThreshold's.`);
  const seen = all.filter((r) => r.kind === 'heldout');
  const at = new Date().toISOString();
  const folder = save(p, 'freeze', {
    kind: 'freeze', course: COURSE, files: now, afterHeldout: seen.length > 0,
    dev: { threshold: settings.threshold, budget: BUDGET, legal: legal.length, falseFlags: flagged, cheats: cheats.length, flaggedCheats: caught },
    at,
  }, FROZEN);
  say(`Froze your detector at ${at}:`);
  for (const f of FROZEN) say(`  ${pad(f, 22)} sha256 ${now[f]}`);
  say(`Saved in ${shown(join(p, folder))} (freeze.json, with a copy of the three files).`);
  if (seen.length) say(`You have already seen a held-out result (first at ${seen[0].at}). This freeze comes after it, so every later held-out result is saved as a later run.`);
  say(`Next: node lab.mjs heldout ${dir}. If any of these files changes, heldout refuses until you freeze again.`);
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------------ restore-frozen

// Puts back the three files as the latest freeze copied them, byte for byte, so that they
// hash as frozen again. The files it replaces are saved first in a folder of their own.
async function restoreFrozen({ plain }) {
  const dir = plain[0];
  const p = project(dir);
  const freeze = records(p).filter((r) => r.kind === 'freeze').at(-1);
  if (!freeze) throw Error(`No freeze yet, so there is nothing to restore: node lab.mjs freeze ${dir} records one.`);
  const folder = join(p, 'attempts', freeze.folder);
  const damaged = FROZEN.filter((f) => !existsSync(join(folder, f)) || sha256(join(folder, f)) !== freeze.files?.[f]);
  if (damaged.length) throw Error(`The copy of ${damaged.join(' and ')} in ${shown(folder)} does not match the hash recorded at ${freeze.at}, so nothing was restored.`);
  const now = hashes(p);
  const changed = FROZEN.filter((f) => now[f] !== freeze.files[f]);
  if (!changed.length) { say(`Your detector files are already the ones you froze at ${freeze.at}. Nothing changed.`); return; }
  const present = changed.filter((f) => now[f] !== null);
  const at = new Date().toISOString();
  const kept = save(p, 'restore', { kind: 'restore', course: COURSE, frozenAt: freeze.at, from: freeze.folder, restored: changed, replaced: present, at }, present);
  for (const f of changed) { mkdirSync(dirname(join(p, f)), { recursive: true }); copyFileSync(join(folder, f), join(p, f)); }
  say(`Restored ${changed.join(', ')} from your freeze at ${freeze.at} (${shown(folder)}).`);
  if (present.length) say(`The files it replaced are kept in ${shown(join(p, kept))}.`);
  say(`Your detector files are now the ones you froze. The line above the scoreboard's table confirms it: node lab.mjs scoreboard ${dir}`);
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------------ heldout

async function heldout({ plain }) {
  const dir = plain[0];
  const p = project(dir);
  const { freeze, runs } = requireFrozen(p, dir, 'heldout');
  const call = caller(p);
  const d = await detector(p);
  const { settings } = d;
  const cases = scored(makeCorpus({ split: 'heldout' }), d, settings, call);
  const r = count(cases.map((x) => ({ label: x.c.label, flagged: x.s >= settings.threshold })));
  const legal = r.fp + r.tn, cheats = r.tp + r.fn;
  const at100 = precisionAt(0.01, r.recall, r.falsePositiveRate);

  // Your own evaluate (given the whole cases: it needs their labels) and precisionAt, compared
  // with the lab's counting of your scores of each session's play.
  let yours;
  try {
    const evaluate = await d.loader.fn('detect/detector.mjs', 'evaluate');
    const mine = await d.loader.fn('detect/detector.mjs', 'precisionAt');
    const e = evaluate(cases.map((x) => x.c), settings);
    const differs = COUNT_FIELDS.find((k) => !(e?.[k] === r[k] || (typeof e?.[k] === 'number' && typeof r[k] === 'number' && Math.abs(e[k] - r[k]) <= 1e-12)));
    const q = mine(0.01, r.recall, r.falsePositiveRate);
    const qOk = q === at100 || (typeof q === 'number' && typeof at100 === 'number' && Math.abs(q - at100) <= 1e-12);
    yours = differs ? `your evaluate differs in ${differs}: ${JSON.stringify(e?.[differs])}, the lab's count ${JSON.stringify(r[differs])}, made from each session's record.inputs and rounds alone; if your features read more of the case, such as its label, that is the difference (check 14.heldout)`
      : !qOk ? `your evaluate agrees; your precisionAt gives ${JSON.stringify(q)}, the formula ${JSON.stringify(at100)} (check 14.counting)`
        : 'your evaluate and precisionAt agree';
  } catch (e) {
    yours = `your evaluate or precisionAt did not run: ${String(e?.message ?? e).split('\n')[0]}`;
  }

  const first = runs.length === 0;
  const folder = save(p, 'heldout', {
    kind: 'heldout', course: COURSE, run: runs.length + 1, first,
    frozenAt: freeze.at, files: freeze.files,
    sessions: cases.length, legal, cheats, threshold: settings.threshold,
    result: r, precisionAt1in100: at100, yourFunctions: yours,
    at: new Date().toISOString(),
  });
  say(`The held-out split: ${cases.length} sessions (${legal} legal, ${cheats} searcher), your detector as frozen at ${freeze.at}, threshold ${settings.threshold}.`);
  say(`  tp ${r.tp}  fn ${r.fn}  fp ${r.fp}  tn ${r.tn}  (counted per session by the lab from your scores; ${yours})`);
  say(`  searcher recall       ${f3(r.recall)} (${r.tp} of ${cheats} flagged)`);
  say(`  false flags           ${r.fp} of ${legal.toLocaleString('en-US')} legal sessions (false positive rate ${r.falsePositiveRate === null ? '-' : r.falsePositiveRate.toFixed(4)})`);
  say(`  precision at 1 in 100 ${f3(at100)}${at100 === null ? '' : ` (with cheaters at 1 session in 100, ${(100 * at100).toFixed(1)}% of the flagged sessions would be cheats)`}`);
  if (first) {
    say(`This is your first held-out result. It stays first in your receipt: ${shown(join(p, folder, 'heldout.json'))}`);
  } else {
    const one = runs[0];
    say(`This is held-out run ${runs.length + 1}, saved after your first in ${shown(join(p, folder, 'heldout.json'))}, marked as a later run.`);
    say(`Your first result, from ${one.at}, stays first: tp ${one.result.tp}  fn ${one.result.fn}  fp ${one.result.fp}  tn ${one.result.tn}, precision at 1 in 100 ${f3(one.precisionAt1in100)}.`);
  }
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------------ recordings

async function recordings({ plain }) {
  const dir = plain[0];
  const p = project(dir);
  const call = caller(p);
  const d = await detector(p, [['detect/detector.mjs', 'chooseThreshold']]);
  const { settings } = d;
  let threshold = settings.threshold;
  let source = `detect/settings.json, threshold ${threshold}`;
  if (!finiteThreshold(settings)) {
    // No threshold stored yet, as while you design your score: use the one tune would choose
    // for your current score on the dev split. Nothing is written, and held-out is not read.
    const budget = settings.budget;
    if (typeof budget !== 'number' || !(budget >= 0 && budget <= 1)) throw Error(`detect/settings.json holds threshold ${JSON.stringify(settings.threshold)} and budget ${JSON.stringify(budget)}; add "budget": 0.002 so that recordings can choose a threshold on the dev split as tune does.`);
    const legal = scored(makeCorpus({ split: 'dev' }).filter((c) => c.label === 'legal'), d, settings, call);
    threshold = call('your chooseThreshold threw on the dev legal scores', () => d.chooseThreshold(legal.map((x) => x.s), budget));
    if (typeof threshold !== 'number' || Number.isNaN(threshold)) throw Error(`chooseThreshold returned ${JSON.stringify(threshold)} on the dev legal scores, not a number`);
    source = `no threshold stored yet, so the one tune would choose for your current score on the dev split: ${threshold}; nothing written`;
  }
  say(`Your detector (${source}) on the recorded adapted searchers in recordings/.`);
  say('Every recorded session is a cheat, so recall is the share flagged; there are no legal sessions to flag falsely.');
  say(`  ${pad('set', 13)} ${lpad('sessions', 8)} ${lpad('hit rate', 18)} ${lpad('flagged', 8)} ${lpad('missed', 7)} ${lpad('recall', 7)}`);
  for (const name of RECORDINGS) {
    const cases = JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(root, 'recordings', `${name}.json`), 'utf8'));
    let shots = 0, hits = 0;
    for (const c of cases) for (const r of c.rounds) if (r.shot) { shots++; if (r.result === 'hit') hits++; }
    const r = count(scored(cases, d, settings, call).map((x) => ({ label: x.c.label, flagged: x.s >= threshold })));
    say(`  ${pad(name, 13)} ${lpad(cases.length, 8)} ${lpad(`${pct(hits, shots)} (${hits}/${shots})`, 18)} ${lpad(r.tp, 8)} ${lpad(r.fn, 7)} ${lpad(f3(r.recall), 7)}`);
  }
}

export const commands = [
  { name: 'features', args: 'PROJECT [--split dev|heldout]', about: 'your features by kind, with robust scales (held-out only after your first held-out result)', run: features },
  { name: 'tune', args: 'PROJECT [--write]', about: 'your score and chooseThreshold on the dev split; --write stores the threshold', run: tune },
  { name: 'freeze', args: 'PROJECT', about: 'record the sha256 of your detector\'s three files before the held-out split', run: freeze },
  { name: 'restore-frozen', args: 'PROJECT', about: 'put back your detector\'s three files as your latest freeze copied them (the replaced files are kept)', run: restoreFrozen },
  { name: 'heldout', args: 'PROJECT', about: 'your frozen detector on the held-out split; the first result is kept', run: heldout },
  { name: 'recordings', args: 'PROJECT', about: 'your detector on the recorded adapted searchers (with no threshold stored, at the one tune would choose on dev)', run: recordings },
];

```

`courses/anti-cheat-engineering-part-two/labcmds/17.mjs`:

```mjs
// Lab command for unit 17: the scoreboard. lab.mjs lists it with its own commands
// (node lab.mjs help).
//
//   scoreboard PROJECT [--sessions N]
//
// Plays the course's clients against your whole defence and prints one table for Lob (each
// legal player model, each protocol cheat, the searching client live against your view and
// once against the full view, the two recordings through your detector), then the courier
// at your window, then your trade under a crash at every write, then each budget of API.md's
// unit 17 with PASS or MISS. The measuring is checks/scoreboard.mjs's, the same code the
// unit 17 checks use; the checks play other seeds.
import { existsSync, readFileSync, readdirSync } from 'node:fs';
import { createHash } from 'node:crypto';
import { dirname, join, resolve } from 'node:path';
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
import { makeLoader } from '../checks/harness.mjs';
import * as sb from '../checks/scoreboard.mjs';

const root = join(dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), '..');
const say = (s = '') => console.log(s);
const grouped = (n) => Number(n).toLocaleString('en-US');
const pad = (s, n) => String(s).padEnd(n);
const lpad = (s, n) => String(s).padStart(n);
const pct2 = (x) => `${(100 * x).toFixed(2)}%`;
const plural = (n, word, many = `${word}s`) => `${grouped(n)} ${n === 1 ? word : many}`;

// The scoreboard's seeds. Lob: session n of row r has server seed 17,000,000 + 100,000 * r + n.
// The corpus splits use 1,000,000+ and 2,000,000+, the recordings 3,000,000+, the author's
// calibration 4,000,000+, the unit 13 and 14 checks 13,000,000+ and 14,000,000+, and the
// unit 17 checks 71,000,000+, so none of them meets these. The courier's runCourier seed is
// 17 (the sweep command uses 1, the unit 15 checks 11 and 29, the unit 17 checks 71).
export const SEEDS = Object.freeze({ lob: 17_000_000, courier: 17 });
// Sessions per row when --sessions is not given.
export const DEFAULTS = Object.freeze({ legal: 500, protocol: 50, searcher: 200, contrast: 50, courier: 200 });

// A market at closing time: four players, five items, 165 coins. The script sells the axe
// on, tries to sell it again from its first owner, refuses one sale for funds, sells the ink
// for nothing and sends the first request again.
export const TRADE_WORLD = Object.freeze({ 'inv:dara': ['axe', 'bell'], 'inv:eli': ['cape'], 'inv:fern': ['drum', 'ink'], 'inv:gil': [], 'coins:dara': 15, 'coins:eli': 80, 'coins:fern': 30, 'coins:gil': 40 });
export const TRADE_SCRIPT = Object.freeze([
  { key: 'm1', seller: 'dara', buyer: 'eli', item: 'axe', price: 35 },
  { key: 'm2', seller: 'eli', buyer: 'gil', item: 'axe', price: 40 },
  { key: 'm3', seller: 'dara', buyer: 'fern', item: 'axe', price: 10 },
  { key: 'm4', seller: 'fern', buyer: 'dara', item: 'drum', price: 60 },
  { key: 'm5', seller: 'fern', buyer: 'eli', item: 'ink', price: 0 },
  { key: 'm1', seller: 'dara', buyer: 'eli', item: 'axe', price: 35 },
]);

const FROZEN = [sb.FILES.settings, sb.FILES.features, sb.FILES.detector];

function project(dir) {
  if (!dir) throw Error('Name your project folder: node lab.mjs scoreboard PROJECT');
  const p = resolve(dir);
  if (!existsSync(join(p, 'PROJECT.json'))) throw Error(`${dir} is not a project folder: make it with a starting route from lesson 12 (node examples/start-chapter.mjs ${dir} write, or supplied)`);
  return p;
}

function sessionsOption(o) {
  if (o.sessions === undefined) return null;
  const n = Number(o.sessions);
  if (o.sessions === true || !Number.isSafeInteger(n) || n < 1 || n > sb.MAX_SESSIONS) throw Error(`--sessions takes a whole number of sessions per row, from 1 to ${grouped(sb.MAX_SESSIONS)}`);
  return n;
}

// Loading a file of yours: a missing file, a missing export or a syntax error, in one line.
async function loaded(get) {
  try {
    return await get();
  } catch (e) {
    throw Error(String(e?.fields?.observed ?? e?.message ?? e).split('\n')[0]);
  }
}

// One line for an error that stopped the scoreboard.
function stopLine(e, p, during) {
  if (e instanceof sb.LearnerError) {
    if (e.notWritten) {
      const named = sb.firstLine(e.error).match(/^(\w+): not written yet/)?.[1] ?? e.fn;
      return `${named} in ${e.file} is not written yet: write it (API.md says what it must do), then run this again.`;
    }
    const where = sb.whereIn(e.error, p);
    const session = e.session ? `, in ${sessionLine(e.session)}` : during ? `, ${during}` : '';
    return `${e.message}${where ? ` (${where})` : ''}${e.call ? `, called as ${e.call}` : ''}${session}.`;
  }
  if (e instanceof sb.SessionError) {
    const where = sb.whereIn(e.error, p) ?? sb.whereInCourse(e.error);
    return `${sessionLine(e.session)} stopped: ${e.error?.name ?? 'Error'}: ${e.message}${where ? ` (${where})` : ''}. Look at what your files hand the server there: the view's message, the recorder's record, the admission's answers.`;
  }
  return `${during ? `${during}: ` : ''}${e?.name ?? 'Error'}: ${sb.firstLine(e)}`;
}
const sessionLine = ({ row, seed }) => `the ${sb.rowOf(row).prose} session with server seed ${seed} (checks/scoreboard.mjs playLobSession({ row: '${row}', seed: ${seed} }))`;

function run(p, during, f) {
  try {
    return f();
  } catch (e) {
    throw Error(stopLine(e, p, during));
  }
}

// Whether your detector's three files are the ones you froze in lesson 14.
function freezeNote(p, dir) {
  const folder = join(p, 'attempts');
  let latest = null;
  for (const name of existsSync(folder) ? readdirSync(folder).sort() : []) {
    const file = join(folder, name, 'freeze.json');
    if (!existsSync(file)) continue;
    try {
      const r = JSON.parse(readFileSync(file, 'utf8'));
      if (r.kind === 'freeze' && (!latest || r.at > latest.at)) latest = r;
    } catch { /* an unreadable record is left to labcmds/14.mjs to report */ }
  }
  if (!latest) return `You have not frozen your detector (node lab.mjs freeze ${dir}); the scoreboard uses your detector files as they are.`;
  const changed = FROZEN.filter((f) => {
    const path = join(p, f);
    const now = existsSync(path) ? createHash('sha256').update(readFileSync(path)).digest('hex') : null;
    return now !== latest.files?.[f];
  });
  return changed.length
    ? `${changed.join(' and ')} changed since your freeze of ${latest.at}; the scoreboard uses the files as they are now.`
    : `Your detector files are the ones you froze at ${latest.at}.`;
}

function verdictLine(pass, budget, measured, advice) {
  say(`  ${pass ? 'PASS' : 'MISS'}  ${budget}: ${measured}${pass || !advice ? '' : ` ${advice}`}`);
}

async function scoreboard({ plain, o }) {
  const dir = plain[0];
  const p = project(dir);
  const n = sessionsOption(o);
  const counts = n ? { legal: n, protocol: n, searcher: n, contrast: n, courier: n } : DEFAULTS;
  const started = performance.now();

  const loader = makeLoader(p);
  const lob = await loaded(() => sb.loadLob(loader));
  if (lob.settingsProblem) throw Error(lob.settingsProblem.replace('PROJECT', dir));
  const rewind = await loaded(() => sb.loadRewind(loader));
  const defence = await loaded(() => loader.json(sb.FILES.defence));
  const { window, problem } = sb.windowOf(defence);
  if (problem) throw Error(problem);
  const trades = await loaded(() => sb.loadTrade(loader));

  const perRow = (row) => counts[row.group];
  const rows = sb.ROWS.map((row) => run(p, `in the ${row.label} sessions`, () => sb.playLobRow({ row: row.id, base: SEEDS.lob, sessions: perRow(row), lob })));
  const recordings = ['delay', 'delay-misses'].map((name) => ({
    name,
    ...run(p, `scoring recordings/${name}.json`, () => sb.scoreRecordings(JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(root, 'recordings', `${name}.json`), 'utf8')), lob)),
  }));
  const courier = run(p, `in the courier sessions (runCourier seed ${SEEDS.courier}, window ${window})`, () => sb.courierAt({ seed: SEEDS.courier, sessions: counts.courier, window, rewind }));
  const trade = run(p, 'in the crash test of your trade', () => sb.crashTrades({ world: TRADE_WORLD, script: TRADE_SCRIPT, ...trades }));

  // ---------------------------------------------------------------- Lob
  say('The scoreboard: the course\'s clients against your whole defence.');
  say();
  say('Lob. Every session is a new createLobServer (public/runtime.mjs) with your admission, your view and your');
  say('recorder, and one client on its own network (public/sim.mjs, public/net.mjs). Your features and score judge');
  say(`each session's record and rounds against ${sb.FILES.settings}'s threshold ${lob.settings.threshold} (flagged at or above it).`);
  say(`Seeds: session n (from 0) of row r (from 0, in the order below) has server seed ${grouped(SEEDS.lob)} + 100,000 × r + n;`);
  say('the client and its two links are seeded from it as public/corpus.mjs seeds them. No corpus split, recording,');
  say('calibration run or check uses these seeds.');
  say(freezeNote(p, dir));
  say();
  say(`  ${pad('row', 22)}${lpad('sessions', 8)}  ${pad('hit rate', 21)}${lpad('refused', 7)}${lpad('stale', 7)}${lpad('flagged', 9)}`);
  for (const t of rows) {
    const note = t.group === 'contrast' ? '   contrast: no budget' : '';
    say(`  ${pad(t.label, 22)}${lpad(grouped(t.sessions), 8)}  ${pad(sb.hitText(t), 21)}${lpad(grouped(t.refusedNotStaleSessions), 7)}${lpad(grouped(t.staleSessions.length), 7)}${lpad(grouped(t.flagged), 9)}${note}`);
  }
  for (const r of recordings) say(`  ${pad(`recording ${r.name}`, 22)}${lpad(grouped(r.sessions), 8)}  ${pad(sb.hitText(r), 21)}${lpad('-', 7)}${lpad('-', 7)}${lpad(grouped(r.flagged), 9)}`);
  say('sessions: played; hit rate: hits over shots in all the row\'s sessions; refused: sessions in which your admission');
  say('refused an input other than as stale; stale: sessions in which it refused an input whose seq was not above the');
  say('newest admitted (replayed, or overtaken on the network by a newer one), which API.md\'s rule refuses; flagged:');
  say('sessions whose score reaches your threshold. The recordings (unit 14) are recorded sessions: scored, not played.');
  const legalStale = rows.filter((t) => t.group === 'legal').flatMap((t) => t.staleSessions.map((s) => ({ ...s, label: t.label })));
  if (legalStale.length) {
    say(`Legal players' stale refusals: ${legalStale.slice(0, 6).map((s) => `${s.label} (server seed ${s.seed}, tick ${s.first.tick}${s.count > 1 ? `, ${s.count} inputs` : ''})`).join('; ')}${legalStale.length > 6 ? `; and ${legalStale.length - 6} more` : ''}.`);
  } else {
    say('Legal players\' stale refusals: none in these sessions.');
  }
  const unscored = rows.filter((t) => t.unscored);
  if (unscored.length) say(`Note: your score gave something other than a finite number in ${unscored.map((t) => `${grouped(t.unscored)} ${t.label} sessions (first: server seed ${t.firstUnscored.seed}, ${JSON.stringify(t.firstUnscored.score) ?? 'undefined'})`).join(', ')}; those are counted as not flagged.`);

  // ---------------------------------------------------------------- courier
  const cv = sb.courierVerdict(courier);
  say();
  say(`Courier. runCourier seed ${SEEDS.courier}, ${grouped(courier.sessions)} sessions per model of 1,200 ticks, at your rewindWindow ${window} (${sb.FILES.defence}),`);
  say('judged by your judgeInteract, measureRtt and positionAt; counted by unit 15\'s rules.');
  say(`  honest       ${plural(courier.honest, 'press', 'presses')} decided; refused although in range at seen: ${grouped(courier.honestRefused)} (${pct2(cv.honest.rate)}); ${courier.deliveries.honest.toFixed(1)} deliveries a session`);
  say(`  naive faker  ${plural(courier.naive, 'press', 'presses')}; accepted while not in range now: ${grouped(courier.naiveAccepted)} (${pct2(cv.naive.rate)}); ${courier.deliveries.naive.toFixed(1)} deliveries a session`);
  say(`  slow-pong    ${plural(courier.slow, 'press', 'presses')}; accepted while not in range now: ${grouped(courier.slowAccepted)} (${pct2(courier.slow ? courier.slowAccepted / courier.slow : 0)}); ${courier.deliveries.slow.toFixed(1)} deliveries a session (no budget: lesson 17, "What the scoreboard doesn't show")`);

  // ---------------------------------------------------------------- trades
  const tv = sb.tradeVerdict(trade);
  say();
  say(`Trades. Your trade and recover on a script of ${trade.requests} requests among 4 players (${trade.writes} writes without a crash): a crash after each`);
  say('write; the server restarts and runs your recover (also crashed after each of its own writes, then run again); the client sends');
  say(`its request again, then the rest of the script. ${grouped(trade.crashPoints)} crash points in trades, ${grouped(trade.recoveryPoints)} in recovery:`);
  say(`  items held twice ${grouped(trade.heldTwice)}, items held by nobody ${grouped(trade.missing)}, coins made or lost ${grouped(trade.coinsMoved)}${trade.coinsWrong ? ` (at ${plural(trade.coinsWrong, 'crash point')})` : ''}${trade.unreached.length ? `; the crash never came at write ${trade.unreached.join(', ')} (your trades made fewer writes than without it)` : ''}`);

  // ---------------------------------------------------------------- budgets
  const pv = sb.protocolVerdict(rows);
  const lv = sb.legalVerdict(rows);
  const sv = sb.searcherVerdict(rows.find((t) => t.row === 'searcher'));
  say();
  say('Budgets (API.md, unit 17). The checks play fresh sessions with other seeds.');
  verdictLine(pv.pass, 'each protocol cheat: every cheating input refused, in every session',
    pv.cheats.map((c) => `${c.row} ${grouped(c.refused)} of ${grouped(c.cheating)}`).join(', ') + '.',
    pv.first && `First admitted: ${sb.rowOf(pv.first.row).label}, server seed ${pv.first.seed}, tick ${pv.first.tick}: ${pv.first.text} (${pv.first.why}); ${pv.first.answer}. Revisit ${sb.LESSON.admission}.`);
  verdictLine(lv.refusals.pass, 'legal players, all six models: no input refused except as stale',
    `${grouped(lv.refusals.sessions)} of ${grouped(lv.sessions)} sessions had one${lv.refusals.stale ? `; ${plural(lv.refusals.stale, 'stale refusal')} (allowed, listed above)` : ''}.`,
    lv.refusals.first && `First: ${sb.rowOf(lv.refusals.first.row).label}, server seed ${lv.refusals.first.seed}, tick ${lv.refusals.first.tick}: ${lv.refusals.first.text}; ${lv.refusals.first.answer}, but the rules admit it: ${lv.refusals.first.why}. Revisit ${sb.LESSON.admission}.`);
  verdictLine(lv.flags.pass, `legal players: at most 1 session in ${sb.BUDGET.legalFlagsOneIn} flagged`,
    `${grouped(lv.flags.flagged)} of ${grouped(lv.flags.sessions)} (at most ${grouped(lv.flags.allowed)}).`,
    `The flagged sessions include ${lv.flags.which.slice(0, 4).map((x) => `${x.row} ${x.seed} (score ${Number(x.score).toFixed(2)})`).join(', ')}. Your threshold must come from the dev split alone (${sb.LESSON.detector}); do not move it to fit these sessions. A change to your detector now means freezing again, and your receipt shows the later freeze.`);
  verdictLine(lv.expert.pass, `expert players: hit rate at least ${percent0(sb.BUDGET.expertHitRate)}`,
    `${sb.percent(lv.expert.rate)} (${grouped(lv.expert.hits)}/${grouped(lv.expert.shots)}).`,
    `Revisit ${lv.refusals.pass ? sb.LESSON.view : sb.LESSON.admission}: experts aim from what your view sends${lv.refusals.pass ? '' : ', and your admission refuses some of their inputs'}.`);
  verdictLine(sv.hit.pass, `the searching client, live against your view: hit rate at most ${percent0(sb.BUDGET.searcherHitRate)}`,
    `${sb.percent(sv.hit.rate)} (${grouped(sv.hit.hits)}/${grouped(sv.hit.shots)}).`,
    `It aims from what your view sends; against the full view it hits ${sb.percent(sb.hitRate(rows.find((t) => t.row === 'searcherFull')))}. Revisit ${sb.LESSON.view}.`);
  verdictLine(sv.flags.pass, `the searching client: at least ${percent0(sb.BUDGET.searcherFlagged)} of its sessions flagged`,
    `${grouped(sv.flags.flagged)} of ${grouped(sv.flags.sessions)} (${sb.percent(sv.flags.sessions ? sv.flags.flagged / sv.flags.sessions : null)}).`,
    `Revisit ${sb.LESSON.detector}.`);
  verdictLine(cv.honest.pass, `courier at your window ${window}: honest presses refused at most ${percent0(sb.BUDGET.honestRefused)}`,
    `${pct2(cv.honest.rate)} (${grouped(cv.honest.refused)} of ${grouped(cv.honest.of)} refused although in range at seen).`,
    `Revisit ${sb.LESSON.window}: lesson 15's table prices every window.`);
  verdictLine(cv.naive.pass, `courier: the naive faker's lies accepted at most ${percent0(sb.BUDGET.naiveAccepted)}`,
    `${pct2(cv.naive.rate)} (${grouped(cv.naive.accepted)} of ${grouped(cv.naive.of)} presses accepted while not in range now).`,
    `Revisit ${sb.LESSON.window}: the rewind must be bounded by the client's own round trip as well as the window.`);
  verdictLine(tv.pass, 'trades: no item in two places and no coin made or lost, after a crash at any write',
    `${grouped(trade.heldTwice)} held twice, ${grouped(trade.missing)} held by nobody, ${grouped(trade.coinsMoved)} coins made or lost, at ${grouped(trade.crashPoints + trade.recoveryPoints)} crash points.`,
    `${trade.first ? `First: ${trade.first.story}: ${[...trade.first.afterRecovery.map((x) => `after recovery ${x}`), ...trade.first.atEnd.map((x) => `at the end ${x}`)].slice(0, 3).join('; ')}. ` : ''}Revisit ${sb.LESSON.trade}.`);
  const verdicts = [pv.pass, lv.refusals.pass, lv.flags.pass, lv.expert.pass, sv.hit.pass, sv.flags.pass, cv.honest.pass, cv.naive.pass, tv.pass];
  const met = verdicts.filter(Boolean).length;
  say(met === verdicts.length
    ? `All ${verdicts.length} budgets met on these sessions. node lab.mjs check ${dir} 17 judges them on sessions you have not seen.`
    : `${met} of ${verdicts.length} budgets met. Each MISS names the lesson to revisit.`);
  say(`Played in ${((performance.now() - started) / 1000).toFixed(1)} s.`);
  if (met !== verdicts.length) process.exitCode = 1;
}

function percent0(x) {
  return `${Math.round(100 * x)}%`;
}

`courses/anti-cheat-engineering-part-two/lessons/12.md`:

```md
# 12 · Lob behind a server

Lob is an artillery game. Each round the player sets an angle and a power and fires one shell, the wind pushes it, and a landing within 12 paces of the moving flag is a hit (README.md, "The two games", has the rest). In Sightline, a separate course you don't need for this one, Lob runs on the player's machine, and you build an engine that reads its memory and presses its keys. A game that runs on the player's machine has handed the player everything: the wind, the flag, the score. This course moves the game to a server. Each player's Lob runs there, three frames every 50 ms tick, and the player's client only draws pictures and sends requests. In each tick the server decides on the messages that have arrived, runs the game, and then sends each client a view, one message about that client's game. In this lesson it sends the full view, `public/full-view.mjs`, which holds everything the game holds, and lesson 13 replaces it.

By the end of this lesson your `server/admission.mjs` will refuse every message outside a five-field vocabulary, every old or repeated message, and every second shot in a round. Your `server/recorder.mjs` will write each session down, and its `replay` will re-run a record from its seed and refuse a record that doesn't hold up.

Part one built the same ideas for the courier arena, in its units M1, M2 and M6: a proximity guard (an interaction counts only within range of its target), admission by sequence number, and replay (re-running a session's record to check it).

## What the client may say

A client may send one kind of message:

```json
{ "v": 1, "seq": 17, "angle": 52, "power": 71, "fire": true }
```

That is the whole vocabulary: a version, a sequence number, the angle and power the player wants, and whether to fire. Everything else is the server's: where the shell flies, where it lands, whether it hit, the score, when the next round starts. `public/session.mjs` turns an admitted message into what Lob understands, presses of its own keys: one press of RIGHT per degree up, UP per point of power, then SPACE to fire.

Run a session and watch the messages go by:

```
node lab.mjs play project
```

On the type-in route it stops at your first unwritten function. Before you write anything, tour the two supplied files that call your code. They are the server's game loop, and they are short.

In `public/runtime.mjs`, read `tick()`. For each text that arrived since the last tick, in arrival order, it asks the game for its facts (the tick, the round, whether the shell is flying), calls your `parseInput`, and, if that accepts, calls your `admit` with the session's admission state and those facts. Only an admitted input reaches the game, through `session.apply`. Notice what the runtime does with an admission: it keeps `decision.next` as the session's new state and tells the recorder with `recorder.admitted(tick, input)`. Your functions never store anything themselves; the server holds the state and hands it back next time. After the messages it calls `session.step()` once, which runs the tick's frames.

In `public/session.mjs`, read `apply` and `step`. `apply` presses keys until the game's angle and power equal the input's, then presses SPACE if the input fires. `step` runs the frames and starts the next round when the result has shown long enough, or when a round has gone unshot too long. Your replay will drive the game through these same two calls, which is why a replayed game runs exactly as the live one did.

## Parse strictly

Write `parseInput(text)`. API.md lists the checks in order, and the first that fails names the reason.

Refuse a message with an unknown field, even a harmless-looking one. A field the server ignores today is a field someone reads tomorrow. A client that sends `"hit": true` is asking the server to believe it, and the answer is no. A parser that drops the field silently never gives that answer and leaves the claim open.

Numbers must be JSON numbers. `"52"` is a string that a lenient parser would turn into 52, and then the server holds a value whose type its own rules never checked. Integers must be whole, because an angle of 52.5 isn't a key press Lob can make. The byte limit comes first so that a client can't make the server parse a megabyte of JSON.

Check `12.parse-accepts` gives your parser messages at every limit, and check `12.parse-refuses` one message for each reason, plus messages with several faults, which must get the first reason in API.md's order.

Question 12a: how many of these five messages does `parseInput` refuse?

```
{"v":1,"seq":4,"angle":52,"power":71,"fire":true}
{"v":1,"seq":5,"angle":52,"power":71,"fire":true,"hit":true}
{"v":1,"seq":6,"angle":"52","power":71,"fire":true}
{"seq":7,"v":1,"fire":false,"power":100,"angle":85}
{"v":1,"seq":8,"angle":52,"power":70.5,"fire":false}
```

Commit your answer with `predict` before reading on:

```
node lab.mjs predict project 12a YOUR_ANSWER
```

### Read the message before reading its fields

`parseInput` has two halves. The first decides whether the text is a message at all: a string, short enough, valid JSON, a plain object, with exactly the five keys. In `server/admission.mjs`, replace the `parse-shape` region, the first of the two regions inside `parseInput`:

<!-- code-example {"file":"examples/admission-checkpoint.mjs","region":"parse-shape","language":"js","title":"Refuse anything that is not a five-key object","change":"Replace the parse-shape region inside parseInput."} -->
```js {"file":"examples/admission-checkpoint.mjs","region":"parse-shape","title":"Refuse anything that is not a five-key object","change":"Replace the parse-shape region inside parseInput."}
  if (typeof text !== 'string') return refuse('text');
  if (Buffer.byteLength(text, 'utf8') > INPUT_MAX_BYTES)
    return refuse('too-long');
  let value;
  try {
    value = JSON.parse(text);
  } catch {
    return refuse('json');
  }
  if (value === null || typeof value !== 'object' || Array.isArray(value))
    return refuse('object');
  const keys = Object.keys(value).sort();
  if (
    keys.length !== INPUT_KEYS.length ||
    keys.some((key, i) => key !== INPUT_KEYS[i])
  )
    return refuse('keys');
```
<!-- /code-example -->

Each line refuses one way a text can fail, in API.md's order, and returns at once, so the first failing reason is the one reported. The length is measured in bytes with `Buffer.byteLength`, not in string units with `text.length`: a letter outside plain English can take two to four bytes, and the limit is about how much the server must read. The limit is tested before `JSON.parse` runs, so the server never parses a longer text. In JavaScript `typeof null` is `'object'`, and so is the type of an array, which is why the object test names both.

The key test sorts the message's own keys and compares them, one by one, with the supplied `INPUT_KEYS`, which is already in sorted order. That one comparison refuses a missing key, an extra key such as `"hit"` and a misspelt one, and it doesn't matter in which order the client wrote them. `refuse(reason)`, supplied at the bottom of the file, builds `{ ok: false, reason }`.

On the type-in route the second half is still a hole. Run the supplied probe, which hands eleven messages to your `parseInput` and prints what it says about each:

```sh
node examples/try-parse.mjs project

### Then check each field's value

Replace the `parse-values` region, just below:

<!-- code-example {"file":"examples/admission-checkpoint.mjs","region":"parse-values","language":"js","title":"Check each field, then build a new input","change":"Replace the parse-values region inside parseInput."} -->
```js {"file":"examples/admission-checkpoint.mjs","region":"parse-values","title":"Check each field, then build a new input","change":"Replace the parse-values region inside parseInput."}
  if (value.v !== 1) return refuse('version');
  if (!inRange(value.seq, SEQ)) return refuse('seq');
  if (!inRange(value.angle, ANGLE)) return refuse('angle');

The limits `SEQ`, `ANGLE` and `POWER` come from `public/rules.mjs`, the one file every module reads its numbers from. The input returned is a new object built field by field, not `value` itself. Nothing the client wrote travels further than these five fields.

The three range tests share one helper. Replace the `in-range` region near the bottom of the file:

<!-- code-example {"file":"examples/admission-checkpoint.mjs","region":"in-range","language":"js","title":"A whole number inside the limits","change":"Replace the in-range region."} -->
```js {"file":"examples/admission-checkpoint.mjs","region":"in-range","title":"A whole number inside the limits","change":"Replace the in-range region."}
function inRange(value, { min, max }) {
  return Number.isSafeInteger(value) && value >= min && value <= max;
}
```
<!-- /code-example -->

`Number.isSafeInteger` is false for a string, for `true`, for a fraction, for `NaN` and for a number too large to hold exactly, so this one test refuses a number sent as a string and a number with a fraction alike. The comparisons with `min` and `max` then run only on a whole number.

## Order and replays

Messages travel over a network. They can be lost, and when the network's delay varies they can arrive in a different order from the one they were sent in. Each carries `seq`, a number the client increases by one for every message it sends. The server keeps the highest `seq` it has admitted and refuses anything at or below it as `stale`. This is part one's M2 rule.

That one rule refuses a message overtaken by a later one, a message the network delivered twice, and a message an attacker recorded and sent again. A gap is fine. A lost message leaves one, and each message holds the player's whole intent (the angle and power they want now, not a change), so a later message makes up for a lost one.

A refused message changes nothing, including the highest `seq`. If a refusal moved it, a client could make the server skip its own messages.

Check `12.admit-order` tests this rule, including that a refusal leaves the state as it was.

Question 12d: a client sends seqs 1, 2, 3, 4, 5. The network loses 3 and delivers 5 before 4. Which seqs does the server admit, in the order it admits them? Answer with the numbers in order, separated by commas:

```
node lab.mjs predict project 12d YOUR_ANSWER
```

## One shot per round

Some rules need facts that only the game has. The runtime passes them to `admit`: the tick, the round, and whether the shell is flying. While it flies, the server refuses everything. A fire in a round that already had a shot is refused as `fired`. The state, `{ lastSeq, firedRound }`, holds the highest seq admitted and the round of the last admitted fire, so a fire in the next round is admitted again.

Write `admit(state, input, facts)`. It must not change the `state` it was given, and instead returns `next`, which the runtime keeps. Check `12.admit-rounds` tests the round rules and the order of the three reasons, `stale`, then `flying`, then `fired` (API.md's table for `admit`).

Question 12b: the state is `{ lastSeq: 7, firedRound: 2 }`, it's round 3 and nothing is flying. These arrive in this order, and no tick passes between them: seq 9 without fire, seq 8 with fire, seq 10 with fire, seq 11 with fire. Which seqs are admitted? Answer with the numbers in order, separated by commas:

```
node lab.mjs predict project 12b YOUR_ANSWER
```

### Decide, and return the next state

Replace the `admit` region of `server/admission.mjs`, the whole function:

<!-- code-example {"file":"examples/admission-checkpoint.mjs","region":"admit","language":"js","title":"Three refusals, then the next state","change":"Replace the complete admit region."} -->
```js {"file":"examples/admission-checkpoint.mjs","region":"admit","title":"Three refusals, then the next state","change":"Replace the complete admit region."}
export function admit(state, input, facts) {
  if (input.seq <= state.lastSeq)
    return { status: 'refused', reason: 'stale', next: state };
  if (facts.flying) return { status: 'refused', reason: 'flying', next: state };
  if (input.fire && state.firedRound === facts.round)
    return { status: 'refused', reason: 'fired', next: state };
  return {
    status: 'admitted',
    next: {
      lastSeq: input.seq,
      firedRound: input.fire ? facts.round : state.firedRound,
    },
  };
}
```
<!-- /code-example -->

The three refusals come in API.md's order, and each returns `next: state`, the state it was given, unchanged. That is how a refusal changes nothing. An admission builds a new object instead of assigning to `state.lastSeq`: the runtime and the checks may still hold the old object, and changing it in place would rewrite a state that should already be history.

`firedRound` moves only when the admitted input fires. An aim, an input that changes angle or power without firing, leaves it alone, so a player may aim as often as they like and still fire once in the round. The round comes from `facts`, the game's own count; nothing in the message can claim a round.

Walk the supplied probe through two rounds. It calls your `admit` once per step, with facts written into the probe, and prints the state after each decision:

```sh
node examples/try-admit.mjs project
```

<!-- code-example {"file":"examples/admit-output.txt","language":"text","title":"admit across two rounds"} -->
```text {"file":"examples/admit-output.txt","title":"admit across two rounds"}
start                         state {"lastSeq":0,"firedRound":0}
seq 1      round 1        admitted        state {"lastSeq":1,"firedRound":0}
seq 2 fire round 1        admitted        state {"lastSeq":2,"firedRound":1}
seq 3      round 1 flying refused flying  state {"lastSeq":2,"firedRound":1} (the same object)
seq 4 fire round 1        refused fired   state {"lastSeq":2,"firedRound":1} (the same object)
seq 5 fire round 2        admitted        state {"lastSeq":5,"firedRound":2}
seq 5      round 2        refused stale   state {"lastSeq":5,"firedRound":2} (the same object)
```
<!-- /code-example -->

Follow `lastSeq` down the right-hand column: it moves only on the admitted lines. The probe adds "(the same object)" when a refusal returns the very state it was given. A refusal that returns a copy with the same values is also correct (API.md says so), and then the probe leaves that note off.

## The protocol cheats

`public/adversaries.mjs` holds four protocol cheats, clients that play like a skilled player (one of the course's legal player models) and break one rule each. `hitClaim` adds `"hit": true` to every fire, and once a session sends a message claiming `"score": 99`. `fireTwice` fires again while its shell flies, and again after it lands. `outOfRange` sends a copy of one input with power 150 every round, and once a session one with angle 4 and one with power 60.5. `replay` re-sends its previous round's fire byte for byte.

```
node lab.mjs clients project
```

With a correct admission it prints, for three sessions of each client:

```
client       sent  admitted  refused  shots  rounds  refused by reason
skilled       315       315        0     36      36  -
hitClaim      513       331      182      0      36  keys 182
fireTwice     387       315       72     36      36  flying 36, fired 36
outOfRange    357       315       42     36      36  angle 3, power 39
replay        348       315       33     36      36  stale 33
```

Every cheating message is refused with its own reason, and every ordinary one admitted. `hitClaim` never fires at all, because each of its fires carries the forbidden field. Check `12.clients` plays the same clients through the server and looks at every decision.

No message can write the score, because there is no field for it, and the score is the game's, on the server. But the score follows from the game's rules, and admission is what enforces them. An admission that let `fireTwice` through would give it two chances at the flag every round, and it would score more.

## Write it down

A server that refuses a message should be able to show what it did admit. Write `createRecorder`. The runtime calls `admitted(tick, input)` for each admitted message, and `finish(end, final)` returns the record. The format is in API.md: the session's seed, the admitted inputs numbered 1, 2, 3 with the tick each was applied in, the number of ticks run, and the final state.

The seed matters most. Lob is deterministic, so the same seed deals the same flags, winds and flag speeds, and the same inputs at the same ticks then give the same game. So a record needs no screenshots and no memory dumps, because seed and inputs are the whole session.

### Keep the inputs, hand back copies

In `server/recorder.mjs`, replace the `recorder` region, the whole of `createRecorder`:

<!-- code-example {"file":"examples/recorder-checkpoint.mjs","region":"recorder","language":"js","title":"Number each admitted input; build the record on finish","change":"Replace the complete recorder region."} -->
```js {"file":"examples/recorder-checkpoint.mjs","region":"recorder","title":"Number each admitted input; build the record on finish","change":"Replace the complete recorder region."}
export function createRecorder({ seed, mode }) {
  const inputs = [];
  return {
    admitted(tick, input) {
      inputs.push({
        n: inputs.length + 1,
        tick,
        seq: input.seq,
        angle: input.angle,
        power: input.power,
        fire: input.fire,
      });
    },
    finish(end, final) {
      return {
        v: 1,
        game: 'lob',
        mode,
        seed,
        inputs: inputs.map((input) => ({ ...input })),
        end,
        final: {
          round: final.round,
          score: final.score,
          shots: final.shots,
          angle: final.angle,
          power: final.power,
        },
      };
    },
  };
}
```
<!-- /code-example -->

The runtime makes one recorder per session, so `inputs` lives in the closure of that call and no two sessions share it. `n` comes from the list's length at the moment of the push, which numbers the inputs in the order the server applied them. Each entry copies the fields it needs by name. It drops `v`, which every admitted input has, and adds `tick`, which the input doesn't carry: the runtime passes the tick in which it decided the message.

`finish` copies again. The record goes to files and to other code, and a caller that edits the record it got must not edit the recorder's own list. `final` keeps only the five fields API.md names, which are the ones replay compares.

```
node lab.mjs record project --out project/run.json
```

With no `--model` or `--seed`, `record` plays the expert player model, and this lesson calls what it saves the default record. Open `project/run.json` and find the first input whose `fire` is true: its `tick` is the tick of the first shot in the session printed at the start of this lesson, because `record` and `play` use the same seeds.

Check `12.recorder` feeds your recorder a session's admitted inputs and compares the record with the format.

## Replay

Write `replay(record, admission)`. It re-runs the session from the seed with `public/session.mjs`, applying each input at its tick, and compares the final state with the record's. It trusts nothing else in the record, so an input your admission would refuse makes the record `refused`, even if its final matches.

Question 12c: take a genuine record and delete one input that doesn't fire, one in the middle of a round, then renumber the rest so that `n` runs 1, 2, 3 again. Does `replay` accept it? Answer `yes` or `no`:

```
node lab.mjs predict project 12c YOUR_ANSWER
```

### Tour the supplied shape test

`replay` first asks the supplied `wellShaped(record)`, at the bottom of `server/recorder.mjs`, whether every field is there, no other field is, and each has its type. Read it. Notice that it tests `seq`, `angle` and `power` only for being numbers: whether a number is a legal angle is your `parseInput`'s question, and the replay asks it later. A record that fails the shape test is refused with reason `shape` before any game runs.

### The order of the inputs

The next reason is `order`. Replace the `in-order` region, below `replay`:

<!-- code-example {"file":"examples/recorder-checkpoint.mjs","region":"in-order","language":"js","title":"Numbered, never back in time, seq always rising","change":"Replace the complete in-order region."} -->
```js {"file":"examples/recorder-checkpoint.mjs","region":"in-order","title":"Numbered, never back in time, seq always rising","change":"Replace the complete in-order region."}
function inOrder({ inputs, end }) {
  return inputs.every((input, i) => {
    const before = inputs[i - 1];
    return (
      input.n === i + 1 &&
      input.tick < end &&
      (!before || (input.tick >= before.tick && input.seq > before.seq))
    );
  });
}
```
<!-- /code-example -->

Each input is compared with the one before it. Ticks may stay the same, because the server can decide two messages in one tick, but never go down. `seq` must strictly rise, because the server admitted each input only above the last one. The test against `end` keeps every input inside the ticks the replay will run; an input at a later tick would otherwise never be applied and never be checked. The first input has no `before`, so only its number and tick are tested.

### Run the session again

Replace the `replay-run` region inside `replay`:

<!-- code-example {"file":"examples/recorder-checkpoint.mjs","region":"replay-run","language":"js","title":"Re-check every input at its own tick","change":"Replace the replay-run region inside replay.","focus":[12,13,14,15,16,17]} -->
```js {"file":"examples/recorder-checkpoint.mjs","region":"replay-run","title":"Re-check every input at its own tick","change":"Replace the replay-run region inside replay.","focus":[12,13,14,15,16,17]}
  if (!inOrder(record)) return { ok: false, reason: 'order' };
  const session = createLobSession({ seed: record.seed, mode: record.mode });
  let state = { lastSeq: 0, firedRound: 0 };
  let next = 0;
  for (let tick = 0; tick < record.end; tick++) {
    while (next < record.inputs.length && record.inputs[next].tick === tick) {
      const { seq, angle, power, fire } = record.inputs[next++];
      const parsed = admission.parseInput(
        JSON.stringify({ v: 1, seq, angle, power, fire }),
      );
      if (!parsed.ok) return { ok: false, reason: 'refused' };
      const { round, flying } = session.facts();
      const decision = admission.admit(state, parsed.input, {
        tick,
        round,
        flying,
      });
      if (decision.status !== 'admitted')
        return { ok: false, reason: 'refused' };
      session.apply(parsed.input);
      state = decision.next;
    }
    session.step();
  }
```
<!-- /code-example -->

This is the runtime's `tick()` again, with the record in place of the network. The loop runs exactly `end` ticks, and before each tick's frames it applies every input recorded for that tick, as the live server did. Each input goes back through your own admission. It is written out as the message a client would have sent and parsed from that text, so a field the shape test let through, such as an angle with a fraction, meets the same parser a live message meets. The marked lines ask `admit` with the facts the replayed game has at that moment, not anything the record claims. That is what refuses a forged second fire: the record can't say which round a tick fell in, and only the re-run game can.

The replay keeps its own admission state, starting where the runtime starts a session, so a record can't set it.

### Compare the end

Replace the last region, `replay-final`:

<!-- code-example {"file":"examples/recorder-checkpoint.mjs","region":"replay-final","language":"js","title":"The re-run game must end where the record says","change":"Replace the replay-final region inside replay."} -->
```js {"file":"examples/recorder-checkpoint.mjs","region":"replay-final","title":"The re-run game must end where the record says","change":"Replace the replay-final region inside replay."}
  const final = session.final();
  if (FINAL_KEYS.some((key) => final[key] !== record.final[key]))
    return { ok: false, reason: 'final' };
  return { ok: true, final };
```
<!-- /code-example -->

The replay returns the final it computed, not the record's. All eight regions are now filled. Replay the record you saved, then a copy with one shot changed:

```
node lab.mjs replay project project/run.json
node lab.mjs tamper project/run.json --out project/bad.json --set inputs.7.power=70
node lab.mjs replay project project/bad.json
```

`tamper` counts inputs from 0, so `inputs.7` is the eighth input of the record, and in the default record it's the first fire. Your replay should accept `run.json` and refuse `bad.json` with reason `final`, because the edited shot lands somewhere else and at another moment, the rounds after it start at other ticks, and the session ends differently from the record. `tamper` never overwrites a file: to run it again, delete `project/bad.json` or choose another name.

Check `12.replay-genuine` replays records the course made, check `12.replay-tampered` replays altered copies that must be refused with the right reason, and check `12.replay-own` replays records your own recorder made, then altered copies of them. Checks `12.replay-genuine` and `12.replay-own` also watch the tick at which your replay hands each input to your `admit`, and it must be the input's own tick.

Replay checks that a record is consistent with the game, in that these inputs, from this seed, give this final. A server that needs its records to be evidence against tampering also signs them when it writes them, the point part one's unit M5 made about hashes, that a digest identifies bytes, not the hand that made them.

```md
# 13 · Hide what the client doesn't draw

Lesson 12's server sends every client the full view, `public/full-view.mjs`: every field of the game, the exact wind, the flag's speed and the countdown to its next change of speed, the game's random state. Part one's courier server did the same with its `/state` endpoint, which returned the whole state. The official client, the game's own client program, draws only part of it on screen, but a client is a program on the player's machine, and any program can read the whole message.

By the end of this lesson your `server/view.mjs` will send only what the screen draws, at the precision the screen draws it (the drawn view), and your `server/leaks.mjs` will find a leak of anything hidden by changing it and watching the bytes. You will measure what hiding costs an honest player as latency grows, and what it costs a client that aims for its player.

This is often called minimizing exposed state. Riot Games has described the same idea, on a much larger scale, for the fog of war in VALORANT, its online team shooter, in which the server doesn't send a client the positions of enemies its player can't see. The server decides what each client may know, because a client can't be trusted to keep secret anything it is sent.

## Start

**After this unit** the same hunt on your view finds nothing: no change to a hidden thing reaches a message, and no message holds a hidden value in any encoding the hunt searches. Your `findLeaks` will find leaks in any view the same way.

The end-of-unit checkpoint, `examples/view-checkpoint.mjs` and `examples/leaks-checkpoint.mjs`, is 53 lines together, counting comments and the region marker lines.

## What the screen draws

The official client draws the status line (angle, power, the wind's arrows, score and shots), the message (`ROUND 3`, `HIT!`, `SHORT BY 37`), the flag, the shell and its trail, the mark where the last shell landed, and the cloud, which drifts across the sky and never touches the shell. Positions are in paces, Lob's unit of distance, and the screen draws each to the nearest pace. API.md's table lists what the game holds against what is drawn. The exact wind is held by the server and never drawn, and the arrows show only its band, one of seven. The flag's speed, the frames until it picks a new one and the random state that will pick it are never drawn either.

## A client is bounded by what it is sent

`public/adversaries.mjs` holds a searching client. It runs its own copy of Lob (the game file ships with the client, so anyone can) and, each round, searches angle and power for the shot whose landing is nearest the flag at the moment of landing. Every shot it fires is a legal input: one fire per round, an angle and a power in range.

With the full view, at 50 ms of latency each way, it hits 100.0% of its shots.

## Precision is information

Write `drawnView(game, info)` with exactly the fields in API.md. `info` is `{ tick, ack }`, the ticks run and the last admitted seq, which the view sends back. Round every position with `Math.round`, because the screen draws whole paces. The flag at 612.43 and the flag at 612.49 are the same picture, and a message that says 612.43 has told the client something the picture didn't. Two messages a tick apart that each carry the flag's exact position give its exact speed.

Send the wind as the arrows, the same string the status line shows. The message is the game's own string, so it carries exactly what the screen shows. "SHORT BY 37" is drawn, so it may be sent.

Check `13.view-fields` compares every field of your view with the game at many moments: before a fire, in flight, after a landing, at a round change.

### Build the message from the game's getters

Tour `public/full-view.mjs` first. It copies every field of the game, adds the exact wind the server keeps, and sends all of it: the view you are replacing. Then, in `server/view.mjs`, replace the `drawn-view` region:

<!-- code-example {"file":"examples/view-checkpoint.mjs","region":"drawn-view","language":"js","title":"Exactly what the screen draws, at its precision","change":"Replace the complete drawn-view region."} -->
```js {"file":"examples/view-checkpoint.mjs","region":"drawn-view","title":"Exactly what the screen draws, at its precision","change":"Replace the complete drawn-view region."}
export function drawnView(game, { tick, ack }) {
  const shell = game.shell();
  const impact = game.impact();
  return {
    v: 1,
    tick,
    ack,
    round: game.round(),
    score: game.score(),
    shots: game.shots(),
    angle: Math.round(game.angle()),
    power: game.power(),
    wind: arrows(game.windLevel()),
    flag: Math.round(game.targetX()),
    shell: shell ? [Math.round(shell.x), Math.round(shell.y)] : null,
    trail: game.trail().map(([x, y]) => [Math.round(x), Math.round(y)]),
    impact: impact ? { x: Math.round(impact.x), age: impact.age } : null,
    message: game.message(),
    cloud: Math.round(game.cloud()),
  };
}
```
<!-- /code-example -->

Each field is read from one getter and nothing else, in API.md's order, which check `13.view-fields` also compares. Every position goes through `Math.round`, because the screen draws whole paces: the flag, the shell, each point of the trail, the impact mark and the cloud. The angle is held as a float and drawn as a whole number, so it is rounded too. The power, the score and the counts are whole numbers already. `game.shell()` and `game.impact()` return null when there is no shell in the air or no mark on screen, and the view sends null then, rather than a stale or made-up position. The impact's age is a whole number of frames that the screen draws as it is.

The wind is the one field that isn't a rounded number: the screen draws arrows, so the view sends arrows, from `game.windLevel()`, the band the status line shows. The helper that turns the band into arrows comes next. On the type-in route it is still a hole, so the probe below stops there. The probe builds three moments of one scripted session (aiming before the first shot, the shell in the air, just after it lands) and prints your message at each, with its size beside the full view's:

```sh
node examples/try-view.mjs project
```

in flight: arrows: not written yet
landed: arrows: not written yet
```
<!-- /code-example -->

Replace the `arrows` region below `drawnView`:

<!-- code-example {"file":"examples/view-checkpoint.mjs","region":"arrows","language":"js","title":"The band as the status line draws it","change":"Replace the complete arrows region."} -->
```js {"file":"examples/view-checkpoint.mjs","region":"arrows","title":"The band as the status line draws it","change":"Replace the complete arrows region."}
function arrows(level) {
  if (level === 0) return '~';
  return (level > 0 ? '>' : '<').repeat(Math.abs(level));
}
```
<!-- /code-example -->

A calm band is a tilde, and each step of band away from calm is one more arrow pointing the way the wind blows. The exact wind never enters this function; only its band does. Run the probe again:
