`courses/anti-cheat-engineering-part-two/public/net.mjs`:

```mjs
// Seeded network links. A link turns the time a message is sent into the time it
// arrives, or null when it is lost. Every message is delayed on its own (the one-way
// delay plus a uniform jitter), so with jitter, messages can overtake each other.
// Outages drop everything sent inside them.
import { makeRandom } from './stats.mjs';

export function link({ seed, oneWayMs, jitterMs = 0, loss = 0, outages = [] }) {
  const random = makeRandom(seed);
  return {
    delay(sentAtMs) {
      // Two draws per message whatever happens, so one lost message never shifts the rest.
      const jitter = random.next();
      const lose = random.next();
      if (outages.some(({ at, ms }) => sentAtMs >= at && sentAtMs < at + ms)) return null;
      if (lose < loss) return null;
      return sentAtMs + oneWayMs + Math.floor(jitter * (jitterMs + 1));
    },
  };
}

`courses/anti-cheat-engineering-part-two/public/players.mjs`:

```mjs
// Legal player models: people playing Lob through the official client.
// A player sees only what screen.show(now) returns. Each round they notice it, think,
// press keys at a human pace (sending an input whenever the values change), fire once,
// read the result and correct toward it the next time.
//
// Their aim is the true mapping from the game itself (where a shell lands for an angle,
// a power and a wind level; the official client could ship such a table), plus what a
// person adds: a per-session bias, per-shot noise, and a lead for the flag's motion
// that is only as good as what they see on screen.
import { createScreen } from './client.mjs';
import { createFlightLab } from './lob.mjs';
import { makeRandom, mixSeed } from './stats.mjs';
import { ANGLE, POWER, FLAG, TICK_MS } from './rules.mjs';

// How each kind of player behaves. Times are medians of lognormal draws, in ms.
// Bias and noise are in paces of landing distance; `lead` is the share of the flag's
// apparent motion they allow for (drawn once per session from the range), over the
// shell's flight, plus their one-way delay for players who `leadsPing`; `learn` is how far
// they move their aim toward correcting each miss.
export const PROFILES = {
  novice:  { reactionMs: 900, fireMs: 5000, angles: [35, 60], lead: [0, 0],       biasSd: 70, noiseSd: 60, learn: 0.2, angleChange: 0.25 },
  skilled: { reactionMs: 600, fireMs: 3000, angles: [40, 55], lead: [0.5, 0.65],  biasSd: 25, noiseSd: 16, learn: 0.4, angleChange: 0.15 },
  expert:  { reactionMs: 450, fireMs: 2000, angles: [30, 50], lead: [0.88, 0.98], biasSd: 15, noiseSd: 8,  learn: 0.6, angleChange: 0.1, leadsPing: true },
};

// The kinds the corpus uses: three skill levels on an ordinary connection, and skilled
// players on three hard ones.
export const PLAYER_KINDS = {
  novice:      { profile: 'novice',  network: { oneWayMs: 30, jitterMs: 10 } },
  skilled:     { profile: 'skilled', network: { oneWayMs: 30, jitterMs: 10 } },
  expert:      { profile: 'expert',  network: { oneWayMs: 30, jitterMs: 10 } },
  highLatency: { profile: 'skilled', network: { oneWayMs: 250, jitterMs: 30 } },
  jitter:      { profile: 'skilled', network: { oneWayMs: 60, jitterMs: 60 } },   // packets overtake each other
  reconnects:  { profile: 'skilled', network: { oneWayMs: 40, jitterMs: 10, outages: true } }, // 2-3 outages of 2-6 s
};

const POLL_MS = [80, 130];       // how often a player glances at the screen
const CADENCE_MS = [80, 250];    // the gap between two inputs while pressing keys
const LEAD_WINDOW_MS = 500;      // the motion they judge the flag's speed from
const ROUND_DEADLINE_MS = 9000;  // a player fires before this long after they saw the round start
const REFIRE_TICKS = 20;         // no acknowledgement a second (plus a round trip) after firing: the fire was lost

// makePlayer(kind, seed, { screen, hooks }) -> a client model for sim.mjs.
//   screen  'drawn' (default) or 'full': the official client's mode
//   hooks   for the protocol cheats in adversaries.mjs only:
//           shapeInput(message, ctx) -> the texts to send for one input
//           onGlance(shown, now, ctx) -> extra texts to send at a glance at the screen
export function makePlayer(kind, seed, { screen: screenMode = 'drawn', hooks = {} } = {}) {
  const spec = PLAYER_KINDS[kind];
  if (!spec) throw new Error(`unknown player kind ${kind}; the kinds are ${Object.keys(PLAYER_KINDS).join(', ')}`);
  const profile = PROFILES[spec.profile];
  const session = makeRandom(mixSeed(seed, 1)); // who this player is today
  const timing = makeRandom(mixSeed(seed, 2));  // when they act
  const hand = makeRandom(mixSeed(seed, 3));    // how their shots scatter
  const screen = createScreen({ mode: screenMode });

  const network = { ...spec.network, outages: spec.network.outages ? drawOutages(session) : [] };
  const preferredAngle = session.int(profile.angles[0], profile.angles[1]);
  const lead = session.uniform(profile.lead[0], profile.lead[1]);
  const bias = session.normal() * profile.biasSd;

  let seq = 0;
  let sent = { angle: 45, power: 60 }; // the game starts at angle 45, power 60
  let correction = 0;                  // paces, learned from results
  let phase = 'watch';                 // watch -> notice -> act -> fired -> watch
  let wakeAt = 0;
  let lastRound = 0;                   // the last round this player started on
  let round = null;                    // this round's plan
  let fired = null;                    // { round, seq, firstTick, refires, text, landAt }
  let samples = [];                    // [ms, flag] of recent glances, for the lead
  let lastMessageAt = null;

  // What a hook (adversaries.mjs) may use: a fresh seq, the round the player is on and
  // the player's last fire.
  const ctx = {
    nextSeq: () => ++seq,
    get round() { return round ? round.number : 0; },
    get lastFire() { return fired; },
  };

  function input(fields, fire, now, out) {
    seq += 1;
    const message = { v: 1, seq, angle: fields.angle, power: fields.power, fire };
    sent = { angle: fields.angle, power: fields.power };
    screen.sent(seq, now);
    const texts = hooks.shapeInput ? hooks.shapeInput(message, ctx) : [JSON.stringify(message)];
    out.push(...texts);
    return texts[texts.length - 1];
  }

  // The flag's speed as it looked on screen over the last half second, paces per second
  // (the slope of a straight line through their glances).
  function apparentSpeed(now) {
    const recent = samples.filter(([t]) => t >= now - LEAD_WINDOW_MS);
    if (recent.length < 2 || recent[recent.length - 1][0] - recent[0][0] < 150) return 0;
    const n = recent.length;
    let st = 0, sf = 0, stt = 0, stf = 0;
    for (const [t, f] of recent) { st += t; sf += f; stt += t * t; stf += t * f; }
    return ((n * stf - st * sf) / (n * stt - st * st)) * 1000;
  }

  // Where to aim: the flag as shown, led by the share of its motion this player allows
  // for over the shell's flight (bouncing off the ends as the flag does). `landAt` is
  // where they want the shell to land; the power they pick for it carries what they have
  // learned, their bias and (for the real shot) their noise.
  function aim(shown, now, noise) {
    const angle = round.angle;
    const speed = apparentSpeed(now);
    let landAt = shown.flag;
    let power = powerFor(angle, shown.wind, landAt + correction + bias);
    // Experts also allow for their own delay, the ping the official client shows.
    const extra = profile.leadsPing ? shown.delayMs / 1000 : 0;
    for (let i = 0; i < 2; i++) {
      landAt = bounce(shown.flag + lead * speed * (flightSeconds(angle, power, shown.wind) + extra));
      power = powerFor(angle, shown.wind, landAt + correction + bias + noise);
    }
    return { angle, power: clamp(Math.round(power), POWER.min, POWER.max), landAt };
  }

  function startRound(shown, now) {
    const deadline = round.seenAt + ROUND_DEADLINE_MS;
    const fireAt = Math.min(now + Math.round(timing.lognormal(profile.fireMs, 0.4)), deadline);
    const walkStart = now + timing.int(100, 300);
    const walkMs = Math.max(1, (fireAt - walkStart) * timing.uniform(0.5, 0.8));
    const angle = timing.chance(profile.angleChange)
      ? clamp(preferredAngle + timing.pick([-3, -2, -1, 1, 2, 3]), ANGLE.min, ANGLE.max)
      : preferredAngle;
    round = { ...round, angle, fireAt, walkStart, walkMs, nextInputAt: walkStart, from: { ...sent } };
    round.target = aim(shown, now, 0);
  }

  function walk(now, out) {
    const f = Math.min(1, (now - round.walkStart) / round.walkMs);
    const angle = Math.round(round.from.angle + (round.target.angle - round.from.angle) * f);
    const power = Math.round(round.from.power + (round.target.power - round.from.power) * f);
    if (angle !== sent.angle || power !== sent.power) input({ angle, power }, false, now, out);
    round.nextInputAt = f < 1 ? now + timing.int(CADENCE_MS[0], CADENCE_MS[1]) : Infinity;
  }

  function watch(shown, now) {
    if (shown && shown.round > lastRound && !shown.flying && !shown.impact) {
      lastRound = shown.round;
      round = { number: shown.round, seenAt: now };
      phase = 'notice';
      wakeAt = now + Math.round(timing.lognormal(profile.reactionMs, 0.35));
      return;
    }
    wakeAt = now + timing.int(POLL_MS[0], POLL_MS[1]);
  }

  return {
    kind,
    network,

    onMessage(body, atMs) {
      const resumed = lastMessageAt !== null && atMs - lastMessageAt > 1000;
      screen.receive(body, atMs);
      lastMessageAt = atMs;
      // The first message after a fire: from here the player counts the server's ticks.
      if (fired && fired.firstTick === null) fired.firstTick = screen.latest().tick;
      // Back after an outage: the next input is max(own seq, server's ack) + 1.
      if (resumed) seq = Math.max(seq, screen.latest().ack);
    },

    nextWake: () => wakeAt,

    wake(now) {
      const out = [];
      const shown = screen.show(now);
      if (shown) {
        samples.push([now, shown.flag]);
        if (samples.length > 16) samples = samples.slice(-16);
        if (hooks.onGlance) out.push(...hooks.onGlance(shown, now, ctx));
      }
      if (phase === 'watch') {
        watch(shown, now);
      } else if (phase === 'notice') {
        if (!shown || shown.round !== round.number || shown.flying || shown.impact) { phase = 'watch'; watch(shown, now); return out; }
        startRound(shown, now);
        phase = 'act';
      }
      if (phase === 'act') {
        if (!shown || shown.round !== round.number || shown.flying || shown.impact) { phase = 'watch'; watch(shown, now); return out; }
        if (now >= round.fireAt) {
          const final = aim(shown, now, hand.normal() * profile.noiseSd);
          const text = input(final, true, now, out);
          fired = { round: round.number, seq, firstTick: null, refires: 0, text, landAt: final.landAt };
          phase = 'fired';
          wakeAt = now + timing.int(POLL_MS[0], POLL_MS[1]);
        } else {
          if (now >= round.nextInputAt) walk(now, out);
          wakeAt = Math.min(round.nextInputAt, round.fireAt, now + 100);
        }
        return out;
      }
      if (phase === 'fired') {
        const miss = shown && shown.round === fired.round ? missFrom(shown.message) : null;
        if (miss !== null) {
          // Correct toward where the shell should have landed: the impact mark against the
          // spot they aimed for (or the message's miss when the mark is not on screen).
          const error = shown.impact ? shown.impact.x - fired.landAt : miss;
          correction -= profile.learn * error;
          phase = 'watch';
          wakeAt = now + timing.int(POLL_MS[0], POLL_MS[1]);
        } else if (shown && shown.round > fired.round) {
          phase = 'watch';
          watch(shown, now);
        } else {
          const wait = REFIRE_TICKS + Math.ceil((2 * (shown ? shown.delayMs : 0)) / TICK_MS);
          const unanswered = fired.firstTick !== null && shown && shown.tick > fired.firstTick + wait && shown.ack < fired.seq;
          if (unanswered && !shown.flying && !shown.impact && fired.refires < 5) {
            // A second of the server's ticks (plus a round trip) since we fired, and it never
            // acknowledged the fire: it was lost on the way. Fire again.
            const text = input(sent, true, now, out);
            fired = { ...fired, seq, firstTick: null, refires: fired.refires + 1, text };
          }
          wakeAt = now + timing.int(POLL_MS[0], POLL_MS[1]);
        }
      }
      return out;
    },
  };
}

// The result message as a signed miss: SHORT BY 37 is -37, LONG BY 5 is 5, HIT! is 0.
function missFrom(message) {
  if (message === 'HIT!') return 0;
  const m = /^(SHORT|LONG) BY (\d+)$/.exec(message);
  if (!m) return null;
  return m[1] === 'SHORT' ? -Number(m[2]) : Number(m[2]);
}

// 2 or 3 outages of 2 to 6 s, spread over the first minute of the session.
function drawOutages(random) {
  const n = random.int(2, 3);
  const slot = Math.floor(60000 / n);
  const outages = [];
  for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) {
    const at = 3000 + i * slot + Math.floor(random.uniform(0, slot - 6000));
    outages.push({ at, ms: random.int(2000, 6000) });
  }
  return outages;
}

// The true mapping. For an angle: where the shell lands and how many frames it flies,
// for every power and every wind level, with the wind at the middle of the level's band
// (the arrows are all a player knows). Computed once from the game, then reused.
let lab = null;
const tables = new Map();

export function windMidpoint(level) {
  if (level >= 3) return 4.375;   // the band is 3.75 to 5
  if (level <= -3) return -4.375;
  return level * 1.5;
}

export function rangeTable(angle) {
  let table = tables.get(angle);
  if (!table) {
    lab ??= createFlightLab();
    table = {};
    for (let level = -3; level <= 3; level++) {
      const x = [], frames = [];
      for (let power = POWER.min; power <= POWER.max; power++) {
        const shot = lab.fly(angle, power, windMidpoint(level));
        x.push(shot.x);
        frames.push(shot.frames);
      }
      table[level] = { x, frames };
    }
    tables.set(angle, table);
  }
  return table;
}

// The power (a fraction, between whole powers) that lands at targetX for this angle and
// wind level, by the table.
export function powerFor(angle, level, targetX) {
  const { x } = rangeTable(angle)[clamp(level, -3, 3)];
  if (targetX <= x[0]) return POWER.min;
  for (let i = 1; i < x.length; i++) {
    if (targetX < x[i]) return POWER.min + i - 1 + (targetX - x[i - 1]) / (x[i] - x[i - 1]);
  }
  return POWER.max;
}

export function flightSeconds(angle, power, level) {
  const { frames } = rangeTable(angle)[clamp(level, -3, 3)];
  return frames[clamp(Math.round(power), POWER.min, POWER.max) - POWER.min] / 60;
}

// A position past either end of the flag's range, folded back the way the flag bounces.
function bounce(x) {
  if (x > FLAG.max) return Math.max(FLAG.min, 2 * FLAG.max - x);
  if (x < FLAG.min) return Math.min(FLAG.max, 2 * FLAG.min - x);
  return x;
}

function clamp(value, lo, hi) {
  return Math.min(hi, Math.max(lo, value));
}

// The protocol and timing constants of the Lob server. Every other module reads its
// numbers from here, so a lesson that quotes one of them quotes this file.

export const TICK_MS = 50;           // the server runs one tick every 50 ms
export const FRAMES_PER_TICK = 3;    // Lob runs at 60 frames a second, so a tick is three frames
export const MODE = 9;               // server wind (1) + moving flag (8)

export const ROUNDS_PER_SESSION = 12;
export const RESULT_TICKS = 20;       // after a landing, the result shows this long, then the server starts the next round
export const ROUND_LIMIT_TICKS = 200; // a round with no shot this long after it started ends unshot

export const INPUT_MAX_BYTES = 200;
export const ANGLE = { min: 5, max: 85 };
export const POWER = { min: 10, max: 100 };
export const SEQ = { min: 1, max: 1_000_000 };

export const HIT_RADIUS = 12;        // a landing within 12 paces of the flag is a hit
export const FLAG = { min: 420, max: 900 }; // the moving flag stays between these and bounces at both

// Lob's key codes, as game_key takes them.
export const KEYS = { LEFT: 1, RIGHT: 2, UP: 3, DOWN: 4, SPACE: 5, NEW_ROUND: 6 };

`courses/anti-cheat-engineering-part-two/public/runtime.mjs`:

```mjs
// The Lob server. Each player who joins gets their own Lob session (session.mjs).
// Text in, text out: receive() queues a client's message; tick() decides on what
// arrived, runs one tick of every game and returns the messages to send.
// The trust decisions are hooks you supply:
//   admission  { parseInput, admit }   unit 12: which messages may change the game
//   view       view(game, info)        unit 13: what each tick's message says
//   recorder   createRecorder          unit 12: records what was admitted (optional)
import { createLobSession } from './session.mjs';
import { MODE, ROUNDS_PER_SESSION } from './rules.mjs';
import { mixSeed } from './stats.mjs';

// The game seed of the index-th player to join (1, 2, 3, ...): a 32-bit mix of the
// server's seed and the index (stats.mjs mixSeed), so every session has its own flags
// and winds and the same server seed always deals the same games.
export function sessionSeed(seed, index) {
  return mixSeed(seed, index);
}

export function createLobServer({
  seed, mode = MODE, admission, view, recorder = null, onEvent = null, rounds = ROUNDS_PER_SESSION,
}) {
  const sessions = [];
  const byToken = new Map();

  function entryFor(token) {
    const entry = byToken.get(token);
    if (!entry) throw new Error(`no session ${token}`);
    return entry;
  }

  function finishRecord(entry) {
    if (entry.recorder && !entry.record) entry.record = entry.recorder.finish(entry.session.tick, entry.session.final());
    return entry.record;
  }

  return {
    // For checks and tools: every session, in join order.
    sessions,
    session: entryFor,

    join() {
      const index = sessions.length + 1;
      const token = `s${index}`;
      const gameSeed = sessionSeed(seed, index);
      const session = createLobSession({ seed: gameSeed, mode, rounds });
      const entry = {
        token,
        seed: gameSeed,
        session,
        game: session.game,
        state: { lastSeq: 0, firedRound: 0 }, // admission state, given to admit and replaced by its `next`
        ack: 0,                              // the last admitted seq, sent back in every view
        queue: [],                           // texts received since the last tick, in arrival order
        decisions: [],                       // every text with what parseInput and admit said
        recorder: recorder ? recorder({ seed: gameSeed, mode }) : null,
        record: null,
        outcomes: () => session.outcomes(),
        final: () => session.final(),
      };
      sessions.push(entry);
      byToken.set(token, entry);
      return token;
    },

    receive(token, text) {
      entryFor(token).queue.push(text);
    },

    // One server tick for every session that is still playing.
    tick() {
      const messages = [];
      for (const entry of sessions) {
        const { session } = entry;
        if (session.over()) continue;
        const arrived = entry.queue;
        entry.queue = [];
        for (const text of arrived) {
          const { tick, round, flying } = session.facts();
          const parsed = admission.parseInput(text);
          let decision = null;
          if (parsed && parsed.ok) {
            decision = admission.admit(entry.state, parsed.input, { tick, round, flying });
            if (decision && decision.status === 'admitted') {
              session.apply(parsed.input);
              entry.state = decision.next;
              entry.ack = parsed.input.seq;
              if (entry.recorder) entry.recorder.admitted(tick, parsed.input);
            }
          }
          const event = { token: entry.token, tick, text, parsed, decision };
          entry.decisions.push(event);
          if (onEvent) onEvent(event);
        }
        session.step();
        if (session.over()) finishRecord(entry);
        messages.push({ token: entry.token, text: JSON.stringify(view(entry.game, { tick: session.tick, ack: entry.ack })) });
      }
      return messages;
    },

    // The session's record: finished when the session ended, or now if it is still playing.
    record: (token) => finishRecord(entryFor(token)),
  };
}

`courses/anti-cheat-engineering-part-two/public/session.mjs`:

```mjs
// One player's Lob game as the server runs it. An admitted intent becomes key presses;
// each server tick runs three frames; the session starts and ends rounds.
// The runtime, the corpus and your replay all drive Lob through this file, so a game
// replayed from a record runs exactly as it ran live.
//
// Ticks are counted as "ticks run so far". The session starts at tick 0 with round 1.
// An intent applied now belongs to tick `session.tick` (it acts before the next tick's
// frames). A view built after step() shows the game after `session.tick` ticks.
import { makeLob } from './lob.mjs';
import {
  MODE, FRAMES_PER_TICK, RESULT_TICKS, ROUND_LIMIT_TICKS, ROUNDS_PER_SESSION, ANGLE, POWER, KEYS,
} from './rules.mjs';

const RESULTS = { 1: 'hit', 2: 'short', 3: 'long' };

export function createLobSession({ seed, mode = MODE, rounds = ROUNDS_PER_SESSION }) {
  const game = makeLob({ seed, mode });
  let tick = 0;
  let over = false;
  let nextRoundAt = null; // the tick the next round starts, once the shell has landed
  const played = [];
  let current = beginRound(game.round(), 0);

  function beginRound(round, start) {
    const outcome = { round, start, shot: null, impact: null, flag: null, miss: null, result: null, inputs: 0 };
    played.push(outcome);
    return outcome;
  }

  // The shell has just landed (this frame). The first landing of a round is its outcome.
  function landed() {
    if (current.impact !== null) return;
    const impact = game.impact().x;
    const flag = game.targetX();
    current.impact = round2(impact);
    current.flag = round2(flag);
    current.miss = round2(impact - flag);
    current.result = RESULTS[game.exports.r_result()] ?? null;
  }

  return {
    game,
    get tick() { return tick; },
    get round() { return current.round; },

    facts: () => ({ tick, round: current.round, flying: game.flying(), fired: current.shot !== null }),

    // Press keys until the game's angle and power equal the intent's (one step per press),
    // then SPACE if the intent fires. The caller has already admitted the intent.
    apply(intent) {
      if (over) return;
      pressToward(game, Math.round(game.angle()), intent.angle, ANGLE, KEYS.RIGHT, KEYS.LEFT);
      pressToward(game, game.power(), intent.power, POWER, KEYS.UP, KEYS.DOWN);
      current.inputs += 1;
      if (intent.fire) {
        const shotsBefore = game.shots();
        game.key(KEYS.SPACE);
        if (game.shots() > shotsBefore && current.shot === null) {
          current.shot = { tick, angle: Math.round(game.angle()), power: game.power() };
        }
      }
    },

    // One server tick: three frames, then round scheduling.
    step() {
      if (over) return;
      let landedNow = false;
      for (let f = 0; f < FRAMES_PER_TICK; f++) {
        const wasFlying = game.flying();
        game.tick(1);
        if (wasFlying && !game.flying()) { landedNow = true; landed(); }
      }
      tick += 1;
      if (landedNow) nextRoundAt = tick + RESULT_TICKS;
      const unshot = current.shot === null && tick - current.start >= ROUND_LIMIT_TICKS;
      const resultShown = nextRoundAt === tick;
      if (!unshot && !resultShown) return;
      nextRoundAt = null;
      if (game.flying()) return; // a shell still in the air: its landing schedules the next round
      if (current.round >= rounds) { over = true; return; }
      game.key(KEYS.NEW_ROUND);
      current = beginRound(game.round(), tick);
    },

    // Per round, in order: { round, start, shot, impact, flag, miss, result, inputs }.
    outcomes: () => played.map((o) => ({ ...o, shot: o.shot && { ...o.shot } })),
    over: () => over,
    final: () => ({ round: game.round(), score: game.score(), shots: game.shots(), angle: Math.round(game.angle()), power: game.power() }),
  };
}

// Press `up` or `down` until the value reaches the target (kept inside its range).
function pressToward(game, value, target, { min, max }, up, down) {
  if (typeof target !== 'number' || !Number.isFinite(target)) return;
  const goal = Math.min(max, Math.max(min, Math.round(target)));
  for (let v = value; v < goal; v++) game.key(up);
  for (let v = value; v > goal; v--) game.key(down);
}

function round2(value) {
  return Math.round(value * 100) / 100;
}

`courses/anti-cheat-engineering-part-two/public/sim.mjs`:

```mjs
// Play one client model against a Lob server over two seeded links.
// The simulation is event-driven, in whole milliseconds: the server ticks at every
// multiple of TICK_MS and sends that tick's message at that moment; the client acts
// whenever it asks to. Inside one millisecond the order is: arrivals at the server,
// the server's tick, arrivals at the client, then the client's own action. So an input
// that arrives exactly on a tick is decided in that tick, and one sent on a tick waits
// for the next.
//
// A client model is an object with three methods:
//   onMessage(body, atMs)   a server message arrived (JSON text, or a view object)
//   nextWake()              the next ms it wants to act at (Infinity for never; a
//                           fraction is rounded up to the next whole ms)
//   wake(atMs)              act now; return the texts to send (an array, maybe empty)
import { TICK_MS } from './rules.mjs';

export function playSession({
  server, client, up, down, rounds = Infinity, keepMessages = false, maxMs = 30 * 60 * 1000,
}) {
  const token = server.join();
  const entry = server.session(token);
  const toServer = []; // { at, order, body }
  const toClient = [];
  const messages = keepMessages ? [] : null;
  let order = 0;
  let ticks = 0;
  let lastWake = -1, wakesAtSameMs = 0;

  for (;;) {
    const nextTick = (ticks + 1) * TICK_MS;
    const now = Math.min(nextTick, Math.ceil(client.nextWake()), earliest(toServer), earliest(toClient));
    if (now > maxMs) break;

    deliver(toServer, now, (m) => server.receive(token, m.body));

    if (now === nextTick) {
      ticks += 1;
      for (const m of server.tick()) {
        if (m.token !== token) continue;
        const body = m.text ?? m.view;
        if (messages) messages.push({ tick: ticks, at: now, text: typeof body === 'string' ? body : JSON.stringify(body) });
        const at = down.delay(now);
        if (at !== null) toClient.push({ at, order: order++, body });
      }
      if (entry.session.over() || roundsEnded(entry.session) >= rounds) break;
    }

    deliver(toClient, now, (m) => client.onMessage(m.body, m.at));

    if (Math.ceil(client.nextWake()) <= now) {
      wakesAtSameMs = now === lastWake ? wakesAtSameMs + 1 : 0;
      lastWake = now;
      if (wakesAtSameMs > 1000) throw new Error(`client keeps asking to act at ${now} ms`);
      for (const text of client.wake(now)) {
        const at = up.delay(now);
        if (at !== null) toServer.push({ at, order: order++, body: text });
      }
    }
  }

  const result = { token, outcomes: entry.session.outcomes(), final: entry.session.final(), ticks };
  if (entry.recorder || entry.record) result.record = server.record(token);
  if (messages) result.messages = messages;
  return result;
}

function roundsEnded(session) {
  return session.over() ? session.round : session.round - 1;
}

function earliest(queue) {
  let t = Infinity;
  for (const m of queue) if (m.at < t) t = m.at;
  return t;
}

// Hand over every message due by `now`, earliest first (ties in the order they were sent).
function deliver(queue, now, handle) {
  for (;;) {
    let best = -1;
    for (let i = 0; i < queue.length; i++) {
      const m = queue[i];
      if (m.at > now) continue;
      if (best < 0 || m.at < queue[best].at || (m.at === queue[best].at && m.order < queue[best].order)) best = i;
    }
    if (best < 0) return;
    handle(queue.splice(best, 1)[0]);
  }
}

`courses/anti-cheat-engineering-part-two/public/stats.mjs`:

```mjs
// Small shared helpers: a seeded random number generator, a seed mixer, and the
// statistics the course uses (median, quantile, mean, sd, correlation).
// Nothing in the course calls Math.random or reads the clock for a result, so every
// run with the same seeds prints the same numbers.

// A seeded generator (mulberry32). Same seed, same sequence, on every machine.
export function makeRandom(seed) {
  let a = seed >>> 0;
  const next = () => {
    a = (a + 0x6d2b79f5) >>> 0;
    let t = Math.imul(a ^ (a >>> 15), 1 | a);
    t = (t + Math.imul(t ^ (t >>> 7), 61 | t)) ^ t;
    return ((t ^ (t >>> 14)) >>> 0) / 4294967296;
  };
  const normal = () => {
    // Box-Muller: two uniforms make one standard normal.
    const u = 1 - next();
    const v = next();
    return Math.sqrt(-2 * Math.log(u)) * Math.cos(2 * Math.PI * v);
  };
  return {
    next,                                                   // uniform in [0, 1)
    uniform: (lo, hi) => lo + (hi - lo) * next(),           // uniform in [lo, hi)
    int: (lo, hi) => lo + Math.floor(next() * (hi - lo + 1)), // integer in lo..hi
    chance: (p) => next() < p,
    normal,
    lognormal: (median, sigma) => median * Math.exp(sigma * normal()),
    pick: (list) => list[Math.floor(next() * list.length)],
  };
}

// Mix two numbers into a new 32-bit seed (murmur3's finalizer over a simple combination).
export function mixSeed(a, b = 0) {
  let h = (Math.imul(a >>> 0, 0x9e3779b1) + Math.imul((b >>> 0) ^ 0x85ebca6b, 0xc2b2ae35)) >>> 0;
  h ^= h >>> 16; h = Math.imul(h, 0x85ebca6b) >>> 0;
  h ^= h >>> 13; h = Math.imul(h, 0xc2b2ae35) >>> 0;
  h ^= h >>> 16;
  return h >>> 0;
}

export function mean(values) {
  if (!values.length) return null;
  let sum = 0;
  for (const v of values) sum += v;
  return sum / values.length;
}

// Population standard deviation (divide by n).
export function sd(values) {
  const m = mean(values);
  if (m === null) return null;
  let sum = 0;
  for (const v of values) sum += (v - m) * (v - m);
  return Math.sqrt(sum / values.length);
}

// Quantile with linear interpolation between the two nearest ranks
// (position (n - 1) * q in the sorted list).
export function quantile(values, q) {
  if (!values.length) return null;
  const sorted = [...values].sort((x, y) => x - y);
  const pos = (sorted.length - 1) * q;
  const lo = Math.floor(pos), hi = Math.ceil(pos);
  return sorted[lo] + (sorted[hi] - sorted[lo]) * (pos - lo);
}

export function median(values) {
  return quantile(values, 0.5);
}

// Pearson correlation of two equal-length lists; null when it is undefined
// (fewer than two pairs, or either list has no variance).
export function correlation(xs, ys) {
  const n = Math.min(xs.length, ys.length);
  if (n < 2) return null;
  const mx = mean(xs.slice(0, n)), my = mean(ys.slice(0, n));
  let sxy = 0, sxx = 0, syy = 0;
  for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) {
    const dx = xs[i] - mx, dy = ys[i] - my;
    sxy += dx * dy; sxx += dx * dx; syy += dy * dy;
  }
  if (sxx === 0 || syy === 0) return null;
  return sxy / Math.sqrt(sxx * syy);
}

`courses/anti-cheat-engineering-part-two/public/store.mjs`:

```mjs
// public/store.mjs (unit 16, supplied): a durable key-value store that can crash between writes.
//
// The game keeps every player's belongings in a store:
//   inv:<player>     a list of item ids, e.g. ['sword', 'lamp']
//   coins:<player>   a whole number
// Each put is durable the moment it returns: a crash never loses a finished put and never
// applies half of one. But nothing is bigger than one put. There is no transaction that
// covers two keys, so if the server dies between the put that gives the buyer the item
// and the put that takes it from the seller, both writes that happened stay happened.
//
// To test code against that, the store can crash on purpose:
//   crashAfter(n)  the n-th put from now is applied and then throws a Crash, as if the
//                  server died the moment that write reached the disk. Every later put
//                  throws Crash too, until restart().
//   restart()      the server starts again: puts work again and the crash is disarmed.
// Reads keep working throughout: the data is on disk; it is the server that stopped.
//
// Values are copied in and out as JSON, so changing an array you got from get() never
// changes the store.
//
// naiveTrade() at the bottom is a trade as it is often first written: four puts in a
// row. Crash it after any of its puts and look at what is left.

export class Crash extends Error {
  constructor(write) {
    super(`crash: the server stopped after write ${write}`);
    this.name = 'Crash';
  }
}

const copy = (value) => JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(value));

/**
 * createStore(initial) -> { get, put, keys, crashAfter, restart, writes, snapshot }
 *   initial      an object of key -> value, e.g. { 'inv:ana': ['sword'], 'coins:ana': 20 }
 *   get(key)     a copy of the value, or undefined when the key is absent
 *   put(key, v)  stores a copy of v; durable at once
 *   keys(prefix) the keys starting with prefix, sorted
 *   writes       how many puts have been applied since the store was made
 *   snapshot()   a copy of everything, as an object with sorted keys
 */
export function createStore(initial = {}) {
  const data = new Map();
  for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(initial)) data.set(key, copy(value));
  let writes = 0;
  let left = null;       // puts until the armed crash, or null
  let down = false;      // true from a crash until restart()

  function keys(prefix = '') {
    return [...data.keys()].filter((key) => key.startsWith(prefix)).sort();
  }

  return {
    get(key) {
      return data.has(key) ? copy(data.get(key)) : undefined;
    },
    put(key, value) {
      if (typeof key !== 'string' || key === '') throw new TypeError('put needs a key: a non-empty string');
      if (value === undefined) throw new TypeError(`put(${JSON.stringify(key)}) needs a value; undefined cannot be stored`);
      if (down) throw new Crash(writes);
      data.set(key, copy(value));
      writes += 1;
      if (left !== null) {
        left -= 1;
        if (left === 0) {
          left = null;
          down = true;
          throw new Crash(writes);
        }
      }
    },
    keys,
    crashAfter(n) {
      if (!Number.isInteger(n) || n < 1) throw new RangeError('crashAfter needs a whole number, 1 or more');
      left = n;
    },
    restart() {
      left = null;
      down = false;
    },
    get writes() {
      return writes;
    },
    snapshot() {
      return Object.fromEntries(keys().map((key) => [key, copy(data.get(key))]));
    },
  };
}

/**
 * The trade most code starts with: check, then four puts in order. No journal and no
 * request key (a `key` in the request is ignored), so the store cannot tell a retry
 * from a new trade, and nothing records a trade that stopped halfway.
 *   request: { seller, buyer, item, price }
 * Returns { ok: true } or { ok: false, reason: 'missing' | 'funds' }.
 */
export function naiveTrade(store, { seller, buyer, item, price }) {
  const sellerItems = store.get(`inv:${seller}`) ?? [];
  const buyerItems = store.get(`inv:${buyer}`) ?? [];
  const sellerCoins = store.get(`coins:${seller}`) ?? 0;
  const buyerCoins = store.get(`coins:${buyer}`) ?? 0;
  if (!sellerItems.includes(item)) return { ok: false, reason: 'missing' };
  if (buyerCoins < price) return { ok: false, reason: 'funds' };
  store.put(`inv:${buyer}`, [...buyerItems, item]);                      // 1. the buyer gets the item
  store.put(`inv:${seller}`, sellerItems.filter((id) => id !== item));   // 2. the seller loses it
  store.put(`coins:${buyer}`, buyerCoins - price);                        // 3. the buyer pays
  store.put(`coins:${seller}`, sellerCoins + price);                      // 4. the seller is paid
  return { ok: true };
}

`courses/anti-cheat-engineering-part-two/reader/code-example.mjs`:

```mjs
// Portable, dependency-free presentation for authored JavaScript/Python examples.
// This is lexical coloring, not a parser or a correctness check.
const escape = value => String(value).replace(/[&<>"']/g, c => ({'&':'&amp;','<':'&lt;','>':'&gt;','"':'&quot;',"'":'&#39;'}[c]));
const keywords = new Set(('async await const let var function return throw new if else for of in try catch finally import from export class true false null undefined def return raise if else elif for in try except finally import from as True False None and or not is with').split(' '));
function color(line, language) {
  if (!['js','javascript','python','py'].includes(language)) return escape(line);
  const pattern = language === 'python' || language === 'py'
    ? /#[^\n]*|"(?:\\.|[^"\\])*"|'(?:\\.|[^'\\])*'|\b(?:0x[\da-fA-F]+|\d+(?:\.\d+)?)\b|\b[A-Za-z_]\w*\b/g
    : /\/\/[^\n]*|"(?:\\.|[^"\\])*"|'(?:\\.|[^'\\])*'|`(?:\\.|[^`\\])*`|\b(?:0x[\da-fA-F]+|\d+(?:\.\d+)?)\b|\b[A-Za-z_$][\w$]*\b/g;
  let result = '', end = 0;
  for (const match of line.matchAll(pattern)) {
    result += escape(line.slice(end, match.index));
    const token = match[0];
    const kind = /^(#|\/\/)/.test(token) ? 'comment' : /^["'`]/.test(token) ? 'string'
      : /^\d/.test(token) ? 'number' : keywords.has(token) ? 'keyword' : null;
    result += kind ? `<span class="cex-${kind}">${escape(token)}</span>` : escape(token);
    end = match.index + token.length;
  }
  return result + escape(line.slice(end));
}
export function renderCode(source, info = '') {
  const match = info.trim().match(/^(\S+)?(?:\s+(\{.*\}))?$/);
  if (!match) throw Error('Invalid code fence metadata');
  const language = match[1] || 'text';
  const meta = match[2] ? JSON.parse(match[2]) : {};
  if (!meta || Array.isArray(meta) || typeof meta !== 'object') throw Error('Code metadata must be an object');
  for (const name of ['file','region','title','change']) {
    if (meta[name] !== undefined && typeof meta[name] !== 'string') throw Error(`Invalid code ${name}`);
  }
  const lines = source.split('\n'), focus = meta.focus || [];
  if (!Array.isArray(focus) || focus.some(n => !Number.isInteger(n) || n < 1 || n > lines.length)) throw Error('Code emphasis must name existing lines');
  const label = meta.title || ({sh:'Terminal command',text:'Observed output',js:'JavaScript',python:'Python'})[language] || language;
  const location = meta.file ? `<span class="cex-location">${escape(meta.file)}${meta.region ? ` · ${escape(meta.region)}` : ''}</span>` : '';
  const change = meta.change ? `<p class="cex-change">${escape(meta.change)}</p>` : '';
  const emphasis = focus.length ? `<span class="cex-emphasis">Emphasized lines: ${focus.join(', ')}.</span>` : '';
  const code = lines.map((line, i) => `<span class="cex-line${focus.includes(i+1) ? ' cex-focus' : ''}">${color(line, language)}</span>`).join('\n');
  return `<figure class="code-example"><figcaption><strong>${escape(label)}</strong>${location}</figcaption>${change}<pre tabindex="0" aria-label="${escape(label)}; code scrolls horizontally when needed"><code>${code}</code></pre><div class="cex-foot">${emphasis} Select code to copy. Scroll horizontally if needed.</div></figure>`;
}

`courses/anti-cheat-engineering-part-two/walkthrough/server/recorder.mjs`:

```mjs
// Unit 12, write route: server/recorder.mjs with the walked-through regions left to fill.
// Lesson 12 shows each region's code and says why it is there. Replace everything between
// a "// region: NAME" line and its "// endregion: NAME" line with that listing, in the
// lesson's order: recorder, in-order, replay-run, replay-final. Keep the marker lines.
// The rest (the import, the key lists, the shape test wellShaped and its two helpers) is
// supplied. API.md, "The record" and "replay", has the format and the reasons.
import { createLobSession } from '../../public/session.mjs';

const RECORD_KEYS = ['end', 'final', 'game', 'inputs', 'mode', 'seed', 'v'];
const INPUT_KEYS = ['angle', 'fire', 'n', 'power', 'seq', 'tick'];
const FINAL_KEYS = ['angle', 'power', 'round', 'score', 'shots'];

// region: recorder
export function createRecorder({ seed, mode }) {
  throw new Error('createRecorder: not written yet');
}
// endregion: recorder

export function replay(record, admission) {
  if (!wellShaped(record)) return { ok: false, reason: 'shape' };
  // region: replay-run
  throw new Error('replay: not written yet');
  // endregion: replay-run
  // region: replay-final
  throw new Error('replay: the final comparison is not written yet');
  // endregion: replay-final
}

// region: in-order
function inOrder({ inputs, end }) {
  throw new Error('inOrder: not written yet');
}
// endregion: in-order

// The record's shape: every field present, nothing extra, each of its type.
function wellShaped(record) {
  if (!isPlainObject(record) || !hasExactly(record, RECORD_KEYS)) return false;
  if (record.v !== 1 || record.game !== 'lob' || record.mode !== 9)
    return false;
  if (
    !Number.isSafeInteger(record.seed) ||
    record.seed < 0 ||
    record.seed > 0xffffffff
  )
    return false;
  if (!Number.isSafeInteger(record.end) || record.end < 0) return false;
  if (!isPlainObject(record.final) || !hasExactly(record.final, FINAL_KEYS))
    return false;
  if (!FINAL_KEYS.every((key) => Number.isSafeInteger(record.final[key])))
    return false;
  if (!Array.isArray(record.inputs)) return false;
  return record.inputs.every(
    (input) =>
      isPlainObject(input) &&
      hasExactly(input, INPUT_KEYS) &&
      Number.isSafeInteger(input.n) &&
      Number.isSafeInteger(input.tick) &&
      input.tick >= 0 &&
      typeof input.seq === 'number' &&
      typeof input.angle === 'number' &&
      typeof input.power === 'number' &&
      typeof input.fire === 'boolean',
  );
}

function isPlainObject(value) {
  return value !== null && typeof value === 'object' && !Array.isArray(value);
}

function hasExactly(object, keys) {
  const own = Object.keys(object).sort();
  return own.length === keys.length && own.every((key, i) => key === keys[i]);
}

// Unit 16, new application: a swap of one item for another, with no coins. Lesson 16, "Use
// the idea on a new case", gives the task; examples/check-swap.mjs checks it. No finished
// swap is supplied.
//
// swap(store, request) -> { ok: true, receipt } or { ok: false, reason }
//   request: { key, a, b, itemA, itemB }: player a gives itemA to player b, and b gives
//   itemB to a. The checks send only well-formed requests.
//   receipt: { key, a, b, itemA, itemB }
//   reason, checked in this order:
//     'self'      a === b
//     'conflict'  a swap under the same key was carried out with a different body
//     'missing'   a does not hold itemA, or b does not hold itemB
//   A request whose key was already carried out with the same body returns the same
//   receipt and writes nothing. A refusal writes nothing. The store may crash after any put.
// recoverSwaps(store) -> the keys of the swaps it finished, sorted
//   Runs when the server restarts after a crash, and may itself crash after any put and be
//   run again. Keep swaps under journal keys of their own, such as swap:<key>.

`courses/anti-cheat-engineering-part-two/walkthrough/trade/trade.mjs`:

```mjs
// Unit 16, write route: trade/trade.mjs with the walked-through regions left to fill.
// Lesson 16 shows each region's code and says why it is there. Replace everything between
// a "// region: NAME" line and its "// endregion: NAME" line with that listing, in the
// lesson's order: finish, recover, trade-key, then trade-journal. Keep the marker lines.
// wellFormed and its two constants are supplied. API.md, unit 16, has the exact rules.

const NAME = /^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,40}$/;
const FIELDS = ['buyer', 'item', 'key', 'price', 'seller'];

function wellFormed(request) {
  if (!request || typeof request !== 'object' || Array.isArray(request))
    return false;
  const keys = Object.keys(request).sort();
  if (
    keys.length !== FIELDS.length ||
    keys.some((key, index) => key !== FIELDS[index])
  )
    return false;
  const names = [request.key, request.seller, request.buyer, request.item];
  return (
    names.every((value) => typeof value === 'string' && NAME.test(value)) &&
    Number.isSafeInteger(request.price) &&
    request.price >= 0
  );
}

// region: finish
function finish(store, key, entry) {
  throw new Error('finish: not written yet');
}

  throw new Error('recover: not written yet');

  // endregion: trade-journal
}

# Anti-cheat Engineering — Courier Lab

Build defensive server-owned rules for an original toy game: authority and
proximity, ordered inputs, independent tests, timing, integrity, replay,
detector evaluation, retention, compatible recovery and a new-mechanic capstone.
This is an educational beta, not production anti-cheat or a security guarantee.

## Clone and start

Use Node.js 22 or later and npm (included with Node). No dependency installation,
account, API key, paid service or private repository access is needed.

```sh
git clone https://github.com/itsHabib/free-to-learn.git
cd free-to-learn
git rev-parse HEAD
cd courses/anti-cheat-engineering/courier-lab
node --version
npm start
```

Open the complete loopback `/learn` URL printed by the server and keep that
terminal open. `/course` links the guided lessons to the source exercises.
Stop with Ctrl-C. Keep the listener on loopback; do not expose it publicly.
The original web introduction remains at
https://freetolearn.world/courses/anti-cheat-engineering/ and the original ZIP
remains at https://freetolearn.world/courses/anti-cheat-engineering/courier-lab.zip.
This Git edition preserves all 228 project files from that published ZIP.

## Make your own source project

From `courier-lab`, use another terminal while taking the guided lessons:

```sh
npm run lab:prepare
npm run order:prepare
npm run core:prepare -- timing --name first
```

Each command prints its new workspace and exact next command. Existing
workspaces are refused, not overwritten. M1 is the proximity guard; M2/M3 share
the ordering workspace. Read the generated `LEARNER.md`, keep each prediction
question unchanged, fill either an answer or an explicit skip reason in
`predictions.json`, edit the learner source and record your explanation/help.
For example, inside the printed timing workspace:

```sh
npm run core:check -- --assistance "describe the help you actually used"
```

Untouched templates are intentionally incomplete. Blank prediction drafts are
refused before grading; that is different from a failed implementation. Revise
in the same workspace to retain first failures and later feedback. Do not copy
worked solutions and describe them as your own unassisted work.

Follow `courier-lab/README.md` for all ten software modules (M1–M7, M9–M11)
and their exact preparation/check commands. M8 native work is optional/excluded.
The final capstone requires your own policy and independent HTTP scenario.
The `author/`, `controls.mjs`, reference policies and labelled examples inside
this published teaching project are intentional public grader/calibration and
worked-example material. They are not private learner submissions or a new
blind-test fixture. They stay outside generated learner workspaces; consulting
them is assistance to disclose.

## Safe offline checks and the HTTP route

These public deterministic checks need no listener or package installation:

```sh
node --test tests/admission.test.mjs tests/clock.test.mjs tests/engine.test.mjs tests/timing.test.mjs tests/recovery.test.mjs

They check the supplied runtime and labelled controls, not your completion of

the course. Repository CI deliberately runs only the safe offline/setup
contract. Complete HTTP/browser learner execution was not rerun for this Git
publication because the validation environment has a retained listener

## Save and recover your work

A Git clone contains starters, not your generated work. Stop the local server
and all checks, keep the original clone, and back up the whole course directory
including hidden files and `courier-lab/artifacts`. From the repository root,
use a NEW archive name in a location you own:

```sh
tar -cf /absolute/path/to/new-courier-backup.tar courses/anti-cheat-engineering
tar -tf /absolute/path/to/new-courier-backup.tar
```

Keep that archive and a separate copy. Do not overwrite your only backup or
extract over existing work. Prepared sessions contain absolute paths to their
trusted reference and history: an unchanged full-session restore must retain
its original absolute location. Moving only a workspace or replacing its
session metadata does not migrate history.

For another machine/location, retain the complete original backup as evidence,
clone again and prepare a NEW named workspace. Copy your own policy/scenario
and explanation into that workspace, complete its exact prediction draft, and
declare prior work/help when checking. It is a new attempt; do not claim the
old session or first-response status moved. The old backup/history remains
readable and unchanged. Browser notebook export/import is separate and belongs
to the original loopback origin. Export it before clearing that origin's data.
See the original README for interrupted-check maintenance; never remove locks
or evidence to force a check through.

`courses/anti-cheat-engineering/courier-lab/admission.mjs`:

```mjs
/** Already-parsed inputs may update intent, never actor identity or game results. */
export function admitInput(state, input, tick) {
  if (input.seq <= state.lastSeq) return { status: 'stale', next: state };
  return {
    status: 'admitted',
    next: {
      lastSeq: input.seq,
      lastSeen: tick,
      expiresAt: tick + 4,
      move: input.move,
      pendingInteract: state.pendingInteract || input.interact,
    },
  };
}

/** The admission tick precedes movement; ticks T+1 through T+4 may move. */
export function movementActive(state, tick) {
  return tick <= state.expiresAt;
}

`courses/anti-cheat-engineering/courier-lab/author/order/adequate-scenario.mjs`:

```mjs
// Author calibration only. Never copied into a learner workspace.
import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
import { join, input, state } from '../../clients/http-client.mjs';

export async function scenario({ base, advance }) {
  const expiring = await join(base);
  await input(base, expiring.token, 10, 'E');
  await advance(3);
  assert.equal((await state(base, expiring.token)).actor.x, 1750, 'three admitted movement ticks');
  await advance(1);
  assert.equal((await state(base, expiring.token)).actor.x, 2000, 'fourth inclusive movement tick');
  await advance(1);
  assert.equal((await state(base, expiring.token)).actor.x, 2000, 'polling must not renew expired intent');

  const ordered = await join(base);
  await input(base, ordered.token, 20, 'E');
  await input(base, ordered.token, 20, 'W', true);
  await advance(1);
  let seen = await state(base, ordered.token);
  assert.equal(seen.actor.x, 1250, 'equal sequence cannot overwrite movement');
  assert.equal(seen.lastDecision, null, 'equal sequence cannot stage interaction');
  await input(base, ordered.token, 19, 'W', true);
  await advance(1);
  seen = await state(base, ordered.token);
  assert.equal(seen.actor.x, 1500, 'older sequence cannot overwrite movement');
  assert.equal(seen.lastDecision, null, 'older sequence cannot stage interaction');
  await input(base, ordered.token, 18, 'idle', true);
  await advance(1);
  await input(base, ordered.token, 17, 'idle', true);
  await advance(1);
  seen = await state(base, ordered.token);
  assert.deepEqual(seen.findings, [], 'stale retries must not become detector observations');
  assert.equal(seen.actor.lastSeq, 20, 'stale requests preserve the admitted sequence');
}

import { withServer } from '../../tests/harness.mjs';
import { DELIVERY_SCHEDULES, runDeliverySchedule } from '../../clients/schedules.mjs';

export async function componentFixtures(root, seed) {
  const results = [];
  async function criterion(name, exercise) {
    try { const evidence = await exercise(); results.push({ name, passed: true, evidence }); }
    catch (error) { results.push({ name, passed: false, failureKind: error instanceof assert.AssertionError ? 'assertion' : 'runner-failure', trace: error.trace, error: { name: error.name, code: error.code, message: error.message, actual: error.actual, expected: error.expected, stack: error.stack } }); }
  }
  await criterion('pure admission contract', async () => {
    const { admitInput, movementActive } = await import(pathToFileURL(join(root, 'admission.mjs')));
    const before = Object.freeze({ lastSeq: 20, lastSeen: 7, expiresAt: 11, move: 'N', pendingInteract: true });
    const input = Object.freeze({ v: 1, seq: 21, move: 'E', interact: false });
    const next = { lastSeq: 21, lastSeen: 9, expiresAt: 13, move: 'E', pendingInteract: true };
    assert.deepEqual(admitInput(before, input, 9), { status: 'admitted', next });
    for (const seq of [20, 19]) assert.deepEqual(admitInput(before, { ...input, seq, interact: true }, 9), { status: 'stale', next: before });
    assert.equal(movementActive(next, 13), true);
    assert.equal(movementActive(next, 14), false);
    assert.equal(movementActive({ lastSeq: 0, lastSeen: 0, expiresAt: 0, move: 'idle', pendingInteract: false }, 1), false);
    return { next, activeThrough: 13, inactiveAt: 14 };
  });
  for (const name of DELIVERY_SCHEDULES) {
    await criterion(name, () => withServer(async (server) => {
      try {
        const result = await runDeliverySchedule(server, name, { seed });
        return { ...result, trace: await server.record() };
      } catch (error) {
        error.trace = await server.record();
        throw error;
      }
    }, { seed, entry: join(root, 'server.mjs') }));
  }
  return results;
}

`courses/anti-cheat-engineering/courier-lab/author/order/variants.mjs`:

```mjs
export const CORRECT_VARIANTS = ['baseline', 'alternate-correct'];
export const WRONG_VARIANTS = ['equal-seq-admitted', 'stale-admitted', 'stale-interact', 'expiry-T+3', 'expiry-T+5', 'read-renews', 'stale-finding'];

const alternate = `// Independent elapsed-time implementation; public expiry is still part of the contract.
export function admitInput(state, input, tick) {
  if (!(input.seq > state.lastSeq)) return { status: 'stale', next: { ...state } };
  const next = Object.assign({}, state);
  Object.assign(next, { move: input.move, lastSeen: tick, lastSeq: input.seq, expiresAt: tick + 4 });
  next.pendingInteract = Boolean(state.pendingInteract || input.interact);
  return { status: 'admitted', next };
}
export function movementActive(state, tick) {
  return state.lastSeq > 0 && tick - state.lastSeen <= 4;
}
`;

function wrapper(body) {
  return `import { admitInput as original, movementActive } from './reference-admission.mjs';\nexport { movementActive };\nexport function admitInput(state, input, tick) {\n${body}\n}\n`;
}

function inject(source, marker, code) {
  if (source.split(marker).length !== 2) throw new Error(`Expected one runtime marker: ${marker}`);
  return source.replace(marker, marker + '\n' + code);
}

/** These mutations exist only in owner-side runtime copies, never server flags. */
export function variantFiles(variant, referencePolicy, referenceEngine) {
  let policy = referencePolicy;
  let engine = referenceEngine;
  if (variant === 'alternate-correct') policy = alternate;
  if (variant === 'equal-seq-admitted') policy = wrapper(`  if (input.seq === state.lastSeq) return original({ ...state, lastSeq: input.seq - 1 }, input, tick);
  return original(state, input, tick);`);
  if (variant === 'stale-admitted') policy = wrapper(`  if (input.seq < state.lastSeq) return original({ ...state, lastSeq: input.seq - 1 }, input, tick);
  return original(state, input, tick);`);
  if (variant === 'stale-interact') policy = wrapper(`  const result = original(state, input, tick);
  if (result.status === 'stale') return { ...result, next: { ...result.next, pendingInteract: state.pendingInteract || input.interact } };
  return result;`);
  if (variant === 'expiry-T+3' || variant === 'expiry-T+5') policy = wrapper(`  const result = original(state, input, tick);
  if (result.status === 'admitted') result.next.expiresAt += ${variant === 'expiry-T+3' ? '-1' : '1'};
  return result;`);
  if (variant === 'read-renews') engine = inject(engine, '// ORDER_LAB_STATE_READ', '  actor.expiresAt = world.tick + 4;');
  if (variant === 'stale-finding') engine = inject(engine, '// ORDER_LAB_ADMISSION_RESULT', "  if (result.status === 'stale') observeDenial(actor.detector, world.tick, 'range', 250001);");
  if (![...CORRECT_VARIANTS, ...WRONG_VARIANTS, 'submitted-component'].includes(variant)) throw new Error(`Unknown assessment variant: ${variant}`);
  return { 'admission.mjs': Buffer.from(policy), 'engine.mjs': Buffer.from(engine), 'reference-admission.mjs': Buffer.from(referencePolicy) };
}

`courses/anti-cheat-engineering/courier-lab/author/order/worker.mjs`:

```mjs
import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
import { pathToFileURL } from 'node:url';
import { basename, join } from 'node:path';
import { startServer } from '../../tests/harness.mjs';
import { request } from '../../clients/http-client.mjs';
import { componentFixtures } from './component-fixtures.mjs';

export function assertionEvidence(error) {
  // Value types cannot establish provenance. The full runtime calibration
  // determines whether a scenario distinguishes correct and incorrect behavior.
  return error instanceof assert.AssertionError && Object.hasOwn(error, 'actual') && Object.hasOwn(error, 'expected');
}

function errorRecord(error) {
  return { name: error.name, code: error.code, message: error.message, actual: error.actual, expected: error.expected, operator: error.operator, stack: error.stack };
}

async function runScenario(seed) {
  const server = await startServer({ seed, entry: join(process.cwd(), 'server.mjs') });
  let error;
  let trace;
  let healthy = false;
  let ticks = 0;
  try {
    const { scenario } = await import(pathToFileURL(join(process.cwd(), 'learner-scenario.mjs')));
    if (typeof scenario !== 'function') throw new Error('learner-scenario.mjs must export async scenario({base, advance}).');
    await scenario({
      base: server.base,
      advance: async (count) => {
        if (!Number.isSafeInteger(count) || count < 1 || count > 100 || ticks + count > 400) throw new Error('Scenario advance budget is 400 ticks, in calls of 1–100.');
        ticks += count;
        return server.advance(count);
      },
    });
  } catch (caught) { error = caught; }
  try {
    const health = await request(server.base, '/health');
    trace = await server.record();
    healthy = health.status === 200 && health.data?.ok === true && trace.dropped === 0;
  } catch (caught) { error = caught; }
  try {
    const exit = await server.stop();
    if (exit.code !== 0) throw new Error(`Runtime exited with ${exit.code ?? exit.signal}.`);
  } catch (caught) { healthy = false; error = caught; }
  const kind = healthy && !error ? 'pass' : healthy && assertionEvidence(error) ? 'assertion' : 'runner-failure';
  return { kind, healthy, ticks, error: error && errorRecord(error), trace, diagnostics: server.diagnostics() };
}

async function main() {
  const [mode, seedValue] = process.argv.slice(2);
  const seed = Number(seedValue);
  if (!Number.isSafeInteger(seed)) throw new Error('Worker needs an integer seed.');
  if (mode === 'scenario') return runScenario(seed);
  if (mode !== 'component') throw new Error('Unknown worker mode.');
  const criteria = await componentFixtures(process.cwd(), seed);
  if (criteria.every((item) => item.passed)) return { kind: 'pass', criteria };
  return { kind: criteria.some((item) => item.failureKind === 'runner-failure') ? 'runner-failure' : 'component-failure', criteria };
}

// Importing assertionEvidence for tests must not launch a worker.
if (basename(process.argv[1] ?? '') === 'worker.mjs' && typeof process.send === 'function') {
  main().then((result) => process.send({ type: 'result', result }, () => process.disconnect())).catch((error) => {
    process.send({ type: 'result', result: { kind: 'runner-failure', healthy: false, error: errorRecord(error) } }, () => process.disconnect());
  });
}

# M11: Build a repair-station rule and test its boundary

Implementation reference for **M11: capstone**. Start with [the guided learning route at `/learn`](/learn) on the reference server, then return here for the exact source contract. This Markdown file does not submit answers or certify mastery. Use the [support and attempt workflow](../learning-support/README.md) for worked siblings, gradual guidance and help recording. A prepared source workspace need not serve `/learn`; keep the reference server open for that route.

A repair station spends credits to restore energy. A retry must not buy the same repair twice, and a nearby client must not be able to choose its own price or position. Build the rule from server state, then write a separate HTTP scenario that can find incorrect implementations.

Your deliverables are `capstone/policy.mjs`, `capstone/scenario.mjs` and your reasoning in `response.md`. This capstone assumes the earlier request-order, authority and bounded-evidence work, plus JavaScript functions, objects, arrays and assertions. The code runs only against the owned local arena.

## Policy contract

Run `npm run core:prepare -- capstone` from the reference project, then enter the printed workspace. The final source files provide exported interfaces with TODO bodies; implement both from this contract after the guided practice. The checker captures both files, the original question, your response and assistance. Keep first answers and failed attempts; append changes instead of replacing the earlier account.

The policy exports `repair(state, actorId, request)`. Inputs are validated. The request has exactly `{requestId,stationId}`. The server resolves `actorId` from its session token. The state owns configuration, stations and actors:

```js
{
  config: { repairCost: 2, repairEnergy: 3, energyCap: 10, rangeMm: 400, receiptLimit: 2 },
  stations: [{ id: 'alpha', x: 0, y: 0 }, { id: 'beta', x: 2000, y: 0 }],
  actors: [{ id: 'actor-1', x: 0, y: 0, energy: 4, credits: 6, receipts: [] }]
}
```

Positions are integer millimetres. The actor is already present. Return `{reason,receipt,state}` with a fresh state and unchanged input objects. Failed operations use `receipt:null`. You do not need another parser inside the policy. HTTP validation remains in the supplied server.

Before implementing or running a scenario, record the required first answers or explicit skip reasons in `predictions.json`, with explanations in `response.md`. Use the rules below to predict retries, exact range boundaries, failed IDs and receipt capacity. These explanations are preserved for review rather than automatically graded.

## Request identity

A **receipt** records one successful resource change. It has exactly `{requestId,stationId,energyAdded,creditsSpent,energy,credits}`. Its balances describe that successful operation, even if later operations change the actor's current balances.

Look for the request ID in this actor's receipts before making a new decision. If the stored station differs, return `conflict` and change nothing. If the station matches, return `duplicate` with the original receipt and the current state. The actor may have moved since success; a retry acknowledges the earlier repair and performs no new repair. Rechecking distance before finding the receipt can incorrectly refuse that acknowledgment.

The ID belongs to the actor's session, not to the whole arena. Another actor can use the same ID for its own operation. IDs are opaque labels; their spelling or ordering does not compute balances. No timestamp or counter decides what a repair costs.

## One resource transaction

For a new ID, apply these checks in order:

| Check | Failure reason |
| --- | --- |
| The station exists | `station` |
| The actor has room for another receipt | `history-full` |
| `(actor.x-station.x)² + (actor.y-station.y)² <= 400²` | `range` |
| Energy is below 10 | `full` |
| Credits are at least 2 | `funds` |

On success, subtract 2 credits, add the smaller of 3 and the space below energy 10, append one receipt, and return `repaired`. These changes form one **transaction**: either all happen or none happen. Do not debit credits before a later check can fail. The complete state comes from the server; a body claiming a different energy, position, price or score is not another source of truth.

For a sibling example, consider a storage service that spends one token to add up to four units, with a capacity of twelve. If it already holds eleven units, the successful operation adds one unit while still spending one token. The receipt records the actual one-unit change. Apply the repair contract's own values when implementing this arena.

## Failed requests

A failed request changes neither balances nor receipt history. The same request ID may later succeed after the actor moves into range or another relevant state changes. Reserving an ID on a failed operation turns a temporary refusal into a permanent one and makes a later retry look like a success that never occurred.

Your pure policy fixtures also include validated states near the energy cap and below the required credits. They test decisions beyond the default session's initial state. An HTTP-only scenario starting at energy 4 cannot by itself establish every possible state transition.

## Bounded receipts

Each actor can retain two successful receipts in this exercise. Once that list is full, a new ID returns `history-full`, before range, energy or funds checks. Existing IDs still resolve normally. Keep the old receipts; evicting one and accepting its ID later would let the same operation be charged again.

This limit is an explicit session boundary. The lab does not invent a safe distributed retry horizon or claim durable storage across crashes. A different system would need a defined session lifecycle and persistence policy. Deleting a learner's original attempt or silently replacing a receipt is not a solution to the bound.

## Independent HTTP tests

Use [the receipt companion](../learning-support/capstone-receipts.md) first if a retry, a receipt and current state are still difficult to keep separate. It works a different storage-locker transaction and then removes steps. [The HTTP companion](../learning-support/http-tests.md) teaches request, observation and assertion construction. Neither contains the assigned repair implementation or its completed HTTP scenario.

Write `async scenario({base,moveActor})` in `capstone/scenario.mjs`. Import `node:assert/strict` and the supplied `./client.mjs`. Native `node:assert` imports and callable `assert(condition)` also work; the runner does not patch assertions, received JSON or `structuredClone`. The helper exports:

| Helper | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `session(base)` | New `{id,token}` from POST `/session` |
| `state(base,token)` | Current server state from GET `/state` |
| `submit(base,token,body)` | `{status,data}` from POST `/repair` |
| `request(base,path,{method,token,json})` | Raw `{status,data}` for boundary tests |

Rule decisions use HTTP 200, including refusals, with `{reason,receipt,state}`. A repair body with extra fields is HTTP 400 and changes no state. A missing or unknown session token is HTTP 401. Both authenticated endpoints derive actor identity from that token. Tokens remain local transport details and must not be copied into your written report.

`moveActor(id,{x,y})` is an owner test control provided directly to your scenario. It is not an HTTP route and cannot alter balances or receipts. Use integer coordinates from -10000 to 10000. Each fresh run allows at most eight sessions and 256 HTTP requests. Use assertions that compare actual state with expected state. Seeing `range` alone does not show that a failed request left credits unchanged.

Each completed successful run must submit a repair and read state. A genuine assertion on a wrong HTTP response may stop that run before its next state read. Compare actual energy, credits, receipt contents and state after a refusal with expected values; methods such as `equal` and `deepEqual` help. Use the supplied HTTP helper directly or from your own captured helper module. The runner checks HTTP participation, then tests whether your complete scenario distinguishes the correct implementations from each named defect. It does not infer which fields an arbitrary assertion compared. A status-only scenario misses the energy-only, receipt-content and refusal-side-effect controls. A single successful run establishes participation, not the quality of your test suite.

The captured scenario runs once against your captured policy, then against two correct implementations and thirteen plausible mistakes: charging a duplicate again; checking range before receipts; ignoring station conflicts; reserving failed IDs; excluding the exact distance edge; charging one credit; adding only two energy; recording the wrong energy in a receipt; debiting a credit on a range refusal; evicting old receipts; ignoring vertical distance; sharing request IDs across actors; and accepting client resource claims. Every run uses a fresh process and imports the scenario and its helpers anew. Module counters do not carry across variants. An assertion must fail on every wrong variant and pass on both correct controls and your submitted policy. A missing import, connection error, arbitrary exception, forged assertion error code or timeout does not detect a defect. Plain JSON and normal assertion behavior are preserved, including copied expected state and in-place sorting. Failure may stop at the first assertion: checking credits before receipts is valid. This finite behavioral panel does not prove arbitrary test correctness or stop a machine owner from tampering with the runner. Each run has a one-second limit; the panel has an absolute eight-second budget that stops and reaps an active worker. Timeouts or exhausted runner budgets are reported as runner failures, never as detected defects. This means the check did not finish; learner code can cause it. Completed criteria and earlier scenario diagnostics remain in the saved result under `error.input`. The first 4096 bytes of scenario output are retained for diagnosis. These are teaching-runner resource limits, not claims about production performance.

The checker supplies no completed HTTP test to your workspace. Decide which observations separate these implementations and write your own requests and assertions. The policy and scenario are judged separately: a passing policy cannot compensate for tests that never check state, and a sensitive scenario does not repair a wrong policy.

## Build in four checked milestones

| Milestone | Evidence to inspect before adding another concern |
| --- | --- |
| Represent one transaction | On paper, name the unchanged input, fresh output, selected actor and all fields one success changes. Use the locker sibling, complete its near-cap case, then use this contract's values independently. |
| Preserve identity and refusal | Trace an earlier success, a later success, then retry the earlier ID. Keep the old receipt alongside current balances. Also trace a failed ID that can later succeed; no failed operation appends a success receipt. |
| Implement the policy | Compare the first failed pure-policy criterion's input and expected/actual output. Fix its decision before revisiting later state differences. Check deep input preservation as well as balances. |
| Author independent HTTP evidence | For each named defect, identify a request sequence and an observed field that would differ. Execute through the supplied helpers, inspect current state, and use ordinary assertions. Both correct controls must pass before a failed wrong variant is meaningful. |

The first two are guided construction work. The final source files are an independent whole task: no helper here decides their branches for you. The checker preserves failed source attempts and reports the policy and scenario separately.

<details><summary>Hint 1 — distinguish a repeated operation from a new one</summary>

Ask whether a successful receipt already exists for this actor and ID before planning a new resource change. This is why retry identity is separate from current distance and balances.

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 2 — write a branch change set</summary>

For each refusal, write “no resource change; no new receipt.” For success, list the energy change, credit change and appended receipt together. Compare your assertions with those sets; checking only `reason` leaves side effects invisible.

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 3 — worked sibling, after a saved attempt</summary>

In the companion's locker example, `A` records 9 units and 4 tokens; `B` later leaves 12 units and 3 tokens. Retrying `A` returns the historical 9/4 receipt but keeps current state 12/3. This suggests two distinct assertions: one on the receipt, another on current resources. Record the viewed section as assistance, then construct your repair case independently.

</details>

The local adapter serializes each synchronous resource transaction, but this exercise does not establish production concurrency safety, remote identity assurance or measured learning. ## Transfer for review

A shared printer charges a quota when it accepts a job. A connection can drop after acceptance, the client can retry, and completed-job details can no longer be retained indefinitely.
