`courses/anti-cheat-engineering/courier-lab/defense.mjs`:

```mjs
const WINDOW_TICKS = 20;
const MAX_OBSERVATIONS = 128;
const MAX_FINDINGS = 128;
const RANGE_SQUARED = 62_500;
const DISTANT_SQUARED = 250_000;

/** Teaching policy: an interaction needs elapsed cooldown and server-known proximity. */
export function interactionDenial(actor, target, tick, { omitProximity = false } = {}) {
  if (tick < actor.nextInteractTick) return 'cooldown';
  const distanceSquared = (actor.x - target.x) ** 2 + (actor.y - target.y) ** 2;
  // LAB_PROXIMITY_GUARD
  if (distanceSquared > RANGE_SQUARED && !omitProximity) return 'range';
  return null;
}

export function createDetector() {
  return {
    buckets: Array.from({ length: WINDOW_TICKS }, () => ({ tick: -1, observations: [] })),
    findings: [],
  };
}

/** Retire observations even when no interaction takes place during a tick. */
export function expireObservations(detector, tick) {
  for (const bucket of detector.buckets) {
    if (bucket.tick > tick - WINDOW_TICKS) continue;
    bucket.tick = -1;
    bucket.observations.length = 0;
  }
}

/** Advisory only: three range denials farther than 500 mm within 20 ticks. */
export function observeDenial(detector, tick, reason, distanceSquared) {
  if (reason !== 'range' || !(distanceSquared > DISTANT_SQUARED)) return;
  expireObservations(detector, tick);
  const bucket = detector.buckets[tick % WINDOW_TICKS];
  if (bucket.tick !== tick) {
    bucket.tick = tick;
    bucket.observations.length = 0;
  }
  // The engine consumes at most one interaction per actor per tick. Keep the
  // detector bounded even if this helper is called repeatedly by an owner test.
  if (bucket.observations.length > 0) return;
  bucket.observations.push({ tick, reason });
  const count = detector.buckets.reduce((total, item) => total + item.observations.length, 0);
  if (count > MAX_OBSERVATIONS) throw new Error('detector observation bound exceeded');
  if (count < 3 || detector.findings.at(-1)?.tick === tick) return;
  detector.findings.push({ kind: 'repeated-invalid-action', tick });
  if (detector.findings.length > MAX_FINDINGS) detector.findings.shift();
}

```

`courses/anti-cheat-engineering/courier-lab/engine.mjs`:

```mjs
import { createDetector, expireObservations, interactionDenial, observeDenial } from './defense.mjs';
import { admitInput, movementActive } from './admission.mjs';

const VERSION = 1;
const MAX_ACTORS = 4;
const MAX_EVENTS = 4096;
const STEP = 250;
const DEPOT = Object.freeze({ x: 1000, y: 1000 });
const ARENA = Object.freeze({ width: 8000, height: 4000, wall: Object.freeze({ x: 4000, y: 0, width: 250, height: 2500 }) });
const DIRECTIONS = Object.freeze({ N: [0, -STEP], S: [0, STEP], E: [STEP, 0], W: [-STEP, 0], idle: [0, 0] });
const INPUT_KEYS = ['interact', 'move', 'seq', 'v'];
const MUTANTS = new Set(['omit-proximity', 'omit-sequence']);

function copy(value) {
  return JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(value));
}

function validInput(input) {
  if (!input || typeof input !== 'object' || Array.isArray(input)) return false;
  const keys = Object.keys(input).sort();
  if (keys.length !== INPUT_KEYS.length || keys.some((key, index) => key !== INPUT_KEYS[index])) return false;
  return input.v === 1 && Number.isSafeInteger(input.seq) && input.seq >= 1 && input.seq <= 1_000_000
    && typeof input.move === 'string' && Object.hasOwn(DIRECTIONS, input.move) && typeof input.interact === 'boolean';
}

function recordEvent(world, event) {
  world.history.push(event);
  if (world.history.length <= MAX_EVENTS) return;
  world.history.shift();
  world.dropped += 1;
}

function requireActor(world, id) {
  const actor = world.actors.find((candidate) => candidate.id === id);
  if (!actor) throw new Error(`unknown actor: ${id}`);
  return actor;
}

function admissionState(actor) {
  return {
    lastSeq: actor.lastSeq, lastSeen: actor.lastSeen, expiresAt: actor.expiresAt,
    move: actor.move, pendingInteract: actor.pendingInteract,
  };
}

/** An owner-only in-memory world. The runtime gates mutant selection before calling this. */
export function createWorld(seed, { mutant } = {}) {
  if (!Number.isSafeInteger(seed)) throw new Error('seed must be a safe integer');
  if (mutant !== undefined && !MUTANTS.has(mutant)) throw new Error('unknown mutant');
  const offset = ((seed % 3) + 3) % 3;
  return { seed, mutant, tick: 0, actors: [], core: { x: 2000 + offset * STEP, y: 1000 }, history: [], dropped: 0 };
}

export function join(world) {
  if (world.actors.length >= MAX_ACTORS) throw new Error('session limit reached');
  const actor = {
    id: `actor-${world.actors.length + 1}`, x: DEPOT.x, y: DEPOT.y,
    score: 0, cargo: false, lastSeq: 0, lastSeen: 0, expiresAt: 0,
    nextInteractTick: 0, move: 'idle', pendingInteract: false,
    lastDecision: null, detector: createDetector(),
  };
  world.actors.push(actor);
  recordEvent(world, { type: 'join', id: actor.id });
  return actor;
}

export function admit(world, id, input) {
  const actor = world.actors.find((candidate) => candidate.id === id);
  const seq = Number.isSafeInteger(input?.seq) ? input.seq : null;
  if (!actor) return { status: 'rejected', reason: 'unknown-actor', tick: world.tick, seq };
  if (!validInput(input)) return { status: 'rejected', reason: 'invalid-input', tick: world.tick, seq };
  recordEvent(world, { type: 'input', id, input: copy(input) });
  const policyState = admissionState(actor);
  if (world.mutant === 'omit-sequence') policyState.lastSeq = input.seq - 1;
  const result = admitInput(policyState, input, world.tick);
  // ORDER_LAB_ADMISSION_RESULT
  actor.lastSeq = result.next.lastSeq;
  actor.lastSeen = result.next.lastSeen;
  actor.expiresAt = result.next.expiresAt;
  actor.move = result.next.move;
  actor.pendingInteract = result.next.pendingInteract;
  const reason = result.status === 'stale' ? 'stale-sequence' : 'accepted';
  return { status: result.status, reason, tick: world.tick, seq: input.seq };
}

function intersectsWall(from, to) {
  const wall = ARENA.wall;
  const overlapsX = Math.max(from.x, to.x) >= wall.x && Math.min(from.x, to.x) <= wall.x + wall.width;
  const overlapsY = Math.max(from.y, to.y) >= wall.y && Math.min(from.y, to.y) <= wall.y + wall.height;
  return overlapsX && overlapsY;
}

function moveActor(world, actor) {
  if (!movementActive(admissionState(actor), world.tick)) return;
  const [dx, dy] = DIRECTIONS[actor.move];
  const target = { x: actor.x + dx, y: actor.y + dy };
  if (target.x < 0 || target.x > ARENA.width || target.y < 0 || target.y > ARENA.height) return;
  if (intersectsWall(actor, target)) return;
  actor.x = target.x;
  actor.y = target.y;
}

function interactionReason(world, actor) {
  const target = actor.cargo ? DEPOT : world.core;
  const denial = interactionDenial(actor, target, world.tick, { omitProximity: world.mutant === 'omit-proximity' });
  if (denial) return denial;
  return actor.cargo ? 'deposit' : 'pickup';
}

function interact(world, actor) {
  if (!actor.pendingInteract) return;
  actor.pendingInteract = false;
  const reason = interactionReason(world, actor);
  const applied = reason === 'pickup' || reason === 'deposit';
  actor.lastDecision = { status: applied ? 'applied' : 'denied', reason, tick: world.tick };
  if (!applied) {
    const target = actor.cargo ? DEPOT : world.core;
    const distanceSquared = (actor.x - target.x) ** 2 + (actor.y - target.y) ** 2;
    observeDenial(actor.detector, world.tick, reason, distanceSquared);
    return;
  }
  if (reason === 'deposit') actor.score += 1;
  actor.cargo = reason === 'pickup';
  actor.nextInteractTick = world.tick + 4;
}

export function advance(world, ticks) {
  if (!Number.isSafeInteger(ticks) || ticks < 1 || ticks > 100) throw new Error('ticks must be an integer from 1 to 100');
  for (let index = 0; index < ticks; index += 1) {
    world.tick += 1;
    for (const actor of world.actors) {
      expireObservations(actor.detector, world.tick);
      moveActor(world, actor);
      interact(world, actor);
    }
    recordEvent(world, { type: 'tick' });
  }
}

export function snapshot(world, id) {
  const actor = requireActor(world, id);
  // ORDER_LAB_STATE_READ
  return {
    tick: world.tick,
    actor: {
      id: actor.id, x: actor.x, y: actor.y, score: actor.score, cargo: actor.cargo,
      lastSeq: actor.lastSeq, expiresAt: actor.expiresAt, nextInteractTick: actor.nextInteractTick,
    },
    core: { ...world.core }, depot: { ...DEPOT }, arena: copy(ARENA),
    lastDecision: actor.lastDecision ? { ...actor.lastDecision } : null,
    findings: actor.detector.findings.map((finding) => ({ ...finding })),
  };
}

export function canonical(world) {
  return { tick: world.tick, actors: world.actors.map((actor) => snapshot(world, actor.id)) };
}

export function events(world) {
  return { version: VERSION, seed: world.seed, events: copy(world.history), dropped: world.dropped, final: canonical(world) };
}

function exactKeys(value, expected) {
  if (!value || typeof value !== 'object' || Array.isArray(value)) return false;
  const keys = Object.keys(value).sort();
  const sorted = [...expected].sort();
  return keys.length === sorted.length && keys.every((key, index) => key === sorted[index]);
}

function replayEvent(world, event) {
  if (event?.type === 'tick' && exactKeys(event, ['type'])) return advance(world, 1);
  if (event?.type === 'join' && exactKeys(event, ['type', 'id'])) {
    if (join(world).id !== event.id) throw new Error('invalid replay join identity');
    return;
  }
  if (event?.type === 'input' && exactKeys(event, ['type', 'id', 'input'])) {
    if (admit(world, event.id, event.input).status === 'rejected') throw new Error('invalid replay input');
    return;
  }
  throw new Error('invalid replay event');
}

function sameJson(left, right) {
  if (left === null || right === null || typeof left !== 'object' || typeof right !== 'object') return left === right;
  if (Array.isArray(left) !== Array.isArray(right)) return false;
  if (Array.isArray(left) && left.length !== right.length) return false;
  const keys = Object.keys(left).sort();
  const otherKeys = Object.keys(right).sort();
  return keys.length === otherKeys.length && keys.every((key, index) => key === otherKeys[index] && sameJson(left[key], right[key]));
}

/** Gameplay replay excludes HTTP authentication and real-time scheduling. */
export function replay(record) {
  if (record?.version !== VERSION) throw new Error('unsupported replay version');
  if (!Number.isSafeInteger(record.dropped) || record.dropped !== 0) throw new Error('cannot replay dropped records');
  if (!Array.isArray(record.events) || record.events.length > MAX_EVENTS) throw new Error('invalid replay events');
  const world = createWorld(record.seed);
  for (const event of record.events) replayEvent(world, event);
  const result = canonical(world);
  if (!sameJson(result, record.final)) throw new Error('replay final state mismatch');
  return result;
}

```

`courses/anti-cheat-engineering/courier-lab/evaluation/LEARNER.md`:

```md
# M7: Evaluate what your signals can support

Implementation reference for **M7: evaluation**. Start with [the guided learning route at `/learn`](/learn) on the reference server, then return here for the exact source contract. This Markdown file does not submit answers or certify mastery. Use the [support and attempt workflow](../learning-support/README.md) for worked siblings, gradual guidance and help recording. A prepared source workspace need not serve `/learn`; keep the reference server open for that route.

A courier can press pickup too early, retry a request, or use automation that sends only legal commands. Build an advisory classifier and a case-level evaluation that makes those differences and its blind spots visible.

This module uses the server authority from M1–M4 and complete replay windows from M6. A **case** is one scripted run for one actor. A **signal** is a denied interaction reconstructed from authoritative replay state, rather than a claim sent by the client. The supplied corpus contains fourteen synthetic cases; it contains no observations of human participants.

From the reference project run `npm run core:prepare -- evaluation`. In the printed workspace, fill the required answers or explicit skip reasons in `predictions.json`, edit `evaluation/policy.mjs`, keep explanations in `response.md`, and run `npm run core:check -- --assistance "none"`, replacing `none` with the help you used. The checker saves your exact source and response for each attempt. Reference solutions and calibration controls are author material; record consulting them as assistance.

## The contract

Export two functions. `classify(signals, settings)` returns a Boolean. `evaluate(cases, settings)` returns exactly `{decisions,metrics}`. Keep both functions independent of file, clock and network operations. Inputs are already validated; your job is the policy and arithmetic. Do not mutate them.

Each signal is `{tick,reason,distanceSquared}`. Ticks are nonnegative integers in nondecreasing order; equal ticks are allowed. Reasons are `range` or `cooldown`, and squared distances are finite and nonnegative. Settings are `{threshold,windowTicks,minDistanceMm}`: positive integer threshold and window, and a finite nonnegative minimum distance. A larger threshold requires more eligible observations; it does not change which observations are eligible.

Each case is `{id,label,signals}` with a unique ID and a Boolean label. The returned decisions preserve that order as `{id,flagged}`. Metrics have exactly these fields: `{total,tp,fp,tn,fn,precision,recall,falsePositiveRate}`. A flag is a request for further review, never an instruction to ban a player.

Before editing, save your explanations of the function inputs and output shapes in `response.md`. Then use the first checker result to identify a specific mismatch, rather than replacing your original explanation.

## Eligible observations

A signal counts only if `reason === 'range'` and `distanceSquared > minDistanceMm ** 2`. The strict comparison matters: with a 500 mm minimum, a denial at exactly 500 mm is ineligible. A denial at 750 mm is eligible because `750² > 500²`. Do not compare a squared distance directly with a distance in millimetres.

Cooldown means an interaction was attempted too soon after a successful action. Re-pressing pickup may produce cooldown denials while the courier is far from its next target. Distance alone does not turn those into eligible range denials. The extractor supplies both kinds so your policy must make this distinction.

Practice before your first check: for a 600 mm minimum, consider a range denial with squared distance 360,000, a cooldown denial with squared distance 1,000,000, and a range denial with squared distance 490,000. Record which can count and why. After checking your code, compare your saved prediction with the released answers and reasons. Use the criterion feedback to repair your comparison or reason filter, then answer the fresh variant without replacing your first prediction.

## Window boundaries

For each possible latest tick, the interval is `(latest-windowTicks, latest]`. The left edge is excluded; the right edge is included. With a four-tick window ending at tick 9, ticks 6, 7, 8 and 9 can count. Tick 5 cannot. If eligible observations occur at ticks 6 and 9 and the threshold is two, that interval flags.

You are asking whether **any** interval qualifies. A burst that qualified earlier still makes `classify` return true when later signals are quiet or ineligible. One implementation can retain eligible ticks, remove every tick at or before the current left edge, and check the remaining count. Another can count each candidate window directly. The engine normally consumes one interaction per actor per tick; the policy contract still counts each supplied observation, including equal-tick entries.

Practice: with threshold two and a seven-tick window, predict the result for eligible ticks 12 and 19, then for 13 and 19. Add an ineligible cooldown at tick 80 to the second case. Explain whether that changes the answer. Save those predictions before the checker. Compare them with the post-check answers, then use its boundary feedback to explain any repair and answer the fresh variant.

## Labels are not features

A **synthetic label** is the author's description of the behavior being evaluated. Here, true denotes the repeated-distant-invalid script. False denotes a script without that repeated-invalid behavior, including legal automation. A separate `declaredAutomation` field describes how the author wrote the script. That metadata is not a violation label and never reaches the policy. None of these names establish that recorded behavior came from a human.

`classify` receives only signals and settings. First generate predictions for all cases. Then compare predictions with labels to score them. Do not infer a prediction from the label, case ID, family name, record, or split. Otherwise you evaluate access to the answer instead of the signal rule.

The honest-delivery and valid-automation twins execute identical legal commands. Their records and signals match; both have a negative violation label, while their `declaredAutomation` metadata differs. Any deterministic function of these signals and the same settings must give both the same prediction. Calling both legal is correct for this violation detector, but it cannot establish which used automation. The report shows this separately as `indistinguishablePair`, rather than counting legal automation as a missed violation. The lack of a denial is not proof of unmodified client execution.

Practice: write one additional observation you would need to distinguish intent, and explain whether it could actually establish intent or would introduce another uncertain proxy. Do not add collection of device identifiers or third-party data to this local exercise.

## One case one vote

The **confusion matrix** counts predictions against labels:

| | Positive label (`true`) | Negative label (`false`) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Flagged | True positive (`tp`) | False positive (`fp`) |
| Not flagged | False negative (`fn`) | True negative (`tn`) |

A case with ten eligible denials is still one case. It contributes one vote in one cell, just like a case with three denials. `total` equals the number of cases and also equals `tp + fp + tn + fn`. Counting each denial would let a noisy script dominate the report and change the unit being measured.

Practice: three cases produce flagged-positive, flagged-negative and unflagged-negative outcomes. The first contains twelve denials and the others contain three and zero. Record the four cell counts and total before checking. Explain why twelve cannot appear in the matrix; after checking, compare your counts with the released answer and try its fresh variant.

## Counts and rates

Report raw counts alongside these rates, without an aggregate accuracy score:

| Rate | Formula | Question answered within this corpus |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Precision | `tp / (tp + fp)` | Of flagged cases, how many have positive labels? |
| Recall | `tp / (tp + fn)` | Of positive cases, how many were flagged? |
| False-positive rate | `fp / (fp + tn)` | Of negative cases, how many were flagged? |

For example, counts `tp=2, fp=1, tn=3, fn=2` yield precision `2/3`, recall `1/2`, and false-positive rate `1/4`. These have different denominators because they ask different questions.

Return `null` when a denominator is zero. With no flagged cases, precision is undefined, not evidence of perfect or terrible precision. With no positive labels, recall is undefined. With no negative labels, false-positive rate is undefined. An empty case list has zero counts and three null rates.

Practice: use one negative quiet case with no signals. Predict every count and rate, including where `null` belongs. Then change only its label to positive and recompute. The post-check answers explain both cases and their denominators; the executable checker also tests those arithmetic rules.

## Exploration and evaluation

Check the classifier and arithmetic before using a report to compare settings.

## Build in four checked milestones

| Milestone | Evidence to inspect |
| --- | --- |
| Eligibility | Work the three-observation example above, retaining only eligible ticks. Keep millimetres and squared millimetres distinct. |
| Any qualifying window | Check a pair exactly on the excluded edge, a pair just inside, and an earlier qualifying burst followed by a late quiet observation. |
| Case decisions and counts | Produce one Boolean per case, preserve case order, then put each case in exactly one matrix cell. |
| Rates and frozen run | Complete the missing denominator exercise below, check zero-denominator cases, then commit settings and source before evaluation. |

Completion: a sibling report has `tp=3, fp=1, tn=4, fn=2`. Fill the three denominators before dividing; identify which denominator contains all negative cases. Then construct a new four-case report of your own without copying those counts. Compare your source's results with its stated labels, while keeping classification independent of labels.

<details><summary>Hint 1 — keep one unit of counting</summary>

The classifier counts eligible observations inside a window; the evaluation counts whole cases. Mixing these units makes a noisy case contribute more than one vote.

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 2 — name each denominator in words</summary>

Precision uses flagged cases, recall uses positive-labeled cases, and false-positive rate uses negative-labeled cases. If the named group is empty, the rate has no denominator and must be `null`.

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 3 — worked sibling, after a saved attempt</summary>

For the earlier counts `tp=2, fp=1, tn=3, fn=2`, there are three flagged cases, four positive cases and four negative cases. The rates are therefore 2/3, 2/4 and 1/4. Record this as assistance and finish the different completion counts yourself.

</details>

## Freeze and interpret the evaluation

The corpus assigns seven stable IDs to `exploration` and seven to `evaluation` before settings are selected. Each split has six negative and one positive synthetic violation label. Use exploration to compare thresholds and window sizes. Include threshold three at windows eight and twenty: the exploration burst fits both, while a differently spaced evaluation burst need not. Commit a prediction before viewing that evaluation comparison. Write your final settings and reason into `response.md` before running evaluation; the report also pins settings, candidate source and corpus SHA-256 hashes. A hash identifies the bytes used; it does not certify the source or the author's labels.

Keep exploration and evaluation counts in separate report sections. If evaluation makes you change settings, preserve that result and call the next run a revision. Repeatedly tuning on evaluation makes it part of exploration; changing a report title does not restore independence. This small shipped corpus is inspectable and is not a secret held-out assessment.

The raw counts measure this chosen mix of scripts. They cannot estimate production prevalence or the probability that a real person will be flagged. In particular, precision changes with the proportion of positive cases, and these author-selected proportions are not a population sample. The report includes a separate no-positive/no-prediction diagnostic so undefined rates remain visible.

Before your evaluation run, record one expected tradeoff and the settings commitment. Afterward, compare it with the report and explain what the twin diagnostic cannot determine. A difference between splits is evidence about these scripts, not proof that one setting will generalize to people. Append repairs and assistance. The repair-station scenario in the response template asks you to apply this reasoning to a different decision; it is reviewed separately and is not an automatically scored learning claim.

# Evaluation author and integration notes

M7 builds a classifier and case-level report for the owned local courier game. No third-party telemetry, accounts or human behavior are collected. `policy.mjs` is the author solution; learner workspaces receive `template.mjs`, `prompt.json`, `LEARNER.md` and `response-template.md`. Keep fixtures, controls and the author solution outside the editable policy location.

Run the focused verification from the project directory:

```sh
node --test tests/evaluation.test.mjs
```

## Policy and assessment

`classify(signals,settings)` and `evaluate(cases,settings)` implement the wave-4 contract. Inputs are validated, signals are sorted and may contain equal-tick entries. An eligible signal is `range` with `distanceSquared > minDistanceMm²`. Any window `(latest-windowTicks,latest]` reaching the threshold flags the case. Labels are consulted only after prediction; the output preserves case order and counts each case once. Undefined denominators return `null`.

`fixtures.mjs` exports `cases()` and async `assess(candidate)` returning `{passed,criteria:[{name,passed,error?}]}`. Nineteen behavioral criteria cover eligibility, every window rather than only the final one, both strict boundaries, equal ticks, case order, one vote per case, label independence, three different denominators and empty sets. Failed criteria include the input, expected/actual result and a specific `LEARNER.md` section. Runtime failures are recorded as failures rather than throwing away the attempt.

`controls.mjs` exports `correctPolicies` and `wrongPolicies`. The two correct policies independently implement a sliding window and direct window counting with grouped metrics. Eleven wrong controls exercise observation-weighted metrics, cooldown inclusion, inclusive left edge, label leakage, total-based denominators, null-to-zero conversion, final-window-only classification, lifetime accumulation, inclusive distance edge, same-tick deduplication and reversed decision order. These are grader calibration controls, not learner submissions or evidence of learning.

## Corpus APIs and schema

`corpus.mjs` exports:

| Export | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| `CORPUS_VERSION` | `courier-synthetic-evaluation-v2`. |
| `DEFAULT_SETTINGS` | Frozen example `{threshold:3,windowTicks:20,minDistanceMm:500}`; illustrative, not a production recommendation. |
| `SPLIT_IDS` | Frozen `exploration` and `evaluation` ID arrays fixed before settings selection. |
| `generateCorpus()` | Deterministically produce fourteen fresh cases through the real recorder wrappers; no files written. |
| `loadCorpus(source?)` | Async generation when omitted; otherwise validate a corpus object, JSON text, filesystem path or file URL. Replay every record, validate labels/splits, and compare extracted signals. Return a detached corpus. |
| `casesForSplit(corpus,split)` | Project the seven stable IDs in their declared order to detached `{id,label,signals}` inputs. Use a generated or loaded corpus. |
| `extractDenials(record)` | Validate via the current telemetry `replayWindow` and `createReplayEngine` facade, replay the retained operations and return `{tick,actorId,reason,distanceSquared}[]`. |
| `extractSignals(record,{actorId='actor-1'}={})` | Project one actor's denials to `{tick,reason,distanceSquared}[]`; refuse unknown actors. |

Corpus envelope:

```text
{
  schema: 'courier-evaluation-corpus-v2', version,
  labelDefinition, limitations,
  splits: {exploration: string[7], evaluation: string[7]},
  cases: [{id, split, family, description, label, declaredAutomation, actorId, record, signals}]
}
```

The evaluation split adds a delayed start, repeated-invalid receipts six ticks apart and three widely separated errors rather than copying the exploration signals. The required comparison uses threshold 3, minimum distance 500 mm, and windows 8 and 20. Exploration flags its tight repeated-invalid burst at both windows. Evaluation does not flag its six-tick-spaced burst at window 8, but flags at window 20. These results make the split distinction observable without pretending the shipped corpus is secret. Each split has six negative and one positive violation label. Families are `honest-delivery`, `pickup-repress`, `anticipatory-presses`, `delayed-reordered-retries`, `isolated-distant-errors`, `repeated-distant-invalid` and `valid-automation`. True means the repeated-distant-invalid script; false means a script without that repeated-invalid behavior. `declaredAutomation` is true only for the legal automated twin and is separate metadata, never a feature passed to the policy. These are author-assigned synthetic labels, never inferred human intentions. Delayed/reordered retries are controlled input arrival order, not a claim about real network delay or a wall clock.

The honest-delivery and valid-automation twins have byte-identical records and identical empty signal arrays within each split. Both have negative violation labels; only their automation metadata and descriptive identity differ. A deterministic signal classifier must return the same decision for them, so the report carries a separate `indistinguishablePair` diagnostic about automation status. Accepting both is correct for the repeated-invalid target, not an unavoidable false negative. Example settings yield seven cases per split with `tp=1,fp=0,tn=6,fn=0`: precision 1, recall 1, false-positive rate 0. These are counts for the script mix only. They do not estimate operational performance, human false-positive rates or prevalence.

Records use `createRecordedEngine` at capacity 256 with no direct state mutation. All generated records retain the complete history (`startIndex=0`); no record hits the capacity limit. Extraction validates the record first, then derives the denied interaction's distance from the replayed post-movement position and current target. It uses neither the client request nor the engine's preconfigured detector findings as evidence. It emits a persisted `lastDecision` only when its tick equals the current replay tick. A rolled window is supported, but signals before the checkpoint are intentionally absent; checkpoint detector buckets are not invented full observations. The fixed depot coordinate, 1000/1000, matches `courier-runtime-1`.

## Committed report APIs

`report.mjs` uses Node core only. It exports:

- `hashValue(value)`: SHA-256 of recursively key-sorted JSON for deterministic settings/corpus identity.
- `prepareEvaluation({settings,source,corpus?})`: async validate and commit exact settings, candidate source bytes and corpus, returning `{schema,corpusVersion,settings,settingsSha256,sourceSha256,corpusSha256,splitIds}`. Preserve this plan before evaluation.
- `runEvaluation(candidate,{plan,source,corpus?})`: async verify the earlier plan against the same source/corpus, then return `{schema,plan,exploration,evaluation,noPositiveNoPrediction,indistinguishablePair,labelDefinition,limitations}`. Each split has `{caseIds,positiveLabels,negativeLabels,result}` and `result` is the candidate's `{decisions,metrics}`. The no-positive diagnostic is a negative quiet case with no positive labels and no predictions under a correct policy. `indistinguishablePair` contains a claim plus a `splits` array with `{split,caseIds,declaredAutomation,identicalSignals,decisions,sameDecision}` for the two legal twins. This metadata is attached after policy evaluation; it is never supplied to `classify` or `evaluate`.
- `REPORT_LIMIT`: required plain-language limitation string.

The caller must bind the imported candidate module to the same captured `source` bytes and preserve plan/report files in the existing attempt flow. A source hash supplied by a caller cannot prove this binding by itself. This module writes no files, changes no earlier attempts and adds no CLI. The parent integration owns file paths, captured-source execution, display and prepare/check registration. It must state output paths and settings, keep exploration/evaluation distinct and record post-evaluation retuning as revision.

The report does not use elapsed time or a random split; re-running the same source, settings and corpus is reproducible. The corpus is shipped and inspectable. It is a fixed synthetic evaluation split, not a secret held-out human assessment.

## Prediction feedback and reviewer key

`feedback.mjs` stays outside prepared workspaces. After the checker has saved the submitted response, the integration calls `postCheckFeedback()` to release `{schema:1,module:'evaluation',predictions}`. Each prediction carries `{id,question,answer,reason,source,freshVariant:{question}}`. The source points to the actual learner section. This supplies numeric answers and reasons even when the submitted code passes first time; it does not silently grade free-form prose or replace the learner's answer.

`reviewerFeedback()` is separate author material: it returns the fresh variants' reference answers plus a rubric and reference answer for the repair-station transfer. It must not be included in the first post-check payload or copied into a learner workspace. The transfer still needs a review; automatic code checks cannot establish the quality of that written reasoning.

## Course-craft trace and remaining acceptance

Executable functions assess the stated production task (`assessment-03`, `projects-03`). Independent correct and wrong controls calibrate the checker (`assessment-09`). Input/expected/actual feedback and section links support repair (`feedback-07`), while the response keeps first predictions, settings and revisions separate. Post-check prediction answers and fresh variants address `feedback-02` and `practice-10`; the author-only transfer rubric makes separate review concrete (`assessment-15`). The transfer asks for a different repair-resource mechanic and is an ungraded review prompt (`assessment-02`), not evidence of learning (`evaluation-01`).

Tests establish deterministic policy behavior, real replay extraction, synthetic label/split integrity, report commitments and calibrated feedback. Parent integration still owns the actual prepare/edit/check path, desktop/mobile presentation and independent technical/cold-reader review. No browser or human-learning claim follows from this module's Node tests.

`courses/anti-cheat-engineering/courier-lab/evaluation/controls.mjs`:

```mjs
import { classify, evaluate } from './policy.mjs';

// Independent brute-force implementation: count each possible window directly.
export function classifyByWindows(signals, settings) {
  for (const endpoint of signals) {
    const count = signals.filter((signal) => signal.tick > endpoint.tick - settings.windowTicks
      && signal.tick <= endpoint.tick && signal.reason === 'range'
      && signal.distanceSquared > settings.minDistanceMm * settings.minDistanceMm).length;
    if (count >= settings.threshold) return true;
  }
  return false;
}

export function evaluateByGroups(cases, settings) {
  const decisions = cases.map(({ id, signals }) => ({ id, flagged: classifyByWindows(signals, settings) }));
  const observations = decisions.map((decision, index) => ({ ...decision, label: cases[index].label }));
  const count = (label, flagged) => observations.filter((item) => item.label === label && item.flagged === flagged).length;
  const tp = count(true, true);
  const fp = count(false, true);
  const tn = count(false, false);
  const fn = count(true, false);
  return {
    decisions,
    metrics: { total: observations.length, tp, fp, tn, fn,
      precision: tp + fp ? tp / (tp + fp) : null,
      recall: tp + fn ? tp / (tp + fn) : null,
      falsePositiveRate: fp + tn ? fp / (fp + tn) : null },
  };
}

export const correctPolicies = {
  'sliding-window': { classify, evaluate },
  'direct-windows-and-groups': { classify: classifyByWindows, evaluate: evaluateByGroups },
};

function withClassifier(replacement) {
  return { classify: replacement, evaluate(cases, settings) {
    // Reuse metric arithmetic, but force each replacement decision through a tiny surrogate signal set.
    const remapped = cases.map((item) => ({ ...item, signals: replacement(item.signals, settings)
      ? Array.from({ length: settings.threshold }, () => ({ tick: 1, reason: 'range', distanceSquared: Number.MAX_VALUE })) : [] }));
    return evaluate(remapped, settings);
  } };
}

export const wrongPolicies = {
  'count-observations-as-votes': { classify, evaluate(cases, settings) {
    const expanded = cases.flatMap((item) => Array.from({ length: Math.max(1, item.signals.length) }, () => item));
    return { ...evaluate(expanded, settings), decisions: evaluate(cases, settings).decisions };
  } },
  'include-cooldown': withClassifier((signals, settings) => classify(signals.map((signal) => ({ ...signal, reason: 'range' })), settings)),
  'include-left-window-edge': withClassifier((signals, settings) => classify(signals, { ...settings, windowTicks: settings.windowTicks + 1 })),
  'label-as-feature': { classify, evaluate(cases, settings) {
    return evaluate(cases.map((item) => ({ ...item, signals: item.label
      ? Array.from({ length: settings.threshold }, () => ({ tick: 1, reason: 'range', distanceSquared: Number.MAX_VALUE })) : [] })), settings);
  } },
  'divide-every-rate-by-total': { classify, evaluate(cases, settings) {
    const result = evaluate(cases, settings);
    const { total, tp, fp } = result.metrics;
    return { ...result, metrics: { ...result.metrics, precision: total ? tp / total : null,
      recall: total ? tp / total : null, falsePositiveRate: total ? fp / total : null } };
  } },
  'undefined-rate-is-zero': { classify, evaluate(cases, settings) {
    const result = evaluate(cases, settings);
    for (const name of ['precision', 'recall', 'falsePositiveRate']) result.metrics[name] ??= 0;
    return result;
  } },
  'only-check-final-window': withClassifier((signals, settings) => {
    const latest = signals.at(-1)?.tick ?? 0;
    return classify(signals.filter((signal) => signal.tick > latest - settings.windowTicks), settings);
  }),
  'ignore-window-expiry': withClassifier((signals, settings) => classify(signals, { ...settings, windowTicks: Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER })),
  'distance-edge-inclusive': withClassifier((signals, settings) => classify(signals.map((signal) => ({
    ...signal, distanceSquared: signal.distanceSquared === settings.minDistanceMm ** 2 ? signal.distanceSquared + 1 : signal.distanceSquared,
  })), settings)),
  'one-observation-per-tick': withClassifier((signals, settings) => classify(signals.filter((signal, index) => index === 0 || signal.tick !== signals[index - 1].tick), settings)),
  'reverse-case-order': { classify, evaluate(cases, settings) {
    const result = evaluate(cases, settings);
    return { ...result, decisions: [...result.decisions].reverse() };
  } },
};

```

`courses/anti-cheat-engineering/courier-lab/evaluation/corpus.mjs`:

```mjs
import { readFile } from 'node:fs/promises';
import { createRecordedEngine, createReplayEngine } from '../telemetry/runtime.mjs';
import { replayWindow } from '../telemetry/policy.mjs';

export const CORPUS_VERSION = 'courier-synthetic-evaluation-v2';
export const DEFAULT_SETTINGS = Object.freeze({ threshold: 3, windowTicks: 20, minDistanceMm: 500 });
const FAMILIES = ['honest-delivery', 'pickup-repress', 'anticipatory-presses', 'delayed-reordered-retries',
  'isolated-distant-errors', 'repeated-distant-invalid', 'valid-automation'];
export const SPLIT_IDS = Object.freeze(Object.fromEntries(['exploration', 'evaluation'].map((split) => [
  split, Object.freeze(FAMILIES.map((family) => `${split}/${family}`)),
])));

const copy = (value) => JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(value));
const input = (seq, move, interact) => ({ v: 1, seq, move, interact });

/** Replay before extracting. Checkpoint history before this retained window is not invented. */
export function extractDenials(record) {
  const engine = createReplayEngine();
  const checked = replayWindow(record, engine);
  if (!checked.ok) throw new Error(`Cannot extract signals from refused replay: ${checked.reason}.`);
  const world = engine.restore(record.checkpoint);
  const denials = [];
  for (const { event } of record.events) {
    engine.apply(world, event);
    if (event.type !== 'tick') continue;
    for (const actor of world.actors) appendDenial(denials, actor, world);
  }
  return denials;
}

function appendDenial(denials, actor, world) {
  const decision = actor.lastDecision;
  if (decision?.status !== 'denied' || decision.tick !== world.tick) return;
  // Denial leaves cargo unchanged; the post-movement state is the state used by interactionDenial.
  const target = actor.cargo ? { x: 1000, y: 1000 } : world.core;
  denials.push({ tick: world.tick, actorId: actor.id, reason: decision.reason,
    distanceSquared: (actor.x - target.x) ** 2 + (actor.y - target.y) ** 2 });
}

export function extractSignals(record, { actorId = 'actor-1' } = {}) {
  const signals = extractDenials(record).filter((event) => event.actorId === actorId)
    .map(({ tick, reason, distanceSquared }) => ({ tick, reason, distanceSquared }));
  if (!record.final.actors.some((entry) => entry.actor.id === actorId)) throw new Error(`Unknown signal actor: ${actorId}.`);
  return signals;
}

function scriptedEngine(seed) {
  const recorder = createRecordedEngine(seed, { capacity: 256 });
  const actor = recorder.join();
  let sequence = 0;
  return {
    recorder,
    step(move = 'idle', interact = false) {
      recorder.admit(actor.id, input(++sequence, move, interact));
      recorder.advance(1);
    },
    reorderedStep(move, interact, staleMove = 'W') {
      sequence += 2;
      recorder.admit(actor.id, input(sequence, move, interact));
      recorder.admit(actor.id, input(sequence - 1, staleMove, true));
      recorder.admit(actor.id, input(sequence, 'idle', true));
      recorder.advance(1);
    },
  };
}

function delivery(script) {
  script.step('E');
  script.step('E');
  script.step('E', true);
  script.step('W');
  script.step('W');
  script.step('W');
  script.step('idle', true);
}

function repress(script) {
  script.step('E');
  script.step('E');
  script.step('E', true);
  for (let index = 0; index < 3; index += 1) script.step('idle', true);
  script.step('W', true);
  script.step('W', true);
  for (let index = 0; index < 3; index += 1) script.step('idle', true);
  script.step('W');
}

function anticipatory(script) {
  for (let index = 0; index < 3; index += 1) script.step('E', true);
  for (let index = 0; index < 3; index += 1) script.step('W', true);
  script.step('idle', true);
}

function reordered(script) {
  script.reorderedStep('E', false);
  script.reorderedStep('E', false);
  script.reorderedStep('E', true);
  script.reorderedStep('W', false);
  script.reorderedStep('W', false);
  script.reorderedStep('W', true);
  script.reorderedStep('idle', true);
}

function isolated(script) {
  script.step('idle', true);
  script.recorder.advance(21);
  script.step('idle', true);
}

function repeated(script) {
  for (let index = 0; index < 5; index += 1) script.step('idle', true);
}

const SCRIPTS = {
  'honest-delivery': delivery,
  'pickup-repress': repress,
  'anticipatory-presses': anticipatory,
  'delayed-reordered-retries': reordered,
  'isolated-distant-errors': isolated,
  'repeated-distant-invalid': repeated,
  'valid-automation': delivery,
};

const DESCRIPTIONS = {
  'honest-delivery': 'Scripted honest-shaped route: legal pickup and delivery.',
  'pickup-repress': 'Scripted honest-shaped re-presses: cooldown denials and one 500 mm range denial.',
  'anticipatory-presses': 'Scripted honest-shaped presses while approaching pickup and depot.',
  'delayed-reordered-retries': 'Scripted honest-shaped ingress order: older and equal sequences retry around legal movement.',
  'isolated-distant-errors': 'Scripted honest-shaped distant mistakes separated by more than the example detector window.',
  'repeated-distant-invalid': 'Scripted repeated remote interaction attempts without approaching the target.',
  'valid-automation': 'Script declared automated; its legal commands are identical to the honest-delivery twin.',
};

/** Fourteen cases, with split IDs fixed before any settings are selected. No human data. */
export function generateCorpus() {
  const cases = [];
  for (const split of Object.keys(SPLIT_IDS)) {
    for (const family of FAMILIES) cases.push(generateCase(split, family));
  }
  return {
    schema: 'courier-evaluation-corpus-v2', version: CORPUS_VERSION,
    labelDefinition: 'true means the scripted repeated-distant-invalid control; false means a control without that repeated-invalid behavior. Declared automation is separate metadata: a legal automated script is not a rule violation. These are author-assigned synthetic labels, not a judgment about a person.',
    limitations: 'Fourteen synthetic cases from the owned local game; no human participants, production prevalence estimate, authentication claim or automatic enforcement.',
    splits: copy(SPLIT_IDS), cases,
  };
}

function generateCase(split, family) {
  // Distinct seeds are deterministic; both intentionally select the same course geometry.
  const script = scriptedEngine(split === 'exploration' ? 0 : 3);
  if (split === 'evaluation') script.recorder.advance(3);
  if (split === 'evaluation' && family === 'repeated-distant-invalid') {
    for (let index = 0; index < 4; index += 1) {
      script.step('idle', true);
      script.recorder.advance(5);
    }
  } else if (split === 'evaluation' && family === 'isolated-distant-errors') {
    for (let index = 0; index < 3; index += 1) {
      script.step('idle', true);
      script.recorder.advance(25);
    }
  } else SCRIPTS[family](script);
  const record = script.recorder.window();
  if (record.startIndex !== 0) throw new Error('Synthetic corpus unexpectedly exceeded its complete recording capacity.');
  return {
    id: `${split}/${family}`, split, family, description: DESCRIPTIONS[family],
    label: family === 'repeated-distant-invalid', declaredAutomation: family === 'valid-automation',
    actorId: 'actor-1', record, signals: extractSignals(record),
  };
}

function validateCorpus(corpus) {
  if (corpus?.schema !== 'courier-evaluation-corpus-v2' || corpus.version !== CORPUS_VERSION) throw new Error('Unsupported evaluation corpus.');
  if (!Array.isArray(corpus.cases) || corpus.cases.length !== 14) throw new Error('The versioned corpus must contain fourteen cases.');
  if (typeof corpus.labelDefinition !== 'string' || typeof corpus.limitations !== 'string') throw new Error('Corpus labels and limitations must be explicit.');
  const ids = corpus.cases.map((item) => item.id);
  if (new Set(ids).size !== ids.length) throw new Error('Corpus case IDs must be unique.');
  for (const split of Object.keys(SPLIT_IDS)) validateSplit(corpus, split);
  for (const item of corpus.cases) validateCase(item);
  return copy(corpus);
}

function validateSplit(corpus, split) {
  if (JSON.stringify(corpus.splits?.[split]) !== JSON.stringify(SPLIT_IDS[split])) throw new Error(`Changed stable ${split} IDs.`);
  const ids = corpus.cases.filter((item) => item.split === split).map((item) => item.id);
  if (JSON.stringify([...ids].sort()) !== JSON.stringify([...SPLIT_IDS[split]].sort())) throw new Error(`Invalid ${split} membership.`);
}

function validateCase(item) {
  const expectedId = `${item.split}/${item.family}`;
  if (!FAMILIES.includes(item.family) || item.id !== expectedId || item.actorId !== 'actor-1') throw new Error(`Invalid corpus case identity: ${item.id}.`);
  const label = item.family === 'repeated-distant-invalid';
  if (item.label !== label) throw new Error(`Changed synthetic label: ${item.id}.`);
  if (item.declaredAutomation !== (item.family === 'valid-automation')) throw new Error(`Changed declared automation metadata: ${item.id}.`);
  if (item.record?.startIndex !== 0) throw new Error(`Corpus case must preserve its full recording: ${item.id}.`);
  const actual = extractSignals(item.record, { actorId: item.actorId });
  if (!createReplayEngine().equal(item.signals, actual)) throw new Error(`Signals do not match replay: ${item.id}.`);
}

/** Load a JSON path/URL, parse JSON text, or validate an object. Omit to generate v2. */
export async function loadCorpus(source) {
  if (source === undefined) return validateCorpus(generateCorpus());
  if (source instanceof URL) return validateCorpus(JSON.parse(await readFile(source, 'utf8')));
  if (typeof source === 'string') {
    const text = source.trimStart().startsWith('{') ? source : await readFile(source, 'utf8');
    return validateCorpus(JSON.parse(text));
  }
  return validateCorpus(source);
}

/** Project precisely the public policy input; record, family and split are never features. */
export function casesForSplit(corpus, split) {
  if (!Object.hasOwn(SPLIT_IDS, split)) throw new Error(`Unknown corpus split: ${split}.`);
  const byId = new Map(corpus.cases.map((item) => [item.id, item]));
  return SPLIT_IDS[split].map((id) => {
    const item = byId.get(id);
    if (!item || item.split !== split || typeof item.label !== 'boolean') throw new Error(`Missing corpus case: ${id}.`);
    return { id, label: item.label, signals: copy(item.signals) };
  });
}

`courses/anti-cheat-engineering/courier-lab/evaluation/custody.mjs`:

```mjs
import { randomUUID } from 'node:crypto';
import { lstat, mkdir, readdir, realpath, writeFile } from 'node:fs/promises';
import { dirname, join, resolve } from 'node:path';
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
import { acquireCheckLock, releaseCheckLock } from '../lab/core/lock.mjs';
import { captureBundle, jsonBytes, regularFile, sha256, verifyReference } from '../lab/core/trust.mjs';
import { casesForSplit, generateCorpus } from './corpus.mjs';
import { prepareEvaluation, runEvaluation } from './report.mjs';

const SCHEMA = 'courier-evaluation-custody-v1';
const EVENT_ID = /^\d{6}-[a-f0-9]{8}-[a-f0-9]{4}-[a-f0-9]{4}-[a-f0-9]{4}-[a-f0-9]{12}$/;
const SESSION_ID = /^[a-f0-9]{8}-[a-f0-9]{4}-[a-f0-9]{4}-[a-f0-9]{4}-[a-f0-9]{12}$/;
const FILES = ['record.json', 'source.mjs', 'corpus.json', 'plan.json', 'exposure.json', 'report.json', 'failure.json'];
const MODULE_ROOT = resolve(dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), '..');
const LIMIT = 4 * 1024 * 1024;

async function directory(root, relative, create = false) {
  let current = root;
  for (const part of relative.split('/')) {
    current = join(current, part);
    if (create) {
      try { await mkdir(current, { mode: 0o700 }); }
      catch (error) { if (error.code !== 'EEXIST') throw error; }
    }
    const stat = await lstat(current);
    if (stat.isSymbolicLink() || !stat.isDirectory()) throw new Error(`Evaluation custody requires a regular directory: ${current}`);
  }
  return current;
}

async function authenticate(workspace, suppliedSession) {
  const requested = resolve(workspace);
  const stat = await lstat(requested);
  if (stat.isSymbolicLink() || !stat.isDirectory()) throw new Error('Use the original prepared workspace directory, without a symlink.');
  workspace = await realpath(requested);
  const sessionBytes = await regularFile(workspace, 'lab/core/session.json');
  const session = JSON.parse(sessionBytes);
  if (session.schema !== 'courier-core-session-v1' || session.module !== 'evaluation' || !SESSION_ID.test(session.sessionId) || !/^[a-f0-9]{64}$/.test(session.referenceManifest)) throw new Error('Evaluation history requires a prepared evaluation workspace.');
  if (suppliedSession && JSON.stringify(suppliedSession) !== JSON.stringify(session)) throw new Error('Prepared evaluation session changed.');
  const root = await realpath(session.referenceRoot);
  if (root !== await realpath(MODULE_ROOT)) throw new Error('Use evaluation custody from this workspace\'s sealed reference snapshot. Prepare a fresh workspace if its snapshot lacks this command.');
  await verifyReference(root, session.referenceManifest);
  const ownerSession = await directory(root, `artifacts/core/sessions/${session.sessionId}`);
  const owner = JSON.parse(await regularFile(ownerSession, 'session.json'));
  if (owner.workspace !== workspace || owner.referenceRoot !== root || owner.referenceManifest !== session.referenceManifest || owner.module !== 'evaluation' || owner.sessionHash !== sha256(sessionBytes)) throw new Error('Prepared evaluation session identity changed.');
  return { workspace, root, ownerSession, session };
}

async function history(context) {
  let base;
  try { base = await directory(context.ownerSession, 'evaluation'); }
  catch (error) { if (error.code === 'ENOENT') return []; throw error; }
  const entries = await readdir(base, { withFileTypes: true });
  if (entries.length > 1000) throw new Error('Evaluation history exceeds its supported 1000-event limit.');
  const result = [];
  for (const entry of entries.sort((a, b) => a.name.localeCompare(b.name))) {
    if (!EVENT_ID.test(entry.name) || !entry.isDirectory() || entry.isSymbolicLink()) throw new Error(`Unexpected evaluation history entry: ${entry.name}`);
    let record;
    try { record = JSON.parse(await regularFile(base, `${entry.name}/record.json`)); }
    catch (error) {
      if (error.code !== 'ENOENT' && !(error instanceof SyntaxError)) throw error;
      // A crash can follow mkdir or interrupt the first record write. Preserve
      // the directory and its raw bytes without inventing a plan or run identity.
      record = { schema: SCHEMA, eventId: entry.name, ordinal: Number(entry.name.slice(0, 6)),
        sessionId: context.session.sessionId, referenceManifest: context.session.referenceManifest,
        kind: 'interrupted', reason: error.code === 'ENOENT' ? 'missing-record' : 'incomplete-record' };
      result.push({ record, directory: join(base, entry.name) });
      continue;
    }
    if (record.schema !== SCHEMA || record.eventId !== entry.name || record.sessionId !== context.session.sessionId || record.referenceManifest !== context.session.referenceManifest || !['explore', 'plan', 'run'].includes(record.kind)) throw new Error(`Invalid evaluation history record: ${entry.name}`);
    result.push({ record, directory: join(base, entry.name) });
  }
  return result;
}

async function optionalFile(root, path) {
  try { return await regularFile(root, path); }
  catch (error) { if (error.code === 'ENOENT') return null; throw error; }
}

async function exposureBefore(events) {
  const exposed = [];
  for (const event of events.filter(({ record }) => ['run', 'interrupted'].includes(record.kind))) {
    if (await optionalFile(event.directory, 'exposure.json')) exposed.push(event.record.eventId);
  }
  return exposed;
}

async function save(path, value) {
  const bytes = jsonBytes(value);
  if (bytes.length > LIMIT) throw new Error('Evaluation evidence exceeds the bounded file size.');
  await writeFile(path, bytes, { flag: 'wx', mode: 0o600 });
}

async function frozenCandidate(context, settings) {
  const { captured } = await captureBundle(context.workspace, ['evaluation/policy.mjs', 'lab/core/session.json']);
  if (sha256(captured['lab/core/session.json']) !== sha256(jsonBytes(context.session))) throw new Error('Prepared session changed while freezing evaluation source.');
  const source = captured['evaluation/policy.mjs'].toString('utf8');
  const corpus = generateCorpus();
  const plan = await prepareEvaluation({ source, settings, corpus });
  return { source, corpus, plan };
}

async function newEvent(context, events, kind, frozen, details = {}) {
  if (events.length >= 1000) throw new Error('Evaluation history reached its 1000-event limit; preserve it and prepare a new workspace.');
  const base = await directory(context.ownerSession, 'evaluation', true);
  const ordinal = events.length + 1;
  const eventId = `${String(ordinal).padStart(6, '0')}-${randomUUID()}`;
  const path = join(base, eventId);
  await mkdir(path, { mode: 0o700 });
  const priorRunIds = await exposureBefore(events);
  const record = {
    schema: SCHEMA, eventId, ordinal, kind, createdAt: new Date().toISOString(),
    sessionId: context.session.sessionId, referenceManifest: context.session.referenceManifest,
    sourceSha256: frozen.plan.sourceSha256, settingsSha256: frozen.plan.settingsSha256,
    corpusSha256: frozen.plan.corpusSha256, corpusVersion: frozen.plan.corpusVersion,
    settings: frozen.plan.settings, priorEvaluationExposure: priorRunIds.length > 0, priorRunIds,
    ...details,
  };
  await save(join(path, 'record.json'), record);
  await writeFile(join(path, 'source.mjs'), frozen.source, { flag: 'wx', mode: 0o600 });
  await save(join(path, 'corpus.json'), frozen.corpus);
  await save(join(path, 'plan.json'), frozen.plan);
  return { eventId, directory: path, record };
}

async function withSession(workspace, operation) {
  const context = await authenticate(workspace);
  const lease = await acquireCheckLock({ ...context, sessionId: context.session.sessionId });
  try { return await operation(context, await history(context)); }
  finally { await releaseCheckLock(lease); }
}

async function candidateFrom(source) {
  // Import the saved bytes, never another read of the mutable learner source.
  return import(`data:text/javascript;base64,${Buffer.from(source).toString('base64')}#${randomUUID()}`);
}

async function executeEvent(event, operation) {
  await save(join(event.directory, 'exposure.json'), {
    schema: 'courier-evaluation-exposure-v1', eventId: event.eventId,
    kind: event.record.kind, startedAt: new Date().toISOString(),
    note: 'Execution has started. Later plans preserve this possible result exposure even if execution fails or is interrupted.',
  });
  try {
    const report = await operation();
    await save(join(event.directory, 'report.json'), report);
    return { ...event, status: 'completed', path: join(event.directory, 'report.json'), report };
  } catch (error) {
    await save(join(event.directory, 'failure.json'), { schema: 'courier-evaluation-failure-v1', eventId: event.eventId, failedAt: new Date().toISOString(), name: error.name, message: error.message });
    const failure = new Error(`Evaluation ${event.record.kind} failed: ${error.message}. Saved evidence: ${event.directory}`, { cause: error });
    failure.evidence = { ...event, status: 'failed', path: join(event.directory, 'failure.json') };
    throw failure;
  }
}

/** Save each exploration setting and exact candidate before exposing its result. */
export async function explore({ workspace, settings }) {
  return withSession(workspace, async (context, events) => {
    const frozen = await frozenCandidate(context, settings);
    const event = await newEvent(context, events, 'explore', frozen);
    return executeEvent(event, async () => {
      const candidate = await candidateFrom(frozen.source);
      if (typeof candidate.evaluate !== 'function') throw new Error('Candidate must export evaluate(cases, settings).');
      const result = await candidate.evaluate(casesForSplit(frozen.corpus, 'exploration'), { ...frozen.plan.settings });
      return { schema: 'courier-exploration-v1', plan: frozen.plan, split: 'exploration', result };
    });
  });
}

/** Commit immutable settings, source and corpus. Every subsequent plan is a declared revision. */
export async function plan({ workspace, settings, revisionReason }) {
  return withSession(workspace, async (context, events) => {
    const previous = events.filter(({ record }) => record.kind === 'plan').at(-1);
    if (previous && (typeof revisionReason !== 'string' || !revisionReason.trim())) throw new Error('A plan already exists. Preserve it and declare --revision <reason> for the next plan.');
    if (revisionReason !== undefined && (typeof revisionReason !== 'string' || !revisionReason.trim() || revisionReason.length > 10000)) throw new Error('Revision reason must be a nonempty string of at most 10000 characters.');
    const frozen = await frozenCandidate(context, settings);
    const event = await newEvent(context, events, 'plan', frozen, {
      attemptKind: previous ? 'revision' : 'first', previousPlanId: previous?.record.eventId ?? null,
      revisionReason: revisionReason?.trim() ?? null,
    });
    return { ...event, planId: event.eventId, status: 'planned', plan: frozen.plan, path: join(event.directory, 'plan.json') };
  });
}

/** Run one committed plan once. Source edits require a new declared plan; old bytes stay executable. */
export async function run({ workspace, planId }) {
  if (typeof planId !== 'string' || !EVENT_ID.test(planId)) throw new Error('Use the plan ID returned by evaluation:plan, not a filesystem path.');
  return withSession(workspace, async (context, events) => {
    const committed = events.find(({ record }) => record.kind === 'plan' && record.eventId === planId);
    if (!committed) throw new Error('Plan does not belong to this prepared evaluation session.');
    if (events.some(({ record }) => record.kind === 'run' && record.planId === planId)) throw new Error('This plan was already started. Preserve its result and create a declared revision to evaluate again.');
    const source = (await regularFile(committed.directory, 'source.mjs')).toString('utf8');
    const corpus = JSON.parse(await regularFile(committed.directory, 'corpus.json'));
    const savedPlan = JSON.parse(await regularFile(committed.directory, 'plan.json'));
    const expected = await prepareEvaluation({ source, corpus, settings: savedPlan.settings });
    if (JSON.stringify(savedPlan) !== JSON.stringify(expected) || expected.sourceSha256 !== committed.record.sourceSha256 || expected.corpusSha256 !== committed.record.corpusSha256 || expected.settingsSha256 !== committed.record.settingsSha256) throw new Error('Committed plan evidence changed. Preserve it and prepare a new session.');
    const frozen = { source, corpus, plan: savedPlan };
    const event = await newEvent(context, events, 'run', frozen, { planId, attemptKind: committed.record.attemptKind });
    return executeEvent(event, async () => runEvaluation(await candidateFrom(source), { source, corpus, plan: savedPlan }));
  });
}

/** Read-only links for a new core submission. Never edits a previous submission or result. */
export async function getEvidenceLinks({ workspace, session }) {
  const context = await authenticate(workspace, session);
  const events = [];
  for (const event of await history(context)) {
    const files = [];
    for (const file of FILES) {
      const bytes = await optionalFile(event.directory, file);
      if (bytes) files.push({ path: join(event.directory, file), sha256: sha256(bytes) });
    }
    const names = files.map(({ path }) => path.split('/').at(-1));
    const completeCapture = ['source.mjs', 'corpus.json', 'plan.json'].every((name) => names.includes(name));
    const status = event.record.kind === 'interrupted' ? 'interrupted' : names.includes('failure.json') ? 'failed' : !completeCapture ? 'interrupted' : names.includes('report.json') ? 'completed' : event.record.kind === 'plan' ? 'planned' : 'interrupted';
    events.push({ ...event.record, status, files });
  }
  return {
    schema: 'courier-evaluation-evidence-v1', sessionId: context.session.sessionId,
    referenceManifest: context.session.referenceManifest, events,
    latestPlanId: events.filter((event) => event.kind === 'plan').at(-1)?.eventId ?? null,
    evaluationExposed: events.some((event) => ['run', 'interrupted'].includes(event.kind) && event.files.some(({ path }) => path.endsWith('/exposure.json'))),
    limits: 'Owner-side append-only local evidence, not an OS security boundary against the machine owner.',
  };
}

import { isDeepStrictEqual } from 'node:util';

const settings = { threshold: 3, windowTicks: 20, minDistanceMm: 500 };
const range = (tick, distanceSquared = 1_000_000) => ({ tick, reason: 'range', distanceSquared });
const burst = [range(1), range(2), range(3)];
const clone = (value) => JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(value));

function classification(name, signals, expected, section, overrides = {}) {
  return { name, method: 'classify', args: [signals, { ...settings, ...overrides }], expected, section };
}

function evaluation(name, cases, metrics, section) {
  return { name, method: 'evaluate', args: [cases, { ...settings }], section, expected: {
    decisions: cases.map(({ id }, index) => ({ id, flagged: metrics.flags[index] })),
    metrics: Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(metrics).filter(([key]) => key !== 'flags')),
  } };
}

/** Small behavioral cases, separate from the synthetic corpus used to explore thresholds. */
export function cases() {
  const mixed = [
    { id: 'positive-a', label: true, signals: burst },
    { id: 'negative-many-observations', label: false, signals: [...burst, range(4), range(5), range(6)] },
    { id: 'miss-a', label: true, signals: [] },
    { id: 'negative-quiet-a', label: false, signals: [] },
    { id: 'positive-b', label: true, signals: burst },
    { id: 'miss-b', label: true, signals: [range(1)] },
    { id: 'negative-quiet-b', label: false, signals: [] },
    { id: 'miss-c', label: true, signals: [] },
  ];
  return [
    classification('empty signals do not flag', [], false, 'eligible-observations'),
    classification('three distant range denials flag', burst, true, 'eligible-observations'),
    classification('cooldown re-presses do not count', burst.map((signal) => ({ ...signal, reason: 'cooldown' })), false, 'eligible-observations'),
    classification('range at the minimum distance does not count', burst.map((signal) => ({ ...signal, distanceSquared: 250_000 })), false, 'eligible-observations'),
    classification('near-boundary denials do not accumulate', [range(1, 62_501), range(2, 249_999), range(3, 250_000), range(4)], false, 'eligible-observations'),
    classification('the left window edge is excluded', [range(1), range(11)], false, 'window-boundaries', { threshold: 2, windowTicks: 10 }),
    classification('one tick inside the window counts', [range(1), range(10)], true, 'window-boundaries', { threshold: 2, windowTicks: 10 }),
    classification('an earlier qualifying burst remains a flag after quiet time', [...burst, { tick: 100, reason: 'cooldown', distanceSquared: 1_000_000 }], true, 'window-boundaries'),
    classification('lifetime total is not a window total', [range(1), range(22), range(43)], false, 'window-boundaries'),
    classification('expire every old observation, not only one', [range(1), range(2), range(21), range(22)], false, 'window-boundaries'),
    classification('equal-tick observations count separately in validated policy input', [range(5), range(5)], true, 'window-boundaries', { threshold: 2 }),
    classification('zero minimum still uses strict distance', [range(1, 0), range(2, 0), range(3, 0)], false, 'eligible-observations', { minDistanceMm: 0 }),
    classification('a positive distance qualifies with zero minimum', [range(1, 1)], true, 'eligible-observations', { threshold: 1, minDistanceMm: 0 }),
    evaluation('one case gets one vote and rates use their own denominators', mixed,
      { total: 8, tp: 2, fp: 1, tn: 2, fn: 3, precision: 2 / 3, recall: 2 / 5, falsePositiveRate: 1 / 3,
        flags: [true, true, false, false, true, false, false, false] }, 'one-case-one-vote'),
    evaluation('identical signals keep the same decision when the label changes', [
      { id: 'same-negative', label: false, signals: burst }, { id: 'same-positive', label: true, signals: burst },
    ], { total: 2, tp: 1, fp: 1, tn: 0, fn: 0, precision: 1 / 2, recall: 1, falsePositiveRate: 1,
      flags: [true, true] }, 'labels-are-not-features'),
    evaluation('many observations still count as one negative case', [{ id: 'one-negative', label: false, signals: [...burst, range(4), range(5), range(6)] }],
      { total: 1, tp: 0, fp: 1, tn: 0, fn: 0, precision: 0, recall: null, falsePositiveRate: 1, flags: [true] }, 'one-case-one-vote'),
    evaluation('no positives and no predictions leave precision and recall undefined', [{ id: 'quiet-negative', label: false, signals: [] }],
      { total: 1, tp: 0, fp: 0, tn: 1, fn: 0, precision: null, recall: null, falsePositiveRate: 0, flags: [false] }, 'counts-and-rates'),
    evaluation('no negative cases leave false-positive rate undefined', [{ id: 'quiet-positive', label: true, signals: [] }],
      { total: 1, tp: 0, fp: 0, tn: 0, fn: 1, precision: null, recall: 0, falsePositiveRate: null, flags: [false] }, 'counts-and-rates'),
    evaluation('an empty case set has zero counts and undefined rates', [],
      { total: 0, tp: 0, fp: 0, tn: 0, fn: 0, precision: null, recall: null, falsePositiveRate: null, flags: [] }, 'counts-and-rates'),
  ].map(clone);
}

function evidence(value) {
  try {
    return JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(value, (_key, item) => {
      if (item === undefined) return { type: 'undefined' };
      if (typeof item === 'number' && !Number.isFinite(item)) return { type: 'number', value: String(item) };
      if (['bigint', 'function', 'symbol'].includes(typeof item)) return { type: typeof item, value: String(item) };
      return item;
    }));
  } catch {
    return { type: 'non-JSON result' };
  }
}

/** Owner-side assessment. Preserve expected/actual/input and a targeted repair pointer. */
export async function assess(candidate) {
  const missing = ['classify', 'evaluate'].filter((name) => typeof candidate?.[name] !== 'function');
  if (missing.length > 0) return { passed: false, criteria: missing.map((name) => ({
    name: `export ${name}`, passed: false, error: {
      message: `Export ${name} as declared in the contract.`, expected: 'function', actual: typeof candidate?.[name],
      source: 'LEARNER.md#the-contract',
    },
  })) };
  const criteria = [];
  for (const item of cases()) {
    let actual;
    const args = clone(item.args);
    try { actual = await candidate[item.method](...args); }
    catch (error) { actual = { threw: String(error?.message ?? error) }; }
    const changedInput = !isDeepStrictEqual(args, item.args);
    const passed = isDeepStrictEqual(actual, item.expected) && !changedInput;
    const criterion = { name: item.name, passed };
    if (!passed) criterion.error = {
      message: changedInput ? `Preserve the supplied inputs while evaluating: ${item.name}.` : `The result violates this requirement: ${item.name}.`,
      input: evidence(item.args), expected: item.expected,
      actual: changedInput ? { result: evidence(actual), inputAfter: evidence(args) } : evidence(actual),
      source: `LEARNER.md#${item.section}`,
    };
    criteria.push(criterion);
  }
  return { passed: criteria.every((item) => item.passed), criteria };
}

```

`courses/anti-cheat-engineering/courier-lab/evaluation/policy.mjs`:

```mjs
/** Flag a case when any open-left, closed-right window has enough eligible denials. */
export function classify(signals, settings) {
  const minimumSquared = settings.minDistanceMm ** 2;
  const ticks = [];
  let first = 0;
  for (const signal of signals) {
    if (signal.reason !== 'range' || signal.distanceSquared <= minimumSquared) continue;
    ticks.push(signal.tick);
    while (ticks[first] <= signal.tick - settings.windowTicks) first += 1;
    if (ticks.length - first >= settings.threshold) return true;
  }
  return false;
}

/** Each case gets one prediction. Labels are consulted only to score predictions. */
export function evaluate(cases, settings) {
  const decisions = cases.map(({ id, signals }) => ({ id, flagged: classify(signals, settings) }));
  const metrics = { total: cases.length, tp: 0, fp: 0, tn: 0, fn: 0 };
  for (let index = 0; index < cases.length; index += 1) {
    const { label } = cases[index];
    const { flagged } = decisions[index];
    if (flagged) {
      metrics[label ? 'tp' : 'fp'] += 1;
      continue;
    }
    metrics[label ? 'fn' : 'tn'] += 1;
  }
  const rate = (numerator, denominator) => denominator === 0 ? null : numerator / denominator;
  return { decisions, metrics: {
    ...metrics,
    precision: rate(metrics.tp, metrics.tp + metrics.fp),
    recall: rate(metrics.tp, metrics.tp + metrics.fn),
    falsePositiveRate: rate(metrics.fp, metrics.fp + metrics.tn),
  } };
}

`courses/anti-cheat-engineering/courier-lab/evaluation/report.mjs`:

```mjs
import { createHash } from 'node:crypto';
import { CORPUS_VERSION, SPLIT_IDS, casesForSplit, loadCorpus } from './corpus.mjs';

export const REPORT_LIMIT = 'Counts and rates describe these fourteen scripted controls only. They do not estimate human false-positive rates, production prevalence or detection of all automation. Flags are advisory.';
const copy = (value) => JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(value));

function stableJson(value) {
  if (Array.isArray(value)) return `[${value.map(stableJson).join(',')}]`;
  if (value && typeof value === 'object') return `{${Object.keys(value).sort().map((key) => `${JSON.stringify(key)}:${stableJson(value[key])}`).join(',')}}`;
  return JSON.stringify(value);
}

export function hashValue(value) {
  return createHash('sha256').update(stableJson(value)).digest('hex');
}

function settingsCopy(settings) {
  if (!settings || Object.keys(settings).sort().join(',') !== 'minDistanceMm,threshold,windowTicks') throw new Error('Settings must contain exactly threshold, windowTicks and minDistanceMm.');
  if (!Number.isSafeInteger(settings.threshold) || settings.threshold <= 0) throw new Error('threshold must be a positive integer.');
  if (!Number.isSafeInteger(settings.windowTicks) || settings.windowTicks <= 0) throw new Error('windowTicks must be a positive integer.');
  if (!Number.isFinite(settings.minDistanceMm) || settings.minDistanceMm < 0) throw new Error('minDistanceMm must be finite and nonnegative.');
  return copy(settings);
}

function indistinguishablePair(corpus, sections) {
  const splits = Object.keys(SPLIT_IDS).map((split) => {
    const pair = ['honest-delivery', 'valid-automation'].map((family) => corpus.cases.find((item) => item.id === `${split}/${family}`));
    const decisions = pair.map(({ id }) => sections[split].result.decisions?.find((decision) => decision.id === id) ?? null);
    return {
      split, caseIds: pair.map(({ id }) => id),
      declaredAutomation: pair.map((item) => item.declaredAutomation),
      identicalSignals: stableJson(pair[0].signals) === stableJson(pair[1].signals),
      decisions: copy(decisions), sameDecision: decisions.every((item) => typeof item?.flagged === 'boolean') && decisions[0].flagged === decisions[1].flagged,
    };
  });
  return {
    claim: 'The legal twins have identical signals but different declared automation metadata. A deterministic signal-only policy cannot distinguish their automation status. Both have a negative rule-violation label, so treating both as legal is not a missed violation.',
    splits,
  };
}

/** Make this commitment before viewing the evaluation split. The caller preserves it with the attempt. */
export async function prepareEvaluation({ settings, source, corpus } = {}) {
  if (typeof source !== 'string' || source.trim().length === 0) throw new Error('Provide the exact candidate source before evaluation.');
  const validated = await loadCorpus(corpus);
  const chosen = settingsCopy(settings);
  return Object.freeze({
    schema: 'courier-evaluation-plan-v1', corpusVersion: CORPUS_VERSION,
    settings: Object.freeze(chosen), settingsSha256: hashValue(chosen),
    sourceSha256: createHash('sha256').update(source).digest('hex'),
    corpusSha256: hashValue(validated), splitIds: copy(SPLIT_IDS),
  });
}

/** Run both splits separately using the previously committed settings and source identity. */
export async function runEvaluation(candidate, { plan, source, corpus } = {}) {
  if (typeof candidate?.evaluate !== 'function') throw new Error('Candidate must export evaluate(cases, settings).');
  const validated = await loadCorpus(corpus);
  const expected = await prepareEvaluation({ settings: plan?.settings, source, corpus: validated });
  if (stableJson(plan) !== stableJson(expected)) throw new Error('Evaluation plan changed: commit settings, source and corpus again before running.');
  const sections = {};
  for (const split of Object.keys(SPLIT_IDS)) {
    const cases = casesForSplit(validated, split);
    const positiveLabels = cases.filter((item) => item.label).length;
    const negativeLabels = cases.length - positiveLabels;
    const result = await candidate.evaluate(cases, copy(plan.settings));
    sections[split] = { caseIds: [...SPLIT_IDS[split]], positiveLabels, negativeLabels, result: copy(result) };
  }
  return {
    schema: 'courier-evaluation-report-v1', plan: copy(plan), ...sections,
    noPositiveNoPrediction: copy(await candidate.evaluate([{ id: 'diagnostic/negative-quiet', label: false, signals: [] }], copy(plan.settings))),
    indistinguishablePair: indistinguishablePair(validated, sections),
    labelDefinition: validated.labelDefinition, limitations: REPORT_LIMIT,
  };
}
