`courses/anti-cheat-engineering/courier-lab/integrity/LEARNER.md`:

```md
# Check owned runtime bytes

Implementation reference for **M5: integrity**. Start with [the guided learning route at `/learn`](/learn) on the reference server, then return here for the exact source contract. This Markdown file does not submit answers or certify mastery. Use the [support and attempt workflow](../learning-support/README.md) for worked siblings, gradual guidance and help recording. A prepared source workspace need not serve `/learn`; keep the reference server open for that route.

An edited `engine.mjs` can still claim to be the same release. Build a startup policy that permits an approved runtime and refuses missing, extra or changed files before that runtime starts.

This lab assumes the earlier Courier exercises and JavaScript objects, arrays and functions. Your artifact is `integrity/policy.mjs`, plus an explanation in `response.md`. You do not need to write cryptography or filesystem code.

## Reference and observation

A **manifest** is an owner-approved list of expected paths and file hashes. A **hash** is a value computed from file bytes; this lab uses SHA-256, represented as 64 hexadecimal characters. Hashing `engine.mjs` after a one-character edit normally produces a different value, even if the edit is only a comment. The comparison concerns exact bytes, not whether the code still looks equivalent.

An **observed inventory** is a list of paths and hashes computed by the supplied file reader. The file reader reads regular files, refuses symbolic links and applies file-count and byte limits. A symbolic link is a filesystem entry that points to another path. Refusing links keeps a listed file from silently naming bytes elsewhere. The launcher chooses its runtime paths independently of the manifest; unlisted files are outside this explicit comparison.

The manifest and the observed inventory have different roles. The manifest says what the owner approved. The observation says what was read now. Replacing the approved hashes with the observed hashes makes changed files pass without approval.

Before continuing, put the required first answers or explicit skip reasons in `predictions.json` and explanations in `response.md`. They are explanations for later review, not automatically graded items: an original approved package; the same release with changed engine bytes; a supported new release with new approved hashes; and an extra observed file. State which result each should produce and why. Keep these answers when you repair the code.

## Follow one comparison

Consider an owner-approved one-file package, `settings.json`. Its expected hash starts with `a91c`. The reader reports the same path, with a hash starting with `b84e`.

First validate the approved record so its path and hash are usable. Then check that the release appears in the supported list. Next compare the path sets: both contain exactly `settings.json`, so there is no missing or extra file. Finally compare the complete hashes. These hashes differ, so the result is `{ok:false, reason:'digest'}`. A recognized release name cannot cancel that mismatch.

Compare this reasoning with your predictions. A missing file fails before hash comparison because there is no complete inventory to compare. An approved update may have different hashes from the older release: compare it with its own approved manifest, not with yesterday's hashes. The fixture update increases the runtime's bounded history capacity from 4096 to 8192 entries while preserving initial gameplay and the existing API. Approval also requires deciding whether that capacity and its cost are acceptable; a matching hash does not make that decision for the owner.

## Your editable policy

Prepare the exercise from the project directory:

```sh
npm run core:prepare -- integrity
```

Change into the exact workspace path printed by preparation, including any chosen name.

Edit `integrity/policy.mjs`. It exports `checkPackage({manifest, observed, supported})`. This is a **pure policy**: it decides from the supplied values and does not change them. It does not read files, fetch data or start the game. The owner-side launcher separately observes files, calls this policy and starts the runtime only after a successful result. Keeping these steps separate lets the same decision be tested without starting a server for every case.

The input is shaped like this; the displayed hash is abbreviated for reading and would fail validation as written:

```js
{
  manifest: {
    schema: 1,
    packageId: 'courier-runtime',
    release: 'courier-runtime-1',
    files: [{ path: 'engine.mjs', sha256: 'a91c…64 hex characters total' }]
  },
  observed: [{ path: 'engine.mjs', sha256: 'a91c…64 hex characters total' }],
  supported: ['courier-runtime-1', 'courier-runtime-2']
}
```

You may reorganize the implementation. The template supplies no completed comparison. Match files by path: changing the array order must not change a verdict. Do not sort an input array in place, because the caller may need its original observation later.

## Decide in order

The order makes a failure explain the first usable decision. For example, a malformed reference cannot tell you whether a package is approved.

| Decision | Required behavior | Result on failure |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Validate the reference | Exactly `schema`, `packageId`, `release`, `files`; schema `1`; package ID `courier-runtime`; nonblank release string; nonempty files list of exact `{path,sha256}` records | `schema` |
| Validate supported releases | An array of nonblank strings; an empty array supports nothing | `schema` |
| Check release support | Exact release string occurs in `supported` | `unsupported-release` |
| Validate and compare inventory | Every observed entry has exactly `path` and `sha256`; all paths are safe and unique; the two lists contain exactly the same paths | `inventory` |
| Compare hashes | Every path has equal complete SHA-256 values; hex letter case is irrelevant | `digest` |
| All decisions pass | Permit this observed package | `{ok:true, reason:'verified'}` |

Every failure returns `{ok:false, reason:'the-reason'}` with the table's reason. A malformed observed hash belongs to `inventory`; unequal, well-formed hashes belong to `digest`.

A **safe relative path** has 1–512 characters and names a file below the package root. It cannot start with `/`, contain a backslash, colon or control character, or contain an empty, `.` or `..` slash-separated segment. `rules/movement.mjs` is valid. `../movement.mjs`, `rules//movement.mjs` and `C:movement.mjs` are not. File matching and release spelling are case-sensitive, but an inventory must not contain two names differing only by letter case: `engine.mjs` and `ENGINE.mjs` can name the same file on some systems. Each segment uses only ASCII letters, digits, dot, underscore or hyphen. Hash values accept either hex letter case. Checking duplicate paths matters even when their hashes match: duplicates cannot stand in for an absent file.

Implement these decisions, then submit a check:

```sh
npm run core:check -- --assistance "none"
```

Replace `none` with the actual hints, reference material or AI help you used. The checker records captured source, the exact prompt and version, help and results as separate attempts. An import error, thrown exception or timeout means the run failed; it is not evidence that your policy detected a changed package.

## Inspect, repair and explain

Separate the first failed decision from its later consequences before changing the policy.

## Build in three checked milestones

1. **Separate structure from trust.** Trace the worked one-file comparison above. Completion: the approved package lists `a.mjs` and `b.mjs`, but the observation lists `a.mjs` twice. Decide the failure phase before comparing hashes. A duplicate is not evidence that both expected files exist.
2. **Match paths, then bytes.** Write the path-set check independently of list order, then compare each corresponding complete hash. Hand-check one reversed inventory and one changed, well-formed digest. Avoid sorting the input itself; callers retain the original observation.
3. **Run the boundary.** Use the core check's first failed criterion to identify structure, release, inventory or digest. Then use the disposable runtime experiment below to distinguish a correct pure verdict from an actual refused startup.

<details><summary>Hint 1 — ask what the record can establish</summary>

A malformed reference cannot establish approval. Validate it before trusting a release name or looking for matching bytes; this gives a meaningful first failure.

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 2 — check inventory membership separately</summary>

Build path-to-hash lookups after path validation. Check uniqueness and equal path sets before comparing any values, so duplicate entries cannot conceal a missing file.

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 3 — worked sibling, after a saved attempt</summary>

The worked `settings.json` package has equal path sets but different complete hashes, so its failure is `digest`. The two-`a.mjs` completion has a defective inventory before hash comparison. Record this as assistance; implement the complete ordered decision table yourself.

</details>

## Inspect the first failed criterion

Read the first failed criterion and its expected and actual values. A missing-file failure points to inventory comparison; an approved-update failure points to comparing against the wrong reference or hard-coding one release. The criterion links back to the decision table. Repair the responsible decision, append your explanation in `response.md`, and run again. Keep the first prediction and failed evidence alongside the revision.

A pass means the submitted policy agrees with the stated cases, including actual runtime bytes and a compatible update. It does not prove that every possible input is correct. The local expected manifest must remain separate from the package being checked: someone who controls both can change both and make a modified package pass. There is no signature, identity authentication, third-party game integration or proof that a remote client is executing the checked bytes. The package must also remain unchanged between observation and import; this lab does not provide a secure concurrent update mechanism.

## Run your policy at the actual startup boundary

From the reference project, create a disposable copy of the owned runtime:

```sh
npm run runtime:copy -- artifacts/package-trial
npm run start:verified -- --package-root artifacts/package-trial --policy artifacts/core/integrity-workspace/integrity/policy.mjs
```

The `--policy` path is your completed source file. The approved manifest remains in the reference project. Stop the server with Ctrl-C, append a comment to the copied `artifacts/package-trial/engine.mjs`, then repeat the startup command. Even a comment changes the bytes, so the old reference must refuse startup. Restore the copied file from the reference before trying a legitimate run again. Do not edit the original runtime or approve the changed copy to make this test pass.

This checks actual disk bytes before a real server import. It does not prove that bytes cannot change later, or that an owner who controls the launcher cannot change the check. The separate approved-update tests change both the reviewed package and its approved reference deliberately; a release label alone does not approve new bytes.

## Transfer for review

A level editor loads a project with required core files and optional community plug-ins. Yesterday's approved project had no plug-ins; today's project adds one. Design where approval of core files and plug-ins should live and how their inventories should be formed before any imports. Explain which new bytes require review, when a missing plug-in should block loading, and what happens if the project can rewrite its own approval record. Give one legal update and one refused update as concrete path/hash examples. This is a new design problem; the executable checker does not grade the explanation.

## Capture, compare and try a fresh case

In a newly prepared workspace, put the required first answers in `predictions.json`; use `response.md` for explanations and later repairs. Keep each question ID and its wording unchanged. Fill an `answer` or an explicit `skipReason` for every question before the first source check. A blank row refuses feedback rather than silently recording an empty attempt. The practice command records your response before revealing its feedback. These prose responses are preserved and ungraded; they are separate from source-check results and `/learn` mastery.

Use the scripts generated in your workspace. Older prepared workspaces may retain the earlier response-only format; do not replace their original records with new templates. Record any worked-example views, final hints, reference code or AI help in your assistance declaration.

// Author-only calibration controls. These are never copied into a learner workspace.
import { checkPackage } from './policy.mjs';

/** An independently structured correct solution: validate, sort, then zip. */
export function sortedPolicy(input) {
  const hasKeys = (value, names) => value !== null && typeof value === 'object'
    && !Array.isArray(value) && Object.keys(value).sort().join('|') === [...names].sort().join('|');
  const validPath = (value) => typeof value === 'string' && value.length > 0 && value.length <= 512
    && !value.startsWith('/') && !/[\\:\x00-\x1f\x7f]/.test(value)
    && value.split('/').every((part) => /^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$/.test(part) && !['.', '..'].includes(part));
  const inventory = (items) => {
    if (!Array.isArray(items) || items.length === 0) return null;
    const sorted = [...items].sort((a, b) => String(a?.path) < String(b?.path) ? -1 : Number(String(a?.path) > String(b?.path)));
    const good = sorted.every((item, index) => hasKeys(item, ['path', 'sha256']) && validPath(item.path)
      && typeof item.sha256 === 'string' && /^[\da-f]{64}$/i.test(item.sha256)
      && (index === 0 || sorted[index - 1].path !== item.path));
    const unique = good && new Set(sorted.map(item => item.path.toLowerCase())).size === sorted.length;
    return unique ? sorted : null;
  };
  const refused = (reason) => ({ ok: false, reason });
  if (!hasKeys(input, ['manifest', 'observed', 'supported'])) return refused('schema');
  const { manifest, observed, supported } = input;
  if (!hasKeys(manifest, ['schema', 'packageId', 'release', 'files'])) return refused('schema');
  if (manifest.schema !== 1 || manifest.packageId !== 'courier-runtime') return refused('schema');
  if (typeof manifest.release !== 'string' || !manifest.release.trim()) return refused('schema');
  const expected = inventory(manifest.files);
  if (!expected || !Array.isArray(supported)) return refused('schema');
  if (supported.some((release) => typeof release !== 'string' || !release.trim())) return refused('schema');
  if (supported.indexOf(manifest.release) < 0) return refused('unsupported-release');
  const actual = inventory(observed);
  if (!actual || actual.length !== expected.length) return refused('inventory');
  if (actual.some((item, index) => item.path !== expected[index].path)) return refused('inventory');
  if (actual.some((item, index) => item.sha256.toUpperCase() !== expected[index].sha256.toUpperCase())) return refused('digest');
  return { ok: true, reason: 'verified' };
}

function patched(input, change) {
  const copy = structuredClone(input);
  change(copy);
  return checkPackage(copy);
}

export const correctPolicies = Object.freeze([
  { name: 'map-policy', checkPackage },
  { name: 'sorted-policy', checkPackage: sortedPolicy },
]);

export const wrongPolicies = Object.freeze([
  { name: 'always-verified', checkPackage: () => ({ ok: true, reason: 'verified' }) },
  { name: 'always-refused', checkPackage: () => ({ ok: false, reason: 'schema' }) },
  { name: 'release-only', checkPackage: ({ manifest, supported }) => supported.includes(manifest?.release)
    ? { ok: true, reason: 'verified' } : { ok: false, reason: 'unsupported-release' } },
  { name: 'trust-observed-digests', checkPackage: (input) => patched(input, (copy) => {
    copy.manifest.files = copy.manifest.files?.map((file) => ({ ...file,
      sha256: copy.observed?.find((actual) => actual.path === file.path)?.sha256 ?? file.sha256 }));
  }) },
  { name: 'ignore-missing-files', checkPackage: (input) => patched(input, (copy) => {
    copy.observed = [...(copy.observed ?? []), ...(copy.manifest.files ?? [])
      .filter((file) => !copy.observed?.some((actual) => actual.path === file.path))];
  }) },
  { name: 'ignore-extra-files', checkPackage: (input) => patched(input, (copy) => {
    copy.observed = copy.observed?.filter((file) => copy.manifest.files?.some((expected) => file.path === expected.path));
  }) },
  { name: 'ignore-release-support', checkPackage: (input) => patched(input, (copy) => {
    copy.supported = [...(copy.supported ?? []), copy.manifest?.release];
  }) },
  { name: 'version-one-only', checkPackage: (input) => input.manifest?.release === 'courier-runtime-2'
    ? { ok: false, reason: 'unsupported-release' } : checkPackage(input) },
  { name: 'erase-manifest-duplicates', checkPackage: (input) => patched(input, (copy) => {
    if (Array.isArray(copy.manifest.files)) copy.manifest.files = [...new Map(copy.manifest.files.map((file) => [file.path, file])).values()];
  }) },
  { name: 'sort-input-in-place', checkPackage: (input) => {
    if (Array.isArray(input.observed)) input.observed.sort((a, b) => String(a?.path).localeCompare(String(b?.path)));
    return checkPackage(input);
  } },
]);

import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
import { mkdtemp, readFile, realpath, rm, writeFile } from 'node:fs/promises';
import { tmpdir } from 'node:os';
import { join } from 'node:path';
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
import { inspect } from 'node:util';
import { observePackage } from './package.mjs';

// Deliberately independent of any manifest's contents. The launcher maintains
// its own complete transitive runtime inventory; these are the fixture's inputs.
export const FIXTURE_RUNTIME_PATHS = Object.freeze(['engine.mjs', 'admission.mjs', 'defense.mjs', 'protocol.mjs']);
const SUPPORTED = ['courier-runtime-1', 'courier-runtime-2'];

/** Author fixture: increase bounded history capacity without changing gameplay. */
export async function writeCompatibleUpdate(project, destination) {
  for (const path of FIXTURE_RUNTIME_PATHS) await writeFile(join(destination, path), await readFile(join(project, path)));
  const engine = await readFile(join(destination, 'engine.mjs'), 'utf8');
  assert.ok(engine.includes('const MAX_EVENTS = 4096;'), 'The compatible-update fixture must name the current history capacity.');
  await writeFile(join(destination, 'engine.mjs'), engine.replace('const MAX_EVENTS = 4096;', 'const MAX_EVENTS = 8192;'));
}

function manifest(files, release = SUPPORTED[0]) {
  return { schema: 1, packageId: 'courier-runtime', release, files: structuredClone(files) };
}

function example(name, input, expected, rule) {
  return { name, input, expected, rule };
}

function evidenceValue(value) {
  if (value === undefined) return { type: 'undefined' };
  try {
    return JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(value));
  } catch {
    return { type: typeof value, display: inspect(value) };
  }
}

function assertionDetails(error) {
  return {
    message: error.message,
    code: error.code,
    operator: error.operator,
    expected: evidenceValue(error.expected),
    actual: evidenceValue(error.actual),
  };
}

/** Actual file bytes underlie both the initial and compatible-update cases. */
export async function integrityCases() {
  const project = await realpath(fileURLToPath(new URL('../', import.meta.url)));
  const files = await observePackage(project, { paths: FIXTURE_RUNTIME_PATHS });
  const original = { manifest: manifest(files), observed: files, supported: SUPPORTED };
  const cases = [];
  const add = (name, change, reason, rule) => {
    const input = structuredClone(original);
    change(input);
    cases.push(example(name, input, { ok: reason === 'verified', reason }, rule));
  };
  add('approved runtime bytes', () => {}, 'verified', 'The complete approved inventory must remain usable.');
  add('inventory order is irrelevant', (input) => input.observed.reverse(), 'verified', 'Match by path, not array position.');
  add('hex letter case is irrelevant', (input) => input.observed.forEach((file) => { file.sha256 = file.sha256.toUpperCase(); }),
    'verified', 'Hex letter case does not change a SHA-256 value.');
  add('missing runtime file', (input) => input.observed.pop(), 'inventory', 'Every approved path must be observed.');
  add('extra runtime file', (input) => input.observed.push({ path: 'extra.mjs', sha256: files[0].sha256 }),
    'inventory', 'An observed path outside the approved inventory must refuse startup.');
  add('same count different path', (input) => { input.observed[0].path = 'replacement.mjs'; },
    'inventory', 'Equal file counts do not establish equal inventories.');
  add('duplicate observation', (input) => { input.observed[1] = structuredClone(input.observed[0]); },
    'inventory', 'Each observed path must occur exactly once.');
  add('case-alias observation', input => { input.observed.push({ ...input.observed[0], path: input.observed[0].path.toUpperCase() }); }, 'inventory', 'Portable inventories reject paths differing only in letter case.');
  add('case-alias approved path', input => { input.manifest.files.push({ ...input.manifest.files[0], path: input.manifest.files[0].path.toUpperCase() }); }, 'schema', 'Portable approved inventories reject case aliases.');
  add('malformed observation', (input) => { input.observed[0].sha256 = 'not-a-digest'; },
    'inventory', 'Malformed observation entries are not a usable inventory.');
  add('unsupported release', (input) => { input.manifest.release = 'courier-runtime-99'; },
    'unsupported-release', 'An unchanged digest does not make an unknown release compatible.');
  add('schema version', (input) => { input.manifest.schema = 2; }, 'schema', 'Only manifest schema 1 is understood.');
  add('wrong package identity', (input) => { input.manifest.packageId = 'another-runtime'; }, 'schema', 'The reference must name courier-runtime.');
  add('blank release', (input) => { input.manifest.release = ' '; }, 'schema', 'A release is a nonempty identifier.');
  add('unrecognized manifest field', (input) => { input.manifest.approved = true; }, 'schema', 'The manifest shape has exactly four fields.');
  add('invalid approved digest', (input) => { input.manifest.files[0].sha256 = '00'; }, 'schema', 'An approved SHA-256 has 64 hexadecimal characters.');
  add('duplicate approved path', (input) => input.manifest.files.push(structuredClone(input.manifest.files[0])),
    'schema', 'Duplicate paths make the approved reference ambiguous.');
  add('empty approved inventory', (input) => { input.manifest.files = []; }, 'schema', 'An empty reference cannot verify this runtime.');
  add('malformed supported list', (input) => { input.supported = [1]; }, 'schema', 'Supported releases must be strings.');
  for (const path of ['../escape.mjs', '/absolute.mjs', 'dir/../escape.mjs', 'dir\\file.mjs', 'dir//file.mjs', './engine.mjs', 'C:engine.mjs', 'nul\u0000.mjs', 'space name.mjs', 'bang!.mjs']) {
    add(`unsafe approved path ${JSON.stringify(path)}`, (input) => { input.manifest.files[0].path = path; },
      'schema', 'Use safe, unique relative paths; see LEARNER.md#decide-in-order.');
  }

  const temporary = await realpath(await mkdtemp(join(tmpdir(), 'ivy-integrity-cases-')));
  try {
    await writeCompatibleUpdate(project, temporary);
    const updated = await observePackage(temporary, { paths: FIXTURE_RUNTIME_PATHS });
    cases.push(example('actual runtime byte change', { ...structuredClone(original), observed: updated },
      { ok: false, reason: 'digest' }, 'The old approved reference must refuse changed engine.mjs bytes.'));
    cases.push(example('supported release label alone', { manifest: manifest(files, SUPPORTED[1]), observed: updated, supported: SUPPORTED },
      { ok: false, reason: 'digest' }, 'A supported release label does not approve new file bytes.'));
    cases.push(example('approved compatible update', { manifest: manifest(updated, SUPPORTED[1]), observed: updated, supported: SUPPORTED },
      { ok: true, reason: 'verified' }, 'A separately approved reference and supported release must permit the updated runtime.'));
  } finally {
    await rm(temporary, { recursive: true, force: true });
  }
  return cases;
}

/** A candidate exception is a runner failure; a returned wrong verdict is feedback. */
export async function assess(candidate, { onCriterion = () => {} } = {}) {
  if (typeof candidate?.checkPackage !== 'function') throw new Error('The policy must export checkPackage.');
  const criteria = [];
  for (const item of await integrityCases()) {
    const input = structuredClone(item.input);
    onCriterion(item.name);
    const before = structuredClone(input);
    const actual = await candidate.checkPackage(input);
    try {
      assert.deepEqual(actual, item.expected, `${item.rule} See LEARNER.md#decide-in-order.`);
      assert.deepEqual(input, before, 'The policy must not mutate its inputs. See LEARNER.md#your-editable-policy.');
      criteria.push({ name: item.name, passed: true });
    } catch (error) {
      criteria.push({ name: item.name, passed: false, error: assertionDetails(error) });
    }
  }
  return { passed: criteria.every((criterion) => criterion.passed), criteria };
}

`courses/anti-cheat-engineering/courier-lab/integrity/package.mjs`:

```mjs
import { createHash } from 'node:crypto';
import { constants } from 'node:fs';
import { lstat, open, realpath } from 'node:fs/promises';
import { isAbsolute, relative, resolve, sep } from 'node:path';

export const DEFAULT_LIMITS = Object.freeze({ maxFiles: 64, maxFileBytes: 1_048_576, maxTotalBytes: 8_388_608 });

function fail(message) {
  throw new Error(`Package observation refused: ${message}`);
}

function safePath(path) {
  if (typeof path !== 'string' || path.length === 0 || path.length > 512) return false;
  if (/[\\:\x00-\x1f\x7f]/.test(path) || path.startsWith('/')) return false;
  return path.split('/').every((part) => /^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$/.test(part) && part !== '.' && part !== '..');
}

function limitsFor(options) {
  const limits = { ...DEFAULT_LIMITS };
  for (const name of Object.keys(limits)) {
    if (options[name] === undefined) continue;
    if (!Number.isSafeInteger(options[name]) || options[name] < 1) fail(`${name} must be a positive safe integer`);
    limits[name] = options[name];
  }
  return limits;
}

function sameIdentity(first, second) {
  return first.dev === second.dev && first.ino === second.ino;
}

function unchanged(first, second) {
  return sameIdentity(first, second) && first.size === second.size
    && first.mtimeNs === second.mtimeNs && first.ctimeNs === second.ctimeNs;
}

function inside(root, path) {
  const part = relative(root, path);
  return part !== '' && part !== '..' && !part.startsWith(`..${sep}`) && !isAbsolute(part);
}

async function inspectPath(root, path) {
  const ancestry = [];
  const parts = path.split('/');
  let location = root;
  for (const [index, part] of parts.entries()) {
    location = resolve(location, part);
    const stat = await lstat(location, { bigint: true });
    if (stat.isSymbolicLink()) fail(`symbolic link at ${path}`);
    if (index < parts.length - 1 && !stat.isDirectory()) fail(`non-directory parent at ${path}`);
    ancestry.push({ location, stat });
  }
  if (!ancestry.at(-1).stat.isFile()) fail(`not a regular file: ${path}`);
  if (!inside(root, await realpath(location))) fail(`path escapes the package: ${path}`);
  return ancestry;
}

async function stableAncestry(ancestry, path) {
  for (const item of ancestry) {
    const now = await lstat(item.location, { bigint: true });
    if (now.isSymbolicLink() || !sameIdentity(item.stat, now)) fail(`path changed while reading ${path}`);
  }
}

async function digestFile(root, path, limits, remaining) {
  const ancestry = await inspectPath(root, path);
  const before = ancestry.at(-1).stat;
  if (before.size > BigInt(limits.maxFileBytes)) fail(`file size limit exceeded: ${path}`);
  if (before.size > BigInt(remaining)) fail('total size limit exceeded');
  const handle = await open(resolve(root, path), constants.O_RDONLY | constants.O_NOFOLLOW | constants.O_NONBLOCK);
  try {
    const opened = await handle.stat({ bigint: true });
    if (!opened.isFile() || !unchanged(before, opened)) fail(`file changed before reading ${path}`);
    const digest = createHash('sha256');
    const buffer = Buffer.alloc(65_536);
    let bytes = 0;
    for (;;) {
      const read = await handle.read(buffer, 0, Math.min(buffer.length, limits.maxFileBytes - bytes + 1), bytes);
      if (read.bytesRead === 0) break;
      bytes += read.bytesRead;
      if (bytes > limits.maxFileBytes || bytes > remaining) fail(`size limit exceeded while reading ${path}`);
      digest.update(buffer.subarray(0, read.bytesRead));
    }
    if (BigInt(bytes) !== opened.size || !unchanged(opened, await handle.stat({ bigint: true }))) fail(`file changed while reading ${path}`);
    await stableAncestry(ancestry, path);
    if (!inside(root, await realpath(resolve(root, path)))) fail(`path escapes the package: ${path}`);
    return { bytes, sha256: digest.digest('hex') };
  } finally {
    await handle.close();
  }
}

/**
 * Hash an explicit, independently chosen runtime inventory. Paths must not be
 * derived from an unapproved manifest. Non-inventoried files are outside this check.
 * Callers must keep the package unchanged between observation and import.
 */
export async function observePackage(root, options = {}) {
  if (typeof root !== 'string' || !root) fail('root must be a directory path');
  if (!options || typeof options !== 'object' || Array.isArray(options)) fail('options must be an object');
  const limits = limitsFor(options);
  const { paths } = options;
  if (!Array.isArray(paths) || paths.length === 0 || paths.length > limits.maxFiles) fail('invalid file inventory or file count limit');
  if (paths.some((path) => !safePath(path)) || new Set(paths.map(path => path.toLowerCase())).size !== paths.length) fail('unsafe or duplicate relative path');
  const absoluteRoot = resolve(root);
  const rootStat = await lstat(absoluteRoot, { bigint: true });
  if (!rootStat.isDirectory() || rootStat.isSymbolicLink()) fail('root must be a real directory');
  const canonicalRoot = await realpath(absoluteRoot);
  if (canonicalRoot !== absoluteRoot) fail('root has a symbolic-link ancestor; use its real path');
  const observed = [];
  let total = 0;
  for (const path of [...paths].sort()) {
    const result = await digestFile(canonicalRoot, path, limits, limits.maxTotalBytes - total);
    total += result.bytes;
    observed.push({ path, sha256: result.sha256 });
  }
  const after = await lstat(absoluteRoot, { bigint: true });
  if (!after.isDirectory() || !sameIdentity(rootStat, after)) fail('root changed while reading');
  return observed;
}

```mjs
const DIGEST = /^[a-fA-F0-9]{64}$/;

function record(value, keys) {
  if (!value || typeof value !== 'object' || Array.isArray(value)) return false;
  const actual = Object.keys(value);
  return actual.length === keys.length && keys.every((key) => Object.hasOwn(value, key));
}

function safePath(path) {
  if (typeof path !== 'string' || path.length === 0 || path.length > 512) return false;
  if (/[\\:\x00-\x1f\x7f]/.test(path) || path.startsWith('/')) return false;
  return path.split('/').every((part) => /^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$/.test(part) && part !== '.' && part !== '..');
}

function validInventory(files) {
  if (!Array.isArray(files) || files.length === 0) return false;
  const seen = new Set();
  for (const file of files) {
    if (!record(file, ['path', 'sha256']) || !safePath(file.path)) return false;
    if (typeof file.sha256 !== 'string' || !DIGEST.test(file.sha256) || seen.has(file.path.toLowerCase())) return false;
    seen.add(file.path.toLowerCase());
  }
  return true;
}

/** Pure policy: compare an approved reference with a separately observed inventory. */
export function checkPackage(input) {
  if (!record(input, ['manifest', 'observed', 'supported'])) return { ok: false, reason: 'schema' };
  const { manifest, observed, supported } = input;
  if (!record(manifest, ['schema', 'packageId', 'release', 'files'])) return { ok: false, reason: 'schema' };
  if (manifest.schema !== 1 || manifest.packageId !== 'courier-runtime') return { ok: false, reason: 'schema' };
  if (typeof manifest.release !== 'string' || manifest.release.trim().length === 0) return { ok: false, reason: 'schema' };
  if (!validInventory(manifest.files)) return { ok: false, reason: 'schema' };
  if (!Array.isArray(supported) || supported.some((release) => typeof release !== 'string' || !release.trim())) {
    return { ok: false, reason: 'schema' };
  }
  if (!supported.includes(manifest.release)) return { ok: false, reason: 'unsupported-release' };
  if (!validInventory(observed) || observed.length !== manifest.files.length) return { ok: false, reason: 'inventory' };
  const actual = new Map(observed.map((file) => [file.path, file.sha256.toLowerCase()]));
  if (manifest.files.some((file) => !actual.has(file.path))) return { ok: false, reason: 'inventory' };
  if (manifest.files.some((file) => actual.get(file.path) !== file.sha256.toLowerCase())) return { ok: false, reason: 'digest' };
  return { ok: true, reason: 'verified' };
}

# Repair a real server rule

Implementation reference for **M1: spatial authority**. Start with [the guided learning route at `/learn`](/learn) on the reference server, then return here for the exact source contract. This Markdown file does not submit answers or certify mastery. Use the [support and attempt workflow](../learning-support/README.md) for worked siblings, gradual guidance and help recording. A prepared source workspace need not serve `/learn`; keep the reference server open for that route.

Your task: restore one server-side proximity check and prove that it blocks a remote pickup while a legitimate delivery still works.

You need Node 22 or newer and a terminal. No extra packages, accounts, drivers or operating-system changes. Use only your local copy of this owned game. The software is a teaching project, not production anti-cheat.

## Prepare your working copy

From the reference project's directory, run `npm run lab:prepare`. It creates `artifacts/workspace` and prints its exact path. Change into that directory and open `predictions.json` and `lab/response.md`. Do not run the checker or consult the worked reference until you have recorded the first predictions below. ## Trace and predict the decision

The client sends `{v, seq, move, interact}`. A **sequence** is a monotonically increasing input number, used to avoid repeating old input. It is not a timestamp. The server stages a direction and, if requested, one interaction. On its next **tick** (a 50 ms simulation step), it moves the courier and evaluates the interaction against server-owned positions.

A pickup changes **cargo**, the server's record that the courier carries the core. A delivery changes **score**. Neither property appears in the accepted request schema: the allowed field names and value types. A modified client can still send `interact:true` from far away. The missing guard must reject that attempt before either server property changes.

The legal radius is 250 millimetres, inclusive. Compare squared distance with the squared radius and use both coordinates. This avoids a square root and keeps integer boundary arithmetic exact. A cooldown is the waiting period after a successful interaction. The existing cooldown decision must remain in place, so the range repair cannot grant another interaction during that wait.

Record the required first answers in `predictions.json` now, before running the checker. Use `lab/response.md` for the calculations and reasons. The cases below identify the boundary to reason about:

| Courier relative to target | Your decision and reason |
| --- | --- |
| 250 mm east, 0 north | |
| 251 mm east, 0 north | |
| 150 mm east, 200 mm north | |
| 200 mm east, 200 mm north | |

## Observe the starter and repair it

The next steps connect the geometry to one source change and its real HTTP evidence.

## Work from a sibling to your own guard

A sibling circular zone has radius 5 units. An offset of `(3,4)` has squared distance `3²+4²=25`, equal to `5²`, so it is inside the inclusive zone. `(4,4)` gives 32 and is outside. Checking each coordinate against 5 would incorrectly accept the second point: a square bounding box is larger than the circle.

Completion: a different zone has radius 10 and offset `(6,8)`. Fill in the two squared terms, their sum, the squared radius and the inclusive decision. Then choose an offset whose individual coordinates are each below 10 but whose distance is outside. Complete the corresponding check in `/learn` before producing your source guard with this project's own radius.

`courses/anti-cheat-engineering/courier-lab/lab/check.mjs`:

```mjs
// Self-contained learner bootstrap. Authenticate the owner bundle before imports.
import { mkdir, readFile, writeFile, lstat, realpath, rename, readdir, mkdtemp, rm } from 'node:fs/promises';
import { dirname, resolve, join } from 'node:path';
import { fileURLToPath, pathToFileURL } from 'node:url';
import { createHash, randomUUID } from 'node:crypto';
import { spawn } from 'node:child_process';
import { tmpdir } from 'node:os';

const hash = (bytes) => createHash('sha256').update(bytes).digest('hex');

async function referenceFile(root, relative) {
  if (typeof relative !== 'string' || relative.startsWith('/') || relative.includes('\\') || /[\u0000-\u001f]/.test(relative) || relative.split('/').some((part) => !part || part === '.' || part === '..')) throw new Error('Invalid reference path.');
  const parts = relative.split('/');
  let info;
  for (let index = 1; index <= parts.length; index += 1) {
    info = await lstat(join(root, ...parts.slice(0, index)));
    if (info.isSymbolicLink()) throw new Error(`Reference symlink refused: ${relative}`);
  }
  if (!info.isFile() || info.size > 4 * 1024 * 1024) throw new Error(`Invalid reference file: ${relative}`);
  return readFile(join(root, relative));
}

async function authenticateReference(root, expectedManifest) {
  const bytes = await referenceFile(root, 'lab/order/reference.json');
  if (expectedManifest && hash(bytes) !== expectedManifest) throw new Error('Reference manifest changed since preparation.');
  const manifest = JSON.parse(bytes);
  if (manifest.schema !== 'courier-order-reference-v1' || !manifest.files || !Object.keys(manifest.files).length) throw new Error('Invalid reference manifest.');
  for (const required of ['lab/trust.mjs', 'lab/check.mjs', 'lab/spatial-reporter.mjs', 'lab/prompt.json', 'lab/reference.json']) {
    if (!Object.hasOwn(manifest.files, required)) throw new Error(`Missing trusted file: ${required}`);
  }
  for (const [path, expected] of Object.entries(manifest.files)) {
    if (!/^[a-f0-9]{64}$/.test(expected) || hash(await referenceFile(root, path)) !== expected) throw new Error(`Trusted reference changed: ${path}`);
  }
}

// OWNER_CHECK_BEGIN
async function previousAttempt(directory) {
  let entries;
  try { entries = await readdir(directory, { withFileTypes: true }); }
  catch (error) { if (error.code === 'ENOENT') return null; throw error; }
  let previous = null;
  let knownFeedback = false;
  let unknownFeedback = false;
  for (const entry of entries.filter((item) => item.isDirectory()).sort((a, b) => b.name.localeCompare(a.name))) {
    let metadata;
    try { metadata = JSON.parse(await readFile(join(directory, entry.name, 'submission.json'))); }
    catch (error) { if (error.code === 'ENOENT') continue; throw error; }
    previous ??= metadata.attemptId ?? entry.name;
    try { await readFile(join(directory, entry.name, 'feedback-started.json')); knownFeedback = true; }
    catch (error) { if (error.code !== 'ENOENT') throw error; unknownFeedback = true; }
  }
  return previous ? { attemptId: previous, feedback: knownFeedback ? true : unknownFeedback ? null : false } : null;
}

function classifyRun(code, signal, events, forced) {
  if (forced || signal) return { kind: 'runner-failure', healthy: false, passed: false, error: forced ?? `Worker terminated by ${signal}.` };
  const summary = events.findLast((event) => event.type === 'test:summary' && event.file === null);
  const cases = events.filter((event) => ['test:pass', 'test:fail'].includes(event.type) && event.details?.type !== 'suite');
  const failures = cases.filter((event) => event.type === 'test:fail');
  const counts = summary?.counts;
  const complete = counts && counts.tests === cases.length && counts.failed === failures.length && counts.cancelled === 0 && counts.passed > 0;
  if (complete && code === 0 && summary.success && failures.length === 0) return { kind: 'pass', healthy: true, passed: true };
  const behavior = failures.every((event) => {
    const error = event.details?.error;
    if (error?.failureType !== 'testCodeFailure') return false;
    const cause = error.cause;
    if (cause?.name === 'AssertionError' && cause.code === 'ERR_ASSERTION') return true;
    return cause?.name === 'InvariantViolation' && cause.code === 'REMOTE_PICKUP';
  });
  if (counts && counts.tests === cases.length && counts.failed === failures.length && counts.cancelled === 0 && code === 1 && !summary.success && failures.length > 0 && behavior) return { kind: 'behavior-failure', healthy: true, passed: false };
  return { kind: 'runner-failure', healthy: false, passed: false, error: 'The test process did not complete a healthy assertion result. See structured-events.jsonl and output.txt for per-test diagnostics.' };
}

async function runSpatialProcess({ execution, reportPath, timeoutMs, outputLimit }) {
  return new Promise((done) => {
    const env = { ...process.env };
    for (const key of ['NODE_TEST_CONTEXT', 'NODE_OPTIONS', 'NODE_PATH']) delete env[key];
    const reporter = join(dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), 'spatial-reporter.mjs');
    const args = ['--test', '--test-reporter=tap', '--test-reporter-destination=stdout', `--test-reporter=${reporter}`, `--test-reporter-destination=${reportPath}`, 'tests/proximity.test.mjs'];
    const child = spawn(process.execPath, args, { cwd: execution, env, detached: true, stdio: ['ignore', 'pipe', 'pipe'] });
    const chunks = [];
    let length = 0;
    let forced;
    const terminate = (reason) => {
      forced ??= reason;
      try { process.kill(-child.pid, 'SIGKILL'); } catch { child.kill('SIGKILL'); }
    };
    const timer = setTimeout(() => terminate('Spatial worker timed out.'), timeoutMs);
    for (const stream of [child.stdout, child.stderr]) stream.on('data', (chunk) => {
      const kept = chunk.subarray(0, Math.max(0, outputLimit - length));
      chunks.push(kept);
      process.stdout.write(kept);
      length += chunk.length;
      if (length > outputLimit) terminate('Spatial worker exceeded its output budget.');
    });
    child.once('error', (error) => { forced = error.message; });
    child.once('close', (code, signal) => {
      clearTimeout(timer);
      const output = Buffer.concat(chunks).toString('utf8');
      done({ code, signal, forced, output, outputBytes: length });
    });
  });
}

export async function executeSpatialTests({ execution, reportPath, timeoutMs = 30000, outputLimit = 1024 * 1024 }) {
  const temporary = reportPath ? null : await mkdtemp(join(tmpdir(), 'ivy-spatial-report-'));
  const destination = resolve(reportPath ?? join(temporary, 'structured-events.jsonl'));
  if (destination.startsWith(resolve(execution) + '/')) throw new Error('Structured evidence must stay outside the execution tree.');
  try {
    const result = await runSpatialProcess({ execution, reportPath: destination, timeoutMs, outputLimit });
    let events = [];
    let forced = result.forced;
    try {
      const info = await lstat(destination);
      if (!info.isFile() || info.isSymbolicLink() || info.size > 1024 * 1024) throw new Error('Invalid structured evidence file.');
      const bytes = await readFile(destination);
      if (bytes.length > 1024 * 1024) throw new Error('Structured evidence exceeded its byte budget.');
      events = bytes.toString('utf8').trim().split('\n').filter(Boolean).map((line) => JSON.parse(line));
    } catch (error) {
      forced ??= `Structured evidence unavailable: ${error.message}`;
    }
    const { forced: _ignored, ...evidence } = result;
    return { ...evidence, ...classifyRun(result.code, result.signal, events, forced), testEvents: events, structuredReportPath: temporary ? null : destination };
  } finally {
    if (temporary) await rm(temporary, { recursive: true, force: true });
  }
}

function validatePrompt(bytes, originalBytes, session) {
  const original = JSON.parse(originalBytes);
  let submitted;
  try { submitted = JSON.parse(bytes); } catch { throw new Error('Prompt changed; restore its original wording before submitting.'); }
  if (session.exercise !== original.id || submitted.id !== original.id || submitted.version !== original.version || hash(bytes) !== hash(originalBytes)) throw new Error('Prompt changed; restore its original id, version and wording before submitting.');
  if (session.prompt && (session.prompt.id !== original.id || session.prompt.version !== original.version || session.prompt.sha256 !== hash(originalBytes))) throw new Error('Prepared prompt identity changed. Preserve the original session and prompt.');
  return { id: original.id, version: original.version, sha256: hash(originalBytes) };
}

/** Owner-side submission path, imported only from authenticated reference bytes. */
export async function checkSubmission({ workspace, session, assistance, fresh = false }) {
  const { captureBundle, hashTree, saveJson, verifyReference, writeBundle } = await import('./trust.mjs');
  const { PREDICTION_CONTRACT, loadPredictionFeedback, predictionTemplate, validatePredictions, predictionCustody, preservePredictionRefusal, prepareFreshPractice, submitFreshPractice } = await import('./core/predictions.mjs');
  const referenceRoot = await realpath(session.referenceRoot ?? resolve(workspace, '../..'));
  const trusted = await verifyReference(referenceRoot, session.referenceManifest);
  if (trusted.bundle['lab/core/predictions.mjs'] && session.predictionContract !== PREDICTION_CONTRACT) throw new Error('Prepared prediction contract changed. Restore the original session.');
  const reference = JSON.parse(trusted.bundle['lab/reference.json']);
  if (reference.sha256 !== session.reference) throw new Error('This spatial workspace belongs to a different reference. Existing attempts are preserved.');
  const originalPrompt = trusted.bundle['lab/prompt.json'];
  const prompt = validatePrompt(await readFile(join(workspace, 'lab/prompt.json')), originalPrompt, session);
  const previous = await previousAttempt(join(workspace, 'artifacts/attempts'));
  const attemptId = `${new Date().toISOString().replaceAll(':', '-')}-${randomUUID()}`;
  let destination = join(workspace, session.predictionContract === PREDICTION_CONTRACT ? 'artifacts/spatial-captures' : 'artifacts/attempts', attemptId);
  await mkdir(destination, { recursive: true, mode: 0o700 });
  const paths = ['defense.mjs', 'lab/response.md', 'lab/prompt.json'];
  if (session.predictionContract === PREDICTION_CONTRACT) {
    const file = fresh ? 'fresh-practice.json' : 'predictions.json';
    try { await readFile(join(workspace, file)); paths.push(file); } catch (error) { if (error.code !== 'ENOENT') throw error; }
  }
  const { captured, hashes } = await captureBundle(workspace, paths, join(destination, 'submitted'));
  validatePrompt(captured['lab/prompt.json'], originalPrompt, session);
  let predictions;
  if (fresh && session.predictionContract !== PREDICTION_CONTRACT) throw new Error('Fresh practice requires a newly prepared workspace.');
  if (session.predictionContract === PREDICTION_CONTRACT) {
    const attempts = join(workspace, 'artifacts/attempts');
    const refusals = join(workspace, 'artifacts/spatial-refusals');
    if (fresh) return submitFreshPractice({ workspace, root: referenceRoot, module: 'spatial', captured, assistance, attempts, directory: join(workspace, 'artifacts/spatial-practice'), refusals });
    const feedback = (await loadPredictionFeedback(referenceRoot, 'spatial')).postCheckFeedback();
    try { predictions = validatePredictions(captured['predictions.json'], predictionTemplate(feedback, 'spatial')); }
    catch (error) { return preservePredictionRefusal({ directory: refusals, captured, assistance, module: 'spatial', stage: 'prediction', error }); }
    await mkdir(attempts, { recursive: true });
    const committed = join(attempts, attemptId);
    await rename(destination, committed);
    destination = committed;
  }
  await writeBundle(destination, { 'defense.mjs': captured['defense.mjs'], 'response.md': captured['lab/response.md'], 'prompt.json': captured['lab/prompt.json'] });
  const execution = join(referenceRoot, 'artifacts/spatial-executions', attemptId);
  await saveJson(join(destination, 'submission.json'), {
    schema: 'courier-spatial-submission-v2',
    reference: session.reference, referenceRoot, referenceManifest: trusted.manifestHash, exercise: session.exercise, prompt,
    attemptId, submittedAt: new Date().toISOString(), assistance, sha256: hashes['defense.mjs'], hashes,
    ...(predictions ? { predictions: predictions.document, ...predictionCustody(predictions, assistance, Boolean(previous?.feedback)) } : {}),
    attemptKind: previous ? 'revision' : 'first', previousAttemptId: previous?.attemptId ?? null,
    priorFeedbackExposure: previous ? previous.feedback : false,
    feedbackProvenance: previous?.feedback === null ? 'Unknown for legacy attempts without a feedback marker.' : 'Recorded feedback markers are separate from self-reported assistance.',
    ownerExecutionRoot: execution, command: 'node --test tests/proximity.test.mjs',
  });
  await mkdir(execution, { recursive: true, mode: 0o700 });
  await writeBundle(execution, { ...trusted.bundle, 'defense.mjs': captured['defense.mjs'] });
  const before = await hashTree(execution);
  await saveJson(join(destination, 'execution-hashes.json'), before);
  await saveJson(join(destination, 'feedback-started.json'), { startedAt: new Date().toISOString(), note: 'Later attempts have prior checker feedback exposure, including interrupted runs.' });
  console.log(`Saved attempt: ${destination}`);
  const result = await executeSpatialTests({ execution, reportPath: join(destination, 'structured-events.jsonl') });
  if (JSON.stringify(before) !== JSON.stringify(await hashTree(execution))) Object.assign(result, { kind: 'runner-failure', healthy: false, passed: false, error: 'Execution files changed while running.' });
  await saveJson(join(destination, 'result.json'), result);
  if (trusted.bundle['lab/feedback.mjs']) {
    const { postCheckFeedback } = await import(pathToFileURL(join(referenceRoot, 'lab/feedback.mjs')));
    const feedback = postCheckFeedback();
    if (predictions) await prepareFreshPractice(workspace, feedback, 'spatial');
    await saveJson(join(destination, 'prediction-feedback.json'), { ...feedback, ...(predictions ? { submittedPredictions: predictions.document } : {}), submittedResponse: captured['lab/response.md'].toString('utf8') });
    console.log(`Compare your captured response with answers and fresh practice: ${join(destination, 'prediction-feedback.json')}`);
  }
  await writeFile(join(destination, 'output.txt'), result.output, { flag: 'wx' });
  const failed = [...result.output.matchAll(/^not ok \d+ - (.+)$/gm)].map((match) => match[1]);
  const label = result.kind === 'pass' ? 'PASS' : result.kind === 'behavior-failure' ? 'FAIL' : 'RUNNER FAILURE';
  console.log(`Criterion summary: ${label} — legitimate delivery; denied remote pickup; inclusive x/y boundaries; circular diagonal; cooldown; no duplicate score.`);
  if (result.kind === 'runner-failure') {
    console.log(`${result.error} This is not a behavioral result for the submitted guard.`);
    return result;
  }
  if (failed.length) console.log(`First failed criterion: ${failed[0]}. See the preserved actual/expected assertion above.`);
  console.log(`\nPost-submission assistance — spatial boundary reasons (feedback-02, feedback-03):
1. 250 mm east, 0 north: 250² = 62,500 mm², so the inclusive boundary accepts equality.
2. 251 mm east, 0 north: 251² = 63,001 mm², outside the radius; deny without changing cargo or score.
3. 150 mm east, 200 mm north: 150² + 200² = 62,500 mm², exactly on the legal circular boundary.
4. 200 mm east, 200 mm north: 200² + 200² = 80,000 mm², outside the circle even though each axis is below 250.
Explanation/transfer rubric — assistance, ungraded: identify the server-owned position/cargo/score; cite the request, measured state and responsible rule; distinguish prevention from advisory findings; explain a fresh repair-station rule using server-owned range, inventory and one-time reward; name a legal-protocol modified client this guard cannot identify. A saved paragraph is not a scored explanation.`);
  return result;
}
// OWNER_CHECK_END

async function main() {
  const workspace = await realpath(resolve(dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), '..'));
  const args = process.argv.slice(2);
  const fresh = args[0] === '--fresh';
  if (fresh) args.shift();
  if (args.length !== 2 || args[0] !== '--assistance' || !args[1]?.trim()) throw new Error('Record help used: npm run lab:check -- --assistance "none" (or describe hints, AI or worked examples).');
  let session;
  try { session = JSON.parse(await readFile(join(workspace, 'lab/session.json'), 'utf8')); }
  catch { throw new Error('Run lab:prepare from the reference, then change into its printed workspace. Reference runs are not learner submissions.'); }
  if (session.prepared !== true) throw new Error('Not a prepared learner workspace.');
  const referenceRoot = await realpath(session.referenceRoot ?? resolve(workspace, '../..'));
  await authenticateReference(referenceRoot, session.referenceManifest);
  const owner = await import(pathToFileURL(join(referenceRoot, 'lab/check.mjs')));
  const result = await owner.checkSubmission({ workspace, session, assistance: args[1], fresh });
  process.exitCode = ['runner-failure', 'submission-refused'].includes(result.kind) ? 2 : Number(!result.passed);
}

if (process.argv[1] && import.meta.url === pathToFileURL(resolve(process.argv[1])).href) {
  try { await main(); }
  catch (error) { console.error(`Submission refused: ${error.message}`); process.exitCode = 2; }
}

`courses/anti-cheat-engineering/courier-lab/lab/core/README.md`:

```md
# Shared core submission runner

From the reference project, after reviewing the final runtime, module and runner
bytes, run `node lab/core/seal.mjs`. Commit `lab/core/reference.json` with those
bytes. The seal independently lists every regular `.mjs`, `.cjs`, `.js`, `.json`
and `.md` file in the project. It includes actual runtime, public, fixture,
template and runner sources. It excludes `artifacts`, `node_modules`, hidden
directories and generated `lab/**/reference.json` files. Excluding all generated
lab manifests avoids cyclic hashes; the old spatial/order seals are neither
changed nor relied upon. A new file or changed file requires a reviewed reseal.

The registry supports `integrity`, `telemetry`, `evaluation`, `retention`, `timing`, `recovery` and `capstone`. Each module supplies
`policy.mjs`, `template.mjs`, `fixtures.mjs`, `prompt.json`, `LEARNER.md` and
`response-template.md`. The prompt declares its `id` and `version`. Fixtures
export `async assess(candidate)` and return
`{ passed, criteria: [{ name, passed, error? }] }`. `candidate` is the imported
learner module. Criteria must be nonempty, uniquely named and agree with the
summary. An error can preserve `message`, `expected`, `actual`, `operator`,
`stack`, `code` and `source` (for a learner-guide feedback pointer). Fixtures catch expected behavioral/assertion failures into
criteria; an uncaught exception is a runner failure.

The parent package supplies these scripts:

```json
{
  "core:prepare": "node lab/core/prepare.mjs",
  "core:check": "node lab/core/check.mjs"
}
```

Run `npm run core:prepare -- integrity` (or `telemetry`) once. This creates
`artifacts/core/<id>-workspace` and refuses to overwrite it. Its minimal package
contains only a usable `core:check` script. It has no author policy, fixtures,
reference runtime or missing test commands. Preparation atomically publishes
the sealed bundle and its exact manifest once at
`artifacts/core/references/<manifestHash>`. Concurrent preparations reuse only a
verified identical snapshot; partial staging directories never become a
reference. Symlinked snapshot directories or files are refused. Run
`npm run core:check -- --assistance "none"` inside the prepared workspace, or
describe the help used. The same commands work directly with Node.

Each prepared session pins that snapshot as its reference root. Later module,
runtime or runner updates and reseals in the original project do not change an
existing workspace's reference. A new preparation uses the current seal. Never
edit a published snapshot: changed snapshot bytes refuse checks and preparation
instead of silently replacing the snapshot or old evidence.

The runner captures all regular workspace files except generated `artifacts`,
`node_modules` and `.git`, including learner helper modules. Required policy,
response, exact prompt, exact guide, session and help metadata must be present.
Help has a `consulted` array of strings and an optional `note`. Double reads and
inventory checks refuse changing submissions. Symlinks and excessive file sizes
are refused. Reference bytes and their inventory are verified before checking.

Authoritative sessions, immutable first/revised submissions, self-reported help,
prompt/version/hash, source hashes, prior feedback exposure and raw results live
under the pinned snapshot's `artifacts/core/{sessions,attempts}`. Each attempt
has `submitted/`, `submission.json`, `assistance.json`, `feedback-started.json`,
`result.json` and `output.txt`. UUIDs, exclusive writes and a session lock keep
earlier attempts intact. Lock metadata records the checker PID and a unique
check ID. Live owners are never displaced. A later checker archives a dead
owner's lock, appends `interrupted.json` to its unfinished attempt, and preserves
its first/revision classification and feedback exposure. Incomplete lock or
recovery metadata refuses clearly without deleting work; retry after an active
initializer finishes. A preparation/capture refusal creates no attempt;
import failures, crashes, timeouts and output overruns preserve an attempt with
`kind: "runner-failure"`. Failed behavioral criteria use
`kind: "behavior-failure"`. CLI exit codes are 0 for pass, 1 for behavior failure,
and 2 for refusal or runner failure. Written explanations are preserved, ungraded.

For an old empty lock, incomplete metadata, or a crashed recovery process, first
stop all checks for the workspace. From the reference project run:

```sh
node lab/core/recover.mjs "/absolute/path/to/the/workspace" --stopped
```

The parent package can expose this as `core:recover`. `--stopped` explicitly
confirms that no check or recovery is starting; ambiguous locks are never
automatically removed. The command validates the prepared session and pinned
reference, refuses any known live check or recovery PID, and renames only the
`checking` directory into a unique `checking-recovered-manual-...` sibling.
Partial metadata and other lock bytes stay in that archive; attempts, feedback
and snapshots are unchanged. Retry the checker afterward. A changed reference
or mismatched session still refuses recovery.

Execution copies live under reference `artifacts/core/executions`, outside the
learner workspace. `trusted/` contains the pinned reference bundle; `candidate/`
contains only captured submission bytes. Fixtures import their runtime relative
to `trusted/`; learner policy is imported from `candidate/`. Workspace files
named like fixtures or runtime cannot replace trusted sources. Before/after
execution hashes detect writes to either execution tree. Workers default to
10 seconds and 1 MiB of stdout/stderr; their result is limited to 512 KiB. The owner reaps the worker process group after normal completion as well as failure. A descendant that deliberately creates a new session is outside this boundary.

This is a local teaching harness, not an OS sandbox or authentication system.
A machine owner can change the launcher, evidence or both sides of a comparison.
Keep sensitive inputs out of it. Reading author/reference material counts as
assistance. These boundaries preserve reproducible learning evidence
(`assessment-09`, `assessment-13`, `practice-10`, `feedback-01`); they do not prove
independent learning or unmodified client execution.


Evaluation exploration and plans use the prepared workspace identity. The owner stores exact source, corpus, settings, revision reasons, exposure and results under `artifacts/core/sessions/<id>/evaluation/`. Each plan runs once. Later plans require an explicit revision reason. A new core submission records links and hashes to this history; no prior submission is rewritten. Evaluation and retention release `prediction-feedback.json` only after capturing the learner response. Fresh variant answers and transfer rubrics stay in author-only modules.

```

`courses/anti-cheat-engineering/courier-lab/lab/core/check.mjs`:

```mjs
// This self-contained bootstrap is the only runner source copied to a learner.
// Authenticate the owner-side modules before importing any of them.
import { createHash } from 'node:crypto';
import { constants } from 'node:fs';
import { lstat, open, realpath } from 'node:fs/promises';
import { dirname, join, resolve } from 'node:path';
import { fileURLToPath, pathToFileURL } from 'node:url';

const hash = (bytes) => createHash('sha256').update(bytes).digest('hex');
const FILE_LIMIT = 4 * 1024 * 1024;

async function read(root, path) {
  if (typeof path !== 'string' || path.includes('\\') || /[\u0000-\u001f]/.test(path) || path.split('/').some((part) => !part || part === '.' || part === '..')) throw new Error('Invalid reference path.');
  const parts = path.split('/');
  let initial;
  for (let index = 1; index <= parts.length; index += 1) {
    const stat = await lstat(join(root, ...parts.slice(0, index)), { bigint: true });
    if (stat.isSymbolicLink()) throw new Error(`Symlinks are not accepted: ${path}`);
    initial = stat;
  }
  if (!initial.isFile() || initial.size > BigInt(FILE_LIMIT)) throw new Error(`Not a bounded regular file: ${path}`);
  const file = await open(join(root, path), constants.O_RDONLY | constants.O_NOFOLLOW | constants.O_NONBLOCK);
  try {
    const before = await file.stat({ bigint: true });
    if (!before.isFile() || before.size > BigInt(FILE_LIMIT)) throw new Error(`Not a bounded regular file: ${path}`);
    if (before.dev !== initial.dev || before.ino !== initial.ino) throw new Error(`File changed during capture: ${path}`);
    const chunks = [];
    let length = 0;
    while (length <= FILE_LIMIT) {
      const buffer = Buffer.allocUnsafe(Math.min(64 * 1024, FILE_LIMIT + 1 - length));
      const { bytesRead } = await file.read(buffer, 0, buffer.length, length);
      if (!bytesRead) break;
      chunks.push(buffer.subarray(0, bytesRead));
      length += bytesRead;
    }
    if (length > FILE_LIMIT) throw new Error(`Not a bounded regular file: ${path}`);
    const after = await file.stat({ bigint: true });
    const current = await lstat(join(root, path), { bigint: true });
    if (!current.isFile() || current.isSymbolicLink()) throw new Error(`File changed during capture: ${path}`);
    for (const key of ['dev', 'ino', 'size', 'mtimeNs', 'ctimeNs']) {
      if (before[key] !== after[key] || before[key] !== current[key]) throw new Error(`File changed during capture: ${path}`);
    }
    return Buffer.concat(chunks, length);
  } finally {
    await file.close();
  }
}

async function main() {
  const args = process.argv.slice(2);
  const fresh = args[0] === '--fresh';
  if (fresh) args.shift();
  if (args.length !== 2 || args[0] !== '--assistance' || !args[1].trim() || args[1].length > 10000) throw new Error('Record help used: npm run core:check -- --assistance "none" (or describe it).');
  const workspace = await realpath(resolve(dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), '../..'));
  const sessionBytes = await read(workspace, 'lab/core/session.json');
  const session = JSON.parse(sessionBytes);
  if (session.schema !== 'courier-core-session-v1' || !/^[a-f0-9-]{36}$/.test(session.sessionId) || !/^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{0,39}$/.test(session.module) || !/^[a-f0-9]{64}$/.test(session.referenceManifest)) throw new Error('Invalid prepared session.');
  const root = await realpath(session.referenceRoot);
  const manifestBytes = await read(root, 'lab/core/reference.json');
  if (hash(manifestBytes) !== session.referenceManifest) throw new Error('Reference manifest changed since preparation.');
  const manifest = JSON.parse(manifestBytes);
  if (manifest.schema !== 'courier-core-reference-v1' || !manifest.files || !Object.keys(manifest.files).length) throw new Error('Invalid reference manifest.');
  for (const path of ['lab/core/trust.mjs', 'lab/core/grade.mjs', 'lab/core/registry.mjs', 'lab/core/worker.mjs']) {
    if (!Object.hasOwn(manifest.files, path)) throw new Error(`Missing trusted runner: ${path}`);
  }
  for (const [path, expected] of Object.entries(manifest.files)) {
    if (!/^[a-f0-9]{64}$/.test(expected) || hash(await read(root, path)) !== expected) throw new Error(`Trusted reference changed: ${path}`);
  }
  const owner = JSON.parse(await read(root, `artifacts/core/sessions/${session.sessionId}/session.json`));
  if (owner.workspace !== workspace || owner.referenceRoot !== root || owner.sessionHash !== hash(sessionBytes)) throw new Error('Prepared session identity changed. Restore the original session.');
  const { checkSubmission } = await import(pathToFileURL(join(root, 'lab/core/grade.mjs')));
  const result = await checkSubmission({ workspace, session, assistance: args[1], fresh });
  process.exitCode = ['runner-failure', 'submission-refused'].includes(result.kind) ? 2 : Number(!result.passed);
}

try { await main(); }
catch (error) {
  console.error(`Submission refused: ${error.message}\nPrepare a workspace from the sealed reference with node lab/core/prepare.mjs <module>.`);
  process.exitCode = 2;
}
