import { mkdir, stat } from 'node:fs/promises';
import { dirname, join, resolve } from 'node:path';
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
import { saveJson, verifyReference, writeBundle } from '../trust.mjs';
import { PREDICTION_CONTRACT, loadPredictionFeedback, predictionTemplate } from '../core/predictions.mjs';
import { snapshotReference } from '../reference-snapshot.mjs';

const root = resolve(dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), '../..');
const destination = join(root, 'artifacts/order-workspace');
try {
  await stat(destination);
  console.error(`A workspace already exists at ${destination}. Existing work was preserved.`);
  process.exitCode = 1;
} catch (error) {
  if (error.code !== 'ENOENT') throw error;
  const trusted = await verifyReference(root);
  const { bundle, manifestHash } = trusted;
  const referenceRoot = await snapshotReference(root, trusted);
  const names = ['server.mjs', 'engine.mjs', 'defense.mjs', 'protocol.mjs', 'clock.mjs', 'telemetry/runtime.mjs', 'learning/service.mjs', 'learning/runtime.mjs', 'learning/grade.mjs',
    'clients/http-client.mjs', 'lab/order/check.mjs', 'lab/order/LEARNER.md', 'lab/order/prompt.json', 'lab/order/seeds.json',
    ...Object.keys(bundle).filter((name) => name.startsWith('public/'))];
  const scaffold = Object.fromEntries(names.map((name) => {
    if (!bundle[name]) throw new Error(`Sealed scaffold is missing ${name}`);
    return [name, bundle[name]];
  }));
  scaffold['admission.mjs'] = bundle['lab/order/admission-template.mjs'];
  scaffold['learner-scenario.mjs'] = bundle['lab/order/scenario-template.mjs'];
  const feedback = (await loadPredictionFeedback(referenceRoot, 'order')).postCheckFeedback();
  scaffold['predictions.json'] = JSON.stringify(predictionTemplate(feedback, 'order'), null, 2) + '\n';
  Object.assign(scaffold, Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(bundle).filter(([path]) => path.startsWith('learning-support/') && path.endsWith('.md'))));
  scaffold['response.md'] = bundle['lab/order/response-template.md'];
  scaffold['package.json'] = JSON.stringify({
    name: 'courier-order-learner-workspace', private: true, type: 'module', engines: { node: '>=22' },
    scripts: { start: 'node server.mjs', 'order:check': 'node lab/order/check.mjs', 'order:practice': 'node lab/order/check.mjs --fresh' },
  }, null, 2) + '\n';
  scaffold['lab/order/help.json'] = Buffer.from(JSON.stringify({ consulted: [], note: 'Record hints, AI help, worked examples or reference consultation here.' }, null, 2) + '\n');
  await mkdir(destination, { recursive: true });
  await writeBundle(destination, scaffold);
  await saveJson(join(destination, 'lab/order/session.json'), {
    prepared: true, exercise: 'courier-order-01', created: new Date().toISOString(),
    referenceRoot, referenceManifest: manifestHash, predictionContract: PREDICTION_CONTRACT,
  });
  console.log(`Created ${destination}\n\ncd "${destination}"\nRead lab/order/LEARNER.md. Complete predictions.json with an answer OR skipReason for every exact question. Edit admission.mjs, learner-scenario.mjs and response.md.\nThen run: node lab/order/check.mjs --assistance "none"\n\nThe reference answers and owner-side judges are outside this workspace.`);
}

`courses/anti-cheat-engineering/courier-lab/lab/order/response-template.md`:

```md
# Input-order reasoning

Assistance used:

## Predictions before editing

For these predictions, use an unobstructed east/west path. There is no pending interaction initially, all named admissions have interact=false, and there are no other inputs except those stated. These are application practice after the worked trace, not an unseen transfer measure.

1. At T1 seq7/W is admitted from x=2000. At T3 seq6/E/interact=true arrives. Predict x, pending interaction and expiry just after T4, and explain.

    const path = relative + '/' + entry.name;
    if (entry.isDirectory()) result.push(...await filesBelow(path));
    if (entry.isFile() && path !== 'lab/order/reference.json') result.push(path);
  }

import { snapshotReference } from './reference-snapshot.mjs';

const hash = (bytes) => createHash('sha256').update(bytes).digest('hex');
const SCAFFOLD = [
  'server.mjs', 'engine.mjs', 'admission.mjs', 'protocol.mjs', 'clock.mjs', 'telemetry/runtime.mjs', 'learning/service.mjs', 'learning/runtime.mjs', 'learning/grade.mjs',

function learnerPage(bytes) {
  return bytes.toString()
    .replace('<a class="edition" href="/order">NEXT: INPUT ORDER →</a>', '<a class="edition" href="#build-title">SOURCE TASK ↓</a>')
    .replace(/<section class="build-section"[\s\S]*?<\/section>/, '<section class="build-section" aria-labelledby="build-title"><div><p class="eyebrow">03 / BUILD THE DEFENSE</p><h2 id="build-title">Restore a guard.<br>Check the result.</h2><p>Read lab/LEARNER.md and record your predictions in predictions.json before the first check. Edit defense.mjs, then run the command below. The owner-side checker saves each attempt before revealing feedback.</p><code>npm run lab:check -- --assistance none</code></div></section>')
    .replace(/<p><a class="next-lesson" href="\/(?:order|course)">[^<]*<\/a><\/p>/g, '');
}

function learnerBootstrap(bytes) {
  const source = bytes.toString();
  const begin = source.indexOf('// OWNER_CHECK_BEGIN');
  const end = source.indexOf('// OWNER_CHECK_END');
  if (begin < 0 || end < begin) throw new Error('The sealed spatial checker has no separate owner section.');
  return source.slice(0, begin) + source.slice(end + '// OWNER_CHECK_END'.length);
}

export async function prepareSpatialWorkspace({ root }) {
  const destination = join(root, 'artifacts', 'workspace');
  try { await stat(destination); throw new Error(`A workspace already exists at ${destination}. Continue there; existing work was preserved.`); }
  catch (error) { if (error.code !== 'ENOENT') throw error; }
  const trusted = await verifyReference(root);
  const { bundle, manifestHash } = trusted;
  const original = bundle['defense.mjs'].toString();
  const reference = JSON.parse(bundle['lab/reference.json']);
  if (hash(original) !== reference.sha256 || !original.includes(reference.guard)) throw new Error('Reference changed: prepare refuses to remove an unverified guard. Use a fresh reference checkout.');
  const prompt = JSON.parse(bundle['lab/prompt.json']);
  if (prompt.id !== 'courier-proximity-01' || !Number.isSafeInteger(prompt.version) || prompt.version < 1) throw new Error('Invalid spatial prompt identity.');
  const referenceRoot = await snapshotReference(root, trusted);
  const scaffold = Object.fromEntries(SCAFFOLD.map((path) => {
    if (!bundle[path]) throw new Error(`Sealed scaffold is missing ${path}.`);
    return [path, bundle[path]];
  }));
  scaffold['public/index.html'] = learnerPage(bundle['public/index.html']);
  scaffold['lab/check.mjs'] = learnerBootstrap(bundle['lab/check.mjs']);
  scaffold['defense.mjs'] = original.replace(reference.guard, '// LAB_PROXIMITY_GUARD\n  // TODO: deny interactions outside the inclusive 250 mm radius.');
  const feedback = (await loadPredictionFeedback(referenceRoot, 'spatial')).postCheckFeedback();
  scaffold['predictions.json'] = JSON.stringify(predictionTemplate(feedback, 'spatial'), null, 2) + '\n';
  Object.assign(scaffold, Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(bundle).filter(([path]) => path.startsWith('learning-support/') && path.endsWith('.md'))));
  scaffold['lab/response.md'] = bundle['lab/response-template.md'];
  scaffold['package.json'] = JSON.stringify({
    name: 'courier-spatial-learner-workspace', private: true, type: 'module', engines: { node: '>=22' },
    scripts: { start: 'node server.mjs', 'lab:check': 'node lab/check.mjs', 'lab:practice': 'node lab/check.mjs --fresh' },
  }, null, 2) + '\n';
  scaffold['lab/session.json'] = JSON.stringify({
    created: new Date().toISOString(), reference: reference.sha256, referenceRoot,
    referenceManifest: manifestHash, exercise: prompt.id, prepared: true,
    historyFormat: 'spatial-v2', predictionContract: PREDICTION_CONTRACT,
    prompt: { id: prompt.id, version: prompt.version, sha256: hash(bundle['lab/prompt.json']) },
  }, null, 2) + '\n';
  await mkdir(destination, { recursive: true });
  await writeBundle(destination, scaffold);
  return { destination };
}

if (process.argv[1] && import.meta.url === pathToFileURL(resolve(process.argv[1])).href) {
  try {
    const root = resolve(dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), '..');
    const { destination } = await prepareSpatialWorkspace({ root });
    console.log(`Created ${destination}\n\ncd "${destination}"\nRead lab/LEARNER.md and complete predictions.json with an answer OR skipReason for each exact question, and keep explanations in lab/response.md BEFORE running a check.\nEdit defense.mjs, then run npm run lab:check -- --assistance none.\n\nThe starter intentionally lacks the proximity guard. Trusted tests, reference answers and manifests stay outside this workspace.`);
  } catch (error) { console.error(error.message); process.exitCode = 1; }
}

`courses/anti-cheat-engineering/courier-lab/lab/reference-snapshot.mjs`:

```mjs
import { lstat, mkdir, mkdtemp, realpath, rename, rm } from 'node:fs/promises';
import { join } from 'node:path';
import { regularFile, sha256, verifyReference, writeBundle } from './trust.mjs';

async function verifySnapshot(path, hash) {
  const info = await lstat(path);
  if (!info.isDirectory() || info.isSymbolicLink()) throw new Error('Legacy reference snapshot must be a directory without symlinks.');
  await verifyReference(path, hash);
  return path;
}

/** New preparations pin bytes once; old sessions and attempts are never changed. */
export async function snapshotReference(source, trusted) {
  const root = await realpath(source);
  let parent = root;
  for (const name of ['artifacts', 'legacy-references']) {
    parent = join(parent, name);
    try { await mkdir(parent, { mode: 0o700 }); }
    catch (error) { if (error.code !== 'EEXIST') throw error; }
    const info = await lstat(parent);
    if (!info.isDirectory() || info.isSymbolicLink()) throw new Error('Legacy snapshot parent must be a directory without symlinks.');
  }
  const destination = join(parent, trusted.manifestHash);
  let exists;
  try { exists = await lstat(destination); }
  catch (error) { if (error.code !== 'ENOENT') throw error; }
  if (exists) return verifySnapshot(destination, trusted.manifestHash);
  const bytes = await regularFile(root, 'lab/order/reference.json');
  if (sha256(bytes) !== trusted.manifestHash) throw new Error('Legacy reference changed while preparing its snapshot.');
  const staging = await mkdtemp(join(parent, '.pending-'));
  try {
    await writeBundle(staging, { ...trusted.bundle, 'lab/order/reference.json': bytes });
    await verifySnapshot(staging, trusted.manifestHash);
    try { await rename(staging, destination); }
    catch (error) { if (!['EEXIST', 'ENOTEMPTY'].includes(error.code)) throw error; }
    return await verifySnapshot(destination, trusted.manifestHash);
  } finally {
    await rm(staging, { recursive: true, force: true });
  }
}

`courses/anti-cheat-engineering/courier-lab/lab/spatial-reporter.mjs`:

```mjs
// Node 22+ custom reporter: serialize typed test events, never parse TAP text.
function errorRecord(error, depth = 0) {
  if (!error || typeof error !== 'object') return { message: String(error) };
  const record = {};
  for (const key of ['name', 'message', 'code', 'failureType', 'operator', 'actual', 'expected', 'observed', 'stack']) {
    if (key in error) record[key] = error[key];
  }
  if ('cause' in error && depth < 3) record.cause = errorRecord(error.cause, depth + 1);
  return record;
}

export default async function* spatialReporter(source) {
  let bytes = 0;
  for await (const event of source) {
    if (!['test:pass', 'test:fail', 'test:summary'].includes(event.type)) continue;
    const data = event.data;
    const record = event.type === 'test:summary'
      ? { type: event.type, counts: data.counts, success: data.success, file: data.file ?? null }
      : {
        type: event.type, name: data.name, nesting: data.nesting, testNumber: data.testNumber,
        file: data.file ?? null, skip: data.skip ?? false, todo: data.todo ?? false,
        details: { type: data.details?.type, ...(data.details?.error ? { error: errorRecord(data.details.error) } : {}) },
      };
    const line = JSON.stringify(record, (_key, value) => typeof value === 'bigint' ? String(value) : value) + '\n';
    bytes += Buffer.byteLength(line);
    if (bytes > 1024 * 1024) throw new Error('Spatial structured evidence exceeded its byte budget.');
    yield line;
  }
}

`courses/anti-cheat-engineering/courier-lab/lab/trust.mjs`:

```mjs
import { createHash } from 'node:crypto';
import { lstat, mkdir, readFile, readdir, writeFile } from 'node:fs/promises';
import { dirname, join, resolve, sep } from 'node:path';

export const sha256 = (bytes) => createHash('sha256').update(bytes).digest('hex');
export const saveJson = (path, value) => writeFile(path, JSON.stringify(value, null, 2) + '\n', { flag: 'wx' });

export async function regularFile(root, relative) {
  const path = resolve(root, relative);
  if (!path.startsWith(resolve(root) + sep)) throw new Error(`File escapes the bundle: ${relative}`);
  const parts = relative.split('/');
  for (let index = 1; index <= parts.length; index += 1) {
    const info = await lstat(join(root, ...parts.slice(0, index)));
    if (info.isSymbolicLink()) throw new Error(`Symlinks are not submitted: ${relative}`);
  }
  if (!(await lstat(path)).isFile()) throw new Error(`Not a regular file: ${relative}`);
  return readFile(path);
}

export async function readBundle(root, paths) {
  return Object.fromEntries(await Promise.all(paths.map(async (path) => [path, await regularFile(root, path)])));
}

export function hashBundle(bundle) {
  return Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(bundle).sort().map(([path, bytes]) => [path, sha256(bytes)]));
}

export async function writeBundle(root, bundle) {
  for (const [path, bytes] of Object.entries(bundle)) {
    await mkdir(dirname(join(root, path)), { recursive: true });
    await writeFile(join(root, path), bytes, { flag: 'wx' });
  }
}

/** Double-read custody detects normal concurrent edits; it is not an owner-hostile sandbox. */
export async function captureBundle(root, paths, destination, afterRead = async () => {}) {
  const captured = await readBundle(root, paths);
  await afterRead();
  const second = await readBundle(root, paths);
  const hashes = hashBundle(captured);
  if (JSON.stringify(hashes) !== JSON.stringify(hashBundle(second))) throw new Error('Submission changed during capture. Save all files and retry.');
  await writeBundle(destination, captured);
  return { captured, hashes };
}

export async function verifyReference(root, expectedManifestHash) {
  const bytes = await regularFile(root, 'lab/order/reference.json');
  if (expectedManifestHash && sha256(bytes) !== expectedManifestHash) throw new Error('Reference manifest changed since preparation.');
  const manifest = JSON.parse(bytes);
  if (manifest.schema !== 'courier-order-reference-v1' || !manifest.files || !Object.keys(manifest.files).length) throw new Error('Reference is not sealed. Run node lab/order/seal.mjs in the reference checkout.');
  const bundle = await readBundle(root, Object.keys(manifest.files));
  const actual = hashBundle(bundle);
  for (const [path, hash] of Object.entries(manifest.files)) {
    if (actual[path] !== hash) throw new Error(`Trusted reference changed: ${path}. Reseal only after reviewing the change.`);
  }
  return { manifest, manifestHash: sha256(bytes), bundle };
}

export async function hashTree(root, prefix = '') {
  const hashes = {};
  for (const entry of (await readdir(join(root, prefix), { withFileTypes: true })).sort((a, b) => a.name.localeCompare(b.name))) {
    const path = prefix + entry.name;
    if (entry.isSymbolicLink()) throw new Error(`Execution contains a symlink: ${path}`);
    if (entry.isDirectory()) Object.assign(hashes, await hashTree(root, path + '/'));
    if (entry.isFile()) hashes[path] = sha256(await readFile(join(root, path)));
  }
  return hashes;
}

```

`courses/anti-cheat-engineering/courier-lab/learning-support/capstone-receipts.md`:

```md
# Reason about receipts before writing the capstone

Use M11 in [the guided route](/learn), then return to [the capstone contract](../capstone/LEARNER.md) for the exact interface, check order and HTTP helpers. This reference works a different resource service and shows how to plan independent observations. It contains no completed repair policy or repair scenario. Record help using the [support workflow](README.md).

## 1. A receipt refers to an operation, not today's balance

A **transaction** changes related resources together. A **receipt** preserves the result of one successful transaction so a retry can acknowledge that same operation without executing it again. **Idempotence** here means that repeating the same accepted request has no additional resource effect. It does not mean returning whatever balances happen to be current.

Work a sibling storage locker: opening a locker costs one token and adds up to four stored units, with a capacity of twelve. Each user has their own successful request IDs. The policy retains three receipts. Its range and authentication rules are outside this smaller example.

The locker begins with 5 units and 5 tokens. Request `A` for locker north succeeds: units become 9, tokens become 4. Save receipt `A` with `unitsAdded:4`, `tokensSpent:1`, `units:9`, `tokens:4`. Request `B` then succeeds: only three units fit, so units become 12 and tokens become 3. Receipt `B` records the actual three-unit addition.

Retrying `A` returns receipt `A`, including the balances 9 and 4 from that success. Current state stays at 12 units and 3 tokens. Returning 12 and 3 as receipt `A` would rewrite history; returning state 9 and 4 would roll back request `B`. The receipt and current state answer different questions.

First completion: begin a second locker at 10 units and 4 tokens. Fill the receipt and current balances after request `C` succeeds, then after an identical retry. Identify which numbers are historical and which describe the current state.

## 2. A failed ID is available; a successful ID is bound

In the sibling, request `D` for an unavailable locker fails. No resource changes and no successful receipt exists. When the locker becomes available, the same ID may succeed. Keeping a success-shaped record for the failure would falsely acknowledge work that never happened.

After successful `A` at locker north, an `A` request naming locker south conflicts. The old ID is already bound to north. It must not buy another operation or replace receipt `A`. Another user may use an `A` of their own because IDs belong to that user's record.

Once the sibling has three successful receipts, a fourth new ID is refused. Existing IDs can still be acknowledged. Discarding the oldest receipt to make space would turn its later retry into a new charge. Capacity is a lifecycle decision, not merely an array-trimming task.

Second completion: make a table with one failed request later retried successfully, a retry after another success, an ID conflict, and a new ID at receipt capacity. Fill “new charge?”, “new receipt?” and “which receipt returned?” for each. Explain the answer before implementing Courier's distinct cost, energy cap and two-receipt limit.

## 3. Implement by decision boundaries

The final capstone provides the interface and checks, not a completed starter algorithm. Keep the reference contract beside your editor. Write one branch at a time and decide which fields it may change.

| Milestone | Evidence to inspect |
| --- | --- |
| Fresh output | Input objects remain unchanged; returned state is a separate value. The actor is found by server-provided `actorId`. |
| Existing successful ID | A matching retry returns its original receipt and current state; a station conflict changes neither. Check before new-operation restrictions. |
| New ID refusal | Each ordered refusal returns `receipt:null`, without changing resources or consuming an ID. |
| One success | Actual energy gain, fixed cost and one complete receipt change together. A near-cap success records only the energy actually added. |

Do not calculate current balances from the spelling of a request ID, assume the request supplies a trustworthy actor or copy constants from this locker example. Courier's supplied state owns configuration, actor balances and station positions.

## 4. Plan independent HTTP evidence

Read [the HTTP test reference](http-tests.md) if request/response/assertion sequencing is unfamiliar. The capstone helper uses different names and a different endpoint from M3; import the helpers listed in its own contract.

For a repair test, save the server state before an action, send the request, inspect `reply.data.reason` and `reply.data.receipt`, then read current state. Compare only fields whose change the case is intended to permit. A refusal reason may change while energy, credits and receipt history must remain equal. A success changes those resources together.

Build a case matrix before writing the scenario:

| Behavior | What a status-only assertion would miss |
| --- | --- |
| Successful repair | Wrong debit, wrong actual energy gain, wrong receipt contents |
| Repeated success ID after later work or motion | Repeated debit, refreshed receipt balances, incorrect range recheck |
| Failed request then retry | An ID consumed by failure; resources changed on the refusal |
| Receipt capacity | Old receipt eviction and later charging of an old operation |
| Different actors | IDs incorrectly shared across actor records |
| Boundary and client claims | Ignored y distance, excluded exact edge, resource fields accepted from a request |

Keep the HTTP and pure-policy evidence separate. `moveActor` moves positions; it cannot manufacture arbitrary credits or energy. Some validated pure-policy cases therefore cover states your default HTTP session cannot reach. Conversely, an HTTP validation failure tests the request boundary before the policy is called.

Your complete scenario must pass both correct implementations and fail all named wrong variants using actual assertions. If a correct control fails, inspect setup and expectations first. If a wrong variant survives, identify the missing observation, not just another request to send. A timeout, import failure or arbitrary thrown error is no behavioral proof.

## Hints for a stuck practice case

<details><summary>Hint 1 — name the two histories</summary>

Separate current resources from the receipt of an earlier success. A retry needs both, because acknowledgment and current state may legitimately contain different balances.

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 2 — write a change set for every branch</summary>

For a refusal, the resource-and-history change set is empty. For a success, list debit, energy increase and appended receipt together. This exposes a mutation performed before a later check can refuse.

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 3 — worked sibling step, after a saved attempt</summary>

After locker requests `A` and `B`, retry `A` returns the old 9-unit/4-token receipt while leaving current state at 12 units/3 tokens. An assertion only on the word “duplicate” misses both a repeated charge and a rewritten receipt. Compare historical receipt fields and current state independently. Record this section as assistance.

</details>

# Construct an HTTP test

Use this reference after the M3 teaching and checks in [the guided route](/learn). It explains how to build the independent scenario described in [the order guide](../lab/order/LEARNER.md#your-scenario). The final scenario remains your work. The [support workflow](README.md) explains prediction capture and assistance.

## 1. Separate the four steps

An HTTP **request** asks the server to do something. The **response status** says how the request was handled. An **authoritative snapshot** reports state held by the server. An **assertion** compares that observed state with what the contract predicts and throws an error on disagreement.

Use four steps: arrange a known starting state, act through the public input path, observe the resulting owner state, then assert the relevant fields. In this lab, `await input(...)` waits for the HTTP response. It does not move the actor. `await advance(n)` invokes the owner's test clock and processes `n` ticks. `await state(...)` reads a snapshot without advancing time.

A `Promise` is an eventual result. An `async` function can use `await` to wait for it. If an input is not awaited, a later snapshot can race the request: a test failure may describe test ordering rather than game ordering. Keep these actions sequential until their order is deliberate.

## 2. Study a complete sibling

This checks the M1 remote-pickup rule, not the M3 ordering defects. In each supplied M3 seed, the new actor begins at `(1000,1000)` and the core is at least 1000 mm away. The interaction radius is 250 mm. The request is well-shaped, so HTTP 200 is expected; after the tick, cargo must still be false.

```js
import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
import { join, input, state } from './clients/http-client.mjs';

export async function scenario({ base, advance }) {
  const { token } = await join(base);
  const reply = await input(base, token, 1, 'idle', true);
  assert.equal(reply.status, 200, 'the owner handles a valid input');
  await advance(1);
  const observed = await state(base, token);
  assert.equal(observed.actor.cargo, false, 'remote interaction grants no cargo');
  assert.equal(observed.lastDecision.reason, 'range', 'owner applies the range rule');
}
```

`assert.equal(actual, expected, message)` places the observation first and the prediction second. A useful message names the rule, not “test 1.” Leave assertion failures uncaught so the runner can distinguish a behavioral disagreement from a completed scenario.

This code is a worked sibling. It can pass while all seven ordering defects survive. It therefore cannot stand in for your independent submission.

## 3. Complete, then remove more support

First completion: reuse the sibling's arrange, request, tick and snapshot. Add an assertion that remote pickup does not increase `observed.actor.score`. Record the expected score before running; derive it from the starting score and the absence of a delivery. Read the result and explain any mismatch.

Second completion: start another fresh actor, save its `x` and `y`, submit an idle input and process one tick. Write both position assertions without copying the finished cargo assertions. This checks your use of observations without yet solving an ordering case. A changed `lastDecision` is allowed; idle position is the property under test.

Now write an independent M3 case. State the expected effect before coding, identify the snapshot fields that can reveal it, then choose requests and tick boundaries that make correct and incorrect behavior differ. Test an ordering rule, not the already solved remote-pickup rule.

## 4. Turn each requirement into an observation

Use the exact limits and helper signatures in the order guide. `advance` is an owner test control, not an HTTP endpoint available to a player. A fresh actor starts with `lastSeq:0`, `expiresAt:0`, `score:0` and `cargo:false`. The server snapshot exposes those fields along with position. It does not expose the private direction or staged interaction bit directly.

| Requirement | Observable evidence to plan |
| --- | --- |
| Older or equal sequences do not change intent | Admit one direction, deliver a conflicting retry, then inspect movement on a named subsequent tick. A receipt alone cannot show retained direction. |
| A stale input cannot stage interaction | Arrange an interaction opportunity and compare cargo/score after the next tick. Reading `lastSeq` alone cannot reveal the staged bit. |
| Four ticks are active and the fifth is not | Record position around both boundary ticks on open floor. A wall can make early and late expiry look identical. |
| Polling is read-only | Compare the same actor before and after snapshots, and inspect movement at the original expiry. No input should occur between the observations. |
| A retry creates no cheating finding | Inspect the `findings` array after the retry, alongside state. A status code is silent about advisory findings. |

Keep a small expected-state table next to the case while writing it. Record processed tick, sequence, position and the specific interaction/finding fields you need. Assertions should follow from that table; do not generate expected values by calling the policy you are testing.

## Milestones

| Milestone | Evidence before moving on |
| --- | --- |
| One valid exchange | The sibling completes with an awaited request, tick and snapshot. Its assertions check the known M1 outcome. |
| One independent ordering case | Explain which wrong behavior changes one of your asserted values. Confirm the case on each seed through `order:check`. |
| Boundary coverage | Include both sides of expiry, stale and equal sequence behavior, read-only polling and findings. The result names which wrong variants survive. |
| Complete scenario | Both correct controls pass and every named wrong variant triggers a real assertion. Preserve the failed attempt and repair only the missing distinction. |

The checker separately assesses your policy and scenario. “Wrong variants survive” means the test still accepts at least one wrong behavior. An import error or timeout does not count as detecting it. “A correct control fails” means your expected result or setup needs inspection before the mutant score is meaningful.

## Hints for a stuck practice case

<details><summary>Hint 1 — identify what the rule owns</summary>

Write which state may change on admission and which changes only on a tick. This prevents an assertion on the HTTP response from standing in for the engine effect.

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 2 — choose a separating moment</summary>

Use two conflicting directions, or inspect the tick on each side of the declared expiry. If both implementations reach the same wall, choose another starting path; the observation must expose the intended difference.

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 3 — worked sibling step, after a saved attempt</summary>

In the remote-pickup sibling, HTTP 200 and `cargo:false` can both be correct. The response accepts an input; only the following tick evaluates the distant interaction. That is why the cargo assertion belongs after `advance(1)` and a new snapshot. Apply that separation of request and effect to your own ordering case. Record this section as assistance.

</details>

# Build a timing predictor one state transition at a time

Start with M4 in [the guided route](/learn), then use [the timing contract](../timing/LEARNER.md#the-contract) for exact fields. This reference supplies smaller worked cases and an implementation sequence. It does not supply `predictTiming`. Record help using the [support workflow](README.md).

## 1. Name the state before the loop

The predictor is a **state machine**: read one action, change only the state that action owns, then append a snapshot. Keep four kinds of state separate:

| State | Meaning | Changed by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Clock reading and fractional remainder | Owner milliseconds already accounted for, plus less than one tick of unused time | `sample` |
| Processed tick and overrun count | Work actually performed, plus callbacks that dropped whole ticks | `sample` |
| Actor and connection state | Position, current private direction, sequence, expiry and connected flag | Relevant actor actions and processed ticks |
| Checkpoint list | Detached observations after each action | Every action |

The action's `id` is a connection label. The returned actor's `id` is generated as `actor-1`, `actor-2`, and so on. Store the private direction for later movement, but do not include it in returned actors. Build a new actor snapshot each time; storing the same mutable object in every checkpoint makes earlier observations change when you process later actions.

## 2. Work a smaller clock

This sibling clock uses **10 ms per tick and at most two processed ticks per sample**, different from Courier's 50 ms and five. It begins at reading 100, tick 0, remainder 0, overruns 0.

For each sample, add `new reading − previous reading + old remainder`. Divide that amount into whole due ticks and a fraction. Process no more than the cap, discard excess whole ticks, retain only the fraction, then save the new reading. An overrun counts the sample that dropped work, not every dropped tick.

| New reading | Available ms | Due ticks | Processed | Dropped | Remainder | Total tick | Overruns |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 107 | 7 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 7 | 0 | 0 |
| 116 | 16 | 1 | 1 | 0 | 6 | 1 | 0 |
| 151 | 41 | 4 | 2 | 2 | 1 | 3 | 1 |
| 151 | 1 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 1 | 3 | 1 |

The delayed sample advances two processed ticks. The two dropped ticks do not remain in a debt queue. The repeated reading advances none. Neither four nor forty requests would themselves add a clock tick.

First completion: start from the final row and sample at 160. Fill available milliseconds, due, processed, dropped, remainder and total tick before checking your calculation. Use the fraction already retained; do not restart at zero.

Second completion: make your own three-row sibling trace with one fractional sample, one capped sample and one repeated reading. Explain why your final tick is the sum of **processed** ticks. Have `/learn` check a new Courier clock case before implementing the full loop.

## 3. Join clock work to actor work

A receipt records delivery of an input, not motion. A new sequence changes private direction and sets expiry from the current processed tick. Each processed tick then checks whether that tick falls within the admitted window. Disconnect changes delivery availability; it does not reverse an input the owner already admitted.

Work a sibling actor with a three-tick intent window. It starts at x=20. Each active step adds 2. An east input admitted at tick 8 expires at 11. Ticks 9, 10 and 11 produce x=22, 24 and 26. Tick 12 leaves x=26. If the connection goes offline just after tick 9, the admitted motion still reaches x=26; a new input while offline changes none of that state. Resuming the same connection restores delivery to the same actor.

Completion: start a different sibling at x=30 with a west input admitted at tick 4 under that three-tick rule. Fill its expiry, positions at ticks 5 through 8 and the effect of retrying the same sequence after resume. Then return to Courier's own **four-tick** window and **250 mm** steps. Do not copy the sibling constants.

If a Courier sample processes several ticks, apply movement once for each processed tick in order. Evaluate expiry at each new tick, not only once at the sample's end. Otherwise a sample crossing expiry can incorrectly move for all or none of its steps.

## 4. Build, check and add one concern

| Milestone | Trace to prepare | Evidence to inspect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Clock only | `sample` actions, no actors; include fractions and a repeated reading | One checkpoint per action, correct `clock`, no receipt, sum of processed ticks |
| One actor | Join, newer input, then samples spanning expiry | Position stays unchanged at receipt; movement stops after the fourth active Courier tick |
| Delivery and identity | Duplicate/older input, disconnect, offline input, resume, fresh join | Rejected inputs leave intent and expiry intact; resume keeps an actor; fresh join adds one |
| Full output | A mixed action record | Old checkpoints retain old values; only input has a receipt and only sample has a clock result |

These are implementation milestones, not separate scoring commands. Use the core check after a coherent source attempt and inspect its first failed checkpoint. Compare the earliest differing field before repairing later outputs. For example, a wrong expiry can explain several later positions; changing each position independently hides the first cause.

## Hints for a stuck practice trace

<details><summary>Hint 1 — decide which clock you mean</summary>

Label each number as client annotation, owner reading or processed tick. Only the current processed tick grants an input's movement window; this avoids turning a client's timestamp into authority.

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 2 — split the sample into two calculations</summary>

Compute whole ticks and fraction first. Compute capped work and dropped work second. The fraction is below one tick even when the callback was badly delayed, so dropped whole work cannot return on the next sample.

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 3 — worked sibling step, after a saved attempt</summary>

In the 10 ms sibling, the jump from 116 to 151 contributes 35 new ms plus the old 6 ms. Forty-one ms means four whole ticks and 1 ms left. The cap processes two, drops two, increments the overrun count once, and advances total tick from 1 to 3. Record this section as assistance, then recompute your own case with Courier's constants.

</details>

```

`courses/anti-cheat-engineering/courier-lab/learning/grade.mjs`:

```mjs
import { isDeepStrictEqual } from 'node:util';

// Format failures are recorded, but are not scored attempts and reveal no key.
export function grade(item, rawAnswer) {
  const type = item.format.type;
  let value;
  if (typeof rawAnswer !== 'string' || rawAnswer.length > 65_536) return invalid('Enter an answer of at most 65,536 characters.');
  if (type === 'number') {
    if (!rawAnswer.trim() || !/^[+-]?(?:\d+\.?\d*|\.\d+)(?:e[+-]?\d+)?$/i.test(rawAnswer.trim())) return invalid('Enter a finite number.');
    value = Number(rawAnswer);
    if (!Number.isFinite(value)) return invalid('Enter a finite number.');
    return scored(value, Math.abs(value - item.expected) <= (item.tolerance ?? 0));
  }
  if (type === 'choice') {
    if (!item.format.options.some((option) => option.value === rawAnswer)) return invalid('Choose one of the listed options.');
    return scored(rawAnswer, rawAnswer === item.expected);
  }
  if (type === 'json') {
    try { value = JSON.parse(rawAnswer); } catch { return invalid('Enter valid JSON. Your original text has been saved; it has not been scored.'); }
    return scored(value, isDeepStrictEqual(value, item.expected));
  }
  throw new Error('Unsupported item format.');
}

function invalid(message) { return { status: 'format-error', message }; }
function scored(value, correct) { return { status: 'scored', value, correct }; }

export function validateItem(item) {
  if (!item || typeof item.id !== 'string' || typeof item.prompt !== 'string' || !item.prompt.trim()) throw new Error('Invalid generated item.');
  if (!Array.isArray(item.objectiveIds) || item.objectiveIds.length === 0) throw new Error('Item needs objectives.');
  if (!['number', 'choice', 'json'].includes(item.format?.type)) throw new Error('Invalid item format.');
  if (item.format.type === 'number' && !Number.isFinite(item.expected)) throw new Error('Expected number must be finite.');
  if (item.tolerance !== undefined && (item.format.type !== 'number' || !Number.isFinite(item.tolerance) || item.tolerance < 0)) throw new Error('Invalid explicit numeric tolerance.');
  if (item.format.type !== 'choice') return;
  const options = item.format.options;
  if (!Array.isArray(options) || options.length < 2 || options.some((option) => typeof option.value !== 'string' || typeof option.label !== 'string')) throw new Error('Invalid choice options.');
  if (new Set(options.map((option) => option.value)).size !== options.length || !options.some((option) => option.value === item.expected)) throw new Error('Invalid choice key.');
}

`courses/anti-cheat-engineering/courier-lab/learning/runtime.mjs`:

```mjs
import { createHash } from 'node:crypto';
import { readFile, readdir } from 'node:fs/promises';
import { join, relative } from 'node:path';
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
import { grade, validateItem } from './grade.mjs';

export const UNIT_IDS = Object.freeze(['spatial', 'order', 'testing', 'timing', 'integrity', 'telemetry', 'evaluation', 'retention', 'recovery', 'capstone']);
export const SCHEMA = 'anti-cheat-learning/v1';

export async function loadUnits() {
  // Conservative owner-source pin: helpers may be imported directly, indirectly,
  // or dynamically. Runtime artifacts and learner files do not change this pin.
  const sourceVersion = await sourceTreeVersion(fileURLToPath(new URL('../', import.meta.url)));
  return Promise.all(UNIT_IDS.map(async (id) => {
    const module = await import(`./units/${id}.mjs`);
    if (module.unit?.id !== id || typeof module.makeItem !== 'function') throw new Error(`Invalid learning unit: ${id}`);
    return { ...module, sourceVersion };
  }));
}

async function sourceTreeVersion(root) {
  const excluded = new Set(['artifacts', 'node_modules', '.tmp', 'tests', '.git']);
  const files = [];
  async function visit(directory) {
    for (const entry of await readdir(directory, { withFileTypes: true })) {
      if (excluded.has(entry.name) || entry.isSymbolicLink()) continue;
      const path = join(directory, entry.name);
      if (entry.isDirectory()) await visit(path);
      if (entry.isFile() && /\.(?:mjs|js|json)$/.test(entry.name)) files.push(path);
    }
  }
  await visit(root);
  const hash = createHash('sha256');
  for (const path of files.sort()) hash.update(relative(root, path)).update('\0').update(await readFile(path)).update('\0');
  return hash.digest('hex');
}

export function catalog(modules) {
  return modules.map(({ unit }) => ({
    ...unit,
    sections: unit.sections.map(({ worked, ...section }) => ({ ...section, worked: { prompt: worked.prompt } })),
    support: { milestones: unit.support?.milestones ?? [], reference: unit.support?.reference },
  }));
}

export function newSession(sessionId, modules, now) {
  return { schema: SCHEMA, sessionId, createdAt: now, catalogVersion: catalogVersion(modules), unitSnapshots: structuredClone(modules.map(({ unit }) => unit)), events: [], items: [], masterySets: [] };
}

function catalogVersion(modules) { return createHash('sha256').update(JSON.stringify(modules.map(({ unit, makeItem, sourceVersion }) => [unit, sourceVersion ?? String(makeItem)]))).digest('hex'); }

function findUnit(modules, id) {
  const module = modules.find(({ unit }) => unit.id === id);
  if (!module) throw problem(400, 'unknown-unit', 'Choose a listed unit.');
  return module;
}

export function findItem(state, id) {
  const item = state.items.find((record) => record.id === id);
  if (!item) throw problem(404, 'unknown-item', 'This item is not in the saved session.');
  return item;
}

export function publicItem(record) {
  const { id, unitId, mode, key, seed, generatedAt, definition, attempts, hints } = record;
  const { prompt, inputs, format, objectiveIds, source, tolerance } = definition;
  return { id, unitId, mode, key, seed, generatedAt, prompt, inputs, format, objectiveIds, source, tolerance, attempts, hints };
}

export function issueItem(state, modules, request, seed, now) {
  if (state.catalogVersion !== catalogVersion(modules)) throw problem(409, 'course-version-changed', 'This record belongs to an earlier course version. Export it, then start a separate session for new items.');
  const { unit, makeItem } = findUnit(modules, request.unitId);
  const { mode, key } = request;
  if (!['practice', 'completion', 'mastery'].includes(mode)) throw problem(400, 'invalid-mode', 'Choose completion, practice, or mastery.');
  const keys = mode === 'mastery' ? unit.masterySlots : unit.sections.map((section) => section.id);
  if (!keys.includes(key)) throw problem(400, 'unknown-key', 'Choose a listed section or mastery slot.');
  const definition = structuredClone(makeItem({ mode, key, seed }));
  validateItem(definition);
  if (definition.objectiveIds.some((id) => !unit.objectives.some((objective) => objective.id === id))) throw new Error('Generated item refers to an unknown objective.');
  const sameCase = state.items.some((record) => {
    if (record.unitId !== unit.id) return false;
    if ((mode === 'mastery' || record.mode === 'mastery') && caseIdentity(record.definition) === caseIdentity(definition)) return true;
    return record.mode === mode && record.key === key && JSON.stringify([record.definition.prompt, record.definition.inputs]) === JSON.stringify([definition.prompt, definition.inputs]);
  });
  if (sameCase) throw problem(409, 'repeated-case', 'The generator repeated a case. Request another fresh item.');
  const record = { id: `${unit.id}-${state.items.length + 1}-${seed}`, unitId: unit.id, mode, key, seed, generatedAt: now, definition, attempts: [], hints: [] };
  state.items.push(record);
  state.events.push({ type: 'item-issued', itemId: record.id, at: now });
  return publicItem(record);
}

export function issueMastery(state, modules, unitId, nextSeed, now) {
  const { unit } = findUnit(modules, unitId);
  if (unit.masterySlots.length !== 3) throw new Error('Mastery requires three authored slots.');
  const items = unit.masterySlots.map((key) => issueFresh(state, modules, { unitId, mode: 'mastery', key }, nextSeed, now));
  const set = { id: `${unitId}-set-${state.masterySets.length + 1}`, unitId, generatedAt: now, itemIds: items.map((item) => item.id) };
  state.masterySets.push(set);
  state.events.push({ type: 'mastery-issued', setId: set.id, at: now });
  return { ...set, items };
}

export function issueFresh(state, modules, input, nextSeed, now) {
  for (let count = 0; count < 32; count += 1) {
    try { return issueItem(state, modules, input, nextSeed(), now); } catch (error) { if (error.code !== 'repeated-case') throw error; }
  }
  throw problem(409, 'case-bank-exhausted', 'A distinct case could not be generated. Your earlier record is unchanged.');
}

function caseIdentity(item) {
  if (item.caseFingerprint !== undefined) return canonicalJson(item.caseFingerprint);
  if (item.inputs && Object.keys(item.inputs).length > 0) {
    // Completed working is teaching scaffolding, not a different problem.
    const { completedSteps, ...inputs } = item.inputs;
    return canonicalJson(inputs);
  }
  return canonicalJson([item.prompt, item.expected]);
}

function canonicalJson(value) {
  if (Array.isArray(value)) return `[${value.map(canonicalJson).join(',')}]`;
  if (value && typeof value === 'object') return `{${Object.keys(value).sort().map((key) => `${JSON.stringify(key)}:${canonicalJson(value[key])}`).join(',')}}`;
  return JSON.stringify(value);
}

function assistanceValues(value) {
  if (!Array.isArray(value) || value.length > 20 || value.some((entry) => typeof entry !== 'string' || entry.length > 2000)) throw problem(400, 'assistance-required', 'Declare assistance as a list, using an empty list for none.');
  return value;
}

export function submit(state, itemId, rawAnswer, assistance, now) {
  if (typeof rawAnswer !== 'string' || rawAnswer.length > 65_536) throw problem(400, 'invalid-answer', 'Submit the original answer as text, up to 65,536 characters.');
  const record = findItem(state, itemId);
  const declared = assistanceValues(assistance);
  const result = grade(record.definition, rawAnswer);
  const scoredBefore = record.attempts.some((attempt) => attempt.status === 'scored');
  const attempt = {
    revision: record.attempts.length + 1, at: now, rawAnswer, status: result.status,
    assistance: declared, assisted: declared.length > 0 || record.hints.length > 0 || scoredBefore || record.attempts.some((attempt) => attempt.assisted) || state.events.some((event) => event.assistedItemIds?.includes(itemId)),
    firstScored: result.status === 'scored' && !scoredBefore,
  };
  if (result.status === 'format-error') attempt.message = result.message;
  if (result.status === 'scored') {
    attempt.answer = result.value;
    attempt.correct = result.correct;
    attempt.feedback = { expected: record.definition.expected, explanation: record.definition.explanation, source: record.definition.source };
  }
  record.attempts.push(attempt);
  state.events.push({ type: 'submission', itemId, revision: attempt.revision, at: now });
  return { item: publicItem(record), attempt };
}

export function hint(state, itemId, now) {
  const record = findItem(state, itemId);
  if (record.mode === 'mastery') throw problem(400, 'mastery-no-hints', 'Mastery items have no hints. Return to the teaching and start a fresh set when ready.');
  const level = record.hints.length;
  if (level >= 3 || !record.definition.hints?.[level]) throw problem(400, 'no-more-hints', 'There are no further hints for this item.');
  if (level === 2 && !record.attempts.some((attempt) => attempt.status === 'scored')) throw problem(409, 'commit-before-solution', 'Commit a valid answer before viewing the worked solution.');
  const reveal = { level: level + 1, text: record.definition.hints[level], at: now };
  record.hints.push(reveal);
  state.events.push({ type: 'hint', itemId, level: reveal.level, at: now });
  return reveal;
}

export function revealWorked(state, modules, { unitId, key, prediction, skipReason }, now) {
  const { unit } = findUnit(state.unitSnapshots.map((unit) => ({ unit })), unitId);
  const section = unit.sections.find((candidate) => candidate.id === key);
  if (!section) throw problem(400, 'unknown-key', 'Choose a listed section.');
  if (typeof prediction !== 'string' || typeof skipReason !== 'string' || prediction.length > 8000 || skipReason.length > 2000 || (!prediction.trim() && !skipReason.trim())) throw problem(400, 'prediction-required', 'Write a prediction or an explicit reason for skipping it before revealing the example.');
  const exposure = { type: 'worked-exposure', unitId, key, prompt: section.worked.prompt, prediction, skipReason, worked: structuredClone(section.worked), assistedItemIds: pendingMastery(state, unitId), at: now };
  state.events.push(exposure);
  return exposure;
}

export function referenceExposure(state, unitId, path, now) {
  const event = { type: 'reference-exposure', unitId, path, assistedItemIds: pendingMastery(state, unitId), at: now };
  state.events.push(event);
  return event;
}

export function visitSection(state, unitId, key, now) {
  const unit = state.unitSnapshots.find((unit) => unit.id === unitId);
  if (!unit?.sections.some((section) => section.id === key)) throw problem(400, 'unknown-section', 'Choose a listed teaching section.');
  const event = { type: 'section-visit', unitId, key, assistedItemIds: pendingMastery(state, unitId), at: now };
  state.events.push(event);
  return event;
}

function pendingMastery(state, unitId) {
  return state.items.filter((record) => record.unitId === unitId && record.mode === 'mastery' && !record.attempts.some((attempt) => attempt.status === 'scored')).map((record) => record.id);
}

function setResult(state, set, unit) {
  const answers = set.itemIds.map((id) => {
    const record = findItem(state, id);
    const first = record.attempts.find((attempt) => attempt.firstScored);
    return { itemId: id, objectiveIds: record.definition.objectiveIds, status: !first ? 'pending' : first.correct && !first.assisted ? 'passed' : 'needs-practice' };
  });
  const objectives = unit.objectives.map(({ id, text }) => {
    const relevant = answers.filter((answer) => answer.objectiveIds.includes(id));
    const status = relevant.length === 0 ? 'unassessed' : relevant.some((answer) => answer.status === 'needs-practice') ? 'needs-practice' : relevant.some((answer) => answer.status === 'pending') ? 'pending' : 'passed';
    return { id, text, status };
  });
  const complete = answers.every((answer) => answer.status !== 'pending');
  const passed = complete && answers.every((answer) => answer.status === 'passed') && objectives.every((objective) => objective.status === 'passed');
  return { ...set, answers, objectives, complete, passed, status: passed ? 'mastered' : complete ? 'needs-practice' : 'in-progress' };
}

export function sessionView(state, modules) {
  const snapshots = state.unitSnapshots.map((unit) => ({ unit }));
  const masterySets = state.masterySets.map((set) => setResult(state, set, findUnit(snapshots, set.unitId).unit));
  const units = snapshots.map(({ unit }) => {
    const sets = masterySets.filter((set) => set.unitId === unit.id);
    const latest = sets.at(-1);
    return { id: unit.id, status: latest?.status ?? 'not-started', objectives: latest?.objectives ?? unit.objectives.map(({ id, text }) => ({ id, text, status: 'unassessed' })), previouslyMastered: sets.some((set) => set.passed) };
  });
  return { schema: state.schema, sessionId: state.sessionId, createdAt: state.createdAt, catalogVersion: state.catalogVersion, items: state.items.map(publicItem), masterySets, units, exposures: state.events.filter((event) => event.type === 'worked-exposure') };
}

export function evidenceExport(state, modules) {
  return { ...sessionView(state, modules), events: state.events, boundary: 'Local practice record. The machine owner can edit files. Generated mastery is not proctored evidence of learning or a credential.' };
}

export function problem(status, code, message) { return Object.assign(new Error(message), { status, code }); }

import { mkdir, open, readFile, rename, unlink } from 'node:fs/promises';
import { randomBytes, randomInt } from 'node:crypto';
import { dirname, resolve, sep } from 'node:path';
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
import { catalog, evidenceExport, hint, issueFresh, issueMastery, loadUnits, newSession, problem, referenceExposure, revealWorked, SCHEMA, sessionView, submit, visitSection } from './runtime.mjs';

const PROJECT = fileURLToPath(new URL('../', import.meta.url));
const MAX_RECORD = 16 * 1024 * 1024;
const MAX_BODY = 96 * 1024;
export const LEARNING_ROUTES = new Map([
  ['/learning/catalog', 'GET'],
  ...['session', 'state', 'item', 'mastery', 'submit', 'hint', 'worked', 'reference', 'visit', 'export'].map((name) => [`/learning/${name}`, 'POST']),
]);

export function createLearningService({ modules = loadUnits, directory = process.env.LEARNING_DATA_DIR || resolve(PROJECT, '.tmp/learning'), now = () => new Date().toISOString(), nextSeed = () => randomInt(1, 0x1_0000_0000), persist = saveAtomic, referenceRoot = PROJECT } = {}) {
  let loaded;
  const locks = new Map();
  const getModules = () => loaded ??= Promise.resolve(typeof modules === 'function' ? modules() : modules).catch((error) => { loaded = undefined; throw problem(503, 'learning-unavailable', `Learning units are unavailable: ${error.message}`); });
  const fileFor = (id) => {
    if (typeof id !== 'string' || !/^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{43}$/.test(id)) throw problem(400, 'session-required', 'Start or restore a learning session.');
    return resolve(directory, `${id}.json`);
  };
  async function readState(id) {
    try {
      const state = JSON.parse(await readFile(fileFor(id), 'utf8'));
      if (state.schema !== SCHEMA || state.sessionId !== id) throw new Error('Invalid record schema.');
      return state;
    } catch (error) {
      if (error.status) throw error;
      if (error.code === 'ENOENT') throw problem(404, 'session-not-found', 'This saved session is unavailable. Keep your session ID and export; start a new session only if intended.');
      throw problem(503, 'record-unreadable', 'The saved record cannot be read. Existing files have not been changed.');
    }
  }
  async function save(state) {
    try { await persist(fileFor(state.sessionId), state); } catch { throw problem(507, 'record-not-saved', 'The record could not be saved. No new feedback or answer has been revealed. Keep your answer and retry after storage is available.'); }
  }
  async function mutate(id, operation) {
    const previous = locks.get(id) ?? Promise.resolve();
    const next = previous.catch(() => {}).then(async () => {
      const state = await readState(id);
      const result = await operation(state, await getModules());
      await save(state);
      return { ...result, progress: sessionView(state, await getModules()).units };
    });
    locks.set(id, next);
    try { return await next; } finally { if (locks.get(id) === next) locks.delete(id); }
  }
  async function reference(state, all, input) {
    const unit = state.unitSnapshots.find((unit) => unit.id === input.unitId);
    if (!unit) throw problem(400, 'unknown-unit', 'Choose a listed unit.');
    const section = input.key === undefined ? undefined : unit.sections.find((entry) => entry.id === input.key);
    if (input.key !== undefined && !section) throw problem(400, 'unknown-key', 'Choose a listed section.');
    const path = section?.source?.path ?? unit.support?.reference;
    if (typeof path !== 'string') throw problem(404, 'reference-unavailable', 'This unit has no reference file.');
    const target = resolve(referenceRoot, path);
    if (!target.startsWith(resolve(referenceRoot) + sep)) throw problem(400, 'invalid-reference', 'The reference must be inside this course.');
    let content;
    try { content = await readFile(target, 'utf8'); } catch { throw problem(404, 'reference-unavailable', 'The reference file is unavailable. Your learning record is unchanged.'); }
    referenceExposure(state, unit.id, path, now());
    return { path, anchor: section?.source?.anchor, content };
  }
  return {
    async request(route, input = {}) {
      if (route === '/learning/catalog') return { units: catalog(await getModules()), boundary: 'Local toy course. The machine owner can inspect keys and edit records. Mastery means all three generated items were correct on unassisted first scored responses; it is not evidence of human learning or a credential.' };
      if (route === '/learning/session') {
        const state = newSession(randomBytes(32).toString('base64url'), await getModules(), now());
        await save(state);
        return sessionView(state, await getModules());
      }
      if (route === '/learning/state') return sessionView(await readState(input.sessionId), await getModules());
      if (route === '/learning/export') return evidenceExport(await readState(input.sessionId), await getModules());
      return mutate(input.sessionId, async (state, all) => {
        if (route === '/learning/item') {
          if (!['completion', 'practice'].includes(input.mode)) throw problem(400, 'invalid-mode', 'Use a completion or practice item, or request a complete mastery set.');
          return { item: issueFresh(state, all, input, nextSeed, now()) };
        }
        if (route === '/learning/mastery') return { set: issueMastery(state, all, input.unitId, nextSeed, now()) };
        if (route === '/learning/submit') return submit(state, input.itemId, input.answer, input.assistance, now());
        if (route === '/learning/hint') return { hint: hint(state, input.itemId, now()) };
        if (route === '/learning/worked') return { exposure: revealWorked(state, all, input, now()) };
        if (route === '/learning/visit') return { visit: visitSection(state, input.unitId, input.key, now()) };
        if (route === '/learning/reference') return reference(state, all, input);
        throw problem(404, 'not-found', 'Unknown learning operation.');
      });
    },
  };
}

export async function saveAtomic(path, state) {
  const bytes = JSON.stringify(state, null, 2) + '\n';
  if (Buffer.byteLength(bytes) > MAX_RECORD) throw new Error('Record capacity reached. Export and start a fresh session.');
  await mkdir(dirname(path), { recursive: true, mode: 0o700 });
  const temporary = `${path}.${randomBytes(8).toString('hex')}.tmp`;
  try {
    const file = await open(temporary, 'wx', 0o600);
    try { await file.writeFile(bytes); await file.sync(); } finally { await file.close(); }
    await rename(temporary, path);
  } finally { await unlink(temporary).catch(() => {}); }
}

export function createLearningHandler(service) {
  return async (request, response) => {
    try {
      const input = request.method === 'POST' ? await readJson(request) : {};
      const body = await service.request(request.url, input);
      send(response, 200, body);
    } catch (error) {
      send(response, error.status ?? 500, { error: error.code ?? 'learning-error', message: error.status ? error.message : 'Learning operation failed. No new result has been revealed.' });
      request.resume();
    }
  };
}

async function readJson(request) {
  if (!/^application\/json(?:\s*;\s*charset=utf-8)?$/i.test(request.headers['content-type'] ?? '')) throw problem(415, 'content-type', 'Use JSON for learning requests.');
  if (Number(request.headers['content-length'] ?? 0) > MAX_BODY) throw problem(413, 'body-too-large', 'The submitted answer is too large.');
  const chunks = [];
  let size = 0;
  for await (const chunk of request) {
    size += chunk.length;
    if (size > MAX_BODY) throw problem(413, 'body-too-large', 'The submitted answer is too large.');
    chunks.push(chunk);
  }
  try {
    const input = JSON.parse(Buffer.concat(chunks).toString('utf8'));
    if (!input || Array.isArray(input) || typeof input !== 'object') throw new Error('Object required.');
    return input;
  } catch { throw problem(400, 'invalid-json', 'Use a JSON object.'); }
}

function send(response, status, body) {
  const bytes = Buffer.from(JSON.stringify(body));
  response.writeHead(status, { 'content-type': 'application/json; charset=utf-8', 'content-length': bytes.length, 'cache-control': 'no-store', 'x-content-type-options': 'nosniff' });
  response.end(bytes);
}

function hashSeed(seed) { let n = 2166136261; for (const c of String(seed)) n = Math.imul(n ^ c.charCodeAt(0), 16777619) >>> 0; return n; }
function stateCase(n, identity) {
  const config = { repairCost: 2 + n % 3, repairEnergy: 2 + n % 4, energyCap: 12, rangeMm: 100, receiptLimit: 2 };
  const request = { requestId: `request-${n % 31}`, stationId: 'alpha' };
  const receipt = { requestId: request.requestId, stationId: 'alpha', energyAdded: 2, creditsSpent: config.repairCost, energy: 8, credits: 7 };
  const actor = { id: 'actor-a', x: 0, y: 0, energy: 3 + n % 7, credits: 10, receipts: [] };
  const state = { config, stations: [{ id: 'alpha', x: 0, y: 0 }, { id: 'beta', x: 500, y: 0 }], actors: [actor, { id: 'actor-b', x: 0, y: 0, energy: 2, credits: 10, receipts: [structuredClone(receipt)] }] };
  if (identity && n % 4 < 2) { actor.receipts.push(receipt); actor.x = 1000; }
  if (identity && n % 4 === 1) request.stationId = 'beta';
  if (!identity && n % 6 === 0) actor.x = 100;
  if (!identity && n % 6 === 1) actor.x = 101;
  if (!identity && n % 6 === 2) actor.energy = config.energyCap;
  if (!identity && n % 6 === 3) actor.credits = config.repairCost - 1;
  if (!identity && n % 6 === 4) { actor.receipts = [{ ...receipt, requestId: 'old-a' }, { ...receipt, requestId: 'old-b' }]; actor.x = 101; }
  if (!identity && n % 6 === 5) request.stationId = 'missing';
  return { state, actorId: actor.id, request };
}
function resultFor({ state, actorId, request }) {
  const actor = structuredClone(state.actors.find((a) => a.id === actorId));
  const previous = actor.receipts.find((r) => r.requestId === request.requestId);
  const result = (reason, receipt = null) => ({ reason, receipt, energy: actor.energy, credits: actor.credits, receiptCount: actor.receipts.length });
  if (previous && previous.stationId !== request.stationId) return result('conflict');
  if (previous) return result('duplicate', previous);
  const station = state.stations.find((s) => s.id === request.stationId);
  if (!station) return result('station');
  if (actor.receipts.length >= state.config.receiptLimit) return result('history-full');
  if ((actor.x - station.x) ** 2 + (actor.y - station.y) ** 2 > state.config.rangeMm ** 2) return result('range');
  if (actor.energy >= state.config.energyCap) return result('full');
  if (actor.credits < state.config.repairCost) return result('funds');
  const energyAdded = Math.min(state.config.repairEnergy, state.config.energyCap - actor.energy);
  actor.energy += energyAdded;
  actor.credits -= state.config.repairCost;
  const receipt = { ...request, energyAdded, creditsSpent: state.config.repairCost, energy: actor.energy, credits: actor.credits };
  actor.receipts.push(receipt);
  return result('repaired', receipt);
}
function observationExperiment(n, base) {
  const actorId = 'actor-a';
  const kind = (n >>> 3) % 3;
  const priorId = `accepted-${n % 101}`;
  const config = { repairCost: 1 + n % 4, repairEnergy: 2 + (n >>> 5) % 5, energyCap: 12 + (n >>> 10) % 5 };
  const priorReceipts = [{ actorId: kind === 2 ? 'actor-b' : actorId, requestId: priorId, stationId: 'alpha', energyAdded: 2, creditsSpent: config.repairCost, energy: 9, credits: 4 }];
  const request = { requestId: kind === 1 ? `fresh-${n % 103}` : priorId, stationId: 'alpha' };
  const savedReceipts = priorReceipts.filter((r) => r.actorId === actorId).map(({ actorId: owner, ...receipt }) => receipt);
  const snapshotBefore = n % 2 === 0 ? { actorId, energy: 1 + (n >>> 14) % 6, credits: config.repairCost + 6 + (n >>> 19) % 8, receipts: savedReceipts } : null;
  const duplicate = priorReceipts.some((r) => r.actorId === actorId && r.requestId === request.requestId);
  const expected = { probe: 'actor-state', when: snapshotBefore ? 'after' : 'before-and-after', operation: duplicate ? 'duplicate' : 'new', creditsDelta: duplicate ? 0 : -config.repairCost, energyInvariant: duplicate ? 'unchanged' : 'add-up-to-cap', receiptCountDelta: duplicate ? 0 : 1, receiptIdentity: duplicate ? 'preserve-existing' : 'record-request', replyAloneSuffices: false };
  const inputs = {
    experiment: 'matching-replies-hidden-state', actorId, request, config, priorReceipts, snapshotBefore,
    preconditions: 'The request has not run. The actor is at alpha, below the energy cap, has enough credits and room for a new receipt. No concurrent action or history eviction occurs during this probe.',
    availableProbes: [
      { id: 'repair-reply', returns: 'The POST reply; the two candidate implementations return identical bytes, even if one changes hidden state incorrectly.' },
      { id: 'actor-state', returns: 'A read-only authoritative snapshot of this actor: energy, credits and successful receipts.' },
      { id: 'other-actor-state', returns: 'A read-only snapshot of actor-b only.' },
      { id: 'station-list', returns: 'Station coordinates, with no actor balances or receipts.' },
    ],
  };
  return { ...base, objectiveIds: ['capstone.identity', 'capstone.transaction', 'capstone.observe'], inputs, expected, hints: [],
    prompt: 'Design the smallest observation experiment that can expose hidden repair side effects when two implementations return matching POST replies. The trigger request has not run. Choose one available probe and schedule its read(s) around that one trigger. A non-null snapshotBefore is a complete saved authoritative baseline and needs no new before-read; historical receipt balances are not a current baseline. Return exactly {probe,when,operation,creditsDelta,energyInvariant,receiptCountDelta,receiptIdentity,replyAloneSuffices}. Use when after or before-and-after; operation duplicate or new; energyInvariant unchanged or add-up-to-cap; receiptIdentity preserve-existing or record-request. Deltas mean after minus before. add-up-to-cap means afterEnergy = min(energyCap,beforeEnergy+repairEnergy). preserve-existing means the original current-actor receipt remains byte-for-byte unchanged; record-request means exactly one new current-actor receipt for this request records the actual change. Choose the schedule and invariant the correct implementation must satisfy, not a guess about the identical replies.',
    explanation: `The experiment is ${JSON.stringify(expected)}. ${duplicate ? 'This request repeats a successful ID for this actor, so balances and receipt history must stay unchanged; the original receipt survives even if its historical balances differ from the current baseline.' : 'No receipt matches this actor and request together, so this is new work: charge once, apply the bounded addition and append one current-actor receipt. An ID used only by another actor does not make this a duplicate.'} ${snapshotBefore ? 'A trustworthy before-snapshot is already saved, so one actor-state read after the trigger is sufficient.' : 'There is no current before-snapshot; read this actor before the trigger and again after it completes to compare the invariant.'} Reading the matching reply, another actor or station coordinates cannot establish this actor’s state transition.` };
}
function generateItem({ mode, key, seed }) {
  if (!['practice', 'completion', 'mastery'].includes(mode)) throw new Error('Unknown capstone item mode');
  const section = mode === 'mastery' ? { identity: 'identity', atomic: 'transaction', transfer: 'observe' }[key] : key;
  if (!unit.sections.some(({ id }) => id === section)) throw new Error('Unknown capstone item key');
  const n = hashSeed(`${mode}:${key}:${seed}`);
  const base = { id: `capstone:${mode}:${key}:${seed}`, objectiveIds: [`capstone.${section}`], format: { type: 'json' }, source: source(section === 'identity' ? 'request-identity' : section === 'transaction' ? 'one-resource-transaction' : 'independent-http-tests') };
  if (mode === 'mastery' && key === 'transfer') return observationExperiment(n, base);
  if (section === 'observe') {
    const config = { repairCost: 1 + n % 4, repairEnergy: 2 + (n >>> 6) % 5, energyCap: 10 + (n >>> 10) % 8 };
    const energy = (n >>> 13) % config.energyCap;
    const credits = config.repairCost + 3 + (n >>> 17) % 15;
    const correctEnergy = Math.min(config.energyCap, energy + config.repairEnergy);
    const correctCredits = credits - config.repairCost;
    const observed = { energy: correctEnergy, credits: correctCredits, receipt: { energy: correctEnergy, credits: correctCredits, energyAdded: correctEnergy - energy, creditsSpent: config.repairCost } };
    if (n % 5 === 1) observed.energy -= 1;
    if (n % 5 === 2) observed.credits += 1;
    if (n % 5 === 3) observed.receipt.energy += 1;
    if (n % 5 === 4) { observed.energy -= 1; observed.receipt.energyAdded -= 1; }
    const expected = { energyMatches: observed.energy === correctEnergy, creditsMatch: observed.credits === correctCredits, receiptMatches: observed.receipt.energy === correctEnergy && observed.receipt.credits === correctCredits && observed.receipt.energyAdded === correctEnergy - energy && observed.receipt.creditsSpent === config.repairCost };
    return { ...base, inputs: { context: 'quota service applying a successful bounded resource grant', before: { energy, credits }, config, observed }, expected,
      prompt: 'All admission checks passed for a new request in a quota service using the repair rule: charge the full cost, add up to the remaining cap, and record the actual change and resulting balances. Independently calculate the expected resource change. Return {energyMatches,creditsMatch,receiptMatches} for the observed result. A correct reason label is not evidence that these values agree.',
      explanation: `The correct energy is ${correctEnergy}, credits ${correctCredits}, energyAdded ${correctEnergy - energy} and creditsSpent ${config.repairCost}. Comparing each promised result gives ${JSON.stringify(expected)}. A test that checks only the returned reason would miss any false entry.`,
      hints: ['Compute the resource change without reading the observed values first.', 'Compare both final balances and all four numeric receipt fields.', `The independent comparisons are ${JSON.stringify(expected)}.`] };
  }
  const inputs = stateCase(n, section === 'identity');
  const expected = resultFor(inputs);
  return { ...base, inputs, expected,
    prompt: `${mode === 'completion' ? 'The request is validated and actor identity is already resolved. Complete the policy decision. ' : ''}Resolve this actor’s existing request ID first: different station is conflict; same station is duplicate with the original receipt. For a new ID check station, receipt capacity, squared circular range (edge included), energy below cap, then funds. On success add min(repairEnergy,remaining space), charge full repairCost and append a receipt. Return {reason,receipt,energy,credits,receiptCount}. Every refusal has receipt:null and unchanged balances/history.`,
    explanation: `The expected decision is ${JSON.stringify(expected)}. Receipts belong to this actor, so another actor’s same ID has no effect. Existing success is checked before current range or capacity. New requests stop at the first failing requirement; no failed check reserves the ID or debits resources. A duplicate returns its original receipt even when current balances differ.`,
    hints: ['Search the named actor’s receipts before looking at the station or current range.', 'For a new ID, stop at the first refusal; calculate all resource effects only after every check passes.', `The complete result projection is ${JSON.stringify(expected)}.`] };
}

export function makeItem(args) {
  const item = generateItem(args);
  if (args.mode === 'mastery') return { ...item, hints: [] };
  if (args.mode === 'completion') {
    const x = item.inputs;
    const actor = x.state?.actors.find((a) => a.id === x.actorId);
    const position = actor?.receipts.findIndex((r) => r.requestId === x.request.requestId);
    const steps = args.key === 'identity'
      ? [`The current actor's receipt lookup is complete: request ${x.request.requestId} occurs at index ${position} (-1 means absent). Another actor's receipt list was excluded. Complete the station comparison or the new-request checks and return the current balances.`]
      : args.key === 'transaction'
        ? [`The available energy space is ${x.state.config.energyCap} − ${actor.energy} = ${x.state.config.energyCap - actor.energy}. Keep that amount for a possible success; first complete all ordered admission checks before changing any resource.`]
        : [`The capacity gap is ${x.config.energyCap} − ${x.before.energy} = ${x.config.energyCap - x.before.energy}. The permitted addition is min(${x.config.repairEnergy}, gap) = ${Math.min(x.config.repairEnergy, x.config.energyCap - x.before.energy)}. Complete the final balance and receipt comparisons independently of the observed values.`];
    return { ...item, inputs: { ...x, completedSteps: steps }, prompt: `Continue from the calculated work in inputs.completedSteps; fill the remaining resource or receipt decisions. ${item.prompt}` };
  }
  return item;
}

const source = (anchor) => ({ path: 'evaluation/LEARNER.md', anchor });
export const unit = {
  id: 'evaluation', title: 'M7 · Count what a detector can support', prerequisites: ['telemetry'],
  objectives: [
    { id: 'evaluation.window', kind: 'procedure', text: 'Classify an ordered signal list with strict distance and time-window boundaries.', prerequisites: ['telemetry.sequence'] },

A later cooldown does not undo this window.'], answer: 'Flagged. If the first eligible tick were 5, that pair would miss the threshold.' },
      completion: { prompt: 'Threshold is 2 and windowTicks is 5. Eligible ticks are 10 and 15.', steps: ['The window ending at 15 has old edge 10.', 'The old edge is excluded.'], missing: 'Supply the count in that window and whether the case flags.' }, source: source('window-boundaries') },
    { id: 'metrics', title: 'Give each case one vote', objectiveIds: ['evaluation.metrics'],
      paragraphs: [
        'A case is one run, even when it contains many signals. Compare its Boolean flag with its Boolean label once. Flagged-positive is a true positive; flagged-negative is a false positive; unflagged-negative is a true negative; unflagged-positive is a false negative.',
        'Precision is tp/(tp+fp), recall is tp/(tp+fn), and falsePositiveRate is fp/(fp+tn). Return null when the denominator is zero. Null means this corpus supplied no denominator for the question; it is not a measured zero or a perfect rate.',
      ],
      worked: { prompt: 'Four runs produce flagged-positive, unflagged-positive, flagged-negative and unflagged-negative. All three rates are 0.5.' },
