function hashSeed(seed) { let n = 2166136261; for (const c of String(seed)) n = Math.imul(n ^ c.charCodeAt(0), 16777619) >>> 0; return n; }
function classify(signals, settings) {
  const eligible = signals.filter((s) => s.reason === 'range' && s.distanceSquared > settings.minDistanceMm ** 2);
  return eligible.some(({ tick }) => eligible.filter((s) => s.tick > tick - settings.windowTicks && s.tick <= tick).length >= settings.threshold);
}
function signalCase(n) {
  const minDistanceMm = 100 + n % 50;
  const windowTicks = 3 + n % 7;
  const latest = 20 + n % 50;
  const variant = n % 5;
  const signal = (tick, reason = 'range', distanceSquared = (minDistanceMm + 1) ** 2) => ({ tick, reason, distanceSquared });
  const signals = [signal(latest - windowTicks + (variant === 0 ? 0 : 1)), signal(latest)];
  if (variant === 2) signals[0].distanceSquared = minDistanceMm ** 2;
  if (variant === 3) signals[0].reason = 'cooldown';
  if (variant === 4) { signals[0].tick = latest; signals.push(signal(latest + 40, 'cooldown')); }
  return { signals, settings: { threshold: 2, windowTicks, minDistanceMm } };
}
function countCases(cases, settings) {
  const metrics = { total: cases.length, tp: 0, fp: 0, tn: 0, fn: 0 };
  for (const c of cases) metrics[classify(c.signals, settings) ? (c.label ? 'tp' : 'fp') : (c.label ? 'fn' : 'tn')] += 1;
  const rate = (x, y) => y === 0 ? null : x / y;
  return { ...metrics, precision: rate(metrics.tp, metrics.tp + metrics.fp), recall: rate(metrics.tp, metrics.tp + metrics.fn), falsePositiveRate: rate(metrics.fp, metrics.fp + metrics.tn) };
}
function generateItem({ mode, key, seed }) {
  if (!['practice', 'completion', 'mastery'].includes(mode)) throw new Error('Unknown evaluation item mode');
  const section = mode === 'mastery' ? { boundary: 'window', counts: 'metrics', transfer: 'claim' }[key] : key;
  if (!unit.sections.some(({ id }) => id === section)) throw new Error('Unknown evaluation item key');
  const n = hashSeed(`${mode}:${key}:${seed}`);
  const base = { id: `evaluation:${mode}:${key}:${seed}`, objectiveIds: [`evaluation.${section}`], format: { type: 'json' }, source: source(section === 'window' ? 'window-boundaries' : section === 'metrics' ? 'counts-and-rates' : 'exploration-and-evaluation') };
  if (section === 'window') {
    const inputs = signalCase(n);
    const expected = { flagged: classify(inputs.signals, inputs.settings) };
    return { ...base, inputs, expected, prompt: 'Return {flagged} for this case. Only range denials strictly beyond minDistanceMm count. Any open-left, closed-right window (t-windowTicks,t] reaching threshold flags the case. Each listed observation counts, including equal-tick entries.',
      explanation: `The result is ${JSON.stringify(expected)}. Square the minimum before comparing distanceSquared; equality is ineligible. Exclude a tick exactly at the old time edge and ignore cooldown entries. Check every eligible ending tick, so a later quiet period cannot erase an earlier qualifying burst.`,
      hints: ['Filter reasons and squared distances before counting.', 'For each eligible ending tick, exclude observations at or before t-windowTicks.', `Applying both strict edges yields ${JSON.stringify(expected)}.`] };
  }
  if (section === 'metrics') {
    const settings = { threshold: 2, windowTicks: 5, minDistanceMm: 10 };
    const cases = Array.from({ length: mode === 'completion' ? 2 + n % 5 : n % 7 }, (_, i) => ({ id: `run-${i}`, label: (n >>> i) % 2 === 1, signals: (n + i) % 3 === 0 ? [] : Array.from({ length: 2 + (i % 3) }, (_, j) => ({ tick: 10 + j, reason: 'range', distanceSquared: 121 })) }));
    const expected = countCases(cases, settings);
    return { ...base, inputs: { cases, settings }, expected, prompt: 'Classify each run using the stated rule, then return exactly {total,tp,fp,tn,fn,precision,recall,falsePositiveRate}. Give each run one vote. Use a JSON number for a defined rate and null for a zero denominator; fractions here terminate or repeat as ordinary division results.',
      explanation: `The case-level totals and rates are ${JSON.stringify(expected)}. The total is the number of runs, not signals. Precision divides flagged positives by all flags; recall divides them by positive labels; falsePositiveRate divides false flags by negative labels. An empty denominator gives null.`,
      hints: ['Classify each case before consulting its label.', 'Make four counts, check that they sum to total, then calculate each denominator.', `The reconciled metric object is ${JSON.stringify(expected)}.`] };
  }
  const twin = signalCase(n);
  const inputs = { domain: 'rejected document edits', evaluationFeedbackSeen: n % 2 === 0, changedSettingsUsingThatFeedback: n % 2 === 0, committedBeforeFirstEvaluation: true, twinSignals: twin.signals, settings: twin.settings, differentAutomationMetadata: true };
  const expected = { report: inputs.evaluationFeedbackSeen ? 'revision' : 'first-committed-evaluation', twinFlagged: classify(twin.signals, twin.settings), twinFlagsMustMatch: true, automationIdentifiable: false };
  return { ...base, inputs, expected, prompt: 'An edit-review service applies the same range-signal classifier and supplied settings to two runs with identical signals. It commits settings before its first evaluation. The supplied booleans say whether it later changed settings using evaluation feedback. Return {report,twinFlagged,twinFlagsMustMatch,automationIdentifiable}, choosing report first-committed-evaluation or revision. Compute their common flag and decide what the evidence permits, not which script you suspect.',
    explanation: `The warranted report is ${JSON.stringify(expected)}. ${inputs.evaluationFeedbackSeen ? 'The later settings use exposed evaluation results, so the later report must retain that revision history.' : 'The initial committed settings precede evaluation feedback.'} Identical classifier inputs require identical flags; automation metadata is not an input and these signals cannot identify automation.`,
    hints: ['Ask whether evaluation information influenced the setting being reported.', 'Compare the classifier’s actual inputs for the two runs.', `The bounded interpretation is ${JSON.stringify(expected)}.`] };
}

export function makeItem(args) {
  const item = generateItem(args);
  if (args.mode === 'mastery') return { ...item, hints: [] };
  if (args.mode === 'completion') {
    const x = item.inputs;
    const minimum = x.settings.minDistanceMm ** 2;
    const eligible = (signals) => signals.filter((s) => s.reason === 'range' && s.distanceSquared > minimum).map((s) => s.tick);
    const first = x.cases?.[0];
    const firstFlag = first ? classify(first.signals, x.settings) : null;
    const cell = firstFlag ? (first.label ? 'tp' : 'fp') : first?.label ? 'fn' : 'tn';
    const steps = args.key === 'window'
      ? [`The squared minimum is ${minimum} mm². Filtering only reason and strict distance leaves eligible ticks ${JSON.stringify(eligible(x.signals))}. Complete the open-left window count.`]
      : args.key === 'metrics'
        ? [`The first case ${first.id} has flagged=${firstFlag} and label=${first.label}, so it contributes one ${cell}. Complete the other ${x.cases.length - 1} cases, then calculate the rates.`]
        : [`Both runs receive ${x.twinSignals.length} signals and the same settings. After applying the squared minimum ${minimum} mm², both have eligible ticks ${JSON.stringify(eligible(x.twinSignals))}. Complete the shared window result and decide what the report can claim.`];
    return { ...item, inputs: { ...x, completedSteps: steps }, prompt: `Continue from the partial calculation in inputs.completedSteps. ${item.prompt}` };
  }
  return item;
}

function hashSeed(seed) {
  let hash = 2166136261;
  for (const char of String(seed)) hash = Math.imul(hash ^ char.charCodeAt(0), 16777619) >>> 0;
  return hash;
}

function comparison(n) {
  const release = `release-${n % 97 + 1}`;
  const digest = ((n % 14) + 1).toString(16).repeat(64);
  const other = ((n % 14) + 2).toString(16).repeat(64);
  const files = [{ path: 'engine.mjs', sha256: digest }, { path: 'rules/range.json', sha256: other }];
  const observed = structuredClone(files).reverse();
  const variant = n % 6;
  if (variant === 1) observed.pop();
  if (variant === 2) observed.push({ path: 'extra.mjs', sha256: digest });
  if (variant === 3) observed[0].sha256 = digest;
  if (variant === 4) observed[0].sha256 = observed[0].sha256.toUpperCase();
  if (variant === 5) observed[0].path = 'rules/Range.json';
  const supported = n % 7 === 0 ? ['another-release'] : [release];
  const inputs = { manifest: { schema: 1, packageId: 'courier-runtime', release, files }, observed, supported };
  let reason = 'verified';
  if (!supported.includes(release)) reason = 'unsupported-release';
  if (reason === 'verified' && [1, 2, 5].includes(variant)) reason = 'inventory';
  if (reason === 'verified' && variant === 3) reason = 'digest';
  return { inputs, expected: { ok: reason === 'verified', reason } };
}

function generateItem({ mode, key, seed }) {
  if (!['practice', 'completion', 'mastery'].includes(mode)) throw new Error('Unknown integrity item mode');
  const section = mode === 'mastery' ? { boundary: 'reference', refusal: 'compare', transfer: 'trust' }[key] : key;
  if (!unit.sections.some(({ id }) => id === section)) throw new Error('Unknown integrity item key');
  const n = hashSeed(`${mode}:${key}:${seed}`);
  const base = { id: `integrity:${mode}:${key}:${seed}`, objectiveIds: [`integrity.${section}`], source: source(section === 'compare' ? 'decide-in-order' : section === 'trust' ? 'inspect-repair-and-explain' : 'reference-and-observation'), format: { type: 'json' } };
  if (section === 'trust') {
    const plugins = Array.from({ length: 2 + n % 4 }, (_, i) => ({ path: `extensions/tool-${i}.mjs`, approvedHash: `approved-${n % 997}-${i}`, observedHash: `approved-${n % 997}-${i}` }));
    if (n % 3 === 0) plugins[n % plugins.length].observedHash = `changed-${n % 991}`;
    const inputs = { coreMatches: true, plugins, packageCanWriteApproval: n % 2 === 0, requestedClaim: 'owner-approved bytes before importing core and every plug-in' };
    const pluginMatches = plugins.every((p) => p.approvedHash === p.observedHash);
    const reason = inputs.packageCanWriteApproval ? 'untrusted-reference' : pluginMatches ? 'matching-only' : 'unapproved-bytes';
    const expected = { start: reason === 'matching-only', assurance: reason };
    return { ...base, inputs, prompt: 'A document viewer imports a core and several extensions. Hashes here are opaque identity labels; all paths and releases are valid. Its rule requires an independent owner-controlled approval record and matching hashes for every import. Return {start,assurance}, choosing assurance from untrusted-reference, unapproved-bytes, or matching-only. An untrusted reference takes priority. Matching-only authorizes this byte comparison, not remote identity or safe behavior.', expected,
      explanation: `The decision is ${JSON.stringify(expected)}. ${inputs.packageCanWriteApproval ? 'The package can rewrite approval, so equality cannot establish owner approval.' : pluginMatches ? 'Every measured inventory matches independent approval. That permits the stated startup check but proves only matching bytes.' : 'An extension does not match its approval, so core matching cannot authorize its bytes.'} A claim of authenticated remote execution would go beyond every branch here.`,
      hints: ['Find who can change the approval record before using equality as evidence.', 'If approval is independent, check every imported component, including the extension.', `The ordered decision gives ${JSON.stringify(expected)}; apply the same order to a fresh case after feedback.`] };
  }
  const { inputs, expected } = comparison(n);
  return { ...base, inputs, prompt: `${mode === 'completion' ? 'The approved record is well formed. Complete the remaining decision. ' : ''}Both inventories contain valid hashes and safe unique paths. Apply release support, exact path membership, then case-insensitive full-hash comparison. Return exactly {ok,reason}; use verified, unsupported-release, inventory or digest.`, expected,
    explanation: `The first decision is ${expected.reason}. Supported releases are ${JSON.stringify(inputs.supported)}; the requested release is ${inputs.manifest.release}. Missing, extra or case-changed paths are inventory failures; hash-letter case alone is allowed. The result is ${JSON.stringify(expected)}.`,
    hints: ['A release label and a matching path are separate checks.', 'Find the first failed stage: support, path set, then full digest.', `The first failing stage gives ${JSON.stringify(expected)}. Do not replace approved hashes with observations.`] };
}

export function makeItem(args) {
  const item = generateItem(args);
  if (args.mode === 'mastery') return { ...item, hints: [] };
  if (args.mode === 'completion') {
    const x = item.inputs;
    const steps = args.key === 'trust'
      ? [`The core comparison is complete: coreMatches=${x.coreMatches}.       : args.key === 'reference'

        : [`The observed hashes have been normalized to lowercase: ${JSON.stringify(x.observed.map((f) => ({ path: f.path, sha256: f.sha256.toLowerCase() })))}. Normalizing hexadecimal letters does not change path spelling. Continue with the ordered release, inventory and digest decisions.`];
    return { ...item, inputs: { ...x, completedSteps: steps }, prompt: `Continue from the calculated work in inputs.completedSteps; supply the remaining decision. ${item.prompt}` };
  }
  return item;
}

export const unit = {
  id: 'order', title: 'M2 · Keep the newest intent', prerequisites: ['spatial'],
  intro: 'An older direction arrives after a newer one. Predict what the owner keeps, which interaction is staged, and the last tick on which movement remains active.',
  difficulty: 'The interacting pieces are sequence comparison, a pending interaction bit and inclusive expiry. Track the five state fields separately before following a tick.',
  objectives: [
    { id: 'order.admission', kind: 'procedure', text: 'Return the unchanged admission state for an equal or older sequence and update it for a newer sequence.', prerequisites: ['spatial.tick-order'] },

      completion: { prompt: 'The same state receives seq 13, move W, interact false at tick 7.', steps: ['13 is strictly larger than 12, so admit it.', 'lastSeq becomes 13 and lastSeen becomes 7.'], missing: 'Compute expiresAt and fill move and pendingInteract.' }, source,
    },

      id: 'coalescing', title: 'Many arrivals, one pending interaction', objectiveIds: ['order.coalescing'],
      paragraphs: [

For newer inputs, pendingInteract becomes oldPending OR input.interact. A later admitted false does not erase a previously admitted true. A stale true does not create a pending action.',
        'No ticks occur between the arrivals in these exercises. At the next tick, the latest admitted direction moves the courier once. function stateCase(n) {
  const tick = 5 + Math.floor(n / 3) % 23;
  const lastSeq = 10 + Math.floor(n / 7) % 40;
  const state = { lastSeq, lastSeen: tick - 2, expiresAt: tick + 2, move: ['N', 'E', 'S', 'W'][n % 4], pendingInteract: Boolean(Math.floor(n / 2) % 2) };
  const input = { v: 1, seq: lastSeq + [-2, 0, 3][n % 3], move: ['S', 'W', 'N', 'E'][n % 4], interact: Boolean(Math.floor(n / 3) % 2) };
  const expected = input.seq <= lastSeq ? { status: 'stale', next: { ...state } } : { status: 'admitted', next: { lastSeq: input.seq, lastSeen: tick, expiresAt: tick + 4, move: input.move, pendingInteract: state.pendingInteract || input.interact } };
  return { inputs: { state, input, tick }, expected, prompt: 'The input is already parsed. Return exactly JSON {status,next}; status is "stale" or "admitted". next must contain exactly lastSeq, lastSeen, expiresAt, move, pendingInteract. pendingInteract is a boolean, move is the retained or new direction string, and the other state fields are numbers.', explanation: `${input.seq} ${input.seq <= lastSeq ? 'is not greater than' : 'is greater than'} ${lastSeq}. ${input.seq <= lastSeq ? 'Return stale and preserve every field, even if the request carries a different direction or true interaction bit.' : `Admit it at tick ${tick}: expiry becomes ${tick + 4}, direction becomes ${input.move}, and pending is ${state.pendingInteract} OR ${input.interact}.`}` };
}

function coalescingCase(n) {
  const lastSeq = 20 + Math.floor(n / 9) % 40;
  const tick = 3 + Math.floor(n / 4) % 15;
  const inputBits = [[true, false, true], [false, true, false], [false, false, true], [true, true, false]][n % 4];
  const sequences = n % 2 ? [lastSeq + 1, lastSeq, lastSeq + 2] : [lastSeq + 2, lastSeq + 3, lastSeq + 1];
  const inputs = sequences.map((seq, index) => ({ seq, move: 'idle', interact: inputBits[index] }));
  const initialPending = Boolean(Math.floor(n / 5) % 2);
  let pending = initialPending;
  let newest = lastSeq;
  for (const input of inputs) {
    if (input.seq <= newest) continue;
    newest = input.seq;
    pending ||= input.interact;
  }
  const cargo = Boolean(Math.floor(n / 3) % 2);
  return {
    inputs: { receiptTick: tick, state: { lastSeq, pendingInteract: initialPending }, arrivals: inputs, actorAtTarget: { cargo, score: 2, move: 'idle', cooldownReady: true }, nextTick: tick + 1 },
    expected: { lastSeq: newest, pendingBeforeTick: pending, attemptedInteractions: Number(pending), cargoAfterTick: pending ? !cargo : cargo, scoreAfterTick: 2 + Number(pending && cargo), pendingAfterTick: false },
    prompt: 'No tick occurs between these arrivals. The idle actor is on the relevant target and cooldown is ready. Trace admission, then one tick. Return JSON {lastSeq,pendingBeforeTick,attemptedInteractions,cargoAfterTick,scoreAfterTick,pendingAfterTick}.',
    explanation: `Only newer sequences can contribute their true bit. The newest admitted sequence is ${newest} and the combined flag is ${pending}. A single flag allows ${Number(pending)} interaction, then is cleared. ${pending && cargo ? 'This is one deposit, so score rises once.' : pending ? 'This is one pickup, so score does not rise.' : 'No interaction is staged, so cargo and score stay put.'}`,
  };
}

function expiryCase(n) {
  const admittedAt = 5 + Math.floor(n / 5) % 27;
  const lastSeq = 30 + Math.floor(n / 7) % 40;
  const probeTick = admittedAt + [3, 4, 5][n % 3];
  const renewal = Math.floor(n / 3) % 3;
  const renewed = renewal === 2;
  const expiresAt = renewed ? probeTick + 4 : admittedAt + 4;
  const inputs = { admittedAt, lastSeq, initialExpiry: admittedAt + 4, probeTick, pollsSinceAdmission: n % 6, arrivalBeforeProbe: renewal ? { seq: lastSeq + (renewed ? 1 : 0), move: 'E', interact: false } : null };
  return { inputs, expected: { activeAtProbe: probeTick <= expiresAt, expiresAt, lastSeq: lastSeq + Number(renewed) }, prompt: 'The original intent is E. Polls are read-only; if an arrival is listed, process it at probeTick before testing movement for that tick. Return JSON {activeAtProbe,expiresAt,lastSeq}.', explanation: `${renewed ? `The strictly newer arrival renews expiry to ${probeTick} + 4 = ${expiresAt}.` : `Neither polls nor an equal-sequence retry renews expiry, so it stays ${expiresAt}.`} Movement is active when probeTick <= expiresAt: ${probeTick} <= ${expiresAt} is ${probeTick <= expiresAt}.` };
}

function transferCase(n) {
  const seq = 40 + Math.floor(n / 4) % 90;
  const initial = { lastSeq: seq, frame: 100 + n % 51 };
  const commands = [
    { kind: 'seek', seq: seq + 2, frame: 300 + n % 91 },
    { kind: 'read' },
    { kind: 'seek', seq: seq + (n % 3), frame: 700 + n % 83 },
    { kind: 'read' },
    ...(n % 2 ? [{ kind: 'seek', seq: seq + 3, frame: 200 + n % 47 }, { kind: 'read' }] : []),
  ];
  let state = { ...initial };
  const framesRead = [];
  for (const command of commands) {
    if (command.kind === 'read') { framesRead.push(state.frame); continue; }
    if (command.seq > state.lastSeq) state = { lastSeq: command.seq, frame: command.frame };
  }
  return { inputs: { initial, commands }, expected: { ...state, framesRead }, prompt: 'An owned replay scrubber applies a seek only if its sequence is strictly newer. A read reports the current frame without changing state. This scrubber has no movement, interaction flag or expiry. Return JSON {lastSeq,frame,framesRead} after all commands, with read results in order.', explanation: `The newer seek selects a frame; the equal or older conflicting seek cannot replace it. Read commands append observations only. The final selection is frame ${state.frame} at sequence ${state.lastSeq}; reads are ${JSON.stringify(framesRead)}. Do not import the game’s four-tick expiry into a contract that has none.` };
}

export function makeItem({ mode, key, seed }) {
  if (!['practice', 'completion', 'mastery'].includes(mode)) throw new TypeError('unknown item mode');
  if (!Number.isSafeInteger(seed) || seed < 0) throw new TypeError('seed must be a non-negative safe integer');
  const valid = mode === 'mastery' ? unit.masterySlots : unit.sections.map((section) => section.id);
  if (!valid.includes(key)) throw new TypeError('unknown order item key');
  const n = seed + (mode === 'completion' ? 137 : mode === 'mastery' ? 277 : 0);
  const builders = { admission: stateCase, coalescing: coalescingCase, expiry: expiryCase, transfer: transferCase };
  const item = builders[key](n);
  if (mode === 'completion') {
    item.inputs.completedSteps = key === 'admission'
      ? [`Compare ${item.inputs.input.seq} with lastSeq ${item.inputs.state.lastSeq}. The input is ${item.inputs.input.seq > item.inputs.state.lastSeq ? 'newer' : 'stale'}; now fill every returned state field.`]
      : key === 'coalescing'
        ? [`The first arrival has sequence ${item.inputs.arrivals[0].seq}, which is newer than ${item.inputs.state.lastSeq}. After it, pending is ${item.inputs.state.pendingInteract || item.inputs.arrivals[0].interact}. Continue with the remaining arrivals.`]
        : [`The original inclusive endpoint is ${item.inputs.admittedAt} + 4 = ${item.inputs.initialExpiry}. Next check whether the listed arrival is new enough to replace this endpoint.`];
  }
  const objectiveIds = key === 'admission' ? ['order.admission'] : key === 'coalescing' ? ['order.admission', 'order.coalescing'] : key === 'expiry' ? ['order.admission', 'order.expiry'] : ['order.admission'];
  return { id: `order:${mode}:${key}:${seed}`, objectiveIds, ...item, prompt: `${mode === 'completion' ? 'Complete the missing state transition after applying the comparison. ' : ''}${item.prompt}`, format: { type: 'json' }, hints: mode === 'mastery' ? [] : ['Separate arrivals from processed ticks and from read-only polls.', 'Reject equal or older sequences before touching direction, expiry or the pending bit.', item.explanation], source };
}

function hashSeed(seed) { let n = 2166136261; for (const c of String(seed)) n = Math.imul(n ^ c.charCodeAt(0), 16777619) >>> 0; return n; }
function evidenceCase(n) {
  const schema = 1 + n % 3;
  const ordinal = 5 + n % 20;
  const release = { id: `r-${n % 41}`, packageHash: `package-${n}`, stateSchema: schema, configId: 'c-target', configHash: `config-${n}` };
  const config = { id: 'c-target', hash: release.configHash, releaseId: release.id, stateSchema: schema, maxInteractionDistanceMm: 250 };
  const snap = (id, order, extra = {}) => ({ id, hash: `snapshot-${id}-${n}`, ordinal: order, stateSchema: schema, configId: config.id, configHash: config.hash, ...extra });
  const evidence = { targetReleaseId: release.id, releases: [release], configurations: [config], snapshots: [snap('future', ordinal + 10, { stateSchema: schema + 1 }), snap('a-ready', ordinal), snap('older', ordinal - 2), snap('Z-ready', ordinal)] };
  const variant = n % 6;
  if (variant === 1) evidence.targetReleaseId = 'missing-release';
  if (variant === 2) config.hash = 'wrong-config-hash';
  if (variant === 3) evidence.snapshots = evidence.snapshots.map((s) => ({ ...s, configId: 'other-config' }));
  if (variant === 4) evidence.snapshots[1].ordinal += 1;
  if (variant === 5) config.releaseId = 'wrong-release';
  return evidence;
}
function select(e) {
  const r = e.releases.find((x) => x.id === e.targetReleaseId);
  if (!r) return { ok: false, reason: 'unknown-target' };
  const c = e.configurations.find((x) => x.id === r.configId);
  if (!c || c.hash !== r.configHash || c.releaseId !== r.id || c.stateSchema !== r.stateSchema) return { ok: false, reason: 'configuration-mismatch' };
  const candidates = e.snapshots.filter((s) => s.stateSchema === r.stateSchema && s.configId === c.id && s.configHash === c.hash);
  const s = candidates.toSorted((a, b) => b.ordinal - a.ordinal || (a.id < b.id ? -1 : a.id > b.id ? 1 : 0))[0];
  if (!s) return { ok: false, reason: 'no-compatible-snapshot' };
  return { ok: true, releaseId: r.id, packageHash: r.packageHash, configId: c.id, configHash: c.hash, snapshotId: s.id, snapshotHash: s.hash };
}
function generateItem({ mode, key, seed }) {
  if (!['practice', 'completion', 'mastery'].includes(mode)) throw new Error('Unknown recovery item mode');
  const section = mode === 'mastery' ? { compatibility: 'tuple', newest: 'selection', transfer: 'loss' }[key] : key;
  if (!unit.sections.some(({ id }) => id === section)) throw new Error('Unknown recovery item key');
  const n = hashSeed(`${mode}:${key}:${seed}`);
  const base = { id: `recovery:${mode}:${key}:${seed}`, objectiveIds: [`recovery.${section}`], format: { type: 'json' }, source: source(section === 'tuple' ? 'compatible-tuples' : section === 'selection' ? 'snapshot-order' : 'what-recovery-loses') };
  if (section === 'loss') {
    const restoredLastSeq = 2 + n % 400;
    const highestBeforeRestore = restoredLastSeq + (n >>> 9) % 20;
    const restoredScore = (n >>> 14) % 30;
    const inputs = { service: 'shared repair credits', highestBeforeRestore, restoredLastSeq, scoreBeforeRestore: restoredScore + (n >>> 20) % 8, restoredScore, snapshotActuallyRestored: true, actionAppliedAfterRestore: n % 2 === 0 };
    const count = highestBeforeRestore - restoredLastSeq;
    const expected = { reopenedStart: count ? restoredLastSeq + 1 : null, reopenedEnd: count ? highestBeforeRestore : null, reopenedCount: count, lostScore: inputs.scoreBeforeRestore - restoredScore, sameActionWorks: inputs.actionAppliedAfterRestore, allAcknowledgedPreserved: count === 0 };
    return { ...base, inputs, expected, prompt: 'A service really restored this older snapshot. In this toy protocol, no separate sequence floor or recovery epoch survives the restore. Return {reopenedStart,reopenedEnd,reopenedCount,lostScore,sameActionWorks,allAcknowledgedPreserved}. Use null endpoints if no sequence reopens. Count inclusive sequence numbers; a successful new action does not compensate lost acknowledgments.',
      explanation: `The result is ${JSON.stringify(expected)}. Subtract restoredLastSeq from highestBeforeRestore for the reopened count, and restoredScore from scoreBeforeRestore for lost score. Action success is the supplied action result, not the restore result. Preserving all acknowledged sequence state requires no reopened range.`,
      hints: ['Keep restored state, original acknowledgments and the new action as three facts.', 'The reopened range starts one above restoredLastSeq and ends at highestBeforeRestore.', `The inclusive range and separate action evidence give ${JSON.stringify(expected)}.`] };
  }
  const inputs = evidenceCase(n);
  const selected = select(inputs);
  const expected = section === 'tuple' && selected.ok ? { ok: true, reason: 'compatible' } : selected;
  return { ...base, inputs, expected, prompt: `Find the declared release, validate configuration ID/hash/release/schema, then filter snapshots by schema and configuration ID/hash. ${section === 'tuple' ? 'Return {ok:true,reason:"compatible"} if at least one compatible snapshot exists.' : 'Among compatible snapshots select greatest ordinal, breaking ties by ascending JavaScript string comparison, and return {ok,releaseId,packageHash,configId,configHash,snapshotId,snapshotHash}.'} On failure return {ok:false,reason}, using unknown-target, configuration-mismatch or no-compatible-snapshot in that order. Preserve every supplied identity.`,
    explanation: `The result is ${JSON.stringify(expected)}. Compatibility must be checked before recency. A same-name configuration with a different hash cannot be used, and a newer snapshot with a different schema cannot win. For equal ordinals, Z-ready sorts before a-ready by JavaScript code-unit comparison. Nothing in this selection establishes that a restore or action already happened.`,
    hints: ['Resolve the declared release first; selecting a different release changes the request.', 'Require every configuration and snapshot identity to agree before ordering candidates.', `Applying those filters and the deterministic order yields ${JSON.stringify(expected)}.`] };
}

export function makeItem(args) {
  const item = generateItem(args);
  if (args.mode === 'mastery') return { ...item, hints: [] };
  if (args.mode === 'completion') {
    const x = item.inputs;
    const release = x.releases?.find((r) => r.id === x.targetReleaseId);
    const config = release && x.configurations.find((c) => c.id === release.configId);
    const candidates = release && config ? x.snapshots.filter((s) => s.stateSchema === release.stateSchema && s.configId === config.id && s.configHash === config.hash) : [];
    const steps = args.key === 'loss'
      ? [`The score difference has been calculated: ${x.scoreBeforeRestore} − ${x.restoredScore} = ${x.scoreBeforeRestore - x.restoredScore}. Complete the reopened sequence interval and distinguish the actual new-action result from the restore result.`]
      : args.key === 'tuple'
        ? [`The declared-target lookup gives ${release ? JSON.stringify({ id: release.id, stateSchema: release.stateSchema, configId: release.configId, configHash: release.configHash }) : 'no matching release'}. Continue the ordered configuration and snapshot checks when the target exists.`]
        : [`Snapshot filtering by the located release schema and configuration identity yields ${JSON.stringify(candidates.map((s) => ({ id: s.id, ordinal: s.ordinal })))}. This provisional list does not validate the configuration against its release; check that first, then complete the ordering and returned identities.`];
    return { ...item, inputs: { ...x, completedSteps: steps }, prompt: `Continue from the partial work in inputs.completedSteps without treating an unchecked identity as approved. ${item.prompt}` };
  }
  return item;
}

const source = (anchor) => ({ path: 'retention/LEARNER.md', anchor });
export const unit = {
  id: 'retention', title: 'M9 · Keep a bounded export', prerequisites: ['evaluation'],
  objectives: [
    { id: 'retention.window', kind: 'procedure', text: 'Apply the exclusive old edge, inclusive current edge and newest-entry count bound.', prerequisites: ['evaluation.window'] },
    { id: 'retention.projection', kind: 'procedure', text: 'Construct exactly four exported fields without changing the source.', prerequisites: ['retention.window'] },
    { id: 'retention.evidence', kind: 'concept', text: 'Determine which inspection question a shortened export can still support.', prerequisites: ['retention.projection', 'evaluation.claim'] },
  ],
  sections: [
    { id: 'window', title: 'Age first, count second', objectiveIds: ['retention.window'],
      paragraphs: [
        'Retention chooses which observations remain in an export. Keep an event when nowTick-maxAgeTicks < tick <= nowTick. The old edge is excluded; the current tick is included. A future event is excluded even when the export has room.',

Keep 25, 29 and 30.', 'Remove future tick 31 before applying the count bound.', 'The newest two eligible events are 29 and 30, in that order.'], answer: 'Retain ticks [29,30].' },

function hashSeed(seed) { let n = 2166136261; for (const c of String(seed)) n = Math.imul(n ^ c.charCodeAt(0), 16777619) >>> 0; return n; }
function retained(events, s) {
  return events.filter((event) => event.tick > s.nowTick - s.maxAgeTicks && event.tick <= s.nowTick).slice(-s.maxEvents).map(({ tick, actorId, reason, distanceSquared }) => ({ tick, actorId, reason, distanceSquared }));
}
function makeEvents(n, now, age) {
  return [now - age - 1, now - age, now - age + 1, now - 2, now - 1, now - 1, now, now + 1].sort((a, b) => a - b).map((tick, i) => ({ tick, actorId: `synthetic-${n % 29}-${i}`, reason: i % 2 ? 'range' : 'cooldown', distanceSquared: (i + 2) ** 2, capability: 'synthetic-not-a-token', device: 'synthetic-device' }));
}
function generateItem({ mode, key, seed }) {
  if (!['practice', 'completion', 'mastery'].includes(mode)) throw new Error('Unknown retention item mode');
  const section = mode === 'mastery' ? { boundary: 'window', projection: 'projection', transfer: 'evidence' }[key] : key;
  if (!unit.sections.some(({ id }) => id === section)) throw new Error('Unknown retention item key');
  const n = hashSeed(`${mode}:${key}:${seed}`);
  const base = { id: `retention:${mode}:${key}:${seed}`, objectiveIds: [`retention.${section}`], format: { type: 'json' }, source: source(section === 'evidence' ? 'reconcile-the-detector-window' : section === 'projection' ? 'four-fields-only' : 'the-count-bound') };
  const settings = { nowTick: 30 + n % 60, maxAgeTicks: 4 + n % 8, maxEvents: 1 + n % 6 };
  const events = makeEvents(n, settings.nowTick, settings.maxAgeTicks);
  if (section !== 'evidence') {
    const output = retained(events, settings);
    const expected = section === 'window' ? { actorIds: output.map((e) => e.actorId) } : output;
    return { ...base, inputs: { events, settings }, expected,
      prompt: `${mode === 'completion' ? 'The input is already in nondecreasing tick order. Complete the selection. ' : ''}Keep events with nowTick-maxAgeTicks < tick <= nowTick, then the newest maxEvents in supplied order. ${section === 'window' ? 'Return {actorIds} containing retained actor IDs in order.' : 'Return the retained array with exactly tick, actorId, reason and distanceSquared on each new record. Do not include synthetic capability/device fields.'}`,
      explanation: `The old edge is ${settings.nowTick - settings.maxAgeTicks}, excluded, and the current edge ${settings.nowTick} is included. Remove future records before taking the newest ${settings.maxEvents}. Equal-tick entries retain source order. The answer is ${JSON.stringify(expected)}; constructing this projection leaves the original records intact.`,
      hints: ['Mark events inside the age interval before using the count limit.', 'Take the eligible tail without sorting tied records, then select only the requested fields.', `The retained answer is ${JSON.stringify(expected)}.`] };
  }
  const detectorWindowTicks = settings.maxAgeTicks + (n % 2 ? 0 : 5);
  const required = events.filter((e) => e.tick > settings.nowTick - detectorWindowTicks && e.tick <= settings.nowTick);
  const output = retained(events, settings);
  const retainedIds = new Set(output.map((e) => e.actorId));
  const expected = { canReconstructWindow: required.every((e) => retainedIds.has(e.actorId)), missingCount: required.filter((e) => !retainedIds.has(e.actorId)).length, otherExportRemains: true };
  return { ...base, inputs: { events, settings, detectorWindowTicks, deletedExport: 'export-A', separateExport: 'export-B' }, expected,
    prompt: 'A document service needs every denial in (nowTick-detectorWindowTicks,nowTick] to recompute an inspection window. It exports with the supplied retention settings, then deletes only export-A; export-B is a separate existing file. Return {canReconstructWindow,missingCount,otherExportRemains}. Count missing source observations, not missing tick values; tied observations are separate.',
    explanation: `The result is ${JSON.stringify(expected)}. The detector needs ${required.length} source observations; compare their identities with the retained four-field records, after both age and count limits. A dropped observation cannot be recovered from the export alone. The named deletion of export-A leaves export-B untouched.`,
    hints: ['Find the complete detector interval separately from the export interval.', 'Compare observation IDs after both export limits, counting tied observations individually.', `There are ${expected.missingCount} missing observations; the complete response is ${JSON.stringify(expected)}.`] };
}

export function makeItem(args) {
  const item = generateItem(args);
  if (args.mode === 'mastery') return { ...item, hints: [] };
  if (args.mode === 'completion') {
    const x = item.inputs;
    const edge = x.settings.nowTick - x.settings.maxAgeTicks;
    const eligible = x.events.filter((e) => e.tick > edge && e.tick <= x.settings.nowTick);
    const steps = args.key === 'window'
      ? [`Age filtering for (${edge},${x.settings.nowTick}] is complete. Eligible actor IDs in source order are ${JSON.stringify(eligible.map((e) => e.actorId))}. Apply the count bound next.`]
      : args.key === 'projection'
        ? [`Selection is complete: the retained source positions are ${JSON.stringify(eligible.slice(-x.settings.maxEvents).map((e) => x.events.indexOf(e)))} (zero-based). Build new four-field records from those positions; do not copy the source objects wholesale.`]
        : [`The export age edge is ${edge}, while the detector's old edge is ${x.settings.nowTick - x.detectorWindowTicks}. Both old edges are exclusive and the current edge is ${x.settings.nowTick}. Compare the actual observation identities after the export count bound.`];
    return { ...item, inputs: { ...x, completedSteps: steps }, prompt: `Continue from inputs.completedSteps and fill the remaining selection or evidence decision. ${item.prompt}` };
  }
  return item;
}

const source = { path: 'lab/LEARNER.md', anchor: 'trace-and-predict-the-decision' };

// Original guided teaching. The owner keeps expected answers out of learner item responses.
export const unit = {
  id: 'spatial', title: 'M1 · Decide from the owner’s positions', prerequisites: [],
  intro: 'A courier requests a pickup while standing away from the core. Calculate whether the owner may change cargo, using its positions and the tick on which it acts.',
  difficulty: 'The hardest case combines two coordinates, movement before interaction, and an inclusive cooldown boundary. Work through one change at a time.',
  objectives: [
    { id: 'spatial.range', kind: 'procedure', text: 'Compute squared distance from owner positions and apply an inclusive interaction radius.', prerequisites: [] },
    { id: 'spatial.tick-order', kind: 'procedure', text: 'Compute the courier’s position and range after one owner movement tick.', prerequisites: ['spatial.range'] },

The courier and target each have x and y coordinates in millimetres. Subtract their x values and their y values to obtain the two separations.',

      ],
      worked: { prompt: 'An idle courier is at (1000, 1200) and the core at (1150, 1000).       completion: { prompt: 'An idle courier is at (1000, 1000) and the target at (1200, 1200). On the next tick, the engine first moves an active courier by 250 mm, then measures range for an interaction. E adds 250 to x; W subtracts 250 from x; N subtracts 250 from y; S adds 250 to y. These exercises use active movement on open floor, away from walls and edges.',
        'Use the position after movement for the range calculation. If a courier begins 500 mm west of its target and moves east, it becomes 250 mm away. If it starts at the boundary and moves away, its old in-range position does not make the new position in range. In this section report only the new x, new y, distanceSquared and withinRange. The next section teaches the other rules needed to decide a complete interaction.',
      ],

function seedNumber(seed) {
  if (!Number.isSafeInteger(seed) || seed < 0) throw new TypeError('seed must be a non-negative safe integer');
  return seed;
}

function answerInteraction(input) {
  const deltas = { E: [250, 0], W: [-250, 0], N: [0, -250], S: [0, 250], idle: [0, 0] };
  const [dx, dy] = deltas[input.move];
  const x = input.actor.x + dx;
  const y = input.actor.y + dy;
  const distanceSquared = (x - input.target.x) ** 2 + (y - input.target.y) ** 2;
  if (input.tick < input.actor.nextInteractTick) return { x, y, reason: 'cooldown', cargo: input.actor.cargo, score: input.actor.score, nextInteractTick: input.actor.nextInteractTick };
  if (distanceSquared > 62500) return { x, y, reason: 'range', cargo: input.actor.cargo, score: input.actor.score, nextInteractTick: input.actor.nextInteractTick };
  return { x, y, reason: input.actor.cargo ? 'deposit' : 'pickup', cargo: !input.actor.cargo, score: input.actor.score + Number(input.actor.cargo), nextInteractTick: input.tick + 4 };
}

function rangeCase(n) {
  const offsets = [[150, 200], [151, 200], [0, 249], [0, 251], [200, 200], [0, 250]];
  const [a, b] = offsets[n % offsets.length];
  const target = { x: 1400 + Math.floor(n / 6) % 29 * 10, y: 1100 + Math.floor(n / 13) % 19 * 10 };
  const actor = { x: target.x + (n % 2 ? -a : a), y: target.y + (n % 3 ? b : -b) };
  const distanceSquared = a * a + b * b;
  return { inputs: { actor, target, radiusMm: 250 }, expected: { distanceSquared, withinRange: distanceSquared <= 62500 }, prompt: 'Use these owner positions before any movement. Return exactly JSON {distanceSquared,withinRange}: distanceSquared is a number; withinRange is true when the position is inside the inclusive radius, otherwise false.', explanation: `Both coordinates count: (${actor.x} − ${target.x})² + (${actor.y} − ${target.y})² = ${distanceSquared}. Compare with 62,500 using ≤, so withinRange is ${distanceSquared <= 62500}. Both coordinate separations belong in this calculation. Equality is allowed; a strict < comparison would incorrectly reject an exact-boundary position.` };
}

function movementRangeCase(n) {
  const move = ['E', 'W', 'N', 'S'][Math.floor(n / 3) % 4];
  const [dx, dy] = { E: [250, 0], W: [-250, 0], N: [0, -250], S: [0, 250] }[move];
  const actor = { x: 1500 + Math.floor(n / 17) % 20 * 10, y: 1500 };
  const separation = [0, 250, 500, 750][n % 4];
  const sign = Math.floor(n / 12) % 2 ? -1 : 1;
  const target = { x: actor.x + sign * dx / 250 * separation, y: actor.y + sign * dy / 250 * separation };
  const x = actor.x + dx;
  const y = actor.y + dy;
  const distanceSquared = (x - target.x) ** 2 + (y - target.y) ** 2;
  return { inputs: { actor, target, move, stepMm: 250, radiusMm: 250, floor: 'unobstructed; movement is active' }, expected: { x, y, distanceSquared, withinRange: distanceSquared <= 62500 }, prompt: 'Move the courier once in the stated direction, then measure range from its new position. Return exactly JSON {x,y,distanceSquared,withinRange}: x, y and distanceSquared are numbers; withinRange is true when distanceSquared <= 62500, otherwise false.', explanation: `${move} moves the courier from (${actor.x}, ${actor.y}) to (${x}, ${y}). Measure from there: (${x} − ${target.x})² + (${y} − ${target.y})² = ${distanceSquared}. The inclusive range comparison gives withinRange=${distanceSquared <= 62500}. Measuring before movement can give a different result.` };
}

function interactionCase(n, moving) {
  const direction = ['E', 'W', 'N', 'S'][Math.floor(n / 3) % 4];
  const delta = { E: [1, 0], W: [-1, 0], N: [0, -1], S: [0, 1] }[direction];
  const actor = { x: 1500 + Math.floor(n / 17) % 20 * 10, y: 1500, cargo: Boolean(Math.floor(n / 2) % 2), score: n % 5, nextInteractTick: 10 + n % 19 };
  const tick = actor.nextInteractTick + (Math.floor(n / 3) % 3 - 1);
  const separation = [250, 500, 750][n % 3];
  const target = { x: actor.x + delta[0] * separation, y: actor.y + delta[1] * separation };
  const inputs = { tick, actor, target, targetKind: actor.cargo ? 'depot' : 'core', move: moving ? direction : 'idle', pendingInteract: true, floor: 'unobstructed; movement is active' };
  const expected = answerInteraction(inputs);
  return { inputs, expected, prompt: 'Process one pending interaction at the stated tick. Movement shown in inputs happens first. Return exactly JSON {x,y,reason,cargo,score,nextInteractTick}. reason is one of "cooldown", "range", "pickup", "deposit"; cargo is a boolean; the other fields are numbers. Apply the cooldown rule before range.', explanation: `The post-movement position is (${expected.x}, ${expected.y}). Cooldown is ready only at tick ${actor.nextInteractTick} or later; the target then must be within 250 mm. The result is ${expected.reason}. A denial preserves cargo, score and cooldown; success ${actor.cargo ? 'deposits once' : 'picks up once'} and sets the next allowed tick to ${tick + 4}.` };
}

function transferCase(n) {
  const offsets = [[240, 320], [241, 320], [0, 399], [0, 401]];
  const [dx, dy] = offsets[n % 4];
  const cost = 3 + Math.floor(n / 4) % 5;
  const inputs = { station: { x: 2000, y: 1600 }, vehicle: { x: 2000 - dx, y: 1600 + dy, energy: cost + (Math.floor(n / 3) % 3 - 1), readyAtTick: 30 + Math.floor(n / 7) % 9 }, radiusMm: 400, cost, currentTick: 30 + Math.floor(n / 7) % 9 + (Math.floor(n / 5) % 2 ? 0 : -1) };
  const d2 = dx * dx + dy * dy;
  let reason = 'repair';
  if (inputs.currentTick < inputs.vehicle.readyAtTick) reason = 'cooldown';
  if (reason === 'repair' && d2 > 160000) reason = 'range';
  if (reason === 'repair' && inputs.vehicle.energy < cost) reason = 'energy';
  const accepted = reason === 'repair';
  return { inputs, expected: { accepted, reason, energy: inputs.vehicle.energy - (accepted ? cost : 0) }, prompt: 'A repair station has a different rule: first reject cooldown, then reject outside its inclusive 400 mm radius, then reject insufficient energy. Only an accepted repair deducts cost once. No movement happens in this request. Return JSON {accepted, reason, energy}; reason is cooldown, range, energy or repair.', explanation: `This action also spends a resource, so position alone cannot authorize it. The squared distance is ${d2}; the limit is 160,000. Check readiness, range and energy in that order. The first applicable result is ${reason}, leaving energy ${inputs.vehicle.energy - (accepted ? cost : 0)}. Denial never spends the cost.` };
}

export function makeItem({ mode, key, seed }) {
  if (!['practice', 'completion', 'mastery'].includes(mode)) throw new TypeError('unknown item mode');
  const valid = mode === 'mastery' ? unit.masterySlots : unit.sections.map((section) => section.id);
  if (!valid.includes(key)) throw new TypeError('unknown spatial item key');
  const n = seedNumber(seed) + (mode === 'completion' ? 127 : mode === 'mastery' ? 263 : 0);
  let item;
  let objectiveIds;
  if (key === 'range' || key === 'boundary') { item = rangeCase(n); objectiveIds = ['spatial.range']; }
  if (key === 'tick-order') { item = movementRangeCase(n); objectiveIds = ['spatial.tick-order', 'spatial.range']; }
  if (key === 'cooldown' || key === 'refusal') { item = interactionCase(n, mode === 'mastery'); objectiveIds = ['spatial.cooldown', 'spatial.tick-order', 'spatial.range']; }
  if (key === 'transfer') { item = transferCase(n); objectiveIds = ['spatial.range', 'spatial.cooldown']; }
  if (mode === 'completion') {
    const { actor, target } = item.inputs;
    item.inputs.completedSteps = key === 'range'
      ? [`The x separation is ${actor.x} − ${target.x} = ${actor.x - target.x}; its square is ${(actor.x - target.x) ** 2}.`]
      : key === 'tick-order'
        ? [`After the one active movement step the position is (${item.expected.x}, ${item.expected.y}). Continue by calculating the squared distance from this position and comparing the radius.`]
        : [`Cargo is ${actor.cargo}, so the relevant target is the ${item.inputs.targetKind}. Its coordinates are (${target.x}, ${target.y}). Continue with the ready-tick comparison.`];
  }
  const hints = ['Identify whether you are measuring before movement or after it.', key === 'range' || key === 'tick-order' ? 'Square the x and y separations from the position being measured, add them, and compare with 62,500 using <=.' : 'Write the two squared separations; check the ready tick before authorizing any state change.', item.explanation];
  return { id: `spatial:${mode}:${key}:${seed}`, objectiveIds, ...item, prompt: `${mode === 'completion' ? 'Completion step: retain the supplied rule and fill the resulting state. ' : ''}${item.prompt}`, format: { type: 'json' }, hints: mode === 'mastery' ? [] : hints, source };
}

const source = (anchor) => ({ path: 'telemetry/LEARNER.md', anchor });
export const unit = {
  id: 'telemetry', title: 'M6 · Reproduce a complete window', prerequisites: ['order', 'integrity'],
  objectives: [
    { id: 'telemetry.checkpoint', kind: 'procedure', text: 'Compute a retained window from its checkpoint instead of a new initial state.', prerequisites: ['order.coalescing'] },

      paragraphs: [
        'A checkpoint saves enough state to continue the game: positions, movement intent, pending interaction, expiry, cooldown and detector history. A public picture of the score leaves some of that state out. Starting again from an empty game can therefore produce a different next tick.',
        'A window consists of a checkpoint followed by a bounded list of operations. The checkpoint describes the state after startIndex. Restore it, then apply every retained operation. An empty window still restores and compares its checkpoint; empty does not mean invalid.',
      ],
      worked: { prompt: 'A small score register is 7 in the checkpoint.     { id: 'sequence', title: 'Check the history before trusting its result', objectiveIds: ['telemetry.sequence'],
      paragraphs: [
        'An absolute index is an operation’s position in the whole recorded history. If startIndex is 40, the next entries must be 41, 42 and so on. endIndex must equal startIndex plus the number of entries. Sorting or renumbering a damaged record would invent evidence.',
        'Check schema, release, completeness, sequence, checkpoint/events and final state in that order. Completeness requires an event array of at most 256 entries and complete:true. A matching final score does not repair a missing index: a stale operation may leave the score unchanged while still belonging in the history.',
      ],
      worked: { prompt: 'A complete supported window starts at 80, contains indices 81 and 83, and ends at 82. Its claimed final score matches a replay.', steps: ['Schema, release and completeness pass.', 'The second entry should be 82 but is 83.', 'Stop at sequence before considering the final score.'], answer: '{"ok":false,"reason":"sequence"}' },
      completion: { prompt: 'A supported record starts at 15, has no events, has complete:true and ends at 15.', steps: ['The array length is zero, within the bound.', 'endIndex equals startIndex plus zero.'], missing: 'Supply whether sequence passes and what state must next be restored.' }, source: source('absolute-order') },
    { id: 'claim', title: 'State exactly what replay establishes', objectiveIds: ['telemetry.claim'],
      paragraphs: [
        'Replay establishes that a supplied checkpoint and operation sequence reproduce a supplied final state under a particular engine. It does not authenticate the producer. A person able to replace the checkpoint, events and final claim can create another internally consistent history.',
        'For an audit, keep consistency and provenance as separate questions. Refusing an inconsistent record means the record cannot support that replay. It does not, by itself, identify cheating, intent, token ownership or actual network timing. The source project performs replay through the real engine; these small questions rehearse its decisions.',
      ],
      worked: { prompt: 'An inventory counter’s exported checkpoint and all later operations reproduce its final total, but the exporter can replace the whole record.', steps: ['The arithmetic and operation sequence are internally consistent.', 'No independent identity or custody evidence was supplied.', 'Report consistency and leave producer authenticity unresolved.'], answer: 'Internally consistent; producer authenticity is not established.' },
      completion: { prompt: 'A rewritten record still replays to its rewritten final claim.', steps: ['The replay calculation agrees with the supplied claim.'], missing: 'Name the identity claim that still needs separate evidence.' }, source: source('repair-and-scope') },
  ],
  masterySlots: ['boundary', 'refusal', 'transfer'],
  support: {
    milestones: ['Compute from a checkpoint, including a zero-change operation.', 'Reject a sequence gap before comparing the final state.', 'Implement replayWindow with the supplied engine facade and run the source checker.'],
    hints: ['Locate the saved state immediately before the retained operations.', 'Check envelope phases before applying any event; never repair the record.', 'After a committed response, use the sibling calculation to separate consistency from provenance.'],
    reference: 'telemetry/LEARNER.md',
  },
};

function hashSeed(seed) {
  let n = 2166136261;
  for (const char of String(seed)) n = Math.imul(n ^ char.charCodeAt(0), 16777619) >>> 0;
  return n;
}

function windowCase(n) {
  const startIndex = 10 + n % 180;
  const initial = 2 + n % 23;
  const deltas = [n % 5, 0, 1 + n % 7];
  const events = deltas.map((add, i) => ({ index: startIndex + i + 1, event: { add } }));
  const record = { schema: 1, runtimeRelease: 'counter-1', startIndex, checkpoint: { score: initial }, events, endIndex: startIndex + events.length, complete: true, final: { score: initial + deltas.reduce((a, b) => a + b, 0) } };
  const variant = n % 7;
  if (variant === 1) record.runtimeRelease = 'counter-2';
  if (variant === 2) record.complete = false;
  if (variant === 3) record.events[1].index += 1;
  if (variant === 4) record.final.score += 1;
  if (variant === 5) record.schema = 2;
  if (variant === 6) { record.events = []; record.endIndex = startIndex; record.final.score = initial; }
  const reason = ['reproduced', 'incompatible', 'incomplete', 'sequence', 'final', 'schema', 'reproduced'][variant];
  return { record, reason };
}

function generateItem({ mode, key, seed }) {
  if (!['practice', 'completion', 'mastery'].includes(mode)) throw new Error('Unknown telemetry item mode');
  const section = mode === 'mastery' ? { boundary: 'checkpoint', refusal: 'sequence', transfer: 'claim' }[key] : key;
  if (!unit.sections.some(({ id }) => id === section)) throw new Error('Unknown telemetry item key');
  const n = hashSeed(`${mode}:${key}:${seed}`);
  const base = { id: `telemetry:${mode}:${key}:${seed}`, objectiveIds: [`telemetry.${section}`], source: source(section === 'checkpoint' ? 'causal-state' : section === 'sequence' ? 'absolute-order' : 'repair-and-scope') };
  if (section === 'checkpoint') {
    const score = 4 + n % 47;
    const additions = n % 4 === 0 && mode !== 'completion' ? [] : [1 + n % 7, 0, 2 + n % 5];
    const expected = additions.reduce((total, add) => total + add, score);
    return { ...base, inputs: { checkpoint: { score }, additions }, format: { type: 'number' }, tolerance: 0,
      prompt: `${mode === 'completion' ? 'The checkpoint has already been restored. Complete the remaining additions. ' : ''}This score-register rehearsal adds each listed value in order to the checkpoint score. Return the final score as an exact integer in score units. An empty list leaves the checkpoint score unchanged.`, expected,
      explanation: `Start from ${score}, then add ${JSON.stringify(additions)}. The result is ${expected} score units. Starting at zero discards history saved in the checkpoint; dropping a zero addition may keep this number but would not preserve the event sequence.`,
      hints: ['The checkpoint is the starting value, not an output to ignore.', 'Add every listed value, preserving the checkpoint when the list is empty.', `${score} + ${additions.length ? additions.join(' + ') : '0'} = ${expected} score units.`] };
  }
  const { record, reason } = windowCase(n);
  const inputs = { engineRelease: 'counter-1', record, producerCanRewriteRecord: true };
  const expected = section === 'sequence' ? { ok: reason === 'reproduced', reason } : { reason, claim: reason === 'reproduced' ? 'consistent-only' : 'not-reproduced' };
  return { ...base, inputs, format: { type: 'json' },
    prompt: `${section === 'claim' ? 'A warehouse register exports this record; the producer can rewrite its contents. ' : ''}The simple engine restores checkpoint.score and adds event.add in order. Apply schema 1, matching release, complete:true and <=256 entries, consecutive absolute indices/end boundary, then final-score equality. ${section === 'claim' ? 'Return {reason,claim}, with claim consistent-only on reproduction or not-reproduced on refusal; replay supplies no producer authentication.' : 'Return {ok,reason}.'} Use reason reproduced for success, or schema, incompatible, incomplete, sequence, final for the first failed phase.`, expected,
    explanation: `The ordered checks give ${reason}, so the answer is ${JSON.stringify(expected)}. Each event index must be startIndex plus its one-based position, even when its addition is zero. A reproduced total establishes agreement within these supplied values; replacing all values can preserve that agreement without authenticating their origin.`,
    hints: ['Check the envelope and sequence before computing a total.', 'After those checks, start from checkpoint.score and compare the computed total with final.score.', `The first applicable phase is ${reason}; the complete response is ${JSON.stringify(expected)}.`] };
}

export function makeItem(args) {
  const item = generateItem(args);
  if (args.mode === 'mastery') return { ...item, hints: [] };
  if (args.mode === 'completion') {
    const x = item.inputs;
    const steps = args.key === 'checkpoint'
      ? [`The checkpoint was restored to ${x.checkpoint.score}. After the first addition ${x.additions[0]}, the register is ${x.checkpoint.score + x.additions[0]}. Apply the remaining ${x.additions.length - 1} operations.`]
      : args.key === 'sequence'
        ? [`The end-boundary arithmetic is ${x.record.startIndex} + ${x.record.events.length} = ${x.record.startIndex + x.record.events.length}. The first retained index, if present, should be ${x.record.startIndex + 1}. Continue through the refusal phases in their stated order.`]
        : [`The retained additions sum to ${x.record.events.reduce((sum, e) => sum + e.event.add, 0)}. This subtotal excludes the saved checkpoint. Check the envelope and sequence, then finish the reproduction and provenance decisions.`];
    return { ...item, inputs: { ...x, completedSteps: steps }, prompt: `Continue from the calculated work in inputs.completedSteps; the final decision is still yours. ${item.prompt}` };
  }
  return item;
}

function observationCase(n) {
  const tick = 2 + n % 17;
  const score = Math.floor(n / 3) % 8;
  const type = n % 3;
  const path = ['actor.cargo', 'actor.score', 'actor.x'][type];
  const expected = [false, score, 1000 + 250 * (2 + Math.floor(n / 3) % 3)][type];
  const actual = [true, score + 1, expected + 250][type];
  const context = ['a remote pickup', 'a remote deposit', 'one movement step after expiry'][type];
  const correct = { tick, 'http.status': 200, [path]: expected };
  const defect = { tick, 'http.status': 200, [path]: actual };
  return { inputs: { action: context, correct, defect, allowedPaths: ['http.status', path] }, expected: { tick, path, expected }, prompt: 'Both traces completed the stated action. Construct the single assertion that passes the correct trace and fails the defect trace. Return JSON {tick,path,expected}. Use an allowed path with different observed values.', explanation: `Both HTTP statuses are 200, so that assertion would pass both versions. At tick ${tick}, ${path} must equal ${JSON.stringify(expected)}; the defect produced ${JSON.stringify(actual)}. This checks the consequence of ${context}, after it happened.` };
}

const maskSets = [
  [3, 6, 5, 1], // any pair among the first three covers all; tie rule is explicit
  [1, 2, 4, 3],
  [7, 1, 2, 4],
  [3, 4, 1, 2],
];

function minimalPlan(assertions, defects) {
  let best = null;
  for (let subset = 1; subset < 2 ** assertions.length; subset += 1) {
    const chosen = assertions.filter((_, index) => subset & 2 ** index);
    const covered = defects.every((defect) => chosen.some((item) => JSON.stringify(item.observed[defect]) !== JSON.stringify(item.expected)));
    if (!covered) continue;
    const ids = chosen.map((item) => item.id).sort();
    if (!best || ids.length < best.length || ids.length === best.length && ids.join(',') < best.join(',')) best = ids;
  }
  return best;
}

function coverageCase(n) {
  const defects = ['equal-seq-admitted', 'expiry-T+3', 'stale-interact'];
  const masks = maskSets[n % maskSets.length];
  const rotation = Math.floor(n / 4) % 4;
  const admittedAt = 5 + Math.floor(n / 7) % 20;
  const initialX = 1000 + Math.floor(n / 9) % 5 * 25;
  const measurements = [
    { fixture: 'duplicate', arrange: `Admit seq 10 E at tick ${admittedAt}; retry seq 10 at tick ${admittedAt + 2}.`, atTick: admittedAt + 2, path: 'actor.expiresAt', expected: admittedAt + 4, defectValue: admittedAt + 6 },
    { fixture: 'fourth-step', arrange: `Admit seq 10 E at tick ${admittedAt} from x=${initialX}; process four ticks on open floor.`, atTick: admittedAt + 4, path: 'actor.x', expected: initialX + 1000, defectValue: initialX + 750 },
    { fixture: 'stale-bit', arrange: 'Before a tick, admit seq 10 idle false, then send seq 9 idle true from an empty courier at its core.', atTick: admittedAt + 1, path: 'actor.cargo', expected: false, defectValue: true },
  ];
  const assertions = masks.map((mask, index) => {
    const id = String.fromCharCode(65 + (index + rotation) % 4);
    const checks = measurements.filter((_, bit) => mask & 2 ** bit);
    const expected = checks.map((check) => check.expected);
    return { id, checks: checks.map(({ fixture, path, atTick }) => ({ fixture, path, atTick })), expected, observed: { correct: expected, ...Object.fromEntries(defects.map((defect, bit) => [defect, checks.map((check) => check.fixture === measurements[bit].fixture ? check.defectValue : check.expected)])) } };
  }).sort((a, b) => a.id.localeCompare(b.id));
  const expected = minimalPlan(assertions, defects);
  return { inputs: { defects, fixtures: measurements.map(({ defectValue, ...measurement }) => measurement), assertions, observationNote: 'Each candidate is one grouped equality assertion over the listed fixture observations in order. Every fixture is reset independently; all correct controls pass.' }, expected, prompt: 'Choose the fewest assertion IDs whose mismatches cover every defect column. Compare observed[defect] with expected as ordered arrays. If several smallest plans exist, choose the alphabetically earliest sorted ID list. Return a JSON array of IDs.', explanation: `The minimal plan is ${JSON.stringify(expected)}. The duplicate fixture exposes expiry renewal; the fourth-step fixture exposes early expiry; the stale-bit fixture exposes a wrongly staged pickup. Take the union of the differing columns. No smaller set covers all three. Equal-sized valid alternatives are resolved by the stated alphabetical rule, not by a claim that they are worse tests.` };
}

function controlsCase(n, transfer = false) {
  const names = transfer ? ['double-charge', 'old-revision', 'poll-writes'] : ['late-expiry', 'stale-admitted', 'read-renews'];
  const states = [
    { correct: 'pass', variant: 'assertion-fail', expected: 4, actual: 5 },
    { correct: 'pass', variant: 'pass', expected: 4, actual: 4 },
    { correct: 'pass', variant: 'timeout', expected: 4, actual: null },
    { correct: 'assertion-fail', variant: 'assertion-fail', expected: 4, actual: 5 },
    { correct: 'pass', variant: 'import-error', expected: 4, actual: null },
  ];
  const runs = names.map((id, index) => ({ id, ...states[(n + index * 2) % states.length], observationTick: 6 + Math.floor(n / 5) % 15, field: transfer ? ['account.charges', 'document.revision', 'document.revision'][index] : ['actor.x', 'actor.lastSeq', 'actor.expiresAt'][index] }));
  const expected = { detected: [], notDetected: [], inconclusive: [] };
  for (const run of runs) {
    if (run.correct !== 'pass' || !['pass', 'assertion-fail'].includes(run.variant)) { expected.inconclusive.push(run.id); continue; }
    if (run.variant === 'pass') { expected.notDetected.push(run.id); continue; }
    expected.detected.push(run.id);
  }
  for (const values of Object.values(expected)) values.sort();
  return { inputs: { context: transfer ? 'Reservation service: retrying a request must charge once, older document revisions must be ignored, and polling must not write. Each row uses a fresh fixture and a contract-specific state assertion.' : 'Each row reruns an isolated game scenario against a correct implementation and one defect.', runs }, expected, prompt: 'Classify the evidence. detected requires a passing correct control plus a completed variant assertion mismatch. notDetected means both pass. All failed correct controls and runs without a completed observation are inconclusive. Return JSON {detected,notDetected,inconclusive}, with alphabetically sorted ID arrays.', explanation: `Detected: ${expected.detected.join(', ') || 'none'}; not detected: ${expected.notDetected.join(', ') || 'none'}; inconclusive: ${expected.inconclusive.join(', ') || 'none'}. A timeout or import error is evidence of an unsuccessful run, not a demonstrated contract defect. A failing correct control invalidates the comparison even when the variant also fails.` };
}

function investigationCase(n) {
  const initialChargeCount = Math.floor(n / 7) % 4;
  const uniqueRequests = 1 + Math.floor(n / 6) % 3;
  const requestIds = Array.from({ length: uniqueRequests }, (_, index) => `reserve-${n % 97}-${index}`).flatMap((id) => [id, id]);
  const expectedChargeCount = initialChargeCount + uniqueRequests;
  const makeRun = () => ({ requestIds: [...requestIds], captureStatus: 'complete', processedRequestCount: requestIds.length, ledger: { source: 'owner', chargeCount: expectedChargeCount } });
  const inputs = {
    contract: 'This owned reservation service charges once for each distinct request ID. Retrying the same ID adds no charge. Start both implementations from the declared initial charge count. Compare owner ledger snapshots only after every request has been processed.',
    fixture: { initialChargeCount, requestIds },
    correctRun: makeRun(),
    candidateRun: makeRun(),
    actions: [
      { value: 'run-correct-control', meaning: 'Run the known-correct implementation on the declared fixture and capture its completed owner ledger.' },
      { value: 'repair-control', meaning: 'Diagnose the known-correct run or setup until it produces the contract value before comparing the candidate.' },
      { value: 'match-request-schedule', meaning: 'Rerun both implementations with exactly the declared request IDs and the same final processing boundary.' },
      { value: 'finish-candidate-observation', meaning: 'Resolve the interrupted capture and obtain the candidate owner ledger after every request is processed.' },
      { value: 'wait-for-worker', meaning: 'Allow the remaining queued requests to be processed, then capture the owner ledger.' },
      { value: 'read-owner-ledger', meaning: 'Replace the client estimate with a completed owner ledger observation.' },
      { value: 'increase-retries', meaning: 'Send one hundred additional copies of the current requests before checking anything else.' },
    ],
    reasons: [
      { value: 'control-absent', meaning: 'There is no correct-control result for this experiment.' },
      { value: 'control-disagrees', meaning: 'The known-correct run already disagrees with the declared contract.' },
      { value: 'different-inputs', meaning: 'The implementations received different request IDs, which can legitimately cause different charge counts.' },
      { value: 'no-completed-observation', meaning: 'The candidate run produced no completed state observation.' },
      { value: 'observation-too-early', meaning: 'The snapshot precedes processing of some requests whose effects the experiment is meant to test.' },
      { value: 'client-value-not-authoritative', meaning: 'A client estimate does not establish the owner ledger’s state.' },
      { value: 'insufficient-load', meaning: 'A higher retry volume alone is needed to make a conclusion valid.' },
    ],
  };
  const branch = n % 6;
  let nextAction;
  let reason;
  if (branch === 0) {
    inputs.correctRun = null;
    inputs.candidateRun.ledger.chargeCount += 1;
    nextAction = 'run-correct-control';
    reason = 'control-absent';
  }
  if (branch === 1) {
    inputs.correctRun.ledger.chargeCount += 1;
    inputs.candidateRun.ledger.chargeCount += 1;
    nextAction = 'repair-control';
    reason = 'control-disagrees';
  }
  if (branch === 2) {
    inputs.candidateRun.requestIds[1] = `different-${n}`;
    inputs.candidateRun.ledger.chargeCount += 1;
    nextAction = 'match-request-schedule';
    reason = 'different-inputs';
  }
  if (branch === 3) {
    inputs.candidateRun.captureStatus = 'timeout';
    inputs.candidateRun.ledger = null;
    nextAction = 'finish-candidate-observation';
    reason = 'no-completed-observation';
  }
  if (branch === 4) {
    inputs.candidateRun.processedRequestCount = 0;
    inputs.candidateRun.ledger.chargeCount = initialChargeCount;
    nextAction = 'wait-for-worker';
    reason = 'observation-too-early';
  }
  if (branch === 5) {
    inputs.candidateRun.ledger.source = 'client-estimate';
    inputs.candidateRun.ledger.chargeCount += 1;
    nextAction = 'read-owner-ledger';
    reason = 'client-value-not-authoritative';
  }
  const selectedReason = inputs.reasons.find((item) => item.value === reason).meaning;
  return { inputs, expected: { nextAction, reason, expectedChargeCount }, prompt: 'You must repair this experiment before judging the candidate’s retry behavior. Choose the single next action that addresses the unresolved evidence problem, and its reason, from the declared value labels. Also compute the final charge count required by the declared fixture, including its initial count. Return exactly JSON {nextAction,reason,expectedChargeCount}; nextAction and reason are label strings, expectedChargeCount is a number. A complete capture can still be too early if queued requests have not all been processed.', explanation: `The declared fixture has ${uniqueRequests} distinct request IDs, so it requires ${initialChargeCount} + ${uniqueRequests} = ${expectedChargeCount} total charges. ${selectedReason} The next action is ${nextAction}. Sending more retries does not repair that evidence gap; obtain a comparable, completed owner observation with a passing correct control before making a defect claim.` };
}

export function makeItem({ mode, key, seed }) {
  if (!['practice', 'completion', 'mastery'].includes(mode)) throw new TypeError('unknown item mode');
  if (!Number.isSafeInteger(seed) || seed < 0) throw new TypeError('seed must be a non-negative safe integer');
  const valid = mode === 'mastery' ? unit.masterySlots : unit.sections.map((section) => section.id);
  if (!valid.includes(key)) throw new TypeError('unknown testing item key');
  const n = seed + (mode === 'completion' ? 139 : mode === 'mastery' ? 281 : 0);
  let item;
  let objectiveIds;
  if (key === 'observe' || key === 'observation') { item = observationCase(n); objectiveIds = ['testing.observe']; }
  if (key === 'coverage' || key === 'minimal-plan') { item = coverageCase(n); objectiveIds = ['testing.observe', 'testing.coverage']; }
  if (key === 'controls') { item = controlsCase(n); objectiveIds = ['testing.controls']; }
  if (key === 'transfer') { item = investigationCase(n); objectiveIds = ['testing.observe', 'testing.controls']; }
  if (mode === 'completion') {
    item.inputs.completedSteps = key === 'observe'
      ? ['The two HTTP statuses agree, so a status assertion cannot distinguish these implementations. Compare the remaining authoritative observation.']
      : key === 'coverage'
        ? [`For ${item.inputs.defects[0]}, the differing rows are ${item.inputs.assertions.filter((row) => JSON.stringify(row.observed[item.inputs.defects[0]]) !== JSON.stringify(row.expected)).map((row) => row.id).join(', ')}. Now cover the other columns with the fewest rows overall.`]
        : [`For the first run, check the correct-control result (${item.inputs.runs[0].correct}) before interpreting its variant result (${item.inputs.runs[0].variant}). Complete all three category arrays.`];
  }
  return { id: `testing:${mode}:${key}:${seed}`, objectiveIds, ...item, prompt: `${mode === 'completion' ? 'Complete the assertion or evidence plan using the supplied observations. ' : ''}${item.prompt}`, format: { type: 'json' }, hints: mode === 'mastery' ? [] : ['Start with the contract value and the completed observation.', 'A mismatch covers only its own defect column; check correct controls before crediting failures.', item.explanation], source };
}

A large elapsed gap can create dropped work, but dropped ticks are not movement and are not extra processed tick numbers.
