function clockCase(n) {
  const startMs = 400 + n % 113;
  const first = 11 + n % 37;
  const second = 41 + Math.floor(n / 3) % 64;
  const third = [0, 249, 301, 777][Math.floor(n / 4) % 4] + Math.floor(n / 17) % 13;
  const readings = [startMs + first, startMs + first + second, startMs + first + second + third];
  const timer = createClock(startMs);
  let tick = 0;
  const expected = readings.map((nowMs) => {
    const clock = timer.sample(nowMs);
    tick += clock.ticks;
    return { tick, ...clock };
  });
  return { inputs: { startMs, readings, initial: { tick: 0, remainder: 0, overruns: 0 }, tickMs: 50, maximumTicksPerSample: 5 }, expected, prompt: 'For each reading, return one JSON object {tick,ticks,dropped,overruns,remainder}; tick is cumulative processed work. Return the objects as an array in reading order.', explanation: `The successive elapsed totals include the retained fractions. The resulting ledger is ${JSON.stringify(expected)}. Dropped whole ticks never enter cumulative tick and never remain as debt; only the remainder below 50 ms carries forward.` };
}

function receiptCase(n) {
  const startMs = 3000 + n % 73;
  const before = (n % 4) * 50 + Math.floor(n / 4) % 20;
  const after = [151, 200, 251, 777][Math.floor(n / 3) % 4] + Math.floor(n / 7) % 19;
  const record = { schema: 1, startMs, actions: [
    { type: 'join', label: 'join', id: 'courier' },
    { type: 'sample', label: 'before-receipt', nowMs: startMs + before },
    { type: 'input', label: 'receipt', id: 'courier', seq: 7 + n % 31, move: n % 2 ? 'E' : 'W', sentAtMs: Math.floor(n / 5) % 2 ? 1 : startMs + before + 9000 },
    { type: 'sample', label: 'after-receipt', nowMs: startMs + before + after },
  ] };
  const { observed } = runInvestigation(record);
  const received = observed.checkpoints[2];
  const final = observed.checkpoints[3];
  const expected = { receiptTick: received.tick, expiresAt: received.actors[0].expiresAt, xAtReceipt: received.actors[0].x, processedTick: final.tick, xAfterSample: final.actors[0].x, clock: final.clock };
  return { inputs: { record, initialActor: { x: 1000, move: 'idle', lastSeq: 0 } }, expected, prompt: 'Run this open-floor record in order. At startMs, processed tick, clock remainder and overruns are all zero. Return JSON {receiptTick,expiresAt,xAtReceipt,processedTick,xAfterSample,clock}; clock is the last sample’s {ticks,dropped,overruns,remainder}. All returned fields are numbers. sentAtMs is only a client annotation.', explanation: `Receipt occurs at processed tick ${received.tick} and keeps x=${received.actors[0].x}. Expiry is ${received.tick}+4=${expected.expiresAt}. The next callback processes ${final.clock.ticks} ticks and drops ${final.clock.dropped}; the final actor is x=${expected.xAfterSample}, tick=${final.tick}. The sentAtMs claim cannot change any of these fields.` };
}

function recoveryCase(n, transfer) {
  const startMs = 500 + n % 97;
  const seq = 10 + Math.floor(n / 3) % 70;
  const gap = [50, 100, 151][n % 3];
  const resumedSeq = seq + [-1, 0, 1][Math.floor(n / 3) % 3];
  const record = { schema: 1, startMs, actions: [
    { type: 'join', label: 'initial-join', id: 'A' },
    { type: 'input', label: 'initial-intent', id: 'A', seq, move: 'E' },
    { type: 'sample', label: 'two-steps', nowMs: startMs + 100 },
    { type: 'disconnect', label: 'outage', id: 'A' },
    { type: 'input', label: 'offline-attempt', id: 'A', seq: seq + 1, move: 'W' },
    { type: 'sample', label: 'during-outage', nowMs: startMs + 100 + gap },
    { type: 'resume', label: 'same-binding', id: 'A' },
    { type: 'input', label: 'resumed-receipt', id: 'A', seq: resumedSeq, move: 'W' },
    { type: 'sample', label: 'after-resume', nowMs: startMs + 200 + gap },
    { type: 'join', label: 'fresh-binding', id: 'B' },
  ] };
  const { observed } = runInvestigation(record);
  const final = observed.checkpoints.at(-1);
  const expected = { tick: final.tick, actors: final.actors, resumedReceipt: observed.checkpoints[7].receipt };
  const inputs = { record, note: 'A disconnect/resume restores the same owner process and binding. B is a fresh join.' };
  let extra = '';
  if (transfer) {
    const restarted = Math.floor(n / 9) % 3 === 0;
    const deadlineMs = 7000 + Math.floor(n / 11) % 101;
    const nowMs = restarted ? 20 + n % 30 : deadlineMs + [-1, 0, 23][Math.floor(n / 13) % 3];
    inputs.reservation = { deadlineMs, nowMs, sameClockOrigin: !restarted, processedGameTicksDuringPause: 0, rule: 'Valid only while nowMs < deadlineMs, if both readings have the same origin.' };
    expected.reservationStatus = restarted ? 'unknown' : nowMs < deadlineMs ? 'valid' : 'expired';
    extra = ' Also return reservationStatus: valid, expired or unknown. A separate maintenance reservation uses the stated absolute owner-clock deadline, not the game’s processed-tick expiry; a restarted clock has no known relation to the saved deadline.';
  }
  return { inputs, expected, prompt: `Trace the complete record. At startMs there are no actors; processed tick, clock remainder and overruns are zero. Joins create actor-1, actor-2 in order, each at x=1000, lastSeq=0, expiresAt=0 and idle. Return JSON {tick,actors,resumedReceipt}; actors is the final ordered array of {id,connection,connected,lastSeq,expiresAt,x}. connected is a boolean; id and connection are strings. resumedReceipt is {status,tick,seq}; status is "admitted", "stale" or "offline". Other fields are numbers.${extra}`, explanation: `The offline attempt is not admitted. Resume retains the actor’s history, so sequence ${resumedSeq} is ${expected.resumedReceipt.status}; a fresh join adds actor-2 at x=1000. The final processed tick is ${final.tick}.${transfer ? ` For the separate reservation the result is ${expected.reservationStatus}: elapsed-deadline rules use a continuing clock origin, while processed game ticks alone cannot decide them.` : ''}` };
}

export function makeItem({ mode, key, seed }) {
  if (!['practice', 'completion', 'mastery'].includes(mode)) throw new TypeError('unknown item mode');
  if (!Number.isSafeInteger(seed) || seed < 0) throw new TypeError('seed must be a non-negative safe integer');
  const valid = mode === 'mastery' ? unit.masterySlots : unit.sections.map((section) => section.id);
  if (!valid.includes(key)) throw new TypeError('unknown timing item key');
  const n = seed + (mode === 'completion' ? 149 : mode === 'mastery' ? 283 : 0);
  let item;
  let objectiveIds;
  if (key === 'clock') { item = clockCase(n); objectiveIds = ['timing.clock']; }
  if (key === 'receipt') { item = receiptCase(n); objectiveIds = ['timing.clock', 'timing.receipt']; }
  if (key === 'recovery' || key === 'transfer') { item = recoveryCase(n, key === 'transfer'); objectiveIds = ['timing.clock', 'timing.receipt', 'timing.recovery']; }
  if (mode === 'completion') {
    item.inputs.completedSteps = key === 'clock'
      ? [`The first sample has already been calculated: ${JSON.stringify(item.expected[0])}. Carry its remainder into the second sample and complete the ledger.`]
      : key === 'receipt'
        ? [`The sample before receipt has processed ${item.expected.receiptTick} ticks. The input arrives at that processed tick; now fill its expiry and subsequent movement.`]
        : ['The initial E input has moved the actor twice before disconnect: x=1500, lastSeq unchanged, expiry=4. Continue from that state; do not restart the actor.'];
  }
  return { id: `timing:${mode}:${key}:${seed}`, objectiveIds, ...item, prompt: `${mode === 'completion' ? 'Complete the checkpoint ledger from the supplied record. ' : ''}${item.prompt}`, format: { type: 'json' }, hints: mode === 'mastery' ? [] : ['Keep owner milliseconds, processed tick and actor state separate.', 'Carry only fractional milliseconds; retain actor state across resume, and admit only strictly newer sequences.', item.explanation], source };
}

`courses/anti-cheat-engineering/courier-lab/protocol.mjs`:

```mjs
const INPUT_KEYS = ['interact', 'move', 'seq', 'v'];
const MOVES = new Set(['N', 'S', 'E', 'W', 'idle']);

function inputProblem(input) {
  if (!input || typeof input !== 'object' || Array.isArray(input)) return 'input-object-required';
  const keys = Object.keys(input).sort();
  if (keys.length !== INPUT_KEYS.length || keys.some((key, index) => key !== INPUT_KEYS[index])) return 'input-keys';
  if (input.v !== 1) return 'input-version';
  if (!Number.isSafeInteger(input.seq) || input.seq < 1 || input.seq > 1_000_000) return 'input-sequence';
  if (!MOVES.has(input.move)) return 'input-move';
  if (typeof input.interact !== 'boolean') return 'input-interact';
  return null;
}

/** Parse only the declared command vocabulary; HTTP byte limits belong to the runtime. */
export function parseInput(text) {
  if (typeof text !== 'string') return { ok: false, reason: 'input-text-required' };
  let input;
  try {
    input = JSON.parse(text);
  } catch {
    return { ok: false, reason: 'invalid-json' };
  }
  const reason = inputProblem(input);
  if (reason) return { ok: false, reason };
  return { ok: true, input };
}

<!doctype html><html lang="en"><head><meta charset="utf-8"><meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width,initial-scale=1"><title>Detector evidence and retention · Courier Lab</title><link rel="stylesheet" href="/style.css"><link rel="stylesheet" href="/order.css"><link rel="stylesheet" href="/evidence.css"><link rel="stylesheet" href="/analysis.css"><link rel="stylesheet" href="/prediction-notebook.css"></head><body>
<header class="site-header"><a class="brand" href="/"><span class="brand-mark" aria-hidden="true">C</span> COURIER LAB</a><a class="edition" href="/course">COURSE MAP →</a></header>
<main class="lesson"><section class="intro"><p class="eyebrow">Modules 07 and 09 / Evaluate the evidence</p><h1>Useful signals.<br>Costly mistakes.</h1><p class="lede">Construct an evaluator that counts what a detector gets right and wrong. Then build a retention policy and measure what it costs to keep the evidence you need.</p><p class="model-note">Synthetic labelled cases from the owned engine · no production accuracy or capacity claim · code editing requires a workstation</p></section>
<nav class="lesson-nav" aria-label="Lesson sections"><a href="#detector">7 · Catches and misses</a><a href="#evaluation-lab">Build the evaluator</a><a href="#retention">9 · Retain and measure</a><a href="#retention-lab">Build the policy</a></nav>
<section id="detector"><p class="eyebrow">07 / A FINDING NEEDS A DENOMINATOR</p><h2>One alarming replay cannot estimate a detector.</h2><p>A detector flags a case for review. A <strong>label</strong> records what the test author knows about that case. Here positive means a synthetic client repeatedly sent invalid actions. A declared legal automation client is negative; its automation metadata is not passed to the classifier. These labels do not establish human intent. A <strong>true positive</strong> is a labelled-positive case that is flagged; a <strong>false positive</strong> is a labelled-negative case that is flagged. Missed positives are false negatives. Correctly unflagged negatives are true negatives.</p><div class="metric-grid"><article><h3>Precision</h3><p>TP / (TP + FP)<br>Of flagged cases, how many have the positive label?</p></article><article><h3>Recall</h3><p>TP / (TP + FN)<br>Of positive cases, how many were flagged?</p></article><article><h3>False-positive rate</h3><p>FP / (FP + TN)<br>Of negative cases, how many were flagged?</p></article></div><p>A zero denominator gives no estimate: report <code>null</code>, not an invented zero. Count each case once. Repeated observations from one case are not additional independent people.</p>
<div class="worked-lab"><div><p class="eyebrow">SAVED EVALUATION / NOT YOUR SUBMISSION</p><label for="evaluation-setting">Inspect a frozen setting</label><select id="evaluation-setting"></select><p>Count range denials strictly beyond the minimum distance in windows (current tick − window size, current tick]. A case is flagged when a window reaches the threshold. Use labels only after predicting flags.</p><pre role="region" id="evaluation-settings" tabindex="0" aria-label="Cases and settings to predict"></pre><button id="show-evaluation" class="primary">Show counts and rates</button><p id="evaluation-note"></p></div><div id="evaluation-results" hidden><div class="confusion" role="group" aria-label="Confusion counts"><div><span>True positive</span><strong id="tp">—</strong></div><div><span>False positive</span><strong id="fp">—</strong></div><div><span>False negative</span><strong id="fn">—</strong></div><div><span>True negative</span><strong id="tn">—</strong></div></div><p id="evaluation-rates" role="status" aria-live="polite"></p><p id="evaluation-feedback"></p><pre role="region" id="evaluation-decisions" tabindex="0" aria-label="Recorded case decisions"></pre></div></div>
<p>Use the exploration split to compare threshold 3 at windows 8 and 20, then compare a low threshold with a stricter one. Record which setting you expect to behave differently on evaluation and why. Freeze your settings before revealing evaluation results. The corpus includes an honest-shaped case and a valid automation case with identical observed signals. A classifier using only those signals must give them the same prediction; changing a threshold cannot create missing information.</p><aside class="callout"><strong>Freeze the experiment before the final run.</strong>Use the exploration split to choose settings. Save the settings and their hash before reading evaluation results. A small synthetic split can catch implementation mistakes and expose tradeoffs; it does not estimate a live game's prevalence or user population.</aside></section>
<section id="evaluation-lab"><p class="eyebrow">07 / CONSTRUCT AND TEST</p><h2>Separate prediction from scoring.</h2><pre class="command">npm run core:prepare -- evaluation</pre><p>In the printed workspace, implement <code>evaluation/policy.mjs</code> from its guide. <code>classify</code> receives signals and settings. <code>evaluate</code> records each prediction before using the label to update its counts. Returning the label as the prediction makes the measurement meaningless.</p><pre class="command">npm run core:check -- --assistance "none"</pre><p>From the reference project, use the prepared evaluation workspace to freeze your completed self-contained policy and settings before running it: The report identifies the corpus, split, settings and source bytes. Exploration, frozen plans and one-use evaluation runs are saved under the prepared session. Later plans require <code>--revision "reason"</code>. The next check links their paths and hashes in a new submission; earlier attempts remain unchanged. Explain the limits of the chosen threshold.</p><pre class="command">npm run evaluation:explore -- /path/to/evaluation-workspace 3 8 500
npm run evaluation:explore -- /path/to/evaluation-workspace 3 20 500
npm run evaluation:plan -- /path/to/evaluation-workspace 3 20 500
npm run evaluation:run -- /path/to/evaluation-workspace &lt;printed-plan-id&gt;</pre><p>A useful transfer question: the next deployment has far fewer positive cases than this corpus. Which of these measurements can you directly carry over, and which need new population evidence? Do not substitute the synthetic labels for observed player intent.</p></section>
<section id="retention"><p class="eyebrow">09 / DATA HAS A PURPOSE AND A COST</p><h2>Keep enough to answer a named question.</h2><p><strong>Retention</strong> is the rule for how long data stays available. The denial-event export in this lesson keeps only tick, actor identifier, reason and squared distance. That is enough for this detector's window calculation; it is not enough to replay the whole game. The richer checkpoint/window format from module 6 has a different purpose.</p><p>Actor identifiers still link behavior inside a run. Removing a capability token or a device field does not make the remaining events anonymous. An age limit and a record-count limit answer different questions: how old can an event be, and how much can the store hold?</p>
<div class="worked-lab"><div><p class="eyebrow">RECORDED LOCAL MEASUREMENTS</p><label for="retention-setting">Inspect a retention setting</label><select id="retention-setting"></select><pre role="region" id="retention-inputs" tabindex="0" aria-label="Retention inputs to predict"></pre><button id="show-retention" class="primary">Show retained data and cost</button><p id="retention-note" role="status" aria-live="polite"></p></div><div id="retention-results" hidden><div class="byte-row"><span>Input JSON bytes</span><strong id="input-bytes">—</strong><div class="byte-track"><div id="input-bar"></div></div></div><div class="byte-row"><span>Export JSON bytes</span><strong id="output-bytes">—</strong><div class="byte-track"><div id="output-bar"></div></div></div><p id="retention-time"></p><pre id="retention-fields" tabindex="0"></pre></div></div>
<p>These elapsed times were measured on a named local runtime, with a stated workload, warmup and sample count. Whole-operation timing includes validation and cloning. Policy-plus-encoding timing isolates less work; neither estimates production capacity. With fewer than 20 samples, the tail shown is the maximum, not p95. Raw samples remain inspectable. They are not a promise for another machine. Serialized byte counts are reproducible for these records; process-memory measurements also include runtime allocation and garbage collection.</p><aside class="callout"><strong>A smaller export can answer fewer questions.</strong>If you retain fewer ticks than the detector's observation window, an older qualifying event disappears before classification. Decide whether that loss is acceptable before celebrating the smaller file.</aside></section>
<section id="retention-lab"><p class="eyebrow">09 / CONSTRUCT, MEASURE, DELETE</p><h2>Make the limits executable.</h2><pre class="command">npm run core:prepare -- retention</pre><p>Implement <code>retention/policy.mjs</code> in the printed workspace. Filter by the stated age boundary, keep the newest permitted count and project to exactly the allowed fields. Preserve input order and leave the input unchanged.</p><pre class="command">npm run core:check -- --assistance "none"</pre><p>From the reference project, use your completed self-contained policy to compare two settings: Export a denial-event file, inspect its fields, then delete that export using the supplied command and verify that the path is gone. This deletes that file only; copied files, earlier reports and original records are separate artifacts.</p><pre class="command">npm run retention:measure -- /path/to/policy.mjs artifacts/measure-01.json 4095:512:64 4095:128:16 --warmup 5 --samples 20
npm run retention:export -- /path/to/policy.mjs artifacts/denials-01.json artifacts/receipt-01.json 256 128
npm run retention:delete -- artifacts/receipt-01.json artifacts/deleted-01.json</pre><p>Every output must be a fresh path; use a new numbered path for each revision. The export source is a named synthetic workload held in memory. These commands run your JavaScript locally; they are not a security sandbox.</p><p>Keep settings, measured counts, byte lengths and runtime metadata with your explanation. State the investigation this export supports and one question that its reduced fields or shorter history can no longer answer. Do not put real player identifiers or external credentials in this teaching corpus.</p></section>

Reports record the actual local runtime used.</p><a class="next-lesson" href="/course">Return to the complete course map →</a></section></main><footer>Count cases, preserve uncertainty, and keep evidence for a purpose.</footer><script type="module" src="/analysis.js"></script></body></html>

import { predictionNotebook } from './prediction-notebook.js';
const $ = id => document.getElementById(id);
let data;
const rate = value => value === null ? 'undefined (no denominator)' : `${(value * 100).toFixed(1)}%`;
function showEvaluation() {
  const entry = data.evaluations[Number($('evaluation-setting').value)];
  const { metrics } = entry.result;
  for (const field of ['tp', 'fp', 'tn', 'fn']) $(field).textContent = metrics[field];
  $('evaluation-rates').textContent = `Precision ${rate(metrics.precision)} · recall ${rate(metrics.recall)} · false-positive rate ${rate(metrics.falsePositiveRate)}`;
  $('evaluation-note').textContent = `${metrics.total} synthetic cases. Positive means repeated invalid actions; declared legal automation remains negative. Compare the counts with your saved prediction and explain any difference. This is not a live user population.`;
  $('evaluation-results').hidden = false;
  $('evaluation-decisions').textContent = JSON.stringify(entry.result.decisions, null, 2);
  $('evaluation-feedback').textContent = 'Count eligible range denials whose squared distance exceeds the minimum squared distance. A window excludes its left endpoint and includes its right endpoint. Flag a case once any such window reaches the threshold. Then use its label to update exactly one count.';
}
function showRetention() {
  const entry = data.retention[Number($('retention-setting').value)];
  $('input-bytes').textContent = entry.inputBytes.toLocaleString();
  $('output-bytes').textContent = entry.outputBytes.toLocaleString();
  $('input-bar').style.width = '100%';
  $('output-bar').style.width = `${Math.min(100, 100 * entry.outputBytes / entry.inputBytes)}%`;
  $('retention-note').textContent = `${entry.outputCount} of ${entry.inputCount} events retained. Compare this with your saved count. This is a denial-event export, not a complete replay.`;
  const whole = entry.timingSummary.wholeOperation, policy = entry.timingSummary.policyAndEncode;
  $('retention-time').textContent = `Whole operation: median ${whole.medianMs.toFixed(3)} ms, ${whole.tailStatistic} ${whole.tailMs.toFixed(3)} ms. Policy + encode: median ${policy.medianMs.toFixed(3)} ms, ${policy.tailStatistic} ${policy.tailMs.toFixed(3)} ms. ${entry.samples} samples after ${entry.warmup} warmups.`;
  $('retention-fields').textContent = JSON.stringify({ settings: entry.settings, keptFields: ['tick', 'actorId', 'reason', 'distanceSquared'], runtime: data.runtime, workload: entry.workload, wholeOperationMs: entry.elapsedMs, policyAndEncodeMs: entry.policyAndEncodeMs }, null, 2);
  $('retention-results').hidden = false;
}
async function start() {
  const response = await fetch('/samples/analysis-cases.json');
  if (!response.ok) throw new Error('Recorded analysis examples could not be loaded.');
  data = await response.json();
  for (const [index, entry] of data.evaluations.entries()) $('evaluation-setting').add(new Option(entry.split === 'diagnostic' ? 'Empty-signal diagnostic' : entry.name, String(index)));
  for (const [index, entry] of data.retention.entries()) $('retention-setting').add(new Option(entry.name, String(index)));
  const evaluationBook = predictionNotebook({ button: $('show-evaluation'), reveal: showEvaluation, hide: () => { $('evaluation-results').hidden = true; $('evaluation-note').textContent = ''; } });
  const retentionBook = predictionNotebook({ button: $('show-retention'), reveal: showRetention, hide: () => { $('retention-results').hidden = true; $('retention-note').textContent = ''; } });
  function selectEvaluation() {
    const index = Number($('evaluation-setting').value), entry = data.evaluations[index];
    const cases = entry.split === 'diagnostic' ? [{ id: 'diagnostic/empty', label: false, signals: [] }] : evaluationInputs.filter(item => item.split === entry.split);
    const inputs = { split: entry.split, settings: entry.settings, settingsHash: entry.settingsHash, corpusVersion: data.corpusVersion, cases };
    $('evaluation-settings').textContent = JSON.stringify(inputs, null, 2);
    evaluationBook.setCase({ id: `evaluation/${index}`, version: 1, question: 'Using the inputs below, predict which cases are flagged and the TP, FP, FN and TN counts. What happens to precision or recall if its denominator is zero? Explain how the window and threshold affect your prediction.', inputs });
  }
  function selectRetention() {
    const index = Number($('retention-setting').value), entry = data.retention[index];
    const inputs = { settings: entry.settings, eventTicks: `One event at each integer tick from 0 through ${entry.inputCount - 1}`, inputCount: entry.inputCount, fieldsKept: ['tick', 'actorId', 'reason', 'distanceSquared'], ageRule: 'Keep nowTick - maxAgeTicks < tick <= nowTick, then the newest maxEvents.' };
    $('retention-inputs').textContent = JSON.stringify(inputs, null, 2);
    retentionBook.setCase({ id: `retention/${index}`, version: 1, question: 'How many events will remain under both limits, and what can this reduced export no longer reconstruct? Predict the direction of the byte-size change; exact runtime and serialized sizes will be measured, not inferred.', inputs });
  }
  $('evaluation-setting').addEventListener('change', selectEvaluation);
  $('retention-setting').addEventListener('change', selectRetention);
  selectEvaluation(); selectRetention();
}
start().catch(error => { $('evaluation-note').textContent = error.message; $('retention-note').textContent = error.message; });

`courses/anti-cheat-engineering/courier-lab/public/app.js`:

```js
const $ = (id) => document.getElementById(id);
const SESSION_KEY = 'ivy.courier.session.v1';
let storageUnavailable = false;
function savedToken() {
  try {
    const saved = sessionStorage.getItem(SESSION_KEY);
    return /^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{43}$/.test(saved ?? '') ? saved : null;
  } catch { storageUnavailable = true; return null; }
}
function rememberToken(value) {
  try {
    if (value) sessionStorage.setItem(SESSION_KEY, value);
    if (!value) sessionStorage.removeItem(SESSION_KEY);
  } catch { storageUnavailable = true; }
}
let token = savedToken();
let connected = false;
let sequence = 0;
let direction = 'idle';
let pendingInteraction = false;
let sending = false;
let pollBusy = false;
let traceUntil = 0;
let lastDecisionKey = '';
const keys = new Map([['ArrowUp','N'],['w','N'],['ArrowLeft','W'],['a','W'],['ArrowDown','S'],['s','S'],['ArrowRight','E'],['d','E']]);
const heldKeys = new Map();

async function request(path, options = {}) {
  const response = await fetch(path, {
    ...options,
    headers: { ...(token ? { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}` } : {}), ...(options.body ? { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' } : {}) },
    signal: AbortSignal.timeout(3000),
  });
  const body = await response.json();
  return { status: response.status, body };
}
function setConnected(value, message) {
  connected = value;
  $('connection').textContent = value ? 'Connected' : 'Disconnected';
  $('connection').classList.toggle('online', value);
  $('connect').textContent = value ? 'Connected to local server' : token ? 'Reconnect session' : 'Connect to server';
  $('connect').disabled = value;
  $('connect').hidden = value;
  $('interact').disabled = !value;
  $('forge').disabled = !value;
  document.querySelectorAll('[data-move]').forEach((button) => { button.disabled = !value; });
  if (message) $('announcement').textContent = message;
  if (value) return;
  direction = 'idle';
  heldKeys.clear();
  pendingInteraction = false;
  updatePressed();
}
function updatePressed() {
  document.querySelectorAll('[data-move]').forEach((button) => button.classList.toggle('pressed', button.dataset.move === direction));
}
function showTrace(input, result, sticky = false) {
  if (!sticky && Date.now() < traceUntil) return;
  if (sticky) traceUntil = Date.now() + 5000;
  $('exchange').textContent = `POST /input\n${JSON.stringify(input, null, 2)}\n\nHTTP ${result.status}\n${JSON.stringify(result.body, null, 2)}`;
}
function render(state) {
  $('score').textContent = state.actor.score;
  $('cargo').textContent = state.actor.cargo ? 'Core aboard' : 'Empty';
  $('tick').textContent = state.tick;
  $('actor').setAttribute('transform', `translate(${state.actor.x} ${state.actor.y})`);
  $('core').setAttribute('transform', `translate(${state.core.x} ${state.core.y})`);
  $('core').style.visibility = state.actor.cargo ? 'hidden' : 'visible';
  $('objective').textContent = state.actor.cargo ? 'Return to the depot. Interact to deliver the core.' : 'Reach the yellow core. Interact to collect it.';
  $('arena-desc').textContent = `Server tick ${state.tick}. Courier at ${state.actor.x}, ${state.actor.y} millimetres. ${state.actor.cargo ? 'Carrying the core.' : 'No cargo.'} Delivered ${state.actor.score}. Core at ${state.core.x}, ${state.core.y}. Depot at 1000, 1000.`;
  $('findings').textContent = `Advisory records: ${state.findings.length}. Three distant range denials (>500 mm) in 20 processed ticks make a record. Cooldown and near-boundary attempts are excluded. This is a review signal, never a ban or proof of intent.`;
  if (!state.lastDecision) return;
  const decision = state.lastDecision;
  $('decision').textContent = `Tick ${decision.tick}: ${decision.status} — ${decision.reason}.`;
  const key = JSON.stringify(decision);
  if (key === lastDecisionKey) return;
  lastDecisionKey = key;
  const messages = { pickup: 'Core collected. Return to the depot.', deposit: 'Delivery confirmed by the server.', range: 'Interaction denied: move within 250 mm of the target.', cooldown: 'Interaction denied: wait four ticks after a successful interaction.' };
  $('announcement').textContent = messages[decision.reason] ?? 'Server decision received.';
}
async function poll() {
  if (!connected || pollBusy) return;
  pollBusy = true;
  try {
    const result = await request('/state');
    if (result.status !== 200) throw new Error('Session unavailable. Restart the page for a new session if the server restarted.');
    render(result.body);
  } catch (error) {
    setConnected(false, `Connection lost. ${error.message}`);
  } finally { pollBusy = false; }
}
async function sendInput(extra = {}) {
  if (!connected || sending) return;
  sending = true;
  const interaction = pendingInteraction;
  pendingInteraction = false;
  const input = { v: 1, seq: ++sequence, move: direction, interact: interaction, ...extra };
  try {
    const result = await request('/input', { method: 'POST', body: JSON.stringify(input) });
    showTrace(input, result, interaction || Object.keys(extra).length > 0);
    if (result.status === 401) throw new Error('Session no longer exists. Reload to start a new session.');
    if ('score' in extra) $('announcement').textContent = `Forged score request: HTTP ${result.status}, ${result.body.reason ?? result.body.error ?? result.body.status}. Check the server score above.`;
  } catch (error) {
    setConnected(false, `Input failed. ${error.message}`);
  } finally { sending = false; }
}
async function connect() {
  $('connect').disabled = true;
  try {
    let result = token ? await request('/state') : null;
    if (result?.status === 401) {
      token = null;
      sequence = 0;
      rememberToken(null);
    }
    if (!token) {
      const joined = await request('/join', { method: 'POST' });
      if (joined.status === 429) throw new Error('All four lab slots are in use. Reuse a saved tab, or restart your local server to begin a fresh run.');
      if (joined.status !== 201) throw new Error(joined.body.reason ?? joined.body.error ?? 'Cannot create session.');
      token = joined.body.token;
      rememberToken(token);
      result = await request('/state');
    }
    if (result.status !== 200) throw new Error('The session is unavailable. Retry once the local server is running.');
    sequence = Math.max(sequence, result.body.actor.lastSeq);
    const notice = storageUnavailable ? ' Session storage is unavailable; this tab works, but reloading may consume another slot.' : ' This tab resumes the same session after a reload.';
    setConnected(true, 'Connected. Move to the core and interact.' + notice);
    render(result.body);
    if ($('exchange').textContent.startsWith('Connect to see')) $('exchange').textContent = 'Send an input to inspect its request and result.';
  } catch (error) { setConnected(false, error.message); }
}
$('connect').addEventListener('click', connect);
$('interact').addEventListener('click', () => { pendingInteraction = true; void sendInput(); });
$('forge').addEventListener('click', () => { if (!sending) void sendInput({ score: 999 }); });
for (const button of document.querySelectorAll('[data-move]')) {
  button.addEventListener('pointerdown', (event) => {
    if (!connected) return;
    event.preventDefault();
    button.setPointerCapture(event.pointerId);
    direction = button.dataset.move;
    updatePressed();
    void sendInput();
  });
  const release = () => { direction = 'idle'; updatePressed(); void sendInput(); };
  button.addEventListener('keydown', (event) => {
    if (!connected || !['Enter', ' '].includes(event.key)) return;
    event.preventDefault();
    direction = button.dataset.move;
    updatePressed();
    if (!event.repeat) void sendInput();
  });
  button.addEventListener('keyup', (event) => {
    if (!['Enter', ' '].includes(event.key)) return;
    event.preventDefault();
    release();
  });
  button.addEventListener('blur', release);
  button.addEventListener('pointerup', release);
  button.addEventListener('pointercancel', release);
  button.addEventListener('lostpointercapture', release);
}
window.addEventListener('keydown', (event) => {
  if (!connected || event.target.closest('input,textarea,select')) return;
  const key = event.key.length === 1 ? event.key.toLowerCase() : event.key;
  if (keys.has(key)) {
    event.preventDefault();
    heldKeys.set(key, keys.get(key));
    direction = [...heldKeys.values()].at(-1);
    updatePressed();
    if (!event.repeat) void sendInput();
  }
  if (event.code !== 'Space' || event.target.closest('button') || event.repeat) return;
  event.preventDefault();
  pendingInteraction = true;
  void sendInput();
});
window.addEventListener('keyup', (event) => {
  const key = event.key.length === 1 ? event.key.toLowerCase() : event.key;
  if (!keys.has(key)) return;
  heldKeys.delete(key);
  direction = [...heldKeys.values()].at(-1) ?? 'idle';
  updatePressed();
  void sendInput();
});
window.addEventListener('blur', () => { direction = 'idle'; heldKeys.clear(); updatePressed(); void sendInput(); });
document.addEventListener('visibilitychange', () => { if (document.hidden) { direction = 'idle'; heldKeys.clear(); updatePressed(); void sendInput(); } });
setConnected(false);
setInterval(() => { if (direction !== 'idle' || pendingInteraction) void sendInput(); }, 100);
setInterval(poll, 150);

if (token) void connect();

```

<section id="timing"><p class="eyebrow">04 / ONE SERVER CLOCK</p><h2>Late delivery does not move the past.</h2><p>A server <strong>tick</strong> advances the simulation once. A network callback delivers a message; it does not necessarily advance a tick. This model processes 50 ms ticks and limits catch-up after a long pause. The accepted input receives its expiry from the server's current tick, not from a client timestamp.</p><p>Input admitted at tick T remains active through T+4. At T+5 it stops unless a newer input renewed it. An equal or older sequence does not renew the expiry. A disconnected browser may stop delivering messages while its existing server actor continues until expiry. Resuming that session preserves the actor; a new session creates a different actor.</p><div class="worked-lab"><div><p class="eyebrow">SAVED ENGINE / CLOCK INVESTIGATION</p><label for="timing-case">Choose a receipt schedule</label><select id="timing-case"></select><pre role="region" id="timing-input" tabindex="0" aria-label="Schedule to predict"></pre><button id="show-timing" class="primary">Reveal checkpoints</button><p>Predict which input still controls movement before revealing the next schedule. These are finite application-level schedules, not a simulation of every network.</p></div><div><p id="timing-summary" role="status" aria-live="polite"></p><pre id="timing-checkpoints" tabindex="0"></pre></div></div>
<pre class="command">npm run core:prepare -- timing</pre><p>In the printed workspace, implement <code>predictTiming(record)</code>. First write predictions and a reconnect explanation in <code>response.md</code>. The checker compares your model with the real engine and clock at each labelled action.</p><pre class="command">npm run core:check -- --assistance "none"</pre><p>Transfer: a pause spans sixteen nominal ticks but only a bounded number are processed. Explain why wall time, processed ticks and client-supplied time cannot be interchanged. Then predict a fresh-sequence input arriving exactly at expiry. Record any hints and retain the first response.</p></section>
<section id="recovery"><p class="eyebrow">10 / A RELEASE IS MORE THAN ITS CODE</p><h2>Choose a compatible recovery point.</h2><p>A <strong>configuration</strong> supplies values such as the allowed interaction radius. A <strong>state schema</strong> specifies the shape of saved data. The trial changes the radius from 250 to 100 mm and writes a new state envelope. A legal boundary pickup now fails. Restoring the old code while retaining the new envelope cannot restore the old state.</p><p>Your selector must return an existing, compatible package/configuration/snapshot tuple. Follow the declared target release, verify configuration identity and select the newest compatible snapshot. Do not invent a migration or silently substitute another release. A hash identifies bytes; it does not authenticate who approved them.</p><div class="worked-lab"><div><p class="eyebrow">SAVED LOCAL ROLLBACK TRIAL</p><label for="recovery-phase">Inspect one phase</label><select id="recovery-phase"><option value="baseline">Baseline legal action</option><option value="candidate">Changed configuration</option><option value="codeOnly">Code-only rollback</option><option value="recovered">Compatible tuple restored</option></select><pre role="region" id="recovery-input" tabindex="0" aria-label="Recovery inputs to predict"></pre><button id="show-recovery" class="primary">Show state and identity</button><p id="recovery-result" role="status" aria-live="polite"></p><p id="recovery-loss"></p></div><div><pre id="recovery-state" tabindex="0"></pre></div></div>

Check from the prepared workspace, then run your completed self-contained policy from the reference project:</p><pre class="command">npm run core:check -- --assistance "none"
# From the reference project:
npm run recovery:trial -- /path/to/policy.mjs artifacts/recovery-01.json</pre><p>The trial uses the real owned engine in memory; it changes no deployed service or files beyond the requested report. Recovery discards actions after the selected snapshot. The restored branch has its own lineage. Returning from acknowledged sequence 12 to saved sequence 3 reopens sequences 4–12 in this model. A real service needs a recovery epoch or an external acknowledgement floor before accepting retries. A new pickup after restore does not reimburse a lost delivery or prove production rollback safety.</p><p>Additional transfer, separate from the worksheet: a repair also sends a physical print job. Restoring old state cannot retract the physical output. State the additional receipt or reconciliation contract you would need before recommending retry.</p></section>
<section id="capstone"><p class="eyebrow">11 / BUILD AND INDEPENDENTLY CHALLENGE</p><h2>A repair has a price. A retry is not another purchase.</h2><p>Build a separate repair-station extension to the owned arena. The server owns position, credits and energy. A request contains only <code>requestId</code> and <code>stationId</code>. At a distance of at most 400 mm, a repair costs two credits and restores three energy, capped at ten. The initial balance is six credits and four energy.</p><p>The first successful ID records a receipt. A retry of that ID for the same station returns the original receipt, even after movement, without charging again. A conflicting station refuses. Failed requests reserve no ID. When the two-receipt capacity is full, new IDs refuse instead of evicting old receipts and reopening a double-charge path.</p><p>Write an explanation before using the worked example. Identify the authority boundary, give a concrete double-charge counterexample, explain the receipt-capacity tradeoff and propose an independent regression test. Transfer to a different resource with a delayed completion and decide when its receipt becomes final.</p><div class="worked-lab"><div><p class="eyebrow">SAVED REAL HTTP / AUTHOR WORKED EXAMPLE</p><label for="repair-step">Inspect a request</label><select id="repair-step"></select><pre role="region" id="repair-input" tabindex="0" aria-label="Request history to predict"></pre><button id="show-repair" class="primary">Show authoritative result</button><p id="repair-result" role="status" aria-live="polite"></p></div><div><pre id="repair-state" tabindex="0"></pre></div></div>
<pre class="command">npm run core:prepare -- capstone</pre><p>Implement both <code>capstone/policy.mjs</code> and <code>capstone/scenario.mjs</code>. The scenario must independently assert HTTP status, server balances, receipts and unchanged state after refusal. It must accept two correct implementations and expose the supplied wrong variants. The panel includes isolated wrong-energy, wrong-receipt and refusal-side-effect controls. Passing shows discrimination on those controls; it does not prove the dataflow of arbitrary assertions. Use ordinary JavaScript assertions on observed values. A test that always throws or checks only status strings cannot pass the panel.</p><pre class="command">npm run core:check -- --assistance "none"

npm run capstone:trace -- /path/to/policy.mjs artifacts/repair-01.json</pre></section>

```js
import { predictionNotebook } from './prediction-notebook.js';
const $ = id => document.getElementById(id);
let data;
function timing() {
  const row = data.timing[Number($('timing-case').value)];
  $('timing-summary').textContent = `${row.observed.checkpoints.length} labelled checkpoints from the real engine. Compare your saved prediction with tick, position, expiry and receipt below; append a revision explaining any difference.`;
  $('timing-checkpoints').textContent = JSON.stringify(row.observed.checkpoints, null, 2);
}
function recovery() {
  const phase = $('recovery-phase').value, row = data.recovery[phase];
  $('recovery-result').textContent = `${phase}: ${row.status} / ${row.reason ?? 'legal action'}`;
  $('recovery-state').textContent = JSON.stringify(row, null, 2);
  const loss = data.recovery.dataLoss;
  $('recovery-loss').textContent = `Recovery discards ${loss.discardedTicks} ticks and ${loss.discardedRecordedOperations} operations; score ${loss.scoreBeforeRecovery} → ${loss.scoreAtRestoredSnapshot}. Acknowledged sequence ${loss.acknowledgedSequences.highestBeforeRestore} returns to ${loss.acknowledgedSequences.restoredLastSeq}; reopened ${loss.acknowledgedSequences.reopened}. Compare this with your prediction and append any repair.`;
}
function repair() {
  const row = data.capstone.steps[Number($('repair-step').value)];
  $('repair-result').textContent = `HTTP ${row.status}: ${row.data.reason}. Compare balances, receipt and unchanged-state expectations with your saved answer.`;
  $('repair-state').textContent = JSON.stringify(row.data, null, 2);
}
const recoveryInputs = phase => {
  const row = data.recovery[phase];
  return { phase, identity: row.identity, inputSeq: row.inputSeq, action: row.action, before: row.before, configurations: data.recovery.identities.configurations, target: data.recovery.identities.targetReleaseId, releases: data.recovery.identities.releases.map(({ id, stateSchema, configId }) => ({ id, stateSchema, configId })) };
};
const repairInputs = index => {
  const requests = data.capstone.trace.slice(0, index + 1).map((entry, i) => ({ request: entry.request, position: { x: entry.state.actors[0].x, y: entry.state.actors[0].y } }));
  return { initial: { credits: 6, energy: 4, receipts: [] }, rules: { cost: 2, energyAdded: 3, energyCap: 10, rangeMm: 400, receiptLimit: 2 }, stations: [{ id: 'alpha', x: 0, y: 0 }, { id: 'beta', x: 2000, y: 0 }], requests };
};
async function start() {
  const response = await fetch('/samples/completion-cases.json');
  if (!response.ok) throw new Error('Saved completion examples unavailable.');
  data = await response.json();
  data.timing.forEach((row, i) => $('timing-case').add(new Option(`Schedule ${i + 1} · ${row.name}`, String(i))));
  data.capstone.steps.forEach((row, i) => $('repair-step').add(new Option(`Request ${i + 1}`, String(i))));
  const timingBook = predictionNotebook({ button: $('show-timing'), reveal: timing, hide: () => { $('timing-summary').textContent = ''; $('timing-checkpoints').textContent = ''; } });
  const recoveryBook = predictionNotebook({ button: $('show-recovery'), reveal: recovery, hide: () => { for (const id of ['recovery-result', 'recovery-state', 'recovery-loss']) $(id).textContent = ''; } });
  const repairBook = predictionNotebook({ button: $('show-repair'), reveal: repair, hide: () => { $('repair-result').textContent = ''; $('repair-state').textContent = ''; } });
  function selectTiming() {
    const index = Number($('timing-case').value), row = data.timing[index];
    // Action labels are result mnemonics in some fixtures. Show neutral step labels before prediction.
    const inputs = { ...row.record, rules: { tickMs: 50, maxCatchUpTicksPerSample: 5, movementPerTickMm: 250, initialX: 1000, inputActiveThrough: 'admission tick + 4 inclusive', leftoverFraction: 'Carry fractional milliseconds; discard whole ticks beyond the catch-up limit.' }, actions: row.record.actions.map((action, i) => ({ ...action, label: `step-${i + 1}` })) };
    $('timing-input').textContent = JSON.stringify(inputs, null, 2);
    timingBook.setCase({ id: `timing/${row.name}`, version: 1, question: 'Predict the processed tick, actor x position, active input expiry and input receipt at each step. Explain whether client timestamps, duplicate sequences or reconnection change them.', inputs });
  }
  function selectRecovery() {
    const phase = $('recovery-phase').value, inputs = recoveryInputs(phase);
    $('recovery-input').textContent = JSON.stringify(inputs, null, 2);
    recoveryBook.setCase({ id: `recovery/${phase}`, version: 1, question: 'Predict whether this package, configuration and state can run together and whether the action applies. Explain the compatibility check and what later acknowledged work a restore can discard.', inputs });
  }
  function selectRepair() {
    const index = Number($('repair-step').value), inputs = repairInputs(index);
    $('repair-input').textContent = JSON.stringify(inputs, null, 2);
    repairBook.setCase({ id: `capstone/request-${index + 1}`, version: 1, question: 'Predict the last request’s reason, energy, credits and receipt. Identify the authority boundary, give a double-charge counterexample, explain the capacity tradeoff and propose an independent regression test.', inputs });
  }
  $('timing-case').addEventListener('change', selectTiming);
  $('recovery-phase').addEventListener('change', selectRecovery);
  $('repair-step').addEventListener('change', selectRepair);
  selectTiming(); selectRecovery(); selectRepair();
}
start().catch(error => { $('timing-summary').textContent = error.message; });

<!doctype html><html lang="en"><head><meta charset="utf-8"><meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width,initial-scale=1"><title>Owned bytes and replay · Courier Lab</title><link rel="stylesheet" href="/style.css"><link rel="stylesheet" href="/order.css"><link rel="stylesheet" href="/evidence.css"><link rel="stylesheet" href="/prediction-notebook.css"></head><body>

<main class="lesson"><section class="intro"><p class="eyebrow">Modules 05–06 / Own the evidence boundary</p><h1>Which bytes?<br>Which history?</h1><p class="lede">Build a package check that can stop the wrong runtime, then a replay policy that refuses incomplete evidence. Both become source files you can run and test.</p><p class="model-note">Owned local teaching project · Node 22+ for coding · phone reading and worked demonstrations supported</p></section>
<nav class="lesson-nav" aria-label="Lesson sections"><a href="#integrity">5 · Owned bytes</a><a href="#integrity-lab">Build the check</a><a href="#replay">6 · Replay</a><a href="#replay-lab">Build the policy</a></nav>
<section id="integrity"><p class="eyebrow">05 / FROM A CLAIM TO AN OBSERVATION</p><h2>A hash compares bytes. Trust chooses the reference.</h2><p>A <strong>digest</strong> is a fixed-size result computed from bytes. This project uses SHA-256. A <strong>manifest</strong> lists approved file paths, digests and a release identifier. The observer reads the owned files; the policy compares those observations with the approved manifest before the launcher starts the server.</p>
<div class="trust-diagram" role="group" aria-label="Approved reference and observed package are separate inputs to the policy"><div class="trusted"><small>OWNER'S APPROVED REFERENCE</small><b>Release + expected digests</b><p>Who may change this?</p></div><div><small>OBSERVED PACKAGE</small><b>Read files → hash bytes</b><p>What is actually on disk?</p></div><div class="policy-node"><small>YOUR POLICY</small><b>Match + compatible?</b><p>Start or refuse.</p></div></div>
<p>The manifest is trusted because of the workflow that supplies it, not because it contains hashes. If the same owner changes both the files and the reference, a match cannot establish that the owner is trustworthy. This lab has no remote attestation or signing authority. Its boundary is an approved local reference versus an observed owned package.</p>
<div class="worked-lab"><div><p class="eyebrow">WORKED INPUTS / NOT A SUBMISSION</p><label for="package-case">Compare this package</label><select id="package-case"><option value="approved">Approved release and bytes</option><option value="changed">Changed bytes, unchanged reference</option><option value="claim">Changed bytes, client claims approval</option><option value="self">Client copies the approved hashes</option><option value="missing">A required file is missing</option><option value="new">Explicitly approved compatible release</option><option value="both">Owner changes both inputs</option></select><button id="compare-package" class="primary">Show recorded comparison</button><div id="package-feedback" hidden><p id="package-verdict" role="status" aria-live="polite"></p><p id="package-detail" class="helper"></p><p id="package-explanation">Validate the reference and supported-list shapes first, then check release support, compare the complete path inventory, and finally compare digests. This order determines the first refusal reason. A match establishes agreement between these two inputs. It does not establish that observations came from a trusted file reader or authenticate who approved the reference. Compare that limit with your saved prediction and append a revision if needed.</p></div></div><pre role="region" id="package-observation" tabindex="0" aria-label="Worked package comparison inputs"></pre></div>
</section>
<section id="integrity-lab"><p class="eyebrow">05 / CONSTRUCT AND TEST</p><h2>Make the launcher earn its decision.</h2><p>From the complete reference project, prepare your independent source exercise:</p><pre class="command">npm run core:prepare -- integrity</pre><p>Change into the printed workspace. Read <code>integrity/LEARNER.md</code>, record predictions in <code>response.md</code>, and implement <code>integrity/policy.mjs</code>. The supplied observer performs bounded file reads and hashing. Your policy must check shape, supported release, inventory and digests; do not replace the approved reference with the observed values.</p><pre class="command">npm run core:check -- --assistance "none"</pre><p>Use an accurate assistance declaration. The checker runs your captured policy against actual owned-file observations and independent expected results. A missing file, a changed byte and an unsupported release are different failure cases. Correct policies must also admit unchanged packages and approved updates.</p><p>Run <code>npm run start:verified</code> in the reference project to see the real launcher check its inventory before starting HTTP. For the failure experiment, use the exercise instructions' disposable package copy; keep the approved reference unchanged. Editing your own package here is an explicit test fixture, never an instruction to modify someone else's game.</p><aside class="callout"><strong>Additional transfer; keep the worksheet response too.</strong>A valid manifest approves a new image asset but the running process loaded an old copy earlier. What did a disk hash establish? What additional observation would you need to make a claim about the running process? Preserve your original answer and append any repair after feedback.</aside></section>
<section id="replay"><p class="eyebrow">06 / REPRODUCE A DECISION</p><h2>A final score leaves out the route.</h2><p>A <strong>causal event</strong> is an operation needed to reproduce later state: joining, admitting an input, or taking a simulation tick. A <strong>checkpoint</strong> records the state just before a retained event window. It includes pending intent, expiry, cooldown and detector history as well as visible position and score. Omitting pending interaction can change the next tick even when two screenshots look identical.</p><p>The recorder keeps a bounded window. Before it runs out of room, it saves a new checkpoint and begins a new complete window. Absolute event indices make missing, duplicated or reordered entries visible. <strong>Replay</strong> restores the checkpoint, applies each event in order and compares the resulting state with the recorded final state.</p>
<figure class="window-diagram"><figcaption>Saved rollover example · indices, not elapsed-time spacing</figcaption><ol><li><b>Boundary 128</b><span>Checkpoint is the state before event 129.</span></li><li><b>Events 129…221</b><span>Every index appears once, in order.</span></li><li><b>Apply the window</b><span>Restore private intent and detector history too.</span></li><li><b>Compare final</b><span>A matching result proves internal consistency.</span></li></ol><p>A gap such as 129, 131 refuses with <code>sequence</code>. An unknown runtime refuses with <code>incompatible</code>. A different final state refuses with <code>final</code>.</p></figure><div class="worked-lab replay-lab"><div><p class="eyebrow">RECORDED OWNED GAME / WORKED DEMONSTRATION</p><label for="trace-case">Inspect this record</label><select id="trace-case"><option value="complete">Complete recorded window</option><option value="rolled">Complete window after rollover</option><option value="missing">One event removed</option><option value="duplicate">An index duplicated</option><option value="version">Unknown runtime release</option><option value="final">Recorded final score changed</option></select><button id="replay-trace" class="primary">Show recorded replay result</button><div id="trace-result" hidden><p id="trace-verdict" role="status" aria-live="polite"></p><button id="back-trace" class="secondary" disabled>Previous recorded event</button><button id="step-trace" class="secondary" disabled>Apply next recorded event</button><p id="trace-step" role="status" aria-live="polite"></p></div></div><div><svg hidden id="replay-arena" viewBox="0 0 8000 4000" role="img" aria-label="Replay position in the arena"><rect width="8000" height="4000" fill="#e4eddf"/><rect x="4000" width="250" height="2500" fill="#bd6650"/><circle id="replay-actor" cx="1000" cy="1000" r="145" fill="#334dbe" stroke="white" stroke-width="55"/></svg><pre role="region" id="trace-observation" tabindex="0" aria-label="Record window metadata"></pre></div></div>
<p>These saved inputs, verdicts and playback frames came from the owned Node game and its replay checker. This browser displays recorded results; the CLI commands below recompute them. Browser playback is an inspectable teaching aid and does not authenticate the record's author. A consistent record can still be fabricated by someone who controls its checkpoint, events and final state. A refused record establishes insufficient or inconsistent evidence, not a player's intent.</p></section>
<section id="replay-lab"><p class="eyebrow">06 / CONSTRUCT AND TEST</p><h2>Refuse a story you cannot reproduce.</h2><pre class="command">npm run core:prepare -- telemetry</pre><p>In the printed workspace, read <code>telemetry/LEARNER.md</code> and implement <code>telemetry/policy.mjs</code>. The supplied engine facade validates checkpoint shape and applies operations. Your policy checks release compatibility, completeness and contiguous event indices, then orchestrates replay and compares the final state. The source exercise's tests include complete rollover windows; rejecting every nonzero starting index is wrong.</p><pre class="command">npm run core:check -- --assistance "none"</pre><p>For an actual server capture, run <code>npm run trace:sample -- artifacts/session-window.json</code> from the reference project. Then run <code>npm run window:replay -- artifacts/session-window.json</code>. The capture script owns a private test clock while its game inputs cross HTTP. No gameplay endpoint lets a client advance time or export other sessions.</p><aside class="callout"><strong>Transfer to a different decision.</strong>A repair station charges one resource on success. The position and balance at the checkpoint match, but its pending request was omitted. Design a test that exposes a changed completion or resource balance after replay. State which data is causal and which personal data you would leave out.</aside><p>Keep all first submissions, feedback and repairs. The checker grades executable behavior; the written transfer needs review. Later modules use these records to measure a detector and decide what evidence to retain.</p></section>
<section class="sources"><h2>Reading and limits</h2><p>For the concrete APIs, see the official <a href="https://nodejs.org/api/crypto.html#cryptocreatehashalgorithm-options">Node hash documentation</a> and <a href="https://nodejs.org/api/fs.html#fspromisesreadfilepath-options">file-reading documentation</a>. The manifest, event format and exercises are original teaching designs. The process/IPC context continues the reading pointers from the earlier lesson.</p><a class="next-lesson" href="/course">Return to the complete course map →</a></section></main><footer>Owned bytes, reproducible decisions, explicit limits.</footer><script type="module" src="/evidence.js"></script></body></html>

`courses/anti-cheat-engineering/courier-lab/public/evidence.js`:

```js
import { predictionNotebook } from './prediction-notebook.js';
const $ = id => document.getElementById(id);
let examples;
let frames = [];
let cursor = 0;
function comparePackage() {
  const example = examples.packages[$('package-case').value];
  const { result } = example;
  $('package-verdict').className = result.ok ? 'pass' : 'refuse';
  $('package-verdict').textContent = result.ok ? 'RECORDED MATCH · these observations met this approved reference.' : `RECORDED REFUSAL · ${result.reason}. The launcher must not start.`;
  const approved = new Map(example.manifest.files.map(file => [file.path, file.sha256.toLowerCase()]));
  const seen = new Map(example.observed.map(file => [file.path, file.sha256.toLowerCase()]));
  const changed = [...new Set([...approved.keys(), ...seen.keys()])].filter(path => approved.get(path) !== seen.get(path));
  $('package-detail').textContent = changed.length ? `Changed or missing in this recorded comparison: ${changed.join(', ')}.` : 'Every observed path and digest matches this reference.';
  $('package-feedback').hidden = false;
}
function loadRecord() {
  const example = examples.traces[$('trace-case').value];
  const { result } = example;
  frames = example.frames ?? [];
  cursor = 0;
  $('trace-verdict').className = result.ok ? 'pass' : 'refuse';
  $('trace-verdict').textContent = result.ok ? 'RECORDED REPLAY · the final state matched. This does not authenticate its author.' : `RECORDED REFUSAL · ${result.reason}. Keep the evidence; do not infer cheating.`;
  $('back-trace').disabled = true;
  $('step-trace').disabled = !result.ok || frames.length < 2;
  $('trace-result').hidden = false;
  $('replay-arena').toggleAttribute('hidden', !result.ok);
  if (!result.ok) $('trace-step').textContent = 'No replay state is shown for this refused record.';
  if (result.ok) $('trace-step').textContent = '';
  if (result.ok && frames.length) renderState();
}
function renderState() {
  const state = frames[cursor];
  $('back-trace').disabled = cursor === 0;
  $('step-trace').disabled = cursor >= frames.length - 1;
  const actor = state.actors[0]?.actor;
  if (actor) { $('replay-actor').setAttribute('cx', actor.x); $('replay-actor').setAttribute('cy', actor.y); }
  $('trace-step').textContent = `Recorded event ${cursor} / ${frames.length - 1} · tick ${state.tick}${actor ? ` · x ${actor.x} · cargo ${actor.cargo ? 'yes' : 'no'} · score ${actor.score}` : ''}`;
}
function stepRecord() {
  if (cursor >= frames.length - 1) return;
  cursor += 1;
  renderState();
  $('step-trace').disabled = cursor >= frames.length - 1;
}
function previousRecord() {
  if (cursor === 0) return;
  cursor -= 1;
  renderState();
}
async function start() {
  const response = await fetch('/samples/evidence-cases.json');
  if (!response.ok) throw new Error('Recorded examples could not be loaded.');
  examples = await response.json();
  const packages = predictionNotebook({ button: $('compare-package'), reveal: comparePackage, hide: () => { $('package-feedback').hidden = true; $('package-verdict').textContent = ''; $('package-detail').textContent = ''; } });
  const traces = predictionNotebook({ button: $('replay-trace'), reveal: loadRecord, hide: () => { $('trace-result').hidden = true; $('replay-arena').setAttribute('hidden', ''); $('trace-verdict').textContent = ''; $('trace-step').textContent = ''; $('step-trace').disabled = true; $('back-trace').disabled = true; } });
  function selectPackage() {
    const id = $('package-case').value;
    const { manifest, observed, supported, clientClaim } = examples.packages[id];
    const inputs = { manifest, observed, supported, clientClaim };
    $('package-observation').textContent = JSON.stringify(inputs, null, 2);
    packages.setCase({ id: `integrity/${id}`, version: 1, question: 'Will this package match the approved reference and supported release list? Name the first refusal reason if any, and explain what a match would establish about the observer.', inputs });
  }
  function selectTrace() {
    const id = $('trace-case').value;
    const { record } = examples.traces[id];
    $('trace-observation').textContent = JSON.stringify(record, null, 2);
    traces.setCase({ id: `replay/${id}`, version: 1, question: 'Will replay accept this record or refuse it? Identify the condition to check first and explain whether a consistent replay authenticates its author.', inputs: record });
  }
  $('package-case').addEventListener('change', selectPackage);
  $('trace-case').addEventListener('change', selectTrace);
  $('step-trace').addEventListener('click', stepRecord);
  $('back-trace').addEventListener('click', previousRecord);
  selectPackage();
  selectTrace();
}
start().catch(error => { for (const id of ['package-verdict', 'trace-verdict']) $(id).textContent = error.message; });

```
