`courses/anti-cheat-engineering/courier-lab/public/learn.js`:

```js
const STORAGE = 'ivy-anti-cheat-learning-v1';
const $ = (selector) => document.querySelector(selector);
let units = [];
let record;
let busy = false;
let referenceReturnId;
const drafts = new Map();

function element(tag, text, className) {
  const node = document.createElement(tag);
  if (text !== undefined) node.textContent = text;
  if (className) node.className = className;
  return node;
}
function button(text, action, secondary = false) {
  const node = element('button', text, secondary ? 'secondary' : '');
  node.type = 'button'; node.addEventListener('click', () => run(action)); return node;
}
function status(message = '', error = false) {
  $('#global-status').textContent = message;
  $('#global-status').className = error ? 'status-error' : '';
  $('#global-status').setAttribute('role', error ? 'alert' : 'status');
}
async function api(route, body) {
  const options = body === undefined ? {} : { method: 'POST', headers: { 'content-type': 'application/json' }, body: JSON.stringify(body) };
  const response = await fetch(`/learning/${route}`, { ...options, signal: AbortSignal.timeout(15_000) });
  const data = await response.json();
  if (!response.ok) throw new Error(data.message ?? data.error ?? 'The local server could not save this action.');
  return data;
}
function session(body = {}) { return { sessionId: record.sessionId, ...body }; }
async function refresh() { record = await api('state', session()); $('#session-id').value = record.sessionId; }
async function enterSection() {
  const { unit, key } = selected();
  if (key !== 'mastery') await api('visit', session({ unitId: unit.id, key }));
}
async function run(action) {
  if (busy) return;
  busy = true;
  document.querySelectorAll('button').forEach((node) => { node.disabled = true; });
  status('Saving…');
  try { await action(); status(); } catch (error) { status(error.message, true); }
  finally { busy = false; document.querySelectorAll('button').forEach((node) => { node.disabled = false; }); }
}
function selected() {
  const [unitId, key] = location.hash.slice(1).split('/');
  const unit = units.find((entry) => entry.id === unitId) ?? units[0];
  return { unit, key: key === 'mastery' || unit.sections.some((section) => section.id === key) ? key : unit.sections[0].id };
}
function paragraph(parent, text, className) { parent.append(element('p', text, className)); }
function list(parent, values, tag = 'ul', className) {
  const node = element(tag, undefined, className);
  values.forEach((value) => node.append(element('li', value)));
  parent.append(node);
}
function link(text, href, current) {
  const node = element('a', text); node.href = href;
  if (current) node.setAttribute('aria-current', 'page');
  return node;
}
function card(parent, eyebrow, title) {
  const node = element('section', undefined, 'card');
  paragraph(node, eyebrow, 'eyebrow'); node.append(element('h3', title)); parent.append(node); return node;
}
function latest(unitId, mode, key) { return record.items.filter((item) => item.unitId === unitId && item.mode === mode && item.key === key).at(-1); }
async function issue(unit, section, mode) {
  await api('item', session({ unitId: unit.id, key: section.id, mode })); await refresh(); render();
}
async function reference(unit, section) {
  referenceReturnId = document.activeElement?.id;
  const result = await api('reference', session({ unitId: unit.id, ...(section ? { key: section.id } : {}) }));
  $('#reference-title').textContent = result.path;
  $('#reference-content').textContent = result.content;
  await refresh(); render(); $('#reference').showModal();
}
function render() {
  const { unit, key } = selected();
  const nav = $('#units'); nav.replaceChildren();
  units.forEach((entry, index) => {
    const item = link('', `#${entry.id}/${entry.sections[0].id}`, entry.id === unit.id);
    item.append(element('span', String(index + 1).padStart(2, '0'), 'unit-number'), element('span', entry.title));
    const progress = record.units.find((value) => value.id === entry.id);
    if (progress?.status === 'mastered') item.append(element('span', 'Mastered', 'unit-state'));
    nav.append(item);
  });
  const root = $('#content'); root.replaceChildren();
  const head = element('header', undefined, 'unit-head');
  paragraph(head, `UNIT ${units.indexOf(unit) + 1} OF ${units.length}`, 'eyebrow'); head.append(element('h2', unit.title));
  if (unit.intro) paragraph(head, unit.intro);
  if (unit.prerequisites.length) paragraph(head, `Builds on: ${unit.prerequisites.map((id) => units.find((entry) => entry.id === id)?.title ?? id).join('; ')}.`, 'small');
  list(head, unit.objectives.map((objective) => objective.text), 'ul', 'objective-list');
  const ref = button('Open implementation reference', () => reference(unit), true); ref.className = 'ref-link'; ref.id = `reference-${unit.id}`; head.append(ref); root.append(head);
  const tabs = element('nav', undefined, 'sections'); tabs.setAttribute('aria-label', 'Unit sections');
  unit.sections.forEach((section, index) => tabs.append(link(`${index + 1}. ${section.title}`, `#${unit.id}/${section.id}`, key === section.id)));
  tabs.append(link('Mastery check', `#${unit.id}/mastery`, key === 'mastery')); root.append(tabs);
  if (key === 'mastery') return renderMastery(root, unit);
  const section = unit.sections.find((entry) => entry.id === key);
  const teaching = element('section', undefined, 'teaching'); teaching.append(element('h3', section.title));
  section.paragraphs.forEach((text, index) => { const p = element('p', text); p.id = `${unit.id}-${section.id}-paragraph-${index + 1}`; teaching.append(p); }); root.append(teaching);
  renderWorked(root, unit, section);
  const completion = latest(unit.id, 'completion', section.id);
  const practice = latest(unit.id, 'practice', section.id);
  const step = card(root, '02 · FINISH A PARTLY SOLVED CASE', 'Complete the missing decision');
  if (!completion) {
    paragraph(step, section.completion.prompt); list(step, section.completion.steps, 'ol', 'step-list');
    paragraph(step, section.completion.missing, 'small');
  }
  if (completion) renderItem(step, completion, unit, section);
  if (!completion) step.append(button('Start completion item', () => issue(unit, section, 'completion')));
  const independent = card(root, '03 · MAKE YOUR OWN DECISION', 'Practice on a fresh case');
  if (practice) renderItem(independent, practice, unit, section);
  if (!practice && completion?.attempts.some((attempt) => attempt.status === 'scored')) independent.append(button('Start independent practice', () => issue(unit, section, 'practice')));
  if (!practice && !completion?.attempts.some((attempt) => attempt.status === 'scored')) paragraph(independent, 'Complete and commit the partly solved case above first. You can visit any other section or the mastery check at any time.', 'muted');
  const next = unit.sections[unit.sections.indexOf(section) + 1];
  root.append(link(next ? `Continue: ${next.title} →` : 'Continue to the mastery check →', `#${unit.id}/${next?.id ?? 'mastery'}`));
}
function renderWorked(root, unit, section) {
  const box = card(root, '01 · WORKED SIBLING CASE', 'Follow a complete example'); box.classList.add('worked');
  paragraph(box, section.worked.prompt);
  const exposure = record.exposures.filter((entry) => entry.unitId === unit.id && entry.key === section.id).at(-1);
  if (exposure) {
    paragraph(box, `Your prediction: ${exposure.prediction || `Skipped: ${exposure.skipReason}`}`, 'small');
    list(box, exposure.worked.steps, 'ol', 'step-list'); paragraph(box, `Worked answer: ${display(exposure.worked.answer)}`); return;
  }
  paragraph(box, 'Predict an answer or the first decision before revealing this sibling example. This is saved, not scored.', 'small');
  const prediction = input(box, 'Your prediction', `prediction-${unit.id}-${section.id}`, 'textarea');
  const skip = input(box, 'Or give a reason to skip the prediction', `skip-${unit.id}-${section.id}`, 'input');
  box.append(button('Save prediction and reveal example', async () => {
    await api('worked', session({ unitId: unit.id, key: section.id, prediction: prediction.value, skipReason: skip.value })); await refresh(); render();
  }));
}
function input(parent, label, id, tag = 'textarea') {
  const caption = element('label', label); caption.htmlFor = id;
  const control = element(tag); control.id = id; control.value = drafts.get(id) ?? '';
  control.addEventListener('input', () => drafts.set(id, control.value)); parent.append(caption, control); return control;
}
function display(value) { return typeof value === 'string' ? value : JSON.stringify(value, null, 2); }
function renderItem(parent, item, unit, section) {
  const group = element('div'); group.dataset.itemId = item.id;
  paragraph(group, item.prompt);
  if (item.inputs && Object.keys(item.inputs).length) group.append(element('pre', JSON.stringify(item.inputs, null, 2)));
  let answer;
  const id = `answer-${item.id}`;
  if (item.format.type === 'choice') {
    const label = element('label', 'Your answer'); label.htmlFor = id;
    answer = element('select'); answer.id = id; answer.append(new Option('Choose an answer', ''));
    item.format.options.forEach((option) => answer.append(new Option(option.label, option.value)));
    answer.value = drafts.get(id) ?? item.attempts.at(-1)?.rawAnswer ?? '';
    answer.addEventListener('change', () => drafts.set(id, answer.value)); group.append(label, answer);
  }
  if (item.format.type !== 'choice') {
    answer = input(group, item.format.type === 'json' ? 'Your answer as JSON' : 'Your numeric answer', id, item.format.type === 'json' ? 'textarea' : 'input');
    answer.value = drafts.get(id) ?? item.attempts.at(-1)?.rawAnswer ?? '';
    if (item.format.type === 'number') answer.inputMode = 'decimal';
    if (item.format.type === 'json') answer.className = 'json';
  }
  const assistance = element('select'); assistance.id = `assistance-${item.id}`;
  assistance.append(new Option('No help beyond this guided teaching', 'none'), new Option('I used other help or saw an answer', 'help'));
  assistance.value = drafts.get(assistance.id) ?? 'none';
  assistance.addEventListener('change', () => drafts.set(assistance.id, assistance.value));
  const caption = element('label', 'Assistance used for this response'); caption.htmlFor = assistance.id;
  group.append(caption, assistance);
  const actions = element('div', undefined, 'actions');
  actions.append(button(item.attempts.length ? 'Save a revision' : 'Commit answer and check', async () => {
    await api('submit', session({ itemId: item.id, answer: answer.value, assistance: assistance.value === 'none' ? [] : ['Learner declared other help or answer exposure'] })); await refresh(); render();
    document.querySelector(`[data-item-id="${item.id}"] .feedback`)?.scrollIntoView({ block: 'nearest' });
  }));
  if (item.mode !== 'mastery') actions.append(button(`Request hint ${Math.min(item.hints.length + 1, 3)}${item.hints.length === 2 ? ' (worked solution)' : ''}`, async () => {
    await api('hint', session({ itemId: item.id })); await refresh(); render();
  }, true));
  group.append(actions);
  item.hints.forEach((hint) => paragraph(group, `Hint ${hint.level}: ${hint.text}`, 'hint'));
  const attempt = item.attempts.at(-1);
  if (attempt) renderFeedback(group, item, attempt, unit, section);
  if (attempt?.status === 'scored' && item.mode !== 'mastery') group.append(button('Try a fresh case on this concept', () => issue(unit, section, item.mode), true));
  parent.append(group);
}
function renderFeedback(group, item, attempt, unit, section) {
  const box = element('div', undefined, `feedback ${attempt.status === 'format-error' ? 'error' : attempt.correct ? '' : 'wrong'}`); box.setAttribute('role', 'status');
  if (attempt.status === 'format-error') {
    box.append(element('strong', 'Saved format error · not scored')); paragraph(box, attempt.message); paragraph(box, `Saved original: ${attempt.rawAnswer}`); group.append(box); return;
  }
  box.append(element('strong', attempt.correct ? 'Correct for this case' : 'This decision needs repair'));
  paragraph(box, `Your committed answer: ${attempt.rawAnswer}`);
  paragraph(box, `Expected: ${display(attempt.feedback.expected)}`);
  paragraph(box, attempt.feedback.explanation);
  paragraph(box, `${attempt.firstScored ? 'First scored response' : 'Revision; the first scored response is preserved'} · ${attempt.assisted ? 'assisted or already exposed' : 'no assistance recorded'}`, 'small');
  if (!attempt.correct) {
    paragraph(box, 'Use the explanation above and the teaching paragraph for this concept, then try a fresh case.', 'small');
    if (section) box.append(link(`Return to “${section.title}”`, `#${unit.id}/${section.id}`));
    const referenceButton = button('Open the linked implementation reference', () => reference(unit, section), true);
    referenceButton.id = `reference-${item.id}`;
    box.append(referenceButton);
  }
  group.append(box);
  const history = element('details', undefined, 'history'); history.append(element('summary', `${item.attempts.length} saved response${item.attempts.length === 1 ? '' : 's'} · original wording and input retained`));
  paragraph(history, item.prompt); history.append(element('pre', JSON.stringify(item.inputs ?? {}, null, 2)));
  item.attempts.forEach((entry) => paragraph(history, `#${entry.revision} ${entry.at} · ${entry.status} · ${entry.rawAnswer}`)); group.append(history);
}
function renderMastery(root, unit) {
  const progress = record.units.find((entry) => entry.id === unit.id);
  const box = element('section', undefined, 'status-box'); box.append(element('h3', 'Three decisions. One high criterion.'));
  paragraph(box, 'All three generated cases must be correct on the first scored response, with no recorded assistance. Format errors are saved but not scored. Revisions help you repair; they cannot replace an initial answer.');
  paragraph(box, 'No hints are available in this check. Returning to teaching or opening a reference while a question is pending marks that response assisted. You can always take a new set.', 'small');
  paragraph(box, `Current status: ${progress.status.replaceAll('-', ' ')}`);
  list(box, progress.objectives.map((objective) => `${objective.status.replaceAll('-', ' ')} — ${objective.text}`)); root.append(box);
  const sets = record.masterySets.filter((set) => set.unitId === unit.id);
  const current = sets.at(-1);
  root.append(button(current ? 'Start a fresh three-item set' : 'Start the three-item check', async () => {
    await api('mastery', session({ unitId: unit.id })); await refresh(); render();
  }));
  if (current) current.itemIds.forEach((id, index) => {
    const item = record.items.find((entry) => entry.id === id);
    const panel = card(root, `GENERATED CASE ${index + 1} OF 3`, item.key);
    renderItem(panel, item, unit);
  });
  if (sets.length > 1) {
    const history = element('details', undefined, 'history'); history.append(element('summary', `${sets.length - 1} earlier sets retained`));
    sets.slice(0, -1).forEach((set) => paragraph(history, `${set.id}: ${set.status} · ${set.generatedAt}`)); root.append(history);
  }
}
async function start() {
  try {
    localStorage.setItem(`${STORAGE}-probe`, '1'); localStorage.removeItem(`${STORAGE}-probe`);
    const catalog = await api('catalog'); units = catalog.units; $('#boundary').textContent = catalog.boundary;
    const saved = localStorage.getItem(STORAGE);
    record = saved ? await api('state', { sessionId: saved }) : await api('session', {});
    localStorage.setItem(STORAGE, record.sessionId); $('#session-id').value = record.sessionId;
    await enterSection(); render(); status();
  } catch (error) { status(`Could not start learning: ${error.message} Your existing session ID and records have not been replaced.`, true); }
}
window.addEventListener('hashchange', () => { if (!record) return; run(async () => { await enterSection(); render(); $('#lesson').focus(); }); });
$('#close-reference').addEventListener('click', () => $('#reference').close());
$('#reference').addEventListener('close', () => {
  const trigger = document.getElementById(referenceReturnId) ?? document.querySelector('.ref-link');
  trigger?.focus();
});
$('#export').addEventListener('click', () => run(async () => {
  if (!record) throw new Error('Restore a saved session before exporting.');
  const data = await api('export', session());
  const url = URL.createObjectURL(new Blob([JSON.stringify(data, null, 2) + '\n'], { type: 'application/json' }));
  const anchor = link('', url); anchor.download = `courier-learning-${record.sessionId.slice(0, 8)}.json`; anchor.click(); setTimeout(() => URL.revokeObjectURL(url), 1000);
}));
$('#restore').addEventListener('click', () => run(async () => {
  const restored = await api('state', { sessionId: $('#session-id').value.trim() });
  localStorage.setItem(STORAGE, restored.sessionId); record = restored; await enterSection(); render();
}));
$('#new-session').addEventListener('click', () => run(async () => {
  const created = await api('session', {}); localStorage.setItem(STORAGE, created.sessionId); record = created; $('#session-id').value = record.sessionId; await enterSection(); render();
}));
await start();

`courses/anti-cheat-engineering/courier-lab/public/order.html`:

```html
<!doctype html><html lang="en"><head><meta charset="utf-8"><meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width,initial-scale=1"><title>Input order · Courier Lab</title><link rel="stylesheet" href="/style.css"><link rel="stylesheet" href="/order.css"></head><body>
<header class="site-header"><a class="brand" href="/"><span class="brand-mark" aria-hidden="true">C</span> COURIER LAB</a><span class="edition">SERVER SYSTEMS / 02–04</span></header>
<main class="lesson"><section class="intro"><p class="eyebrow">Build a rule. Write a test that can catch it.</p><h1>Old input.<br>New consequences.</h1><p class="lede">Implement an admission policy and write an HTTP test that detects a broken one. Keep legal retries working. Your code runs in a real local server; your test sends the same requests as the browser.</p><p class="model-note">Owned teaching project · protocol robustness and false-positive control · workstation required to edit and execute; phone reading supported</p></section>
<nav class="lesson-nav" aria-label="Lesson sections"><a href="/course">Course map</a><a href="#boundary">1 Boundary</a><a href="#trace">2 Trace</a><a href="#build">3 Build</a><a href="#prove">4 Prove</a><a href="#explain">5 Explain</a></nav>
<section id="boundary"><p class="eyebrow">01 / WHAT CROSSES THE BOUNDARY?</p><h2>A request proposes an intention.</h2><p>A <strong>process</strong> is a running program with its own state. The browser and Node server run separately. Changing a browser variable does not directly change the server's cargo. A request is a message crossing that boundary. The server decides which message affects its state.</p><div class="boundary-flow" role="group" aria-label="Client sends intention over HTTP to parsing, admission, then simulation tick and authoritative state"><div><b>Client</b><small>direction + interaction</small></div><span aria-hidden="true">→</span><div><b>HTTP</b><small>parse four fields</small></div><span aria-hidden="true">→</span><div><b>Admission</b><small>newer sequence?</small></div><span aria-hidden="true">→</span><div><b>Tick</b><small>move, then interact</small></div><span aria-hidden="true">→</span><div><b>State</b><small>server position + cargo</small></div></div><p>A <strong>sequence number</strong> orders this session's inputs; it is not a timestamp. The server accepts a number greater than the last admitted number. A repeated or older number is <strong>stale</strong>: it must change nothing. Numbers may have gaps.</p><p>A <strong>tick</strong> is one 50 ms simulation step. An intention admitted at tick T stays active through T+4. At T+5 it expires. A fresh intention replaces the direction and renews that lifetime. Sending more requests cannot buy extra steps within one tick.</p></section>
<section id="trace"><p class="eyebrow">02 / WORKED TRACE</p><h2>Acceptance and application are different decisions.</h2><p>This example begins at (1000,1000). East adds 250 mm to x per active tick. It is a worked example, not a scored prediction.</p><div class="table-scroll"><table><thead><tr><th>Tick</th><th>Request / step</th><th>Consequence</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>T0</td><td>seq 10, east; no interaction</td><td>Admitted. Expiry is T4.</td></tr><tr><td>T1–T2</td><td>Two server ticks</td><td>x=1500, y=1000.</td></tr><tr><td>T2</td><td>seq 9, west; interaction</td><td>Stale. Direction, expiry and pending interaction stay unchanged.</td></tr><tr><td>T3–T4</td><td>Two more ticks</td><td>x=2000. No interaction was staged.</td></tr><tr><td>T5</td><td>No fresh input</td><td>x stays 2000. No catch-up movement.</td></tr></tbody></table></div><p>Now imagine the client lost the response to seq10 and sent it again. The retry is stale, but that says nothing about the player's intent. Counting every retry as cheating would punish a normal recovery path.</p><aside class="callout"><strong>The supported envelope is explicit.</strong> Movement can remain continuous while the gap between fresh admissions is at most four ticks. A longer gap stops movement. The tests deliberately include both outcomes. Their seeded delivery order is an application-level model; it is not a reproduction of every physical network condition.</aside></section>
<section id="build"><p class="eyebrow">03 / YOUR TWO ARTIFACTS</p><h2>Implement the policy. Author the scenario.</h2><p>From the reference project directory:</p><pre class="command">npm run order:prepare</pre><p>Change into the printed <code>artifacts/order-workspace</code> directory. Read <code>lab/order/LEARNER.md</code>. Record your predictions in <code>response.md</code> before editing. The prepared copy contains an incomplete policy and scenario; the author solution and judging fixtures stay outside it.</p><ol><li><strong>admission.mjs</strong> exports <code>admitInput(state,input,tick)</code> and <code>movementActive(state,tick)</code>. Implement strictly newer admission, unchanged stale state, T+4 expiry, latest direction and coalesced interaction. Leave the engine's movement, score, parser and clock alone.</li><li><strong>learner-scenario.mjs</strong> exports <code>async scenario({base,advance})</code>. Use supplied HTTP helpers and ordinary assertions. Send a newer direction, then an older conflicting input, advance the owner test clock, and inspect authoritative state. Also test expiry, same-tick renewal, duplicate retry and state polling. At least one test must catch a wrong state even if the response text looks plausible.</li></ol><p>The bounded <code>advance</code> function belongs to your owner-side test harness. A gameplay client receives no such capability. The server has no HTTP time-control route.</p><pre class="command">npm run order:check -- --assistance "none"</pre><p>Use an accurate help declaration, such as “read the worked reference” or “used an AI hint.” The command records the submitted files, response, prompt version, seeds, help, runtime identities and actual results. Each revision gets a new attempt; earlier attempts stay intact.</p></section>
<section id="practice"><p class="eyebrow">BEFORE THE INDEPENDENT SCENARIO</p><h2>Turn a returned value into an assertion.</h2><p>An assertion compares an observed value with a contract. The prepared guide includes a complete M1 remote-pickup example, then a missing-assertion exercise. It introduces <code>async</code>, <code>await</code> and the arrange → act → observe → assert sequence. Complete that practice before writing ordering tests. Waiting for HTTP does not advance the owner clock, and HTTP 200 does not prove a gameplay effect succeeded.</p></section>
<section id="prove"><p class="eyebrow">04 / A PASS MUST DISCRIMINATE</p><h2>“It ran” is a weak test.</h2><p>The checker evaluates your two artifacts independently. Trusted fixtures test your policy. Your scenario runs against two correct implementations and deliberately wrong implementations. An empty scenario misses defects. A scenario that always throws rejects correct code. Neither passes.</p><div class="assessment-grid"><article><h3>Your policy</h3><p>Must preserve legal state under the declared schedules, including ordinary retries and button re-presses.</p></article><article><h3>Your scenario</h3><p>Must accept both correct implementations and catch the specified wrong states. A crash or timeout is a broken run, not a detected guard defect.</p></article></div><p>Expect separate results for duplicate admission, stale interaction, early/late expiry, reads renewing intent and retries being counted as findings. Inspect the first failed criterion and its observed/expected state, then repair the relevant artifact. Keep the raw output for investigation.</p><p>A local workspace is under its owner's control. This checker helps you preserve and examine your work; it is not a tamper-proof credential or a sandbox for hostile code.</p></section>
<section id="explain"><p class="eyebrow">05 / TRANSFER THE REASONING</p><h2>Explain what the evidence leaves open.</h2><p>Complete <code>response.md</code> with the original predictions and later repairs. Explain why a stale input must not stage an interaction, why a state read must not renew movement, and why a human re-press can be a false positive for a naive detector.</p><p>Then consider an owned replay scrubber receiving <code>{seq, frame}</code> seek commands. Transfer newer-command admission and read-only observation to it, and explain why a four-tick movement lifetime does not automatically apply. Give one stale-command test and one read-only polling test. This written transfer needs review; the checker does not mark your prose correct.</p><p>In this instanced courier game, sequence and expiry enforce control semantics. They do not yet prevent a timed score advantage. Server-owned pickup and score still prevent unearned state. Keep those claims separate.</p></section>
<section class="sources"><h2>Reading pointers</h2><p>The lesson and exercises are original. For systems context, see Stewart N. Weiss, <em>System Programming in Linux</em>: Chapter 1 “Processes,” Chapter 12 “Why Do We Need IPC?” and Chapter 14 “Introduction to Client-Server Applications.” The Linux examples are context, not setup instructions for this Node lab.</p><p>For the actual runtime APIs, use the official <a href="https://nodejs.org/api/child_process.html">Node child-process</a> and <a href="https://nodejs.org/api/http.html">HTTP</a> documentation. A Node child-process fork is not the Unix C fork interface. No kernel installation or OS-security change is required.</p><a class="next-lesson" href="/">Return to the live Courier Lab →</a></section>

`courses/anti-cheat-engineering/courier-lab/public/prediction-notebook.js`:

```js
// Local teaching evidence, not an authenticated assessment record.
const PREFIX = 'courier-predictions-v1:';
const clone = value => JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(value));

export function createPredictionStore(storage, makeId = () => crypto.randomUUID(), now = () => new Date().toISOString()) {
  function read() {
    const events = [];
    for (let index = 0; index < storage.length; index += 1) {
      const key = storage.key(index);
      if (!key?.startsWith(PREFIX)) continue;
      const event = JSON.parse(storage.getItem(key));
      if (event?.schema !== 1 || typeof event.id !== 'string' || !Number.isSafeInteger(event.sequence) || !['answer', 'reveal'].includes(event.kind) || !event.case?.id || !event.case?.version || typeof event.case.question !== 'string') {
        throw new Error('An existing notebook entry cannot be read. It has been left unchanged.');
      }
      events.push(event);
    }
    return events.sort((a, b) => a.sequence - b.sequence || a.at.localeCompare(b.at) || a.id.localeCompare(b.id));
  }
  function forCase(subject) {
    return read().filter(event => event.case.id === subject.id && event.case.version === subject.version);
  }
  function append(subject, detail) {
    const prior = read();
    const related = prior.filter(event => event.case.id === subject.id && event.case.version === subject.version);
    const id = makeId();
    const event = { schema: 1, id, sequence: Math.max(0, ...prior.map(item => item.sequence)) + 1, at: now(), case: clone(subject), ...detail };
    if (detail.kind === 'answer') event.priorExposure = related.some(item => item.kind === 'reveal');
    const key = PREFIX + id;
    if (storage.getItem(key) !== null) throw new Error('Notebook entry ID already exists. Please try again.');
    const serialized = JSON.stringify(event);
    storage.setItem(key, serialized);
    if (storage.getItem(key) !== serialized) throw new Error('The notebook save could not be verified.');
    return clone(event);
  }
  return { read, forCase, append };
}

function node(tag, className, text) {
  const element = document.createElement(tag);
  if (className) element.className = className;
  if (text) element.textContent = text;
  return element;
}

export function predictionNotebook({ button, reveal, hide }) {
  const root = node('div', 'prediction-notebook');
  const label = node('label', '', 'Your prediction and reason');
  const question = node('p', 'prediction-question');
  const input = node('textarea');
  input.id = button.id + '-answer';
  input.rows = 4;
  label.htmlFor = input.id;
  const status = node('p', 'prediction-status');
  status.setAttribute('role', 'status');
  status.setAttribute('aria-live', 'polite');
  const history = node('details', 'prediction-history');
  const historyTitle = node('summary', '', 'Saved answers and assistance');
  const entries = node('ol');
  history.append(historyTitle, entries);
  const worked = node('button', 'secondary', 'View as worked example');
  worked.type = 'button';
  worked.id = button.id + '-worked';
  const exportButton = node('button', 'secondary', 'Export notebook');
  exportButton.type = 'button';
  const note = node('p', 'prediction-note', 'Saved in this browser only. Keep an export with your source worksheet and declare any worked examples you viewed. This notebook does not grade understanding or authenticate attempts. Navigation stays open.');
  button.before(root);
  root.append(question, label, input, button, status, history, worked, exportButton, note);
  let subject;
  let store;
  const getStore = () => store ??= createPredictionStore(window.localStorage);
  const fail = error => {
    hide();
    status.textContent = `Not saved — results remain hidden. ${error.message} Keep a copy of your answer and try again when browser storage is available.`;
    status.classList.add('save-error');
  };
  function refresh() {
    const saved = getStore().forCase(subject);
    entries.replaceChildren();
    let answers = 0;
    for (const event of saved) {
      const item = node('li');
      if (event.kind === 'answer') {
        answers += 1;
        item.textContent = `${answers === 1 ? 'First answer' : `Revision ${answers - 1}`} · ${event.priorExposure ? 'after result exposure' : 'before result exposure'} · ${event.at}\n${event.answer}`;
      }
      if (event.kind === 'reveal') item.textContent = `Result viewed · ${event.mode === 'worked-example' ? 'worked-example assistance' : 'after saved answer'} · ${event.at}`;
      entries.append(item);
    }
    const exposed = saved.some(event => event.kind === 'reveal');
    status.classList.remove('save-error');
    status.textContent = `${answers ? `${answers} saved answer${answers === 1 ? '' : 's'}. The first is kept.` : 'No answer saved for this case.'} ${exposed ? 'This result has already been viewed; later answers are marked after exposure.' : 'Result has not been viewed in this notebook.'}`;
    button.textContent = answers ? 'Save revision and reveal' : 'Record and reveal';
    return saved;
  }
  function commit(mode) {
    hide();
    try {
      if (mode === 'prediction' && !input.value.trim()) {
        status.textContent = 'Write a prediction and reason before recording, or choose View as worked example.';
        input.focus();
        return;
      }
      if (mode === 'prediction') getStore().append(subject, { kind: 'answer', answer: input.value.trim() });
      getStore().append(subject, { kind: 'reveal', mode });
      refresh();
      reveal();
    } catch (error) { fail(error); }
  }
  button.addEventListener('click', () => commit('prediction'));
  worked.addEventListener('click', () => commit('worked-example'));
  exportButton.addEventListener('click', () => {
    try {
      const url = URL.createObjectURL(new Blob([JSON.stringify({ schema: 1, note: 'Local browser teaching evidence; not authenticated or graded.', events: getStore().read() }, null, 2)], { type: 'application/json' }));
      const link = node('a');
      link.href = url;
      link.download = 'courier-prediction-notebook.json';
      link.click();
      setTimeout(() => URL.revokeObjectURL(url), 1000);
    } catch (error) { fail(error); }
  });
  return {
    setCase(next) {
      subject = clone(next);
      hide();
      question.textContent = subject.question;
      input.value = '';
      try {
        const saved = refresh().filter(event => event.kind === 'answer');
        input.value = saved.at(-1)?.answer ?? '';
      } catch (error) { fail(error); }
    },
  };
}

<!doctype html><html lang="en"><head><meta charset="utf-8"><meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width,initial-scale=1"><title>Reading and source limits · Courier Lab</title><link rel="stylesheet" href="/style.css"><link rel="stylesheet" href="/order.css"></head><body><header class="site-header"><a class="brand" href="/course">COURIER LAB / COURSE MAP</a></header><main class="lesson"><section class="intro"><p class="eyebrow">Reading map / original course</p><h1>Read the source.<br>Keep its limits.</h1><p class="lede">The exercises and toy rules are original. These readings supply context; they do not certify the model or require a purchase.</p></section><section><h2>Primary technical accounts</h2><p><a href="https://gafferongames.com/post/what_every_programmer_needs_to_know_about_game_networking/">Glenn Fiedler: What Every Programmer Needs To Know About Game Networking</a> explains client/server state, prediction and correction. Use it to compare a client claim with server authority; its examples do not specify this course's tick or sequence contract.</p><p><a href="https://www.riotgames.com/en/news/demolishing-wallhacks-valorants-fog-war">Riot Games: Demolishing Wallhacks with VALORANT's Fog of War</a> is a historical first-party account of reducing unnecessary state and handling visibility, performance and repair. Study architecture and evidence limits, without reproducing third-party attack tools or assuming its measurements apply here.</p><p><a href="https://nodejs.org/api/perf_hooks.html#performancenow">Node's performance API</a> describes the clock used for the timing investigation and retention measurements. Its zero belongs to the current process; raw readings from different process lifetimes cannot establish elapsed time across a restart. <a href="https://nodejs.org/api/process.html#processmemoryusage">Node's memory reporting</a> distinguishes memory categories; serialized JSON bytes are a different measure.</p><p><a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/drivers/debugger/getting-started-with-windows-debugging">Microsoft's debugging overview</a> introduces user/kernel mode, symbols and host/target terminology for optional later native study. No driver installation or OS change belongs to this software core.</p></section><section><h2>Optional book context</h2><p>The local library registry verified these book identities from title/copyright metadata. Most remain bibliographic pointers. Two short sections of <em>System Programming in Linux</em> were additionally read: chapter 1 “Processes” and chapter 2 “System Calls.” They ground the distinction between stored program bytes, a running instance, and an OS interface; they do not validate this course’s Node runtime or provide its game rules. Full chapters were not reviewed.</p><ul><li>Bruce Dang, Alexandre Gazet and Elias Bachaalany, <em>Practical Reverse Engineering</em> (2014): architecture and owned-native analysis context.</li><li>Dennis Andriesse, <em>Practical Binary Analysis</em> (2019): reasoning from an owned binary and reproducible observations.</li><li>Sy Brand, <em>Building a Debugger</em> (2025): debugger mechanisms after introductory use.</li><li>Stewart N. Weiss, <em>System Programming in Linux</em>: process and system-interface context. Local copyright says 2026; EPUB metadata says 2025.</li><li>Michael Hale Ligh and colleagues, <em>The Art of Memory Forensics</em> (2014): evidence interpretation, with historical tool limits.</li></ul><p>Use existing lawful access if helpful. No book purchase, chapter redistribution or employer material is needed. Exact passage-level assignments require an additional source check.</p></section><section><h2>Original model assumptions</h2><p>The 50 ms tick, 250 mm pickup, 400 mm repair radius, expiry, receipt capacity, scripted labels, hashes and local rollback scenarios are explicit teaching choices. They are tested as contracts; they are not attributed to the readings. The earlier browser-only movement model is a separate teaching aid. The full source register and original review evidence remain in the repository under <code>docs/features/anti-cheat-engineering</code>.</p></section></main><footer>Original explanations and exercises; no copied chapters.</footer></body></html>

`courses/anti-cheat-engineering/courier-lab/recovery/LEARNER.md`:

```md
# M10: Recover code, configuration and state together

Implementation reference for **M10: recovery**. Start with [the guided learning route at `/learn`](/learn) on the reference server, then return here for the exact source contract. This Markdown file does not submit answers or certify mastery. Use the [support and attempt workflow](../learning-support/README.md) for worked siblings, gradual guidance and help recording. A prepared source workspace need not serve `/learn`; keep the reference server open for that route.

A courier can pick up a core at the legal 250 mm edge. A candidate release narrows its configuration to 100 mm and stores state in a new format. Select a complete recovery tuple and verify that the same legal pickup works again, while accounting for later actions the older snapshot loses.

This exercise builds on authoritative gameplay, configuration identities and causal checkpoints. It runs only the owned local game. From the reference project run `npm run core:prepare -- recovery`, fill the required answers or explicit skip reasons in `predictions.json`, edit `recovery/policy.mjs` and keep explanations in `response.md` in the printed workspace, then run `npm run core:check -- --assistance "none"`. Replace `none` with the help used. The checker preserves first and revised source, responses and feedback; consulting the author implementation counts as assistance.

## The contract

Export `selectRecovery(evidence)`. This pure function selects identities; the trial runner performs the actual restore. Inputs are already validated and deeply immutable. Use no files, clocks or network operations, and do not inspect or change the stored state body.

The input contains `targetReleaseId`, `releases`, `configurations` and `snapshots`. IDs are unique within each list. A release identifies its package, state decoder and required configuration. A configuration is versioned separately. A snapshot is a named saved state with a declared schema, configuration provenance and ordering number.

| Evidence | Fields used by selection |
| --- | --- |
| Release | `id`, `packageHash`, `stateSchema`, `configId`, `configHash` |
| Configuration | `id`, `hash`, `releaseId`, `stateSchema`, `maxInteractionDistanceMm` |
| Snapshot | `id`, `hash`, `ordinal`, `stateSchema`, `configId`, `configHash`, opaque `state` |

Hashes are opaque identity strings here. Copy them from the selected evidence; do not invent a plausible hash. `ordinal` is a nonnegative safe integer representing declared snapshot order, not a wall-clock time. Extra provenance fields may exist and do not change the selection rules.

Read the worked examples, then complete the different required cases in `predictions.json` before coding; use `response.md` for explanations. These are practice and explanation, not an unseen mastery test. Describe what the three selected artifacts do. Predict what happens if the package returns to the baseline but configuration and state remain from the candidate. Keep that prediction before reading the trial results.

## Declared target

Find the release whose `id` equals `targetReleaseId`. An absent target returns exactly `{ok:false,reason:'unknown-target'}`. Choosing a familiar baseline when the caller requested another release hides a failed recovery plan. A candidate can be a valid declared target when all its artifacts are compatible; the function does not decide which release an operator should want.

The order of refusal checks is target, configuration, then snapshot. If a target is absent and snapshots are empty, report the missing target first. This makes one defective request produce one reproducible explanation.

Practice: a caller requests release `r3`, while the evidence lists only `r1` and `r2`. Record your return value and explain why choosing `r1` would overstep the request. Use the checker feedback to correct the rule and append a second example of your own.

## Compatible tuples

A **recovery tuple** joins one package, one configuration and one saved state. Find the configuration named by `release.configId`. Require its hash to equal `release.configHash`, its `releaseId` to equal the release ID, and its schema to equal `release.stateSchema`. Return exactly `{ok:false,reason:'configuration-mismatch'}` if the configuration is missing or any of those checks fails.

Next filter snapshots. The snapshot schema must equal the release schema, and its configuration ID and hash must match the selected configuration. If no snapshot meets all three requirements, return exactly `{ok:false,reason:'no-compatible-snapshot'}`. A familiar filename or a recently created snapshot is not enough.

For example, release `r1` requires configuration `c1` with hash `h1` and schema 1. A snapshot with schema 1 and `c1/h2` is incompatible even though the names look right. The hash records a different configuration identity. A schema-2 snapshot is also incompatible even if you replace its displayed label with 1: the decoder needs the actual old structure.

Practice: compare snapshots `A={schema:1,config:c1/hash:h1}` and `B={schema:2,config:c1/hash:h1}` for that release. Explain which evidence is missing if neither the snapshot schema nor its configuration provenance is recorded. Do not propose rewriting those fields as a recovery method.

## Snapshot order

Choose the compatible snapshot with the greatest `ordinal`. Break a tie by ascending JavaScript string comparison of `id`: if both have ordinal 8, `a-ready` precedes `z-ready`. This means UTF-16 code-unit order, as used by `<`, rather than language-aware `localeCompare`; for example, `Z-ready` precedes `a-ready`. Do not sort the immutable source array in place. You can filter into a new array and sort it, or scan while keeping the best candidate.

Suppose compatible snapshots have ordinals 2 and 6, while an incompatible candidate snapshot has ordinal 10. Select ordinal 6. This preserves more compatible history than ordinal 2 and avoids treating recency as compatibility. Success returns exactly:

```text
{ok:true,releaseId,packageHash,configId,configHash,snapshotId,snapshotHash}
```

Every value comes from the chosen existing artifacts. Return no replacement state or additional fields. Practice with the input array in the order `[ordinal 10, ordinal 2, ordinal 6]`; record why the output is unchanged when the array is reversed. Then compute the tie case before running the checker.

## State compatibility

The trial uses the existing courier engine for movement, cooldown, pickup and delivery. The baseline state envelope is `{schema:1,checkpoint}`. The candidate envelope is `{schema:2,payload:{world:checkpoint}}`. The inner checkpoint still contains real engine state, but the old decoder does not accept the new envelope. Code-only recovery therefore refuses it instead of treating an unknown structure as an empty or fresh game.

The candidate also changes the configured interaction range from 250 mm to 100 mm. A narrow adapter checks that configuration before forwarding an idle interaction to the unchanged engine. A denied configured action advances the real world with `interact:false`; it does not fabricate an engine range denial. The report distinguishes the adapter's `configuration-range` reason from the engine's own decision.

Both defects matter. Restoring only configuration cannot make the old decoder understand the new state. Restoring only the package leaves the narrower configuration in place and the state incompatible. In this exercise recovery selects a known compatible tuple; it does not perform a reverse migration.

Practice: identify which check protects against a wrong configuration with the right name, and which protects against a new-format snapshot with the old configuration identity. Explain why a schema label change alone does not recover its contents.

## Run the recovery trial

Check selection in small steps before interpreting a restored world.

## Build in three checked milestones

1. **Resolve the declared target and configuration.** Trace one missing-target case and one same-name/wrong-hash configuration. Record the first refusal and why later snapshot choices are not yet meaningful.
2. **Choose among compatible snapshots.** Use the worked ordinal-2/6/10 case above. Completion: compatible snapshots `z-ready` and `a-ready` both have ordinal 8; an incompatible snapshot has ordinal 11. Fill the selected ID, then repeat with the array reversed. Do not choose by input position or mutate the array.
3. **Verify the restored behavior and its cost.** Use the checker and actual trial to inspect the selected identities, restored action and discarded history separately. A valid selection object is only the first part of that evidence.

<details><summary>Hint 1 — separate compatibility from recency</summary>

First ask which snapshots the selected package and configuration can interpret. Only then compare ordinals. A newer incompatible snapshot does not become readable by being newer.

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 2 — preserve the selected evidence</summary>

Copy identity values from the chosen artifacts. Do not rewrite a schema label or invent a matching hash; selection is not migration.

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 3 — worked sibling, after a saved attempt</summary>

In the ordinal-2/6/10 example, ordinal 10 is incompatible, so ordinal 6 is the most recent usable state. It can restore behavior while losing later acknowledged work. Record this as assistance, then solve the separate tie completion and inspect the trial's loss report.

</details>

## Observe an actual restore

The owner-side checker invokes `runTrial` with your selection function. Keep the four observations separate: `baseline`, `candidate`, `codeOnly` and `recovered`. Each shows relevant package, configuration and snapshot identities. A successful selection still needs an actual restore and action; returning `ok:true` cannot make the runner claim that pickup worked.

The trial first reaches the pickup boundary and saves a baseline checkpoint. It executes a pickup and delivery, returns to the boundary, converts the current state to the candidate envelope, and tries pickup under the narrowed configuration. Code-only recovery attempts to load that candidate state with the old decoder. Full recovery loads the named compatible baseline snapshot and reruns the original idle pickup through the engine.

Record the settings and source/report identity shown by your integrated runner, each phase's result, and the actor's before/after cargo and score. Each attempted action also records `inputSeq` and `lineage`, the branch of history it belongs to. The original branch uses `original`; a successful restore names its source snapshot and tick, such as `restored-from:baseline-ready@tick3`. A refused restore has no new action or branch, so these fields are null. A stale last decision is not a new decision; the candidate report preserves the earlier deposit while marking the new configured action denied.

## What recovery loses

The recovered snapshot is older than the failed candidate. A later completed delivery disappears from the restored score, along with intervening movement, inputs and the earlier pickup. The runner reports original and restored ticks, discarded recorded operations, score difference and successful post-snapshot actions. Each lost successful action retains its original lineage and input sequence. The new successful pickup is a new action in the recovered branch; it does not replay or compensate the discarded delivery.

`dataLoss.restored` records whether a snapshot was actually restored. `restoredActionApplied` records whether the following interaction succeeded. Restoring the older, farther-away snapshot can make the first value true and the second false. Do not infer a successful action from a successful restore.

The failed candidate acknowledged inputs through sequence 12, but the selected snapshot remembers only sequence 3. `dataLoss.acknowledgedSequences` therefore reports `highestBeforeRestore:12`, `restoredLastSeq:3` and the reopened range `4–12`. The new branch pickup uses sequence 4 again. A production recovery design would need additional coordination, such as a recovery epoch that distinguishes branches or a retained sequence floor that prevents reuse, with defined client retry behavior. This trial implements neither; the lineage label only makes the consequence visible.

Practice: explain the difference between “the same legal action works again” and “no acknowledged action was lost.” Describe what additional coordination would be needed before making the second claim in a system with external payments or shared resources. This toy restore has no database transaction, compensation log or concurrent clients and makes no production rollback guarantee.

Append each correction and assistance declaration in `response.md`. The new repair-service scenario at the end asks for the same compatibility and loss reasoning with a different state change. It is a separate review prompt, not an automatically scored proof of transfer or human learning.

## Capture, compare and try a fresh case

In a newly prepared workspace, put the required first answers in `predictions.json`; use `response.md` for explanations and later repairs. Keep each question ID and its wording unchanged. Fill an `answer` or an explicit `skipReason` for every question before the first source check. A blank row refuses feedback rather than silently recording an empty attempt. The guide's additional trace questions are practice notes, not extra required JSON fields.

After a check accepts and captures the submission, inspect its `prediction-feedback.json` beside the result. Compare your first answer with the answer and governing reason, then append a correction without erasing the original. Complete the new `fresh-practice.json` answers or skip reasons and run `npm run core:practice -- --assistance "none"` from that workspace, replacing `none` with actual help. The practice command records your response before revealing its feedback. These prose responses are preserved and ungraded; they are separate from source-check results and `/learn` mastery.

Use the scripts generated in your workspace. Older prepared workspaces may retain the earlier response-only format; do not replace their original records with new templates. Record any worked-example views, final hints, reference code or AI help in your assistance declaration.

`courses/anti-cheat-engineering/courier-lab/recovery/README.md`:

```md
# Recovery author and integration notes

M10 teaches recovery of package, configuration and state as a compatible tuple. All actions run in the owned local courier world. No files are changed by the trial; no deployment, OS change, third-party account or production migration is involved.

From the project directory:

```sh
node --test tests/recovery.test.mjs
```

## Policy contract

`policy.mjs` exports the author implementation `selectRecovery(evidence)`. The learner receives `template.mjs`, `prompt.json`, `LEARNER.md` and `response-template.md`. The shared core runner imports owner-side `fixtures.mjs`, whose async `assess(candidate)` returns `{passed,criteria}`. Do not copy the author policy or controls into the learner workspace.

Evidence has `{targetReleaseId,releases,configurations,snapshots}`. Release fields are `{id,packageHash,stateSchema,configId,configHash}`. Configuration fields are `{id,hash,releaseId,stateSchema,maxInteractionDistanceMm}`. Snapshot fields are `{id,hash,ordinal,stateSchema,configId,configHash,state}`. Additional provenance fields are allowed. Arrays have unique IDs, ordinals are nonnegative safe integers, hashes are opaque identity strings and all evidence is deeply frozen.

Selection first resolves the declared release, then checks its named configuration's exact hash, release ID and schema, then filters snapshots by matching schema, configuration ID and hash. Greatest ordinal wins; ties use ascending JavaScript string order of ID. Success is exactly `{ok:true,releaseId,packageHash,configId,configHash,snapshotId,snapshotHash}`. Refusals are exactly `{ok:false,reason}` with `unknown-target`, `configuration-mismatch` or `no-compatible-snapshot`, in that precedence order. The selector does not decode, modify or manufacture state.

`controls.mjs` supplies two correct implementations (filter/sort and independent scan) and eleven isolated wrong controls: code-only tuple, newest regardless of compatibility, oldest compatible snapshot, ignored target, ignored configuration hash, ignored schema, invented configuration, silent target fallback, mutation of source evidence, array-order tie breaking and locale collation. Sixteen pure fixture cases and one actual-game trial criterion calibrate the checker. A mixed-case `a-ready`/`Z-ready` fixture distinguishes locale collation from the required UTF-16 code-unit order. Failures retain input, expected/actual behavior and a teaching-section link.

## Trial APIs

`runtime.mjs` exports:

| API | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `TRIAL_VERSION` | `courier-recovery-trial-v2` |
| `RECOVERY_LIMIT` | Required limitation text about local scope and lost actions. |
| `hashValue(value)` | SHA-256 of recursively key-sorted JSON. |
| `createTrialEvidence()` | Async, deterministic frozen `{evidence,baseline,candidate,codeOnly,live,postSnapshotActions,current,currentEventIndex,action,limitations}`. |
| `runTrial(candidatePolicy)` | Async; candidate has `selectRecovery(evidence)`. Returns `{schema,baseline,candidate,codeOnly,recovered,selection,identities,dataLoss,limitations}`. |

Successful action observations contain `{phase,lineage,inputSeq,identity,action,status,reason,before,after,engineDecision}`. `lineage` is `original` for the continuing pre-recovery branch, or `restored-from:<snapshotId>@tick<tick>` for a restored branch. `inputSeq` is the actual sequence admitted to the engine. `identity` contains release/package, configuration/hash, snapshot/hash and state schema. Before/after state is `{tick,actor,lastDecision}` from the existing engine's canonical snapshot. Refused restores contain `{phase,lineage:null,inputSeq:null,status:'refused',reason}` and identity when it can be resolved: no new action or branch has run. A code-only observation also records separate state/configuration incompatibility flags.

`identities` contains the exact validated selection evidence, including named state bodies, to keep provenance inspectable. `dataLoss` reports `restored`, `restoredActionApplied`, `fromTick`, `restoredTick`, `discardedTicks`, `discardedRecordedOperations`, `scoreBeforeRecovery`, `scoreAtRestoredSnapshot`, `lostScore`, `acknowledgedSequences`, `discardedSuccessfulActions` and a limitation note. A failed restore has null restore/loss counts; it must not claim recovery happened. An actual restore followed by a refused interaction has `restored:true` and `restoredActionApplied:false`. This v2 report replaces the ambiguous v1 `applied` field; it does not rewrite earlier saved v1 reports.

`acknowledgedSequences` contains `{highestBeforeRestore,restoredLastSeq,reopened}`. `reopened` is an inclusive range string, or null when no acknowledged sequence became reusable or no restore occurred. Each discarded successful action contains `{lineage,inputSeq,tick,status,reason}`. The correct trial reports highest sequence 12, restored sequence 3, and reopened range `4–12`; the new branch action uses sequence 4. These sequence numbers are taken from real actor state, rather than inferred from tick numbers.

The runner computes package identities from hashes of the real engine, admission, defense, telemetry runtime and recovery adapter source, plus release/schema descriptors. Configuration hashes identify their complete JSON bodies. Snapshot hashes identify actual saved state. Hashes identify bytes and declared bundles; they do not authenticate their producer or prove a deployment occurred.

## Real game behavior and its bounds

The trial moves a real actor to x=1750, y=1000, saves baseline state at tick 3, then performs pickup at tick 4 and delivery at tick 8 through the existing engine. It returns to the pickup boundary at tick 11. The baseline configuration allows 250 mm; the candidate allows 100 mm. The narrow adapter checks range for an idle interaction against authoritative position before forwarding the interaction bit to the unchanged engine. If blocked, it still admits an idle non-interaction input and advances the real world. The report calls this `configuration-range`, with `engineDecision:null`; it never mislabels that adapter denial as an engine proximity decision.

State v1 is `{schema:1,checkpoint}`. Forward capture for the candidate produces v2 `{schema:2,payload:{world:checkpoint}}`. The old decoder rejects v2 before attempting restore. The code-only trial deliberately keeps candidate state/configuration with the old package. Full recovery loads the compatible named baseline state and repeats the same idle pickup. No selector rewrites either envelope.

The correct run has baseline pickup applied, candidate configured denial, code-only `state-schema` refusal and recovered pickup applied. The current trial reaches tick 12; recovery returns to tick 3, discarding 9 ticks and 18 recorded operations. The completed delivery's score is lost (1 to 0), along with the post-snapshot pickup and deposit. The recovered pickup is a new branch action and does not compensate those losses. All original phase objects remain separate. A recovery epoch or an independently retained sequence floor, with coordinated client retry behavior, would be needed to prevent an acknowledged input from being accepted on the restored branch. Neither is implemented: `lineage` is evidence, not an admission safeguard.

Parent integration owns CLI/report paths, source capture, module registration and browser presentation. Preserve the failed trial and later recovery as separate evidence, state the output path and settings, and display package/configuration/state identities. The trial writes no files itself, so the existing attempt runner remains responsible for immutable saved reports and first attempts.

## Course-craft trace

Exact policy requirements and the engine trial assess an executable recovery decision (`assessment-03`, `projects-03`). Independent correct/wrong controls calibrate the checker (`assessment-09`). Expected/actual feedback links a repair paragraph (`feedback-07`); original and revised responses stay separate. The repair-service transfer changes both state and an external side effect and remains an ungraded review prompt (`assessment-02`). These deterministic checks do not establish human learning, production rollback safety or rendered usability (`evaluation-01`). Parent technical review, cold-reader and desktop/mobile checks remain integration acceptance work.

```mjs
import { selectRecovery } from './policy.mjs';
const copy = (value) => JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(value));

/** Independently select by scanning and retaining the best compatible identity. */
export function selectByScan(evidence) {
  let target;
  for (const release of evidence.releases) if (release.id === evidence.targetReleaseId) target = release;
  if (!target) return { ok: false, reason: 'unknown-target' };
  const settings = evidence.configurations.find((config) => config.id === target.configId);
  if (!settings || settings.hash !== target.configHash || settings.stateSchema !== target.stateSchema
    || settings.releaseId !== target.id) return { ok: false, reason: 'configuration-mismatch' };
  let best;
  for (const saved of evidence.snapshots) {
    if (saved.configId !== settings.id || saved.configHash !== settings.hash || saved.stateSchema !== target.stateSchema) continue;
    if (!best || saved.ordinal > best.ordinal || (saved.ordinal === best.ordinal && saved.id < best.id)) best = saved;
  }
  if (!best) return { ok: false, reason: 'no-compatible-snapshot' };
  return { ok: true, releaseId: target.id, packageHash: target.packageHash, configId: settings.id,
    configHash: settings.hash, snapshotId: best.id, snapshotHash: best.hash };
}

export const correctPolicies = { 'filter-and-sort': { selectRecovery }, 'single-scan': { selectRecovery: selectByScan } };

function overrideSnapshot(evidence, choose) {
  const result = selectRecovery(evidence);
  if (!result.ok) return result;
  const saved = choose(evidence, result);
  return saved ? { ...result, snapshotId: saved.id, snapshotHash: saved.hash } : result;
}

function rewrite(evidence, edit) {
  const changed = copy(evidence);
  edit(changed);
  return selectRecovery(changed);
}

export const wrongPolicies = {
  'code-only': { selectRecovery(evidence) {
    const result = selectRecovery(evidence);
    if (!result.ok) return result;
    const candidate = evidence.releases.at(-1);
    const saved = [...evidence.snapshots].sort((a, b) => b.ordinal - a.ordinal)[0];
    return { ...result, configId: candidate.configId, configHash: candidate.configHash, snapshotId: saved.id, snapshotHash: saved.hash };
  } },
  'newest-without-compatibility': { selectRecovery: (evidence) => overrideSnapshot(evidence,
    (e) => [...e.snapshots].sort((a, b) => b.ordinal - a.ordinal)[0]) },
  'oldest-compatible': { selectRecovery: (evidence) => overrideSnapshot(evidence,
    (e, result) => e.snapshots.filter((saved) => saved.configId === result.configId && saved.configHash === result.configHash
      && saved.stateSchema === e.releases.find((release) => release.id === result.releaseId).stateSchema).sort((a, b) => a.ordinal - b.ordinal)[0]) },
  'ignore-declared-target': { selectRecovery: (evidence) => selectRecovery({ ...evidence, targetReleaseId: evidence.releases.at(-1).id }) },
  'ignore-config-hash': { selectRecovery: (evidence) => rewrite(evidence, (e) => {
    const release = e.releases.find((item) => item.id === e.targetReleaseId);
    if (!release) return;
    e.snapshots.forEach((saved) => { if (saved.configId === release.configId) saved.configHash = release.configHash; });
  }) },
  'ignore-state-schema': { selectRecovery: (evidence) => rewrite(evidence, (e) => {
    const release = e.releases.find((item) => item.id === e.targetReleaseId);
    if (!release) return;
    e.snapshots.forEach((saved) => { if (saved.configId === release.configId) saved.stateSchema = release.stateSchema; });
  }) },
  'invent-missing-configuration': { selectRecovery: (evidence) => rewrite(evidence, (e) => {
    const release = e.releases.find((item) => item.id === e.targetReleaseId);
    if (release && !e.configurations.some((item) => item.id === release.configId)) e.configurations.push({
      id: release.configId, hash: release.configHash, releaseId: release.id, stateSchema: release.stateSchema,
    });
  }) },
  'fall-back-from-unknown-target': { selectRecovery: (evidence) => selectRecovery({ ...evidence,
    targetReleaseId: evidence.releases.some((item) => item.id === evidence.targetReleaseId) ? evidence.targetReleaseId : evidence.releases[0].id }) },
  'rewrite-original-state': { selectRecovery(evidence) {
    evidence.snapshots.sort((a, b) => b.ordinal - a.ordinal);
    evidence.snapshots[0].stateSchema = evidence.releases[0].stateSchema;
    return selectRecovery(evidence);
  } },
  'last-array-entry-on-tie': { selectRecovery: (evidence) => overrideSnapshot(evidence, (e, result) => {
    const selected = e.snapshots.find((item) => item.id === result.snapshotId);
    return e.snapshots.findLast((item) => item.ordinal === selected.ordinal && item.configId === result.configId);
  }) },
  'locale-collation-on-tie': { selectRecovery: (evidence) => overrideSnapshot(evidence, (e, result) => {
    const release = e.releases.find((item) => item.id === result.releaseId);
    return e.snapshots.filter((item) => item.stateSchema === release.stateSchema
      && item.configId === result.configId && item.configHash === result.configHash)
      .sort((left, right) => right.ordinal - left.ordinal || left.id.localeCompare(right.id))[0];
  }) },
};

import { isDeepStrictEqual } from 'node:util';
import { runTrial } from './runtime.mjs';

const copy = (value) => JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(value));
const digest = (letter) => letter.repeat(64);
function freeze(value) {
  if (!value || typeof value !== 'object') return value;
  Object.values(value).forEach(freeze);
  return Object.freeze(value);
}

function sample() {
  return {
    targetReleaseId: 'baseline',
    releases: [
      { id: 'baseline', packageHash: digest('a'), stateSchema: 1, configId: 'baseline-config', configHash: digest('b') },
      { id: 'candidate', packageHash: digest('c'), stateSchema: 2, configId: 'candidate-config', configHash: digest('d') },
    ],
    configurations: [
      { id: 'baseline-config', hash: digest('b'), releaseId: 'baseline', stateSchema: 1, maxInteractionDistanceMm: 250 },
      { id: 'candidate-config', hash: digest('d'), releaseId: 'candidate', stateSchema: 2, maxInteractionDistanceMm: 100 },
    ],
    snapshots: [
      { id: 'older', ordinal: 1, stateSchema: 1, configId: 'baseline-config', configHash: digest('b'), hash: digest('e'), state: { untouched: 'old' } },
      { id: 'candidate-state', ordinal: 5, stateSchema: 2, configId: 'candidate-config', configHash: digest('d'), hash: digest('f'), state: { untouched: 'candidate' } },
      { id: 'ready', ordinal: 3, stateSchema: 1, configId: 'baseline-config', configHash: digest('b'), hash: digest('1'), state: { untouched: 'ready' } },
    ],
  };
}

function chosen(evidence, releaseId, snapshotId) {
  const release = evidence.releases.find((item) => item.id === releaseId);
  const saved = evidence.snapshots.find((item) => item.id === snapshotId);
  return { ok: true, releaseId, packageHash: release.packageHash, configId: release.configId,
    configHash: release.configHash, snapshotId, snapshotHash: saved.hash };
}

function fixture(name, edit, outcome, section) {
  const evidence = sample();
  edit(evidence);
  return { name, evidence, expected: typeof outcome === 'string'
    ? chosen(evidence, evidence.targetReleaseId, outcome) : outcome, section };
}

export function cases() {
  return [
    fixture('select the newest compatible baseline tuple', () => {}, 'ready', 'compatible-tuples'),
    fixture('honor a declared candidate target when its tuple is compatible', (e) => { e.targetReleaseId = 'candidate'; }, 'candidate-state', 'declared-target'),
    fixture('array order does not define snapshot age', (e) => { e.snapshots.reverse(); }, 'ready', 'snapshot-order'),
    fixture('equal ordinals use ascending snapshot ID', (e) => {
      e.snapshots.unshift({ ...e.snapshots[2], id: 'a-ready', hash: digest('2') });
    }, 'a-ready', 'snapshot-order'),
    fixture('snapshot ID ties use code-unit order rather than locale collation', (e) => {
      const ready = e.snapshots[2];
      e.snapshots[2] = { ...ready, id: 'a-ready' };
      e.snapshots.unshift({ ...ready, id: 'Z-ready', hash: digest('6') });
    }, 'Z-ready', 'snapshot-order'),
    fixture('refuse an absent declared target', (e) => { e.targetReleaseId = 'missing'; }, { ok: false, reason: 'unknown-target' }, 'declared-target'),
    fixture('refuse a missing target configuration', (e) => { e.configurations.shift(); }, { ok: false, reason: 'configuration-mismatch' }, 'compatible-tuples'),
    fixture('configuration name alone cannot replace its pinned hash', (e) => { e.configurations[0].hash = digest('9'); }, { ok: false, reason: 'configuration-mismatch' }, 'compatible-tuples'),
    fixture('configuration belongs to the target release', (e) => { e.configurations[0].releaseId = 'candidate'; }, { ok: false, reason: 'configuration-mismatch' }, 'compatible-tuples'),
    fixture('configuration schema must match the decoder', (e) => { e.configurations[0].stateSchema = 2; }, { ok: false, reason: 'configuration-mismatch' }, 'compatible-tuples'),
    fixture('no compatible state means refuse, not manufacture a snapshot', (e) => { e.snapshots = [e.snapshots[1]]; }, { ok: false, reason: 'no-compatible-snapshot' }, 'compatible-tuples'),
    fixture('a newer wrong-configuration snapshot is not compatible', (e) => {
      e.snapshots.push({ ...e.snapshots[2], id: 'wrong-config', ordinal: 10, configId: 'candidate-config', hash: digest('3') });
    }, 'ready', 'compatible-tuples'),
    fixture('a newer snapshot with the wrong configuration hash is not compatible', (e) => {
      e.snapshots.push({ ...e.snapshots[2], id: 'wrong-hash', ordinal: 10, configHash: digest('9'), hash: digest('4') });
    }, 'ready', 'compatible-tuples'),
    fixture('a newer state schema cannot be relabeled to fit the old decoder', (e) => {

function evidence(value) {
  try { return JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(value, (_key, item) => item === undefined ? { type: 'undefined' } : item)); }
  catch { return { type: 'non-JSON result' }; }
}

/** Test immutable inputs, exact identities, refusals and the actual recovery trial. */
export async function assess(candidate) {
  if (typeof candidate?.selectRecovery !== 'function') return { passed: false, criteria: [{ name: 'export selectRecovery(evidence)', passed: false,
    error: { message: 'Export the selection function declared in the contract.', expected: 'function', actual: typeof candidate?.selectRecovery, source: 'LEARNER.md#the-contract' } }] };
  const criteria = [];
  for (const item of cases()) {
    let actual;
    try { actual = await candidate.selectRecovery(freeze(copy(item.evidence))); }
    catch (error) { actual = { threw: String(error?.message ?? error) }; }
    const passed = isDeepStrictEqual(actual, item.expected);
    const criterion = { name: item.name, passed };
    if (!passed) criterion.error = { message: `The selection violates this requirement: ${item.name}.`,
      input: item.evidence, expected: item.expected, actual: evidence(actual), source: `LEARNER.md#${item.section}` };
    criteria.push(criterion);
  }
  const trial = await runTrial(candidate);
  const expected = { status: 'applied', reason: 'pickup', snapshotId: 'baseline-ready', lostScore: 1 };
  const actual = { status: trial.recovered.status, reason: trial.recovered.reason,
    snapshotId: trial.recovered.identity?.snapshotId ?? null, lostScore: trial.dataLoss.lostScore };
  const passed = isDeepStrictEqual(actual, expected);
  const criterion = { name: 'restore the full tuple and rerun the legal action through the owned engine', passed };
  if (!passed) criterion.error = { message: 'Recovery must restore compatible code, configuration and named state, then execute the legal action.',
    expected, actual, source: 'LEARNER.md#run-the-recovery-trial' };
  criteria.push(criterion);
  return { passed: criteria.every((item) => item.passed), criteria, evidence: { trial } };
}

`courses/anti-cheat-engineering/courier-lab/recovery/policy.mjs`:

```mjs
/** Select identities only. Never rewrite state to make a snapshot appear compatible. */
export function selectRecovery(evidence) {
  const release = evidence.releases.find((item) => item.id === evidence.targetReleaseId);
  if (!release) return { ok: false, reason: 'unknown-target' };
  const config = evidence.configurations.find((item) => item.id === release.configId);
  if (!config || config.hash !== release.configHash || config.releaseId !== release.id
    || config.stateSchema !== release.stateSchema) return { ok: false, reason: 'configuration-mismatch' };
  const snapshots = evidence.snapshots.filter((item) => item.stateSchema === release.stateSchema
    && item.configId === config.id && item.configHash === config.hash);
  snapshots.sort((left, right) => right.ordinal - left.ordinal || (left.id < right.id ? -1 : left.id > right.id ? 1 : 0));
  const snapshot = snapshots[0];
  if (!snapshot) return { ok: false, reason: 'no-compatible-snapshot' };
  return { ok: true, releaseId: release.id, packageHash: release.packageHash,
    configId: config.id, configHash: config.hash, snapshotId: snapshot.id, snapshotHash: snapshot.hash };
}

- Original and restored action lineage / input sequence:
- Highest acknowledged sequence before restore / restored last sequence / reopened range:
- Whether state was restored / whether the following action applied:
- Why recovery did not preserve all acknowledged history:
- What a recovery epoch or retained sequence floor would need to coordinate beyond this trial:

## Revision log

Append later code changes, results, reasoning and assistance. Preserve the original trial, whether it passed or failed, and the first answers above. A new successful branch does not overwrite or erase the failed candidate evidence.

## Transfer for review (not automatically graded)

A repair service changes a saved job from `{remainingTicks:4,charged:true}` to `{schedule:{remaining:4},receipt:{charged:true}}`. An older package only reads the first format. A customer payment completed after the last old-format snapshot. Describe a compatible recovery tuple, one test of resumed repair behavior, and the financial action a snapshot restore cannot undo safely by itself. State what you would refuse to claim without a transaction or compensation mechanism. Keep your first answer and append corrections.
