`courses/anti-cheat-engineering/courier-lab/recovery/runtime.mjs`:

```mjs
import { createHash } from 'node:crypto';
import { readFile } from 'node:fs/promises';
import { createWorld, join, admit, advance, canonical } from '../engine.mjs';
import { capture, restore, RUNTIME_RELEASE } from '../telemetry/runtime.mjs';

export const TRIAL_VERSION = 'courier-recovery-trial-v2';
export const RECOVERY_LIMIT = 'Owned local deterministic trial only. Restoring an older snapshot discards later state and actions, and reopens acknowledged sequence numbers. No recovery epoch or retained sequence floor is implemented. This is not a transactionally safe production rollback or a deployment.';

const copy = (value) => JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(value));
function stableJson(value) {
  if (Array.isArray(value)) return `[${value.map(stableJson).join(',')}]`;
  if (value && typeof value === 'object') return `{${Object.keys(value).sort().map((key) => `${JSON.stringify(key)}:${stableJson(value[key])}`).join(',')}}`;
  return JSON.stringify(value);
}
export const hashValue = (value) => createHash('sha256').update(stableJson(value)).digest('hex');

function freeze(value) {
  if (!value || typeof value !== 'object') return value;
  for (const item of Object.values(value)) freeze(item);
  return Object.freeze(value);
}

async function packages() {
  const paths = ['../engine.mjs', '../admission.mjs', '../defense.mjs', '../telemetry/runtime.mjs', './runtime.mjs'];
  const files = await Promise.all(paths.map(async (path) => [path, createHash('sha256').update(await readFile(new URL(path, import.meta.url))).digest('hex')]));
  const sourceHashes = Object.fromEntries(files);
  const make = (id, stateSchema, configId) => ({ id, stateSchema, configId,
    packageHash: hashValue({ id, stateSchema, runtimeRelease: RUNTIME_RELEASE, sourceHashes }), sourceHashes });
  return [make('courier-baseline', 1, 'range-250-v1'), make('courier-candidate', 2, 'range-100-v2')];
}

function configuration(release, range) {
  const body = { id: release.configId, releaseId: release.id, stateSchema: release.stateSchema, maxInteractionDistanceMm: range };
  return { ...body, hash: hashValue(body) };
}

function encodeState(world, stateSchema) {
  const checkpoint = capture(world);
  if (stateSchema === 1) return { schema: 1, checkpoint };
  if (stateSchema === 2) return { schema: 2, payload: { world: checkpoint } };
  throw new Error('Unsupported state schema.');
}

function snapshot(id, ordinal, world, release, config, eventIndex) {
  const state = encodeState(world, release.stateSchema);
  return { id, ordinal, stateSchema: release.stateSchema, configId: config.id, configHash: config.hash,
    hash: hashValue(state), state, eventIndex };
}

function identities(release, config, saved) {
  return { releaseId: release.id, packageHash: release.packageHash, configId: config.id,
    configHash: config.hash, snapshotId: saved.id, snapshotHash: saved.hash, stateSchema: saved.stateSchema };
}

function decode(release, config, saved) {
  // Check state first so a code-only rollback visibly fails on the incompatible state, too.
  if (saved.stateSchema !== release.stateSchema || saved.state.schema !== release.stateSchema) throw new Error('state-schema');
  if (hashValue(saved.state) !== saved.hash) throw new Error('snapshot-hash');
  if (config.id !== release.configId || config.hash !== release.configHash || config.releaseId !== release.id
    || config.stateSchema !== release.stateSchema) throw new Error('configuration-mismatch');
  const { hash, ...body } = config;
  if (hashValue(body) !== hash || saved.configId !== config.id || saved.configHash !== hash) throw new Error('configuration-mismatch');
  const checkpoint = release.stateSchema === 1 ? saved.state.checkpoint : saved.state.payload?.world;
  return restore(checkpoint);
}

function state(world) {
  const observed = canonical(world);
  return { tick: observed.tick, actor: observed.actors[0].actor, lastDecision: observed.actors[0].lastDecision };
}

function move(world, direction) {
  const actor = world.actors[0];
  admit(world, actor.id, { v: 1, seq: actor.lastSeq + 1, move: direction, interact: false });
  advance(world, 1);
}

/** A deliberately narrow configuration gate around the unchanged real game. */
function attempt(world, config, phase, identity, lineage = 'original') {
  const before = state(world);
  const actor = world.actors[0];
  const target = actor.cargo ? { x: 1000, y: 1000 } : world.core;
  const distanceSquared = (actor.x - target.x) ** 2 + (actor.y - target.y) ** 2;
  const configured = distanceSquared <= config.maxInteractionDistanceMm ** 2;
  // The fixed trial action is idle + interact, so the gate and engine see the same position.
  const inputSeq = actor.lastSeq + 1;
  admit(world, actor.id, { v: 1, seq: inputSeq, move: 'idle', interact: configured });
  advance(world, 1);
  const after = state(world);
  const decision = after.lastDecision?.tick === after.tick ? after.lastDecision : null;
  return { phase, lineage, inputSeq, identity, action: { move: 'idle', interact: true, distanceSquared, baselineRadiusMm: 250 },
    status: configured ? decision?.status ?? 'no-decision' : 'denied',
    reason: configured ? decision?.reason ?? 'no-decision' : 'configuration-range',
    before, after, engineDecision: decision };
}

/** Build immutable versioned evidence using actual owned movement, pickup and delivery. */
export async function createTrialEvidence() {
  const releases = await packages();
  const configurations = [configuration(releases[0], 250), configuration(releases[1], 100)];
  for (let index = 0; index < releases.length; index += 1) releases[index].configHash = configurations[index].hash;
  const [baselineRelease, candidateRelease] = releases;
  const [baselineConfig, candidateConfig] = configurations;
  const world = createWorld(0);
  join(world);
  move(world, 'E');
  move(world, 'E');
  const older = snapshot('baseline-before-approach', 1, world, baselineRelease, baselineConfig, world.history.length);
  move(world, 'E');
  const ready = snapshot('baseline-ready', 2, world, baselineRelease, baselineConfig, world.history.length);
  const baseline = attempt(world, baselineConfig, 'baseline', identities(baselineRelease, baselineConfig, ready));
  move(world, 'W');
  move(world, 'W');
  move(world, 'W');
  const delivery = attempt(world, baselineConfig, 'post-snapshot-delivery', identities(baselineRelease, baselineConfig, ready));
  move(world, 'E');
  move(world, 'E');
  move(world, 'E');
  const live = state(world);
  const converted = snapshot('candidate-converted', 3, world, candidateRelease, candidateConfig, world.history.length);
  const candidateWorld = decode(candidateRelease, candidateConfig, converted);
  const candidate = attempt(candidateWorld, candidateConfig, 'candidate', identities(candidateRelease, candidateConfig, converted));
  const incompatible = snapshot('candidate-after-failure', 4, candidateWorld, candidateRelease, candidateConfig,
    world.history.length + candidateWorld.history.length);
  const evidence = { targetReleaseId: baselineRelease.id, releases, configurations, snapshots: [incompatible, older, ready, converted] };
  const codeOnly = { phase: 'code-only', lineage: null, inputSeq: null, identity: identities(baselineRelease, candidateConfig, incompatible),
    status: 'refused', reason: null, stateIncompatible: incompatible.stateSchema !== baselineRelease.stateSchema,
    configurationIncompatible: candidateConfig.hash !== baselineRelease.configHash };
  try { decode(baselineRelease, candidateConfig, incompatible); }
  catch (error) { codeOnly.reason = error.message; }
  return freeze({ evidence, baseline, candidate, codeOnly, live,
    postSnapshotActions: [baseline, delivery].map((observation) => ({ lineage: observation.lineage, inputSeq: observation.inputSeq, tick: observation.after.tick,
      status: observation.status, reason: observation.reason })),
    current: candidate.after, currentEventIndex: incompatible.eventIndex,
    action: { move: 'idle', interact: true, baselineRadiusMm: 250 }, limitations: RECOVERY_LIMIT });
}

function recoveryRefusal(reason, identity) {
  return { phase: 'recovered', lineage: null, inputSeq: null, status: 'refused', reason, ...(identity ? { identity } : {}) };
}

function recover(selection, trial) {
  if (selection?.ok !== true) return recoveryRefusal(selection?.reason ?? 'invalid-selection');
  const { evidence } = trial;
  const release = evidence.releases.find((item) => item.id === selection.releaseId && item.packageHash === selection.packageHash);
  const config = evidence.configurations.find((item) => item.id === selection.configId && item.hash === selection.configHash);
  const saved = evidence.snapshots.find((item) => item.id === selection.snapshotId && item.hash === selection.snapshotHash);
  if (!release || !config || !saved || release.id !== evidence.targetReleaseId) return recoveryRefusal('identity-mismatch');
  try {
    const world = decode(release, config, saved);
    return attempt(world, config, 'recovered', identities(release, config, saved), `restored-from:${saved.id}@tick${world.tick}`);
  } catch (error) {
    return recoveryRefusal(error.message, identities(release, config, saved));
  }
}

/** No files, deployment or existing sessions change. Policy sees frozen detached evidence. */
export async function runTrial(candidatePolicy) {
  if (typeof candidatePolicy?.selectRecovery !== 'function') throw new Error('Export selectRecovery(evidence).');
  const trial = await createTrialEvidence();
  let selection;
  try { selection = await candidatePolicy.selectRecovery(freeze(copy(trial.evidence))); }
  catch (error) { selection = { ok: false, reason: 'policy-error', error: String(error?.message ?? error) }; }
  const recovered = recover(selection, trial);
  const saved = trial.evidence.snapshots.find((item) => item.id === selection?.snapshotId && item.hash === selection?.snapshotHash);
  const restoredTick = recovered.before?.tick;
  const highestBeforeRestore = trial.current.actor.lastSeq;
  const restoredLastSeq = recovered.before?.actor.lastSeq ?? null;
  const reopened = restoredLastSeq !== null && restoredLastSeq < highestBeforeRestore
    ? `${restoredLastSeq + 1}\u2013${highestBeforeRestore}` : null;
  const dataLoss = {
    restored: restoredTick !== undefined, restoredActionApplied: recovered.status === 'applied',
    fromTick: trial.current.tick, restoredTick: restoredTick ?? null,
    discardedTicks: restoredTick === undefined ? null : trial.current.tick - restoredTick,
    discardedRecordedOperations: restoredTick === undefined ? null : trial.currentEventIndex - saved.eventIndex,
    scoreBeforeRecovery: trial.current.actor.score, scoreAtRestoredSnapshot: recovered.before?.actor.score ?? null,
    lostScore: restoredTick === undefined ? null : trial.current.actor.score - recovered.before.actor.score,
    acknowledgedSequences: { highestBeforeRestore, restoredLastSeq, reopened },
    discardedSuccessfulActions: restoredTick === undefined ? [] : trial.postSnapshotActions.filter((item) => item.status === 'applied' && item.tick > restoredTick),
    note: 'Lost actions belong to the original lineage; the restored pickup belongs to a new branch. Restoring the checkpoint does not compensate deliveries, merge later history or prevent reuse of acknowledged sequence numbers.',
  };
  return { schema: TRIAL_VERSION, baseline: trial.baseline, candidate: trial.candidate, codeOnly: trial.codeOnly,
    recovered, selection, identities: copy(trial.evidence), dataLoss, limitations: RECOVERY_LIMIT };
}

```

```md
# M9: Keep a useful, bounded export

Implementation reference for **M9: retention**. Start with [the guided learning route at `/learn`](/learn) on the reference server, then return here for the exact source contract. This Markdown file does not submit answers or certify mastery. Use the [support and attempt workflow](../learning-support/README.md) for worked siblings, gradual guidance and help recording. A prepared source workspace need not serve `/learn`; keep the reference server open for that route.

Implement `retain(events, settings)` so an owner can keep a small denial-event export without copying every field available at capture time. Then measure what two limits save and explain which later questions the smaller export cannot answer. This exercise assumes the earlier replay and detector work, plus JavaScript arrays and objects.

A denial event describes an interaction that the game refused. An **export** is a file made for later inspection. A **retention limit** decides which observations remain in that file. The game may need much more state to continue running or reproduce a history; this exercise changes only the export.

Use synthetic data only. Do not substitute live accounts, actual tokens, addresses or device data into this lab.

## The contract

From the reference project run:

```sh
npm run core:prepare -- retention
```

Open the printed workspace and edit `retention/policy.mjs`. The function takes an event array and `{nowTick,maxAgeTicks,maxEvents}` and returns an array. The source events are already in nondecreasing tick order. Equal-tick events retain their original order. `nowTick` is a nonnegative integer and both bounds are positive integers. Each event already has an integer tick, string actor ID and reason, and a finite nonnegative squared distance.

Keep only events newer than `nowTick-maxAgeTicks` and no later than `nowTick`. Among those, retain the newest `maxEvents` as four-field records. You can assume the inputs are valid. This exercise assesses the retention decisions, rather than an additional parser. Optional input validation must not change the result for valid inputs. Keep filesystem work, wall clocks and measurements out of your policy; the supplied owner helpers handle them.

Before inspecting a run, record the required first answers or explicit skip reasons in `predictions.json` and explanations in `response.md`: where the old edge belongs, how a count limit treats a tie, and what remains after deleting one export. These predictions are reviewed alongside your work and are not automatically graded.

## The tick window

Keep an event only when:

```text
nowTick - maxAgeTicks < event.tick <= nowTick
```

The left edge is exclusive; an event exactly that old is removed. The current tick is inclusive. A future event is removed even if there is room in the file. `maxAgeTicks` measures game ticks, not seconds. The setting says nothing about wall-clock retention without a separate mapping between those units.

Follow a small sibling example. Suppose the current tick is 20 and the age bound is 5. The old edge is 15. Ticks 14 and 15 fall outside the window, ticks 16 and 20 fall inside, and tick 21 is in the future. Filtering by age before limiting the count matters: future observations must not displace usable observations.

Compare this with your edge prediction and append any correction. Do not replace the original prediction.

## The count bound

After selecting the window, keep at most `maxEvents` of its newest entries. Because the input is already sorted, the newest entries form its tail. Return that tail in the supplied order. You do not need to sort anything, fill missing ticks or combine events that share a tick.

For a separate example, the eligible entries are `A@16, B@18, C@18, D@20` and the count bound is three. The result is `B@18, C@18, D@20`. B still precedes C because that was their observed order. A count bound can shorten the useful history even when the age bound would permit older entries.

In `response.md`, explain what would happen if there were six eligible entries at the current tick and the count bound were four. State which property chooses between the tied entries.

## Four fields only

Each returned event has exactly:

```js
{ tick, actorId, reason, distanceSquared }
```

Copy those values explicitly. Extra fields such as `capability`, `address` and `device` occur only as synthetic examples in the supplied source. Copying the source object wholesale defeats the export's narrow purpose. Deleting unwanted fields from a source object also breaks the contract: a caller may still need the original event. Construct the retained objects without changing the input array, its objects or the settings.

The retained actor ID is **pseudonymous**: it labels an actor without directly naming a person. Its repeated actions still describe behavior and may be linkable to other information. Removing an address does not establish anonymity. The four-field format is minimization for this exercise, not a claim that those fields are appropriate for every real system.

Submit your source after the first predictions:

```sh
npm run core:check -- --assistance "none"
```

Replace `none` with the actual help used. The core runner captures the exact question, source, response and assistance and preserves first and revised attempts separately. After that capture, its prediction feedback gives the keyed answers and reasons, plus fresh questions. Compare them with your saved first predictions and append any correction; the written answers remain ungraded. Read the first failed code criterion's expected and actual result and its teaching link. Fix the decision it identifies, append why the change addresses that failure, and check again. A pass means agreement with the stated cases; it does not prove every possible input or establish learning gains.

## Export and deletion scope

Finish the selection policy before interpreting the export helper or a deletion receipt.

## Build in three checked milestones

1. **Window first.** Trace the worked age window above, including both edges and a future observation. Completion: `nowTick=30`, `maxAgeTicks=4`, and source ticks 26, 27, 29, 30, 31. Decide eligibility before considering a count bound. Keep that calculation separate from the required first predictions.
2. **Count and projection.** For the eligible completion entries, apply a count bound of two and construct only the four named fields. Hand-check a tie using source order. Keep the source objects unchanged: projection means producing a smaller new record, not deleting fields from a caller's record.
3. **Inspect and measure.** Use the first failed core criterion to locate a window, count, order, shape or mutation error. After repairing the policy, run the declared measurement settings and check what they remove. A smaller file alone does not establish useful evidence.

<details><summary>Hint 1 — decide what is eligible</summary>

Filter the age interval before applying the count bound. Otherwise a future or expired event can take a slot that belongs to an eligible observation.

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 2 — use the supplied order</summary>

The input is already sorted and equal-tick entries keep their order. The newest eligible entries form a tail; sorting or deduplicating would add a rule the contract never requested.

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 3 — worked sibling, after a saved attempt</summary>

At tick 20 with age 5, the exclusive old edge is 15. From eligible `A@16, B@18, C@18, D@20`, a count of three keeps B, C and D in that order. Record this as assistance; finish the different tick-30 completion yourself.

</details>

## Define one deletion's scope

The reference `store.mjs` helper applies a policy, checks the output bounds and four-field shape, encodes it, then writes one new file. It refuses an existing destination and an export over its declared byte limit. Its receipt reports settings, counts, byte length, path and a digest of the bytes. It does not save the raw source events or make a backup.

`deleteExport(receipt)` checks that the receipt still names the same regular file and removes that export. A missing or changed file produces an error. Record the actual path and successful deletion result. Deleting this file does not erase another export, an explicit copy someone made, a learner attempt or a causal checkpoint. Do not claim all captured data was deleted.

A **causal checkpoint** stores enough state to continue replay, such as pending intent, positions and detector history. This minimized export stores only selected denial observations. It cannot replace a checkpoint, and replay requirements do not justify silently adding checkpoint state to this export.

## Measure the tradeoff

The supplied `measureRetention` helper uses the named `courier-denials-v1` synthetic workload: 4,096 events ending at tick 4,095. Declare at least two settings, a warmup count and a measured sample count in `response.md` before inspecting results. From the reference project, run the following shape with your workspace policy and a new output path; each setting is `nowTick:maxAgeTicks:maxEvents`:

```sh
npm run retention:measure -- <workspace>/retention/policy.mjs <new-report>.json 4095:512:64 4095:128:16 --warmup 5 --samples 20
```

Substitute your declared values. The report echoes the actual settings and counts used, along with workload name, size and digest, Node version, platform, architecture, retained counts, elapsed samples and JSON byte lengths. Compare that echo with your declaration before interpreting the results. Omitting settings and counts uses the stated defaults of 2048/1024 and 256/128 at tick 4095, with two warmups and five measured samples; do not describe that default run as your different declaration. The digest identifies the exact workload bytes without putting source identifiers in the report.

The report measures two scopes. **Whole operation** includes source validation, copying, the policy, mutation checks, output validation and JSON encoding. **Policy plus encoding** adds the measured policy call to JSON encoding and byte counting; it excludes those validation and copying steps. Both exclude disk I/O. Warmup exercises the same operation before measured samples. Keep every elapsed sample for both scopes instead of reporting only the fastest. With fewer than 20 samples, the summary calls its largest observation the maximum; it does not call it p95. With at least 20 samples, p95 is the nearest-rank sample percentile, still not a stable estimate of production tail latency.

JSON bytes are the direct cost these limits change. Whole-operation time may change little because validation and copying still inspect the complete input. Compare the two scopes before attributing elapsed time to retention. Process allocations, garbage collection, other work on the machine and runtime warmup affect both timings; encoded JSON bytes do not measure the process's total memory use. This local sequential exercise provides no production capacity estimate.

Record which observations disappear under the smaller setting, using tick ranges and counts rather than copying discarded identifiers. A smaller file is only useful if the evidence it keeps can still support the question being asked.

## Reconcile the detector window

Suppose an advisory detector examines the previous 20 ticks, while the export retains only the previous 8 ticks. At tick 40, relevant observations occurred at ticks 23, 29 and 37. In `response.md`, explain which observations remain in the export, which past threshold decision cannot be independently recomputed from it, and how a count limit could discard more evidence. Distinguish the detector's live causal state from what an auditor can establish using this export alone.

Explain what separate policy would govern any live rate-limit state or another saved copy. This is an ungraded design review; preserve your first answer and append repairs. ```md
# Retention author and integration notes

The learner implements `retain(events, {nowTick,maxAgeTicks,maxEvents})`. Inputs are validated and sorted. The age window is exclusive on the old edge and inclusive at now; then keep the newest count in stable input order and create exactly `{tick,actorId,reason,distanceSquared}`. Input validation is intentionally outside the assessed pure policy; the owner helper validates its own integration boundary. No dependency on the evaluation module is needed.

`template.mjs`, `prompt.json`, `LEARNER.md` and `response-template.md` are learner inputs. Keep reference `policy.mjs`, `fixtures.mjs` and `controls.mjs` out of the editable solution slot. The parent integration owns registry, prepare/check commands and browser views. The guide uses that shared runner contract; it does not introduce another attempt store.

Exports:

- `fixtures.mjs`: `cases()` and async `assess(candidate) -> {passed,criteria}`. Each failed criterion contains `message`, `expected`, `actual` and a `LEARNER.md` source. Synthetic extra field values are redacted from failure displays. Eight annotated wrong controls and two separately structured correct controls calibrate it.
- `store.mjs`: `validateEvents(events)`, `validateSettings(settings)`, `buildExport(events,settings,{policy=retain,maxBytes=1048576,measure=false}={}) -> {payload,json,summary}`. Source arrays have at most `MAX_SOURCE_EVENTS=100000`; ticks and limits use safe integers; actor ID/reason strings have 1–128 characters. Unknown source fields are discarded by the policy. Output validation checks four fields, age/count, source values and stable subsequence order; the assessment additionally checks newest selection. `payload` has `{schema:1,kind:'minimized-denial-events',settings,events}`; newline-terminated UTF-8 `json` is what byte counts measure. Summary contains only settings, counts, byte length and limit. When `measure:true`, the return value also has `timings:{policyMs,encodeMs,policyAndEncodeMs}`. Policy and encoding are timed separately, leaving input/output validation, cloning and mutation checks outside their sum. Encoding includes UTF-8 byte counting.
- `writeExport(path,events,settings,options={}) -> Promise<receipt>` applies `buildExport` and writes exactly one new file, mode 0600, with exclusive creation. Its parent directory must already exist. Existing destinations and oversize output are refused. The receipt adds absolute `path`, `kind` and SHA-256. No source file or backup is written.
- `deleteExport(receipt) -> Promise<{path,deleted,jsonBytes,scope}>` deletes that unchanged regular file after checking its digest. It refuses missing, changed or symbolic-link paths. It does not delete other copies, other exports, learner evidence or checkpoints. This local helper is not a secure concurrent file replacement protocol or a forensic disk-erasure guarantee.
- `measure.mjs`: `createSyntheticWorkload(eventCount=4096) -> {name:'courier-denials-v1',version:1,events}` and `measureRetention({workload,settings,warmup=2,samples=5,policy=retain}={})`. `settings` is an array of 2–16 setting objects; defaults compare age/count 2048/1024 and 256/128 at the workload's final tick. Warmup is 0–100, samples 1–100. Schema 2 reports echo the selected `settings`, `warmup` and `samples`. Each run retains its `elapsedMs` and `jsonByteSamples` fields and adds raw `policyMs`, `encodeMs`, and `policyAndEncodeMs` arrays. `timingSummary.wholeOperation` summarizes `elapsedMs`; `timingSummary.policyAndEncode` summarizes the narrower sum. Both contain `{sampleCount,medianMs,maxMs,p95Ms,tailStatistic,tailMs}`. Below 20 samples, `p95Ms` is null, `tailStatistic` is `max` and `tailMs` is the observed maximum. At 20 or more samples, `p95Ms` uses nearest rank, `tailStatistic` is `p95` and `tailMs` is that sample percentile; this does not establish a population tail estimate. `summarizeTimings(values)` computes that summary without mutating its input. Reports include workload SHA-256, retained count, Node version, platform and architecture, and no event identifiers or source values. Source events are synthesized and kept only in memory.
- `feedback.mjs`: `postCheckFeedback()` returns keyed prediction answers, reasons, teaching links and fresh variant questions. The owner releases it only after capturing the submitted response; it is not part of a fresh workspace and does not claim to grade prose. `reviewerFeedback()` separately returns fresh-variant answers, the reconciliation key and a transfer rubric/reference design for advisory review. Do not display reviewer material in ordinary check feedback.

Example integration from the project directory, after selecting the submitted policy:

```js
import { writeExport, deleteExport } from './retention/store.mjs';
import { createSyntheticWorkload, measureRetention } from './retention/measure.mjs';
import { retain } from './retention/policy.mjs';

const workload = createSyntheticWorkload();
const settings = [
  { nowTick: 4095, maxAgeTicks: 2048, maxEvents: 1024 },
  { nowTick: 4095, maxAgeTicks: 256, maxEvents: 128 },
];
const report = measureRetention({ workload, settings, warmup: 2, samples: 5, policy: retain });
const receipt = await writeExport('/existing/scratch/denials.json', workload.events, settings[1], { policy: retain });
const deletion = await deleteExport(receipt);
// Persist report, receipt and deletion if wanted; do not persist workload.events.
```

Retained actor IDs remain pseudonymous behavior. This export is not an anonymous data set and is not a causal replay checkpoint. Shrinking it may make a prior detector decision unreconstructable from the export even while the live detector has state supporting its own decision. JSON bytes are the directly changed cost: whole-operation timing may be dominated by validating and cloning the same input. JSON size is not total process memory; local sequential elapsed samples do not establish production capacity. No timing threshold appears in the tests.

Run from the project directory:

```sh
node --test tests/retention.test.mjs
```

Tests exercise real scratch-file creation and deletion, unchanged neighboring exports, byte bounds, report omission of source data and calibration. This source-only module has no UI; desktop/mobile rendering, shared CLI integration and cold-reader review remain integration acceptance work.

Course-craft trace: `assessment-03` links the outcome to executable source; `assessment-09` is covered by two correct and eight intended wrong controls; `feedback-07` supplies expected/actual behavior and repair links; predictions and appended response history support `practice-08` and attempt preservation. Post-capture keys and fresh questions support `feedback-02` and `practice-10`. Transfer remains ungraded advisory review with a separate rubric and reference design (`assessment-02`, `assessment-15`). Measurement scopes and small-sample labels address `evaluation-02`; no test is a claim of human learning (`evaluation-01`).

`courses/anti-cheat-engineering/courier-lab/retention/controls.mjs`:

```mjs
const project = ({ tick, actorId, reason, distanceSquared }) => ({ tick, actorId, reason, distanceSquared });
const eligible = (event, settings) => event.tick > settings.nowTick - settings.maxAgeTicks && event.tick <= settings.nowTick;
const filtered = (events, settings) => events.filter((event) => eligible(event, settings));

// Independently structured implementations; neither imports the reference policy.
export const correctPolicies = [
  { name: 'forward bounded queue', retain(events, settings) {
    const result = [];
    for (const event of events) {
      if (!eligible(event, settings)) continue;
      result.push(project(event));
      if (result.length > settings.maxEvents) result.shift();
    }
    return result;
  } },
  { name: 'reverse scan then restore order', retain(events, settings) {
    const newest = [];
    for (let index = events.length - 1; index >= 0 && newest.length < settings.maxEvents; index -= 1) {
      const event = events[index];
      if (event.tick > settings.nowTick || event.tick <= settings.nowTick - settings.maxAgeTicks) continue;
      newest.push({ tick: event.tick, actorId: event.actorId, reason: event.reason, distanceSquared: event.distanceSquared });
    }
    return newest.reverse();
  } },
];

export const wrongPolicies = [
  { name: 'include old boundary', intended: 'exclude the old edge', retain: (events, settings) => events.filter((event) => event.tick >= settings.nowTick - settings.maxAgeTicks && event.tick <= settings.nowTick).slice(-settings.maxEvents).map(project) },
  { name: 'retain future events', intended: 'exclude the old edge', retain: (events, settings) => events.filter((event) => event.tick > settings.nowTick - settings.maxAgeTicks).slice(-settings.maxEvents).map(project) },
  { name: 'keep oldest count', intended: 'keep the newest count', retain: (events, settings) => filtered(events, settings).slice(0, settings.maxEvents).map(project) },
  { name: 'copy excluded fields', intended: 'retain exactly the four', retain: (events, settings) => filtered(events, settings).slice(-settings.maxEvents).map((event) => ({ ...event })) },
  { name: 'delete source fields in place', intended: 'source unchanged', retain(events, settings) {
    const result = filtered(events, settings).slice(-settings.maxEvents);
    for (const event of result) {
      delete event.capability;
      delete event.address;
      delete event.device;
    }
    return result;
  } },
  { name: 'ignore count limit', intended: 'keep the newest count', retain: (events, settings) => filtered(events, settings).map(project) },
  { name: 'reverse equal-tick order', intended: 'equal-tick order', retain: (events, settings) => filtered(events, settings).reverse().slice(0, settings.maxEvents).map(project) },
  { name: 'round measured distance', intended: 'retain exactly the four', retain: (events, settings) => filtered(events, settings).slice(-settings.maxEvents).map((event) => ({ ...project(event), distanceSquared: Math.round(event.distanceSquared) })) },
];

import { isDeepStrictEqual } from 'node:util';

const event = (tick, actorId = `actor-${tick}`, reason = 'range', distanceSquared = 640_000) => ({
  tick, actorId, reason, distanceSquared,
  capability: 'synthetic-capability-example', address: 'synthetic-address-example', device: 'synthetic-device-example',
});
const kept = (tick, actorId = `actor-${tick}`, reason = 'range', distanceSquared = 640_000) => ({ tick, actorId, reason, distanceSquared });

/** Visible synthetic checks. The expected results do not call the reference policy. */
export function cases() {
  return [
    { name: 'empty input stays empty', events: [], settings: { nowTick: 10, maxAgeTicks: 4, maxEvents: 3 }, expected: [], section: 'the-contract' },
    { name: 'zero is a valid current tick', events: [event(0), event(1)], settings: { nowTick: 0, maxAgeTicks: 1, maxEvents: 2 }, expected: [kept(0)], section: 'the-tick-window' },
    { name: 'exclude the old edge and include now', events: [event(7), event(8), event(9), event(12), event(13)], settings: { nowTick: 12, maxAgeTicks: 4, maxEvents: 9 }, expected: [kept(9), kept(12)], section: 'the-tick-window' },
    { name: 'keep the newest count after filtering', events: [event(1), event(4), event(6), event(8), event(9), event(11)], settings: { nowTick: 9, maxAgeTicks: 6, maxEvents: 2 }, expected: [kept(8), kept(9)], section: 'the-count-bound' },
    { name: 'equal-tick order is stable at the count cut', events: [event(5, 'first'), event(5, 'second'), event(5, 'third'), event(6, 'fourth')], settings: { nowTick: 6, maxAgeTicks: 2, maxEvents: 3 }, expected: [kept(5, 'second'), kept(5, 'third'), kept(6, 'fourth')], section: 'the-count-bound' },
    { name: 'sparse input needs no gap filling', events: [event(2), event(30), event(80)], settings: { nowTick: 70, maxAgeTicks: 60, maxEvents: 4 }, expected: [kept(30)], section: 'the-tick-window' },
    { name: 'retain exactly the four allowed values', events: [event(10, 'synthetic-blue', 'cooldown', 0), event(11, 'synthetic-red', 'range', 562_500.25)], settings: { nowTick: 11, maxAgeTicks: 5, maxEvents: 5 }, expected: [kept(10, 'synthetic-blue', 'cooldown', 0), kept(11, 'synthetic-red', 'range', 562_500.25)], section: 'four-fields-only' },
    { name: 'all old or future events leave no export events', events: [event(1), event(3), event(9)], settings: { nowTick: 8, maxAgeTicks: 5, maxEvents: 1 }, expected: [], section: 'the-tick-window' },
  ];
}

function evidence(value) {
  const seen = new WeakSet();
  try {
    return JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(value, (key, item) => {
      if (['capability', 'address', 'device'].includes(key)) return '<excluded field; value redacted>';
      if (item === undefined) return { type: 'undefined' };
      if (typeof item === 'number' && !Number.isFinite(item)) return { type: 'number', value: String(item) };
      if (['function', 'symbol', 'bigint'].includes(typeof item)) return { type: typeof item };
      if (!item || typeof item !== 'object') return item;
      if (seen.has(item)) return { type: 'repeated or circular reference' };
      seen.add(item);
      return item;
    }));
  } catch {
    return { type: 'unserializable result' };
  }
}

/** Expected/actual feedback describes the violated requirement and its teaching source. */
export async function assess(candidate) {
  if (typeof candidate?.retain !== 'function') return { passed: false, criteria: [{ name: 'export retain(events, settings)', passed: false, error: {
    message: 'Export the retain function declared in the contract.', expected: 'function', actual: typeof candidate?.retain, source: 'LEARNER.md#the-contract',
  } }] };
  const criteria = [];
  for (const item of cases()) {
    const events = structuredClone(item.events);
    const settings = { ...item.settings };
    let actual;
    try {
      actual = await candidate.retain(events, settings);
      const passed = isDeepStrictEqual(actual, item.expected);
      const criterion = { name: item.name, passed };
      if (!passed) criterion.error = { message: `The result violates this requirement: ${item.name}.`, expected: item.expected, actual: evidence(actual), source: `LEARNER.md#${item.section}` };
      criteria.push(criterion);
    } catch (error) {
      criteria.push({ name: item.name, passed: false, error: {
        message: 'Return a retained array for these validated inputs.', expected: item.expected, actual: { threw: String(error?.message ?? error) }, source: `LEARNER.md#${item.section}`,
      } });
    }
    const unchanged = { eventsUnchanged: isDeepStrictEqual(events, item.events), settingsUnchanged: isDeepStrictEqual(settings, item.settings) };
    const passed = unchanged.eventsUnchanged && unchanged.settingsUnchanged;
    const criterion = { name: `${item.name}: source unchanged`, passed };
    if (!passed) criterion.error = { message: 'Keep the original events and settings available for their original purpose.', expected: { eventsUnchanged: true, settingsUnchanged: true }, actual: unchanged, source: 'LEARNER.md#four-fields-only' };
    criteria.push(criterion);
  }
  return { passed: criteria.every(({ passed }) => passed), criteria };
}

`courses/anti-cheat-engineering/courier-lab/retention/measure.mjs`:

```mjs
import { performance } from 'node:perf_hooks';
import { createHash } from 'node:crypto';
import { buildExport, validateEvents, validateSettings, MAX_SOURCE_EVENTS } from './store.mjs';
import { retain } from './policy.mjs';

export const WORKLOAD_NAME = 'courier-denials-v1';

/** A small run has an observed maximum, not a useful tail percentile estimate. */
export function summarizeTimings(values) {
  if (!Array.isArray(values) || values.length < 1 || values.some((value) => !Number.isFinite(value) || value < 0)) throw new TypeError('Timings must be a nonempty array of finite nonnegative milliseconds.');
  const sorted = [...values].sort((left, right) => left - right);
  const middle = Math.floor(sorted.length / 2);
  const medianMs = sorted.length % 2 === 0 ? (sorted[middle - 1] + sorted[middle]) / 2 : sorted[middle];
  const maxMs = sorted.at(-1);
  const p95Ms = sorted.length >= 20 ? sorted[Math.ceil(sorted.length * 0.95) - 1] : null;
  return { sampleCount: sorted.length, medianMs, maxMs, p95Ms, tailStatistic: p95Ms === null ? 'max' : 'p95', tailMs: p95Ms ?? maxMs };
}

/** Synthetic source fields are examples, never credentials or captured traffic. */
export function createSyntheticWorkload(eventCount = 4096) {
  if (!Number.isSafeInteger(eventCount) || eventCount < 1 || eventCount > MAX_SOURCE_EVENTS) throw new RangeError(`eventCount must be 1–${MAX_SOURCE_EVENTS}.`);
  const events = Array.from({ length: eventCount }, (_, tick) => ({
    tick, actorId: `synthetic-actor-${tick % 8}`, reason: tick % 4 === 0 ? 'cooldown' : 'range',
    distanceSquared: 562_500 + (tick % 31) * 10_000,
    capability: `synthetic-example-${tick % 8}`, address: `synthetic-address-${tick % 8}`, device: `synthetic-device-${tick % 3}`,
  }));
  return { name: WORKLOAD_NAME, version: 1, events };
}

/** Measure this local sequential operation; no wall-time threshold is implied. */
export function measureRetention({ workload = createSyntheticWorkload(), settings, warmup = 2, samples = 5, policy = retain } = {}) {
  if (workload?.name !== WORKLOAD_NAME || workload.version !== 1) throw new TypeError(`Use the named ${WORKLOAD_NAME} workload.`);
  validateEvents(workload.events);
  if (!Number.isSafeInteger(warmup) || warmup < 0 || warmup > 100) throw new RangeError('warmup must be 0–100.');
  if (!Number.isSafeInteger(samples) || samples < 1 || samples > 100) throw new RangeError('samples must be 1–100.');
  const nowTick = workload.events.at(-1)?.tick ?? 0;
  const settingsList = settings ?? [
    { nowTick, maxAgeTicks: 2048, maxEvents: 1024 },
    { nowTick, maxAgeTicks: 256, maxEvents: 128 },
  ];
  if (!Array.isArray(settingsList) || settingsList.length < 2 || settingsList.length > 16) throw new RangeError('Compare 2–16 settings.');
  const selectedSettings = settingsList.map(validateSettings);
  const runs = selectedSettings.map((setting) => {
    for (let index = 0; index < warmup; index += 1) buildExport(workload.events, setting, { policy, measure: true });
    const elapsedMs = [];
    const policyMs = [];
    const encodeMs = [];
    const policyAndEncodeMs = [];
    const jsonByteSamples = [];
    let summary;
    for (let index = 0; index < samples; index += 1) {
      const start = performance.now();
      const result = buildExport(workload.events, setting, { policy, measure: true });
      elapsedMs.push(performance.now() - start);
      policyMs.push(result.timings.policyMs);
      encodeMs.push(result.timings.encodeMs);
      policyAndEncodeMs.push(result.timings.policyAndEncodeMs);
      jsonByteSamples.push(result.summary.jsonBytes);
      summary = result.summary;
    }
    return { ...summary, elapsedMs, policyMs, encodeMs, policyAndEncodeMs, jsonByteSamples,
      timingSummary: { wholeOperation: summarizeTimings(elapsedMs), policyAndEncode: summarizeTimings(policyAndEncodeMs) } };
  });
  const sourceJson = JSON.stringify(workload.events);
  return {
    schema: 2, kind: 'retention-measurement',
    workload: { name: workload.name, version: workload.version, eventCount: workload.events.length, inputJsonBytes: Buffer.byteLength(sourceJson, 'utf8'), sha256: createHash('sha256').update(sourceJson).digest('hex') },
    environment: { node: process.version, platform: process.platform, arch: process.arch },
    operation: 'Whole operation: validate, clone, retain, validate output and encode JSON; no disk I/O',
    policyAndEncodeOperation: 'Policy call plus JSON encoding and byte counting; excludes source validation, cloning, mutation checks and output validation',
    settings: selectedSettings, warmup, samples, runs,
    limits: 'Local sequential synthetic workload. JSON bytes are the direct cost changed by the limits; whole-operation time can be dominated by fixed validation and cloning. Timings include allocation and garbage-collection noise. Fewer than 20 samples report an observed maximum, not p95; even a reported p95 is only this sample percentile, not a capacity estimate. No production capacity or anonymization claim.',
  };
}

`courses/anti-cheat-engineering/courier-lab/retention/policy.mjs`:

```mjs
/** Retain the newest eligible denial events; inputs have already been validated. */
export function retain(events, { nowTick, maxAgeTicks, maxEvents }) {
  return events
    .filter(({ tick }) => tick > nowTick - maxAgeTicks && tick <= nowTick)
    .slice(-maxEvents)
    .map(({ tick, actorId, reason, distanceSquared }) => ({ tick, actorId, reason, distanceSquared }));
}

`courses/anti-cheat-engineering/courier-lab/retention/store.mjs`:

```mjs
import { createHash } from 'node:crypto';
import { open, lstat, readFile, unlink } from 'node:fs/promises';
import { resolve, dirname, basename } from 'node:path';
import { regularFile } from '../lab/core/trust.mjs';
import { isDeepStrictEqual } from 'node:util';
import { performance } from 'node:perf_hooks';
import { retain } from './policy.mjs';

export const MAX_SOURCE_EVENTS = 100_000;
export const DEFAULT_MAX_EXPORT_BYTES = 1_048_576;
const FIELDS = ['tick', 'actorId', 'reason', 'distanceSquared'];
const digest = (bytes) => createHash('sha256').update(bytes).digest('hex');

export function validateSettings(settings) {
  if (!settings || !Number.isSafeInteger(settings.nowTick) || settings.nowTick < 0) throw new TypeError('nowTick must be a nonnegative safe integer.');
  for (const key of ['maxAgeTicks', 'maxEvents']) {
    if (!Number.isSafeInteger(settings[key]) || settings[key] <= 0) throw new TypeError(`${key} must be a positive safe integer.`);
  }
  return { nowTick: settings.nowTick, maxAgeTicks: settings.maxAgeTicks, maxEvents: settings.maxEvents };
}

function validateEvent(event) {
  if (!event || typeof event !== 'object' || Array.isArray(event)) throw new TypeError('Each source event must be an object.');
  if (!Number.isSafeInteger(event.tick) || event.tick < 0) throw new TypeError('Event ticks must be nonnegative safe integers.');
  for (const key of ['actorId', 'reason']) {
    if (typeof event[key] !== 'string' || event[key].length === 0 || event[key].length > 128) throw new TypeError(`${key} must contain 1–128 characters.`);
  }
  if (!Number.isFinite(event.distanceSquared) || event.distanceSquared < 0) throw new TypeError('distanceSquared must be finite and nonnegative.');
}

export function validateEvents(events) {
  if (!Array.isArray(events) || events.length > MAX_SOURCE_EVENTS) throw new TypeError(`Source events must be an array of at most ${MAX_SOURCE_EVENTS} entries.`);
  let previousTick = -1;
  for (const event of events) {
    validateEvent(event);
    if (event.tick < previousTick) throw new TypeError('Source events must already be in nondecreasing tick order.');
    previousTick = event.tick;
  }
}

function validateOutput(output, source, settings) {
  if (!Array.isArray(output) || output.length > settings.maxEvents) throw new TypeError('Policy output must be an array within maxEvents.');
  let sourceIndex = 0;
  const detached = [];
  for (const original of output) {
    if (!original || typeof original !== 'object' || Reflect.ownKeys(original).length !== FIELDS.length || FIELDS.some((key) => !Object.hasOwn(original, key))) throw new TypeError('Policy output may contain only tick, actorId, reason and distanceSquared.');
    const event = { tick: original.tick, actorId: original.actorId, reason: original.reason, distanceSquared: original.distanceSquared };
    validateEvent(event);
    if (event.tick <= settings.nowTick - settings.maxAgeTicks || event.tick > settings.nowTick) throw new TypeError('Policy output must lie inside the retention window.');
    while (sourceIndex < source.length && !FIELDS.every((key) => source[sourceIndex][key] === event[key])) sourceIndex += 1;
    if (sourceIndex === source.length) throw new TypeError('Policy output must preserve source values and order.');
    sourceIndex += 1;
    detached.push(event);
  }
  return detached;
}

/** Build a minimized artifact in memory. Extra source fields never enter it. */
export function buildExport(events, settings, { policy = retain, maxBytes = DEFAULT_MAX_EXPORT_BYTES, measure = false } = {}) {
  validateEvents(events);
  const selectedSettings = validateSettings(settings);
  if (typeof policy !== 'function') throw new TypeError('policy must be a function.');
  if (!Number.isSafeInteger(maxBytes) || maxBytes < 1) throw new TypeError('maxBytes must be a positive safe integer.');
  const source = structuredClone(events);
  const input = structuredClone(events);
  const policySettings = { ...selectedSettings };
  const policyStart = measure ? performance.now() : 0;
  const retained = policy(input, policySettings);
  const policyMs = measure ? performance.now() - policyStart : 0;
  if (!isDeepStrictEqual(input, source) || !isDeepStrictEqual(policySettings, selectedSettings)) throw new TypeError('Policy must not mutate source events or settings.');
  const output = validateOutput(retained, source, selectedSettings);
  const payload = { schema: 1, kind: 'minimized-denial-events', settings: selectedSettings, events: output };
  const encodeStart = measure ? performance.now() : 0;
  const json = `${JSON.stringify(payload)}\n`;
  const jsonBytes = Buffer.byteLength(json, 'utf8');
  const encodeMs = measure ? performance.now() - encodeStart : 0;
  if (jsonBytes > maxBytes) throw new RangeError(`Export exceeds maxBytes (${jsonBytes} > ${maxBytes}). No export was written.`);
  const result = { payload, json, summary: { settings: selectedSettings, inputCount: events.length, retainedCount: retained.length, removedCount: events.length - retained.length, jsonBytes, maxBytes } };
  if (measure) result.timings = { policyMs, encodeMs, policyAndEncodeMs: policyMs + encodeMs };
  return result;
}

/** Write one new export, without replacing an existing file or making a backup. */
export async function writeExport(path, events, settings, options = {}) {
  const { json, summary } = buildExport(events, settings, options);
  const absolutePath = resolve(path);
  const file = await open(absolutePath, 'wx', 0o600);
  try {
    await file.writeFile(json, 'utf8');
  } catch (error) {
    await file.close();
    await unlink(absolutePath);
    throw error;
  }
  await file.close();
  return { path: absolutePath, kind: 'minimized-denial-events', sha256: digest(json), ...summary };
}

/** Delete only the unchanged export named by a writeExport receipt. */
export async function deleteExport(receipt) {
  if (!receipt || receipt.kind !== 'minimized-denial-events' || typeof receipt.path !== 'string' || !/^[a-f0-9]{64}$/.test(receipt.sha256)) throw new TypeError('Use the receipt returned by writeExport.');
  const info = await lstat(receipt.path);
  if (!info.isFile() || info.isSymbolicLink()) throw new TypeError('The export path must still name a regular file.');
  if (info.size > DEFAULT_MAX_EXPORT_BYTES) throw new RangeError('Export exceeds the deletion read bound.');
  const bytes = await regularFile(dirname(receipt.path), basename(receipt.path));
  if (digest(bytes) !== receipt.sha256) throw new Error('Export bytes changed; refusing to delete a different artifact.');
  await unlink(receipt.path);
  return { path: receipt.path, deleted: true, jsonBytes: bytes.length, scope: 'This export only. Other copies and original records are unaffected.' };
}

import http from 'node:http';
import { readFile } from 'node:fs/promises';
import { randomBytes } from 'node:crypto';
import { performance } from 'node:perf_hooks';
import { snapshot, events, canonical } from './engine.mjs';
import { createRecordedEngine } from './telemetry/runtime.mjs';
import { parseInput } from './protocol.mjs';
import { createClock, TICK_MS } from './clock.mjs';
import { createLearningHandler, createLearningService, LEARNING_ROUTES } from './learning/service.mjs';

const MAX_BODY_BYTES = 512;
const MAX_SESSIONS = 4;
const REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS = 5_000;
const HEADER_TIMEOUT_MS = 6_000;
const ASSETS = new Map([
  ['/learn', ['learn.html', 'text/html; charset=utf-8']],
  ['/learn.html', ['learn.html', 'text/html; charset=utf-8']],
  ['/learn.js', ['learn.js', 'text/javascript; charset=utf-8']],

  ['/evidence.js', ['evidence.js', 'text/javascript; charset=utf-8']],
  ['/prediction-notebook.js', ['prediction-notebook.js', 'text/javascript; charset=utf-8']],
  ['/prediction-notebook.css', ['prediction-notebook.css', 'text/css; charset=utf-8']],
  ['/sources', ['sources.html', 'text/html; charset=utf-8']],
  ['/completion', ['completion.html', 'text/html; charset=utf-8']],
  ['/completion.js', ['completion.js', 'text/javascript; charset=utf-8']],
  ['/samples/completion-cases.json', ['samples/completion-cases.json', 'application/json; charset=utf-8']],
  ['/analysis', ['analysis.html', 'text/html; charset=utf-8']],
  ['/analysis.css', ['analysis.css', 'text/css; charset=utf-8']],
  ['/analysis.js', ['analysis.js', 'text/javascript; charset=utf-8']],
  ['/samples/analysis-cases.json', ['samples/analysis-cases.json', 'application/json; charset=utf-8']],
  ['/course', ['course.html', 'text/html; charset=utf-8']],
  ['/samples/evidence-cases.json', ['samples/evidence-cases.json', 'application/json; charset=utf-8']],
]);
const METHODS = new Map([
  ...LEARNING_ROUTES,
  ...Array.from(ASSETS.keys(), (route) => [route, 'GET']),
  ['/health', 'GET'], ['/state', 'GET'], ['/join', 'POST'], ['/input', 'POST'],
]);
const MUTANTS = new Set(['omit-proximity', 'omit-sequence']);

function numericOption(value, name, maximum) {
  if (!/^(0|[1-9]\d*)$/.test(value ?? '')) throw new Error(`Invalid ${name}.`);
  const number = Number(value);
  if (!Number.isSafeInteger(number) || number > maximum) throw new Error(`Invalid ${name}.`);
  return number;
}

function optionsFrom(argv) {
  const options = { port: 0, seed: 17, test: false };
  const seen = new Set();
  for (let index = 0; index < argv.length; index += 1) {
    const flag = argv[index];
    if (seen.has(flag)) throw new Error('Duplicate option.');
    seen.add(flag);
    if (flag === '--test') {
      options.test = true;
      continue;
    }
    if (flag === '--port') {
      options.port = numericOption(argv[++index], 'port', 65_535);
      continue;
    }
    if (flag === '--seed') {
      options.seed = numericOption(argv[++index], 'seed', Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER);
      continue;
    }
    if (flag === '--mutant') {
      options.mutant = argv[++index];
      if (!MUTANTS.has(options.mutant)) throw new Error('Unknown mutant.');
      continue;
    }
    throw new Error('Unknown option.');
  }
  if (options.test && (typeof process.send !== 'function' || !process.connected)) throw new Error('--test requires parent IPC.');
  if (options.mutant && !options.test) throw new Error('Mutants require --test and parent IPC.');
  return options;
}

function headerValues(request, name) {
  const values = [];
  for (let index = 0; index < request.rawHeaders.length; index += 2) {
    if (request.rawHeaders[index].toLowerCase() === name) values.push(request.rawHeaders[index + 1]);
  }
  return values;
}

function originAllowed(request, port) {
  const hosts = new Set([`127.0.0.1:${port}`, `localhost:${port}`]);
  const host = headerValues(request, 'host');
  if (host.length !== 1 || !hosts.has(host[0])) return false;
  const origin = headerValues(request, 'origin');
  const origins = new Set(Array.from(hosts, (value) => `http://${value}`));
  return origin.length === 0 || (origin.length === 1 && origins.has(origin[0]));
}

function json(response, status, body, extraHeaders = {}) {
  if (response.destroyed || response.writableEnded) return;
  const bytes = Buffer.from(JSON.stringify(body));
  response.writeHead(status, {
    'content-type': 'application/json; charset=utf-8',
    'content-length': bytes.length,
    'cache-control': 'no-store',
    'x-content-type-options': 'nosniff',
    ...extraHeaders,
  });
  response.end(bytes);
}

function failure(status, reason) {
  return Object.assign(new Error(reason), { status, reason });
}

function hasBody(request) {
  return request.headers['transfer-encoding'] !== undefined || request.headers['content-length'] !== undefined && request.headers['content-length'] !== '0';
}

function requireJson(request) {
  const values = headerValues(request, 'content-type');
  if (values.length !== 1 || !/^application\/json(?:\s*;\s*charset=utf-8)?$/i.test(values[0])) {
    throw failure(415, 'content-type');
  }
}

function readBody(request) {
  const declared = request.headers['content-length'];
  if (declared !== undefined && (!/^\d+$/.test(declared) || Number(declared) > MAX_BODY_BYTES)) {
    throw failure(413, 'body-too-large');
  }
  return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
    const chunks = [];
    let length = 0;
    let finished = false;
    const timer = setTimeout(() => finish(failure(408, 'request-timeout')), REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS);
    const onData = (chunk) => {
      length += chunk.length;
      if (length > MAX_BODY_BYTES) return finish(failure(413, 'body-too-large'));
      chunks.push(chunk);
    };
    const onEnd = () => finish(null, Buffer.concat(chunks).toString('utf8'));
    const onError = () => finish(failure(400, 'incomplete-body'));
    function finish(error, text) {
      if (finished) return;
      finished = true;
      clearTimeout(timer);
      request.off('data', onData);
      request.off('end', onEnd);
      request.off('error', onError);
      request.off('aborted', onError);
      if (error) return reject(error);
      resolve(text);
    }
    request.on('data', onData);
    request.once('end', onEnd);
    request.once('error', onError);
    request.once('aborted', onError);
  });
}

function actorFor(request, sessions) {
  const values = headerValues(request, 'authorization');
  if (values.length !== 1) throw failure(401, 'unauthorized');
  const match = /^Bearer ([A-Za-z0-9_-]{43})$/.exec(values[0]);
  const id = match && sessions.get(match[1]);
  if (!id) throw failure(401, 'unauthorized');
  return id;
}

function validJoinBody(text) {
  if (text.length === 0) return true;
  try {
    const value = JSON.parse(text);
    return value !== null && !Array.isArray(value) && typeof value === 'object' && Object.keys(value).length === 0;
  } catch {
    return false;
  }
}

function ownerRequest(message) {
  if (!message || typeof message !== 'object' || Array.isArray(message)) return false;
  const id = message.requestId;
  const validId = typeof id === 'string' && id.length > 0 && id.length <= 128 || Number.isSafeInteger(id) && id >= 0;
  if (!validId) return false;
  const keys = Object.keys(message).sort().join(',');
  if (message.type === 'advance') return keys === 'requestId,ticks,type' && Number.isSafeInteger(message.ticks) && message.ticks >= 1 && message.ticks <= 100;
  return ['record', 'window', 'shutdown'].includes(message.type) && keys === 'requestId,type';
}

function sendOwner(message) {
  if (!process.connected || typeof process.send !== 'function') return Promise.resolve();
  return new Promise((resolve) => process.send(message, () => resolve()));
}

async function main() {
  const options = optionsFrom(process.argv.slice(2));
  const recording = createRecordedEngine(options.seed, options.mutant ? { mutant: options.mutant } : {});
  const world = recording.world;
  const sessions = new Map();
  const transport = [];
  let port;
  let timer;
  let closing = false;
  const learning = createLearningHandler(createLearningService());
  const tick = () => canonical(world).tick;
  const logTransport = (route, status, reason) => {
    transport.push({ tick: tick(), route: METHODS.has(route) ? route : 'unknown', status, reason });
    if (transport.length > 128) transport.shift();
  };

  async function handle(request, response) {
    const route = request.url;
    try {
      if (closing) throw failure(503, 'shutting-down');
      if (!originAllowed(request, port)) throw failure(403, 'host-or-origin');
      const method = METHODS.get(route);
      if (!method) throw failure(404, 'not-found');
      if (request.method !== method) {
        json(response, 405, { error: 'method-not-allowed' }, { allow: method });
        logTransport(route, 405, 'method-not-allowed');
        request.resume();
        return;
      }
      if (method === 'GET' && hasBody(request)) throw failure(400, 'unexpected-body');
      if (LEARNING_ROUTES.has(route)) return await learning(request, response);
      if (route === '/health') return json(response, 200, { ok: true, tick: tick() });
      if (route === '/state') return json(response, 200, snapshot(world, actorFor(request, sessions)));
      if (route === '/input') {
        const id = actorFor(request, sessions);
        requireJson(request);
        const parsed = parseInput(await readBody(request));
        if (!parsed.ok) throw failure(400, parsed.reason);
        const decision = recording.admit(id, parsed.input);
        logTransport(route, 200, decision.status);
        return json(response, 200, decision);
      }
      if (route === '/join') {
        if (hasBody(request) || request.headers['content-type'] !== undefined) requireJson(request);
        if (!validJoinBody(await readBody(request))) throw failure(400, 'join-body');
        if (sessions.size >= MAX_SESSIONS) throw failure(429, 'session-limit');
        const actor = recording.join();
        const token = randomBytes(32).toString('base64url');
        sessions.set(token, actor.id);
        logTransport(route, 201, 'joined');
        return json(response, 201, { id: actor.id, token });
      }
      const [file, type] = ASSETS.get(route);
      const bytes = await readFile(new URL(`./public/${file}`, import.meta.url));
      response.writeHead(200, { 'content-type': type, 'content-length': bytes.length, 'cache-control': 'no-store', 'x-content-type-options': 'nosniff' });
      response.end(bytes);
    } catch (error) {
      const status = error.status ?? 500;
      const reason = error.reason ?? 'internal-error';
      logTransport(route, status, reason);
      json(response, status, { error: reason });
      request.resume();
    }
  }

  // Node validates these two options together in its constructor. Set their
  // independent contract values afterwards; body reads also have a hard deadline.
  const server = http.createServer({ maxHeaderSize: 8_192, connectionsCheckingInterval: 1_000 }, (request, response) => {
    // An aborted body can emit an error after the body promise has settled.
    request.on('error', () => {});
    void handle(request, response);
  });
  server.requestTimeout = REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS;
  server.headersTimeout = HEADER_TIMEOUT_MS;
  server.keepAliveTimeout = REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS;
  server.maxConnections = 32;

  async function shutdown(code = 0, reply) {
    if (closing) return;
    closing = true;
    clearInterval(timer);
    if (reply) await sendOwner(reply);
    await new Promise((resolve) => {
      server.close(resolve);
      server.closeAllConnections();
    });
    process.exit(code);
  }

  process.once('SIGTERM', () => void shutdown());
  process.once('SIGINT', () => void shutdown());
  process.once('disconnect', () => void shutdown());
  await new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
    server.once('error', reject);
    server.listen(options.port, '127.0.0.1', resolve);
  });
  port = server.address().port;
  server.removeAllListeners('error');
  server.on('error', () => {
    process.stderr.write('Server failure.\n');
    void shutdown(1);
  });
  if (!options.test) {
    const clock = createClock(performance.now());
    timer = setInterval(() => {
      try {
        const { ticks } = clock.sample(performance.now());
        if (ticks > 0) recording.advance(ticks);
      } catch {
        process.stderr.write('Clock failure.\n');
        void shutdown(1);
      }
    }, TICK_MS);
  }

  if (options.test) process.on('message', async (message) => {
    if (closing) return;
    if (!ownerRequest(message)) {
      const requestId = typeof message?.requestId === 'string' || Number.isSafeInteger(message?.requestId) ? message.requestId : null;
      await sendOwner({ requestId, ok: false, error: 'invalid-owner-message' });
      return;
    }
    try {
      if (message.type === 'advance') recording.advance(message.ticks);
      if (message.type === 'window') {
        await sendOwner({ requestId: message.requestId, ok: true, window: recording.window() });
        return;
      }
      if (message.type === 'record') {
        await sendOwner({ requestId: message.requestId, ok: true, record: events(world) });
        return;
      }
      if (message.type === 'shutdown') {
        await shutdown(0, { requestId: message.requestId, ok: true, tick: tick() });
        return;
      }
      await sendOwner({ requestId: message.requestId, ok: true, tick: tick() });
    } catch {
      await sendOwner({ requestId: message.requestId, ok: false, error: 'owner-operation-failed' });
    }
  });

  const ready = { type: 'ready', port };
  process.stdout.write(`${JSON.stringify(ready)}\n`);
  if (!options.test) process.stdout.write(`Open http://127.0.0.1:${port}/learn for the guided course.\n`);
  await sendOwner(ready);
}

main().catch((error) => {
  process.stderr.write(`Server startup failed: ${error.message}\n`);
  process.exit(1);
});

`courses/anti-cheat-engineering/courier-lab/telemetry/LEARNER.md`:

```md
# M6: Reproduce a bounded history

Implementation reference for **M6: causal replay**. Start with [the guided learning route at `/learn`](/learn) on the reference server, then return here for the exact source contract. This Markdown file does not submit answers or certify mastery. Use the [support and attempt workflow](../learning-support/README.md) for worked siblings, gradual guidance and help recording. A prepared source workspace need not serve `/learn`; keep the reference server open for that route.

Implement a policy that decides whether one recorded window reproduces its claimed final gameplay state. A screenshot of a score is not enough: the replay needs both the state before the window and every operation inside it.

From the reference project run `npm run core:prepare -- telemetry`. In the printed workspace, fill the required answers or explicit skip reasons in `predictions.json`, edit `telemetry/policy.mjs`, and keep explanations in `response.md`. Then run `npm run core:check -- --assistance "none"` (or describe the help used). The checker captures your exact files and records first and revised attempts separately. A passing run establishes agreement with these cases; it does not establish production security or learning gains.

## The contract

Your function is `replayWindow(record, engine)`. It returns either `{ok:true,state}` or `{ok:false,reason}`. `state` is the canonical gameplay result produced by the supplied engine.

A **checkpoint** is enough private game state to continue execution: actor positions and scores, movement intent, pending interactions, expiry, cooldown and detector history. A public snapshot omits some of this state. A **window** combines a checkpoint with a bounded sequence of later operations. This lets the recorder replace older history without pretending that the game began again at its initial position.

The record has eight fields:

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `schema` | Envelope version; only `1` is supported. |
| `runtimeRelease` | Rules used for this record; must equal `engine.release`. |
| `startIndex` | Absolute index of the last operation before this window. |
| `checkpoint` | State immediately after `startIndex`, before the first retained operation. |
| `events` | Up to 256 entries, each exactly `{index,event}`. |
| `endIndex` | Absolute index of the last retained operation; equal to `startIndex` for an empty window. |
| `complete` | Must be `true`; the producer claims no gap inside this window. |
| `final` | Claimed canonical state after all retained operations. |

Refuse unexpected envelope fields. A checkpoint does not contain a bearer token, a password or the old event log. Do not add those fields to a record.

## Complete windows

The recorder takes a new checkpoint **before** the next operation would exceed its capacity. It then records that operation as the first entry in the new window. The old window is replaced; the new window is complete on its own.

```text
older operations ... 40 | checkpoint | operation 41 | operation 42 | final
                  startIndex = 40                      endIndex = 42
```

There are two retained operations here. The checkpoint represents the world after operation 40. Replaying starts from that checkpoint, not from a newly seeded empty world. A zero-event window is also meaningful: restore the checkpoint and compare it directly with `final`.

The event array must exist, contain at most 256 entries and have `complete:true`. Return `incomplete` if any of those requirements fails. Capacity is a storage bound, not a reason to silently accept only the tail of an incomplete record.

## Absolute order

`startIndex` and `endIndex` are nonnegative safe integers. For the example above, the entry indices must be `41,42`, in that order, and `endIndex` must be `42`. Each entry contains only `index` and `event`.

Return `sequence` for missing, repeated or reordered indices, invalid boundaries, an invalid indexed entry or an end boundary that disagrees with the array length. Do not sort entries, renumber them, fill a gap or drop a stale input. A stale input can leave the gameplay state unchanged while still being part of the observed operation history. Final-state equality alone cannot reveal its removal.

Before editing, save the required predictions in `predictions.json` and keep your explanation in `response.md`. Explain why a reordered pair can be invalid even when both operations happen to produce the same final state.

## Causal state

The supplied facade has five members:

| Member | Use |
| --- | --- |
| `release` | Supported runtime release string. |
| `restore(checkpoint)` | Return a fresh mutable game world; throw if the checkpoint is invalid. |
| `apply(world,event)` | Apply one operation; throw if the event is invalid. |
| `canonical(world)` | Return detached public gameplay state. |
| `equal(left,right)` | Compare JSON values, ignoring object key order. |

Events are `join`, `input` and `tick`. Each tick is one recorded operation. Valid input includes requests that the engine classifies as stale. The facade owns their detailed schemas and limits, so use it instead of implementing another movement or detector model in your policy.

For example, an actor may have staged an interaction before a rollover. If the checkpoint saved only the public position, the first retained tick would lose that interaction. Similarly, two retained detector observations may cause the next denied interaction to produce a finding. Resetting the detector during restore changes that result.

Catch checkpoint or event failures and return `event`. Never continue after a failed application, since you no longer have a reproduction of the supplied history.

## Final comparison

After restoring and applying all entries, compute `engine.canonical(world)` and compare it with `record.final` through `engine.equal`. Return `final` if the final state is absent or differs. Report success with the state you computed, rather than copying the claim in `record.final`.

Check in this order: schema, release, completeness, sequence, checkpoint/events, then final comparison. Return `schema` for an unsupported schema or unexpected envelope field, and `incompatible` for a release mismatch. This order makes a failure reproducible when a record has more than one defect.

## Capture and replay a real session

First isolate the policy decisions, then inspect a real captured window.

## Build in three checked milestones

1. **Validate the envelope and sequence.** In the worked `startIndex=40` window above, only indices 41 and 42 are permitted. Completion: a window starts at 70 and has three events; fill its required indices and end boundary. Decide the failure phase if the middle index is repeated. Do this before calling the engine.
2. **Restore and apply.** Use the supplied facade to restore one checkpoint and apply each retained event in its given order. A zero-event window still restores; it does not construct a fresh initial world. Stop at a failed restore or event instead of comparing a partial execution with the claimed final state.
3. **Compare computed state.** Return the state obtained from `canonical`, not the input's claim. Use the first failed core criterion to separate an invalid record from valid execution whose final claim is wrong. Preserve the input objects while testing.

<details><summary>Hint 1 — identify the starting world</summary>

The checkpoint already includes the effects before the retained window. Recreating an empty world loses intent and history that the first event may depend on.

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 2 — separate order from outcome</summary>

Validate absolute indices before execution. Two stale inputs may produce the same final gameplay state in either order, while only the recorded order is a valid reproduction.

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 3 — worked sibling, after a saved attempt</summary>

For the window beginning after operation 40, two retained operations require indices 41 and 42 and `endIndex:42`. A record containing 41 and 43 fails `sequence` even if the final score happens to match. Record this as assistance, then implement the general bounds and application loop independently.

</details>

## Run a real capture

From the reference project run `npm run trace:sample -- artifacts/session-window.json`, then `npm run window:replay -- artifacts/session-window.json`. The capture script drives the actual server over HTTP and obtains a record through its owner-only test channel. The normal game has no HTTP time or export route. The replay runs a separate deterministic world; it does not change a live player's state.

Keep the original record. In a new copy, remove an event, duplicate an index or change the final score and run the replay command again. Name the failure phase before examining the verdict. A refused record means the supplied evidence could not support this replay, not that a person cheated.

## Repair and scope

Each failed criterion names a requirement and shows expected and observed results. Follow its section link, inspect the condition your code accepted or rejected, and append your repair explanation to `response.md`. Run again with the actual help you used. Keep your first prediction and first attempt available.

Browser playback is a teaching aid. The owner-side checker replays through the real engine. Neither one authenticates the producer of the record: someone who can rewrite both the checkpoint and its claimed final state may produce a different internally consistent history. Replay also does not prove token ownership, actual network timing, packet order or a trustworthy wall clock. Those need evidence outside this deterministic window.

The response template ends with a new repair-station scenario. Use it to explain which facts belong in a checkpoint and which claims replay cannot settle; it is a review prompt, not an automatically scored proof of transfer.

## Capture, compare and try a fresh case

In a newly prepared workspace, put the required first answers in `predictions.json`; use `response.md` for explanations and later repairs. Keep each question ID and its wording unchanged. Fill an `answer` or an explicit `skipReason` for every question before the first source check. A blank row refuses feedback rather than silently recording an empty attempt. The guide's additional trace questions are practice notes, not extra required JSON fields.

After a check accepts and captures the submission, inspect its `prediction-feedback.json` beside the result. Compare your first answer with the answer and governing reason, then append a correction without erasing the original. Complete the new `fresh-practice.json` answers or skip reasons and run `npm run core:practice -- --assistance "none"` from that workspace, replacing `none` with actual help. The practice command records your response before revealing its feedback. These prose responses are preserved and ungraded; they are separate from source-check results and `/learn` mastery.

Use the scripts generated in your workspace. Older prepared workspaces may retain the earlier response-only format; do not replace their original records with new templates. Record any worked-example views, final hints, reference code or AI help in your assistance declaration.
