`courses/anti-cheat-engineering/courier-lab/tests/telemetry.test.mjs`:

```mjs
import test from 'node:test';
import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
import { createWorld, join, admit, advance, canonical, events, replay } from '../engine.mjs';
import { createDetector } from '../defense.mjs';
import { capture, restore, createRecordedEngine, createReplayEngine, equal, RUNTIME_RELEASE } from '../telemetry/runtime.mjs';
import { replayWindow } from '../telemetry/policy.mjs';
import { assess, cases } from '../telemetry/fixtures.mjs';
import { correctPolicies, wrongPolicies } from '../telemetry/controls.mjs';
import * as template from '../telemetry/template.mjs';

const input = (seq, move = 'idle', interact = false) => ({ v: 1, seq, move, interact });
const clone = (value) => JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(value));
const facade = createReplayEngine();

function replayWorld(record) {
  const world = facade.restore(record.checkpoint);
  for (const { event } of record.events) facade.apply(world, event);
  return world;
}

function deny(engine, actor, seq) {
  engine.admit(actor.id, input(seq, 'idle', true));
  engine.advance(1);
}

test('a new recorder exposes a detached, complete zero-event window', () => {
  const recorder = createRecordedEngine(-5);
  const record = recorder.window();
  assert.deepEqual(Object.keys(record).sort(), ['checkpoint', 'complete', 'endIndex', 'events', 'final', 'runtimeRelease', 'schema', 'startIndex']);
  assert.deepEqual([record.schema, record.runtimeRelease, record.startIndex, record.endIndex, record.complete], [1, RUNTIME_RELEASE, 0, 0, true]);
  assert.deepEqual(replayWindow(record, facade), { ok: true, state: canonical(recorder.world) });
  record.checkpoint.core.x = -1;
  record.final.tick = 100;
  assert.equal(recorder.window().checkpoint.core.x, 2250);
  assert.equal(recorder.world.tick, 0);
});

test('complete windows replay the existing engine, including stale input and interaction coalescing', () => {
  const recorder = createRecordedEngine(17);
  const actor = recorder.join();
  const staged = input(2, 'E', true);
  recorder.admit(actor.id, staged);
  staged.move = 'W';
  assert.equal(recorder.admit(actor.id, input(1, 'W', true)).status, 'stale');
  recorder.admit(actor.id, input(3, 'idle', false));
  recorder.advance(2);
  const record = recorder.window();
  assert.deepEqual(record.events.map(({ index }) => index), [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6]);
  assert.equal(record.events[1].event.input.move, 'E');
  assert.equal(record.events[2].event.input.seq, 1);
  assert.deepEqual(actor.lastDecision, { status: 'denied', reason: 'range', tick: 1 });
  assert.equal(actor.x, 1000);
  assert.deepEqual(replayWindow(record, facade), { ok: true, state: canonical(recorder.world) });
  assert.deepEqual(capture(replayWorld(record)), capture(recorder.world));
});

test('rollover checkpoints the prior state before a causal operation and keeps absolute indices', () => {
  const recorder = createRecordedEngine(17, { capacity: 2 });
  const actor = recorder.join();
  recorder.admit(actor.id, input(1, 'E', true));
  const prior = capture(recorder.world);
  const older = recorder.window();
  recorder.advance(1);
  const rolled = recorder.window();
  assert.deepEqual([rolled.startIndex, rolled.endIndex, rolled.events.length], [2, 3, 1]);
  assert.deepEqual(rolled.checkpoint, prior);
  assert.deepEqual(rolled.events, [{ index: 3, event: { type: 'tick' } }]);
  assert.deepEqual(replayWindow(rolled, facade), { ok: true, state: canonical(recorder.world) });
  recorder.advance(7);
  const latest = recorder.window();
  assert.deepEqual([latest.startIndex, latest.endIndex], [8, 10]);
  assert.deepEqual(latest.events.map(({ index }) => index), [9, 10]);
  assert.deepEqual(replayWindow(latest, facade), { ok: true, state: canonical(recorder.world) });
  assert.deepEqual([older.startIndex, older.endIndex, older.checkpoint.tick], [0, 2, 0]);
  assert.deepEqual(replayWindow(older, facade).state, older.final);
});

test('rejected operations do not roll a full window or consume indices', () => {
  const recorder = createRecordedEngine(0, { capacity: 1 });
  const actor = recorder.join();
  const before = recorder.window();
  assert.equal(recorder.admit('unknown', input(1)).status, 'rejected');
  assert.equal(recorder.admit(actor.id, { ...input(1), token: 'secret' }).status, 'rejected');
  for (const ticks of [0, -1, 101, 0.5, Infinity, NaN, '2']) assert.throws(() => recorder.advance(ticks), /ticks must/);
  assert.deepEqual(recorder.window(), before);
  recorder.admit(actor.id, input(1));
  const full = recorder.window();
  recorder.admit(actor.id, input(1, 'E', true));
  assert.equal(recorder.window().endIndex, full.endIndex + 1);
  assert.equal(recorder.window().events[0].event.input.seq, 1);
  assert.equal(replayWindow(recorder.window(), facade).ok, true);
});

test('capture and restore preserve pending interaction, movement, expiry and cooldown for future execution', () => {
  const recorder = createRecordedEngine(0);
  const actor = recorder.join();
  recorder.admit(actor.id, input(1, 'E'));
  recorder.advance(3);
  recorder.admit(actor.id, input(2, 'E', true));
  const checkpoint = capture(recorder.world);
  const continuation = restore(checkpoint);
  assert.deepEqual(capture(continuation), checkpoint);
  recorder.advance(1);
  advance(continuation, 1);
  assert.equal(actor.cargo, true);
  const afterFirstTick = canonical(recorder.world);
  assert.deepEqual(capture(continuation), capture(recorder.world));
  admit(continuation, actor.id, input(3, 'idle', true));
  recorder.admit(actor.id, input(3, 'idle', true));
  recorder.advance(1);
  advance(continuation, 1);
  assert.equal(actor.lastDecision.reason, 'cooldown');
  assert.deepEqual(capture(continuation), capture(recorder.world));
  recorder.advance(10);
  advance(continuation, 10);
  assert.deepEqual(capture(continuation), capture(recorder.world));
  const missingIntent = clone(checkpoint);
  missingIntent.actors[0].move = 'idle';
  const changed = restore(missingIntent);
  advance(changed, 1);
  assert.notDeepEqual(canonical(changed), afterFirstTick);
  assert.equal(changed.actors[0].x, 1750);
  assert.equal(changed.actors[0].lastDecision.reason, 'pickup');
});

test('restored detector buckets affect the next finding and age out at the same tick', () => {
  const recorder = createRecordedEngine(17);
  const actor = recorder.join();
  deny(recorder, actor, 1);
  deny(recorder, actor, 2);
  recorder.admit(actor.id, input(3, 'idle', true));
  const checkpoint = capture(recorder.world);
  const restored = restore(checkpoint);
  const erased = clone(checkpoint);
  erased.actors[0].detector = createDetector();
  const withoutEvidence = restore(erased);
  recorder.advance(1);
  advance(restored, 1);
  advance(withoutEvidence, 1);
  assert.deepEqual(restored.actors[0].detector.findings, [{ kind: 'repeated-invalid-action', tick: 3 }]);
  assert.deepEqual(withoutEvidence.actors[0].detector.findings, []);
  assert.deepEqual(capture(restored), capture(recorder.world));
  recorder.advance(20);
  advance(restored, 20);
  assert.deepEqual(restored.actors[0].detector.buckets, createDetector().buckets);
  assert.deepEqual(capture(restored), capture(recorder.world));
});

test('strict restore rejects missing, unknown, inconsistent and unbounded checkpoint state', () => {
  const recorder = createRecordedEngine(17);
  const actor = recorder.join();
  deny(recorder, actor, 1);
  const checkpoint = capture(recorder.world);
  const edits = [
    (c) => { c.schema = 2; },
    (c) => { c.token = 'secret'; },
    (c) => { c.seed = Infinity; },
    (c) => { c.tick = -1; },
    (c) => { c.tick = Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER; },
    (c) => { c.core.x = 2000; },
    (c) => { c.actors.push(...Array.from({ length: 4 }, () => clone(c.actors[0]))); },
    (c) => { c.actors[0].id = 'actor-2'; },
    (c) => { c.actors[0].x = NaN; },
    (c) => { c.actors[0].x = 4000; },
    (c) => { c.actors[0].y = 4001; },
    (c) => { c.actors[0].cargo = 1; },
    (c) => { c.actors[0].score = -1; },
    (c) => { c.actors[0].lastSeq = 1_000_001; },
    (c) => { c.actors[0].expiresAt = 99; },
    (c) => { c.actors[0].lastSeen = 2; },
    (c) => { c.actors[0].move = 'NE'; },
    (c) => { c.actors[0].pendingInteract = null; },
    (c) => { c.actors[0].nextInteractTick = 99; },
    (c) => { c.actors[0].lastDecision.reason = 'ban'; },
    (c) => { c.actors[0].detector.buckets.pop(); },
    (c) => { delete c.actors[0].detector.buckets[0]; },
    (c) => { c.actors[0].detector.findings = new Array(1); },
    (c) => { c.actors[0].detector.buckets[1].observations[0].reason = 'cooldown'; },
    (c) => { c.actors[0].detector.buckets[1].tick = 21; },
    (c) => { c.actors[0].detector.findings = Array.from({ length: 129 }, () => ({ kind: 'repeated-invalid-action', tick: 1 })); },
  ];
  for (const key of ['lastSeq', 'lastSeen', 'expiresAt', 'nextInteractTick', 'move', 'pendingInteract', 'lastDecision', 'detector']) {
    edits.push((c) => { delete c.actors[0][key]; });
  }
  for (const edit of edits) {
    const changed = clone(checkpoint);
    edit(changed);
    assert.throws(() => restore(changed), /invalid checkpoint/);
  }
  const detached = restore(checkpoint);
  detached.actors[0].detector.buckets[1].observations.length = 0;
  assert.equal(checkpoint.actors[0].detector.buckets[1].observations.length, 1);
});

test('facade refuses unknown events and invalid payloads without accepting arbitrary state writes', () => {
  const recorder = createRecordedEngine(17);
  const actor = recorder.join();
  const world = restore(capture(recorder.world));
  const invalid = [null, [], { type: 'teleport', x: 2 }, { type: 'tick', count: 2 },
    { type: 'join', id: actor.id }, { type: 'input', id: 'missing', input: input(1) },
    { type: 'input', id: actor.id, input: { ...input(1), v: 2 } },
    { type: 'input', id: actor.id, input: { ...input(1), seq: Infinity } },
    { type: 'input', id: actor.id, input: { ...input(1), seq: 1_000_001 } },
    { type: 'input', id: actor.id, input: { ...input(1), score: 100 } },
    { type: 'input', id: actor.id, input: { ...input(1), move: 'NE' } },
    { type: 'input', id: actor.id, input: { ...input(1), interact: 'true' } }];
  const before = capture(world);
  for (const event of invalid) assert.throws(() => facade.apply(world, event), /invalid/);
  assert.deepEqual(capture(world), before);
});

test('learner policy distinguishes all refusal reasons and rejects sequence gaps even for no-op stale input', () => {
  for (const item of cases()) assert.deepEqual(replayWindow(item.record, facade), item.expected, item.name);
  const source = cases()[0].record;
  const missingStale = clone(source);
  missingStale.events.splice(3, 1);
  assert.deepEqual(canonical(replayWorld(missingStale)), source.final);
  assert.deepEqual(replayWindow(missingStale, facade), { ok: false, reason: 'sequence' });
  const badShapes = [null, [], 1, 'record', {}, { ...source, schema: '1' }];
  for (const record of badShapes) assert.deepEqual(replayWindow(record, facade), { ok: false, reason: 'schema' });
  for (const events of [null, {}, 'events']) assert.deepEqual(replayWindow({ ...source, events }, facade), { ok: false, reason: 'incomplete' });
});

test('canonical comparison ignores key order but rejects missing fields, extra fields and invalid numbers', () => {
  assert.equal(equal({ a: [1, true, null], b: 'x' }, { b: 'x', a: [1, true, null] }), true);
  for (const pair of [[{ a: 1 }, { a: 1, b: 2 }], [[1], [1, 2]], [NaN, NaN], [Infinity, Infinity], [undefined, undefined]]) {
    assert.equal(equal(...pair), false);
  }
  const cyclic = {};
  cyclic.cyclic = cyclic;
  assert.equal(equal(cyclic, cyclic), false);
});

test('assessment accepts two independent policies and rejects every plausible wrong control by behavior', async () => {
  for (const [name, candidate] of Object.entries(correctPolicies)) {
    const result = await assess(candidate);
    assert.equal(result.passed, true, `${name}: ${JSON.stringify(result.criteria.filter((criterion) => !criterion.passed))}`);
  }
  for (const [name, candidate] of Object.entries(wrongPolicies)) {
    const result = await assess(candidate);
    assert.equal(result.passed, false, name);
    assert.ok(result.criteria.some((criterion) => !criterion.passed && Object.hasOwn(criterion.error, 'expected') && Object.hasOwn(criterion.error, 'actual')), name);
    assert.ok(result.criteria.every((criterion) => !criterion.error?.actual?.threw), `${name} was rejected only by throwing`);
  }
  assert.equal((await assess({})).passed, false);
  assert.equal((await assess(template)).passed, false);
  const rewritesExpected = await assess({
    replayWindow(record) {
      record.final.actors.length = 0;
      record.final.tick = -1;
      return { ok: true, state: record.final };
    },
  });
  assert.equal(rewritesExpected.criteria[0].passed, false);
  assert.ok(rewritesExpected.criteria[0].error.expected.state.actors.length > 0);
  const crashed = await assess({ replayWindow() { throw new Error('broken policy'); } });
  assert.equal(crashed.passed, false);
  assert.deepEqual(crashed.criteria[0].error.actual, { threw: 'broken policy' });
});
```

`courses/anti-cheat-engineering/courier-lab/timing/LEARNER.md`:

```md
# Investigate delay, expiry and recovery

Implementation reference for **M4: timing**. Start with [the guided learning route at `/learn`](/learn) on the reference server, then return here for the exact source contract. This Markdown file does not submit answers or certify mastery. Use the [support and attempt workflow](../learning-support/README.md) for worked siblings, gradual guidance and help recording. A prepared source workspace need not serve `/learn`; keep the reference server open for that route.

Goal: predict what the owner processes when requests arrive late or a connection disappears, then explain a safe recovery. Allow roughly 30–50 minutes including code and repairs; this estimate has not been tried with learners.

## Prepare and predict

From the reference project run `npm run core:prepare -- timing`. Change into the printed workspace. Read this guide and complete the required answers or explicit skip reasons in `predictions.json`; keep explanations in `response.md` before editing `timing/policy.mjs` or running its checker. You will compare a pure prediction function with the existing game engine and owner clock, rather than replace either mechanism.

A **receipt** is an input reaching the owner. A **processed tick** is one simulation step the owner actually performs. A **connection binding** links one client label to one server actor. A **resume** uses that same binding; a **fresh join** creates another actor. A **callback** is a function the runtime invokes when work is ready. Here callback time means the owner clock reading when that function runs. Client send time, server receipt tick and owner elapsed time answer different questions.

## Receipt and movement

The owner receives a parsed input containing a sequence and E, W or idle direction. Its optional `sentAtMs` annotation records what the client claimed; it cannot grant earlier movement. Only a strictly larger sequence is admitted. Admission sets expiry using the current processed tick, replaces direction and leaves position unchanged until the next tick.

This partial worked example shows how to read the fields without solving the assessment: an idle input admitted at tick 6 has `receipt:{status:'admitted',tick:6,seq:1}` and expiry 10. Position remains at 1000 because idle is not motion. An observed tick of 6 is an owner state, not six requests and not a client timestamp.

## Four processed ticks

An input admitted at T can move on T+1, T+2, T+3 and T+4. At T+5 it cannot move unless a newer input renewed the window. Each eligible E/W step changes x by 250 mm. The scripts stay on open floor so a wall or arena edge cannot hide an expiry defect. They do not teach collision prediction.

## Retries and reordering

A repeated sequence is stale even if the prior response was lost. An older conflicting sequence is also stale. Neither changes position, direction or expiry. A new sequence received after a gap grants a new four-tick window; it cannot repay steps that never ran. This is protocol behavior, not evidence that a retry came from a cheater.

## Owner clock

Every sample uses elapsed milliseconds since the previous sample plus the retained fraction. Divide by 50 and take whole ticks. Process at most five; drop excess whole ticks and keep only the fraction. Increment overruns once for a callback that dropped work. For example, an idle world sampled at 26 ms then 51 ms performs zero ticks with remainder 26, followed by one tick with remainder 1. It must not discard the first fraction.

Dropped work is not processed time. A callback delayed by seconds does not make the actor leap through every nominal tick. Nor does sampling twice at the same millisecond create a step.

## A clock has an origin

A **monotonic clock** measures elapsed time without going backward when the calendar clock is corrected. Its readings are meaningful relative to an origin. In Node, `performance.now()` measures milliseconds from the start of the current process; see the [official API](https://nodejs.org/api/perf_hooks.html#performancenow). It is not the number of simulation ticks processed.

Worked comparison: in one process, readings 120 ms and 170 ms are 50 ms apart. If a new process starts and reads 20 ms, subtracting the old 170 from the new 20 does not measure a negative interval. Those readings use different origins. The application needs a declared cross-restart time contract before it can decide what survived. This is a design consequence of the API's process-relative origin, not a guarantee supplied by a timestamp.

Completion practice: the same process reads 45 ms, then 95 ms. Record the elapsed interval. A restarted process next reads 10 ms. Can those three numbers alone establish how long the restart took? Compare your explanation with the origin rule above, then tackle the separate reservation-deadline transfer in response.md.

## Connection recovery

The mechanism models a delivery outage by preventing inputs on a disconnected binding from reaching admission. The owner engine keeps running. Disconnect does not delete an actor, clear its last sequence or instantly stop already-admitted motion. The old window expires normally.

Resume restores that binding. Its position, last sequence and expiry persist, so retrying an already admitted sequence remains stale. A fresh join uses a different connection label and creates the next server actor at its starting state. The old actor remains until the owned world is discarded. This matches the game engine's actor lifetime; it does not model production session cleanup, TCP retransmission, tokens or restart authentication. No bearer token is exported.

## The contract

Implement `predictTiming(record)` without file, network or real-time APIs. The owner validates each record before use. Input has `schema:1`, `startMs` and up to 80 labelled `actions`:

| type | Extra fields | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| join | id | New connection and actor; at most four |
| input | id, seq, move; optional sentAtMs | Attempt delivery; move is E, W or idle |
| sample | nowMs | Finite nondecreasing owner reading |
| disconnect | id | Pause delivery on an existing binding |
| resume | id | Restore the same binding |

Return `{ok:true,checkpoints}` with one checkpoint after every action. A checkpoint has `label`, processed `tick`, ordered `actors`, `receipt` and `clock`. Each actor has `{id,connection,connected,lastSeq,expiresAt,x}`. IDs are actor-1 onward; starting x is 1000, lastSeq and expiresAt are zero. Keep private direction state inside your function. Other state starts idle and the clock starts at `startMs`, tick 0, remainder 0 and overruns 0.

Only input actions have a receipt: `{status,tick,seq}`. Status is admitted, stale or offline. Only sample actions have a clock result: `{ticks,dropped,overruns,remainder}`. Use `null` for the other actions. Do not insert client time into these outputs or mutate the input record.

## Build in four checked milestones

Work through [the timing predictor companion](../learning-support/timing-predictor.md) before constructing the whole function. It supplies a complete smaller clock trace, a partial trace, and a smaller actor trace. Its 10 ms/two-tick clock and three-tick movement window are sibling rules, not this contract's constants.

1. **Clock state.** Write a trace with only sample actions. Track previous owner reading, fractional remainder, processed tick and overruns. Check each row with the worked calculation, including a repeated reading and a delay above the cap. This isolates clock arithmetic from actor logic.
2. **One actor.** Add join, one admitted input and enough samples to cross expiry. At the input checkpoint, position must be unchanged. At subsequent checkpoints, list each processed tick before adding movement. This catches movement at receipt and an off-by-one expiry separately.
3. **Delivery and identity.** Add a duplicate, older sequence, disconnect, offline input, resume and fresh join. Check which actor record persists and which sequence/expiry fields remain unchanged. Offline delivery is not a new sequence admission.
4. **Checkpoint output.** Build a fresh returned actor object after each action, excluding private direction. Inspect earlier checkpoints after later actions: old positions and flags must not change. The number and order of checkpoints must match actions, including joins and disconnects.

These milestones are source-construction aids, not additional commands or progress scores. The core checker reports the first differing checkpoint after a captured attempt. Identify the earliest differing field; later positions can be consequences of one wrong clock or expiry value.

<details><summary>Hint 1 — separate ownership</summary>

Write an action-to-fields table before the loop. Only a sample advances the processed tick; only admitted input replaces direction and expiry. This keeps a client annotation from changing owner time.

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 2 — split each sample</summary>

Calculate due whole ticks and the fraction before applying the five-tick cap. Then process each permitted tick in order, checking expiry at that tick. The actor may be active for only part of a multi-tick sample.

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 3 — worked sibling, after a saved attempt</summary>

Open the companion's “Work a smaller clock” example. Its available 41 ms contains four 10 ms ticks, of which two are processed and two dropped, leaving 1 ms. Total tick grows by two, not four. Record the viewed section as assistance, then recalculate your own case with this guide's 50 ms and cap of five.

</details>

## Check, inspect and repair

Run `npm run core:check -- --assistance "none"` from the prepared workspace, or describe actual help. Read the first failed investigation and checkpoint; its JSON preserves expected/observed state and a link back to this guide. Match the discrepancy to a clock, receipt or identity rule. Append a repair explanation instead of rewriting your original prediction, then run again. Existing submissions and source hashes remain preserved by the core runner.

The checker uses ten finite investigations and is calibrated against two independently implemented correct predictors plus eleven wrong controls. Passing means these predictions agree with the named engine cases. Your reasoning and reservation-deadline transfer are saved but not automatically scored. The transfer changes the expiry contract: explain where processed-tick reasoning stops applying. The exercise has not measured human learning, production recovery safety or malicious-client detection.

## Capture, compare and try a fresh case

In a newly prepared workspace, put the required first answers in `predictions.json`; use `response.md` for explanations and later repairs. Keep each question ID and its wording unchanged. Fill an `answer` or an explicit `skipReason` for every question before the first source check. A blank row refuses feedback rather than silently recording an empty attempt. The guide's additional trace questions are practice notes, not extra required JSON fields.

After a check accepts and captures the submission, inspect its `prediction-feedback.json` beside the result. Compare your first answer with the answer and governing reason, then append a correction without erasing the original. Complete the new `fresh-practice.json` answers or skip reasons and run `npm run core:practice -- --assistance "none"` from that workspace, replacing `none` with actual help. The practice command records your response before revealing its feedback. These prose responses are preserved and ungraded; they are separate from source-check results and `/learn` mastery.

Use the scripts generated in your workspace. Older prepared workspaces may retain the earlier response-only format; do not replace their original records with new templates. Record any worked-example views, final hints, reference code or AI help in your assistance declaration.
```

```md
# Timing module integration

`policy.mjs` is the standalone author solution; copy only `template.mjs` to the
learner's `timing/policy.mjs`. The remaining standard descriptor files are
`fixtures.mjs`, `prompt.json`, `LEARNER.md`, and `response-template.md`.

No author solution or control belongs in a prepared learner workspace.

and `investigations()`. A record is `{schema:1,startMs,actions}`. `actions` use
the labelled join/input/sample/disconnect/resume contract in the exact prompt.
`runInvestigation` returns `{record,observed:{ok:true,checkpoints},receipts}`.
It uses the existing `clock.mjs` and `engine.mjs`, including `join`, `admit` and
`advance`; it does not implement a second game engine. Scripts are finite and
must remain on unobstructed floor. Record export contains connection labels and
actor IDs, never bearer tokens. A disconnect is an explicit delivery gate in
this harness, not a TCP emulator. Existing engine actors remain in the world.

The pure learner API is `predictTiming(record) -> {ok:true,checkpoints}`.

`{label,tick,actors:[{id,connection,connected,lastSeq,expiresAt,x}],receipt,clock}`.
`receipt` is null except for input actions, where it is `{status,tick,seq}`.
`clock` is null except for samples, where it is
```

`courses/anti-cheat-engineering/courier-lab/timing/controls.mjs`:

```mjs
import { predictTiming, predictWithDefect } from './policy.mjs';

/** Independent interval calculation: count eligible ticks instead of stepping. */
export function predictByIntervals(record) {
  const rows = [];
  const actors = [];
  let tick = 0;
  let previous = record.startMs;
  let carry = 0;
  let overrunCount = 0;
  for (const event of record.actions) {
    let result = null;
    let elapsedClock = null;
    const found = actors.findIndex((actor) => actor.connection === event.id);
    if (event.type === 'join') actors.push({ id: `actor-${actors.length + 1}`, connection: event.id, connected: true, lastSeq: 0, expiresAt: 0, x: 1000, delta: 0 });
    if (event.type === 'disconnect' || event.type === 'resume') actors[found].connected = event.type === 'resume';
    if (event.type === 'input') {
      const current = actors[found];
      const status = !current.connected ? 'offline' : event.seq > current.lastSeq ? 'admitted' : 'stale';
      result = { status, tick, seq: event.seq };
      if (status === 'admitted') actors[found] = { ...current, lastSeq: event.seq, expiresAt: tick + 4, delta: { E: 250, W: -250, idle: 0 }[event.move] };
    }
    if (event.type === 'sample') {
      const milliseconds = event.nowMs - previous + carry;
      const quota = Math.trunc(milliseconds / 50);
      const processed = Math.min(5, quota);
      carry = milliseconds % 50;
      previous = event.nowMs;
      if (quota > processed) overrunCount += 1;
      elapsedClock = { ticks: processed, dropped: quota - processed, overruns: overrunCount, remainder: carry };
      for (const current of actors) {
        const eligible = Math.max(0, Math.min(tick + processed, current.expiresAt) - tick);
        current.x += eligible * current.delta;
      }
      tick += processed;
    }
    rows.push({ label: event.label, tick, actors: actors.map(({ delta, ...actor }) => ({ ...actor })), receipt: result, clock: elapsedClock });
  }
  return { ok: true, checkpoints: rows };
}

export const correctPolicies = {
  'tick-by-tick': { predictTiming },
  'interval-intersection': { predictTiming: predictByIntervals },
};

export const wrongPolicies = Object.fromEntries([
```

```mjs
import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
import { isDeepStrictEqual } from 'node:util';
import { investigations, runInvestigation } from './runtime.mjs';

function safe(value) {
  try { return JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(value, (_key, item) => item === undefined ? { type: 'undefined' } : item)); }
  catch { return { type: 'non-JSON result' }; }
}

/** Expected checkpoints are measured from the actual engine and owner clock. */
export async function assess(candidate) {
  if (typeof candidate?.predictTiming !== 'function') return {
    passed: false, criteria: [{ name: 'export predictTiming(record)', passed: false, error: {
      message: 'Export the pure predictTiming function.', expected: 'function', actual: typeof candidate?.predictTiming, source: 'LEARNER.md#the-contract',
    } }],
  };
  const criteria = [];
  for (const item of investigations()) {
    const actualRun = runInvestigation(item.record);
    const offered = structuredClone(item.record);
    let predicted;
    try {
      predicted = await candidate.predictTiming(offered);
      assert.deepEqual(offered, item.record, 'Do not mutate the input record.');
      assert.deepEqual(predicted, actualRun.observed);
      criteria.push({ name: item.name, passed: true });
    } catch (error) {
      const index = actualRun.observed.checkpoints.findIndex((checkpoint, i) => {
        try { assert.deepEqual(predicted?.checkpoints?.[i], checkpoint); return false; } catch { return true; }
      });
      const mutated = !isDeepStrictEqual(offered, item.record);
      const expected = mutated ? item.record : index < 0 ? actualRun.observed : actualRun.observed.checkpoints[index];
      const observed = mutated ? offered : index < 0 ? predicted : predicted?.checkpoints?.[index];
      criteria.push({ name: item.name, passed: false, error: {
        message: `Timing prediction differs${index < 0 || mutated ? '' : ` at ${expected.label}`}: ${error.message}`,
        expected, actual: safe(observed), source: `LEARNER.md#${mutated ? 'the-contract' : item.section}`,
      } });
    }
  }
  return { passed: criteria.every((item) => item.passed), criteria };
}
```

`courses/anti-cheat-engineering/courier-lab/timing/policy.mjs`:

```mjs
/** Pure prediction for validated, unobstructed owner-clock investigations. */
export function predictTiming(record) {
  return predictWithDefect(record);
}

function moveActors(actors, initialTick, ticks, defect) {
  for (let count = 1; count <= ticks; count += 1) {
    for (const actor of actors) {
      const end = actor.expiresAt + (defect === 'expire-early' ? -1 : defect === 'expire-late' ? 1 : 0);
      if (initialTick + count > end) continue;
      actor.x += actor.move === 'E' ? 250 : actor.move === 'W' ? -250 : 0;
    }
  }
}

/** Author calibration entry point; learner preparation copies template.mjs only. */
export function predictWithDefect(record, defect = '') {
  let now = record.startMs;
  let remainder = 0;
  let tick = 0;
  let overruns = 0;
  const actors = [];
  const checkpoints = [];
  for (const action of record.actions) {
    let receipt = null;
    let clock = null;
    const actor = actors.find((item) => item.connection === action.id);
    if (action.type === 'join') {
      if (defect === 'rejoin-reuses-actor' && actors.length) {
        actors[0].connection = action.id;
        actors[0].connected = true;
      } else actors.push({ id: `actor-${actors.length + 1}`, connection: action.id, connected: true, lastSeq: 0, expiresAt: 0, x: 1000, move: 'idle' });
    }
    if (action.type === 'disconnect') {
      actor.connected = false;
      if (defect === 'disconnect-clears-intent') actor.move = 'idle';
    }
    if (action.type === 'resume') {
      actor.connected = true;
      if (defect === 'resume-resets-state') Object.assign(actor, { lastSeq: 0, expiresAt: 0, x: 1000, move: 'idle' });
    }
    if (action.type === 'input') {
      const newer = action.seq > actor.lastSeq || defect === 'stale-replaces-intent' || defect === 'duplicate-renews' && action.seq === actor.lastSeq;
      const status = !actor.connected ? 'offline' : newer ? 'admitted' : 'stale';
      receipt = { status, tick, seq: action.seq };
      if (status === 'admitted') {
        const receivedAt = defect === 'client-time-authority' ? Math.floor((action.sentAtMs ?? now) / 50) : tick;
        Object.assign(actor, { lastSeq: action.seq, expiresAt: receivedAt + 4, move: action.move });
        if (defect === 'movement-at-receipt') actor.x += action.move === 'E' ? 250 : action.move === 'W' ? -250 : 0;
      }
    }
    if (action.type === 'sample') {
      const elapsed = action.nowMs - now + remainder;
      const due = Math.floor(elapsed / 50);
      const ticks = defect === 'unbounded-catch-up' ? due : Math.min(due, 5);
      const dropped = due - ticks;
      remainder = defect === 'discard-fraction' ? 0 : elapsed - due * 50;
      now = action.nowMs;
      if (dropped > 0) overruns += 1;
      clock = { ticks, dropped, overruns, remainder };
      moveActors(actors, tick, ticks, defect);
      tick += ticks;
    }
    checkpoints.push({
      label: action.label, tick,
      actors: actors.map(({ move, ...item }) => ({ ...item })), receipt, clock,
    });
  }
  return { ok: true, checkpoints };
}
```

`courses/anti-cheat-engineering/courier-lab/timing/runtime.mjs`:

```mjs
import { createWorld, join, admit, advance } from '../engine.mjs';
import { createClock } from '../clock.mjs';

const copy = (value) => JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(value));
const exact = (value, keys) => value !== null && typeof value === 'object' && !Array.isArray(value) && Object.keys(value).sort().join(',') === keys.sort().join(',');
const finite = (value) => typeof value === 'number' && Number.isFinite(value) && value >= 0;

/** Only finite, small scripts on the open floor are accepted by this mechanism. */
export function validateInvestigation(record) {
  if (!exact(record, ['schema', 'startMs', 'actions']) || record.schema !== 1 || !finite(record.startMs)) throw new Error('Invalid timing record envelope.');
  if (!Array.isArray(record.actions) || !record.actions.length || record.actions.length > 80) throw new Error('Timing records require 1–80 actions.');
  const ids = new Set();
  const labels = new Set();
  let now = record.startMs;
  for (const action of record.actions) {
    if (!action || typeof action.label !== 'string' || !action.label || labels.has(action.label)) throw new Error('Action labels must be unique nonempty strings.');
    labels.add(action.label);
    if (action.type === 'sample') {
      if (!exact(action, ['type', 'label', 'nowMs']) || !finite(action.nowMs) || action.nowMs < now || action.nowMs - now > 5000) throw new Error('Invalid bounded owner-clock sample.');
      now = action.nowMs;
      continue;
    }
    if (action.type === 'input') {
      const keys = ['type', 'label', 'id', 'seq', 'move', ...(Object.hasOwn(action, 'sentAtMs') ? ['sentAtMs'] : [])];
      if (!exact(action, keys) || !ids.has(action.id) || !Number.isSafeInteger(action.seq) || action.seq < 1 || action.seq > 1000000 || !['E', 'W', 'idle'].includes(action.move)) throw new Error('Invalid timing input.');
      if (Object.hasOwn(action, 'sentAtMs') && !finite(action.sentAtMs)) throw new Error('Invalid client-time annotation.');
      continue;
    }
    if (!exact(action, ['type', 'label', 'id']) || typeof action.id !== 'string' || !action.id) throw new Error('Invalid connection action.');
    if (action.type === 'join') {
      if (ids.has(action.id) || ids.size >= 4) throw new Error('Join requires a new connection label, at most four per record.');
      ids.add(action.id);
      continue;
    }
    if (!['disconnect', 'resume'].includes(action.type) || !ids.has(action.id)) throw new Error('Unknown connection action.');
  }
}

function stepOpenFloor(world, ticks) {
  for (let count = 0; count < ticks; count += 1) {
    for (const actor of world.actors) {
      if (world.tick + 1 > actor.expiresAt) continue;
      const target = actor.x + (actor.move === 'E' ? 250 : actor.move === 'W' ? -250 : 0);
      if (target < 0 || target > 3750) throw new Error('Timing investigations must stay on unobstructed floor (x=0..3750).');
    }
    advance(world, 1);
  }
}

/** A delivery outage gates receipts; it never deletes or rewinds an engine actor. */
export function runInvestigation(record) {
  validateInvestigation(record);
  const world = createWorld(17);
  const timer = createClock(record.startMs);
  const connections = new Map();
  const checkpoints = [];
  const receipts = [];
  for (const action of record.actions) {
    let receipt = null;
    let clock = null;
    const connection = connections.get(action.id);
    if (action.type === 'join') connections.set(action.id, { actor: join(world), connected: true });
    if (action.type === 'disconnect') connection.connected = false;
    if (action.type === 'resume') connection.connected = true;
    if (action.type === 'input') {
      const response = connection.connected ? admit(world, connection.actor.id, { v: 1, seq: action.seq, move: action.move, interact: false }) : { status: 'offline', tick: world.tick, seq: action.seq };
      receipt = { status: response.status, tick: response.tick, seq: response.seq };
      receipts.push({ label: action.label, connection: action.id, actorId: connection.actor.id, ...receipt, ...(Object.hasOwn(action, 'sentAtMs') ? { sentAtMs: action.sentAtMs } : {}) });
    }
    if (action.type === 'sample') {
      clock = timer.sample(action.nowMs);
      if (clock.ticks) stepOpenFloor(world, clock.ticks);
    }
    checkpoints.push({ label: action.label, tick: world.tick, actors: [...connections].map(([id, item]) => ({
      id: item.actor.id, connection: id, connected: item.connected,
      lastSeq: item.actor.lastSeq, expiresAt: item.actor.expiresAt, x: item.actor.x,
    })), receipt, clock });
  }
  return { record: copy(record), observed: { ok: true, checkpoints }, receipts };
}

const action = (type, label, fields = {}) => ({ type, label, ...fields });
const joinTab = (id = 'tab-a') => action('join', `join-${id}`, { id });
const input = (label, seq, move, fields = {}) => action('input', label, { id: 'tab-a', seq, move, ...fields });
const sample = (label, nowMs) => action('sample', label, { nowMs });
const record = (...actions) => ({ schema: 1, startMs: 0, actions });

/** The action scripts are observations to investigate, not a production workload. */
export function investigations() {
  return [
    { name: 'receipt-before-movement', section: 'receipt-and-movement', record: record(joinTab(), input('admitted-at-zero', 1, 'E'), sample('first-owner-tick', 50)) },
    { name: 'inclusive-expiry', section: 'four-processed-ticks', record: record(joinTab(), input('start', 1, 'E'), sample('fourth-tick', 200), sample('fifth-tick-stopped', 250)) },
    { name: 'delayed-client-time', section: 'receipt-and-movement', record: record(joinTab(), sample('owner-waited', 150), input('delayed-receipt', 1, 'E', { sentAtMs: 0 }), sample('four-after-receipt', 350)) },
    { name: 'duplicate-retry', section: 'retries-and-reordering', record: record(joinTab(), input('original', 4, 'E'), sample('three-ticks', 150), input('duplicate-opposite', 4, 'W'), sample('original-expiry', 200), sample('no-renewal', 250)) },
    { name: 'reordered-older-input', section: 'retries-and-reordering', record: record(joinTab(), input('newer-first', 9, 'E'), sample('one-tick', 50), input('older-arrives', 8, 'W'), sample('continue-east', 100)) },
    { name: 'fractional-callbacks', section: 'owner-clock', record: record(joinTab(), input('start', 1, 'E'), sample('fraction-24', 24), sample('fraction-49', 49), sample('whole-tick', 50), sample('same-sample', 50), sample('fraction-99', 99), sample('next-tick', 100)) },
    { name: 'bounded-pause', section: 'owner-clock', record: record(joinTab(), input('start', 1, 'E'), sample('long-pause', 826.5), input('renew-after-pause', 2, 'W'), sample('remainder-carries', 850)) },
    { name: 'outage-and-resume', section: 'connection-recovery', record: record(joinTab(), input('start', 5, 'E'), action('disconnect', 'link-lost', { id: 'tab-a' }), sample('still-active-server-intent', 100), input('undelivered-input', 6, 'W'), sample('intent-expired', 250), action('resume', 'same-binding-restored', { id: 'tab-a' }), input('retry-original', 5, 'W'), input('fresh-recovery-input', 6, 'W'), sample('recovered-one-step', 300)) },
    { name: 'fresh-rejoin', section: 'connection-recovery', record: record(joinTab(), input('old-session-start', 10, 'E'), action('disconnect', 'old-link-lost', { id: 'tab-a' }), sample('old-intent-continues', 50), joinTab('tab-b'), action('input', 'new-session-sequence-one', { id: 'tab-b', seq: 1, move: 'W' }), sample('independent-actors', 100)) },
    { name: 'renew-on-boundary', section: 'four-processed-ticks', record: record(joinTab(), input('start', 20, 'E'), sample('at-boundary', 200), input('fresh-boundary-reversal', 21, 'W'), sample('new-window-fourth', 400), sample('stop-again', 450)) },
  ];
}
```

```mjs
import { open, unlink } from 'node:fs/promises';
import { dirname, basename, resolve, join } from 'node:path';
import { regularFile, saveJson, verifyReference } from '../lab/core/trust.mjs';
import { readJsonFile } from './read-json.mjs';
import { pathToFileURL } from 'node:url';
import { measureRetention, createSyntheticWorkload } from '../retention/measure.mjs';
import { writeExport, deleteExport } from '../retention/store.mjs';

async function sourceAt(path) {
  const absolute = resolve(path);
  return (await regularFile(dirname(absolute), basename(absolute))).toString('utf8');
}
async function capturedModule(source) {
  // Exact captured bytes are imported, not a second read of the learner's path.
  return import(`data:text/javascript;base64,${Buffer.from(source).toString('base64')}`);
}
async function saveOperation(path, operation) {
  const file = await open(resolve(path), 'wx', 0o600);
  try {
    const result = await operation();
    await file.writeFile(JSON.stringify(result, null, 2) + '\n');
    return result;
  } catch (error) {
    await file.close();
    await unlink(resolve(path));
    throw error;
  } finally { await file.close(); }
}
async function custodyFor(workspace) {
  const session = JSON.parse(await regularFile(resolve(workspace), 'lab/core/session.json'));
  if (session.schema !== 'courier-core-session-v1' || session.module !== 'evaluation' || typeof session.referenceRoot !== 'string') throw new Error('Use a prepared evaluation workspace.');
  const { bundle } = await verifyReference(session.referenceRoot, session.referenceManifest);
  if (!bundle['evaluation/custody.mjs']) throw new Error('This earlier workspace has no evaluation custody. Preserve it and prepare a fresh named evaluation workspace.');
  return import(pathToFileURL(join(session.referenceRoot, 'evaluation/custody.mjs')));
}

function measurementOptions(args) {
  const settings = [];
  const options = {};
  for (let index = 0; index < args.length; index += 1) {
    const item = args[index];
    if (item === '--warmup' || item === '--samples') {
      const key = item.slice(2);
      if (Object.hasOwn(options, key) || args[index + 1] === undefined) throw new Error(`Supply ${item} once with an integer.`);
      options[key] = Number(args[++index]);
      continue;
    }
    if (!/^\d+:\d+:\d+$/.test(item)) throw new Error('Each retention setting must be nowTick:maxAgeTicks:maxEvents.');
    const [nowTick, maxAgeTicks, maxEvents] = item.split(':').map(Number);
    settings.push({ nowTick, maxAgeTicks, maxEvents });
  }
  return { ...options, ...(settings.length ? { settings } : {}) };
}

export async function runAnalysisCli(args) {
  const [action, ...rest] = args;
  if (action === 'explore' && rest.length === 4) {
    const [workspace, threshold, windowTicks, minDistanceMm] = rest;
    const api = await custodyFor(workspace);
    return api.explore({ workspace, settings: { threshold: Number(threshold), windowTicks: Number(windowTicks), minDistanceMm: Number(minDistanceMm) } });
  }
  if (action === 'plan' && (rest.length === 4 || (rest.length === 6 && rest[4] === '--revision'))) {
    const [workspace, threshold, windowTicks, minDistanceMm, , revisionReason] = rest;
    const api = await custodyFor(workspace);
    return api.plan({ workspace, settings: { threshold: Number(threshold), windowTicks: Number(windowTicks), minDistanceMm: Number(minDistanceMm) }, revisionReason });
  }
  if (action === 'run' && rest.length === 2) {
    const [workspace, planId] = rest;
    const api = await custodyFor(workspace);
    return api.run({ workspace, planId });
  }
  if (action === 'measure' && rest.length >= 2) {
    const source = await sourceAt(rest[0]);
    const candidate = await capturedModule(source);
    if (typeof candidate.retain !== 'function') throw new Error('Policy must export retain.');
    const report = measureRetention({ policy: candidate.retain, ...measurementOptions(rest.slice(2)) });
    await saveJson(resolve(rest[1]), report);
    return { path: resolve(rest[1]), report };
  }
  if (action === 'export' && rest.length === 5) {
    const [policyPath, output, receiptPath, maxAgeTicks, maxEvents] = rest;
    const candidate = await capturedModule(await sourceAt(policyPath));
    if (typeof candidate.retain !== 'function') throw new Error('Policy must export retain.');
    const workload = createSyntheticWorkload();
    const receipt = await saveOperation(receiptPath, () => writeExport(output, workload.events, { nowTick: 4095, maxAgeTicks: Number(maxAgeTicks), maxEvents: Number(maxEvents) }, { policy: candidate.retain }));
    return { receiptPath: resolve(receiptPath), receipt };
  }
  if (action === 'delete' && rest.length === 2) {
    const receipt = await readJsonFile(resolve(rest[0]));
    const result = await saveOperation(rest[1], () => deleteExport(receipt));
    return result;
  }
  throw new Error('Usage: analysis-cli.mjs explore <evaluation-workspace> <threshold> <windowTicks> <minDistanceMm> | plan <evaluation-workspace> <threshold> <windowTicks> <minDistanceMm> [--revision "reason"] | run <evaluation-workspace> <plan-id> | measure <policy.mjs> <new-report.json> [nowTick:maxAgeTicks:maxEvents ...] [--warmup N] [--samples N] | export <policy.mjs> <new-export.json> <new-receipt.json> <maxAgeTicks> <maxEvents> | delete <receipt.json> <new-deletion.json>. Only run code you intend to execute locally.');
}
if (process.argv[1]?.endsWith('analysis-cli.mjs')) {
  try { console.log(JSON.stringify(await runAnalysisCli(process.argv.slice(2)), null, 2)); }
  catch (error) { console.error(`Analysis refused: ${error.message}`); process.exitCode = 2; }
}
```

```mjs
const errors = [];

const priorUnits = new Set();

for (const { unit } of modules) {
  for (const objective of unit.objectives) {
    check(!allObjectives.has(objective.id), `Duplicate objective ${objective.id}`);
    allObjectives.add(objective.id);
  }
}
for (const { unit, makeItem } of modules) {
  for (const prerequisite of unit.prerequisites ?? []) check(priorUnits.has(prerequisite), `${unit.id}: unit prerequisite ${prerequisite} is missing or later`);
  priorUnits.add(unit.id);
  const sourceFile = resolve(project, 'learning/units', `${unit.id}.mjs`);
  const source = await readFile(sourceFile, 'utf8');
  const localIds = new Set(unit.objectives.map(({ id }) => id));
  const objectiveRows = unit.objectives.map((objective) => {
    check(['fact', 'concept', 'procedure', 'principle'].includes(objective.kind), `${objective.id}: missing kind`);
    for (const prerequisite of objective.prerequisites ?? []) {
      check(known.has(prerequisite), `${objective.id}: prerequisite ${prerequisite} is missing or later`);
    }
    known.add(objective.id);
    return { ...objective, sections: [], practiceKeys: [], completionKeys: [], masteryKeys: [] };
  });
  check(unit.sections.length >= 2 && unit.sections.length <= 4, `${unit.id}: expected 2–4 focused sections`);
  check(unit.masterySlots.length === 3, `${unit.id}: expected three mastery slots`);
  const sectionRows = unit.sections.map((section) => {
    check(section.paragraphs?.length > 0 && section.worked?.steps?.length > 0 && section.completion?.steps?.length > 0, `${unit.id}/${section.id}: missing teaching ladder`);
    for (const id of section.objectiveIds) {
      check(localIds.has(id), `${unit.id}/${section.id}: unknown objective ${id}`);
      objectiveRows.find((row) => row.id === id)?.sections.push(section.id);
    }
    const words = section.paragraphs.join(' ').trim().split(/\s+/).length;
    return { id: section.id, title: section.title, objectiveIds: section.objectiveIds, teachingWords: words, source: section.source };
  });
  const items = [];
  for (const mode of ['completion', 'practice', 'mastery']) {
    for (const key of mode === 'mastery' ? unit.masterySlots : unit.sections.map(({ id }) => id)) {
      const signatures = new Set();
      const answers = new Set();
      const objectives = new Set();
      for (let seed = 1; seed <= 128; seed += 1) {
        const item = makeItem({ mode, key, seed });
        validateItem(item);
        const answer = item.format.type === 'json' ? JSON.stringify(item.expected) : String(item.expected);
        const result = grade(item, answer);
        check(result.status === 'scored' && result.correct, `${unit.id}/${mode}/${key}/${seed}: authored key rejected`);
        check(item.explanation?.trim().length > 20, `${item.id}: insufficient explanation`);
        check(mode === 'mastery' ? item.hints.length === 0 : item.hints.length === 3, `${item.id}: wrong hint policy`);
        for (const id of item.objectiveIds) { check(localIds.has(id), `${item.id}: unknown objective ${id}`); objectives.add(id); }
        signatures.add(JSON.stringify([item.prompt, item.inputs]));
        answers.add(JSON.stringify(item.expected));
      }
      check(signatures.size > 1 && answers.size > 1, `${unit.id}/${mode}/${key}: seeds do not change cases and answers`);
      for (const id of objectives) objectiveRows.find((row) => row.id === id)?.[`${mode}Keys`].push(key);
      items.push({ mode, key, objectiveIds: [...objectives], seedsChecked: 128, distinctCases: signatures.size, distinctAnswers: answers.size });
    }
  }
  for (const objective of objectiveRows) {
    for (const role of ['sections', 'completionKeys', 'practiceKeys', 'masteryKeys']) check(objective[role].length > 0, `${objective.id}: no ${role}`);
  }
  units.push({ id: unit.id, title: unit.title, prerequisites: unit.prerequisites, sourceFile: `learning/units/${unit.id}.mjs`, sourceSha256: createHash('sha256').update(source).digest('hex'), objectives: objectiveRows, sections: sectionRows, items });
}
const report = {
  schema: 'ivy-learning-structure/v1',
  checkedAt: new Date().toISOString(),
  scope: 'Declared objective sequence, teaching/item links, generated keys and case variation. Not a semantic transfer, difficulty, accessibility or learning-effect verdict.',
  units, errors,
};
const output = JSON.stringify(report, null, 2) + '\n';
if (process.argv[2]) await writeFile(resolve(process.argv[2]), output);
else process.stdout.write(output);
if (errors.length) { process.stderr.write(errors.slice(0, 20).join('\n') + `\n${errors.length} failures; see the complete JSON report.\n`); process.exitCode = 1; }
```

`courses/anti-cheat-engineering/courier-lab/tools/read-json.mjs`:

```mjs
import { constants } from 'node:fs';
import { lstat, open } from 'node:fs/promises';

/** Local lesson inputs must be stable, regular and bounded before parsing. */
export async function readJsonFile(path,{maxBytes=1024*1024}={}){
  const original=await lstat(path,{bigint:true});
  if(!original.isFile()||original.isSymbolicLink()) throw new Error('Input must be a regular file, not a link or pipe.');
  if(original.size>BigInt(maxBytes)) throw new Error(`Input exceeds ${maxBytes} bytes.`);
  const file=await open(path,constants.O_RDONLY|constants.O_NOFOLLOW|constants.O_NONBLOCK);
  try{
    const before=await file.stat({bigint:true});
    if(!before.isFile()||before.dev!==original.dev||before.ino!==original.ino) throw new Error('Input changed before reading.');
    const chunks=[];
    let size=0;
    for(;;){
      const buffer=Buffer.alloc(Math.min(65536,maxBytes-size+1));
      const {bytesRead}=await file.read(buffer,0,buffer.length,size);
      if(bytesRead===0) break;
      size+=bytesRead;
      if(size>maxBytes) throw new Error(`Input exceeds ${maxBytes} bytes.`);
      chunks.push(buffer.subarray(0,bytesRead));
    }
    const after=await file.stat({bigint:true});
    const current=await lstat(path,{bigint:true});
    if(['dev','ino','size','mtimeNs','ctimeNs'].some(key=>before[key]!==after[key]||before[key]!==current[key])) throw new Error('Input changed while reading.');
    return JSON.parse(Buffer.concat(chunks).toString('utf8'));
  }finally{await file.close();}
}
```

`courses/anti-cheat-engineering/courier-lab/verified-server.mjs`:

```mjs
import { realpath } from 'node:fs/promises';
import { dirname, resolve } from 'node:path';
import { fileURLToPath, pathToFileURL } from 'node:url';
import { observePackage } from './integrity/package.mjs';
import { checkPackage } from './integrity/policy.mjs';
import { readJsonFile } from './tools/read-json.mjs';

// This launcher/observer and the approval process are the local trust anchor.
// The inventory is independent of the manifest being checked.
export const RUNTIME_FILES = Object.freeze([
  'server.mjs', 'engine.mjs', 'admission.mjs', 'defense.mjs', 'protocol.mjs', 'clock.mjs',
  'telemetry/runtime.mjs', 'telemetry/policy.mjs',
  'learning/service.mjs', 'learning/runtime.mjs', 'learning/grade.mjs',
]);
const ROOT = dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url));
export const SUPPORTED_RELEASES = Object.freeze(['courier-runtime-1', 'courier-runtime-2']);

export async function checkLaunch({ root = ROOT, manifestPath = resolve(ROOT, 'trusted/runtime-manifest.json'), policy = { checkPackage } } = {}) {
  const manifest = await readJsonFile(manifestPath,{maxBytes:64*1024});
  const observed = await observePackage(await realpath(root), { paths: RUNTIME_FILES });
  return { result: await policy.checkPackage({manifest,observed,supported:[...SUPPORTED_RELEASES]}), manifest, observed };
}

async function main() {
  const args = process.argv.slice(2);
  const serverArgs = [];
  let root=ROOT;
  let manifestPath=resolve(ROOT,'trusted/runtime-manifest.json');
  let policy={checkPackage};
  for(let i=0;i<args.length;i+=1){
    const flag=args[i];
    if(flag==='--package-root'||flag==='--manifest'||flag==='--policy'){
      const value=args[++i];
      if(!value) throw new Error(`${flag} needs a path.`);
      if(flag==='--package-root') root=resolve(value);
      if(flag==='--manifest') manifestPath=resolve(value);
      if(flag==='--policy') policy=await import(pathToFileURL(resolve(value)));
      continue;
    }
    serverArgs.push(flag);
  }
  root=await realpath(root);
  const {result,manifest,observed}=await checkLaunch({root,manifestPath,policy});
  if(result?.ok!==true) throw new Error(`Runtime refused: ${result?.reason??'invalid policy result'}`);
  process.stdout.write(JSON.stringify({type:'verified',release:manifest.release,files:observed.length})+'\n');
  process.argv=[process.argv[0],resolve(root,'server.mjs'),...serverArgs];
  await import(pathToFileURL(resolve(root,'server.mjs')));
}

if(process.argv[1]&&import.meta.url===pathToFileURL(resolve(process.argv[1])).href){
  main().catch((error)=>{process.stderr.write(`Verified startup failed: ${error.message}\n`);process.exitCode=1;});
}
```

`courses/blockchain-laboratory/CONTRACT.md`:

```md
# Laboratory protocol v1

This is a deliberately small account-state protocol, not an implementation of a public chain.

## Shared values

`ctx = {network, publicKeys}` uses network `classroom-v1` and a Map from fixed account names `a,b,c,d` to ephemeral Ed25519 public keys. Genesis is `{a:{balance:100,nonce:0},b:{balance:40,nonce:0},c:{balance:0,nonce:0},d:{balance:0,nonce:0}}`. Counters never have financial value. There is no issuance or reward operation.

A transaction has exactly `network, from, to, amount, nonce, signature`. `from` and `to` must name known accounts, amount is a positive safe integer, nonce a nonnegative safe integer, signature exactly 128 lowercase hexadecimal characters. Network must match. Use supplied `txBytes(tx)`: UTF-8 JSON array `["LAB:TX:1",network,from,to,amount,nonce]`. Object property order is irrelevant. The signature covers the network and nonce as well as the value. No strings-to-numbers coercion, unknown fields or unsafe integers are accepted.

Failures return `{ok:false,code}`. Codes are `SHAPE`, `NETWORK`, `ACCOUNT`, `AMOUNT`, `NONCE`, `SIGNATURE`, `FUNDS`, `OVERFLOW`, `PARENT`, `HEIGHT`, `ROOT`, `TRANSACTIONS`. Successful validation returns `{ok:true}`; transition returns `{ok:true,state}`. No function may mutate its arguments.

## Learner functions

* `validateEnvelope(tx,ctx)`: structural/type checks before signature verification. Use supplied `verifyTx`. State validity is a later layer.
* `applyTx(state,tx,ctx)`: validate envelope; require sender nonce exactly equal to transaction nonce, sufficient funds, safe resulting balance and safe incremented nonce. Copy state, debit/credit and increment sender nonce exactly once. A self-transfer keeps its balance but still requires sufficient funds and consumes the nonce. Reject atomically.
* `stateRoot(state)`: sort account names by JavaScript's default string order. Hash each `accountBytes(name,record)` with `leafHash`. Pair adjacent nodes with `branchHash`, duplicating the last node at each odd level. Wrap the result with `rootHash(count,top)`; the empty top is `sha256(empty bytes)`. This custom count-bound tree uses RFC-inspired domain separation but is not RFC 9162's tree construction.
* `verifyProof(root,name,record,proof)`: proof is `{index,count,siblings}` where siblings are 64-character lowercase hex hashes from bottom to top. Check integer bounds, exact path length, shape and odd-level duplicated sibling consistency. Rebuild left/right by index parity and halve the index with floor each level. Root must match the count-bound commitment. This verifies membership at a position, not nonmembership or sortedness of all unseen leaves. A trusted root is a prerequisite.
* `selectMempool(state,txs,ctx,limit)`: limit is a nonnegative safe integer. Use repeated passes over input arrival order; append each first eligible valid transaction and advance a private state. Skip duplicates by supplied `txId`. Revisit future-nonce or not-yet-funded candidates after other transactions make progress. Stop at limit or a pass with no progress. Conflicting ready spends use first eligible arrival order. Do not mutate input. This is local policy; valid blocks need not use it.
* `validateBlock(block,parent,ctx)`: block has exactly `parent,height,transactions,stateRoot`; transactions is an array of at most 16. Parent is a supplied validated record `{id,height,state}`. Require exact parent ID, height `parent.height+1`, valid sequential transactions and an exact recomputed root. Return `{ok:true,id:blockId(block),height,state,block}`. The outer runtime handles duplicate and unknown-parent buffering. No claimed height or root is trusted before validation.
* `chooseHead(records)`: records are already validated candidates. Return the ID with largest height, then lexicographically smallest ID. Empty input returns `null`. This synthetic rule has no Sybil resistance, weight, real-time notion or finality.
* `verifyCertificate(votes,height,id,ctx)`: validators are the four keys in ctx. Require an array of votes, nonnegative safe integer target height and a 64-character lowercase hex target ID; otherwise return false. Each vote has exactly `voter,height,blockId,signature`; require a valid supplied `verifyVote` for the exact requested height and block ID. Ignore invalid/foreign/mismatched votes and duplicates. Reserve a voter identity only after all shape, membership, target and signature checks succeed: a forged, malformed or wrong-target packet must not suppress a later valid matching vote from that identity, regardless of arrival order. Valid duplicates still count once. Return true for at least 3 distinct valid validators. This is a fixed-height certificate checker, not a complete Byzantine consensus protocol. It does not choose a head or establish validity of the block.
* `reconcile(oldPath,newPath,pending,ctx)`: paths are supplied arrays of validated records beginning with genesis and ending at the old/new heads. Gather transactions from old path blocks in order, then pending; exclude all transaction IDs included anywhere on the new path; pass remaining candidates through `selectMempool` at the new head's state with limit 16. Return `{head:newTip.id,state:copyOfNewTipState,mempool}`. This drops currently ineligible transactions by design; a production pool might quarantine them separately. No undo arithmetic or copied old-head balances.

## Optional module 09

The core protocol below retains its original assumptions. Module 09 adds a separate `planVote(journal,request)` interface in `work/vote-guard.mjs`, fully specified in [lesson 09](lessons/09-restart.md). Its supplied model adds atomic journal persistence and serial requests across simulated crashes; the rollback incident deliberately violates persistence. It does not alter `verifyCertificate`, `chooseHead`, `reconcile` or the core simulation.

## Assumptions (modules 01–08)

The scheduler can delay, duplicate and reorder messages and model a complete cut. All nodes run the same protocol and share genesis/key membership. Honest participants retain their fixed-height vote and never sign a competing value for that height. At most one of four validators equivocates for the certificate safety argument. Signatures/hashes are treated as ideal for the model. Eventual complete delivery and a finite set of proposed blocks imply convergence of the synthetic fork rule, but indefinite delay or endless adversarial extensions defeat this liveness argument. There is no modeled durable restart, timeout protocol, view change, authenticated peer channel, stake, mining or deployment security.

```

`courses/blockchain-laboratory/COURSE.md`:

```md
# Course contract

**Goal:** Given a new partition/reorganization trace, implement and defend a node's accept/reject, state, pending-transaction and certificate decisions under explicit assumptions.

Audience: programmers comfortable with JavaScript, maps, immutable data and tests, who know basic distributed-system delay/failure concepts and the distinction between hashes, public keys and signatures. Probability is useful for later consensus study, but this laboratory does not derive probabilistic finality. A learner unable to explain “a signature authenticates a message but does not decide whether the spend is valid” should begin with module 01's worked example.

Estimated study budget is 6–9 hours including implementation and report writing, not a tested duration. The course authoring sprint is separate from learner time. Modules 01–03 are procedures, 04–06 combine procedures with principles, and 07–08 require reasoning under assumptions. Difficulty is expected to rise with the number of interacting invariants: 01 shape+identity; 02 identity+nonce+balance; 03 encoding+position+path; 04 dependency+policy+state; 05 parent+transactions+commitment; 06 validation+order; 07 membership+identity+intersection; 08 all earlier mechanisms under reordered delivery. Human calibration remains unperformed.

## Supplied and built

Supplied: Node's Ed25519 and SHA-256 implementation, ephemeral fixture keys, a canonical byte encoder, signed example creation, a deterministic message scheduler, text/HTML readers, attempt recording and checks. None of this is an assignment to implement cryptography, networking, persistence infrastructure or UI.

Built by the learner: envelope rules, pure transition, Merkle root and verifier, bounded dependency-aware mempool, block validation, fork choice, distinct-voter certificate verification and reorganization. Every function is used again in a later exercise or the final node simulation. No fee market, proof of work, peer discovery, anonymous networking, wallet interface or production consensus is taught. This deliberately avoids the separate Swarm/Messenger ownership areas. No reusable implementation from those courses is assumed or copied.

## Progression and evidence

Read a worked example, commit the local practice answer, implement the current function, inspect the first diagnostic and repair. Each lesson ends with a changed case and a checkpoint. Navigation is always open. Practice questions test reasoning separately from executable checks. Passing code tests establishes the enumerated behaviors only; prose is assessed with the rubric below, not keyword scoring.

For the final report, preserve your prediction before running `simulate transfer`. Record the actual selected history, two rejected claims, final balances/nonces, a stale proof decision, pending transaction decisions and the exact assumption required for a certificate to be unique. Identify one change to the network/adversary model that breaks your claim. Include the source hash printed by your run. A structurally changed incident is supplied, but it is part of the delivered course, not a secret held-out measurement.

## Report rubric (human/reviewer evaluated)

1. **Validity:** explains a concrete rejection using the appropriate layer; distinguishes authentic, valid, selected and certified.
2. **State:** derives balances/nonces in order, conserves the initial 140 counters and ties a proof to its exact root.
3. **Recovery:** revalidates orphan transactions against the new head; does not resurrect a conflicting nonce or drop a newly ready dependency.
4. **Consensus:** distinguishes deterministic agreement after common delivery from irreversible finality. Derives the 3-of-4 intersection and states the honest non-equivocation and fixed-height limits.
5. **Evidence:** prediction, actual trace, mismatch explanation, repair and source identity remain separate. Names simulation and browser limits accurately.

Each dimension is 0 (absent/incorrect), 1 (partly supported), or 2 (correct with a concrete trace or counterexample). Readiness for a target-learner trial requires all executable checks and 2 in every dimension. This is a local project criterion, not a validated mastery threshold. Independent fresh instances and human learning evidence are still needed before a mastery claim.

## Optional extension: vote memory across restart

Module 09 makes one previously assumed invariant executable: a fixed validator must remember its decision before a signed vote becomes observable. Learners add a separate pure vote planner and test persistence/send ordering, idempotent retry, malformed history and a bounded crash schedule. They then rotate identities and intentionally roll back storage to explain where that guarantee stops. It depends on module 07; modules 01–08 and their existing completion checks are unchanged. Allow an additional uncalibrated 60–90 minutes. The lesson includes a separate four-dimension report rubric.

This does not introduce real disk durability, a production signer or a complete consensus protocol. The supplied in-memory model executes effect plans serially and atomically preserves each committed journal entry across modeled crashes. Rollback deliberately violates that assumption. Fixed validator keys persist only inside the fixture for one process and are never exported.

## Scope reconciliation

This constructs the previously undated “behind-the-scenes crypto” idea under the user's later launch instruction. The original content gate is superseded for this isolated build; its no-real-assets and no-publication boundaries remain. The referenced Todoist item is unchanged. Existing Ivy and slate sources/catalogs are read-only reference material. Course integration remains owned by the existing integration lead.

```
