`courses/blockchain-laboratory/lessons/06-forks.md`:

```md
# 06 · Two honest histories

Two nodes accept different valid branches during a partition. Implement a shared ordering rule and state exactly what agreement after delivery does—and does not—establish.

Your artifact is `chooseHead`. It receives validated records only. You do not validate advertised headers inside a sorting function; module 05 establishes the precondition.

## Agreement needs a shared total order

Consider two observations. Node X receives valid height-2 branch F, then valid height-2 branch A. Node Y receives A, then F. If each keeps the first arrival, they remain split despite possessing identical evidence. If each chooses the smaller ID on equal height, they converge after both messages arrive.

Our order is greatest height, then lexicographically smallest ID. Worked example: candidates (height 2, ID c), (height 3, ID f), (height 3, ID a) select a. Height dominates ID; the tie rule only applies at equal height. The input list must not be sorted in place because other code may retain its order.

Complete the comparator: when heights differ, prefer the larger. When they match, use explicit string comparison. Neither current wall-clock time nor local arrival position belongs in this protocol order.

{{practice:06a}}

## Convergence is conditional; finality is stronger

Now compare two more observations. A finite set of valid records eventually reaches every honest node: all compute the same maximum, so they converge. A sender keeps generating longer valid branches, or some messages are delayed forever: the assumptions of that convergence argument no longer hold. A shared sorting rule does not cause missing information to arrive or limit an adversary's proposals.

Even when all nodes select one head now, a longer competing branch can arrive later. This rule permits reorganization. It supplies no irreversible finality and no economic or computational cost for building length. Calling it “longest chain” must not smuggle in assumptions from proof-of-work systems. The lab has no mining or stake, and is not a security design for an open network.

Safety means a prohibited outcome never occurs under declared assumptions. Liveness means a required outcome eventually occurs under declared assumptions. “All nodes eventually select the same tip after this finite schedule is fully delivered” is a modest convergence property. “A certified value at a fixed height cannot conflict with another certified value” will be a different safety property in the next module.

{{practice:06b}}

## Checkpoint and changed case

Implement and run `node lab.mjs check 06`. Keep a written counterexample to the statement “the selected transaction is final.” You need only a valid later branch that wins the ordering rule.

For a changed case, two nodes have identical validated records but different local mempools. Predict whether head selection differs. Then let one node miss a single height-4 record. Explain why a temporary disagreement no longer demonstrates a comparator bug. Distinguish different computations over the same input from the same computation over different input.

`courses/blockchain-laboratory/lessons/07-quorum.md`:

```md
# 07 · What can a quorum promise?

One side of a partition repeats the same signed vote three times. Verify distinct authenticated voters and explain why safety can require waiting.

Your artifact is `verifyCertificate`. The lab has four fixed validators and asks for three distinct matching votes. A vote binds the voter, height and block ID in a separate signed message domain. This checker is not a complete consensus protocol: it contains no leader election, round changes, locking protocol or durable restart logic.

## Count identities, not packets

Worked example: votes from a, b and c for block X at height 2 form a three-voter certificate. Packets [a,a,b] do not. A vote by c for X at height 3 does not join the height-2 certificate. A vote by c for Y at height 2 does not support X. Invalid packets may be ignored; they must not prevent three other valid matching votes from forming a certificate.

Your verifier first checks that the target is a nonnegative safe integer height and a 64-character lowercase hex block ID, and that votes arrive as an array. It then checks each vote's exact shape, fixed membership, matching target and signature before adding the voter to a Set. Complete the last step: return true only if the Set has at least three names. Do not count the same key twice because the envelope was copied.

The order of those steps matters. Suppose a forged packet names a, followed by genuine matching votes from a, b and c. Reserving a's name before checking the forged signature would discard the later genuine vote and hide an available quorum. Even an authentic vote for another height must not reserve that identity for this height. Before adding an identity, decide which checks must already have succeeded. Then compare the forged-first and forged-last orders: both must recognize the same three valid voters. This prevents invalid evidence from suppressing progress; it does not create any new consensus or network-liveness guarantee.

Consider two size-three subsets of four validators. They overlap in at least 3+3−4=2 validators. If at most one validator equivocates, at least one overlapping validator is honest. If honest validators never sign competing values for the same height, two conflicting certificates at that height cannot both form. Every “if” in that sentence is part of the result.

{{practice:07a}}

## The cost of preserving the rule

In a 2+2 partition, neither side can collect three local identities. Duplicating packets would not create a quorum; lowering the threshold would change the overlap argument. Waiting preserves the declared fixed-height safety rule but prevents local progress.

Healing the partition is not by itself a complete liveness proof. If honest validators already cast incompatible votes and never change them, a three-vote certificate may remain impossible even after messages resume. Real consensus protocols need additional rules to move through rounds safely. We deliberately have not implemented those rules, so do not claim general Byzantine consensus or eventual certificate formation.

A certificate also does not replace block validity. Three keys can sign a false state claim; your node still validates the block. Conversely, a valid selected branch may have no certificate. Keep the layers separate in both code and your incident report.

{{practice:07b}}

## Checkpoint and changed case

Run `node lab.mjs check 07`. Then write two short arguments: one for fixed-height uniqueness under the stated fault bound, one showing loss of liveness in a 2+2 cut. Use identities and sets, not a vague claim that “a majority is secure.”

For a changed case, permit two equivocating validators. Construct two different sets of three voters that overlap only in those two. Each remaining honest validator can sign one value without breaking its rule, yet both certificates can form. This is a counterexample outside the original fault bound, not a contradiction of the bound. Explain why a correct cryptographic signature does not stop an authorized signer from signing incompatible messages.

```

# 08 · Recover without inventing history

A partition heals after both sides executed valid but conflicting transactions. Rebuild from the winning branch and investigate the pending work that survives.

Your artifact is `reconcile`, followed by an incident report from the supplied finite scheduler. This is the integration task: every earlier mechanism is exercised, while the transport, keys and trace recorder remain supplied.

## Revalidate from the selected state

Worked example: old branch spends a nonce 0 sending 20 to b. The selected new branch spends a nonce 0 sending 30 to c. The old transaction was authentic and valid when first accepted; it is ineligible now because the new state already consumed nonce 0. Returning it to a ready pool without revalidation resurrects a conflict.

Do not reverse old balance arithmetic into whichever state happens to be current. The supplied path records already carry the deterministic result of every validated branch. Select the new tip's state, gather old-branch transactions plus pending candidates, remove transaction IDs included on the new path, then rerun the bounded mempool policy. Return a copy of the new state. Pending transfers are not yet committed balances.

Complete the final step: a still-valid orphan b→c can fund a waiting c→d. Repeated eligible selection must discover the dependency even if c→d appears earlier among candidates. This is module 04 returning inside a different problem, not a separate algorithm to improvise.

{{practice:08a}}

## Storage policy has observable consequences

The ready-only pool returns eligible candidates and drops the rest. During a sequence of intermediate head changes, a candidate may become temporarily ineligible and be forgotten. If a later state would permit it, correct validation cannot recover input that no longer exists. A separate retained candidate queue, journal or rebroadcast mechanism could address that liveness concern; our runtime does not pretend it has one.

The simulator therefore reports two observations separately: the live ready pool after all intermediate updates, and one recovery using an explicitly retained set of original candidates. Differences are evidence of the declared policy, not a reason to fabricate a successful rebroadcast. Generated ephemeral keys can change equal-height ID ties between processes; the selected final longer branch and retained-candidate result are stable, while intermediate trace details can differ.

On healing, left receives a fabricated high-height claim and a false-root claim, then R3, R2, R1 in reverse ancestry order, plus a duplicate R1. Right receives L2 before L1. A copied vote packet tries to turn two voter identities into three votes. A peer also presents a genuine proof of c's old L2 record as evidence about the current selected state.

```md
# 09 · Remember your vote after a crash

The node restarts. Its signing key still works. Does it remember what it promised?

Module 07's uniqueness argument assumes that honest validators never vote for two different values at one height. A perfectly valid signature does not enforce that rule. In this extension you build the missing vote guard, crash it between effects, and connect one forgotten decision to two conflicting certificates.

This is an optional 60–90 minute project after module 07; the estimate has not been calibrated with learners. Keep your existing work/protocol.mjs. Your new artifact is work/vote-guard.mjs plus a short restart report. Only your own trusted local code belongs in this runner.

## One forgotten vote is enough to change the fault bound

Four validators are a, b, c and d; three distinct votes certify a target. Validator a deliberately signs both X and Y. Validator b sends a vote for X, crashes before remembering it durably, and then signs Y. Validator c signs only X; d signs only Y.

X now has a/b/c. Y has a/b/d. Both sets have three authentic votes. Their intersection is a/b: one malicious signer and one signer whose restart broke its promise. The original “at most one equivocator” assumption is false. The certificate checker is correct to recognize both sets; it cannot repair the history of signing.

Write those two voter sets before you code. Identify which participant's behavior you can prevent with a local journal and which behavior you cannot prevent if a participant deliberately bypasses it.

## Save the decision before it can leave

The supplied model executes an ordered list of effects. A persist effect atomically appends one record to durable history before the next effect runs. A send effect signs the record and makes the vote observable. A crash discards the remaining effects, but keeps committed history. A failed persist aborts the rest of the list. Only one request runs at a time.

Worked example: the journal is empty and the request is X at height 7. If you send first, a crash between sending and persistence leaves peers holding X while your recovered journal is empty. A later request for Y looks new. If you persist first, the same crash leaves X remembered but unsent. After recovery, resending X is safe; changing the decision to Y is not.

A stored but unsent vote may delay progress. That cost is real. Do not delete the record just because you cannot find a receipt from a peer: absence of an acknowledgement does not establish that a vote was never observed.

{{practice:09a}}

## Implement the planner

Run these commands from the course directory:

```sh
node lab.mjs lesson 09
node restart.mjs start
node restart.mjs check
```

The first check must fail with NOT_IMPLEMENTED. Edit work/vote-guard.mjs. The starter is separate so you do not have to replace or extend your earlier protocol implementation. Starting again refuses to overwrite it.

Implement planVote(journal, request), a pure function. Every vote record has exactly height and blockId. Height is a nonnegative safe integer; blockId is 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters. The journal is an array of these records for one fixed validator key on classroom-v1. It contains every committed decision; nothing is pruned in this model. Requests are assumed to name already validated blocks. You do not implement signatures or block validity again.

First validate the complete journal. Malformed history, or two different block IDs at one height, returns exactly {ok:false,code:'JOURNAL'}. Identical duplicate records are permitted, including when they are not adjacent. Inspect the whole history even if an earlier entry matches the request. Next validate the request; malformed requests return {ok:false,code:'REQUEST'}. Then apply the decision rule.

For a previously unseen height, return {ok:true,effects:[...]} with exactly two effects: persist the requested vote, then send it. Each effect is {type:'persist'|'send',vote:{height,blockId}}. For the same height and same block ID already recorded, return only the send effect; retries must not grow the journal. For the same height with a different block ID, return {ok:false,code:'CONFLICT'} with no effects. Never mutate the journal or request.

This is a map of decisions by height, not just a highest-height watermark. A new lower height is allowed if absent from the journal; an old recorded height remains protected after higher decisions. Real protocols can impose other height/round/step rules. Do not import those rules into this interface.

Start by answering three implementation questions: what data structure makes conflict lookup clear, why must journal validation finish before returning a retry, and which effect can safely occur first? The source supplies validVote and sameVote helpers in lib/restart-model.mjs if useful; using them is optional.

Run node restart.mjs check after each repair. The checks include retries, malformed recovery, write failure and all 729 three-request schedules built from three requests and three crash cuts. That is a bounded exploration, not a proof for arbitrary inputs. Receipts preserve your source before execution under work/restart-attempts/.

## Predict, crash, compare

Before running the experiment, create work/restart-report.md. Predict these three cases for X followed, after restart, by conflicting Y: crash before effect 0; crash after effect 0; finish both effects and restart. For each, write the recovered journal, emitted votes and possible certificates. Then repeat your prediction for the deliberately wrong send-before-persist planner.

```sh
node restart.mjs simulate crash
```

This uses your earlier verifyCertificate and first runs module 07's checks, including the accepted eligibility-before-dedup repair. If that prerequisite fails, the experiment stops. Inspect learner.rows and sendBeforePersistControl.rows in the receipt. With a correct guard, no crash-only row should contain two certificates. The unsafe control should expose the gap after its first effect. Explain why “allSignaturesAuthentic: true” can coexist with conflicting certificates.

The two block IDs are synthetic names. The certificate experiment does not execute their transactions or choose a head. Its evidence concerns signing discipline only. Unlike simulate transfer from module 08, this experiment is deterministic at the decision level, but each run has new ephemeral keys and signatures. Its receipt includes public keys and signed votes; it does not export private keys. Compare decisions and memberships, not signature bytes between runs.

## Changed case: the disk lies about the past

Now change one assumption: after a crash, the storage layer restores an empty old snapshot, erasing even a committed vote. The validator identities rotate to d as the malicious signer, c as the restarted signer, b voting only X and a voting only Y; the height is 19. Predict the outcome with your correct guard before running:

```sh
node restart.mjs simulate rollback
```

Find a row in which X was persisted and sent before the snapshot rollback, yet Y is later sent too. Name both quorums and their intersection. Why can't a pure function distinguish an erased empty journal from a genuinely fresh one? What assumption must a stronger system provide outside this function? Discuss a trusted non-rollbackable record or exclusive signer as an assumption to investigate, not as a security feature implemented here.

{{practice:09b}}

## Deliver evidence and state the boundary

Your report should contain the saved predictions, the source hashes and receipt paths, a concrete unsafe crash trace, a concrete safe trace, and the changed-case counterexample. Explain the difference between a duplicate retransmission and a conflicting vote. Explain why rejecting every request would satisfy silence but fail the project's progress requirements. Include one additional threat outside the model, such as two concurrent processes sharing a signing key with separate journals.

A reviewer awards 0 (missing or incorrect), 1 (partly supported), or 2 (correct with a concrete trace) for each: effect ordering and retry behavior; derivation of the two certificate sets; explanation of the rollback indistinguishability; honest distinction between modeled crashes and real persistence. The project target is passing executable checks and 2 in each reasoning dimension. It is not a validated mastery threshold.

The journal is an in-memory model, not a filesystem implementation. The fixture holds one key pair per identity across simulated crashes inside a single process, then discards it at process exit. We do not test fsync, torn writes, real power loss, key migration, concurrent signers, adversarial storage or network transport. Modules 01–08 retain their original assumptions. This extension supplies no locking across consensus rounds, proof of finality or guaranteed progress after split votes.

For context, Tendermint's documentation describes flushing its consensus write-ahead log before processing its validator's own messages to support deterministic recovery. Our much smaller decision journal isolates one ordering lesson; it is not Tendermint's WAL or signing protocol. See SOURCES.md for the reference.

```mjs
import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
import { fixture, clone, sha256, txBytes, txId, proofFor, blockId, verifyVote, accountBytes, leafHash, branchHash, rootHash } from './support.mjs';

export function cases(p) {
  const out=[];
  const add=(module,id,requirement,run)=>out.push({module,id,requirement,run});
  const makeBlock=(f,parent,transactions)=>{
    let state=clone(parent.state);

    const f=fixture(),g=genesis(f),oldTx=f.transaction('b','c',5,0),pendingTx=f.transaction('b','d',6,0);
    const old=record(f,makeBlock(f,g,[oldTx]),g),next=record(f,makeBlock(f,g,[f.transaction('a','d',1,0)]),g);

    const many=Array.from({length:17},(_,n)=>f.transaction('a','b',1,n));
    assert.equal(p.reconcile([g],[g],many,f.ctx).mempool.length,16,'reconcile uses limit 16');
  });
  return out;
}

export async function runChecks(protocol,scope='all') {
  const selected=cases(protocol).filter(c=>scope==='all'||c.module===scope),results=[];
  if(!selected.length) throw new Error(`Unknown check scope ${scope}`);
  for(const c of selected) {
    try {await c.run();results.push({module:c.module,id:c.id,requirement:c.requirement,ok:true});}
    catch(error) {results.push({module:c.module,id:c.id,requirement:c.requirement,ok:false,diagnostic:error.message,actual:error.actual,expected:error.expected});}
  }
  return {scope,total:results.length,passed:results.filter(r=>r.ok).length,results};
}

export async function sourceIdentity(root){
  const files={};for(const name of learnerFiles)files[name]=sha256(await readFile(join(root,name)));
  return {algorithm:'SHA-256',files,hash:sha256(JSON.stringify(files))};
}

`courses/blockchain-laboratory/lib/restart-checks.mjs`:

```mjs
import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
import {clone,sha256} from './support.mjs';
import {executePlan,conflicts,sameVote} from './restart-model.mjs';

const vote=(height,label)=>({height,blockId:sha256(label)});
function freeze(x) { if(x && typeof x==='object') {Object.values(x).forEach(freeze);Object.freeze(x);} return x; }
const effect=(type,v)=>({type,vote:v});
const yes=effects=>({ok:true,effects});
const no=code=>({ok:false,code});

export function runRestartChecks(planVote) {
  const results=[];
  const test=(id,requirement,fn)=>{try{fn();results.push({id,requirement,ok:true});}catch(e){results.push({id,requirement,ok:false,diagnostic:e.message});}};
  const x=vote(7,'x'), y=vote(7,'y'), z=vote(12,'z');
  test('new-vote','Persist a new decision before sending it',()=>assert.deepEqual(planVote([],x),yes([effect('persist',x),effect('send',x)])));
  test('same-vote-retry','Retry an identical durable vote without growing the journal',()=>assert.deepEqual(planVote([x],x),yes([effect('send',x)])));
  test('same-height-conflict','Reject a competing value even after reconstructed startup',()=>assert.deepEqual(planVote(JSON.parse(JSON.stringify([x])),y),no('CONFLICT')));
  test('remember-all-heights','Later heights do not erase earlier decisions; independent lower heights are allowed',()=>{
    assert.deepEqual(planVote([x,z],y),no('CONFLICT'));
    assert.deepEqual(planVote([z],x),yes([effect('persist',x),effect('send',x)]));
  });
  test('duplicate-recovery','Identical replayed journal records are harmless',()=>assert.deepEqual(planVote([x,z,x],x),yes([effect('send',x)])));
  test('bad-journal','Malformed or internally conflicting history fails closed, even at unrelated heights',()=>{
    for(const j of [null,{},[null],[{...x,height:-1}],[{...x,blockId:'not-a-hash'}],[{...x,extra:true}],[x,y],[z,{...z,blockId:x.blockId}]]) assert.deepEqual(planVote(j,x),no('JOURNAL'));
    assert.deepEqual(planVote([x,y],null),no('JOURNAL'),'Journal validation precedes request validation');
  });
  test('bad-request','Reject malformed heights, IDs and shapes without a side effect',()=>{
    for(const r of [null,{},[],{...x,height:1.5},{...x,height:-1},{...x,height:Infinity},{...x,height:Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER+1},{...x,height:'7'},{...x,blockId:x.blockId.toUpperCase()},{...x,blockId:'a'.repeat(63)},{...x,extra:1}]) assert.deepEqual(planVote([],r),no('REQUEST'));
    for(const height of [0,Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER]) {const r={...x,height};assert.deepEqual(planVote([],r),yes([effect('persist',r),effect('send',r)]));}
  });
  test('pure-inputs','Planning never edits its journal or request',()=>{
    const j=freeze([clone(x)]),r=freeze(clone(z)),before=JSON.stringify({j,r});
    const result=planVote(j,r); assert.equal(result.ok,true); assert.equal(JSON.stringify({j,r}),before);
  });
  test('crash-cuts','Every boundary preserves non-equivocation across a restart and competing request',()=>{
    for(const cut of [0,1,2]) {
      const first=executePlan(planVote,[],x,{cut});
      const second=executePlan(planVote,JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(first.durable)),y);
      assert.equal(conflicts([...first.sent,...second.sent]),false,`Conflicting emissions at cut ${cut}`);
      if(cut===0) assert.deepEqual(second.sent,[y],'Nothing committed before first persist: Y can proceed');
      if(cut===1) {assert.deepEqual(first.sent,[]);assert.equal(second.decision.ok,false,'A durable unsent X still blocks Y');}
    }
  });
  test('retry-after-crash','The same vote remains sendable after every crash boundary',()=>{
    for(const cut of [0,1,2]) {
      const first=executePlan(planVote,[],x,{cut});
      const retry=executePlan(planVote,first.durable,x);
      assert.deepEqual(retry.sent,[x]);assert.deepEqual(retry.durable,[x]);
    }
  });
  test('storage-failure','A failed durable write stops the effect sequence before any send',()=>{
    const result=executePlan(planVote,[],x,{failPersist:true});assert.deepEqual(result.sent,[]);assert.deepEqual(result.durable,[]);
  });
  let explored=0;
  test('bounded-schedules','Explore all three-request schedules over two values, two heights and every effect cut',()=>{
    const requests=[x,y,z];
    function visit(journal,sent,depth) {
      if(depth===3) {explored++;return;}
      for(const request of requests) for(const cut of [0,1,2]) {
        const result=executePlan(planVote,journal,request,{cut});
        const combined=[...sent,...result.sent];
        assert.equal(conflicts(combined),false,`Conflicting emissions: ${JSON.stringify(combined)}`);
        for(const emitted of result.sent) assert.ok(result.durable.some(saved=>sameVote(saved,emitted)),'Sent vote is absent from durable history');
        visit(JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(result.durable)),combined,depth+1);
      }
    }
    visit([],[],0);assert.equal(explored,729);
  });
  return {passed:results.filter(r=>r.ok).length,total:results.length,exploredSchedules:explored,results,
    scope:'Public executable contract and 729 bounded schedules. Not exhaustive over arbitrary programs, storage faults or real networks.'};
}

`courses/blockchain-laboratory/lib/restart-model.mjs`:

```mjs
import {clone, exactKeys, hex64, fixture, sha256, verifyVote} from './support.mjs';

export const validVote = vote => exactKeys(vote, ['height','blockId']) &&
  Number.isSafeInteger(vote.height) && vote.height >= 0 && hex64(vote.blockId);
export const sameVote = (a,b) => a.height === b.height && a.blockId === b.blockId;

// The model owns persistence and transport; the learner owns the ordered plan.
// Each persist atomically becomes durable before the next effect. A crash cuts
// between effects, discarding the unexecuted suffix, never committed journal data.
export function executePlan(planVote, journal, request, {cut=Infinity,failPersist=false}={}) {
  const durable=clone(journal), sent=[], trace=[];
  const decision=planVote(clone(journal),clone(request));
  if (!decision || typeof decision.ok !== 'boolean') throw new Error('planVote must return an ok decision');
  if (!decision.ok) {
    if (!exactKeys(decision,['ok','code']) || !['JOURNAL','REQUEST','CONFLICT'].includes(decision.code)) throw new Error('Invalid rejection decision');
    return {durable,sent,trace:[{event:'reject',code:decision.code}],decision};
  }
  if (!exactKeys(decision,['ok','effects']) || !Array.isArray(decision.effects) || decision.effects.length > 2) throw new Error('A successful plan needs at most two effects');
  for (const [index,effect] of decision.effects.entries()) {
    if (index >= cut) { trace.push({event:'crash',beforeEffect:index}); break; }
    if (!exactKeys(effect,['type','vote']) || !['persist','send'].includes(effect.type) || !validVote(effect.vote) || !sameVote(effect.vote,request)) throw new Error('Effects must persist/send only the requested vote');
    if (effect.type === 'persist') {
      if (failPersist) { trace.push({event:'persist-failed',vote:clone(effect.vote)}); break; }
      durable.push(clone(effect.vote));
    }
    if (effect.type === 'send') sent.push(clone(effect.vote));
    trace.push({event:effect.type,vote:clone(effect.vote)});
  }
  return {durable,sent,trace,decision};
}

export function conflicts(votes) {
  return votes.some((a,i)=>votes.slice(i+1).some(b=>a.height===b.height && a.blockId!==b.blockId));
}

// This deliberately wrong ordering is a public counterexample, not a solution.
export function sendBeforePersist(journal,request) {
  const old=journal.find(v=>v.height===request.height);
  if(old && !sameVote(old,request)) return {ok:false,code:'CONFLICT'};
  return {ok:true,effects:[{type:'send',vote:clone(request)},...(old?[]:[{type:'persist',vote:clone(request)}])]};
}

// Finite, reproducible schedule of requests/cuts. Signatures vary per process,
// while the votes, journal decisions and certificate membership stay the same.
export function restartIncident(planVote,verifyCertificate,{rollback=false,transfer=false}={}) {
  const f=fixture();
  const height=transfer?19:7;
  const x={height,blockId:sha256(transfer?'transfer-left':'restart-left')};
  const y={height,blockId:sha256(transfer?'transfer-right':'restart-right')};
  const [byzantine,restarted,leftOnly,rightOnly]=transfer?['d','c','b','a']:['a','b','c','d'];
  const cuts=[0,1,2];
  const rows=cuts.map(cut=>{
    const first=executePlan(planVote,[],x,{cut});
    const recovered=rollback?[]:first.durable;
    const second=executePlan(planVote,recovered,y);
    const emitted=[...first.sent,...second.sent];
    const votesX=[f.vote(byzantine,height,x.blockId),f.vote(leftOnly,height,x.blockId)];
    const votesY=[f.vote(byzantine,height,y.blockId),f.vote(rightOnly,height,y.blockId)];
    for(const vote of emitted) {
      if(sameVote(vote,x)) votesX.push(f.vote(restarted,height,x.blockId));
      if(sameVote(vote,y)) votesY.push(f.vote(restarted,height,y.blockId));
    }
    const certificateX=verifyCertificate(votesX,height,x.blockId,f.ctx);
    const certificateY=verifyCertificate(votesY,height,y.blockId,f.ctx);
    if(typeof certificateX!=='boolean'||typeof certificateY!=='boolean') throw new Error('verifyCertificate must return boolean');
    return {cut,first:first.trace,recoveredJournal:clone(recovered),second:second.trace,
      votesX,votesY,allSignaturesAuthentic:[...votesX,...votesY].every(v=>verifyVote(v,f.ctx)),
      certificateX,certificateY,conflictingCertificates:certificateX&&certificateY,
      restartedValidatorEquivocated:conflicts(emitted)};
  });
  return {height,x,y,roles:{byzantine,restarted,leftOnly,rightOnly},rollback,
    publicKeys:Object.fromEntries([...f.ctx.publicKeys].map(([name,key])=>[name,key.export({format:'pem',type:'spki'})])),rows,
    scope:'Finite in-memory crash model; keys survive modeled crashes within one process. No actual fsync, process restart, network, block-validity, round-change or general-finality claim.'};
}

`courses/blockchain-laboratory/lib/simulator.mjs`:

```mjs
import { fixture, clone, blockId, txId, proofFor, exactKeys } from './support.mjs';
import { createPublicKey } from 'node:crypto';

// A bounded in-process delivery model. It opens no sockets and models no clock drift.
export class LocalNode {
  constructor(name, protocol, ctx, genesis) {
    this.name=name;this.p=protocol;this.ctx=ctx;this.records=new Map([[genesis.id,clone(genesis)]]);
    this.head=genesis.id;this.buffer=[];this.pending=[];this.events=[];
  }
  path(id=this.head) {
    const out=[];let r=this.records.get(id);
    while(r){out.unshift(r);r=r.block?this.records.get(r.block.parent):null;}
    return out;
  }
  receive(block,label='block') {
    if(!exactKeys(block,['parent','height','transactions','stateRoot'])){this.events.push({label,decision:'rejected',code:'SHAPE'});return;}
    if(!Array.isArray(block.transactions)||block.transactions.length>16){this.events.push({label,decision:'rejected',code:'TRANSACTIONS'});return;}
    let id;try{id=blockId(block);}catch{this.events.push({label,decision:'rejected',code:'SHAPE'});return;}
    if(this.records.has(id)){this.events.push({label,decision:'duplicate'});return;}
    const parent=this.records.get(block.parent);
    if(!parent){this.buffer.push({block,label});this.events.push({label,decision:'buffered: parent missing'});return;}
    const result=this.p.validateBlock(block,parent,this.ctx);
    if(!result.ok){this.events.push({label,decision:'rejected',code:result.code});return;}
    this.records.set(result.id,result);
    const oldPath=this.path(),next=this.p.chooseHead([...this.records.values()]);
    if(!this.records.has(next)) throw new Error('chooseHead returned an unknown record');
    if(next!==this.head){const rebuilt=this.p.reconcile(oldPath,this.path(next),this.pending,this.ctx);this.head=rebuilt.head;this.pending=rebuilt.mempool;}
    this.events.push({label,decision:'accepted',selected:this.head===id,height:result.height});
    const ready=this.buffer.filter(x=>this.records.has(x.block.parent));
    this.buffer=this.buffer.filter(x=>!this.records.has(x.block.parent));
    for(const item of ready)this.receive(item.block,item.label);
  }
}

function build(protocol,f,parent,transactions) {
  let state=clone(parent.state);
  for(const tx of transactions){const r=protocol.applyTx(state,tx,f.ctx);if(!r.ok)throw new Error(`Scenario construction failed: ${r.code}`);state=r.state;}
  const block={parent:parent.id,height:parent.height+1,transactions,stateRoot:protocol.stateRoot(state)};
  const record={id:blockId(block),height:block.height,state,block};return record;
}

export function simulate(protocol,mode='partition') {
  if(!['partition','transfer'].includes(mode))throw new Error('Use partition or transfer');
  const f=fixture(),g={id:'0'.repeat(64),height:0,state:f.state};
  const t={
    leftSpend:f.transaction('a','b',30,0),leftFund:f.transaction('b','c',8,0),leftChild:f.transaction('c','d',5,0),
    rightSpend:f.transaction('a','c',50,0),rightReturn:f.transaction('c','a',12,0),rightNext:f.transaction('a','d',2,1),
    waitingB:f.transaction('b','a',4,1),waitingC:f.transaction('c','d',6,1),
  };
  const L1=build(protocol,f,g,[t.leftSpend]);
  const L2=build(protocol,f,L1,[t.leftFund,t.leftChild]);
  const R1=build(protocol,f,g,[t.rightSpend]);
  const R2=build(protocol,f,R1,[t.rightReturn]);
  const R3=build(protocol,f,R2,[t.rightNext]);
  const scenario={version:1,mode,genesis:g,transactions:t,
    publicKeys:[...f.ctx.publicKeys].map(([name,key])=>[name,key.export({type:'spki',format:'pem'})]),
    blocks:Object.fromEntries(Object.entries({L1,L2,R1,R2,R3}).map(([name,r])=>[name,r.block])),
    votes:[f.vote('a',2,L2.id),f.vote('a',2,L2.id),f.vote('b',2,L2.id)]};
  return replayScenario(protocol,scenario);
}

export function replayScenario(protocol,scenario){
  if(scenario?.version!==1 || !['partition','transfer'].includes(scenario.mode))throw new Error('Unsupported replay scenario');
  const mode=scenario.mode,g=clone(scenario.genesis),t=clone(scenario.transactions);
  const f={ctx:{network:'classroom-v1',publicKeys:new Map(scenario.publicKeys.map(([name,key])=>[name,createPublicKey(key)]))}};
  const records={};
  for(const [name,parent] of [['L1',g],['L2','L1'],['R1',g],['R2','R1'],['R3','R2']]){
    const p=typeof parent==='string'?records[parent]:parent;
    const r=protocol.validateBlock(scenario.blocks[name],p,f.ctx);
    if(!r.ok)throw new Error(`Replay valid branch ${name} failed: ${r.code}`);
    records[name]=r;
  }
  const {L1,L2,R1,R2,R3}=records;
  const labels=new Map([[g.id,'genesis'],[L1.id,'L1'],[L2.id,'L2'],[R1.id,'R1'],[R2.id,'R2'],[R3.id,'R3']]);
  const txLabels=new Map(Object.entries(t).map(([k,v])=>[txId(v),k]));
  const left=new LocalNode('left',protocol,f.ctx,g),right=new LocalNode('right',protocol,f.ctx,g);
  left.receive(L1.block,'L1');left.receive(L2.block,'L2');right.receive(R1.block,'R1');right.receive(R2.block,'R2');right.receive(R3.block,'R3');
  const before={left:labels.get(left.head),right:labels.get(right.head)};
  const staleProof=proofFor(L2.state,'c');
  const votes=scenario.votes;
  const duplicateCertificate=protocol.verifyCertificate(votes,2,L2.id,f.ctx);
  if(mode==='transfer') {
    left.pending=[t.waitingB,t.waitingC];
    const forged={...R3.block,height:999,stateRoot:'f'.repeat(64)};
    left.receive(forged,'forged-height');
    left.receive({...R3.block,stateRoot:'f'.repeat(64)},'forged-root');
    left.receive(R3.block,'R3');left.receive(R2.block,'R2');left.receive(R1.block,'R1');left.receive(R1.block,'R1-duplicate');
  } else {
    left.receive(R1.block,'R1');left.receive(R2.block,'R2');left.receive(R3.block,'R3');
  }
  right.receive(L2.block,'L2');right.receive(L1.block,'L1');
  // Rebuild once against the final branch from the original abandoned path,
  // preserving candidates that the strict ready-only pool would drop during intermediate heads.
  // The incident report makes this difference visible instead of hiding it.
  const recovery=protocol.reconcile([g,L1,L2],[g,R1,R2,R3],mode==='transfer'?[t.waitingB,t.waitingC]:[],f.ctx);
  const after={left:labels.get(left.head),right:labels.get(right.head)};
  const state=left.records.get(left.head).state;
  return {
    model:'In-process, finite delivery schedule; ephemeral keys; no network service',mode,before,after,
    converged:left.head===right.head,state,total:Object.values(state).reduce((n,a)=>n+a.balance,0),
    staleProofAccepted:protocol.verifyProof(protocol.stateRoot(state),'c',L2.state.c,staleProof),
    duplicateCertificateAccepted:duplicateCertificate,
    livePool:left.pending.map(x=>txLabels.get(txId(x))??txId(x)),
    recoveryFromRetainedCandidates:recovery.mempool.map(x=>txLabels.get(txId(x))??txId(x)),
    leftEvents:left.events,rightEvents:right.events,
    note:'The ready-only live pool may discard candidates during intermediate reorgs. The retained-candidate recovery is a separate explicit call, not hidden durable pool storage.',
    scenario:clone(scenario),
  };
}

```mjs
import { createHash, generateKeyPairSync, sign, verify } from 'node:crypto';

export const NETWORK = 'classroom-v1';
export const clone = x => structuredClone(x);
export const sha256 = bytes => createHash('sha256').update(bytes).digest('hex');
export const hex64 = x => typeof x === 'string' && /^[0-9a-f]{64}$/.test(x);
export const hex128 = x => typeof x === 'string' && /^[0-9a-f]{128}$/.test(x);
export const exactKeys = (x, keys) => x !== null && typeof x === 'object' && !Array.isArray(x) && Object.keys(x).sort().join('|') === [...keys].sort().join('|');
export const txBytes = tx => Buffer.from(JSON.stringify(['LAB:TX:1', tx.network, tx.from, tx.to, tx.amount, tx.nonce]));
export const txId = tx => sha256(Buffer.concat([txBytes(tx), Buffer.from(String(tx.signature))]));
export const accountBytes = (name, record) => Buffer.from(JSON.stringify([name, record.balance, record.nonce]));
export const leafHash = bytes => sha256(Buffer.concat([Buffer.from([0]), bytes]));
export const branchHash = (left, right) => sha256(Buffer.concat([Buffer.from([1]), Buffer.from(left, 'hex'), Buffer.from(right, 'hex')]));
export function rootHash(count, top) {
  const n = Buffer.alloc(4); n.writeUInt32BE(count);
  return sha256(Buffer.concat([Buffer.from([2]), n, Buffer.from(top, 'hex')]));
}
export const blockId = block => sha256(Buffer.from(JSON.stringify(['LAB:BLOCK:1', block.parent, block.height, block.transactions.map(txId), block.stateRoot])));
export const voteBytes = vote => Buffer.from(JSON.stringify(['LAB:VOTE:1', NETWORK, vote.voter, vote.height, vote.blockId]));
export function verifyTx(tx, ctx) {
  try { return verify(null, txBytes(tx), ctx.publicKeys.get(tx.from), Buffer.from(tx.signature, 'hex')); }
  catch { return false; }
}
export function verifyVote(vote, ctx) {
  try { return verify(null, voteBytes(vote), ctx.publicKeys.get(vote.voter), Buffer.from(vote.signature, 'hex')); }
  catch { return false; }
}
export function fixture() {
  const keys = new Map(['a','b','c','d'].map(name => [name, generateKeyPairSync('ed25519')]));
  const ctx = {network: NETWORK, publicKeys: new Map([...keys].map(([k,v]) => [k,v.publicKey]))};
  const state = {a:{balance:100,nonce:0}, b:{balance:40,nonce:0}, c:{balance:0,nonce:0}, d:{balance:0,nonce:0}};
  function transaction(from, to, amount, nonce, extra={}) {
    const tx = {network:NETWORK,from,to,amount,nonce,...extra};
    return {...tx,signature:sign(null,txBytes(tx),keys.get(from).privateKey).toString('hex')};
  }
  function vote(voter,height,id) {
    const v = {voter,height,blockId:id};
    return {...v,signature:sign(null,voteBytes(v),keys.get(voter).privateKey).toString('hex')};
  }
  return {ctx,state,transaction,vote};
}

// Proof production is supplied scaffolding. Learners implement the independent verifier.
export function proofFor(state, name) {
  const names = Object.keys(state).sort(); let index = names.indexOf(name);
  if (index < 0) throw new Error('No membership proof for an absent account');
  const proof = {index,count:names.length,siblings:[]};
  let level = names.map(k=>leafHash(accountBytes(k,state[k])));
  while (level.length > 1) {
    proof.siblings.push(level[index ^ 1] ?? level[index]);
    const next = [];
    for (let i=0; i<level.length; i+=2) next.push(branchHash(level[i],level[i+1] ?? level[i]));
    level = next; index = Math.floor(index/2);
  }
  return proof;
}

'use strict';
(() => {
  const data=JSON.parse(document.getElementById('practice-data').textContent);
  const key='blockchain-lab-practice-v1:'+data.identity.hash;
  const status=document.getElementById('storage-status');let history=[],storageOK=true;
  try{const saved=localStorage.getItem(key);if(saved){history=JSON.parse(saved);if(!Array.isArray(history))throw new Error('Invalid history');}}
  catch(error){storageOK=false;status.textContent='Saved history could not be read. Existing data has not been replaced. Use terminal practice or export the current readable history.';}
  const refreshers=[];
  const el=(tag,text)=>{const node=document.createElement(tag);if(text!==undefined)node.textContent=text;return node;};
  function save(attempt){
    if(!storageOK)throw new Error('History is unavailable; no response committed.');
    const next=[...history,attempt];localStorage.setItem(key,JSON.stringify(next));history=next;
  }
  for(const box of document.querySelectorAll('[data-item]')){
    const item=data.items.find(x=>x.id===box.dataset.item),form=el('form'),fieldset=el('fieldset');
    fieldset.append(el('legend','Practice '+item.id));fieldset.append(el('h3',item.question));
    item.options.forEach((option,i)=>{const label=el('label'),input=el('input');input.type='radio';input.name=item.id;input.value=String(i);input.required=true;label.append(input,el('span',option));fieldset.append(label);});
    const button=el('button','Commit response'),result=el('div'),previous=el('p');button.type='submit';result.className='result';result.setAttribute('role','status');previous.className='history';
    const refresh=()=>{
      const tries=history.filter(x=>x.item===item.id);
      if(!tries.length){previous.textContent='No response committed yet. Feedback appears after saving.';return;}
      const latest=tries.at(-1);
      previous.textContent=`${tries.length} saved attempt(s). First choice: ${tries[0].choice+1}. Latest choice: ${latest.choice+1}. Revisions remain in your export.`;
      const chosen=fieldset.querySelector(`input[value="${latest.choice}"]`);if(chosen)chosen.checked=true;
      result.textContent=latest.feedback??'Saved choice restored. Submit again for current feedback; the historical record has not been regraded.';
    };refreshers.push(refresh);refresh();
    form.append(fieldset,button,result,previous);box.append(form);
    form.addEventListener('submit',event=>{event.preventDefault();const checked=form.querySelector('input:checked');if(!checked)return;
      const choice=Number(checked.value),attempt={item:item.id,question:item.question,options:item.options,choice,at:new Date().toISOString(),courseHash:data.identity.hash,assistance:history.some(x=>x.item===item.id)?'prior feedback available':'not declared',feedback:`${choice===item.answer?'Correct.':'Revise this answer.'} Correct answer: ${item.options[item.answer]}\n${item.feedback[choice]}`};
      try{save(attempt);result.textContent=`${choice===item.answer?'Correct.':'Revise this answer.'} Correct answer: ${item.options[item.answer]}\n${item.feedback[choice]}`;refresh();}
      catch(error){result.textContent='Response was not saved; feedback withheld. Export existing work and use terminal practice. '+error.message;}
    });
  }
  // Reader builds have distinct identities. Restore only explicitly chosen,
  // exactly compatible old questions/options; never rewrite older storage.
  if(storageOK && history.length===0){
    const candidates=[];
    for(const oldKey of Object.keys(localStorage).filter(k=>k.startsWith('blockchain-lab-practice-v1:')&&k!==key)){
      try{
        const records=JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem(oldKey));
        const compatible=Array.isArray(records)&&records.length&&records.every(record=>{
          const item=data.items.find(x=>x.id===record.item);
          return item&&record.question===item.question&&JSON.stringify(record.options)===JSON.stringify(item.options)&&Number.isInteger(record.choice)&&record.choice>=0&&record.choice<item.options.length&&typeof record.at==='string';
        });
        if(compatible)candidates.push(...records);
      }catch{ /* Keep unreadable history intact; it is not an import candidate. */ }
    }
    if(candidates.length){
      const restore=el('button','Restore earlier practice');restore.id='restore-practice';restore.type='button';
      const description=el('p','Compatible practice from an earlier build is available. Restore its choices here while keeping the earlier records.');
      status.before(description,restore);
      restore.addEventListener('click',()=>{
        try{
          const records=[...new Map(candidates.map(record=>[JSON.stringify(record),record])).values()].sort((a,b)=>a.at.localeCompare(b.at));
          localStorage.setItem(key,JSON.stringify(records));history=records;for(const refresh of refreshers)refresh();
          restore.disabled=true;status.textContent=`Restored ${records.length} saved attempt(s). Earlier build records remain unchanged.`;
        }catch(error){status.textContent='Earlier practice was not restored. Original records are unchanged. '+error.message;}
      });
    }
  }
  document.getElementById('export').addEventListener('click',()=>{
    const blob=new Blob([JSON.stringify({kind:'practice only',courseIdentity:data.identity,history},null,2)],{type:'application/json'}),url=URL.createObjectURL(blob),a=el('a');
    a.href=url;a.download='blockchain-lab-practice.json';a.click();setTimeout(()=>URL.revokeObjectURL(url),1000);status.textContent='Practice export requested. It contains first and revised choices, not code checks or a mastery certificate.';
  });
})();

```mjs
import {readFile,writeFile,mkdir,copyFile,unlink} from 'node:fs/promises';
import {constants} from 'node:fs';
import {dirname,join} from 'node:path';
import {fileURLToPath,pathToFileURL} from 'node:url';
import {randomUUID} from 'node:crypto';
import {sha256} from './lib/support.mjs';
import {sourceIdentity} from './lib/identity.mjs';
import {runRestartChecks} from './lib/restart-checks.mjs';
import {restartIncident,sendBeforePersist} from './lib/restart-model.mjs';
import {runChecks} from './lib/checks.mjs';

const root=dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url));
const work=join(root,'work');
const [command,arg,...rest]=process.argv.slice(2);

async function main() {
  if(command==='start' && !arg) {
    await mkdir(work,{recursive:true});
    try {await copyFile(join(root,'starter/vote-guard.mjs'),join(work,'vote-guard.mjs'),constants.COPYFILE_EXCL);}
    catch(error) {if(error.code==='EEXIST') throw new Error('Work already exists; start refused to overwrite work/vote-guard.mjs.');throw error;}
    console.log('Created work/vote-guard.mjs. Read node lab.mjs lesson 09, then run node restart.mjs check. The starter must fail.');return;
  }
  if(!['check','simulate'].includes(command)) {
    console.log('Commands: node restart.mjs start | check | simulate crash | simulate rollback');return;
  }
  if(rest.length || (command==='check' && arg) || (command==='simulate' && !['crash','rollback'].includes(arg))) throw new Error('Use check, simulate crash, or simulate rollback.');
  const id=new Date().toISOString().replaceAll(':','-')+'-'+randomUUID().slice(0,8);
  const directory=join(work,'restart-attempts',id);
  const files=command==='check'?['vote-guard.mjs']:['vote-guard.mjs','protocol.mjs'];
  const sources={};
  for(const name of files) sources[name]=await readFile(join(work,name),'utf8');
  await mkdir(directory,{recursive:true});
  for(const [name,source] of Object.entries(sources)) await writeFile(join(directory,name),source,{flag:'wx'});
  const receipt={id,command,scenario:arg??null,startedAt:new Date().toISOString(),runtime:process.version,
    assistance:process.env.LAB_ASSISTANCE??'not declared',
    sourceHashes:Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(sources).map(([name,source])=>[name,sha256(source)])),
    courseIdentity:await sourceIdentity(root),status:'started'};
  await writeFile(join(directory,'submission.json'),JSON.stringify(receipt,null,2),{flag:'wx'});
  const temporary=[];
  async function load(name) {
    // Import the snapshotted bytes beside learner work, preserving ../lib imports.
    const path=join(work,`.restart-${id}-${name}`);temporary.push(path);
    await writeFile(path,sources[name],{flag:'wx'});return import(pathToFileURL(path).href);
  }
  let result;
  try {
    const guard=await load('vote-guard.mjs');
    if(command==='check') {
      result=runRestartChecks(guard.planVote);
      if(result.passed!==result.total) process.exitCode=1;
    }
    if(command==='simulate') {
      const p=await load('protocol.mjs');
      const prerequisites=await runChecks(p,'07');
      if(prerequisites.passed!==prerequisites.total) {
        result={blocked:'Pass module 07 before interpreting certificate results.',prerequisites};process.exitCode=1;
      }
      if(prerequisites.passed===prerequisites.total) {
        result={prerequisites,learner:restartIncident(guard.planVote,p.verifyCertificate,{rollback:arg==='rollback',transfer:arg==='rollback'})};
        if(arg==='crash') result.sendBeforePersistControl=restartIncident(sendBeforePersist,p.verifyCertificate);
        result.interpretation=arg==='rollback'?
          'An erased committed journal is outside the crash-only guarantee. Even the correct guard can double-sign after rollback; the fault bound must count that signer.':
          'Compare your ordered effects with the deliberately unsafe control. Inspect certificates and identities; command completion is not a safety verdict.';
      }
    }
  } catch(error) {result={executionError:error.message};process.exitCode=2;}
  finally {for(const path of temporary) await unlink(path).catch(()=>{});}
  const finished={...receipt,status:'finished',finishedAt:new Date().toISOString(),result};
  await writeFile(join(directory,'result.json'),JSON.stringify(finished,null,2),{flag:'wx'});
  console.log(JSON.stringify(finished,null,2));
}
main().catch(error=>{console.error(error.message);process.exitCode=2;});

`courses/boundary-lab/README.md`:

```md
# Build a boundary you can defend

This runnable **portable-core slice** accompanies Low-Level Sandbox Security. You repair the security decisions in a tiny image-filter plugin host. The supplied app already knows how to execute bytecode and display test results. Your work is to decide what it may execute, access and change.

This is a teaching model, not a production sandbox. Guest programs are tiny bytecode capsules. Everything currently runs inside one ordinary process. **Linux syscall/process confinement is not implemented or tested.** Do not run downloaded native programs or use real secrets. All fixtures contain original synthetic bytes.

## Start

Requires an existing Rust/Cargo toolchain and Python 3.12+; tested here with Rust/Cargo 1.97.1 and Python 3.14.6 on macOS arm64. The project has no external Cargo dependencies. No installation or network connection is part of these commands.

Start in a fresh directory containing `sandbox-model.zip`, with no existing `boundary-lab` subdirectory. The archive extracts to `boundary-lab/`. If you have already extracted it, enter that directory and start with the first `cargo` command below.

```sh
python3 -m zipfile -e sandbox-model.zip .
cd boundary-lab
cargo run --offline -- status
cargo run --offline -- demo
python3 run.py check core --attempt attempts/first \
  --prediction "The image will work, but at least one boundary will fail."
```

The initial demo succeeds and the security checks fail intentionally. Read the expected and observed behavior before editing. An exit code of 1 from the initial checks means the starter still violates public requirements; it is not a broken installation. Code 2 from `native` means the required native profile is unavailable. An unknown command uses 64.

The attempt runner snapshots your actual source and prediction **before** compiling. It records output, exit status, source and binary hashes in a new directory. It refuses an existing attempt directory. Use a different name after a repair and `--parent-attempt first` to link the revision. `--help-used` takes a text argument, for example `--help-used "read the public API types"`; it is not a boolean switch. Omit it when there was no assistance (the recorded default is `none`). Keep your explanation beside those files; a pass is not a substitute for an argument.

The runner also compares supplied scaffold files with `scaffold-manifest.json` and refuses accidental changes to the checks or runtime. Only `src/learner.rs` is the intended edit surface. This local manifest is not tamper-proof certification; a reviewer must compare the package and receipt with the known original when assessing work. Keep your own additional tests separate from the required checks. The capture runner is currently qualified only for POSIX hosts.

## Your work

Edit only `src/learner.rs` for the core exercises. The public argument types and enums are declared in [`src/model.rs`](src/model.rs); read them alongside the policy signatures when you need exact field names. That file also contains supplied type/default helpers, not a reference policy to copy. For the delayed-operation driver named in module 8, its public event and function declarations are in [`src/schedule.rs`](src/schedule.rs). Keep those files unchanged and retain any source-reading assistance in your attempt record. Its deliberately wrong policies cover admission, complete memory ranges, capability authorization, modeled syscall/seal decisions, resource accounting and delayed-operation authorization. The remaining Rust files supply the machine, canonical decoder, safe physical guards, synthetic filters, deterministic queue and public checks. Do not remove those guards or change expected results to obtain a pass.

The model uses eight u32 registers and at most 64 KiB guest memory. ADD wraps as u32 arithmetic; memory-range calculations must meet the mathematical contract rather than accidentally inherit that wrap. A handle combines a 16-bit generation with a 16-bit slot. The trusted job is an argument supplied by the broker; the request's `claimed_job` is untrusted.

## Learning sequence

1. [State the promises](lessons/01-promises.md)
2. [Admit only programs you understand](lessons/02-admission.md)
3. [Keep guest memory inside its world](lessons/03-memory.md)
4. [Make authority explicit](lessons/04-authority.md)
5. [Seal the OS boundary — practical portion unavailable](lessons/05-native.md)
6. [Bound work and make failure precise](lessons/06-budgets.md)
7. [Break, repair and defend](lessons/07-investigation.md)
8. [Transfer: delayed authority](lessons/08-transfer.md)

These are cumulative module slices with practice and evidence requirements, not a claim that all 24 planned full lessons or the complete course have been delivered. Module 5 includes runnable pure policy-model decisions and an explicit native practical hold. All portable exercises can be explored without a Linux environment.

```sh
python3 run.py check memory --attempt attempts/memory-01 \
  --prediction "State the exact failing family you expect and why."
python3 run.py check authority --attempt attempts/authority-01 \
  --prediction "State which actor determines the job identity."
cargo run --offline -- check all
cargo run --offline -- native
```

Available practice groups: `admission`, `memory`, `authority`, `syscall` (model only), `budget`, `runtime`, `wire`, `transfer`, `core` (all except transfer), and `all`. All 84 test cases in this package are public, including ten transfer cases. Final independent schedules, instructor solutions and grading controls are not in the learner export.

## Evidence and completion

For each repaired policy, retain: original prediction; exact initial result; revised source; reason the boundary failed; a useful positive control; a negative control; and the scope of your conclusion. Mark help honestly. The runtime's emergency stop and physical arena checks are supplied safety backstops; hitting one does not count as your security policy working.

The portable project is successful when all public checks pass **and** your report defends the five policy decisions on fresh cases. The full course additionally requires qualified Linux confinement, independent review, real learner trials and live Free to Learn delivery. None of those follows from a green portable test run.

Retain applicable notices. These licenses do not claim complete course qualification or authorize deployment.

<h1>Build a boundary<br>you can defend.</h1>
<p>Make the image filter work. Discover what else it can do. Repair its authority, memory and work limits—and keep evidence of why the repair holds.</p>
<div class="chips"><span class="chip">Original synthetic fixtures</span><span class="chip">Portable Rust lab</span><span class="chip">No accounts or network needed</span></div></header>
