```rs
//! Public practice cases. These cases and their expectations are intentionally inspectable.
use crate::{codec, model::*, runtime::*};

#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct Check {
    pub id: &'static str,
    pub group: &'static str,
    pub passed: bool,
    pub expected: String,
    pub actual: String,
    pub concept: &'static str,
}

fn case(
    id: &'static str,
    group: &'static str,
    passed: bool,
    expected: impl Into<String>,
    actual: impl Into<String>,
    concept: &'static str,
) -> Check {
    Check {
        id,
        group,
        passed,
        expected: expected.into(),
        actual: actual.into(),
        concept,
    }
}

pub fn tile_world(size: usize) -> World {
    World {
        objects: vec![
            (0..size).map(|x| x as u8).collect(),
            vec![0; size],
            b"SYNTHETIC-ONLY".to_vec(),
        ],
        grants: vec![
            Grant {
                job: 1,
                slot: 1,
                generation: 1,
                object: 0,
                rights: Rights::READ,
                base: 0,
                len: size as u32,
                epoch: 1,
            },
            Grant {
                job: 1,
                slot: 2,
                generation: 1,
                object: 1,
                rights: Rights::WRITE,
                base: 0,
                len: size as u32,
                epoch: 1,
            },
            Grant {
                job: 2,
                slot: 1,
                generation: 1,
                object: 2,
                rights: Rights::READ,
                base: 0,
                len: 14,
                epoch: 1,
            },
        ],
    }
}

/// Supplied useful application program. Writing image filters is not the learner task.
pub fn negative_filter(size: u32) -> Program {
    use Instruction::*;
    Program {
        memory_len: size,
        initial: vec![],
        code: vec![
            Const {
                dst: 0,
                value: 0x10001,
            },
            Const { dst: 1, value: 0 },
            Const { dst: 2, value: 0 },
            Const {
                dst: 3,
                value: size,
            },
            Const { dst: 5, value: 255 },
            Const {
                dst: 6,
                value: u32::MAX,
            },
            Const {
                dst: 7,
                value: 0x10002,
            },
            Invoke {
                write: false,
                handle: 0,
                offset: 1,
                mem: 2,
                len: 3,
                claimed_job: 1,
            },
            Const {
                dst: 2,
                value: size,
            },
            Jz { reg: 2, target: 16 },
            Add { dst: 2, a: 2, b: 6 },
            Load8 { dst: 4, addr: 2 },
            Xor { dst: 4, a: 4, b: 5 },
            Store8 { addr: 2, src: 4 },
            Jz { reg: 2, target: 16 },
            Jump { target: 10 },
            Invoke {
                write: true,
                handle: 7,
                offset: 1,
                mem: 2,
                len: 3,
                claimed_job: 1,
            },
            Halt,
        ],
    }
}

pub fn identity_filter(size: u32) -> Program {
    use Instruction::*;
    Program {
        memory_len: size,
        initial: vec![],
        code: vec![
            Const {
                dst: 0,
                value: 0x10001,
            },
            Const { dst: 1, value: 0 },
            Const { dst: 2, value: 0 },
            Const {
                dst: 3,
                value: size,
            },
            Const {
                dst: 7,
                value: 0x10002,
            },
            Invoke {
                write: false,
                handle: 0,
                offset: 1,
                mem: 2,
                len: 3,
                claimed_job: 1,
            },
            Invoke {
                write: true,
                handle: 7,
                offset: 1,
                mem: 2,
                len: 3,
                claimed_job: 1,
            },
            Halt,
        ],
    }
}

pub fn two_chunk_negative_filter() -> Program {
    let mut code = Vec::new();
    for chunk in 0..2_u32 {
        let start = code.len() as u32;
        let block = negative_filter(4096);
        for mut instruction in block
            .code
            .into_iter()
            .filter(|i| !matches!(i, Instruction::Halt))
        {
            match &mut instruction {
                Instruction::Const { dst: 1, value } => *value = chunk * 4096,
                Instruction::Jump { target } | Instruction::Jz { target, .. } => *target += start,
                _ => {}
            }
            code.push(instruction);
        }
    }
    code.push(Instruction::Halt);
    Program {
        code,
        initial: vec![],
        memory_len: 4096,
    }
}

pub fn evaluate<P: Policy>(group: &str) -> Vec<Check> {
    let mut checks = Vec::new();
    if group == "all" || group == "core" || group == "admission" {
        admission::<P>(&mut checks);
    }
    if group == "all" || group == "core" || group == "memory" {
        memory::<P>(&mut checks);
    }
    if group == "all" || group == "core" || group == "authority" {
        authority::<P>(&mut checks);
    }
    if group == "all" || group == "core" || group == "budget" {
        budget::<P>(&mut checks);
    }
    if group == "all" || group == "core" || group == "runtime" {
        runtime::<P>(&mut checks);
        composed_runtime::<P>(&mut checks);
    }
    if group == "all" || group == "core" || group == "wire" {
        wire(&mut checks);
    }
    if group == "all" || group == "core" || group == "syscall" {
        syscall_model::<P>(&mut checks);
    }
    if group == "all" || group == "transfer" {
        transfer::<P>(&mut checks);
    }
    checks
}

fn syscall_model<P: Policy>(out: &mut Vec<Check>) {
    let samples = [
        ("S01", Abi::NativeX86_64, Call::Read, 3, true),
        ("S02", Abi::NativeX86_64, Call::Write, 4, true),
        ("S03", Abi::NativeX86_64, Call::Read, 9, false),
        ("S04", Abi::NativeX86_64, Call::Write, 3, false),
        ("S05", Abi::X32, Call::Read, 3, false),
        ("S06", Abi::Other, Call::Read, 3, false),
        ("S07", Abi::NativeX86_64, Call::Unknown, 0, false),
        ("S08", Abi::NativeX86_64, Call::Exit, 0, true),
        // 5.3 "READ on descriptor 3": a lower descriptor and the write descriptor are other uses.
        ("S13", Abi::NativeX86_64, Call::Read, 0, false),
        ("S14", Abi::NativeX86_64, Call::Read, 4, false),
        // 5.3 "X32, other ABIs ... are denied": this holds for EXIT too.
        ("S15", Abi::X32, Call::Exit, 0, false),
    ];
    for (id, abi, call, fd, expected) in samples {
        let query = SyscallQuery { abi, call, fd };
        let actual = P::modeled_syscall(query);
        out.push(case(
            id,
            "syscall",
            actual == expected,
            expected.to_string(),
            format!("model {query:?}: {actual}"),
            "5.2: model only; ABI and exact descriptor are part of the decision",
        ));
    }
    for (id, nnp, filter, descriptors, expected) in [
        ("S09", true, true, true, true),
        ("S10", false, true, true, false),
        ("S11", true, false, true, false),
        ("S12", true, true, false, false),
    ] {
        let actual = P::modeled_seal(SealEvidence {
            nnp_verified: nnp,
            filter_installed: filter,
            descriptors_clean: descriptors,
        });
        out.push(case(
            id,
            "syscall",
            actual == expected,
            expected.to_string(),
            actual.to_string(),
            "5.1: all preconditions are required; this boolean is not a native seal receipt",
        ));
    }
}

fn admission<P: Policy>(out: &mut Vec<Check>) {
    use Instruction::*;
    let samples = [
        ("A01", vec![Halt], true),
        ("A02", vec![], false),
        ("A03", vec![Unknown(250), Halt], false),
        ("A04", vec![Const { dst: 8, value: 0 }, Halt], false),
        ("A05", vec![Jump { target: 9 }, Halt], false),
        ("A06", vec![Const { dst: 0, value: 0 }], false),
        ("A07", vec![Jump { target: 0 }], true),
        ("A08", vec![Jz { reg: 0, target: 3 }, Halt], false),
        // 2.2 "every operation": the unsupported operation is not the first instruction.
        ("A09", vec![Const { dst: 0, value: 0 }, Unknown(250), Halt], false),
        // 2.2: the branch target is legal, but the false path of JZ falls off the end.
        ("A10", vec![Const { dst: 0, value: 0 }, Jz { reg: 0, target: 0 }], false),
        // 2.2 "target an existing instruction index": the length itself is not an index.
        ("A11", vec![Jump { target: 1 }], false),
        // 2.2 "Registers are numbered 0 through 7" holds for every operand of every operation.
        ("A12", vec![Invoke { write: false, handle: 0, offset: 1, mem: 2, len: 8, claimed_job: 1 }, Halt], false),
    ];
    for (id, code, valid) in samples {
        let actual = P::validate(&code);
        out.push(case(
            id,
            "admission",
            actual.is_ok() == valid,
            if valid {
                "admitted"
            } else {
                "rejected before execution"
            },
            format!("input={code:?}; observed={actual:?}"),
            "2.2: admission checks every operation and edge; it does not prove termination",
        ));
    }
}

fn memory<P: Policy>(out: &mut Vec<Check>) {
    let samples = [
        ("M01", 16, 15, 1, true),
        ("M02", 16, 16, 1, false),
        ("M03", 16, 8, 9, false),
        ("M04", 16, 16, 0, true),
        ("M05", 16, 17, 0, false),
        ("M06", 16, u32::MAX - 1, 8, false),
        ("M07", 0, 0, 0, true),
        ("M08", 16, 0, 16, true),
        ("M09", u32::MAX, u32::MAX - 1, 8, false),
    ];
    for (id, logical, offset, len, allowed) in samples {
        let actual = P::range(logical, offset, len);
        out.push(case(
            id,
            "memory",
            actual == allowed,
            allowed.to_string(),
            format!("range({logical}, {offset}, {len}) = {actual}"),
            "3.2: the complete mathematical interval must fit; arithmetic must not wrap",
        ));
    }
}

fn authority<P: Policy>(out: &mut Vec<Check>) {
    let world = tile_world(16);
    let base = Request {
        handle: 0x10001,
        claimed_job: 1,
        write: false,
        offset: 0,
        len: 16,
    };
    let samples = [
        ("C01", base, Some(0)),
        (
            "C02",
            Request {
                claimed_job: 2,
                ..base
            },
            Some(0),
        ),
        (
            "C03",
            Request {
                write: true,
                ..base
            },
            None,
        ),
        ("C04", Request { handle: 1, ..base }, None),
        (
            "C05",
            Request {
                offset: 12,
                len: 5,
                ..base
            },
            None,
        ),
        (
            "C06",
            Request {
                handle: 0x10002,
                write: true,
                ..base
            },
            Some(1),
        ),
        (
            "C07",
            Request {
                handle: 0x10002,
                ..base
            },
            None,
        ),
        (
            "C08",
            Request {
                offset: 16,
                len: 0,
                ..base
            },
            Some(0),
        ),
        (
            "C09",
            Request {
                handle: 0x10009,
                len: 0,
                ..base
            },
            None,
        ),
        (
            "C10",
            Request {
                offset: u32::MAX,
                len: 2,
                ..base
            },
            None,
        ),
    ];
    for (id, request, expected) in samples {
        let actual = P::authorize(&world.grants, 1, request);
        out.push(case(id, "authority", actual.as_ref().ok().copied() == expected,
            format!("grant index {expected:?}"), format!("actual_job=1; request={request:?}; observed={actual:?}"),
            "4.2: channel principal, full live handle, rights and complete capability range all matter"));
    }
    // 4.2 "The request's offset is relative to that window. First establish authority for the complete
    // relative range": the window is bytes 8..24 of a 32-byte object; 12 + 8 is past its 16 bytes.
    let mut windowed = tile_world(32);
    windowed.grants[0].base = 8;
    windowed.grants[0].len = 16;
    // 4.1 "Choosing a grant table from the claim lets one principal ask the broker to exercise another
    // principal's authority": only job 2 holds handle 0x10007.
    let mut other_only = tile_world(16);
    other_only.grants[2].slot = 7;
    let extra = [
        ("C11", &windowed, Request { offset: 12, len: 8, ..base }, None),
        // 4.2 "A zero-byte operation still needs a live handle and the right."
        ("C12", &world, Request { write: true, len: 0, ..base }, None),
        ("C13", &other_only, Request { handle: 0x10007, claimed_job: 2, len: 14, ..base }, None),
    ];
    for (id, case_world, request, expected) in extra {
        let actual = P::authorize(&case_world.grants, 1, request);
        out.push(case(id, "authority", actual.as_ref().ok().copied() == expected,
            format!("grant index {expected:?}"), format!("actual_job=1; request={request:?}; observed={actual:?}"),
            "4.2: channel principal, full live handle, rights and complete capability range all matter"));
    }
}

fn budget<P: Policy>(out: &mut Vec<Check>) {
    let b = Budget {
        fuel: 1,
        calls: 1,
        read_bytes: 4,
        write_bytes: 4,
    };
    let samples = [
        ("B01", b, Cost::Step, Some(Budget { fuel: 0, ..b })),
        ("B02", Budget { fuel: 0, ..b }, Cost::Step, None),
        (
            "B03",
            b,
            Cost::Read(4),
            Some(Budget {
                calls: 0,
                read_bytes: 0,
                ..b
            }),
        ),
        ("B04", b, Cost::Read(5), None),
        ("B05", Budget { calls: 0, ..b }, Cost::Write(0), None),
        (
            "B06",
            b,
            Cost::Write(4),
            Some(Budget {
                calls: 0,
                write_bytes: 0,
                ..b
            }),
        ),
        ("B07", Budget::default(), Cost::Read(4097), None),
        // 6.1 "A zero-byte call consumes a call, because the crossing itself is work."
        ("B08", b, Cost::Write(0), Some(Budget { calls: 0, ..b })),
        // 6.1 "The maximum payload of one call is 4,096 bytes": for a write as for a read.
        ("B09", Budget::default(), Cost::Write(4097), None),
        // 6.1 "Read and write budgets are separate": an empty read budget does not stop a write.
        (
            "B10",
            Budget { read_bytes: 0, ..b },
            Cost::Write(4),
            Some(Budget {
                calls: 0,
                read_bytes: 0,
                write_bytes: 0,
                ..b
            }),
        ),
    ];
    for (id, before, cost, expected) in samples {
        let actual = P::charge(before, cost);
        out.push(case(id, "budget", actual.as_ref().ok().copied() == expected,
            format!("{expected:?}"), format!("before={before:?}; cost={cost:?}; observed={actual:?}"),
            "6.1: charge before effects, preserving independent fuel, calls, read and write budgets"));
    }
}

fn runtime<P: Policy>(out: &mut Vec<Check>) {
    use Instruction::*;
    for (id, size, invert) in [
        ("R01", 64, true),
        ("R02", 4096, true),
        ("R03", 64, false),
        ("R04", 0, true),
    ] {
        let mut world = tile_world(size);
        let expected: Vec<u8> = world.objects[0]
            .iter()
            .map(|b| if invert { b ^ 255 } else { *b })
            .collect();
        let p = if invert {
            negative_filter(size as u32)
        } else {
            identity_filter(size as u32)
        };
        let result = run::<P>(&p, 1, &mut world, Budget::default());
        out.push(case(
            id,
            "runtime",
            result.outcome.is_ok() && world.objects[1] == expected,
            "useful exact tile output",
            format!(
                "{:?}; steps={}; output_matches={}",
                result.outcome,
                result.steps,
                world.objects[1] == expected
            ),
            "7.2: a repair must preserve useful behavior, including an empty allowed input",
        ));
    }
    let mut world = tile_world(1);
    let leak = Program {
        memory_len: 1,
        initial: vec![],
        code: vec![
            Const { dst: 0, value: 1 },
            Load8 { dst: 1, addr: 0 },
            Const { dst: 0, value: 0 },
            Store8 { addr: 0, src: 1 },
            Halt,
        ],
    };
    let r = run::<P>(&leak, 1, &mut world, Budget::default());
    out.push(case(
        "R05",
        "runtime",
        r.outcome == Err(Fault::MemoryDenied),
        "MemoryDenied",
        format!("{:?}; guest_bytes={:?}", r.outcome, r.memory),
        "3.1: guard marker 167 is synthetic; this is logical isolation, not native exploitation",
    ));

    let mut original = identity_filter(1);
    let admitted = admit::<P>(&original);
    original.code = vec![Unknown(250)];
    let r = admitted.map(|a| run_admitted::<P>(&a, 1, &mut world, Budget::default()).outcome);
    out.push(case(
        "R06",
        "runtime",
        r == Ok(Ok(())),
        "original admitted program remains stable",
        format!("{r:?}"),
        "2.3: admission owns an immutable snapshot, independent of later source edits",
    ));

    let mut p = identity_filter(1);
    p.code.insert(p.code.len() - 1, Const { dst: 2, value: 1 });
    p.code.insert(p.code.len() - 1, Load8 { dst: 4, addr: 2 });
    let mut world = tile_world(1);
    world.objects[0][0] = 99;
    let before = world.objects.clone();
    let r = run::<P>(&p, 1, &mut world, Budget::default());
    out.push(case(
        "R07",
        "runtime",
        r.outcome == Err(Fault::MemoryDenied) && world.objects == before,
        "failed job leaves published objects unchanged",
        format!("{:?}; unchanged={}", r.outcome, world.objects == before),
        "6.2: earlier staged writes must not publish on a later trap",
    ));

    let p = Program {
        memory_len: 1,
        initial: vec![],
        code: vec![Halt],
    };
    let r = run::<P>(
        &p,
        1,
        &mut world,
        Budget {
            fuel: 0,
            ..Budget::default()
        },
    );
    out.push(case(
        "R08",
        "runtime",
        r.outcome == Err(Fault::BudgetExhausted) && r.steps == 0,
        "zero fuel: no instruction, including HALT",
        format!("{:?}; steps={}", r.outcome, r.steps),
        "6.1: work cannot happen before its charge",
    ));
}

fn composed_runtime<P: Policy>(out: &mut Vec<Check>) {
    let mut world = tile_world(8192);
    let expected: Vec<_> = world.objects[0].iter().map(|b| b ^ 255).collect();
    let r = run::<P>(
        &two_chunk_negative_filter(),
        1,
        &mut world,
        Budget::default(),
    );
    out.push(case(
        "R09",
        "runtime",
        r.outcome.is_ok() && world.objects[1] == expected,
        "128x64 tile transformed through two 4096-byte broker chunks",
        format!(
            "{:?}; steps={}; output_matches={}",
            r.outcome,
            r.steps,
            world.objects[1] == expected
        ),
        "6.1: cumulative budgets allow legitimate multiple calls, not only one demonstration",
    ));
    let mut world = tile_world(32);
    world.grants[0].base = 8;
    world.grants[0].len = 16;
    world.grants[1].base = 4;
    world.grants[1].len = 16;
    let mut expected = vec![0; 32];
    expected[4..20].copy_from_slice(&world.objects[0][8..24]);
    let r = run::<P>(&identity_filter(16), 1, &mut world, Budget::default());
    out.push(case(
        "R10",
        "runtime",
        r.outcome.is_ok() && world.objects[1] == expected,
        "only the authorized nonzero-base windows are read and written",
        format!(
            "{:?}; output_matches={}",
            r.outcome,
            world.objects[1] == expected
        ),
        "4.2: request offsets are relative to the capability, not the complete object",
    ));
    let looping = Program {
        code: vec![Instruction::Jump { target: 0 }],
        initial: vec![],
        memory_len: 1,
    };
    let r = run::<P>(
        &looping,
        1,
        &mut world,
        Budget {
            fuel: 3,
            ..Budget::default()
        },
    );
    out.push(case("R11", "runtime", r.outcome == Err(Fault::BudgetExhausted) && r.steps == 3,
        "valid loop: BudgetExhausted after exactly three steps", format!("{:?}; steps={}", r.outcome, r.steps),
        "6.1: structural validity permits loops; the learner fuel policy must stop them before the emergency guard"));
}

fn wire(out: &mut Vec<Check>) {
    let p = negative_filter(64);
    let bytes = codec::encode(&p);
    let valid = codec::decode(&bytes);
    out.push(case(
        "W01",
        "wire",
        valid.as_ref().map(|q| &q.code) == Ok(&p.code),
        "canonical round trip",
        format!("{} bytes; decoded={}", bytes.len(), valid.is_ok()),
        "2.1: framing is supplied, admission remains learner work",
    ));
    for (id, bad) in [
        ("W02", bytes[..bytes.len() - 1].to_vec()),
        ("W03", {
            let mut x = bytes.clone();
            x.push(0);
            x
        }),
        ("W04", {
            let mut x = bytes.clone();
            x[20] = 1;
            x
        }),
    ] {
        let result = codec::decode(&bad);
        out.push(case(
            id,
            "wire",
            result.is_err(),
            "InvalidImage",
            format!(
                "{}",
                if result.is_err() {
                    "rejected"
                } else {
                    "accepted"
                }
            ),
            "2.1: lengths and canonical fields are not advisory",
        ));
    }
}

fn transfer<P: Policy>(out: &mut Vec<Check>) {
    let world = tile_world(16);
    let request = Queued {
        principal: 1,
        handle: 0x10002,
        admitted_epoch: 1,
        write: true,
        offset: 0,
        len: 16,
    };
    let mut revoked = world.grants.clone();
    revoked.retain(|g| !(g.job == 1 && g.slot == 2));
    let mut replaced = world.grants.clone();
    replaced[1].generation = 2;
    replaced[1].epoch = 2;
    let samples = [
        ("Q01", world.grants.clone(), 1, request, true),
        ("Q02", revoked, 2, request, false),
        ("Q03", replaced, 2, request, false),
        ("Q04", world.grants.clone(), 8, request, true),
        (
            "Q05",
            world.grants,
            1,
            Queued {
                principal: 2,
                ..request
            },
            false,
        ),
    ];
    for (id, grants, epoch, req, expected) in samples {
        let actual = P::queued(&grants, epoch, req);
        out.push(case(id, "transfer", actual == expected, expected.to_string(), actual.to_string(),
            "8.2: public interface practice only; independent final schedules are not in this package"));
    }
    use crate::schedule::{simulate, Event};
    let request = Request {
        handle: 0x10002,
        claimed_job: 1,
        write: true,
        offset: 0,
        len: 2,
    };
    for (id, principal, slot, expected) in [("Q06", 1, 2, false), ("Q07", 2, 1, true)] {
        let initial = tile_world(4);
        let events = vec![
            Event::Queue {
                principal: 1,
                request,
                payload: vec![7, 8],
            },
            Event::Revoke { principal, slot },
            Event::Commit { index: 0 },
        ];
        let report = simulate::<P>(&initial, &events);
        let correct = report
            .as_ref()
            .map(|r| {
                r.decisions == vec![expected]
                    && r.world.objects[1][..2] == if expected { [7, 8] } else { [0, 0] }
            })
            .unwrap_or(false);
        out.push(case(id, "transfer", correct, format!("commit={expected}; matching actual object effect"),
            format!("{:?}", report.as_ref().map(|r| (&r.decisions, &r.world.objects[1]))),
            "8.2: the supplied deterministic queue reveals the actual delayed effect; no service is built"));
    }
    competing_slot_schedules::<P>(out);

}

/// Revocation must bind to the whole handle, even when a live grant has the
/// same principal, generation, epoch, rights and usable range. The other
/// principal's independent write must still happen, and no decoy bytes change.
fn competing_slot_schedules<P: Policy>(out: &mut Vec<Check>) {
    use crate::schedule::{simulate, Event};
    for (id, variant, revoke_target) in [("Q08", false, true), ("Q09", true, true), ("Q10", true, false)] {
        let (job, other_job, slot, decoy_slot, generation, epoch) = if variant {
            (41, 72, 12, 2, 3, 19)
        } else {
            (11, 22, 5, 8, 9, 41)
        };
        let (bases, offsets, grant_len) = if variant {
            ([3, 2, 1], [2, 1], 5)
        } else {
            ([2, 3, 1], [1, 2], 4)
        };
        let grant = |principal, grant_slot, object, grant_epoch| Grant {
            job: principal, slot: grant_slot, generation, object,
            rights: Rights::WRITE, base: bases[object], len: grant_len,
            epoch: grant_epoch,
        };
        let mut initial = World {
            objects: vec![vec![10; 10], vec![20; 10], vec![30; 10]],
            grants: vec![
                grant(job, slot, 0, epoch),
                grant(other_job, slot, 1, epoch + 2),
                grant(job, decoy_slot, 2, epoch),
            ],
        };
        if variant {
            initial.grants.rotate_left(2);
        }
        let handle = (u32::from(generation) << 16) | u32::from(slot);
        let payloads = if variant { [[91, 92], [101, 102]] } else { [[161, 162], [177, 178]] };
        let mut events = vec![
            Event::Queue {
                principal: job,
                request: Request { handle, claimed_job: other_job, write: true, offset: offsets[0], len: 2 },
                payload: payloads[0].to_vec(),
            },
            Event::Queue {
                principal: other_job,
                request: Request { handle, claimed_job: job, write: true, offset: offsets[1], len: 2 },
                payload: payloads[1].to_vec(),
            },
            Event::Revoke { principal: job, slot: if revoke_target { slot } else { decoy_slot } },
        ];
        let order = if variant { [1, 0] } else { [0, 1] };
        events.extend(order.iter().map(|index| Event::Commit { index: *index }));
        let expected_decisions: Vec<bool> = order.iter().map(|i| *i == 1 || !revoke_target).collect();
        // Compare complete objects: denial changes zero bytes, and success
        // changes exactly the intended granted window, never the decoy object.
        let mut expected_objects = initial.objects.clone();
        for i in 0..2 {
            if i == 1 || !revoke_target {
                let start = (bases[i] + offsets[i]) as usize;
                expected_objects[i][start..start + 2].copy_from_slice(&payloads[i]);
            }
        }
        let report = simulate::<P>(&initial, &events);
        let correct = report.as_ref().map(|r| {
            r.decisions == expected_decisions && r.world.objects == expected_objects
        }).unwrap_or(false);
        out.push(case(id, "transfer", correct,
            format!("decisions={expected_decisions:?}; exact objects={expected_objects:?}"),
            format!("{:?}", report.as_ref().map(|r| (&r.decisions, &r.world.objects))),
            "8.2: same generation is not the same handle; revoke one slot while preserving independent effects"));
    }
}
```

```rs
//! Supplied canonical framing. Sixteen-byte records; no evaluator or native code loader.
use crate::model::*;

fn word(b: &[u8], start: usize) -> u32 {
    u32::from_le_bytes(
        b[start..start + 4]
            .try_into()
            .expect("bounded supplied decoder"),
    )
}

pub fn decode(bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<Program, Fault> {
    if bytes.len() < 32
        || bytes.len() > 131_104
        || &bytes[..4] != b"SBX1"
        || word(bytes, 4) != 1
        || bytes[20..32].iter().any(|b| *b != 0)
    {
        return Err(Fault::InvalidImage);
    }
    let count = word(bytes, 8) as usize;
    let data_len = word(bytes, 12) as usize;
    let memory_len = word(bytes, 16);
    if count == 0
        || count > 4096
        || memory_len > 65_536
        || data_len > memory_len as usize
        || bytes.len() != 32 + count * 16 + data_len
    {
        return Err(Fault::InvalidImage);
    }
    let mut code = Vec::with_capacity(count);
    for b in bytes[32..32 + count * 16].chunks_exact(16) {
        if b[6] != 0 || b[7] != 0 {
            return Err(Fault::InvalidImage);
        }
        let (dst, a, c, d, e) = (b[1], b[2], b[3], b[4], b[5]);
        let imm = word(b, 8);
        let aux = word(b, 12);
        let instruction = match b[0] {
            0 => Instruction::Halt,
            1 => Instruction::Const { dst, value: imm },
            2 => Instruction::Add { dst, a, b: c },
            3 => Instruction::Xor { dst, a, b: c },
            4 => Instruction::Load8 { dst, addr: a },
            5 => Instruction::Store8 { addr: dst, src: a },
            6 => Instruction::Jump { target: imm },
            7 => Instruction::Jz {
                reg: dst,
                target: imm,
            },
            8 if dst <= 1 => Instruction::Invoke {
                write: dst == 1,
                handle: a,
                offset: c,
                mem: d,
                len: e,
                claimed_job: imm,
            },
            n => Instruction::Unknown(n),
        };
        // Canonical unused fields must be zero, so there is one representation per record.
        let canonical = encode_instruction(&instruction);
        if aux != 0 || canonical != b {
            return Err(Fault::InvalidImage);
        }
        code.push(instruction);
    }
    Ok(Program {
        code,
        initial: bytes[32 + count * 16..].to_vec(),
        memory_len,
    })
}

fn encode_instruction(i: &Instruction) -> [u8; 16] {
    let mut b = [0; 16];
    let imm = match *i {
        Instruction::Halt => 0,
        Instruction::Const { dst, value } => {
            b[0] = 1;
            b[1] = dst;
            value
        }
        Instruction::Add { dst, a, b: c } | Instruction::Xor { dst, a, b: c } => {
            b[0] = if matches!(i, Instruction::Add { .. }) {
                2
            } else {
                3
            };
            b[1] = dst;
            b[2] = a;
            b[3] = c;
            0
        }
        Instruction::Load8 { dst, addr } => {
            b[0] = 4;
            b[1] = dst;
            b[2] = addr;
            0
        }
        Instruction::Store8 { addr, src } => {
            b[0] = 5;
            b[1] = addr;
            b[2] = src;
            0
        }
        Instruction::Jump { target } => {
            b[0] = 6;
            target
        }
        Instruction::Jz { reg, target } => {
            b[0] = 7;
            b[1] = reg;
            target
        }
        Instruction::Invoke {
            write,
            handle,
            offset,
            mem,
            len,
            claimed_job,
        } => {
            b[0] = 8;
            b[1] = u8::from(write);
            b[2] = handle;
            b[3] = offset;
            b[4] = mem;
            b[5] = len;
            claimed_job
        }
        Instruction::Unknown(n) => {
            b[0] = n;
            0
        }
    };
    b[8..12].copy_from_slice(&imm.to_le_bytes());
    b
}

pub fn encode(program: &Program) -> Vec<u8> {
    let mut bytes = vec![0; 32];
    bytes[..4].copy_from_slice(b"SBX1");
    bytes[4..8].copy_from_slice(&1_u32.to_le_bytes());
    bytes[8..12].copy_from_slice(&(program.code.len() as u32).to_le_bytes());
    bytes[12..16].copy_from_slice(&(program.initial.len() as u32).to_le_bytes());
    bytes[16..20].copy_from_slice(&program.memory_len.to_le_bytes());
    for i in &program.code {
        bytes.extend_from_slice(&encode_instruction(i));
    }
    bytes.extend_from_slice(&program.initial);
    bytes
}
```

```rs
//! LEARNER WORK. Five intentionally wrong policies for bounded, synthetic data only.
//! Each TODO names a public contract, not an implementation recipe.
//! The supplied runtime adds physical memory and finite-step guards. They do not
//! make these logical policies correct and must not be counted as your repair.

use crate::model::*;

pub struct Learner;

impl Policy for Learner {
    fn validate(code: &[Instruction]) -> Result<(), Fault> {
        // TODO M2: every instruction and control-flow edge must satisfy admission.
        if code.is_empty() {
            return Err(Fault::InvalidProgram);
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    fn range(logical_len: u32, offset: u32, _len: u32) -> bool {
        // TODO M3: implement the complete mathematical range contract.
        offset <= logical_len
    }

    fn authorize(grants: &[Grant], _actual_job: u32, request: Request) -> Result<usize, Fault> {
        // TODO M4: resolve authority from the real principal, live handle, right and range.
        grants
            .iter()
            .position(|g| g.job == request.claimed_job && g.slot == request.handle as u16)
            .ok_or(Fault::AuthorityDenied)
    }

    fn charge(mut before: Budget, cost: Cost) -> Result<Budget, Fault> {
        // TODO M6: charge before work, including cumulative copy/call costs.
        match cost {
            Cost::Step => before.fuel = before.fuel.saturating_sub(1),
            Cost::Read(n) | Cost::Write(n) if n > 4096 => return Err(Fault::BudgetExhausted),
            _ => {}
        }
        Ok(before)
    }

    fn queued(_grants: &[Grant], current_epoch: u32, request: Queued) -> bool {
        // TODO M8: decide whether this queued operation still has authority at commit.
        request.admitted_epoch <= current_epoch
    }

    fn modeled_syscall(_query: SyscallQuery) -> bool {
        // TODO M5 MODEL ONLY: enforce the documented ABI and descriptor policy.
        true
    }

    fn modeled_seal(evidence: SealEvidence) -> bool {
        // TODO M5 MODEL ONLY: require every precondition; no real kernel call occurs.
        evidence.nnp_verified
    }
}
```

```rs
use boundary_lab::{checks, learner::Learner, *};

fn main() {
    let args: Vec<String> = std::env::args().skip(1).collect();
    match args.first().map(String::as_str).unwrap_or("status") {
        "status" => {
            println!("Boundary Lab: portable Rust teaching model. No OS sandbox or Linux seal is present.");
            println!("Learner: src/learner.rs. Commands: demo | check [core|admission|memory|authority|syscall|budget|runtime|wire|transfer|all] | native");
            println!("The starter has deliberate logical security defects. Never feed it real secrets or hostile native code.");
        }
        "native" => {
            println!("NOT RUN: Linux syscall confinement is not implemented or qualified. Portable checks cannot satisfy module 5.");
            std::process::exit(2);
        }
        "demo" => {
            let mut world = checks::tile_world(64);
            let r = run::<Learner>(
                &checks::negative_filter(64),
                1,
                &mut world,
                Budget::default(),
            );
            println!(
                "Portable synthetic 8x8 negative filter: {:?}; {} steps",
                r.outcome, r.steps
            );
            println!("input first row:  {:?}", &world.objects[0][..8]);
            println!("output first row: {:?}", &world.objects[1][..8]);
            println!("Useful output is not proof of isolation. Run check core to see the counterexamples.");
            if r.outcome.is_err() {
                std::process::exit(1);
            }
        }
        "check" => {
            let group = args.get(1).map(String::as_str).unwrap_or("core");
            let checks = checks::evaluate::<Learner>(group);
            if checks.is_empty() {
                eprintln!("Unknown group: {group}");
                std::process::exit(64);
            }
            for c in &checks {
                println!(
                    "{} {} [{}]\n  expected: {}\n  observed: {}\n  concept: {}",
                    if c.passed { "PASS" } else { "FAIL" },
                    c.id,
                    c.group,
                    c.expected,
                    c.actual,
                    c.concept
                );
            }
            let passed = checks.iter().filter(|c| c.passed).count();
            println!("{passed}/{} public practice checks passed. Linux native: NOT RUN. This is not course completion.", checks.len());
            if passed != checks.len() {
                std::process::exit(1);
            }
        }
        other => {
            eprintln!("Unknown command: {other}");
            std::process::exit(64);
        }
    }
}
```

```rs
//! Supplied types and semantics. Learners edit learner.rs, not these safeguards.

#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Instruction {
    Halt,
    Const {
        dst: u8,
        value: u32,
    },
    Add {
        dst: u8,
        a: u8,
        b: u8,
    },
    Xor {
        dst: u8,
        a: u8,
        b: u8,
    },
    Load8 {
        dst: u8,
        addr: u8,
    },
    Store8 {
        addr: u8,
        src: u8,
    },
    Jump {
        target: u32,
    },
    Jz {
        reg: u8,
        target: u32,
    },
    Invoke {
        write: bool,
        handle: u8,
        offset: u8,
        mem: u8,
        len: u8,
        claimed_job: u32,
    },
    Unknown(u8),
}

impl Instruction {
    pub fn registers(&self) -> Vec<u8> {
        match *self {
            Self::Halt | Self::Jump { .. } | Self::Unknown(_) => vec![],
            Self::Const { dst, .. } => vec![dst],
            Self::Add { dst, a, b } | Self::Xor { dst, a, b } => vec![dst, a, b],
            Self::Load8 { dst, addr } => vec![dst, addr],
            Self::Store8 { addr, src } => vec![addr, src],
            Self::Jz { reg, .. } => vec![reg],
            Self::Invoke {
                handle,
                offset,
                mem,
                len,
                ..
            } => vec![handle, offset, mem, len],
        }
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub struct Program {
    pub code: Vec<Instruction>,
    pub initial: Vec<u8>,
    pub memory_len: u32,
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Fault {
    InvalidImage,
    InvalidProgram,
    MemoryDenied,
    AuthorityDenied,
    BudgetExhausted,
    PhysicalGuard,
    UnsupportedEnvironment,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Rights {
    pub read: bool,
    pub write: bool,
}

impl Rights {
    pub const READ: Self = Self {
        read: true,
        write: false,
    };
    pub const WRITE: Self = Self {
        read: false,
        write: true,
    };
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub struct Grant {
    pub job: u32,
    pub slot: u16,
    pub generation: u16,
    pub object: usize,
    pub rights: Rights,
    pub base: u32,
    pub len: u32,
    pub epoch: u32,
}

impl Grant {
    pub fn handle(&self) -> u32 {
        (u32::from(self.generation) << 16) | u32::from(self.slot)
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug)]
pub struct Request {
    pub handle: u32,
    pub claimed_job: u32,
    pub write: bool,
    pub offset: u32,
    pub len: u32,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Budget {
    pub fuel: u32,
    pub calls: u32,
    pub read_bytes: u32,
    pub write_bytes: u32,
}

impl Default for Budget {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self {
            fuel: 100_000,
            calls: 64,
            read_bytes: 65_536,
            write_bytes: 65_536,
        }
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug)]
pub enum Cost {
    Step,
    Read(u32),
    Write(u32),
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub struct World {
    pub objects: Vec<Vec<u8>>,
    pub grants: Vec<Grant>,
}

/// Supplied trusted-configuration check; malformed grants are not a guest policy challenge.
pub fn valid_world(world: &World) -> bool {
    if world.objects.len() > 4
        || world.grants.len() > 4
        || world.objects.iter().any(|o| o.len() > 65_536)
    {
        return false;
    }
    let mut slots = Vec::new();
    for grant in &world.grants {
        let Some(object) = world.objects.get(grant.object) else {
            return false;
        };
        let Some(end) = grant.base.checked_add(grant.len) else {
            return false;
        };
        if end as usize > object.len() || slots.contains(&(grant.job, grant.slot)) {
            return false;
        }
        slots.push((grant.job, grant.slot));
    }
    true
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug)]
pub struct Queued {
    pub principal: u32,
    pub handle: u32,
    pub admitted_epoch: u32,
    pub write: bool,
    pub offset: u32,
    pub len: u32,
}

/// Pure policy-model values. These are not a syscall ABI or a kernel filter.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Abi {
    NativeX86_64,
    X32,
    Other,
}
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Call {
    Read,
    Write,
    Exit,
    Unknown,
}
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug)]
pub struct SyscallQuery {
    pub abi: Abi,
    pub call: Call,
    pub fd: u32,
}
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug)]
pub struct SealEvidence {
    pub nnp_verified: bool,
    pub filter_installed: bool,
    pub descriptors_clean: bool,
}

/// These are the learner-owned security decisions. Native syscall sealing is NOT implemented.
pub trait Policy {
    fn validate(code: &[Instruction]) -> Result<(), Fault>;
    fn range(logical_len: u32, offset: u32, len: u32) -> bool;
    fn authorize(grants: &[Grant], actual_job: u32, request: Request) -> Result<usize, Fault>;
    fn charge(before: Budget, cost: Cost) -> Result<Budget, Fault>;
    fn queued(grants: &[Grant], current_epoch: u32, request: Queued) -> bool;
    fn modeled_syscall(query: SyscallQuery) -> bool;
    fn modeled_seal(evidence: SealEvidence) -> bool;
}
```

`courses/boundary-lab/src/runtime.rs`:

```rs
//! Supplied portable execution machinery. No unsafe code, OS filter, processes or network.
use crate::model::*;

#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub struct Admitted {
    program: Program,
}

#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct RunReport {
    pub outcome: Result<(), Fault>,
    pub steps: u32,
    pub memory: Vec<u8>,
    pub remaining: Budget,
}

pub fn admit<P: Policy>(program: &Program) -> Result<Admitted, Fault> {
    if program.code.is_empty()
        || program.code.len() > 4096
        || program.memory_len > 65_536
        || program.initial.len() > program.memory_len as usize
    {
        return Err(Fault::InvalidImage);
    }
    P::validate(&program.code)?;
    // Supplied ownership boundary: execution never borrows the caller's mutable image.
    Ok(Admitted {
        program: program.clone(),
    })
}

pub fn run<P: Policy>(program: &Program, job: u32, world: &mut World, budget: Budget) -> RunReport {
    match admit::<P>(program) {
        Ok(admitted) => run_admitted::<P>(&admitted, job, world, budget),
        Err(fault) => RunReport {
            outcome: Err(fault),
            steps: 0,
            memory: vec![],
            remaining: budget,
        },
    }
}

pub fn run_admitted<P: Policy>(
    admitted: &Admitted,
    job: u32,
    world: &mut World,
    budget: Budget,
) -> RunReport {
    if !valid_world(world) {
        return RunReport {
            outcome: Err(Fault::InvalidImage),
            steps: 0,
            memory: vec![],
            remaining: budget,
        };
    }
    let program = &admitted.program;
    let logical = program.memory_len as usize;
    // Sixteen synthetic guard bytes make logical escape observable without native UB.
    let mut arena = vec![0_u8; logical + 16];
    arena[logical..].fill(0xA7);
    arena[..program.initial.len()].copy_from_slice(&program.initial);
    let mut staged = world.clone();
    let mut remaining = budget;
    let mut steps = 0;
    let outcome = interpret::<P>(
        program,
        job,
        &mut staged,
        &mut arena,
        &mut remaining,
        &mut steps,
    );
    if outcome.is_ok() {
        *world = staged;
    }
    RunReport {
        outcome,
        steps,
        memory: arena[..logical].to_vec(),
        remaining,
    }
}

fn checked_slice<P: Policy>(
    logical: u32,
    arena_len: usize,
    offset: u32,
    len: u32,
) -> Result<std::ops::Range<usize>, Fault> {
    if !P::range(logical, offset, len) {
        return Err(Fault::MemoryDenied);
    }
    let end = offset.checked_add(len).ok_or(Fault::PhysicalGuard)?;
    if end as u64 > arena_len as u64 {
        return Err(Fault::PhysicalGuard);
    }
    Ok(offset as usize..end as usize)
}

fn invoke<P: Policy>(
    program: &Program,
    actual_job: u32,
    request: Request,
    mem: u32,
    world: &mut World,
    arena: &mut [u8],
    remaining: &mut Budget,
) -> Result<(), Fault> {
    let guest = checked_slice::<P>(program.memory_len, arena.len(), mem, request.len)?;
    let grant_index = P::authorize(&world.grants, actual_job, request)?;
    let grant = world
        .grants
        .get(grant_index)
        .ok_or(Fault::PhysicalGuard)?
        .clone();
    let start = grant
        .base
        .checked_add(request.offset)
        .ok_or(Fault::PhysicalGuard)? as usize;
    let end = start
        .checked_add(request.len as usize)
        .ok_or(Fault::PhysicalGuard)?;
    let object = world
        .objects
        .get_mut(grant.object)
        .ok_or(Fault::PhysicalGuard)?;
    let target = object.get_mut(start..end).ok_or(Fault::PhysicalGuard)?;
    let cost = if request.write {
        Cost::Write(request.len)
    } else {
        Cost::Read(request.len)
    };
    let next = P::charge(*remaining, cost)?;
    if request.write {
        target.copy_from_slice(&arena[guest]);
    } else {
        arena[guest].copy_from_slice(target);
    }
    *remaining = next;
    Ok(())
}

fn interpret<P: Policy>(
    program: &Program,
    job: u32,
    world: &mut World,
    arena: &mut [u8],
    remaining: &mut Budget,
    steps: &mut u32,
) -> Result<(), Fault> {
    let mut registers = [0_u32; 8];
    let mut pc = 0_usize;
    loop {
        // A supplied emergency guard protects the lab if learner fuel logic is broken.
        // Hitting it is PhysicalGuard, never a successful budget-policy verdict.
        if *steps >= 100_001 {
            return Err(Fault::PhysicalGuard);
        }
        let instruction = program.code.get(pc).ok_or(Fault::PhysicalGuard)?;
        if instruction.registers().iter().any(|r| *r >= 8) {
            return Err(Fault::PhysicalGuard);
        }
        *remaining = P::charge(*remaining, Cost::Step)?;
        *steps += 1;
        pc += 1;
        match *instruction {
            Instruction::Halt => return Ok(()),
            Instruction::Const { dst, value } => registers[dst as usize] = value,
            Instruction::Add { dst, a, b } => {
                registers[dst as usize] = registers[a as usize].wrapping_add(registers[b as usize])
            }
            Instruction::Xor { dst, a, b } => {
                registers[dst as usize] = registers[a as usize] ^ registers[b as usize]
            }
            Instruction::Load8 { dst, addr } => {
                let range = checked_slice::<P>(
                    program.memory_len,
                    arena.len(),
                    registers[addr as usize],
                    1,
                )?;
                registers[dst as usize] = u32::from(arena[range.start]);
            }
            Instruction::Store8 { addr, src } => {
                let range = checked_slice::<P>(
                    program.memory_len,
                    arena.len(),
                    registers[addr as usize],
                    1,
                )?;
                arena[range.start] = registers[src as usize] as u8;
            }
            Instruction::Jump { target } => pc = target as usize,
            Instruction::Jz { reg, target } => {
                if registers[reg as usize] == 0 {
                    pc = target as usize;
                }
            }
            Instruction::Invoke {
                write,
                handle,
                offset,
                mem,
                len,
                claimed_job,
            } => {
                let request = Request {
                    handle: registers[handle as usize],
                    claimed_job,
                    write,
                    offset: registers[offset as usize],
                    len: registers[len as usize],
                };
                invoke::<P>(
                    program,
                    job,
                    request,
                    registers[mem as usize],
                    world,
                    arena,
                    remaining,
                )?;
            }
            Instruction::Unknown(_) => return Err(Fault::PhysicalGuard),
        }
    }
}
```

`courses/boundary-lab/src/schedule.rs`:

```rs
//! Supplied deterministic event driver; no threads, services, timers or OS authority.
use crate::model::*;

#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub enum Event {
    Queue {
        principal: u32,
        request: Request,
        payload: Vec<u8>,
    },
    Revoke {
        principal: u32,
        slot: u16,
    },
    Commit {
        index: usize,
    },
}

#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct ScheduleReport {
    pub world: World,
    pub decisions: Vec<bool>,
    pub epoch: u32,
}

struct Pending {
    request: Queued,
    object: usize,
    start: usize,
    payload: Vec<u8>,
    used: bool,
}

pub fn simulate<P: Policy>(initial: &World, events: &[Event]) -> Result<ScheduleReport, Fault> {
    if events.len() > 128 || !valid_world(initial) {
        return Err(Fault::InvalidImage);
    }
    let mut world = initial.clone();
    let mut pending = Vec::<Pending>::new();
    let mut decisions = Vec::new();
    let mut epoch = world.grants.iter().map(|g| g.epoch).max().unwrap_or(0);
    for event in events {
        match event {
            Event::Queue {
                principal,
                request,
                payload,
            } => {
                if !request.write || payload.len() != request.len as usize || payload.len() > 4096 {
                    return Err(Fault::InvalidImage);
                }
                let i = P::authorize(&world.grants, *principal, *request)?;
                let grant = world.grants.get(i).ok_or(Fault::PhysicalGuard)?;
                let start = grant
                    .base
                    .checked_add(request.offset)
                    .ok_or(Fault::PhysicalGuard)? as usize;
                let end = start
                    .checked_add(payload.len())
                    .ok_or(Fault::PhysicalGuard)?;
                world
                    .objects
                    .get(grant.object)
                    .and_then(|o| o.get(start..end))
                    .ok_or(Fault::PhysicalGuard)?;
                pending.push(Pending {
                    request: Queued {
                        principal: *principal,
                        handle: request.handle,
                        admitted_epoch: grant.epoch,
                        write: true,
                        offset: request.offset,
                        len: request.len,
                    },
                    object: grant.object,
                    start,
                    payload: payload.clone(),
                    used: false,
                });
            }
            Event::Revoke { principal, slot } => {
                world
                    .grants
                    .retain(|g| !(g.job == *principal && g.slot == *slot));
                epoch = epoch.checked_add(1).ok_or(Fault::PhysicalGuard)?;
            }
            Event::Commit { index } => {
                let item = pending.get_mut(*index).ok_or(Fault::InvalidImage)?;
                if item.used {
                    return Err(Fault::InvalidImage);
                }
                item.used = true;
                let permit = P::queued(&world.grants, epoch, item.request);
                decisions.push(permit);
                if permit {
                    let end = item.start + item.payload.len();
                    let bytes = world
                        .objects
                        .get_mut(item.object)
                        .and_then(|o| o.get_mut(item.start..end))
                        .ok_or(Fault::PhysicalGuard)?;
                    bytes.copy_from_slice(&item.payload);
                }
            }
        }
    }
    Ok(ScheduleReport {
        world,
        decisions,
        epoch,
    })
}
```

`courses/compiler-optimizer/API.md`:

```md
# Kernel IR v1 and learner interfaces

This is the executable local profile, version `kernel-ir/1`. It implements the original small IR; it does not parse LLVM. Inputs must already have the normalized SSA shape described here. Unsupported shapes are rejected rather than silently translated.

## Files and functions

The supplied `start` command creates `optimizer.mjs` and `support/runtime.mjs`, `support/editor.mjs`, `support/evidence.mjs`, `support/investigation.mjs`. Your module exports the following functions. They can use the supplied support imports. Synchronous functions are simplest; the transformation/reduction checks also await their return values.

| Function | Return value |
|---|---|
| `compare(sourceResult, targetResult)` | Boolean; true only for equal completed observations |
| `dominators(program)` | Object mapping each block ID to a sorted array of its dominator IDs |
| `scalar(program, contract)` | Editor artifact with useful constant folding, pure reuse and dead-result cleanup |
| `constants(program, contract)` | Editor artifact with convergent conditional constant/phi/edge simplification |
| `aliases(program, leftID, rightID, contract)` | `must`, `may` or `no` based on static pointer facts |
| `memory(program, contract)` | Editor artifact with safe block-local load reuse/forwarding |
| `loops(program, contract)` | Editor artifact with supported scalar/load LICM |
| `decide(report)` | `{accept: boolean, reason: string}` |
| `reduce(program, input, transform)` | `{program, input, explanation}` preserving a smaller legal wrong-result witness |

`decide(report)` receives `validation:{status,complete}`, `proof:{ok}`, `identitiesCurrent` and `cost:{complete,before,after,sameWorkload}`. A positive decision requires exhaustive completed domain success, successful proof, current identities, complete comparable costs and a strict aggregate improvement. Full generated reports also contain `validation.counts`, `cases` and subject/domain digests; these extra diagnostic fields are not required on the public policy-check interface. Do not require them to exist or infer success from missing required fields. Reject explicit incomplete or contradictory evidence. The status describes only the declared finite domain, not universal correctness.

An Editor artifact is `{program, events}`. Start with `new Editor(program, contract)` and finish with `.finish()`. Read `.program` to inspect the current snapshot. Mutating it directly produces an unreported delta and is rejected when the chain is replayed.

Supported `.edit(operation)` requests:

| Operation | Meaning / checked premise |
|---|---|
| `{kind:'fold', id, value}` | Replace a scalar constant computation or equal-constant phi with the exact canonical value |
| `{kind:'reuse', id, other}` | Reuse an identical total pure expression that is available at the replaced definition |
| `{kind:'dead', id}` | Remove an unused total-pure definition; loads and effects are excluded |
| `{kind:'branch', block}` | Select the edge of a literal-bool branch; atomically clean unreachable blocks and obsolete phi inputs |
| `{kind:'memory', id, priorIndex}` | Replace this load with a preceding same-block same-location access's value; intervening may-alias stores block it |
| `{kind:'move', id, header}` | Move eligible invariant work to the supported loop preheader; loads require explicit nontrapping/nonalias proof |

`priorIndex` is the index in the current block's current instruction array, not an index from an earlier snapshot. Recompute facts after edits. The editor throws a localized reason when a premise fails; catching that reason does not establish that your analysis was correct. The checker independently replays the complete edit chain and compares the full resulting program.

The supplied runtime exports `cfg`, `definitions`, `uses`, `literal`, `evaluate`, `valueJSON`, `verify`, `run`, `observation`, `equivalent`, `cost`, `digest`, `clone` and `canonical`. `cfg` gives `{successors, predecessors}`. Definition records include block and index (`block:null` for parameters, `index:-1` for phis). The independent verifier uses graph removal, while the learner dominance task should implement its own analysis.

## Program and input representation

A program has exactly `version:1`, `name`, `params`, `returns`, `entry`, `blocks`. A parameter has `id,type`. A block has `id,phis,instructions,term`. Identifiers use ASCII letters/underscore initially and then letters, digits, underscore, dot or hyphen, up to 64 characters. Block and value namespaces are separate; value definitions are globally unique.

A phi is `{id,type,incoming:{predecessorBlock:valueID,...}}`. Its incoming keys exactly match predecessor blocks. Ordinary instructions are either `{id,op,type,args:[valueID,...]}`, scalar `{id,op:'const',type,value}`, or an effect `{op,args}`. Terminators are `{op:'br',target}`, `{op:'cbr',cond,yes,no}`, `{op:'ret',value}` or `{op:'trap',code}`.

Types are `i8`, `i32`, `bool`, `ptr<i8>`, `ptr<i32>`. Returns are scalar. The entry has no predecessor or phi. All blocks must be structurally reachable; conditional successors must differ. Ordinary definitions dominate their uses; phi uses are checked at predecessor terminators. All selected phi inputs read the old predecessor state simultaneously.

Instructions: `const`; word `add/sub/mul/and/or/xor`; comparisons `eq/ne/ult/ule/slt/sle`; `ptradd`; `load/store`; `emit`. Comparisons take two same-width words and return bool. There are no implicit casts, division, shifts, floats, calls or hidden intrinsics.

A job JSON file contains `{program, inputs:[input,...], contract}` or `{program, domain, contract}`. An input is exactly `{args,heap}`. `args` names every parameter. A heap object is `{type:'i8' or 'i32',cells:[canonicalWord,...]}` keyed by object ID. A pointer is `{object:objectID,offset:canonicalSignedDecimal}`. The object must exist with the matching element type. Pointer offsets may be out of bounds until dereferenced.

Word literals in JSON are **unsigned decimal strings**, with no leading zeros except `"0"`, within the type's range. Bools are JSON true/false. Runtime word values are BigInts; `valueJSON` converts them back to strings. Arithmetic wraps modulo 2^width. Signed comparisons interpret the high bit as negative. `ptradd` adds the signed view of an i32 word to the mathematical offset, without truncating the resulting pointer offset.

The frozen contract optionally has `offsets:{pointerID:decimalString}`, `minLengths:{pointerID:nonnegativeSafeInteger}` and `distinct:[[pointerID,pointerID],...]`. These are validated on each invocation. They cannot be strengthened by an optimization. All pointer arguments may alias unless the contract or a same-base constant-offset calculation proves otherwise.

## Execution and observation

Load/store checks element bounds. A failed access produces a defined `bounds` trap; a failed store performs no partial write. Pointer construction does not trap. Emit appends a typed scalar event; duplicate events remain duplicated. Explicit trap codes are identifiers other than reserved `bounds`.

Normal results contain `kind:'return'`, `type`, `value`, `heap`, `events`, `steps`, `counts`. Traps contain `kind:'trap'`, `code` and the same state/counters. Compare all initial heap objects, return type/value or trap code, and ordered typed events. Exclude counters. Unknown and invalid results are not completed observations.

The default run limit is 100,000 steps. A phi group is one atomic fuel step, while each assigned phi contributes one unit of modeled work. Every ordinary instruction and terminator consumes one step. Return/trap on the final allowed step completes normally. Event count is capped at 4,096. Programs are capped at 64 blocks and 512 definitions; inputs at 64 objects and 4,096 cells. CLI JSON input is capped at 1 MiB. An eight-second worker limit separately bounds learner execution.

These are resource/profile limits, not proof that a program diverges. The current verifier reports size/profile rejection as `invalid`; fuel/event exhaustion is `unknown`. The finer planning distinction between legal-but-oversized programs and malformed programs remains a known qualification gap.

## Evidence and cost

`validate` checks a nonempty explicit input list. Duplicate inputs are invalid. Its five statuses are `COUNTEREXAMPLE`, `EXHAUSTIVE_WITHIN_DOMAIN`, `SAMPLED_NO_DIFFERENCE`, `UNKNOWN`, `INVALID`. Default coverage is capped at 4,096 cases and two million combined executed steps; the API can raise the case cap to 65,536. A required case not executed remains in the denominator.

The supplied `domains.mjs` expands a finite Cartesian manifest into that list. A domain has `{version:1,axes:[axis,...],heaps:[heap,...]}` with exactly one axis per parameter. An axis is `{parameter:'x',values:['0','1']}` or, for words, `{parameter:'x',range:{from:'0',to:'255',step:'1'}}`. Ranges are inclusive with positive steps. Duplicate axis values or heaps, illegal inputs and products above 65,536 are rejected before execution. Enumeration follows axis/value order, then heap order. The receipt records the manifest, cardinality and generated-input hash. A generated domain above the execution cap remains incomplete; generation never silently authorizes a smaller domain.

`reportFor` adds independent rewrite-chain evidence, unit-cost totals and exact input/program/contract identities. A finite input list does not establish correctness elsewhere. A valid rule chain is evidence under the supplied checker and interpreter, not a machine-checked theorem about them.

The cost model counts executed operations, excludes the phi-group fuel bookkeeping and includes each phi assignment. Lower total work on the same listed inputs is the default benefit criterion; individual inputs may get more expensive and remain visible in per-case results. Actual hardware speed is not measured.

`pipeline WORK JOB.json scalar,constants,memory,loops --learner-policy` evaluates up to eight ordered passes. Every stage has its own before/selected-after identities, candidate evidence and decision. Unsupported, failing or unhelpful candidates retain the previous program. A rejected stage cannot disappear behind a later success. The aggregate chain is checked again from the original source, and the full pipeline must still reduce the declared cost before its output is selected.

## Investigation support

`support/investigation.mjs` supplies `inspectWitness(program,input,transform,{contract,fuel})`. It returns `INTERESTING` only for valid normal returns differing in value/type or heap, `NOT_INTERESTING` for completed non-witnesses or invalid candidates, and `UNRESOLVED` for transform failure or execution exhaustion. This course's investigation target excludes event-only discrepancies. Transform functions must be synchronous; the owned CLI worker bounds accidental nontermination.

`structuralMeasure(program)` returns blocks, definitions/instructions including parameters/effects, and operand occurrences. `measure(program,input)` extends that lexicographic vector with heap-object count, heap-cell count and numeric-value complexity. Value complexity sums the binary magnitude bit lengths of program constants, scalar arguments, pointer offsets and heap cells (zero costs zero; a negative offset adds one sign bit; bool false/true cost zero/one). `smaller(a,b)` compares these vectors. The legacy `evidence.size` export is an alias for this vector, not a serialized-byte score. Program/display names, SSA/block/object identifiers, property ordering, whitespace and serialization length carry no weight. Values with the same bit length can tie; this is a declared reduction order, not a ranking of every conceivable simplification. `assessNeighborhood(program,input,transform,candidates,options)` evaluates a supplied finite list of `{program,input}` candidates, records unresolved/unstarted counts and reports `NO_SMALLER_IN_LIST` only when all listed neighbors complete without a smaller witness. The learner must justify that the list covers their declared reduction family before claiming relative 1-minimality. It never proves a global minimum. Choose and implement the reduction/search decisions yourself.

## Final project

Create `project.mjs` exporting `investigate(program, foreignPass)`. It returns `{input, reduced, repair, explanation}`. `input` demonstrates a valid normal-return wrong result; `reduced` is a smaller valid source that regenerates the discrepancy through the same pass; `repair(program)` returns a checked Editor artifact. Keep the signature. The final project must strictly decrease `structuralMeasure`; changing only names, input values or unused literal values is insufficient on this deliberately reducible program. U08 may instead demonstrate a strict full-measure decrease through genuine witness-input simplification. Explain the violated premise, reduction method, retained wins and evidence limits.

No final-project implementation is supplied. Its concrete checks accept alternative valid witnesses, reduced programs and repairs. They require real retained scalar optimization and do not automatically judge the causal quality of your explanation.

```

```md
# Sources and status

The course code, kernel examples, prose and control specifications were created originally in this task. No existing course source, private answer key, paid book chapter or third-party routine was copied. No new public redistribution license is chosen by this local candidate.

Conceptual references:

- [LLVM Language Reference](https://llvm.org/docs/LangRef.html): SSA well-formedness and precise instruction semantics.
- [LLVM Alias Analysis](https://llvm.org/docs/AliasAnalysis.html): conservative alias distinctions.
- [LLVM Loop Terminology](https://llvm.org/docs/LoopTerminology.html): natural-loop and canonical-form concepts.
- [LLVM Undefined Behavior](https://llvm.org/docs/UndefinedBehavior.html): why LLVM's UB assumptions must not be imported into this defined-trap IR.
- [Necula, Translation Validation for an Optimizing Compiler, PLDI 2000](https://people.eecs.berkeley.edu/~necula/Papers/tv_pldi00.pdf).
- [Lopes et al., Alive2, PLDI 2021](https://web.ist.utl.pt/nuno.lopes/pubs/alive2-pldi21.pdf): bounded validation and its limits.
- [LLVM reducer documentation](https://llvm.org/docs/CommandGuide/llvm-reduce.html): explicit interestingness testing.

These are citations, not compatibility claims. Kernel IR v1 is an original smaller language with defined traps, no UB/poison and no floating point. It does not implement Alive2 or use an SMT solver.

The nine-unit scope is authorized for local construction. Independent exact-artifact review, rendered browser/phone/accessibility checks, first-time human tryout, permitted integration, explicit publication and verified Free to Learn delivery remain separate pending stages.
```

# Compiler Optimizer

Build a local optimizer for integer kernels, inspect its evidence, and investigate a wrong-result transformation. You implement the analyses and optimization decisions; the supplied runtime executes your IR and checks the proposed edits.

This is a **local development candidate with nine implemented units**. Deterministic author checks are separate from independent course review, browser/accessibility checks and human learning evidence. Nothing here is published on Free to Learn.

## Run locally

Use Node 26.x. Development observed **Node 26.5.1 on macOS arm64**; other operating systems and Node versions are not qualified. No npm install, external service, solver, API key, GPU or model download is needed.

From the extracted course directory:

```sh
node cli.mjs start work
node cli.mjs lesson 01
node cli.mjs question 01a
node cli.mjs answer 01a work YOUR_LETTER --help-used none
node cli.mjs check 01 work --help-used none
```

Edit **work/optimizer.mjs**. The initial TODO failures are intentional and name the required function. `start` refuses an existing destination. Use unit numbers 01 through 09; there is no score gate on reading or later checks. Open `index.html` directly for the offline reading/practice interface; it does not execute learner code. Browser interaction is implemented but **not yet browser-qualified**. Use the tested terminal route if local browser storage is unavailable.

The reader can commit reasoning choices before feedback, preserve attempts locally, export them and merge an earlier export. Its practice history is separate from terminal code history. Export both when using both routes. It refuses to reveal new answer feedback if it cannot save the commitment. Reading does not require storage or an account.

Node runs your code with your normal local permissions. The eight-second owned-worker limit catches accidental nontermination; it is **not a hostile-code sandbox**. Only run code you choose to trust. No learner code or results are automatically transmitted anywhere.

## The cumulative project

| Units | You build | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 01–03 | Observation comparison, dominance, scalar rewrites | Useful scalar optimizer with replayable edit evidence |
| 04–06 | Conditional constants, alias/effect decisions, loop motion | The same optimizer handles branches, memory and supported loops |
| 07–08 | Evidence/cost policy and reduction decisions | Reproducible acceptance/rejection and smaller wrong-result witnesses |
| 09 | A fresh investigation and narrow repair | A portable report and repaired optimizer that retains valid wins |

After unit 03:


`optimize` records a report and its selected output program under the new `work/.attempts/<id>/receipt.json`, and prints the result. Use `branch`, `memory` or `loop` examples with the corresponding `constants`, `memory` or `loops` pass. The ordinary product route checks evidence independently before adopting a result. Add `--learner-policy` after unit 07 to apply your policy as well.

Compare pass orders with `node cli.mjs pipeline work calibration.json scalar,constants --learner-policy --help-used none`. Its receipt preserves accepted and rejected stage candidates plus an aggregate check. The scalar example declares all 256 i8 inputs through a finite-domain manifest; the generated list and coverage remain explicit.

Every check snapshots your exact implementation and supplied dependencies before execution. Practice records the original question and committed answer before revealing feedback. First attempts, later revisions, actual help and failed results remain separate. Status labels a receipt historical after source or course changes. These editable local records are not credentials.

Export includes current code, dependencies and the preserved source/question/result history. Restore requires the matching course identity and a new destination. Export refuses to overwrite a file and stops above 16 MiB rather than dropping history; keep earlier exports and the original work directory if the limit is reached. No automatic migration or destructive reset is provided.

Exit 0 means the requested check/adoption succeeded; 1 means a criterion failed or a candidate was retained; 2 means invalid invocation or file/format failure; 3 means learner module execution failed or timed out. A program's defined bounds trap is an observation, not a CLI crash.

## Scope and evidence

Read [API.md](API.md) for exact Kernel IR v1 behavior and interfaces, and [RUBRIC.md](RUBRIC.md) before the final investigation. The instruction set has fixed-width integers, typed arrays and explicit effects. It has no frontend, LLVM compatibility, floating point, native code generation or universal-correctness guarantee.

Short mechanism readings accompany substantial coding and investigation. Their length is a deliberate prototype choice; reading and project times have not been measured. The public checker is a learning tool with inspectable cases, not a hidden exam. Independent held-out measurement and human tryouts remain pending.
