`courses/compiler-optimizer/RUBRIC.md`:

```md
# Investigation and evidence rubric

Use this after committing your first attempt. A mechanical pass and a sound explanation are separate results.

1. **Semantic claim.** Name the preserved return type/value, heap and event behavior. State word width, wrap and signed comparison rules. Do not appeal to a different language's overflow behavior.
2. **Original witness.** Preserve the original source, exact input and faulty pipeline. Both programs are valid and terminate normally with different scalar or heap results. A crash or fuel cutoff alone does not qualify.
3. **Causal diagnosis.** Name the transformation's violated premise and show how the witness exercises it. Distinguish observed facts from hypotheses. A sentence saying only “the outputs differ” is insufficient.
4. **Reduction.** Regenerate the target from each reduced source. Preserve the signature and input contract. Remove irrelevant structure, retain the original witness and name the reduction family and stopping condition. Cosmetic names, SSA spelling and serialization differences are not reductions. U08 also permits a genuine witness-input complexity decrease; U09 requires a structural decrease in its supplied source. Do not call a best-found result globally minimal.
5. **Repair.** Fix or conservatively decline the invalid transformation while retaining a legitimate optimization. Show the original witness fixed, neighboring cases checked and a correct useful scalar win. Disabling every transformation is insufficient.
6. **Evidence limits.** State the exact tested input set, runtime/checker identity and remaining unknowns. Separate model cost from wall-clock performance. Report help and keep first/revised attempts.

An optional reviewer may critique your exported work against this rubric. Any model feedback is advisory. Do not transmit personal data or assume a hosted reviewer exists; the course makes no automatic external calls.

Author QA, source-blind interface trials and human learning studies answer different questions. No local score is a credential or evidence of general compiler mastery.

```

`courses/compiler-optimizer/cases.mjs`:

```mjs
// Original, public kernel cases. Expected results are shown by checks after commit.
const c = (id, type, value) => ({ id, op: 'const', type, value });
const op = (id, opcode, type, ...args) => ({ id, op: opcode, type, args });
const block = (id, instructions, term, phis = []) => ({ id, phis, instructions, term });
const p = (name, params, returns, blocks) => ({ version: 1, name, params, returns, entry: blocks[0].id, blocks });
const param = (id, type) => ({ id, type });
export const emptyInput = args => ({ args, heap: {} });
export function scalarKernel() {
  return p('calibrate', [param('x', 'i8')], 'i8', [block('entry', [
    c('gain', 'i8', '3'), c('biasA', 'i8', '4'), c('biasB', 'i8', '5'),
    op('bias', 'add', 'i8', 'biasA', 'biasB'), op('scaled', 'mul', 'i8', 'x', 'gain'),
    op('duplicate', 'mul', 'i8', 'x', 'gain'), op('answer', 'add', 'i8', 'duplicate', 'bias'),
    c('unused', 'i8', '255')
  ], { op: 'ret', value: 'answer' })]);
}
export function wordKernel(type = 'i32', opcode = 'mul') {
  return p('word', [param('a', type), param('b', type)], ['eq','ne','ult','ule','slt','sle'].includes(opcode) ? 'bool' : type,
    [block('entry', [op('answer', opcode, ['eq','ne','ult','ule','slt','sle'].includes(opcode) ? 'bool' : type, 'a', 'b')], { op: 'ret', value: 'answer' })]);
}
export function reuseKernel(opcode='add') {
  return p('reuse_live_values',[param('x','i8'),param('y','i8')],'i8',[block('entry',[
    op('first',opcode,'i8','x','y'),op('second',opcode,'i8','y','x'),op('answer','sub','i8','first','second')
  ],{op:'ret',value:'answer'})]);
}
export function deadKernel() {
  return p('dead_chain',[param('x','i8')],'i8',[block('entry',[c('unused','i8','13'),op('unused_sum','add','i8','x','unused')],{op:'ret',value:'x'})]);
}
export function equalPhiKernel() {
  const program=diamond(false);program.name='equal_phi';
  program.blocks[1].instructions[0].value='7';program.blocks[2].instructions[0].value='7';
  program.blocks[3].instructions=[c('one','i8','1'),op('answer','add','i8','value','one')];program.blocks[3].term.value='answer';return program;
}
export function forwardingKernel() {
  return p('forward_store',[param('p','ptr<i8>'),param('v','i8')],'i8',[block('entry',[
    {op:'store',args:['p','v']},{op:'emit',args:['v']},op('answer','load','i8','p')
  ],{op:'ret',value:'answer'})]);
}
export function pointerAliasKernel() {
  return p('pointer_aliases',[param('p','ptr<i8>'),param('index','i32')],'i8',[block('entry',[
    c('zero','i32','0'),c('one','i32','1'),c('minusOne','i32','4294967295'),
    op('same','ptradd','ptr<i8>','p','zero'),op('next','ptradd','ptr<i8>','p','one'),op('back','ptradd','ptr<i8>','next','minusOne'),op('unknown','ptradd','ptr<i8>','p','index'),op('answer','load','i8','p')
  ],{op:'ret',value:'answer'})]);
}
export function diamond(constant = false) {
  return p('choose', constant ? [] : [param('gate', 'bool')], 'i8', [
    block('entry', constant ? [c('gate', 'bool', false)] : [], { op: 'cbr', cond: 'gate', yes: 'left', no: 'right' }),
    block('left', [c('a', 'i8', '10')], { op: 'br', target: 'join' }),
    block('right', [c('b', 'i8', '20')], { op: 'br', target: 'join' }),
    block('join', [], { op: 'ret', value: 'value' }, [{ id: 'value', type: 'i8', incoming: { left: 'a', right: 'b' } }])
  ]);
}
export function swapLoop() {
  return p('swap', [param('n', 'i32')], 'i32', [
    block('entry', [c('a0','i32','3'),c('b0','i32','9'),c('zero','i32','0'),c('one','i32','1'),c('ten','i32','10')], {op:'br',target:'head'}),
    block('head', [op('continue','ult','bool','iter','n')], {op:'cbr',cond:'continue',yes:'body',no:'exit'}, [
      {id:'a',type:'i32',incoming:{entry:'a0',body:'b'}},{id:'b',type:'i32',incoming:{entry:'b0',body:'a'}},{id:'iter',type:'i32',incoming:{entry:'zero',body:'next'}}]),
    block('body',[op('next','add','i32','iter','one')],{op:'br',target:'head'}),
    block('exit',[op('tens','mul','i32','a','ten'),op('answer','add','i32','tens','b')],{op:'ret',value:'answer'})
  ]);
}
export function memoryKernel() {
  return p('memory', [param('p','ptr<i8>'),param('q','ptr<i8>'),param('v','i8')], 'i8', [block('entry', [
    op('saved','load','i8','p'),{op:'store',args:['q','v']},op('answer','load','i8','p')
  ],{op:'ret',value:'answer'})]);
}
export function memoryInput(aliased = true) {
  return {args:{p:{object:'A',offset:'0'},q:{object:aliased?'A':'B',offset:'0'},v:'7'},heap:{A:{type:'i8',cells:['4']},...(aliased?{}:{B:{type:'i8',cells:['5']}})}};
}
export function trapKernel() {
  return p('trap_case',[param('p','ptr<i8>')],'i8',[block('entry',[
    c('nine','i8','9'),c('event','i8','42'),c('one','i32','1'),{op:'store',args:['p','nine']},{op:'emit',args:['event']},
    op('outside','ptradd','ptr<i8>','p','one'),op('answer','load','i8','outside')
  ],{op:'ret',value:'answer'})]);
}
export function loopKernel({write = false, scalar = false} = {}) {
  const params = [param('n','i32'),param('p','ptr<i8>')];
  if(write) params.push(param('q','ptr<i8>'));
  const body = scalar ? [op('read','add','i8','a','b')] : [op('read','load','i8','p')];
  body.push(op('sumNext','add','i8','sum','read'));
  if(write) body.push(op('updated','add','i8','read','one8'),{op:'store',args:['q','updated']});
  body.push(op('next','add','i32','iter','one'));
  return p('accumulate',params,'i8',[
    block('entry',[c('zero','i32','0'),c('one','i32','1'),c('zero8','i8','0'),...(write?[c('one8','i8','1')]:[]),...(scalar?[c('a','i8','2'),c('b','i8','3')]:[])],{op:'br',target:'head'}),
    block('head',[op('more','ult','bool','iter','n')],{op:'cbr',cond:'more',yes:'body',no:'exit'},[
      {id:'iter',type:'i32',incoming:{entry:'zero',body:'next'}},{id:'sum',type:'i8',incoming:{entry:'zero8',body:'sumNext'}}]),
    block('body',body,{op:'br',target:'head'}),block('exit',[],{op:'ret',value:'sum'})]);
}
export function loopInput(n = '2', cells = ['1'], write = false) {
  return {args:{n,p:{object:'A',offset:'0'},...(write?{q:{object:'A',offset:'0'}}:{})},heap:{A:{type:'i8',cells}}};
}
export function transferKernel() {
  return p('packet_window', [param('sample','i8'),param('bias','i8')], 'i8', [
    block('entry',[c('zero','i8','0'),c('yesValue','i8','1'),c('noValue','i8','2'),c('k1','i8','3'),c('k2','i8','4'),
      op('irrelevant','mul','i8','k1','k2'),op('shifted','add','i8','sample','bias'),op('flag','slt','bool','shifted','bias')],
      {op:'cbr',cond:'flag',yes:'flagged',no:'clear'}),
    block('flagged',[],{op:'ret',value:'yesValue'}),block('clear',[],{op:'ret',value:'noValue'})]);
}
// A supplied foreign pass for the final investigation. Its correctness is unknown
// to the learner; its implementation is intentionally inspectable.
export function foreignPass(program) {
  const candidate = structuredClone(program);
  const defs = new Map(candidate.blocks.flatMap(b => b.instructions.filter(i=>i.id).map(i=>[i.id,i])));
  for (const b of candidate.blocks) for (const i of b.instructions) {
    if(i.op !== 'slt') continue;
    const sum = defs.get(i.args[0]);
    if(sum?.op !== 'add' || sum.args[1] !== i.args[1]) continue;
    const zero = [...defs.values()].find(d=>d.op==='const'&&d.type===sum.type&&d.value==='0');
    if(zero) i.args = [sum.args[0],zero.id];
  }
  return candidate;
}

`courses/compiler-optimizer/checks.mjs`:

```mjs
// Public requirement checks. Source inspection is permitted; these are not secret exams.
import { clone, run, equivalent, observation, cfg, dominates, verify, digest, cost } from './runtime.mjs';
import { Editor, checkChain } from './editor.mjs';
import { validate, reportFor, wrongResult, size } from './evidence.mjs';
import * as C from './cases.mjs';
import {measure,structuralMeasure,smaller} from './investigation.mjs';
const value = x => C.emptyInput({x:String(x)});
export const unitTitles = ['Observable behavior','SSA and dominance','Scalar optimizer','Conditional constants','Aliases and effects','Loop motion','Evidence and cost','Reduce a miscompilation','Unfamiliar optimization'];
function assert(value,message) { if(!value) throw new Error(message); }
export function faultyMemory(program) {
  const p=clone(program);
  for(const b of p.blocks) {
    const loads=b.instructions.filter(i=>i.op==='load');
    if(loads.length<2) continue;
    const first=loads[0],last=loads.at(-1);
    for(const i of b.instructions) if(i.args) i.args=i.args.map(id=>id===last.id?first.id:id);
    if(b.term.value===last.id)b.term.value=first.id;
    b.instructions=b.instructions.filter(i=>i.id!==last.id);
  }
  return p;
}
export async function grade(unit, learner, project = null) {
  const results=[];
  const check=async(name,fn)=>{try{await fn();results.push({name,ok:true});}catch(e){results.push({name,ok:false,message:e.message,repair:`Read lessons/${String(unit).padStart(2,'0')}.md and revise the named requirement.`});}};
  const artifact=async(fn,p,inputs,contract={},benefit=false)=>{
    const result=await learner[fn](clone(p),clone(contract));
    assert(result?.program && Array.isArray(result.events),`${fn} must return Editor.finish()`);
    const proof=checkChain(p,result,contract);assert(proof.ok,`Rewrite evidence rejected: ${proof.reason}`);
    const report=reportFor(p,result,inputs,{contract});
    assert(report.validation.status==='EXHAUSTIVE_WITHIN_DOMAIN',`Behavior changed or unresolved: ${report.validation.status}; witness ${JSON.stringify(report.validation.cases.find(c=>c.status!=='equal'))}`);
    if(benefit) assert(report.cost.after<report.cost.before,`Required useful opportunity was missed: before=${report.cost.before}, after=${report.cost.after}`);
    return result;
  };
  if(unit===1){
    const p=C.memoryKernel(),i=C.memoryInput(true),a=run(p,i),b=run(faultyMemory(p),i);
    await check('Equal completed observations; internal cost ignored',()=>assert(learner.compare(a,{...clone(a),steps:999,counts:{}})===true,'Same observations must compare equal despite cost counters'));
    await check('Return value matters',()=>assert(learner.compare(a,b)===false,'The alias witness returns different values'));
    await check('Heap, effects, trap codes and types matter',()=>{
      for(const changed of [{...clone(a),heap:{A:{type:'i8',cells:['8']}}},{...clone(a),events:[{type:'i8',value:'1'}]},{...clone(a),type:'i32'}]) assert(learner.compare(a,changed)===false,`Missed observable difference: ${JSON.stringify(changed)}`);
      const t={kind:'trap',code:'bounds',heap:{},events:[]};assert(learner.compare(t,{...t,code:'other'})===false,'Trap code differs');
    });
    await check('Unknown and invalid are never equivalence',()=>{for(const kind of ['unknown','invalid']) assert(learner.compare({kind},{kind})===false,`${kind} is not completed semantics`);});
  }
  if(unit===2){
    for(const [name,p] of [['diamond',C.diamond()],['loop with phis',C.swapLoop()]]) await check(name,()=>{
      const actual=learner.dominators(clone(p));
      for(const b of p.blocks){const expected=p.blocks.filter(a=>dominates(p,a.id,b.id)).map(x=>x.id).sort();assert(JSON.stringify([...(actual[b.id]??[])].sort())===JSON.stringify(expected),`${b.id}: expected dominators ${expected}; received ${JSON.stringify(actual[b.id])}`);}
    });
    await check('Analysis ignores textual block ordering',()=>{const p=C.diamond();p.blocks.reverse();const actual=learner.dominators(p);assert(JSON.stringify([...actual.join].sort())===JSON.stringify(['entry','join']),'Join is dominated by entry and itself; neither arm dominates it');});
  }
  if(unit===3){
    await check('Useful scalar kernel with all i8 inputs',()=>artifact('scalar',C.scalarKernel(),Array.from({length:256},(_,x)=>value(x)),{},true));
    const pairs=[['0','0'],['1','2'],['127','128'],['255','3']].map(([x,y])=>C.emptyInput({x,y}));
    await check('Reuse two live commutative expressions',()=>artifact('scalar',C.reuseKernel(),pairs,{},true));
    await check('Noncommutative operands are not interchangeable',()=>artifact('scalar',C.reuseKernel('sub'),pairs));
    await check('Remove an unused total dependency chain',()=>artifact('scalar',C.deadKernel(),[value(0),value(255)],{},true));
    await check('Large multiplication folds exactly',async()=>{const p=C.wordKernel();p.params=[];p.blocks[0].instructions.unshift({id:'a',op:'const',type:'i32',value:'4294967295'},{id:'b',op:'const',type:'i32',value:'4294967295'});await artifact('scalar',p,[C.emptyInput({})],{},true);});
    await check('Trap-bearing unused work is preserved',()=>artifact('scalar',C.trapKernel(),[{args:{p:{object:'A',offset:'0'}},heap:{A:{type:'i8',cells:['4']}}}]));
  }
  if(unit===4){
    await check('Constant branch and phi simplify usefully',()=>artifact('constants',C.diamond(true),[C.emptyInput({})],{},true));
    await check('Unknown branch stays correct on both edges',()=>artifact('constants',C.diamond(false),[C.emptyInput({gate:false}),C.emptyInput({gate:true})]));
    await check('Loop-carried values do not freeze at entry',()=>artifact('constants',C.swapLoop(),[0,1,2,3].map(n=>C.emptyInput({n:String(n)}))));
    await check('Equal incoming values expose a further fold',()=>artifact('constants',C.equalPhiKernel(),[C.emptyInput({gate:false}),C.emptyInput({gate:true})],{},true));
  }
  if(unit===5){
    const p=C.memoryKernel();
    await check('Static alias facts are conservative',()=>{assert(learner.aliases(p,'p','p',{})==='must','Same pointer must alias itself');assert(learner.aliases(p,'p','q',{})==='may','Different parameter names do not prove separation');assert(learner.aliases(p,'p','q',{distinct:[['p','q']]})==='no','Explicit validated separation should be recognized');});
    await check('Constant offsets compose; unknown offsets remain conservative',()=>{const q=C.pointerAliasKernel();for(const [a,b,want]of [['p','same','must'],['p','next','no'],['p','back','must'],['p','unknown','may']])assert(learner.aliases(q,a,b,{})===want,`${a}/${b}: expected ${want}`);});
    await check('Alias write prevents reuse',()=>artifact('memory',p,[C.memoryInput(true),C.memoryInput(false)]));
    await check('Proven distinct objects enable useful reuse',()=>artifact('memory',p,[C.memoryInput(false)],{distinct:[['p','q']]},true));
    await check('Forward a completed store across a retained event',()=>artifact('memory',C.forwardingKernel(),[0,255].map(v=>({args:{p:{object:'A',offset:'0'},v:String(v)},heap:{A:{type:'i8',cells:['4']}}})),{},true));
  }
  if(unit===6){
    await check('Total scalar work moves usefully',()=>artifact('loops',C.loopKernel({scalar:true}),[0,1,3,5].map(n=>C.loopInput(String(n))),{},true));
    await check('Safe load motion with frozen preconditions',()=>artifact('loops',C.loopKernel(),[0,1,3,5].map(n=>C.loopInput(String(n))),{offsets:{p:'0'},minLengths:{p:1}},true));
    await check('Zero-trip possibly empty heap does not gain a trap',()=>artifact('loops',C.loopKernel(),[C.loopInput('0',[]),C.loopInput('2',['5'])]));
    await check('Loop alias write remains visible',()=>artifact('loops',C.loopKernel({write:true}),[C.loopInput('2',['1'],true),C.loopInput('3',['255'],true)]));
  }
  if(unit===7){
    const good={validation:{status:'EXHAUSTIVE_WITHIN_DOMAIN',complete:true},proof:{ok:true},identitiesCurrent:true,cost:{complete:true,before:12,after:8,sameWorkload:true}};
    await check('Accept a supported useful translation',()=>assert(learner.decide(clone(good))?.accept===true,'Complete supported lower-cost result should be accepted'));
    for(const status of ['COUNTEREXAMPLE','SAMPLED_NO_DIFFERENCE','UNKNOWN','INVALID']) await check(`Reject ${status}`,()=>assert(learner.decide({...clone(good),validation:{status,complete:status==='SAMPLED_NO_DIFFERENCE'}})?.accept===false,`${status} does not justify default adoption`));
    await check('Reject stale/unsupported/incomplete/noncomparable/no-win reports',()=>{for(const bad of [{...clone(good),identitiesCurrent:false},{...clone(good),proof:{ok:false}},{...clone(good),validation:{...good.validation,complete:false}},{...clone(good),cost:{...good.cost,sameWorkload:false}},{...clone(good),cost:{...good.cost,complete:false}},{...clone(good),cost:{...good.cost,after:12}}]) assert(learner.decide(bad)?.accept===false,'An unmet identity/proof/cost requirement was ignored');});
  }
  if(unit===8){
    await check('Reduce the original wrong-result behavior',async()=>{
      const p=C.memoryKernel();p.blocks[0].instructions.unshift({id:'irrelevant',op:'const',type:'i8',value:'42'});
      const input=C.memoryInput(true),reduced=await learner.reduce(clone(p),clone(input),faultyMemory);
      assert(reduced?.program&&reduced.input,'Return program and input');assert(wrongResult(reduced.program,reduced.input,faultyMemory),'Reduced candidate must remain a legal normal-return wrong result');
      assert(smaller(measure(reduced.program,reduced.input),measure(p,input)),'Reduce structure or numeric witness complexity; names and serialization do not count');
      assert(digest(reduced.program.params)===digest(p.params)&&reduced.program.returns===p.returns,'Preserve the parameter/return contract');
      assert(typeof reduced.explanation==='string'&&reduced.explanation.trim().length>=30,'Explain your reduction family and stopping condition for rubric review');
    });
  }
  if(unit===9){
    await check('Independent investigation project exists',()=>assert(typeof project?.investigate==='function','Create project.mjs exporting investigate(program, foreignPass); see API.md. No project solution is supplied.'));
    if(typeof project?.investigate==='function') await check('Fresh witness, meaningful reduction and useful repair',async()=>{
      const p=C.transferKernel(),result=await project.investigate(clone(p),C.foreignPass);
      assert(wrongResult(p,result.input,C.foreignPass),'Your input must demonstrate a legal normal-return wrong result');
      assert(wrongResult(result.reduced,result.input,C.foreignPass),'Reduced source must regenerate the same class of wrong result');
      assert(smaller(structuralMeasure(result.reduced),structuralMeasure(p)),'The final project requires fewer blocks, definitions/instructions or operands; cosmetic and literal-only changes do not count');
      assert(digest(result.reduced.params)===digest(p.params)&&result.reduced.returns===p.returns,'Keep the function signature');
      assert(typeof result.repair==='function','Return repair(program) for the foreign pass replacement');
      const fixed=await result.repair(clone(p)),grid=[0,1,2,63,127,128,129,255].flatMap(sample=>[0,1,20,127,128,255].map(bias=>C.emptyInput({sample:String(sample),bias:String(bias)})));
      assert(checkChain(p,fixed).ok,'Repaired transform must carry valid checked edits');
      assert(validate(p,fixed.program,grid).status==='EXHAUSTIVE_WITHIN_DOMAIN','Repair changes behavior on boundary domain');
      assert(wrongResult(p,result.input,C.foreignPass)&&equivalent(run(p,result.input),run(fixed.program,result.input)),'Repair must fix your original witness');
      const sample=C.scalarKernel(),win=await result.repair(clone(sample));assert(checkChain(sample,win).ok,'Repair must preserve checked-edit protocol');
      const report=reportFor(sample,win,[value(0),value(10),value(255)]);assert(report.validation.status==='EXHAUSTIVE_WITHIN_DOMAIN'&&report.cost.after<report.cost.before,'Disabling all optimization is not a useful repair');
      assert(typeof result.explanation==='string'&&result.explanation.trim().length>=40,'Include a causal explanation and limits for rubric review; prose is not auto-certified');
    });
  }
  if(!Number.isInteger(unit)||unit<1||unit>9)throw new Error('Unit must be 01 through 09');
  return {unit,title:unitTitles[unit-1],passed:results.length>0&&results.every(r=>r.ok),results,reasoningReview:unit===9?'Manual/self-review required; mechanical success is not causal-explanation acceptance':null};
}

`courses/compiler-optimizer/cli.mjs`:

```mjs
#!/usr/bin/env node
import { readFile, writeFile, mkdir, readdir, copyFile, access } from 'node:fs/promises';
import { dirname, join, resolve } from 'node:path';
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
import { execFile } from 'node:child_process';
import { promisify } from 'node:util';
import { randomUUID } from 'node:crypto';
import { digest, run, verify } from './runtime.mjs';
import { parseJSON } from './json.mjs';
import * as C from './cases.mjs';
import { normalizeJob } from './domains.mjs';
const root=dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)),execute=promisify(execFile);
const support=['runtime.mjs','editor.mjs','evidence.mjs','investigation.mjs'];
async function exists(path){try{await access(path);return true;}catch{return false;}}
async function identity(){const manifest=parseJSON(await readFile(join(root,'course.json'),'utf8'));const files={};for(const name of manifest.publicFiles)files[name]=await readFile(join(root,name),'utf8');return digest(files);}
async function initialize(work){await mkdir(work);await mkdir(join(work,'support'));await copyFile(join(root,'starter.mjs'),join(work,'optimizer.mjs'));for(const name of support)await copyFile(join(root,name),join(work,'support',name));await mkdir(join(work,'.attempts'));}
async function source(work){const files={'optimizer.mjs':await readFile(join(work,'optimizer.mjs'),'utf8')};for(const name of support)files[`support/${name}`]=await readFile(join(work,'support',name),'utf8');if(await exists(join(work,'project.mjs')))files['project.mjs']=await readFile(join(work,'project.mjs'),'utf8');return files;}
async function saveFiles(folder,files){await mkdir(join(folder,'support'),{recursive:true});for(const [name,text]of Object.entries(files))await writeFile(join(folder,name),text,{flag:'wx'});}
async function attempt(work,request,help){
  const files=await source(work),courseIdentity=await identity(),sourceIdentity=digest(files);
  const id=`${new Date().toISOString().replace(/[:.]/g,'-')}-${randomUUID().slice(0,8)}`,folder=join(work,'.attempts',id);
  await mkdir(folder,{recursive:true});await saveFiles(join(folder,'snapshot'),files);
  const questionText=request.action==='check'?await readFile(join(root,'lessons',`${String(request.unit).padStart(2,'0')}.md`),'utf8'):JSON.stringify(request.job);
  const saved={...request,id,createdAt:new Date().toISOString(),courseIdentity,sourceIdentity,questionText,helpUsed:help??'not declared',modulePath:join(folder,'snapshot','optimizer.mjs'),projectPath:files['project.mjs']?join(folder,'snapshot','project.mjs'):null};
  await writeFile(join(folder,'request.json'),JSON.stringify(saved,null,2),{flag:'wx'});
  let processError=null;
  try{await execute(process.execPath,[join(root,'worker.mjs'),join(folder,'request.json'),join(folder,'result.json')],{timeout:8000,maxBuffer:1024*1024});}catch(error){processError={message:error.message,killed:error.killed===true};}
  let result;
  if(await exists(join(folder,'result.json')))result=parseJSON(await readFile(join(folder,'result.json'),'utf8'),{maxBytes:16*1024*1024,maxNodes:500000});
  else{result={passed:false,error:processError?.killed?'Execution timed out; this is not a semantic result':processError?.message??'Worker produced no result'};await writeFile(join(folder,'result.json'),JSON.stringify(result,null,2),{flag:'wx'});}
  const receipt={id,courseIdentity,sourceIdentity,questionText,sourceFiles:files,helpUsed:saved.helpUsed,result,processError};
  await writeFile(join(folder,'receipt.json'),JSON.stringify(receipt,null,2),{flag:'wx'});
  return receipt;
}
function example(name){
  if(name==='scalar')return {program:C.scalarKernel(),domain:{version:1,axes:[{parameter:'x',range:{from:'0',to:'255',step:'1'}}],heaps:[{}]},contract:{}};
  if(name==='branch')return {program:C.diamond(true),inputs:[C.emptyInput({})],contract:{}};
  if(name==='memory')return {program:C.memoryKernel(),inputs:[C.memoryInput(false)],contract:{distinct:[['p','q']]}};
  if(name==='loop')return {program:C.loopKernel(),inputs:[0,1,3,5].map(n=>C.loopInput(String(n))),contract:{offsets:{p:'0'},minLengths:{p:1}}};
  if(name==='transfer')return {program:C.transferKernel(),inputs:[C.emptyInput({sample:'0',bias:'0'})],contract:{}};
  throw new Error('Example must be scalar, branch, memory, loop, or transfer');
}
async function history(work){const folder=join(work,'.attempts'),restored=join(work,'restored-history.json');const results=await exists(restored)?parseJSON(await readFile(restored,'utf8'),{maxBytes:16*1024*1024,maxNodes:500000}):[];if(!await exists(folder))return results;for(const name of (await readdir(folder)).sort()){const path=join(folder,name,'receipt.json');if(await exists(path))results.push(parseJSON(await readFile(path,'utf8'),{maxBytes:16*1024*1024,maxNodes:500000}));}return results;}
async function main(){
  const args=process.argv.slice(2),command=args.shift();
  if(command==='start'){const work=resolve(args[0]??'work');await initialize(work);console.log(`Created ${work}\nEdit optimizer.mjs. Start with: node cli.mjs check 01 ${work} --help-used none`);return;}
  if(command==='lesson'){const n=String(Number(args[0])).padStart(2,'0');if(!/^0[1-9]$/.test(n))throw new Error('Lesson must be 01..09');console.log(await readFile(join(root,'lessons',`${n}.md`),'utf8'));return;}
  if(command==='question'||command==='answer'){
    const bank=parseJSON(await readFile(join(root,'practice.json'),'utf8')),item=bank.items.find(i=>i.id===args[0]);if(!item)throw new Error('Use an item ID such as 01a or 01b');
    const question={id:item.id,prompt:item.prompt,choices:item.choices};
    if(command==='question'){console.log(JSON.stringify(question,null,2));return;}
    const work=resolve(args[1]??'work'),choice=args[2];if(!Object.hasOwn(item.choices,choice))throw new Error('Choose one of the listed letters');
    const files=await source(work),id=`${new Date().toISOString().replace(/[:.]/g,'-')}-${randomUUID().slice(0,8)}`,folder=join(work,'.attempts',id),helpAt=args.indexOf('--help-used');await mkdir(folder,{recursive:true});
    const request={id,question,choice,helpUsed:helpAt>=0?args[helpAt+1]:'not declared',courseIdentity:await identity(),sourceIdentity:digest(files),sourceFiles:files};
    await writeFile(join(folder,'request.json'),JSON.stringify(request,null,2),{flag:'wx'});
    const result={unit:item.unit,item:item.id,passed:choice===item.correct,committed:choice,correct:item.correct,reason:item.why,next:item.next};
    await writeFile(join(folder,'receipt.json'),JSON.stringify({...request,result},null,2),{flag:'wx'});console.log(JSON.stringify(result,null,2));process.exitCode=result.passed?0:1;return;
  }
  if(command==='example'){const job=example(args[0]);if(args[1]){await writeFile(resolve(args[1]),JSON.stringify(job,null,2),{flag:'wx'});console.log(resolve(args[1]));}else console.log(JSON.stringify(job,null,2));return;}
  if(command==='run'){const job=normalizeJob(parseJSON(await readFile(resolve(args[0]),'utf8')));console.log(JSON.stringify({validity:verify(job.program),domain:job.evidence,results:job.inputs.map(input=>run(job.program,input,{contract:job.contract??{}}))},null,2));return;}
  if(command==='check'){
    const unit=Number(args[0]),work=resolve(args[1]??'work'),helpAt=args.indexOf('--help-used');if(!Number.isInteger(unit)||unit<1||unit>9)throw new Error('Check one unit 01..09');
    const receipt=await attempt(work,{action:'check',unit},helpAt>=0?args[helpAt+1]:undefined);console.log(JSON.stringify({id:receipt.id,courseIdentity:receipt.courseIdentity,sourceIdentity:receipt.sourceIdentity,result:receipt.result},null,2));process.exitCode=receipt.result.error?3:receipt.result.passed?0:1;return;
  }
  if(command==='optimize'||command==='pipeline'){
    const work=resolve(args[0]),job=normalizeJob(parseJSON(await readFile(resolve(args[1]),'utf8'))),pass=args[2]??'scalar',helpAt=args.indexOf('--help-used');
    const receipt=await attempt(work,{action:command,job,pass,passes:pass.split(','),useLearnerPolicy:args.includes('--learner-policy')},helpAt>=0?args[helpAt+1]:undefined);console.log(JSON.stringify({id:receipt.id,result:receipt.result},null,2));process.exitCode=receipt.result.error?3:receipt.result.passed?0:1;return;
  }
  if(command==='status'){const work=resolve(args[0]??'work'),currentSource=digest(await source(work)),currentCourse=await identity();console.log(JSON.stringify((await history(work)).map(r=>({id:r.id,passed:r.result.passed,unit:r.result.unit,current:r.sourceIdentity===currentSource&&r.courseIdentity===currentCourse,helpUsed:r.helpUsed})),null,2));return;}
  if(command==='export'){const work=resolve(args[0]),target=resolve(args[1]);const files=await source(work),receipts=await history(work),payload={format:'optimizer-work/1',courseIdentity:await identity(),files,sourceIdentity:digest(files),receipts};const text=JSON.stringify(payload,null,2);if(Buffer.byteLength(text)>16*1024*1024)throw new Error('Export exceeds 16 MiB; existing work remains unchanged');parseJSON(text,{maxBytes:16*1024*1024,maxNodes:500000});await writeFile(target,text,{flag:'wx'});console.log(`Exported exact work and ${receipts.length} immutable receipts to ${target}`);return;}
  if(command==='restore'){
    const saved=parseJSON(await readFile(resolve(args[0]),'utf8'),{maxBytes:16*1024*1024,maxNodes:500000}),target=resolve(args[1]);
    if(saved.format!=='optimizer-work/1'||saved.courseIdentity!==await identity()||saved.sourceIdentity!==digest(saved.files))throw new Error('Invalid or different-course export; keep it and use the matching course package');
    const allowed=['optimizer.mjs','project.mjs',...support.map(n=>`support/${n}`)];if(!saved.files||typeof saved.files!=='object'||Array.isArray(saved.files)||Object.entries(saved.files).some(([n,v])=>!allowed.includes(n)||typeof v!=='string')||allowed.filter(n=>n!=='project.mjs').some(n=>typeof saved.files[n]!=='string')||!Array.isArray(saved.receipts))throw new Error('Malformed export');
    for(const receipt of saved.receipts)if(!receipt||typeof receipt.id!=='string'||typeof receipt.courseIdentity!=='string'||typeof receipt.sourceIdentity!=='string'||!receipt.sourceFiles||digest(receipt.sourceFiles)!==receipt.sourceIdentity||!receipt.result||typeof receipt.result.passed!=='boolean')throw new Error('Malformed or mismatched historical receipt');
    await mkdir(target);await saveFiles(target,saved.files);await mkdir(join(target,'.attempts'));
    await writeFile(join(target,'restored-history.json'),JSON.stringify(saved.receipts,null,2),{flag:'wx'});
    console.log(`Restored into ${target}; prior receipt history is preserved in restored-history.json. New attempts remain separate.`);return;
  }
  console.log('Commands: start WORK | lesson 01 | question 01a | answer 01a WORK LETTER --help-used none | check 01 WORK --help-used none | example scalar JOB.json | run JOB.json | optimize WORK JOB.json scalar | pipeline WORK JOB.json scalar,constants | status WORK | export WORK FILE.json | restore FILE.json NEW_WORK');
}
main().catch(error=>{console.error(error.message);process.exitCode=2;});

`courses/compiler-optimizer/domains.mjs`:

```mjs
// Supplied finite-domain enumeration; no solver or random sampling is hidden here.
import {clone,digest,literal,validateInput,verify} from './runtime.mjs';
const shape=(x,keys)=>x&&typeof x==='object'&&!Array.isArray(x)&&Object.keys(x).every(k=>keys.includes(k))&&keys.every(k=>Object.hasOwn(x,k));
export function expandDomain(program,manifest,contract={}) {
  if(!verify(program).ok)throw new Error('domain.invalid_program');
  if(!shape(manifest,['version','axes','heaps'])||manifest.version!==1||!Array.isArray(manifest.axes)||!Array.isArray(manifest.heaps)||manifest.heaps.length===0)throw new Error('domain.shape');
  if(manifest.axes.length!==program.params.length||new Set(manifest.axes.map(a=>a.parameter)).size!==manifest.axes.length)throw new Error('domain.parameters');
  const axes=manifest.axes.map(axis=>{
    const parameter=program.params.find(p=>p.id===axis.parameter);if(!parameter)throw new Error('domain.unknown_parameter');
    let values;
    if(shape(axis,['parameter','values'])){if(!Array.isArray(axis.values))throw new Error('domain.values');values=clone(axis.values);}
    else if(shape(axis,['parameter','range'])&&shape(axis.range,['from','to','step'])&&['i8','i32'].includes(parameter.type)){
      const from=literal(parameter.type,axis.range.from),to=literal(parameter.type,axis.range.to),step=literal(parameter.type,axis.range.step);
      if(step===0n||to<from||(to-from)/step+1n>65536n)throw new Error('domain.range_limit');
      values=[];for(let value=from;value<=to;value+=step)values.push(value.toString());
    }else throw new Error('domain.axis_shape');
    if(!values.length||new Set(values.map(digest)).size!==values.length)throw new Error('domain.empty_or_duplicate_axis');
    return {parameter:parameter.id,values};
  });
  if(new Set(manifest.heaps.map(digest)).size!==manifest.heaps.length)throw new Error('domain.duplicate_heap');
  const count=axes.reduce((n,a)=>n*BigInt(a.values.length),BigInt(manifest.heaps.length));if(count>65536n)throw new Error('domain.case_limit');
  let argumentsList=[{}];for(const axis of axes)argumentsList=argumentsList.flatMap(args=>axis.values.map(value=>({...args,[axis.parameter]:value})));
  const inputs=argumentsList.flatMap(args=>manifest.heaps.map(heap=>({args:clone(args),heap:clone(heap)})));
  for(const input of inputs)validateInput(program,input,contract);
  return {inputs,evidence:{kind:'finite-cartesian',manifest:clone(manifest),manifestIdentity:digest(manifest),inputIdentity:digest(inputs),planned:Number(count),distinct:inputs.length,order:'axis order, each listed value in order, then heap order'}};
}
export function normalizeJob(job) {
  if(!job||typeof job!=='object'||Object.keys(job).some(k=>!['program','inputs','domain','contract'].includes(k))||!job.program||Object.hasOwn(job,'inputs')===Object.hasOwn(job,'domain'))throw new Error('job: provide exactly one of inputs or domain');
  const contract=job.contract??{};
  if(Object.hasOwn(job,'domain')){const expanded=expandDomain(job.program,job.domain,contract);return {program:job.program,contract,...expanded};}
  if(!Array.isArray(job.inputs))throw new Error('job.inputs');
  return {program:job.program,contract,inputs:job.inputs,evidence:{kind:'explicit-list',inputIdentity:digest(job.inputs),planned:job.inputs.length,distinct:new Set(job.inputs.map(digest)).size}};
}

`courses/compiler-optimizer/editor.mjs`:

```mjs
// Supplied checked edit language. Learners choose analyses and transformations.
import { clone, digest, canonical, definitions, uses, cfg, dominates, pureOps, literal, evaluate, valueJSON, verify, validateContract } from './runtime.mjs';
const commutative = new Set(['add', 'mul', 'and', 'or', 'xor', 'eq', 'ne']);
function need(value, reason) { if (!value) throw new Error(reason); }
function locate(p, id) {
  for (const block of p.blocks) {
    const index = block.instructions.findIndex(i => i.id === id);
    if (index >= 0) return { block, instruction: block.instructions[index], index, phi: false };
    const phi = block.phis.find(i => i.id === id);
    if (phi) return { block, instruction: phi, index: -1, phi: true };
  }
  throw new Error(`edit.missing_definition:${id}`);
}
function drop(p, id) { for (const b of p.blocks) { b.instructions = b.instructions.filter(i => i.id !== id); b.phis = b.phis.filter(i => i.id !== id); } }
function redirect(p, from, to) {
  for (const b of p.blocks) {
    for (const phi of b.phis) for (const edge of Object.keys(phi.incoming)) if (phi.incoming[edge] === from) phi.incoming[edge] = to;
    for (const i of b.instructions) if (i.args) i.args = i.args.map(id => id === from ? to : id);
    if (b.term.value === from) b.term.value = to;
    if (b.term.cond === from) b.term.cond = to;
  }
}
function constantResult(p, i) {
  if (i.op === 'const') return i.value;
  const defs = definitions(p);
  if (i.incoming) {
    const values = Object.values(i.incoming).map(id => defs.get(id));
    need(values.length && values.every(v => v?.op === 'const' && v.type === i.type && canonical(v.value) === canonical(values[0].value)), 'fold.phi_not_constant');
    return values[0].value;
  }
  need(pureOps.has(i.op) && i.op !== 'ptradd', 'fold.not_scalar');
  const values = i.args.map(id => defs.get(id));
  need(values.every(v => v?.op === 'const'), 'fold.operands_not_constant');
  return valueJSON(evaluate(i.op, i.type, values.map(v => literal(v.type, v.value)), values[0].type));
}
function expressionKey(i) {
  let args = [...(i.args ?? [])];
  if (commutative.has(i.op)) args.sort();
  return canonical({ op: i.op, type: i.type, args, ...(i.op === 'const' ? { value: i.value } : {}) });
}
function address(p, id, seen = new Set()) {
  if (seen.has(id)) return null;
  seen.add(id); const d = definitions(p).get(id);
  if (d?.block === null && d.type.startsWith('ptr<')) return { root: id, offset: 0n };
  if (d?.op !== 'ptradd') return null;
  const delta = definitions(p).get(d.args[1]);
  if (delta?.op !== 'const') return null;
  const base = address(p, d.args[0], seen);
  return base && { root: base.root, offset: base.offset + BigInt.asIntN(32, BigInt(delta.value)) };
}
function alias(p, a, b, contract) {
  if (a === b) return 'must';
  const x = address(p, a), y = address(p, b);
  if (!x || !y) return 'may';
  if (x.root === y.root) return x.offset === y.offset ? 'must' : 'no';
  if ((contract.distinct ?? []).some(pair => pair.includes(x.root) && pair.includes(y.root))) return 'no';
  return 'may';
}
function loopShape(p, header) {
  const graph = cfg(p);
  const latches = graph.predecessors[header].filter(id => dominates(p, header, id));
  need(latches.length === 1, 'loop.requires_single_latch');
  const nodes = new Set([header]), queue = [...latches];
  while (queue.length) { const id = queue.pop(); if (nodes.has(id)) continue; nodes.add(id); queue.push(...graph.predecessors[id]); }
  const outside = graph.predecessors[header].filter(id => !nodes.has(id));
  need(outside.length === 1 && graph.successors[outside[0]].length === 1, 'loop.requires_preheader');
  for (const id of nodes) for (const next of graph.successors[id]) if (!nodes.has(next)) need(graph.predecessors[next].every(x => nodes.has(x)), 'loop.requires_dedicated_exits');
  return { nodes, preheader: outside[0] };
}
function cleanup(p) {
  const graph = cfg(p), seen = new Set(), queue = [p.entry];
  while (queue.length) { const id = queue.pop(); if (seen.has(id)) continue; seen.add(id); queue.push(...graph.successors[id]); }
  p.blocks = p.blocks.filter(b => seen.has(b.id));
  const after = cfg(p);
  for (const b of p.blocks) for (const phi of b.phis) for (const edge of Object.keys(phi.incoming)) if (!after.predecessors[b.id].includes(edge)) delete phi.incoming[edge];
}
function apply(p, edit, contract) {
  if (edit.kind === 'branch') {
    const b = p.blocks.find(b => b.id === edit.block), condition = definitions(p).get(b?.term.cond);
    need(b?.term.op === 'cbr' && condition?.op === 'const' && condition.type === 'bool', 'branch.condition_not_constant');
    b.term = { op: 'br', target: condition.value ? b.term.yes : b.term.no }; cleanup(p); return;
  }
  const at = locate(p, edit.id), i = at.instruction;
  if (edit.kind === 'fold') {
    const value = constantResult(p, i); need(canonical(edit.value) === canonical(value), 'fold.wrong_value');
    const replacement = { id: i.id, op: 'const', type: i.type, value };
    if (at.phi) { drop(p, i.id); at.block.instructions.unshift(replacement); return; }
    at.block.instructions[at.index] = replacement; return;
  }
  if (edit.kind === 'dead') { need(!uses(p).some(u => u.id === i.id) && pureOps.has(i.op), 'dead.used_or_effectful'); drop(p, i.id); return; }
  if (edit.kind === 'reuse') {
    const other = locate(p, edit.other);
    need(!at.phi && !other.phi && pureOps.has(i.op) && expressionKey(i) === expressionKey(other.instruction), 'reuse.not_same_total_expression');
    need(dominates(p, other.block.id, at.block.id) && (other.block.id !== at.block.id || other.index < at.index), 'reuse.not_available');
    redirect(p, i.id, other.instruction.id); drop(p, i.id); return;
  }
  if (edit.kind === 'memory') {
    need(i.op === 'load', 'memory.target_not_load');
    const prior = at.block.instructions[edit.priorIndex];
    need(edit.priorIndex >= 0 && edit.priorIndex < at.index && ['load', 'store'].includes(prior?.op), 'memory.prior_access');
    need(alias(p, prior.args[0], i.args[0], contract) === 'must', 'memory.address_not_same');
    for (const middle of at.block.instructions.slice(edit.priorIndex + 1, at.index)) if (middle.op === 'store') need(alias(p, middle.args[0], i.args[0], contract) === 'no', 'memory.intervening_alias_write');
    redirect(p, i.id, prior.op === 'load' ? prior.id : prior.args[1]); drop(p, i.id); return;
  }
  if (edit.kind === 'move') {
    need(!at.phi, 'move.phi'); const loop = loopShape(p, edit.header), defs = definitions(p);
    need(loop.nodes.has(at.block.id), 'move.not_in_loop');
    for (const arg of i.args ?? []) { const d = defs.get(arg); need(d.block === null || (!loop.nodes.has(d.block) && dominates(p, d.block, loop.preheader)), 'move.variant_operand'); }
    if (i.op === 'load') {
      const a = address(p, i.args[0]); need(a && Object.hasOwn(contract.offsets ?? {}, a.root), 'move.no_static_offset');
      const offset = BigInt(contract.offsets[a.root]) + a.offset;
      need(offset >= 0n && offset < BigInt(contract.minLengths?.[a.root] ?? 0), 'move.may_trap');
      for (const b of p.blocks.filter(b => loop.nodes.has(b.id))) for (const op of b.instructions) if (op.op === 'store') need(alias(p, i.args[0], op.args[0], contract) === 'no', 'move.alias_write');
    } else need(pureOps.has(i.op), 'move.effectful');
    drop(p, i.id); p.blocks.find(b => b.id === loop.preheader).instructions.push(i); return;
  }
  throw new Error(`edit.unsupported:${edit.kind}`);
}
export class Editor {
  constructor(program, contract = {}) { need(verify(program).ok,'editor.invalid_source');validateContract(program,contract);this.program = clone(program); this.contract = clone(contract); this.events = []; }
  edit(operation) {
    const before = digest(this.program), candidate = clone(this.program);
    apply(candidate, operation, this.contract);
    const validity = verify(candidate); need(validity.ok, `edit.invalid_output:${validity.errors.join(',')}`);
    this.events.push({ operation: clone(operation), before, after: digest(candidate) }); this.program = candidate; return this;
  }
  finish() { return { program: clone(this.program), events: clone(this.events) }; }
}
export function checkChain(original, artifact, contract = {}) {
  try {
    need(verify(original).ok,'chain.invalid_source');validateContract(original,contract);
    need(artifact && Array.isArray(artifact.events) && artifact.events.length <= 2048, 'chain.shape');
    let current = clone(original);
    for (const event of artifact.events) {
      need(digest(current) === event.before, 'chain.stale_before'); apply(current, event.operation, contract);
      need(digest(current) === event.after, 'chain.wrong_after'); need(verify(current).ok, 'chain.invalid_intermediate');
    }
    need(digest(current) === digest(artifact.program), 'chain.unreported_delta'); need(verify(current).ok, 'chain.invalid_output');
    return { ok: true, events: artifact.events.length };
  } catch (error) { return { ok: false, reason: error.message }; }
}

`courses/compiler-optimizer/evidence.mjs`:

```mjs
import { digest, run, equivalent, observation, cost, verify } from './runtime.mjs';
import { checkChain } from './editor.mjs';
export function validate(before, after, inputs, options = {}) {
  const { contract = {}, fuel = 10000, mode = 'exhaustive', maxCases = 4096, totalFuel = 2000000 } = options;
  if(!Array.isArray(inputs)||!Number.isSafeInteger(maxCases)||maxCases<1||maxCases>65536||!Number.isSafeInteger(totalFuel)||totalFuel<0||totalFuel>2000000)throw new Error('validation.invalid_domain_or_budget');
  const base = { semantics: 'kernel-ir/1', before: digest(before), after: digest(after), contract: digest(contract), domain: digest(inputs), mode, fuel,
    counts: { planned: inputs.length, started: 0, equal: 0, different: 0, unknown: 0, invalid: 0, unstarted: inputs.length }, cases: [] };
  const invalid = reason => ({ ...base, status: 'INVALID', reason, complete: false });
  if (!verify(before).ok || !verify(after).ok) return invalid('Invalid program');
  if (!inputs.length || new Set(inputs.map(digest)).size !== inputs.length || !['exhaustive','sample'].includes(mode)) return invalid('Empty, duplicate, or malformed domain');
  let remaining=totalFuel;
  for (const input of inputs.slice(0, maxCases)) {
    if(remaining<=0)break;
    const source = run(before,input,{fuel:Math.min(fuel,remaining),contract});remaining-=source.steps??0;
    const target = run(after,input,{fuel:Math.min(fuel,remaining),contract});remaining-=target.steps??0;
    base.counts.started++; base.counts.unstarted--;
    const entry = { input, source, target };
    if (source.kind === 'invalid' || target.kind === 'invalid') { base.counts.invalid++; entry.status='invalid'; }
    else if (!observation(source) || !observation(target)) { base.counts.unknown++; entry.status='unknown'; }
    else if (equivalent(source,target)) { base.counts.equal++; entry.status='equal'; }
    else { base.counts.different++; entry.status='different'; }
    base.cases.push(entry);
  }
  if (base.counts.invalid) return {...base,status:'INVALID',reason:'Invalid invocation',complete:false};
  const complete = !base.counts.unknown && !base.counts.unstarted;
  const status = base.counts.different ? 'COUNTEREXAMPLE' : !complete ? 'UNKNOWN' : mode === 'sample' ? 'SAMPLED_NO_DIFFERENCE' : 'EXHAUSTIVE_WITHIN_DOMAIN';
  return {...base,status,complete};
}
export function reportFor(before, artifact, inputs, options = {}) {
  const validation = validate(before,artifact.program,inputs,options);
  const proof = checkChain(before,artifact,options.contract ?? {});
  const beforeCost = validation.cases.reduce((s,c)=>s+cost(c.source),0), afterCost=validation.cases.reduce((s,c)=>s+cost(c.target),0);
  return { validation, proof, identitiesCurrent:true, cost:{complete:validation.complete,before:beforeCost,after:afterCost,model:'unit IR operations',sameWorkload:true}, artifact };
}
export function wrongResult(program,input,transform) {
  try {
    const target=transform(program); if(!verify(program).ok || !verify(target).ok) return false;
    const a=run(program,input,{fuel:10000}),b=run(target,input,{fuel:10000});
    return a.kind==='return' && b.kind==='return' && (a.type!==b.type || a.value!==b.value || digest(a.heap)!==digest(b.heap));
  } catch { return false; }
}
// Legacy helper name uses the same semantic vector; compare with smaller().
export { measure as size } from './investigation.mjs';

Implement <code>compare(sourceResult, targetResult)</code> so the workbench can distinguish equal completed behavior from a discrepancy or an unfinished run.</p><p>Prerequisites: functions, arrays and basic compiler terminology. Read the observation shapes in API.md. The interpreter, input reader and execution limits are supplied.</p><h3>Decide what can be observed</h3><p>Kernel IR returns an i8, i32 or bool value. It can also store into input arrays, append typed events, or terminate with a defined trap. All of those observations matter. Instruction identifiers, elapsed work and the arrangement of blocks do not.</p><p>Consider two runs that return i8 6. The first emits i8 2 and then i8 5; the second emits i8 5 and then i8 2. The return values agree, but the ordered event sequences differ. Comparing the event set would lose information.</p><p>For a normal return, compare the return type and value, all heap object identities/types/cells, and events in order. For a trap, compare its code and the heap/events that existed before it. Object-map key order is irrelevant; cell and event order are meaningful.</p><p>Commit a decision before seeing feedback:</p><pre><code>node cli.mjs question 01a
node cli.mjs answer 01a work YOUR_LETTER --help-used none</code></pre><h3>Separate program behavior from an incomplete experiment</h3><p>A bounds trap is part of this IR's meaning. Running out of fuel is an incomplete observation of the program. Two loops reaching the same fuel limit have not demonstrated equivalent final behavior.</p><p>A useful comparator first asks whether both results completed as return or trap. It then compares the relevant fields. It must return false for unknown or invalid results; the surrounding validator will classify those separately rather than call them counterexamples.</p><p>Do not compare every property indiscriminately: optimization is expected to change counters. Do not discard fields just because the current example does not use them.</p><h3>Build and repair</h3><p>Implement <code>compare</code> in work/optimizer.mjs. Start with a field inventory on paper, then write the code. Create a local pair whose only difference is a trap code and another whose only difference is a counter. Run:</p><pre><code>node cli.mjs check 01 work --help-used none</code></pre><p>The checker snapshots your code before executing it. A failed check names the missed requirement. Keep that first attempt and repair the function rather than replacing its history.</p><p>Use item <code>01b</code> to check the distinction between equal prefixes and completed outcomes. In U05 and the final investigation, the same comparator will expose bugs that a return-only comparison misses.</p><div class="practice-panel"></div></section><section id="unit-02" data-unit="2" aria-label="Unit 02"><h2>SSA, control flow and dominance</h2><p>A substituted value may be numerically right yet unavailable on a path. Implement <code>dominators(program)</code> so your optimizer can establish where a definition is usable.</p><p>Prerequisite: U01, directed graphs and sets. The supplied <code>cfg</code> utility returns predecessor and successor lists; you own the dominance analysis.</p><h3>Compute availability across every path</h3><p>Block A dominates block B when every entry-to-B path passes through A. Each block dominates itself. The entry dominates every reachable block.</p><p>For a diamond E → L/R → J, the dominator sets are E:{E}, L:{E,L}, R:{E,R}, J:{E,J}. Neither arm dominates J because the other arm supplies a path avoiding it.</p><p>A practical fixed-point procedure initializes entry to {entry} and every other reachable block to the set of all blocks. Repeatedly replace a non-entry block's set with itself plus the intersection of its predecessors' sets. Stop only when every set is unchanged. Initializing all non-entry blocks to just themselves would discard necessary facts rather than compute this solution.</p><p>Apply the procedure by hand to a graph with a backedge before coding. Return sorted arrays keyed by block ID; block storage order must not influence the answer.</p><p>Commit item <code>02a</code> using <code>question</code> and <code>answer</code>.</p><h3>A phi uses values on edges</h3><p>A phi selects the value associated with the predecessor that actually transferred control. Its incoming values must be available at their own predecessor terminators, not necessarily on every path into the successor.</p><p>In a loop, a body-defined next counter can feed a header phi on the backedge even though the body does not dominate the first entry into the header. The initial incoming value handles that first entry.</p><p>All selected phi inputs are read from the predecessor environment before any new phi result is written. This matters when two loop variables exchange values. The supplied interpreter implements this rule; your analysis must not reject valid backedge uses.</p><p>Commit item <code>02b</code>, then implement the analysis and run:</p><pre><code>node cli.mjs check 02 work --help-used none</code></pre><h3>Transfer the analysis</h3><p>Reorder the blocks of a valid program without changing its edges and check that dominance is unchanged. Add a second path into a join and reconsider which definitions remain available. In U03, use this relation before reusing an expression across blocks.</p><p>The independent supplied verifier checks SSA legality by a different graph method. It is an oracle for this workbench, not a substitute for implementing the target analysis.</p><div class="practice-panel"></div></section><section id="unit-03" data-unit="3" aria-label="Unit 03"><h2>A useful scalar optimizer</h2><p>The calibration kernel computes the same multiplication twice and carries unnecessary constant work. Implement <code>scalar(program, contract)</code> to reduce its executed work while emitting a checked edit chain.</p><p>Prerequisites: U01–U02. Use the supplied Editor; return <code>editor.finish()</code>. You choose opportunities and ordering. The editor checks the rule premises and records exact before/after identities.</p><h3>Fold only under the declared arithmetic</h3><p>An i8 multiplication of constants 90 and 3 produces 14: the mathematical product 270 wraps modulo 256. An i32 multiplication of the same constants produces 270. Use the supplied word primitives rather than JavaScript Number multiplication for arbitrary i32 operands.</p><p>A constant fold requires known constant operands and the exact operation/type. The result becomes a typed constant with the original result ID. Folding can make its original constants unused, but that is a separate edit.</p><p>For example, after establishing the correct result for a particular definition, an edit has this shape:</p><pre><code>editor.edit({kind: 'fold', id: chosenID, value: canonicalValue});</code></pre><p>This is an edit request, not permission to invent a value. Wrong values are rejected.</p><h3>Reuse and remove with distinct premises</h3><p>Reuse requires the same total, pure expression and an available earlier result. Addition and multiplication permit operand-order normalization; signed comparisons do not. A definition in one arm of a diamond is not available in the other arm merely because the expressions match.</p><p>Dead-result removal requires no remaining use, including return, branch, phi and effect operands, and a total pure instruction. An unused load can still trap. Store and emit are observable even without result IDs.</p><p>Commit items <code>03a</code> and <code>03b</code> before looking at their feedback. Implement folding, safe reuse and dead-result cleanup. Revisit opportunities after an edit: folding can expose dead constants, and reuse can make a definition unnecessary. Avoid unbounded loops when no edit succeeds.</p><h3>Project A: run your optimizer</h3><pre><code>node cli.mjs check 03 work --help-used none
node cli.mjs example scalar calibration.json
node cli.mjs optimize work calibration.json scalar --help-used none</code></pre><p>The report compares every listed input, checks the whole edit chain and reports unit-cost IR work. The output program is adopted only when the required evidence and improvement hold. A no-op implementation is safe but does not complete this project.</p><p>Inspect a rejected edit, repair its premise and rerun. Then try your pass on a kernel with a trap-bearing load. Saving one multiplication never justifies changing whether a trap occurs.</p><div class="practice-panel"></div></section><section id="unit-04" data-unit="4" aria-label="Unit 04"><h2>Conditional constants and dataflow</h2><p>A constant condition can make an edge unreachable, which can make a phi constant. Implement <code>constants(program, contract)</code> as a convergent sequence of justified value and control-flow simplifications.</p><p>Prerequisite: Project A. Your earlier scalar pass can be factored into a helper, but its edits must stay in one continuous evidence chain.</p><h3>Values and control flow inform each other</h3><p>Suppose entry branches on the known false value. Only its false successor executes. A downstream phi no longer needs the removed edge's value. If its remaining input is a constant, the phi can be replaced with that constant, exposing more scalar folds.</p><p>Do not confuse a currently unseen edge with an impossible edge. In a general constant-propagation analysis, value facts distinguish not-yet-known, one known constant, and varying/unknown values. Joining different possible constants loses the constant claim. Executable edges determine which incoming values contribute.</p><p>Our checked-edit core is deliberately conservative: first fold provable literal computations, simplify a branch whose condition is now a literal, repair the CFG, and fold phis whose remaining inputs agree. Repeat to a fixed point. This teaches the coupling without making an unverified sparse solver part of the trusted base.</p><p>Commit item <code>04a</code>.</p><h3>Make iteration explicit</h3><p>Keep a worklist or repeat a full sweep. Either is acceptable at this scale. The loop must stop when there are no new justified edits. Recompute or invalidate dependent facts after changing the program; the old digest identifies the old graph.</p><p>A header phi with initial value zero and a backedge increment is not the constant zero merely because you visited entry first. Test at least two loop iterations. A single first-trip test cannot expose a frozen loop-carried fact.</p><p>The editor's branch operation removes newly unreachable blocks and obsolete phi inputs as one verified transaction. Do not manually omit that cleanup or claim stale analysis applies to the new program.</p><h3>Build and transfer</h3><pre><code>node cli.mjs question 04b
node cli.mjs answer 04b work YOUR_LETTER --help-used none
node cli.mjs check 04 work --help-used none
node cli.mjs example branch branch.json
node cli.mjs optimize work branch.json constants --help-used none</code></pre><p>Keep an unknown-input diamond unchanged unless your facts justify a transformation. Test a loop with values that change after the first backedge. Correct refusal on such a case matters as much as removing a constant branch.</p><p>This implementation path is a conservative conditional simplifier, not a claim to support every optimization available in LLVM SCCP.</p><div class="practice-panel"></div></section><section id="unit-05" data-unit="5" aria-label="Unit 05"><h2>Aliases and effects</h2><p>Two parameter names can reference the same cell. Implement <code>aliases</code> and <code>memory</code> so a memory optimization depends on static evidence rather than an input that happened to work.</p><p>Prerequisites: U02–U04. The heap model, pointer arithmetic and checked memory edits are supplied.</p><h3>Distinguish names, objects and cells</h3><p>A pointer is an object ID plus an element offset. Different objects cannot overlap in this IR. Two offsets within one typed object name the same cell only when the offsets are equal. No byte reinterpretation or object lifetime change exists.</p><p>For static analysis, a pointer parameter is a symbolic base. A ptradd by a constant changes its symbolic offset. Two expressions with the same base and equal offsets must alias; the same base with different offsets cannot alias. Different unknown parameter bases may alias unless the frozen contract explicitly separates their objects.</p><p>A concrete run with p on object A and q on object B does not establish a static NoAlias claim for every invocation.</p><p>Commit items <code>05a</code> and <code>05b</code>.</p><h3>Reuse a value across only safe effects</h3><p>Consider a load through p, a store through q, then another load through p. If q may alias p, the store invalidates the saved value. If the contract proves distinct objects, the saved value can still serve the later load.</p><p>Scan backward from a load or maintain available memory values while scanning forward. A same-location earlier load or store supplies a value. A possibly aliasing intervening store blocks reuse. An emit does not change memory in this language, but it must remain in the event sequence.</p><p>The earlier access also matters for traps. If it fails, execution never reaches the later load. If it succeeds, fixed object size and the identical address make the later access in bounds. This is more precise than declaring every load pure.</p><h3>Extend the same tool</h3><pre><code>node cli.mjs check 05 work --help-used none
node cli.mjs example memory memory.json
node cli.mjs optimize work memory.json memory --help-used none</code></pre><p>The memory example includes an explicit object-separation contract. Your pass must also preserve the aliasing case without that contract. Unknown facts may justify refusing an optimization; always returning MayAlias misses the required provable case.</p><p>Review the whole output heap after a change. A return-only check would miss a store incorrectly discarded or reordered.</p><div class="practice-panel"></div></section><section id="unit-06" data-unit="6" aria-label="Unit 06"><h2>Move loop work without changing behavior</h2><p>A computation repeated inside a loop may be moved once to its preheader. Implement <code>loops(program, contract)</code> so the move remains valid for zero-trip loops and aliased memory.</p><p>Prerequisites: dominance, conditional constants and alias/effect reasoning.</p><h3>Find a supported natural loop</h3><p>A backedge from latch L to header H has H dominating L. Starting from L, walk predecessors backward until H to collect the loop's blocks. The required profile has one latch and one outside predecessor serving as preheader. Exits are dedicated to the loop. Unsupported shapes should remain unchanged.</p><p>A value is invariant when its operands are available outside the loop or are values you have already moved in a valid order. Moving an instruction changes availability, so revisit dependent instructions.</p><p>For total scalar arithmetic, executing it earlier cannot add a trap or event. It can change work on a zero-trip input. That is a profitability issue, addressed separately in U07.</p><p>Commit item <code>06a</code>.</p><h3>A load needs more than an invariant pointer</h3><p>A pointer can stay fixed while a store changes its contents. A load can also be skipped by the original program and trap if executed speculatively.</p><p>Our required load-motion profile is narrow: the frozen contract establishes a fixed, in-bounds address, and no loop store may alias it. The contract is checked on every input. A single observed nonempty array is not a proof for future arrays.</p><p>The editor records the move and checks the loop, availability, bounds and write premises. Your analysis chooses which operation to propose. It does not gain permission to invent a stronger contract.</p><p>Commit item <code>06b</code>.</p><h3>Project B: optimize loop kernels</h3><pre><code>node cli.mjs check 06 work --help-used none
node cli.mjs example loop loop.json
node cli.mjs optimize work loop.json loops --help-used none</code></pre><p>Inspect three outcomes: a scalar move, a safe load move under explicit preconditions, and refusal of a load that may see an aliasing write. Include a zero-trip invocation with an empty object when no nonempty contract exists.</p><p>A valid implementation need not optimize every loop. It must recognize the stated supported opportunity and preserve behavior on the refusal controls. General symbolic range analysis, unrolling and vectorization are outside this core.</p><div class="practice-panel"></div></section><section id="unit-07" data-unit="7" aria-label="Unit 07"><h2>Evidence, pass order and cost</h2><p>A report that says “all tests passed” is incomplete without its subjects, domain and limits. Implement <code>decide(report)</code> to select a supported, beneficial translation and retain the previous program otherwise.</p><p>Prerequisites: Projects A and B. Hashing, execution, case accounting and report serialization are supplied.</p><h3>Read the evidence before the number</h3><p>EXHAUSTIVE_WITHIN_DOMAIN means every member of a declared nonempty finite domain completed equally. It does not mean every input of every size was checked. SAMPLED_NO_DIFFERENCE is weaker. UNKNOWN means required execution or coverage did not finish. INVALID means the subjects, inputs or evidence are malformed/inconsistent. COUNTEREXAMPLE records a completed mismatch.</p><p>A demonstrated counterexample is useful even if some other cases were not completed. A cutoff on the last case prevents an exhaustive success. Neither conclusion depends on whether the average runtime looked good.</p><p>Commit item <code>07a</code>.</p><p>Every receipt binds the original/candidate programs, input contract and listed inputs. The edit-chain check detects changes that were never described by a rewrite event. Current identities, successful rule checks and completed domain coverage are separate requirements.</p><h3>Decide whether the change earns its place</h3><p>This workbench counts executed IR operations with unit weights. Phi assignments count as value work; their simultaneous group is one interpreter fuel step. This model is reproducible, but it is not machine cycles.</p><p>Compare identical input lists. A safe hoist may add a load on a zero-trip input while saving many loads on longer runs. Report those per-input changes and the total under the chosen workload. Do not call an aggregate benefit a worst-case speedup.</p><p>Commit item <code>07b</code>. Require current identities, a checked rule chain, exhaustive required-domain success, complete comparable costs and a strict aggregate improvement. A correct no-op ties the baseline rather than improving it.</p><h3>Project C: make a defensible decision</h3><pre><code>node cli.mjs check 07 work --help-used none
node cli.mjs optimize work calibration.json scalar --learner-policy --help-used none
node cli.mjs pipeline work calibration.json scalar,constants --learner-policy --help-used none</code></pre><p>Inspect a retained candidate as well as an adopted one. In a multi-pass experiment, keep every boundary; a later pass can mask an earlier bad transformation. Evidence remains local and editable, so its digest is a binding identifier rather than an authenticity certificate.</p><p>Run <code>scalar,constants</code> and then <code>constants,scalar</code> on your branch example. Explain a stage that changes nothing, a stage that exposes a later opportunity, and whether the final costs differ. No order is required to win. The pipeline records each rejected candidate before continuing from the last accepted program, then checks the aggregate chain. An intermediate failure remains visible even when the final candidate is useful.</p><p>Inspect the scalar job's <code>domain</code>: one inclusive i8 range and an empty heap produce exactly 256 distinct inputs. Change its upper endpoint to 127. The new receipt may still say EXHAUSTIVE_WITHIN_DOMAIN, but its domain identity and claim are smaller. Restore the original range before comparing costs. A product of two full i8 axes has 65,536 cases; the default execution cap will leave unstarted cases, so it must not be relabeled exhaustive.</p><p>Translation validation checks a particular translation; it complements rather than replaces compiler testing. See the original <a href="https://people.eecs.berkeley.edu/~necula/Papers/tv_pldi00.pdf">Necula paper</a> and the bounded-checking discussion in <a href="https://web.ist.utl.pt/nuno.lopes/pubs/alive2-pldi21.pdf">Alive2</a>.</p><div class="practice-panel"></div></section><section id="unit-08" data-unit="8" aria-label="Unit 08"><h2>Reduce a miscompilation</h2><p>A small, stable wrong-result example is easier to explain and repair than a large failing program. Implement <code>reduce(program, input, transform)</code> so simplification preserves the same legal miscompilation.</p><p>Prerequisite: U07. The guided fault reuses memory incorrectly; the final investigation uses a different optimization.</p><h3>Define the interestingness predicate first</h3><p>For each proposed source and input, regenerate the target using the supplied transform. Verify both programs, execute them from separate fresh heaps and require normal returns that differ in value or observable heap. A parser crash, a new bounds trap or an exhausted budget is not the required wrong-result witness.</p><p>Suppose irrelevant constant arithmetic is removed and the same source/target return discrepancy persists. That is useful reduction. Removing a definition used by the return and making the program invalid is not.</p><p>Commit item <code>08a</code>.</p><p>Keep three internal decisions: interesting, not interesting, and unresolved. You may skip an unresolved candidate and preserve the best known witness, but you cannot use it as evidence that no smaller witness exists.</p><p>The supplied <code>inspectWitness</code> helper reports those three states and preserves both executions. Start with a deliberately tiny fuel budget and observe UNRESOLVED, then restore enough fuel. This is an execution-budget experiment, not a new counterexample. An exception inside the faulty transform is also unresolved; it cannot certify a clean neighborhood.</p><h3>Reduce structure and input without losing identity</h3><p>Try a finite family of legal changes, such as deleting unused total computations or simplifying an input value. A supplied Editor can enforce structural safety for eligible source changes; the interestingness check still has to rerun the faulty transform.</p><p>Accept only a strictly smaller candidate under a declared measure. Keep the signature, semantics and faulty pipeline fixed. Never manually edit only the target to preserve an apparent discrepancy. Recheck the final witness from fresh state.</p><p>Use the supplied lexicographic <code>measure</code>: block count, definitions/instructions, operand occurrences, heap objects, heap cells, then numeric-value complexity. Numeric complexity counts magnitude bits (plus a sign bit for a negative offset), not printed characters. Simplifying a witness word from 7 to 0 decreases it; shortening the program name or renaming an SSA value does not. Property order and whitespace also do not count. A smaller value cannot compensate for adding a block. Values can tie under this declared order; do not claim every possible simplification is ranked. Keep a trace of candidates, decisions and the best accepted witness. You design the candidate family and search order; the helper supplies execution and accounting.</p><p>A greedy reducer can produce a useful best-found result. Claim 1-minimality only after checking every permitted single-step reduction of the final candidate with no interesting or unresolved neighbor. That is still not a global minimum.</p><p>Pass that final candidate list to <code>assessNeighborhood</code>. Its NO_SMALLER_IN_LIST report establishes only the list it actually inspected. Explain why your list covers your declared family, or label the result best-found. A family containing only one convenient edit is weak evidence even when completely checked.</p><p>Commit item <code>08b</code>.</p><h3>Build the investigation artifact</h3><pre><code>node cli.mjs check 08 work --help-used none
node cli.mjs export work investigation.json</code></pre><p>Return the reduced program, input and a short explanation of your reduction family and stopping condition. The checker demands a preserved normal-return discrepancy and actual simplification; it accepts different reduced forms.</p><p>The export preserves your first attempts and exact code. Use the rubric to explain the causal violation, not only the fact that two numbers differ. See <a href="https://llvm.org/docs/CommandGuide/llvm-reduce.html">llvm-reduce</a> for the role of an explicit interestingness test in a production tool.</p><div class="practice-panel"></div></section><section id="unit-09" data-unit="9" aria-label="Unit 09"><h2>Transfer: an unfamiliar optimization</h2><p>A foreign pass rewrites a packet-window kernel. Investigate it without a worked diagnosis, then replace its faulty behavior while retaining useful optimization.</p><p>Prerequisites: U01–U08. Create your own work/project.mjs; no project implementation is supplied. API.md specifies its interface.</p><h3>Establish an original witness</h3><p>Your project receives the original program and an inspectable transform. Read the IR and the transform, state a hypothesis and search for an input satisfying the declared signature. Require valid source and target programs, normal returns and a value or heap discrepancy.</p><p>The precise issue is not given here. Use the integer, control-flow and effect rules already established. A familiar-looking algebraic transformation is not evidence that its premises hold.</p><p>Retain the original program and input before reducing. The automated check will regenerate the target itself; an invented target or a manually edited output is not accepted.</p><p>Commit item <code>09a</code>.</p><h3>Reduce, explain and repair</h3><p>Return a structurally smaller source that still exposes the discrepancy through the same foreign transform. This supplied program contains irrelevant executable work: decrease its block, definition/instruction or operand count under <code>structuralMeasure</code>. Shortening names, reformatting JSON, or changing only an unused literal cannot satisfy this final-project requirement. Different valid structural reductions are welcome. Explain which semantic premise fails, why your reduced example isolates it and which alternatives you ruled out.</p><p>Return a repair function that emits checked Editor artifacts. The repair may conservatively decline the problematic transformation, but it must preserve genuine optimization wins on the supplied scalar kernel. Returning every input unchanged is not a useful optimizer.</p><p>The checker tests your witness, reduced source, repaired boundary behavior and retained wins. Your explanation has a separate rubric review; passing mechanical checks does not certify the causal argument.</p><h3>Deliver a portable investigation</h3><pre><code>node cli.mjs question 09b
node cli.mjs answer 09b work YOUR_LETTER --help-used none
node cli.mjs check 09 work --help-used none
node cli.mjs export work final-investigation.json
node cli.mjs restore final-investigation.json restored-work
node cli.mjs check 09 restored-work --help-used &quot;restored my own work&quot;</code></pre><p>State the input domain you checked and distinguish it from untested cases. Describe the cost model and at least one legitimate optimization retained by the repair. Keep original and revised attempts, and disclose help.</p><p>This is a local course project with a bounded verifier. It is not evidence of general LLVM compatibility or universal compiler correctness. The course itself also remains a local candidate until its learner flow, human tryout and authorized public release are verified.</p><div class="practice-panel"></div></section></main></div><footer>Local course candidate · No accounts, external scripts or automatic submissions · See README.md for supported runtime and evidence limits.</footer><script type="application/json" id="reader-data">{"bank":{"format":"optimizer-practice/1","items":[{"id":"01a","unit":1,"prompt":"Two completed runs return the same i8 value.
