`courses/compiler-optimizer/investigation.mjs`:

```mjs
// Supplied execution/accounting tools. Learners choose reductions and stopping rules.
import {clone,digest,run,verify,equivalent} from './runtime.mjs';

// Counts, not spelling: alpha-renaming and JSON presentation carry no weight.
export function structuralMeasure(program) {
  const definitions=program.params.length+program.blocks.reduce((n,b)=>n+b.phis.length+b.instructions.length,0);
  const operands=program.blocks.reduce((n,b)=>n+b.phis.reduce((s,p)=>s+Object.keys(p.incoming).length,0)+b.instructions.reduce((s,i)=>s+(i.args?.length??0),0),0);
  return [program.blocks.length,definitions,operands];
}
function valueComplexity(value) {
  if(typeof value==='boolean')return Number(value);
  if(value&&typeof value==='object')return valueComplexity(value.offset);
  const n=BigInt(value),magnitude=n<0n?-n:n;
  return (magnitude===0n?0:magnitude.toString(2).length)+(n<0n?1:0);
}
export function measure(program,input) {
  const objects=Object.values(input.heap),cells=objects.reduce((n,o)=>n+o.cells.length,0);
  const literals=program.blocks.flatMap(b=>b.instructions.filter(i=>i.op==='const').map(i=>i.value));
  const values=[...literals,...Object.values(input.args),...objects.flatMap(o=>o.cells)];
  return [...structuralMeasure(program),objects.length,cells,values.reduce((sum,v)=>sum+valueComplexity(v),0)];
}
export function smaller(left,right) {
  if(!Array.isArray(left)||!Array.isArray(right)||left.length!==right.length)throw new Error('measure.shape');
  for(let n=0;n<left.length;n++){if(left[n]<right[n])return true;if(left[n]>right[n])return false;}return false;
}
export function inspectWitness(program,input,transform,{contract={},fuel=10000}={}) {
  const identity={source:digest(program),input:digest(input),contract:digest(contract)};
  if(!verify(program).ok)return {...identity,status:'NOT_INTERESTING',reason:'invalid source'};
  let target;
  try{target=transform(clone(program));}catch(error){return {...identity,status:'UNRESOLVED',reason:'transform failed',error:error.message};}
  if(target&&typeof target.then==='function')return {...identity,status:'UNRESOLVED',reason:'async transforms require a separate runner'};
  if(!verify(target).ok)return {...identity,status:'NOT_INTERESTING',reason:'invalid target'};
  const sourceResult=run(program,input,{contract,fuel}),targetResult=run(target,input,{contract,fuel});
  const result={...identity,target:digest(target),sourceResult,targetResult};
  if(sourceResult.kind==='unknown'||targetResult.kind==='unknown')return {...result,status:'UNRESOLVED',reason:'execution budget'};
  if(sourceResult.kind!=='return'||targetResult.kind!=='return')return {...result,status:'NOT_INTERESTING',reason:'normal returns required'};
  // The investigation target is a wrong result, not only a reordered event trace.
  const wrong=sourceResult.type!==targetResult.type||sourceResult.value!==targetResult.value||digest(sourceResult.heap)!==digest(targetResult.heap);
  return {...result,status:wrong?'INTERESTING':'NOT_INTERESTING',reason:wrong?'normal-return value or heap mismatch':equivalent(sourceResult,targetResult)?'same observation':'event-only difference outside this investigation target'};
}
export function assessNeighborhood(program,input,transform,candidates,{contract={},fuel=10000,maxCandidates=256}={}) {
  if(!Array.isArray(candidates)||!Number.isSafeInteger(maxCandidates)||maxCandidates<0||maxCandidates>4096)throw new Error('neighborhood.shape');
  const base=inspectWitness(program,input,transform,{contract,fuel}),baseMeasure=measure(program,input),seen=new Set(),results=[];
  for(const candidate of candidates.slice(0,maxCandidates)){
    if(!candidate?.program||!candidate.input)throw new Error('candidate.shape');
    const key=digest({program:candidate.program,input:candidate.input});if(seen.has(key))throw new Error('candidate.duplicate');seen.add(key);
    const signature=digest(candidate.program.params)===digest(program.params)&&candidate.program.returns===program.returns;
    const decreases=verify(candidate.program).ok&&signature&&smaller(measure(candidate.program,candidate.input),baseMeasure);
    const result=decreases?inspectWitness(candidate.program,candidate.input,transform,{contract,fuel}):{status:'NOT_INTERESTING',reason:'not a legal signature-preserving decrease'};
    results.push({candidate:key,measure:decreases?measure(candidate.program,candidate.input):null,...result});
  }
  const unstarted=candidates.length-results.length,unresolved=results.filter(x=>x.status==='UNRESOLVED').length,interesting=results.filter(x=>x.status==='INTERESTING').length;
  return {base,measure:baseMeasure,candidates:digest(candidates),planned:candidates.length,started:results.length,unstarted,unresolved,interesting,results,
    status:base.status!=='INTERESTING'?'BASE_NOT_ESTABLISHED':interesting?'SMALLER_WITNESS':unstarted||unresolved?'UNRESOLVED':'NO_SMALLER_IN_LIST',
    limitation:'The caller must establish that the supplied list covers the declared reduction family. No global-minimum claim.'};
}

// Supplied bounded JSON reader. Native JSON.parse alone loses duplicate keys.
export function parseJSON(text, {maxBytes=1024*1024,maxNodes=50000}={}) {
  if(typeof text!=='string'||Buffer.byteLength(text)>maxBytes)throw new Error('json.size_limit');
  let at=0,nodes=0;
  const white=()=>{while(/[\x20\t\r\n]/.test(text[at]??'!'))at++;};
  const string=()=>{const start=at++;while(at<text.length){const char=text[at++];if(char==='\\'){at++;continue;}if(char==='"')return JSON.parse(text.slice(start,at));}throw new Error('json.unterminated_string');};
  const value=depth=>{
    if(depth>80||++nodes>maxNodes)throw new Error('json.structure_limit');white();
    if(text[at]==='"'){string();return;}
    if(text[at]==='{'){
      at++;white();const keys=new Set();if(text[at]==='}'){at++;return;}
      while(true){white();if(text[at]!=='"')throw new Error('json.object_key');const key=string();if(keys.has(key))throw new Error(`json.duplicate_key:${key}`);keys.add(key);white();if(text[at++]!==':')throw new Error('json.colon');value(depth+1);white();const end=text[at++];if(end==='}')return;if(end!==',')throw new Error('json.object_separator');}
    }
    if(text[at]==='['){at++;white();if(text[at]===']'){at++;return;}while(true){value(depth+1);white();const end=text[at++];if(end===']')return;if(end!==',')throw new Error('json.array_separator');}}
    const token=/^(?:true|false|null|-?(?:0|[1-9][0-9]*)(?:\.[0-9]+)?(?:[eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?)/.exec(text.slice(at));
    if(!token)throw new Error('json.value');at+=token[0].length;
  };
  value(0);white();if(at!==text.length)throw new Error('json.trailing_data');return JSON.parse(text);
}

`courses/compiler-optimizer/lessons/01.md`:

```md
# What must an optimization preserve?

A faster kernel is unusable if it changes the records it returns or modifies. Implement `compare(sourceResult, targetResult)` so the workbench can distinguish equal completed behavior from a discrepancy or an unfinished run.

Prerequisites: functions, arrays and basic compiler terminology. Read the observation shapes in API.md. The interpreter, input reader and execution limits are supplied.

## Decide what can be observed

Kernel IR returns an i8, i32 or bool value. It can also store into input arrays, append typed events, or terminate with a defined trap. All of those observations matter. Instruction identifiers, elapsed work and the arrangement of blocks do not.

Consider two runs that return i8 6. The first emits i8 2 and then i8 5; the second emits i8 5 and then i8 2. The return values agree, but the ordered event sequences differ. Comparing the event set would lose information.

For a normal return, compare the return type and value, all heap object identities/types/cells, and events in order. For a trap, compare its code and the heap/events that existed before it. Object-map key order is irrelevant; cell and event order are meaningful.

Commit a decision before seeing feedback:

```sh
node cli.mjs question 01a
node cli.mjs answer 01a work YOUR_LETTER --help-used none
```

## Separate program behavior from an incomplete experiment

A bounds trap is part of this IR's meaning. Running out of fuel is an incomplete observation of the program. Two loops reaching the same fuel limit have not demonstrated equivalent final behavior.

A useful comparator first asks whether both results completed as return or trap. It then compares the relevant fields. It must return false for unknown or invalid results; the surrounding validator will classify those separately rather than call them counterexamples.

Do not compare every property indiscriminately: optimization is expected to change counters. Do not discard fields just because the current example does not use them.

## Build and repair

Implement `compare` in work/optimizer.mjs. Start with a field inventory on paper, then write the code. Create a local pair whose only difference is a trap code and another whose only difference is a counter. Run:

```sh
node cli.mjs check 01 work --help-used none
```

The checker snapshots your code before executing it. A failed check names the missed requirement. Keep that first attempt and repair the function rather than replacing its history.

Use item `01b` to check the distinction between equal prefixes and completed outcomes. In U05 and the final investigation, the same comparator will expose bugs that a return-only comparison misses.

`courses/compiler-optimizer/lessons/02.md`:

```md
# SSA, control flow and dominance

A substituted value may be numerically right yet unavailable on a path. Implement `dominators(program)` so your optimizer can establish where a definition is usable.

Prerequisite: U01, directed graphs and sets. The supplied `cfg` utility returns predecessor and successor lists; you own the dominance analysis.

## Compute availability across every path

Block A dominates block B when every entry-to-B path passes through A. Each block dominates itself. The entry dominates every reachable block.

For a diamond E → L/R → J, the dominator sets are E:{E}, L:{E,L}, R:{E,R}, J:{E,J}. Neither arm dominates J because the other arm supplies a path avoiding it.

A practical fixed-point procedure initializes entry to {entry} and every other reachable block to the set of all blocks. Repeatedly replace a non-entry block's set with itself plus the intersection of its predecessors' sets. Stop only when every set is unchanged. Initializing all non-entry blocks to just themselves would discard necessary facts rather than compute this solution.

Apply the procedure by hand to a graph with a backedge before coding. Return sorted arrays keyed by block ID; block storage order must not influence the answer.

Commit item `02a` using `question` and `answer`.

## A phi uses values on edges

A phi selects the value associated with the predecessor that actually transferred control. Its incoming values must be available at their own predecessor terminators, not necessarily on every path into the successor.

In a loop, a body-defined next counter can feed a header phi on the backedge even though the body does not dominate the first entry into the header. The initial incoming value handles that first entry.

All selected phi inputs are read from the predecessor environment before any new phi result is written. This matters when two loop variables exchange values. The supplied interpreter implements this rule; your analysis must not reject valid backedge uses.

Commit item `02b`, then implement the analysis and run:

```sh
node cli.mjs check 02 work --help-used none
```

## Transfer the analysis

Reorder the blocks of a valid program without changing its edges and check that dominance is unchanged. Add a second path into a join and reconsider which definitions remain available. In U03, use this relation before reusing an expression across blocks.

The independent supplied verifier checks SSA legality by a different graph method. It is an oracle for this workbench, not a substitute for implementing the target analysis.

```

`courses/compiler-optimizer/lessons/03.md`:

```md
# A useful scalar optimizer

The calibration kernel computes the same multiplication twice and carries unnecessary constant work. Implement `scalar(program, contract)` to reduce its executed work while emitting a checked edit chain.

Prerequisites: U01–U02. Use the supplied Editor; return `editor.finish()`. You choose opportunities and ordering. The editor checks the rule premises and records exact before/after identities.

## Fold only under the declared arithmetic

An i8 multiplication of constants 90 and 3 produces 14: the mathematical product 270 wraps modulo 256. An i32 multiplication of the same constants produces 270. Use the supplied word primitives rather than JavaScript Number multiplication for arbitrary i32 operands.

A constant fold requires known constant operands and the exact operation/type. The result becomes a typed constant with the original result ID. Folding can make its original constants unused, but that is a separate edit.

For example, after establishing the correct result for a particular definition, an edit has this shape:

```js
editor.edit({kind: 'fold', id: chosenID, value: canonicalValue});
```

This is an edit request, not permission to invent a value. Wrong values are rejected.

## Reuse and remove with distinct premises

Reuse requires the same total, pure expression and an available earlier result. Addition and multiplication permit operand-order normalization; signed comparisons do not. A definition in one arm of a diamond is not available in the other arm merely because the expressions match.

Dead-result removal requires no remaining use, including return, branch, phi and effect operands, and a total pure instruction. An unused load can still trap. Store and emit are observable even without result IDs.

Commit items `03a` and `03b` before looking at their feedback. Implement folding, safe reuse and dead-result cleanup. Revisit opportunities after an edit: folding can expose dead constants, and reuse can make a definition unnecessary. Avoid unbounded loops when no edit succeeds.

## Project A: run your optimizer

```sh
node cli.mjs check 03 work --help-used none
node cli.mjs example scalar calibration.json
node cli.mjs optimize work calibration.json scalar --help-used none
```

The report compares every listed input, checks the whole edit chain and reports unit-cost IR work. The output program is adopted only when the required evidence and improvement hold. A no-op implementation is safe but does not complete this project.

Inspect a rejected edit, repair its premise and rerun. Then try your pass on a kernel with a trap-bearing load. Saving one multiplication never justifies changing whether a trap occurs.

```

`courses/compiler-optimizer/lessons/04.md`:

```md
# Conditional constants and dataflow

A constant condition can make an edge unreachable, which can make a phi constant. Implement `constants(program, contract)` as a convergent sequence of justified value and control-flow simplifications.

Prerequisite: Project A. Your earlier scalar pass can be factored into a helper, but its edits must stay in one continuous evidence chain.

## Values and control flow inform each other

Suppose entry branches on the known false value. Only its false successor executes. A downstream phi no longer needs the removed edge's value. If its remaining input is a constant, the phi can be replaced with that constant, exposing more scalar folds.

Do not confuse a currently unseen edge with an impossible edge. In a general constant-propagation analysis, value facts distinguish not-yet-known, one known constant, and varying/unknown values. Joining different possible constants loses the constant claim. Executable edges determine which incoming values contribute.

Our checked-edit core is deliberately conservative: first fold provable literal computations, simplify a branch whose condition is now a literal, repair the CFG, and fold phis whose remaining inputs agree. Repeat to a fixed point. This teaches the coupling without making an unverified sparse solver part of the trusted base.

Commit item `04a`.

## Make iteration explicit

Keep a worklist or repeat a full sweep. Either is acceptable at this scale. The loop must stop when there are no new justified edits. Recompute or invalidate dependent facts after changing the program; the old digest identifies the old graph.

A header phi with initial value zero and a backedge increment is not the constant zero merely because you visited entry first. Test at least two loop iterations. A single first-trip test cannot expose a frozen loop-carried fact.

The editor's branch operation removes newly unreachable blocks and obsolete phi inputs as one verified transaction. Do not manually omit that cleanup or claim stale analysis applies to the new program.

## Build and transfer

```sh
node cli.mjs question 04b
node cli.mjs answer 04b work YOUR_LETTER --help-used none
node cli.mjs check 04 work --help-used none
node cli.mjs example branch branch.json
node cli.mjs optimize work branch.json constants --help-used none
```

Keep an unknown-input diamond unchanged unless your facts justify a transformation. Test a loop with values that change after the first backedge. Correct refusal on such a case matters as much as removing a constant branch.

This implementation path is a conservative conditional simplifier, not a claim to support every optimization available in LLVM SCCP.

```

`courses/compiler-optimizer/lessons/05.md`:

```md
# Aliases and effects

Two parameter names can reference the same cell. Implement `aliases` and `memory` so a memory optimization depends on static evidence rather than an input that happened to work.

Prerequisites: U02–U04. The heap model, pointer arithmetic and checked memory edits are supplied.

## Distinguish names, objects and cells

A pointer is an object ID plus an element offset. Different objects cannot overlap in this IR. Two offsets within one typed object name the same cell only when the offsets are equal. No byte reinterpretation or object lifetime change exists.

For static analysis, a pointer parameter is a symbolic base. A ptradd by a constant changes its symbolic offset. Two expressions with the same base and equal offsets must alias; the same base with different offsets cannot alias. Different unknown parameter bases may alias unless the frozen contract explicitly separates their objects.

A concrete run with p on object A and q on object B does not establish a static NoAlias claim for every invocation.

Commit items `05a` and `05b`.

## Reuse a value across only safe effects

Consider a load through p, a store through q, then another load through p. If q may alias p, the store invalidates the saved value. If the contract proves distinct objects, the saved value can still serve the later load.

Scan backward from a load or maintain available memory values while scanning forward. A same-location earlier load or store supplies a value. A possibly aliasing intervening store blocks reuse. An emit does not change memory in this language, but it must remain in the event sequence.

The earlier access also matters for traps. If it fails, execution never reaches the later load. If it succeeds, fixed object size and the identical address make the later access in bounds. This is more precise than declaring every load pure.

## Extend the same tool

```sh
node cli.mjs check 05 work --help-used none
node cli.mjs example memory memory.json
node cli.mjs optimize work memory.json memory --help-used none
```

The memory example includes an explicit object-separation contract. Your pass must also preserve the aliasing case without that contract. Unknown facts may justify refusing an optimization; always returning MayAlias misses the required provable case.

Review the whole output heap after a change. A return-only check would miss a store incorrectly discarded or reordered.

```

`courses/compiler-optimizer/lessons/06.md`:

```md
# Move loop work without changing behavior

A computation repeated inside a loop may be moved once to its preheader. Implement `loops(program, contract)` so the move remains valid for zero-trip loops and aliased memory.

Prerequisites: dominance, conditional constants and alias/effect reasoning.

## Find a supported natural loop

A backedge from latch L to header H has H dominating L. Starting from L, walk predecessors backward until H to collect the loop's blocks. The required profile has one latch and one outside predecessor serving as preheader. Exits are dedicated to the loop. Unsupported shapes should remain unchanged.

A value is invariant when its operands are available outside the loop or are values you have already moved in a valid order. Moving an instruction changes availability, so revisit dependent instructions.

For total scalar arithmetic, executing it earlier cannot add a trap or event. It can change work on a zero-trip input. That is a profitability issue, addressed separately in U07.

Commit item `06a`.

## A load needs more than an invariant pointer

A pointer can stay fixed while a store changes its contents. A load can also be skipped by the original program and trap if executed speculatively.

Our required load-motion profile is narrow: the frozen contract establishes a fixed, in-bounds address, and no loop store may alias it. The contract is checked on every input. A single observed nonempty array is not a proof for future arrays.

The editor records the move and checks the loop, availability, bounds and write premises. Your analysis chooses which operation to propose. It does not gain permission to invent a stronger contract.

Commit item `06b`.

## Project B: optimize loop kernels

```sh
node cli.mjs check 06 work --help-used none
node cli.mjs example loop loop.json
node cli.mjs optimize work loop.json loops --help-used none
```

Inspect three outcomes: a scalar move, a safe load move under explicit preconditions, and refusal of a load that may see an aliasing write. Include a zero-trip invocation with an empty object when no nonempty contract exists.

A valid implementation need not optimize every loop. It must recognize the stated supported opportunity and preserve behavior on the refusal controls. General symbolic range analysis, unrolling and vectorization are outside this core.

```

`courses/compiler-optimizer/lessons/07.md`:

```md
# Evidence, pass order and cost

A report that says “all tests passed” is incomplete without its subjects, domain and limits. Implement `decide(report)` to select a supported, beneficial translation and retain the previous program otherwise.

Prerequisites: Projects A and B. Hashing, execution, case accounting and report serialization are supplied.

## Read the evidence before the number

EXHAUSTIVE_WITHIN_DOMAIN means every member of a declared nonempty finite domain completed equally. It does not mean every input of every size was checked. SAMPLED_NO_DIFFERENCE is weaker. UNKNOWN means required execution or coverage did not finish. INVALID means the subjects, inputs or evidence are malformed/inconsistent. COUNTEREXAMPLE records a completed mismatch.

A demonstrated counterexample is useful even if some other cases were not completed. A cutoff on the last case prevents an exhaustive success. Neither conclusion depends on whether the average runtime looked good.

Commit item `07a`.

Every receipt binds the original/candidate programs, input contract and listed inputs. The edit-chain check detects changes that were never described by a rewrite event. Current identities, successful rule checks and completed domain coverage are separate requirements.

## Decide whether the change earns its place

This workbench counts executed IR operations with unit weights. Phi assignments count as value work; their simultaneous group is one interpreter fuel step. This model is reproducible, but it is not machine cycles.

Compare identical input lists. A safe hoist may add a load on a zero-trip input while saving many loads on longer runs. Report those per-input changes and the total under the chosen workload. Do not call an aggregate benefit a worst-case speedup.

Commit item `07b`. Require current identities, a checked rule chain, exhaustive required-domain success, complete comparable costs and a strict aggregate improvement. A correct no-op ties the baseline rather than improving it.

## Project C: make a defensible decision

```sh
node cli.mjs check 07 work --help-used none
node cli.mjs optimize work calibration.json scalar --learner-policy --help-used none
node cli.mjs pipeline work calibration.json scalar,constants --learner-policy --help-used none
```

Inspect a retained candidate as well as an adopted one. In a multi-pass experiment, keep every boundary; a later pass can mask an earlier bad transformation. Evidence remains local and editable, so its digest is a binding identifier rather than an authenticity certificate.

Run `scalar,constants` and then `constants,scalar` on your branch example. Explain a stage that changes nothing, a stage that exposes a later opportunity, and whether the final costs differ. No order is required to win. The pipeline records each rejected candidate before continuing from the last accepted program, then checks the aggregate chain. An intermediate failure remains visible even when the final candidate is useful.

Inspect the scalar job's `domain`: one inclusive i8 range and an empty heap produce exactly 256 distinct inputs. Change its upper endpoint to 127. The new receipt may still say EXHAUSTIVE_WITHIN_DOMAIN, but its domain identity and claim are smaller. Restore the original range before comparing costs. A product of two full i8 axes has 65,536 cases; the default execution cap will leave unstarted cases, so it must not be relabeled exhaustive.

Translation validation checks a particular translation; it complements rather than replaces compiler testing. See the original [Necula paper](https://people.eecs.berkeley.edu/~necula/Papers/tv_pldi00.pdf) and the bounded-checking discussion in [Alive2](https://web.ist.utl.pt/nuno.lopes/pubs/alive2-pldi21.pdf).

`courses/compiler-optimizer/lessons/08.md`:

```md
# Reduce a miscompilation

A small, stable wrong-result example is easier to explain and repair than a large failing program. Implement `reduce(program, input, transform)` so simplification preserves the same legal miscompilation.

Prerequisite: U07. The guided fault reuses memory incorrectly; the final investigation uses a different optimization.

## Define the interestingness predicate first

For each proposed source and input, regenerate the target using the supplied transform. Verify both programs, execute them from separate fresh heaps and require normal returns that differ in value or observable heap. A parser crash, a new bounds trap or an exhausted budget is not the required wrong-result witness.

Suppose irrelevant constant arithmetic is removed and the same source/target return discrepancy persists. That is useful reduction. Removing a definition used by the return and making the program invalid is not.

Commit item `08a`.

Keep three internal decisions: interesting, not interesting, and unresolved. You may skip an unresolved candidate and preserve the best known witness, but you cannot use it as evidence that no smaller witness exists.

The supplied `inspectWitness` helper reports those three states and preserves both executions. Start with a deliberately tiny fuel budget and observe UNRESOLVED, then restore enough fuel. This is an execution-budget experiment, not a new counterexample. An exception inside the faulty transform is also unresolved; it cannot certify a clean neighborhood.

## Reduce structure and input without losing identity

Try a finite family of legal changes, such as deleting unused total computations or simplifying an input value. A supplied Editor can enforce structural safety for eligible source changes; the interestingness check still has to rerun the faulty transform.

Accept only a strictly smaller candidate under a declared measure. Keep the signature, semantics and faulty pipeline fixed. Never manually edit only the target to preserve an apparent discrepancy. Recheck the final witness from fresh state.

Use the supplied lexicographic `measure`: block count, definitions/instructions, operand occurrences, heap objects, heap cells, then numeric-value complexity. Numeric complexity counts magnitude bits (plus a sign bit for a negative offset), not printed characters. Simplifying a witness word from 7 to 0 decreases it; shortening the program name or renaming an SSA value does not. Property order and whitespace also do not count. A smaller value cannot compensate for adding a block. Values can tie under this declared order; do not claim every possible simplification is ranked. Keep a trace of candidates, decisions and the best accepted witness. You design the candidate family and search order; the helper supplies execution and accounting.

A greedy reducer can produce a useful best-found result. Claim 1-minimality only after checking every permitted single-step reduction of the final candidate with no interesting or unresolved neighbor. That is still not a global minimum.

Pass that final candidate list to `assessNeighborhood`. Its NO_SMALLER_IN_LIST report establishes only the list it actually inspected. Explain why your list covers your declared family, or label the result best-found. A family containing only one convenient edit is weak evidence even when completely checked.

Commit item `08b`.

## Build the investigation artifact

```sh
node cli.mjs check 08 work --help-used none
node cli.mjs export work investigation.json
```

Return the reduced program, input and a short explanation of your reduction family and stopping condition. The checker demands a preserved normal-return discrepancy and actual simplification; it accepts different reduced forms.

The export preserves your first attempts and exact code. Use the rubric to explain the causal violation, not only the fact that two numbers differ. See [llvm-reduce](https://llvm.org/docs/CommandGuide/llvm-reduce.html) for the role of an explicit interestingness test in a production tool.

# Transfer: an unfamiliar optimization

A foreign pass rewrites a packet-window kernel. Investigate it without a worked diagnosis, then replace its faulty behavior while retaining useful optimization.

`courses/compiler-optimizer/pipeline.mjs`:

```mjs
// Supplied pass orchestration. Learners implement passes and the acceptance policy.
import {clone,digest} from './runtime.mjs';
import {reportFor} from './evidence.mjs';
export const passNames=['scalar','constants','memory','loops'];
export function supported(report) {
  return report.identitiesCurrent===true&&report.proof?.ok===true&&report.validation?.status==='EXHAUSTIVE_WITHIN_DOMAIN'&&report.validation.complete===true&&report.cost?.complete===true&&report.cost.sameWorkload===true&&report.cost.after<report.cost.before;
}
export async function runPipeline(learner,program,inputs,order,{contract={},policy=null,domainEvidence=null}={}) {
  if(!Array.isArray(order)||!order.length||order.length>8||order.some(name=>!passNames.includes(name)))throw new Error('pipeline.order: choose 1..8 supported passes');
  let current=clone(program),events=[];const stages=[];
  for(const [index,name]of order.entries()){
    const before=digest(current);
    try{
      if(typeof learner[name]!=='function')throw new Error(`Missing learner pass: ${name}`);
      const artifact=await learner[name](clone(current),clone(contract));
      const report=reportFor(current,artifact,inputs,{contract});report.domainEvidence=clone(domainEvidence);
      const decision=policy?await policy(clone(report)):{accept:supported(report),reason:'Supplied finite-evidence and unit-cost policy'};
      const adopted=decision?.accept===true&&supported(report);
      if(adopted){current=clone(artifact.program);events.push(...clone(artifact.events));}
      stages.push({index,name,before,selectedAfter:digest(current),adopted,decision,report});
    }catch(error){stages.push({index,name,before,selectedAfter:digest(current),adopted:false,error:error.message});}
  }
  const artifact={program:current,events},report=reportFor(program,artifact,inputs,{contract});report.domainEvidence=clone(domainEvidence);
  const adopted=stages.some(stage=>stage.adopted)&&supported(report);
  return {passed:adopted,adopted,order,stages,report,outputProgram:adopted?current:clone(program)};
}

```mjs
// Pure practice-state contract shared by the offline reader and Node checks.
export function emptyPractice(revision){return {format:'optimizer-practice/1',revision,attempts:[]};}
export function inspectPractice(value,bank,revision){
  if(!value||value.format!=='optimizer-practice/1'||value.revision!==revision||!Array.isArray(value.attempts)||value.attempts.length>200)throw new Error('Use a practice export from this exact reader revision (at most 200 attempts).');
  const ids=new Set();
  for(const attempt of value.attempts){
    const item=bank.items.find(item=>item.id===attempt.item);
    if(!item||typeof attempt.id!=='string'||ids.has(attempt.id)||typeof attempt.at!=='string'||!Number.isFinite(Date.parse(attempt.at))||typeof attempt.helpUsed!=='string'||attempt.helpUsed.length>500||!Object.hasOwn(item.choices,attempt.choice)||JSON.stringify(attempt.question)!==JSON.stringify({prompt:item.prompt,choices:item.choices}))throw new Error('Malformed practice attempt. Your current history remains intact.');
    ids.add(attempt.id);
  }
  if(JSON.stringify(value).length>1024*1024)throw new Error('Practice export exceeds the 1 MiB profile.');
  return structuredClone(value);
}
export function commitPractice(state,bank,itemID,choice,helpUsed,{id,at}){
  inspectPractice(state,bank,state.revision);
  const item=bank.items.find(item=>item.id===itemID);if(!item||!Object.hasOwn(item.choices,choice))throw new Error('Choose an answer before committing.');
  if(typeof helpUsed!=='string'||helpUsed.length>500)throw new Error('Keep the help note at 500 characters or fewer.');
  const next=structuredClone(state);next.attempts.push({id,at,item:itemID,question:{prompt:item.prompt,choices:structuredClone(item.choices)},choice,helpUsed:helpUsed.trim()||'not declared'});
  return inspectPractice(next,bank,state.revision);
}
export function mergePractice(current,incoming,bank){
  inspectPractice(current,bank,current.revision);inspectPractice(incoming,bank,current.revision);
  const next=structuredClone(current),known=new Map(next.attempts.map(a=>[a.id,a]));
  for(const attempt of incoming.attempts){if(known.has(attempt.id)){if(JSON.stringify(known.get(attempt.id))!==JSON.stringify(attempt))throw new Error('Conflicting attempt ID; current history remains intact.');}else{next.attempts.push(structuredClone(attempt));known.set(attempt.id,attempt);}}
  return inspectPractice(next,bank,current.revision);
}
export function practiceFeedback(bank,attempt){const item=bank.items.find(item=>item.id===attempt.item);if(!item)throw new Error('Unknown item.');return {passed:attempt.choice===item.correct,correct:item.correct,reason:item.why,next:item.next};}

`courses/compiler-optimizer/runtime.mjs`:

```mjs
// Supplied Kernel IR v1 runtime. This is course infrastructure, not learner work.
import { createHash } from 'node:crypto';

export const VERSION = 'kernel-ir/1';
export const clone = value => structuredClone(value);
export const wordTypes = new Set(['i8', 'i32']);
export const pureOps = new Set(['const', 'add', 'sub', 'mul', 'and', 'or', 'xor', 'eq', 'ne', 'ult', 'ule', 'slt', 'sle', 'ptradd']);
const binary = new Set(['add', 'sub', 'mul', 'and', 'or', 'xor']);
const compareOps = new Set(['eq', 'ne', 'ult', 'ule', 'slt', 'sle']);
const types = new Set(['i8', 'i32', 'bool', 'ptr<i8>', 'ptr<i32>']);
const identifier = /^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_.-]{0,63}$/;
const validIdentifier = value => typeof value === 'string' && identifier.test(value);
const record = value => value !== null && typeof value === 'object' && !Array.isArray(value);
const integer = /^(0|[1-9][0-9]*)$/;
const signedInteger = /^(0|-?[1-9][0-9]*)$/;
const width = type => type === 'i8' ? 8 : 32;
export const digest = value => createHash('sha256').update(canonical(value)).digest('hex');
export function canonical(value) {
  if (Array.isArray(value)) return `[${value.map(canonical).join(',')}]`;
  if (value && typeof value === 'object') return `{${Object.keys(value).sort().map(k => `${JSON.stringify(k)}:${canonical(value[k])}`).join(',')}}`;
  return JSON.stringify(value);
}
export function literal(type, value) {
  if (type === 'bool' && typeof value === 'boolean') return value;
  if (!wordTypes.has(type) || typeof value !== 'string' || value.length > 10 || !integer.test(value)) throw new Error('literal.canonical_type');
  const number = BigInt(value);
  if (number >= 1n << BigInt(width(type))) throw new Error('literal.range');
  return number;
}
export function valueJSON(value) { return typeof value === 'bigint' ? value.toString() : clone(value); }
export function evaluate(op, type, values, operandType = type) {
  const [a, b] = values;
  if (op === 'ptradd') return { object: a.object, offset: (BigInt(a.offset) + BigInt.asIntN(32, b)).toString() };
  if (op === 'eq') return a === b;
  if (op === 'ne') return a !== b;
  if (op === 'ult') return a < b;
  if (op === 'ule') return a <= b;
  if (op === 'slt') return BigInt.asIntN(width(operandType), a) < BigInt.asIntN(width(operandType), b);
  if (op === 'sle') return BigInt.asIntN(width(operandType), a) <= BigInt.asIntN(width(operandType), b);
  let answer;
  if (op === 'add') answer = a + b;
  if (op === 'sub') answer = a - b;
  if (op === 'mul') answer = a * b;
  if (op === 'and') answer = a & b;
  if (op === 'or') answer = a | b;
  if (op === 'xor') answer = a ^ b;
  if (answer === undefined) throw new Error(`opcode.unsupported:${op}`);
  return BigInt.asUintN(width(type), answer);
}
export function cfg(program) {
  const successors = Object.fromEntries(program.blocks.map(block => [block.id,
    block.term.op === 'br' ? [block.term.target] : block.term.op === 'cbr' ? [...new Set([block.term.yes, block.term.no])] : []]));
  const predecessors = Object.fromEntries(program.blocks.map(block => [block.id, []]));
  for (const [from, targets] of Object.entries(successors)) for (const target of targets) {
    if (!predecessors[target]) throw new Error(`cfg.missing_block:${target}`);
    predecessors[target].push(from);
  }
  return { successors, predecessors };
}
function reachable(graph, entry, excluded = null) {
  const seen = new Set(); const queue = [entry];
  while (queue.length) {
    const id = queue.pop();
    if (id === excluded || seen.has(id)) continue;
    seen.add(id); queue.push(...(graph.successors[id] ?? []));
  }
  return seen;
}
// Independent checker: dominance by graph reachability with a node removed.
// Learner analysis is assessed separately and is never trusted by this verifier.
export function dominates(program, a, b) {
  if (a === b) return true;
  return !reachable(cfg(program), program.entry, a).has(b);
}
export function definitions(program) {
  const map = new Map(program.params.map(p => [p.id, { ...p, block: null, index: -2 }]));
  for (const block of program.blocks) {
    for (const phi of block.phis) map.set(phi.id, { ...phi, op: 'phi', block: block.id, index: -1 });
    block.instructions.forEach((i, index) => { if (i.id) map.set(i.id, { ...i, block: block.id, index }); });
  }
  return map;
}
export function uses(program) {
  const result = [];
  for (const block of program.blocks) {
    for (const phi of block.phis) for (const [edge, id] of Object.entries(phi.incoming)) result.push({ id, block: edge, index: Infinity, phi: phi.id });
    block.instructions.forEach((instruction, index) => (instruction.args ?? []).forEach(id => result.push({ id, block: block.id, index })));
    if (block.term.cond) result.push({ id: block.term.cond, block: block.id, index: Infinity });
    if (block.term.value) result.push({ id: block.term.value, block: block.id, index: Infinity });
  }
  return result;
}
export function verify(program) {
  const errors = [];
  const fail = message => errors.push(message);
  try {
    const keys = (object, allowed) => { if (!object || Array.isArray(object) || Object.keys(object).some(k => !allowed.includes(k)) || allowed.some(k => !Object.hasOwn(object,k))) throw new Error('schema.fields'); };
    keys(program,['version','name','params','returns','entry','blocks']);
    if (program.version !== 1 || !validIdentifier(program.name) || !Array.isArray(program.params) || !Array.isArray(program.blocks)) throw new Error('program.shape');
    if (!['i8', 'i32', 'bool'].includes(program.returns)) fail('return.type');
    if (program.blocks.length < 1 || program.blocks.length > 64) throw new Error('program.block_limit');
    const blockIDs = program.blocks.map(b => b.id);
    if (new Set(blockIDs).size !== blockIDs.length || blockIDs.some(id => !validIdentifier(id))) throw new Error('block.duplicate_or_invalid');
    if (!blockIDs.includes(program.entry)) throw new Error('entry.missing');
    const names = new Set();
    const define = item => {
      if (!validIdentifier(item.id) || names.has(item.id) || !types.has(item.type)) throw new Error(`definition.invalid:${item.id}`);
      names.add(item.id);
    };
    program.params.forEach(p=>{keys(p,['id','type']);define(p);});
    for (const block of program.blocks) {
      keys(block,['id','phis','instructions','term']);
      if (!Array.isArray(block.phis) || !Array.isArray(block.instructions)) throw new Error('block.shape');
      block.phis.forEach(p=>{keys(p,['id','type','incoming']);define(p);});
      for (const i of block.instructions) {
        if (!pureOps.has(i.op) && !['load', 'store', 'emit'].includes(i.op)) throw new Error(`opcode.unsupported:${i.op}`);
        if (i.op === 'store' || i.op === 'emit') {
          keys(i,['op','args']);
          if (i.id !== undefined || i.type !== undefined) fail('effect.has_result');
          continue;
        }
        keys(i,i.op==='const'?['id','op','type','value']:['id','op','type','args']);
        define(i);
        if (i.op === 'const') literal(i.type, i.value);
      }
      const term = block.term;
      if (!term || !['br', 'cbr', 'ret', 'trap'].includes(term.op)) throw new Error('terminator.invalid');
      keys(term,term.op==='br'?['op','target']:term.op==='cbr'?['op','cond','yes','no']:term.op==='ret'?['op','value']:['op','code']);
      if (term.op === 'cbr' && term.yes === term.no) fail('cfg.duplicate_successor_normalize_first');
      if (term.op === 'trap' && (!validIdentifier(term.code) || term.code === 'bounds')) fail('trap.invalid_code');
    }
    if (names.size > 512) fail('program.definition_limit');
    const graph = cfg(program); const defs = definitions(program);
    if (graph.predecessors[program.entry].length || program.blocks.find(b => b.id === program.entry).phis.length) fail('entry.has_predecessor_or_phi');
    if (reachable(graph, program.entry).size !== program.blocks.length) fail('cfg.unreachable_block');
    const getType = id => { if (!defs.has(id)) throw new Error(`use.undefined:${id}`); return defs.get(id).type; };
    for (const block of program.blocks) {
      for (const phi of block.phis) {
        if (canonical(Object.keys(phi.incoming).sort()) !== canonical([...graph.predecessors[block.id]].sort())) fail(`phi.edges:${phi.id}`);
        for (const value of Object.values(phi.incoming)) if (getType(value) !== phi.type) fail(`phi.type:${phi.id}`);
      }
      for (const i of block.instructions) {
        const ts = (i.args ?? []).map(getType);
        if (i.op === 'const' && (i.args ?? []).length) fail('const.arity');
        if (binary.has(i.op) && (ts.length !== 2 || !wordTypes.has(i.type) || ts.some(t => t !== i.type))) fail(`binary.type:${i.id}`);
        if (compareOps.has(i.op) && (ts.length !== 2 || i.type !== 'bool' || ts[0] !== ts[1] || !wordTypes.has(ts[0]))) fail(`compare.type:${i.id}`);
        if (i.op === 'ptradd' && (ts.length !== 2 || ts[0] !== i.type || !i.type.startsWith('ptr<') || ts[1] !== 'i32')) fail(`ptradd.type:${i.id}`);
        if (i.op === 'load' && (ts.length !== 1 || ts[0] !== `ptr<${i.type}>` || !wordTypes.has(i.type))) fail(`load.type:${i.id}`);
        if (i.op === 'store' && (ts.length !== 2 || ts[0] !== `ptr<${ts[1]}>` || !wordTypes.has(ts[1]))) fail('store.type');
        if (i.op === 'emit' && (ts.length !== 1 || !['i8', 'i32', 'bool'].includes(ts[0]))) fail('emit.type');
      }
      if (block.term.op === 'cbr' && getType(block.term.cond) !== 'bool') fail('branch.requires_bool');
      if (block.term.op === 'ret' && getType(block.term.value) !== program.returns) fail('return.mismatch');
    }
    for (const use of uses(program)) {
      const def = defs.get(use.id);
      if (!def) { fail(`use.undefined:${use.id}`); continue; }
      if (def.block === null) continue;
      if (!dominates(program, def.block, use.block) || (def.block === use.block && def.index >= use.index)) fail(`ssa.non_dominating_use:${use.id}:${use.block}`);
    }
  } catch (error) { fail(error.message); }
  return { ok: errors.length === 0, errors };
}
export function validateContract(program,contract={}) {
  if(!record(contract)||Object.keys(contract).some(k=>!['offsets','minLengths','distinct'].includes(k)))throw new Error('contract.shape');
  for(const key of ['offsets','minLengths'])if(Object.hasOwn(contract,key)&&!record(contract[key]))throw new Error(`contract.${key}_shape`);
  const pointerIDs=new Set(program.params.filter(p=>p.type.startsWith('ptr<')).map(p=>p.id));
  for(const [id,value] of Object.entries(contract.offsets??{}))if(!pointerIDs.has(id)||typeof value!=='string'||value.length>1000||!signedInteger.test(value))throw new Error('contract.offset_shape');
  for(const [id,value] of Object.entries(contract.minLengths??{}))if(!pointerIDs.has(id)||!Number.isSafeInteger(value)||value<0||value>4096)throw new Error('contract.length_shape');
  if(contract.distinct!==undefined&&!Array.isArray(contract.distinct))throw new Error('contract.distinct_shape');
  for(const pair of contract.distinct??[])if(!Array.isArray(pair)||pair.length!==2||pair[0]===pair[1]||pair.some(id=>!pointerIDs.has(id)))throw new Error('contract.distinct_shape');
  return true;
}
export function validateInput(program, input, contract = {}) {
  if (!record(input) || !record(input.args) || !record(input.heap)) throw new Error('input.shape');
  if(Object.keys(input).some(k=>!['args','heap'].includes(k)))throw new Error('input.fields');
  if (canonical(Object.keys(input.args).sort()) !== canonical(program.params.map(p => p.id).sort())) throw new Error('input.parameters');
  if (Object.keys(input.heap).length > 64) throw new Error('input.object_limit');
  let cells = 0;
  for (const [id, object] of Object.entries(input.heap)) {
    if(!record(object)||Object.keys(object).some(k=>!['type','cells'].includes(k)))throw new Error('heap.fields');
    if (!validIdentifier(id) || !wordTypes.has(object.type) || !Array.isArray(object.cells)) throw new Error('heap.shape');
    object.cells.forEach(value => literal(object.type, value)); cells += object.cells.length;
  }
  if (cells > 4096) throw new Error('heap.cell_limit');
  const values = new Map();
  for (const p of program.params) {
    const value = input.args[p.id];
    if (!p.type.startsWith('ptr<')) { values.set(p.id, literal(p.type, value)); continue; }
    if (!record(value) || Object.keys(value).some(k=>!['object','offset'].includes(k)) || !validIdentifier(value.object) || typeof value.offset !== 'string' || !signedInteger.test(value.offset) || value.offset.length > 1000) throw new Error('pointer.shape');
    if (!Object.hasOwn(input.heap, value.object) || p.type !== `ptr<${input.heap[value.object].type}>`) throw new Error('pointer.object_type');
    values.set(p.id, clone(value));
  }
  validateContract(program,contract);
  for (const [id, offset] of Object.entries(contract.offsets ?? {})) if (values.get(id)?.offset !== offset) throw new Error('contract.offset');
  for (const [id, count] of Object.entries(contract.minLengths ?? {})) if (!values.get(id)?.object || input.heap[values.get(id).object].cells.length < count) throw new Error('contract.length');
  for (const [a, b] of contract.distinct ?? []) if (!values.get(a)?.object || !values.get(b)?.object || values.get(a).object === values.get(b).object) throw new Error('contract.distinct');
  return values;
}
export function run(program, input, { fuel = 100000, contract = {} } = {}) {
  const validity = verify(program);
  if (!validity.ok) return { kind: 'invalid', errors: validity.errors };
  let env;
  try { env = validateInput(program, input, contract); } catch (e) { return { kind: 'invalid', errors: [e.message] }; }
  if (!Number.isSafeInteger(fuel) || fuel < 0 || fuel > 1000000) return { kind: 'invalid', errors: ['fuel.invalid'] };
  const heap = clone(input.heap), events = [], counts = {};
  const defs = definitions(program), blocks = new Map(program.blocks.map(b => [b.id, b]));
  let current = program.entry, previous = null, steps = 0;
  const tick = op => { if (steps >= fuel) return false; steps++; counts[op] = (counts[op] ?? 0) + 1; return true; };
  const finish = extra => ({ ...extra, heap, events, steps, counts });
  const access = pointer => {
    const object = heap[pointer.object]; const index = BigInt(pointer.offset);
    if (index < 0n || index >= BigInt(object.cells.length)) return null;
    return { object, index: Number(index) };
  };
  while (true) {
    const block = blocks.get(current);
    if (block.phis.length) {
      if (!tick('phi_group')) return finish({ kind: 'unknown', reason: 'fuel' });
      const incoming = block.phis.map(phi => [phi.id, env.get(phi.incoming[previous])]);
      for (const [id, value] of incoming) env.set(id, value);
      counts.phi_values = (counts.phi_values ?? 0) + incoming.length;
    }
    for (const i of block.instructions) {
      if (!tick(i.op)) return finish({ kind: 'unknown', reason: 'fuel' });
      const args = (i.args ?? []).map(id => env.get(id));
      if (i.op === 'const') { env.set(i.id, literal(i.type, i.value)); continue; }
      if (i.op === 'emit') {
        if (events.length >= 4096) return finish({ kind: 'unknown', reason: 'event_limit' });
        events.push({ type: defs.get(i.args[0]).type, value: valueJSON(args[0]) }); continue;
      }
      if (i.op === 'load' || i.op === 'store') {
        const location = access(args[0]);
        if (!location) return finish({ kind: 'trap', code: 'bounds' });
        if (i.op === 'load') env.set(i.id, literal(i.type, location.object.cells[location.index]));
        if (i.op === 'store') location.object.cells[location.index] = valueJSON(args[1]);
        continue;
      }
      env.set(i.id, evaluate(i.op, i.type, args, defs.get(i.args[0]).type));
    }
    const t = block.term;
    if (!tick(t.op)) return finish({ kind: 'unknown', reason: 'fuel' });
    if (t.op === 'ret') return finish({ kind: 'return', type: program.returns, value: valueJSON(env.get(t.value)) });
    if (t.op === 'trap') return finish({ kind: 'trap', code: t.code });
    previous = current; current = t.op === 'br' ? t.target : env.get(t.cond) ? t.yes : t.no;
  }
}
export function observation(result) {
  if (result.kind === 'return') return { kind: result.kind, type: result.type, value: result.value, heap: result.heap, events: result.events };
  if (result.kind === 'trap') return { kind: result.kind, code: result.code, heap: result.heap, events: result.events };
  return null;
}
export function equivalent(a, b) { const x = observation(a), y = observation(b); return x !== null && y !== null && canonical(x) === canonical(y); }
export function cost(result) { return Object.entries(result.counts ?? {}).reduce((sum, [op, n]) => sum + (op === 'phi_group' ? 0 : n), 0); }

import { readFile, writeFile } from 'node:fs/promises';
import { pathToFileURL } from 'node:url';
import { grade } from './checks.mjs';
import { reportFor } from './evidence.mjs';
import { clone } from './runtime.mjs';
import { runPipeline } from './pipeline.mjs';
const [requestPath,resultPath]=process.argv.slice(2);
try {
  const request=JSON.parse(await readFile(requestPath,'utf8'));
  const learner=await import(pathToFileURL(request.modulePath).href);
  if(request.useLearnerPolicy&&typeof learner.decide!=='function')throw new Error('Missing learner evidence policy: decide(report)');
  let result;
  if(request.action==='check'){
    const project=request.projectPath?await import(pathToFileURL(request.projectPath).href):null;
    result=await grade(request.unit,learner,project);
  } else if(request.action==='pipeline'){
    const {program,inputs,contract={},evidence=null}=request.job;
    result=await runPipeline(learner,program,inputs,request.passes,{contract,domainEvidence:evidence,policy:request.useLearnerPolicy?learner.decide:null});
  } else {
    const {program,inputs,contract={}}=request.job;
    if(!['scalar','constants','memory','loops'].includes(request.pass))throw new Error('Unknown pass');
    const artifact=await learner[request.pass](clone(program),clone(contract));
    const report=reportFor(program,artifact,inputs,{contract});
    report.domainEvidence=request.job.evidence??null;
    const decision=request.useLearnerPolicy?await learner.decide(clone(report)):{accept:report.proof.ok&&report.validation.status==='EXHAUSTIVE_WITHIN_DOMAIN'&&report.cost.complete&&report.cost.after<report.cost.before,reason:'Supplied finite-evidence and unit-cost policy'};
    // Product safety checks do not trust a learner policy to override proof/behavior.
    const adopt=decision?.accept===true&&report.proof.ok&&report.validation.status==='EXHAUSTIVE_WITHIN_DOMAIN'&&report.cost.complete&&report.cost.sameWorkload&&report.cost.after<report.cost.before;
    result={passed:adopt,decision,adopted:adopt,report,outputProgram:adopt?artifact.program:program};
  }
  await writeFile(resultPath,JSON.stringify(result,null,2),'utf8');
} catch(error){await writeFile(resultPath,JSON.stringify({passed:false,error:error.message},null,2),'utf8');process.exitCode=1;}

`courses/compiler-optimizer/zip.mjs`:

```mjs
// Small original ZIP-STORED writer for reproducible, dependency-free packages.
import { writeFile } from 'node:fs/promises';
function crc32(bytes){let crc=0xffffffff;for(const byte of bytes){crc^=byte;for(let bit=0;bit<8;bit++)crc=(crc>>>1)^((crc&1)?0xedb88320:0);}return (crc^0xffffffff)>>>0;}
export async function writeZip(path,entries){
  const locals=[],centrals=[];let offset=0;
  for(const [name,data] of entries){
    if(name.startsWith('/')||name.split('/').some(x=>x==='..'||x==='')||name.includes('\\'))throw new Error('Invalid ZIP entry');
    const bytes=Buffer.isBuffer(data)?data:Buffer.from(data),filename=Buffer.from(name),crc=crc32(bytes);
    const local=Buffer.alloc(30);local.writeUInt32LE(0x04034b50,0);local.writeUInt16LE(20,4);local.writeUInt16LE(0x800,6);local.writeUInt16LE(33,12);local.writeUInt32LE(crc,14);local.writeUInt32LE(bytes.length,18);local.writeUInt32LE(bytes.length,22);local.writeUInt16LE(filename.length,26);
    locals.push(local,filename,bytes);
    const central=Buffer.alloc(46);central.writeUInt32LE(0x02014b50,0);central.writeUInt16LE(20,4);central.writeUInt16LE(20,6);central.writeUInt16LE(0x800,8);central.writeUInt16LE(33,14);central.writeUInt32LE(crc,16);central.writeUInt32LE(bytes.length,20);central.writeUInt32LE(bytes.length,24);central.writeUInt16LE(filename.length,28);central.writeUInt32LE(offset,42);
    centrals.push(central,filename);offset+=local.length+filename.length+bytes.length;
  }
  const centralSize=centrals.reduce((n,b)=>n+b.length,0),end=Buffer.alloc(22);end.writeUInt32LE(0x06054b50,0);end.writeUInt16LE(entries.length,8);end.writeUInt16LE(entries.length,10);end.writeUInt32LE(centralSize,12);end.writeUInt32LE(offset,16);
  await writeFile(path,Buffer.concat([...locals,...centrals,end]),{flag:'wx'});
}

`courses/firmware-forensics/README.md`:

```md
# Firmware Forensics — learner package

This private course uses original inert EDUFW1 files. Nothing is flashed, booted,
executed as firmware or sent to a service. Python 3.10+ and Node 22+ must already
be installed. Tested on macOS arm64 with Python 3.14.6 and Node 26.5.1.

Unpack into a new directory. The **package root** contains `work.py`,
`check_core.py`, `lab/` and `trust/`. Run this README's commands from that root:

```sh
python3 work.py 001-first
python3 check_core.py --stage parser attempts/001-first > attempts/001-first/core-first.json
node trust/check.mjs attempts/001-first/trust.mjs > attempts/001-first/trust-first.json

```

Use `--stage parser` through unit 02. It runs the scaffold and parser, inventory
and dependency checks without the later analysis or investigation checks. After
you write your first investigation in unit 05, run the complete check on your
latest attempt with a new output filename, for example:

```sh
python3 check_core.py --stage full attempts/005-analysis > attempts/005-analysis/core-full.json
```

Omitting `--stage` still runs the complete check for older saved commands.

The TODO starters deliberately fail. Keep those first source files and outputs.

Create another numbered attempt before repairing submitted code. Record help in
help.json. Use a fresh output filename every run; shell redirection can overwrite.
All code executes locally as you; do not run unknown submissions from other people.

Read the seven-unit reader in `reader/`. To open it offline, run
`python3 -m http.server 8118 --bind 127.0.0.1` here and open `/reader/` locally.
The course is complete with sound off. JavaScript records optional reasoning
checks in browser storage; the reading and all terminal labs are ordinary files.
Export browser reasoning separately from your terminal attempt folders.

about an incomplete course, Linux-only testing and pending signatures/final
capstone describe that earlier component. The Mac testing statement above applies
to this integrated package with its root-level wrappers; it does not qualify every
low-level command in the historical lab.

Read `lab/README.md`, `lab/FORMAT.md` and `lab/lessons/` for core contracts. For the
integrated course, keep using `work.py` and `check_core.py` from the package root.
If you follow the embedded README's standalone examples, first run `cd lab`; its
relative paths, including `attempts/`, are then inside `lab/`. Run `cd ..` to return
to the package root. Those `lab/attempts/` records are separate from the root
`attempts/` records; do not mix the two workflows.

This package adds the signature exercise in `trust/README.md` and the final
investigation in `capstone.md`.
Core origin is always unverified. The signature extension uses public RFC test
keys and calls only the classroom manifest relationship verified. It authenticates
no vendor and authorizes no hardware use. A signature-gate pass does not override
the Python configuration policy; both must appear in your final report.

The extractor rejects symlinked destinations. `check_core.py` chooses a canonical
temporary test directory on macOS while leaving that rule unchanged. For manual
extraction use a fresh directory under your home directory.

Expected completed code checks: scaffold 5, parser 49, analysis 31, unfamiliar
core integration 6, trust 154, plus two RFC vectors and four negative controls.
Passing these open cases is limited behavioral evidence. Review your capstone explanation and first-attempt history with the rubric;
optional help can come from your own LLM account. Human learning outcomes remain

# Sources, provenance and limits

  Ed25519 tests 1 and 2 supply public test material for known-answer checks. The

  checked 2026-10-27: built-in Ed25519 verification, `verify(null, bytes, key, signature)`.

  feedback-01/02/07, assessment-02/09/13, accessibility-01/03 and evaluation-01/03.

# Final investigation: a logger release changes

You receive two original inert captures (`trust/fixtures/capstone-a.efw` and
`capstone-b.efw`), their manifests and signatures, a partial capture, the classroom
public key and `capstone-policy.json`. The names and physical layout differ from
the guided case. Do not read author solutions before submitting your first report.

Create a new attempt using `python3 work.py 007-capstone --from-attempt attempts/006-investigation`.
Adjust the previous attempt name to your actual last revision. Submit `findings.md`
with the following evidence and keep all commands and JSON outputs alongside it.

1. Before inspection, predict whether a higher release number guarantees admission.
2. Use your parser to inventory both captures. Show one header/table/range calculation.
   Map all dependencies and explain a valid dependency-first ordering.
3. Use your analysis to classify additions, removals, content changes and metadata
   changes by component identity. Cite exact fields and distinguish physical order.
4. Verify both raw manifest signatures and capture bindings using your trust policy.
   Name which key was pinned, who published its test seed, and the limit of that trust.
5. Inspect local configuration policy with the Python CLI. Combine that evidence
   with the signature/binding/release results into a reasoned **hold or admit for
   further classroom review**. A pass in the signature command is only one condition.
6. Determine what can be concluded from the partial capture. Preserve its failure;
   do not repair the file to manufacture a complete inventory.
7. Copy capstone-policy.json into your attempt and change minimum_release from
   20 to 22. Predict the result, then point the Python command's --policy option
   at that copy and change the signature command's numeric floor from 20 to 22.
   The commands receive the floor separately. Keep both original outputs and
   both revised outputs under different filenames; compare release-policy fields
   while preserving the signature and capture-binding observations.
8. Write one competing explanation for a change and one observation that would
   distinguish it. State remaining unknowns: author intent, vendor identity,
   actual execution, hardware state and production safety.

An example invocation supplies paths, not an answer:

cd ..
node trust/verify.mjs trust/fixtures/capstone-b.efw trust/fixtures/capstone-b.json trust/fixtures/capstone-b.sig trust/fixtures/lab-public.hex 20 attempts/007-capstone/trust.mjs

`courses/firmware-forensics/check_core.py`:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Run the frozen core checks with macOS's canonical temporary directory."""
import argparse,json,os,subprocess,sys,tempfile
from pathlib import Path
ROOT=Path(__file__).resolve().parent
def main():
    p=argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__);p.add_argument('attempt',type=Path);p.add_argument('--stage',choices=('parser','full'),default='full',help='parser runs scaffold and parser/map checks; full adds analysis and investigation (default)');a=p.parse_args()
    attempt=a.attempt.resolve(strict=True)
    env=dict(os.environ,TMPDIR=str(Path(tempfile.gettempdir()).resolve()))
    commands=[['-m','unittest','discover','-s','checks','-v'],
      ['checks/check_parser.py','--parser',str(attempt/'parser.py')]]
    if a.stage=='full':
        commands.extend([
          ['checks/check_submission.py','--parser',str(attempt/'parser.py'),'--analysis',str(attempt/'analysis.py')],
          ['checks/check_investigation.py','--parser',str(attempt/'parser.py'),'--analysis',str(attempt/'analysis.py')]])
    results=[]
    for command in commands:
        r=subprocess.run([sys.executable,*command],cwd=ROOT/'lab',env=env,capture_output=True,text=True)
        results.append({'command':[sys.executable,*command],'exit':r.returncode,'stdout':r.stdout,'stderr':r.stderr})
    print(json.dumps({'schema':1,'status':'pass' if all(r['exit']==0 for r in results) else 'fail','TMPDIR':env['TMPDIR'],'results':results},indent=2))
    return 0 if all(r['exit']==0 for r in results) else 1
if __name__=='__main__':sys.exit(main())

```

`courses/firmware-forensics/lab/FORMAT.md`:

```md
# EDUFW1 v1 format — original teaching format

All integer fields are unsigned little-endian. Offsets are absolute from byte 0.
Strings are ASCII, with zero padding; there may be no nonzero bytes after the
first NUL. No path, compression, code execution or embedded archive semantics.
Limits: file ≤ 1 MiB, 1–32 components, manifest/policy JSON ≤ 128 KiB.

## Header: 20 bytes (`<8sHHII`)

| Offset | Length | Field | Rule |
|---|---:|---|---|
| 0 | 8 | magic | `45 44 55 46 57 31 00 00` (`EDUFW1\0\0`) |
| 8 | 2 | format version | exactly 1 |
| 10 | 2 | component count | 1..32 |
| 12 | 4 | table offset | exactly 20 |
| 16 | 4 | total size | exactly the actual file length |

## Each table entry: 80 bytes (`<24s12sIII32s`)

| Relative offset | Length | Field | Rule |
|---|---:|---|---|
| 0 | 24 | name | unique `[a-z][a-z0-9_-]{0,23}` |
| 24 | 12 | kind | `[a-z][a-z0-9_-]{0,11}` |
| 36 | 4 | payload offset | at or after end of complete table |
| 40 | 4 | payload size | positive; range wholly inside file |
| 44 | 4 | component version | positive uint32 |
| 48 | 32 | declared SHA-256 | raw digest of payload bytes |

Payload ranges must cover every byte after the table exactly once: no overlap,
gaps or trailing unclaimed bytes. Table order and physical payload order need
not be alphabetical. A declared hash mismatch is recorded separately from format
validity, because a forensic inventory should still identify damaged components.

A parser must bound the **table** before iterating entries and bound each payload
before slicing it. Integer arithmetic in Python does not wrap, but a size check
still matters: Python slices silently truncate out-of-range requests. We compare
`size <= len(data) - offset` after proving the offset is in range.

## JSON manifest and policy

See `fixtures/release-1.json` and `fixtures/policy.json` for complete examples.
Unknown/missing fields, duplicate JSON keys, non-finite numbers, booleans where
integers are required, invalid hashes, duplicate component names/dependencies,
and oversized input are rejected. A missing dependency or cycle is a manifest
consistency finding rather than an accidental recursion error.

The manifest declares format, release number, whole-container digest, and an
exact component inventory (name, kind, version, payload digest, `requires`). All
referenced dependencies must exist and the declaration must be acyclic. The
reported dependency-first order is **not evidence of actual execution**.

Policy has schema 1, a positive `minimum_release`, a list of required component
names and scalar `required_config` values. The `config` component must have kind
`config`; its bytes must parse as a JSON object. Required values are compared
with both their types and values (`true` is not numeric `1`). Extra configuration
fields are allowed: this policy is a required-value policy, not a closed schema.
A release below the floor is a local policy finding, not proof of cryptographic
anti-rollback enforcement.

The provided manifest, fixture index and policy are local teaching inputs. An
attacker who can replace a payload **and** its hashes can make them consistent.
None is signed; no trusted key, certificate, digest acquisition channel or vendor
identity is established by this slice.

```

`courses/firmware-forensics/lab/README.md`:

```md
# Firmware Evidence Lab — learner-parser milestone 0.3.1

**Build the parser → inventory components → map dependencies → investigate changes.**

This finite milestone extends the accepted 0.2 working slice. You now implement
three core functions in `parser.py` and two analysis functions in `analysis.py`.
The selected parser really drives the CLI and investigation; there is no supplied
parser fallback and no reference solution inside this learner package.

This is **not the complete seven-milestone course**. EDUFW1 is our original inert
teaching format: **not UEFI, not bootable, not production firmware**. All payloads
are descriptions or JSON, never executed. No flashing, malware, persistence,
evasion, credentials, private keys, downloads or external services are involved.

## Requirements and boundaries

- Python 3.10+ language features, standard library, terminal and writable directory.
  No pip packages or elevated privileges. Tested only on Linux x86-64/Python
  3.12.14; other Python versions, macOS, Windows and BSD are unverified.
- After receiving this package and an existing interpreter, every mandatory step
  is local/offline. The example commands use `python3`.
- Run from the unpacked folder containing `fwlab.py`.
- Selected Python submissions execute as ordinary local code. This is **not a
  sandbox** for running somebody else's untrusted submission.
- Hashes check consistency, **not authenticated origin**. Signatures, certificates,
  trusted roots and measured-boot correlation remain pending course stages.

## 1. Preserve a first attempt

```sh
python3 -m unittest discover -s checks -v
python3 tools/attempt.py 001-first
python3 checks/check_parser.py --parser attempts/001-first/parser.py > attempts/001-first/parser-check.json
```

The supplied scaffold suite should pass **5 tests**. The parser checker should
exit **1** because all three starter functions are TODOs. Keep that first failure.
The attempt contains both sources, a help log and initial source hashes.

```sh
python3 tools/attempt.py 002-parser --from-file attempts/001-first/analysis.py --parser-from attempts/001-first/parser.py
```

Read [Build a bounded parser and component map](lessons/00-build-parser-and-map.md)
and [FORMAT.md](FORMAT.md). Implement in `attempts/002-parser/parser.py`:

1. `parse_container(data)` — validate byte layout; return the supplied data classes.
2. `component_inventory(container)` — compute evidence for every component.
3. `map_dependencies(components)` — find missing nodes/cycles and a valid ordering.

The starter docstrings define exact return values and error behavior. Checks are
open learning aids, not secret exams. Do not change tests or fixture bytes to get
a pass. Each failed case names the contract that needs work.

```sh
python3 checks/check_parser.py --parser attempts/002-parser/parser.py > attempts/002-parser/parser-check.json
```

Success is exit **0**, `status: pass`, **49/49**. The checker tests independently
permuted table/payload layouts, unfamiliar names, size/count boundaries, malformed
ranges, safe labels, mismatched hashes, missing dependencies and cycles. It accepts
**any valid dependency-first order**, not one memorized reference ordering.

## 2. Run your parser on actual files

```sh
python3 fwlab.py inspect fixtures/release-1.efw --manifest fixtures/release-1.json --policy fixtures/policy.json --parser attempts/002-parser/parser.py > attempts/002-parser/intake.json
python3 fwlab.py extract fixtures/release-1.efw extracted-release-1 --parser attempts/002-parser/parser.py
```

The inventory and dependency graph come from **your selected source**. Inspect
records its SHA-256. Extraction writes data only into a new directory, rejecting
existing output, symlinked ancestors, unsafe/duplicate names and mismatched
component hashes. It retains a second name check even if your parser is wrong.
Read the text/JSON files; do not execute them or treat extraction as verification
of origin. Use another unused destination name on repeat runs.

`inspect` exits 0 when supplied checks find no inconsistency, **3** for
hash/manifest/local-policy findings, and **2** for malformed data or an operation
error. Exit 0 does **not** mean authenticated, approved, benign or safe to flash.
Absent manifest/policy checks are not positive evidence. Omitting `--parser` fails
rather than silently using a reference.

## 3. Add the change investigation

```sh
python3 tools/attempt.py 003-analysis --from-file attempts/002-parser/analysis.py --parser-from attempts/002-parser/parser.py
```

Keep the implemented parser, then build `compare_components` and
`summarize_trust` in the new `analysis.py`. Read
[Evidence and change](lessons/01-evidence-and-change.md).

```sh
python3 checks/check_submission.py --analysis attempts/003-analysis/analysis.py --parser attempts/003-analysis/parser.py > attempts/003-analysis/analysis-check.json
python3 fwlab.py investigate fixtures/release-1.efw fixtures/release-2-observed.efw --old-manifest fixtures/release-1.json --new-manifest fixtures/release-2-observed.json --policy fixtures/policy.json --analysis attempts/003-analysis/analysis.py --parser attempts/003-analysis/parser.py > attempts/003-analysis/investigation.json
```

The analysis checker expects **31/31**, exit 0. Investigation output binds both
selected sources and both container hashes. Its exit 0 means analysis ran—not
that its output is correct; rerun the checkers after changes.

## 4. Unfamiliar-input investigation bridge

Follow [the case brief](fixtures/case-study/BRIEF.md), without first reading the
integration check's expected results. The captures use new names, independently
reordered tables/payloads, mixed changes and an incomplete capture. Write your
facts, hypotheses and unknowns before checking:

```sh
python3 checks/check_investigation.py --parser attempts/003-analysis/parser.py --analysis attempts/003-analysis/analysis.py > attempts/003-analysis/case-check.json
```

This integration check expects **6/6** and includes a changed release-floor
requirement. It checks computed results, **not the quality of your written
reasoning**. Use [the rubric](rubric.md), retain original findings, and put revised
work in a fresh numbered attempt. This is a capstone-progression exercise, not the
full-course independent capstone or proof of competence.

## Attempts, help and restore

Every new attempt uses a new name. Record help in that attempt's `help.json`.
Both sources are loaded afresh; a stale saved pass cannot substitute for execution.
To restore both TODO starters without erasing anything:

```sh
python3 tools/attempt.py 004-restored
```

This is explicit file-copy history, not a hosted attempt UI. No LLM or staffed
feedback is required; the rubric contains an optional learner-owned critique prompt.

## Supplied versus built; stopping point

**You build:** binary parser/layout checks, inventory, dependency graph, change
classifier, evidence summary, investigation and changed-policy explanation.

**Supplied:** immutable data-class contract and format constants, bounded file I/O,
strict JSON/manifest/policy checks, defensive extraction, CLI wiring, original
inert fixtures, tests and copy-based attempts. Hash convenience properties do not
replace the learner's inventory or confer authenticity.

**Not delivered:** complete seven-unit course, signature/certificate/root
verification, measured-boot/log correlation, real firmware execution, full final
capstone, other-platform validation, served download or publication. The graph
is a manifest declaration, not an observed hardware boot chain.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Bounded unfamiliar-input integration check, not full-course certification."""
import argparse
from copy import deepcopy
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from hashlib import sha256
import json
from pathlib import Path
import sys
import uuid
ROOT=Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1];sys.path.insert(0,str(ROOT))
from fwcourse.container import FormatError
from fwcourse.evidence import inspect_file,inspect_bytes,load_json
from fwcourse.runner import load_analysis,load_parser


def main():
    ap=argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__);ap.add_argument('--parser',required=True);ap.add_argument('--analysis',required=True);args=ap.parse_args()
    report={'run_id':str(uuid.uuid4()),'created_at_utc':datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(),'checks':[],'status':'fail'}
    def check(name,body):
        try:body();report['checks'].append({'check':name,'result':'pass'})
        except Exception as exc:report['checks'].append({'check':name,'result':'fail','detail':f'{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}'})
    def equal(a,b):
        if a!=b:raise AssertionError(f'expected {b!r}; got {a!r}')
    try:
        parser,report['parser_sha256']=load_parser(args.parser);analysis,report['analysis_sha256']=load_analysis(args.analysis)
        f=ROOT/'fixtures/case-study'
        a=inspect_file(f/'capture-a.efw',f/'capture-a.json',f/'policy.json',parser_module=parser)
        b=inspect_file(f/'capture-b.efw',f/'capture-b.json',f/'policy.json',parser_module=parser)
        check('baseline evidence axes',lambda:equal(analysis.summarize_trust(a),{'integrity':'match','manifest':'match','origin':'unverified','policy':'pass'}))
        check('new evidence axes distinguish self-consistency from policy',lambda:equal(analysis.summarize_trust(b),{'integrity':'match','manifest':'match','origin':'unverified','policy':'fail'}))
        check('named local-policy finding',lambda:equal(b['policy_findings'],['config_policy_mismatch:boot_mode']))
        expected=[{'name':n,'status':s,'fields_changed':fields} for n,s,fields in [('boot','unchanged',[]),('calibration','content_changed',['sha256']),('config','content_changed',['sha256']),('legacy-notes','removed',[]),('readme','added',[]),('runtime','metadata_changed',['version'])]]
        check('unfamiliar identity-based release changes',lambda:equal(analysis.compare_components(a['components'],b['components']),expected))
        def partial():
            try:parser.parse_container((f/'capture-partial.efw').read_bytes())
            except FormatError:return
            raise AssertionError('partial capture must not be silently repaired')
        check('partial capture rejected before comparison',partial)
        def policy_change():
            policy=load_json(f/'policy.json');policy['minimum_release']=12
            changed=inspect_bytes((f/'capture-a.efw').read_bytes(),load_json(f/'capture-a.json'),policy,parser_module=parser)
            equal(changed['policy_findings'],['release_below_minimum'])
            equal(analysis.summarize_trust(changed),{'integrity':'match','manifest':'match','origin':'unverified','policy':'fail'})
        check('changed release-floor requirement',policy_change)
        report['input_sha256']={name:sha256((f/name).read_bytes()).hexdigest() for name in ['capture-a.efw','capture-a.json','capture-b.efw','capture-b.json','policy.json']}
        if all(c['result']=='pass' for c in report['checks']):report['status']='pass'
    except Exception as exc:report['load_or_intake_error']=f'{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}'
    report['passed']=sum(c['result']=='pass' for c in report['checks']);report['total']=len(report['checks'])
    print(json.dumps(report,indent=2,sort_keys=True));return 0 if report['status']=='pass' else 1


if __name__=='__main__':sys.exit(main())
