`courses/firmware-forensics/trust/verify.mjs`:

```mjs
import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { resolve } from 'node:path';
import { pathToFileURL, fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
import { randomUUID } from 'node:crypto';
import { evidence, sha256 } from './crypto.mjs';

export async function loadPolicy(source) {
  const path = resolve(source); const bytes = readFileSync(path);
  const module = await import(pathToFileURL(path).href + '?sha256=' + sha256(bytes));
  if (typeof module.assessEvidence !== 'function') throw new Error('Source must export assessEvidence');
  return {assess:module.assessEvidence, source:{path,sha256:sha256(bytes)}};
}
export async function inspect({capture, manifest, signature, key, minimumRelease, source}) {
  const captureBytes = readFileSync(capture), manifestBytes = readFileSync(manifest);
  const signatureBytes = signature === '-' ? null : readFileSync(signature);
  const signatureText = signatureBytes === null ? null : signatureBytes.toString('utf8').trim();
  const keyBytes=readFileSync(key);
  const publicKey = keyBytes.toString('utf8').trim();
  const facts = evidence(captureBytes,manifestBytes,signatureText,publicKey,minimumRelease);
  const policy = await loadPolicy(source);
  const result = policy.assess(structuredClone(facts));
  // The selected result is reported verbatim, never silently repaired by an answer key.
  return {schema:1,runId:randomUUID(),createdAt:new Date().toISOString(),source:policy.source,
    captureSha256:sha256(captureBytes),manifestSha256:sha256(manifestBytes),signatureSha256:signatureBytes===null?null:sha256(signatureBytes),keyFileSha256:sha256(keyBytes),publicKey,facts,result,
    limits:'Classroom key only. Public test seed; no vendor authentication, certificate chain, hardware state or safety claim.'};
}
if (process.argv[1] && resolve(process.argv[1]) === fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)) {
  try {
    const [capture,manifest,signature,key,floor,source,...extra] = process.argv.slice(2);
    if (!source || extra.length) throw new Error('Usage: node trust/verify.mjs CAPTURE MANIFEST SIGNATURE_OR_- PUBLIC_KEY MINIMUM_RELEASE LEARNER_SOURCE');
    const report = await inspect({capture,manifest,signature,key,minimumRelease:Number(floor),source});
    console.log(JSON.stringify(report,null,2));
    process.exitCode = report.result?.admission === 'accept' ? 0 : 3;
  } catch (error) { console.error(JSON.stringify({status:'error',error:error.message})); process.exitCode=2; }
}

```

`courses/firmware-forensics/work.py`:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Preserve three sources in a fresh, numbered attempt. Never overwrite."""
from pathlib import Path
from hashlib import sha256
from datetime import datetime,timezone
import argparse,json,re,sys
ROOT=Path(__file__).resolve().parent
def main():
    p=argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    p.add_argument('name');p.add_argument('--from-attempt',type=Path);p.add_argument('--root',type=Path,default=ROOT/'attempts')
    a=p.parse_args()
    if not re.fullmatch(r'[0-9]{3}-[a-z][a-z0-9-]*',a.name):p.error('Use NNN-lowercase-name')
    original=a.from_attempt
    files={name:(original/name if original else ROOT/path).read_bytes() for name,path in [('parser.py','lab/starter/parser.py'),('analysis.py','lab/starter/analysis.py'),('trust.mjs','trust/starter/trust.mjs')]}
    if original: files['help.json']=(original/'help.json').read_bytes()
    else: files['help.json']=b'{"help_used":[],"notes":"Record help before revising."}\n'
    a.root.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True);dest=a.root/a.name;dest.mkdir(exist_ok=False)
    for name,data in files.items():(dest/name).write_bytes(data)
    (dest/'attempt.json').write_text(json.dumps({'schema':1,'name':a.name,'created':datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(),'from':str(original) if original else 'starters','initial_sha256':{n:sha256(b).hexdigest() for n,b in files.items()},'instruction':'Keep the first submitted sources and outputs; create another numbered attempt before repair.'},indent=2)+'\n')
    print(dest.resolve())
if __name__=='__main__':
    try:main()
    except OSError as e: print('Attempt refused: '+str(e),file=sys.stderr);sys.exit(2)

```

`courses/game-playing-agent-league/CAPSTONE.md`:

```md
# Build a league you can defend

Your final product is a small population of game-playing policies and an evidence packet that lets another person reproduce the comparison. A policy that loses honestly can satisfy a learning objective. An impressive win rate from an invalid comparison cannot.

The game, seeded runtime, immutable snapshots, replay records, worker cancellation, file formats and reader are supplied. You build the baseline decision, position evaluation, bounded search, learned features and fitting, report, opponent sampler, counterpolicy and finite-game gap calculation. You also make the experimental decisions and explain what the results support.

## The population

Keep six named roles: supplied random baseline, supplied greedy baseline, your hand-evaluated search, your learned-value search, an earlier learned snapshot, and your counterpolicy. Up to two additional policies are allowed. A new display name alone does not make a different policy. Explain the actual behavioral difference and preserve the source, parameters and lineage of each snapshot.

The supplied counterpolicy adapter can model either the known greedy policy or uniform legal-action choice. Your `responsePolicy` performs the search against that declared distribution. It does not receive secret access to an opponent's source or future random draws. Evaluate the response against its intended target, then show what happens against other members of the population. A specialized response may expose a weakness and still be a poor general competitor.

Use the earlier modules to build this population cumulatively. `roster` supplies the configuration plumbing; it does not establish that the roles were implemented correctly or that two parameter vectors produce different decisions.

## Separate development, selection and final evaluation

Start with the small development files. Run checks, inspect failures and change policies freely there. Save the first broken implementation and the repair; the local journal does this for code checks and practice responses.

Before your final season, write a short plan containing:

- the policy identities and parameter settings;
- your intended opponent distribution and the question being answered;
- the scenario-generation procedure, seeds and grouping rule;
- which scenarios and outcomes have already influenced development or selection;
- the common decision budget and the recorded total training computation;
- the paired-seat and policy-randomness schedule;
- the summary, uncertainty procedure and decision rule you intend to use;
- what result would change your current belief.

For the bounded course final, use 16 distinct scenario groups, both seat assignments and two declared policy-randomness seeds for every unordered policy pair. The decision budget is 256 hypothetical transitions per move. Six policies produce `15 × 16 × 2 × 2 = 960` scheduled games; eight produce 1,792. All planned slots must be accounted for. Host interruption is an incomplete experiment. A recorded policy forfeit is reported as such, alongside game outcomes.

The loader rejects repeated or horizontally reflected starting positions within a roster. You must also compare groups across training, development, selection and final rosters. Different seed numbers alone do not prove that the resulting starting positions are different. Internal positions can still recur; state the actual separation you established rather than calling every transition unseen.

Once final results have influenced your choices, that roster is selection evidence. Preserve it and collect fresh final evidence if you want a new confirmatory comparison. Do not relabel the old run.

## Build the report from the records

Your report must show the payoff matrix, declared denominators, failures, actual simulation credits and uncertainty based on scenario blocks. The two seat assignments and repeated policy seeds belonging to one starting scenario stay together when resampled. Show the number of independent groups; a larger number of bootstrap resamples is not a larger experiment.

The course uses an approximate 95% paired scenario-block percentile interval with a stated resampling seed and 2,000 resamples. Its interpretation depends on the sampling model and independence of groups. If the small sample or scenario construction does not justify a strong population claim, say so. Avoid presenting a conditional checkpoint comparison as evidence about all possible training runs.

If you claim one training method is better than another, repeat each method with at least five independently declared training seeds under matched resources. Treat those runs as training replicates, separate from scenario blocks. A single trained checkpoint can support a narrower statement about that checkpoint. It cannot estimate variability across training.

Describe at least one cross-play relationship that a single scalar ranking hides. You do not need to manufacture a cycle in the real game. If the tested population is transitive, report that observation and use the separate finite matrix exercise to demonstrate that you understand nontransitivity.

For exploitability, keep two kinds of evidence separate. The tiny supplied finite game can support an exact gap calculation within its complete matrix/tree. A bounded response search in the main game only measures the vulnerability discovered by that search and budget. Failure to find a response is not a proof that none exists.

## Explain one result in detail

Choose a position where two policies make different decisions. Include the exact starting state, actor, legal actions, source identities, depth/budget and relevant replay. Explain how a backed-up value or opponent model changes the selected move. Show one failure or limitation as well as any improvement.

This explanation should be checkable against the trace. “The model learned a better strategy” is not enough by itself. Name the feature or estimate, the reply it changes, and the observed consequence. If the learned model is weaker, explain the evidence without rewriting the question after seeing the outcome.

## Submit a reproducible packet

Include your frozen learner source, configuration files, fitted model/training artifacts, raw season, learner report, journal export and written interpretation. Preserve all hashes recorded in those artifacts. State the Node version and platform used. Record commands in the order a reviewer can actually run them from the extracted package.

Use `verify` for trajectory replay and `verify --configuration` for re-execution of the declared policies. A successful trajectory check alone does not prove that the recorded policy chose those actions. A source change after a successful check invalidates the claim that the current source was checked; rerun and retain the earlier result as history.

The package supports direct `.mjs` policy files in `lib/` and `learner/`. Keep policy dependencies inside the captured package and use the supplied randomness and simulation oracle. Outside files, dynamic external imports, wall-clock decisions, network calls and direct engine transitions are outside this experiment's reproducibility contract. The local worker is a cancellation mechanism, not a hostile-code service.

## The independent transfer stage

Before receiving the administered challenge, freeze your source and write a falsifiable prediction about which parts of your policy and evaluation would survive an unfamiliar rule or information change. Retain that prediction even if it is wrong.

The instructor supplies the separate challenge after this freeze: the rules, the simulator, conformance examples, the challenge identity, and the budget and evaluation instructions. Its contract and private control set are not in the learner delivery, and no patched simulator ships in this package. The nine module 8 analysis items can be completed without it; stop executable transfer work until the challenge is supplied. Apply the same resource limits, preserve the first attempt, and distinguish assistance from independent repair. Explain which assumption failed and why your repair is general within the new contract. If no code change is needed, establish that with evidence; cosmetic edits earn no credit.

After the challenge is revealed, it is revision material. A second independent transfer assessment requires a fresh challenge. The journal is a useful local history, not an authenticated credential or proof of independent work.

## Review boundaries

Software checks establish finite behavior: legal actions, accounting, data identities, numerical fixtures and tested repairs. A separate reviewer evaluates your experimental reasoning and the match between claims and evidence. A fresh learner attempt evaluates whether the course actually teaches these skills. Publication and a verified live learner flow are separate course-release requirements; this local package does not claim them.

```

# Game-Playing Agent League — local course candidate

**Build a champion. Then build the agent that breaks it.** Construct search and learned policies, train against a population, and defend a league result with reproducible evidence. The final challenge changes an assumption after you freeze your prediction.

This is an original local course candidate, not a published or accepted Free to Learn course. Its eight-module sequence is described below. Read [VERIFY.md](VERIFY.md) for the exact checks completed in this run. No human learner study or rendered browser verification is claimed.

## Start

Use **Node.js 22 or later** and a text editor. Development checks in this run use Node 26.5.1 on macOS arm64; other Node versions and platforms are not yet verified. No package installation, model download, GPU, API key, account, network connection or server is needed.

```sh
node cli.mjs doctor
node cli.mjs list
node cli.mjs lesson 1.1
```

Open `index.html` directly to read the lesson viewer and inspect saved games. The command line is the authoritative place to commit responses and execute your code. The viewer reads only files you choose; it makes no external requests. The rendered page still needs browser and accessibility verification.

Prerequisites: arrays, functions, recursion, basic algorithmic complexity, probability, averages and variance. For the learned value model, you should be comfortable with vectors, a weighted sum, a loss and a gradient update. No machine-learning framework is assumed. Plan roughly 30–40 hours across multiple sessions; that estimate awaits learner trials.

The supplied game is a 5×5 version of Breakthrough. Each player starts with five pawns and advances toward the other edge. Straight moves require an empty destination; diagonal moves may enter empty space or capture. Reaching the far edge, removing every opposing pawn, or leaving the next player without a legal move wins. Terminal utilities are +1 and -1. Small, deterministic rules let you inspect the actual decisions behind a result.

## What you build

| Module | Your cumulative work | Supplied support |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1. Establish a fair game | `chooseAction` in `learner/baseline.mjs`: legal, reproducible decisions | Rules, legal moves, observations, seeded randomness, record formats |
| 2. Search adversarial replies | `evaluate` and `search`: player-aware values and bounded planning | Counted simulation oracle, transparent practice trees, game adapter |
| 3. Learn a value model | `features` and `fit`: state features and a fitted linear value | Outcome-labelled episodes, group split, metrics, learned-policy adapter |
| 4. Run an honest tournament | `summarize`: complete denominators, payoff matrix, block uncertainty | Frozen schedule, seat pairing, raw records, bootstrap utility |
| 5. Train against a population | `sampleOpponent`: sampling from a weighted immutable archive | Bounded self-play loop, model snapshots and lineage |
| 6. Find counterstrategies | `responsePolicy` and `nashGap`: a modeled response and exact finite-game gap | Declared opponent model, tiny exact oracle and comparison fixtures |
| 7. Run and defend your league | Frozen six-role population, replayable season and defensible report | Configuration assembly, export, source bundles and replay verification |
| 8. Adapt to a rule change | Prediction, first transfer attempt, repair and limited claims | Nine analysis items and worked examples, completable now; no patched simulator ships. An instructor supplies the challenge separately, after your freeze |

Module 3 checks board information separately from requested-player perspective. Material-only, advancement, relative-count and other meaningful representations are supported; not every move or balanced position must change a vector. Bias, player ID or ply alone cannot replace a board measurement.

The starter functions are intentionally incomplete. They should fail their first code checks. You implement the named target logic; you do not need to build a web app, game engine, database or file format.

`learner/league-policy.mjs`, `learner/learned-policy.mjs` and `learner/counter-policy.mjs` are supplied glue. The counterpolicy adapter exposes a declared greedy or uniform opponent model; it does not reveal the opponent's future randomness. Public checks and feedback are practice material. Private qualification controls and reference implementations are excluded from this learner package.

## Commit, inspect feedback, repair

Each lesson supplies exact item IDs:

```sh
node cli.mjs attempt 1.1-p1 --answer 'my reasoning' --confidence medium
node cli.mjs feedback 1.1-p1
node cli.mjs hint 1.1-p1 --level 1
node cli.mjs history
```

Feedback is released after a response is saved. It shows a reasoned answer and self-check criteria; it does not automatically grade arbitrary prose. Original questions, first answers, confidence, assistance and revisions remain in `work/attempts.json`. A later revision does not replace the first response. Navigation is always open.

Run the code check for the module you are working on:

```sh
node cli.mjs check 1
node cli.mjs check 2
node cli.mjs check 3
node cli.mjs check 4
node cli.mjs check 5
node cli.mjs check 6
```

`check evaluation` and `check search` isolate the two parts of module 2. Each code attempt captures learner, runtime and public-checker source before execution, then saves the actual feedback. Changes during execution invalidate the result. An eight-second worker limit catches runaway practice checks. Passing a finite practice check is not a proof of correctness on arbitrary inputs or a full-course pass.

## Run real games, fit, train and report

Begin with the supplied policies. These commands demonstrate the scaffold, not learner accomplishment:

```sh
node cli.mjs demo --seed 7 --out ./work/demo-7.json
node cli.mjs verify ./work/demo-7.json
node cli.mjs league development-league.json --out ./work/behavior.json
node cli.mjs verify ./work/behavior.json --configuration development-league.json
```

The development league has two policies, three starting scenarios and both seats: six real games. `verify` checks recorded action trajectories. Adding `--configuration` reruns the exact policy snapshots and compares their decisions and simulation credits. Both checks are useful; they establish different things.

After implementing module 3, fit your value model using those games:

```sh
node cli.mjs fit ./work/behavior.json --out ./work/value-model.json
node cli.mjs roster ./work/value-model.json --out ./work/value-league.json
node cli.mjs league ./work/value-league.json --out ./work/value-season.json
```

`fit` uses your features and fitting code. `roster` supplies the JSON assembly for random, greedy, hand-evaluated search and learned-value search. The default fit uses seed 41, 400 epochs and learning rate 0.05, with a scenario-group training/validation split. Its small dataset is a learning exercise, not persuasive evidence of playing strength.

After implementing the population sampler, run a bounded training experiment:

```sh
node cli.mjs train development-training.json --out ./work/training.json
node cli.mjs roster ./work/training.json --out ./work/population-league.json
```

The training configuration declares three generations, twelve games per generation, a 64-credit decision budget and its fitting recipe. Every learned snapshot and its lineage are retained. The six-role roster also needs your module-6 counterpolicy before it can play successfully.

After modules 4 and 6, run and interpret that population:

```sh
node cli.mjs league ./work/population-league.json --out ./work/population-season.json
node cli.mjs verify ./work/population-season.json --configuration ./work/population-league.json
node cli.mjs report ./work/population-season.json --out ./work/population-report.json
```

`report` executes your summarizer against the actual records. A valid replay does not automatically make its statistical interpretation correct. Inspect the declared uncertainty unit and denominators. Use the report practice checker and an independent evidence review.

Existing output files are never overwritten. Choose a new name for a new run. League/training work is interrupted after 60 seconds; interrupted work is marked incomplete, not scored as a loss. Reduce the development configuration if needed. A completed final season requires its entire declared roster.

Read [CAPSTONE.md](CAPSTONE.md) before freezing final evaluation. A final course roster has six named roles, sixteen independent scenario groups, both seats, two policy-randomness seeds and a common 256-credit budget. Role labels do not establish correct implementations; source and evidence review remain necessary.

## Keep your work

```sh
node cli.mjs export ./my-attempts.json
node cli.mjs import ./my-attempts.json
```

Exports refuse to overwrite existing files. Imports validate versions and hashes, retain imported provenance, and reject conflicting versions of the same record. Unsupported or corrupt data is preserved for recovery rather than reinterpreted. `--journal /path/to/another.json` selects a separate history. The 16 MiB journal limit refuses further appends rather than dropping old attempts.

If saving fails, the command stops before releasing new feedback. If a process is interrupted while holding a journal lock, inspect the journal and its `.lock` file before manually clearing a stale lock. The tool does not delete your work automatically. Keep the original readable/exportable bytes when investigating a problem. Hashes detect accidental changes; they are not authenticated credentials or proof that work was independent.

## Experimental and runtime boundaries

Run only your own trusted local code. Node workers provide cancellation, not security containment for submissions from strangers. All hypothetical game transitions must use the supplied counted oracle. Direct engine calls would evade that accounting and invalidate the comparison.

Worker JavaScript heaps are capped at 192 MiB old generation and 32 MiB young generation, with a 4 MiB stack. These are reliability limits, not a 256 MiB process-memory guarantee: native allocations, buffers and host overhead are outside those caps. A worker error or allocation failure produces an incomplete operation, not a fabricated match result.

Policy entry modules must be direct `.mjs` files in `lib/` or `learner/`. Keep dependencies inside the captured package and use the supplied seeded randomness. External or dynamically loaded dependencies, wall-clock decisions and uncaptured data are outside this course's reproducibility contract. Restoring an exact source bundle is distinct from proving that its experimental design is sound.

A low validation loss need not improve play. Beating one bot need not improve population performance. A bounded counterstrategy is empirical evidence about its target and budget, not a universal exploitability proof. The independent transfer challenge is not included here; after it is revealed it becomes revision material. Live Free to Learn delivery, rendered interaction checks and a fresh learner flow remain separate acceptance requirements.

`courses/game-playing-agent-league/SOURCES.md`:

```md
# Sources and scope

The small game implementation, course text, exercise scaffolding and local tooling in this package were written for this course. No Arcfield, duel-director, MIT lecture text or external library source was copied into the learner package.

The design draws on these primary references:

- [OpenSpiel framework paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/1908.09453): game/state interfaces and distinctions among game classes.
- [OpenSpiel Breakthrough implementation](https://github.com/google-deepmind/open_spiel/tree/master/open_spiel/games/breakthrough): an external rules reference. The course uses a declared 5×5 configuration and its own action encoding.
- [MIT 6.034, search in games](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/6-034-artificial-intelligence-fall-2010/resources/lecture-6-search-games-minimax-and-alpha-beta/): foundational minimax and alpha-beta concepts. MIT material is linked, not republished; its terms apply on the linked site.
- [Stanford CS229 notes](https://cs229.stanford.edu/main_notes.pdf): linear least-squares fitting and optimization.
- [Policy-Space Response Oracles](https://arxiv.org/abs/1711.00832): overfitting to training partners and learning against populations. This teaching league is not a reproduction of the paper's experiments.
- [Alpha-Rank](https://arxiv.org/abs/1903.01373): strategic interactions and ranking. The course's matrix/graph view is not an implementation of Alpha-Rank.
- [Deep Reinforcement Learning at the Edge of the Statistical Precipice](https://arxiv.org/abs/2108.13264): uncertainty in comparisons and independent training-run variability.
- [SciPy bootstrap documentation](https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy/reference/generated/scipy.stats.bootstrap.html): paired resampling and interval-method distinctions. SciPy is not a required dependency.

Examples and reported toy numbers in lessons are illustrative unless explicitly accompanied by a retained run record. A successful local checker run is evidence for its finite contract, not a proof of optimal play, learning gains, or generalization to all games. The public practice feedback is available in this package; it is not a hidden assessment.

```

`courses/game-playing-agent-league/VERIFY.md`:

```md
# Verification and limits of this candidate

This is a local learner package, not a certificate of learning or a live Free to Learn release.

On November 4, 2026, the author-side suite passed 84 tests on Node 26.5.1, macOS arm64. The tests covered rule invariants and actual replay, seeded policies, budget and forfeit handling, wrong and valid alternative implementations, grouped statistics, fitting, sampling, exact finite-game gaps, transfer tactics, and attempt/import preservation. Node 22 is the intended minimum; it was not available for a separate test in this run.

An end-to-end engineering run used private reference implementations through the same learner CLI. It passed all six code-check groups, fit a model from recorded games, trained three generations over 36 games, ran a 90-game six-policy development league, and ran a 960-game final-shaped roster. Both trajectory and exact-policy replay passed, and the learner report function consumed the actual records. Export/import and first-answer/revision records were exercised. Those reference solutions and their raw source bundles are deliberately absent from this package.

The private rule-change instrument accepted two different correct search implementations and rejected turn-alternation assumptions, a wrong evaluation perspective, weak action selection and budget overruns. Automated success leaves manual transfer review pending. The challenge is separately released by an administrator after the base submission is frozen; its private grading cases are never included here.

Version 0.1.1 separately checks board sensitivity at a fixed player/actor/ply and requested-player perspective across diverse positions. Independent material-only, relative-count, advancement and positional representations pass; player-only, ply-only and constant representations fail. A quiet move may leave a material feature unchanged. These finite checks do not prove strategic usefulness.

The starter files in this package still contain unfinished learner functions. Their initial checks should fail. This is expected and helps establish that the package has not substituted a finished reference solution for your work.

Not run: rendered browser interaction, accessibility audit, mobile-device verification, a fresh human learner trial, live deployment, or live Free to Learn flow. The reader and replay viewer received static structure/JavaScript checks only. The course therefore remains a candidate with these release gates open.

Practice feedback is self-assessed; a local file cannot keep its answer material secret. Hashes preserve source/version identity and detect accidental change, not independent authorship or authenticity. A full course assessment also requires examining the learner's reasoning, assistance, experimental choices and unfamiliar transfer work.

```

      "Explains why, in terms of whether the set of opponents was exhausted or sampled; your own wording counts if the three scopes stay distinct."
    ],
    "kind": "public-practice-self-check"
  }
}

```mjs
import {initialState, createState, GameError} from '../lib/game.mjs';
import {checkFeatures, predictLinear} from '../lib/training.mjs';
import {createRng} from '../lib/rng.mjs';
import {createPlan} from '../lib/league.mjs';
import {blockBootstrap} from '../lib/statistics.mjs';
import {copyData, deepFreeze} from '../lib/identity.mjs';

function suite(name, cases) {
  const checks = cases.map(([id, requirement, run]) => {
    try { const observed = run(); return {id, ok: true, requirement, ...(observed === undefined ? {} : {observed})}; }
    catch (error) { return {id, ok: false, requirement, reason: error.message, ...(error.input ? {failureInput: error.input} : {})}; }
  });
  return {ok: checks.every(check => check.ok), scope: 'public-practice', name, checks,
    limitation: 'These finite public controls are not a hidden assessment, proof of general correctness, or evidence of human learning.'};
}
function requireThat(condition, message, input) { if (!condition) throw Object.assign(new Error(message), {input}); }
function rejects(run, message) { let rejected = false; try { run(); } catch { rejected = true; } requireThat(rejected, message); }
function close(actual, expected, tolerance = 1e-9) { requireThat(Number.isFinite(actual) && Math.abs(actual - expected) <= tolerance, `Expected ${expected} within ${tolerance}; received ${actual}.`); }

// Public practice positions deliberately vary several plausible feature families.
// All are nonterminal, currentPlayer=0, ply=0: metadata cannot substitute for a board measurement.
function featurePosition(id, own, other) {
  const board = Array(25).fill(-1);
  for (const cell of own) board[cell] = 0;
  for (const cell of other) board[cell] = 1;
  return {id, state: createState({board, currentPlayer: 0, ply: 0})};
}
const FEATURE_POSITIONS = [
  {id: 'opening', state: initialState()},
  featurePosition('material-ahead', [6, 8], [18]),
  featurePosition('material-behind', [6], [16, 18]),
  featurePosition('balanced-counts', [6], [18]),
  featurePosition('advanced', [16], [18]),
  featurePosition('wide-arrangement', [10], [19]),
  featurePosition('central-arrangement', [12], [19]),
  featurePosition('mixed-advantage', [12, 13], [18]),
];
function featureObservations(features) {
  let dimensions;
  return FEATURE_POSITIONS.map(({id, state}) => ({id, vectors: [0, 1].map(player => {
    function extract() {
      const input = copyData(state), before = JSON.stringify(input);
      const vector = Array.from(checkFeatures(features(input, player)));
      requireThat(JSON.stringify(input) === before, 'Feature extraction changed its input state.', {id, player});
      if (dimensions === undefined) dimensions = vector.length;
      requireThat(vector.length === dimensions, 'Feature dimension changed between positions or perspectives.', {id, player});
      return vector;
    }
    const vector = extract();
    requireThat(JSON.stringify(vector) === JSON.stringify(extract()), 'Feature extraction changed on repeated identical input.', {id, player});
    return vector;
  })}));
}

export function checkValueModel({features, fit}) {
  const samples = [-1, -0.5, 0, 0.5, 1].map((x, index) => ({x: [1, x], target: 0.2 + 0.6 * x, episodeId: `e${index}`, scenarioId: `s${index}`}));
  return suite('Value features and fitting', [
    ['features-contract', 'Features have one bounded, reproducible dimension and do not mutate any supplied position.', () => {
      const vectors = featureObservations(features);
      return {dimensions: vectors[0].vectors[0].length, positions: vectors.length};
    }],
    ['features-board-sensitivity', 'At each fixed player perspective, distinguish at least some boards across material, advancement and arrangement changes; actor and ply stay fixed.', () => {
      const observations = featureObservations(features);
      const distinct = [0, 1].map(player => new Set(observations.map(item => JSON.stringify(item.vectors[player]))).size);
      requireThat(distinct.every(count => count > 1),
        'The feature vector did not change across the tested boards for a fixed requested player. Player ID, ply or a constant alone cannot represent a position.',
        {positions: FEATURE_POSITIONS.map(item => ({id: item.id, state: item.state})), distinctVectorsByPlayer: distinct});
      return {distinctVectorsByPlayer: distinct, everyMoveMustChangeFeatures: false};
    }],
    ['features-perspective', 'Preserve the requested player perspective on at least one feature-relevant position; balanced positions may legitimately have equal vectors.', () => {
      const observations = featureObservations(features);
      const witnesses = observations.filter(item => JSON.stringify(item.vectors[0]) !== JSON.stringify(item.vectors[1])).map(item => item.id);
      requireThat(witnesses.length > 0,
        'The tested representation never distinguishes the requested player. Keep the value target and feature perspective aligned; no exact sign convention or vector shape is required.');
      return {perspectiveWitnesses: witnesses};
    }],
    ['features-range', 'Stay inside [-1, 1] on positions with a material difference of two or more pawns.', () => {
      for (const [own, other] of [[[5, 6, 8], [18]], [[6], [15, 16, 18]], [[5, 6, 7, 8, 9], [18]]]) {
        const {state} = featurePosition('wide-material-gap', own, other);
        for (const player of [0, 1]) {
          let vector;
          try { vector = Array.from(features(copyData(state), player)); } catch (error) { throw Object.assign(new Error(`features threw: ${error.message}`), {input: {state, player}}); }
          requireThat(vector.every(value => Number.isFinite(value) && Math.abs(value) <= 1), 'learner/value-model.mjs: "Return 1–32 finite values in [-1,1]". A raw pawn count leaves that range once the difference reaches two, and cli fit then refuses the features.', {state, player, vector});
        }
      }
    }],
    ['features-no-outcome', 'Use only the observable board, not the recorded outcome (lesson 3.1).', () => {
      const won = createState({board: (() => { const b = Array(25).fill(-1); b[22] = 0; b[8] = 1; return b; })(), currentPlayer: 1, ply: 0});
      requireThat(won.terminal, 'Fixture error: this position must be terminal.');
      // Returns are fixed by the board, so no valid state differs only in returns. A feature that calls the supplied game
      // functions (legalActions, observe, validateState) correctly refuses this contradictory copy with GameError
      // INVALID_TERMINAL; that refusal is not an outcome leak and is accepted (v3, after Pine's review).
      const flipped = {...copyData(won), returns: [...won.returns].reverse()};
      const refused = [];
      for (const player of [0, 1]) {
        const a = JSON.stringify(Array.from(features(copyData(won), player)));
        let b;
        try { b = JSON.stringify(Array.from(features(copyData(flipped), player))); }
        catch (error) { if (error instanceof GameError || error?.code === 'INVALID_TERMINAL') { refused.push(player); continue; } throw error; }
        requireThat(a === b, 'Two states with the same board and different recorded returns got different features. learner/value-model.mjs: "Do not use final outcomes"; lesson 3.1: features measure "another quantity your policy can compute before the outcome."', {player, board: won.board});
      }
      return refused.length ? {contradictoryStateRefusedByGameValidation: refused} : undefined;
    }],
    ['fit-synthetic', 'Fit an original small regression fixture rather than returning a fixed vector.', () => {
      const input = copyData([samples[3], samples[0], samples[4], samples[1], samples[2]]), before = JSON.stringify(input); // Lane ALP: unsorted, so a sort is visible
      const model = fit(input, {seed: 13, epochs: 600, learningRate: 0.1});
      requireThat(JSON.stringify(input) === before, 'Fitting mutated supplied training examples (their order or contents changed). Train on the caller\'s examples without changing them.');
      const errors = samples.map(example => (predictLinear(model.weights, example.x) - example.target) ** 2);
      const mse = errors.reduce((sum, value) => sum + value, 0) / errors.length;
      requireThat(mse < 0.002, `Synthetic-fit MSE ${mse} is too large; verify labels, update direction and coefficient order.`, samples);
      return {meanSquaredError: mse};
    }],
    ['fit-changed-labels', 'Changed training labels must produce corresponding changed predictions.', () => {
      const changed = samples.map(example => ({...example, target: -0.3 - 0.4 * example.x[1]}));
      const model = fit(copyData(changed), {seed: 19, epochs: 600, learningRate: 0.1});
      const mse = changed.reduce((sum, example) => sum + (predictLinear(model.weights, example.x) - example.target) ** 2, 0) / changed.length;
      requireThat(mse < 0.002, `Changed-label MSE ${mse} is too large. A model cannot ignore its data.`, changed);
      return {meanSquaredError: mse};
    }],
    ['fit-invalid', 'Reject nonfinite and inconsistent training examples instead of producing unusable parameters.', () => {
      rejects(() => fit([{x: [1, NaN], target: 1}], {seed: 1, epochs: 2, learningRate: 0.1}), 'NaN input was not rejected.');
      rejects(() => fit([{x: [1], target: 1}, {x: [1, 0], target: 0}], {seed: 1, epochs: 2, learningRate: 0.1}), 'Inconsistent dimensions were not rejected.');
      rejects(() => fit([{x: [1, 0], target: NaN}, {x: [1, 1], target: 1}], {seed: 1, epochs: 2, learningRate: 0.1}), 'A NaN target was not rejected. Lesson 3.2: "do not allow NaN weights to reach search"; reject nonfinite examples, including targets.');
    }],
  ]);
}

export function checkSampler(sampleOpponent) {
  const archive = [{id: 'first', weight: 0.2}, {id: 'middle', weight: 0.3}, {id: 'last', weight: 0.5}];
  return suite('Opponent archive sampling', [
    ['sampler-frequency', 'Sample the declared distribution, including its last entry.', () => {
      const rng = createRng(91), counts = {first: 0, middle: 0, last: 0}, before = JSON.stringify(archive);
      for (let i = 0; i < 8000; i++) { const id = sampleOpponent(archive, rng); requireThat(Object.hasOwn(counts, id), `Unknown opponent ${id}.`); counts[id]++; }
      requireThat(JSON.stringify(archive) === before, 'Sampler mutated its archive.');
      for (const entry of archive) requireThat(Math.abs(counts[entry.id] / 8000 - entry.weight) < 0.03, `Observed ${entry.id} frequency ${counts[entry.id] / 8000} differs from ${entry.weight}.`, archive);
      return counts;
    }],
    ['sampler-reproduce', 'A fixed seed and archive reproduce the same selected IDs.', () => {
      const one = createRng(7), two = createRng(7);
      const a = Array.from({length: 40}, () => sampleOpponent(archive, one)), b = Array.from({length: 40}, () => sampleOpponent(archive, two));
      requireThat(JSON.stringify(a) === JSON.stringify(b), 'Seeded sampling did not reproduce.');
    }],
    ['sampler-zero-mass', 'Never select a zero-probability opponent.', () => {
      const fixed = [{id: 'never', weight: 0}, {id: 'only', weight: 1}, {id: 'also-never', weight: 0}], rng = createRng(12);
      for (let i = 0; i < 30; i++) requireThat(sampleOpponent(fixed, rng) === 'only', 'A zero-weight item was selected.');
    }],
    ['sampler-sum', 'Reject weights whose sum is plainly not one (lesson 5.2: "rejects an unnormalized roster").', () => {
      // Lane ALP v2: gross sums only (0.7 and 1.5). No numeric tolerance is declared in the course, so values near one are left to the author.
      for (const bad of [[{id: 'first', weight: 0.2}, {id: 'middle', weight: 0.3}, {id: 'last', weight: 0.2}], [{id: 'first', weight: 0.2}, {id: 'middle', weight: 0.3}, {id: 'last', weight: 1}]])
        rejects(() => sampleOpponent(bad, createRng(1)), `Weights summing to ${bad.reduce((s, e) => s + e.weight, 0).toFixed(2)} were accepted. Lesson 5.2: the contract requires probabilities summing to one; reject an unnormalized roster.`);
    }],
    ['sampler-invalid', 'Reject negative, unnormalized, nonfinite or duplicate-ID archive distributions.', () => {
      for (const bad of [[], [{id: 'a', weight: -1}, {id: 'b', weight: 2}], [{id: 'a', weight: 0.5}], [{id: 'a', weight: NaN}], [{id: 'a', weight: 0.5}, {id: 'a', weight: 0.5}]]) rejects(() => sampleOpponent(bad, createRng(1)), 'Invalid archive was not rejected.');
    }],
  ]);
}

export function reportPracticeFixture() {
  const plan = createPlan({policies: [{id: 'A'}, {id: 'B'}], scenarios: [{id: 'scenario-1', stateHash: 'state-1'}, {id: 'scenario-2', stateHash: 'state-2'}, {id: 'scenario-3', stateHash: 'state-3'}], seeds: [3, 9], budget: 16});
  const records = plan.roster.map(slot => {
    const valueForA = slot.scenarioId === 'scenario-3' ? -1 : 1;
    const first = slot.policies[0] === 'A' ? valueForA : -valueForA;
    return {slotId: slot.id, record: {planId: plan.id, scenario: {id: slot.scenarioId}, policySnapshots: slot.policies.map(id => ({id})), policySeeds: [...slot.policySeeds], budget: plan.budget, status: 'completed', result: {returns: [first, -first]}}};
  });
  return {plan, records};
}

// Lane ALP proposal: A's result depends on the scenario, A's seat and the replicate, so a reducer that keeps only one seat
// or one replicate gets different scenario blocks. Expected blocks, in scenario order: 0.5, 1, -0.5.
const SEAT_REPLICATE_VALUES = {'scenario-1': [[1, 1], [-1, 1]], 'scenario-2': [[1, 1], [1, 1]], 'scenario-3': [[-1, 1], [-1, -1]]};
export function reportSeatReplicateFixture() {
  const {plan} = reportPracticeFixture();
  const records = plan.roster.map(slot => {
    const seatOfA = slot.policies.indexOf('A'), replicate = plan.replicateSeeds.indexOf(slot.replicate);
    const valueForA = SEAT_REPLICATE_VALUES[slot.scenarioId][seatOfA][replicate];
    const first = seatOfA === 0 ? valueForA : -valueForA;
    return {slotId: slot.id, record: {planId: plan.id, scenario: {id: slot.scenarioId}, policySnapshots: slot.policies.map(id => ({id})), policySeeds: [...slot.policySeeds], budget: plan.budget, status: 'completed', result: {returns: [first, -first]}}};
  });
  return {plan, records};
}

export function checkReport(summarize) {
  return suite('Complete paired evaluation', [
    ['report-paired', 'Use the planned denominator, normalize seat perspective and aggregate by scenario.', () => {
      const {records, plan} = reportPracticeFixture(), before = JSON.stringify({records, plan});
      const result = summarize(records, plan);
      requireThat(result.complete === true && result.expected === 12 && result.observed === 12, 'A complete 12-game roster was not recognized.');
      close(result.matrix?.[0]?.[1], 1 / 3); close(result.matrix?.[1]?.[0], -1 / 3);
      const comparison = result.comparisons?.find(item => item.pair?.[0] === 'A' && item.pair?.[1] === 'B');
      requireThat(comparison?.units === 3 && comparison.blocks?.length === 3, 'The interval must use three scenario blocks, not twelve games.');
      const values = comparison.blocks.map(block => block.value).sort((a, b) => a - b);
      requireThat(JSON.stringify(values) === JSON.stringify([-1, 1, 1]), 'Incorrect scenario-block values.', records);
      close(comparison.estimate, 1 / 3);
      const expectedInterval=blockBootstrap(values,{seed:1,resamples:2000,confidence:0.95}).interval;
      requireThat(Array.isArray(comparison.interval)&&comparison.interval.length===2,'Missing interval');
      comparison.interval.forEach((v,i)=>close(v,expectedInterval[i]));
      requireThat(JSON.stringify({records, plan}) === before, 'Report generation changed its input evidence.');
    }],
    ['report-missing', 'Missing evidence leaves the planned denominator visible and the result incomplete.', () => {
      const {records, plan} = reportPracticeFixture(), missing = records.pop();
      const result = summarize(records, plan);
      requireThat(result.complete === false && result.expected === 12 && result.observed === 11 && result.missing?.includes(missing.slotId), 'A missing game was hidden or counted as a result.');
    }],
    ['report-duplicate', 'Recognize duplicate match IDs without counting the same game twice.', () => {
      const {records, plan} = reportPracticeFixture(); records.push(copyData(records[0]));
      const result = summarize(records, plan);
      requireThat(result.complete === false && result.expected === 12 && result.observed === 12 && result.duplicates?.includes(records[0].slotId), 'Duplicate evidence was double-counted or hidden.');
    }],
    ['report-conflict', 'Conflicting results for one slot cannot establish a complete comparison.', () => {
      const {records, plan} = reportPracticeFixture(), conflict = copyData(records[0]); conflict.record.result.returns.reverse(); records.push(conflict);
      const result = summarize(records, plan);
      requireThat(result.complete === false && result.observed <= 12, 'Conflicting duplicate evidence was silently accepted.');
    }],
    ['report-seat-and-replicate', 'Average both seats and every replicate inside each scenario block (lessons 4.1 and 4.2).', () => {
      const {records, plan} = reportSeatReplicateFixture();
      const result = summarize(records, plan);
      requireThat(result.complete === true && result.expected === 12 && result.observed === 12, 'A complete 12-game roster was not recognized.');
      const comparison = result.comparisons?.find(item => item.pair?.[0] === 'A' && item.pair?.[1] === 'B');
      const values = (comparison?.blocks ?? []).map(block => block.value).sort((a, b) => a - b);
      requireThat(JSON.stringify(values) === JSON.stringify([-0.5, 0.5, 1]), `Scenario blocks ${JSON.stringify(values)} are not [-0.5, 0.5, 1]. Lesson 4.1: "If each scenario has two seats and two randomness replicates, first aggregate those four games into a scenario block." Reporting only one seat or one replicate answers a different question.`, records);
      close(comparison.estimate, 1 / 3); close(result.matrix?.[0]?.[1], 1 / 3); close(result.matrix?.[1]?.[0], -1 / 3);
    }],
    ['report-mismatch', 'Reject a result for a slot the plan does not contain, or one that names the wrong scenario (lesson 4.1).', () => {
      for (const kind of ['unknown-slot', 'scenario']) {
        const {records, plan} = reportPracticeFixture();
        if (kind === 'unknown-slot') { const extra = copyData(records[0]); extra.slotId = 'not-a-slot-in-this-plan'; records.push(extra); }
        if (kind === 'scenario') records[0].record.scenario.id = records[0].record.scenario.id === 'scenario-1' ? 'scenario-2' : 'scenario-1';
        const result = summarize(records, plan);
        requireThat(result.complete === false && result.invalid?.length > 0, `A result with ${kind === 'unknown-slot' ? 'an unknown slot ID' : 'a mismatched scenario'} was accepted. Lesson 4.1: the slot ID "is the denominator's unit of identity", and the record "names its plan, scenario and policy snapshots so the reducer can reject a mismatched result."`);
        if (kind === 'unknown-slot') requireThat(result.observed === 12, 'A result for a slot outside the plan was counted as an observation.');
      }
    }],
    ['report-wrong-plan', 'Reject wrong-plan, wrong-seat and unresolved infrastructure records.', () => {
      for (const field of ['plan', 'seat', 'seed', 'budget', 'failure']) {
        const {records, plan} = reportPracticeFixture();
        if (field === 'plan') records[0].record.planId = 'other';
        if (field === 'seat') records[0].record.policySnapshots.reverse();
        if (field === 'seed') records[0].record.policySeeds[0]^=1;
        if (field === 'budget') records[0].record.budget+=1;
        if (field === 'failure') { records[0].record.status = 'infrastructure-failure'; records[0].record.result = null; }
        const result = summarize(records, plan);
        const unresolvedFailure = field === 'failure' && result.missing?.includes(records[0].slotId);
        requireThat(result.complete === false && (result.invalid?.length > 0 || unresolvedFailure),
          `Invalid ${field} record was accepted. Infrastructure failures may be reported as invalid evidence or as their unresolved planned slot; neither can establish completeness.`);
      }
    }],
  ]);
}

export function checkGap(nashGap) {
  return suite('Restricted-game Nash gap', [
    ['gap-cycle', 'Correctly compute a cyclic matrix gap and name both unilateral responses.', () => {
      const matrix = [[0, -1, 1], [1, 0, -1], [-1, 1, 0]], uniform = [1 / 3, 1 / 3, 1 / 3];
      close(nashGap(matrix, uniform, uniform), 0);
      close(nashGap(matrix, [1, 0, 0], [1, 0, 0]), 2);
    }],
    ['gap-rectangular', 'Handle different row/column roster sizes and mixed weights.', () => close(nashGap([[1, -1, 0], [0, 1, -1]], [0.5, 0.5], [0.2, 0.3, 0.5]), 0.4)],
    ['gap-dimensions', 'Reject a mixture whose length differs from the matrix, and infinite payoffs (lesson 6.2).', () => {
      for (const [matrix, x, y] of [[[[1, 0], [0, 1]], [0.5, 0.5], [0.5, 0.25, 0.25]], [[[1, 0], [0, 1]], [1 / 3, 1 / 3, 1 / 3], [0.5, 0.5]], [[[Infinity, 0], [0, 1]], [0.5, 0.5], [0.5, 0.5]]])
        rejects(() => nashGap(matrix, x, y), 'Lesson 6.2: "Validate its shape, finite entries and the distributions\' dimensions and probabilities." This input was accepted.');
    }],
    ['gap-invalid', 'Reject malformed matrices/distributions instead of coercing missing payoffs to zero.', () => {
      for (const [matrix, x, y] of [[[[]], [1], []], [[[NaN]], [1], [1]], [[[1, 2], [0]], [0.5, 0.5], [0.5, 0.5]], [[[0]], [0.2], [1]], [[[0]], [-1], [1]]]) rejects(() => nashGap(matrix, x, y), 'An invalid empirical game was accepted.');
    }],
  ]);
}

function responseContext({optimisticTrap = false, responder = 0, tied = false, budget = 20, left = null, maxDepth = 2, heuristics = null, model = null} = {}) {
  const leaf = value => ({terminal: true, returns: responder === 0 ? [value, -value] : [-value, value], currentPlayer: -1});
  const nodes = {
    root: {terminal: false, returns: null, currentPlayer: responder, actions: [{id: 11, to: 'left'}, {id: 29, to: 'right'}]},
    left: {terminal: false, returns: null, currentPlayer: 1 - responder, actions: [{id: 3, to: 'a'}, {id: 8, to: 'b'}]},
    right: {terminal: false, returns: null, currentPlayer: 1 - responder, actions: [{id: 4, to: 'c'}, {id: 9, to: 'd'}]},
    a: leaf(1), b: leaf(-1), c: leaf(tied ? 0.8 : 0.4), d: leaf(tied ? 0.8 : 0.4),
  };
  let used = 0, exceeded = false;
  const state = id => deepFreeze({id, ...copyData(nodes[id])});
  const oracle = {next(s, action) { if (used >= budget) { exceeded=true; throw new Error('Response budget exceeded.'); } used++; const edge = nodes[s.id].actions?.find(edge => edge.id === action); if (!edge) throw new Error('Illegal tree action.'); return state(edge.to); },
    legal: s => nodes[s.id].actions?.map(edge => edge.id) ?? [], terminal: s => nodes[s.id].terminal, returns: s => nodes[s.id].returns,
    currentPlayer: s => nodes[s.id].currentPlayer, get used() {return used;}, get remaining() {return budget - used;}, get exceeded(){return exceeded;}};
  return {state: state('root'), player: responder, legalActions: [11, 29], parameters: {maxDepth}, oracle, rng: createRng(1),
    evaluate: (s, p) => { const h = heuristics?.[s.id] ?? 0; return p === responder ? h : -h; },
    opponentPolicy(s) { const actions = nodes[s.id].actions; if (model) return model(s, actions); if (s.id === 'left') { const [p3, p8] = left ?? (optimisticTrap ? [0.1, 0.9] : [0.9, 0.1]); return [{actionId: 3, probability: p3}, {actionId: 8, probability: p8}]; } return actions.map(edge => ({actionId: edge.id, probability: 1 / actions.length})); }};
}
export function checkResponse(responsePolicy) {
  return suite('Counterpolicy against a fixed opponent model', [
    ['response-budget', 'Inadequate computation returns a legal fallback without hiding an overrun.',()=>{for(const budget of [0,1,3]){const context=responseContext({budget});const answer=responsePolicy(context);requireThat(context.legalActions.includes(answer?.actionId??answer),'Illegal fallback');requireThat(!context.oracle.exceeded && context.oracle.used<=budget,'Caught or uncaught budget overrun');}}],
    ['response-expectation', 'Use opponent probabilities: expected-value response can differ from minimax.', () => {
      const context = responseContext(), answer = responsePolicy(context); const action = answer?.actionId ?? answer;
      requireThat(action === 11, `Expected action 11 (return 0.8), not worst-case action 29 (return 0.4); got ${action}.`);
      requireThat(context.oracle.used <= 20, 'Response exceeded its simulation budget.');
    }],
    ['response-not-optimism', 'An opponent is not assumed to select the action most favorable to you.', () => {
      const answer = responsePolicy(responseContext({optimisticTrap: true}));
      requireThat((answer?.actionId ?? answer) === 29, 'Expected action 29; the tempting branch has mean -0.8 under this opponent.');
    }],
    ['response-mean', 'Average over the model, not only its most likely reply (lesson 6.1).', () => {
      const answer = responsePolicy(responseContext({left: [0.6, 0.4]}));
      requireThat((answer?.actionId ?? answer) === 29, 'Expected action 29 (mean 0.4), not 11 (mean 0.6 - 0.4 = 0.2). Lesson 6.1: "At a modeled opponent turn, average over its declared probabilities." Following only the most likely reply gives 11.');
    }],
    ['response-model', 'Reject an invalid opponent model instead of using it (lesson 6.1).', () => {
      const bad = {
        'sum above one': (s, actions) => actions.map(edge => ({actionId: edge.id, probability: 0.7})),
        'negative probability': (s, actions) => actions.map((edge, i) => ({actionId: edge.id, probability: i === 0 ? 1.5 : -0.5})),
        'illegal action': (s, actions) => [{actionId: 999, probability: 1}],
        'nonfinite probability': (s, actions) => actions.map(edge => ({actionId: edge.id, probability: NaN})),
      };
      for (const [name, model] of Object.entries(bad)) rejects(() => responsePolicy(responseContext({model})), `An opponent model with ${name} was used. Lesson 6.1: "Probabilities must be finite, nonnegative and sum to one within the declared tolerance. Every action must be legal in that state. An invalid distribution is a model error."`);
    }],
    ['response-depth', 'Respect parameters.maxDepth: evaluate at the horizon instead of searching past it (lesson 6.1).', () => {
      const answer = responsePolicy(responseContext({maxDepth: 1, heuristics: {left: -0.5, right: 0.3}}));
      requireThat((answer?.actionId ?? answer) === 29, 'With maxDepth 1 the horizon values are left -0.5 and right 0.3, so the response is 29. Lesson 6.1: the context supplies parameters.maxDepth, and "resource limits still apply". Searching past the horizon gives 11.');
    }],
    ['response-perspective', 'The responder may be either player; ties accept either maximizing action.', () => {
      const answer = responsePolicy(responseContext({responder: 1})); requireThat((answer?.actionId ?? answer) === 11, 'Player-1 utility was inverted.');
      const tied = responsePolicy(responseContext({tied: true})); requireThat([11, 29].includes(tied?.actionId ?? tied), 'A tied maximizing move was not returned.');
    }],
  ]);
}

```mjs
/** Public practice-check plumbing. This is not a held-out assessment. */
export function actionOf(result) {
  return Number.isInteger(result) ? result : result?.actionId;
}

export function requireCondition(condition, message, details = {}) {
  if (condition) return;
  const error = new Error(message);
  error.details = details;
  throw error;
}

export function runCheck(id, requirement, execute, lesson) {
  try {
    const evidence = execute() ?? {};
    return { id, ok: true, requirement, lesson, ...evidence };
  } catch (error) {
    return {
      id, ok: false, requirement, lesson,
      reason: error?.message ?? String(error),
      ...(error?.details ?? {}),
    };
  }
}

export function report(kind, checks) {
  return {
    schemaVersion: 1,
    kind,
    ok: checks.every(check => check.ok),
    scope: 'public-practice',
    claim: 'Finite public practice checks, not a hidden assessment, security audit, or evidence of learning.',
    checks,
  };
}

export function synchronousResult(fn, argument) {
  const result = fn(argument);
  requireCondition(!result || typeof result.then !== 'function',
    'This exercise uses synchronous decisions; returning a Promise is not an action.');
  return result;
}

/**
 * A small supplied game-tree adapter. Values are part of the game's declared
 * payoffs, not learner answers. Expected choices are checked by the caller.
 * It deliberately has the same oracle shape as the real game runner.
 */
export function makeTreeContext(fixture, {
  budget = 256, maxDepth = 3, seed = 17,
} = {}) {
  let used = 0;
  let overrun = false;
  let randomState = seed >>> 0;
  const nodes = fixture.nodes;
  function state(id) {
    const node = nodes[id];
    if (!node) throw new Error(`Unknown supplied tree state ${id}`);
    return Object.freeze({
      gameId: 'public-practice-tree', rulesHash: fixture.id,
      id, currentPlayer: node.player ?? 0,
      terminal: Object.hasOwn(node, 'value'),
      returns: Object.hasOwn(node, 'value') ? Object.freeze([node.value, -node.value]) : null,
      ply: node.ply ?? 0,
      board: Object.freeze([]),
    });
  }
  const root = state(fixture.root ?? 'root');
  function nodeFor(input) {
    requireCondition(input?.rulesHash === fixture.id && nodes[input?.id],
      'The search passed a state from another game or invented a tree state.');
    return nodes[input.id];
  }
  const oracle = Object.freeze({
    legal(input) {
      return Object.keys(nodeFor(input).moves ?? {}).map(Number).sort((a, b) => a - b);
    },
    next(input, action) {
      if (used >= budget) {
        overrun = true;
        throw new Error('SIMULATION_BUDGET_EXCEEDED');
      }
      used += 1;
      const node = nodeFor(input);
      requireCondition(Number.isInteger(action) && Object.hasOwn(node.moves ?? {}, action),
        'The search simulated an illegal action.', { observed: action, failureInput: input });
      return state(node.moves[action]);
    },
    terminal(input) { return Object.hasOwn(nodeFor(input), 'value'); },
    returns(input) {
      const node = nodeFor(input);
      return Object.hasOwn(node, 'value') ? [node.value, -node.value] : null;
    },
    currentPlayer(input) { return nodeFor(input).player ?? 0; },
    get used() { return used; },
    get remaining() { return Math.max(0, budget - used); },
    get overrun() { return overrun; },
    get exceeded() { return overrun; },
  });
  const context = Object.freeze({
    state: root, observation: root, player: root.currentPlayer,
    legalActions: Object.freeze(oracle.legal(root)),
    seed, parameters: Object.freeze({ maxDepth }), oracle,
    rng() {
      randomState = (Math.imul(randomState, 1664525) + 1013904223) >>> 0;
      return randomState / 4294967296;
    },
    evaluate(input, player) {
      const node = nodeFor(input);
      const value = Object.hasOwn(node, 'value') ? node.value : (node.heuristic ?? 0);
      return player === 0 ? value : -value;
    },
  });
  return context;
}

`courses/game-playing-agent-league/checks/index.mjs`:

```mjs
import { createState, initialState, generateScenario, legalActions, next } from '../lib/game.mjs';
import { createDecisionContext } from '../lib/runner.mjs';
import { actionOf, makeTreeContext, report, requireCondition, runCheck, synchronousResult } from './check-utils.mjs';
import { PRACTICE_TREES } from './practice-trees.mjs';

function callable(value, name) {
  requireCondition(typeof value === 'function', `Export ${name} as a function from the learner file.`);
}

function decision(fn, context) {
  const before = JSON.stringify(context.state);
  const output = synchronousResult(fn, context);
  const action = actionOf(output);
  requireCondition(Number.isInteger(action) && context.legalActions.includes(action),
    'Return an integer action from context.legalActions.',
    { failureInput: { state: context.state, legalActions: context.legalActions }, observed: output });
  requireCondition(JSON.stringify(context.state) === before,
    'The policy changed the supplied state. Decisions must leave observations unchanged.');
  requireCondition(!context.oracle.exceeded && !context.oracle.overrun,
    'Catching a budget error does not erase the overrun. Check oracle.remaining before simulating.');
  return action;
}

export function checkBaseline(chooseAction) {
  const checks = [];
  checks.push(runCheck('B01', 'Choose a legal action in several supplied game positions.', () => {
    callable(chooseAction, 'chooseAction');
    const states = [initialState(), ...[3, 19, 47, 101].map(seed => generateScenario(seed, 5).state)];
    for (const [index, state] of states.entries()) {
      decision(chooseAction, createDecisionContext(state, { seed: 100 + index, budget: 0 }));
    }
    return { positions: states.length };
  }, '01.1'));
  checks.push(runCheck('B02', 'Repeat a decision with the same state and supplied seed.', () => {
    callable(chooseAction, 'chooseAction');
    for (const seed of [0, 1, 2, 7, 43, 500, 4294967295]) {
      const state = initialState();
      const first = decision(chooseAction, createDecisionContext(state, { seed, budget: 0 }));
      const repeat = decision(chooseAction, createDecisionContext(state, { seed, budget: 0 }));
      requireCondition(first === repeat,
        'The same seed and state produced different decisions. Use context.rng(), not ambient randomness or persistent counters.',
        { failureInput: { seed, state }, observed: { first, repeat } });
    }
    return { repeatedSeeds: 7, boundary: 'same process; the supplied runner also supports a fresh-process policy rerun' };
  }, '01.2'));
  checks.push(runCheck('B03', 'A baseline works for either player without a simulation budget.', () => {
    callable(chooseAction, 'chooseAction');
    const state = generateScenario(23, 1).state;
    const context = createDecisionContext(state, { seed: 8, budget: 0 });
    decision(chooseAction, context);
    requireCondition(context.oracle.used === 0, 'The baseline attempted a simulation with zero credits.');
    return { actor: state.currentPlayer, simulationCredits: 0 };
  }, '01.3'));
  checks.push(runCheck('B04', 'Equal-width sampling over many seeds always lands inside the legal-action list.', () => {
    callable(chooseAction, 'chooseAction');
    const states = [initialState(), ...[3, 19, 47].map(seed => generateScenario(seed, 5).state)];
    for (const state of states) for (let i = 0; i < 300; i++) {
      const seed = Math.imul(i + 1, 2654435761) >>> 0; // spread over uint32; consecutive seeds start with similar values
      const context = createDecisionContext(state, { seed, budget: 0 });
      const output = synchronousResult(chooseAction, context), action = actionOf(output);
      requireCondition(Number.isInteger(action) && context.legalActions.includes(action),
        'Lesson 1.2: values lie in [0,1); "Divide the unit interval into" as many equal slots as there are legal actions. This seed selected outside the legal list, which an index of floor(r * (n + 1)) or similar does.',
        { failureInput: { seed, state, legalActions: context.legalActions }, observed: output });
    }
    return { seedsPerState: 300, states: states.length };
  }, '01.2'));
  return report('baseline', checks);
}

function position(pawns0, pawns1, currentPlayer = 0) {
  const board = Array(25).fill(-1);
  for (const cell of pawns0) board[cell] = 0;
  for (const cell of pawns1) board[cell] = 1;
  return createState({ board, currentPlayer });
}

function evaluated(evaluate, state, player) {
  const before = JSON.stringify(state);
  const value = evaluate(state, player);
  requireCondition(typeof value === 'number' && Number.isFinite(value),
    'Evaluation must return a finite number.', { failureInput: { state, player }, observed: value });
  requireCondition(JSON.stringify(state) === before, 'Evaluation changed its input state.');
  return value;
}

export function checkEvaluation(evaluate) {
  const checks = [];
  checks.push(runCheck('E01', 'Terminal values equal the requested player’s official return.', () => {
    callable(evaluate, 'evaluate');
    const states = [position([22], [8]), position([17], [2])];
    for (const state of states) for (const player of [0, 1]) {
      const value = evaluated(evaluate, state, player);
      requireCondition(value === state.returns[player],
        'A terminal result is exact and is measured from the requested player’s perspective.',
        { failureInput: { state, player }, observed: value, expected: state.returns[player] });
    }
    return { terminalPlayerCases: 4 };
  }, '02.1'));
  checks.push(runCheck('E02', 'Nonterminal values are bounded and reverse sign with the requested player.', () => {
    callable(evaluate, 'evaluate');
    const states = [initialState(), position([10, 12], [18]), position([6], [12, 14]), position([17], [8])];
    const values = [];
    for (const state of states) {
      const v0 = evaluated(evaluate, state, 0);
      const v1 = evaluated(evaluate, state, 1);
      requireCondition(Math.abs(v0) <= 0.99 && Math.abs(v1) <= 0.99,
        'A nonterminal estimate must stay inside [-0.99, 0.99], below a proved win.',
        { failureInput: state, observed: [v0, v1] });
      requireCondition(Math.abs(v0 + v1) < 1e-10,
        'The same zero-sum position must have opposite evaluations for the two requested players.',
        { failureInput: state, observed: [v0, v1] });
      values.push(v0);
    }
    requireCondition(new Set(values.map(value => value.toFixed(10))).size > 1,
      'This evaluator assigns the same score to every tested nonterminal position. Add a state-dependent feature; no exact weight vector is required.',
      { observed: values });
    return { positions: states.length, valuesForPlayer0: values, exactWeightsRequired: false };
  }, '02.1'));
  checks.push(runCheck('E03', 'Repeated evaluation is pure and deterministic.', () => {
    callable(evaluate, 'evaluate');
    const state = position([10, 13], [6, 19], 1);
    for (const player of [0, 1]) {
      const first = evaluated(evaluate, state, player);
      const second = evaluated(evaluate, state, player);
      requireCondition(first === second, 'Evaluation changed without any change in state or requested player.',
        { failureInput: { state, player }, observed: [first, second] });
    }
  }, '02.1'));
  checks.push(runCheck('E04', 'Even a lopsided nonterminal position stays inside [-0.99, 0.99].', () => {
    callable(evaluate, 'evaluate');
    const states = [position([15, 16, 17, 18, 19], [24]), position([15, 16, 17, 18, 19], [24], 1), position([0], [5, 6, 7, 8, 9], 1), position([0], [5, 6, 7, 8, 9])];
    for (const state of states) {
      requireCondition(!state.terminal, 'Fixture error: this teaching position must be nonterminal.', { failureInput: state });
      for (const player of [0, 1]) {
        const value = evaluated(evaluate, state, player);
        requireCondition(Math.abs(value) <= 0.99,
          'Lesson 2.1: "Nonterminal heuristic scores in this course lie between -0.99 and +0.99. Terminal outcomes remain exactly -1 and +1." Cap or squash the score.',
          { failureInput: { state, player }, observed: value });
      }
    }
    return { positions: states.length };
  }, '02.1'));
  return report('evaluation', checks);
}

export function checkSearch(search, { evaluate } = {}) {
  const checks = PRACTICE_TREES.map((fixture, index) => runCheck(`S${String(index + 1).padStart(2, '0')}`,
    fixture.requirement, () => {
      callable(search, 'search');
      const context = makeTreeContext(fixture, { maxDepth: fixture.maxDepth, budget: 256 });
      const action = decision(search, context);
      requireCondition(fixture.expected.includes(action),
        'The selected action does not meet this practice tree’s requested search contract. Trace the actual actor, horizon and terminal returns.',
        { failureInput: { tree: fixture, maxDepth: fixture.maxDepth }, observed: action, acceptedActions: fixture.expected });
      return { action, simulationCredits: context.oracle.used };
    }, index === 5 ? '02.3' : '02.2'));

  for (const budget of [0, 1, 3]) {
    checks.push(runCheck(`S-budget-${budget}`, 'An insufficient budget still returns a legal move without an extra simulation.', () => {
      callable(search, 'search');
      const context = makeTreeContext(PRACTICE_TREES[0], { budget, maxDepth: 4 });
      const action = decision(search, context);
      requireCondition(context.oracle.used <= budget && !context.oracle.overrun,
        'A simulation exceeded the allowed credits, even if its exception was caught.');
      return { budget, action, simulationCredits: context.oracle.used, strengthClaim: 'none at inadequate budget' };
    }, '02.3'));
  }
  checks.push(runCheck('S-terminal-first', 'Test for a terminal state before applying the depth limit or the heuristic.', () => {
    callable(search, 'search');
    const fixture = { id: 'terminal-at-horizon', maxDepth: 1, nodes: {
      root: { player: 0, moves: { 1: 'win', 2: 'promising' } },
      win: { value: 1, heuristic: 0.5 },
      promising: { player: 1, heuristic: 0.9, moves: { 21: 'draw' } },
      draw: { value: 0 },
    } };
    const base = makeTreeContext(fixture, { maxDepth: 1, budget: 16 });
    const context = { ...base, evaluate(input, player) { const h = fixture.nodes[input?.id]?.heuristic ?? 0; return player === 0 ? h : -h; } };
    const action = decision(search, context);
    requireCondition(action === 1,
      'Lesson 2.1: "Terminal handling comes before any depth limit or heuristic." Move 1 reaches a terminal win (+1) on the last allowed edge; the heuristic would score it 0.5 and prefer move 2 (0.9).',
      { failureInput: { tree: fixture, maxDepth: 1 }, observed: action, acceptedActions: [1] });
    return { action, simulationCredits: context.oracle.used };
  }, '02.1'));
  checks.push(runCheck('S-game', 'Connect the same search to the supplied real game and recognize an immediate win.', () => {
    callable(search, 'search');
    callable(evaluate, 'evaluate');
    for (const player of [0, 1]) {
      const state = position([17], [7], player);
      const context = { ...createDecisionContext(state, { budget: 64, seed: 9, parameters: { maxDepth: 2 } }), evaluate };
      const action = decision(search, context);
      const result = next(state, action).state;
      requireCondition(result.terminal && result.returns[player] === 1,
        'This teaching position has a legal immediate win. The returned move did not take one.',
        { failureInput: { state, legalActions: legalActions(state) }, observed: { action, result } });
    }
    return { winningSeats: 2 };
  }, '02.2'));
  return report('search', checks);
}
