# 6.3 Read cycles that a single ranking hides

Agent A beats B, B beats C, and C beats A. You will recognize this nontransitive structure and explain why a single ordered leaderboard cannot capture every matchup.

## Read the pairwise relation first

A relation is transitive when A being above B and B above C implies A above C. Competitive policies need not satisfy that property. Different strategies can expose different weaknesses. Nontransitivity therefore concerns interactions, not merely uncertainty in a scalar skill number.

Consider an explicitly synthetic exact matrix with zeros on its diagonal: A earns +1 against B and -1 against C; B earns +1 against C and -1 against A; C earns +1 against A and -1 against B. Against a uniform mixture of the other listed strategies, no one is a universal champion. Yet choosing any single policy leaves a clear counter-policy in the set.

A directed graph makes this structure visible. Draw an edge from a policy to one it defeats under the declared comparison rule. The three edges above form a directed cycle. Retain the underlying matrix: a graph alone can hide the size and uncertainty of each advantage.

**Commit 6.3-p1.** A scoreboard sorts the synthetic cycle by policy name after all three receive the same average. Explain what the order means and why calling the first row the strongest policy would be misleading. Identify the information a reader needs beside the scalar score.

```sh
node cli.mjs attempt 6.3-p1 --answer 'your leaderboard interpretation'
node cli.mjs feedback 6.3-p1
```

## Do not manufacture a cycle from missing or noisy results

In the real league, pairwise payoffs are estimates from finite games. An unplayed pair is unknown, not a tie. A tiny positive mean is not automatically a reliable directional edge. Show the complete count, interval procedure, comparison status and any missing games for each pair.

If you inspect many potential edges, recall the selection problem from 4.3. A cycle found after searching many noisy comparisons is descriptive unless the simultaneous inference or confirmation plan supports a stronger claim. Do not choose the edge threshold after looking at the plot merely to make a dramatic loop appear.

The course includes an exact analytic cycle control so that you can demonstrate correct reasoning even if your particular game population does not develop a natural cycle. A genuinely transitive-looking population is a valid observation. Failing to produce a dramatic cycle is not a reason to alter results.

**Commit 6.3-p2.** A beats B in complete paired evidence and B beats C, but A versus C was never run. What graph can you draw? What claim must remain open, and which missing comparison would resolve it under the same plan?

```sh
node cli.mjs attempt 6.3-p2 --answer 'your graph and missing evidence'
node cli.mjs feedback 6.3-p2
```

## Choose a population for a declared opponent distribution

A mixture can reduce the weakness of committing to one predictable policy. In the exact cyclic example, a uniform mixture has zero restricted gap against those three strategies. That conclusion depends on the complete specified matrix. Adding a stronger unlisted response can change it.

The league samples a member once per game. Its average payoff against an independently sampled opposing mixture is the corresponding weighted matrix average when the matrix describes those same frozen policies and conditions. Mixing policies anew at every turn changes the policy and requires new evaluation; the old matrix is no longer sufficient.

A single scalar remains useful for a specific decision—for example, expected utility against a stated opponent mixture. Label that mixture and keep the payoff structure visible. A policy can be best for today's target distribution without being generally best or safe against every response.

**Commit 6.3-p3.** A deployment expects one opponent 90% of the time and the other two only 5% each. Explain why the best expected-return choice may differ from a low-gap mixture. Propose a report that shows the tradeoff and a test for what happens if the opponent distribution changes.

```sh
node cli.mjs attempt 6.3-p3 --answer 'your objective tradeoff and test'
node cli.mjs feedback 6.3-p3
```

# 7.1 Assemble a replayable season

Your newest policy has beaten every opponent you tried yesterday, but yesterday's files do not say which parameters or starting positions were used. Assemble a season whose claim can be checked by rerunning the same decisions and games.

## The season is a declared experiment

A season starts with an evaluation plan. The plan names the rules, the exact policy snapshots, the starting scenarios, both seat assignments, the random seeds and the budget. Freeze those fields before the first scored game. A friendly display name such as `champion` is not enough: changing its parameters changes the policy even when the name stays the same.

The six required roles are a supplied random baseline, a supplied greedy baseline, your search policy, your learned-value search policy, an older learned snapshot and a counter-policy. They should differ in behavior or learned parameters. Merely giving the same program six names does not create a league. You may add two more variants if you have a reason to compare them.

For every unordered pair of policies, play both seat assignments on the same starting scenario. Repeat using the declared policy-randomness seeds. This arrangement makes the roster explicit and preserves useful pairing. The two seat games are related observations; they are not two independent draws of a new scenario.

**Commit before continuing:** item `7.1-p1` asks you to calculate the complete match count for a declared small season. Use `node cli.mjs attempt 7.1-p1 --answer 'your count and reasoning'`, then request feedback.

**Practice 7.1-p1:** A season has six policies, three scenarios, both seats and two randomness replicates. How many games are planned? Explain the unit you counted.

## From a missing result to a complete denominator

Suppose a three-policy season uses two scenarios, both seats and one randomness replicate. There are three unordered policy pairs and four games per pair. The plan therefore expects twelve uniquely identified games. If eleven records exist, the report does not silently redefine the season as eleven games. It identifies the missing key.

A policy that returns an illegal action can legitimately forfeit under the declared rules. A host process that crashes before it records a result does not establish that either policy lost. Preserve that failure and retry the same planned game with a linked reason. A duplicate retry must not count twice. Two different outcomes for the same supposedly deterministic match identity are an inconsistency to investigate, not an invitation to keep the favorable one.

Coverage is part of the result. Before computing a headline, reconcile expected keys, completed results, policy failures and unresolved infrastructure failures. This work is evaluation logic, not a demand that you build a database or job scheduler; the supplied host owns storage and execution.

**Apply it:** commit item `7.1-p2` before viewing feedback. Decide what a report should do with one missing game and one duplicate result.

**Practice 7.1-p2:** Your planned twelve-game season has eleven distinct results and a duplicate of one of those results. May you report twelve completed games? What should happen next?

## Two different kinds of replay

Trajectory replay starts from the recorded initial state and applies the recorded actions through the supplied game engine. It checks the next state and the official result at every step. This establishes that the actions form the reported game. It does not establish that the named policy chose those actions.

Policy rerun goes further. It loads the same policy code and parameters, gives them the same observations and private random stream, enforces the same budget and compares the decisions. Then trajectory replay checks the consequences. Both identities matter. A correct board animation can display a fabricated attribution.

The viewer is a way to inspect where a game changed. It displays data; it does not certify that the data is authentic. Use the command-line verifier for the recorded rules and source identity. If a later rule patch changes the game's semantics, keep the old rule identity with old records. Never recompute an old match with new rules while retaining the old label.

**Transfer:** item `7.1-p3` gives a replay that is legal but has the wrong policy hash. Explain the strongest claim it still supports and the claim it cannot support.

**Practice 7.1-p3:** A recorded action sequence replays legally to the reported winner, but its named policy hash differs from the supplied policy file. What can you claim?

## Build and retain

Assemble a development season through the supplied league runner using your actual learner functions. Inspect a loss, trace its first consequential decision and link that game ID in your notes. Then freeze the final plan and execute its entire roster. Keep the plan, snapshots, raw matches, coverage report and your written claim together. If your learner functions are unfinished, finish their earlier checks first; a supplied demonstration is useful for learning the interface but does not replace your season.

The module's evidence is a complete reproducible season, not a particular champion. Record the first report and any repaired report as different attempts.

# 7.2 Choose a population rather than one lucky winner

Your highest-scoring policy loses consistently to an older opponent that the training loop nearly discarded. Choose a retained population and a deployment distribution using the opponents and evidence you actually have.

## A policy's score depends on who it meets

An average score is an expectation under an opponent distribution. Changing that distribution can change the ordering of policies. If a league contains many copies of an easy opponent, a specialist against that opponent may look impressive. Its score does not establish robustness against a different pool.

Begin with the pairwise payoff matrix. Each entry states how one frozen policy performs against another under the same scenario and seat schedule. Missing entries remain missing. They are not draws. Look for large weaknesses, not just the row with the largest average. If the confidence intervals are broad, distinguish an apparent advantage from a supported one.

As a worked comparison, imagine two candidates. Candidate A scores well against the most frequent training opponents but has a large loss against a rare archived one. Candidate B is slightly worse against the frequent opponents and much better against the rare one. Under the current frequency weighting, A can have the larger average. Under a policy that protects against the worst measured matchup, B can be preferable. Neither conclusion is meaningful until the selection objective is stated.

**Commit:** item `7.2-p1` asks which information is missing from a claim that one candidate is simply “better.” State the objective and evidence you would need, then inspect feedback.

**Practice 7.2-p1:** Policy A has the higher mean score while policy B has the better worst measured matchup. What is missing from the statement that A is better?

## Retaining a policy can have experimental value

An archived policy can be useful even when it is not selected for deployment. It can expose a weakness in newer policies. Removing it from active training may save computation, but removing its records destroys evidence about forgetting. Keep the immutable snapshot and its results even when its active sampling weight becomes zero.

Retention therefore has two decisions: what remains in the archive, and what receives current training probability. The supplied host retains history. You choose active opponents and weights. A fixed budget forces tradeoffs: spreading samples over more policies improves coverage but leaves fewer samples per matchup. Repeatedly sampling only the newest rival can produce fast local improvement and miss older failures.

Use your earlier sampler and admission rule. Compare the candidate against the same frozen evaluation pool used for its predecessor. If a new policy improves one family and harms another, preserve both facts. A defensible admission rule can retain the candidate for its complementary behavior while keeping the predecessor. It need not pretend that every accepted policy dominates all earlier ones.

**Apply it:** commit item `7.2-p2` about retaining a losing historical policy before revealing the answer.

**Practice 7.2-p2:** An old policy loses to most of the pool but exposes a reproducible weakness in the newest candidate. Give a defensible reason to retain it.

## A mixture has precise semantics

In this course, a mixture chooses one frozen policy at the start of each game and uses it throughout that game. The choice is private to that side. This produces a distribution over complete policies. Choosing a different policy at every move is a different strategy: moves that make sense as part of one plan may interact badly with another policy's continuation.

A matrix-distribution helper may suggest mixture weights. Inspect its reported restricted gap, numerical tolerance and iteration budget. An optimizer stopping is not a certificate of exact equilibrium. More importantly, even an exact solution of the measured policy matrix protects only against the strategies represented by that matrix. A new opponent can still expose a weakness.

Uniform weights are a useful baseline, not a universal solution. A nonuniform distribution is acceptable when you state what it optimizes and evaluate the actual resulting policy-selection procedure. Keep its random seed and weights with the deployment snapshot. Avoid choosing weights after seeing the final test results and then reporting those same results as independent confirmation.

**Transfer:** item `7.2-p3` compares per-game and per-move switching. Explain why the old matrix cannot automatically certify the new behavior.

**Practice 7.2-p3:** You evaluated a mixture that chooses one policy per game. You now choose a fresh policy each move using the same weights. Does the old payoff matrix certify the new policy?

## Your deliverable

Retain six distinct policy roles and state which ones receive training and deployment weight. Explain one inclusion and one exclusion or reduced weight using observed matchups. Compare your choice with uniform historical sampling under equal budgets. A negative or inconclusive comparison is allowed; the artifact must still contain a valid distribution, complete evaluation and honest interpretation.

# 7.3 Audit the evidence behind the headline

A report says the league has become harder to exploit, but its newer run used more search and omitted two failed games. Audit the evidence before accepting the headline.

## Start with the claim's subject

“This frozen policy scored higher on these sixteen scenarios” is a different claim from “this training method produces stronger policies.” The first concerns one set of code and parameters. The second concerns a distribution over training runs. Replaying many games from one trained policy does not create independent training runs.

Name the subject, comparison and domain. Include the game/rule version, opponent pool, scenario-generation process, training replicas, evaluation replicas and compute budget. The final report can be concise because those details live in linked manifests. It cannot omit them from the evidence entirely.

As a worked audit, consider a new checkpoint compared with an older checkpoint at the same rules and scenario roster. The new checkpoint receives twice as many simulation calls per decision. A higher score supports a comparison between those two deployed configurations. It does not isolate the contribution of training. To investigate learning, compare them at a matched budget or report the combined configuration change explicitly.

**Commit:** item `7.3-p1` asks you to rewrite an overbroad result into a claim the supplied evidence can support.

**Practice 7.3-p1:** One trained checkpoint beats its predecessor on a fixed roster, but used twice the search budget. Rewrite the claim without attributing the gain to learning alone.

## Check identity, coverage and independence

First verify identity. The policy source, parameter file and rule hashes in the report must match the executed records. Second verify coverage. Every expected game has one qualified result or a visible unresolved failure. Third inspect independence and selection. Did the reported final scenarios influence feature choice, training duration, opponent weights or checkpoint selection?

If they did, the run is useful exploratory evidence. It is no longer untouched confirmation of the final choice. Preserve it, label it and use a fresh confirmation set for a new confirmatory claim. Rewriting filenames or reseeding the same disclosed tiny roster does not necessarily create a genuinely new test.

The same care applies to intervals. Show the resampling unit and count. Correlated moves are not independent samples. A narrow interval produced by resampling thousands of moves from a few games can be very precise about the wrong experiment. Repeatedly checking an ordinary interval and stopping when it looks favorable also changes its interpretation.

**Apply it:** commit item `7.3-p2` about a final set used to choose between three model variants. Then compare your disposition with the feedback.

**Practice 7.3-p2:** You chose the best of three feature variants after looking at final-test scores. How should those scores now be labeled, and what would confirmation require?

## Search for a reason your interpretation could fail

An audit is stronger when it contains a counterexample. Inspect the policy's worst measured matchup, a failed or low-performing training run, and a scenario where the apparent improvement reverses. Ask whether the mechanism in your explanation predicts these cases too.

If you claim lower exploitability, identify the responder family and its search/training budget. A responder finding no profitable deviation does not prove that none exists. For a tiny game you can enumerate, exact best-response evidence can support an exact gap. For the larger league, your result normally remains empirical vulnerability to tested responders.

Include a valid alternative explanation. Perhaps a value model improved tactical ordering rather than its numerical accuracy. Perhaps a population helped because it retained a particular counter, not because more opponents are always better. An ablation can distinguish these explanations. If it was not run, record the uncertainty rather than inventing a mechanism from the outcome alone.

**Transfer:** item `7.3-p3` asks what to report when the counter-policy fails to find a win. The correct level of confidence depends on what was searched, not on the desired story.

**Practice 7.3-p3:** A responder searched for ten minutes and found no winning policy. Is the champion unexploitable? State a defensible conclusion.

## Evidence to retain

Keep your frozen plan, source and parameter identities, complete match roster, failures, interval configuration, first report and revised report. Link at least one replay supporting your diagnosis. Have another person or a fresh process rerun from those artifacts without relying on your working directory's unnamed current files.

Passing the audit means your claims match your evidence. It does not mean your policy must win, that your method is universally best, or that the course has proved a learning effect.

# 8.1 Freeze a prediction before the patch

Your league is about to receive a rule change, and you want to know whether its design transfers. Commit a prediction and evaluation plan before learning the exact change.

## Prediction creates a comparison with your earlier understanding

A useful prediction names an assumption and a consequence. “Something might break” cannot distinguish insight from hindsight. “My route planner's proof needs every edge cost to be nonnegative, so I expect its greedy search can return a wrong route once a change makes an edge negative” can be checked. It also names what would show it wrong: the greedy route still matching an exhaustive search on every test map built around a negative edge. The worked example below develops this case.

Your prediction is not a scored guess of a secret answer. It records what your current model of the system implies. If it is wrong, retain it and explain why. Editing the prediction after seeing the patch removes the evidence of that change in understanding.

As a worked example from another domain, a route planner assumes all edges have nonnegative cost. A new discount can introduce a negative edge. Before seeing the map, the author predicts that a greedy shortest-path implementation may fail and names the condition needed by its proof. The value lies in connecting the algorithm's premise to its behavior, not in guessing the exact discounted road.

**Commit:** item `8.1-p1` asks for a testable transfer prediction about an assumption your own agent makes. Save it before you open lesson 8.2, this item's feedback or any challenge text. Navigation is open, so keeping this order is your own discipline. The item also asks you to declare what you had read before predicting. If you have already read 8.2, say so: that is an exposure record, not a fault, and the prediction then counts as assisted practice.

**Practice 8.1-p1:** Write a testable prediction about one assumption your current search or value model makes. Name the consequence you expect and an observation that would show the prediction was wrong. Then declare what you had read before predicting: lesson 8.2, this item's feedback, or any rule-change or challenge text.

## Freeze the experiment as well as the prose

Save the old policy source and parameters, ordinary-game results, responder configuration, training budget and evaluation plan. Do not overwrite the champion in place. A before/after comparison needs a real before artifact.

The plan should separate adaptation from evaluation. Allocate the same allowed simulation credits to the methods being compared. Name the ordinary-rule checks you will rerun as well as the new-rule checks. Otherwise an adaptation that handles the patch by breaking ordinary play could be called an unqualified improvement.

Decide how you will treat an incomplete adaptation run. A host interruption is not a loss. An illegal policy action is a policy failure under the declared contract. Preserve those distinctions, as in the earlier season. They do not disappear because this is the capstone.

**Apply it:** commit item `8.1-p2` about an old checkpoint overwritten by the adaptation process. Identify what evidence was lost and what can still be recovered honestly.

**Practice 8.1-p2:** You overwrote the old champion parameters while adapting. Why is this a problem, and what can you honestly do now?

## A practice patch is not a held-out assessment

This package ships worked examples and analysis items. It ships no patched game simulator and no runnable practice patch. The rule change discussed in lesson 8.2 is hypothetical, and because every learner can read it, it is not a secret assessment item. The independently administered capstone uses a new instance issued separately from the public package. Its exact rule, starting positions and scoring controls should not have appeared in your worked examples.

For that separately issued challenge, the instructor supplies the changed simulator and its written rules. You are not expected to guess hidden rules or implement a new engine. Your work is to reason about the changed assumptions and adapt the policy, learned representation or experiment where needed.

If you have already seen the challenge's private controls or reference answer, label that attempt assisted and use a fresh independently issued instance for a claim of unassisted transfer. Do not hide prior exposure. That record helps distinguish a learning exercise from measurement.

**Transfer:** item `8.1-p3` asks whether a new seed for a publicly disclosed worked patch automatically creates a held-out test, and which kind of novelty would matter.

**Practice 8.1-p3:** A learner has read a worked solution to a public rule patch. They rerun it with a new random seed. Is this automatically an unassisted held-out transfer assessment? Which kind of novelty would matter?

## Your before artifact

Export the prediction, old snapshots and plan. Record assistance used in reaching the prediction. Then stop changing the before artifact. When the challenge arrives, keep the instructor's rule version and challenge identity with your new work. The final lesson compares your prediction with the actual failure or success; it does not erase the first answer.

## What you can complete now, and where to stop

All nine analysis items in this module, `8.1-p1` to `8.3-p3`, can be completed now. They ask for reasoning about worked examples and hypothetical cases, and none of them needs a patched simulator. Commit `8.1-p1` first, then work through lessons 8.2 and 8.3.

When the nine items are committed, freeze and export the before artifact as described above, if you have not already. Then stop executable work. Do not write a rule patch, a second engine or a stand-in for the challenge. Executable adaptation starts only when an instructor supplies a versioned challenge: the rules, the simulator, conformance examples, the challenge identity, and the budget and evaluation instructions.

`courses/game-playing-agent-league/lessons/08-2-adapt.md`:

```md
# 8.2 Adapt under the original compute budget

This lesson uses a hypothetical rule change to practise diagnosis. No patched game simulator ships in this package. Answer the three analysis items using the worked examples below. The executable adaptation steps apply after an instructor supplies a versioned challenge.

## Read the new contract before changing the code

The base game alternates players, but your search interface exposes the actual current player. Those facts were deliberately separate. If a new rule sometimes gives the same player another move, a recursion that simply negates every returned value may apply the wrong perspective. A recursion that asks who acts next has a chance to remain correct without a structural rewrite.

When an instructor supplies a challenge, do not infer its rules from an animation. Read the instructor's written rules, inspect the supplied conformance examples and check the state fields. Keep the rule version and challenge identity with your work. New counters can matter to future legal moves. Two equal boards with different remaining privileges are different states and need different cache identities.

As a worked diagnostic on a generic tree, suppose the root and its child are both controlled by the maximizing player. At the child, the player can select between two outcomes. Treating that child as an opponent turn predicts the wrong choice. The mistake concerns who owns the decision, not the arithmetic sign of the terminal reward. Use an explicit actor trace to identify where your implementation's assumption diverges.

**Commit:** item `8.2-p1` asks you to locate the kind of component that can fail even when the visible board and legal-action encoding stay the same.

**Practice 8.2-p1:** The board and action IDs look unchanged, but a new visible phase field changes who moves next. Name two components that may still be wrong.

## Reproduce one failure before making a broad repair

**Conditional on an instructor-supplied challenge:** the steps in this section are executable work. They apply once an instructor has supplied the rules and the simulator. Until then, read them as the method that item `8.2-p2` asks you to reason about.

Run the frozen old policy under the instructor-supplied rules and the fixed evaluation plan. Find one small failing trace. Record its initial state, rule identity, action sequence and first consequential decision. A smaller witness is easier to reason about than an average season score.

State a hypothesis before editing. Perhaps the search backup assumes alternation, the transposition key omits a new counter, or the learned feature representation collapses strategically different states. Make the narrow change that addresses the hypothesis. Reproduce the witness, then test fresh positions. A patch that hardcodes the observed action can fix one replay while leaving the actual assumption unchanged.

If your generic policy already handles the changed rule, do not add a meaningless edit to look busy. Demonstrate that it obeys the new contract, explain why, and test the new state field and actor cases. Transfer can be preservation of a valid abstraction.

**Apply it:** commit item `8.2-p2` comparing a hardcoded trace repair with a state-representation repair. Then inspect feedback and revise your diagnosis if needed.

**Practice 8.2-p2:** A repair returns the known winning move whenever the failing board appears. Another repair includes the new phase in the state representation and follows the actual actor. Which better addresses the hypothesis, and what must still be tested?

## Learning and evaluation can break independently of search

**Conditional on an instructor-supplied challenge:** refitting a model and running the evaluations described below are executable work. Item `8.2-p3` can be answered now from the reasoning alone.

A value model may have learned returns under the ordinary rule distribution. Correct search does not make those estimates automatically calibrated under the patch. New counters may need representation; different move sequences can change which training examples occur. If you refit the model, retain its new training provenance and count its computation against the adaptation budget.

Evaluate both ordinary and changed rules. Keep the original budget, opponent identities and declared scenario process for each comparison. If you choose among multiple adaptation candidates using a selection set, freeze the choice before final evaluation. A patch does not excuse test-set tuning.

For response search, distinguish a responder's limited failure from the absence of any exploit. The new game may enlarge the set of relevant strategies. Your old response family might simply be too narrow to detect the new weakness.

**Transfer:** item `8.2-p3` asks what you can conclude when the ordinary policy's score holds but its new-rule feature errors grow. Keep prediction quality, playing strength and uncertainty separate.

**Practice 8.2-p3:** After a patch, win rate appears unchanged but value prediction error increases. Does unchanged win rate prove the model still represents the game equally well?

## Your adapted artifact

**Conditional on an instructor-supplied challenge:** this artifact exists only after you have adapted to a supplied challenge. Keep the original policy, adapted policy or justified unchanged policy, explanation of the changed premise, minimal witness, fresh checks, training credits and both evaluation reports. The host and game remain supplied to you; the changed game comes from the instructor. Your capstone demonstrates the target reasoning and policy changes; it does not require building a second game engine.

```

`courses/game-playing-agent-league/lessons/08-3-defend-transfer.md`:

```md
# 8.3 Defend what transferred and what did not

Suppose your adapted policy wins more often under the changed rules but regresses on ordinary play. These gains and regressions are hypothetical until an instructor-supplied challenge produces actual results. Defend a conclusion that preserves both results and the limits of the experiment.

## Compare the prediction with the actual mechanism

Retrieve your pre-patch prediction without rewriting it. Identify the assumptions that survived, the ones that failed and the evidence supporting each judgment. If you predicted a search bug but the real problem was a value feature, explain the distinction. A revised mental model is useful evidence of learning; a retroactively perfect prediction is not.

Use a causal explanation proportional to the evidence. If changing one cache key fixes the minimal witness and several fresh structurally similar positions, that supports the cache hypothesis. It does not prove that every remaining loss has the same cause. If you changed search, features and training budget at once, the result describes that combined configuration. An ablation is needed to separate their contributions.

**Commit:** item `8.3-p1` asks you to explain a hypothetical mismatch between the original prediction and the observed repair, and to name one observation that would weaken your new explanation.

**Practice 8.3-p1:** Your prediction blamed turn alternation, but fixing an omitted state counter repairs the witness. How should the final report handle the original prediction, and what observation would weaken your new explanation?

## The report needs a complete comparison

Show the old and adapted configurations on ordinary and changed rules. Name the opponent pool, scenario set, seeds, budgets and unresolved failures for each cell. Do not omit ordinary-rule regression because the headline concerns adaptation. A deployment decision can legitimately prefer the adapted policy for the new rules while keeping the earlier one for the old rules.

As a worked decision, imagine an adaptation that fixes every issued conformance case but has an uncertain tournament difference. You can conclude that it satisfies those contract cases. You cannot conclude that it improves average playing strength if the comparison is too noisy. Conversely, a high observed win rate does not excuse an illegal action in a contract case. Correctness and empirical performance answer different questions.

If there are too few independent scenarios or training replicas to distinguish candidates, say so. A wider honest interval is more useful than a narrow one obtained by counting correlated moves as independent evidence. Keep the finite-roster average visible even when you cannot generalize confidently beyond it.

**Apply it:** commit item `8.3-p2` about a hypothetical adaptation with new-rule gains and ordinary-rule losses. State a deployment recommendation with its domain.

**Practice 8.3-p2:** The adapted policy improves under the new rule and regresses under the old rule. Give a scoped deployment recommendation.

## Explain the response boundary

The capstone should include an attempt to find a counter-strategy. Report the responder family, computation and observed outcome. An exact tiny-game best response supports a statement about that tiny game. An approximate responder against the actual league supports a statement about the tested search, not universal robustness.

If a new opponent breaks the adapted policy, retain the loss and consider whether it changes the recommended population. The purpose of the league is to reveal weaknesses as well as improvements. A course that ends with every failed experiment removed would teach the wrong habit.

A separately issued held-out assessment is evidence about your performance on that instance. It is not a guarantee of transfer to every game, every rule change or every future adversary. Keep assistance and prior exposure visible. The report's confidence should grow with independent evidence, not with the amount of code written.

**Transfer:** item `8.3-p3` asks you to distinguish an exact tiny-game result, a finite empirical season and an unbounded claim of robustness. Give each the correct scope.

**Practice 8.3-p3:** Separate these claims: exact zero gap in an enumerated tiny game; no exploit found in a six-policy season; no adversary can ever beat the agent. Which are supported by their stated evidence?

## Final evidence package

Until an instructor-supplied challenge has produced actual results, you have no before/after numbers of your own. Your module 8 evidence then consists of the nine committed analysis items and the frozen before artifact, and it claims no transfer result.

Export your first prediction, original and revised work, all assistance records, rule identities, before/after plans, raw matches, coverage, numerical summaries and selected replays. The package should let a reviewer reconstruct the decisions rather than rely on your summary alone.

The full course is accepted only after the complete learner flow and independent assessment are verified. Its eventual publication is a separate operational step: a local package is not a live Free to Learn course. Your own capstone is complete when it satisfies the issued rubric with reproducible evidence, whether the final recommendation is one champion, a mixture or a carefully bounded inconclusive result.

```

`courses/game-playing-agent-league/lib/check-worker.mjs`:

```mjs
// Local reliability boundary only. A Node worker is not a hostile-code sandbox.
import {parentPort, workerData} from 'node:worker_threads';
import {pathToFileURL} from 'node:url';
import {join} from 'node:path';
try {
  const checks = await import('../checks/index.mjs');
  let result;
  if (workerData.module === '1') {
    const {chooseAction} = await import(pathToFileURL(join(workerData.root, 'learner/baseline.mjs')));
    result = await checks.checkBaseline(chooseAction);
  } else if (['2', 'evaluation', 'search'].includes(workerData.module)) {
    const {evaluate} = await import(pathToFileURL(join(workerData.root, 'learner/evaluation.mjs')));
    if (workerData.module === 'evaluation') result = await checks.checkEvaluation(evaluate);
    else {
      const {search} = await import(pathToFileURL(join(workerData.root, 'learner/search.mjs')));
      if (workerData.module === 'search') result = await checks.checkSearch(search, {evaluate});
      else {
        result = {evaluation: await checks.checkEvaluation(evaluate), search: await checks.checkSearch(search, {evaluate})};
        result.ok = result.evaluation.ok && result.search.ok;
      }
    }
  } else {
    const advanced = await import('../checks/advanced.mjs');
    const load = file => import(pathToFileURL(join(workerData.root, 'learner', file)));
    if (workerData.module === '3') result = await advanced.checkValueModel(await load('value-model.mjs'));
    if (workerData.module === '4') result = await advanced.checkReport((await load('report.mjs')).summarize);
    if (workerData.module === '5') result = await advanced.checkSampler((await load('opponent-sampler.mjs')).sampleOpponent);
    if (workerData.module === '6') {
      const implementation=await load('vulnerability.mjs');
      const gap=await advanced.checkGap(implementation.nashGap);
      const response=await advanced.checkResponse(implementation.responsePolicy);
      result={ok:gap.ok&&response.ok,gap,response};
    }
  }
  parentPort.postMessage(result);
} catch (error) {
  parentPort.postMessage({ok: false, error: error.message, scope: 'Learner code failed to load or run. The source attempt remains saved.'});
}

`courses/game-playing-agent-league/lib/fit-worker.mjs`:

```mjs
import {parentPort,workerData} from 'node:worker_threads';
import {readFile} from 'node:fs/promises';
import {pathToFileURL} from 'node:url';
import {join} from 'node:path';
import {validateSeason} from './league.mjs';
import {examplesFromMatches,partitionEpisodes,fitAndEvaluate} from './training.mjs';
import {captureSourceBundle} from './league-config.mjs';
import {sha256} from './identity.mjs';
try {
  const bytes=await readFile(workerData.season,'utf8'),season=JSON.parse(bytes);
  validateSeason(season);
  const {codeManifest,codeBundle}=await captureSourceBundle(workerData.root);
  const {features,fit}=await import(pathToFileURL(join(workerData.root,'learner/value-model.mjs')));
  const examples=examplesFromMatches(season.matches,features);
  const split=partitionEpisodes(examples,{seed:41,fraction:0.75});
  const model=fitAndEvaluate({...split,fit,configuration:{seed:41,epochs:400,learningRate:0.05}});
  const after=await captureSourceBundle(workerData.root);
  if(sha256(after.codeManifest)!==sha256(codeManifest)) throw new Error('Source changed during fitting. Run again with a stable source version.');
  parentPort.postMessage({ok:true,model:{schemaVersion:1,type:'league-value-model',model,codeManifest,codeBundle,
    seasonHash:sha256(bytes),examples:examples.length,trainingScenarioIds:split.trainingScenarioIds,validationScenarioIds:split.validationScenarioIds,
    scenarios:season.matches.map(entry=>entry.record.scenario).filter((scenario,index,array)=>array.findIndex(item=>item.id===scenario.id)===index),
    scope:'A fitted value model on recorded behavior. A low validation loss is not a playing-strength result.'}});
} catch(error) {parentPort.postMessage({ok:false,error:error.message});}

`courses/game-playing-agent-league/lib/game.mjs`:

```mjs
/** Original supplied game rules for this course. No third-party source copied. */
import { canonicalJSON, copyData, deepFreeze, sha256 } from './identity.mjs';
import { createRng, uint32 } from './rng.mjs';

const ROWS = 5;
const COLUMNS = 5;
const CELLS = ROWS * COLUMNS;
const RULES = {
  id: 'breakthrough-5x5-v1', rows: ROWS, columns: COLUMNS, initialRanks: 1,
  advance: 1, diagonalEmpty: true, capture: 'diagonal-only',
  wins: ['far-rank', 'elimination', 'opponent-without-legal-move'],
  utility: 'terminal-zero-sum', turn: 'alternate',
};
export const RULES_HASH = sha256(RULES);
export const GAME = deepFreeze({
  schemaVersion: 1, gameId: RULES.id, rulesVersion: '1.0.0', rulesHash: RULES_HASH,
  rows: ROWS, columns: COLUMNS, players: 2, information: 'perfect',
  dynamics: 'sequential', chance: 'none', utility: 'zeroSum',
});

export class GameError extends Error {
  constructor(code, message) { super(message); this.name = 'GameError'; this.code = code; }
}

function playerId(player) {
  if (player !== 0 && player !== 1) throw new GameError('INVALID_PLAYER', 'Player must be 0 or 1.');
}

function validBoard(board) {
  if (!Array.isArray(board) || board.length !== CELLS || !Array.from(board).every(cell => cell === -1 || cell === 0 || cell === 1)) {
    throw new GameError('INVALID_BOARD', 'Board must contain exactly 25 values from -1, 0 and 1.');
  }
  for (const player of [0, 1]) {
    if (board.filter(cell => cell === player).length > 5) throw new GameError('INVALID_BOARD', 'A side may have at most five pawns.');
  }
}

export function encodeAction(from, to) {
  if (!Number.isInteger(from) || !Number.isInteger(to) || from < 0 || from >= CELLS || to < 0 || to >= CELLS) {
    throw new GameError('INVALID_ACTION', 'Action cells must be integers in 0..24.');
  }
  return from * CELLS + to;
}

export function decodeAction(actionId) {
  if (!Number.isInteger(actionId) || actionId < 0 || actionId >= CELLS * CELLS) {
    throw new GameError('INVALID_ACTION', 'Action ID must be an integer in 0..624.');
  }
  return { from: Math.floor(actionId / CELLS), to: actionId % CELLS };
}

function rawLegal(board, player) {
  const actions = [];
  const direction = player === 0 ? 1 : -1;
  for (let from = 0; from < CELLS; from++) {
    if (board[from] !== player) continue;
    const row = Math.floor(from / COLUMNS) + direction;
    if (row < 0 || row >= ROWS) continue;
    const column = from % COLUMNS;
    for (const delta of [-1, 0, 1]) {
      const nextColumn = column + delta;
      if (nextColumn < 0 || nextColumn >= COLUMNS) continue;
      const to = row * COLUMNS + nextColumn;
      if (board[to] === player || (delta === 0 && board[to] !== -1)) continue;
      actions.push(encodeAction(from, to));
    }
  }
  return actions.sort((a, b) => a - b);
}

function boardWinner(board, currentPlayer) {
  const counts = [board.filter(cell => cell === 0).length, board.filter(cell => cell === 1).length];
  const reached = [board.slice(20).includes(0), board.slice(0, 5).includes(1)];
  if ((!counts[0] && !counts[1]) || (reached[0] && reached[1])) throw new GameError('INVALID_BOARD', 'Board has contradictory terminal outcomes.');
  if (reached[0] || counts[1] === 0) return 0;
  if (reached[1] || counts[0] === 0) return 1;
  if (rawLegal(board, currentPlayer).length === 0) return 1 - currentPlayer;
  return null;
}

/** Explicit teaching positions are permitted; reachability is a separate property. */
export function createState({ board, currentPlayer = 0, ply = 0 } = {}) {
  validBoard(board);
  playerId(currentPlayer);
  if (!Number.isInteger(ply) || ply < 0 || ply > 40) throw new GameError('INVALID_PLY', 'Ply must be an integer in 0..40.');
  const winner = boardWinner(board, currentPlayer);
  const potential = board.reduce((sum, player, index) => player === -1 ? sum : sum + (player === 0 ? ROWS - 1 - Math.floor(index / COLUMNS) : Math.floor(index / COLUMNS)), 0);
  if (ply + potential > 40) throw new GameError('INVALID_PLY', 'Ply plus remaining pawn distance cannot exceed the initial bound of 40.');
  return deepFreeze({
    schemaVersion: 1, gameId: GAME.gameId, rulesHash: RULES_HASH,
    rows: ROWS, columns: COLUMNS, board: board.slice(), currentPlayer, ply,
    terminal: winner !== null, returns: winner === null ? null : winner === 0 ? [1, -1] : [-1, 1],
  });
}

export function initialState() {
  return createState({ board: [...Array(5).fill(0), ...Array(15).fill(-1), ...Array(5).fill(1)] });
}

export function validateState(state) {
  if (!state || typeof state !== 'object' || state.schemaVersion !== 1 || state.gameId !== GAME.gameId || state.rulesHash !== RULES_HASH || state.rows !== ROWS || state.columns !== COLUMNS) {
    throw new GameError('WRONG_RULES', 'State does not belong to breakthrough-5x5-v1.');
  }
  const expected = createState(state);
  if (state.terminal !== expected.terminal || canonicalJSON(state.returns) !== canonicalJSON(expected.returns)) {
    throw new GameError('INVALID_TERMINAL', 'Terminal flag/returns disagree with the board.');
  }
  return true;
}

export function legalActions(state) {
  validateState(state);
  return state.terminal ? [] : rawLegal(state.board, state.currentPlayer);
}

export function next(state, actionId) {
  validateState(state);
  if (state.terminal) throw new GameError('GAME_OVER', 'No move is legal after termination.');
  const { from, to } = decodeAction(actionId);
  if (!rawLegal(state.board, state.currentPlayer).includes(actionId)) throw new GameError('ILLEGAL_ACTION', `Action ${actionId} is not legal for player ${state.currentPlayer}.`);
  const board = state.board.slice();
  const actor = state.currentPlayer;
  const capture = board[to] === 1 - actor;
  board[from] = -1;
  board[to] = actor;
  const result = createState({ board, currentPlayer: 1 - actor, ply: state.ply + 1 });
  const winner = result.terminal ? result.returns.indexOf(1) : null;
  const reason = !result.terminal ? null : (Math.floor(to / COLUMNS) === (actor === 0 ? ROWS - 1 : 0)) ? 'far-rank' : !board.includes(1 - actor) ? 'elimination' : 'no-legal-move';
  return { state: result, event: deepFreeze({ ply: state.ply, actor, actionId, from, to, capture, winner, terminalReason: reason }) };
}

export function observe(state, player = state.currentPlayer) {
  validateState(state);
  playerId(player);
  return deepFreeze({ ...copyData(state), perspective: player, legalActions: !state.terminal && player === state.currentPlayer ? rawLegal(state.board, player) : [] });
}

export function stateKey(state) {
  validateState(state);
  return sha256({ schemaVersion: 1, gameId: state.gameId, rulesHash: state.rulesHash, rows: ROWS, columns: COLUMNS,
    board: state.board, currentPlayer: state.currentPlayer, ply: state.ply, terminal: state.terminal, returns: state.returns });
}

export function remainingPotential(state) {
  validateState(state);
  return state.board.reduce((sum, player, index) => player === -1 ? sum : sum + (player === 0 ? ROWS - 1 - Math.floor(index / COLUMNS) : Math.floor(index / COLUMNS)), 0);
}

export function formatBoard(state) {
  validateState(state);
  const symbols = { '-1': '.', '0': 'A', '1': 'B' };
  return Array.from({ length: ROWS }, (_, row) => state.board.slice(row * COLUMNS, (row + 1) * COLUMNS).map(value => symbols[value]).join(' ')).join('\n');
}

/** Legal prefixes are reproducible; this single generator does not enforce split deduplication. */
export function generateScenario(seed = 0, prefixPlies = 6) {
  uint32(seed);
  if (!Number.isInteger(prefixPlies) || prefixPlies < 0 || prefixPlies > 20) throw new RangeError('prefixPlies must be an integer in 0..20.');
  const rng = createRng(seed);
  let state = initialState();
  const prefix = [];
  for (let index = 0; index < prefixPlies && !state.terminal; index++) {
    const choices = legalActions(state);
    const selected = choices[Math.floor(rng() * choices.length)];
    const result = next(state, selected).state;
    if (result.terminal) break; // Final tournament starts remain playable.
    prefix.push(selected);
    state = result;
  }
  const stateHash = stateKey(state);
  return deepFreeze({ id: `prefix-${seed}-${prefix.length}-${stateHash.slice(0, 10)}`, generator: 'legal-prefix-lcg-v1', seed,
    requestedPrefixPlies: prefixPlies, prefix, state, stateHash, origin: 'legal-prefix' });
}

export function verifyScenario(scenario) {
  if (!scenario || typeof scenario !== 'object' || typeof scenario.id !== 'string' || !scenario.id) throw new TypeError('Scenario needs a nonempty ID.');
  validateState(scenario.state);
  if (stateKey(scenario.state) !== scenario.stateHash) throw new GameError('SCENARIO_MISMATCH', 'Scenario state hash does not match.');
  if (scenario.origin === 'legal-prefix') {
    if (!Array.isArray(scenario.prefix)) throw new GameError('SCENARIO_MISMATCH', 'Legal-prefix scenario needs its prefix.');
    let state = initialState();
    for (const action of scenario.prefix) state = next(state, action).state;
    if (stateKey(state) !== scenario.stateHash) throw new GameError('SCENARIO_MISMATCH', 'Prefix does not produce the declared state.');
  } else if (scenario.origin !== 'teaching-position') {
    throw new GameError('SCENARIO_MISMATCH', 'Scenario must declare legal-prefix or teaching-position origin.');
  }
  if (scenario.state.terminal) throw new GameError('SCENARIO_TERMINAL', 'A match must start from a nonterminal state.');
  return true;
}

export function teachingScenario(id, state) {
  validateState(state);
  return deepFreeze({ id, origin: 'teaching-position', state: copyData(state), stateHash: stateKey(state) });
}

`courses/game-playing-agent-league/lib/identity.mjs`:

```mjs
/** Supplied: canonical JSON identity for data, never an authenticity claim. */
import { createHash } from 'node:crypto';

export function canonicalJSON(value) {
  if (value === null || typeof value === 'string' || typeof value === 'boolean') return JSON.stringify(value);
  if (typeof value === 'number') {
    if (!Number.isFinite(value)) throw new TypeError('Identity data must contain only finite numbers.');
    return JSON.stringify(Object.is(value, -0) ? 0 : value);
  }
  if (Array.isArray(value)) return `[${Array.from(value, canonicalJSON).join(',')}]`;
  if (typeof value !== 'object' || Object.getPrototypeOf(value) !== Object.prototype) {
    throw new TypeError('Identity data must be plain JSON values.');
  }
  return `{${Object.keys(value).sort().map(key => `${JSON.stringify(key)}:${canonicalJSON(value[key])}`).join(',')}}`;
}

export const sha256 = value => createHash('sha256').update(typeof value === 'string' ? value : canonicalJSON(value)).digest('hex');

export function deepFreeze(value) {
  if (value && typeof value === 'object' && !Object.isFrozen(value)) {
    for (const child of Object.values(value)) deepFreeze(child);
    Object.freeze(value);
  }
  return value;
}

export const copyData = value => JSON.parse(canonicalJSON(value));

`courses/game-playing-agent-league/lib/journal.mjs`:

```mjs
import {readFile, writeFile, mkdir, rename, open, unlink} from 'node:fs/promises';
import {dirname, resolve} from 'node:path';
import {createHash, randomUUID} from 'node:crypto';

export const JOURNAL_VERSION = 1;
const digest = value => createHash('sha256').update(JSON.stringify(value)).digest('hex');
const MAX_BYTES = 16 * 1024 * 1024;
const own = (value, key) => Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(value, key);
const recordObject = value => value && typeof value === 'object' && !Array.isArray(value);

export function validateJournal(document, depth = 0, globalIds = new Map()) {
  if (depth > 4) throw new Error('Imported journals are nested too deeply. Export a flat working history instead.');
  if (!recordObject(document) || document.schemaVersion !== JOURNAL_VERSION || !Array.isArray(document.records)) {
    throw new Error('Unsupported or malformed journal. The original file has not been changed.');
  }
  if (document.records.length > 20000) throw new Error('Journal exceeds the supported record limit.');
  const ids = new Set();
  let previousHash = null;
  for (const record of document.records) {
    if (!recordObject(record) || typeof record.id !== 'string' || ids.has(record.id) || typeof record.type !== 'string' || !recordObject(record.data)) {
      throw new Error('Journal contains an invalid or duplicate record. The original file is preserved.');
    }
    const {hash, ...body} = record;
    if (record.previousHash !== previousHash || hash !== digest(body)) throw new Error(`Journal integrity mismatch at ${record.id}. No records were overwritten.`);
    if(globalIds.has(record.id) && globalIds.get(record.id)!==hash) throw new Error(`Journal contains conflicting imported versions of record ${record.id}. Both originals must be preserved for review.`);
    globalIds.set(record.id,hash);
    if (record.type === 'import') validateJournal(record.data.document, depth + 1, globalIds);
    ids.add(record.id);
    previousHash = hash;
  }
  return document;
}

export async function readJournal(path) {
  try {
    const bytes = await readFile(path);
    if (bytes.length > MAX_BYTES) throw new Error('Journal exceeds 16 MiB. Export/read the original before beginning a new journal.');
    return validateJournal(JSON.parse(bytes.toString('utf8')));
  } catch (error) {
    if (error.code === 'ENOENT') return {schemaVersion: JOURNAL_VERSION, records: []};
    if (error instanceof SyntaxError) throw new Error('Journal is not valid JSON. The original file is preserved for recovery.');
    throw error;
  }
}

export function flattenedRecords(document) {
  validateJournal(document);
  const result = [];
  const seen = new Set();
  function add(records) {
    for (const record of records) {
      if (record.type === 'import') { add(record.data.document.records); continue; }
      if (seen.has(record.id)) continue;
      seen.add(record.id);
      result.push(record);
    }
  }
  add(document.records);
  return result;
}

export async function appendRecord(path, type, data) {
  if (!recordObject(data)) throw new Error('Journal data must be an object.');
  path = resolve(path);
  await mkdir(dirname(path), {recursive: true});
  const lockPath = `${path}.lock`;
  let lock;
  try { lock = await open(lockPath, 'wx'); }
  catch (error) {
    if (error.code === 'EEXIST') throw new Error(`Another journal operation is active, or a previous operation stopped. Preserve ${path}; inspect ${lockPath} before manually clearing the lock.`);
    throw new Error(`Cannot save an attempt: ${error.message}. No feedback/check was released.`);
  }
  let temporary;
  try {
    const document = await readJournal(path);
    const body = {id: randomUUID(), type, createdAt: new Date().toISOString(), previousHash: document.records.at(-1)?.hash ?? null, data};
    const record = {...body, hash: digest(body)};
    const next = {...document, records: [...document.records, record]};
    validateJournal(next);
    const encoded = JSON.stringify(next, null, 2) + '\n';
    if (Buffer.byteLength(encoded) > MAX_BYTES) throw new Error('Journal would exceed 16 MiB; export existing work and use a new journal.');
    temporary = `${path}.${randomUUID()}.part`;
    const handle = await open(temporary, 'wx', 0o600);
    try { await handle.writeFile(encoded); await handle.sync(); } finally { await handle.close(); }
    await rename(temporary, path);
    return record;
  } finally {
    await lock.close();
    await unlink(lockPath);
  }
}

export async function exportJournal(source, destination) {
  if (resolve(source) === resolve(destination)) throw new Error('Export destination must differ from the active journal.');
  const document = await readJournal(source);
  await writeFile(destination, JSON.stringify(document, null, 2) + '\n', {flag: 'wx', mode: 0o600});
  return document.records.length;
}

export async function importJournal(destination, source) {
  if (resolve(source) === resolve(destination)) throw new Error('Cannot import a journal into itself.');
  const bytes = await readFile(source);
  if (bytes.length > MAX_BYTES) throw new Error('Import exceeds 16 MiB; original journals are unchanged.');
  let document;
  try { document = validateJournal(JSON.parse(bytes.toString('utf8'))); }
  catch (error) { throw new Error(`Import rejected: ${error.message}`); }
  const sourceHash = digest(document);
  const current = await readJournal(destination);
  if (current.records.some(record => record.type === 'import' && record.data.sourceHash === sourceHash)) return {duplicate: true};
  const importedIds = new Map(flattenedRecords(current).map(record => [record.id, record.hash]));
  for (const record of flattenedRecords(document)) {
    if (importedIds.has(record.id) && importedIds.get(record.id) !== record.hash) throw new Error(`Import conflicts with existing record ${record.id}. Both originals are preserved.`);
  }
  await appendRecord(destination, 'import', {sourceHash, document});
  return {duplicate: false, records: document.records.length};
}

export function latestAttempt(document, itemId) {
  return flattenedRecords(document).filter(record => record.type === 'attempt' && record.data.itemId === itemId).at(-1) ?? null;
}

export function assistanceFor(document, itemId) {
  return flattenedRecords(document).filter(record => ['feedback', 'hint'].includes(record.type) && record.data.itemId === itemId)
    .map(record => ({type: record.type, level: record.data.level ?? null, recordId: record.id}));
}

export function questionHash(item) {
  if (!recordObject(item) || !own(item, 'question')) throw new Error('Item has no question.');
  return digest({id: item.id, question: item.question});
}

import {readFile, readdir} from 'node:fs/promises';
import {resolve, dirname, join, relative, sep} from 'node:path';
import {pathToFileURL} from 'node:url';
import {createHash} from 'node:crypto';
import {generateScenario} from './game.mjs';
import {snapshotPolicy} from './runner.mjs';

const hash = value => createHash('sha256').update(value).digest('hex');
export function scenarioGroupKey(scenario) {
  const state=scenario.state;
  const normal=JSON.stringify([state.currentPlayer,state.board]);
  const mirrored=Array.from({length:25},(_,index)=>state.board[Math.floor(index/5)*5+4-index%5]);
  const reflection=JSON.stringify([state.currentPlayer,mirrored]);
  return normal<reflection?normal:reflection;
}
export async function captureSourceBundle(courseRoot) {
  const codeManifest={},codeBundle={};
  for(const folder of ['lib','learner','checks']) {
    for(const file of (await readdir(join(courseRoot,folder))).sort()) {
      if(!/\.(mjs|json)$/.test(file)) continue;
      const bytes=await readFile(join(courseRoot,folder,file));
      codeManifest[`${folder}/${file}`]=hash(bytes);
      codeBundle[`${folder}/${file}`]=bytes.toString('utf8');
    }
  }
  for(const file of ['cli.mjs','package.json']) {
    const bytes=await readFile(join(courseRoot,file));
    codeManifest[file]=hash(bytes);
    codeBundle[file]=bytes.toString('utf8');
  }
  return {codeManifest,codeBundle};
}
export async function loadLeagueConfiguration(filename, courseRoot) {
  const source = await readFile(filename, 'utf8');
  const config = JSON.parse(source);
  if(config.schemaVersion!==1 || !Array.isArray(config.policies) || config.policies.length<2 || config.policies.length>8) throw new Error('League configuration needs schemaVersion 1 and two to eight policies.');
  if(!Array.isArray(config.scenarioSeeds)||config.scenarioSeeds.length<1||config.scenarioSeeds.length>16) throw new Error('Provide one to sixteen scenario seeds.');
  if(!Array.isArray(config.policySeeds)||config.policySeeds.length<1||config.policySeeds.length>2) throw new Error('Provide one or two policy-randomness seeds.');
  for(const seed of [...config.scenarioSeeds,...config.policySeeds]) if(!Number.isInteger(seed)||seed<0||seed>0xffffffff) throw new Error('All seeds must be unsigned32 integers.');
  if(new Set(config.scenarioSeeds).size!==config.scenarioSeeds.length || new Set(config.policySeeds).size!==config.policySeeds.length) throw new Error('Seed rosters cannot contain duplicates.');
  if(!Number.isInteger(config.budget)||config.budget<0||config.budget>1024) throw new Error('Budget must be an integer from zero through1024.');
  if(!['development','selection','final'].includes(config.partition)) throw new Error('Declare development, selection or final partition.');
  if(config.partition==='final') {
    const required=['random-baseline','greedy-baseline','search','learned-search','historical-learned','counterpolicy'];
    const roles=config.policies.map(entry=>entry.role);
    if(required.some(role=>!roles.includes(role)) || config.scenarioSeeds.length!==16 || config.policySeeds.length!==2 || config.budget!==256) throw new Error('The final course roster requires all six declared policy roles, sixteen independent scenario groups, two policy seeds and a common 256-credit budget. Use development for smaller practice runs. Role declarations still require source review.');
  }
  const root=resolve(courseRoot);
  const {codeManifest,codeBundle}=await captureSourceBundle(root);
  const policies=[];
  for(const entry of config.policies) {
    if(typeof entry.module!=='string'||typeof entry.export!=='string'||typeof entry.name!=='string') throw new Error('Each policy needs name, module and export strings.');
    const path=resolve(dirname(filename),entry.module);
    const within=relative(root,path);
    if(within.startsWith('..'+sep)||within==='..'||!['lib','learner'].some(folder=>within.startsWith(folder+sep))||within.split(sep).length!==2||!within.endsWith('.mjs')) throw new Error('Policy entry modules must be direct .mjs files in this package’s lib/ or learner/ folders so the local code manifest captures them. Nested, external and dynamically loaded policy dependencies are outside this course contract.');
    const loaded=await import(pathToFileURL(path));
    if(typeof loaded[entry.export]!=='function') throw new Error(`No policy export ${entry.export} in ${entry.module}.`);
    const sourceIdentity=JSON.stringify({module:within,export:entry.export,codeManifest});
    policies.push(snapshotPolicy({name:entry.name,decide:loaded[entry.export],source:sourceIdentity,parameters:entry.parameters??{},configuration:entry.configuration??{},metadata:{...entry.metadata,...(entry.role?{role:entry.role}:{})}}));
  }
  const scenarios=config.scenarioSeeds.map(seed=>generateScenario(seed,config.prefixPlies??6));
  const boardKeys=scenarios.map(scenarioGroupKey);
  if(new Set(boardKeys).size!==boardKeys.length) throw new Error('Scenario seeds generated duplicate or reflected starting boards. Choose distinct groups before freezing evaluation.');
  return {config,configHash:hash(source),codeManifest,codeBundle,policies,scenarios};
}

`courses/game-playing-agent-league/lib/league.mjs`:

```mjs
import {sha256, copyData, deepFreeze} from './identity.mjs';
import {deriveSeed} from './rng.mjs';
import {runMatch, verifyReplay} from './runner.mjs';

function unique(values, name) {
  if (!Array.isArray(values) || !values.length || Array.from(values).some(value => value === undefined || value === null) || new Set(values).size !== values.length) throw new Error(`${name} must be nonempty and unique.`);
}

export function createPlan({policies, scenarios, seeds = [1, 2], budget = 256, partition = 'development'}) {
  if (!Array.isArray(policies) || policies.length < 2 || policies.length > 8) throw new Error('A season supports 2–8 policy snapshots. The complete-course capstone requires its six named roles.');
  unique(policies.map(policy => policy.id), 'Policy IDs');
  unique(scenarios.map(scenario => scenario.id), 'Scenario IDs');
  if (policies.some(policy => typeof policy.id !== 'string' || !policy.id) || scenarios.some(scenario => typeof scenario.id !== 'string' || !scenario.id || typeof scenario.stateHash !== 'string' || !scenario.stateHash)) throw new Error('Policy and scenario identities must be explicit strings.');
  unique(seeds, 'Replicate seeds');
  if (seeds.some(seed => !Number.isInteger(seed) || seed < 0 || seed > 0xffffffff)) throw new Error('Replicate seeds must be uint32 integers.');
  if (!Number.isInteger(budget) || budget < 0 || budget > 1024) throw new Error('Budget must be an integer from 0 through 1024.');
  if (!['development', 'training', 'selection', 'final'].includes(partition)) throw new Error('Unknown experiment partition.');
  const definition = {
    schemaVersion: 1, type: 'league-plan', policyIds: policies.map(policy => policy.id),
    scenarioIds: scenarios.map(scenario => scenario.id), scenarioHashes: scenarios.map(scenario => scenario.stateHash),
    replicateSeeds: [...seeds], budget, partition, scoring: 'seat-paired-zero-sum-utility',
    samplingUnit: 'scenario-block', intervalMethod: 'paired-scenario-block-percentile', confidence: 0.95,
  };
  const id = sha256(definition), roster = [];
  for (let left = 0; left < policies.length; left++) {
    for (let right = left + 1; right < policies.length; right++) {
      for (const scenario of scenarios) for (const replicate of seeds) for (const seat of [0, 1]) {
        const pair = [policies[left].id, policies[right].id];
        const assignments = seat === 0 ? pair : [...pair].reverse();
        const slot = {scenarioId: scenario.id, pair, policies: assignments, seat, replicate,
          policySeeds: assignments.map(policy => deriveSeed(id, scenario.id, replicate, policy))};
        roster.push({id: sha256({plan: id, ...slot}), ...slot});
      }
    }
  }
  return deepFreeze({...definition, id, roster});
}

export function validatePlan(plan) {
  if (!plan || !Array.isArray(plan.policyIds) || !Array.isArray(plan.scenarioIds) || !Array.isArray(plan.scenarioHashes) || plan.scenarioIds.length !== plan.scenarioHashes.length) throw new Error('Incomplete plan identity.');
  const rebuilt = createPlan({policies: plan.policyIds.map(id => ({id})), scenarios: plan.scenarioIds.map((id, index) => ({id, stateHash: plan.scenarioHashes[index]})), seeds: plan.replicateSeeds, budget: plan.budget, partition: plan.partition});
  if (sha256(rebuilt) !== sha256(plan)) throw new Error('Plan definition, ID or schedule has been altered.');
  return true;
}

export function runLeague({policies, scenarios, plan}) {
  const expected = createPlan({policies, scenarios, seeds: plan.replicateSeeds, budget: plan.budget, partition: plan.partition});
  if (sha256(expected) !== sha256(plan)) throw new Error('Plan does not match the supplied frozen snapshots/scenarios.');
  const byPolicy = new Map(policies.map(policy => [policy.id, policy]));
  const byScenario = new Map(scenarios.map(scenario => [scenario.id, scenario]));
  const matches = plan.roster.map(slot => ({slotId: slot.id, record: runMatch({
    policies: slot.policies.map(id => byPolicy.get(id)), scenario: byScenario.get(slot.scenarioId),
    policySeeds: slot.policySeeds, budget: plan.budget, planId: plan.id,
  })}));
  return {schemaVersion: 1, type: 'league-season', plan: copyData(plan), matches,
    scope: plan.partition === 'final' ? 'Frozen-checkpoint final roster; not a general training-algorithm comparison.' : 'Development/training/selection season; no confirmatory claim.'};
}

export function validateSeason(season) {
  if (!season || season.type !== 'league-season' || !season.plan?.roster || !Array.isArray(season.matches)) throw new Error('Malformed season.');
  validatePlan(season.plan);
  const roster = new Map(season.plan.roster.map(slot => [slot.id, slot]));
  const seen = new Set();
  for (const entry of season.matches) {
    const slot = roster.get(entry.slotId);
    if (!slot || seen.has(entry.slotId)) throw new Error('Unknown or duplicate scheduled match.');
    const record = entry.record;
    const expectedScenarioHash = season.plan.scenarioHashes[season.plan.scenarioIds.indexOf(slot.scenarioId)];
    if (record.planId !== season.plan.id || record.scenario.id !== slot.scenarioId || record.scenario.stateHash !== expectedScenarioHash || record.budget !== season.plan.budget || sha256(record.policySeeds) !== sha256(slot.policySeeds) || sha256(record.policySnapshots.map(policy => policy.id)) !== sha256(slot.policies)) throw new Error('Match identity disagrees with its planned slot.');
    verifyReplay(record);
    seen.add(entry.slotId);
  }
  if (seen.size !== roster.size) throw new Error(`Incomplete season: ${roster.size - seen.size} scheduled matches are missing.`);
  return {ok: true, matches: seen.size, replay: 'trajectory verified; rerun policies separately for policy reproducibility'};
}

`courses/game-playing-agent-league/lib/rng.mjs`:

```mjs
/** Supplied deterministic PRNG. Not suitable for security or secret generation. */
import { sha256 } from './identity.mjs';

export function uint32(value, label = 'seed') {
  if (!Number.isInteger(value) || value < 0 || value > 0xffffffff) throw new RangeError(`${label} must be a uint32.`);
  return value;
}

export function createRng(seed = 0) {
  let state = uint32(seed);
  const random = () => {
    // A documented 32-bit LCG; all integer arithmetic wraps modulo 2^32.
    state = (Math.imul(state, 1664525) + 1013904223) >>> 0;
    return state / 0x100000000;
  };
  random.state = () => state;
  return random;
}

export const deriveSeed = (...parts) => Number.parseInt(sha256(parts).slice(0, 8), 16) >>> 0;

export function shuffle(values, random) {
  const result = values.slice();
  for (let index = result.length - 1; index > 0; index--) {
    const selected = Math.floor(random() * (index + 1));
    [result[index], result[selected]] = [result[selected], result[index]];
  }
  return result;
}

import {readFile} from 'node:fs/promises';
import {relative,dirname,join} from 'node:path';
import {captureSourceBundle,scenarioGroupKey} from './league-config.mjs';
import {generateScenario} from './game.mjs';
import {sha256} from './identity.mjs';

export async function makeDevelopmentRoster(filename,destination,root) {
  const bytes=await readFile(filename,'utf8'),artifact=JSON.parse(bytes);
  if(!['league-value-model','league-training'].includes(artifact.type)) throw new Error('Expected a fitted value model or completed population-training artifact.');
  const current=await captureSourceBundle(root);
  for(const file of ['learner/value-model.mjs','learner/search.mjs','lib/training.mjs','lib/game.mjs']) {
    if(current.codeManifest[file]!==artifact.codeManifest[file]) throw new Error(`Model-producing dependency ${file} changed. Refit with current code or restore the original dependency before constructing a roster.`);
  }
  const module=file=>relative(dirname(destination),join(root,file)).split('\\').join('/');
  const learned=artifact.type==='league-training'?artifact.generations.at(-1):{model:artifact.model,snapshot:{id:sha256(artifact.model)}};
  const base=[
    {name:'supplied-random',role:'random-baseline',module:module('lib/supplied-policies.mjs'),export:'randomPolicy'},
    {name:'supplied-greedy',role:'greedy-baseline',module:module('lib/supplied-policies.mjs'),export:'greedyPolicy'},
    {name:'learner-search',role:'search',module:module('learner/league-policy.mjs'),export:'decide',parameters:{maxDepth:3}},
    {name:'learner-learned-search',role:'learned-search',module:module('learner/learned-policy.mjs'),export:'decide',parameters:{maxDepth:3,weights:learned.model.weights},metadata:{sourceArtifactHash:sha256(bytes),sourceSnapshotId:learned.snapshot.id}},
  ];
  if(artifact.type==='league-training') {
    if(artifact.generations.length<2) throw new Error('A population roster needs at least two learned generations so the historical role is real.');
    const historical=artifact.generations[0];
    base.push({name:'historical-learned-search',role:'historical-learned',module:module('learner/learned-policy.mjs'),export:'decide',parameters:{maxDepth:3,weights:historical.model.weights},metadata:{sourceArtifactHash:sha256(bytes),sourceSnapshotId:historical.snapshot.id}},
      {name:'learner-counter-greedy',role:'counterpolicy',module:module('learner/counter-policy.mjs'),export:'decide',parameters:{maxDepth:3,opponentModel:'greedy'}});
  }
  const used=new Set((artifact.scenarios??[]).map(scenarioGroupKey)),scenarioSeeds=[];
  for(let seed=701;scenarioSeeds.length<3&&seed<10000;seed++) {
    const key=scenarioGroupKey(generateScenario(seed,6));
    if(!used.has(key)){scenarioSeeds.push(seed);used.add(key);}
  }
  return {schemaVersion:1,partition:'development',budget:256,prefixPlies:6,scenarioSeeds,policySeeds:[13],policies:base,
    _note:'Supplied assembly only. This is a small development roster with new scenario groups. A six-role final roster, frozen selection protocol and independent review remain separate requirements.'};
}
