# Source grounding and scope

Consulted November 4, 2026. This is an original educational protocol, not copied Tor implementation code. No third-party code was downloaded or installed. Examples and traces are produced by this package’s executed reference using installed Node crypto.

| Source | Used for | What it does not justify |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Tor Protocol Specification](https://spec.torproject.org/tor-spec/index.html) | The distinction between implementation specifications and a design explanation; the course is explicitly not wire-compatible. | That this toy implements the Tor specification. |
| [Tor relay-cell routing](https://spec.torproject.org/tor-spec/routing-relay-cells.html) | Directional relay processing as conceptual grounding. | Substituting the toy’s nested JSON/GCM envelopes for Tor cells. |
| [Tor Project: Counter Galois Onion](https://blog.torproject.org/introducing-cgo/) | Per-relay shared-key layers, why integrity and tag design matter, and why an old simplified account should not be represented as current Tor cryptography. | A claim that our per-layer GCM is CGO or that passing local tests establishes anonymity. |
| [Tor Project: remaining attacks](https://support.torproject.org/about-tor/security/attacks-on-onion-routing/) | The explicit limit involving an observer able to compare traffic at the client and destination/exit. | A claim that one matching short trace proves identity. |
| [Tor Project: HTTPS encryption and Tor](https://support.torproject.org/about-tor/security/https-encryption-and-tor/) | Separating relay routing privacy from endpoint content encryption and endpoint knowledge. | That this lab includes TLS, browser privacy defenses or a working Tor Browser. |
| [Node crypto documentation](https://nodejs.org/api/crypto.html) | The installed API family: createCipheriv, createDecipheriv, setAAD, setAuthTag, final and randomBytes; GCM authentication handling. | Qualification of every Node release. The local runtime is tested separately. |

The Node documentation fetched by the research tool identified v26.13.0; the actual installed implementation tested here is v26.5.1 with OpenSSL 3.6.3. The supplied adapters use the installed built-in cryptographic APIs; private instructor controls are excluded from this learner edition. There is no invented cipher, hash construction or random generator in the course.

The 0.2.0 browser successor adds the platform's built-in Web Crypto AES-GCM adapter. Offline tests use installed Node Web Crypto and compare its ciphertext/tag with native Node AES-256-GCM for a fixed ephemeral test key and context. Both implementations use the same nonce, tag length and associated-data encoding. The exact worker bundle and UI handlers are also exercised with Node worker_threads and a minimal DOM adapter. These are source/adapter checks, not actual browser, CSP, layout or accessibility acceptance. No new web fetch, library installation or external protocol test was used for this successor.

Course conventions preserve learner-owned projects, source/attempt identities, commit-before-feedback and positive learner export allowlists. These conventions are not a claim of human learning or browser acceptance.

`courses/onion-network-course/observatory/WORKSHOP.md`:

```md
# The reply never arrived. What happened?

Build an experiment that distinguishes a lost forward message from a lost reply, then decide what can recover. You control several circuits, the order of events and the fault boundary. Your eight protocol functions still do the work. This workshop supplies a scheduler and observer views, not a replacement implementation.

Start after module 5 with your working **browser-format** source. Complete module 6 for the final observer argument. Budget 35–55 minutes as an untested planning estimate. You can run an unfinished implementation: step errors are preserved and later steps continue. Nothing here automatically awards a pass or forces a particular valid path.

## Run an experiment

In the existing workbench, keep your code in **Your browser project source** and expand **Multi-circuit failure and recovery workshop**. The loaded scenario is `scenarios/recovery.json`. Use **Edit**, **Move up**, **Move down**, **Remove**, and the action form to change its steps. **Add step** appends a new step; **Update step** replaces the selected step. Disabled fields do not apply to that action. Commit observer predictions, then choose **Run experiment**. It runs the exact current code and scenario in the existing disposable worker.

**Save experiment draft** keeps the scenario separately from your code draft. **Download scenario** and **Load scenario JSON** exchange experiment instructions and predictions, never executable protocol code. **Export project history** includes the original source, complete scenario, scenario SHA-256, experiment contract, question hash, build/worker identities, declared help and actual results. A later scenario revision creates a new attempt. A changed scenario or prediction makes the displayed earlier result visibly stale.

The installed Node route uses the same bundled worker, without a browser or server:

```sh
node tools/browser-lab.mjs workshop scenarios/recovery.json learner/browser-solution.js none-declared
```

Replace `learner/browser-solution.js` with the path to **your** completed browser-format source. The distributed starter still contains TODOs; it is not a working solution. The command saves a new `browser-attempts/<id>/submission.json` and `result.json`. Exit zero means the scenario executed, including any recorded step failures; it does **not** mean your protocol or claims passed. A malformed scenario or worker failure exits nonzero. No tool silently converts the synchronous `learner/solution.mjs` API.

## Experiment 1: Two circuits, three views

The starter uses a three-hop `alpha` restricted to cedar/birch/maple and a two-hop `beta` restricted to elm/ash. Your path selector chooses the order. These lengths make disjoint paths possible with five relays; a two-hop path is not a promise of equivalent privacy.

1. Before running, predict what **client**, **archive**, and a relay of your choice can directly establish when `alpha` loses a reply. State at least one claim each cannot establish.
2. Run. Start with the **client** evidence view. It sees a sent lookup and no usable reply. Switch to **archive**: did it receive the lookup? Compare with the operator view only after writing your initial conclusion.
3. Inspect the step that takes birch offline, the next `alpha` send, and the later `beta` send. Which receiver sets changed before failure? Does the failure of one circuit close every other circuit? Support the answer with events, not the scenario's intention.
4. Inspect recovery and the two replay probes. Distinguish old bytes offered to fresh keys from old bytes offered to the closed circuit. Inspect the new circuit's first successful sequence and identity. Why can a fresh circuit use zero without reusing the old encryption key/nonce pair?
5. Change only the first fault to `drop-forward` at hop zero. Add revised predictions and rerun. Compare the two saved scenarios. Which client observations are compatible with both experiments? Which archive observations distinguish them?

The `failed` list is knowledge you explicitly supply to recovery. The client does not learn a hidden failure location from a missing reply. Offline directory entries also constrain path selection. Online and trustworthy are different properties.

## Experiment 2: Move the boundary, keep the packet

Load `scenarios/integrity.json`. A **send** captures the original forward bytes before any injected corruption. A **replay** injects those exact captured bytes, including into another circuit if you name one. It does not wrap a new request.

Predict the first corruption, first replay and second replay separately. Then move the corruption from hop zero to hop one. Keep your code and every other scenario step unchanged. Explain why authenticating nothing at the entry is different from accepting at the entry and failing at the middle: replaying from the start now meets the entry's already-recorded sequence. A later genuine packet is only guaranteed to remain admissible at a receiver whose rejected input did not change its state; upstream receivers may already have accepted it.

Do the same with the dropped message. A drop occurs **before** the selected relay receives or authenticates anything. A corrupted message reaches that relay and may produce a local rejection. Use received/rejected events and the operator's receiver-state snapshots to separate the cases. A replay with broken replay protection may reach the archive again and only fail later from return-key nonce reuse. Do not mistake that later error for successful replay protection.

Design a repair experiment using `recover`, a fresh `send`, and optional `close`. There is no automatic retry: your scenario must request it. Repeating this fictional read-only lookup is suitable for the exercise. Nothing demonstrates exactly-once effects for a purchase, balance change or arbitrary message.

## Experiment 3: Recovery is allowed to stop

Load `scenarios/exhaustion.json`. Predict recovery when only two relays remain online for a three-hop circuit. Restoring capacity does not resurrect the closed circuit or its keys. Determine the explicit next action that permits a fresh lookup.

Try a different legitimate path order in your implementation. Keep valid alternatives rather than forcing cedar to be first. Demonstrate either a qualifying replacement of the old length or a justified stop. Run the existing module checks separately to establish conformance; the workshop intentionally displays faulty implementation behavior too.

## Submit the evidence

Keep three scenario attempts: a baseline, a single-boundary change, and your own recovery design. Include their source/scenario hashes and declared help. For each, cite step numbers and an observer-specific event supporting your claim. Name a plausible alternative explanation the client cannot rule out. Add a short explanation of why the operator's combined trace is stronger than any relay's projection. The reviewer should assess causal reasoning and valid recovery choices, not exact prose, relay order, or one preferred sequence of experiments.

Your reasoning stays **UNASSESSED** until someone reviews it. A nonempty prediction, lack of thrown steps, or a green module check does not establish mastery or anonymity.

## Scenario format

A JSON scenario has `version: 1`, a `title`, a `predictions` array of `{ "observer": "client", "claim": "..." }`, and an ordered `steps` array. The supplied files are editable starting points with no answer predictions.

| Action | Required fields | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `open` | `circuit`, `length` (2–4), `avoid` (relay list) | Calls your path selector and creates fresh circuit keys. |
| `send` | `circuit`, unique `packet`, `item` (`luna` or `tide`) | Allocates a new sequence, captures your forward packet, then delivers it. |
| `replay` | `circuit`, `packet` | Injects an earlier captured forward packet at this circuit's entry. |
| `offline` / `online` | `relays` | Changes directory availability for later actions. No automatic close or reopen. |
| `recover` | `circuit`, unique `replacement`, `failed` (relay list) | Closes the original, invokes your recovery plan, and creates its replacement if any. |
| `close` | `circuit` | Closes this circuit and invalidates its key handles. |

A send may have `fault: { "kind": "drop-forward", "hop": 1 }`, `fault: { "kind": "corrupt-forward", "hop": 0 }`, or `fault: { "kind": "drop-reply" }`. Omit `fault` for normal delivery. Hop zero is the actual entry selected by your code. `drop-reply` discards the reply immediately after archive processing and before return wrapping. These are declared function-call boundaries, not measured network losses. An offline relay stops forward delivery before receipt. Multiple interventions take effect in path order.

Use only `cedar`, `birch`, `maple`, `elm`, `ash`. Circuits and packets have distinct short letter-led names. Scenarios support 1–32 steps, at most 8 circuit creations, and up to 12 predictions of 2,000 characters each. These bounds keep local reports manageable; they do not constrain a path selector to a preferred answer. Static schema errors stop before steps run. A valid step that names a missing circuit, references an uncaptured packet or uses a nonexistent hop produces a recorded runtime error; subsequent steps still run. No earlier attempt is overwritten.

## What the evidence cannot establish

Steps run sequentially. There is no concurrency, clock, realistic timeout, congestion, packet fragmentation, relay service or external traffic. A `no-reply` client event is a synthetic missing-response observation, without the operator's fault code or location. The client knows its configured path and explicit recovery inputs. Relays see local receipt/rejection and accepted forwarding; the exit and archive see the fictional lookup because this toy has no endpoint encryption.

Step numbers and circuit aliases are shared teaching labels, not evidence that real observers can identify the same traffic. Operator state, fault script and the complete exported result are deliberately available for learning. The observer selector is a projection, not an access control boundary. Closing invalidates key handles but cannot promise secure erasure of JavaScript memory. The worker closes all remaining circuits after recording the final snapshot. None of this is Tor, a Tor deployment tool, a real anonymity guarantee or secure messaging.

Real browser execution, storage behavior, layout and accessibility acceptance remain **NOT_RUN** in this build. Use the offline worker command in this delivery environment; it requires no server, installation or network.

// Narrow assertion adapter for the course's public cases; not a general test framework.
function failure(actual,expected,message) {
  const error=new Error(message??`Expected ${JSON.stringify(expected)}, observed ${JSON.stringify(actual)}`);
  error.code='ERR_ASSERTION';error.actual=actual;error.expected=expected;throw error;
}
function equivalent(a,b) {
  if(Object.is(a,b))return true;
  if(!a||!b||typeof a!=='object'||typeof b!=='object'||Array.isArray(a)!==Array.isArray(b))return false;
  const keys=Object.keys(a),other=Object.keys(b);
  return keys.length===other.length&&keys.every(k=>Object.hasOwn(b,k)&&equivalent(a[k],b[k]));
}
export const assert={
  equal:(a,b,message)=>{if(!Object.is(a,b))failure(a,b,message);},
  notEqual:(a,b,message)=>{if(Object.is(a,b))failure(a,`different from ${b}`,message);},
  ok:(value,message)=>{if(!value)failure(value,true,message);},
  deepEqual:(a,b,message)=>{if(!equivalent(a,b))failure(a,b,message);},
};

export async function evaluate(implementation, through = 6) {
  const results=[];
  for (const test of cases.filter(c=>c.module<=through)) {
    try { await test.run(implementation); results.push({...summary(test),pass:true}); }
    catch(error) { results.push({...summary(test),pass:false,code:error.code??error.name,detail:error.message,
      ...(error.actual !== undefined ? {actual:error.actual,expected:error.expected}: {})}); }
  }
  return {passed:results.filter(r=>r.pass).length,total:results.length,results};
}
function summary(test) { return {id:test.id,module:test.module,requirement:test.requirement,input:test.input,lesson:`lessons/0${test.module}.md`}; }

`courses/onion-network-course/observatory/browser/crypto.mjs`:

```mjs
// Browser adapter: only the platform's vetted AES-GCM implementation encrypts data.
export class LabError extends Error {
  constructor(code, detail=code) {super(detail);this.name='LabError';this.code=code;}
}
export function requireThat(condition,code,detail) {if(!condition)throw new LabError(code,detail);}
export const utf8=value=>new TextEncoder().encode(value);
export function toBase64(bytes) {
  let text='';for(const byte of bytes)text+=String.fromCharCode(byte);return btoa(text);
}
export function fromBase64(text) {
  return Uint8Array.from(atob(text),c=>c.charCodeAt(0));
}
export function context(circuitId,relayId,direction,seq) {
  requireThat(typeof circuitId==='string'&&typeof relayId==='string','BAD_CONTEXT');
  requireThat(['forward','backward'].includes(direction),'BAD_DIRECTION');
  requireThat(Number.isSafeInteger(seq)&&seq>=0&&seq<1024,'BAD_SEQUENCE');
  return {protocol:'onion-lab-v1',circuitId,relayId,direction,seq};
}
export function createCryptoPlatform(provider=globalThis.crypto) {
  requireThat(provider?.subtle&&provider?.getRandomValues,'CRYPTO_UNAVAILABLE','This environment needs built-in Web Crypto.');
  const materials=new WeakMap();
  function freshKey() {
    const handle=Object.freeze({kind:'ephemeral-toy-key'}),raw=provider.getRandomValues(new Uint8Array(32));
    const promise=provider.subtle.importKey('raw',raw,'AES-GCM',false,['encrypt','decrypt']).finally(()=>raw.fill(0));
    materials.set(handle,{promise,used:new Set(),active:true});return handle;
  }
  function destroyKey(handle) {
    const material=materials.get(handle);if(material)material.active=false;materials.delete(handle);
    // CryptoKey/JS memory cannot be securely erased by this application.
  }
  function materialFor(handle) {
    const material=materials.get(handle);requireThat(material?.active,'KEY_UNAVAILABLE');return material;
  }
  const aad=ctx=>utf8(JSON.stringify(context(ctx.circuitId,ctx.relayId,ctx.direction,ctx.seq)));
  const nonce=seq=>{const bytes=new Uint8Array(12);new DataView(bytes.buffer).setUint32(8,seq);return bytes;};
  async function seal(handle,ctx,value) {
    const additionalData=aad(ctx),material=materialFor(handle);
    requireThat(!material.used.has(ctx.seq),'NONCE_REUSE','Use a fresh sequence or rebuild with fresh keys.');
    const plaintext=utf8(JSON.stringify(value));requireThat(plaintext.length<=262144,'OVERSIZE');
    // Reserve synchronously, before any await, so concurrent calls cannot reuse a nonce.
    material.used.add(ctx.seq);
    const key=await material.promise;requireThat(material.active,'KEY_UNAVAILABLE');
    const combined=new Uint8Array(await provider.subtle.encrypt({name:'AES-GCM',iv:nonce(ctx.seq),additionalData,tagLength:128},key,plaintext));
    return {seq:ctx.seq,ciphertext:toBase64(combined.slice(0,-16)),tag:toBase64(combined.slice(-16))};
  }
  async function open(handle,ctx,packet) {
    const additionalData=aad(ctx),material=materialFor(handle);
    requireThat(packet&&packet.seq===ctx.seq&&typeof packet.ciphertext==='string'&&typeof packet.tag==='string','BAD_PACKET');
    requireThat(packet.ciphertext.length<=350000,'OVERSIZE');
    const key=await material.promise;requireThat(material.active,'KEY_UNAVAILABLE');
    try {
      const ciphertext=fromBase64(packet.ciphertext),tag=fromBase64(packet.tag);requireThat(tag.length===16,'AUTH_FAILED');
      const combined=new Uint8Array(ciphertext.length+tag.length);combined.set(ciphertext);combined.set(tag,ciphertext.length);
      const plaintext=await provider.subtle.decrypt({name:'AES-GCM',iv:nonce(ctx.seq),additionalData,tagLength:128},key,combined);
      return JSON.parse(new TextDecoder('utf-8',{fatal:true}).decode(plaintext));
    }catch {throw new LabError('AUTH_FAILED','Ciphertext, tag, context or key did not authenticate.');}
  }
  return {freshKey,destroyKey,seal,open,context,requireThat,LabError};
}
const platform=createCryptoPlatform();
export const {freshKey,destroyKey,seal,open}=platform;

`courses/onion-network-course/observatory/browser/network.mjs`:

```mjs
// Supplied in-process harness. There are no sockets, DNS calls or external relays.
const randomUUID=()=>globalThis.crypto.randomUUID();
import { freshKey, destroyKey, requireThat, LabError } from './crypto.mjs';
import {utf8,toBase64,fromBase64} from './crypto.mjs';

export const directory = () => ['cedar', 'birch', 'maple', 'elm', 'ash'].map(id => ({ id, online: true }));
export const sampleRequest = () => ({ operation: 'lookup', item: 'luna' });
const catalog = { luna: 'Luna: a fictional lunar atlas', tide: 'Tide: a fictional ocean atlas' };

export function establish(path, relays = directory()) {
  requireThat(path.length >= 2 && new Set(path).size === path.length, 'BAD_PATH');
  requireThat(path.every(id => relays.some(r => r.id === id && r.online)), 'BAD_PATH');
  const circuitId = randomUUID();
  const hops = path.map(relayId => ({ circuitId, relayId, forwardKey: freshKey(), backwardKey: freshKey() }));
  // Omniscient setup is deliberately supplied. It is NOT a handshake or Tor telescoping.
  const states = hops.map((hop, i) => ({ ...hop, previous: path[i - 1] ?? 'client',
    next: path[i + 1] ?? 'archive', seenForward: new Set() }));
  return { id: circuitId, path: [...path], hops, states, nextSeq: 0, received: new Set(), closed: false, trace: [] };
}
export function closeCircuit(circuit) {
  circuit.closed = true;
  for (const hop of circuit.hops) { destroyKey(hop.forwardKey); destroyKey(hop.backwardKey); }
}
const bytes = packet => utf8(JSON.stringify(packet)).length;

export async function deliverForward(implementation, circuit, packet, { failAt = null, modifyAt = null, dropAt = null, onReceive = () => {} } = {}) {
  requireThat(!circuit.closed, 'CIRCUIT_CLOSED');
  let body = packet;
  for (const state of circuit.states) {
    if (state.relayId === failAt) throw new LabError('RELAY_DOWN', state.relayId);
    if (state.relayId === dropAt) throw new LabError('FORWARD_LOST', state.relayId);
    if (state.relayId === modifyAt) body = tamper(body);
    const size = bytes(body);
    onReceive({observer:state.relayId,previous:state.previous,seq:body.seq,bytes:size,phase:'received'});
    let layer;
    try { layer = await implementation.peelForward(state, body); }
    catch(error) { onReceive({observer:state.relayId,phase:'rejected',code:error.code??error.name}); throw error; }
    circuit.trace.push({ direction: 'forward', observer: state.relayId, previous: state.previous,
      next: layer.next, seq: body.seq, bytes: size, payload: layer.next === 'archive' ? layer.body : '[encrypted inner packet]' });
    body = layer.body;
  }
  return body;
}
export async function deliverBackward(implementation, circuit, reply, seq) {
  let packet = reply;
  for (let i = circuit.hops.length - 1; i >= 0; i--) {
    const hop = circuit.hops[i];
    packet = await implementation.addReturnLayer(hop, packet, seq);
    circuit.trace.push({ direction: 'backward', observer: hop.relayId,
      previous: circuit.path[i + 1] ?? 'archive', next: circuit.path[i - 1] ?? 'client', seq, bytes: bytes(packet),
      payload: i === circuit.hops.length - 1 ? reply : '[encrypted inner packet]' });
  }
  return packet;
}
export function archive(request) {
  requireThat(request?.operation === 'lookup' && Object.hasOwn(catalog, request.item), 'BAD_REQUEST');
  return { item: request.item, record: catalog[request.item] };
}
export async function exchange(implementation, circuit, request = sampleRequest(), fault = {}) {
  requireThat(!circuit.closed, 'CIRCUIT_CLOSED');
  const seq = circuit.nextSeq++;
  requireThat(seq < 1024, 'REBUILD_REQUIRED');
  const packet = await implementation.wrapRequest(circuit.hops, request, seq);
  const arrived = await deliverForward(implementation, circuit, packet, fault);
  const reply = archive(arrived);
  circuit.trace.push({ direction: 'endpoint', observer: 'archive', previous: circuit.path.at(-1), payload: arrived });
  if (fault.dropReply) throw new LabError('REPLY_LOST', 'Archive received the lookup; client did not receive its reply.');
  const response = await deliverBackward(implementation, circuit, reply, seq);
  // The caller's request sequence is the expected identity at EVERY return layer.
  // Do not replace seq with a value read from an incoming packet.
  const unwrapped = await implementation.unwrapReply(circuit.hops, response, seq);
  // Client replay tracking is supplied; M4 applies the same rule to relay state.
  requireThat(!circuit.received.has(seq), 'REPLAY');
  circuit.received.add(seq);
  return unwrapped;
}
export function tamper(packet) {
  const altered = structuredClone(packet);
  const bytes = fromBase64(altered.ciphertext);
  requireThat(bytes.length > 0, 'BAD_PACKET');
  bytes[0] ^= 1;
  altered.ciphertext = toBase64(bytes);
  return altered;
}
export async function recover(implementation, oldCircuit, relays, failedIds) {
  closeCircuit(oldCircuit);
  const plan = await implementation.recoveryPlan(relays, failedIds, oldCircuit.path);
  if (plan.action === 'stop') return { plan, circuit: null };
  requireThat(plan.action === 'rebuild', 'BAD_PLAN');
  requireThat(!plan.path.some(id => failedIds.includes(id)), 'BAD_PLAN');
  return { plan, circuit: establish(plan.path, relays) };
}
export function views(circuit) {
  // A pedagogical projection, NOT isolation from the local process operator.
  return Object.fromEntries([...circuit.path, 'archive'].map(id =>
    [id, circuit.trace.filter(event => event.observer === id)]));
}

import {seal,open,context,requireThat,LabError} from './crypto.mjs';
import {directory,establish,exchange,deliverForward,deliverBackward,archive,tamper,recover,views} from './network.mjs';
import {evaluate,cases} from './cases.mjs';
import {runWorkshop} from './workshop.mjs';

const functionNames=['selectPath','wrapRequest','peelForward','addReturnLayer','unwrapReply','acceptSequence','recoveryPlan','correlate'];
export function compileLearner(source) {
  requireThat(typeof source==='string'&&source.length>0&&source.length<=100000,'BAD_SOURCE','Use a nonempty project under 100,000 characters.');
  // Executed only inside the disposable worker, never in the document's global scope.
  const compile=new Function('seal','open','context','requireThat','LabError',
    '"use strict";\n'+source+'\nreturn {'+functionNames.map(n=>`${n}:typeof ${n}==="function"?${n}:undefined`).join(',')+'};');
  const implementation=compile(seal,open,context,requireThat,LabError);
  for(const name of functionNames)requireThat(typeof implementation[name]==='function','MISSING_FUNCTION',`Define ${name} using the browser starter.`);
  return implementation;
}
async function observed(action) {
  try{return {outcome:'returned',value:await action()};}
  catch(error){return {outcome:'threw',code:error.code??error.name,detail:error.message};}
}
export async function diagnose(impl,options={}) {
  const mode=options.mode??'round-trip',item=options.item??'luna',length=Number(options.length??3);
  requireThat(['round-trip','tamper','replay','wrong-request','failed-hop','lost-reply'].includes(mode),'BAD_SCENARIO');
  requireThat(['luna','tide'].includes(item)&&[2,3,4].includes(length),'BAD_SCENARIO');
  const path=await impl.selectPath(directory(),[],length),circuit=establish(path);
  const request={operation:'lookup',item},events=[];let replacement=null;
  if(mode==='round-trip'||mode==='lost-reply') {
    events.push({action:mode,...await observed(()=>exchange(impl,circuit,request,{dropReply:mode==='lost-reply'}))});
  }else if(mode==='failed-hop') {
    events.push({action:'send through failed middle relay',...await observed(()=>exchange(impl,circuit,request,{failAt:path[1]}))});
    const next=await recover(impl,circuit,directory(),[path[1]]);replacement=next.circuit;
    events.push({action:'recovery plan',plan:next.plan,oldClosed:circuit.closed});
    if(replacement)events.push({action:'replacement lookup',...await observed(()=>exchange(impl,replacement,request))});
  }else {
    const seq=mode==='wrong-request'?7:0;
    const packet=await impl.wrapRequest(circuit.hops,request,seq),state=circuit.states[0];
    if(mode==='tamper')events.push({action:'altered packet',...await observed(()=>impl.peelForward(state,tamper(packet))),seenAfter:[...state.seenForward]});
    const forward=await observed(()=>deliverForward(impl,circuit,packet));
    events.push({action:'original forward',...forward});
    if(forward.outcome==='returned') {
      const reply=archive(forward.value);
      circuit.trace.push({direction:'endpoint',observer:'archive',previous:path.at(-1),payload:forward.value});
      const response=await deliverBackward(impl,circuit,reply,seq);
      if(mode==='wrong-request')events.push({action:'reply 7 offered to request 8',...await observed(()=>impl.unwrapReply(circuit.hops,response,8))});
      events.push({action:'matching reply',...await observed(()=>impl.unwrapReply(circuit.hops,response,seq))});
    }
    if(mode==='replay')events.push({action:'repeated forward packet',...await observed(()=>impl.peelForward(state,packet)),seenAfter:[...state.seenForward]});
  }
  return {mode:'learner-code simulation',scenario:mode,path,events,trace:circuit.trace,views:views(circuit),
    replacement:replacement?{path:replacement.path,trace:replacement.trace,views:views(replacement)}:null,
    visibility:'These are local observer projections. The single worker operator can inspect all state; this is not anonymity.'};
}
export async function runProject(request) {
  const {source,command='check',through=6,options={}}=request;
  requireThat(['check','diagnose','capstone','workshop'].includes(command),'BAD_COMMAND');
  requireThat(Number.isInteger(through)&&through>=1&&through<=6,'BAD_MODULE');
  const impl=compileLearner(source);
  if(command==='workshop')return runWorkshop(impl,options.scenario);
  if(command==='diagnose')return diagnose(impl,options);
  const checks=await evaluate(impl,command==='capstone'?6:through);
  if(command==='check'||checks.passed!==checks.total)return {kind:command,checks,scenarios:'NOT_RUN unless capstone checks all pass'};
  const scenarios=[];
  for(const mode of ['round-trip','tamper','replay','wrong-request','failed-hop','lost-reply'])scenarios.push(await diagnose(impl,{mode,item:'tide'}));
  const transfer=[
    {id:'A',entry:[0,4,13,18],tolerance:1,candidates:[{id:'A',times:[50,54,63,68]},{id:'B',times:[80,85,93,98]},{id:'C',times:[100,104,114,121]}]},
    {id:'B',entry:[0,1,2,3],tolerance:0,candidates:[{id:'P',times:[20,21,22,23]},{id:'Q',times:[60,61,62,63]},{id:'R',times:[90,91,92,93]}]},
  ];
  for(const task of transfer)task.retained=await impl.correlate(task.entry,task.candidates,task.tolerance);
  return {kind:'capstone',checks,scenarios,transfer,reasoning:'UNASSESSED: apply the written capstone rubric.'};
}
export const requirements=cases.map(({id,module,requirement,input})=>({id,module,requirement,input}));

`courses/onion-network-course/observatory/browser/session.mjs`:

```mjs
// Testable controller used by the real UI. Storage/worker are injected; no DOM or sockets.
export async function digest(text) {
  return [...new Uint8Array(await globalThis.crypto.subtle.digest('SHA-256',new TextEncoder().encode(text)))].map(x=>x.toString(16).padStart(2,'0')).join('');
}
export const storagePrefix='circuit-observatory/code/v1/';
export function createProjectSession({storage,makeWorker,buildId,runtimeHash,requirements,
  workshopContract,onStatus=()=>{},onResult=()=>{},timeoutMs=10000}) {
  let active=null;
  const unsaved=[];
  function put(kind,id,value) {
    const key=storagePrefix+kind+'/'+id;
    if(storage.getItem(key)!==null)throw new Error('Refusing to overwrite an existing project record.');
    const serialized=JSON.stringify(value);storage.setItem(key,serialized);
    if(storage.getItem(key)!==serialized)throw new Error('Project storage did not retain the record.');
  }
  function history() {
    const out=[];
    for(let i=0;i<storage.length;i++) {
      const key=storage.key(i);
      if(key?.startsWith(storagePrefix))out.push(JSON.parse(storage.getItem(key)));
    }
    return out.sort((a,b)=>a.createdAt.localeCompare(b.createdAt));
  }
  async function run({source,command,through=6,options={},assistance='none-declared',prediction=''}) {
    if(active)throw new Error('Stop or finish the current run before starting another.');
    if(typeof source!=='string'||source.length>100000||!source.trim())throw new Error('Use nonempty source under 100,000 characters.');
    // Snapshot before awaiting any hashing, so edits made while hashing belong to a later run.
    const snapshot={source,command,through,options:structuredClone(options),assistance,prediction};
    const token={id:globalThis.crypto.randomUUID(),cancelled:false};active=token;
    let record;
    try {
      if(command==='workshop'&&!workshopContract)throw new Error('The experiment contract is unavailable.');
      const question=command==='workshop'?{contract:workshopContract,scenario:snapshot.options.scenario}:command==='check'?requirements.filter(x=>x.module<=through):requirements;
      record={kind:'submission',id:token.id,createdAt:new Date().toISOString(),...snapshot,
        sourceHash:await digest(snapshot.source),question,questionHash:await digest(JSON.stringify(question)),buildId,runtimeHash,
        ...(command==='workshop'?{scenarioHash:await digest(JSON.stringify(snapshot.options.scenario))}: {})};
      if(token.cancelled)return;
      put('submission',record.id,record);
    } catch(error) {if(active===token)active=null;onStatus('Submission not saved; no code executed.');throw error;}
    if(token.cancelled)return;
    let worker,timer,finished=false;
    function finish(result) {
      if(finished)return;finished=true;clearTimeout(timer);worker?.terminate();active=null;
      const receipt={kind:'result',id:record.id,createdAt:new Date().toISOString(),sourceHash:record.sourceHash,
        questionHash:record.questionHash,buildId,runtimeHash,result,
        ...(record.scenarioHash?{scenarioHash:record.scenarioHash}:{})};
      let saved=true;
      try{put('result',record.id,receipt);}catch(error){saved=false;unsaved.push(receipt);onStatus(`Result is not saved: ${error.message}. Export it now; the submitted source is retained.`);}
      if(saved)onStatus('Run finished. Source and result saved as a new attempt.');
      onResult({submission:record,receipt,saved});
    }
    token.finish=finish;
    try {
      worker=makeWorker();
      worker.onmessage=event=>{if(event.data?.id===record.id&&event.data.type==='result')finish(event.data.result);};
      worker.onerror=event=>{event.preventDefault?.();finish({executionFailure:true,code:'WORKER_ERROR',detail:event.message??'Worker failed to start or execute.'});};
      timer=setTimeout(()=>finish({executionFailure:true,code:'TIMEOUT',detail:`Stopped after ${timeoutMs/1000} seconds; simplify the loop and retry.`}),timeoutMs);
      onStatus('Running your committed source in a disposable worker…');
      worker.postMessage({id:record.id,request:snapshot});
    }catch(error){finish({executionFailure:true,code:'WORKER_UNAVAILABLE',detail:error.message});}
    return record;
  }
  function cancel() {
    if(!active)return;
    active.cancelled=true;
    if(active.finish)active.finish({executionFailure:true,code:'CANCELLED',detail:'Stopped by the learner.'});
    else {active=null;onStatus('Cancelled before execution.');}
  }
  function exportRecords() {
    const records=[],invalidRecords=[];
    for(let i=0;i<storage.length;i++) {
      const key=storage.key(i);if(!key?.startsWith(storagePrefix))continue;
      const raw=storage.getItem(key);
      try{records.push(JSON.parse(raw));}catch(error){invalidRecords.push({key,raw,error:error.message});}
    }
    return {buildId,runtimeHash,records,invalidRecords,unsavedResults:[...unsaved]};
  }
  return {run,cancel,history,exportRecords,isRunning:()=>Boolean(active)};
}

`courses/onion-network-course/observatory/browser/workshop.mjs`:

```mjs
// Ordered, entirely in-process experiments. This schedules the existing learner protocol.
import {requireThat,LabError} from './crypto.mjs';
import {directory,establish,closeCircuit,deliverForward,deliverBackward,archive,recover} from './network.mjs';

const relayIds=directory().map(r=>r.id);
const fields={open:['circuit','length','avoid'],send:['circuit','packet','item','fault'],
  replay:['circuit','packet'],offline:['relays'],online:['relays'],recover:['circuit','replacement','failed'],close:['circuit']};
const fail=message=>{throw new LabError('BAD_SCENARIO',message);};
const object=value=>value&&typeof value==='object'&&!Array.isArray(value);
function only(value,keys,label) {
  if(!object(value)||Object.keys(value).some(k=>!keys.includes(k)))fail(`${label}: use only ${keys.join(', ')}.`);
}
function alias(value,label) {if(typeof value!=='string'||!(/^[a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9_-]{0,31}$/).test(value))fail(`${label}: use a short letter-led name.`);}
function relays(value,label) {if(!Array.isArray(value)||value.some(x=>!relayIds.includes(x))||new Set(value).size!==value.length)fail(`${label}: use distinct supplied relay names.`);}
export function validateWorkshop(input) {
  only(input,['version','title','predictions','steps'],'Scenario');
  if(input.version!==1||typeof input.title!=='string'||!input.title.trim()||input.title.length>160)fail('Use version 1 and a title of 1–160 characters.');
  if(!Array.isArray(input.predictions)||input.predictions.length>12)fail('Use a predictions array (up to 12 claims).');
  for(const p of input.predictions) {
    only(p,['observer','claim'],'Prediction');
    if(!['client','archive','operator',...relayIds].includes(p.observer)||typeof p.claim!=='string'||!p.claim.trim()||p.claim.length>2000)fail('Each prediction needs a supplied observer and a claim of 1–2000 characters.');
  }
  if(!Array.isArray(input.steps)||input.steps.length<1||input.steps.length>32)fail('Use 1–32 ordered steps.');
  for(const [i,s] of input.steps.entries()) {
    const label=`Step ${i+1}`;
    if(!object(s)||!Object.hasOwn(fields,s.action))fail(`${label}: unknown action.`);
    only(s,['action',...fields[s.action]],label);
    for(const key of ['circuit','packet','replacement'])if(fields[s.action].includes(key))alias(s[key],`${label} ${key}`);
    if(s.action==='open') {if(![2,3,4].includes(s.length))fail(`${label}: length must be 2, 3 or 4.`);relays(s.avoid,`${label} avoid`);}
    if(['online','offline'].includes(s.action))relays(s.relays,`${label} relays`);
    if(s.action==='recover')relays(s.failed,`${label} failed`);
    if(s.action==='send') {
      if(!['luna','tide'].includes(s.item))fail(`${label}: choose luna or tide.`);
      if(s.fault!==undefined) {
        only(s.fault,['kind','hop'],`${label} fault`);
        if(!['drop-forward','corrupt-forward','drop-reply'].includes(s.fault.kind))fail(`${label}: unknown fault.`);
        if(s.fault.kind==='drop-reply') {if(s.fault.hop!==undefined)fail(`${label}: drop-reply has no hop.`);}
        else if(!Number.isInteger(s.fault.hop)||s.fault.hop<0||s.fault.hop>3)fail(`${label}: hop is a zero-based index from 0 to 3.`);
      }
    }
  }
  const created=input.steps.filter(s=>['open','recover'].includes(s.action));
  const names=created.map(s=>s.action==='open'?s.circuit:s.replacement);
  if(names.length>8||new Set(names).size!==names.length)fail('Use at most 8 distinct circuit names; never replace an earlier name.');
  const packets=input.steps.filter(s=>s.action==='send').map(s=>s.packet);
  if(new Set(packets).size!==packets.length)fail('Every send needs a new packet name. Use replay to repeat captured bytes.');
  return structuredClone(input);
}

export const workshopContract={id:'multi-circuit-workshop-v1',version:1,
  requirement:'Run learner-authored ordered steps with the submitted protocol; keep failed steps and observer-scoped evidence. Written claims are unassessed.',
  semantics:'Sequential logical steps, not time or concurrent network simulation. Explicit recovery only; no automatic retry. Relay downtime is known to the experiment operator. Client sees no reply without the hidden fault cause. Packet replay sends captured forward bytes; new sends allocate a fresh sequence. Existing module contracts still apply.',
  limits:{steps:32,circuits:8,predictions:12},actions:fields};

export async function runWorkshop(impl,input) {
  const scenario=validateWorkshop(input),network=directory(),circuits=new Map(),captures=new Map();
  const observations=Object.fromEntries(['client',...relayIds,'archive'].map(id=>[id,[]]));
  const steps=[];
  let index=0;
  const record=(observer,event)=>observations[observer]?.push({step:index+1,...event});
  const snapshot=c=>({id:c.id,path:[...c.path],closed:c.closed,nextSeq:c.nextSeq,received:[...c.received],
    relayState:c.states.map(s=>({relay:s.relayId,seen:[...s.seenForward]}))});
  function circuit(name) {requireThat(circuits.has(name),'UNKNOWN_CIRCUIT',name);return circuits.get(name);}
  async function forward(c,name,packet,expectedSeq,fault={},clientWaiting=true) {
    const start=c.trace.length;
    let reachedClient=false;
    try {
      const destination=fault.hop===undefined?null:c.path[fault.hop];
      requireThat(fault.hop===undefined||destination,'BAD_HOP','The selected hop is outside this actual path.');
      const failed=c.path.find(id=>!network.find(r=>r.id===id).online);
      const request=await deliverForward(impl,c,packet,{failAt:failed,
        dropAt:fault.kind==='drop-forward'?destination:null,modifyAt:fault.kind==='corrupt-forward'?destination:null,
        onReceive:event=>record(event.observer,{...event,circuit:name,direction:'forward'})});
      let reply;
      try {reply=archive(request);}
      catch(error) {record('archive',{circuit:name,phase:'rejected',payload:request,code:error.code??error.name});throw error;}
      c.trace.push({direction:'endpoint',observer:'archive',previous:c.path.at(-1),payload:request});
      if(fault.kind==='drop-reply')throw new LabError('REPLY_LOST','Archive received the read-only lookup.');
      const response=await deliverBackward(impl,c,reply,expectedSeq);
      reachedClient=true;
      // Preserve accepted request binding at every return layer, including replay experiments.
      const unwrapped=await impl.unwrapReply(c.hops,response,expectedSeq);
      requireThat(!c.received.has(expectedSeq),'REPLAY');c.received.add(expectedSeq);
      record('client',{circuit:name,phase:'reply',seq:expectedSeq,payload:unwrapped});
      return unwrapped;
    } catch(error) {
      if(clientWaiting)record('client',{circuit:name,phase:'no-reply',detail:'No usable reply observed. The hidden fault cause and endpoint receipt are not established by this observation.'});
      if(!clientWaiting&&reachedClient)record('client',{circuit:name,phase:'rejected-reply',code:error.code??error.name});
      throw error;
    } finally {
      for(const event of c.trace.slice(start))record(event.observer,{...event,circuit:name,phase:'accepted'});
    }
  }
  try {
    for(index=0;index<scenario.steps.length;index++) {
      const action=scenario.steps[index],entry={step:index+1,input:action};
      try {
        if(action.action==='open') {
          const path=await impl.selectPath(network,action.avoid,action.length),c=establish(path,network);
          circuits.set(action.circuit,c);entry.value={path};record('client',{phase:'opened',circuit:action.circuit,path});
        }
        if(['offline','online'].includes(action.action)) {
          for(const id of action.relays)network.find(r=>r.id===id).online=action.action==='online';
          entry.value={relays:action.relays,online:action.action==='online'};
          // This is operator fault injection, not an oracle supplied to every observer.
        }
        if(action.action==='send') {
          const c=circuit(action.circuit);requireThat(!c.closed,'CIRCUIT_CLOSED');
          requireThat(action.fault?.hop===undefined||action.fault.hop<c.path.length,'BAD_HOP');
          const seq=c.nextSeq++;requireThat(seq<1024,'REBUILD_REQUIRED');
          const packet=await impl.wrapRequest(c.hops,{operation:'lookup',item:action.item},seq);
          captures.set(action.packet,{packet:structuredClone(packet),origin:action.circuit,seq});
          record('client',{phase:'sent',circuit:action.circuit,seq,item:action.item});
          entry.value=await forward(c,action.circuit,packet,seq,action.fault);
        }
        if(action.action==='replay') {
          requireThat(captures.has(action.packet),'UNKNOWN_PACKET',action.packet);
          const c=circuit(action.circuit);requireThat(!c.closed,'CIRCUIT_CLOSED');
          // Replay is experiment-operator injection; it is not a new client send or new encryption.
          const captured=captures.get(action.packet);
          entry.value=await forward(c,action.circuit,structuredClone(captured.packet),captured.seq,{},false);
        }
        if(action.action==='recover') {
          const old=circuit(action.circuit);requireThat(!old.closed,'CIRCUIT_CLOSED');
          record('client',{phase:'recovery-requested',circuit:action.circuit,failed:action.failed});
          const next=await recover(impl,old,network,action.failed);
          if(next.circuit)circuits.set(action.replacement,next.circuit);
          entry.value={plan:next.plan,oldClosed:old.closed,replacement:next.circuit?action.replacement:null};
          record('client',{phase:'recovered',circuit:action.circuit,...entry.value});
        }
        if(action.action==='close') {
          closeCircuit(circuit(action.circuit));entry.value={closed:true};record('client',{phase:'closed',circuit:action.circuit});
        }
        entry.outcome='returned';
      } catch(error) {entry.outcome='threw';entry.code=error.code??error.name;entry.detail=error.message;}
      entry.state=Object.fromEntries([...circuits].map(([name,c])=>[name,snapshot(c)]));
      steps.push(entry);
    }
    return {kind:'workshop',title:scenario.title,contract:workshopContract.id,predictions:scenario.predictions,
      reasoning:'UNASSESSED: compare your claims with observer evidence; step errors are experimental outcomes, not a course score.',
      steps,observations,circuits:Object.fromEntries([...circuits].map(([name,c])=>[name,snapshot(c)])),
      captures:[...captures].map(([name,c])=>({name,origin:c.origin,seq:c.seq})),
      visibility:'Operator-only steps and state contain the fault script and all circuits. Observer projections contain their local evidence. Shared step numbers and circuit names are teaching labels, not wire identifiers or timing measurements. Single-process simulation; no anonymity guarantee.',
      cleanup:'All remaining circuit key handles are discarded after this snapshot; closed fields describe the end of the authored steps.'};
  } finally {for(const c of circuits.values())closeCircuit(c);}
}

`courses/onion-network-course/observatory/checks/cases.mjs`:

```mjs
// Public requirement checks. These are practice feedback, not hidden certification.
import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
import { context, seal, open } from '../runtime/crypto.mjs';
import { directory, establish, exchange, deliverForward, deliverBackward, sampleRequest,
  tamper, recover, views } from '../runtime/network.mjs';

const cases = [];
const add = (id, module, requirement, input, run) => cases.push({ id, module, requirement, input, run });
const circuit = () => establish(['cedar', 'birch', 'maple']);
const errorCode = (fn, code) => {
  let observed='NO_ERROR';
  try { fn(); } catch(error) { observed=error.code??error.name; }
  assert.equal(observed,code,`Expected ${code}; observed ${observed}`);
};
function validPath(path, relays, failed, length) {
  assert.equal(path.length, length, 'Keep the requested number of hops.');
  assert.equal(new Set(path).size, length, 'Each relay must occur only once.');
  assert.ok(path.every(id => relays.some(r => r.id === id && r.online) && !failed.includes(id)),
    'Only online, permitted, non-failed relay IDs may occur.');
}

add('M1-distinct', 1, 'Choose three distinct available relays.', { length: 3 }, impl => {
  const relays = directory(); validPath(impl.selectPath(relays, [], 3), relays, [], 3);
});
add('M1-filter', 1, 'Respect both failed and offline relays without mutating the directory.',
  { failed: ['cedar'], offline: 'birch' }, impl => {
    const relays = directory(); relays[1].online = false; const before = structuredClone(relays);
    validPath(impl.selectPath(relays, ['cedar']), relays, ['cedar'], 3); assert.deepEqual(relays, before);
  });
add('M1-no-path', 1, 'Stop explicitly if too few distinct relays remain.', { available: 2 }, impl => {
  errorCode(() => impl.selectPath(directory().slice(0, 2)), 'NO_PATH');
});
add('M1-duplicate-directory', 1, 'Duplicate directory rows do not create distinct hops.', { ids: ['cedar', 'cedar', 'birch'] }, impl => {
  errorCode(() => impl.selectPath([{id:'cedar',online:true},{id:'cedar',online:true},{id:'birch',online:true}]), 'NO_PATH');
});

add('M2-layer-order', 2, 'Only the intended next relay can open the remaining onion.', { route: ['cedar','birch','maple'], seq: 0 }, impl => {
  const c = circuit(); let packet = impl.wrapRequest(c.hops, sampleRequest(), 0);
  for (let i = 0; i < c.hops.length; i++) {
    const hop = c.hops[i];
    const layer = open(hop.forwardKey, context(c.id, hop.relayId, 'forward', 0), packet);
    assert.equal(layer.next, c.path[i+1] ?? 'archive'); packet = layer.body;
  }
  assert.deepEqual(packet, sampleRequest());
});
add('M2-no-plaintext', 2, 'The outer packet exposes neither destination nor request.', { item:'luna' }, impl => {
  const c = circuit(); const encoded = JSON.stringify(impl.wrapRequest(c.hops, sampleRequest(), 1));
  for (const word of ['luna', 'lookup', 'archive', 'maple']) assert.ok(!encoded.includes(word), `Outer packet exposed ${word}`);
});
add('M2-context-binding', 2, 'Bind circuit, relay and direction to authentication.', { wrongContext: ['circuit','relay','direction'] }, impl => {
  const c = circuit(); const hop = c.hops[0]; const packet = impl.wrapRequest(c.hops, sampleRequest(), 2);
  const contexts = [context('other', hop.relayId,'forward',2), context(c.id,'elm','forward',2), context(c.id,hop.relayId,'backward',2)];
  for (const ctx of contexts) errorCode(() => open(hop.forwardKey, ctx, packet), 'AUTH_FAILED');
});
add('M2-two-hops', 2, 'Construct from the supplied hop list, without hard-coding three layers.', { hops:2 }, impl => {
  const c = establish(['elm','ash']); const first = impl.wrapRequest(c.hops, {operation:'lookup',item:'tide'}, 5);
  let packet = first;
  for (const hop of c.hops) packet = open(hop.forwardKey, context(c.id,hop.relayId,'forward',5),packet).body;
  assert.equal(packet.item,'tide');
});

add('M3-forward', 3, 'Peel exactly one authenticated layer and preserve the inner packet.', { request:sampleRequest() }, impl => {
  const c = circuit(); const packet = impl.wrapRequest(c.hops,sampleRequest(),0);
  assert.deepEqual(deliverForward(impl,c,packet),sampleRequest());
});
add('M3-return', 3, 'Wrap reply exit-to-entry and unwrap entry-to-exit using backward keys.', { seq:4 }, impl => {
  const c = circuit(); const reply = {record:'fictional atlas'};
  const packet = deliverBackward(impl,c,reply,4);
  assert.deepEqual(impl.unwrapReply(c.hops,packet,4),reply);
  errorCode(() => open(c.hops[0].forwardKey,context(c.id,c.path[0],'backward',4),packet),'AUTH_FAILED');
});
add('M3-return-request-binding', 3, 'Bind a reply to the caller\'s expected request sequence, not the packet\'s claimed sequence.',
  { packetSequence:7, expectedSequence:8, correctExpectedSequence:7 }, impl => {
    const c=establish(['elm','ash']), reply={record:'reply to request 7'};
    const packet=deliverBackward(impl,c,reply,7);
    errorCode(()=>impl.unwrapReply(c.hops,packet,8),'BAD_PACKET');
    assert.deepEqual(impl.unwrapReply(c.hops,packet,7),reply,
      'Rejecting the wrong expected sequence must not prevent the correctly matched reply.');
  });
add('M3-return-inner-binding', 3, 'Every return layer must bind to the same caller-supplied expected sequence.',
  { outerSequence:8, innerSequence:7, expectedSequence:8 }, impl => {
    const c=establish(['elm','ash']);
    const inner=impl.addReturnLayer(c.hops[1],{record:'reply to request 7'},7);
    const mixed=impl.addReturnLayer(c.hops[0],inner,8);
    errorCode(()=>impl.unwrapReply(c.hops,mixed,8),'BAD_PACKET');
  });
add('M3-return-independent', 3, 'Stateless reply unwrapping permits correctly matched replies out of order and on independent circuits.',
  { arrivalSequences:[9,2], independentCircuitSequence:9 }, impl => {
    const a=establish(['elm','ash']), b=establish(['elm','ash']);
    const early={record:'reply 2'}, late={record:'reply 9'}, separate={record:'independent reply 9'};
    const p2=deliverBackward(impl,a,early,2), p9=deliverBackward(impl,a,late,9);
    const independent=deliverBackward(impl,b,separate,9);
    assert.deepEqual(impl.unwrapReply(a.hops,p9,9),late);
    assert.deepEqual(impl.unwrapReply(a.hops,p2,2),early);
    assert.deepEqual(impl.unwrapReply(b.hops,independent,9),separate);
    assert.deepEqual(impl.unwrapReply(a.hops,p2,2),early,
      'Unwrap is stateless: replay acceptance remains the receiver\'s separate responsibility.');
    errorCode(()=>impl.unwrapReply(b.hops,p9,9),'AUTH_FAILED');
  });
add('M3-wrong-route', 3, 'Reject an authenticated instruction that disagrees with local successor state.', { next:'ash', expected:'birch' }, impl => {
  const c = circuit(); const s = c.states[0];
  const packet = seal(s.forwardKey,context(c.id,s.relayId,'forward',6),{next:'ash',body:{}});
  errorCode(() => impl.peelForward(s,packet),'BAD_ROUTE');
});
add('M3-missing-body', 3, 'Reject an authenticated matching route without a body before consuming its sequence.', { missing:'body' }, impl => {
  const c=circuit(), s=c.states[0];
  const packet=seal(s.forwardKey,context(c.id,s.relayId,'forward',10),{next:s.next});
  errorCode(()=>impl.peelForward(s,packet),'BAD_ROUTE');
  assert.equal(s.seenForward.size,0,'Rejected payload must not consume the sequence.');
});
add('M3-end-to-end', 3, 'Use the learner functions for the entire request and return.', { item:'luna' }, impl => {
  const c=circuit(); assert.deepEqual(exchange(impl,c),{item:'luna',record:'Luna: a fictional lunar atlas'});
  const v = views(c);
  assert.equal(v.cedar[0].payload,'[encrypted inner packet]');
  assert.equal(v.birch[0].payload,'[encrypted inner packet]');
  assert.deepEqual(v.maple[0].payload,sampleRequest());
  assert.equal(v.archive[0].previous,'maple');
});

add('M4-replay', 4, 'A relay must reject a repeated valid packet on the same circuit.', { repeatSeq:0 }, impl => {
  const c=circuit(); const packet=impl.wrapRequest(c.hops,sampleRequest(),0);
  impl.peelForward(c.states[0],packet); errorCode(()=>impl.peelForward(c.states[0],packet),'REPLAY');
});
add('M4-tamper-first', 4, 'An invalid tag must not consume the sequence number.', { tamper:'ciphertext', then:'original' }, impl => {
  const c=circuit(); const packet=impl.wrapRequest(c.hops,sampleRequest(),0);
  errorCode(()=>impl.peelForward(c.states[0],tamper(packet)),'AUTH_FAILED');
  assert.equal(c.states[0].seenForward.size,0,'Authenticate before changing freshness state.');
  assert.equal(impl.peelForward(c.states[0],packet).next,'birch');
});
add('M4-header-tamper', 4, 'Changing the visible sequence must fail authentication.', { from:0,to:1 }, impl => {
  const c=circuit(); const packet=impl.wrapRequest(c.hops,sampleRequest(),0); packet.seq=1;
  errorCode(()=>impl.peelForward(c.states[0],packet),'AUTH_FAILED');
  assert.equal(c.states[0].seenForward.size,0);
});
add('M4-freshness-policy', 4, 'Accept unseen in-range values even out of order; reject replay and invalid values.', { arrival:[8,2,8] }, impl => {
  const seen=new Set(); impl.acceptSequence(seen,8); impl.acceptSequence(seen,2);
  errorCode(()=>impl.acceptSequence(seen,8),'REPLAY');
  for (const seq of [-1,1024,1.5,NaN,'5',null]) errorCode(()=>impl.acceptSequence(seen,seq),'BAD_SEQUENCE');
  assert.deepEqual([...seen].sort((a,b)=>a-b),[2,8]);
});
add('M4-circuit-separation', 4, 'A packet from another circuit must fail without poisoning this circuit.', { reusedSeq:0 }, impl => {
  const a=circuit(), b=circuit(); const packet=impl.wrapRequest(a.hops,sampleRequest(),0);
  errorCode(()=>impl.peelForward(b.states[0],packet),'AUTH_FAILED');
  assert.equal(b.states[0].seenForward.size,0);
});
add('M4-return-tamper', 4, 'Return authentication must complete before any reply is accepted.', { tamper:'return-ciphertext' }, impl => {
  const c=circuit(); const packet=deliverBackward(impl,c,{record:'atlas'},9);
  errorCode(()=>impl.unwrapReply(c.hops,tamper(packet),9),'AUTH_FAILED');
});
add('M4-bad-route-state', 4, 'A rejected route must not mutate freshness state.', { next:'wrong' }, impl => {
  const c=circuit(), s=c.states[0]; const packet=seal(s.forwardKey,context(c.id,s.relayId,'forward',12),{next:'wrong',body:{}});
  errorCode(()=>impl.peelForward(s,packet),'BAD_ROUTE'); assert.equal(s.seenForward.size,0);
});

add('M5-rebuild', 5, 'Replace a broken circuit with distinct available relays and fresh circuit identity.', { failed:['birch'] }, impl => {
  const c=circuit(); errorCode(()=>exchange(impl,c,sampleRequest(),{failAt:'birch'}),'RELAY_DOWN');
  const next=recover(impl,c,directory(),['birch']);
  assert.equal(c.closed,true); assert.equal(next.plan.action,'rebuild');
  validPath(next.circuit.path,directory(),['birch'],3); assert.notEqual(next.circuit.id,c.id);
  assert.equal(exchange(impl,next.circuit).item,'luna');
  errorCode(()=>exchange(impl,c),'CIRCUIT_CLOSED');
});
add('M5-stop', 5, 'Report no path instead of weakening the requested route.', { failed:['cedar','birch','maple'] }, impl => {
  assert.deepEqual(impl.recoveryPlan(directory(),['cedar','birch','maple'],['cedar','birch','maple']),{action:'stop',reason:'NO_PATH'});
});
add('M5-old-packet', 5, 'Fresh circuit keys reject old packets even when a relay is reused.', { failed:['birch'] }, impl => {
  const c=circuit(); const packet=impl.wrapRequest(c.hops,sampleRequest(),0);
  const next=recover(impl,c,directory(),['birch']).circuit;
  errorCode(()=>impl.peelForward(next.states[0],packet),'AUTH_FAILED');
});
add('M5-lost-reply', 5, 'A lost reply does not prove that the archive did not receive the request.', { dropReply:true }, impl => {
  const c=circuit(); errorCode(()=>exchange(impl,c,sampleRequest(),{dropReply:true}),'REPLY_LOST');
  assert.equal(c.trace.filter(e=>e.observer==='archive').length,1);
  const next=recover(impl,c,directory(),[]).circuit; assert.equal(exchange(impl,next).item,'luna');
});

add('M6-shift', 6, 'Compare inter-event gaps, allowing an unknown constant delay.', { entry:[0,4,13],candidate:[50,54,63] }, impl => {
  assert.deepEqual(impl.correlate([0,4,13],[{id:'x',times:[50,54,63]},{id:'y',times:[50,59,63]}],0),['x']);
});
add('M6-ambiguity', 6, 'Keep every plausible match; matching is not proof of identity.', { matchingCandidates:2 }, impl => {
  const candidates=[{id:'x',times:[20,24,33]},{id:'y',times:[70,75,83]},{id:'z',times:[10,14]}];
  assert.deepEqual([...impl.correlate([0,4,13],candidates,1)],['x','y']);
});
add('M6-none', 6, 'Return no matches for incompatible or insufficient observations.', { events:1 }, impl => {
  assert.deepEqual(impl.correlate([0],[{id:'x',times:[10]}],1),[]);
  assert.deepEqual(impl.correlate([0,4,13],[{id:'x',times:[10,20,30]}],0),[]);
});

export { cases };
export async function evaluate(implementation, through = 6) {
  const results=[];
  for (const test of cases.filter(c=>c.module<=through)) {
    try { await test.run(implementation); results.push({...summary(test),pass:true}); }
    catch(error) { results.push({...summary(test),pass:false,code:error.code??error.name,detail:error.message,
      ...(error.actual !== undefined ? {actual:error.actual,expected:error.expected}: {})}); }
  }
  return {passed:results.filter(r=>r.pass).length,total:results.length,results};
}
function summary(test) { return {id:test.id,module:test.module,requirement:test.requirement,input:test.input,lesson:`lessons/0${test.module}.md`}; }

`courses/onion-network-course/observatory/examples/browser-sibling.js`:

```js
// One layer only. Helpers are supplied by the workbench.
async function oneLayerExample(key) {
  const ctx = context('sibling-circuit', 'oak', 'forward', 0);
  const packet = await seal(key, ctx, {next:'archive', body:{operation:'lookup', item:'tide'}});
  const opened = await open(key, ctx, packet);
  return {packetFields:Object.keys(packet), opened};
}

// A complete ONE-layer sibling example. It does not solve the multi-hop project.
import { freshKey, seal, open, context } from '../runtime/crypto.mjs';
const key=freshKey();
const ctx=context('sibling-circuit','oak','forward',0);
const packet=seal(key,ctx,{next:'archive',body:{operation:'lookup',item:'tide'}});
const opened=open(key,ctx,packet);
console.log(JSON.stringify({packetFields:Object.keys(packet),opened},null,2));

# 1. Choose a path and name the observer

Choose a three-relay path and distinguish a relay’s local view from the simulator’s complete view.

Your build: selectPath returns three distinct usable relay IDs or reports NO_PATH.

Dependencies: JavaScript entry skills.

## A request with several observers

You want the fictional archive to receive a lookup without giving one ordinary relay both the client label and the archive request. A relay is a program that forwards traffic. A circuit is an ordered path through relays. In our running path, client → cedar → birch → maple → archive, cedar is the entry, birch is the middle and maple is the exit. These are roles on this path, not permanent properties of the programs.

Every arrow is a function call in one local execution context: a Node process on the CLI path or a disposable worker in the browser. A packet is a JavaScript object handed to the next function. The process operator can inspect all objects, keys and calls. We will deliberately restrict the trace shown for each relay to what that relay receives or sends. This restricted trace is a teaching view, not a security boundary.

A neighbor is the program immediately before or after a relay. Cedar’s incoming neighbor is client and its outgoing neighbor is birch. Knowing a neighbor is different from knowing the final destination or reading a request. The next modules add encryption so that opening one layer will reveal only the next instruction and an inner packet. # 2. Wrap the onion from the destination outward

Construct a nested authenticated packet that each relay can open exactly one layer at a time.

Your build: wrapRequest builds the entry packet using a separate forward key for each hop.

Dependencies: 1.

## What a layer promises

Plaintext is the value before encryption. Ciphertext is its encrypted representation. A symmetric key is a secret shared by the sender and the intended opener of a layer. The client shares a different forward key with each relay. Sharing the cedar key with birch would defeat the intended separation.

Authenticated encryption checks that ciphertext and its associated context have not changed before returning plaintext. The supplied seal and open functions use AES-256-GCM from Node’s installed crypto library on the CLI path and built-in Web Crypto in the browser. You do not implement AES or an authentication algorithm. seal returns a packet containing a sequence number, ciphertext and an authentication tag. The tag is checked by open; a failed check throws AUTH_FAILED without returning any plaintext.

Associated data is authenticated context that need not be secret. Here it binds a layer to the protocol version, circuit ID, relay ID, direction and sequence. A circuit ID labels one run’s circuit. A direction distinguishes traffic toward the archive from traffic toward the client. A sequence identifies a packet position within a direction. Binding these fields prevents a ciphertext from being accepted in another context merely because someone changes an outer label. The context is reconstructed locally, not trusted from a peer’s assertion.

**Commit practice q2:** A packet authenticated for circuit red is offered under circuit blue with the same key and sequence. Can open accept it under the changed context? Enter true or false.

Run `node tools/practice.mjs q2` to see the submission route. Commit before reading its feedback; then continue.

## Build inside, open outside

Each forward plaintext has two fields: next, the successor’s label, and body, the value to forward. At the exit, next is archive and body is the lookup. At an earlier relay, body is the entire encrypted packet for its successor. The earlier relay can read next after authenticating its own layer, but it lacks the successor’s key.

Consider a two-hop sibling path through oak and yew. First make a yew layer containing the archive instruction and lookup. Then place that encrypted packet inside an oak layer whose next field names yew. The outermost key therefore belongs to the first relay even though that layer was constructed last. Opening follows oak then yew; construction follows yew then oak.

For the running three-hop path, start with the request as a current body. Visit hops from the last index to zero. At each visit, create next from the following hop’s relayId, using archive when there is no following hop. Seal that instruction with the current hop’s forwardKey and its context, and use the resulting packet as the new current body. Return the final packet. Do not attach the request or the full route beside the ciphertext: doing so would disclose the facts the layers are meant to hide.

**Commit practice q3:** For path client → A → B → C → D → archive, list relay IDs in the order the client must SEAL layers. Enter a JSON array.

Run `node tools/practice.mjs q3` to see the submission route. Commit before reading its feedback; then continue.

## Keep nonces unique

A nonce is an input to an encryption operation that must not repeat under the same key. GCM can fail catastrophically if a key and nonce pair is reused. In this toy, the wrapper encodes the sequence in a 12-byte nonce, uses fresh keys for every hop and direction of every new circuit, and rejects a second seal with the same key and sequence. The visible sequence is not a secret.

Changing only the circuit ID in associated data would not make nonce reuse safe. Associated data binds meaning; it does not create a new encryption key. The supplied circuit setup creates new key handles and keeps their bytes private inside the crypto wrapper. This is a trusted in-process setup, not an authenticated key exchange. A real remote relay cannot obtain its key by reaching into this process.

Implement wrapRequest and run the cumulative module 2 check. It tests both two-hop and three-hop paths, so hard-coding cedar, birch or maple will fail. Read the executed one-layer sibling in examples/sibling.mjs if the API is unfamiliar. Your task is to compose that operation into the onion, keeping the original request out of all unencrypted packet fields.

**Commit application t2:** A developer resets sequence to zero while retaining the same encryption key, and changes the circuit ID in associated data. Is the key/nonce pair fresh? Enter true or false.

Run `node tools/practice.mjs t2` to see the submission route. Commit before reading its feedback; then continue.

## Build and check

Implement wrapRequest with seal and context. Run: node tools/lab.mjs check 2

# 3. Forward one layer and bring the reply back

Open a single local instruction and build the reverse encryption path for the archive reply.

Your build: peelForward, addReturnLayer and unwrapReply complete an offline round trip.

Dependencies: 1, 2.

## A relay has local state

Each relay state contains its own relayId, circuitId, previous and next neighbor, its two key handles, and a seenForward set. It contains neither the complete path nor the other relays’ keys. The harness knows the whole circuit to connect the calls; the learner’s peelForward function receives only one state and one packet.

Open the packet using this relay’s forward key and the forward context. Check that the opened value contains body and that its next field equals the successor recorded during setup. Authentication says that the layer came from a holder of the key and has not been altered. It does not say that the instruction is valid for the local circuit. This separate route check detects a bug or an inconsistent instruction even when its tag is valid.

For a sibling circuit whose local state says next is yew, a valid layer saying next is ash must be rejected with BAD_ROUTE. The relay should not reinterpret the circuit or forward to a new program because a packet asks it to. On success, return the opened next and body unchanged. The harness forwards body to the next relay. In module 4 you will add freshness immediately before returning; for now you may leave the supplied seenForward set untouched.

**Commit practice q4:** A local relay state records next=Q. Its packet authenticates and opens to {next:R, body:...}. Enter the error code the route check should produce, as a JSON string.

Run `node tools/practice.mjs q4` to see the submission route. Commit before reading its feedback; then continue.

## The reply gains layers

The archive sends its reply to the exit. The exit can read the archive’s reply because our fictional archive has no separate endpoint encryption. The exit encrypts the reply with its backward key. Each earlier relay adds its own backward layer around the packet it receives, without opening that inner packet. Thus the reply gains layers as it approaches the client.

For oak → yew → archive, yew first wraps the reply, then oak wraps yew’s packet. The client opens oak’s layer, then yew’s layer. This reverse-direction behavior is not the forward routine run backward: forward relays remove layers; backward relays add them. Separate forward and backward keys prevent the two directions from using the same key and nonce pair when each begins at sequence zero.

Implement addReturnLayer as one seal with the backward key and context. Implement unwrapReply by opening each hop’s backward layer in path order. The caller’s expectedSeq must be used in every layer’s context. unwrapReply verifies the cryptographic layers but has no replay state argument; the supplied client tracks received sequence numbers only after successful matched unwrapping. A pure decrypt function and a stateful receiver have different jobs. Keep those jobs explicit.

**Commit practice q5:** For client → A → B → C → archive, list the order the client OPENS the return layers.

Run `node tools/practice.mjs q5` to see the submission route. Commit before reading its feedback; then continue.

## Bind the reply to its request

An authentic reply can belong to a different request. Suppose the client is waiting for request twelve but receives an unchanged reply for request eleven. Its tag may be genuine. If you derive the expected sequence from that packet, you only establish which sequence the packet claims; you never compare it with the request the caller expects.

Use the caller’s expectedSeq for every open operation. In the sibling case, passing twelve into open rejects the packet for eleven with BAD_PACKET before releasing a reply. Supplying eleven later can still open that same genuine packet. Also reject an onion whose outer layer matches twelve but whose inner layer belongs to eleven: checking only the outside leaves a gap at the next hop.

Request matching does not require increasing arrival order. Two calls may unwrap reply twelve and then reply eleven, provided each supplies its own matching expected sequence. Independent circuits may also use the same sequence under different keys. These are valid matches. Replay acceptance remains a separate stateful receiver decision; do not add a global seen set or maximum sequence to unwrapReply.

**Commit practice q3binding:** The caller expects request 18. The reply outer layer is authentic for 18, but its inner layer is authentic for 17. Enter the error code unwrapReply must produce, as a JSON string.

Run `node tools/practice.mjs q3binding` to see the submission route. Commit before reading its feedback; then continue.

## Inspect an actual round trip

Run the module 3 check, then the demo command. The demo uses your functions for both directions. It returns the fictional archive record and shows a trace grouped by observer. Inspect cedar, birch, maple and archive separately before reading the complete group.

Cedar sees the client neighbor and birch. Birch sees cedar and maple. Maple sees birch, the archive instruction and the plaintext lookup; the archive sees maple as its caller. The trace records packet sizes and sequences as well as payload visibility. Encryption does not hide that a packet was forwarded, and our variable-size JSON encoding leaks more structure than a fixed-size cell design would. The toy also shares one circuit ID across hop states and carries the same sequence across layers. Colluding observers can use those labels; the separate timing exercise deliberately omits them. This is another reason these views do not establish anonymity.

These view fields are projections that the harness writes after each action, not evidence that JavaScript has isolated three adversarial machines. To inspect causality, open the offline workbench, commit its prediction, and step through the generated demonstration. The trace data comes from a reference execution, clearly marked as a demonstration. Your own CLI run and saved source establish whether your build performs the same required behaviors.

# 4. Separate authenticity from freshness

Reject changed and repeated packets while preserving receiver state when authentication fails.

Your build: acceptSequence and peelForward enforce bounded, circuit-local replay tracking.

Dependencies: 2, 3.

## A valid packet can be old

A replay is a previously valid packet sent again. Copying ciphertext does not alter its tag, so authenticated encryption alone can accept the copy. A receiver needs state to distinguish a fresh packet from one it has already accepted.

The toy’s freshness policy is explicit: accept an unseen integer sequence from zero through 1023, reject a repeated value with REPLAY, and reject an out-of-range or non-integer value with BAD_SEQUENCE. The seenForward set belongs to one relay on one circuit. It is bounded by the finite sequence range. The policy permits out-of-order arrival; accepting sequence eight does not by itself forbid an unseen sequence two. This is a teaching policy, not a claim about Tor’s ordering rules.

Before you modify the relay, predict what happens if an altered packet arrives before the original packet with the same sequence. Use the distinction between authentication and receiver state. Then implement acceptSequence: validate the range, reject membership, and add only a fresh sequence.

**Commit prediction p4:** A receiver first sees a damaged packet with sequence 7, then the genuine packet with sequence 7. Should the genuine packet be accepted under the stated policy? Enter true or false.

Run `node tools/practice.mjs p4` to see the submission route. Commit before reading its feedback; then continue.

## Commit state after validation

The receiver’s order is open, validate the route, then accept the sequence. Only after those steps should the harness receive a body to forward. If you add a sequence before authenticating, a forged packet can occupy the set entry and cause a later genuine packet to be rejected as a replay. The forged packet would have changed application state without proving anything.

For a sibling receiver with an empty set, a damaged sequence five throws AUTH_FAILED and leaves the set empty. A genuine sequence five can then be accepted and recorded. The next copy of that genuine packet authenticates but throws REPLAY. If its authenticated next field is wrong, it throws BAD_ROUTE and also leaves the set unchanged.

The lab deliberately keeps a circuit available after a rejected packet so you can inspect this distinction. It is not prescribing recovery behavior for a production anonymity protocol. Real protocols may tear down a circuit after an integrity failure. Our exact contract is local rejection without state mutation, which the checker can reproduce without any external traffic.

**Commit practice q6:** A relay has accepted sequences 9 and 3. A valid sequence 4 arrives. Is it fresh under this lab’s policy? Enter true or false.

Run `node tools/practice.mjs q6` to see the submission route. Commit before reading its feedback; then continue.

## Test the reason for rejection

Run the cumulative module 4 check. It changes a ciphertext byte, changes the visible sequence, replays a valid packet, sends a packet to another circuit, and corrupts a return packet. A tag failure should not be reported as a replay. A replay should not be accepted merely because its tag is valid. These distinct outcomes make debugging useful.

When a test fails, first inspect the named input and error code, then inspect the state mutation nearest that code. If the original packet cannot pass after a damaged one, inspect when seenForward was changed. If a packet crosses circuit boundaries, inspect the context used by open and which key handle you supplied. Avoid fixing a symptom by catching every error and returning success.

Authentication protects a message relative to a key. It does not protect against the legitimate exit reading the plaintext that it is meant to receive. It also does not hide timing, lengths or endpoint identifiers. Carry this distinction into the recovery work: a fresh circuit solves some state problems, but it does not erase observations already made.

**Commit application t4:** Two fresh circuits have different keys and different seenForward sets. Each receives its own valid sequence 0. How many packets are accepted in total?

Run `node tools/practice.mjs t4` to see the submission route. Commit before reading its feedback; then continue.
