async function evaluate(implementation, through = 6) {
  const results=[];
  for (const test of cases.filter(c=>c.module<=through)) {
    try { await test.run(implementation); results.push({...summary(test),pass:true}); }
    catch(error) { results.push({...summary(test),pass:false,code:error.code??error.name,detail:error.message,
      ...(error.actual !== undefined ? {actual:error.actual,expected:error.expected}: {})}); }
  }
  return {passed:results.filter(r=>r.pass).length,total:results.length,results};
}
function summary(test) { return {id:test.id,module:test.module,requirement:test.requirement,input:test.input,lesson:`lessons/0${test.module}.md`}; }

return {cases,evaluate};
})();
const BrowserWorkshop=(()=>{
const {requireThat,LabError}=BrowserCrypto; const {directory,establish,closeCircuit,deliverForward,deliverBackward,archive,recover}=BrowserNetwork;
// Ordered, entirely in-process experiments. This schedules the existing learner protocol.

const relayIds=directory().map(r=>r.id);
const fields={open:['circuit','length','avoid'],send:['circuit','packet','item','fault'],
  replay:['circuit','packet'],offline:['relays'],online:['relays'],recover:['circuit','replacement','failed'],close:['circuit']};
const fail=message=>{throw new LabError('BAD_SCENARIO',message);};
const object=value=>value&&typeof value==='object'&&!Array.isArray(value);
function only(value,keys,label) {
  if(!object(value)||Object.keys(value).some(k=>!keys.includes(k)))fail(`${label}: use only ${keys.join(', ')}.`);
}
function alias(value,label) {if(typeof value!=='string'||!(/^[a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9_-]{0,31}$/).test(value))fail(`${label}: use a short letter-led name.`);}
function relays(value,label) {if(!Array.isArray(value)||value.some(x=>!relayIds.includes(x))||new Set(value).size!==value.length)fail(`${label}: use distinct supplied relay names.`);}
function validateWorkshop(input) {
  only(input,['version','title','predictions','steps'],'Scenario');
  if(input.version!==1||typeof input.title!=='string'||!input.title.trim()||input.title.length>160)fail('Use version 1 and a title of 1–160 characters.');
  if(!Array.isArray(input.predictions)||input.predictions.length>12)fail('Use a predictions array (up to 12 claims).');
  for(const p of input.predictions) {
    only(p,['observer','claim'],'Prediction');
    if(!['client','archive','operator',...relayIds].includes(p.observer)||typeof p.claim!=='string'||!p.claim.trim()||p.claim.length>2000)fail('Each prediction needs a supplied observer and a claim of 1–2000 characters.');
  }
  if(!Array.isArray(input.steps)||input.steps.length<1||input.steps.length>32)fail('Use 1–32 ordered steps.');
  for(const [i,s] of input.steps.entries()) {
    const label=`Step ${i+1}`;
    if(!object(s)||!Object.hasOwn(fields,s.action))fail(`${label}: unknown action.`);
    only(s,['action',...fields[s.action]],label);
    for(const key of ['circuit','packet','replacement'])if(fields[s.action].includes(key))alias(s[key],`${label} ${key}`);
    if(s.action==='open') {if(![2,3,4].includes(s.length))fail(`${label}: length must be 2, 3 or 4.`);relays(s.avoid,`${label} avoid`);}
    if(['online','offline'].includes(s.action))relays(s.relays,`${label} relays`);
    if(s.action==='recover')relays(s.failed,`${label} failed`);
    if(s.action==='send') {
      if(!['luna','tide'].includes(s.item))fail(`${label}: choose luna or tide.`);
      if(s.fault!==undefined) {
        only(s.fault,['kind','hop'],`${label} fault`);
        if(!['drop-forward','corrupt-forward','drop-reply'].includes(s.fault.kind))fail(`${label}: unknown fault.`);
        if(s.fault.kind==='drop-reply') {if(s.fault.hop!==undefined)fail(`${label}: drop-reply has no hop.`);}
        else if(!Number.isInteger(s.fault.hop)||s.fault.hop<0||s.fault.hop>3)fail(`${label}: hop is a zero-based index from 0 to 3.`);
      }
    }
  }
  const created=input.steps.filter(s=>['open','recover'].includes(s.action));
  const names=created.map(s=>s.action==='open'?s.circuit:s.replacement);
  if(names.length>8||new Set(names).size!==names.length)fail('Use at most 8 distinct circuit names; never replace an earlier name.');
  const packets=input.steps.filter(s=>s.action==='send').map(s=>s.packet);
  if(new Set(packets).size!==packets.length)fail('Every send needs a new packet name. Use replay to repeat captured bytes.');
  return structuredClone(input);
}

const workshopContract={id:'multi-circuit-workshop-v1',version:1,
  requirement:'Run learner-authored ordered steps with the submitted protocol; keep failed steps and observer-scoped evidence. Written claims are unassessed.',
  semantics:'Sequential logical steps, not time or concurrent network simulation. Explicit recovery only; no automatic retry. Relay downtime is known to the experiment operator. Client sees no reply without the hidden fault cause. Packet replay sends captured forward bytes; new sends allocate a fresh sequence. Existing module contracts still apply.',
  limits:{steps:32,circuits:8,predictions:12},actions:fields};

async function runWorkshop(impl,input) {
  const scenario=validateWorkshop(input),network=directory(),circuits=new Map(),captures=new Map();
  const observations=Object.fromEntries(['client',...relayIds,'archive'].map(id=>[id,[]]));
  const steps=[];
  let index=0;
  const record=(observer,event)=>observations[observer]?.push({step:index+1,...event});
  const snapshot=c=>({id:c.id,path:[...c.path],closed:c.closed,nextSeq:c.nextSeq,received:[...c.received],
    relayState:c.states.map(s=>({relay:s.relayId,seen:[...s.seenForward]}))});
  function circuit(name) {requireThat(circuits.has(name),'UNKNOWN_CIRCUIT',name);return circuits.get(name);}
  async function forward(c,name,packet,expectedSeq,fault={},clientWaiting=true) {
    const start=c.trace.length;
    let reachedClient=false;
    try {
      const destination=fault.hop===undefined?null:c.path[fault.hop];
      requireThat(fault.hop===undefined||destination,'BAD_HOP','The selected hop is outside this actual path.');
      const failed=c.path.find(id=>!network.find(r=>r.id===id).online);
      const request=await deliverForward(impl,c,packet,{failAt:failed,
        dropAt:fault.kind==='drop-forward'?destination:null,modifyAt:fault.kind==='corrupt-forward'?destination:null,
        onReceive:event=>record(event.observer,{...event,circuit:name,direction:'forward'})});
      let reply;
      try {reply=archive(request);}
      catch(error) {record('archive',{circuit:name,phase:'rejected',payload:request,code:error.code??error.name});throw error;}
      c.trace.push({direction:'endpoint',observer:'archive',previous:c.path.at(-1),payload:request});
      if(fault.kind==='drop-reply')throw new LabError('REPLY_LOST','Archive received the read-only lookup.');
      const response=await deliverBackward(impl,c,reply,expectedSeq);
      reachedClient=true;
      // Preserve accepted request binding at every return layer, including replay experiments.
      const unwrapped=await impl.unwrapReply(c.hops,response,expectedSeq);
      requireThat(!c.received.has(expectedSeq),'REPLAY');c.received.add(expectedSeq);
      record('client',{circuit:name,phase:'reply',seq:expectedSeq,payload:unwrapped});
      return unwrapped;
    } catch(error) {
      if(clientWaiting)record('client',{circuit:name,phase:'no-reply',detail:'No usable reply observed. The hidden fault cause and endpoint receipt are not established by this observation.'});
      if(!clientWaiting&&reachedClient)record('client',{circuit:name,phase:'rejected-reply',code:error.code??error.name});
      throw error;
    } finally {
      for(const event of c.trace.slice(start))record(event.observer,{...event,circuit:name,phase:'accepted'});
    }
  }
  try {
    for(index=0;index<scenario.steps.length;index++) {
      const action=scenario.steps[index],entry={step:index+1,input:action};
      try {
        if(action.action==='open') {
          const path=await impl.selectPath(network,action.avoid,action.length),c=establish(path,network);
          circuits.set(action.circuit,c);entry.value={path};record('client',{phase:'opened',circuit:action.circuit,path});
        }
        if(['offline','online'].includes(action.action)) {
          for(const id of action.relays)network.find(r=>r.id===id).online=action.action==='online';
          entry.value={relays:action.relays,online:action.action==='online'};
          // This is operator fault injection, not an oracle supplied to every observer.
        }
        if(action.action==='send') {
          const c=circuit(action.circuit);requireThat(!c.closed,'CIRCUIT_CLOSED');
          requireThat(action.fault?.hop===undefined||action.fault.hop<c.path.length,'BAD_HOP');
          const seq=c.nextSeq++;requireThat(seq<1024,'REBUILD_REQUIRED');
          const packet=await impl.wrapRequest(c.hops,{operation:'lookup',item:action.item},seq);
          captures.set(action.packet,{packet:structuredClone(packet),origin:action.circuit,seq});
          record('client',{phase:'sent',circuit:action.circuit,seq,item:action.item});
          entry.value=await forward(c,action.circuit,packet,seq,action.fault);
        }
        if(action.action==='replay') {
          requireThat(captures.has(action.packet),'UNKNOWN_PACKET',action.packet);
          const c=circuit(action.circuit);requireThat(!c.closed,'CIRCUIT_CLOSED');
          // Replay is experiment-operator injection; it is not a new client send or new encryption.
          const captured=captures.get(action.packet);
          entry.value=await forward(c,action.circuit,structuredClone(captured.packet),captured.seq,{},false);
        }
        if(action.action==='recover') {
          const old=circuit(action.circuit);requireThat(!old.closed,'CIRCUIT_CLOSED');
          record('client',{phase:'recovery-requested',circuit:action.circuit,failed:action.failed});
          const next=await recover(impl,old,network,action.failed);
          if(next.circuit)circuits.set(action.replacement,next.circuit);
          entry.value={plan:next.plan,oldClosed:old.closed,replacement:next.circuit?action.replacement:null};
          record('client',{phase:'recovered',circuit:action.circuit,...entry.value});
        }
        if(action.action==='close') {
          closeCircuit(circuit(action.circuit));entry.value={closed:true};record('client',{phase:'closed',circuit:action.circuit});
        }
        entry.outcome='returned';
      } catch(error) {entry.outcome='threw';entry.code=error.code??error.name;entry.detail=error.message;}
      entry.state=Object.fromEntries([...circuits].map(([name,c])=>[name,snapshot(c)]));
      steps.push(entry);
    }
    return {kind:'workshop',title:scenario.title,contract:workshopContract.id,predictions:scenario.predictions,
      reasoning:'UNASSESSED: compare your claims with observer evidence; step errors are experimental outcomes, not a course score.',
      steps,observations,circuits:Object.fromEntries([...circuits].map(([name,c])=>[name,snapshot(c)])),
      captures:[...captures].map(([name,c])=>({name,origin:c.origin,seq:c.seq})),
      visibility:'Operator-only steps and state contain the fault script and all circuits. Observer projections contain their local evidence. Shared step numbers and circuit names are teaching labels, not wire identifiers or timing measurements. Single-process simulation; no anonymity guarantee.',
      cleanup:'All remaining circuit key handles are discarded after this snapshot; closed fields describe the end of the authored steps.'};
  } finally {for(const c of circuits.values())closeCircuit(c);}
}

return {validateWorkshop,workshopContract,runWorkshop};
})();
const BrowserRunner=(()=>{
const {seal,open,context,requireThat,LabError}=BrowserCrypto; const {directory,establish,exchange,deliverForward,deliverBackward,archive,tamper,recover,views}=BrowserNetwork; const {evaluate,cases}=BrowserChecks; const {runWorkshop}=BrowserWorkshop;

const functionNames=['selectPath','wrapRequest','peelForward','addReturnLayer','unwrapReply','acceptSequence','recoveryPlan','correlate'];
function compileLearner(source) {
  requireThat(typeof source==='string'&&source.length>0&&source.length<=100000,'BAD_SOURCE','Use a nonempty project under 100,000 characters.');
  // Executed only inside the disposable worker, never in the document's global scope.
  const compile=new Function('seal','open','context','requireThat','LabError',
    '"use strict";\n'+source+'\nreturn {'+functionNames.map(n=>`${n}:typeof ${n}==="function"?${n}:undefined`).join(',')+'};');
  const implementation=compile(seal,open,context,requireThat,LabError);
  for(const name of functionNames)requireThat(typeof implementation[name]==='function','MISSING_FUNCTION',`Define ${name} using the browser starter.`);
  return implementation;
}
async function observed(action) {
  try{return {outcome:'returned',value:await action()};}
  catch(error){return {outcome:'threw',code:error.code??error.name,detail:error.message};}
}
async function diagnose(impl,options={}) {
  const mode=options.mode??'round-trip',item=options.item??'luna',length=Number(options.length??3);
  requireThat(['round-trip','tamper','replay','wrong-request','failed-hop','lost-reply'].includes(mode),'BAD_SCENARIO');
  requireThat(['luna','tide'].includes(item)&&[2,3,4].includes(length),'BAD_SCENARIO');
  const path=await impl.selectPath(directory(),[],length),circuit=establish(path);
  const request={operation:'lookup',item},events=[];let replacement=null;
  if(mode==='round-trip'||mode==='lost-reply') {
    events.push({action:mode,...await observed(()=>exchange(impl,circuit,request,{dropReply:mode==='lost-reply'}))});
  }else if(mode==='failed-hop') {
    events.push({action:'send through failed middle relay',...await observed(()=>exchange(impl,circuit,request,{failAt:path[1]}))});
    const next=await recover(impl,circuit,directory(),[path[1]]);replacement=next.circuit;
    events.push({action:'recovery plan',plan:next.plan,oldClosed:circuit.closed});
    if(replacement)events.push({action:'replacement lookup',...await observed(()=>exchange(impl,replacement,request))});
  }else {
    const seq=mode==='wrong-request'?7:0;
    const packet=await impl.wrapRequest(circuit.hops,request,seq),state=circuit.states[0];
    if(mode==='tamper')events.push({action:'altered packet',...await observed(()=>impl.peelForward(state,tamper(packet))),seenAfter:[...state.seenForward]});
    const forward=await observed(()=>deliverForward(impl,circuit,packet));
    events.push({action:'original forward',...forward});
    if(forward.outcome==='returned') {
      const reply=archive(forward.value);
      circuit.trace.push({direction:'endpoint',observer:'archive',previous:path.at(-1),payload:forward.value});
      const response=await deliverBackward(impl,circuit,reply,seq);
      if(mode==='wrong-request')events.push({action:'reply 7 offered to request 8',...await observed(()=>impl.unwrapReply(circuit.hops,response,8))});
      events.push({action:'matching reply',...await observed(()=>impl.unwrapReply(circuit.hops,response,seq))});
    }
    if(mode==='replay')events.push({action:'repeated forward packet',...await observed(()=>impl.peelForward(state,packet)),seenAfter:[...state.seenForward]});
  }
  return {mode:'learner-code simulation',scenario:mode,path,events,trace:circuit.trace,views:views(circuit),
    replacement:replacement?{path:replacement.path,trace:replacement.trace,views:views(replacement)}:null,
    visibility:'These are local observer projections. The single worker operator can inspect all state; this is not anonymity.'};
}
async function runProject(request) {
  const {source,command='check',through=6,options={}}=request;
  requireThat(['check','diagnose','capstone','workshop'].includes(command),'BAD_COMMAND');
  requireThat(Number.isInteger(through)&&through>=1&&through<=6,'BAD_MODULE');
  const impl=compileLearner(source);
  if(command==='workshop')return runWorkshop(impl,options.scenario);
  if(command==='diagnose')return diagnose(impl,options);
  const checks=await evaluate(impl,command==='capstone'?6:through);
  if(command==='check'||checks.passed!==checks.total)return {kind:command,checks,scenarios:'NOT_RUN unless capstone checks all pass'};
  const scenarios=[];
  for(const mode of ['round-trip','tamper','replay','wrong-request','failed-hop','lost-reply'])scenarios.push(await diagnose(impl,{mode,item:'tide'}));
  const transfer=[
    {id:'A',entry:[0,4,13,18],tolerance:1,candidates:[{id:'A',times:[50,54,63,68]},{id:'B',times:[80,85,93,98]},{id:'C',times:[100,104,114,121]}]},
    {id:'B',entry:[0,1,2,3],tolerance:0,candidates:[{id:'P',times:[20,21,22,23]},{id:'Q',times:[60,61,62,63]},{id:'R',times:[90,91,92,93]}]},
  ];
  for(const task of transfer)task.retained=await impl.correlate(task.entry,task.candidates,task.tolerance);
  return {kind:'capstone',checks,scenarios,transfer,reasoning:'UNASSESSED: apply the written capstone rubric.'};
}
const requirements=cases.map(({id,module,requirement,input})=>({id,module,requirement,input}));

return {compileLearner,diagnose,runProject,requirements};
})();
// Appended to the bundled adapters. One committed project per disposable worker.
const deliver=self.postMessage.bind(self);
const blockNetwork=()=>{throw new BrowserCrypto.LabError('NETWORK_DISABLED','Only the supplied simulated relays are available.');};
for(const name of ['fetch','XMLHttpRequest','WebSocket','EventSource','importScripts']) {
  Object.defineProperty(self,name,{value:blockNetwork,writable:false,configurable:false});
}
let started=false;
self.addEventListener('message',async event=>{
  if(started)return;started=true;
  const {id,request}=event.data??{};
  try{
    const result=await BrowserRunner.runProject(request);
    BrowserCrypto.requireThat(JSON.stringify(result).length<=1000000,'RESULT_TOO_LARGE','The result exceeded the local one-million-character limit.');
    deliver({id,type:'result',result});
  }
  catch(error){deliver({id,type:'result',result:{executionFailure:true,code:error.code??error.name,detail:error.message}});}
});

/* Scenario authoring and observer projections; shares the existing source editor/session. */
const WorkshopUI=(()=>{
  function mount({container,make,initial,onChange}) {
    let scenario=structuredClone(initial),editIndex=null;
    const titleLabel=make('label','Experiment title'),title=make('input');title.value=scenario.title;title.id='workshop-title';titleLabel.append(title);container.append(titleLabel);
    const notice=make('p','Change or reorder the steps, then commit observer predictions before running your current code. No step runs while you edit.','small');container.append(notice);
    const guide=make('a','Workshop tasks and scenario format');guide.href='../WORKSHOP.md';container.append(guide);
    const list=make('ol');list.id='workshop-steps';container.append(list);
    const controls=make('div',undefined,'project-controls');container.append(controls);
    function input(label,id,options) {
      const wrapper=make('label',label),node=make(options?'select':'input');node.id=id;
      if(options)for(const value of options){const option=make('option',String(value));option.value=String(value);node.append(option);}
      wrapper.append(node);controls.append(wrapper);return node;
    }
    const action=input('Action','workshop-action',['open','send','replay','offline','online','recover','close']);
    const circuit=input('Circuit name','workshop-circuit');circuit.value='alpha';
    const packet=input('Packet name','workshop-packet');packet.value='newPacket';
    const replacement=input('Replacement name','workshop-replacement');replacement.value='delta';
    const length=input('Path length','workshop-length',[3,2,4]);
    const relays=input('Relay names (comma separated)','workshop-relays');
    const item=input('Record','workshop-item',['luna','tide']);
    const fault=input('Injected fault','workshop-fault',['none','drop-forward','corrupt-forward','drop-reply']);
    const hop=input('Fault at hop (0 = entry)','workshop-hop',[0,1,2,3]);
    const hint=make('p','','small');container.append(hint);
    function enable() {
      circuit.disabled=['offline','online'].includes(action.value);packet.disabled=!['send','replay'].includes(action.value);
      replacement.disabled=action.value!=='recover';length.disabled=action.value!=='open';
      relays.disabled=!['open','offline','online','recover'].includes(action.value);
      item.disabled=action.value!=='send';fault.disabled=action.value!=='send';
      hop.disabled=action.value!=='send'||!['drop-forward','corrupt-forward'].includes(fault.value);
      hint.textContent=action.value==='open'?'Relay names are excluded from this path.':action.value==='recover'?'Relay names are the failures you tell recoveryPlan about; offline relays also remain unavailable.':action.value==='send'?'Use a new packet name. A fault affects this delivery only; the original bytes are captured before injection.':action.value==='replay'?'Inject the exact saved forward packet into the named circuit; no re-encryption.':'Relay names apply to online/offline actions. Closed circuits are never reopened by restoring a relay.';
    }
    action.onchange=enable;fault.onchange=enable;enable();
    const apply=make('button','Add step','secondary'),cancel=make('button','Cancel step edit','secondary');container.append(apply,cancel);
    const message=make('p','','small');message.setAttribute('role','status');container.append(message);
    function changed(){onChange?.();}
    function reset(){editIndex=null;apply.textContent='Add step';cancel.disabled=true;}
    function draw(){
      list.replaceChildren();
      scenario.steps.forEach((step,i)=>{
        const row=make('li');row.append(make('code',JSON.stringify(step)));
        for(const [label,fn] of [
          ['Edit',()=>{editIndex=i;action.value=step.action;circuit.value=step.circuit??'alpha';packet.value=step.packet??'newPacket';replacement.value=step.replacement??'delta';length.value=String(step.length??3);relays.value=(step.avoid??step.failed??step.relays??[]).join(', ');item.value=step.item??'luna';fault.value=step.fault?.kind??'none';hop.value=String(step.fault?.hop??0);apply.textContent='Update step';cancel.disabled=false;enable();}],
          ['Move up',()=>{[scenario.steps[i-1],scenario.steps[i]]=[step,scenario.steps[i-1]];reset();draw();changed();}],
          ['Move down',()=>{[scenario.steps[i+1],scenario.steps[i]]=[step,scenario.steps[i+1]];reset();draw();changed();}],
          ['Remove',()=>{scenario.steps.splice(i,1);reset();draw();changed();}]
        ]) {const button=make('button',label,'secondary');button.setAttribute('aria-label',`${label} step ${i+1}`);button.disabled=label==='Move up'&&i===0||label==='Move down'&&i===scenario.steps.length-1;button.onclick=fn;row.append(button);}
        list.append(row);
      });
    }
    apply.onclick=()=>{
      if(editIndex===null&&scenario.steps.length>=32){message.textContent='Use at most 32 steps.';return;}
      const step={action:action.value},names=relays.value.split(',').map(x=>x.trim()).filter(Boolean);
      if(!['offline','online'].includes(step.action))step.circuit=circuit.value.trim();
      if(step.action==='open'){step.length=Number(length.value);step.avoid=names;}
      if(['send','replay'].includes(step.action))step.packet=packet.value.trim();
      if(step.action==='send'){step.item=item.value;if(fault.value!=='none'){step.fault={kind:fault.value};if(fault.value!=='drop-reply')step.fault.hop=Number(hop.value);}}
      if(['offline','online'].includes(step.action))step.relays=names;
      if(step.action==='recover'){step.replacement=replacement.value.trim();step.failed=names;}
      if(editIndex===null)scenario.steps.push(step);else scenario.steps[editIndex]=step;
      reset();draw();changed();message.textContent='Scenario updated; nothing executed. The worker validates the complete scenario before running steps.';
    };
    cancel.onclick=reset;
    const predictionFields=[];
    container.append(make('h4','Predict before running'));
    const predictions=make('div',undefined,'workshop-predictions');container.append(predictions);
    for(const observer of ['client','cedar','birch','maple','elm','ash','archive','operator']) {
      const label=make('label',`${observer}: direct fact, inference, or still unknown?`),field=make('input');field.id=`prediction-${observer}`;
      field.value=scenario.predictions.filter(p=>p.observer===observer).map(p=>p.claim).join('\n');field.maxLength=2000;
      label.append(field);predictions.append(label);predictionFields.push({observer,field});field.addEventListener('input',changed);
    }
    title.addEventListener('input',changed);reset();draw();
    function snapshot(){return {version:1,title:title.value,predictions:predictionFields.filter(p=>p.field.value.trim()).map(p=>({observer:p.observer,claim:p.field.value})),steps:structuredClone(scenario.steps)};}
    function load(value){
      if(value?.version!==1||typeof value.title!=='string'||!Array.isArray(value.steps)||value.steps.length>32||!value.steps.every(s=>s&&typeof s==='object'&&!Array.isArray(s))||!Array.isArray(value.predictions)||!value.predictions.every(p=>p&&typeof p.observer==='string'&&typeof p.claim==='string'))throw new Error('Not a version 1 workshop scenario.');
      if(Object.keys(value).some(k=>!['version','title','predictions','steps'].includes(k))||value.predictions.length>12||value.predictions.some(p=>Object.keys(p).some(k=>!['observer','claim'].includes(k))||!predictionFields.some(f=>f.observer===p.observer)))throw new Error('Unknown scenario fields or observers; existing draft preserved.');
      if(predictionFields.some(p=>value.predictions.filter(x=>x.observer===p.observer).map(x=>x.claim).join('\n').length>2000))throw new Error('Keep each observer prediction within 2,000 characters.');
      scenario=structuredClone(value);title.value=value.title;
      for(const p of predictionFields)p.field.value=value.predictions.filter(x=>x.observer===p.observer).map(x=>x.claim).join('\n');
      reset();draw();changed();
    }
    return {snapshot,load};
  }
  function render({container,make,result}) {
    const area=make('div',undefined,'trace');area.append(make('h3',`Experiment · ${result.title}`),make('p',result.reasoning));
    area.append(make('p','Predictions committed before execution:'));
    for(const p of result.predictions)area.append(make('p',`${p.observer}: ${p.claim}`));
    const label=make('label','Evidence view '),select=make('select');select.id='workshop-observer';
    for(const id of ['client',...Object.keys(result.observations).filter(x=>x!=='client'),'operator']){const option=make('option',id==='operator'?'Operator — all steps, causes and state':id);option.value=id;select.append(option);}
    label.append(select);area.append(label);const view=make('div');view.id='workshop-evidence';area.append(view);
    function draw(){
      view.replaceChildren();const id=select.value;
      view.append(make('p',id==='operator'?'This view exposes the fault script and all receiver state. It is not any single relay’s knowledge.':'Only local observations are shown. Absence here does not prove nothing happened elsewhere. Step numbers and circuit aliases are teaching labels, not timing evidence.','small'));
      const events=id==='operator'?result.steps:result.observations[id];
      if(!events.length)view.append(make('p','No recorded events for this observer.'));
      for(const event of events)view.append(make('pre',JSON.stringify(event,null,2)));
    }
    select.onchange=draw;draw();area.append(make('p',result.visibility,'small'));container.append(area);
  }
  return {mount,render};
})();

`courses/onion-network-course/onion-process-lab/LIMITS.md`:

```md
# What this build can and cannot demonstrate

You can demonstrate independent relay heaps and process lifetimes, local circuit installation, layered authenticated encryption, asynchronous request/reply forwarding, replay control, failure ambiguity and fresh circuit recovery.

You cannot infer anonymity from these demonstrations:

- One local operator controls the client, routing broker, relay programs, keys and complete traces. Same-user processes are not an adversarial security boundary.
- The qualified links are IPC messages routed by that operator. They have no Internet latency, route diversity, independent administration, congestion model or link authentication.
- Even the optional TCP path remains on one loopback host with trusted IPC key provisioning. Running a socket would not fix the trust model.
- Setup gives the client and relay raw fresh secrets; there is no authenticated key exchange, directory consensus, guard choice, telescoping handshake, TLS or independent identity verification.
- All hops use the same circuit ID and sequence. Combined observer logs can link traffic directly. Sizes and times are visible; packets are variable-size JSON, without padding or mixing. Encrypted contents do not hide traffic patterns.
- The exit sees archive requests and replies. There is no application end-to-end encryption beyond the exit. The archive is fictional and internal.
- Restarting a process loses replay and circuit state. Recovery uses new keys; there is no durable replay protection or restoration of old sessions.
- Fresh keys on rebuild do not establish forward secrecy. Secrets and key copies can remain in JavaScript/native memory. Closing is resource management, not verifiable erasure.
- Losing a reply cannot establish that an application action did not occur. The lab repeats only safe read-only lookups. It provides no exactly-once guarantee.
- The lab has no public exits, SOCKS proxy, onion services, general destination access or Tor interoperability. Do not use it for private communications or real anonymity.

The original course's synthetic timing-correlation exercise remains useful. It is a separate exercise: this build's shared circuit labels and operator trace already reveal more than timing alone. Do not use local timestamps to claim a realistic traffic-analysis benchmark.

The first loopback startup in the authoring environment failed before readiness. The initial driver preserved the generic exit but not the underlying listener error code. It was not retried or worked around through a permission change. Accordingly, TCP runtime behavior remains unverified; IPC evidence must not be relabeled as a network-socket test.

```

`courses/onion-network-course/onion-process-lab/PROTOCOL.md`:

```md
# Process lab contract

This is a new teaching protocol derived from Circuit Observatory 0.3.0. The same core cryptographic model is used, but relay execution is asynchronous and occurs in separate operating-system processes. It is not a Tor wire format.

## Process and transport boundary

`runtime/lab.mjs` is the client and trusted controller. Each `runtime/relay-process.mjs` instance loads **your** `learner/protocol.mjs`, owns its own `Map`, and invokes your `installCircuit` and `handleCell`. Importing your module must not start other programs or perform top-level work.

Default data transport uses Node child-process IPC. A relay asks the parent to deliver a cell to the next child. The parent forwards the nested ciphertext without running another relay's handler itself. Setup, fault controls, observer events and data share this trusted parent. These are simulated links between real processes, not independent hosts or TCP connections.

The optional TCP adapter instead opens one `127.0.0.1` listener per relay on an OS-assigned port. Only the data path uses TCP; setup remains trusted IPC. One connection carries one request and one response, each encoded as a four-byte unsigned big-endian length followed by UTF-8 JSON. Maximum frame size is 1 MiB. A decoder accepts fragments, rejects oversized frames, and permits one frame per connection; later data is ignored after acceptance. Response failures and deadlines become `DELIVERY_FAILED` on upstream forwarding. This adapter is supplied, syntax-checked and **unqualified at runtime**. Its initial listener startup failed; no successful TCP exchange is claimed.

Neither transport has a relay handshake or authenticates the previous neighbor. `previous` is expected topology metadata, not verified sender identity. A key-holding local controller can inject cells into any relay. All supplied destinations are local relay IDs. The archive is a read-only function in the exit process, not an Internet service.

## Learner API

### `selectPath(directory, failedIds = [], length = 3)`

Return exactly `length` distinct online IDs excluding all failed IDs. Directory rows contain `id`, `online`, and runtime metadata; ignore fields you do not need. Duplicate directory IDs must not create duplicate hops. Preserve inputs. Throw `LabError('NO_PATH')` if there are too few. Any valid order is accepted.

### `async createCircuit(path, control)`

The caller supplies a valid distinct ordered path. Generate a fresh `randomUUID()` circuit ID and two independent `freshSecret()` values for every hop. Import them into client key handles using `importSecret`. Construct:

```text
circuit: {id, hops}
client hop: {circuitId, relayId, next, forwardKey, backwardKey}
setup config: {circuitId, relayId, previous, next, forwardSecret, backwardSecret}
```

For hop `i`, `previous` is the preceding ID or `client`, and `next` is the following ID or `archive`. Await `control.install(relayId, config)` for each hop. Send only that relay's keys and two neighbors, never the full route or other keys. Do not return a circuit until all installations acknowledge.

On a setup error, attempt `control.close(id, circuitId)` for **every attempted installation**, including the failing one: an acknowledgment can fail after installation. Destroy client handles you created with `destroyKey` and rethrow the original error. A cleanup failure must not replace the original cause. `control.close` returns a Promise. It is safe to close a state that was never installed. No persistent keys or accounts are used.

### `installCircuit(config, states)`

Reject an existing ID with `CIRCUIT_EXISTS` before changing anything. Import the two supplied secrets. Store only:

```text
{circuitId, relayId, previous, next, forwardKey, backwardKey, seenForward: new Set()}
```

under `states.set(circuitId, state)`. Do not store the input config's raw key strings. The supplied controller checks the relay identity and allowed neighbors before invoking this function. A replacement process starts with no circuit state; restarting a PID does not revive its old circuits.

### `wrapRequest(hops, body, seq)`

Build exit-to-entry. Every plaintext layer is `{next: hop.next, body: inner}`. At the exit `inner` is the archive request; elsewhere it is the next encrypted packet. Use the hop's `forwardKey` and `context(circuitId, relayId, 'forward', seq)`. Return the entry packet.

### `async handleCell(state, packet, io)`

Open exactly one forward layer using local keys and the incoming sequence. Validate `instruction.next === state.next` and presence of its `body`, otherwise `BAD_ROUTE`. Reject a sequence already in `state.seenForward` with `REPLAY`. Record a fresh sequence **after authentication and route validation, but before the first await**.

Call `io.observe({next: state.next, seq, bodyKind})`, where bodyKind is `encrypted-packet` at non-exits and `plaintext-request` at the exit. This metadata is for the report, not a cryptographic input.

If the configured successor is `archive`, await `io.archive(instruction.body)`. Otherwise await `io.forward(state.next, instruction.body)`. Do not choose an arbitrary address from incoming data. The supplied `io.forward` restricts destinations to the established successor and local directory.

Wrap the result with the local `backwardKey` and backward context at the same sequence. Return the encrypted packet. Propagate failures. A downstream failure leaves the accepted forward sequence consumed; do not clear it or try to encrypt another backward packet under the same key/nonce.

### `unwrapReply(hops, packet, expectedSeq)`

Open entry-to-exit using each hop's backward key. Use the caller's `expectedSeq` for **every** context, never the packet's claimed sequence. Return the final value only after all layers authenticate. A mixed outer/inner sequence must fail even if both packets were genuinely generated.

### `recoveryPlan(directory, failedIds, oldPath)`

Return `{action:'rebuild', path}` with the same length and valid selection rules, or `{action:'stop', reason:'NO_PATH'}`. No silent shortening or reuse of failed IDs. The supplied lifecycle closes the old circuit, creates fresh state with new keys and ID, and restarts at sequence zero. It never resends an application request automatically.

## Crypto and lifecycle

`context(circuitId, relayId, direction, seq)` accepts sequences 0–1023. `seal` and `open` use installed Node AES-256-GCM, a 96-bit sequence nonce and a 128-bit tag. Keys are fresh per circuit, hop and direction. The wrapper rejects repeated sealing with the same handle/sequence as `NONCE_REUSE`. These handles are process-local. Trusted setup imports the same secret separately in the client and its relay.

`open` releases JSON only after authentication succeeds. A context/packet sequence mismatch is `BAD_PACKET`; altered tag, ciphertext or authenticated context is `AUTH_FAILED`. Authentication does not detect a repeated authentic packet; your replay set does. Fresh out-of-order sequences are allowed.

The client reserves a new sequence before building/sending. A failure still consumes it. Sequence 1024 requires rebuild (`REBUILD_REQUIRED`). Closing invalidates local key handles and attempts relay cleanup, and rejects later sends with `CIRCUIT_CLOSED`. `destroyKey` overwrites its own buffer; it cannot erase all JavaScript/native copies or raw setup strings, and does not imply forward secrecy.

## Failure observations

`DELIVERY_FAILED` can mean an unavailable process, downstream rejection, closed connection, timeout, or lost reply. It does **not** prove which hop failed or whether the archive processed a request. Operator traces and explicit controls have more information than the client. Direct diagnostic injection at a relay can expose its local `AUTH_FAILED`, `REPLAY`, `BAD_ROUTE` or `UNKNOWN_CIRCUIT` code; an upstream forwarding path deliberately collapses downstream errors.

The state limit is 32 active circuits per relay; the sequence space is 1024 per circuit; operator event retention is 2000 rows. Large onions can exceed the 256 KiB plaintext-per-layer crypto limit. These are lab bounds, not flow control or denial-of-service defenses. Experiments use short three-hop paths and tiny fictional records.

`courses/onion-network-course/onion-process-lab/README.md`:

```md
# Build and run your own local onion relays

This extension takes Circuit Observatory beyond calling simulated relays in one JavaScript process. You implement a client and a relay protocol, start **four separate Node processes**, create a three-hop circuit, and carry an encrypted request and reply through it. Then you kill a real relay process and decide how to recover.

The qualified transport is **local IPC with simulated links**, routed by the parent process. This is a local onion-routing prototype, not a distributed anonymity network. An optional loopback TCP adapter is included but was **not qualified**: its first startup failed before readiness in the authoring environment, and was not retried. No public network, Tor service, account or secret from outside the lab is used.

## Start

Use an already installed Node runtime with `node:crypto`. The author control was tested on Node **v26.5.1**. No dependencies or installation are needed. If that runtime is unavailable, record the blocker; do not install software or change permissions for this lab.

```sh
node tools/check.mjs 1
```

The starter deliberately reports `TODO_P1`. Read [lesson 1](lessons/01.md), edit `learner/protocol.mjs`, and repeat. All seven exported functions belong to you; the starter never loads an instructor answer. Checks are cumulative and later functions can remain unfinished until their lesson.

| Lesson | You build | Run |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [1. Processes and paths](lessons/01.md) | `selectPath` and a process/observer map | `node tools/check.mjs 1` |
| [2. Create relay state](lessons/02.md) | `createCircuit` and `installCircuit` | `node tools/check.mjs 2` |
| [3. Build the outgoing onion](lessons/03.md) | `wrapRequest` | `node tools/check.mjs 3` |
| [4. Forward and return](lessons/04.md) | `handleCell` and `unwrapReply` | `node tools/check.mjs 4` |
| [5. Kill a relay and recover](lessons/05.md) | `recoveryPlan` and a controlled experiment | `node tools/check.mjs all` |
| [6. Defend the claim](lessons/06.md) | Evidence report, including limits of the transport | [report template](REPORT.md) |

This follows the original course's six lessons. Reuse your reasoning about path choice, reverse wrapping, request binding and replay protection. The synchronous `peelForward`/`addReturnLayer` split becomes one asynchronous server handler. Existing browser and CLI solution files are separate artifacts and are not imported automatically.

## Operate the system you wrote

After lesson 4:

```sh
node tools/lab.mjs demo
node tools/lab.mjs interactive
```

The launcher starts four child processes and prints their PIDs. At the interactive prompt enter one command per line:

```text
directory
open alpha
send alpha luna
view r1
quit
```

`open` prints the actual chosen path. Do not assume a particular relay is the middle hop if you chose a different valid order. Read [lesson 5](lessons/05.md) before stopping a relay. `quit` and end-of-input close circuits and terminate the children created by this launcher. Only this lab's child processes are stopped. A parent disconnection also asks surviving children to release local resources.

Rows labeled `operator` combine all process observations for debugging. A row labeled `client` is narrower evidence. A learner's handler must call `io.observe` with metadata only, as specified in [PROTOCOL.md](PROTOCOL.md). Do not print keys or use personal data. The only application requests are fictional, read-only `luna` and `tide` lookups served at the exit.

The public checks are readable in `checks/requirements.mjs`. They exercise your submitted code in the client and child processes. A pass is finite behavior evidence, not proof of learning or security. Make predictions before running the scenarios and submit your own explanation, source and captured output using [REPORT.md](REPORT.md). Nothing is automatically uploaded or graded.

## What is supplied

The runtime supplies process launching/termination, parent-child IPC, a bounded TCP framing adapter, AES-256-GCM primitives, a tiny archive and a command prompt. You supply circuit setup policy and state, layered requests, replay decisions, asynchronous forwarding, layered replies and replacement selection. Read the [contract](PROTOCOL.md) before implementation.

All code runs with your ordinary Node permissions. The processes and launcher are **not a sandbox for untrusted submissions**, and a loop in your client code can hang the launcher. Supplied I/O operations have deadlines; that is not an execution time limit on arbitrary learner code.

The local operator owns all the processes and keys. Fresh keys are delivered over a trusted IPC setup channel, without relay authentication or a cryptographic handshake. There is no independent relay trust, production anonymity, Tor interoperability, public exit, secure erasure, or forward-secrecy claim. The [limitations](LIMITS.md) are part of the assignment.

`courses/onion-network-course/onion-process-lab/SOURCES.md`:

```md
# Design lineage and sources

The earlier Circuit Observatory 0.3.0 component supplied transport and placed relays in one process; its protocol described forward movement as function calls. The process project extends that model with learner-owned relay handlers and circuit installation. Earlier editions and histories remain separate; no automatic source conversion or history migration is performed.

The supplied crypto wrapper derives from that course's `runtime/crypto.mjs`. The protocol label is changed to `onion-process-lab-v1`; fresh-secret/import functions are added for trusted parent-child provisioning. The teaching model retains separate directional keys, sequence-scoped GCM nonces, expected-request reply binding and authenticate-before-replay-state mutation. No upstream file is overwritten.

- [Node crypto documentation](https://nodejs.org/api/crypto.html): supplied AES-GCM APIs. The wrapper calls authentication finalization before exposing plaintext; the protocol learner does not implement a cryptographic primitive.
- [Tor circuit-creation specification](https://spec.torproject.org/tor-spec/creating-circuits.html): Tor creates and extends circuits with handshakes and protocol cells. This lab's direct controller installation and JSON packets are deliberately different and provide none of those protocol compatibility claims.

Documentation reviewed 2026-11-05. Public documentation was read for grounding; no experiment sent data to those sites, public Tor, or any external destination. Runtime test traffic stayed in local IPC. The included loopback adapter remains unqualified.

`courses/onion-network-course/onion-process-lab/checks/requirements.mjs`:

```mjs
// Public behavior checks, not worked implementations.
import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
import {pathToFileURL} from 'node:url';
import {resolve} from 'node:path';
import {startLab} from '../runtime/lab.mjs';
import {open, seal, context, importSecret, freshSecret} from '../runtime/crypto.mjs';
import {encode, decoder, MAX_FRAME} from '../runtime/wire.mjs';
export async function runChecks(source, stage = 'all') {
  const level = stage === 'all' ? 5 : Number(stage);
  assert.ok(Number.isInteger(level) && level >= 1 && level <= 5, 'Use 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 or all.');
  const p = await import(pathToFileURL(resolve(source)));
  const results = [];
  const check = async (name, run) => {
    try { await run(); results.push({name,pass:true}); }
    catch (e) {results.push({name,pass:false,code:e.code,message:e.message});}
  };
  await check('P1 distinct available path; exclusions; unchanged directory; explicit shortage', () => {
    const directory = [{id:'a',online:true},{id:'b',online:false},{id:'a',online:true},{id:'c',online:true},{id:'d',online:true},{id:'e',online:true}];
    const before = JSON.stringify(directory);
    const path = p.selectPath(directory,['c'],3);
    assert.equal(path.length,3); assert.equal(new Set(path).size,3);
    assert.ok(path.every(id => ['a','d','e'].includes(id))); assert.equal(JSON.stringify(directory),before);
    assert.throws(() => p.selectPath(directory,['a','c'],3), {code:'NO_PATH'});
  });
  if (level === 1) return {results,events:[]};
  await check('P2 partial setup rolls back already attempted relays', async () => {
    const attempted = [], closed = [];
    await assert.rejects(p.createCircuit(['a','b','c'],{
      install:async id => {attempted.push(id);if (id === 'b') throw Object.assign(new Error('setup fault'),{code:'SETUP_FAULT'});},
      close:async id => {closed.push(id);}
    }),{code:'SETUP_FAULT'});
    assert.deepEqual(attempted,['a','b']); assert.ok(closed.includes('a')); assert.ok(closed.includes('b'));
  });
  // In-process contract checks; no relay processes are started for these.
  const recordSetup = async path => {
    const configs = [];
    const circuit = await p.createCircuit(path, {install: async (id, config) => {configs.push({id, config: {...config}});}, close: async () => {}});
    return {circuit, configs};
  };
  await check('P2 setup sends each relay only its own two keys and two neighbors', async () => {
    const {configs} = await recordSetup(['a', 'b', 'c']);
    const allowed = ['backwardSecret', 'circuitId', 'forwardSecret', 'next', 'previous', 'relayId'];
    for (const {id, config} of configs) {
      assert.deepEqual(Object.keys(config).sort(), allowed, 'relay ' + id + ' received fields beyond its own state');
      assert.equal(config.relayId, id);
    }
  });
  await check('P2 forward and backward secrets are independent for every hop', async () => {
    const {configs} = await recordSetup(['a', 'b', 'c']);
    const secrets = configs.flatMap(({config}) => [config.forwardSecret, config.backwardSecret]);
    assert.equal(new Set(secrets).size, secrets.length, 'a secret is reused across directions or hops');
  });
  if (level >= 4) await check('P4 a downstream failure leaves the accepted sequence consumed (no second forward)', async () => {
    const {circuit, configs} = await recordSetup(['a', 'b', 'c']);
    const states = new Map(); p.installCircuit(configs[0].config, states);
    const state = states.get(circuit.id), packet = p.wrapRequest(circuit.hops, {operation: 'lookup', item: 'luna'}, 5);
    let forwards = 0;
    const io = {observe() {}, archive: async () => assert.fail('entry must not serve the archive'),
      forward: async () => {forwards++; throw Object.assign(new Error('down'), {code: 'DELIVERY_FAILED'});}};
    await assert.rejects(p.handleCell(state, packet, io), {code: 'DELIVERY_FAILED'});
    await assert.rejects(p.handleCell(state, packet, io), {code: 'REPLAY'});
    assert.equal(forwards, 1, 'the resent packet was forwarded again');
  });
  // Contract-derived regression cases: setup secrecy and consumed failed sequences.
  await check('P2 setup values name no relay beyond the two neighbors; UUID circuit id', async () => {
    // PROTOCOL.md: "Generate a fresh randomUUID() circuit ID" and "Send only that relay's keys and two
    // neighbors, never the full route or other keys."
    const path = ['relay-north', 'relay-east', 'relay-south', 'relay-west'], calls = [];
    const circuit = await p.createCircuit(path, {install: async (...args) => {calls.push(args);}, close: async () => {}});
    assert.match(circuit.id, /^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}$/, 'the circuit id is not a randomUUID() value');
    assert.equal(calls.length, path.length);
    for (const args of calls) {
      const [id, config] = args, known = [id, config.previous, config.next], sent = JSON.stringify(config);
      assert.equal(config.circuitId, circuit.id);
      for (const other of path) if (!known.includes(other)) assert.ok(!sent.includes(other), 'relay ' + id + ' was told about ' + other);
    }
  });
  await check('P2 secrets are fresh for every circuit, not only within one', async () => {
    // PROTOCOL.md: "Keys are fresh per circuit, hop and direction."
    const first = await recordSetup(['a', 'b', 'c']), second = await recordSetup(['a', 'b', 'c']);
    assert.notEqual(first.circuit.id, second.circuit.id);
    const secrets = [...first.configs, ...second.configs].flatMap(({config}) => [config.forwardSecret, config.backwardSecret]);
    assert.equal(new Set(secrets).size, secrets.length, 'a secret from one circuit is used again in another');
  });
  if (level >= 4) await check('P4 a failure at any relay, with DELIVERY_FAILED, leaves the sequence consumed, also a moment later', async () => {
    // PROTOCOL.md: "Propagate failures. A downstream failure leaves the accepted forward sequence consumed;
    // do not clear it or try to encrypt another backward packet under the same key/nonce."
    for (const position of [0, 1, 2]) for (const code of ['DELIVERY_FAILED']) {
      const {circuit, configs} = await recordSetup(['a', 'b', 'c']);
      const states = new Map(); p.installCircuit(configs[position].config, states);
      const state = states.get(circuit.id), seq = 6;
      let packet = p.wrapRequest(circuit.hops, {operation: 'lookup', item: 'luna'}, seq);
      for (let i = 0; i < position; i++) packet = open(circuit.hops[i].forwardKey, context(circuit.id, circuit.hops[i].relayId, 'forward', seq), packet).body;
      let attempts = 0;
      const down = async () => {attempts++; throw Object.assign(new Error('down'), {code});};
      const io = {observe() {}, archive: down, forward: down};
      const where = 'hop ' + position + ', error ' + code;
      await assert.rejects(p.handleCell(state, packet, io), {code}, where + ': the failure was not propagated');
      await new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, 25));
      await assert.rejects(p.handleCell(state, packet, io), {code: 'REPLAY'}, where + ': the resent packet was accepted');
      assert.equal(attempts, 1, where + ': the resent packet went downstream again');
    }
  });
  let lab;
  try {
    lab = await startLab(source);
    await check('P2 four different relay PIDs; local IPC endpoints; neighbor-only state; duplicate install rejected', async () => {
      const dir = lab.directory(); assert.equal(new Set(dir.map(r => r.pid)).size,4);
      assert.ok(dir.every(r => r.pid !== process.pid && r.endpoint.transport === 'ipc'));
      const c = await lab.open();
      for (let i = 0; i < c.hops.length; i++) {
        const h = c.hops[i], view = (await lab.snapshot(h.relayId)).find(s => s.circuitId === c.id);
        assert.equal(view.previous,c.hops[i-1]?.relayId || 'client');
        assert.equal(view.next,c.hops[i+1]?.relayId || 'archive'); assert.deepEqual(view.seen,[]);
        await assert.rejects(lab.control.install(h.relayId,{...view,forwardSecret:freshSecret(),backwardSecret:freshSecret()}),{code:'CIRCUIT_EXISTS'});
      }
      await lab.close(c);
    });
    if (level >= 3) await check('P3 nested layers match established successors; plaintext absent from envelope; no nonce reuse', async () => {
      const c = await lab.open();
      let packet = p.wrapRequest(c.hops,{operation:'lookup',item:'tide'},12);
      assert.ok(!JSON.stringify(packet).includes('lookup'));
      for (let i = 0; i < c.hops.length; i++) {
        const h = c.hops[i], inner = open(h.forwardKey,context(c.id,h.relayId,'forward',12),packet);
        assert.equal(inner.next,c.hops[i+1]?.relayId || 'archive'); packet = inner.body;
      }
      assert.deepEqual(packet,{operation:'lookup',item:'tide'});
      assert.throws(() => p.wrapRequest(c.hops,{},12),{code:'NONCE_REUSE'}); await lab.close(c);
    });
    if (level >= 4) {
      await check('P4 real round trip; return payload; each relay forwards once; exit alone serves archive', async () => {
        const c = await lab.open(), start = lab.events.length;
        assert.deepEqual(await lab.send(c,'luna'),{item:'luna',record:'Fictional lunar atlas'});
        const events = lab.events.slice(start).filter(e => e.circuitId === c.id);
        assert.deepEqual(events.filter(e => e.kind === 'forward').map(e => e.relayId).sort(),c.hops.slice(0,-1).map(h => h.relayId).sort());
        assert.deepEqual(events.filter(e => e.kind === 'archive').map(e => e.relayId),[c.hops.at(-1).relayId]);
        await lab.close(c);
      });
      await check('P4 authentication and route failure do not consume receiver sequence', async () => {
        const c = await lab.open(), entry = c.hops[0];
        const packet = p.wrapRequest(c.hops,{operation:'lookup',item:'luna'},17);
        const corrupt = {...packet,tag:Buffer.alloc(16).toString('base64')};
        await assert.rejects(lab.raw(entry.relayId,{type:'cell',circuitId:c.id,packet:corrupt}),{code:'AUTH_FAILED'});
        assert.deepEqual((await lab.snapshot(entry.relayId)).find(s => s.circuitId === c.id).seen,[]);
        const wrong = seal(entry.forwardKey,context(c.id,entry.relayId,'forward',18),{next:'forbidden',body:{}});
        await assert.rejects(lab.raw(entry.relayId,{type:'cell',circuitId:c.id,packet:wrong}),{code:'BAD_ROUTE'});
        assert.deepEqual((await lab.snapshot(entry.relayId)).find(s => s.circuitId === c.id).seen,[]);
        const reply = await lab.raw(entry.relayId,{type:'cell',circuitId:c.id,packet});
        assert.equal(p.unwrapReply(c.hops,reply,17).item,'luna'); await lab.close(c);
      });
      await check('P4 concurrent duplicate: one archive effect, one success, one REPLAY', async () => {
        const c = await lab.open(), entry = c.hops[0].relayId;
        const packet = p.wrapRequest(c.hops,{operation:'lookup',item:'tide'},8);
        const cell = {type:'cell',circuitId:c.id,packet};
        const attempts = await Promise.allSettled([lab.raw(entry,cell),lab.raw(entry,cell)]);
        assert.equal(attempts.filter(r => r.status === 'fulfilled').length,1);
        assert.equal(attempts.find(r => r.status === 'rejected')?.reason.code,'REPLAY');
        assert.equal(lab.events.filter(e => e.kind === 'archive' && e.circuitId === c.id).length,1); await lab.close(c);
      });
      await check('P4 every return layer binds caller expected sequence, including mixed inner layer', async () => {
        const c = await lab.open();
        const keys = c.hops.map(() => {const secret = freshSecret();return {writer:importSecret(secret),reader:importSecret(secret)};});
        const hops = c.hops.map((h,i) => ({...h,backwardKey:keys[i].reader}));
        let body = {item:'luna'};
        for (let i = hops.length - 1; i >= 0; i--) body = seal(keys[i].writer,context(c.id,hops[i].relayId,'backward',i === 1 ? 3 : 4),body);
        assert.throws(() => p.unwrapReply(hops,body,4),{code:'BAD_PACKET'});
        const requestPacket = p.wrapRequest(c.hops,{operation:'lookup',item:'luna'},10);
        const reply = await lab.raw(c.hops[0].relayId,{type:'cell',circuitId:c.id,packet:requestPacket});
        assert.throws(() => p.unwrapReply(c.hops,reply,11),{code:'BAD_PACKET'});
        await lab.close(c);
      });
      await check('P4 fresh out-of-order sequences accepted; other circuit keys rejected', async () => {
        const a = await lab.open(), b = await lab.open();
        for (const seq of [9,2]) {
          const packet = p.wrapRequest(a.hops,{operation:'lookup',item:'luna'},seq);
          const reply = await lab.raw(a.hops[0].relayId,{type:'cell',circuitId:a.id,packet});
          assert.equal(p.unwrapReply(a.hops,reply,seq).item,'luna');
        }
        const old = p.wrapRequest(a.hops,{operation:'lookup',item:'luna'},7);
        await assert.rejects(lab.raw(b.hops[0].relayId,{type:'cell',circuitId:b.id,packet:old}),{code:'AUTH_FAILED'});
        await lab.close(a); await lab.close(b);
      });
    }
    if (level >= 5) {
      await check('P5 real relay death; healthy independent circuit; fresh replacement; old circuit retired', async () => {
        const a = await lab.open(), failed = a.hops[1].relayId;
        const b = await lab.open([failed]);
        const oldPacket = p.wrapRequest(a.hops,{operation:'lookup',item:'luna'},40);
        await lab.stop(failed);
        await assert.rejects(lab.send(a),{code:'DELIVERY_FAILED'});
        assert.equal((await lab.send(b,'tide')).item,'tide');
        const replacement = await lab.recover(a,[failed]);
        assert.notEqual(replacement.id,a.id); assert.ok(replacement.hops.every(h => h.relayId !== failed));
        assert.equal(replacement.nextSequence,0); assert.equal((await lab.send(replacement)).item,'luna');
        await assert.rejects(lab.send(a),{code:'CIRCUIT_CLOSED'});
        await assert.rejects(lab.raw(a.hops[0].relayId,{type:'cell',circuitId:a.id,packet:oldPacket}),{code:'UNKNOWN_CIRCUIT'});
        await assert.rejects(lab.raw(replacement.hops[0].relayId,{type:'cell',circuitId:replacement.id,packet:oldPacket}),{code:'AUTH_FAILED'});
        await lab.close(b); await lab.close(replacement); await lab.start(failed);
      });
      await check('P5 lost reply preserves archive receipt; explicit retry uses fresh circuit', async () => {
        const c = await lab.open(); await lab.dropNextReply(c.hops.at(-1).relayId);
        await assert.rejects(lab.send(c),{code:'DELIVERY_FAILED'});
        assert.equal(lab.events.filter(e => e.kind === 'archive' && e.circuitId === c.id).length,1);
        const next = await lab.recover(c,[]); assert.equal((await lab.send(next)).item,'luna'); await lab.close(next);
      });
      await check('P5 shortage stops instead of shortening path; sequence exhaustion requires rebuild', async () => {
        const c = await lab.open();
        c.nextSequence = 1024; await assert.rejects(lab.send(c),{code:'REBUILD_REQUIRED'});
        const failed = lab.directory().slice(0,2).map(r => r.id);
        const plan = p.recoveryPlan(lab.directory(),failed,c.hops.map(h => h.relayId));
        assert.deepEqual(plan,{action:'stop',reason:'NO_PATH'});
        await assert.rejects(lab.recover(c,failed),{code:'NO_PATH'}); assert.equal(c.closed,true);
      });
    }
  } catch (error) {results.push({name:'relay startup or infrastructure',pass:false,code:error.code,message:error.message});}
  finally {await lab?.shutdown();}
  return {results,events:lab?.events || []};
}

export function checkWire() {
  const frame = encode({hello:'fragmented'}); let value, error;
  const push = decoder(v => {value=v;}, e => {error=e;});
  for (const byte of frame) push(Buffer.from([byte]));
  assert.deepEqual(value,{hello:'fragmented'}); assert.equal(error,undefined);
  const oversized = Buffer.alloc(4); oversized.writeUInt32BE(MAX_FRAME+1);
  decoder(() => assert.fail('accepted oversized frame'),e => {error=e;})(oversized);
  assert.equal(error.code,'FRAME_SIZE');
}

# 1. A relay becomes a process

In Circuit Observatory, a call into the next relay happened inside one process. Here a relay owns a separate heap and PID. The protocol is still yours, but an `await` can allow another request to arrive while the first one waits. A crashed process really loses its state.

Before code, draw five boxes: the client/controller and four relay processes. Connect three relays into one path. Mark which fourth relay could replace a failed member. # 2. Install a circuit without giving every relay the route

A running relay starts with an empty map. A circuit must exist before an encrypted request can be interpreted. In this lab, a trusted controller provisions it. This is an intentional simplification of key exchange, not a simulation of a Tor handshake.

Implement `createCircuit(path, control)` and `installCircuit(config, states)`. Use the exact object shapes in [the contract](../PROTOCOL.md). The imports in your starter include `randomUUID`, `freshSecret`, `importSecret` and `destroyKey`.

For each hop, generate two independent secrets and retain two client handles. Send only that hop's keys, previous ID and next ID. In path order, await installation before proceeding to the next hop. An `install` acknowledgment means the child has stored its local state; it does not establish trust in an independently operated relay.

The receiver must reject an existing circuit ID before mutating it. Its stored state contains imported handles and a new replay set, not raw setup secret strings. Different circuits on the same relay must have independent sets and keys.

**Predict before testing:** If installation at the second relay fails, is the first relay still holding keys? What if the second relay installed successfully but the acknowledgment was lost? Your rollback should attempt cleanup of every attempted installation, including the one whose result was uncertain. Preserve the original setup error.

**Done when:** setup and rollback checks pass; each participating process stores a local circuit; close removes it; you can explain why storing every relay's secret at every hop would defeat the exercise.

If stuck: build a table with columns index, previous, relay, next. The first and last boundary values are `client` and `archive`. Track an attempted hop before awaiting its installation.

# 3. Construct the outgoing onion

Reuse the idea from the earlier course: the client builds the deepest layer first. The exit must eventually read `{operation:'lookup', item:'luna'}`, while the entry should obtain a successor ID and an encrypted inner packet.

Implement `wrapRequest(hops, body, seq)`. Each layer encrypts `{next, body}` under the hop's forward handle and context. The context authenticates protocol label, circuit, relay, direction and sequence. The supplied crypto wrapper implements AES-GCM; do not replace it with encoding, XOR or a homemade cipher.

```md
# 4. Write the relay server's behavior

This is the main new implementation task. A child process invokes your `async handleCell(state, packet, io)` for each incoming cell. Your code must decide whether to accept it, which local operation to call, and what to return upstream.

Implement these decisions in order:

1. Authenticate and open one layer with the local forward key.
2. Validate the established successor and presence of a body.
3. Reject a previously accepted sequence; record a new sequence synchronously.
4. Observe metadata, then await either the configured next relay or the archive at the exit.
5. Add this relay's backward layer around the resulting body.

The contract gives `io.forward`, `io.archive` and `io.observe`; each has a different role. Calling the archive at an entry is an error, not a shortcut. Your code is executing separately inside every process, so no shared in-memory route traversal is needed.

**Predict the concurrency bug:** Suppose requests A and B carry the same authentic packet. A checks the replay set, then waits for the next relay. B arrives during that wait. What happens if A adds its sequence only after receiving the reply? Write a six-step timeline. Place the state mutation where the two requests cannot both pass.

Implement `unwrapReply` at the client. The exit returns the innermost backward layer; each preceding relay adds another layer. The client opens entry-to-exit. Bind every layer to the caller's expected sequence, including inner layers.

```sh
node tools/check.mjs 4
node tools/lab.mjs demo
```

Public checks cover actual child-process forwarding, concurrent duplicate delivery, tampering before replay-state mutation, route validation, mixed reply sequences, out-of-order fresh requests and wrong-circuit keys. Inspect the forward and archive events in the demo and explain which facts are operator-only.

**Done when:** your client receives the fictional record and all P4 checks pass. Include one wrong implementation you tried, its failure, and the corrected reasoning in your report.

If stuck: `await` is the point at which another request can enter. Authentication and route validation must happen before recording, and recording must happen before that first wait. Forward and backward keys are deliberately different.

`courses/onion-network-course/onion-process-lab/runtime/crypto.mjs`:

```mjs
// Supplied platform code. Do not implement your own cryptographic primitive.
import { createCipheriv, createDecipheriv, randomBytes } from 'node:crypto';

export class LabError extends Error {
  constructor(code, detail = code) { super(detail); this.name = 'LabError'; this.code = code; }
}
export const requireThat = (condition, code, detail) => {
  if (!condition) throw new LabError(code, detail);
};

// Key material stays in this process and is never written into reports or exports.
const materials = new WeakMap();
export function freshKey() {
  const handle = Object.freeze({ kind: 'ephemeral-toy-key' });
  materials.set(handle, { bytes: randomBytes(32), used: new Set() });
  return handle;
}
export function destroyKey(handle) {
  const material = materials.get(handle);
  if (material) material.bytes.fill(0);
  materials.delete(handle);
  // JS/crypto-library copies may remain: this is NOT a secure-erasure guarantee.
}
export function context(circuitId, relayId, direction, seq) {
  requireThat(typeof circuitId === 'string' && typeof relayId === 'string', 'BAD_CONTEXT');
  requireThat(['forward', 'backward'].includes(direction), 'BAD_DIRECTION');
  requireThat(Number.isSafeInteger(seq) && seq >= 0 && seq < 1024, 'BAD_SEQUENCE');
  return { protocol: 'onion-process-lab-v1', circuitId, relayId, direction, seq };
}
function aad(ctx) {
  // Canonical construction prevents object-key order from changing authentication.
  return Buffer.from(JSON.stringify(context(ctx.circuitId, ctx.relayId, ctx.direction, ctx.seq)));
}
function materialFor(handle) {
  const material = materials.get(handle);
  requireThat(material, 'KEY_UNAVAILABLE', 'Key handle is unknown or its circuit is closed.');
  return material;
}
function nonceFor(seq) {
  const nonce = Buffer.alloc(12);
  nonce.writeUInt32BE(seq, 8);
  return nonce;
}
export function seal(handle, ctx, value) {
  const authenticated = aad(ctx);
  const material = materialFor(handle);
  // Every handle belongs to one hop and one direction of one circuit.
  // Reject reuse even with changed associated data: GCM needs unique key/nonce pairs.
  requireThat(!material.used.has(ctx.seq), 'NONCE_REUSE', 'Use a fresh sequence or rebuild with fresh keys.');
  const plaintext = Buffer.from(JSON.stringify(value));
  requireThat(plaintext.length <= 262144, 'OVERSIZE');
  const cipher = createCipheriv('aes-256-gcm', material.bytes, nonceFor(ctx.seq));
  cipher.setAAD(authenticated);
  const ciphertext = Buffer.concat([cipher.update(plaintext), cipher.final()]);
  material.used.add(ctx.seq);
  return { seq: ctx.seq, ciphertext: ciphertext.toString('base64'), tag: cipher.getAuthTag().toString('base64') };
}
export function open(handle, ctx, packet) {
  const authenticated = aad(ctx);
  const material = materialFor(handle);
  requireThat(packet && packet.seq === ctx.seq && typeof packet.ciphertext === 'string'
    && typeof packet.tag === 'string', 'BAD_PACKET');
  requireThat(packet.ciphertext.length <= 350000, 'OVERSIZE');
  try {
    const tag = Buffer.from(packet.tag, 'base64');
    requireThat(tag.length === 16, 'AUTH_FAILED');
    const decipher = createDecipheriv('aes-256-gcm', material.bytes, nonceFor(ctx.seq));
    decipher.setAAD(authenticated);
    decipher.setAuthTag(tag);
    // No plaintext escapes until final() has authenticated the complete packet.
    const plaintext = Buffer.concat([decipher.update(Buffer.from(packet.ciphertext, 'base64')), decipher.final()]);
    return JSON.parse(plaintext.toString('utf8'));
  } catch {
    throw new LabError('AUTH_FAILED', 'Ciphertext, tag, context or key did not authenticate.');
  }
}

// Trusted local setup only: a fresh secret is sent over parent-child IPC.
export const freshSecret = () => randomBytes(32).toString('hex');
export function importSecret(hex) {
  requireThat(typeof hex === 'string' && /^[a-f0-9]{64}$/.test(hex), 'BAD_KEY');
  const handle = Object.freeze({kind: 'ephemeral-process-lab-key'});
  materials.set(handle, {bytes: Buffer.from(hex, 'hex'), used: new Set()});
  return handle;
}
