fit       7 rounds, 17 shots exact, arrows, flag-moves  learnFit
physics   3 rounds, 3 shots  arrows                     learnPhysics
motion    2 rounds, 0 shots  none                       learnMotion
```

The labels, which the picker reads:

- controls: `Press each key and watch the status line`
- search: `Search memory for the values (about 6 rounds; what it finds stops working if the state moves or is scrambled, and it needs the wind on the screen)`
- reader: `Test what the code says about the state (3 rounds against the screen): ` then `sayReader`
- fit: `Fire 14 practice shots and fit an aim to them (about 7 rounds and 17 shots; good to about 10 paces)`
- physics: `Test what the code says about a shot with 3 check shots (3 rounds, 3 shots): ` then `sayPhysics(code)`, with no host
- motion: `Test what the code says about the flag by watching it for 2 rounds: ` then `sayMover`

#### The functions

- `controlsHold(host, kit)` is true when the keys in the kit still do what
  they did. It is false when the kit has no controls, status line or message.
  For the angle and then the power it reads the value on the status line
  (false when the line shows none), presses the up key and then the down key,
  or the down key first when the value is at its top (85 for the angle, 100
  for the power), and ticks 2 frames after each press. The value after the
  first press must be one step from where it was. It starts no round.
- `learnControls(host, kit, env)` returns `kit.controls` at once, and logs it,
  when `controlsHold` is true. Otherwise it works the controls out by
  pressing keys, and asks the decision model nothing. It presses each key
  except `'Space'`, ticking 2 frames after each, and watches the changed
  strings. A string on which `changedLabel` names `angle` or `power` is the
  status line, and the key is that value's up key when the number after the
  label rose, its down key when it fell. A key that turns a string into text
  starting with `ROUND` is the new-round key. `fire` is the first key in
  `KEYS` that nothing claimed. It throws `could not work out the controls`
  unless all six are known. It then sets `kit.controls` and `kit.statusLine`,
  presses the new-round key once more, and sets `kit.message` to the first
  changed string, other than the status line, that starts with a capital
  letter and has no lower-case letter (`null` when there is none). It
  returns the controls. Working the controls out starts two rounds.
- `choose(env, what, text, options)` returns the index of the option the
  picker picked. `options` is a list of strings or of objects with a `label`;
  it calls `env.models.decide(text, labels, options)`. With one option or
  none it returns 0 without asking. It returns 0 when `choice` is not a whole
  number from 0 to `options.length - 1` and when the picker throws. It logs
  each pick as a `'decision'` line, `pick ` and then `what`, with the label
  picked or what went wrong. It never throws for a bad answer or a picker
  that is not available; an `OutOfBudget` error it throws again. The search
  passes it to `findValues` as
  `{ decide: (text, labels) => choose(env, 'the next experiment', text, labels) }`.
- `learnFit(host, kit, env)` first makes sure the landing slot is known:
  while `kit.found.landing` is not set, it starts a new round and fires a
  sighting shot with `testShot` at angle 5 and the next power in `SIGHTERS`.
  Such a shot always falls short of the flag, so its message gives a
  distance. Sighting shots go into no list. Then it fires the 14 `PRACTICE`
  shots with `testShot`, starting a new round before shots 1, 5, 9 and 13.
  Every fourth shot (the 4th, 8th and 12th) is held back; the fit is fitted
  on the other 11 with `fitShots` and judged by `judgeFit` on both lists.
  It sets `kit.shots` (all 14) and `kit.fit`: `{ coef, game }` when the fit
  is accepted, `null` otherwise. It logs how many shots were fitted and held
  back, the two worst misses and the verdict.
- `analyse(host)` is what the passes find in the game's code, worked out once
  per game and kept for each `gameId`: `look` calls it every time it reads
  through a reader, so it must not lift the game again. It lifts every
  function with `liftAll(parseModule(host.binary()))`, takes `game_key` as
  the key handler and `game_tick` as the frame function, and returns:

```js
{
  lifted,     // liftAll's Map
  launch,     // launchOf(key handler), or null
  aim,        // aimValues(key handler, launch), or null
  flight,     // flightOf(frame function, launch), or null
  decode,     // decoding of aim.angle.value, keyed by the
              // place its stepper writes, or null
  simulate,   // simulator(launch, aim, flight), or null
  constants,  // loads of fields the launch reads that no
              // function writes
  flag,       // flagOf(frame function, flight, decode.key)
  readers,    // [{ raw, reader, mover }]
}
```

Each finding is `null` when one it needs is. `constants` is constant
tracking: the `f32.load`s inside the launch's `trig` stores whose place
`xrefs` shows no store writing, each once; such a field is set when the game
starts. `readers` has one entry for each place in `flag.raws`: `reader` is
`readerFrom(aim, flight, raw)` and `mover` is `moverOf(frame function, raw)`.
A finding that needs a function you have not written yet, one that throws
"not written yet", is `null` (an empty list for `readers`) until you write
it, so `analyse` works from module 05 on.

- `sayPhysics(code, host = null)` is the sentence
  `A shot starts on key code K: game_key writes +A +B ... from the angle, the power and +C (no store through the pointer writes it; V now), and sets +F; game_tick moves the shell with N stores while +F is set and writes the landing to +L.`
  The offsets after `writes` are those of the launch's `trig` stores, in
  order. Each constant reads `+C (no store through the pointer writes it; V now)`.
  Several follow `the power and`, separated by `, `, as in
  `the power and +C (...), +D (...), and sets +F`; with none the sentence
  reads `from the angle, the power, and sets +F`. `; V now` is the
  constant's value, read through its pointer, and is there only when `host`
  is given and the pointer can be followed.
  `F` is the flying flag's offset, `N` the flight's stores less the landing,
  and `L` the landing's offset.
- `sayReader(code, cand)` is the sentence
  `The state is the struct at P, HOW: angle at +A, power at +B, flag at +C, WIND.`
  `P` is the place of the angle's stored word without its offset; HOW is
  `values stored as they are`, `values stored XORed with the word at +K` or
  `values stored with the word at +K added`, by `code.decode`; `A` and `B`
  are the offsets of the angle's and the power's stored words, and `C` that
  of `cand.raw`. WIND is `the wind is not used` when the flight has no wind;
  otherwise `wind at +W`, with `W` the offset of `windWord`, or `wind` when
  the code keeps no wind word, followed by
  `, or from the server in builds that take it from there` when the wind
  expression calls `server_wind`.
- `sayMover(cand)` is the sentence
  `game_tick moves the flag with N stores, to +A +B.` (`1 store` for one),
  with the offsets the flag motion writes, each once, in the order of its
  stores.
- `fire(host, kit, env, plan)` reads the state with `look`, presses the angle
  keys until the angle, counted press by press from the angle read and
  rounded, equals `plan.angle`, and does the same for the power (at most 200
  presses each).
  Then it presses fire and ticks one frame at a time until the message at
  `kit.message` is not empty, for at most 1,500 frames. It returns
  `{ text, frames, hit }`: the message, how many ticks that took, and whether
  the message starts with `HIT`.
- `learnPhysics(host, kit, env)` tests the physics the code describes with
  the check shots. If `analyse` has no `simulate`, it logs that the code shows
  no launch and flight and returns `null`. If the wind `look` reads is not a
  number, no check shot could be compared on this build: it logs so and
  returns `null`, leaving `kit.physics` as it is. Otherwise it logs
  `sayPhysics(code, host)` and fires the 3 `CHECK_SHOTS`, each in a new
  round: it sets the barrel as `fire` does, simulates the shot from memory
  as it is before the shot leaves, fires it, and takes the landing from the
  message (`SHORT BY 37` is 37 paces before the flag, to the nearest pace),
  with the flag read when it lands. A check shot that hits says only "within 12
  paces", so it is fired again in a new round with 7 more power, and then
  with 7 less. The physics is confirmed when all 3 shots were measured and
  each landed within 1 pace of its simulated landing after the same number of
  frames. It logs the result and sets `kit.physics`: `{ game, says }` when
  confirmed, `null` when refuted.
- `look(host, kit, env)` returns the state now,
  `{ angle, power, wind, wind_arrows, target_x }`. With a reader in the kit it
  is `readState` with that reader (`analyse(host).readers[kit.reader.which]`)
  and `kit.statusLine`. Otherwise it reads the addresses in `kit.found`: the
  angle and the power with their types, the wind and the flag as floats, and
  `wind_arrows` is `null`. With neither it throws
  `nothing in the kit reads the state`.
- `learnReader(host, kit, env, which)` tests reader `which` of `analyse`: it
  logs `sayReader`, then runs `checkReader` for 3 rounds with
  `() => readState(host, reader, kit.statusLine)`, the kit's status line and
  its new-round key. It logs the verdict and the first two problems. When
  the reader is confirmed it sets `kit.reader` to `{ game, which, says }`,
  deletes `kit.found` and returns `kit.reader`; otherwise it returns `null`.
- `learnMotion(host, kit, env, which)` tests the flag motion of reader
  `which`: it logs `sayMover`, then runs `judgeMotion` for 2 rounds of 300
  frames with `look`, the kit's new-round key and
  `(frames) => flagPath(host.memory(), mover, reader.flag, frames)`. When the
  flag motion is confirmed it sets `kit.mover` to `{ game, which, says }` and
  returns it; otherwise it returns `null`.
- `checkKit(host, kit, level, env)` returns the first problem for this level,
  most basic first, or `null` when the kit is ready. The evidence starts with
  `'exact'` when `level.radius` is under 12. While the decoder or the lifter
  is not written yet, it goes on as if the code suggested nothing, and a menu
  can be empty. The problems, in order:
1. The controls: when `controlsHold` is false, the problem is
   `the controls are not known on this game`, with `controls`.
2. The state. `'arrows'` is recorded when the status line shows arrows. A
   reader in the kit is tested against the screen now, at no cost in rounds:
   the angle within 0.5, the power equal once rounded, a number wind within
   0.051, and the flag within 12 paces of the cloth. A reader that fails is
   deleted, and the why says how it failed:
   `the reader in the kit fails here` when `look` throws,
   `the reader in the kit reads angle A and power P; the screen shows S and T`
   when the angle or the power disagrees or the line shows no number for
   them, `the reader in the kit reads wind W; the screen shows S` for the
   wind, and `the reader in the kit puts the flag where the screen does not`
   for the flag. When no reader reads the state and the kit has found
   addresses, they are tested a round later: the engine starts a new round
   and compares them with the status line, in this order, and the first
   test that fails gives the why. A line with no angle and power gives
   `the status line shows no angle and power to compare with`, with no
   evidence. An angle or a power the addresses no longer hold gives
   `a round later the addresses found by searching no longer hold what the screen shows (angle A there, S on screen)`
   and `'moves'`; it names the angle even when only the power is wrong, A
   read at the found address and S on the line. A line that shows only
   arrows gives
   `the screen shows only wind arrows, so an address for the wind is no use`
   and `'arrows'`. A wind more than 0.051 from the line's gives
   `the address found for the wind holds W; the screen shows S` and
   `'moves'`. Addresses that fail are deleted. When nothing reads the state,
   the problem's why is the sentence of the last test that failed, or
   `nothing reads the state yet` when no test ran, and its menu has `search`
   first and then each reader of `analyse`.
3. The flag: when the kit has no flag motion and the flag moves on its own
   (read, 20 frames, read, 20 frames, read: it moves when two readings in a
   row differ by more than 0.001), `'flag-moves'` is recorded and the problem
   is `the flag moves while nothing is happening, and nothing in the kit says how`,
   with `motion` for each reader that has a flag motion. A kit with a flag
   motion records `'flag-moves'` too.
4. The aim: the kit is ready when it has the physics for this game, or, when
   none of `'exact'`, `'arrows'` and `'flag-moves'` was recorded, a fit for
   this game. Otherwise the problem is `this level needs the exact physics`
   (when one of those three was recorded) or `nothing in the kit aims yet`,
   with `fit` when none of the three was recorded and the kit has found
   addresses, then `physics` when `analyse` has `simulate`.

- `heuristic(problem, options)` is the rule the decision model is measured
  against: the index of the cheapest option whose `limits` hold none of
  `problem.evidence`, the cost counted as rounds × 100 + shots, so rounds
  first and then shots, and the first of equals. 0 when every option is ruled
  out.
- `aimFor(host, kit, state, env, delay = 1)` returns the setting to fire for
  `state` with the best part in the kit, or `null`. With the physics, it
  predicts with `simulate` on the game's memory as it is now. With a flag
  motion in the kit as well, it takes the reader's flag path for the next 700
  frames, and if the path is not all one value it returns `lead` for it and
  `delay`, with `moving: true` set on the plan. Otherwise, with `state.wind`
  not a number it returns `aimBand`, and with a number `search` for that wind
  and `state.target_x`. With only a fit and a wind that is a number, it is
  `search` on the fit's predictions, with `frames` `null`. With neither, it is
  `nearest` on `kit.shots`, and `null` with no shots.
- `playRounds(host, level, kit, env)` plays `level.rounds` rounds with
  `kit.decider`, or `{ who: 'code', frames: 1 }` when the kit has none. In
  each round it starts a new round, then looks and plans until the plan can be
  fired. It plans with `aimFor` for a delay of `decider.plan`, or
  `decider.frames` when there is no `plan`. Right after each plan it reads the
  clock: once the frames it has let pass in the round while looking, waits
  included, reach 600, it fires that plan, ready or not, without asking. A
  plan for a moving flag is fired only when `ready(plan)`; otherwise the
  engine lets a frame pass and looks again. When `decider.who` is `'model'` it
  then asks, through `choose`, `fire or wait`, with the text
  `The planned shot lands in F frames, M paces from where the flag will be.`
  (`M` to one decimal place) and the options `Fire now` and
  `Wait and look again`. After a wait it ticks `decider.frames` frames before
  it looks and plans again. Before the shot leaves it ticks `decider.frames`
  frames, the delay the plan was made for, then fires with `fire`. When `look`
  throws, it logs that it cannot play and why, fires nothing, and returns at
  once. When `aimFor` returns `null` it logs that nothing in the kit can aim
  and fires nothing in that round. It returns `{ hits, rounds }`, with
  `rounds` being `level.rounds`.
- `pickDecider(env, budget = FRAME_BUDGET)` times three decisions on a
  fire-or-wait question, by their `ms`. The middle time in frames,
  `Math.round(ms * 60 / 1000)` and at least 1, is the delay to plan for; the
  spread is the slowest time less the fastest, in frames. It returns
  `{ who: 'model', frames }` when the spread is at most `budget`, and
  `{ who: 'code', frames: 1 }` when it is more or the picker is not
  available. It logs the times and the choice.
- `sweep(newHost, level, kit, env, latencies)` plays the level's rounds twice
  for each delay in `latencies`, each time on a fresh host from `newHost()`:
  once with
  `kit.decider = { who: 'code', frames: latency }`, where the plan is made for
  the delay, and once with `{ who: 'code', frames: latency, plan: 1 }`, where
  the plan is made for a delay of 1 and the shot still leaves `latency`
  frames later. It returns `[{ latency, planned, unplanned }]`, with
  `latency` the delay tried and the other two in hits, and puts
  `kit.decider` back.
- `playLevel(host, level, kit, env)` gets the kit ready for the level and
  plays it. If `kit.game` is not this game's `gameId`, the kit's status line,
  message, found addresses, practice shots, fit, physics, reader and flag
  motion belong to another game and are deleted, and `kit.game` is set. It
  learns on `metered(host, kit, allowance(level))`, repeating at most 10
  times: `checkKit`; if there is no problem, stop; keep the options not yet
  tried on this level whose cost fits what is left of the allowance; if none
  is left, log `nothing left to try that fits the budget` (check 03-budget
  looks for those words) and stop; `choose` one, with the text
  `Level N, NAME: ABOUT Problem: WHY. Left for learning: R rounds and S shots.`
  and each option given with the `problem`; run it on the metered host and
  log what it spent. When `OutOfBudget` stops a check or a repair, it logs
  the error and stops repairing. Then it sets `kit.decider` to
  `{ who: 'code', frames: 1 }`, or to `pickDecider`'s answer when the kit
  has a reader, the physics and a flag motion and the flag's path over the
  next 120 frames is not all one value. It returns `playRounds` on the host
  it was given.

```

`courses/sightline/README.md`:

```md
# Sightline

In this course you build Sightline, an engine that works out a small artillery game from the outside, aims for you, and keeps hitting as the game gets harder to read. The game is Lob, written in C and compiled to WebAssembly, a compact binary format that browsers and Node can run. You set a barrel's angle and power, fire, and try to land within 12 paces of a flag while the wind pushes the shell sideways.

Your engine never sees Lob's source code. It gets the game's file as bytes, its memory, key presses, the screen and time. With those it climbs ten levels. Each level is a build of the game that breaks something the engine relied on at the level before: the target shrinks, the game's values move, then they are scrambled, then the exact wind leaves the game's memory, then the flag starts to move. The last three levels are Lob II, another game of the same kind that the engine has never seen. Every level has a budget of rounds and shots, and a level that goes over it isn't passed.

No model writes any of the engine's code. You write all of it: a memory search, experiments, a decoder for the game's WebAssembly, and analysis passes over the decoded code, of the kind reverse-engineering tools run on a program. The passes lift each function into expressions that say what every store writes and under which conditions, evaluate them with the game's own arithmetic, follow cross-references, track constants, take slices, and find the shapes of the launch, the flight, the landing, the hit test and the flag motion. From what they find, the engine builds a simulator of each shot, a reader for state that moves and is scrambled, and the flag's path. Every finding is a hypothesis until the engine has tested it against the game: check shots for the physics, the screen for the reader, two rounds of watching for the flag.

One model takes part, and it writes no code. It's a decision model, a small language model (a program that reads text and writes text, and can be wrong) that picks an option from a menu your code wrote, such as searching memory for the values or testing what the code says about the state. The course measures its picks against always taking option 0, picking at random, and a heuristic you write.

## What the measurement found

Measured with the course's own engine, climbing all ten levels:

- Your heuristic, which takes the cheapest option that nothing the engine has seen on the level rules out, cleared every level.
- Always option 0 failed level 3: it searched memory that moves every round and ran out of the rounds the level leaves for learning.
- Random picks failed some levels, all of them on the new game. Over 20 climbs, level 8 failed 5 times, level 9 8 times and level 10 6 times. The 5 climbs that lost level 8 lost levels 9 and 10 with it, so most of the losses on those two levels followed from losing level 8.
- Two decision models on Ollama, `llama3.2:1b` and `qwen2.5:7b`, each cleared all ten levels in one climb, and neither beat the heuristic on any level. Each also replayed levels 3 and 9 from the kit that option 0 leaves. `llama3.2:1b` picked unlike the heuristic on 1 of the 5 menus of repairs it answered, searching memory on level 8 where the heuristic tests what the code says about the state, and passed anyway, using all 24 rounds that level allows. `qwen2.5:7b` picked what the heuristic picks on all 4 of its menus of repairs. The one time it was allowed to decide when to fire, on level 9 replayed, it answered "wait" to 72 of 79 questions, and its shots hit only because the engine fires a fresh plan when a round's time runs out.

On these games the decision model didn't beat the heuristic, and the course says so. On these menus it couldn't have, because the cheapest option that nothing rules out always worked, and firing a ready plan at once ("Fire now") was a good answer every time, so a picker could only match the heuristic or lose to it. A menu where the cheapest option that nothing rules out sometimes fails is where a picker could earn its place. What you build around the decision model is the menu it picks from, the loop that keeps every level inside its budget (the budget is what makes a poor order cost something), and the heuristic it's measured against.

## Who it is for

You can follow this course if you write JavaScript for Node 22 comfortably: functions, arrays, objects, ES modules and `async`/`await`, and running `node` in a terminal. The mathematics is high-school level: algebra, square roots, and the sine and cosine of an angle. Hexadecimal and bits are taught where they are first needed. No WebAssembly, reverse engineering or machine learning background is assumed.

## What you need

- Node 22 or newer.
- A terminal.

Nothing else: no package install, no account, no API key and no network connection. Every check runs offline, with stand-ins for the decision model. To ask a real one, install Ollama, a program that runs language models on your own computer, pull `llama3.2:1b`, and add `--picker live` to `level` or `climb`, or `live` to the list after `measure --pickers` (`--model` names another model). No check uses it.

## How to start

Run these from the course folder, the folder that holds this README and `lab.mjs`:

```
node lab.mjs start ./work
node lab.mjs serve
```

`start` creates `work/` with the nine starter files you write, plus one finished file the course gives you, `opcodes.mjs`. `serve` prints a local address. Open it in a browser to read the lessons, answer the practice questions and read the API page. Read the lessons on that page. The practice questions appear only there, and so does the pause at each prediction. The rest of the lesson appears once you have committed an answer to each of its questions. The files in `lessons/` hold the lesson text with a marker where each question goes, and show the text after every prediction at once. Read lesson 01 first. Each lesson gives an order to write its functions in and the checks to run after each step, such as `node lab.mjs check 01 ./work --only 01-strings`. When the last step is done, run the module's whole check, `node lab.mjs check 01 ./work`. Each failure names the requirement, shows the input, what your code returned and what was required, and names the lesson section that covers it. Modules build on each other, so keep them in order.

The files in `lessons/` hold the same text, but there a practice question is only a `{{practice:ID}}` line, and the text after a `{{gate:ID}}` line is what the page opens once you commit that question. Read in the browser to answer each question before its answer shows. The page opens that text in your browser once you commit, but the server sends any part to any request and keeps no record of answers, so this keeps your reading order rather than locking anything. `lessons/practice.mjs` holds every practice question with its answer, because the page checks your answers on your own computer. Leave it unread until you've committed your own.

Your engine keeps what it learns in a kit that it carries from level to level. `node lab.mjs level 1 ./work` plays a level with your engine and prints every step it took, and `node lab.mjs climb ./work` starts from an empty kit and plays the levels in order. `node lab.mjs --help` lists every command. `API.md` gives every function and the exact rules the checks hold it to, on one page. `checks/` and `fixtures/` are the course's test code and recorded data. They hold answers to things the lessons ask you to find yourself, so leave them unread until you have passed the module they belong to.

## The ten levels

| Level | Name | Game and defences | To pass | Budget |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Open range | Lob, plain | 7 of 10 within 12 paces | 28 rounds, 30 shots |
| 2 | Bullseye | Lob, plain | 9 of 10 within 3 paces | 24 rounds, 16 shots |
| 3 | Moving memory | Lob, state moves | 9 of 10 within 12 paces | 18 rounds, 12 shots |
| 4 | Scrambled | Lob, state moves and is scrambled | 9 of 10 within 12 paces | 16 rounds, 12 shots |
| 5 | Wind off the client | Lob, as level 4, wind on a server | 8 of 10 within 12 paces | 16 rounds, 12 shots |
| 6 | Moving flag | Lob, as level 4, flag moves | 9 of 10 within 12 paces | 16 rounds, 12 shots |
| 7 | Everything at once | Lob, all four defences | 8 of 10 within 12 paces | 16 rounds, 12 shots |
| 8 | A new game | Lob II | 8 of 10 within 12 paces | 24 rounds, 16 shots |
| 9 | A new game, hidden | Lob II, state moves and is scrambled | 8 of 10 within 12 paces | 18 rounds, 12 shots |
| 10 | A new game, everything | Lob II, every defence it has | 7 of 10 within 12 paces | 16 rounds, 12 shots |

The referee, the part of the course that watches the game itself, counts the last 10 shots that land on a level, and each budget includes those 10 rounds and shots. Each level starts from the kit the level before it left.

## The modules

1. Text in memory: pull the strings out of the game's memory, find the status line and the message by what changes when a key is pressed, and work out the controls by pressing keys, keeping keys that still work.
2. Pin the values: find where the game keeps the angle, the power, the wind and the flag by filtering memory across experiments chosen from a menu, and see why, on Lob, a pick from a menu on which every option works can't matter.
3. An aim from practice shots: fire practice shots, fit an aim to them by least squares, judge the fit on shots it never saw, and play level 1 inside its budget of rounds and shots.
4. Take the code apart: decode the game's WebAssembly into listings with block depths and exact numbers.
5. Lift the code: lift functions into guarded expressions, evaluate them with the game's own arithmetic, find the launch, the flight and the landing by their shapes, and install the physics they make only after check shots confirm it. Level 2.
6. The game fights back: read the state's place and encoding out of the code, test a reader built from it against the screen, and have the engine find what a level broke and pick a repair within the budget, with your heuristic to measure the decision model against. Levels 3 to 5.
7. Race the clock: slice the flag motion out of the code, judge the path it predicts frame by frame, lead a moving flag, and measure what decision time costs when it's planned for and when it isn't. Levels 6 and 7.
8. A game you have never seen: the same passes, tests and loop climb levels 8 to 10, and you measure every picker over the whole climb. The checks can run your passes only on the two games, so nothing checks that a pass holds no special case for either.

## The one rule

The engine never runs the game file. It may read the file's bytes, decode and lift them, and evaluate what it lifted on a copy of memory, but it may not load the file as a WebAssembly module and run it. Running a copy would answer every question without understanding any of them, and the referee's rules forbid it. A check scans your files for it, and the checks run your files with WebAssembly taken away.

## How long it takes

About 23 hours in total. This is an estimate and hasn't been measured with learners. Nothing is timed, so take as long as you need.

## How progress is saved

Your progress is the code in `work/`. Checks read your files fresh on every run, so you can stop at any point and pick up later by running the next check. The kit your engine builds is saved under `work/kits/` each time it passes a level. Practice answers you commit in the browser view are kept by that browser, on that computer.

## Scope

The course works on two small WebAssembly games that it ships, Lob and Lob II, read only through each game's file, its memory, key presses, the screen and time. It covers memory scanning, a WebAssembly decoder for the instructions the games use, a lifter and the passes over what it makes, a least-squares fit, tests that confirm or refute what a search or a pass found, budgets of rounds and shots, and one decision model measured against stand-ins. Each defence is paired with the step that gets past it: state that moves, values that are scrambled, a wind kept off the client and a flag that moves.

It doesn't cover native programs, operating-system process memory, real games or anti-cheat systems, and it doesn't teach getting past anyone else's protections. The passes are written for the code these two games compile to, and they aren't a general decompiler. No model writes code and no model is trained. The engine only reads the game files the course ships.

## Licence

Original software is MIT, and original lesson prose and illustrations are CC BY 4.0, attributed to Free to Learn.

```

`courses/sightline/checks/01.mjs`:

```mjs
import { fail, expectSame, show, CONTROLS, observed, envWith } from './harness.mjs';
import { makeGame } from '../host.mjs';

export const title = 'Text in memory';
const L = 'lesson 01';
const enc = (s) => Uint8Array.from([...s].map((c) => c.charCodeAt(0)));

// A picker that must not be asked: module 01 has no menu.
const silent = () => {
  const calls = [];
  return { calls, async decide(text) { calls.push(text); throw new Error('no decision is needed to work out the controls'); } };
};

export const cases = [
  {
    id: '01-strings', title: 'findStrings finds the help text, the status line and ROUND 1, and only runs that end in a zero byte',
    requirement: 'findStrings keeps runs of minLen or more printable bytes (32 to 126, or a newline) that end in a zero byte, with the address of their first byte.',
    reread: `${L}, finding strings`,
    async run({ fn }) {
      const findStrings = await fn('scan.mjs', 'findStrings');
      const { host, truth } = makeGame({ mode: 0, seed: 1 });
      const found = findStrings(host.memory());
      if (!Array.isArray(found)) fail({ checked: 'findStrings returns a list', observed: `findStrings returned ${show(found, 80)}`, expected: 'a list of { addr, text }' });
      const help = found.find((s) => typeof s?.text === 'string' && s.text.includes('LOB, a tiny artillery range') && s.text.includes('Land within 12 paces'));
      if (!help) fail({ checked: 'findStrings on a fresh game finds the help text as one string', input: 'the memory of a fresh game', observed: `${found.length} strings; none holds both the first and the last line of the help text. First few: ${show(found.slice(0, 4).map((s) => s.text), 200)}`, expected: 'one string from "LOB, a tiny artillery range." to "Land within 12 paces of the flag to score."' });
      if (!found.some((s) => s.addr === truth.lineAddr() && s.text === truth.line())) fail({ checked: 'findStrings finds the status line at its address', observed: show(found.map((s) => [s.addr, s.text.slice(0, 20)]), 300), expected: `{ addr: ${truth.lineAddr()}, text: ${JSON.stringify(truth.line())} }` });
      if (!found.some((s) => s.addr === truth.msgAddr() && s.text === 'ROUND 1')) fail({ checked: 'findStrings finds the message', observed: show(found.map((s) => s.text.slice(0, 20)), 300), expected: `{ addr: ${truth.msgAddr()}, text: "ROUND 1" }` });
      expectSame(findStrings(enc('AB\0WIND +2.3\0\x01\x02\0')), [{ addr: 3, text: 'WIND +2.3' }], { checked: 'findStrings on a small example', input: '"AB\\0WIND +2.3\\0\\x01\\x02\\0"', what: 'strings' });
      expectSame(findStrings(enc('AB\0WIND +2.3\0'), 10), [], { checked: 'findStrings with minLen 10', input: '"AB\\0WIND +2.3\\0", minLen 10', what: 'strings' });
      expectSame(findStrings(enc('HELLO\x01WORLD\0')), [{ addr: 6, text: 'WORLD' }], { checked: 'a run ended by byte 1 is dropped', input: '"HELLO\\x01WORLD\\0"', what: 'strings' });
      expectSame(findStrings(enc('ABCDEFGH')), [], { checked: 'a run that reaches the end of memory is dropped', input: '"ABCDEFGH" with no zero byte', what: 'strings' });
      expectSame(findStrings(enc('RIGHT\nLEFT\0')), [{ addr: 0, text: 'RIGHT\nLEFT' }], { checked: 'a newline does not end a string', input: '"RIGHT\\nLEFT\\0"', what: 'strings' });
      expectSame(findStrings(enc('ABCD\0ABC\0')), [{ addr: 0, text: 'ABCD' }], { checked: 'a string of exactly minLen characters counts, one shorter does not', input: '"ABCD\\0ABC\\0", minLen 4', what: 'strings' });
    },
  },
  {
    id: '01-read', title: 'readCString stops at a zero byte, at max, and at the end of memory',
    requirement: 'readCString(bytes, addr, max = 256) returns the text from addr up to the first zero byte, at most max characters, and never reads past the end.',
    reread: `${L}, finding strings`,
    async run({ fn }) {
      const readCString = await fn('scan.mjs', 'readCString');
      const bytes = enc('AB\0WIND +2.3\0');
      expectSame([readCString(bytes, 3), readCString(bytes, 0), readCString(enc('ABCDEFGH\0'), 0, 4), readCString(enc('ABC'), 1)], ['WIND +2.3', 'AB', 'ABCD', 'BC'], { checked: 'readCString on four cases', input: 'address 3 and 0 of "AB\\0WIND +2.3\\0"; "ABCDEFGH\\0" with max 4; address 1 of "ABC" with no zero byte', what: 'texts' });
    },
  },
  {
    id: '01-wordy', title: 'wordy needs 6 characters and three letters in a row',
    requirement: 'wordy(text) is true when text has at least 6 characters and a run of 3 letters.',
    reread: `${L}, what changes when you press a key`,
    async run({ fn }) {
      const wordy = await fn('scan.mjs', 'wordy');
      expectSame([wordy('D+CE'), wordy('SCORE 1/2'), wordy('A1B2C3'), wordy('ROUND 4'), wordy('ABCDE'), wordy('AB CDE')], [false, true, false, true, false, true], { checked: 'wordy on six texts', input: '"D+CE", "SCORE 1/2", "A1B2C3", "ROUND 4", "ABCDE", "AB CDE"', what: 'results' });
    },
  },
  {
    id: '01-changed', title: 'changedStrings keeps wordy strings at the same address whose text changed',
    requirement: 'A changed string is one whose address held a string before and holds different, wordy text now; a string at a new address is not a change, and neither are a moving number\'s bytes.',
    reread: `${L}, what changes when you press a key`,
    async run({ fn }) {
      const changedStrings = await fn('scan.mjs', 'changedStrings');
      const snapshot = await fn('scan.mjs', 'snapshot');
      const before = new Uint8Array(48), after = new Uint8Array(48);
      before.set([0x44, 0x2a, 0x43, 0x45, 0], 0); after.set([0x44, 0x2b, 0x43, 0x45, 0], 0);
      before.set(enc('ANGLE 45 POWER 60\0'), 20); after.set(enc('ANGLE 46 POWER 60\0'), 20);
      after.set(enc('NEW TEXT\0'), 8);

    },

    },
  },

`courses/sightline/checks/02.mjs`:

```mjs
import { fail, expectSame, show, CONTROLS, observed, scripted, envWith } from './harness.mjs';
import { makeGame } from '../host.mjs';

export const title = 'Pin the values';
const L = 'lesson 02';

function slots(values) {
  const buf = new ArrayBuffer(values.length * 4), dv = new DataView(buf);
  values.forEach(([type, v], i) => (type === 'f32' ? dv.setFloat32(i * 4, v, true) : dv.setInt32(i * 4, v, true)));
  return new Uint8Array(buf);
}
const all = (n) => Uint32Array.from({ length: n }, (_, i) => i);

// The game seen through a view that adds a second copy of the flag at one-eighth
// scale, the way a minimap keeps one. It moves in step with the flag, so only the
// slope of the line against the screen tells the two apart. The copy sits in free
// memory near the top that a fresh game leaves zero, and the real game never sees it.
function withMinimap(host, truth) {
  const fresh = host.memory();
  let at = -1;
  for (let a = fresh.length - 16; a > fresh.length / 2; a -= 4) if (fresh.subarray(a, a + 16).every((x) => x === 0)) { at = a + 4; break; }
  if (at < 0) throw new Error('no free memory for the minimap copy');
  return {
    binary: () => host.binary(),
    memory: () => { const m = host.memory().slice(); new DataView(m.buffer).setFloat32(at, truth.targetX() / 8 + 3, true); return m; },
    write: (addr, type, value) => host.write(addr, type, value),
    press: (key) => host.press(key),
    tick: (n) => host.tick(n),
    screen: () => host.screen(),
    minimapAt: at,
  };
}
// The game seen through a view that keeps the wind and the flag at two other addresses,
// in free memory near the top, and leaves a constant where Lob keeps them (+8 and +16 from
// the angle). A search that measures finds them at their new places; one that assumes Lob's
// layout reports the old ones.
function withMovedFields(host, truth) {
  const fresh = host.memory();
  let at = -1;
  for (let a = fresh.length - 64; a > fresh.length / 2; a -= 4) if (fresh.subarray(a, a + 24).every((x) => x === 0)) { at = a + 4; break; }
  if (at < 0) throw new Error('no free memory for the moved fields');
  const base = truth.stateBase(), windAt = at, flagAt = at + 12;
  return {
    binary: () => host.binary(),
    memory: () => {
      const real = host.memory(), m = real.slice();
      const r = new DataView(real.buffer, real.byteOffset, real.byteLength), v = new DataView(m.buffer);
      v.setFloat32(windAt, r.getFloat32(base + 8, true), true);
      v.setFloat32(flagAt, r.getFloat32(base + 16, true), true);
      v.setFloat32(base + 8, 99.5, true);
      v.setFloat32(base + 16, 640.25, true);
      return m;
    },
    write: (addr, type, value) => host.write(addr, type, value),
    press: (key) => host.press(key),
    tick: (n) => host.tick(n),
    screen: () => host.screen(),
    windAt, flagAt,
  };
}
const asList = (c) => ({ f32: c?.f32 ? Array.from(c.f32) : c?.f32, i32: c?.i32 ? Array.from(c.i32) : c?.i32 });

export const cases = [

    id: '02-views', title: 'viewsOf, allSlots, count and list',
    requirement: 'viewsOf gives the same bytes as 32-bit floats and as signed integers; allSlots numbers every 4-byte slot; count adds both types; list gives { type, slot, addr }, floats first.',
    reread: `${L}, slots and candidates`,
    async run({ fn }) {
      const viewsOf = await fn('scan.mjs', 'viewsOf'), allSlots = await fn('scan.mjs', 'allSlots');
      const count = await fn('scan.mjs', 'count'), list = await fn('scan.mjs', 'list');
      const bytes = slots([['f32', 45], ['i32', -7], ['f32', 2.5]]);
      const v = viewsOf(bytes);
      expectSame([v.f32[0], v.i32[1], v.f32[2], v.f32.length], [45, -7, 2.5, 3], { checked: 'viewsOf on three slots', input: 'float 45, integer -7, float 2.5', what: '[f32[0], i32[1], f32[2], length]' });
      expectSame(Array.from(allSlots(bytes)), [0, 1, 2], { checked: 'allSlots on 12 bytes', what: 'slots' });
      const c = { f32: Uint32Array.from([2]), i32: Uint32Array.from([0, 1]) };
      expectSame(count(c), 3, { checked: 'count of one float and two integer candidates', what: 'count' });
      expectSame(count({ f32: null, i32: null }), 0, { checked: 'count of nothing scanned', what: 'count' });
      expectSame(list(c), [{ type: 'f32', slot: 2, addr: 8 }, { type: 'i32', slot: 0, addr: 0 }, { type: 'i32', slot: 1, addr: 4 }], { checked: 'list', what: 'candidates' });

      }
      const { host, truth } = makeGame({ mode: 0, seed: 47 });

      try { f = await findValues(view, CONTROLS); } catch (e) { if (String(e?.message).includes('not written yet')) throw e; error = String(e?.message ?? e); }
      if (f?.flag?.addr !== truth.stateBase() + 16) fail({ checked: 'findValues with a minimap copy of the flag in memory', input: `the flag at ${truth.stateBase() + 16}; a copy at one-eighth scale at ${view.minimapAt}`, observed: error ? `it stopped with "${error}"` : `flag ${show(f?.flag)}`, expected: `the flag at ${truth.stateBase() + 16}: the copy moves in step with the screen too, but with a slope of 1/8` });

    },

`courses/sightline/checks/03.mjs`:

import { fail, expectSame, show, fixtureJson, CONTROLS, observed, envWith, gameIdOf, playOn, sayScore, ruleFor, levelNo } from './harness.mjs';
import { makeGame } from '../host.mjs';
import { referee } from '../levels.mjs';

export const title = 'An aim from practice shots';
const L = 'lesson 03';

// The addresses a search finds on Lob, worked out here from the game itself.
const foundFor = (truth) => {
  const base = truth.stateBase();
  return { angle: { addr: base, type: 'f32' }, power: { addr: base + 4, type: 'i32' }, wind: { addr: base + 8, type: 'f32' }, flag: { addr: base + 16, type: 'f32' }, statusLine: truth.lineAddr(), message: truth.msgAddr() };
};
const shots = () => fixtureJson('shots-seed7.json').shots;
const split = (list) => ({ fitOn: list.filter((_, i) => i % 4 !== 3), heldOut: list.filter((_, i) => i % 4 === 3) });

// The best whole power for each angle by trying them all, for a predictor that
// grows with power; the first angle, in the order asked, within `enough`.
function brute(predict, at, { enough, order }) {
  const angles = [];
  for (let a = 5; a <= 85; a++) angles.push(a);
  if (order === 'middle') angles.sort((a, b) => Math.abs(a - 45) - Math.abs(b - 45) || a - b);
  let best = null;
  for (const angle of angles) {
    for (let power = 10; power <= 100; power++) {
      const r = predict(angle, power), t = r ? at(r.frames) : null;
      if (!r || typeof t !== 'number') continue;
      const miss = Math.abs(r.x - t);
      if (!best || miss < best.miss) best = { angle, power, miss };
    }
    if (best && best.miss <= enough) break;
  }
  return best;
}

    id: '03-test-shot', title: 'testShot reads each landing: from the message until the landing slot is known, then from the slot',
    requirement: 'testShot sets the barrel, fires and waits for the message. A miss gives the flag plus or minus the miss, and the slots in memory within 0.6 of that landing become candidates, narrowed on the next miss; once one is left it is found.landing and landings are read from it. A hit before then gives the flag\'s place.',
    reread: `${L}, test shots and the landing spot`,
    async run({ fn }) {
      const testShot = await fn('learn.mjs', 'testShot');
      const ref = referee({ game: 'lob', mode: 0, seed: 23 });
      const found = foundFor(ref.truth);
      // A decoy: a float below the state that holds the first landing (plus 0.2) and
      // then something else, the way a stale copy might. Only narrowing across misses
      // tells it from the real landing slot.
      const base = ref.truth.stateBase(), decoyAt = base - 32;
      let landings = 0, lastFlying = false;
      const view = { ...ref.host, memory: () => {
        const flying = ref.truth.flying();
        if (lastFlying && !flying) landings++;
        lastFlying = flying;
        const m = ref.host.memory().slice();
        if (landings >= 1) new DataView(m.buffer).setFloat32(decoyAt, landings === 1 ? ref.truth.impactX() + 0.2 : ref.truth.impactX() + 50, true);
        return m;
      } };
      const rows = [];
      for (const power of [70, 55, 40]) {
        ref.host.press('KeyN'); ref.host.tick(2);
        const s = testShot(view, found, CONTROLS, 5, power);
        rows.push({ s, real: ref.shots[ref.shots.length - 1] });
      }
      for (const [i, { s, real }] of rows.entries()) {
        if (!s || s.angle !== 5 || s.power !== [70, 55, 40][i] || !(Math.abs(s.impact_x - real.impact) <= 0.5)) fail({ checked: `testShot at angle 5, power ${[70, 55, 40][i]}`, input: 'seed 23; the shell lands far short of the flag', observed: show(s), expected: `angle 5, power ${[70, 55, 40][i]}, impact_x within 0.5 of where it landed (${real.impact.toFixed(2)})` });
        if (!Number.isInteger(s.frames) || s.frames < 10) fail({ checked: 'frames in testShot\'s result', observed: show(s.frames), expected: 'the number of frames the shot flew before its message appeared' });
      }
      if (!found.landing || found.landing.addr !== ref.truth.stateBase() + 56) fail({ checked: 'found.landing after three misses', input: `a decoy at ${decoyAt} held the first landing (plus 0.2) and then another number`, observed: show(found.landing ?? found.landingCandidates), expected: `{ addr: ${ref.truth.stateBase() + 56}, type: 'f32' }: the misses narrow the candidates to the one slot that keeps holding the landing` });
      ref.host.press('KeyN'); ref.host.tick(2);
      const exact = testShot(ref.host, found, CONTROLS, 40, 85);
      if (!(Math.abs(exact.impact_x - ref.shots[ref.shots.length - 1].impact) < 1e-3)) fail({ checked: 'a landing read once the slot is known', observed: show(exact), expected: `impact_x ${ref.shots[ref.shots.length - 1].impact} exactly, read from the slot` });
      // On seed 44 the first shot of a fresh game at angle 30, power 70 hits.
      const hit = referee({ game: 'lob', mode: 0, seed: 44 });
      const f2 = foundFor(hit.truth);
      const h = testShot(hit.host, f2, CONTROLS, 30, 70);
      if (!hit.truth.message().startsWith('HIT') || !(Math.abs(h.impact_x - h.target_x) < 1e-6)) fail({ checked: 'a hit before the landing slot is known', input: 'seed 44, angle 30, power 70', observed: `${hit.truth.message()}; ${show(h)}`, expected: 'HIT!, with impact_x the flag\'s place: a hit says only "within 12 paces"' });

    id: '03-search', title: 'search finds a whole-number setting that lands where the flag will be',
    requirement: 'search(predict, at, { enough, order }) tries angles in the order asked; for each, powers every 10, then halves each gap where the landing passes the target down to neighbouring whole powers; it stops at the first setting within `enough`, and returns { angle, power, x, frames, miss } or null.',
    reread: `${L}, from a fit to a shot`,
    async run({ fn }) {
      const search = await fn('learn.mjs', 'search');
      const range = (a, p) => ({ x: 90 + (p * p * Math.sin((2 * a * Math.PI) / 180)) / 8, frames: Math.round(p * Math.sin((a * Math.PI) / 180)) });
      let calls = 0;
      const counted = (a, p) => { calls++; return range(a, p); };
      for (const [target, opts] of [[600, { enough: 0.5, order: 'middle' }], [431, { enough: 2, order: 'low' }]]) {

        const plan = search(counted, () => target, opts);
        const want = brute(range, () => target, opts);
        if (!plan || plan.angle !== want.angle || plan.power !== want.power || !(Math.abs(plan.miss - want.miss) < 1e-9) || plan.x !== range(plan.angle, plan.power).x || plan.frames !== range(plan.angle, plan.power).frames) fail({ checked: `search for a landing at ${target}, ${opts.order} order, enough ${opts.enough}`, observed: show(plan), expected: `{ angle: ${want.angle}, power: ${want.power}, miss: ${want.miss.toFixed(3)} }: the first angle in that order with a setting within ${opts.enough}, and its best whole power` });
        if (calls > 600) fail({ checked: 'how many settings search tried', observed: `${calls}`, expected: 'at most a few hundred: powers every 10, then halving, and stopping at the first good setting' });
      }
      const moving = search(range, (frames) => 500 + 2 * frames, { enough: 0.5, order: 'middle' });
      const wantMoving = brute(range, (frames) => 500 + 2 * frames, { enough: 0.5, order: 'middle' });
      if (!moving || moving.angle !== wantMoving.angle || moving.power !== wantMoving.power) fail({ checked: 'search when the target depends on the flight time', input: 'at(frames) = 500 + 2 frames', observed: show(moving), expected: `{ angle: ${wantMoving.angle}, power: ${wantMoving.power} }: each setting is compared with at(its own frames)` });

    id: '03-learn-fit', title: 'learnFit fires sighting shots, then 14 practice shots, and keeps a fit only if its judge accepts it',
    requirement: 'learnFit fires sighting shots at angle 5 (powers 70, 55, 40) until the landing slot is known, then the 14 practice shots with a new round before every fourth; it fits on 11 and judges on the 4th, 8th and 12th; kit.shots holds the 14, and kit.fit is { coef, game } only if the judge accepted.',
    reread: `${L}, practice shots, some held back`,
    timeLimitMs: 20000,
    async run({ fn }) {

      // On seeds 44 and 50 a fresh game's first shot at angle 30, power 70 would hit.
      for (const seed of [23, 44, 50]) {
        const ref = referee({ game: 'lob', mode: 0, seed });

        if (off >= 0) fail({ checked: `the practice landings in kit.shots (seed ${seed})`, input: `the practice shots' messages began ${real.slice(0, 3).map((x) => `"${x.message}"`).join(', ')}`, observed: `practice shot ${off + 1} is recorded at ${show(kit.shots[off]?.impact_x)}; it landed at ${real[off]?.impact.toFixed(3)}`, expected: 'every landing exact: fire the sighting shots first, so the landing slot is known before a practice shot can hit' });
        const sighters = ref.shots.length - 14;
        if (sighters < 1 || sighters > 3) fail({ checked: `sighting shots before the practice shots (seed ${seed})`, observed: `${sighters}`, expected: 'from 1 to 3, at angle 5, until the landing slot is known' });
        if (!((seen.presses.KeyN ?? 0) >= 4)) fail({ checked: `new rounds during learnFit (seed ${seed})`, observed: `${seen.presses.KeyN ?? 0}`, expected: 'a new round before each sighting shot and before the 1st, 5th, 9th and 13th practice shot' });

      }
    },
  },
  {
    id: '03-budget', title: 'playLevel stays inside a level\'s budget, even one too small to learn anything',
    requirement: 'playLevel learns with metered(host, kit, allowance(level)), offers only options whose estimated cost fits what is left, stops repairing when OutOfBudget is thrown, and still plays the scored rounds; it never goes over the budget and never throws for it.',
    reread: `${L}, the budget`,

`courses/sightline/checks/05.mjs`:

```mjs
import { fail, expectSame, show, CONTROLS, envWith, gameIdOf, playOn, sayScore, ruleFor, kitBy, levelNo } from './harness.mjs';
import { makeGame, gameBytes } from '../host.mjs';
import { referee } from '../levels.mjs';

export const title = 'Lift the code';
const L = 'lesson 05';

// Where an address expression points, in the checker's own words: [N] for a fixed
// address, *[N]+16 for field 16 of the struct whose address is kept at N.
function where(addr, offset = 0) {
  if (!addr || typeof addr !== 'object') return '?';
  if (addr.op === 'const') return `[${addr.value + offset}]`;
  if (addr.op === 'load') return `*${where(addr.addr, addr.offset)}+${offset}`;
  return `(computed)+${offset}`;
}
const storeAt = (st) => where(st.addr, st.offset);
const realStores = (f) => (f?.stores ?? []).filter((st) => !st.inLoop);

// Memory as the evaluator reads it, from the game as it is now.
function liveEnv(host, extra = {}) {
  const bytes = host.memory();
  const view = new DataView(bytes.buffer, bytes.byteOffset, bytes.byteLength);
  const load = (type, a) => {
    if (a < 0 || a + 4 > bytes.byteLength) return null;
    if (type === 'i32.load') return view.getInt32(a, true);
    if (type === 'f32.load') return view.getFloat32(a, true);
    if (type === 'i32.load8_u') return bytes[a];
    return null;
  };
  return { load, call: (name, args) => (name.endsWith('.sin') ? Math.sin(args[0]) : name.endsWith('.cos') ? Math.cos(args[0]) : null), memo: new Map(), ...extra };
}

// Three tiny functions, assembled here byte by byte in a module shaped like Lob's (an import of
// env.sin, one memory, exports), for lift to try before it meets a whole game function:
//   a: [100]+4 = param0 + 1                          (a straight line)
//   b: [400]   = the word at [400] + 1               (a load, as a stepper makes)
//   c: block; br_if 0 when param0 == 0; [300] = 5; end; [304] = 9
// In c the store to 300 runs only when param0 is not 0, and the store to 304 after the
// block runs on every path, since br_if 0 only takes its path to the same block's end.
const leb = (n) => { const out = []; do { let b = n & 0x7f; n >>>= 7; if (n) b |= 0x80; out.push(b); } while (n); return out; };
const sleb = (n) => { const out = []; for (;;) { const b = n & 0x7f; n >>= 7; if ((n === 0 && !(b & 0x40)) || (n === -1 && (b & 0x40))) { out.push(b); return out; } out.push(b | 0x80); } };
const section = (id, bytes) => [id, ...leb(bytes.length), ...bytes];
const named = (text) => [...leb(text.length), ...[...text].map((c) => c.charCodeAt(0))];
const TINY = {
  a: [0x41, ...sleb(100), 0x20, 0x00, 0x41, ...sleb(1), 0x6a, 0x36, 0x02, 0x04, 0x0b],
  b: [0x41, ...sleb(400), 0x41, ...sleb(400), 0x28, 0x02, 0x00, 0x41, ...sleb(1), 0x6a, 0x36, 0x02, 0x00, 0x0b],
  c: [0x02, 0x40, 0x20, 0x00, 0x45, 0x0d, 0x00, 0x41, ...sleb(300), 0x41, ...sleb(5), 0x36, 0x02, 0x00, 0x0b,
      0x41, ...sleb(304), 0x41, ...sleb(9), 0x36, 0x02, 0x00, 0x0b],
};
function tinyModule() {
  const names = Object.keys(TINY);
  const body = (code) => { const b = [0x00, ...code]; return [...leb(b.length), ...b]; };
  return Uint8Array.from([0x00, 0x61, 0x73, 0x6d, 0x01, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00,
    ...section(1, [0x02, 0x60, 0x01, 0x7d, 0x01, 0x7d, 0x60, 0x01, 0x7f, 0x00]),
    ...section(2, [0x01, ...named('env'), ...named('sin'), 0x00, 0x00]),
    ...section(3, [names.length, ...names.map(() => 0x01)]),
    ...section(5, [0x01, 0x00, 0x01]),
    ...section(7, [names.length, ...names.flatMap((n, i) => [...named(n), 0x00, i + 1])]),
    ...section(10, [names.length, ...names.flatMap((n) => body(TINY[n]))])]);
}
// The checker's own reading of an expression, enough for the tiny functions: a constant,
// param0, i32.add, i32.eqz and an i32 load from a memory that holds 41 at 400.
function value(e, p0) {
  if (!e || typeof e !== 'object') return undefined;
  if (e.op === 'const') return e.value;
  if (e.op === 'param') return e.index === 0 ? p0 : undefined;
  if (e.op === 'load') { const a = value(e.addr, p0); return a === undefined ? undefined : a + (e.offset ?? 0) === 400 ? 41 : 0; }
  const [x, y] = (e.args ?? []).map((a) => value(a, p0));
  if (e.op === 'i32.add') return x === undefined || y === undefined ? undefined : (x + y) | 0;
  if (e.op === 'i32.eqz') return x === undefined ? undefined : x === 0 ? 1 : 0;
  return undefined;
}

async function lifted(fn, game = 'lob', mode = 0, seed = 1) {
  const parseModule = await fn('wasm.mjs', 'parseModule');
  const liftAll = await fn('lift.mjs', 'liftAll');
  const g = makeGame({ game, mode, seed });
  const all = liftAll(parseModule(g.host.binary()));
  if (!(all instanceof Map) || !all.get('game_key') || !all.get('game_tick')) fail({ checked: `liftAll on ${game}.wasm`, observed: all instanceof Map ? `a Map with ${[...all.keys()].slice(0, 6).join(', ')}` : show(all, 80), expected: 'a Map from each defined function\'s name to what lift returns, with game_key and game_tick among them' });
  return { ...g, all, key: all.get('game_key'), tick: all.get('game_tick') };
}

const setBarrel = (host, truth, angle, power) => {
  while (Math.round(truth.angle()) !== angle) host.press(truth.angle() < angle ? 'ArrowRight' : 'ArrowLeft');
  while (truth.power() !== power) host.press(truth.power() < power ? 'ArrowUp' : 'ArrowDown');
};
const fireReal = (host, truth) => { host.press('Space'); let f = 0; while (truth.flying()) { host.tick(1); f++; } return { x: truth.impactX(), frames: f }; };
