```mjs
import {TAPES,FIXTURES} from './beam-fixture-data.mjs';
const insist=(ok,message)=>{if(!ok)throw new Error('beam: '+message);};
const same=(a,b)=>{
  if(a===b)return true;
  if(!a||!b||typeof a!=='object'||typeof b!=='object'||Array.isArray(a)!==Array.isArray(b))return false;
  const ak=Object.keys(a).sort(),bk=Object.keys(b).sort();
  return ak.length===bk.length&&ak.every((k,i)=>k===bk[i]&&same(a[k],b[k]));
};
const close=(a,b)=>typeof a==='number'&&Number.isFinite(a)&&Math.abs(a-b)<=1e-10+1e-9*Math.max(Math.abs(a),Math.abs(b));
const label=(p,g)=>`C([${p}];[${g}])`;
const inputFor=id=>{const t=TAPES.find(x=>x.id===id);return t.base?{...TAPES.find(x=>x.id===t.base),...t}:t;};
const promptFor=t=>t.prompt||Array(t.promptRepeat.count).fill(t.promptRepeat.token);
function logitsFor(t,prefix){
  if(t.literalLogits)return Array.from({length:32},(_,i)=>t.literalLogits.scores[i]??t.literalLogits.default);
  const state=prefix.length?(t.allPrefixes||t.states?.[prefix.join(',')]||{defaultWeight:1}):t.root;
  return Array.from({length:32},(_,i)=>Math.log(state.weights?.[i]??state.defaultWeight)+(t.addToEveryLogit||0));
}
function compare(a,b){
  if(a.logProbability!==b.logProbability)return a.logProbability>b.logProbability?-1:1;
  const n=Math.min(a.generated.length,b.generated.length);
  for(let i=0;i<n;i++)if(a.generated[i]!==b.generated[i])return a.generated[i]-b.generated[i];
  return a.generated.length-b.generated.length;
}
function candidates(result,width,vocabSize){
  insist(result&&Array.isArray(result.candidates)&&result.candidates.length>0&&result.candidates.length<=width,'return a nonempty candidates array within beamWidth');
  for(const c of Array.from(result.candidates)){
    insist(c&&Array.isArray(c.generated)&&c.generated.length>0&&Array.from(c.generated).every(x=>Number.isInteger(x)&&x>=0&&x<vocabSize),'candidate must have dense valid generated IDs');
    insist(typeof c.logProbability==='number'&&Number.isFinite(c.logProbability)&&['eos','context','limit'].includes(c.stop)&&typeof c.text==='string','finite score, decoded text and stop are required');
  }
  insist(new Set(result.candidates.map(c=>JSON.stringify(c.generated))).size===result.candidates.length,'duplicate candidate');
  for(let i=1;i<result.candidates.length;i++)insist(compare(result.candidates[i-1],result.candidates[i])<=0,'rank by exact score then numeric IDs');
  return result.candidates;
}
async function fixtureRun(api,project,c,control={}){
  const tape=inputFor(c.id),prompt=Object.freeze([...promptFor(tape)]),trace=[],violations=[],reads=[],issued=new Map();
  const config=Object.freeze(Object.defineProperties({}, {
    vocabSize:{enumerable:true,get(){reads.push('vocabSize');return 32;}},
    maxContext:{enumerable:true,get(){reads.push('maxContext');return 32;}}
  }));
  const model=Object.freeze({config}),sentinel=new Error('original beam runtime failure');let runtimeFailed=false;
  const require=(ok,message)=>{if(!ok){violations.push(message);insist(false,message);}};
  const issue=prefix=>{
    const cache=Object.freeze({label:label(prompt,prefix),position:prompt.length+prefix.length});
    issued.set(cache.label,{cache,prefix:[...prefix]});return cache;
  };
  const guarded=fn=>(...args)=>{try{return fn(...args);}catch(error){if(error!==sentinel)violations.push(String(error.message));throw error;}};
  const change=(kind,prefix,logits)=>control.changeLogits?control.changeLogits(kind,prefix,logits):logits;
  const methods={
    prefill:guarded((m,p)=>{
      require(!runtimeFailed,'work after original runtime failure');require(m===model&&same(p,prompt),'prefill inputs');
      require(!trace.length,'one initial prefill');const cache=issue([]);trace.push({kind:'prefill',label:cache.label,position:cache.position});
      if(control.throwAt==='prefill'){runtimeFailed=true;throw sentinel;}
      return {logits:change('prefill',[],logitsFor(tape,[])),cache};
    }),
    decodeStep:guarded((m,token,parent)=>{
      require(!runtimeFailed,'work after original runtime failure');require(m===model&&Number.isInteger(token)&&token>=0&&token<32,'decode inputs');
      const previous=issued.get(parent?.label);require(previous&&parent.position===previous.cache.position,'issued parent-cache value/position');
      const child=[...previous.prefix,token],cache=issue(child),row=[child.length,child,token,parent.label,parent.position,cache.label,cache.position];
      trace.push({kind:'decodeStep',row});
      if(control.throwAt==='decode'&&child.join(',')==='7'){runtimeFailed=true;throw sentinel;}
      return {logits:change('decodeStep',child,logitsFor(tape,child)),cache};
    }),
    decode:guarded(ids=>api.decode(ids)),
  };
  const runtime=new Proxy(Object.freeze(methods),{get(target,key){require(Object.hasOwn(target,key),'only prefill/decodeStep/decode are allowed; attempted '+String(key));return target[key];}});
  let value,error;
  try{value=await project.beamDecode(runtime,model,control.prompt??prompt,control.options??{beamWidth:c.beamWidth,maxNewTokens:c.maxNewTokens});}catch(e){error=e;}
  insist(!violations.length,'retained checker violation: '+violations[0]);
  for(const {cache,prefix}of issued.values())insist(same(cache,{label:label(prompt,prefix),position:prompt.length+prefix.length}),'caller/sibling cache changed');
  if(control.reject){
    insist(error&&value===undefined,'invalid input or runtime output must reject, not return candidates');
    if(control.throwAt)insist(error===sentinel,'propagate original runtime error');
    return {id:control.id,rejected:true,message:String(error.message),trace,inferenceCalls:trace.length,
      validationTiming:'Recorded only. Zero prefill on invalid options/prompt is not an added acceptance criterion.'};
  }
  if(error)throw error;
  const actual=candidates(value,c.beamWidth,32);insist(actual.length===c.final.length,'fixture candidate count');
  const comparisons=actual.map((got,i)=>{
    const expected=c.final[i];insist(same(got.generated,expected.generated)&&got.stop===expected.stop,'fixture IDs/ranking/stop');
    insist(got.text===api.decode(expected.generated),'decode generated IDs without prompt');
    insist(close(got.logProbability,expected.logProbability),'full-vocabulary cumulative log probability');
    return {generated:got.generated,actual:got.logProbability,expected:expected.logProbability,error:Math.abs(got.logProbability-expected.logProbability),limit:1e-10+1e-9*Math.max(Math.abs(got.logProbability),Math.abs(expected.logProbability))};
  });
  const observed=trace.filter(x=>x.kind==='decodeStep').map(x=>JSON.stringify(x.row)).sort(),expected=c.ledger.map(x=>JSON.stringify(x)).sort();
  insist(trace[0]?.kind==='prefill'&&trace.filter(x=>x.kind==='prefill').length===1&&same(observed,expected),'parent/child/position call ledger');
  insist(trace.length<=1+c.beamWidth*(c.maxNewTokens-1),'inference operation bound');
  insist(reads.includes('vocabSize')&&reads.includes('maxContext'),'read validated model metadata; source must also use it');
  return {id:c.id,run:c.run,result:value,comparisons,trace,metadataReads:reads};
}
export async function checkBeamFixtures(api,project){
  insist(typeof project.beamDecode==='function','create project.mjs exporting beamDecode(runtime,model,prompt,{beamWidth,maxNewTokens}); lesson08 defines the bounded extension');
  const records=[];for(const c of FIXTURES)records.push(await fixtureRun(api,project,c));
  const c=FIXTURES.find(x=>x.id==='sequence-score-beats-greedy'&&x.run==='w2');
  const invalid=[];
  for(const [field,bad]of [['beamWidth',[0,5,1.5,null,'2']],['maxNewTokens',[0,5,1.5,null,'2']]])for(const value of bad)invalid.push({id:field+'='+JSON.stringify(value),options:{beamWidth:2,maxNewTokens:2,[field]:value}});
  for(const p of [[],Array(32).fill(4),[32],[-1],[1.5],['4'],[null],Array(1)])invalid.push({id:'invalid-prompt-'+invalid.length,prompt:p});
  const badVectors=[Array(31).fill(0),Array(33).fill(0),Array(32),Array(32).fill(NaN),Array(32).fill(Infinity),Array(32).fill(-Infinity),Array(32).fill(null),Array(32).fill('0')];
  for(const [i,vector]of badVectors.entries()){
    invalid.push({id:'prefill-logits-'+i,changeLogits:(kind,prefix,original)=>kind==='prefill'?vector:original});
    invalid.push({id:'decode-logits-'+i,changeLogits:(kind,prefix,original)=>prefix.join(',')==='7'?vector:original});
  }
  invalid.push({id:'nonfinite-computed-score',changeLogits:()=>Array.from({length:32},(_,i)=>i===6?1e308:-1e308)});
  invalid.push({id:'prefill-error',throwAt:'prefill'},{id:'decode-error',throwAt:'decode'});
  for(const control of invalid)records.push(await fixtureRun(api,project,c,{...control,reject:true}));
  return records;
}
export async function checkBeamRuntime(api,project,model){
  insist(typeof project.beamDecode==='function','create the capstone beamDecode export');
  const records=[];
  for(const [prompt,beamWidth,maxNewTokens]of [[[4],1,2],[[4,5],1,4],[Array(31).fill(4),1,4],[[4,5],2,2],[[6,7,3],4,4]]){
    const callerPrompt=[...prompt],snapshots=[],calls=[],violations=[],before=JSON.stringify({model,prompt:callerPrompt});
    const require=(ok,msg)=>{if(!ok){violations.push(msg);insist(false,msg);}};
    const methods={
      prefill(...args){calls.push({kind:'prefill'});const value=api.prefill(...args);snapshots.push([value.cache,JSON.stringify(value.cache)]);return value;},
      decodeStep(...args){calls.push({kind:'decodeStep',token:args[1],position:args[2]?.position});const value=api.decodeStep(...args);snapshots.push([value.cache,JSON.stringify(value.cache)]);return value;},
      decode:api.decode,
    };
    const runtime=new Proxy(methods,{get(target,key){require(Object.hasOwn(target,key),'only prefill/decodeStep/decode are allowed');return target[key];}});
    const value=await project.beamDecode(runtime,model,callerPrompt,{beamWidth,maxNewTokens});
    insist(!violations.length,'retained checker violation: '+violations[0]);
    const actual=candidates(value,beamWidth,model.config.vocabSize),comparisons=[];
    insist(calls.filter(x=>x.kind==='prefill').length===1&&calls.length<=1+beamWidth*(maxNewTokens-1),'actual inference count/bound');
    for(const c of actual){
      insist(c.generated.length<=maxNewTokens&&prompt.length+c.generated.length<=model.config.maxContext,'actual candidate exceeds limits');
      const eos=c.generated.indexOf(0);insist(eos<0||eos===c.generated.length-1,'generation after EOS');
      const stop=eos>=0?'eos':prompt.length+c.generated.length===model.config.maxContext?'context':'limit';
      insist(c.stop===stop&&(stop!=='limit'||c.generated.length===maxNewTokens),'actual stop/budget');
      insist(c.text===api.decode(c.generated),'actual decoded text');
      let state=api.prefill(model,prompt),score=0;
      for(let i=0;i<c.generated.length;i++){
        const z=state.logits;insist(Array.isArray(z)&&z.length===model.config.vocabSize&&Array.from(z).every(Number.isFinite),'finite runtime logits');
        // Independent probability-ratio score for these ordinary fixture logits.
        const max=Math.max(...z),denominator=z.reduce((s,x)=>s+Math.exp(x-max),0);
        score+=Math.log(Math.exp(z[c.generated[i]]-max)/denominator);
        if(i+1<c.generated.length)state=api.decodeStep(model,c.generated[i],state.cache);
      }
      insist(close(c.logProbability,score),'actual score differs from independent fresh-prefix replay');
      comparisons.push({generated:c.generated,actual:c.logProbability,replayed:score,error:Math.abs(c.logProbability-score)});
    }
    if(beamWidth===1){
      const greedy=api.generate(model,prompt,{maxNewTokens,temperature:0,topK:model.config.vocabSize,seed:1});
      insist(same(actual[0].generated,greedy.generated)&&actual[0].text===greedy.text&&actual[0].stop===greedy.stop,'width-one greedy parity');
    }
    for(const [cache,encoded]of snapshots)insist(JSON.stringify(cache)===encoded,'actual caller/sibling cache changed');
    insist(JSON.stringify({model,prompt:callerPrompt})===before,'caller model/prompt changed');
    records.push({prompt,beamWidth,maxNewTokens,result:value,calls,comparisons,widthOneGreedyCompared:beamWidth===1});
  }
  return records;
}

import {check} from './checks.mjs';
const root=new URL('./',import.meta.url);
const load=async name=>{const r=await fetch(new URL(name,root));if(!r.ok)throw new Error(`cannot read ${name}: ${r.status}`);return r.text();};
function moduleURL(source){const resolved=source.replace(/(['"])\.\/(numeric|spec)\.mjs\1/g,(_,q,name)=>q+new URL(name+'.mjs',root).href+q);return URL.createObjectURL(new Blob([resolved],{type:'text/javascript'}));}
self.onmessage=async({data})=>{
 const urls=[];
 try{
   const config=JSON.parse(await load('course.json')),entry=moduleURL(data.source);urls.push(entry);
   const api=await import(entry);let project={};
   if(data.project.trim()){const u=moduleURL(data.project);urls.push(u);project=await import(u);}
   let fixture={};
   if(config.id==='small-llm-runtime'){const manifest=JSON.parse(await load('fixtures/manifest.json'));fixture={text:await load('fixtures/tiny-original.json'),digest:manifest.sha256,golden:JSON.parse(await load('fixtures/golden.json'))};}
   self.postMessage({kind:'check',report:await check(api,data.lesson,project,fixture)});
 }catch(error){self.postMessage({kind:'execution-error',message:String(error.message??error)});}
 finally{urls.forEach(URL.revokeObjectURL);}
};

function same(a,b) {
 if(a===b)return true;
 if(!a||!b||typeof a!=='object'||typeof b!=='object'||Array.isArray(a)!==Array.isArray(b))return false;
 if(Array.isArray(a))return a.length===b.length&&Array.from(a).every((value,i)=>same(value,b[i]));
 const keys=Object.keys(a).sort(),other=Object.keys(b).sort();
 return keys.length===other.length&&keys.every((key,i)=>key===other[i]&&same(a[key],b[key]));
}
// Short printable form of a value; long arrays/objects are cut so a failure stays readable.
export function brief(value,limit=80){
 let text;try{text=JSON.stringify(value);}catch{text=undefined;}
 if(text===undefined)text=String(value);
 return text.length>limit?text.slice(0,limit-3)+'...':text;
}
// First place where observed differs from expected, as {path,expected,observed}; null when equal.
export function firstDifference(observed,expected,path=''){
 if(same(observed,expected))return null;
 if(Array.isArray(expected)&&Array.isArray(observed)){
  for(let i=0;i<Math.min(observed.length,expected.length);i++){const d=firstDifference(observed[i],expected[i],`${path}[${i}]`);if(d)return d;}
  return {path,expected:`${expected.length} items`,observed:`${observed.length} items`};
 }
 const plain=x=>x&&typeof x==='object'&&!Array.isArray(x);
 if(plain(expected)&&plain(observed)){
  for(const key of [...new Set([...Object.keys(expected),...Object.keys(observed)])].sort()){
   if(!Object.hasOwn(expected,key))return {path:`${path}.${key}`,expected:'no such field',observed:brief(observed[key])};
   if(!Object.hasOwn(observed,key))return {path:`${path}.${key}`,expected:brief(expected[key]),observed:'missing'};
   const d=firstDifference(observed[key],expected[key],`${path}.${key}`);if(d)return d;
  }
 }
 return {path,expected:brief(expected),observed:brief(observed)};
}
const equal=(a,b,label='result')=>{const d=firstDifference(a,b);if(d)throw new Error(`${label}${d.path}: expected ${d.expected}; observed ${d.observed}`);};
const reject=async fn=>{let caught=false;try{await fn();}catch{caught=true;}if(!caught)throw new Error('expected rejection; observed acceptance');};
const leaves=(x,path='',out=[])=>{if(Array.isArray(x))Array.from(x).forEach((v,i)=>leaves(v,`${path}[${i}]`,out));else out.push([path,x]);return out;};
// Numeric comparison that reports only the first value outside tolerance, with its index.
export function close(a,b,tol=1e-8,label='values'){
 const av=leaves(a),bv=leaves(b);
 if(av.length!==bv.length||av.some(([p],i)=>p!==bv[i][0]))throw new Error(`${label}: expected ${bv.length} numbers shaped like ${brief(b,40)}; observed ${Array.isArray(a)?av.length+' numbers':brief(a)}`);
 const bad=av.map(([,v],i)=>!Number.isFinite(v)||Math.abs(v-bv[i][1])>tol);
 const first=bad.indexOf(true);if(first<0)return;
 throw new Error(`${label}${av[first][0]}: expected ${bv[first][1]} (within ${tol}); observed ${brief(av[first][1])}. ${bad.filter(Boolean).length} of ${bv.length} numbers are outside tolerance.`);
}

function inputCacheChange(before,after,when){
 let original;try{original=JSON.parse(before);}catch{original=before;}
 const d=firstDifference(after,original);
 return `decodeStep changed its input cache ${when}: cache${d?.path??''} was ${d?.expected??'different'} and is now ${d?.observed??'different'}. Return a new cache and leave the one you were given unchanged.`;
}

 {id:'capstone-stream-runtime',lesson:'08',input:'actual original model: streamed events and full result parity',run:async(a,p,f)=>{if(typeof p.streamGenerate!=='function')throw new Error('Create project.mjs exporting streamGenerate(runtime,model,prompt,options); lesson08 defines consumer delivery.');return checkStreamRuntime(a,p,await model(a,f));}},
];
// Lesson section to reread for each public case (first matching id prefix).
const SECTIONS=[
 ['loader-','Loader mechanism and worked example'],['tokenizer-','Tokens and execution model'],
 ['softmax-','Softmax mechanism'],['silu-','Activation'],
 ['normalization-','Normalization mechanism'],['mlp-','Gated MLP mechanism'],
 ['rotary-','Position and head layout'],['attention-','Attention mechanism and worked example'],['forward-','Full block execution order'],
 ['cache-prefill','Cache execution model'],['cache-incremental-parity','Worked parity trace; Validation and isolation'],['cache-','Validation and isolation'],
 ['sampling-seed-values','Pinned random sequence'],['sampling-','Ranking and probabilities'],
 ['generation-pinned-seed','Return contract'],['generation-last-slot','Worked limit trace'],['generation-','Generation execution model'],
 ['capstone-generator-audit','Product and public interface; Investigation input'],['capstone-beam-','Bounded search extension'],['capstone-stream-','Deliver the first token before completion'],
];
export const sectionFor=id=>SECTIONS.find(([prefix])=>id.startsWith(prefix))?.[1]??'';
function nextStep(c,project) {
 if(c.lesson!=='08')return `Reread lesson ${c.lesson}, "${sectionFor(c.id)}". Edit runtime.mjs and rerun node lab.mjs check ${c.lesson}.`;
 if(c.id.startsWith('capstone-stream-'))return typeof project?.streamGenerate==='function'?'Follow the printed failure in API.md and lesson08; complete the named runtime prerequisite or repair the consumer loop, preserve the attempt and rerun.':'In project.mjs export streamGenerate(runtime,model,prompt,options); lesson08 defines token delivery and completion. Preserve the failed attempt and rerun.';
 if(c.id.startsWith('capstone-beam-'))return typeof project?.beamDecode==='function'?'beamDecode was found. Use the score/IDs/stop or parent-cache call diagnostic to compare your project with lesson08, Bounded search extension. Runtime prerequisite errors still need their earlier module check.':'Create your own beamDecode export in project.mjs; read lesson08, Bounded search extension, then rerun module08.';
 if(typeof project?.runProject!=='function')return 'Create project.mjs exporting async function runProject(runtime,model,spec), as described in lesson 08, Product and public interface; then rerun module 08.';
 return 'runProject was found, so this failure may come from project.mjs (its generation or differences) or from runtime.mjs methods the capstone also calls (loadModel, prefill, generate). Use the message to decide which; if it names an earlier module, repair and check that module first. Then compare with lesson 08, Product and public interface, and rerun module 08.';
}
export async function check(api,lesson,project={},fixture={}) {
 const selected=cases.filter(c=>lesson==='all'||c.lesson===lesson);if(!selected.length)throw new Error(`unknown lesson ${lesson}`);
 const results=[];
 for(const c of selected){try{await c.run(api,project,fixture);results.push({id:c.id,lesson:c.lesson,pass:true});}catch(e){results.push({id:c.id,lesson:c.lesson,pass:false,input:c.input,requirement:REQUIREMENTS[c.lesson],section:sectionFor(c.id),message:String(e?.message??e),next:nextStep(c,project)});}}
 return {course:COURSE,lesson,pass:results.every(r=>r.pass),results};
}

// Plain-language summary of a check receipt for the terminal and the browser.
// The machine-readable receipt stays unchanged in result.json (and behind lab.mjs --json).
export function formatResult(result,{lesson,footer=""}={}){
 const cut=text=>{const s=String(text??"");return s.length>500?s.slice(0,497)+"...":s;};
 if(result?.kind!=="check")return [`Execution error before any check result: ${cut(result?.message)}`,"Next: fix the error (often an import, syntax or endless-loop problem in your file), then rerun. This attempt was kept.",footer].filter(Boolean).join("\n");
 const rows=Array.isArray(result.report?.results)?result.report.results:[],failed=rows.filter(r=>!r.pass),passed=rows.filter(r=>r.pass);
 const scope=lesson==="trained"?"Trained profile":lesson==="all"?"All modules":`Module ${lesson}`;
 const lines=[`${scope}: ${passed.length} of ${rows.length} checks passed.`];
 for(const r of failed){
  lines.push("",`FAIL ${r.id}${r.lesson?` (lesson ${r.lesson})`:""}`);
  if(r.requirement)lines.push(`  Requirement: ${r.requirement}`);
  if(r.input!==undefined)lines.push(`  Input: ${typeof r.input==="string"?cut(r.input):brief(r.input,200)}`);
  lines.push(`  Problem: ${cut(r.message)}`,`  Next: ${r.next}`);
 }
 if(passed.length)lines.push("",`Passed: ${passed.map(r=>r.id).join(", ")}`);
 if(footer)lines.push("",footer);
 return lines.join("\n");
}

`courses/small-llm-runtime/fixtures/trained/publisher-profile.md`:

```md
This 260K model is a tiny model and it was trained as follows:

```
python train.py \
    --out_dir="outmini" \
    --batch_size=128 \
    --max_seq_len=512 \
    --gradient_accumulation_steps=1 \
    --vocab_source="custom" \
    --vocab_size=512 \
    --dim=64 \
    --n_layers=5 \
    --n_heads=8 \
    --n_kv_heads=4 \
    --multiple_of=4 \
    --learning_rate=1e-3 \
    --dropout=0.05 \
    --weight_decay=0.01 \
    --max_iters=100000 \
    --beta2=0.99 \
    --warmup_iters=1000 \
    --eval_interval=2000 \
    --eval_iters=100 \
    --compile=True
```

You'll notice that `n_kv_heads` is 4 while `n_heads` is 8, so two heads at a time share their key,value projections, i.e. this model is 2X multiquery. You'll also notice that we're using a custom tokenizer with 512 tokens. The model trained for ~10 minutes (?) on my A100 and achieves validation loss of 1.2968.

Sampling this model at temperature 0.0 (i.e. deterministic greedy argmax sampling) gives:

```
$ ./run stories260K/stories260K.bin -z stories260K/tok512.bin -t 0.0
Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the park. One day, she saw a big, red ball. She wanted to play with it, but it was too high.
Lily's mom said, "Lily, let's go to the park." Lily was sad and didn't know what to do. She said, "I want to play with your ball, but I can't find it."
Lily was sad and didn't know what to do. She said, "I'm sorry, Lily. I didn't know what to do."
Lily didn't want to help her mom, so she said, "I'm sorry, mom. I didn't know what to do." Her mom said, "Don't worry, Lily. We can help you.
```

You can reproduce the same in Python by running `sample.py`:

```
$ python sample.py --checkpoint=stories260K/stories260K.pt --tokenizer=stories260K/tok512.model --temperature=0.0 --max_new_tokens=257
```

I hardcoded max tokens to be 257 manually because the `sample.py` script doesn't currently terminate on the special BOS token like the run.c script does. Sampling at 1.0 with topp of 0.9 gives a bit more reasonable samples:

```
$ ./run stories260K/stories260K.bin -z stories260K/tok512.bin -t 1.0 -p 0.9 -s 133742
Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his toys and eat sandwiches. One day, Timmy's mom told him it was time to rest for a while. Timmy's friend Billy came over and took him a down.
Timmy's mom saw that Timmy was sad, but Timmy said, "I didn't understand what is it! We need to find some leafs." Timmy thought about it and took a deep breath on a spoon. He hoped it was important to be kind and continued to find its image next time.
After they finished getting, Timmy's dad came up to his house and promised to help Timmy.
```

Hey you can't expect too much from a 260K parameter model. I'm even mildly shocked we get this far :D

```

import {readFileSync,writeFileSync,mkdirSync,existsSync,readdirSync,lstatSync,renameSync,realpathSync,openSync,fstatSync,closeSync,constants} from 'node:fs';

# 01 · Load exactly one model

A model file can have familiar dimensions and still contain the wrong bytes or tensor names. Build a loader that accepts exactly the original teaching model this course defines.

Goal: validate a checkpoint and convert text into its token IDs. Prerequisites are the entry JavaScript and matrix skills. The supplied numeric.mjs backend is complete and independent of the tensor course.

## Pinned model

PocketDecoder-v1 is an original, deliberately tiny decoder-only teaching architecture. It has model width 8, two heads of width 4, two blocks, hidden width 16, vocabulary size 32 and context length 32. It uses binary64 numbers on the CPU. This format makes no compatibility claim with another model family.

The included 21,661-byte checkpoint was generated from an original deterministic script. Its parameters are untrained. It supports arithmetic and cache investigations, not claims about language quality. No pretrained checkpoint was downloaded or packaged. An external asset would need its own redistribution review and is outside this offline route.

## Loader mechanism and worked example

The file format is ivy-pocket-json-v1. A tensor has shape and data fields; matrices store row-major data and map a row vector through a [inputWidth,outputWidth] weight. spec.mjs defines the exact configuration and vocabulary. fixtures/manifest.json supplies the expected SHA-256 of the checkpoint bytes.

First compare the byte digest. Then parse JSON and validate the format, configuration, vocabulary, tensor inventory, shapes and finite numeric values. The embedding shape is [32,8]; a query matrix in either block is [8,8]. A correctly hashed file with a missing query matrix must still fail. A shape [4,16] also contains 64 values but has different semantics and must fail.

{{practice:r01-bytes}}

{{practice:r01-order}}

Compare object members by name and value. Preserve order for arrays such as vocabulary entries. Byte identity is a separate check.

## Tokens and execution model

A token ID is an integer index into the vocabulary. IDs 0 through 3 represent EOS, unknown, newline and space. IDs 4 through 29 represent lowercase a through z, followed by period and comma. Iterate Unicode code points; an unsupported code point maps to unknown ID 1. Do not drop it. Decoding omits EOS, renders unknown as the replacement character, and rejects out-of-range or noninteger IDs.

Worked tokenization: "a b" becomes [4,3,5]. A prompt is a nonempty token array. There is no automatic beginning-of-sequence token. Later, each ID selects one embedding row, which becomes the first hidden vector for that position.

{{practice:r01-tokens}}

## Complete and build

Before coding, write down the order of your loader checks: digest, format, config fields, vocabulary, tensor names and shapes, then finite numeric values. Every check runs before any weight is used. In runtime.mjs implement loadModel, encode and decode. sha256 is supplied because file hashing is outside the course's target skills. Return the validated model with fingerprint equal to the expected digest. Keep its parameters immutable during inference.

Run module 01. The malformed controls carry newly computed matching hashes, so a loader that checks only the hash and then accepts the bytes fails them. Those controls test rejection only: a stub that always throws also passes them while failing the valid-checkpoint cases. A few passing rejection cases therefore do not show a usable loader or a module pass. The tokenizer check includes an unsupported Unicode code point and a newline.

## Repair and changed problem

Hint 1: distinguish byte identity from schema validity. Hint 2: compare the exact required name set before validating values. Hint 3: report the tensor name whose shape or values failed. A JavaScript null is not a finite model weight.

Create a malformed checkpoint that has the correct number of values but a wrong semantic shape. Rehash it locally and explain why it must be rejected. Keep this distinction for module 05: a cache also needs more than matching array lengths.

```

`courses/small-llm-runtime/lessons/02.md`:

# 02 · Keep probabilities finite

Exponentiating a large score directly can overflow before you divide by the total. Implement probabilities whose result depends on score differences rather than a common score offset.

Goal: compute stable softmax and the pinned activation. Depends on module 01.

## Softmax mechanism

A logit is a score before conversion into probabilities. Softmax assigns exp(score)/sum(exp(scores)). Subtract the largest valid score from every score before exponentiating. The common exponential factor cancels, while the largest exponential becomes one. Divide each exponential by their sum. The result contains nonnegative probabilities summing to one within numeric precision.

This runtime uses -Infinity to mark a masked score: a score excluded from the distribution. Its exponential is zero.

{{practice:r02-types}}

Numeric validation must reject strings, null and missing values. The attention mask is the one explicit nonfinite exception. Every input must be a Number. Reject strings, null and missing elements; the only permitted nonfinite score is the -Infinity mask.

 Reject an empty row, NaN, positive Infinity or a row with every key masked. An all-masked row has no distribution to normalize. Converting it to a uniform row would invent attention to invalid positions.

## Worked example

Scores [1000,1001,-Infinity] become [-1,0,-Infinity]. Exponentiating gives [exp(-1),1,0], then normalization gives [1/(1+e),e/(1+e),0]. The softmax-extreme check compares this result with the shifted scores [-1000,-999,-Infinity]. The probabilities must agree.

{{practice:r02-shift}}

## Activation

An activation transforms a hidden coordinate before another projection. The pinned MLP uses SiLU(x)=x/(1+exp(-x)). Large positive x approaches x; large negative x approaches zero. At x=0 the result is zero. With binary64, exp(1000) overflows to Infinity, but -1000 divided by that positive infinite denominator still yields finite negative zero. Avoid expressions that multiply Infinity by zero and produce NaN.

The silu-extreme check executes inputs [-1000,0,1000]. Numeric behavior at these extremes matters even though the tiny checkpoint rarely reaches them. A stable method must preserve the defined operation, not simply clip every value to a convenient constant.

{{practice:r02-mask}}

## Complete and build

Warm up by hand: for scores [1000,1001,-Infinity], subtracting the maximum gives exponentials [e^-1, 1, 0]. Divide each by their sum and confirm that the row sums to one and the masked entry is zero. Then write the complete softmax implementation, including validation. Implement silu as a separate scalar operation. Run module 02.

The supplied numeric backend does not provide these target operations. It supplies finite-vector checking, vector addition, elementwise multiplication and row-vector matrix projection. You own the probability and activation logic.

## Repair hints

Hint 1: inspect shifted scores before exponentiating. Hint 2: compare the same scores with a common offset added. Hint 3: distinguish a legitimate zero probability from a nonfinite total. If every key is masked, return a clear error before division.

## Changed problem

An attention implementation masks a whole row because its prefix length was computed incorrectly. Decide whether the probability function should conceal that state or expose it, then construct a public case showing the chosen behavior. Later modules return to this distinction when an invalid cache looks like a numeric failure. Keep an extreme-score case in your regression checks while adding normalization and attention.

```

# 03 · Build a decoder block

A decoder block changes each position's vector while preserving its model width. Build its normalization and gated feed-forward calculation before adding communication between positions.

Goal: apply learned RMS normalization and the pinned gated MLP. Depends on module 02. Matrix projection is supplied by numeric.mjs.

## Normalization mechanism

RMSNorm divides a vector by the square root of its mean squared coordinate plus epsilon, then multiplies each coordinate by its learned gain. The model's epsilon is 1e-5. A gain vector has the same width as the input. Validate all values and require positive finite epsilon.

Worked normalization: x=[2,-2], gains=[1,2], epsilon=1. The mean square is 4, so the divisor is sqrt(5). The output is [2/sqrt(5),-4/sqrt(5)]. A zero input remains zero because epsilon keeps the denominator positive.



{{practice:r03-normalize}}

This RMS normalization rescales by root mean square and learned gains without mean subtraction.

{{practice:r03-extremes}}

Squaring or dividing can overflow. Rearrange the same formula to keep intermediate magnitudes bounded.

Finite coordinates can overflow when squared. To preserve the same formula at large magnitudes, divide by the largest absolute coordinate before squaring, compute the scaled root mean square, then restore its scale. Combine that result with sqrt(epsilon) using a stable hypotenuse calculation. Handle the all-zero vector separately. The large-finite check uses opposite values of magnitude 1e300; their normalized magnitudes should remain one before gains are applied.

## Gated MLP mechanism

An MLP here is a position-wise calculation that projects the model vector into a wider hidden vector and back. SwiGLU uses two input projections. Apply SiLU to x@w1, multiply that vector elementwise by x@w3, then project through w2. With model width d and hidden width f, w1 and w3 have shape [d,f], while w2 has shape [f,d]. There are no bias vectors in this pinned architecture.

```text
x [d] -> w1 [d,f] -> SiLU --+
                           multiply -> w2 [f,d] -> output [d]
x [d] -> w3 [d,f] ----------+
```

Worked gating before the final projection: an activated branch [2,3] and gate [4,0] produce [8,0]. Adding those branches would implement a different block. The executable MLP check uses a nonidentity output matrix to expose both a missing gate and a transposed-weight convention.

{{practice:r03-gate}}

## Complete and build

Warm up by hand: RMSNorm of [2,-2] with epsilon 1 is [2,-2]/sqrt(5) before the gain; with gains [1,2] it becomes [2/sqrt(5),-4/sqrt(5)]. For a gated MLP, the activated branch and the gate branch are multiplied element by element before the output projection. Implement rmsNorm and mlp in runtime.mjs, using the supplied matrix projection if you wish. Run module 03.

In the complete decoder, these operations sit inside residual paths. A residual adds the block output back to its input, so the vector width must agree. Module 04 specifies the complete order; do not guess the order from tensor names.

## Repair hints

Hint 1: label every vector and matrix width. Hint 2: inspect the two hidden projections before multiplying. Hint 3: use unequal values and a nonidentity w2 to distinguish a transposed matrix from an omitted gate. If an all-zero case passes, still test nonzero gains; zero cannot expose a missing gain multiplication.

## Changed problem

Construct a vector whose mean is nonzero and compare RMS normalization with a deliberately centered variant. Explain which operation the pinned model requests and how your case distinguishes them. Also challenge a naive square with large finite coordinates. Keep the results as normalization regressions while implementing attention. This returns to module 01's rule that equal array sizes do not make two numerical meanings interchangeable.

```

```md
# 04 · Attend to the prefix

A token may use earlier tokens, but it must not use a future token. Implement the full-prefix path first so cached decoding later has a clear numerical comparison.

Goal: implement causal attention, positional rotations and complete full-prefix logits. Depends on modules 01–03.

## Attention mechanism and worked example

A query is the current position's comparison vector. A key is a stored comparison vector for one accessible position. A value is that position's information vector. Attention computes dot(query,key)/sqrt(headWidth), applies softmax across accessible positions, then returns the probability-weighted sum of value vectors. The number of keys is the prefix length, not the head width.

For query [1,1], keys [[1,0],[0,1]] have equal scores, so both probabilities are one half. Values [[2,4],[8,-2]] therefore produce [5,1]. Unequal scores must include the sqrt(headWidth) divisor; the nonuniform attention check distinguishes a missing scale.

At zero-based position p, causal attention sees positions 0 through p inclusive. Exclude later positions before normalizing. A prefix's logits must stay unchanged when only the later suffix changes.

{{practice:r04-causal}}

## Position and head layout

The eight projected coordinates split into two adjacent heads of four coordinates. Within each head, rotate adjacent pairs [0,1] and [2,3]. For pair starting at local coordinate j, angle=position/(ropeBase^(j/headWidth)). Replace [a,b] by [a*cos(angle)-b*sin(angle), a*sin(angle)+b*cos(angle)]. The base is 10000. Apply this rotation to queries and keys, never values. These exact pair and frequency conventions belong to this teaching architecture.

At position zero every angle is zero. At a later position, a pair's norm is preserved but its orientation changes. The rotary-position check executes two pairs at position three and distinguishes using the whole model width in the frequency denominator from the required head width.

A cache stores results for the tokens already processed in the prefix.

{{practice:r04-position}}

The new token follows the already processed prefix; its zero-based position equals the old cache length.

## Full block execution order

For each block: RMS-normalize its input using attnNorm; project wq, wk and wv; rotate each query and key at its sequence position; run causal attention independently in each head; concatenate heads; project wo; add the block input. Then RMS-normalize that residual with ffnNorm, run the gated MLP, and add its output to the residual. Repeat for both blocks. Finally apply finalNorm and lmHead to produce 32 logits per position.

Return {logits,cache} from forward(model,tokens). logits contains one vector per input position. cache has format pocket-cache-v1, model fingerprint, position equal to token count, and one {keys,values} object per block. Each row has model width eight after the two heads are concatenated. Keys are already rotated. This cache representation is the output of full computation, not permission to change earlier rows.

## Build, repair and changed problem

Start from the worked example above: probabilities [0.5,0.5] applied to values [[2,4],[8,-2]] give [5,1]. Then implement rotary, attention and forward. Run module 04. Full-prefix logits are compared with a separate scalar-loop implementation, with tolerance 1e-10 on the original fixture. Future-suffix independence is tested separately.

Hints: inspect one head; inspect one position's accessible keys; compare after each residual addition. Construct a suffix change that would influence an unmasked implementation but cannot influence a causal prefix. Keep its observed logits for module 05's cache-parity investigation.

```

`courses/small-llm-runtime/lessons/05.md`:

```md
# 05 · Reuse keys and values

Recomputing an entire prefix is a useful reference route. A cache avoids recomputing old keys and values, but it adds state whose identity and contents must remain correct.

Goal: make one-token cached decode agree with full-prefix computation. Depends on module 04. Numeric parity comes before a performance claim.

## Cache execution model

prefill(model,tokens) computes the prompt once. Return its last logit vector and the full cache. The cache position counts processed tokens. For a prefix of length p, the appended token uses zero-based rotary position p. Each block appends one rotated key row and one unrotated value row. The new query attends to all cached rows including the new row.

```text
prefill [a,b,c] -> rows at positions 0,1,2; cache.position=3
decode token d -> compute new query/key at position 3
               -> append one key/value per block
               -> attend to positions 0..3
               -> return last logits; new cache.position=4
```

The new token's input to the next block is its current residual output, not its original embedding. Earlier rows in that next block are already present in its separate cache.

## Worked parity trace

Start with prompt [4]. Append [5,3,6,7] one token at a time. After each append, compare decodeStep's logits with the last logits from forward on the entire prefix. The cache-incremental-parity check also compares each position with the independent scalar oracle. Agreement at only the first position cannot catch an offset that begins to fail later.

{{practice:r05-length}}

## Validation and isolation

Before any mutation, validate cache format, fingerprint, position, block count, row counts, row widths and finite values. Each key/value list must have exactly position rows. A cache at the context limit cannot accept another decode step. Reject a cache from another checkpoint even if dimensions agree.

decodeStep returns a new cache and leaves its input unchanged. This lets two requests continue from the same prefix without corrupting one another. It is acceptable to share genuinely immutable old rows; copying rows is simpler for this small model. New outer arrays that still mutate shared inner arrays do not satisfy isolation.

{{practice:r05-isolation}}

## Complete and build

Start from the per-token computation you wrote for forward in module 04. Add the append step first (one rotated key row and one value row per block), then replace recomputation of old rows with reads from the cache. Implement prefill and decodeStep(model,token,cache). Return {logits,cache}. Run module 05.

The validation check intentionally breaks a later block's key length. If your code appends to an earlier block before discovering it, it has already damaged the input. Validate the whole cache first, then compute the new state.

## Repair hints and changed problem

Hint 1: compare cache.position with every row count. Hint 2: compare the new key before attention. Hint 3: compare one block's output with a full-prefix trace before inspecting later blocks. Avoid changing sampling while diagnosing numeric parity; no token draw is needed here.

Fork one valid prefix into two different next tokens. Check both results against full recomputation and verify that the shared original prefix remains byte-for-byte unchanged. The capstone changes the failure again: a cache will have valid dimensions but incorrect content.

```

`courses/small-llm-runtime/lessons/06.md`:

```md
# 06 · Make sampling reproducible

Identical logits can produce different sampled tokens. Make that choice reproducible so a cache repair can be tested without also changing the random experiment.

Goal: implement the pinned seeded generator, temperature and top-k controls. Depends on module 02; this module can be checked without a completed attention runtime.

## Ranking and probabilities

Temperature zero selects a highest-scoring token without drawing randomness. Resolve equal scores by ascending token ID. With positive temperature, divide retained scores by temperature, compute stable softmax, draw a number u in [0,1), and select the first cumulative probability greater than u.

topK retains the K highest scores before softmax. Sort by descending score and then ascending token ID; K must be an integer between one and vocabulary size. This runtime requires all 32 sampling logits to be finite. Attention masks belong in attention, not in the final output distribution. Reject negative or nonfinite temperature and invalid random draws.

A positive temperature can be very small. Subtract the largest retained logit before dividing by temperature; otherwise finite positive logits can overflow during division before softmax gets a chance to shift them. This preserves the same distribution and leaves the largest scaled score at zero.

## Worked sampling example

Two retained tokens have equal logits, so each has probability one half. If their sorted IDs are 2 and 4, draw 0.25 selects 2 and draw 0.75 selects 4. The half-open interval rule handles exact boundaries: draw 0.5 belongs to the second interval. A draw of one is invalid rather than a request for the final token.

{{practice:r06-greedy}}

## Pinned random sequence

The seed is an unsigned 32-bit integer. Maintain state as an unsigned 32-bit integer and update it with state=(1664525*state+1013904223) modulo 2^32. Use Math.imul for the low 32 bits of multiplication. Return state/4294967296. The API rng(seed) returns a function that performs one update per call. This recurrence is a reproducibility contract for the teaching runtime, not a source of security randomness.

A seed alone does not define an experiment. Changing how many draws occur changes later tokens. Greedy sampling must consume no draw. Keep ranking and tie behavior stable as well.

{{practice:r06-draw}}

## Complete and build

Warm up by hand: ranked IDs [3,8,9] with probabilities [0.2,0.3,0.5] have cumulative bounds 0.2, 0.5 and 1, so draws 0, 0.49 and 0.5 select 3, 8 and 9. Next compute those probabilities from ranked logits. Implement rng and sample(logits,{temperature,topK},random). The random function argument makes fixed-draw tests possible; the complete generator will supply rng(seed). Run module 06.

The checks include tied maxima, cumulative-interval boundaries, repeated seed sequences and invalid controls. They establish agreement with the pinned sampling rule on those cases; they do not assess generated text quality.

## Repair hints

Hint 1: print the ranked token IDs before exponentiating. Hint 2: use a supplied draw instead of a seed while testing one distribution. Hint 3: compare the first random state and count draws. If two identical seeded runs disagree, inspect accidental calls to Math.random or shared generator state.

## Changed problem

Create a logit vector with a tie exactly at the top-k cutoff. Decide which token remains, then use draws on both sides of a cumulative boundary. Keep this test when integrating generation. A different model checkpoint or prompt can change logits; a different seed changes only the sampling experiment after those logits are computed.

```

`courses/small-llm-runtime/lessons/07.md`:

```md
# 07 · Generate under limits

Connect prompt processing, cached decode and sampling into a local generator. Make its stopping reason explicit so a short result can be distinguished from an execution failure.

Goal: return generated tokens, text and an execution trace under deterministic limits. Depends on modules 01–06.

## Generation execution model

Validate a nonempty prompt and generation settings. Run prefill once. Its last logits predict the next token. Sample that token, append it to generated IDs and the complete token list, then either stop or feed the token into decodeStep to obtain logits for the following draw. Do not run prefill again on every iteration in the cached path.

```text
prompt -> prefill -> next logits -> sample token
                                  -> append and test stop
                                  -> decode appended token -> next logits
```

The sampled token that fills the context is returned. No later decode step is allowed. EOS is token zero: include it in generated IDs, omit it from decoded text and report stop="eos". If the requested number of new tokens is exhausted, report stop="limit". If context capacity ends first, report stop="context". A legitimate stop is not an execution error.

## Worked limit trace

A prompt with 31 tokens leaves one slot in context 32. Even if maxNewTokens is eight, at most one token may be appended. A prompt already at 32 returns no new tokens and stop="context". maxNewTokens=0 returns the unchanged prompt, no generated IDs and no draws. If the first sampled token is EOS, stop immediately after that one ID.

{{practice:r07-context}}

## Return contract

generate(model,prompt,{maxNewTokens=8,seed=1,temperature=1,topK=32}) returns {tokens,generated,text,stop,trace}. tokens includes the original prompt. generated contains only appended IDs. text decodes generated IDs only. Each trace record is {position,token}: position is the zero-based index the sampled token takes in tokens, so the first generated token has position prompt.length. Keep model, prompt, controls and seed in the caller's experiment notes.

The original fixture is untrained. Output is a local numerical demonstration, even if a string happens to resemble words. No pretrained model permission or language benchmark has been assumed. Your useful product here is a correct, inspectable execution runtime.

{{practice:r07-stop}}

## Complete and build

Build the loop from your tested prefill, decodeStep and sample. Before writing the stop tests, hand-trace the one-slot case: a 31-token prompt with maxNewTokens 8 samples one token and stops ("eos" if that token is 0, otherwise "context") without another decode step. Then implement generate and run module 07. The EOS control uses an original modified output head that makes greedy ranking choose EOS. Repeated-seed runs must return the same complete result and trace.

## Repair hints

Hint 1: count prompt tokens and newly appended tokens separately. Hint 2: inspect which logits produced the first token. Hint 3: test zero limit, full context and EOS without waiting for a long run. Do not label a stopped generation as a failed check merely because it produced fewer tokens than the requested maximum.

## Changed problem

Run the same prompt with greedy output and with a seeded positive temperature. Keep the numerical runtime fixed. Explain which differences come from sampling and which would signal an incorrect cache. Then prepare a second prompt for the capstone; its cache investigation will compare logits before sampling so random variation cannot conceal the cause.

```

`courses/small-llm-runtime/lessons/08.md`:

```md
# 08 · Your generator and cache investigation

Deliver a local generator and investigate a cache whose lengths, widths and numeric values look valid. Reproduce the discrepancy before proposing a repair.

Goal: deliver generated tokens before completion, diagnose unfamiliar cache content corruption and implement bounded beam search. Depends on all preceding modules. No project.mjs starter or completed investigation is supplied.

## Product and public interface

Create project.mjs yourself. Export async function runProject(runtime,model,spec). runtime is your implementation, and model is a validated original fixture. spec supplies prompt token IDs, a cache claimed to represent that prompt, maxNewTokens, seed and topK. Return {generation,differences}. generation must be the complete result of your runtime's local generate call under those settings.

differences is an array of numeric audit findings. Each finding identifies zero-based layer, component "keys" or "values", and maxError against a fresh replay of the stated prompt. Treat differences at or below 1e-8 as numeric agreement. A valid cache must produce no findings. Your report must go beyond naming an array: show the observed logit divergence and explain a plausible mechanism consistent with the evidence.

## Deliver the first token before completion

Also export streamGenerate(runtime,model,prompt,options={}) from your project.
Return an async iterator. It emits token events {type:'token',index,position,token},
then one {type:'complete',result} event with generate's full result. API.md
defines defaults, validation, stop precedence and failure behavior. You may use
an async generator or another iterator with the same observable behavior.

An async iterator has next(), which returns a promise for {value,done}. An
async generator is declared with async function* and pauses at each yield;
its caller resumes it with the next pull. A normal async function that returns
an array has already collected the result. A consumer can observe each event:

```js
for await (const event of streamGenerate(runtime,model,prompt,options)) {
  console.log(event);
}
```

Before implementing it, predict the calls and events for a prompt with one
context slot left, an EOS on the first draw, and a zero-token limit. Keep those
predictions and your first check result. Distinguish prompt IDs from generated
IDs; EOS is a generated event even though it adds no decoded text.

Use your existing prefill, sample, rng, decodeStep and decode. A consumer must
receive token0 before decode for token1 begins. Gathering the full result and
yielding it afterwards does not satisfy streaming. A later decode error must
reject its pull while the consumer retains the earlier prefix. It cannot be
turned into a successful result. The checks use a guarded runtime boundary to
expose buffering, then compare complete streamed results with your generate on
the original model. Repeated and interleaved streams must keep their own RNGs.

Write a small consumer in your project experiment, retain its ordered pull,
token, completion/error and runtime-call evidence in data.json and REPORT.md,
and rerun it after export. Report model/prompt/options and source identities.
Arbitrary additional script filenames are not automatically exported; preserve
their readable source in data.json or a separate explicit evidence bundle.
This baseline delivery exercise remains separate from cache diagnosis and the
distinct beam-search extension. It does not qualify pretrained language output.

## Investigation input

fixtures/mystery-cache.json contains the checkpoint identity, original prompt and a dimension-valid cache. The reason for its discrepancy is not stated in this lesson. Recompute a trusted state using the full-prefix route you tested against the independent scalar oracle. Compare components, test the supplied cache on the next token, and retain the first failing evidence. Validate shape and model identity before comparing contents.

{{practice:r08-audit}}

## Your choices

Choose two additional prompts within the 32-position context. Keep the same model bytes, seed and sampling settings when comparing a cache repair. Record full-prefix versus cached logit errors at more than one appended position. Use a repaired cache to reproduce the trusted seeded generation. Also test a valid cache so an audit that always declares corruption cannot pass.

The public acceptance case uses a new prompt and a content corruption with valid dimensions. It checks generation parity, a numeric component finding and a valid-cache false-positive control. The check does not grade the quality of your causal explanation. RUBRIC.md states that separate reasoning requirement.

## Bounded search extension

Add your own beamDecode(runtime,model,prompt,{beamWidth,maxNewTokens}) export to
project.mjs. API.md freezes the exact result, scoring, cache and stop contracts.
Width and new-token budget are both 1..4. The function uses your existing prefill,
decodeStep and tokenizer; it does not introduce another inference engine.

A greedy step chooses the best token now. A beam keeps a bounded set of prefixes,
so a different first token can later have a higher whole-sequence score. Sum
full-vocabulary log probabilities, expand the active prefixes, carry stopped
prefixes, and prune one combined pool. A carried EOS keeps its original score.
Numeric token IDs break exact ties. A log-probability tolerance is for comparing
results, not for turning unequal scores into ties.

Build in stages. First check width 1 against greedy generation. Next separate
whole-sequence scoring from last-token-only scoring on a tiny positive-weight
branching tape. Then retain multiple branches and trace each decode's parent
prefix and position. Siblings may share an unchanged parent cache; advancing one
sibling's cache and giving it to another sibling changes the conditional model.
Finally cover EOS carry, context/step bounds and the maximum 13 inference calls.
The public checks give finite score and call-ledger diagnostics for these builds.

Before running those checks, record your predicted retained prefixes and first
possible failure. Public cases disclose their expectations; passing them alone
is not an unfamiliar transfer experiment. Choose a different short branching
tape using the same 32-token model boundary, positive integer weights and no
more than two new tokens. Derive full-vocabulary conditional probabilities and
independently enumerate the complete tiny tree, including EOS stopping. State
why pruning preserves the candidates you compare; beam search is not generally
globally optimal. Explain a case where width 2 differs from greedy.

Keep a deliberately wrong accumulated-score or branch-state version, its first
observed failure, and a controlled repair with the tape/settings held fixed.
Record source identities, prompt, weights/logits, scores, retained IDs, stop
reasons, parent/child cache calls and assistance. A copied public outcome or a
claim that a shared object is always wrong cannot replace that evidence.

## Explain the limits

Report which arrays and positions were checked, maximum absolute logit discrepancy, chosen tolerance and the exact checkpoint digest. Describe whether the evidence isolates position handling, row order, model identity or another mechanism. If several causes remain possible, name the next discriminating experiment instead of declaring a cause from shapes alone.

{{practice:r08-evidence}}

## Repair and export

The hint ladder is: locate the first divergent position; locate the first divergent block or component; compare a smaller explicit prefix under fixed sampling. No replacement project implementation is supplied. You may choose the optional critique prompt and your own LLM account, but its opinion remains separate from numeric results and declared assistance.

Export the runnable learner project ZIP and a REPORT.md containing your chosen prompts, original failing evidence, controlled repair and limits. Unzip into a fresh directory and rerun the checks. The artifact must include your readable runtime and project code, not just a transcript of generated letters. For CLI export, put optional tree data in work/data.json and the report in work/REPORT.md; those names are already allowlisted. Browser project export preserves code and recorded workspace history; retain a separate report or custom experiment file explicitly rather than assuming every local file is included. A passing fixture run establishes the stated numeric agreement; it establishes neither language quality nor human learning.

## Finish on the pinned trained model

The pocket project above is the small numerical slice. It does not replace the
required trained end product. Continue with [Finish the trained runtime](trained.html),
whose offline source is TRAINED.md. Adapt the same learned loader, tokenizer,
block/cache and generation mechanisms to the single bundled Stories260K profile.
It supplies a readable binary/layout/BPE/GQA contract and staged checks, never a
completed trained decoder or capstone. Preserve the pocket code and its history.

Create trained.mjs and trained-project.mjs in the terminal workspace, run
`node lab.mjs check trained ./work --help-used TEXT`, and export using the same lab.
The browser workbench/export contains earlier pocket drafts; the trained CLI route
keeps final code and prerequisite/runtime dependencies. Your final handoff needs
actual trained generation, early consumer delivery, a fresh cache investigation,
bounded beam output, first failure/repair, declared help and fresh standalone replay.
The longer final reference guide is deliberate: implementation and diagnosis,
rather than an additional numbered lesson, carry this adaptation. Reading and
project times have not been measured.

import {readFileSync,existsSync} from 'node:fs';
import {pathToFileURL} from 'node:url';
import {check} from './checks.mjs';
const root=new URL('./',import.meta.url),config=JSON.parse(readFileSync(new URL('course.json',root),'utf8'));
process.on('message',async data=>{
 try{

`courses/small-llm-runtime/numeric.mjs`:

```mjs
// Supplied standalone CPU backend. No tensor-course code or external package.
export function finiteVector(x,n,label='vector') {
 if(!Array.isArray(x) || x.length!==n || Array.from(x).some(v=>!Number.isFinite(v))) throw new Error(`${label} must contain ${n} finite numbers`);
 return x;
}
export const zeros=n=>Array(n).fill(0);
export const dot=(a,b)=>{finiteVector(b,a.length);return a.reduce((s,v,i)=>s+v*b[i],0);};
export function linear(x,weight) {
 const [m,n]=weight.shape; finiteVector(x,m,'linear input'); finiteVector(weight.data,m*n,'weight');
 const out=zeros(n);
 for(let j=0;j<n;j++) for(let i=0;i<m;i++) out[j]+=x[i]*weight.data[i*n+j];
 return out;
}
export const add=(a,b)=>{finiteVector(b,a.length);return a.map((v,i)=>v+b[i]);};
export const multiply=(a,b)=>{finiteVector(b,a.length);return a.map((v,i)=>v*b[i]);};
export const row=(weight,i)=>weight.data.slice(i*weight.shape[1],(i+1)*weight.shape[1]);

// Practice answers are typed in plain words. A boolean accepts yes/no/true/false, a number
// accepts a plain number, a list accepts comma- or space-separated numbers (brackets optional)
// and a word answer is compared without case or surrounding quotes. Anything else is a
// format problem the learner can correct; it is not recorded or graded.
export function answerFormat(expected){
 if(typeof expected==="boolean")return "Answer yes or no.";
 if(typeof expected==="number")return "Answer with a number.";
 if(Array.isArray(expected))return "Answer with a list of numbers, such as 1, 2, 3.";
 return "Answer with one word.";
}
// Short form for the answer box label, e.g. "Your answer (yes or no)".
export const answerLabel=expected=>typeof expected==="boolean"?"yes or no":typeof expected==="number"?"a number":Array.isArray(expected)?"numbers separated by commas":"one word";
export function parseAnswer(text,expected){
 const raw=String(text??"").trim(),problem=()=>({ok:false,hint:`That answer could not be read. ${answerFormat(expected)} Nothing was recorded; correct it and commit again.`});
 if(!raw)return problem();
 const number=/^[-+]?(\d+(\.\d*)?|\.\d+)(e[-+]?\d+)?$/i;
 if(typeof expected==="boolean"){const word=raw.toLowerCase();if(word==="yes"||word==="true")return {ok:true,value:true};if(word==="no"||word==="false")return {ok:true,value:false};return problem();}
 if(typeof expected==="number")return number.test(raw)?{ok:true,value:Number(raw)}:problem();
 if(Array.isArray(expected)){const parts=raw.replace(/^\[|\]$/g,"").split(/[\s,]+/).filter(Boolean);return parts.length&&parts.every(p=>number.test(p))?{ok:true,value:parts.map(Number)}:problem();}
 const word=raw.replace(/^["']+|["']+$/g,"").trim().toLowerCase();
 return word&&!/\s/.test(word)?{ok:true,value:word}:problem();
}
export const describeAnswer=value=>typeof value==="boolean"?(value?"yes":"no"):Array.isArray(value)?value.join(", "):String(value);

export function rmsNorm(x,g,epsilon=CONFIG.epsilon) {

 if(!(epsilon>0) || !Number.isFinite(epsilon)) throw new Error('invalid normalization epsilon');

export function rotary(x,position,base=CONFIG.ropeBase) {
 if(x.length%2 || !Number.isSafeInteger(position) || position<0 || !(base>0)) throw new Error('rotary needs even width and nonnegative integer position');
 const out=[...x];
 for(let j=0;j<x.length;j+=2) { const theta=position/(base**(j/x.length)),c=Math.cos(theta),s=Math.sin(theta); out[j]=x[j]*c-x[j+1]*s;out[j+1]=x[j]*s+x[j+1]*c; }
 return out;
}
export function attention(query,keys,values) {
 if(!keys.length || keys.length!==values.length) throw new Error('attention needs matching nonempty key/value rows');
 keys.forEach(k=>finiteVector(k,query.length)); values.forEach(v=>finiteVector(v,query.length));
 const p=softmax(keys.map(k=>dot(query,k)/Math.sqrt(query.length)));
 return query.map((_,i)=>p.reduce((s,v,j)=>s+v*values[j][i],0));
}
function ropeHeads(x,pos,c) {
 const h=c.dim/c.heads, out=[];
 for(let head=0;head<c.heads;head++) out.push(...rotary(x.slice(head*h,(head+1)*h),pos,c.ropeBase));
 return out;
}
function attendHeads(q,ks,vs,c) {
 const h=c.dim/c.heads,out=[];
 for(let head=0;head<c.heads;head++) { const slice=x=>x.slice(head*h,(head+1)*h);out.push(...attention(slice(q),ks.map(slice),vs.map(slice))); }
 return out;
}
const weight=(m,l,n)=>m.weights[`layers.${l}.${n}`];
export function forward(m,tokens) {
 validIds(tokens);
 const c=m.config;
 if(tokens.length>c.maxContext) throw new Error('context limit exceeded');
 let xs=tokens.map(t=>row(m.weights.embedding,t));const layers=[];
 for(let l=0;l<c.layers;l++) {
   const norm=xs.map(x=>rmsNorm(x,weight(m,l,'attnNorm').data,c.epsilon));
   const qs=norm.map((x,p)=>ropeHeads(linear(x,weight(m,l,'wq')),p,c));
   const keys=norm.map((x,p)=>ropeHeads(linear(x,weight(m,l,'wk')),p,c)),values=norm.map(x=>linear(x,weight(m,l,'wv')));
   xs=xs.map((x,p)=>add(x,linear(attendHeads(qs[p],keys.slice(0,p+1),values.slice(0,p+1),c),weight(m,l,'wo'))));
   xs=xs.map(x=>add(x,mlp(rmsNorm(x,weight(m,l,'ffnNorm').data,c.epsilon),weight(m,l,'w1'),weight(m,l,'w2'),weight(m,l,'w3'))));
   layers.push({keys,values});
 }

function validIds(ids,empty=false) {
 if(!Array.isArray(ids) || (!empty && !ids.length) || ids.some(i=>!Number.isInteger(i) || i<0 || i>=32)) throw new Error('tokens must be valid integer IDs; prompt must be nonempty');
}
export function softmax(xs) {
 if(!Array.isArray(xs)||!xs.length||Array.from(xs).some(x=>typeof x!=='number'||(x!==-Infinity&&!Number.isFinite(x)))||xs.every(x=>x===-Infinity))throw new Error('softmax needs numeric scores and at least one finite unmasked value');
 const max=Math.max(...xs), ex=xs.map(v=>Math.exp(v-max)), sum=ex.reduce((a,b)=>a+b,0);
 return ex.map(v=>v/sum);
}
export function rmsNorm(x,g,epsilon=CONFIG.epsilon) {
 finiteVector(x,g.length); finiteVector(g,x.length);
 if(!(epsilon>0) || !Number.isFinite(epsilon)) throw new Error('invalid normalization epsilon');
 if(!x.length)throw new Error('normalization needs a nonempty vector');
 const peak=Math.max(...x.map(Math.abs));if(peak===0)return x.map(()=>0);
 const mean=x.reduce((s,v)=>s+(v/peak)**2,0)/x.length,denominator=Math.hypot(peak*Math.sqrt(mean),Math.sqrt(epsilon));
 return x.map((v,i)=>(v/denominator)*g[i]);
}
export function silu(x) { if(!Number.isFinite(x)) throw new Error('SiLU input must be finite'); return x/(1+Math.exp(-x)); }
export function mlp(x,w1,w2,w3) { return linear(multiply(linear(x,w1).map(silu),linear(x,w3)),w2); }
export function rotary(x,position,base=CONFIG.ropeBase) {
 if(x.length%2 || !Number.isSafeInteger(position) || position<0 || !(base>0)) throw new Error('rotary needs even width and nonnegative integer position');
 const out=[...x];
 for(let j=0;j<x.length;j+=2) { const theta=position/(base**(j/x.length)),c=Math.cos(theta),s=Math.sin(theta); out[j]=x[j]*c-x[j+1]*s;out[j+1]=x[j]*s+x[j+1]*c; }
 return out;
}
export function attention(query,keys,values) {
 if(!keys.length || keys.length!==values.length) throw new Error('attention needs matching nonempty key/value rows');
 keys.forEach(k=>finiteVector(k,query.length)); values.forEach(v=>finiteVector(v,query.length));
 const p=softmax(keys.map(k=>dot(query,k)/Math.sqrt(query.length)));
 return query.map((_,i)=>p.reduce((s,v,j)=>s+v*values[j][i],0));
}
function ropeHeads(x,pos,c) {
 const h=c.dim/c.heads, out=[];
 for(let head=0;head<c.heads;head++) out.push(...rotary(x.slice(head*h,(head+1)*h),pos,c.ropeBase));
 return out;
}
function attendHeads(q,ks,vs,c) {
 const h=c.dim/c.heads,out=[];
 for(let head=0;head<c.heads;head++) { const slice=x=>x.slice(head*h,(head+1)*h);out.push(...attention(slice(q),ks.map(slice),vs.map(slice))); }
 return out;
}
const weight=(m,l,n)=>m.weights[`layers.${l}.${n}`];
export function forward(m,tokens) {
 validIds(tokens);
 const c=m.config;
 if(tokens.length>c.maxContext) throw new Error('context limit exceeded');
 let xs=tokens.map(t=>row(m.weights.embedding,t));const layers=[];
 for(let l=0;l<c.layers;l++) {
   const norm=xs.map(x=>rmsNorm(x,weight(m,l,'attnNorm').data,c.epsilon));
   const qs=norm.map((x,p)=>ropeHeads(linear(x,weight(m,l,'wq')),p,c));
   const keys=norm.map((x,p)=>ropeHeads(linear(x,weight(m,l,'wk')),p,c)),values=norm.map(x=>linear(x,weight(m,l,'wv')));
   xs=xs.map((x,p)=>add(x,linear(attendHeads(qs[p],keys.slice(0,p+1),values.slice(0,p+1),c),weight(m,l,'wo'))));
   xs=xs.map(x=>add(x,mlp(rmsNorm(x,weight(m,l,'ffnNorm').data,c.epsilon),weight(m,l,'w1'),weight(m,l,'w2'),weight(m,l,'w3'))));
   layers.push({keys,values});
 }
 return {logits:xs.map(x=>linear(rmsNorm(x,m.weights.finalNorm.data,c.epsilon),m.weights.lmHead)),cache:{format:'pocket-cache-v1',fingerprint:m.fingerprint,position:tokens.length,layers}};
}
export function prefill(m,tokens) { const {logits,cache}=forward(m,tokens);return {logits:logits.at(-1),cache}; }
function validCache(m,cache) {
 const c=m.config;
 if(cache?.format!=='pocket-cache-v1' || cache.fingerprint!==m.fingerprint || !Number.isSafeInteger(cache.position) || cache.position<1 || cache.position>=c.maxContext || cache.layers?.length!==c.layers) throw new Error('invalid, full or foreign cache');
 cache.layers.forEach(layer=>{
   if(layer.keys?.length!==cache.position || layer.values?.length!==cache.position) throw new Error('cache length does not match position');
   layer.keys.forEach(k=>finiteVector(k,c.dim,'cache key'));layer.values.forEach(v=>finiteVector(v,c.dim,'cache value'));
 });
}
export function decodeStep(m,token,cache) {
 validIds([token]);validCache(m,cache);
 const c=m.config,position=cache.position,layers=[];let x=row(m.weights.embedding,token);
 for(let l=0;l<c.layers;l++) {
   const z=rmsNorm(x,weight(m,l,'attnNorm').data,c.epsilon),q=ropeHeads(linear(z,weight(m,l,'wq')),position,c);
   const keys=[...cache.layers[l].keys.map(k=>[...k]),ropeHeads(linear(z,weight(m,l,'wk')),position,c)], values=[...cache.layers[l].values.map(v=>[...v]),linear(z,weight(m,l,'wv'))];
   x=add(x,linear(attendHeads(q,keys,values,c),weight(m,l,'wo')));
   x=add(x,mlp(rmsNorm(x,weight(m,l,'ffnNorm').data,c.epsilon),weight(m,l,'w1'),weight(m,l,'w2'),weight(m,l,'w3')));
   layers.push({keys,values});
 }
 return {logits:linear(rmsNorm(x,m.weights.finalNorm.data,c.epsilon),m.weights.lmHead),cache:{format:'pocket-cache-v1',fingerprint:m.fingerprint,position:position+1,layers}};
}
export function rng(seed) {
 if(!Number.isSafeInteger(seed) || seed<0 || seed>0xffffffff) throw new Error('seed must be an unsigned 32-bit integer');
 let state=seed>>>0;
 return ()=>{state=(Math.imul(state,1664525)+1013904223)>>>0;return state/4294967296;};
}
export function sample(logits,{temperature=1,topK=logits.length}={},random=Math.random) {
 finiteVector(logits,32,'sampling logits');
 if(!Number.isFinite(temperature) || temperature<0 || !Number.isInteger(topK) || topK<1 || topK>logits.length) throw new Error('invalid sampling controls');
 const ranked=logits.map((v,i)=>({v,i})).sort((a,b)=>b.v-a.v || a.i-b.i).slice(0,topK);
 if(temperature===0) return ranked[0].i;
 const ps=softmax(ranked.map(t=>(t.v-ranked[0].v)/temperature)),u=random();
 if(!Number.isFinite(u) || u<0 || u>=1) throw new Error('random draw must be in [0,1)');
 let total=0;
 for(let j=0;j<ps.length;j++){total+=ps[j];if(u<total) return ranked[j].i;}
 return ranked.at(-1).i;
}
export function generate(...args){throw new Error("TODO module 07: implement the current runtime layer; supplied support completes earlier dependencies only.");}

export function decodeStep(m,token,cache) {

 const c=m.config,position=cache.position,layers=[];let x=row(m.weights.embedding,token);
 for(let l=0;l<c.layers;l++) {
   const z=rmsNorm(x,weight(m,l,'attnNorm').data,c.epsilon),q=ropeHeads(linear(z,weight(m,l,'wq')),position,c);
   const keys=[...cache.layers[l].keys.map(k=>[...k]),ropeHeads(linear(z,weight(m,l,'wk')),position,c)], values=[...cache.layers[l].values.map(v=>[...v]),linear(z,weight(m,l,'wv'))];
   x=add(x,linear(attendHeads(q,keys,values,c),weight(m,l,'wo')));
   x=add(x,mlp(rmsNorm(x,weight(m,l,'ffnNorm').data,c.epsilon),weight(m,l,'w1'),weight(m,l,'w2'),weight(m,l,'w3')));
   layers.push({keys,values});
 }
 return {logits:linear(rmsNorm(x,m.weights.finalNorm.data,c.epsilon),m.weights.lmHead),cache:{format:'pocket-cache-v1',fingerprint:m.fingerprint,position:position+1,layers}};
}
export function rng(seed) {
 if(!Number.isSafeInteger(seed) || seed<0 || seed>0xffffffff) throw new Error('seed must be an unsigned 32-bit integer');
 let state=seed>>>0;
 return ()=>{state=(Math.imul(state,1664525)+1013904223)>>>0;return state/4294967296;};
}
export function sample(logits,{temperature=1,topK=logits.length}={},random=Math.random) {
 finiteVector(logits,32,'sampling logits');
 if(!Number.isFinite(temperature) || temperature<0 || !Number.isInteger(topK) || topK<1 || topK>logits.length) throw new Error('invalid sampling controls');
 const ranked=logits.map((v,i)=>({v,i})).sort((a,b)=>b.v-a.v || a.i-b.i).slice(0,topK);
 if(temperature===0) return ranked[0].i;
 const ps=softmax(ranked.map(t=>(t.v-ranked[0].v)/temperature)),u=random();
 if(!Number.isFinite(u) || u<0 || u>=1) throw new Error('random draw must be in [0,1)');
 let total=0;
 for(let j=0;j<ps.length;j++){total+=ps[j];if(u<total) return ranked[j].i;}
 return ranked.at(-1).i;
}
export function generate(m,prompt,{maxNewTokens=8,seed=1,temperature=1,topK=32}={}) {
 validIds(prompt);
 if(!Number.isInteger(maxNewTokens) || maxNewTokens<0 || prompt.length>m.config.maxContext) throw new Error('invalid generation limit');
 if(!Number.isFinite(temperature)||temperature<0||!Number.isInteger(topK)||topK<1||topK>32)throw new Error('invalid sampling controls');
 const random=rng(seed),tokens=[...prompt],generated=[],trace=[];
 if(maxNewTokens===0) return {tokens,generated,text:'',stop:'limit',trace};
 if(prompt.length===m.config.maxContext) return {tokens,generated,text:'',stop:'context',trace};
 let state=prefill(m,prompt),stop='limit';
 for(let i=0;i<maxNewTokens;i++) {
   const token=sample(state.logits,{temperature,topK},random);generated.push(token);tokens.push(token);trace.push({position:state.cache.position,token});
   if(token===0) {stop='eos';break;}
   if(tokens.length===m.config.maxContext) {stop='context';break;}
   if(i+1<maxNewTokens) state=decodeStep(m,token,state.cache);
 }
 return {tokens,generated,text:decode(generated),stop,trace};
}

`courses/small-llm-runtime/render.mjs`:

```mjs
export const escape=s=>String(s).replace(/[&<>"']/g,c=>({'&':'&amp;','<':'&lt;','>':'&gt;','"':'&quot;',"'":'&#39;'}[c]));
const inline=s=>escape(s).replace(/`([^`]+)`/g,'<code>$1</code>').replace(/\*\*([^*]+)\*\*/g,'<strong>$1</strong>');
export function renderMarkdown(md){
 let code=false,list=false,parts=[];
 for(const line of md.split('\n')){
   if(line.startsWith('```')){if(list){parts.push('</ul>');list=false;}parts.push(code?'</code></pre>':'<pre><code>');code=!code;continue;}
   if(code){parts.push(escape(line)+'\n');continue;}
   if(/^[-*] /.test(line)){if(!list){parts.push('<ul>');list=true;}parts.push('<li>'+inline(line.slice(2))+'</li>');continue;}
   if(list){parts.push('</ul>');list=false;}
   if(!line.trim())continue;
   if(/^#{1,3} /.test(line)){const n=line.indexOf(' ');parts.push(`<h${n}>${inline(line.slice(n+1))}</h${n}>`);continue;}
   const m=line.match(/^\{\{practice:([a-z0-9-]+)\}\}$/);if(m){parts.push(`<div class="practice" data-practice="${m[1]}"></div>`);continue;}
   parts.push('<p>'+inline(line)+'</p>');
 }
 if(list)parts.push('</ul>');if(code)throw new Error('unclosed code fence');return parts.join('\n');
}

import {CONFIG,VOCAB} from './spec.mjs';

const same=(a,b)=>{
  if(a===b)return true;
  if(!a||!b||typeof a!=='object'||typeof b!=='object'||Array.isArray(a)!==Array.isArray(b))return false;
  if(Array.isArray(a))return a.length===b.length&&Array.from(a).every((v,i)=>same(v,b[i]));
  const ak=Object.keys(a).sort(),bk=Object.keys(b).sort();
  return same(ak,bk)&&ak.every(k=>same(a[k],b[k]));
};
const insist=(condition,message)=>{if(!condition)throw new Error('stream: '+message);};
const decode=ids=>ids.map(id=>id===0?'':id===1?'\ufffd':VOCAB[id]).join('');
const options=(maxNewTokens,temperature=0,topK=1,seed=1)=>({maxNewTokens,seed,temperature,topK});

  {id:'EOS-at-token-limit',prompt:[4,5],options:options(1),tapes:[{0:1}],ids:[0],stop:'eos'},
  {id:'EOS-at-context-and-token-limit',prompt:Array(31).fill(4),options:options(1),tapes:[{0:1}],ids:[0],stop:'eos'},
  {id:'late-decode-error',prompt:[4,5],options:options(3),tapes:[{6:1}],ids:[6],error:true},
  {id:'invalid-empty-prompt',prompt:[],options:options(1),tapes:[],ids:[],invalid:true},

  {id:'invalid-seed',prompt:[4],options:{...options(1),seed:4294967296},tapes:[],ids:[],invalid:true},
