function samplingOptionsMessage(controls,expected){
 const kind=value=>value===null?'null':typeof value==='number'?String(value):typeof value==='undefined'?'missing':typeof value;
 try{const keys=controls&&typeof controls==='object'?Object.keys(controls).sort():[];const observed=keys.slice(0,8).map(key=>key.slice(0,40));return `sample input/controls: expected only {temperature:${expected.temperature},topK:${expected.topK}}; observed keys ${JSON.stringify(observed)}${keys.length>8?' (truncated)':''}, temperature=${kind(controls?.temperature)}, topK=${kind(controls?.topK)}. Pass resolved {temperature,topK}; seed belongs to rng(seed), maxNewTokens to generation. Extra-field values are not printed.`;}catch{return 'sample input/controls: unreadable sampling options; pass only resolved {temperature,topK}, not seed or maxNewTokens';}
}
function tapeRun(api,project,model,s) {
  insist(typeof project.streamGenerate==='function','export streamGenerate(runtime,model,prompt,options) from your project.mjs; lesson08 defines the iterator');
  const calls=[],events=[],counter={prefill:0,decode:0,sample:0,draw:0,rng:0};
  const violations=[];
  const guard=(condition,message)=>{if(!condition){violations.push(message);insist(false,message);}};
  const noViolations=()=>insist(!violations.length,'retained checker violation: '+violations[0]);
  let delivered=0,terminal=false;
  const sentinel=Object.assign(new Error('original later decode failure'),{code:'TAPE_E1'});
  const logits=index=>{const scores=Array(32).fill(-1000);for(const [id,score]of Object.entries(s.tapes[index]??{}))scores[Number(id)]=score;return scores;};
  const note=name=>{calls.push(name);guard(!terminal,'runtime work after a terminal token');};
  const runtime={
    prefill(m,p){note('prefill');counter.prefill++;guard(counter.prefill===1&&same(p,s.prompt)&&m===model,'prefill input/count');return {logits:logits(0),cache:{position:p.length,tape:0}};},
    decodeStep(m,token,cache){note('decodeStep');guard(counter.decode<delivered,'decode before consumer received its preceding token');counter.decode++;guard(m===model&&token===s.ids[counter.decode-1]&&cache.tape===counter.decode-1&&cache.position===s.prompt.length+counter.decode-1,'decode token/cache alignment');if(s.error)throw sentinel;return {logits:logits(counter.decode),cache:{position:cache.position+1,tape:counter.decode}};},
    sample(scores,controls,random){note('sample');guard(counter.sample<=delivered,'sample prefetched before consumer receipt');guard(same(scores,logits(counter.sample)),'sample input/controls: logits differ from the current sampling step');const expected={temperature:s.options.temperature,topK:s.options.topK},matches=same(controls,expected);guard(matches,matches?'':samplingOptionsMessage(controls,expected));counter.sample++;return api.sample(scores,controls,random);},
    rng(seed){note('rng');counter.rng++;guard(counter.rng===1&&seed===s.options.seed,'per-stream RNG creation');const random=api.rng(seed);return ()=>{note('draw');counter.draw++;return random();};},
    decode:api.decode,
    generate(){guard(false,'complete-generate shortcut cannot prove incremental delivery');},
  };
  const prompt=[...s.prompt],before=JSON.stringify(prompt),modelBefore=JSON.stringify(model);
  const iterator=project.streamGenerate(runtime,model,prompt,{...s.options});
  insist(iterator&&typeof iterator.next==='function'&&typeof iterator[Symbol.asyncIterator]==='function','return an async iterator');
  insist(!calls.length,'construction must be lazy');
  const next=async()=>{calls.push('pull');try{const value=await iterator.next();calls.push(value.done?'done':'recv');return value;}finally{noViolations();}};
  const unchanged=()=>{noViolations();insist(JSON.stringify(prompt)===before,'caller prompt changed');insist(JSON.stringify(model)===modelBefore,'caller model changed');};
  const endAfterError=async()=>{const count=calls.length;let end,rejected=false;try{end=await iterator.next();}catch{rejected=true;}insist(rejected||end?.done,'event after runtime or validation error');insist(calls.length===count,'post-error runtime work');unchanged();};
  const finish=async()=>{
    if(s.invalid){let error;try{await next();}catch(e){error=e;}insist(error,'invalid prompt/options accepted');insist(counter.prefill+counter.decode+counter.sample+counter.rng+counter.draw===0,'work before invalid-input rejection');await endAfterError();return {id:s.id,calls,counter,events,rejected:true};}
    for(let index=0;index<s.ids.length;index++) {
      const step=await next(),expected={type:'token',index,position:s.prompt.length+index,token:s.ids[index]};
      insist(!step.done&&same(step.value,expected),'token order/index/position for '+s.id);
      events.push(step.value);delivered++;
      terminal=!s.error&&(s.ids[index]===0||s.prompt.length+delivered===CONFIG.maxContext||delivered===s.options.maxNewTokens);
    }
    if(s.error){let error;try{await next();}catch(e){error=e;}insist(error===sentinel,'later failure must reject with original error and retain its delivered prefix');await endAfterError();return {id:s.id,calls,counter,events,rejected:true};}
    const completed=await next(),expected=result(s.prompt,s.ids,s.stop);
    insist(!completed.done&&same(completed.value,{type:'complete',result:expected}),'complete reconstruction/stop/text for '+s.id);
    const count=JSON.stringify(counter);
    for(let i=0;i<2;i++)insist((await next()).done,'event after completion');
    insist(JSON.stringify(counter)===count,'work after completion');
    insist(counter.prefill===(s.ids.length?1:0)&&counter.decode===Math.max(0,s.ids.length-1)&&counter.sample===s.ids.length,'prefill/decode/sample counts');
    insist(counter.draw===(s.options.temperature>0?s.ids.length:0),'RNG draw count');
    insist(s.ids.length?counter.rng<=1:counter.rng===0,'RNG work for empty generation');
    unchanged();
    return {id:s.id,calls,counter,events,result:completed.value.result};
  };
  return {iterator,finish};
}

export async function checkStreamDelivery(api,project,model) {
  const records=[];
  for(const s of scenarios)records.push(await tapeRun(api,project,model,s).finish());
  const seeded=scenarios.find(s=>s.id==='seeded-two-way-tie');
  records.push(await tapeRun(api,project,model,{...seeded,id:'seeded-repeat'}).finish());
  records.push(...await Promise.all(['A','B'].map(id=>tapeRun(api,project,model,{...seeded,id:'seeded-interleave-'+id}).finish())));
  return records;
}

export async function checkStreamRuntime(api,project,model) {
  insist(typeof project.streamGenerate==='function','create the capstone streamGenerate export');
  const records=[];
  for(const [prompt,opts]of [[[4,5],options(3,1,2)],[[4],options(2)],[[4,5],options(0,1,2)],[Array(32).fill(4),options(1)],[Array(31).fill(4),options(4)],[Array(32).fill(4),options(0)]]) {
    let delivered=0,prefills=0,decodes=0,samples=0;
    const violations=[];
    const guard=(condition,message)=>{if(!condition){violations.push(message);insist(false,message);}};
    const noViolations=()=>insist(!violations.length,'retained checker violation: '+violations[0]);
    const runtime={...api,prefill(...args){prefills++;return api.prefill(...args);},decodeStep(...args){guard(decodes<delivered,'actual runtime decode before first consumer receipt');decodes++;return api.decodeStep(...args);},sample(...args){guard(samples<=delivered,'actual runtime sample prefetch');samples++;return api.sample(...args);},generate(){guard(false,'buffered generate shortcut');}};
    const events=[];let completed;
    const iterator=project.streamGenerate(runtime,model,[...prompt],opts);
    const maxTokens=Math.min(opts.maxNewTokens,model.config.maxContext-prompt.length);
    for(let pull=0;pull<maxTokens+2;pull++) {
      const step=await iterator.next();noViolations();if(step.done)break;
      const event=step.value;
      if(event.type==='token'){insist(!completed&&delivered<maxTokens&&event.index===delivered&&event.position===prompt.length+delivered,'actual token sequence');delivered++;events.push(event);continue;}
      insist(event.type==='complete'&&!completed,'exactly one actual complete event');completed=event.result;
    }
    insist((await iterator.next()).done&&(await iterator.next()).done,'actual iterator must finish');
    noViolations();
    insist(completed&&same(completed,api.generate(model,prompt,opts)),'actual stream/generate result parity');
    insist(same(events.map(e=>e.token),completed.generated),'actual events/final IDs differ');
    insist(prefills===(delivered?1:0)&&decodes===Math.max(0,delivered-1)&&samples===delivered,'actual runtime call counts');
    records.push({prompt,options:opts,events,result:completed,calls:{prefills,decodes,samples}});
  }
  return records;
}

// Finite disclosed checks for learner-owned trained.mjs and trained-project.mjs.
// No author/runtime solution is imported. Goldens come from the independent scalar path.
const MODEL_SHA='b0a507e7ad0f626624f17112325e66691f9076d622e1d3274d103d00299f2696';
const TOKEN_SHA='037cb335abb25d1fa9e8ecae30ed2a3a8ace9302862ebcdc05d51a6bbb10c312';
const fail=message=>{throw new Error(message);};
const must=(value,message)=>{if(!value)fail(message);};
const finite=x=>typeof x==='number'&&Number.isFinite(x);
function equal(a,b,label='value'){
 if(Array.isArray(b)){must(Array.isArray(a)&&a.length===b.length,`${label}: array length/type differs`);for(let i=0;i<b.length;i++){must(i in a,`${label}: missing element${i}`);equal(a[i],b[i],`${label}[${i}]`);}return;}
 if(b&&typeof b==='object'){must(a&&typeof a==='object'&&!Array.isArray(a),`${label}: object required`);for(const k of Object.keys(b))equal(a[k],b[k],`${label}.${k}`);return;}
 must(a===b,`${label}: expected ${JSON.stringify(b)}, got ${JSON.stringify(a)}`);
}
function close(a,b,label){must(Array.isArray(a)&&a.length===b.length,`${label}: vector length/type differs`);let maximum=0;for(let i=0;i<b.length;i++){const error=Math.abs(a[i]-b[i]),limit=1e-10+1e-10*Math.max(Math.abs(a[i]),Math.abs(b[i]));must(finite(a[i])&&error<=limit,`${label}[${i}]: observed${a[i]}, expected${b[i]}, error${error}, limit${limit}`);maximum=Math.max(maximum,error);}return maximum;}
async function reject(fn,label){let rejected=false;try{await fn();}catch{rejected=true;}must(rejected,label+' must reject');}
const required=(object,key,file='trained.mjs')=>{must(typeof object?.[key]==='function',`Export ${key} from work/${file}; TRAINED.md gives the interface`);return object[key];};
const sameIds=(a,b)=>Array.isArray(a)&&a.length===b.length&&b.every((x,i)=>a[i]===x);
const briefIds=x=>{const t=JSON.stringify(x)??String(x);return t.length>80?t.slice(0,77)+'...':t;};
const load=(a,f)=>required(a,'loadModel')(f.modelBytes,f.tokenizerBytes);
function view(a,m){return {forward:(model,prompt)=>required(a,'forward')(model,prompt),encode:(text,options)=>required(a,'encode')(m,text,options),prefill:(model,prompt)=>required(a,'prefill')(model,prompt),decodeStep:(model,t,c)=>required(a,'decodeStep')(model,t,c),generate:(model,prompt,options)=>required(a,'generate')(model,prompt,options),decode:ids=>required(a,'decode')(m,ids),sample:(logits,options,random)=>required(a,'sample')(logits,options,random),rng:seed=>required(a,'rng')(seed)};}
const clone=x=>JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(x));
const trace=(prompt,ids)=>ids.map((token,index)=>({position:prompt.length+index,token}));
function componentCache(m,position){const rows=()=>Array.from({length:position},()=>Object.freeze(Array(32).fill(0)));return Object.freeze({format:'stories260k-cache-v1',fingerprint:m.fingerprint,tokenizerFingerprint:m.tokenizerFingerprint,position,layers:Object.freeze(Array.from({length:5},()=>Object.freeze({keys:Object.freeze(rows()),values:Object.freeze(rows())})))});}
function retainBoundaryFailures(facade,violations){for(const key of ['prefill','decodeStep']){const call=facade[key];facade[key]=(...args)=>{try{return call(...args);}catch(error){violations.push(String(error?.message??error));throw error;}};}return facade;}
function observeRuntime(facade,onCall){
 for(const [name,call]of Object.entries(facade)){
  if(typeof call!=='function')continue;
  facade[name]=(...args)=>{onCall(name);const result=call(...args);if(name!=='rng'||typeof result!=='function')return result;return(...drawArgs)=>{onCall('rng.draw');return result(...drawArgs);};};
 }
 return facade;
}
function generationShape(result,prompt){must(result&&typeof result==='object','generation object required');must(Array.isArray(result.generated),'generated IDs required');must(typeof result.text==='string','generation text required');must(['eos','context','limit'].includes(result.stop),'declared stop required');equal(result.tokens,[...prompt,...result.generated],'complete tokens');equal(result.trace,trace(prompt,result.generated),'trace');}

 return {pass:results.every(x=>x.pass),passed:results.filter(x=>x.pass).length,total:results.length,results};
}

```mjs
// Supplied local launcher. It loads and calls the learner's code, not an author decoder.
import {readFileSync,existsSync} from 'node:fs';
import {resolve,join} from 'node:path';
import {pathToFileURL} from 'node:url';
const root=new URL('./',import.meta.url);
export async function loadWork(directory){
 const work=resolve(directory),api=await import(pathToFileURL(join(work,'trained.mjs')).href);
 const project=existsSync(join(work,'trained-project.mjs'))?await import(pathToFileURL(join(work,'trained-project.mjs')).href):{};
 if(typeof api.loadModel!=='function')throw new Error('Export loadModel from work/trained.mjs; read TRAINED.md');
 const model=await api.loadModel(readFileSync(new URL('fixtures/trained/stories260K.bin',root)),readFileSync(new URL('fixtures/trained/tok512.bin',root)));
 const runtime={prefill:(m,p)=>api.prefill(m,p),decodeStep:(m,t,c)=>api.decodeStep(m,t,c),forward:(m,p)=>api.forward(m,p),generate:(m,p,o)=>api.generate(m,p,o),encode:(text,options)=>api.encode(model,text,options),decode:ids=>api.decode(model,ids),rng:seed=>api.rng(seed),sample:(logits,options,random)=>api.sample(logits,options,random)};
 return {work,api,project,model,runtime};
}
const write=object=>new Promise((resolveWrite,reject)=>process.stdout.write(JSON.stringify(object)+'\n',error=>error?reject(error):resolveWrite()));
async function main(){
 const [directory,text,...flags]=process.argv.slice(2);if(directory===undefined||text===undefined||flags.length%2)throw new Error('Usage: node trained-run.mjs WORK PROMPT [--mode generate|stream|beam] [--max-new-tokens N] [--seed N] [--temperature N] [--top-k N] [--beam-width N]');
 const options={maxNewTokens:16,seed:1,temperature:1,topK:512};let mode='generate',beamWidth=2;const seen=new Set();
 for(let i=0;i<flags.length;i+=2){const flag=flags[i],value=flags[i+1];if(seen.has(flag))throw new Error('duplicate flag '+flag);seen.add(flag);if(flag==='--mode'){if(!['generate','stream','beam'].includes(value))throw new Error('mode must be generate, stream or beam');mode=value;continue;}const number=Number(value);if(value.trim()===''||!Number.isFinite(number))throw new Error('numeric flag required '+flag);if(flag==='--max-new-tokens')options.maxNewTokens=number;else if(flag==='--seed')options.seed=number;else if(flag==='--temperature')options.temperature=number;else if(flag==='--top-k')options.topK=number;else if(flag==='--beam-width')beamWidth=number;else throw new Error('unknown flag '+flag);}
 if(!Number.isInteger(options.maxNewTokens)||options.maxNewTokens<0||options.maxNewTokens>512||!Number.isSafeInteger(options.seed)||options.seed<0||options.seed>0xffffffff||options.temperature<0||!Number.isInteger(options.topK)||options.topK<1||options.topK>512)throw new Error('invalid generation controls; read TRAINED.md');
 if(mode==='beam'&&(!Number.isInteger(beamWidth)||beamWidth<1||beamWidth>4||options.maxNewTokens<1||options.maxNewTokens>4))throw new Error('beam width and token budget must be integers1..4; specify --max-new-tokens');
 if(mode==='beam'&&['--seed','--temperature','--top-k'].some(flag=>seen.has(flag)))throw new Error('Beam uses full-vocabulary temperature1 scores and no RNG; omit sampling flags.');
 if(mode!=='beam'&&seen.has('--beam-width'))throw new Error('--beam-width applies only to --mode beam.');
 const {api,project,model,runtime}=await loadWork(directory),prompt=api.encode(model,text),identity={modelSha256:model.fingerprint,tokenizerSha256:model.tokenizerFingerprint,promptText:text,prompt,mode,options:mode==='beam'?{beamWidth,maxNewTokens:options.maxNewTokens}:options};
 if(mode==='generate'){await write({...identity,result:await api.generate(model,prompt,options)});return;}
 if(mode==='beam'){if(typeof project.beamDecode!=='function')throw new Error('Export beamDecode in trained-project.mjs');await write({...identity,beamWidth,result:await project.beamDecode(runtime,model,prompt,{beamWidth,maxNewTokens:options.maxNewTokens})});return;}
 if(typeof project.streamGenerate!=='function')throw new Error('Export streamGenerate in trained-project.mjs');
 await write({type:'start',...identity});
 for await(const event of project.streamGenerate(runtime,model,prompt,options))await write(event);
}
if(process.argv[1]&&import.meta.url===pathToFileURL(resolve(process.argv[1])).href){try{await main();}catch(error){console.error('Trained run failed: '+String(error?.message??error));process.exitCode=1;}}

`courses/small-llm-runtime/zip.mjs`:

```mjs
// Original dependency-free stored ZIP writer, used in Node and the browser.
const enc=new TextEncoder(),table=Array.from({length:256},(_,n)=>{let c=n;for(let k=0;k<8;k++)c=c&1?0xedb88320^(c>>>1):c>>>1;return c>>>0;});
const crc=bytes=>{let c=0xffffffff;for(const b of bytes)c=table[(c^b)&255]^(c>>>8);return (c^0xffffffff)>>>0;};
const bytes=x=>typeof x==='string'?enc.encode(x):new Uint8Array(x);
function header(size){const b=new Uint8Array(size);return {b,v:new DataView(b.buffer)};}
function concat(parts){const out=new Uint8Array(parts.reduce((s,p)=>s+p.length,0));let i=0;for(const p of parts){out.set(p,i);i+=p.length;}return out;}
export function zipFiles(files){
 const local=[],central=[];let cursor=0;
 for(const [name,input] of files){
   if(!name || name.startsWith('/') || name.includes('\\') || name.split('/').some(x=>x==='..'||!x))throw new Error(`invalid archive path ${name}`);
   const n=enc.encode(name),data=bytes(input),sum=crc(data),h=header(30),c=header(46);
   h.v.setUint32(0,0x04034b50,true);h.v.setUint16(4,20,true);h.v.setUint16(6,0x800,true);h.v.setUint16(12,33,true);h.v.setUint32(14,sum,true);h.v.setUint32(18,data.length,true);h.v.setUint32(22,data.length,true);h.v.setUint16(26,n.length,true);
   c.v.setUint32(0,0x02014b50,true);c.v.setUint16(4,20,true);c.v.setUint16(6,20,true);c.v.setUint16(8,0x800,true);c.v.setUint16(14,33,true);c.v.setUint32(16,sum,true);c.v.setUint32(20,data.length,true);c.v.setUint32(24,data.length,true);c.v.setUint16(28,n.length,true);c.v.setUint32(42,cursor,true);
   local.push(h.b,n,data);central.push(c.b,n);cursor+=h.b.length+n.length+data.length;
 }
 const dir=concat(central),end=header(22);end.v.setUint32(0,0x06054b50,true);end.v.setUint16(8,files.length,true);end.v.setUint16(10,files.length,true);end.v.setUint32(12,dir.length,true);end.v.setUint32(16,cursor,true);
 return concat([...local,dir,end.b]);
}

`courses/time-travel-debugger-part-two/API.md`:

```md
# Part two: API

Every function you write, with its inputs and outputs. The course supplies the
files under `public/`, the program listings under `programs/` and the game
files under `targets/`. You write the files under "Your files". Each starter
function throws an error containing "not written yet" until you write it.

## Words used here

- An **instruction** is one entry of a function's `code` in a program listing.
- **at** is an instruction's index in its function's `code`, counted from 0.
  An instruction is named by its function index and its `at`: `(8, 112)`.
  This is part one's `pc`, one per function.
- A **tick** is one instruction executed, as in part one. A **position** is a
  moment between instructions: position `t` is the state after `t`
  instructions, so a tick number also names a position (tick 96,568 is the
  moment just after instruction 96,568). The instruction executed next is
  instruction number `t + 1`, and its event says `tick: t + 1`.
- A **call** is one call into the game from outside: `game_init`,
  `game_key`, `game_tick` or one of the getters such as `r_px`. A **game
  frame** is one call to `game_tick`, 1/60 of a second of game time. A bare
  **frame** is always a call frame: one function call in progress, an entry
  of `state.frames`.
- The game shows three pieces of text, each read from memory through a
  getter: the **status line** (`r_line_ptr`: angle, power, wind and score),
  the **message line** (`r_msg_ptr`: ROUND 1, HIT!, SHORT BY 10) and the
  **help text** (`r_help_ptr`). Lob II keeps the same three texts in memory,
  but its eight getters, `g0` to `g7`, are named so they don't say what they
  hold, and none of them returns its help text's address.
- A **run** is the calls of one recording, one after another, on one machine.
- A **write** is the bytes one store instruction changed or rewrote:
  `{ address, size, before, after }`, where `before` and `after` are arrays of
  `size` byte values.
- **Memory** is the game's linear memory, a `Uint8Array` of 131072 bytes
  (two WebAssembly pages of 64 KiB; your debugger's snapshot pages in lesson
  10 are its own, smaller choice). An **address** is an index into it.

## Supplied by the course

### programs/NAME.json and public/program.mjs

A program listing is the `.wasm` file decoded into JSON when the course was
built:

```js
{ format: 'ttd2-program-1', name, sha256,
  types: [{ params, results }],      // type names: 'i32', 'i64', 'f32', 'f64'
  imports: [{ module, name, type }], // functions only; they take indexes 0, 1, ...
  functions: [{ index, type, locals, code, offsets }],
  exports: [{ name, kind, index }],  // kind 'func' or 'memory'
  globals: [{ type, mutable, init }],
  memory: { min, max },              // in 64 KiB pages
  data: [{ offset, bytes }],         // bytes as hex text in the file
  codeSectionStart }
```

`code` holds one array per instruction, its name first and its immediates
after it: `['i32.const', 5]`, `['local.get', 2]`, `['call', 6]`,
`['br_if', 1]`, `['block', null]` (null: the block leaves no value),
`['f32.store', 2, 20]` (alignment, then offset). `offsets[k]` is the file
offset of instruction `k`'s first byte in the `.wasm` file. `locals` lists
the types of the function's locals after its parameters.

`loadProgram(json)` turns a listing into the object your machine receives. It
adds `program.func(index)`, `program.typeOf(index)` and
`program.exportIndex(name)`, turns `"42n"` constants into BigInts and data
hex into `Uint8Array`s. `readProgram('lob')` reads and loads
`programs/lob.json`.

### public/world.mjs

`makeWorld(seed)` returns `{ imports, answered }`. `imports` has the four
functions the games import: `sin(x)`, `cos(x)`, `server_round(round)` and
`server_wind()`. The two server functions answer from a seed the game never
sees, and their answers change from call to call.

### public/hash.mjs

`hashMemory(memory)` is the SHA-256 of the memory bytes as hex text. Every
recording, check and lab command uses it.

### public/sessions.mjs

`session({ seed, mode, shots, ... })` returns a list of calls,
`[{ name, args }]`, that plays a game: `game_init(seed, mode)`, then key
presses and frames. Key codes: 1 left, 2 right, 3 up, 4 down, 5 space (fire),
6 N (new round).

`mode` adds up the game's defences, tricks a real game uses: 1 asks the
server for the wind (`server_wind`), so its exact value never enters memory;
2 moves the game's state to a new address at every new round after the
first, and changes the pointer to it; 4 stores angle, power, wind and flag
combined with a key that changes every round (XOR in Lob, addition in
Lob II); 8, in Lob only, slides the flag along the ground. Mode 0 has none.

## Your files

### machine.mjs (lesson 08)

```js
export class Machine {
  constructor(program, imports)
  state                 // everything the machine knows, one plain object
  running               // true while a call is unfinished
  begin(name, args)     // start a call to an export; runs nothing yet
  step()                // run one instruction; returns its event
  invoke(name, args)    // begin, then step until the call returns; returns its result
}
```

- `program` is a listing (as JSON or as `loadProgram` returns it).
  `imports` has one function per import name.
- At the start, memory is `memory.min * 65536` zero bytes with each data
  segment copied in at its offset, and each global holds its `init`.
- `state` must hold, at least: `memory` (a `Uint8Array`), `globals` (an
  array), `frames` (one entry per function call in progress, outermost first,
  each with `func` and `at`: the function and the `at` of the next
  instruction it will run), `tick` (instructions run so far) and `calls`
  (calls begun so far). Anything else your machine needs goes in `state`
  too.
- `structuredClone(machine.state)` must work, and after
  `machine.state = copy` the machine must carry on from the copied moment
  exactly. Lessons 09 to 13 rely on this.
- `step()` returns `{ tick, func, at, op, writes }`: the tick of this
  instruction, which instruction it was, its name, and the writes it made
  (`[]` for most instructions; one write for a store). Every instruction the
  machine runs is one tick, `block`, `loop`, `br` and `end` included; a branch
  runs no instruction on its way to its target. A branch to a `loop` goes to
  the instruction after the `loop`, which doesn't run again, so the branch's
  own tick is the only one.
- `invoke` returns a number for `i32` and `f32` results, `undefined` when the
  function returns nothing. An `f32` value is a JavaScript number rounded with
  `Math.fround`. An `i32` value is signed, as Node's engine returns it, so the
  bits of 4,294,967,295 come back as -1.
- A trap (division by zero, an access outside memory) throws an `Error` whose
  message starts with `trap:`. A load or store that traps reads or writes
  nothing (check `08.memory` looks at memory afterwards). The checks start a
  new machine after a trap, so the rest of what it leaves in `state` (stack,
  frames, tick) is up to you.
- Every instruction your machine runs goes through `step()`. The checks count
  calls to `step()` to measure replay costs.

### recorder.mjs (lesson 09)

```js
export function record(program, imports, calls)          // returns a recording
export function replay(program, recording, { check })    // returns { machine, results, hashes }
export function firstDivergence(program, original, tampered)  // returns a tick or null
```

A recording is plain JSON:

```js
{ format: 'ttd2-recording-1', program, sha256,
  calls:   [{ name, args }],          // every call into the game, in order
  results: [value or null],           // what each call returned
  answers: [{ name, args, result }],  // every import call the game made, in order
  hashes:  [hex] }                    // hashMemory after each call
```

- `program` is the listing's `name` (`lob`, `lob2`, `ladder/1`), which
  `debug.mjs` uses to find `programs/NAME.json`, and `sha256` is the listing's
  `sha256`.
- `result` in an answer is what the import function returned, before your
  machine converts it to the import's type. The course's worlds return values
  that already have that type.
- A recording holds only finite numbers, as JSON does, and the checks compare
  its answers with -0 and 0 counted as one number. The world's answers are
  always finite.
- `record` runs the calls on a new machine whose imports are the given ones,
  keeping every answer they return.
- `replay` runs the recording's calls on a new machine and answers each import
  call from `answers`, in order, without any world. If the game's next import
  call does not match the next entry of `answers` (another import, or other
  arguments), `replay` throws an error with a `divergence` field
  `{ tick, call, reason }`. Its tick is the number of instructions the machine
  had finished before the call instruction that asked; that instruction's own
  event would have `tick + 1`. With `check: true` (the default) a call whose result or memory hash
  differs from the recording also throws, with the tick at which that call
  returned.
- `firstDivergence` returns the smallest tick after which the tampered
  recording's replay has different memory from the original's, or `null`
  when the two never differ, even if an answer or a call was changed (a key
  the game ignores, an answer changed to the value it had). The tick is
  counted in the tampered replay. `tampered` is a copy of `original` with some
  answers or calls changed; its `hashes` are the original's. The checks'
  tampers change memory in a way that lasts at least to the end of the call
  where it starts, so comparing hashes at the ends of calls and then
  bisecting inside the first call that ends differently finds their ticks.
  The checks count the instructions it runs. If, before memory differs, the
  tampered replay asks for an import its recording can't answer, the checks
  don't test the result. The course's worked solution then counts memory as
  different from the call instruction that asked, and returns that
  instruction's tick.

### debugger.mjs (lessons 10 and 12)

```js
export class Debugger {
  constructor(program, recording, options)
  tick                  // the current position
  end                   // the position after the run's last instruction
  seek(tick)            // move there; returns the new position
  step(n = 1)           // forward n instructions, stopping at end
  stepBack(n = 1)       // back n instructions, stopping at 0
  read(address, size)   // the memory bytes at the current position, a Uint8Array
  state()               // a structuredClone of the machine's whole state at the current position
  where()               // { tick, call, func, at }: what runs next
  continue(stops)       // forward to the next stop: { reason, tick }
  continueBack(stops)   // backward to the previous stop: { reason, tick }
  lastWrite(address)    // the last write to that byte at or before here, or null
  stack()               // lesson 12: [{ func, at }], outermost first
  stepOut()             // lesson 12: forward until the current function has returned
  snapshots             // [{ tick, pages }], see below
}
// stops = { breakpoints: [{ func, at }], watches: [{ address, size }], functions: [index] }
```

- The debugger replays `recording` with the program; it never needs a world.
- A new `Debugger` stands at position 0. `seek`, `step`, `stepBack` and
  `stepOut` return the new position. The course's worked solution throws a
  `RangeError` when `seek` is given a position outside 0 to `end`, and the
  checks never ask for one.
- The **next instruction** at position `t` is the one the run executes as
  instruction number `t + 1`. Between two calls it is the first instruction
  of the next call. `where()` names it: `{ tick, call, func, at }`, where
  `tick` is the current position `t` and `call` is the index in
  `recording.calls` of the call the next instruction belongs to. At
  `end`, `func` and `at` are `null` and `call` is `recording.calls.length`.
- Between calls no function is running: `stack()` is `[]` and `state()` is
  the machine with no frames, before the next call has begun.
- A **breakpoint** `{ func, at }` stops at a position whose next instruction is
  that one. A **function stop** (lesson 12) stops where a call to that function
  begins: the next instruction is `(func, 0)`.
- A **watch** `{ address, size }` stops right after an instruction that wrote
  at least one byte in `[address, address + size)` and changed it.
- `continue` and `continueBack` always move: they look at positions strictly
  after, or strictly before, the current one, and stop at the nearest match.
  With no match they stop at `end` (`reason: 'end'`) or at 0
  (`reason: 'start'`). Otherwise `reason` is `'breakpoint'`, `'watchpoint'`
  or `'function'`. (Part one's `run` stopped without moving when it stood on
  a breakpoint; `continue` does not.)
- Position 0 can hold a stop too. A breakpoint or a function stop on the run's
  first instruction fires there, and `continueBack` reports it rather than
  `'start'`. No watch fires at 0, because no instruction comes before it.
- When several stops fire at one position, the checks accept any of their
  reasons. The worked solution reports `'watchpoint'` first, then
  `'breakpoint'`, then `'function'`.
- `lastWrite(address)` returns `{ tick, func, at, address, size }` for the
  instruction with the greatest tick at or before the current position that
  wrote the byte at `address`, whether or not the value changed. `address` in
  the result is where that write starts. The method does not move the
  debugger; the `last-write` and `who` commands of `debug.mjs` then move to
  the write's tick, so `answer` can name it.
- **Snapshots.** `snapshots` lists the snapshots the debugger has kept, in
  order of `tick`. `pages` is an array of `Uint8Array`s whose concatenation
  is the memory at that tick. A page no instruction wrote since the previous
  snapshot must be the very same `Uint8Array` object as in the previous
  snapshot. You choose how often to take a snapshot, and the page size, up to
  16 KiB: with larger pages nearly every snapshot copies most of memory. All
  your snapshots together may hold at most a quarter of the bytes that a full
  copy of memory per snapshot would, counting a page that several snapshots
  share once.
- **stepOut between calls.** The checks test `stepOut` only inside a call.
  Between calls it's yours to define (lesson 12). The worked solution runs the
  whole next call and stops where it has returned.
- **Budgets.** Opening the debugger may replay the run at most about twice.
  After that, going back one instruction, or continuing back to a stop a few
  thousand instructions away, may replay at most 20,000 instructions, which a
  snapshot every few thousand instructions meets and a replay from the start
  does not. The checks count instructions through `step()`, and a debugger
  that stands at position `t` must have counted at least `t`.

### query.mjs (lesson 11)

```js
export function buildIndex(program, recording)   // returns an index
index.end                                         // instructions in the run
index.lastWriter(address, beforeTick)             // { tick, func, at, address, size } or null
index.sources(tick)                               // { stores, answers, args, initial }
```

- `lastWriter(address, beforeTick)` is the write to the byte at `address` made
  by the instruction with the greatest tick below `beforeTick`, or `null`.
- `sources(tick)` takes the tick of a store instruction (anything else
  throws) and returns where the value it stored came from:
  - `stores`: the ticks of every earlier store on the value's chain;
  - `answers`: indexes into `recording.answers` of import results on the chain;
  - `args`: `[call, index]` pairs, arguments of calls into the game on the chain
    (the call's index in `recording.calls`, the argument's index in its `args`);
  - `initial`: addresses of bytes on the chain that were loaded before any
    store had written them.
  Each list is sorted in increasing order, without repeats.
- The chain follows values, not addresses: a value depends on every operand
  of the instruction that produced it, except the address operand of a load
  or store. A load depends on the bytes it read, so on the stores that last
  wrote them. `local.get`, `local.set`, `local.tee`, `global.get` and
  `global.set` pass a value along unchanged, and so does a call to a defined
  function (arguments into its parameters, its result back out). A call to an
  import gives a value that depends only on that answer: its arguments are not
  followed. Constants depend on nothing.
- The rules in detail, where a case could go either way:
  - `select` depends on all three of its operands, the two values and the
    condition, whichever value it picks.
  - A store depends on its whole value operand, even when it writes only its
    low 1 or 2 bytes, and it becomes the last writer of every byte it writes,
    changed or not.
  - A load depends on each byte it reads separately: on several stores if
    several wrote those bytes, and on `initial` addresses for bytes no store
    wrote before it (zero bytes and data-segment bytes alike).
  - Comparisons, conversions and reinterpretations follow their operands like
    arithmetic.
  - Decisions are not followed: a `br_if` condition and which way a branch went
    are on no chain. A branch or `return` passes on only the values it keeps.
  - A call to a defined function makes argument `i` its local `i`; locals
    beyond the parameters, a global's starting value and constants depend on
    nothing.
  - The store asked about is not in its own `stores` list. `args` is sorted
    by call, then argument index.
- `sources` throws for a tick that is not a store's. `lastWriter` returns the
  whole write, its start and size, even for a byte inside a wider store; the
  debugger's `lastWrite` at position `p` is `lastWriter(address, p + 1)`.
- The index does not report the size of memory. Every recording in this course
  is of Lob or Lob II, whose memory is 131,072 bytes (see "Memory" above), so
  code built on an index can take that size as fixed. What `lastWriter` does
  for an address outside memory is not part of this contract and no check asks
  it (the supplied `examples/query-checkpoint.mjs` throws), so code that must
  refuse such an address tests it against 131,072 itself.
- `buildIndex` may replay the recording once or twice. Answering a question
  must not replay it again; the checks count instructions.

### names.mjs (lesson 12)

```js
export function functionNames(bytes)   // { [index]: name } from the file's "name" section, {} if it has none
export function lineAt(lines, offset)  // { line, column } of the last row at or before offset, or null
```

- `bytes` is a whole `.wasm` file as a `Uint8Array`. Lesson 12 gives the
  layout of its sections and of the name section.
- `lines` is the `rows` array of a line-table file `lines/NAME.json`:
  `{ offset, line, column }` in increasing `offset`, where `offset` is a file
  offset like the listing's `offsets`.

### investigations/N.txt (lesson 13)

One debugger command per line, for `node debug.mjs`. The last `answer`
command the script runs is your answer for ladder build N.

The **first bad write** of a ladder build is the earliest store in its run
that leaves a byte of memory holding a value a correct build wouldn't hold there
at the same point of the run. In every build here, the run first goes wrong at a
store the build makes, never by leaving out a store a correct build makes. Up
to that store the build makes the same stores as a correct build, store for
store, so the same point of the run means after the same earlier stores.

### debug.mjs (lessons 10 to 13)

`node debug.mjs PROJECT TARGET [SCRIPT]` runs your files on a recording, or on
ladder build N, and `help` lists its commands. It wraps
`Machine.prototype.step`, so it counts every `step()` of every machine of your
`Machine` class, whoever makes it. That includes your Debugger's first pass,
the index that `who` and `sources` build, and the machines that `getters`,
`answer` and `writes` run on a copy of the state. The count is what `cost`
shows and what the ladder's budgets limit. `diverge` and `compare` run Node's
engine and add nothing to it.

## The 62 instructions

Both games use exactly these. `a` and `b` are the two operands, `b` the one on
top of the stack; a comparison pushes 1 or 0.

| Instructions | What they do |
| --- | --- |
| `block T`, `loop T`, `end` | open a block or a loop (`T`: `null`, or the type of the value it leaves); `end` closes the innermost one, or returns from the function at its last `end` |
| `br N`, `br_if N`, `return` | branch to the block `N` levels out (`br_if` pops a condition and branches if it is not 0); `return` leaves the function |
| `call F` | call function `F`: an import runs outside and its result is pushed; a defined function gets a new frame |
| `local.get`, `local.set`, `local.tee`, `global.get`, `global.set` | read or write a local or a global; `tee` writes and keeps the value |
| `select` | pop a condition `c`, then `b`, then `a`; push `a` if `c` is not 0, else `b` |
| `i32.const`, `i64.const`, `f32.const` | push a constant |
| `i32.load`, `f32.load`, `i32.load8_u` | load 4 bytes as an integer, 4 bytes as a float, or 1 byte as 0 to 255 |
| `i32.store`, `f32.store`, `i32.store8`, `i32.store16`, `i64.store` | store 4, 4, 1, 2 or 8 bytes, lowest byte first |
| `i32.add`, `i32.sub`, `i32.mul` | wrap to 32 bits |
| `i32.div_s`, `i32.div_u`, `i32.rem_s`, `i32.rem_u` | divide or take the remainder, signed or unsigned; divide by 0 traps, and so does `div_s` of -2,147,483,648 by -1 |
| `i32.and`, `i32.or`, `i32.xor` | bitwise |
| `i32.shl`, `i32.shr_s`, `i32.shr_u` | shift by the low 5 bits of `b`; `shr_s` copies the sign bit in, `shr_u` zeros |
| `i32.eqz`, `i32.ne` | is `a` zero; are `a` and `b` different |
| `i32.lt_s`, `i32.gt_s`, `i32.le_s`, `i32.ge_s` | signed comparisons |
| `i32.lt_u`, `i32.gt_u` | unsigned comparisons |
| `f32.add`, `f32.sub`, `f32.mul`, `f32.div`, `f32.sqrt` | 32-bit float arithmetic, rounded with `Math.fround` |
| `f32.neg` | flip the sign, so 0 becomes -0 |
| `f32.lt`, `f32.gt`, `f32.le`, `f32.ge` | float comparisons (false when either is NaN) |
| `f32.convert_i32_s`, `f32.convert_i32_u` | integer to float, reading the integer as signed or unsigned |
| `f64.promote_f32`, `f32.demote_f64` | to and from 64-bit floats, used only around `sin` and `cos` |
| `i32.reinterpret_f32`, `f32.reinterpret_i32` | keep the 32 bits, read them as the other type |
| `i32.trunc_sat_f32_s` | drop the fraction; NaN gives 0, and values beyond the `i32` range give its largest or smallest |

```

```md
# Build a time-travel debugger, part two: debug a real game

Part one built a debugger for a machine of 7 instructions and 8 memory cells. Part two takes it to a real compiled program called Lob, a small artillery game of 2,806 instructions over 131,072 bytes of memory, written in C and compiled to WebAssembly, a machine code that runs in browsers and in Node. You write the machine that runs it, record and replay its runs, step backwards through those recordings, question them, give your debugger names and a call stack, and end by finding planted bugs in six later builds of Lob and of Lob II, a second artillery game built the same way (`targets/lob2.wasm`), with your own tool.

Lob is the game that Sightline, a separate course, works out from the outside, and here you debug it from the inside.

## What you build

Six units, numbered after part one's seven. Each one adds to the same project.

- **08 A machine worth debugging.** An interpreter for the 62 WebAssembly instructions Lob and Lob II use. Node's own WebAssembly engine is the answer key. Then part one's debugger runs on it unchanged, and you measure what copying the whole state on every step costs.
- **09 Record and replay.** Record every answer the outside world gives the game, replay a run exactly without it, and find the first instruction at which a tampered recording parts from the original by bisecting memory hashes. The unit mirrors rr, a record-and-replay debugger for Linux programs.
- **10 Run backwards.** Snapshots that copy only the pages of memory written since the previous one, plus step back, continue back, and "who last wrote this byte", each replaying from a snapshot, so an answer a few thousand instructions back costs a few thousand.
- **11 Question a recording.** An index built in one replay: the last write to any byte before any tick, and the chain of values a stored value was computed from.
- **12 Stack and names.** Function names from the binary's name section, the call stack, stops at named functions, and line numbers from the compiler's line table.
- **13 The ladder.** Six later builds, five of Lob and one of Lob II, each with one planted bug, rising in difficulty. For each, your debugger names the first bad write inside a replay budget.

## Before you start

Part one is the prerequisite. Its ideas (ticks, events and traces, checkpoints and replay, breakpoints, watchpoints and reverse search) are used without being taught again. It's a separate course, "Build a time-travel debugger", and this copy doesn't include it. If you haven't taken it, read its lessons 01 to 06 there, which build its debugger. Its lesson 07 is a capstone investigation that adds no new feature. `fallback/part-one-debugger.mjs` is part one's worked debugger, supplied so part two can be done alone. Reading it spoils part one.

You need Node.js 22 or later and nothing else: no install, no account, no network. You write JavaScript modules, and the lessons use typed arrays, `DataView`, `BigInt` and `structuredClone`. The course was built and checked with Node 26.5.1 on macOS, and its continuous integration runs Node 22 on Linux.

## Start

Read [lesson 08](lessons/08.md), or open [its formatted offline edition](lessons/08.html) in your browser. It starts with a runnable getter, then lets you choose a fresh project with either the important interpreter methods left for you to type in from listings printed in the lesson (the type-in route) or a complete supplied interpreter. The code you design yourself is each unit's new application and, in unit 13, the investigations of builds 2 to 6. Supporting opcode code is provided on both routes; an AI-assisted route is also explained. Choose your route there before creating `project/`. The browser edition reads locally without a server; commands still run in your terminal from the folder containing `lab.mjs`.

For a completely blank implementation instead of the guided build, the original commands remain available:

```sh
node lab.mjs start project
node lab.mjs check project 08
```

`API.md` is the contract for every function you write. `node lab.mjs` lists every lab command. Existing project folders are never overwritten; resume your own work or choose a new name for a fresh route.

Each lesson asks questions before it explains their answers, including, in each unit's failure and repair, how its prescribed break will turn out before you run it. Commit an answer with `node lab.mjs predict project ID ANSWER`, and the lab then shows the right answer and why. After a wrong answer it points to the section that teaches the idea and gives you a fresh case to try, or, when the course has no other case, lists the question in `status` as due for another try after your next lesson. `practice.json` holds those questions with their answers, because the lab checks them on your own computer. Leave it unread until you've committed your own. Each `check` saves your files and the results under `project/attempts/`, and `node lab.mjs status project` lists your checks and predictions. The lessons also ask you to keep notes in `project/report.md`. They're yours, and no check reads them.

## What was measured

Numbers from the course's own worked solution on the authoring Mac, 2026-11-13. The course's numbers check, which isn't part of this copy, re-derives every count from the course's files. The timings vary from computer to computer and with how busy the computer is, so they are given as ranges that held on the authoring Mac both idle and busy, with its idle measurement named as one point in each.

- Agreement with Node's engine: 33 runs of both games in every mode, 37,620 calls and 34,647,332 instructions on the worked solution's machine. After every call its result, every getter and the memory hash agree with Node's.
- Part one's debugger on the real game (`node lab.mjs wall`, the fallback debugger on the worked solution's machine): a run of 1,043,331 instructions that the machine alone finishes in 20 to 500 ms (about 50 ms on the idle authoring Mac). Copying the whole state, 131,072 bytes of memory, on every step makes each step 100 to 800 times slower than the machine alone (about 240 times on the idle authoring Mac): 5 to 150 microseconds instead of 0.02 to 0.5 (about 12 instead of about 0.05). So one pass takes 5 to 150 seconds instead of a fraction of a second (about 12 seconds), and one backward question at the end of the run, with its answer 1,000 ticks back, is estimated at 1.5 to 50 hours (about 3 hours).
- Replay budgets, counted as calls to your machine's `step`: in unit 09, finding where a tampered recording parts may run three times what the worked solution runs (1,025,000 to 1,362,000 instructions on the checks' recordings). In unit 10, each backward question near the end of a 654,610-instruction run may replay 20,000 instructions, and the worked solution, with a snapshot every 1,000 instructions, needs at most 1,872.
- The ladder: the first bad writes lie 3,611 to 370,147 instructions before the end of their recordings. The worked investigations replay 278,551 to 1,308,230 instructions, and the budgets are 856,000 to 2,617,000.

## What this course doesn't claim

- No person has taken it yet. A fresh AI agent worked through units 08 to 13 from the learner copy. That run is evidence the instructions can be followed, not that the course teaches.
- The time estimates, roughly 40 to 60 hours for the six units, are guesses.
- Checks cover their named cases. In a test run before release, an AI agent working from API.md, the supplied files and the check output passed every check in about 27 minutes without opening a lesson. So a pass shows that your code met the checks' cases, not that you've learned what the lessons teach. The lessons' reasoning is practised in the prediction questions, and no check grades them.
- The C sources of Lob and Lob II aren't part of this course. Sightline asks its learners to work out what they say from the compiled code. `targets/MANIFEST.json` still lists the hashes of `lob.c` and `lob2.c`, which the course's own build verifies and this copy leaves out.

The checks run your own JavaScript with your normal permissions. They aren't a sandbox, so run code you understand.

```

`courses/time-travel-debugger-part-two/checks/08.mjs`:

```mjs
// Unit 08: a machine worth debugging. The answer key is Node's own WebAssembly
// engine: it runs the games beside your machine here, and it ran the small
// programs in fixtures/08/programs.json when the course was built (their results,
// traps, import calls and memory are Node's). Instruction counts and the order
// instructions run in, which Node cannot show, follow the rules in lesson 08.
import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { join } from 'node:path';
import { fail, show, program as readProgram, wasmBytes, courseRoot, NOT_WRITTEN, CheckFailure, firstDifference, same, countSteps } from './harness.mjs';
import { loadProgram } from '../public/program.mjs';
import { makeWorld } from '../public/world.mjs';
import { session, plan } from '../public/sessions.mjs';
import { hashMemory } from '../public/hash.mjs';

export const title = 'A machine worth debugging';

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- shared with tools/make-fixtures.mjs

// The imports the small programs call. Each one notes its calls in `log`.
export function syntheticImports(log) {
  return {
    add3: (a, b, c) => { log.push(['add3', [a, b, c]]); return (a * 100 + b * 10 + c) | 0; },
    third: (x) => { log.push(['third', [x]]); return x / 3; },            // returns f32: the machine rounds the answer
    scale: (x) => { log.push(['scale', [x]]); return x * 1.0000001; },    // f64 in, f64 out
    tap: (x) => { log.push(['tap', [x]]); },                               // returns nothing
  };
}
// Numbers JSON cannot hold travel as strings.
export const enc = (x) => Object.is(x, -0) ? '-0' : Number.isNaN(x) ? 'NaN' : x === Infinity ? 'Infinity' : x === -Infinity ? '-Infinity' : x;
export const dec = (x) => x === '-0' ? -0 : x === 'NaN' ? NaN : x === 'Infinity' ? Infinity : x === '-Infinity' ? -Infinity : x;

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- helpers

const cache = new Map();
function fixture(name) {
  if (!cache.has(name)) cache.set(name, JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(courseRoot, 'checks', 'fixtures', '08', `${name}.json`), 'utf8')));
  return cache.get(name);
}

export const WIDTH = { 'i32.store8': 1, 'i32.store16': 2, 'i32.store': 4, 'f32.store': 4, 'i64.store': 8 };
const fromHex = (h) => Array.from(Buffer.from(h, 'hex'));
const bytesOf = (v) => (ArrayBuffer.isView(v) || Array.isArray(v)) ? Array.from(v) : v;
const plural = (n, word) => `${Number(n).toLocaleString('en-US')} ${word}${n === 1 ? '' : 's'}`;

function whereInWork(error, workDir) {
  for (const line of String(error?.stack ?? '').split('\n')) {
    const i = workDir ? line.indexOf(workDir) : -1;
    if (i >= 0) {
      const m = line.slice(i + workDir.length).match(/^\/?([^:]+):(\d+)/);
      if (m) return ` (${m[1]} line ${m[2]})`;
    }
  }
  return '';
}

// Run learner code; an unexpected error becomes a failure that says where it happened.
// "not written yet" and check failures pass through unchanged.
function attempt(run, { checked, input, expected, workDir }) {
  try { return run(); } catch (error) {
    if (error instanceof CheckFailure || String(error?.message ?? '').includes(NOT_WRITTEN)) throw error;
    fail({ checked, input, observed: `your code threw ${error?.name ?? 'an error'}: ${String(error?.message ?? error).split('\n')[0]}${whereInWork(error, workDir)}`, expected });
  }
}

function newMachine(Machine, program, imports, context) {
  return attempt(() => new Machine(program, imports), { checked: `new Machine(program, imports) for ${program.name}`, expected: 'a machine', ...context });
}

const asView = (m) => ArrayBuffer.isView(m) ? Buffer.from(m.buffer, m.byteOffset, m.byteLength) : Buffer.from(m);
// The first address where two memories differ, with the bytes around it, or null.
function memoryDifference(ours, theirs) {
  if (!ArrayBuffer.isView(ours) && !Array.isArray(ours)) return { address: null, text: `state.memory is ${show(ours, 60)}, not a Uint8Array` };
  const a = asView(ours), b = asView(theirs);
  if (a.length === b.length && Buffer.compare(a, b) === 0) return null;
  if (a.length !== b.length) return { address: null, text: `yours has ${plural(a.length, 'byte')}, Node's engine ${plural(b.length, 'byte')}` };
  let k = 0;
  while (a[k] === b[k]) k++;
  const from = Math.max(0, k - 2), to = Math.min(a.length, k + 6);
  return { address: k, ours: Array.from(a.subarray(from, to)), theirs: Array.from(b.subarray(from, to)), from };
}
const memoryText = (d, who = "Node's engine") => d.address === null ? d.text : `first difference at address ${d.address}: bytes ${d.from} to ${d.from + d.ours.length - 1} are ${show(d.ours)} on yours and ${show(d.theirs)} on ${who}`;

const pick = (e) => ({ tick: e?.tick, func: e?.func, at: e?.at, op: e?.op, writes: Array.isArray(e?.writes) ? e.writes.map(w => ({ address: w?.address, size: w?.size, before: bytesOf(w?.before), after: bytesOf(w?.after) })) : e?.writes });
const opAt = (program, func, at) => program.func(func)?.code?.[at]?.[0];
const insText = (program, func, at) => { const ins = program.func(func)?.code?.[at]; return ins ? `(${func}, ${at}) ${ins.filter(x => x !== null).join(' ')}` : `(${func}, ${at})`; };
const body = (program, name) => program.func(program.exportIndex(name)).code.map(ins => ins.filter(x => x !== null).join(' ')).join(' · ');

// How control moves, for messages about the order instructions run in.
const RULES = 'A branch to a block goes to just after its end (that end does not run); a branch to a loop goes to just after the loop instruction (the loop instruction does not run again); a call goes to instruction 0 of the function it calls; return, and a function\'s last end, go back to just after the call.';

function hintAfter(program, func, at) {
  const op = opAt(program, func, at);
  if (op === 'br' || op === 'br_if') return 'The instruction before it was a branch. ' + RULES;
  if (op === 'call') return 'The instruction before it was a call. A call to a defined function goes to its instruction 0; a call to an import runs no instruction of the program and goes on just after the call.';
  if (op === 'return' || op === 'end') return 'The instruction before it ended a block or returned. ' + RULES;
  return RULES;
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- the small programs

// Run every call of one topic's programs on your machine; compare with what Node did.
async function runPrograms(topic, { cls, workDir }) {
  const Machine = await cls('machine.mjs', 'Machine');
  // Note every event, as lessons 09 to 13 count instructions: by wrapping Machine.prototype.step.
  const proto = Machine.prototype, original = proto.step;
  if (typeof original !== 'function') fail({ checked: 'step() is a method of your Machine class', observed: 'Machine.prototype.step is not a function', expected: 'class Machine { step() { ... } }: lessons 09 to 13 count instructions by counting calls to Machine.prototype.step' });
  let events = [];
  proto.step = function (...a) { const e = original.apply(this, a); events.push(e); return e; };
  for (const entry of fixture('programs').programs.filter(p => p.topic === topic)) {
    const program = loadProgram(entry.listing);
    for (const run of entry.runs) {
      let m = null, log = [], before = [];
      for (const call of run.calls) {
        const args = call.args.map(dec);
        const label = `${call.name}(${args.map(x => show(x)).join(', ')})`;
        const input = `${label} in the ${program.name} program${before.length ? `, after ${before.join(', ')} on the same machine` : ', on a new machine'}; the function: ${body(program, call.name)} (checks/fixtures/08/programs.json has the whole program)`;
        const context = { input, workDir };
        if (!m) {
          log = [];
          m = newMachine(Machine, program, syntheticImports(log), context);
        }
        log.length = 0; events = [];
        const tick0 = m.state?.tick;
        let result, error = null;
        try { result = m.invoke(call.name, args); } catch (e) {
          if (e instanceof CheckFailure || String(e?.message ?? '').includes(NOT_WRITTEN)) throw e;
          error = e;
        }
        const message = error ? String(error?.message ?? error).split('\n')[0] : '';
        if (call.trap) {
          if (!error) fail({ checked: `${label} traps`, input, observed: `your machine returned ${show(result)}`, expected: `a trap: Node's engine stops with "${call.trap}". Throw an Error whose message starts with "trap:"` });
          if (!message.startsWith('trap:')) fail({ checked: `${label} traps`, input, observed: `your machine threw ${error?.name ?? 'Error'}: ${message}${whereInWork(error, workDir)}`, expected: `an Error whose message starts with "trap:" (Node's engine says "${call.trap}")` });
        } else if (error) {
          fail({ checked: `${label} runs to its end`, input, observed: `your machine threw ${error?.name ?? 'Error'}: ${message}${whereInWork(error, workDir)}`, expected: `the call returns ${call.result === null ? 'nothing' : show(dec(call.result))}, as on Node's engine` });
        } else {
          const want = call.result === null ? undefined : dec(call.result);
          if (!Object.is(result, want)) fail({ checked: `the result of ${label}`, input, observed: `your machine returned ${show(result)}`, expected: `${show(want)}, as on Node's engine${typeof want === 'number' && typeof result === 'number' && Number.isInteger(want) && result === want ? ' (an i32 is never -0)' : ''}` });
        }
        const wantLog = (call.imports ?? []).map(([n, a]) => [n, a.map(dec)]);
        if (!same(log, wantLog)) fail({ checked: `the imports ${label} calls, with their arguments in order`, input, observed: `your machine called ${show(log.map(([n, a]) => `${n}(${a.map(x => show(x)).join(', ')})`))}`, expected: `${show(wantLog.map(([n, a]) => `${n}(${a.map(x => show(x)).join(', ')})`))}, as on Node's engine. A call to an import pops its arguments; the first argument is the deepest of them on the stack`, diff: firstDifference(log, wantLog) });
        if (!call.trap) {
          const ran = m.state.tick - tick0;
          if (ran !== events.length) fail({ checked: `every instruction of ${label} goes through step()`, input, observed: `state.tick went up by ${ran} but Machine.prototype.step ran ${plural(events.length, 'time')}`, expected: 'invoke begins the call, then calls this.step() until the call returns; step() adds 1 to state.tick. Lessons 09 to 13 count instructions by counting calls to Machine.prototype.step' });
          if (call.trace) checkTrace(program, events, call.trace, { label, input });
          if (call.ticks !== undefined && events.length !== call.ticks) fail({ checked: `how many instructions ${label} runs`, input, observed: plural(events.length, 'instruction'), expected: `${plural(call.ticks, 'instruction')}. ${RULES}` });
          if (call.writes) {
            const ours = events.flatMap(e => (e.writes ?? []).map(w => ({ address: w.address, size: w.size, before: bytesOf(w.before), after: bytesOf(w.after) })));
            const want = call.writes.map(([address, size, b, a]) => ({ address, size, before: fromHex(b), after: fromHex(a) }));
            if (!same(ours, want)) fail({ checked: `the writes ${label} reports`, input, observed: show(ours), expected: `${show(want)}: one write per store, { address, size, before, after }, address being where the first byte goes (the popped address plus the offset), before read from memory before the store`, diff: firstDifference(ours, want) });
          }
        }
        if (call.memory) {
          const memory = m.state.memory;
          const expected = new Uint8Array(entry.listing.memory.min * 65536);
          for (const [a, v] of call.memory) expected[a] = v;
          const d = memoryDifference(memory, expected);
          if (d) fail({ checked: `memory after ${label}`, input, observed: memoryText(d), expected: call.trap ? 'memory unchanged by the store that traps: a store that would reach past the end writes nothing' : 'the bytes Node\'s engine holds after the same calls; values are stored lowest byte first, at the popped address plus the offset' });
        }
        before.push(label);
        if (call.trap || entry.fresh) { m = null; before = []; }
      }
    }
  }
}

function checkTrace(program, events, flat, { label, input }) {
  const n = Math.max(events.length, flat.length / 2);
  for (let k = 0; k < n; k++) {
    const e = events[k];
    const wf = flat[2 * k], wa = flat[2 * k + 1];
    if (e && wf !== undefined && e.func === wf && e.at === wa && e.op === opAt(program, wf, wa)) continue;
    const prev = k > 0 ? `After instruction ${k} of the call, ${insText(program, flat[2 * k - 2], flat[2 * k - 1])}, ` : 'At the start of the call, ';
    const ours = e ? `${insText(program, e.func, e.at)}${e.op !== opAt(program, e.func, e.at) ? ` (but your event's op is ${show(e.op)})` : ''}` : 'nothing: your call had ended';
    const want = wf !== undefined ? insText(program, wf, wa) : 'nothing: the call has ended';
    fail({ checked: `the order in which ${label} runs its instructions`, input, observed: `${prev}your machine ran ${ours}`, expected: `${want}. ${k > 0 ? hintAfter(program, flat[2 * k - 2], flat[2 * k - 1]) : RULES}` });
  }
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- Node beside your machine

async function nodeGame(game, imports) {
  const { instance } = await WebAssembly.instantiate(wasmBytes(`targets/${game}.wasm`), { env: imports });
  return instance.exports;
}
const getterNames = (program) => program.exports.filter(e => e.kind === 'func' && !e.name.startsWith('game_')).map(e => e.name);
const callText = (c) => `${c.name}(${c.args.join(', ')})`;

// Run a session on your machine and on Node's engine with the same answers;
// compare after every call.
async function agree(Machine, game, { seed, mode, world, shots, flight }, workDir) {
  const program = readProgram(game);
  const calls = session({ seed, mode, plan: plan({ seed, shots, flight }) });
  const w1 = makeWorld(world), w2 = makeWorld(world);
  const describe = `${game}: session({ seed: ${seed}, mode: ${mode}, plan: plan({ seed: ${seed}, shots: ${shots}, flight: ${flight} }) }), ${calls.length} calls, both answered by makeWorld(${world})`;
  const m = newMachine(Machine, program, w1.imports, { input: describe, workDir });
  const node = await nodeGame(game, w2.imports);
  const getters = getterNames(program);
  for (let k = 0; k < calls.length; k++) {
    const c = calls[k];
    const at = `call ${k}, ${callText(c)}`;
    const input = `${describe}; the calls before it: ${calls.slice(Math.max(0, k - 3), k).map(callText).join(', ') || 'none'}`;
    const ours = attempt(() => m.invoke(c.name, c.args), { checked: `${at} runs on your machine`, input, expected: `the call runs to its end, as on Node's engine`, workDir });
    const theirs = node[c.name](...c.args);
    if (!Object.is(ours, theirs)) fail({ checked: `what ${at} returns`, input, observed: `yours returned ${show(ours)}`, expected: `${show(theirs)}, as on Node's engine` });
    for (const g of getters) {
      const x = attempt(() => m.invoke(g, []), { checked: `the getter ${g} after ${at}`, input, expected: 'a number', workDir });
      const y = node[g]();
      if (!Object.is(x, y)) fail({ checked: `${g}() after ${at}`, input, observed: `yours returns ${show(x)}`, expected: `${show(y)}, as on Node's engine. Every call before this one agreed` });
    }
    const d = memoryDifference(m.state.memory, new Uint8Array(node.memory.buffer));
    if (d) fail({ checked: `memory after ${at}`, input, observed: memoryText(d), expected: 'the same 131,072 bytes as Node\'s engine. Every call before this one agreed, so an instruction this call ran stored something else, or somewhere else' });
  }
  return { calls: calls.length, ticks: m.state.tick };
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- the cases

const store = (op) => WIDTH[op] !== undefined;

export const cases = [
  {
    id: '08.memory-starts',
    title: 'A new machine holds the program\'s starting memory and globals, and has run nothing',
    requirement: 'state.memory is a Uint8Array of memory.min × 65,536 bytes, zero except each data segment copied in at its offset; state.globals holds each global\'s init value; state.tick and state.calls are 0, state.frames is empty and running is false.',
    async run({ cls, workDir }) {
      const Machine = await cls('machine.mjs', 'Machine');
      const shape = (m, program, input, length, globals, expectedMemory, who) => {
        const s = m.state;
        if (!s || typeof s !== 'object') fail({ checked: 'machine.state', input, observed: `machine.state is ${show(s)}`, expected: 'one plain object holding everything the machine knows' });
        if (!(s.memory instanceof Uint8Array)) fail({ checked: 'state.memory is a Uint8Array', input, observed: `state.memory is ${s.memory === undefined ? 'missing' : Object.prototype.toString.call(s.memory)}`, expected: `a Uint8Array of ${plural(length, 'byte')}` });
        if (s.memory.length !== length) fail({ checked: 'the size of state.memory', input, observed: plural(s.memory.length, 'byte'), expected: `${plural(length, 'byte')}: memory.min (${program.memory.min}) times 65,536` });
        const d = memoryDifference(s.memory, expectedMemory);
        if (d) fail({ checked: 'the bytes of a new machine\'s memory', input, observed: memoryText(d, who), expected: `zero everywhere except the data segments, each copied in at its offset (${program.data.map(x => `${x.bytes.length} bytes at ${x.offset}`).join(', ')})` });
        const gl = s.globals;
        if (!Array.isArray(gl) && !ArrayBuffer.isView(gl)) fail({ checked: 'state.globals', input, observed: `state.globals is ${show(gl)}`, expected: `an array: ${show(globals)}` });
        if (!same(Array.from(gl), globals)) fail({ checked: 'the globals of a new machine', input, observed: show(Array.from(gl)), expected: `${show(globals)}: each global's init value from the listing`, diff: firstDifference(Array.from(gl), globals) });
        if (s.tick !== 0) fail({ checked: 'state.tick of a new machine', input, observed: show(s.tick), expected: '0: no instruction has run' });
        if (s.calls !== 0) fail({ checked: 'state.calls of a new machine', input, observed: show(s.calls), expected: '0: no call has begun' });
        if (!Array.isArray(s.frames) || s.frames.length !== 0) fail({ checked: 'state.frames of a new machine', input, observed: show(s.frames), expected: '[]: an empty array, no call in progress' });
        const running = attempt(() => m.running, { checked: 'machine.running', input, expected: 'false', workDir });
        if (running !== false) fail({ checked: 'machine.running of a new machine', input, observed: show(running), expected: 'false' });
      };
      for (const game of ['lob', 'lob2']) {
        const program = readProgram(game);
        const input = `new Machine(readProgram('${game}'), makeWorld(1).imports)`;
        const m = newMachine(Machine, program, makeWorld(1).imports, { input, workDir });
        const node = await nodeGame(game, makeWorld(1).imports);
        shape(m, program, input, program.memory.min * 65536, program.globals.map(g => g.init), new Uint8Array(node.memory.buffer), 'Node\'s engine before any call');
      }
      const layout = fixture('programs').layout;
      const program = loadProgram(layout.listing);
      const input = `a small program with one page of memory, three data segments (${program.data.map(x => `${x.bytes.length} bytes at ${x.offset}`).join(', ')}) and three globals (checks/fixtures/08/programs.json, "layout")`;
      const expected = new Uint8Array(layout.length);
      for (const [a, v] of layout.memory) expected[a] = v;
      shape(newMachine(Machine, program, {}, { input, workDir }), program, input, layout.length, layout.globals, expected, 'Node\'s engine');
    },

  {
    id: '08.frames',
    title: 'A call to a defined function pushes a frame, and its caller waits at the instruction after the call',
    requirement: 'When a call instruction calls a function the program defines, step() pushes a frame { func: the callee, at: 0 } on top of state.frames, and the caller\'s frame names, as its at, the instruction after the call: that is where it carries on when the callee returns.',
    timeLimitMs: 20000,
    async run({ cls, workDir }) {
      const Machine = await cls('machine.mjs', 'Machine');
      const program = readProgram('lob');
      const view = (m) => (Array.isArray(m.state.frames) ? m.state.frames.map((f) => ({ func: f?.func, at: f?.at })) : m.state.frames);
      for (const [seed, mode, call] of [[3, 0, 'game_init'], [8, 1, 'game_init']]) {
        const input = `new Machine(readProgram('lob'), makeWorld(${seed}).imports), begin('${call}', [${seed}, ${mode}]), then step()`;
        const m = newMachine(Machine, program, makeWorld(seed).imports, { input, workDir });
        attempt(() => m.begin(call, [seed, mode]), { checked: `begin('${call}', ...)`, input, expected: 'the call begins', workDir });
        let found = 0;
        while (m.running && found < 2) {
          const frames = m.state.frames;
          const top = frames[frames.length - 1];
          const ins = program.func(top.func).code[top.at];
          const depth = frames.length;
          const e = pick(attempt(() => m.step(), { checked: 'step()', input, expected: 'an event', workDir }));
          if (ins[0] !== 'call' || ins[1] < program.imports.length) continue;
          found++;
          const after = view(m);
          const caller = after[depth - 1], callee = after[depth];
          const where = `${input}: the call at instruction ${e.at} of function ${e.func}, to function ${ins[1]}`;
          if (after.length !== depth + 1 || !callee || callee.func !== ins[1] || callee.at !== 0) fail({ checked: 'the frame a call pushes', input: where, observed: `state.frames is ${show(after)}`, expected: `${depth + 1} frames, the last { func: ${ins[1]}, at: 0 }` });

          while (m.running && m.state.frames.length > depth) m.step();
          const back = view(m)[depth - 1];
          if (!back || back.func !== e.func || back.at !== e.at + 1) fail({ checked: 'where the caller carries on after the callee returns', input: where, observed: `the caller's frame is ${show(back)} after the return`, expected: `{ func: ${e.func}, at: ${e.at + 1} }` });
        }
        if (found < 2) fail({ checked: 'game_init calls two defined functions', input, observed: `${found} found`, expected: 'new_round and update_hud are both called' });
      }
    },
