`courses/time-travel-debugger-part-two/fallback/part-one-debugger.mjs`:

```mjs
// Part one's worked debugger (courses/time-travel-debugger), supplied so part two
// can be done without part one. It is the answer to part one: reading it spoils
// that course. `node lab.mjs wall` uses it when you do not name your own.
import { initial, execute, validateProgram, clone, matches } from './vm.mjs';
export class Debugger {
  constructor(program) {
    this.program = validateProgram(program); this.state = initial(); this.events = [];
    this.breakpoints = []; this.watches = new Set(); this.points = [{ label: 'initial', tick: 0, state: initial() }];
  }
  inspect() { return clone(this.state); }
  step() {
    if (this.state.halted) return null;
    const { state, event } = execute(this.program, this.state);
    this.state = state;
    if (this.events.length < state.tick) this.events.push(clone(event));
    return clone(event);
  }
  addBreakpoint(spec) {
    if (!spec || !Number.isInteger(spec.pc) || spec.pc < 0 || spec.pc >= this.program.length) throw Error('Breakpoint: pc is outside program.');
    if (spec.condition) matches(this.state, spec.condition);
    this.breakpoints.push(clone(spec));
  }
  watch(address) {
    if (!Number.isInteger(address) || address < 0 || address > 7) throw Error('Watchpoint: address must be 0–7.');
    this.watches.add(address);
  }
  run(limit = 1000) {
    if (!Number.isInteger(limit) || limit < 1 || limit > 10000) throw Error('Run: limit must be an integer from 1–10000.');
    for (let n = 0; n < limit; n++) {
      if (this.state.halted) return this.stop('halt');
      if (this.breakpoints.some(b => b.pc === this.state.pc && (!b.condition || matches(this.state, b.condition)))) return this.stop('breakpoint');
      const event = this.step();
      const changed = event.writes.find(w => this.watches.has(w.address) && w.before !== w.after);
      if (changed) return { ...this.stop('watchpoint'), write: clone(changed) };
      if (this.state.halted) return this.stop('halt');
    }
    return this.stop('limit');
  }
  stop(reason) { return { reason, tick: this.state.tick, pc: this.state.pc }; }
  trace() { return clone(this.events); }
  checkpoint(label) {
    if (typeof label !== 'string' || !label.trim()) throw Error('Checkpoint: provide a label.');
    const point = { label, tick: this.state.tick, state: this.inspect() };
    this.points.push(clone(point)); return clone(point);
  }
  seek(tick) {
    if (!Number.isInteger(tick) || tick < 0 || tick > this.events.length) throw Error('Seek: tick must be within the recorded history.');
    const point = this.points.filter(p => p.tick <= tick).sort((a,b) => b.tick-a.tick)[0];
    let state = clone(point.state);
    while (state.tick < tick) state = execute(this.program, state).state;
    this.state = state; return this.inspect();
  }
  reverseFind(condition, beforeTick = this.state.tick) {
    matches(this.state, condition);
    if (!Number.isInteger(beforeTick) || beforeTick < 0 || beforeTick > this.events.length + 1) throw Error('Reverse search: invalid exclusive bound.');
    const original = this.inspect();
    for (let tick = beforeTick - 1; tick >= 0; tick--) {
      this.seek(tick);
      if (matches(this.state, condition)) return tick;
    }
    this.state = original; return null;
  }
}

```

`courses/time-travel-debugger-part-two/lab.mjs`:

```mjs
#!/usr/bin/env node
// The lab for part two. Run `node lab.mjs` with no arguments for the commands.
import { existsSync, mkdirSync, readFileSync, writeFileSync, readdirSync, rmSync, cpSync, statSync } from 'node:fs';
import { createHash, randomUUID } from 'node:crypto';
import { dirname, join, resolve, basename } from 'node:path';
import { fileURLToPath, pathToFileURL } from 'node:url';
import { runUnit, UNITS, listCases } from './checks/run.mjs';
import { readProgram, loadProgram } from './public/program.mjs';
import { availableParallelism } from 'node:os';
import { makeWorld } from './public/world.mjs';
import { hashMemory } from './public/hash.mjs';
import { session, plan } from './public/sessions.mjs';
// Plain reads and writes, not fs.copyFileSync: copying file metadata can fail
// with EPERM where the project folder belongs to another user.
const copyFileSync = (from, to) => writeFileSync(to, readFileSync(from));

const root = dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url));
const config = JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(root, 'course.json'), 'utf8'));
const sha = (x) => createHash('sha256').update(x).digest('hex');
const say = (s = '') => console.log(s);

const USAGE = `Usage: node lab.mjs COMMAND ...
  start PROJECT                     make your project folder with the starter files
  check PROJECT NN|all [--help-used TEXT]
                                    run the checks of unit NN (08 to 13) on your files
  status PROJECT                    list your saved check attempts and the predictions you
                                    committed, and the questions still waiting for one
  question ID                       show a prediction question (IDs are in the lessons)
  predict PROJECT ID ANSWER [--help-used TEXT]
                                    commit an answer before reading on, then see the reason
  agree PROJECT [--game lob|lob2] [--seed N] [--mode M]
                                    run your machine beside Node's WebAssembly engine
  wall PROJECT [--part-one FILE] [--steps N]
                                    measure part one's debugger on the real game
  record PROJECT --out FILE [--game lob] [--seed 5] [--mode 1] [--shots 2] [--world 42]
                                    record a game with your record() and save the recording
  replay PROJECT FILE               replay a recording with your replay()
  tamper FILE --out FILE (--answer K --add X | --answer K --arg X | --call K --key CODE)
                                    copy a recording with one answer's result or argument,
                                    or one key press, changed (numbered from 0)
  diverge PROJECT ORIGINAL TAMPERED find where they part with your firstDivergence()
  decoder FILE                      check your own Sightline decoder against the listings
  ladder                            list the capstone builds, their symptoms and budgets
  investigate PROJECT N             run investigations/N.txt and show its answer and cost`;

function project(dir) {
  const p = resolve(dir);
  if (!existsSync(join(p, 'PROJECT.json'))) throw Error(`${dir} is not a project folder: run node lab.mjs start ${dir} first`);
  return p;
}

function start(dir) {
  const target = resolve(dir);
  mkdirSync(target); // refuses an existing folder, so a project is never overwritten
  for (const f of config.workFiles) {
    mkdirSync(dirname(join(target, f)), { recursive: true });
    copyFileSync(join(root, 'starter', f), join(target, f));
  }
  writeFileSync(join(target, 'PROJECT.json'), JSON.stringify({ course: config.id, started: new Date().toISOString() }, null, 2) + '\n');
  writeFileSync(join(target, 'report.md'), '# Investigation notes\n\n## Predictions\n\n## Evidence\n\n## Explanations\n\n## Help used\n');
  say(`Created ${dir} with ${config.workFiles.join(', ')}.`);
  say(`Read lessons/08.md, then run: node lab.mjs check ${dir} 08`);
  say('The untouched starter fails every check with "not written yet".');
}

function line(r) {
  if (r.pass) return `PASS ${r.id}`;
  if (r.kind === 'timeout') return `FAIL ${r.id}: did not finish within ${r.limitMs / 1000} s`;
  if (r.kind === 'not-written') return `FAIL ${r.id}: ${r.message}`;
  if (r.kind === 'failure') return `FAIL ${r.id}: ${r.fields.checked ?? r.title}`;
  return `FAIL ${r.id}: ${r.message}${r.where ? ` (${r.where})` : ''}`;
}

async function check(dir, unit, help) {
  const p = project(dir);
  const units = unit === 'all' ? UNITS : [unit];
  if (!units.every((u) => UNITS.includes(u))) throw Error(`Choose a unit: ${UNITS.join(', ')} or all`);
  const attempt = join(p, 'attempts', `${new Date().toISOString().replaceAll(':', '-')}-${randomUUID().slice(0, 8)}`);
  mkdirSync(attempt, { recursive: true });
  copyFileSync(join(p, 'PROJECT.json'), join(attempt, 'PROJECT.json'));
  // The chapter route commands record where units 08 to 12 started; a receipt keeps them.
  const meta = JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(attempt, 'PROJECT.json'), 'utf8'));
  const initialRoute = {};
  for (const key of ['unit08_start_route', 'unit09_start_route', 'unit10_start_route', 'unit11_start_route', 'unit12_start_route']) if (['write', 'supplied'].includes(meta[key])) initialRoute[key] = meta[key];
  for (const f of config.workFiles) if (existsSync(join(p, f))) { mkdirSync(dirname(join(attempt, f)), { recursive: true }); copyFileSync(join(p, f), join(attempt, f)); }
  let allPass = true;
  const saved = [];
  for (const u of units) {
    const { title } = await listCases(u);
    say(`Unit ${u}: ${title}`);
    const report = await runUnit(p, u, { jobs: Math.min(4, availableParallelism()) });
    for (const r of report.results) {
      say(line(r));
      if (!r.pass && r.requirement) say(`     requirement: ${r.requirement}`);
      if (!r.pass && r.kind === 'failure') {
        const f = r.fields;
        if (f.input) say(`     input:    ${f.input}`);
        if (f.observed) say(`     yours:    ${f.observed}`);
        if (f.expected) say(`     required: ${f.expected}`);
        if (f.diff) say(`     first difference: ${f.diff}`);
      }
      if (!r.pass && r.reread) say(`     read ${r.reread}`);
    }
    const passed = report.results.filter((r) => r.pass).length;
    say(`${passed} of ${report.results.length} checks pass in unit ${u}.\n`);
    allPass &&= report.pass;
    saved.push({ unit: u, results: report.results.map(({ id, pass, kind, fields, message, ms, requirement }) => ({ id, pass, kind, requirement, fields, message, ms })) });
  }
  writeFileSync(join(attempt, 'receipt.json'), JSON.stringify({ course: config.id, ...initialRoute, help_used: help, units: saved, at: new Date().toISOString() }, null, 2) + '\n');
  if (units.length > 1) say(allPass ? `All ${units.length} units pass.` : 'Some checks fail.');
  say(`Help used (--help-used): ${help}`);
  say(`Saved this attempt in ${attempt}. A pass covers these cases only.`);
  process.exitCode = allPass ? 0 : 1;
}

// Every prediction saved under attempts/, oldest first.
function predictions(p) {
  const folder = join(p, 'attempts');
  if (!existsSync(folder)) return [];
  return readdirSync(folder).sort().map((name) => join(folder, name, 'prediction.json')).filter((f) => existsSync(f)).map((f) => JSON.parse(readFileSync(f, 'utf8')));
}

// The questions the lessons ask, in the order a reader meets them.
function askedInOrder() {
  const asked = Object.entries(practice()).filter(([, q]) => !q.retryOnly).map(([id, q]) => {
    const file = join(root, 'lessons', `${q.lesson}.md`);
    const at = existsSync(file) ? readFileSync(file, 'utf8').indexOf(`predict project ${id} `) : -1;
    return { id, lesson: q.lesson, at: at < 0 ? Infinity : at };
  });
  return asked.sort((a, b) => a.lesson.localeCompare(b.lesson) || a.at - b.at).map((x) => x.id);
}

function status(dir) {
  const p = project(dir);
  const folder = join(p, 'attempts');
  const names = existsSync(folder) ? readdirSync(folder).sort() : [];
  say('Check attempts:');
  let checks = 0;
  for (const name of names) {
    const file = join(folder, name, 'receipt.json');
    if (!existsSync(file)) continue;
    const r = JSON.parse(readFileSync(file, 'utf8'));
    for (const u of r.units) { say(`  ${name} unit ${u.unit}: ${u.results.filter((x) => x.pass).length} of ${u.results.length} pass (help used: ${r.help_used ?? 'not declared'}${r.unit08_start_route ? '; unit 08 initial route: ' + r.unit08_start_route : ''}${r.unit09_start_route ? '; unit 09 initial route: ' + r.unit09_start_route : ''}${r.unit10_start_route ? '; unit 10 initial route: ' + r.unit10_start_route : ''}${r.unit11_start_route ? '; unit 11 initial route: ' + r.unit11_start_route : ''}${r.unit12_start_route ? '; unit 12 initial route: ' + r.unit12_start_route : ''})`); checks++; }
  }
  if (!checks) say('  none yet');
  // The new applications' checkers (examples/check-*.mjs) keep their own receipts:
  // slice-receipt.json, trim-receipt.json, rfind-receipt.json, vsources-receipt.json,
  // nline-receipt.json, changes-receipt.json.
  say('New-application attempts:');
  let applications = 0;
  for (const name of names) {
    const dir = join(folder, name);
    if (!statSync(dir).isDirectory()) continue;
    for (const file of readdirSync(dir).filter((f) => f.endsWith('-receipt.json'))) {
      let r;
      try { r = JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(dir, file), 'utf8')); } catch { continue; }
      const results = Array.isArray(r.results) ? r.results : [];
      say(`  ${name} ${r.application ?? file.replace('-receipt.json', '')}: ${results.filter((x) => x.pass).length} of ${results.length} cases pass (help used: ${r.help_used ?? 'not declared'})`);
      applications++;
    }
  }
  if (!applications) say('  none yet');
  const committed = predictions(p);
  const items = practice();
  // A question can be replaced by a new version; an answer to an earlier version stays in the
  // record, marked as such, and doesn't count as an answer to the current one.
  const current = (x) => (x.version ?? 1) === (items[x.id]?.version ?? 1);
  say('Predictions committed:');
  // A prediction lists its help only when it was declared with --help-used. Older records
  // saved the words "not declared" for an undeclared one, so those are left out too.
  const declared = (x) => x.help_used !== undefined && x.help_used !== 'not declared';
  for (const x of committed) say(`  ${x.id}: ${current(x) ? '' : '(an earlier version of this question) '}${x.correct ? 'right' : 'wrong'}, answer ${x.answer}${declared(x) ? ` (help used: ${x.help_used})` : ''}`);
  if (!committed.length) say('  none yet');
  const done = new Set(committed.filter(current).map((x) => x.id));
  const waiting = askedInOrder().filter((id) => !done.has(id));
  say(waiting.length ? `Asked in the lessons, not committed yet: ${waiting.join(', ')}` : 'Every question the lessons ask has a committed answer.');
  // practice-10: a question missed with no fresh case left in the course is asked again later.
  // Predictions are in time order, so the map keeps each question's latest answer.
  const latest = new Map(committed.filter(current).map((x) => [x.id, x]));
  const due = [...latest.values()].filter((x) => !x.correct && !items[x.id]?.retry).map((x) => x.id);
  if (due.length) say(`Due for another try, after your next lesson: ${due.join(', ')}. Ask each with node lab.mjs question ID, then commit it again.`);
}

const practice = () => JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(root, 'practice.json'), 'utf8'));
function item(id) {
  const q = practice()[id];
  if (!q) throw Error(`Unknown question ${id}. The lessons name each one.`);
  return q;
}
function normal(a) { return String(a).trim().toLowerCase().replace(/\s+/g, ' '); }
function predict(dir, id, answer, help) {
  const p = project(dir);
  const q = item(id);
  if (typeof answer !== 'string' || !answer.trim()) throw Error(`Give an answer: node lab.mjs predict ${dir} ${id} ANSWER`);
  const accepted = [q.expected, ...(q.accept ?? [])].map(normal);
  const correct = accepted.includes(normal(answer));
  const earlier = predictions(p).filter((x) => x.id === id && (x.version ?? 1) === (q.version ?? 1));
  const record = { kind: 'prediction', id, version: q.version, question: q.question, answer, ...(help === undefined ? {} : { help_used: help }), correct, expected: q.expected, at: new Date().toISOString() };
  const folder = join(p, 'attempts', `${new Date().toISOString().replaceAll(':', '-')}-${id}`);
  mkdirSync(folder, { recursive: true });
  writeFileSync(join(folder, 'prediction.json'), JSON.stringify(record, null, 2) + '\n');
  say(`Your answer: ${answer}`);
  if (help !== undefined) say(`Help used (--help-used): ${help}`);
  if (earlier.length) say(`You committed ${id} before, answering ${earlier.map((x) => `${x.answer} (${x.correct ? 'right' : 'wrong'})`).join(' and ')}. This answer is saved as well.`);
  say(correct ? 'Correct.' : `Not this time. The answer is ${q.expected}.`);
  const wrong = (q.wrong ?? []).find((w) => normal(w.answer) === normal(answer));
  say(wrong ? wrong.feedback : q.reason);
  // A re-ask sits in a later lesson's list of earlier ideas; the idea is taught where its original is.
  const home = q.variantOf ? item(q.variantOf) : q;
  if (!correct && home.section) say(q.retry && q.retry !== id
    ? `Read lesson ${home.lesson}, "${home.section}", then try a fresh case of the same idea: node lab.mjs question ${q.retry}`
    : `Read lesson ${home.lesson}, "${home.section}". The course has no other case of this idea, so ask this one again after your next lesson: node lab.mjs status project lists it as due, and node lab.mjs question ${id} shows it.`);
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------------ agree

async function learnerMachine(p) {
  const mod = await import(pathToFileURL(join(p, 'machine.mjs')).href);
  if (typeof mod.Machine !== 'function') throw Error(`${join(p, 'machine.mjs')} exports no Machine class`);
  return mod.Machine;
}

async function agree(dir, opts) {
  const p = project(dir);
  const Machine = await learnerMachine(p);
  const game = opts.game ?? 'lob';
  const seed = Number(opts.seed ?? 11), mode = Number(opts.mode ?? 1);
  const program = readProgram(game);
  const calls = session({ seed, mode, plan: plan({ seed, shots: 3 }) });
  const w1 = makeWorld(seed + 100), w2 = makeWorld(seed + 100);
  const m = new Machine(program, w1.imports);
  const { instance } = await WebAssembly.instantiate(readFileSync(join(root, 'targets', `${game}.wasm`)), { env: w2.imports });
  const getters = program.exports.filter((e) => e.kind === 'func' && !e.name.startsWith('game_')).map((e) => e.name);
  const started = performance.now();
  for (let k = 0; k < calls.length; k++) {
    const { name, args } = calls[k];
    const a = m.invoke(name, args), b = instance.exports[name](...args);
    if (!Object.is(a ?? null, b ?? null)) return say(`Call ${k} (${name}): yours returned ${a}, Node's engine ${b}.`);
    if (hashMemory(m.state.memory) !== hashMemory(new Uint8Array(instance.exports.memory.buffer))) return say(`Memory differs after call ${k} (${name} ${args.join(' ')}). Compare the bytes with a watch on the write that differs.`);
    for (const g of getters) {
      const x = m.invoke(g, []), y = instance.exports[g]();
      if (!Object.is(x, y)) return say(`After call ${k} (${name}), ${g} returns ${x} on yours and ${y} on Node's engine.`);
    }
  }
  const ms = performance.now() - started;
  say(`${game} seed ${seed} mode ${mode}: your machine and Node's engine agree after every one of ${calls.length} calls`);
  say(`(return values, ${getters.length} getters and the memory hash each time). Your machine ran ${m.state.tick} instructions in ${(ms / 1000).toFixed(2)} s.`);
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------------ wall

async function wall(dir, opts) {
  const p = project(dir);
  const Machine = await learnerMachine(p);
  const partOne = opts['part-one'] ? resolve(opts['part-one']) : join(root, 'fallback', 'part-one-debugger.mjs');
  if (!existsSync(partOne)) throw Error(`no part-one debugger at ${partOne}`);
  const steps = Number(opts.steps ?? 20000);
  const work = join(p, '.wall');
  rmSync(work, { recursive: true, force: true });
  mkdirSync(work, { recursive: true });
  copyFileSync(join(root, 'public', 'part-one-vm.mjs'), join(work, 'vm.mjs'));
  copyFileSync(partOne, join(work, 'debugger.mjs'));
  const { Debugger } = await import(pathToFileURL(join(work, 'debugger.mjs')).href);
  const program = readProgram('lob');
  const calls = session({ seed: 3, mode: 0, plan: plan({ seed: 3, shots: 3 }) });
  // Mode 0 asks only sin and cos, whose answers depend on their arguments alone,
  // so part one's debugger can run any stretch of the game again by itself.
  const imports = makeWorld(1).imports;

  let t = performance.now();
  const plain = new Machine(program, imports);
  for (const c of calls) plain.invoke(c.name, c.args);
  const plainMs = performance.now() - t;
  const total = plain.state.tick;

  const s = { Machine, program, imports, calls, length: Math.max(...program.functions.map((f) => f.code.length)) };
  const d = new Debugger(s);
  const bytes = structuredClone(d.inspect()).machine.memory.byteLength;
  t = performance.now();
  let n = 0;
  for (; n < steps; n++) d.step();
  const stepMs = (performance.now() - t) / n;
  const plainStepMs = plainMs / total;

  // Part one's reverseFind replays from the nearest checkpoint for every earlier
  // tick it tries. Time one real search: on a fresh debugger, checkpoint where
  // game_init ends (its first 61,000 or so instructions only clear memory),
  // step 3,000 more and ask for the byte value one write about 30 ticks back replaced.
  const initMachine = new Machine(program, imports);
  initMachine.invoke(calls[0].name, calls[0].args);
  const init = initMachine.state.tick;
  const d2 = new Debugger(s);
  for (let k = 0; k < init; k++) d2.step();
  d2.checkpoint('after game_init');
  for (let k = 0; k < 3000; k++) d2.step();
  const now = init + 3000;
  const write = d2.trace().filter((e) => e.tick <= now - 30 && e.writes.some((w) => (w.before & 255) !== (w.after & 255))).at(-1);
  if (!write) throw Error(`No write changed a byte between tick ${init} and tick ${now - 30}, so there is no value to search back for.`);
  const w = write.writes.find((x) => (x.before & 255) !== (x.after & 255));
  const address = w.address, equals = w.before & 255;
  t = performance.now();
  const found = d2.reverseFind({ kind: 'mem', address, equals });
  const searchMs = performance.now() - t;

  const day = (ms) => ms < 1000 ? `${ms.toFixed(0)} ms` : ms < 120000 ? `${(ms / 1000).toFixed(1)} s` : ms < 7200000 ? `${(ms / 60000).toFixed(0)} min` : ms < 172800000 ? `${(ms / 3600000).toFixed(1)} hours` : `${(ms / 86400000).toFixed(0)} days`;
  // One question asked at the end of the run whose answer lies 1,000 ticks back:
  // part one tries 1,000 earlier ticks and replays each from tick 0.
  const questionSteps = 1000 * total;
  const result = {
    run: { calls: calls.length, instructions: total },
    copy_bytes_per_step: bytes,
    microseconds_per_step_with_copy: +(stepMs * 1000).toFixed(2),
    microseconds_per_step_machine_alone: +(plainStepMs * 1000).toFixed(3),
    slowdown: +(stepMs / plainStepMs).toFixed(0),
    one_pass_with_copies_ms: +(stepMs * total).toFixed(0),
    one_pass_machine_alone_ms: +plainMs.toFixed(0),
    reverse_find: { from_tick: now, checkpoint_at: init, found, ticks_back: found === null ? null : now - found, ms: +searchMs.toFixed(0) },
    question_1000_back_at_end_ms: +(questionSteps * stepMs).toFixed(0),
    part_one: partOne === join(root, 'fallback', 'part-one-debugger.mjs') ? 'fallback' : partOne,
  };
  writeFileSync(join(p, 'wall.json'), JSON.stringify(result, null, 2) + '\n');
  say(`Part one's debugger (${result.part_one === 'fallback' ? 'the supplied fallback' : basename(partOne)}) on your machine, Lob seed 3 mode 0:`);
  say(`  the run: ${calls.length} calls, ${total} instructions; your machine alone runs it in ${day(plainMs)}`);
  say(`  every step copies the whole state: ${bytes} bytes of memory and the rest`);
  say(`  measured over ${n} steps: ${(stepMs * 1000).toFixed(1)} microseconds a step, against ${(plainStepMs * 1000).toFixed(2)} for your machine alone (${result.slowdown} times slower)`);
  say(`  one pass over the whole run with copies: ${day(stepMs * total)}`);
  say(found === null
    ? `  one reverseFind from tick ${now}, with a checkpoint at tick ${init}: ${day(searchMs)}, and it found no tick`
    : `  one reverseFind from tick ${now}, with a checkpoint at tick ${init}, for a value ${now - found} ticks back: ${day(searchMs)} (it found tick ${found})`);
  say(`  the same kind of question at the end of the run, answer 1,000 ticks back: about ${day(questionSteps * stepMs)}`);
  say(`Saved ${join(p, 'wall.json')}.`);
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------------ record and replay

async function learnerRecorder(p) {
  const Machine = await learnerMachine(p);
  const proto = Machine.prototype;
  if (!proto.__counted) {
    const original = proto.step;
    const c = { count: 0, reset() { this.count = 0; } };
    proto.step = function (...args) { c.count++; return original.apply(this, args); };
    Object.defineProperty(proto, '__counted', { value: c });
  }
  const rec = await import(pathToFileURL(join(p, 'recorder.mjs')).href);
  return { ...rec, cost: proto.__counted };
}

async function recordCmd(dir, o) {
  const p = project(dir);
  if (!o.out) throw Error('Name the file to write: --out FILE');
  const game = o.game ?? 'lob', seed = Number(o.seed ?? 5), mode = Number(o.mode ?? 1), shots = Number(o.shots ?? 2), worldSeed = Number(o.world ?? 42);
  const { record } = await learnerRecorder(p);
  const calls = session({ seed, mode, plan: plan({ seed, shots }) });
  const recording = record(readProgram(game), makeWorld(worldSeed).imports, calls);
  writeFileSync(resolve(o.out), JSON.stringify(recording) + '\n');
  const kinds = {};
  for (const a of recording.answers ?? []) kinds[a.name] = (kinds[a.name] ?? 0) + 1;
  say(`Recorded ${game} seed ${seed} mode ${mode}, ${shots} shots, world ${worldSeed}: ${recording.calls?.length} calls, ${recording.answers?.length} answers (${Object.entries(kinds).map(([k, v]) => `${k} ${v}`).join(', ')}).`);
  say(`Wrote ${o.out}, ${JSON.stringify(recording).length} bytes.`);
}

async function replayCmd(dir, file) {
  const p = project(dir);
  const { replay, cost } = await learnerRecorder(p);
  const recording = JSON.parse(readFileSync(resolve(file), 'utf8'));
  cost.reset();
  try {
    const r = replay(readProgram(recording.program), recording);
    say(`Replayed ${recording.calls.length} calls without the world: every result and memory hash matches the recording (${cost.count} instructions).`);
    return r;
  } catch (e) {
    if (e.divergence) say(`The replay left its recording at tick ${e.divergence.tick}, call ${e.divergence.call}: ${e.divergence.reason}`);
    else throw e;
  }
}

function tamperCmd(file, o) {
  if (!o.out) throw Error('Name the file to write: --out FILE');
  const r = JSON.parse(readFileSync(resolve(file), 'utf8'));
  if (o.answer !== undefined) {
    const a = r.answers[Number(o.answer)];
    if (!a) throw Error(`The recording has ${r.answers.length} answers, numbered from 0.`);
    if (o.arg !== undefined) {
      if (!a.args.length) throw Error(`Answer ${o.answer} (${a.name}) has no argument to change.`);
      const before = a.args[0];
      a.args[0] = a.args[0] + Number(o.arg);
      say(`Answer ${o.answer} (${a.name}) now says it was asked ${a.name}(${a.args[0]}), not ${a.name}(${before}).`);
    } else {
      const before = a.result;
      a.result = Math.fround(a.result + Number(o.add ?? 0.25));
      say(`Answer ${o.answer} (${a.name}) changed from ${before} to ${a.result}.`);
    }
  } else if (o.call !== undefined) {
    const c = r.calls[Number(o.call)];
    if (!c || c.name !== 'game_key') throw Error(`Call ${o.call} is not a key press.`);
    say(`Call ${o.call} changed from key ${c.args[0]} to key ${o.key}.`);
    c.args = [Number(o.key)];
  } else throw Error('Say what to change: --answer K --add X, or --call K --key CODE');
  writeFileSync(resolve(o.out), JSON.stringify(r) + '\n');
  say(`Wrote ${o.out}. Its hashes are still the original's.`);
}

async function divergeCmd(dir, a, b) {
  const p = project(dir);
  const { firstDivergence, cost } = await learnerRecorder(p);
  const original = JSON.parse(readFileSync(resolve(a), 'utf8')), tampered = JSON.parse(readFileSync(resolve(b), 'utf8'));
  cost.reset();
  const t = firstDivergence(readProgram(original.program), original, tampered);
  say(t === null ? 'The two replays never differ.' : `Memory first differs after tick ${t}.`);
  say(`Your firstDivergence ran ${cost.count} instructions.`);
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------------ decoder

async function decoder(file) {
  if (!file) throw Error('Name your decoder: node lab.mjs decoder FILE');
  if (!existsSync(resolve(file)) || !statSync(resolve(file)).isFile()) throw Error(`no decoder at ${resolve(file)}`);
  const mod = await import(pathToFileURL(resolve(file)).href);
  if (typeof mod.parseModule !== 'function' || typeof mod.decode !== 'function') throw Error(`${file} must export parseModule(bytes) and decode(mod, index), as Sightline's wasm.mjs does`);
  const norm = (v) => typeof v === 'bigint' ? `${v}n` : Array.isArray(v) ? v.map(norm) : v;
  for (const game of ['lob', 'lob2']) {
    const program = JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(root, 'programs', `${game}.json`), 'utf8'));
    const m = mod.parseModule(new Uint8Array(readFileSync(join(root, 'targets', `${game}.wasm`))));
    let compared = 0;
    for (const f of program.functions) {
      const ours = f.code.map((ins, k) => ({ offset: f.offsets[k], code: ins }));
      const theirs = mod.decode(m, f.index).map((i) => ({ offset: i.offset, code: [i.op, ...norm(i.imm)] }));
      for (let k = 0; k < Math.max(ours.length, theirs.length); k++) {
        if (JSON.stringify(ours[k]) !== JSON.stringify(theirs[k])) {
          return say(`${game}: function ${f.index}, instruction ${k}: your decoder gives ${JSON.stringify(theirs[k])}, the listing has ${JSON.stringify(ours[k])}.`);
        }
        compared++;
      }
    }
    say(`${game}: your decoder gives the same ${compared} instructions (name, immediates and file position) as programs/${game}.json.`);
  }
  say('Your listings and the supplied ones are the same, so nothing else changes: keep using programs/*.json.');
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------------ ladder

function ladder() {
  const rungs = JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(root, 'ladder.json'), 'utf8'));
  for (const r of rungs) {
    say(`${r.title}: ${r.wasm}, recording ${r.recording}`);
    say(`  ${r.symptom}`);
    say(`  replay budget: ${r.budget ?? 'not set'} instructions\n`);
  }
  say('Write your investigation in investigations/N.txt and run node lab.mjs investigate PROJECT N.');
}

async function investigate(dir, n) {
  const p = project(dir);
  const { runInvestigation } = await import(pathToFileURL(join(root, 'debug.mjs')).href);
  const rungs = JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(root, 'ladder.json'), 'utf8'));
  const rung = rungs.find((r) => String(r.n) === String(n));
  if (!rung) throw Error(`No build ${n}; node lab.mjs ladder lists them.`);
  const script = join(p, 'investigations', `${n}.txt`);
  if (!existsSync(script)) throw Error(`Write ${script} first: one debugger command per line.`);
  const r = await runInvestigation(p, rung, readFileSync(script, 'utf8'), { echo: true });
  say(`\nInstructions replayed: ${r.replayed}${rung.budget ? ` of a budget of ${rung.budget}` : ''}.`);
  say(r.answer ? `Your answer: function ${r.answer.func}${r.answer.name ? ` (${r.answer.name})` : ''}, instruction ${r.answer.at}, address ${r.answer.address}, tick ${r.answer.tick}.` : 'The script gave no answer: end it with the answer command.');
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------------ main

function options(rest) {
  const o = {}, plain = [];
  for (let i = 0; i < rest.length; i++) {
    if (rest[i].startsWith('--')) {
      if (i + 1 >= rest.length) throw Error(`${rest[i]} needs a value after it.`);
      o[rest[i].slice(2)] = rest[i + 1]; i++;
    } else plain.push(rest[i]);
  }
  return { o, plain };
}

const [verb, ...rest] = process.argv.slice(2);
try {
  const { o, plain } = options(rest);
  if (!verb) say(USAGE);
  else if (verb === 'start') start(plain[0] ?? (() => { throw Error('Name a new folder: node lab.mjs start project'); })());
  else if (verb === 'check') await check(plain[0], plain[1], o['help-used'] ?? 'not declared');
  else if (verb === 'status') status(plain[0]);
  else if (verb === 'question') { const q = item(plain[0]); say(q.question); say(`Answer format: ${q.format}`); say(`Commit with: node lab.mjs predict PROJECT ${plain[0]} ANSWER`); }
  else if (verb === 'predict') predict(plain[0], plain[1], plain.slice(2).join(' '), o['help-used']);
  else if (verb === 'agree') await agree(plain[0], o);
  else if (verb === 'wall') await wall(plain[0], o);
  else if (verb === 'decoder') await decoder(plain[0]);
  else if (verb === 'record') await recordCmd(plain[0], o);
  else if (verb === 'replay') await replayCmd(plain[0], plain[1]);
  else if (verb === 'tamper') tamperCmd(plain[0], o);
  else if (verb === 'diverge') await divergeCmd(plain[0], plain[1], plain[2]);
  else if (verb === 'ladder') ladder();
  else if (verb === 'investigate') await investigate(plain[0], plain[1]);
  else { say(USAGE); process.exitCode = 2; }
} catch (e) {
  console.error(e.code === 'EEXIST' ? 'That folder exists: choose a new name. Nothing was overwritten.' : e.message);
  process.exitCode = 2;
}

```

  <main id="chapter"><h1 id="08-a-machine-worth-debugging">08 · A machine worth debugging</h1>
<p>Part one&#39;s machine had 7 instructions and 8 memory cells, so its hardest bug could be found by reading the program. Lob, the artillery game this part debugs, is 2,806 instructions in 25 functions over 131,072 bytes of memory, and one game frame of it, one call to <code>game_tick</code> with no shell in the air, runs 827 of them. By the end of this lesson your <code>machine.mjs</code> will run Lob and a second game, Lob II, one instruction at a time and agree with Node&#39;s own WebAssembly engine after every call, and you will have measured what part one&#39;s debugger costs on it.</p>
<p>Part two assumes part one&#39;s ideas: a tick is one instruction, a trace is a list of events, a checkpoint is a saved state you can replay from, running the program again from that moment. If you skipped part one, read its lessons 01 to 06, which build its debugger (it&#39;s a separate course, not part of this copy). You can use the supplied <code>fallback/part-one-debugger.mjs</code> wherever this course asks for your part-one debugger.</p>
<h2 id="start">Start</h2>
<p>Run these commands from this course&#39;s directory, with Node 22 or later. No packages or network access are needed. First borrow the finished interpreter for one minute:</p>
<figure class="code-example"><figcaption><strong>Terminal command</strong></figcaption><pre tabindex="0" aria-label="Terminal command; code scrolls horizontally when needed"><code><span class="cex-line">node examples/step-getter.mjs</span></code></pre><div class="cex-foot"> Select code to copy. Scroll horizontally if needed.</div></figure>
<p>It executes the real game&#39;s <code>r_px</code> getter one instruction at a time. The game has not been initialized: its pointer and the bytes read through that pointer are zero. This is a probe of the interpreter, not a moving shell yet.</p>
<figure class="code-example"><figcaption><strong>Four instructions through cold memory</strong><span class="cex-location">examples/getter-output.txt</span></figcaption><pre tabindex="0" aria-label="Four instructions through cold memory; code scrolls horizontally when needed"><code><span class="cex-line">begin: tick=0, running=true</span>
<span class="cex-line">1 i32.const stack=[0]</span>
<span class="cex-line">2 i32.load stack=[0]</span>
<span class="cex-line">3 f32.load stack=[0]</span>
<span class="cex-line">4 end stack=[]</span>
<span class="cex-line">returned=0; this is cold memory, before game_init</span></code></pre><div class="cex-foot"> Select code to copy. Scroll horizontally if needed.</div></figure>
<p>Notice that <code>begin</code> leaves the tick at zero. The final <code>end</code> is an instruction too; it returns the value and empties the stack. You will build those boundaries below, then use the same interpreter to run the whole game.</p>
<p><strong>Code scope:</strong> walk through six marked changes, about 125 lines including blank lines, in <code>project/machine.mjs</code>. The roughly 650-line end checkpoint supplies the remaining opcode cases, program loading and format/opcode checks; you will tour those parts where their behavior matters. It implements this unit&#39;s Machine only, not the later recorder, debugger, query engine or capstone answers.</p>
<p><strong>Time:</strong> allow about 25–35 minutes to read and 2–4 hours to implement, diagnose and try the new application. These are planning estimates, not measured learner times. You can stop after any section; save the file and keep the same project next time.</p>
<p>Choose a route. Each command below refuses an existing path, including an empty folder; use a new name if you already have <code>project/</code>.</p>
<ul>
<li><strong>Type in the important parts:</strong> <code>node examples/start-chapter.mjs project write</code>. This copies <code>starter/machine-build.mjs</code>, with six deliberate holes and the supporting implementation supplied. Type or paste each located listing below.</li>
<li><strong>Start with working code:</strong> <code>node examples/start-chapter.mjs project supplied</code>. This copies <code>examples/machine-checkpoint.mjs</code>. Follow each trace and inspect each marked region instead of transcribing it, then do the failure/repair and new application. This is supplied implementation, not your own from-scratch work.</li>
<li><strong>Use AI for the changes:</strong> start with the type-in route (<code>write</code>). Give it <code>API.md</code>, this lesson and your file, one region at a time. Ask it to explain each state change; test and inspect what it writes. Record the actual assistance you used.</li>
</ul>
<p>On the type-in route every hole is filled from a listing printed in full in the lesson. The code you design yourself is each unit&#39;s new application (in this unit, the budgeted runner near the end) and, in unit 13, the investigations of builds 2 to 6.</p>
<p>Prefer a completely blank implementation? The original <code>node lab.mjs start project</code> route remains available. It creates method stubs without the supporting opcode implementation; filling those from the API is extra work beyond this walkthrough.</p>
<p>Run the initial check with the description matching your starting code:</p>
<figure class="code-example"><figcaption><strong>Terminal command</strong></figcaption><pre tabindex="0" aria-label="Terminal command; code scrolls horizontally when needed"><code><span class="cex-line"># Type-in route (write), including AI users before requesting changes:</span>
<span class="cex-line">node lab.mjs check project 08 --help-used &quot;chapter write starter; six regions unfinished&quot;</span>
<span class="cex-line"># Supplied route:</span>
<span class="cex-line">node lab.mjs check project 08 --help-used &quot;supplied Machine checkpoint; initial baseline&quot;</span></code></pre><div class="cex-foot"> Select code to copy. Scroll horizontally if needed.</div></figure>
<p>The helper records the initial <code>write</code> or <code>supplied</code> route in <code>PROJECT.json</code>. That describes where you began, not who wrote your current code. Keep using <code>--help-used</code> to record the actual assistance for each attempt.</p>
<p>The type-in route initially fails all checks with <code>not written yet</code>. The supplied route should pass them. Either result is a baseline, not evidence of understanding. The lab retains this attempt and your code under <code>project/attempts/</code>.</p>
<p>Edit only your project. Keep the <code>// region: NAME</code> and <code>// endregion: NAME</code> markers. A listing replaces <strong>everything between its matching pair</strong>, including any unfinished method there; it does not add a second copy of the method. The six replacements are <code>initial-state</code>, <code>call-entry</code>, <code>step-start</code>, <code>return-frame</code>, <code>branch</code> and <code>memory</code>, in that order. The listings omit those marker lines. <code>API.md</code> remains the complete Machine contract.</p>
<p>To recover later without losing edits, create <code>project-recovery</code> with the supplied route and compare its file with yours. Do not copy a checkpoint over your attempt.</p>
<h2 id="what-you-are-given">What you are given</h2>
<p>Lob was written in C and compiled to WebAssembly, a machine code that runs in browsers and in Node. You get the compiled file, <code>targets/lob.wasm</code>, and the same file decoded into a JSON listing, <code>programs/lob.json</code>. Decoding is taught in the Sightline course. Here you start from the listing. <code>API.md</code> ends with a table of all 62 instructions Lob and Lob II use.</p>
<p>The game is played through calls from outside: <code>game_init(seed, mode)</code> starts it, <code>game_key(code)</code> presses a key, and each call to <code>game_tick()</code> is one <strong>game frame</strong>, 1/60 of a second. The mode adds up the game&#39;s defences, switches worth 1, 2, 4 and 8 that <code>API.md</code> describes under &quot;public/sessions.mjs&quot;, and mode 0 has none. Between calls, exported functions called <strong>getters</strong>, such as <code>r_px</code> below, each return one value of the game.</p>
<p>The game shows three pieces of text, each kept in memory in a buffer of its own, apart from the game&#39;s state: the <strong>status line</strong> (angle, power, wind and score), the <strong>message line</strong> (ROUND 1, HIT!, SHORT BY 10) and the <strong>help text</strong>. The help text says the angle runs from 5 to 85, the power from 10 to 100, a shell landing within 12 paces of the flag scores, and the N key starts a new <strong>round</strong>, with a new flag position and new wind.</p>
<p>Lob II, the second game, was written separately and compiled the same way. Its file is <code>targets/lob2.wasm</code>, and its listing <code>programs/lob2.json</code>. It takes the same calls and keys and keeps the same three texts in memory, and its help text gives the same rules. Its eight getters, <code>g0</code> to <code>g7</code>, are deliberately named so they don&#39;t say what they hold, because Sightline asks its learners to work that out, and none of them returns the help text&#39;s address. Your machine runs both games, and one build in lesson 13 is a build of Lob II.</p>
<p>The listing has one entry per function. Here is the whole of function 14, the getter <code>r_px</code>, which returns the shell&#39;s horizontal position:</p>
<figure class="code-example"><figcaption><strong>WebAssembly instructions and stack trace</strong></figcaption><pre tabindex="0" aria-label="WebAssembly instructions and stack trace; code scrolls horizontally when needed"><code><span class="cex-line">0  [&quot;i32.const&quot;, 0]</span>
<span class="cex-line">1  [&quot;i32.load&quot;, 2, 78112]</span>
<span class="cex-line">2  [&quot;f32.load&quot;, 2, 40]</span>
<span class="cex-line">3  [&quot;end&quot;]</span></code></pre><div class="cex-foot"> Select code to copy. Scroll horizontally if needed.</div></figure>
<p>Each instruction is a name followed by its immediates, the numbers written into the code. A load&#39;s two immediates are an alignment hint, which you can ignore, and an offset.</p>
<p>WebAssembly is a <strong>stack machine</strong>. Instructions take their operands from the top of a value stack and push their results back on it. Trace <code>r_px</code> by hand, writing the stack after each instruction, top on the right:</p>
<figure class="code-example"><figcaption><strong>WebAssembly instructions and stack trace</strong></figcaption><pre tabindex="0" aria-label="WebAssembly instructions and stack trace; code scrolls horizontally when needed"><code><span class="cex-line">0  i32.const 0           [0]</span>
<span class="cex-line">1  i32.load offset 78112 [g]          reads 4 bytes at 0 + 78112</span>
<span class="cex-line">2  f32.load offset 40    [px]         reads 4 bytes at g + 40</span>
<span class="cex-line">3  end                   the function returns px</span></code></pre><div class="cex-foot"> Select code to copy. Scroll horizontally if needed.</div></figure>
<p><code>i32.load</code> pops an address, adds its offset, and pushes the 32-bit integer stored there. Address 78112 holds the address of the game&#39;s state, a pointer this course calls <code>g</code>. <code>f32.load</code> pops that pointer, adds 40 and pushes the 32-bit float stored there, the shell&#39;s position. At <code>end</code> the function returns what is left on the stack.</p>
<p>Function 12, <code>r_target_x</code>, returns the flag&#39;s position. The game keeps that position combined by exclusive or (<code>i32.xor</code>, below) with a key at <code>g + 92</code>, and the key is 0 unless mode 4 is on. It has one local variable, local 0:</p>
<figure class="code-example"><figcaption><strong>WebAssembly instructions and stack trace</strong></figcaption><pre tabindex="0" aria-label="WebAssembly instructions and stack trace; code scrolls horizontally when needed"><code><span class="cex-line">0  [&quot;i32.const&quot;, 0]</span>
<span class="cex-line">1  [&quot;i32.load&quot;, 2, 78112]</span>
<span class="cex-line">2  [&quot;local.tee&quot;, 0]</span>
<span class="cex-line">3  [&quot;i32.load&quot;, 2, 92]</span>
<span class="cex-line">4  [&quot;local.get&quot;, 0]</span>
<span class="cex-line">5  [&quot;i32.load&quot;, 2, 16]</span>
<span class="cex-line">6  [&quot;i32.xor&quot;]</span>
<span class="cex-line">7  [&quot;f32.reinterpret_i32&quot;]</span>
<span class="cex-line">8  [&quot;end&quot;]</span></code></pre><div class="cex-foot"> Select code to copy. Scroll horizontally if needed.</div></figure>
<p><code>local.get 0</code> pushes local 0&#39;s value. <code>local.tee 0</code> stores the top of the stack in local 0 and leaves it on the stack. <code>i32.xor</code> pops two integers and pushes their bitwise exclusive or.</p>

<h2 id="one-plain-object">One plain object</h2>
<p>Your machine keeps everything it knows in one object, <code>machine.state</code>: the memory, the globals (the program&#39;s global variables, which start at values the listing gives), the value stack, the frames, the tick count and the count of calls begun. A <strong>frame</strong> is one function call in progress. It holds which function is running, <code>func</code>, the index of its next instruction in that function&#39;s code, <code>at</code>, its locals and whatever your machine needs to return from it.</p>
<p>Everything has to be in that one object, because every later lesson copies or compares the machine&#39;s state. Lesson 09 hashes it, lesson 10 saves pieces of it and restores them, and the last section of this lesson runs part one&#39;s debugger on it unchanged. <code>structuredClone(machine.state)</code> has to make a complete copy, and <code>machine.state = copy</code> has to put the machine back at that exact moment. State kept anywhere else, in a closure or a field outside <code>state</code>, is state those copies miss.</p>
<p>What isn&#39;t state stays outside: the program, and anything you compute once from it, such as where each block (next section) ends.</p>
<p>A run starts with <code>begin(name, args)</code>, which pushes the first frame and runs nothing. <code>step()</code> runs exactly one instruction and returns its event, <code>{ tick, func, at, op, writes }</code>, which holds its tick, which instruction ran, that instruction&#39;s name and the writes it made, as part one&#39;s events did. <code>invoke(name, args)</code> begins a call and steps until the call returns. Checks <code>08.memory-starts</code> and <code>08.one-step</code> look at a new machine and at its first step.</p>
<h3 id="allocate-the-state-you-will-later-restore">Allocate the state you will later restore</h3>
<p>In <code>project/machine.mjs</code>, replace the <code>initial-state</code> region inside the constructor:</p>
<figure class="code-example"><figcaption><strong>Initialize mutable state</strong><span class="cex-location">examples/machine-checkpoint.mjs · initial-state</span></figcaption><p class="cex-change">Replace initial-state inside the constructor.</p><pre tabindex="0" aria-label="Initialize mutable state; code scrolls horizontally when needed"><code><span class="cex-line">    <span class="cex-keyword">const</span> memory = <span class="cex-keyword">new</span> Uint8Array(this.program.memory.min * PAGE);</span>
<span class="cex-line">    <span class="cex-keyword">for</span> (<span class="cex-keyword">const</span> d <span class="cex-keyword">of</span> this.program.data) memory.set(d.bytes, d.offset);</span>
<span class="cex-line">    this.state = {</span>
<span class="cex-line">      memory,</span>
<span class="cex-line">      globals: this.program.globals.map((g) =&gt; g.init),</span>
<span class="cex-line">      stack: [],</span>
<span class="cex-line">      frames: [],</span>
<span class="cex-line">      tick: <span class="cex-number">0</span>,</span>
<span class="cex-line">      calls: <span class="cex-number">0</span>,</span>
<span class="cex-line">      result: <span class="cex-keyword">undefined</span>,</span>
<span class="cex-line">    };</span></code></pre><div class="cex-foot"> Select code to copy. Scroll horizontally if needed.</div></figure>
<p>A new typed array starts filled with zero. The data segments then install the compiled program&#39;s text at exact byte addresses. Globals copy their initial values; the stacks and counters start empty. The constructor&#39;s supplied prefix loads the program, matches each block with its end and binds imports. Those facts do not change while the guest runs, so they sit outside <code>state</code>.</p>
<h3 id="separate-starting-a-call-from-executing-it">Separate starting a call from executing it</h3>
<p>Replace the whole <code>call-entry</code> region. It contains the <code>running</code> getter and three methods, not just <code>begin</code>:</p>
<figure class="code-example"><figcaption><strong>Start, enter and finish a call</strong><span class="cex-location">examples/machine-checkpoint.mjs · call-entry</span></figcaption><p class="cex-change">Replace the complete call-entry region.</p><pre tabindex="0" aria-label="Start, enter and finish a call; code scrolls horizontally when needed"><code><span class="cex-line">  get running() {</span>
<span class="cex-line">    <span class="cex-keyword">return</span> this.state.frames.length &gt; <span class="cex-number">0</span>;</span>
<span class="cex-line">  }</span>
<span class="cex-line"></span>
<span class="cex-line">  <span class="cex-comment">// Start a call to an export. Nothing runs until step().</span></span>
<span class="cex-line">  begin(name, args = []) {</span>
<span class="cex-line">    <span class="cex-keyword">if</span> (this.running)</span>
<span class="cex-line">      <span class="cex-keyword">throw</span> Error(<span class="cex-string">`Machine: ${name} called while another call is unfinished`</span>);</span>
<span class="cex-line">    <span class="cex-keyword">const</span> e = this.program.exports.find(</span>
<span class="cex-line">      (x) =&gt; x.name === name &amp;&amp; x.kind === <span class="cex-string">&#39;func&#39;</span>,</span>
<span class="cex-line">    );</span>
<span class="cex-line">    <span class="cex-keyword">if</span> (!e) <span class="cex-keyword">throw</span> Error(<span class="cex-string">`Machine: no exported function named ${name}`</span>);</span>
<span class="cex-line">    <span class="cex-keyword">const</span> type = this.program.typeOf(e.index);</span>
<span class="cex-line">    <span class="cex-keyword">if</span> (args.length !== type.params.length)</span>
<span class="cex-line">      <span class="cex-keyword">throw</span> Error(</span>
<span class="cex-line">        <span class="cex-string">`Machine: ${name} takes ${type.params.length} arguments, got ${args.length}`</span>,</span>
<span class="cex-line">      );</span>
<span class="cex-line">    this.state.calls++;</span>
<span class="cex-line">    this.state.result = <span class="cex-keyword">undefined</span>;</span>
<span class="cex-line">    this.enter(</span>
<span class="cex-line">      e.index,</span>
<span class="cex-line">      args.map((a, i) =&gt; coerce(type.params[i], a)),</span>
<span class="cex-line">    );</span>
<span class="cex-line">  }</span>
<span class="cex-line"></span>
<span class="cex-line">  <span class="cex-comment">// Run a whole export call and return its result.</span></span>
<span class="cex-line">  invoke(name, args = []) {</span>
<span class="cex-line">    this.begin(name, args);</span>
<span class="cex-line">    while (this.running) this.step();</span>
<span class="cex-line">    <span class="cex-keyword">return</span> this.state.result;</span>
<span class="cex-line">  }</span>
<span class="cex-line"></span>
<span class="cex-line">  enter(index, args) {</span>
<span class="cex-line">    <span class="cex-keyword">const</span> fn = this.prepared.get(index);</span>
<span class="cex-line">    <span class="cex-keyword">const</span> locals = [...args, ...fn.locals.map(zeroOf)];</span>
<span class="cex-line">    this.state.frames.push({</span>
<span class="cex-line">      func: index,</span>
<span class="cex-line">      at: <span class="cex-number">0</span>,</span>
<span class="cex-line">      locals,</span>
<span class="cex-line">      base: this.state.stack.length,</span>
<span class="cex-line">      labels: [],</span>
<span class="cex-line">    });</span>
<span class="cex-line">  }</span></code></pre><div class="cex-foot"> Select code to copy. Scroll horizontally if needed.</div></figure>
<p><code>begin</code> checks the export and argument count before entering the call. <code>enter</code> appends a frame whose <code>base</code> remembers the caller&#39;s stack height. Arguments lead the locals; declared locals follow, initialized to zero. No instruction has executed yet. <code>invoke</code> is only a convenience loop over the same <code>step</code> that the debugger will use.</p>
<p>Trace <code>begin(&#39;r_px&#39;)</code>: one frame is added, its next instruction is zero, <code>calls</code> increases once and <code>tick</code> stays unchanged. A nested guest <code>call</code> uses <code>enter</code>, not <code>begin</code>: it must not look like a new call from outside.</p>
<h3 id="execute-exactly-one-instruction">Execute exactly one instruction</h3>
<p>Replace the <code>step-start</code> region at the opening of <code>step</code>. The supplied <code>switch</code> starts immediately after its closing region marker; leave it in place.</p>
<figure class="code-example"><figcaption><strong>Capture an instruction boundary</strong><span class="cex-location">examples/machine-checkpoint.mjs · step-start</span></figcaption><p class="cex-change">Replace step-start; retain the following switch.</p><pre tabindex="0" aria-label="Capture an instruction boundary; code scrolls horizontally when needed"><code><span class="cex-line">  step() {</span>
<span class="cex-line cex-focus">    <span class="cex-keyword">const</span> s = this.state;</span>
<span class="cex-line cex-focus">    <span class="cex-keyword">const</span> frame = s.frames[s.frames.length - <span class="cex-number">1</span>];</span>
<span class="cex-line">    <span class="cex-keyword">if</span> (!frame)</span>
<span class="cex-line">      <span class="cex-keyword">throw</span> Error(<span class="cex-string">&#39;Machine: no call in progress; use begin(name, args) first&#39;</span>);</span>
<span class="cex-line">    <span class="cex-keyword">const</span> fn = this.prepared.get(frame.func);</span>
<span class="cex-line">    <span class="cex-keyword">const</span> at = frame.at;</span>
<span class="cex-line">    <span class="cex-keyword">const</span> ins = fn.code[at];</span>
<span class="cex-line">    <span class="cex-keyword">const</span> op = fn.ops[at];</span>
<span class="cex-line">    <span class="cex-keyword">const</span> event = {</span>
<span class="cex-line">      tick: s.tick + <span class="cex-number">1</span>,</span>
<span class="cex-line">      func: frame.func,</span>
<span class="cex-line">      at,</span>
<span class="cex-line">      op: ins[<span class="cex-number">0</span>],</span>
<span class="cex-line">      writes: [],</span>
<span class="cex-line">    };</span>
<span class="cex-line">    <span class="cex-keyword">const</span> st = s.stack;</span>
<span class="cex-line">    frame.at = at + <span class="cex-number">1</span>;</span></code></pre><div class="cex-foot"><span class="cex-emphasis">Emphasized lines: 2, 3.</span> Select code to copy. Scroll horizontally if needed.</div></figure>
<p>The event identifies the instruction <strong>before</strong> it executes. Advance <code>frame.at</code> before dispatch: an ordinary instruction then falls through to its successor, and a branch can replace that next position. The supplied tail of <code>step</code>, after the switch, increments <code>s.tick</code> and returns this event. A trapped instruction throws before that tail and is not counted as completed.</p>
<p>Tour the supplied switch now: <code>i32.const</code> pushes its immediate, <code>local.get</code> reads the current frame and <code>end</code> either closes a label or calls <code>leave</code>. Every access uses the <code>s</code> or <code>frame</code> fetched during this step. Holding a frame from an earlier call to <code>step</code> would break restoration when a debugger replaces the whole state.</p>
<p>Replace <code>return-frame</code>, the <code>leave</code> method below <code>branch</code>:</p>
<figure class="code-example"><figcaption><strong>Return to the caller</strong><span class="cex-location">examples/machine-checkpoint.mjs · return-frame</span></figcaption><p class="cex-change">Replace return-frame with this leave method.</p><pre tabindex="0" aria-label="Return to the caller; code scrolls horizontally when needed"><code><span class="cex-line">  leave(frame) {</span>
<span class="cex-line">    <span class="cex-keyword">const</span> s = this.state;</span>
<span class="cex-line">    <span class="cex-keyword">const</span> type = this.program.typeOf(frame.func);</span>
<span class="cex-line">    <span class="cex-keyword">const</span> results = type.results.length</span>
<span class="cex-line">      ? s.stack.slice(s.stack.length - type.results.length)</span>
<span class="cex-line">      : [];</span>
<span class="cex-line">    s.stack.length = frame.base;</span>
<span class="cex-line">    s.frames.pop();</span>
<span class="cex-line">    <span class="cex-keyword">if</span> (s.frames.length) s.stack.push(...results);</span>
<span class="cex-line">    <span class="cex-keyword">else</span> s.result = results[<span class="cex-number">0</span>];</span>
<span class="cex-line">  }</span></code></pre><div class="cex-foot"> Select code to copy. Scroll horizontally if needed.</div></figure>
<p>Save the result before cutting the stack back to <code>frame.base</code>. A nested call puts its result on the caller&#39;s stack; the outermost call puts it in <code>state.result</code>. On <code>r_px</code>&#39;s last instruction the stack holds its one result. That value survives the cut, the last frame disappears and <code>running</code> becomes false.</p>
<p>At this point the type-in route still cannot run the getter: <code>memory</code> is unfinished, and full-game checks also reach the unfinished <code>branch</code> region. A check now should retain those expected failures rather than suggest you broke the call boundary:</p>
<figure class="code-example"><figcaption><strong>Terminal command</strong></figcaption><pre tabindex="0" aria-label="Terminal command; code scrolls horizontally when needed"><code><span class="cex-line">node lab.mjs check project 08 --help-used &quot;followed state and call listings&quot;</span></code></pre><div class="cex-foot"> Select code to copy. <h2 id="blocks-loops-and-branches">Blocks, loops and branches</h2>
<p>WebAssembly has no jump to an arbitrary position. Code is nested in blocks, and a branch names a block by its <strong>depth</strong>, where 0 is the innermost block around the branch and 1 the one around that.</p>
<ul>
<li><code>block</code> opens a block. A branch to it goes forward to just after its <code>end</code>.</li>
<li><code>loop</code> opens a loop. A branch to it goes backward to just after the <code>loop</code> instruction, so the loop runs again.</li>
<li><code>br N</code> always branches to the block N levels out. <code>br_if N</code> pops an integer and branches only if it isn&#39;t zero.</li>
<li><code>end</code> closes the innermost block. The last <code>end</code> of a function returns from it, and so does <code>return</code>.</li>
</ul>
<p>Your machine needs, for each frame, a stack of open blocks: for each one, where a branch to it goes and how tall the value stack was when it opened. A branch cuts the value stack back to that height. A block that leaves a value, written <code>[&quot;block&quot;, &quot;i32&quot;]</code>, keeps its top value across the cut. Lob&#39;s blocks never do, but the checks test it, so here is one traced, top of the stack on the right:</p>
<figure class="code-example"><figcaption><strong>WebAssembly instructions and stack trace</strong></figcaption><pre tabindex="0" aria-label="WebAssembly instructions and stack trace; code scrolls horizontally when needed"><code><span class="cex-line">0  i32.const 7           [7]</span>
<span class="cex-line">1  block i32             [7]        the block opens at height 1</span>
<span class="cex-line">2  i32.const 1           [7, 1]</span>
<span class="cex-line">3  i32.const 2           [7, 1, 2]</span>
<span class="cex-line">4  br 0                  [7, 2]     keep the top value, cut to height 1, push it back</span>
<span class="cex-line">5  i32.const 9                      skipped: the branch went past the block&#39;s end</span>
<span class="cex-line">6  end                              skipped too</span>
<span class="cex-line">7  ...                   [7, 2]     the block left 2</span></code></pre><div class="cex-foot"> Select code to copy. Scroll horizontally if needed.</div></figure>
<p>The branch kept one value because the block leaves one. A plain <code>block</code> keeps none, and a branch to a <code>loop</code> keeps none either.</p>
<p>Here is the loop that starts <code>game_init</code>, function 4, shortened. It clears 12,288 bytes of memory, 8 bytes each time round:</p>
<figure class="code-example"><figcaption><strong>WebAssembly instructions and stack trace</strong></figcaption><pre tabindex="0" aria-label="WebAssembly instructions and stack trace; code scrolls horizontally when needed"><code><span class="cex-line">0   [&quot;i32.const&quot;, -12288]</span>
<span class="cex-line">1   [&quot;local.set&quot;, 2]</span>
<span class="cex-line">2   [&quot;loop&quot;, null]</span>
<span class="cex-line">3   [&quot;local.get&quot;, 2]</span>
<span class="cex-line">4   [&quot;i32.const&quot;, 78112]</span>
<span class="cex-line">5   [&quot;i32.add&quot;]</span>
<span class="cex-line">6   [&quot;i32.const&quot;, 0]</span>
<span class="cex-line">7   [&quot;i32.store8&quot;, 0, 0]</span>
<span class="cex-line">    ... the same five instructions for the next 7 bytes ...</span>
<span class="cex-line">43  [&quot;local.get&quot;, 2]</span>
<span class="cex-line">44  [&quot;i32.const&quot;, 8]</span>
<span class="cex-line">45  [&quot;i32.add&quot;]</span>
<span class="cex-line">46  [&quot;local.tee&quot;, 2]</span>
<span class="cex-line">47  [&quot;br_if&quot;, 0]</span>
<span class="cex-line">48  [&quot;end&quot;]</span></code></pre><div class="cex-foot"> Select code to copy. Scroll horizontally if needed.</div></figure>
<p>Local 2 starts at -12,288 and goes up by 8 each time round. <code>br_if 0</code> branches back to instruction 3 while local 2 isn&#39;t zero, so the loop ends when local 2 reaches 0.</p>
<p>Question 08b: how many times does <code>br_if 0</code> branch back to instruction 3? Commit before reading on:</p>
<figure class="code-example"><figcaption><strong>Terminal command</strong></figcaption><pre tabindex="0" aria-label="Terminal command; code scrolls horizontally when needed"><code><span class="cex-line">node lab.mjs predict project 08b YOUR_ANSWER</span></code></pre><div class="cex-foot"> Select code to copy. Scroll horizontally if needed.</div></figure>
<p>This loop is why <code>game_init</code> alone runs more than 70,000 instructions before the game draws anything. Check <code>08.control</code> runs small programs with nested blocks, loops, branches out of several levels and blocks that leave a value.</p>
<h3 id="implement-the-branch-destination">Implement the branch destination</h3>
<p>Replace <code>branch</code> in <code>project/machine.mjs</code>:</p>
<figure class="code-example"><figcaption><strong>Jump without losing the enclosing state</strong><span class="cex-location">examples/machine-checkpoint.mjs · branch</span></figcaption><p class="cex-change">Replace the branch region.</p><pre tabindex="0" aria-label="Jump without losing the enclosing state; code scrolls horizontally when needed"><code><span class="cex-line">  branch(frame, depth) {</span>
<span class="cex-line">    <span class="cex-keyword">const</span> st = this.state.stack;</span>
<span class="cex-line">    <span class="cex-comment">// A branch past every open block targets the function body itself: it returns.</span></span>
<span class="cex-line">    <span class="cex-keyword">if</span> (depth === frame.labels.length) {</span>
<span class="cex-line">      this.leave(frame);</span>
<span class="cex-line">      <span class="cex-keyword">return</span>;</span>
<span class="cex-line">    }</span>
<span class="cex-line">    <span class="cex-keyword">const</span> label = frame.labels[frame.labels.length - <span class="cex-number">1</span> - depth];</span>
<span class="cex-line">    <span class="cex-keyword">const</span> kept = label.arity ? st.slice(st.length - label.arity) : [];</span>
<span class="cex-line">    st.length = label.height;</span>
<span class="cex-line">    st.push(...kept);</span>
<span class="cex-line">    <span class="cex-keyword">if</span> (label.loop) {</span>
<span class="cex-line">      frame.labels.length -= depth; <span class="cex-comment">// keep the loop&#39;s own label</span></span>
<span class="cex-line">      frame.at = label.end + <span class="cex-number">1</span>; <span class="cex-comment">// back to the first instruction inside the loop</span></span>
<span class="cex-line">    } <span class="cex-keyword">else</span> {</span>
<span class="cex-line">      frame.labels.length -= depth + <span class="cex-number">1</span>;</span>
<span class="cex-line">      frame.at = label.end + <span class="cex-number">1</span>; <span class="cex-comment">// just past the block&#39;s end</span></span>
<span class="cex-line">    }</span>
<span class="cex-line">  }</span></code></pre><div class="cex-foot"> Select code to copy. Scroll horizontally if needed.</div></figure>
<p>The label records both the instruction destination and the stack height to restore. Save a result before shortening the stack, as you did when returning. A loop keeps its own label so the next iteration can branch to it again; a block removes its label because execution has left it. Branching beyond all open labels returns from the function body itself.</p>
<p>Tour <code>prepare</code> near the bottom of the supplied file. It pairs each opening <code>block</code> or <code>loop</code> with an <code>end</code> using a temporary stack. The dispatch cases install that precomputed position in a runtime label. Preparation handles code nesting; <code>frame.labels</code> handles the particular nesting active during execution.</p>
<h2 id="memory-widths-order-and-writes">Memory: widths, order and writes</h2>
<p>Memory is a <code>Uint8Array</code> of 131,072 bytes, because the listing&#39;s <code>memory.min</code> is 2 pages of 65,536. At the start every byte is 0 except the data segments, which the machine copies in at their offsets. Lob&#39;s one segment puts 281 bytes of text at address 65,536.</p>
<p>A load or store adds its offset to an address popped from the stack. The address is unsigned. The 32 bits of <code>-4</code> mean 4,294,967,292, far outside memory, and an access that reaches past the last byte is a <strong>trap</strong>. A trap stops the program. Throw an <code>Error</code> whose message starts with <code>trap:</code>.</p>
<p>Values are stored <strong>little-endian</strong>, lowest byte first. <code>i32.store</code> of 300 writes the bytes <code>2C 01 00 00</code>, because 300 is <code>0x0000012C</code>. Use a <code>DataView</code> with its little-endian flag set rather than shifting bytes by hand, and make it from <code>state.memory</code> when you use it. A view made once in the constructor keeps writing to the old memory after <code>machine.state = copy</code>. Lob uses these widths:</p>
<ul>
<li><code>i32.load</code> and <code>i32.store</code>, 4 bytes</li>
<li><code>f32.load</code> and <code>f32.store</code>, 4 bytes as a float</li>
<li><code>i32.load8_u</code>, 1 byte read as 0 to 255</li>
<li><code>i32.store8</code> and <code>i32.store16</code>, the low 1 or 2 bytes of an integer</li>
<li><code>i64.store</code>, 8 bytes of an <code>i64.const</code> value, which <code>loadProgram</code> (supplied in <code>public/program.mjs</code>) gives you as a BigInt.</li>
</ul>
<p>Every store reports a write in its event, <code>{ address, size, before, after }</code>, with <code>before</code> and <code>after</code> as arrays of byte values. Read <code>before</code> from memory before you store. Lesson 10 builds watchpoints, which stop when a watched byte changes, and &quot;who last wrote this address&quot; on these writes, so a store that writes the same value it found still reports a write.</p>
<p>Question 08c: an <code>i32.store</code> with offset 0 pops the value 1,000 and then the address 70,000. What is the byte at address 70,001 afterwards? Commit:</p>
<figure class="code-example"><figcaption><strong>Terminal command</strong></figcaption><pre tabindex="0" aria-label="Terminal command; code scrolls horizontally when needed"><code><span class="cex-line">node lab.mjs predict project 08c YOUR_ANSWER</span></code></pre><div class="cex-foot"> Select code to copy. Scroll horizontally if needed.</div></figure>
<p>Check <code>08.memory</code> runs loads and stores of every width, offsets, byte order and out-of-bounds traps. <code>08.writes</code> checks that every store in a run of Lob reports the bytes it wrote, and that nothing else reports a write.</p>
<h3 id="read-the-current-memory-then-report-the-write">Read the current memory, then report the write</h3>
<p>Replace <code>memory</code>, containing both <code>view</code> and <code>store</code>:</p>
<figure class="code-example"><figcaption><strong>Address the restored memory</strong><span class="cex-location">examples/machine-checkpoint.mjs · memory</span></figcaption><p class="cex-change">Replace the complete memory region.</p><pre tabindex="0" aria-label="Address the restored memory; code scrolls horizontally when needed"><code><span class="cex-line">  view(base, offset, size) {</span>
<span class="cex-line">    <span class="cex-keyword">const</span> address = (base &gt;&gt;&gt; <span class="cex-number">0</span>) + offset;</span>
<span class="cex-line cex-focus">    <span class="cex-keyword">const</span> memory = this.state.memory;</span>
<span class="cex-line">    <span class="cex-keyword">if</span> (address + size &gt; memory.length)</span>
<span class="cex-line">      <span class="cex-keyword">throw</span> trap(<span class="cex-string">`out of bounds memory access at ${address}`</span>);</span>
<span class="cex-line cex-focus">    <span class="cex-keyword">return</span> <span class="cex-keyword">new</span> DataView(memory.buffer, memory.byteOffset + address, size);</span>
<span class="cex-line">  }</span>
<span class="cex-line"></span>
<span class="cex-line">  store(event, base, offset, size, write) {</span>
<span class="cex-line">    <span class="cex-keyword">const</span> view = this.view(base, offset, size);</span>
<span class="cex-line">    <span class="cex-keyword">const</span> address = view.byteOffset - this.state.memory.byteOffset;</span>
<span class="cex-line">    <span class="cex-keyword">const</span> before = Array.<span class="cex-keyword">from</span>(</span>
<span class="cex-line">      this.state.memory.subarray(address, address + size),</span>
<span class="cex-line">    );</span>
<span class="cex-line">    write(view);</span>
<span class="cex-line">    event.writes.push({</span>
<span class="cex-line">      address,</span>
<span class="cex-line">      size,</span>
<span class="cex-line">      before,</span>
<span class="cex-line">      after: Array.<span class="cex-keyword">from</span>(this.state.memory.subarray(address, address + size)),</span>
<span class="cex-line">    });</span>
<span class="cex-line">  }</span></code></pre><div class="cex-foot"><span class="cex-emphasis">Emphasized lines: 3, 6.</span> Select code to copy. Scroll horizontally if needed.</div></figure>
<p><code>base &gt;&gt;&gt; 0</code> changes the reading of its 32 bits, then ordinary addition includes the offset. Do not wrap that sum back to 32 bits: a huge address must trap, not wrap to the beginning of memory. <code>memory.byteOffset</code> matters if the byte array is a view into a larger buffer. The event&#39;s address stays relative to the guest&#39;s memory, so <code>store</code> subtracts that host-buffer offset again.</p>
<p><code>before</code> and <code>after</code> are copied arrays, not live views. A later guest write must not rewrite an earlier event&#39;s evidence. <code>write(view)</code> is supplied by each opcode case: for example, <code>i32.store</code> pops the value, pops the address, and passes a function that calls <code>setInt32</code> with the little-endian flag.</p>
<p>All six holes are now filled. Run your file through the same probe as the first win, then the unit&#39;s real checks:</p>

If not, follow the named check&#39;s first mismatch back to its section; preserve the failure and your explanation before editing. The next sections explain the supplied number and import cases you just exercised.</p>
<p>What each of the unit&#39;s checks runs, and what it compares:</p>
<ul>
<li><code>08.memory-starts</code> looks at a new machine that has run nothing, and <code>08.one-step</code> begins <code>game_init</code> and compares its first steps with the listing.</li>
<li><code>08.frames</code> follows the calls <code>game_init</code> makes and compares the frames after each call instruction.</li>
<li><code>08.control</code>, <code>08.memory</code> and <code>08.numbers</code> run small programs and compare results, loads, stores and traps with Node&#39;s engine.</li>
<li><code>08.writes</code> runs Lob and compares the writes every store reports with Node&#39;s memory.</li>
<li><code>08.lob-agrees</code> and <code>08.lob2-agrees</code> run whole sessions of Lob and Lob II from the start, and after every call compare the result, every getter and all of memory with Node&#39;s engine.</li>

<h3 id="break-a-restoration-boundary-then-repair-it">Break a restoration boundary, then repair it</h3>
<p>In your project only, make <code>view</code> reuse a memory reference captured during construction. Inside the <code>initial-state</code> region, after the <code>this.state = { ... };</code> statement and before the <code>// endregion: initial-state</code> line, add <code>this.cachedMemory = this.state.memory;</code>. In <code>view</code>, change <code>const memory = this.state.memory;</code> to <code>const memory = this.cachedMemory;</code>. Leave <code>store</code> as it is.</p>
