<h2 id="last-writers-indexed">Last writers, indexed</h2>
<p>Build the index during one replay. For every byte of memory, keep the list of ticks at which an instruction wrote it, in increasing order. Keep, beside each tick, what you need to report: the instruction&#39;s function and <code>at</code>, and where the write started and its size.</p>
<p><code>lastWriter(address, beforeTick)</code> is then a binary search in that byte&#39;s list for the greatest tick below <code>beforeTick</code>. A byte written a thousand times is answered in about ten comparisons.</p>
<p>The lists hold one entry per byte written, so a 4-byte store adds four entries. Lesson 09&#39;s recording makes 65,859 of them. Typed arrays that grow by doubling hold that many numbers in a few megabytes, while arrays of objects would hold the same in far more.</p>
<p>Tour the supplied <code>List</code> near the top of your <code>query.mjs</code> now. It is that growing typed array: <code>push</code> doubles the array when it is full, and <code>done()</code> returns a copy of exactly what was pushed. Then tour the supplied lines at the start of <code>buildIndex</code>. They make one machine whose imports answer from the recording, as lesson 09&#39;s <code>replay</code> did, and <code>prepared</code>, which gives every instruction of every function a kind from the table <code>KIND</code> (<code>&#39;load&#39;</code>, <code>&#39;binary&#39;</code>, <code>&#39;call&#39;</code> and so on), so the replay looks up how an instruction moves values without reading its name again. An instruction outside the table stops the index before it runs anything.</p>
<h3 id="keep-every-write">Keep every write</h3>
<p>In <code>project/query.mjs</code>, replace the <code>keep-writes</code> region:</p>
<figure class="code-example"><figcaption><strong>Keep each write, and who last wrote each byte so far</strong><span class="cex-location">examples/query-checkpoint.mjs · keep-writes</span></figcaption><p class="cex-change">Replace the keep-writes region.</p><pre tabindex="0" aria-label="Keep each write, and who last wrote each byte so far; code scrolls horizontally when needed"><code><span class="cex-line">  <span class="cex-comment">// Every write, one entry in each list, in tick order.</span></span>
<span class="cex-line">  <span class="cex-keyword">const</span> wTick = <span class="cex-keyword">new</span> List(Int32Array);</span>
<span class="cex-line">  <span class="cex-keyword">const</span> wFunc = <span class="cex-keyword">new</span> List(Int32Array);</span>
<span class="cex-line">  <span class="cex-keyword">const</span> wAt = <span class="cex-keyword">new</span> List(Int32Array);</span>
<span class="cex-line">  <span class="cex-keyword">const</span> wAddress = <span class="cex-keyword">new</span> List(Int32Array);</span>
<span class="cex-line">  <span class="cex-keyword">const</span> wSize = <span class="cex-keyword">new</span> List(Int32Array);</span>
<span class="cex-line">  <span class="cex-comment">// Per byte: the tick of the store that last wrote it so far, 0 if none.</span></span>
<span class="cex-line">  <span class="cex-keyword">const</span> writer = <span class="cex-keyword">new</span> Int32Array(memorySize);</span>
<span class="cex-line">  <span class="cex-keyword">const</span> keepWrites = (event, t) =&gt; {</span>
<span class="cex-line">    <span class="cex-keyword">for</span> (<span class="cex-keyword">const</span> w <span class="cex-keyword">of</span> event.writes) {</span>
<span class="cex-line">      wTick.push(t);</span>
<span class="cex-line">      wFunc.push(event.func);</span>
<span class="cex-line">      wAt.push(event.at);</span>
<span class="cex-line">      wAddress.push(w.address);</span>
<span class="cex-line">      wSize.push(w.size);</span>
<span class="cex-line">      writer.fill(t, w.address, w.address + w.size);</span>
<span class="cex-line">    }</span>
<span class="cex-line">  };</span></code></pre><div class="cex-foot"> Select code to copy. Scroll horizontally if needed.</div></figure>
<p>The replay calls <code>keepWrites</code> after every instruction with the instruction&#39;s event and tick. Each write goes into five lists at the same position, so write number <code>w</code> is <code>wTick[w]</code>, <code>wFunc[w]</code>, <code>wAt[w]</code>, <code>wAddress[w]</code> and <code>wSize[w]</code>. The replay runs in tick order, so the lists are in tick order without any sorting. <code>writer</code> is different: it holds, for every byte, only the latest store that wrote it. <code>lastWriter</code> doesn&#39;t use it. The chains later in this lesson do, because a load needs to know which store wrote each byte it reads at the moment it reads it.</p>
<h3 id="group-the-writes-by-byte">Group the writes by byte</h3>
<p>After the replay, <code>makeIndex</code> turns the writes into one list per byte. Replace the <code>by-byte</code> region:</p>
<figure class="code-example"><figcaption><strong>One list of writes per byte, still in tick order</strong><span class="cex-location">examples/query-checkpoint.mjs · by-byte</span></figcaption><p class="cex-change">Replace the by-byte region.</p><pre tabindex="0" aria-label="One list of writes per byte, still in tick order; code scrolls horizontally when needed"><code><span class="cex-line">  <span class="cex-comment">// Per byte, the writes that touched it in tick order:</span></span>
<span class="cex-line">  <span class="cex-comment">// byteWrites[byteStart[a]] up to byteWrites[byteStart[a + 1]].</span></span>
<span class="cex-line">  <span class="cex-keyword">const</span> byteStart = <span class="cex-keyword">new</span> Int32Array(memorySize + <span class="cex-number">1</span>);</span>
<span class="cex-line">  <span class="cex-keyword">for</span> (<span class="cex-keyword">let</span> w = <span class="cex-number">0</span>; w &lt; writes.tick.length; w++)</span>
<span class="cex-line">    <span class="cex-keyword">for</span> (<span class="cex-keyword">let</span> i = <span class="cex-number">0</span>; i &lt; writes.size[w]; i++)</span>
<span class="cex-line">      byteStart[writes.address[w] + i + <span class="cex-number">1</span>]++;</span>
<span class="cex-line">  <span class="cex-keyword">for</span> (<span class="cex-keyword">let</span> a = <span class="cex-number">0</span>; a &lt; memorySize; a++) byteStart[a + <span class="cex-number">1</span>] += byteStart[a];</span>
<span class="cex-line">  <span class="cex-keyword">const</span> byteWrites = <span class="cex-keyword">new</span> Int32Array(byteStart[memorySize]);</span>
<span class="cex-line">  <span class="cex-keyword">const</span> next = byteStart.slice(<span class="cex-number">0</span>, memorySize);</span>
<span class="cex-line">  <span class="cex-keyword">for</span> (<span class="cex-keyword">let</span> w = <span class="cex-number">0</span>; w &lt; writes.tick.length; w++)</span>
<span class="cex-line">    <span class="cex-keyword">for</span> (<span class="cex-keyword">let</span> i = <span class="cex-number">0</span>; i &lt; writes.size[w]; i++)</span>
<span class="cex-line">      byteWrites[next[writes.address[w] + i]++] = w;</span></code></pre><div class="cex-foot"> Select code to copy. Scroll horizontally if needed.</div></figure>
<p>All the per-byte lists live in one <code>Int32Array</code>, <code>byteWrites</code>, one after another, and <code>byteStart[a]</code> is where byte <code>a</code>&#39;s list begins. The first loop counts how many writes cover each byte, the second turns the counts into starting places, and the third puts each write&#39;s number at the next free place of every byte it covers. Writes are placed in tick order, so each byte&#39;s list is in tick order too, which is what the binary search needs.</p>
<h3 id="binary-search-one-byte-s-list">Binary search one byte&#39;s list</h3>
<p>Replace the <code>last-writer</code> region:</p>
<figure class="code-example"><figcaption><strong>lastWriter: the greatest tick below beforeTick</strong><span class="cex-location">examples/query-checkpoint.mjs · last-writer</span></figcaption><p class="cex-change">Replace the last-writer region.</p><pre tabindex="0" aria-label="lastWriter: the greatest tick below beforeTick; code scrolls horizontally when needed"><code><span class="cex-line">  <span class="cex-keyword">const</span> lastWriter = (address, beforeTick) =&gt; {</span>
<span class="cex-line">    <span class="cex-keyword">if</span> (!Number.isInteger(address) || address &lt; <span class="cex-number">0</span> || address &gt;= memorySize)</span>
<span class="cex-line">      <span class="cex-keyword">throw</span> Error(</span>
<span class="cex-line">        <span class="cex-string">`lastWriter: ${address} is not an address in memory (0 to ${memorySize - 1})`</span>,</span>
<span class="cex-line">      );</span>
<span class="cex-line">    <span class="cex-keyword">if</span> (typeof beforeTick !== <span class="cex-string">&#39;number&#39;</span> || Number.isNaN(beforeTick))</span>
<span class="cex-line">      <span class="cex-keyword">throw</span> Error(<span class="cex-string">`lastWriter: beforeTick must be a number, got ${beforeTick}`</span>);</span>
<span class="cex-line">    <span class="cex-comment">// Binary search for the first write at or after beforeTick.</span></span>
<span class="cex-line">    <span class="cex-keyword">let</span> lo = byteStart[address];</span>
<span class="cex-line">    <span class="cex-keyword">let</span> hi = byteStart[address + <span class="cex-number">1</span>];</span>
<span class="cex-line">    while (lo &lt; hi) {</span>
<span class="cex-line">      <span class="cex-keyword">const</span> mid = (lo + hi) &gt;&gt; <span class="cex-number">1</span>;</span>
<span class="cex-line">      <span class="cex-keyword">if</span> (writes.tick[byteWrites[mid]] &lt; beforeTick) lo = mid + <span class="cex-number">1</span>;</span>
<span class="cex-line">      <span class="cex-keyword">else</span> hi = mid;</span>
<span class="cex-line">    }</span>
<span class="cex-line">    <span class="cex-keyword">if</span> (lo === byteStart[address]) <span class="cex-keyword">return</span> <span class="cex-keyword">null</span>;</span>
<span class="cex-line">    <span class="cex-keyword">const</span> w = byteWrites[lo - <span class="cex-number">1</span>];</span>
<span class="cex-line">    <span class="cex-keyword">return</span> {</span>
<span class="cex-line">      tick: writes.tick[w],</span>
<span class="cex-line">      func: writes.func[w],</span>
<span class="cex-line">      at: writes.at[w],</span>
<span class="cex-line">      address: writes.address[w],</span>
<span class="cex-line">      size: writes.size[w],</span>
<span class="cex-line">    };</span>
<span class="cex-line">  };</span></code></pre><div class="cex-foot"> Select code to copy. Scroll horizontally if needed.</div></figure>
<p>The loop narrows <code>lo</code> and <code>hi</code> to the first write at or after <code>beforeTick</code>, so the write just before it, at <code>lo - 1</code>, is the answer. If there is none, nothing wrote the byte before that tick. The answer is the whole write, its start and size, even when the byte is inside a wider store. The debugger&#39;s <code>lastWrite</code> at position <code>p</code> is <code>lastWriter(address, p + 1)</code>, because the instruction at tick <code>p</code> has already run at position <code>p</code>.</p>
<p>Question 11a: in Lob, seed 3, mode 0 (no defences), how many times is the byte at the address <code>g + 72</code> written during <code>game_init</code> and the first 10 game frames, where <code>g</code> is the 4 bytes at 78,112? <code>g + 72</code> is the lowest byte of the game-frame counter, which counts game frames. Commit:</p>
<figure class="code-example"><figcaption><strong>Observed output</strong></figcaption><pre tabindex="0" aria-label="Observed output; code scrolls horizontally when needed"><code><span class="cex-line">node lab.mjs predict project 11a YOUR_ANSWER</span></code></pre><div class="cex-foot"> Select code to copy. Scroll horizontally if needed.</div></figure>
<p>Check <code>11.last-writer</code> asks generated questions about recordings you haven&#39;t seen and compares with a scan of every write. It and the other checks this lesson names make up unit 11&#39;s checks, which one command runs:</p>
<figure class="code-example"><figcaption><strong>Terminal command</strong></figcaption><pre tabindex="0" aria-label="Terminal command; code scrolls horizontally when needed"><code><span class="cex-line">node lab.mjs check project 11 --help-used &quot;describe what helped&quot;</span></code></pre><div class="cex-foot"> Select code to copy. Scroll horizontally if needed.</div></figure>
<p>On the type-in route they still fail with &quot;not written yet&quot; at this point, because <code>buildIndex</code> runs the regions that follow values before it returns. Run the command again once the <code>sources</code> region is filled.</p>
<h2 id="where-a-value-came-from">Where a value came from</h2>
<p>When a stored value is wrong, the question is why. The store copied a value off the stack, and that value was computed by an earlier instruction from its operands. Those came from loads, constants, locals or calls, and each load read bytes some earlier store had written. Following those links backward from a store gives the <strong>chain</strong> of the stored value.</p>
<p><code>sources(tick)</code> takes the tick of a store and returns the chain&#39;s ends and joints:</p>
<ul>
<li><code>stores</code>: every earlier store on the chain, by tick</li>
<li><code>answers</code>: every import answer on the chain, by its index in <code>recording.answers</code></li>
<li><code>args</code>: every argument of a call into the game on the chain, as <code>[call, index]</code>, the call&#39;s index in <code>recording.calls</code> and the argument&#39;s index</li>
<li><code>initial</code>: every byte on the chain that was loaded before any store had written it, from the data segment or the zeros memory starts with.</li>
</ul>
<p>The chain follows values, not addresses. A load depends on the bytes it read, not on the address it read them from, and a store passes on the value it stored, not its address. Otherwise every value in Lob would depend on the pointer <code>g</code>, and every chain would hold the same few hundred stores. The rules, from <code>API.md</code>:</p>
<ul>
<li>a value depends on every operand of the instruction that produced it, except the address of a load or store</li>
<li><code>local.get</code>, <code>local.set</code>, <code>local.tee</code>, <code>global.get</code> and <code>global.set</code> pass a value along unchanged, and so does a call to a defined function, whose arguments become its parameters and whose result comes back</li>
<li>an import&#39;s result depends only on that answer</li>
<li>a constant depends on nothing.</li>
</ul>
<p><code>API.md</code> settles the cases that could go either way: <code>select</code> depends on its condition as well as both values, a one-byte store on the whole value it was given, and a load of bytes written by several stores on all of them.</p>
<h2 id="how-to-follow-a-value">How to follow a value</h2>
<p>Replay once and give every value a <strong>producer</strong>, the tick of the instruction that made it. Keep a producer beside every entry of the value stack, every local of every frame, every global and every byte of memory, and update them as each instruction runs:</p>
<ul>
<li>an arithmetic instruction pops its operands&#39; producers and pushes its own tick</li>
<li>a constant pushes its own tick, with no inputs</li>
<li><code>local.get</code> pushes the producer stored with the local, and <code>local.set</code> stores the popped producer with the local</li>
<li>a load pushes its own tick and records, as its inputs, the producers of the bytes it read, which are the stores that last wrote them</li>
<li>a store records its value operand&#39;s producer as its input and becomes the producer of the bytes it wrote</li>
<li>an import call pushes its own tick, recorded as answer number k</li>
<li>a call to a defined function moves the producers of its arguments into the new frame&#39;s locals, and its return moves the result&#39;s producer back</li>
<li>an argument of a call into the game gets a producer of its own, reported as <code>[call, index]</code>. The other locals, and each global&#39;s starting value, have none.</li>
</ul>
<p>Branches cut the stack back, so cut the producers back with it, keeping a block&#39;s result.</p>
<p>Record, for each tick, the producers it took as inputs. <code>sources(tick)</code> then walks backward from the store&#39;s input. Visit a tick, add its inputs to the walk, note each store, answer and argument met, and never visit a tick twice. The walk only touches the chain, so most questions finish in a few thousand steps whatever the recording&#39;s length.</p>
<p>The seven listings below build that procedure. Three of their choices save memory without changing any answer: a constant gets the producer &quot;nothing&quot; instead of its own tick, since nothing can be on its chain; a value computed from a single producer takes that producer instead of a tick of its own, since its chain is the same; and an import call&#39;s value takes its answer&#39;s producer directly.</p>
<h3 id="number-the-leaves">Number the leaves</h3>
<p>A producer has to fit in one slot of an <code>Int32Array</code>. Replace the <code>leaves</code> region:</p>
<figure class="code-example"><figcaption><strong>One whole number for every kind of producer</strong><span class="cex-location">examples/query-checkpoint.mjs · leaves</span></figcaption><p class="cex-change">Replace the leaves region.</p><pre tabindex="0" aria-label="One whole number for every kind of producer; code scrolls horizontally when needed"><code><span class="cex-line">  <span class="cex-comment">// A producer is one whole number: 0 is nothing (a constant), t &gt; 0 is the</span></span>
<span class="cex-line">  <span class="cex-comment">// instruction at tick t, and the leaves are negative: the answers first, then</span></span>
<span class="cex-line">  <span class="cex-comment">// every argument of every call, then the initial bytes by address.</span></span>
<span class="cex-line">  <span class="cex-keyword">const</span> nAnswers = recording.answers.length;</span>
<span class="cex-line">  <span class="cex-keyword">const</span> argBase = [];</span>
<span class="cex-line">  <span class="cex-keyword">let</span> nArgs = <span class="cex-number">0</span>;</span>
<span class="cex-line">  <span class="cex-keyword">for</span> (<span class="cex-keyword">const</span> c <span class="cex-keyword">of</span> calls) {</span>
<span class="cex-line">    argBase.push(nArgs);</span>
<span class="cex-line">    nArgs += c.args.length;</span>
<span class="cex-line">  }</span>
<span class="cex-line">  <span class="cex-keyword">const</span> argCall = <span class="cex-keyword">new</span> Int32Array(nArgs);</span>
<span class="cex-line">  <span class="cex-keyword">const</span> argPos = <span class="cex-keyword">new</span> Int32Array(nArgs);</span>
<span class="cex-line">  calls.forEach((c, k) =&gt;</span>
<span class="cex-line">    c.args.forEach((_, i) =&gt; {</span>
<span class="cex-line">      argCall[argBase[k] + i] = k;</span>
<span class="cex-line">      argPos[argBase[k] + i] = i;</span>
<span class="cex-line">    }),</span>
<span class="cex-line">  );</span>
<span class="cex-line">  <span class="cex-keyword">const</span> answerId = (a) =&gt; -<span class="cex-number">1</span> - a;</span>
<span class="cex-line">  <span class="cex-keyword">const</span> argId = (k, i) =&gt; -<span class="cex-number">1</span> - nAnswers - argBase[k] - i;</span>
<span class="cex-line">  <span class="cex-keyword">const</span> initialId = (address) =&gt; -<span class="cex-number">1</span> - nAnswers - nArgs - address;</span></code></pre><div class="cex-foot"> Select code to copy. Scroll horizontally if needed.</div></figure>
<p>The <strong>leaves</strong> are the producers a chain ends at: an answer, an argument of a call into the game, or an initial byte. Ticks are positive, so the leaves take the negative numbers, one range after another: answer <code>a</code> is <code>-1 - a</code>, then every argument of every call, in call order, then every byte of memory by address. <code>argBase[k]</code> is where call <code>k</code>&#39;s arguments start in that range, and <code>argCall</code> and <code>argPos</code> turn an argument&#39;s number back into <code>[call, index]</code> when <code>sources</code> reports it. The number 0 is left for nothing.</p>
<h3 id="producers-beside-the-machine-s-values">Producers beside the machine&#39;s values</h3>
<p>Replace the <code>producers</code> region:</p>
<figure class="code-example"><figcaption><strong>What the index records per tick, and the producers of what the machine holds</strong><span class="cex-location">examples/query-checkpoint.mjs · producers</span></figcaption><p class="cex-change">Replace the producers region.</p><pre tabindex="0" aria-label="What the index records per tick, and the producers of what the machine holds; code scrolls horizontally when needed"><code><span class="cex-line">  <span class="cex-comment">// Per tick: where its inputs start in deps, and whether it was a store.</span></span>
<span class="cex-line">  <span class="cex-keyword">const</span> depStart = <span class="cex-keyword">new</span> List(Int32Array);</span>
<span class="cex-line">  <span class="cex-keyword">const</span> deps = <span class="cex-keyword">new</span> List(Int32Array);</span>
<span class="cex-line">  <span class="cex-keyword">const</span> isStore = <span class="cex-keyword">new</span> List(Uint8Array);</span>
<span class="cex-line">  depStart.push(<span class="cex-number">0</span>); <span class="cex-comment">// tick 0 is no instruction</span></span>
<span class="cex-line">  isStore.push(<span class="cex-number">0</span>);</span>
<span class="cex-line"></span>
<span class="cex-line">  <span class="cex-comment">// The producers of what the machine holds right now: one per stack value,</span></span>
<span class="cex-line">  <span class="cex-comment">// one per global, and the frames with one per local.</span></span>
<span class="cex-line">  <span class="cex-keyword">let</span> P = <span class="cex-keyword">new</span> Int32Array(<span class="cex-number">1024</span>);</span>
<span class="cex-line">  <span class="cex-keyword">let</span> sp = <span class="cex-number">0</span>;</span>
<span class="cex-line">  <span class="cex-keyword">const</span> G = <span class="cex-keyword">new</span> Int32Array(program.globals.length);</span>
<span class="cex-line">  <span class="cex-keyword">const</span> frames = []; <span class="cex-comment">// { func, locals, base, labels: [{ height, arity, loop }] }</span></span>
<span class="cex-line">  <span class="cex-keyword">const</span> push = (id) =&gt; {</span>
<span class="cex-line">    <span class="cex-keyword">if</span> (sp === P.length) {</span>
<span class="cex-line">      <span class="cex-keyword">const</span> bigger = <span class="cex-keyword">new</span> Int32Array(P.length * <span class="cex-number">2</span>);</span>
<span class="cex-line">      bigger.set(P);</span>
<span class="cex-line">      P = bigger;</span>
<span class="cex-line">    }</span>
<span class="cex-line">    P[sp++] = id;</span>
<span class="cex-line">  };</span>
<span class="cex-line"></span>
<span class="cex-line">  <span class="cex-comment">// A computed value. With no operand producer it is nothing; with one, it</span></span>
<span class="cex-line">  <span class="cex-comment">// carries that operand&#39;s chain, so it takes its producer; with more, it is</span></span>
<span class="cex-line">  <span class="cex-comment">// tick t, whose inputs are the operands&#39; producers.</span></span>
<span class="cex-line">  <span class="cex-keyword">const</span> scratch = <span class="cex-keyword">new</span> Int32Array(<span class="cex-number">8</span>);</span>
<span class="cex-line">  <span class="cex-keyword">let</span> nScratch = <span class="cex-number">0</span>;</span>
<span class="cex-line">  <span class="cex-keyword">const</span> add = (id) =&gt; {</span>
<span class="cex-line">    <span class="cex-keyword">if</span> (id === <span class="cex-number">0</span>) <span class="cex-keyword">return</span>;</span>
<span class="cex-line">    <span class="cex-keyword">for</span> (<span class="cex-keyword">let</span> i = <span class="cex-number">0</span>; i &lt; nScratch; i++) <span class="cex-keyword">if</span> (scratch[i] === id) <span class="cex-keyword">return</span>;</span>
<span class="cex-line">    scratch[nScratch++] = id;</span>
<span class="cex-line">  };</span>
<span class="cex-line">  <span class="cex-keyword">const</span> made = (t) =&gt; {</span>
<span class="cex-line">    <span class="cex-keyword">if</span> (nScratch === <span class="cex-number">0</span>) <span class="cex-keyword">return</span> <span class="cex-number">0</span>;</span>
<span class="cex-line">    <span class="cex-keyword">if</span> (nScratch === <span class="cex-number">1</span>) <span class="cex-keyword">return</span> scratch[<span class="cex-number">0</span>];</span>
<span class="cex-line">    <span class="cex-keyword">for</span> (<span class="cex-keyword">let</span> i = <span class="cex-number">0</span>; i &lt; nScratch; i++) deps.push(scratch[i]);</span>
<span class="cex-line">    <span class="cex-keyword">return</span> t;</span>
<span class="cex-line">  };</span></code></pre><div class="cex-foot"> Select code to copy. Scroll horizontally if needed.</div></figure>
<p><code>depStart</code>, <code>deps</code> and <code>isStore</code> are what the index keeps for the questions. Tick <code>t</code>&#39;s inputs are <code>deps[depStart[t]]</code> up to <code>deps[depStart[t + 1]]</code>, so every tick costs one number in <code>depStart</code> and one byte in <code>isStore</code>, however many inputs it has. <code>P</code> and <code>sp</code> mirror the machine&#39;s value stack, one producer per value, <code>G</code> mirrors the globals, and each frame will hold one producer per local. These last only as long as the replay.</p>
<p><code>add</code> and <code>made</code> make a computed value&#39;s producer. <code>add</code> collects the operands&#39; producers, leaving out nothing (0) and repeats. <code>made(t)</code> returns 0 if none was collected, the one producer if only one was, and otherwise records them all as tick <code>t</code>&#39;s inputs and returns <code>t</code>. An <code>i32.add</code> of a loaded value and a constant therefore passes on the load&#39;s producer, and its chain is the load&#39;s chain, as the rules ask.</p>
<h3 id="branches-returns-and-calls">Branches, returns and calls</h3>
<p>Replace the <code>frames</code> region:</p>
<figure class="code-example"><figcaption><strong>Cut the producers back as the stack is cut back</strong><span class="cex-location">examples/query-checkpoint.mjs · frames</span></figcaption><p class="cex-change">Replace the frames region.</p><pre tabindex="0" aria-label="Cut the producers back as the stack is cut back; code scrolls horizontally when needed"><code><span class="cex-line">  <span class="cex-comment">// A branch keeps its target&#39;s results and cuts the producers back with the</span></span>
<span class="cex-line">  <span class="cex-comment">// stack; a loop&#39;s label stays, because the loop can be branched to again.</span></span>
<span class="cex-line">  <span class="cex-keyword">const</span> branch = (frame, depth) =&gt; {</span>
<span class="cex-line">    <span class="cex-keyword">const</span> label = frame.labels[frame.labels.length - <span class="cex-number">1</span> - depth];</span>
<span class="cex-line">    <span class="cex-keyword">for</span> (<span class="cex-keyword">let</span> i = <span class="cex-number">0</span>; i &lt; label.arity; i++)</span>
<span class="cex-line">      P[label.height + i] = P[sp - label.arity + i];</span>
<span class="cex-line">    sp = label.height + label.arity;</span>
<span class="cex-line">    frame.labels.length -= label.loop ? depth : depth + <span class="cex-number">1</span>;</span>
<span class="cex-line">  };</span>
<span class="cex-line">  <span class="cex-comment">// A return hands the results&#39; producers back to the caller; the outermost</span></span>
<span class="cex-line">  <span class="cex-comment">// call&#39;s result leaves the machine.</span></span>
<span class="cex-line">  <span class="cex-keyword">const</span> leave = () =&gt; {</span>
<span class="cex-line">    <span class="cex-keyword">const</span> frame = frames.pop();</span>
<span class="cex-line">    <span class="cex-keyword">const</span> n = prepared.get(frame.func).results;</span>
<span class="cex-line">    <span class="cex-keyword">for</span> (<span class="cex-keyword">let</span> i = <span class="cex-number">0</span>; i &lt; n; i++) P[frame.base + i] = P[sp - n + i];</span>
<span class="cex-line">    sp = frame.base + (frames.length ? n : <span class="cex-number">0</span>);</span>
<span class="cex-line">  };</span>
<span class="cex-line">  <span class="cex-comment">// A call&#39;s arguments become the new frame&#39;s first locals; the other locals</span></span>
<span class="cex-line">  <span class="cex-comment">// start as nothing.</span></span>
<span class="cex-line">  <span class="cex-keyword">const</span> enter = (func, args) =&gt; {</span>
<span class="cex-line">    <span class="cex-keyword">const</span> locals = <span class="cex-keyword">new</span> Int32Array(args.length + prepared.get(func).locals);</span>
<span class="cex-line">    locals.set(args);</span>
<span class="cex-line">    frames.push({ func, locals, base: sp, labels: [] });</span>
<span class="cex-line">  };</span></code></pre><div class="cex-foot"> Select code to copy. Scroll horizontally if needed.</div></figure>
<p>These three follow lesson 08&#39;s branch and return. A label remembers the stack&#39;s height when its block began and how many results the block leaves. <code>branch</code> copies those results&#39; producers down to that height and cuts <code>sp</code> there, so the values a branch drops take their producers with them. A branch to a <code>loop</code> keeps the loop&#39;s label, because the loop can be branched to again. <code>leave</code> does the same for a function&#39;s results, and <code>enter</code> starts a frame whose first locals are the producers of the call&#39;s arguments and whose other locals are nothing.</p>
<h3 id="move-the-producers-instruction-by-instruction">Move the producers instruction by instruction</h3>
<p>Replace the <code>follow</code> region:</p>
<figure class="code-example"><figcaption><strong>follow: one case per kind of instruction</strong><span class="cex-location">examples/query-checkpoint.mjs · follow</span></figcaption><p class="cex-change">Replace the follow region.</p><pre tabindex="0" aria-label="follow: one case per kind of instruction; code scrolls horizontally when needed"><code><span class="cex-line">  <span class="cex-comment">// Move the producers as the instruction at tick t is about to move values.</span></span>
<span class="cex-line">  <span class="cex-comment">// stack is the machine&#39;s value stack before the instruction runs.</span></span>
<span class="cex-line">  <span class="cex-keyword">const</span> follow = (kind, ins, frame, t, stack) =&gt; {</span>
<span class="cex-line">    switch (kind) {</span>
<span class="cex-line">      case <span class="cex-string">&#39;block&#39;</span>:</span>
<span class="cex-line">        frame.labels.push({ height: sp, arity: ins[<span class="cex-number">1</span>] ? <span class="cex-number">1</span> : <span class="cex-number">0</span>, loop: <span class="cex-keyword">false</span> });</span>
<span class="cex-line">        break;</span>
<span class="cex-line">      case <span class="cex-string">&#39;loop&#39;</span>:</span>
<span class="cex-line">        frame.labels.push({ height: sp, arity: <span class="cex-number">0</span>, loop: <span class="cex-keyword">true</span> });</span>
<span class="cex-line">        break;</span>
<span class="cex-line">      case <span class="cex-string">&#39;br&#39;</span>:</span>
<span class="cex-line">        branch(frame, ins[<span class="cex-number">1</span>]);</span>
<span class="cex-line">        break;</span>
<span class="cex-line">      case <span class="cex-string">&#39;br_if&#39;</span>:</span>
<span class="cex-line">        sp--; <span class="cex-comment">// the condition is a decision: on no chain</span></span>
<span class="cex-line">        <span class="cex-keyword">if</span> (stack[stack.length - <span class="cex-number">1</span>] !== <span class="cex-number">0</span>) branch(frame, ins[<span class="cex-number">1</span>]);</span>
<span class="cex-line">        break;</span>
<span class="cex-line">      case <span class="cex-string">&#39;end&#39;</span>:</span>
<span class="cex-line">        <span class="cex-keyword">if</span> (frame.labels.length) frame.labels.pop();</span>
<span class="cex-line">        <span class="cex-keyword">else</span> leave();</span>
<span class="cex-line">        break;</span>
<span class="cex-line">      case <span class="cex-string">&#39;return&#39;</span>:</span>
<span class="cex-line">        leave();</span>
<span class="cex-line">        break;</span>
<span class="cex-line">      case <span class="cex-string">&#39;call&#39;</span>: {</span>
<span class="cex-line">        <span class="cex-keyword">const</span> n = program.typeOf(ins[<span class="cex-number">1</span>]).params.length;</span>
<span class="cex-line">        <span class="cex-keyword">if</span> (ins[<span class="cex-number">1</span>] &lt; nImports) {</span>
<span class="cex-line">          sp -= n; <span class="cex-comment">// an import&#39;s arguments are not followed</span></span>
<span class="cex-line">          <span class="cex-keyword">if</span> (program.typeOf(ins[<span class="cex-number">1</span>]).results.length)</span>
<span class="cex-line">            push(answerId(answered.position()));</span>
<span class="cex-line">        } <span class="cex-keyword">else</span> {</span>
<span class="cex-line">          <span class="cex-keyword">const</span> args = P.slice(sp - n, sp);</span>
<span class="cex-line">          sp -= n;</span>
<span class="cex-line">          enter(ins[<span class="cex-number">1</span>], args);</span>
<span class="cex-line">        }</span>
<span class="cex-line">        break;</span>
<span class="cex-line">      }</span>
<span class="cex-line">      case <span class="cex-string">&#39;local.get&#39;</span>:</span>
<span class="cex-line">        push(frame.locals[ins[<span class="cex-number">1</span>]]);</span>
<span class="cex-line">        break;</span>
<span class="cex-line">      case <span class="cex-string">&#39;local.set&#39;</span>:</span>
<span class="cex-line">        frame.locals[ins[<span class="cex-number">1</span>]] = P[--sp];</span>
<span class="cex-line">        break;</span>
<span class="cex-line">      case <span class="cex-string">&#39;local.tee&#39;</span>:</span>
<span class="cex-line">        frame.locals[ins[<span class="cex-number">1</span>]] = P[sp - <span class="cex-number">1</span>];</span>
<span class="cex-line">        break;</span>
<span class="cex-line">      case <span class="cex-string">&#39;global.get&#39;</span>:</span>
<span class="cex-line">        push(G[ins[<span class="cex-number">1</span>]]);</span>
<span class="cex-line">        break;</span>
<span class="cex-line">      case <span class="cex-string">&#39;global.set&#39;</span>:</span>
<span class="cex-line">        G[ins[<span class="cex-number">1</span>]] = P[--sp];</span>
<span class="cex-line">        break;</span>
<span class="cex-line">      case <span class="cex-string">&#39;const&#39;</span>:</span>
<span class="cex-line">        push(<span class="cex-number">0</span>);</span>
<span class="cex-line">        break;</span>
<span class="cex-line">      case <span class="cex-string">&#39;unary&#39;</span>:</span>
<span class="cex-line">        break; <span class="cex-comment">// the same operand, so the same chain</span></span>
<span class="cex-line">      case <span class="cex-string">&#39;binary&#39;</span>:</span>
<span class="cex-line">        nScratch = <span class="cex-number">0</span>;</span>
<span class="cex-line">        add(P[sp - <span class="cex-number">2</span>]);</span>
<span class="cex-line">        add(P[sp - <span class="cex-number">1</span>]);</span>
<span class="cex-line">        sp -= <span class="cex-number">1</span>;</span>
<span class="cex-line">        P[sp - <span class="cex-number">1</span>] = made(t);</span>
<span class="cex-line">        break;</span>
<span class="cex-line">      case <span class="cex-string">&#39;select&#39;</span>:</span>
<span class="cex-line">        nScratch = <span class="cex-number">0</span>;</span>
<span class="cex-line">        add(P[sp - <span class="cex-number">3</span>]);</span>
<span class="cex-line">        add(P[sp - <span class="cex-number">2</span>]);</span>
<span class="cex-line">        add(P[sp - <span class="cex-number">1</span>]);</span>
<span class="cex-line">        sp -= <span class="cex-number">2</span>;</span>
<span class="cex-line">        P[sp - <span class="cex-number">1</span>] = made(t);</span>
<span class="cex-line">        break;</span>
<span class="cex-line">      case <span class="cex-string">&#39;load&#39;</span>:</span>
<span class="cex-line">        load(ins, t, stack);</span>
<span class="cex-line">        break;</span>
<span class="cex-line">      case <span class="cex-string">&#39;store&#39;</span>:</span>
<span class="cex-line">        store();</span>
<span class="cex-line">        break;</span>
<span class="cex-line">    }</span>
<span class="cex-line">  };</span></code></pre><div class="cex-foot"> Select code to copy. Scroll horizontally if needed.</div></figure>
<p><code>follow</code> runs just before the machine runs the instruction, while the operands are still on the machine&#39;s stack, and does to <code>P</code> what the instruction is about to do to the stack. Most cases are one line. <code>br_if</code> drops its condition&#39;s producer without recording it anywhere, which is &quot;decisions are not followed&quot; in code; it reads the condition&#39;s value from the machine&#39;s stack only to know whether the branch will be taken. An import call drops its arguments&#39; producers and pushes the leaf of the answer the machine is about to use. A call to a defined function moves its arguments&#39; producers into the new frame. Loads and stores go to the next region.</p>
<h3 id="loads-and-stores-bytes-not-addresses">Loads and stores: bytes, not addresses</h3>
<p>Replace the <code>memory</code> region:</p>
<figure class="code-example"><figcaption><strong>A load depends on the bytes it reads; a store on its value</strong><span class="cex-location">examples/query-checkpoint.mjs · memory</span></figcaption><p class="cex-change">Replace the memory region.</p><pre tabindex="0" aria-label="A load depends on the bytes it reads; a store on its value; code scrolls horizontally when needed"><code><span class="cex-line">  <span class="cex-comment">// A load depends on the bytes it read, each on the store that last wrote</span></span>
<span class="cex-line">  <span class="cex-comment">// it, or on the byte itself if no store has. Its address is not followed.</span></span>
<span class="cex-line">  <span class="cex-keyword">const</span> load = (ins, t, stack) =&gt; {</span>
<span class="cex-line">    <span class="cex-keyword">const</span> address = (stack[stack.length - <span class="cex-number">1</span>] &gt;&gt;&gt; <span class="cex-number">0</span>) + ins[<span class="cex-number">2</span>];</span>
<span class="cex-line">    nScratch = <span class="cex-number">0</span>;</span>
<span class="cex-line">    <span class="cex-keyword">for</span> (<span class="cex-keyword">let</span> i = <span class="cex-number">0</span>; i &lt; LOAD_SIZE[ins[<span class="cex-number">0</span>]]; i++) {</span>
<span class="cex-line">      <span class="cex-keyword">if</span> (address + i &gt;= memorySize) break;</span>
<span class="cex-line">      <span class="cex-keyword">const</span> w = writer[address + i];</span>
<span class="cex-line">      add(w !== <span class="cex-number">0</span> ? w : initialId(address + i));</span>
<span class="cex-line">    }</span>
<span class="cex-line">    P[sp - <span class="cex-number">1</span>] = made(t);</span>
<span class="cex-line">  };</span>
<span class="cex-line">  <span class="cex-comment">// A store&#39;s only input is its value&#39;s producer; its address is not</span></span>
<span class="cex-line">  <span class="cex-comment">// followed. keepWrites then makes this tick the writer of every byte.</span></span>
<span class="cex-line">  <span class="cex-keyword">const</span> store = () =&gt; {</span>
<span class="cex-line">    <span class="cex-keyword">const</span> value = P[--sp];</span>
<span class="cex-line">    sp--;</span>
<span class="cex-line">    <span class="cex-keyword">if</span> (value !== <span class="cex-number">0</span>) deps.push(value);</span>
<span class="cex-line">  };</span></code></pre><div class="cex-foot"> Select code to copy. Scroll horizontally if needed.</div></figure>
<p>A load reads its address from the machine&#39;s stack and looks up, in <code>writer</code>, the store that last wrote each byte it is about to read. A byte no store has written gives its initial leaf. The load&#39;s result replaces the address&#39;s producer on top of <code>P</code>, so the address is never an input. A store pops its value&#39;s producer and records it as its only input, then drops the address&#39;s producer. After the machine runs it, <code>keepWrites</code> makes this tick the writer of every byte it wrote, so the next load of those bytes depends on this store.</p>
<h3 id="replay-once">Replay once</h3>
<p>Replace the <code>replay</code> region:</p>
<figure class="code-example"><figcaption><strong>Replay every call, keeping the producers in step with the machine</strong><span class="cex-location">examples/query-checkpoint.mjs · replay</span></figcaption><p class="cex-change">Replace the replay region.</p><pre tabindex="0" aria-label="Replay every call, keeping the producers in step with the machine; code scrolls horizontally when needed"><code><span class="cex-line">  <span class="cex-keyword">for</span> (<span class="cex-keyword">let</span> k = <span class="cex-number">0</span>; k &lt; calls.length; k++) {</span>
<span class="cex-line">    m.begin(calls[k].name, calls[k].args);</span>
<span class="cex-line">    enter(</span>
<span class="cex-line">      program.exportIndex(calls[k].name),</span>
<span class="cex-line">      calls[k].args.map((_, i) =&gt; argId(k, i)),</span>
<span class="cex-line">    );</span>
<span class="cex-line">    while (m.running) {</span>
<span class="cex-line">      <span class="cex-keyword">const</span> top = s.frames[s.frames.length - <span class="cex-number">1</span>];</span>
<span class="cex-line">      <span class="cex-keyword">const</span> frame = frames[frames.length - <span class="cex-number">1</span>];</span>
<span class="cex-line">      <span class="cex-keyword">const</span> fn = prepared.get(top.func);</span>
<span class="cex-line">      <span class="cex-keyword">const</span> ins = fn.code[top.at];</span>
<span class="cex-line">      <span class="cex-keyword">const</span> kind = fn.kinds[top.at];</span>
<span class="cex-line">      <span class="cex-keyword">const</span> t = s.tick + <span class="cex-number">1</span>;</span>
<span class="cex-line">      depStart.push(deps.n);</span>
<span class="cex-line">      isStore.push(kind === <span class="cex-string">&#39;store&#39;</span> ? <span class="cex-number">1</span> : <span class="cex-number">0</span>);</span>
<span class="cex-line">      follow(kind, ins, frame, t, s.stack);</span>
<span class="cex-line">      <span class="cex-keyword">const</span> asked = answered.position();</span>
<span class="cex-line">      <span class="cex-keyword">const</span> event = m.step();</span>
<span class="cex-line">      keepWrites(event, t);</span>
<span class="cex-line">      <span class="cex-comment">// The producers must still match the machine: its stack, its frames and</span></span>
<span class="cex-line">      <span class="cex-comment">// the answers it has used.</span></span>
<span class="cex-line">      <span class="cex-keyword">const</span> used = kind === <span class="cex-string">&#39;call&#39;</span> &amp;&amp; ins[<span class="cex-number">1</span>] &lt; nImports ? <span class="cex-number">1</span> : <span class="cex-number">0</span>;</span>
<span class="cex-line">      <span class="cex-keyword">if</span> (</span>
<span class="cex-line">        frame.func !== top.func ||</span>
<span class="cex-line">        sp !== s.stack.length ||</span>
<span class="cex-line">        frames.length !== s.frames.length ||</span>
<span class="cex-line">        answered.position() !== asked + used ||</span>
<span class="cex-line">        (event.writes.length !== <span class="cex-number">0</span>) !== (kind === <span class="cex-string">&#39;store&#39;</span>)</span>
<span class="cex-line">      )</span>
<span class="cex-line">        <span class="cex-keyword">throw</span> Error(</span>
<span class="cex-line">          <span class="cex-string">`buildIndex: lost track of the machine at tick ${t} (${ins[0]} at (${event.func}, ${event.at}))`</span>,</span>
<span class="cex-line">        );</span>
<span class="cex-line">    }</span>
<span class="cex-line">    <span class="cex-keyword">const</span> result = s.result === <span class="cex-keyword">undefined</span> ? <span class="cex-keyword">null</span> : s.result;</span>
<span class="cex-line">    <span class="cex-keyword">if</span> (!Object.<span class="cex-keyword">is</span>(result, recording.results[k]))</span>
<span class="cex-line">      <span class="cex-keyword">throw</span> Error(</span>
<span class="cex-line">        <span class="cex-string">`buildIndex: call ${k} returned ${result}, the recording says ${recording.results[k]}`</span>,</span>
<span class="cex-line">      );</span>
<span class="cex-line">  }</span>
<span class="cex-line">  depStart.push(deps.n);</span></code></pre><div class="cex-foot"> Select code to copy. Scroll horizontally if needed.</div></figure>
<p>Each call begins with a frame whose locals are the call&#39;s argument leaves. Then, for every instruction, the loop records where its inputs start, moves the producers with <code>follow</code>, lets your machine run it and keeps its writes. After each instruction it compares the producers with the machine: the same stack height, the same number of frames, one answer used by an import call and none otherwise, and writes exactly when the instruction was a store. A mistake in <code>follow</code> then stops the replay at the first tick where the two part, instead of giving wrong chains later. After each call, the result must be the recorded one, as in lesson 09.</p>
<h3 id="walk-back-from-a-store">Walk back from a store</h3>
<p>Replace the <code>sources</code> region:</p>
<figure class="code-example"><figcaption><strong>sources: visit each producer on the chain once</strong><span class="cex-location">examples/query-checkpoint.mjs · sources</span></figcaption><p class="cex-change">Replace the sources region.</p><pre tabindex="0" aria-label="sources: visit each producer on the chain once; code scrolls horizontally when needed"><code><span class="cex-line">  <span class="cex-comment">// seenTick[t] === epoch: tick t was visited during the current question.</span></span>
<span class="cex-line">  <span class="cex-keyword">const</span> { nAnswers, nArgs, argCall, argPos } = leaves;</span>
<span class="cex-line">  <span class="cex-keyword">const</span> seenTick = <span class="cex-keyword">new</span> Int32Array(end + <span class="cex-number">1</span>);</span>
<span class="cex-line">  <span class="cex-keyword">const</span> seenLeaf = <span class="cex-keyword">new</span> Int32Array(nAnswers + nArgs + memorySize);</span>
<span class="cex-line">  <span class="cex-keyword">let</span> epoch = <span class="cex-number">0</span>;</span>
<span class="cex-line">  <span class="cex-keyword">const</span> sources = (tick) =&gt; {</span>
<span class="cex-line">    <span class="cex-keyword">if</span> (!Number.isInteger(tick) || tick &lt; <span class="cex-number">1</span> || tick &gt; end || !isStore[tick])</span>
<span class="cex-line">      <span class="cex-keyword">throw</span> Error(</span>
<span class="cex-line">        <span class="cex-string">`sources: tick ${tick} is not the tick of a store instruction`</span>,</span>
<span class="cex-line">      );</span>
<span class="cex-line">    epoch++;</span>
<span class="cex-line">    <span class="cex-keyword">const</span> stores = [];</span>
<span class="cex-line">    <span class="cex-keyword">const</span> answers = [];</span>
<span class="cex-line">    <span class="cex-keyword">const</span> args = [];</span>
<span class="cex-line">    <span class="cex-keyword">const</span> initial = [];</span>
<span class="cex-line">    <span class="cex-keyword">const</span> todo = [];</span>
<span class="cex-line">    <span class="cex-keyword">for</span> (<span class="cex-keyword">let</span> i = depStart[tick]; i &lt; depStart[tick + <span class="cex-number">1</span>]; i++)</span>
<span class="cex-line">      todo.push(deps[i]);</span>
<span class="cex-line">    while (todo.length) {</span>
<span class="cex-line">      <span class="cex-keyword">const</span> id = todo.pop();</span>
<span class="cex-line">      <span class="cex-keyword">if</span> (id &gt; <span class="cex-number">0</span>) {</span>
<span class="cex-line">        <span class="cex-keyword">if</span> (seenTick[id] === epoch) continue;</span>
<span class="cex-line">        seenTick[id] = epoch;</span>
<span class="cex-line">        <span class="cex-keyword">if</span> (isStore[id]) stores.push(id);</span>
<span class="cex-line">        <span class="cex-keyword">for</span> (<span class="cex-keyword">let</span> i = depStart[id]; i &lt; depStart[id + <span class="cex-number">1</span>]; i++)</span>
<span class="cex-line">          todo.push(deps[i]);</span>
<span class="cex-line">        continue;</span>
<span class="cex-line">      }</span>
<span class="cex-line">      <span class="cex-keyword">const</span> leaf = -<span class="cex-number">1</span> - id;</span>
<span class="cex-line">      <span class="cex-keyword">if</span> (seenLeaf[leaf] === epoch) continue;</span>
<span class="cex-line">      seenLeaf[leaf] = epoch;</span>
<span class="cex-line">      <span class="cex-keyword">if</span> (leaf &lt; nAnswers) answers.push(leaf);</span>
<span class="cex-line">      <span class="cex-keyword">else</span> <span class="cex-keyword">if</span> (leaf &lt; nAnswers + nArgs) args.push(leaf - nAnswers);</span>
<span class="cex-line">      <span class="cex-keyword">else</span> initial.push(leaf - nAnswers - nArgs);</span>
<span class="cex-line">    }</span>
<span class="cex-line">    <span class="cex-keyword">const</span> up = (a, b) =&gt; a - b;</span>
<span class="cex-line">    <span class="cex-keyword">return</span> {</span>
<span class="cex-line">      stores: stores.sort(up),</span>
<span class="cex-line">      answers: answers.sort(up),</span>
<span class="cex-line">      args: args.sort(up).map((x) =&gt; [argCall[x], argPos[x]]),</span>
<span class="cex-line">      initial: initial.sort(up),</span>
<span class="cex-line">    };</span>
<span class="cex-line">  };</span></code></pre><div class="cex-foot"> Select code to copy. Scroll horizontally if needed.</div></figure>
<p>The walk starts from the store&#39;s inputs, its value&#39;s producer, and keeps a list of producers still to visit. A tick is visited once: it is noted if it was a store, and its own inputs join the list. A leaf goes into its list according to its range. <code>seenTick</code> and <code>seenLeaf</code> mark what this question has visited with the number <code>epoch</code>, which goes up by one for every question, so nothing has to be cleared between questions. The store asked about is never in its own list, because the walk starts from its inputs.</p>
<p>Here is one chain, worked through. In <code>project/run42.json</code> the first shot is fired by call 19, and on the first game frame of its flight, call 20, the shell&#39;s new position is stored at <code>g + 40</code> at tick 89,345. <code>sources(89345)</code> holds 16 stores and 2 answers:</p>
<ul>
<li>the position and the horizontal speed that firing stored, at ticks 88,529 and 88,553 in call 19, because this game frame&#39;s position is the last position plus the speed times the game frame&#39;s length, plus the wind&#39;s push</li>
<li>the speed was the power times a constant times the cosine of the angle, so the chain holds the 11 stores of the power made by the presses of up in calls 2 to 12, and before them the store at tick 69,170 in <code>game_init</code> that set the starting power of 60 (an 8-byte store that wrote the angle and the power together)</li>
<li>the key at <code>g + 92</code>, stored at tick 69,157, because the game keeps the power XORed with it, as it keeps the flag&#39;s position in lesson 08&#39;s <code>r_target_x</code>, and with mode 4 off the key is 0</li>
<li>the cannon&#39;s position at <code>g + 20</code>, stored at tick 69,167, from which the shell&#39;s first position was computed</li>
<li>answer 1, the cosine of the barrel&#39;s angle, and answer 3, this game frame&#39;s wind.</li>
</ul>
<p>By rule, the angle isn&#39;t on the chain, because it reached the outside world only as the argument of <code>cos</code>, and an import&#39;s arguments aren&#39;t followed. Nor is the pointer <code>g</code>, because it was only ever an address.</p>
<p>Question 11b: in lesson 09&#39;s recording, made with the server defences on, the shell&#39;s position is stored at <code>g + 40</code> on every game frame of a flight. How many <code>server_wind</code> answers are on the chain of the position stored on the tenth game frame of the first flight? Commit:</p>
<figure class="code-example"><figcaption><strong>Observed output</strong></figcaption><pre tabindex="0" aria-label="Observed output; code scrolls horizontally when needed"><code><span class="cex-line">node lab.mjs predict project 11b YOUR_ANSWER</span></code></pre><div class="cex-foot"> Select code to copy. Scroll horizontally if needed.</div></figure>
<p>Checks <code>11.sources-lob</code> and <code>11.sources-lob2</code> ask generated questions about Lob and Lob II recordings, and <code>11.sources-rules</code> asks about a small program built to use the rules Lob never needs: a global that carries a value, a function that takes arguments and returns a result, a block that leaves a value, a branch that drops values. Every address that small program loads from or stores to is a constant, or computed only from constants, such as a loop counter that starts at a constant. Each check compares your four lists one by one. The lists it expects were worked out by a brute force that carries every value&#39;s full set of sources forward through the whole recording, a different method from the walk above, so the same mistake is unlikely in both.</p>
<p>All ten regions are filled. Run the unit&#39;s checks, describing what you did:</p>
<figure class="code-example"><figcaption><strong>Terminal command</strong></figcaption><pre tabindex="0" aria-label="Terminal command; code scrolls horizontally when needed"><code><span class="cex-line"># After filling the type-in route&#39;s starter from the listings:</span>
<span class="cex-line">node lab.mjs check project 11 --help-used &quot;filled ten regions from chapter listings&quot;</span>
<span class="cex-line"># After following the supplied route:</span>
<span class="cex-line">node lab.mjs check project 11 --help-used &quot;supplied query checkpoint; followed the explanations and tours&quot;</span></code></pre><div class="cex-foot"> Select code to copy. Scroll horizontally if needed.</div></figure>
<p>Every unit 11 check should pass. If one fails, its first mismatch names the section to reread. Keep the failing attempt and your explanation before you edit.</p>
<h2 id="cost">Cost</h2>
<p><code>buildIndex</code> may replay the recording once or twice, and after that no question may replay it. Check <code>11.no-replay</code> counts the instructions your machine runs while hundreds of questions are answered, and expects none.</p>
<p>See what your index kept for lesson 09&#39;s recording, and what asking it costs:</p>
<figure class="code-example"><figcaption><strong>Observed output</strong></figcaption><pre tabindex="0" aria-label="Observed output; code scrolls horizontally when needed"><code><span class="cex-line">node examples/show-index.mjs project project/run42.json</span></code></pre><div class="cex-foot"> Select code to copy. Scroll horizontally if needed.</div></figure>
<figure class="code-example"><figcaption><strong>What the index holds, and the instructions run to ask it</strong><span class="cex-location">examples/index-output.txt</span></figcaption><pre tabindex="0" aria-label="What the index holds, and the instructions run to ask it; code scrolls horizontally when needed"><code><span class="cex-line">project/run42.json: 652927 instructions in 759 calls</span>
<span class="cex-line">building the index ran 652927 instructions on your machine</span>
<span class="cex-line">per-byte lists: 65859 entries, for 12301 bytes written at least once</span>
<span class="cex-line">the most written byte is 65508, written 2944 times; a binary search in its list takes at most 12 comparisons</span>
<span class="cex-line">sources asked about all 36810 stores: the longest chain holds 739 stores</span>
<span class="cex-line">instructions run while answering those questions: 0</span></code></pre><div class="cex-foot"> Select code to copy. Scroll horizontally if needed.</div></figure>
<p>Building the index ran exactly one replay of the run. The per-byte lists hold the 65,859 entries counted earlier, for 12,301 bytes. The most written byte lies in the C stack just below 65,536, and a binary search finds any write in its list in at most 12 comparisons. The script then asked <code>sources</code> about every store of the run, and your machine ran no instruction while it did: everything a question needs was kept during the replay.</p>
<figure class="code-example"><figcaption><strong>Observed output</strong></figcaption><pre tabindex="0" aria-label="Observed output; code scrolls horizontally when needed"><code><span class="cex-line">node debug.mjs project project/run42.json</span></code></pre><div class="cex-foot"> Select code to copy. Scroll horizontally if needed.</div></figure>
<p>As in lesson 10, you can also put the commands in a file, one per line, and pass it as the last argument, for a session with no keyboard.</p>
<p>In <code>debug.mjs</code>, <code>who ADDR</code> asks your index for the last writer, and <code>sources</code> asks for the chain of the store at the current tick. Stand right after a store with <code>who</code> or <code>last-write</code>, then ask <code>sources</code>. <h2 id="decisions-are-not-followed">Decisions are not followed</h2>
<p>Decisions aren&#39;t on a chain. A <code>br_if</code> pops a condition and branches, and the branch decides which instructions run, but no value flows from the condition into what those instructions compute.</p>

<h2 id="use-it-on-a-new-case-where-a-value-in-memory-came-from">Use it on a new case: where a value in memory came from</h2>
<p><code>sources</code> answers for a store at a tick. When you look at memory in the debugger, you see a value at a position instead, with no store in sight. Write <code>valueSources(index, { address, size, position })</code> in <code>project/value-sources.mjs</code>, which both route commands created. If you didn&#39;t use them, copy <code>starter/value-sources.mjs</code> to <code>project/value-sources.mjs</code> first. No finished version is supplied, and none of the listings above does this. Its contract:</p>
<ul>
<li>It returns <code>{ stores, answers, args, initial }</code>, in the same form as <code>sources</code>, for the value held by the <code>size</code> bytes at <code>address</code> at position <code>position</code>, the moment after <code>position</code> instructions.</li>
<li>For each byte, if a store wrote it at or before that position, the last such store and everything on that store&#39;s chain belong to the answer. A byte no store had written by then is an <code>initial</code> byte itself.</li>
<li>So the stores that last wrote the bytes are in <code>stores</code> themselves, unlike <code>sources</code>, which leaves out the store it was asked about. Bytes written by different stores bring the chains of all of them, as a load of those bytes would.</li>
<li>Each list is sorted in increasing order without repeats, and <code>args</code> by call, then argument index.</li>
<li>Refuse with an error: an <code>address</code>, <code>size</code> or <code>position</code> that isn&#39;t a whole number, a <code>size</code> below 1, bytes outside memory, or a position outside 0 to <code>index.end</code>.</li>
<li>Memory is 131,072 bytes in every recording of Lob and Lob II, two WebAssembly pages of 64 KiB (<code>API.md</code>, &quot;Memory&quot;), so bytes outside memory are any below address 0 or at 131,072 and above. The index doesn&#39;t report memory&#39;s size, and <code>API.md</code> doesn&#39;t say what <code>lastWriter</code> does with an address outside memory, so test the bytes against 131,072 yourself before you ask it anything.</li>
<li>Use only <code>index.end</code>, <code>index.lastWriter</code>, <code>index.sources</code> and that fixed size of memory, so your function works with any index that meets <code>API.md</code>.</li>
</ul>
<p>The budget holds for every question, whatever the bytes or the position, a refused one included: <code>valueSources</code> may run no instruction, because <code>lastWriter</code> and <code>sources</code> answer from the index without replaying. The checker counts your machine&#39;s <code>step</code> calls while each call to <code>valueSources</code> runs. Building the two indexes it asks is not counted, and the whole check must finish within 120 seconds.</p>
<p>Before you write code, answer two questions in <code>project/report.md</code>. Which <code>beforeTick</code> do you pass to <code>lastWriter</code> for a value at position <code>p</code>, and what goes wrong with the other choice? Two bytes of a 4-byte value were written by one store: how many times does that store appear in your answer, and why? Keep that first reasoning. Then run the checker on the unfinished file, implement, and run it again, describing assistance honestly each time:</p>
<figure class="code-example"><figcaption><strong>Terminal command</strong></figcaption><pre tabindex="0" aria-label="Terminal command; code scrolls horizontally when needed"><code><span class="cex-line">node examples/check-value-sources.mjs project --help-used &quot;initial attempt; nothing written&quot;</span>
<span class="cex-line">node examples/check-value-sources.mjs project --help-used &quot;describe what helped your implementation&quot;</span></code></pre><div class="cex-foot"> Select code to copy. Scroll horizontally if needed.</div></figure>
<p>The checker copies <code>machine.mjs</code>, <code>recorder.mjs</code>, <code>query.mjs</code>, <code>value-sources.mjs</code>, <code>PROJECT.json</code> and your <code>report.md</code> into a new folder under <code>project/attempts/</code> before it runs anything, and saves its results beside them in <code>vsources-receipt.json</code>. `courses/time-travel-debugger-part-two/lessons/11.md`:

```md
# 11 · Question a recording

Lesson 10's `lastWrite` searches backward one snapshot at a time, so a byte last written long ago, on a page other code writes all the time, costs about as much as a replay from the start. And a single last write rarely explains a wrong value, because that write copied a value computed from other values. By the end of this lesson your `query.mjs` will build an index of a recording in one replay and then tell you, without replaying, who last wrote this byte before this tick, and which stores, answers and arguments the value stored at this tick was computed from.

## Start

Run these commands from this course's directory, in the project you used for lessons 08 to 10. Before this lesson your debugger moves backward through `project/run42.json`, but `project/query.mjs` is a stub, so `who` and `sources` in `debug.mjs` stop with "not written yet". After it, both answer from an index of the recording, built once, and no later question replays anything.

Your machine and recorder must pass their checks first, `node lab.mjs check project 08` and `node lab.mjs check project 09`, because the index replays the recording on your machine with your recorder's `recordedImports`. `debug.mjs` also needs lesson 10's debugger to pass `node lab.mjs check project 10`. If any of them fails and you want to go on with this lesson, make a new project with `node examples/start-chapter.mjs project11 supplied`, then `node examples/start-recorder.mjs project11 supplied` and `node examples/start-debugger.mjs project11 supplied`, record its run with `node lab.mjs record project11 --world 42 --out project11/run42.json`, and use `project11` wherever this lesson says `project`.

**Code scope:** walk through ten marked regions of `project/query.mjs`, 320 lines including blank lines: `keep-writes`, `by-byte`, `last-writer`, `leaves`, `producers`, `frames`, `follow`, `memory`, `replay` and `sources`. The rest of the file is supplied, 178 lines: the imports, the table that sorts the 62 instructions by how they move values, a typed array that grows, the check that the recording belongs to the program, the machine set up to answer from the recording, and the call that hands what the replay kept to the questions. Two of those supplied parts are toured below. The finished file, the end-of-unit checkpoint, is `examples/query-checkpoint.mjs`, 518 lines.

**Time:** allow about 40 to 50 minutes to read and 2 to 4 hours to implement, diagnose and try the new application. These are planning estimates, not measured learner times.
