`courses/time-travel-debugger-part-two/public/code-example.mjs`:

```mjs
// Portable, dependency-free presentation for authored JavaScript/Python examples.
// This is lexical coloring, not a parser or a correctness check.
const escape = value => String(value).replace(/[&<>"']/g, c => ({'&':'&amp;','<':'&lt;','>':'&gt;','"':'&quot;',"'":'&#39;'}[c]));
const keywords = new Set(('async await const let var function return throw new if else for of in try catch finally import from export class true false null undefined def return raise if else elif for in try except finally import from as True False None and or not is with').split(' '));
function color(line, language) {
  if (!['js','javascript','python','py'].includes(language)) return escape(line);
  const pattern = language === 'python' || language === 'py'
    ? /#[^\n]*|"(?:\\.|[^"\\])*"|'(?:\\.|[^'\\])*'|\b(?:0x[\da-fA-F]+|\d+(?:\.\d+)?)\b|\b[A-Za-z_]\w*\b/g
    : /\/\/[^\n]*|"(?:\\.|[^"\\])*"|'(?:\\.|[^'\\])*'|`(?:\\.|[^`\\])*`|\b(?:0x[\da-fA-F]+|\d+(?:\.\d+)?)\b|\b[A-Za-z_$][\w$]*\b/g;
  let result = '', end = 0;
  for (const match of line.matchAll(pattern)) {
    result += escape(line.slice(end, match.index));
    const token = match[0];
    const kind = /^(#|\/\/)/.test(token) ? 'comment' : /^["'`]/.test(token) ? 'string'
      : /^\d/.test(token) ? 'number' : keywords.has(token) ? 'keyword' : null;
    result += kind ? `<span class="cex-${kind}">${escape(token)}</span>` : escape(token);
    end = match.index + token.length;
  }
  return result + escape(line.slice(end));
}
export function renderCode(source, info = '') {
  const match = info.trim().match(/^(\S+)?(?:\s+(\{.*\}))?$/);
  if (!match) throw Error('Invalid code fence metadata');
  const language = match[1] || 'text';
  const meta = match[2] ? JSON.parse(match[2]) : {};
  if (!meta || Array.isArray(meta) || typeof meta !== 'object') throw Error('Code metadata must be an object');
  for (const name of ['file','region','title','change']) {
    if (meta[name] !== undefined && typeof meta[name] !== 'string') throw Error(`Invalid code ${name}`);
  }
  const lines = source.split('\n'), focus = meta.focus || [];
  if (!Array.isArray(focus) || focus.some(n => !Number.isInteger(n) || n < 1 || n > lines.length)) throw Error('Code emphasis must name existing lines');
  const label = meta.title || ({sh:'Terminal command',text:'Observed output',js:'JavaScript',python:'Python'})[language] || language;
  const location = meta.file ? `<span class="cex-location">${escape(meta.file)}${meta.region ? ` · ${escape(meta.region)}` : ''}</span>` : '';
  const change = meta.change ? `<p class="cex-change">${escape(meta.change)}</p>` : '';
  const emphasis = focus.length ? `<span class="cex-emphasis">Emphasized lines: ${focus.join(', ')}.</span>` : '';
  const code = lines.map((line, i) => `<span class="cex-line${focus.includes(i+1) ? ' cex-focus' : ''}">${color(line, language)}</span>`).join('\n');
  return `<figure class="code-example"><figcaption><strong>${escape(label)}</strong>${location}</figcaption>${change}<pre tabindex="0" aria-label="${escape(label)}; code scrolls horizontally when needed"><code>${code}</code></pre><div class="cex-foot">${emphasis} Select code to copy. Scroll horizontally if needed.</div></figure>`;
}

// Supplied by the course: the one memory hash every part of the course uses,
// so a hash in a recording means the same thing to your code, the lab and the checks.
import { createHash } from 'node:crypto';
export function hashMemory(memory) {
  return createHash('sha256').update(memory).digest('hex');
}

`courses/time-travel-debugger-part-two/public/part-one-vm.mjs`:

```mjs
// Supplied by the course: part one's vm.mjs interface on top of YOUR part-two
// machine. `node lab.mjs wall` copies this file next to a part-one debugger as
// vm.mjs, so that debugger runs unchanged on a real game.
//
// Part one's debugger only ever does three things with a state: it copies it
// (clone), hands it to execute(program, state), which returns a new state, and
// tests it with matches(state, condition). Here a state is
//   { pc, tick, halted, call, machine }
// where machine is your Machine's whole state object. execute() copies the
// whole state with structuredClone and runs one instruction on the copy: that
// copy, 131,072 bytes of memory and all, is what lab.mjs wall measures.
//
// The program part one's Debugger is constructed with is a session object the
// lab builds: { Machine, program, imports, calls, length }. Machine is your class,
// program a loaded listing, calls the list of calls to run one after another.
let current = null;

export const clone = (value) => structuredClone(value);

export function validateProgram(session) {
  if (!session || typeof session.Machine !== 'function' || !Array.isArray(session.calls) || !session.calls.length) {
    throw Error('VM adapter: build the session with lab.mjs wall');
  }
  current = { session, machine: new session.Machine(session.program, session.imports) };
  return session;
}

export function initial() {
  if (!current) throw Error('VM adapter: validateProgram must run before initial');
  const m = new current.session.Machine(current.session.program, current.session.imports);
  return { pc: 0, tick: 0, halted: false, call: 0, machine: m.state };
}

const asNumber = (bytes) => bytes.reduce((n, b, i) => n + b * 2 ** (8 * i), 0);

export function execute(session, state) {
  if (state.halted) throw Error('VM: halted; no instruction executed.');
  const next = structuredClone(state);
  const m = current.machine;
  m.state = next.machine;
  if (!m.running) {
    const c = session.calls[next.call];
    m.begin(c.name, c.args);
  }
  const e = m.step();
  if (!m.running) next.call++;
  next.tick++;
  next.halted = next.call >= session.calls.length;
  const top = m.state.frames[m.state.frames.length - 1];
  next.pc = top ? top.at : 0;
  const event = {
    tick: next.tick, pc: state.pc, op: e.op, emitted: [],
    writes: e.writes.map((w) => ({ address: w.address, before: asNumber(w.before), after: asNumber(w.after) })),
  };
  return { state: next, event };
}

// Part one's conditions. { kind: 'mem', address, equals } reads one byte of the
// game's memory; part one's registers do not exist here.
export function matches(state, condition) {
  if (!condition || condition.kind !== 'mem' || !Number.isInteger(condition.address) || !Number.isSafeInteger(condition.equals)) {
    throw Error('Condition: on the game use {kind:"mem",address:A,equals:V}, where A is a byte address.');
  }
  const memory = state.machine.memory;
  if (condition.address < 0 || condition.address >= memory.length) throw Error(`Condition: address must be 0-${memory.length - 1}.`);
  return memory[condition.address] === condition.equals;
}

```

`courses/time-travel-debugger-part-two/public/program.mjs`:

```mjs
// Supplied by the course: reads a program listing (programs/NAME.json) into
// plain objects. It decodes nothing; the listing was decoded from the .wasm file
// when the course was built (decoding is taught in Sightline).
//
// loadProgram(json or object) returns the listing with three conveniences:
//   program.func(index)    the defined function with that index (imports come first,
//                          so the first defined function has index imports.length)
//   program.typeOf(index)  { params, results } of any function, import or defined
//   program.exportIndex(name)  the function index of an exported function
// Constants are converted: an "i64.const" value "42n" becomes the BigInt 42n,
// and each data segment's hex text becomes a Uint8Array named `bytes`.
import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
import { dirname, join } from 'node:path';

const here = dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url));

export function readProgram(name) {
  return loadProgram(JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(here, '..', 'programs', `${name}.json`), 'utf8')));
}

export function loadProgram(source) {
  if (source && source.loaded === true) return source;
  const p = typeof source === 'string' ? JSON.parse(source) : structuredClone(source);
  if (p?.format !== 'ttd2-program-1') throw Error('loadProgram: not a program listing (format ttd2-program-1)');
  for (const f of p.functions) {
    f.code = f.code.map(ins => ins[0] === 'i64.const' ? [ins[0], BigInt(String(ins[1]).replace(/n$/, ''))] : ins);
  }
  p.data = p.data.map(d => ({ offset: d.offset, bytes: Uint8Array.from(Buffer.from(d.bytes, 'hex')) }));
  const byIndex = new Map(p.functions.map(f => [f.index, f]));
  Object.defineProperties(p, {
    loaded: { value: true },
    func: { value: index => { const f = byIndex.get(index); if (!f) throw Error(`no defined function with index ${index}`); return f; } },
    typeOf: { value: index => index < p.imports.length ? p.types[p.imports[index].type] : p.types[byIndex.get(index)?.type] },
    exportIndex: { value: name => { const e = p.exports.find(x => x.kind === 'func' && x.name === name); if (!e) throw Error(`no exported function named ${name}`); return e.index; } },
  });
  return p;
}

```

`courses/time-travel-debugger-part-two/public/sessions.mjs`:

```mjs
// Supplied by the course: lists of calls that play a game of Lob or Lob II.
//
// session({ seed, mode, plan }) returns [{ name, args }]: game_init(seed, mode),
// then one entry per key press or frame in the plan. A plan is a list of steps:
//   ['up', 5]       press a key five times (left, right, up, down, fire, new)
//   ['frames', 240] let 240 frames pass (240 calls to game_tick)
// The keys: left lowers the barrel, right raises it, up and down change the
// power, fire shoots, new starts a new round (only between shots).
//
// plan({ seed, shots }) makes a plan that aims and fires `shots` times, choosing
// how far to turn the barrel and change the power from its own seed, waits for
// each shell to land and starts a new round after it.
export const KEYS = Object.freeze({ left: 1, right: 2, up: 3, down: 4, fire: 5, new: 6 });

export function session({ seed = 1, mode = 0, plan: steps = [] } = {}) {
  const calls = [{ name: 'game_init', args: [seed, mode] }];
  for (const [what, n = 1] of steps) {
    if (what === 'frames') { for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) calls.push({ name: 'game_tick', args: [] }); continue; }
    const code = KEYS[what];
    if (!code) throw Error(`session: unknown step ${what}`);
    for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) calls.push({ name: 'game_key', args: [code] });
  }
  return calls;
}

export function plan({ seed = 1, shots = 3, flight = 360 } = {}) {
  let x = (seed * 2246822519 + 7) >>> 0 || 1;
  const pick = (n) => { x ^= x << 13; x >>>= 0; x ^= x >>> 17; x ^= x << 5; x >>>= 0; return x % n; };
  const steps = [];
  for (let s = 0; s < shots; s++) {
    const turn = pick(21) - 10, push = pick(31) - 15;
    if (turn) steps.push([turn > 0 ? 'right' : 'left', Math.abs(turn)]);
    if (push) steps.push([push > 0 ? 'up' : 'down', Math.abs(push)]);
    steps.push(['frames', 2 + pick(5)]);
    steps.push(['fire']);
    steps.push(['frames', flight]);
    if (s < shots - 1) steps.push(['new']);
    steps.push(['frames', 2]);
  }
  return steps;
}

```

`courses/time-travel-debugger-part-two/public/world.mjs`:

```mjs
// Supplied by the course: the outside world the game talks to. Lob imports four
// functions from it: sin(x) and cos(x), which the game uses to aim a shot, and
// two "server" calls: server_round(round), the wind level the server announces
// for a new round, and server_wind(), the exact wind the server reports while a
// shell is in the air. The server's answers come from a seed the game never
// sees and change from call to call, the way a real server's do, so a run can
// only be repeated by recording them.
//
// makeWorld(seed) returns { imports, answered } where imports is the object a
// machine is built with and answered counts the calls answered so far.
export function makeWorld(seed = 1) {
  let x = (seed * 2654435761) >>> 0 || 0x9e3779b9;
  const next = () => { x ^= x << 13; x >>>= 0; x ^= x >>> 17; x ^= x << 5; x >>>= 0; return x / 4294967296; };
  let gust = 0;
  const world = { answered: 0 };
  world.imports = {
    sin: (v) => { world.answered++; return Math.sin(v); },
    cos: (v) => { world.answered++; return Math.cos(v); },
    server_round: (round) => { world.answered++; gust = (next() * 2 - 1) * 4; return Math.max(-3, Math.min(3, Math.round(gust / 1.5))) | 0; },   // | 0: never -0
    server_wind: () => { world.answered++; return Math.fround(gust + (next() * 2 - 1) * 0.6); },
  };
  return world;
}

```

`courses/time-travel-debugger-part-two/starter/debugger-build.mjs`:

```mjs
// Unit 10 debugger: run backwards over one recording. API.md, "debugger.mjs", is
// the contract. Lesson 12 adds stack(), stepOut() and function stops to this file.
//
// Position t is the state after t instructions of the whole run, counted across
// calls. Between two calls no function is running, and the next instruction is
// the first one of the next call. The constructor replays the recording once and
// keeps a snapshot every `every` instructions; a page of memory that no
// instruction wrote since the previous snapshot is that snapshot's page object.
//
// Options: { every = 1000, pageSize = 4096, check = true }. With check, the first
// pass compares memory after every call with the recording's hash.
import { createHash } from 'node:crypto';
import { Machine } from './machine.mjs';
import { recordedImports, ReplayDivergence } from './recorder.mjs';

export class Debugger {
  // region: constructor
  constructor() {
    throw Error('constructor: not written yet (lesson 10)');
  }
  // endregion: constructor

  // region: first-pass
  firstPass() {
    throw Error('first-pass: not written yet (lesson 10)');
  }
  // endregion: first-pass

  // region: capture
  capture() {
    throw Error('capture: not written yet (lesson 10)');
  }
  // endregion: capture

  // region: restore
  restore() {
    throw Error('restore: not written yet (lesson 10)');
  }
  // endregion: restore

  // rr's checksum mode: after each call, memory must be what the recording says.
  checkCall(k) {
    const want = this.recording.hashes?.[k];
    const { memory, tick } = this.machine.state;
    const hash = createHash('sha256').update(memory).digest('hex');
    if (want !== undefined && hash !== want)
      throw new ReplayDivergence({
        tick,
        call: k,
        reason: `memory after call ${k} differs from the recording`,
      });
  }

  // region: move
  forward() {
    throw Error('move: not written yet (lesson 10)');
  }

  moveTo() {
    throw Error('move: not written yet (lesson 10)');
  }

  seek() {
    throw Error('move: not written yet (lesson 10)');
  }

  step() {
    throw Error('move: not written yet (lesson 10)');
  }

  stepBack() {
    throw Error('move: not written yet (lesson 10)');
  }
  // endregion: move

  read(address, size) {
    const memory = this.machine.state.memory;
    if (
      !Number.isInteger(address) ||
      !Number.isInteger(size) ||
      address < 0 ||
      size < 0 ||
      address + size > memory.length
    )
      throw RangeError(
        `read: ${size} bytes at ${address} are not inside memory`,
      );
    return memory.slice(address, address + size);
  }

  // The instruction that runs next: the innermost frame's or, between calls, the
  // first instruction of the next call's function. null at end.
  nextInstruction() {
    const { frames, calls } = this.machine.state;
    const top = frames.at(-1);
    if (top) return { func: top.func, at: top.at };
    if (calls < this.callFunc.length)
      return { func: this.callFunc[calls], at: 0 };
    return null;
  }

  where() {
    const { frames, calls } = this.machine.state;
    const next = this.nextInstruction();
    return {
      tick: this.tick,
      call: frames.length ? calls - 1 : calls,
      func: next ? next.func : null,
      at: next ? next.at : null,
    };
  }

  state() {
    return globalThis.structuredClone(this.machine.state);
  }

  // region: stops
  stopHere() {
    throw Error('stops: not written yet (lesson 10)');
  }

  continue() {
    throw Error('stops: not written yet (lesson 10)');
  }
  // endregion: stops

  // region: search-back
  continueBack() {
    throw Error('search-back: not written yet (lesson 10)');
  }

  searchBack() {
    throw Error('search-back: not written yet (lesson 10)');
  }

  mayHaveWritten() {
    throw Error('search-back: not written yet (lesson 10)');
  }
  // endregion: search-back

  // region: last-write
  lastWrite() {
    throw Error('last-write: not written yet (lesson 10)');
  }
  // endregion: last-write

  // region: stack
  stack() {
    throw Error('stack: not written yet (lesson 12)');
  }
  // endregion: stack

  // region: step-out
  stepOut() {
    throw Error('stepOut: not written yet (lesson 12)');
  }
  // endregion: step-out
}

// Whether a write changed a byte inside one of the watched ranges. A byte the
// store rewrote with the same value does not count. A watch without a size
// watches one byte.
function changesWatched(write, watches) {
  for (let i = 0; i < write.size; i++) {
    const byte = write.address + i;
    if (
      write.before[i] !== write.after[i] &&
      watches.some((w) => byte >= w.address && byte < w.address + (w.size ?? 1))
    )
      return true;
  }
  return false;
}

// The pages that hold the bytes [address, address + size).
function pagesOf(address, size, pageSize) {
  const pages = [];
  const last = Math.floor((address + size - 1) / pageSize);
  for (let p = Math.floor(address / pageSize); p <= last; p++) pages.push(p);
  return pages;
}

function whole(n, what, least = 0) {
  if (!Number.isInteger(n) || n < least)
    throw RangeError(
      `${what}: ${n} is not a whole number of at least ${least}`,
    );
  return n;
}

`courses/time-travel-debugger-part-two/starter/machine-build.mjs`:

```mjs
// Unit 08 Machine. Runs the program listings in programs/*.json
// one instruction at a time, keeping everything it knows in one plain object
// (machine.state), so a debugger can copy, compare and restore it.
//
// state = { memory, globals, stack, frames, tick, calls, result }
//   memory  Uint8Array, the linear memory
//   globals the global variables (numbers)
//   stack   the value stack (numbers; an i64 is a BigInt)
//   frames  one entry per function call in progress, innermost last:
//           { func, at, locals, base, labels }, labels = [{ end, height, arity, loop }]
//   tick    instructions executed since the machine was made
//   calls   export calls started
//   result  what the last finished export call returned (undefined for none)
const PAGE = 65536;

// The course hands the machine a program already loaded (public/program.mjs
// loadProgram). A raw listing is accepted too and loaded the same way here, so
// this file needs nothing but itself.
export function loaded(program) {
  if (program?.loaded === true) return program;
  if (program?.format !== 'ttd2-program-1')
    throw Error('Machine: not a program listing (format ttd2-program-1)');
  const p = globalThis.structuredClone(program);
  for (const f of p.functions)
    f.code = f.code.map((ins) =>
      ins[0] === 'i64.const'
        ? [ins[0], BigInt(String(ins[1]).replace(/n$/, ''))]
        : ins,
    );
  p.data = p.data.map((d) => ({
    offset: d.offset,
    bytes:
      typeof d.bytes === 'string'
        ? Uint8Array.from(Buffer.from(d.bytes, 'hex'))
        : d.bytes,
  }));
  const byIndex = new Map(p.functions.map((f) => [f.index, f]));
  Object.defineProperties(p, {
    loaded: { value: true },
    func: { value: (index) => byIndex.get(index) },
    typeOf: {
      value: (index) =>
        index < p.imports.length
          ? p.types[p.imports[index].type]
          : p.types[byIndex.get(index)?.type],
    },
    exportIndex: {
      value: (name) =>
        p.exports.find((x) => x.kind === 'func' && x.name === name)?.index,
    },
  });
  return p;
}

export class Machine {
  constructor(program, imports = {}) {
    this.program = loaded(program);
    // Per function: a number for each instruction (faster to switch on than its name)
    // and, for each block, the position of its matching end.
    this.prepared = new Map(
      this.program.functions.map((f) => [f.index, prepare(f)]),
    );
    this.imports = this.program.imports.map((i) => {
      const f = imports[i.name];
      if (typeof f !== 'function')
        throw Error(`Machine: no function given for the import ${i.name}`);
      return f;
    });
    // region: initial-state
    throw Error("initial-state: not written yet (lesson 08)");
    // endregion: initial-state
  }

  // region: call-entry
  get running() { return this.state.frames.length > 0; }
  begin() { throw Error("call-entry: not written yet (lesson 08)"); }
  invoke(name, args = []) {
    this.begin(name, args);
    while (this.running) this.step();
    return this.state.result;
  }
  enter() { throw Error("call-entry: not written yet (lesson 08)"); }
  // endregion: call-entry

  // Execute one instruction. Returns { tick, func, at, op, writes }, where each
  // write is { address, size, before, after } with before and after as byte arrays.
  // region: step-start
  step() {
    throw Error("step-start: not written yet (lesson 08)");
    // endregion: step-start
    switch (op) {
      case 0:
        /* block */ frame.labels.push({
          end: fn.ends[at],
          height: st.length,
          arity: ins[1] ? 1 : 0,
          loop: false,
        });
        break;
      case 1:
        /* loop */ frame.labels.push({
          end: at,
          height: st.length,
          arity: 0,
          loop: true,
        });
        break;
      case 2:
        /* br */ this.branch(frame, ins[1]);
        break;
      case 3:
        /* br_if */ if (st.pop() !== 0) this.branch(frame, ins[1]);
        break;
      case 4 /* end */:
        if (frame.labels.length) frame.labels.pop();
        else this.leave(frame);
        break;
      case 5:
        /* return */ this.leave(frame);
        break;
      case 6: /* call */ {
        const callee = ins[1];
        const type = this.program.typeOf(callee);
        const args = st.splice(
          st.length - type.params.length,
          type.params.length,
        );
        if (callee < this.imports.length) {
          const r = this.imports[callee](...args);
          if (type.results.length) st.push(coerce(type.results[0], r));
        } else this.enter(callee, args);
        break;
      }
      case 7:
        /* local.get */ st.push(frame.locals[ins[1]]);
        break;
      case 8:
        /* local.set */ frame.locals[ins[1]] = st.pop();
        break;
      case 9:
        /* local.tee */ frame.locals[ins[1]] = st[st.length - 1];
        break;
      case 10:
        /* global.get */ st.push(s.globals[ins[1]]);
        break;
      case 11:
        /* global.set */ s.globals[ins[1]] = st.pop();
        break;
      case 12: /* select */ {
        const c = st.pop(),
          b = st.pop(),
          a = st.pop();
        st.push(c !== 0 ? a : b);
        break;
      }
      case 13:
        /* i32.const */ st.push(ins[1]);
        break;
      case 14:
        /* i64.const */ st.push(ins[1]);
        break;
      case 15:
        /* f32.const */ st.push(Math.fround(ins[1]));
        break;
      // loads: [align, offset]
      case 20:
        st.push(this.view(st.pop(), ins[2], 4).getInt32(0, true));
        break; // i32.load
      case 21:
        st.push(this.view(st.pop(), ins[2], 1).getUint8(0));
        break; // i32.load8_u
      case 22:
        st.push(this.view(st.pop(), ins[2], 4).getFloat32(0, true));
        break; // f32.load
      // stores: [align, offset]
      case 30: {
        const v = st.pop();
        this.store(event, st.pop(), ins[2], 4, (d) => d.setInt32(0, v, true));
        break;
      } // i32.store
      case 31: {
        const v = st.pop();
        this.store(event, st.pop(), ins[2], 1, (d) => d.setUint8(0, v & 255));
        break;
      } // i32.store8
      case 32: {
        const v = st.pop();
        this.store(event, st.pop(), ins[2], 2, (d) =>
          d.setUint16(0, v & 65535, true),
        );
        break;
      } // i32.store16
      case 33: {
        const v = st.pop();
        this.store(event, st.pop(), ins[2], 4, (d) => d.setFloat32(0, v, true));
        break;
      } // f32.store
      case 34: {
        const v = st.pop();
        this.store(event, st.pop(), ins[2], 8, (d) =>
          d.setBigInt64(0, v, true),
        );
        break;
      } // i64.store
      // i32 arithmetic and comparisons
      case 40:
        st.push(st.pop() === 0 ? 1 : 0);
        break; // i32.eqz
      case 41: {
        const b = st.pop(),
          a = st.pop();
        st.push(a !== b ? 1 : 0);
        break;
      } // i32.ne
      case 42: {
        const b = st.pop(),
          a = st.pop();
        st.push(a < b ? 1 : 0);
        break;
      } // i32.lt_s
      case 43: {
        const b = st.pop() >>> 0,
          a = st.pop() >>> 0;
        st.push(a < b ? 1 : 0);
        break;
      } // i32.lt_u
      case 44: {
        const b = st.pop(),
          a = st.pop();
        st.push(a > b ? 1 : 0);
        break;
      } // i32.gt_s
      case 45: {
        const b = st.pop() >>> 0,
          a = st.pop() >>> 0;
        st.push(a > b ? 1 : 0);
        break;
      } // i32.gt_u
      case 46: {
        const b = st.pop(),
          a = st.pop();
        st.push(a <= b ? 1 : 0);
        break;
      } // i32.le_s
      case 47: {
        const b = st.pop(),
          a = st.pop();
        st.push(a >= b ? 1 : 0);
        break;
      } // i32.ge_s
      case 48: {
        const b = st.pop(),
          a = st.pop();
        st.push((a + b) | 0);
        break;
      } // i32.add
      case 49: {
        const b = st.pop(),
          a = st.pop();
        st.push((a - b) | 0);
        break;
      } // i32.sub
      case 50: {
        const b = st.pop(),
          a = st.pop();
        st.push(Math.imul(a, b));
        break;
      } // i32.mul
      case 51: {
        const b = st.pop(),
          a = st.pop(); // i32.div_s
        if (b === 0) throw trap('integer divide by zero');
        if (a === -2147483648 && b === -1) throw trap('integer overflow');
        st.push((a / b) | 0);
        break;
      }
      case 52: {
        const b = st.pop() >>> 0,
          a = st.pop() >>> 0; // i32.div_u
        if (b === 0) throw trap('integer divide by zero');
        st.push(Math.floor(a / b) | 0);
        break;
      }
      case 53: {
        const b = st.pop(),
          a = st.pop(); // i32.rem_s
        if (b === 0) throw trap('integer divide by zero');
        st.push(b === -1 ? 0 : (a % b) | 0);
        break;
      }
      case 54: {
        const b = st.pop() >>> 0,
          a = st.pop() >>> 0; // i32.rem_u
        if (b === 0) throw trap('integer divide by zero');
        st.push((a % b) | 0);
        break;
      }
      case 55: {
        const b = st.pop(),
          a = st.pop();
        st.push(a & b);
        break;
      } // i32.and
      case 56: {
        const b = st.pop(),
          a = st.pop();
        st.push(a | b);
        break;
      } // i32.or
      case 57: {
        const b = st.pop(),
          a = st.pop();
        st.push(a ^ b);
        break;
      } // i32.xor
      case 58: {
        const b = st.pop(),
          a = st.pop();
        st.push(a << (b & 31));
        break;
      } // i32.shl
      case 59: {
        const b = st.pop(),
          a = st.pop();
        st.push(a >> (b & 31));
        break;
      } // i32.shr_s
      case 60: {
        const b = st.pop(),
          a = st.pop();
        st.push((a >>> (b & 31)) | 0);
        break;
      } // i32.shr_u
      // f32
      case 70: {
        const b = st.pop(),
          a = st.pop();
        st.push(Math.fround(a + b));
        break;
      } // f32.add
      case 71: {
        const b = st.pop(),
          a = st.pop();
        st.push(Math.fround(a - b));
        break;
      } // f32.sub
      case 72: {
        const b = st.pop(),
          a = st.pop();
        st.push(Math.fround(a * b));
        break;
      } // f32.mul
      case 73: {
        const b = st.pop(),
          a = st.pop();
        st.push(Math.fround(a / b));
        break;
      } // f32.div
      case 74:
        st.push(Math.fround(Math.sqrt(st.pop())));
        break; // f32.sqrt
      case 75:
        st.push(-st.pop());
        break; // f32.neg
      case 76: {
        const b = st.pop(),
          a = st.pop();
        st.push(a < b ? 1 : 0);
        break;
      } // f32.lt
      case 77: {
        const b = st.pop(),
          a = st.pop();
        st.push(a > b ? 1 : 0);
        break;
      } // f32.gt
      case 78: {
        const b = st.pop(),
          a = st.pop();
        st.push(a <= b ? 1 : 0);
        break;
      } // f32.le
      case 79: {
        const b = st.pop(),
          a = st.pop();
        st.push(a >= b ? 1 : 0);
        break;
      } // f32.ge
      case 80:
        st.push(Math.fround(st.pop()));
        break; // f32.convert_i32_s
      case 81:
        st.push(Math.fround(st.pop() >>> 0));
        break; // f32.convert_i32_u
      case 82:
        st.push(Math.fround(st.pop()));
        break; // f32.demote_f64
      case 83:
        break; // f64.promote_f32
      case 84: {
        SCRATCH.setFloat32(0, st.pop(), true);
        st.push(SCRATCH.getInt32(0, true));
        break;
      } // i32.reinterpret_f32
      case 85: {
        SCRATCH.setInt32(0, st.pop(), true);
        st.push(SCRATCH.getFloat32(0, true));
        break;
      } // f32.reinterpret_i32
      case 86: {
        const x = st.pop(); // i32.trunc_sat_f32_s
        st.push(
          Number.isNaN(x)
            ? 0
            : x >= 2147483647
              ? 2147483647
              : x <= -2147483648
                ? -2147483648
                : Math.trunc(x) | 0,
        );
        break;
      }
      default:
        throw Error(`Machine: instruction ${ins[0]} is not supported`);
    }
    s.tick++;
    return event;
  }

  // region: branch
  branch() { throw Error("branch: not written yet (lesson 08)"); }
  // endregion: branch

  // region: return-frame
  leave() { throw Error("return-frame: not written yet (lesson 08)"); }
  // endregion: return-frame

  // region: memory
  view() { throw Error("memory: not written yet (lesson 08)"); }
  store() { throw Error("memory: not written yet (lesson 08)"); }
  // endregion: memory
}

const SCRATCH = new DataView(new ArrayBuffer(8));
function trap(message) {
  const e = Error(`trap: ${message}`);
  e.trap = true;
  return e;
}
function zeroOf(type) {
  return type === 'i64' ? 0n : 0;
}
function coerce(type, v) {
  if (type === 'i32') return v | 0;
  if (type === 'f32') return Math.fround(v);
  if (type === 'i64') return BigInt.asIntN(64, BigInt(v));
  return +v;
}
const OPS = {
  block: 0,
  loop: 1,
  br: 2,
  br_if: 3,
  end: 4,
  return: 5,
  call: 6,
  'local.get': 7,
  'local.set': 8,
  'local.tee': 9,
  'global.get': 10,
  'global.set': 11,
  select: 12,
  'i32.const': 13,
  'i64.const': 14,
  'f32.const': 15,
  'i32.load': 20,
  'i32.load8_u': 21,
  'f32.load': 22,
  'i32.store': 30,
  'i32.store8': 31,
  'i32.store16': 32,
  'f32.store': 33,
  'i64.store': 34,
  'i32.eqz': 40,
  'i32.ne': 41,
  'i32.lt_s': 42,
  'i32.lt_u': 43,
  'i32.gt_s': 44,
  'i32.gt_u': 45,
  'i32.le_s': 46,
  'i32.ge_s': 47,
  'i32.add': 48,
  'i32.sub': 49,
  'i32.mul': 50,
  'i32.div_s': 51,
  'i32.div_u': 52,
  'i32.rem_s': 53,
  'i32.rem_u': 54,
  'i32.and': 55,
  'i32.or': 56,
  'i32.xor': 57,
  'i32.shl': 58,
  'i32.shr_s': 59,
  'i32.shr_u': 60,
  'f32.add': 70,
  'f32.sub': 71,
  'f32.mul': 72,
  'f32.div': 73,
  'f32.sqrt': 74,
  'f32.neg': 75,
  'f32.lt': 76,
  'f32.gt': 77,
  'f32.le': 78,
  'f32.ge': 79,
  'f32.convert_i32_s': 80,
  'f32.convert_i32_u': 81,
  'f32.demote_f64': 82,
  'f64.promote_f32': 83,
  'i32.reinterpret_f32': 84,
  'f32.reinterpret_i32': 85,
  'i32.trunc_sat_f32_s': 86,
};

function prepare(f) {
  const ops = f.code.map((ins) => {
    const n = OPS[ins[0]];
    if (n === undefined)
      throw Error(`Machine: instruction ${ins[0]} is not supported`);
    return n;
  });
  const ends = new Array(f.code.length).fill(-1);
  const open = [];
  f.code.forEach((ins, i) => {
    if (ins[0] === 'block' || ins[0] === 'loop') open.push(i);
    else if (ins[0] === 'end' && open.length) ends[open.pop()] = i;
  });
  return { code: f.code, ops, ends, locals: f.locals };
}

// Unit 12: names and lines. API.md, "names.mjs", is the contract.
// functionNames reads the function names a .wasm file keeps in its "name"
// custom section; lineAt finds the C line of a file offset in a line table.
//
// A .wasm file is 8 fixed bytes ("\0asm" and a version), then sections: an id
// byte, the section's size in bytes, then its contents. Sizes, counts, indexes
// and lengths are LEB128 numbers; a name is its length followed by its bytes.

// Reads a .wasm file from a position, one value at a time.
class Reader {
  constructor(bytes, pos = 0) {
    this.bytes = bytes;
    this.pos = pos;
  }

  byte() {
    if (this.pos >= this.bytes.length)
      throw Error(`functionNames: the file ends early (at byte ${this.pos})`);
    return this.bytes[this.pos++];
  }

  // region: leb128
  u32() {
    throw Error('leb128: not written yet (lesson 12)');
  }

  name() {
    throw Error('leb128: not written yet (lesson 12)');
  }
  // endregion: leb128
}

`courses/time-travel-debugger-part-two/starter/query-build.mjs`:

```mjs
// Unit 11 query: question a recording. API.md, "query.mjs", is the contract.
//
// buildIndex replays the recording once on your machine and keeps two things:
// every write, so that lastWriter can name the last write of a byte before any
// tick, and for every value the program makes, the producers it was made from,
// so that sources can follow a stored value back to where it came from. Both
// questions are answered from what was kept, without running the program again.
//
// It reads the machine's state.stack (the value stack) and state.result (what a
// finished call returned), which lesson 08's machine keeps.
import { Machine } from './machine.mjs';
import { recordedImports } from './recorder.mjs';

// How each of the 62 instructions moves values. Every instruction a program
// uses must be in exactly one of these.
const KIND = {
  block: 'block',
  loop: 'loop',
  br: 'br',
  br_if: 'br_if',
  end: 'end',
  return: 'return',
  call: 'call',
  'local.get': 'local.get',
  'local.set': 'local.set',
  'local.tee': 'local.tee',
  'global.get': 'global.get',
  'global.set': 'global.set',
  select: 'select',
  'i32.const': 'const',
  'i64.const': 'const',
  'f32.const': 'const',
  'i32.load': 'load',
  'f32.load': 'load',
  'i32.load8_u': 'load',
  'i32.store': 'store',
  'i32.store8': 'store',
  'i32.store16': 'store',
  'f32.store': 'store',
  'i64.store': 'store',
};
const LOAD_SIZE = { 'i32.load': 4, 'f32.load': 4, 'i32.load8_u': 1 };
for (const op of [
  'i32.eqz',
  'f32.sqrt',
  'f32.neg',
  'f32.convert_i32_s',
  'f32.convert_i32_u',
  'f32.demote_f64',
  'f64.promote_f32',
  'i32.reinterpret_f32',
  'f32.reinterpret_i32',
  'i32.trunc_sat_f32_s',
])
  KIND[op] = 'unary';
for (const op of [
  'i32.ne',
  'i32.lt_s',
  'i32.lt_u',
  'i32.gt_s',
  'i32.gt_u',
  'i32.le_s',
  'i32.ge_s',
  'i32.add',
  'i32.sub',
  'i32.mul',
  'i32.div_s',
  'i32.div_u',
  'i32.rem_s',
  'i32.rem_u',
  'i32.and',
  'i32.or',
  'i32.xor',
  'i32.shl',
  'i32.shr_s',
  'i32.shr_u',
  'f32.add',
  'f32.sub',
  'f32.mul',
  'f32.div',
  'f32.lt',
  'f32.gt',
  'f32.le',
  'f32.ge',
])
  KIND[op] = 'binary';

// A typed array that grows by doubling: push one number, and done() for a
// copy of exactly what was pushed.
class List {
  constructor(Type, size = 1 << 16) {
    this.a = new Type(size);
    this.n = 0;
  }
  push(x) {
    if (this.n === this.a.length) {
      const bigger = new this.a.constructor(this.a.length * 2);
      bigger.set(this.a);
      this.a = bigger;
    }
    this.a[this.n++] = x;
  }
  done() {
    return this.a.slice(0, this.n);
  }
}

export function buildIndex(program, recording) {
  if (recording?.format !== 'ttd2-recording-1')
    throw Error('buildIndex: not a recording (format ttd2-recording-1)');
  if (program.sha256 && recording.sha256 && program.sha256 !== recording.sha256)
    throw Error(
      `buildIndex: the recording was made with another program (${recording.program})`,
    );
  const calls = recording.calls;

  // One machine, its imports answered from the recording as in lesson 09.
  let m;
  const answered = recordedImports(program, recording, () => m);
  m = new Machine(program, answered.imports);
  const s = m.state;
  const memorySize = s.memory.length;
  const nImports = program.imports.length;

  // Each defined function's instructions, sorted by how they move values.
  const prepared = new Map();
  for (const f of program.functions) {
    const kinds = f.code.map((ins) => {
      if (!KIND[ins[0]])
        throw Error(`buildIndex: instruction ${ins[0]} is not one of the 62`);
      return KIND[ins[0]];
    });
    prepared.set(f.index, {
      code: f.code,
      kinds,
      locals: f.locals.length,
      results: program.typeOf(f.index).results.length,
    });
  }

  // region: keep-writes
  throw Error('keep-writes: not written yet (lesson 11)');
  // endregion: keep-writes

  // region: leaves
  throw Error('leaves: not written yet (lesson 11)');
  // endregion: leaves

  // region: producers
  throw Error('producers: not written yet (lesson 11)');
  // endregion: producers

  // region: frames
  throw Error('frames: not written yet (lesson 11)');
  // endregion: frames

  // region: follow
  throw Error('follow: not written yet (lesson 11)');
  // endregion: follow

  // region: memory
  throw Error('memory: not written yet (lesson 11)');
  // endregion: memory

  // region: replay
  throw Error('replay: not written yet (lesson 11)');
  // endregion: replay

  return makeIndex({
    end: s.tick,
    memorySize,
    leaves: { nAnswers, nArgs, argCall, argPos },
    depStart: depStart.done(),
    deps: deps.done(),
    isStore: isStore.done(),
    writes: {
      tick: wTick.done(),
      func: wFunc.done(),
      at: wAt.done(),
      address: wAddress.done(),
      size: wSize.done(),
    },
  });
}

function makeIndex({
  end,
  memorySize,
  leaves,
  depStart,
  deps,
  isStore,
  writes,
}) {
  // region: by-byte
  throw Error('by-byte: not written yet (lesson 11)');
  // endregion: by-byte

  // region: last-writer
  throw Error('last-writer: not written yet (lesson 11)');
  // endregion: last-writer

  // region: sources
  throw Error('sources: not written yet (lesson 11)');
  // endregion: sources

  return { end, lastWriter, sources };
}

// find the first tick where a tampered replay's memory parts from the original.

`courses/time-travel-debugger/BROWSER-LIMITS.md`:

```md
# Browser fallback scope

The course's full Node route supports the supplied Node runtime. checker.html is a bounded fallback for debugger modules importing only ./vm.mjs. It executes the same public criteria in a module worker and retains source/help/results first. It supports module workers, data-module imports, crypto.subtle and localStorage; the supported execution path is the package-local loopback preview described below. Independent browser acceptance remains separate. Node-only imports and dynamic imports require the Node route.

The debugger fallback supplies the course VM, not a Node filesystem or a general-purpose module loader. Custom modules, Node-only APIs, dynamic imports and CLI export/replay require Node. Unsupported browser execution is an execution error; it does not establish that a Node-valid debugger violates the public contract.

Earlier-layer source is explicit optional assistance. A new assisted draft preserves all older drafts and attempts. At stage07 the provided complete earlier tool is for practice; it cannot be claimed as learner-owned engine/debugger implementation. The capstone program/client, experiments and reasoning must be the learner's work. The cumulative own-code path remains available. Neither route certifies mastery or human learning.

This is a concrete platform-scope decision for independent review, not an assertion that arbitrary Node code runs in every browser. No staff, paid model or account is required.

## Supported launch and file-origin limit

Run `node serve.mjs` in the extracted directory and open `http://127.0.0.1:8128/checker.html`. Use `node serve.mjs --port 0` if you need an available local port and open the printed URL. Keep the server open while checking. The helper uses Node built-ins, binds only 127.0.0.1, accepts GET/HEAD only, snapshots a fixed learner reader/checker/SVG allowlist at startup, rejects path traversal and symlinked assets, and serves no project/author/review directory. Restart it after changing course assets. It needs no install, internet connection or security-setting change.

The tested Chromium direct-file route opened the editor but emitted an opaque module-worker error for both unfinished and complete controls. No browser-internal cause is claimed. File pages therefore show an actionable notice and disable checks before hashing or worker creation. Source/history export remains usable. Browser storage is per origin, so changing a port or moving from file to loopback does not silently migrate old attempts; keep the old JSON/source exports and declare the transition in a new draft. Saved old results are never reinterpreted as current checks.

```

`courses/time-travel-debugger/README.md`:

```md
# Build a time-travel debugger

Build a debugger for a small deterministic virtual machine, then diagnose an unfamiliar program. You own control, inspection, stopping rules, tracing, replay and reverse state search. The supplied VM is original teaching infrastructure. It has no access to native processes.


## Entry skills and boundaries

This course is for a programmer comfortable editing/running JavaScript ES modules, writing functions and classes, using objects/arrays/Map, reading exceptions and passing quoted arguments in a terminal. The debugger assumes you can follow nested object mutation; the supplied VM defines its own instruction set. This is not a first programming course. If these prerequisites are unfamiliar, use the reduced examples and completion cases, then decide whether to review JavaScript first. No extra runtime or paid account is required.

## Start offline

Use Node.js. The local construction run uses **v26.5.1 on macOS**; other Node versions and operating systems are unqualified. No npm install, API key, paid service or internet connection is needed.

1. Open index.html for the complete reader, or read lessons/01.md.
2. In this extracted directory, run `node lab.mjs start project` once.
3. Read contracts.md and lesson 01. Edit only project/solution.mjs for target logic.
4. Run `node lab.mjs check project 01 --help-used none`. The untouched starter is expected to fail with named unfinished methods.
5. Work through lessons 01–07 and the matching checks. Run your debugger with `node debug.mjs project/solution.mjs programs/counter.json`.

Navigation stays open. The chapters are one cumulative tool, not seven unrelated projects. You may implement and check any milestone directly; tests run cumulatively to preserve earlier behavior. Earlier learner code is reused by design within this one project. The explicit start-for route below supplies prior layers for an independent unit attempt; the cumulative route still builds your own complete tool.

## Builds you keep

01 inspector; 02 conditional loop runner; 03 memory-change investigator; 04 trace recorder; 05 replay viewer; 06 reverse state search; 07 diagnosis tool and report. Read capstone.md for the less-guided final investigation and learner-owned extension. Timings are estimates until tried by people.

`node lab.mjs question 01a` shows a prediction. `node lab.mjs predict project 01a ANSWER --help-used none` commits it before feedback; 01b is a changed case. Each coding check saves source, report, question/version, assistance and actual results in project/attempts before execution. Editing code does not revise earlier attempts. Local receipts are editable records, not credentials.

`node lab.mjs export project NEW_EXPORT_DIRECTORY` copies your code, report and attempts without overwriting an existing destination. Your project is nested at `NEW_EXPORT_DIRECTORY/project/`. Keep this course package and invoke the exported solution by its full path. For example, from this course directory after completing your project:

```sh
node lab.mjs export project ./my-debugger-export
node lab.mjs check ./my-debugger-export/project 07 --help-used "export replay"
node debug.mjs ./my-debugger-export/project/solution.mjs programs/counter.json
```

Use the help description that matches your actual assistance. No restore/import path is provided and no old receipt is promoted to current.

## Optional help and acceptance limits

own-llm.md contains a copyable critique prompt for your own account. Nothing sends your work automatically. Deterministic checks cover their named cases; diagnosis reasoning uses a rubric. Author controls are outside this package. The Node terminal course is publicly available. Independent AI learner runs are separate evidence, not a human mastery claim. Human difficulty/time trials, rendered desktop/mobile inspection and actual browser ZIP receipt remain unqualified. Node runs the full toolchain; checker.html supplies the bounded offline fallback described below, with actual browser acceptance pending.

The runner executes your trusted local JavaScript with your normal process permissions. It is not a security sandbox; run code you understand.

## Earlier-layer assistance

To attempt a unit independently, run `node lab.mjs start-for NEW_DIRECTORY NN --use-prior`. This creates a new project with completed earlier layers and unfinished current logic. It refuses existing destinations and records exactly which layers were supplied in PROJECT.json and every check receipt. support.json intentionally contains readable earlier-layer worked source; it is assistance, not hidden assessment material or a submission you can claim to have implemented. Stage07 provides a practice tool/engine, not a learner-owned full implementation or capstone report. Keep and repair your cumulative project if you want your own complete artifact. No staff or model reply is required.

Human effectiveness and difficulty are unverified. The launch route uses learner-run checks and optional critique from the learner's own account; it introduces no staffed/human-trial requirement. Independent engineering, packaging/download and actual platform acceptance remain separate.

## Browser fallback and its limits

Open checker.html for an offline code editor and on-demand worker checks using the same public criteria. It preserves all submitted code/help/results and can export source plus the complete local history. The earlier-layer button creates a separate assisted draft. It requires a browser supporting module workers, data-module imports, crypto.subtle and localStorage; actual browser route/download acceptance is still pending. This debugger fallback accepts the supplied ./vm.mjs import. Use Node for custom modules, Node-only APIs and CLI export/replay. Unsupported browser execution is an execution error, not evidence that a Node-valid debugger violates the course contract. No staffed reply or paid model is involved.

## Run the browser checker offline

In this extracted course directory, run `node serve.mjs`, then open `http://127.0.0.1:8128/checker.html`. Keep the terminal open; Ctrl+C stops it. The helper uses the same tested Node runtime as the CLI. It binds only 127.0.0.1 and serves an explicit read-only reader/checker/SVG list, never projects, directory listings or author files. No package install or internet connection is needed. If the port is already used, run `node serve.mjs --port 0` and open the exact URL it prints. The default port stays fixed so the same browser origin can retain local attempts across restarts.

Directly opening checker.html as a file displays the local-preview command and refuses check execution; editing and source/history downloads remain available. Export any existing file-page work before switching origin. Browser state is per origin: the loopback page does not automatically import or reinterpret file-page attempts. Keep the old JSON export, start a new draft at the local URL, paste your own downloaded source and declare help. All prior records retain their saved source, assessment and verdict. The Node CLI route needs no preview server.

`courses/time-travel-debugger/capstone.md`:

```md
# Capstone: a fresh diagnosis and a familiar rehearsal

The earlier dispatch.json task is a familiar rehearsal, not an unfamiliar transfer. A dispatch summary starts with four quantities: 12, 9, 6 and 3. The intended report is their sum, but a reviewer reports that the final shipment is missing. programs/dispatch.json is the original program to investigate; its intended loop should account for every listed quantity. Verify the reported symptom rather than assuming it is true. If the program satisfies the stated expectation, report that finding with evidence and propose a different falsifiable explanation for the complaint. A diagnosis is allowed to conclude that the supplied complaint is unsupported.

Your fresh supplied investigation is programs/transfer.json, which the earlier lessons do not assign: it should emit the last value written to cell 5 after a three-visit update loop. It emits a different value. Diagnose this case without a walkthrough. Preserve the original input. Put any proposed repair in a new file and confirm both the observed symptom and the changed result.

Deliver your debugger and a report containing: expected behavior; source/program identity; reproducible commands from a fresh instance; first observed divergence; relevant trace segment and state; causal hypothesis; at least one counterexperiment; corrected-program experiment if appropriate; limits and help used. An unsupported bug claim is a failure even if a patch changes output.

Build one debugging query of your own over the debugger's trace or state. State the question it answers and retain the query, input and reproducible result; explain how the result supports or challenges your diagnosis. A small client helper using existing methods is sufficient.

Rubric: evidence must reproduce; state and event boundaries must be used correctly; cause must explain the symptom; the counterexperiment must distinguish the hypothesis from another explanation; the new query must answer its stated question and contribute evidence to the investigation; conclusions must fit the observations. Alternative valid investigations may use breakpoints, watchpoints or trace search in different orders. Stage 07 only checks debugger behavior, not this report's reasoning.

Finally create a small program of your own with an explicit intended behavior and a plausible bug. Provide its input and diagnosis as a separate investigation. Do not submit author controls or a copied implementation as your work. There is no automated mastery certificate or required model critique.

If you already read the earlier teaching-v3 exercise07b, retain that attempt and treat this supplied investigation as assisted rehearsal. Use a new program of your own for fresh diagnosis practice. The revised exercise does not turn earlier exposed work into an unaided first attempt.

```

`courses/time-travel-debugger/contracts.md`:

```md
# Original deterministic VM: frozen behavioral contract v1

Learner contract v1, adopted 2026-10-27. Implement the debugger behavior defined here over the supplied original VM. This course does not access native processes.

## VM

State is `{pc,tick,regs:{a,b,c,d},mem,output,halted}`. Initially pc=0, tick=0, all four registers and all eight memory cells are 0, output=[], halted=false. Registers hold JavaScript safe integers; overflow raises an execution error before state changes. Memory addresses are integer 0–7. Programs have 1–256 instructions. No clock, randomness, I/O inputs or external side effects.

Operands called `value` are a safe integer literal or one of the register names. Instructions:

- `{op:"set",reg:"a",value:3}` assigns an operand.
- `{op:"add",reg:"a",value:-1}` adds an operand.
- `{op:"load",reg:"b",address:0}` copies a memory cell into a register.
- `{op:"store",address:0,value:"a"}` writes an operand to a memory cell.
- `{op:"jnz",value:"a",target:2}` jumps if the operand is nonzero; target is an in-program instruction index.
- `{op:"emit",value:"a"}` appends the operand to output.
- `{op:"halt"}` sets halted=true.

Every executed instruction increments tick once. Normally pc advances by one; taken jnz replaces that next pc. Halt also advances pc and tick. Falling off a program without halt raises an error. A halted step is a no-op returning null.

## Debugger interface and boundaries

Construct `new Debugger(program)`. The program and returned observations are deep copies. `inspect()` returns the detached current state. `step()` bypasses breakpoints, executes one instruction and returns its event, or null if already halted.

`addBreakpoint({pc,condition?})` adds a breakpoint. Conditions are `{kind:"reg",name:"a",equals:2}` or `{kind:"mem",address:0,equals:2}`. `run(limit=1000)` checks breakpoints **before** execution, including at the current pc. A false condition does not stop. An immediate rerun at the same breakpoint stops again; step bypasses it. Explicit run limit is integer 1–10000 and counts only instructions executed by that call.

`watch(address)` stops **after** a store changes that watched cell. Same-value stores are events but do not stop. Stops are `{reason,tick,pc}` where reason is breakpoint, watchpoint, halt or limit. A watchpoint additionally has `write:{address,before,after}`. A run executing halt reports halt even if halt was the last budgeted instruction. Already halted run reports halt without execution. Watchpoint pc is the next instruction, and tick includes the store.

Events are `{tick,pc,op,writes,emitted}`. Event tick is the post-instruction tick; event pc is the executed instruction's pre-state pc. A store includes one `{address,before,after}` even for a same-value store. Only emit populates emitted. `trace()` returns detached events from the farthest recorded frontier in tick order. Seeking does not shrink that frontier; re-executing known ticks does not duplicate events.

## Replay, checkpoints and sessions

`checkpoint(nonemptyLabel)` stores an internal deep snapshot and returns `{label,tick,state}` detached from it. `seek(tick)` accepts integer 0 through recorded frontier inclusive, replays from an internal checkpoint or genesis, replaces current state and returns detached state. Seeking beyond recorded history is an error. A checkpoint is an observation, not a portable restore token. No external checkpoint/session import API exists.

`reverseFind(condition,beforeTick=currentTick)` searches strictly **earlier** ticks in descending order, including tick0. Valid explicit bound is 0 through frontier+1. It returns the nearest matching tick and positions the debugger there. With no match it returns null and preserves the state before the call. It uses the same condition forms as breakpoints.

Each debugger instance owns its program, trace and checkpoints. A new instance starts at genesis and cannot consume another instance's session. No persisted execution sessions, source replacement or branching external input are supported in v1. The supported interface cannot import an external session. Learner check receipts separately bind exact solution and assessment hashes and label changed source historical.

There is no dedicated reverse-last-write method. A debugger user can search the detached trace backwards for a write to an address and seek to the event tick minus one to inspect the cause. reverseFind is not an event/write search.

## Tiny supplied program for independent fixture design

This is original public input, with no answer trace:

```json
[
  {"op":"set","reg":"a","value":2},
  {"op":"store","address":3,"value":"a"},
  {"op":"add","reg":"a","value":-1},
  {"op":"jnz","value":"a","target":1},
  {"op":"emit","value":"a"},
  {"op":"halt"}
]
```

Use exact command sequences and observed states in your report. These requirements define the project, not a guarantee that finite checks prove correctness or learning.

```mjs
#!/usr/bin/env node
import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { resolve } from 'node:path';
import { pathToFileURL } from 'node:url';
import { createInterface } from 'node:readline/promises';
const [source,programPath,scriptPath]=process.argv.slice(2);
if(!source||!programPath){console.error('Usage: node debug.mjs PROJECT/solution.mjs programs/PROGRAM.json [COMMANDS.json]');process.exit(2);}
try {
 const { Debugger }=await import(pathToFileURL(resolve(source)).href);
 const d=new Debugger(JSON.parse(readFileSync(programPath)));
 const command=text=>{
  const [verb,a,b,c]=text.trim().split(/\s+/);
  if(verb==='inspect')return d.inspect();
  if(verb==='step'){const count=Number(a??1);if(!Number.isInteger(count)||count<1||count>10000)throw Error('Step count must be 1–10000.');let e;for(let n=0;n<count;n++)e=d.step();return {event:e,state:d.inspect()};}
  if(verb==='run')return d.run(Number(a??1000));
  if(verb==='break'){d.addBreakpoint({pc:Number(a),...(b?{condition:{kind:'reg',name:b,equals:Number(c)}}:{})});return 'breakpoint added; step bypasses a breakpoint at the current pc';}
  if(verb==='watch'){d.watch(Number(a));return 'watchpoint added';}
  if(verb==='trace')return d.trace();
  if(verb==='checkpoint')return d.checkpoint(a??'manual');
  if(verb==='seek')return d.seek(Number(a));
  if(verb==='find')return d.reverseFind(a==='mem'?{kind:'mem',address:Number(b),equals:Number(c)}:{kind:'reg',name:b,equals:Number(c)});
  if(verb==='help')return 'inspect | step [N] | run [LIMIT] | break PC [REG VALUE] | watch ADDRESS | trace | checkpoint LABEL | seek TICK | find reg NAME VALUE | find mem ADDRESS VALUE | quit';
  throw Error('Unknown command. Enter help.');
 };
 if(scriptPath){for(const text of JSON.parse(readFileSync(scriptPath))){console.log('> '+text);console.log(JSON.stringify(command(text),null,2));}}
 else {
  const rl=createInterface({input:process.stdin,output:process.stdout});console.log(command('help'));
  for(;;){const text=await rl.question('vm> ');if(text.trim()==='quit')break;try{console.log(JSON.stringify(command(text),null,2));}catch(e){console.error(e.message);}}
  rl.close();
 }
}catch(e){console.error(e.message);process.exitCode=2;}

import { pathToFileURL } from 'node:url';
import { suite, stages } from './public/checks.mjs';
const [source, stage] = process.argv.slice(2);
if (!stages.includes(stage)) throw Error('Unknown stage.');
const api = await import(pathToFileURL(source).href);
const results = suite(api, stage);
console.log('IVY_RESULT:' + JSON.stringify({ stage, results }));

```

<p>A program emitted the wrong number. Build a tool that pauses it and shows the state that produced the number. Your first usable build is a single-step inspector for the supplied VM.</p>
<h2>Before the worked result</h2>
<p>This case uses the terms and interface in contracts.md. Read the input in <code>node lab.mjs question 01a</code>, then save your answer with <code>node lab.mjs predict project 01a YOUR_ANSWER --help-used none</code> before reading the worked result below. This is practice, not a mastery claim. If you need the unit&#x27;s terms first, study them and label the answer assisted rather than an unaided prediction.</p>
<p>A virtual machine (VM) is a program that executes a defined instruction set. This VM is a teaching model. Its four registers are named a, b, c and d; each holds one integer. Its eight memory cells are numbered 0–7. The program counter, pc, selects the next instruction. Tick counts instructions already executed. Output holds emitted integers. None of these is a native process address or a hardware register.</p>
<p>Read contracts.md before coding. The supplied vm.mjs validates a program, constructs the initial state and executes an instruction. You own the Debugger class that calls it. Keep that boundary: changing VM semantics to make a check pass would produce a different machine.</p>
<p>A reduced example is set c=5, add c=2, halt. The example runner records the before and after states using the supplied machine. First predict what a step changes, then compare your prediction with the saved output. A step changes both the register and the instruction position. Inspection changes neither. After halt, a further step returns null and does not increase tick.</p>
<p>Implement inspect and step in project/solution.mjs. Inspection must return a detached copy. If changing a displayed memory array changes the running VM, a debugging observation has become a program edit. The public checker deliberately mutates a returned observation to distinguish those behaviors. Returning a shallow copy is insufficient because registers and memory are nested values.</p>
<p>Run the first check. An unfinished-method message is an expected starting result; use its named method and lesson pointer to choose the next edit. A syntax error is an execution error, not a failed behavioral requirement. The saved attempt contains your original code, report, question identity and actual output. Repair the code and run again; keep the first attempt.</p>
<p>Your intermediate product is useful now: run debug.mjs with counter.json and first-session.json to inspect a state, execute one instruction and inspect again. It should be your implementation producing those observations.</p>
<p>For transfer, create a program that writes a register to memory and later loads it into a different register. Predict the state after each instruction without a walkthrough, then use your inspector to investigate any difference. In your report, explain why an output alone cannot identify which earlier state was wrong.</p>
<h2>Representation</h2>

Conditional breakpoints</h1>
<p>Single stepping a loop wastes attention on states you already understand. Extend your inspector so it runs until a selected instruction is about to execute under a condition you choose.</p>
<h2>Before the worked result</h2>
<p>This case uses the terms and interface in contracts.md. Read the input in <code>node lab.mjs question 02a</code>, then save your answer with <code>node lab.mjs predict project 02a YOUR_ANSWER --help-used none</code> before reading the worked result below. This is practice, not a mastery claim. If you need the unit&#x27;s terms first, study them and label the answer assisted rather than an unaided prediction.</p>
<p>A breakpoint is a request to pause before an instruction. Its pc refers to the next instruction, not the instruction that just finished. A conditional breakpoint additionally tests the current state. The supplied condition helper compares a named register or memory cell with an integer. A false condition means execution continues.</p>
<p>Consider a sibling program that decreases d through a loop and stores d on each visit. To inspect the second store&#x27;s input, place a breakpoint on the store and test the register before it writes. Stopping after the store would answer a different question: what it changed. The example runner makes that boundary visible as a stop record beside a state snapshot.</p>
<p>Add addBreakpoint and run. Check halted state first. At every instruction boundary, test breakpoints before executing. Count only the instructions executed by this call against its limit. A tight loop must eventually return a limit stop. Reaching the limit is an ordinary result; malformed limits are invocation errors. If the last permitted instruction is halt, report halt.</p>
<p>An immediate rerun from a breakpoint will stop there again. This is deliberate: no instruction has run and the breakpoint still applies. An explicit step bypasses breakpoints for one instruction. That rule makes the tool predictable and avoids a hidden one-time suppression rule. Tell the user how to proceed in the command output.</p>
<p>Run stage 02 and read the condition case carefully if it fails. A breakpoint at the right pc but wrong loop iteration is not close enough. Check the register before the instruction rather than after executing it. Record the actual stop tick and state in your report, then revise and rerun.</p>
<p>The intermediate build is a loop investigator. Use break PC REG VALUE in debug.mjs to focus on one visit to a repeated instruction. Preserve the original program and enter a different condition to test whether your hypothesis depends on a particular iteration.</p>
<p>For transfer, write a loop with two different stores. Use the JavaScript addBreakpoint API to select one store with a memory condition; the terminal break command supports register conditions. Explain why the breakpoint belongs before that instruction and which observation would refute your hypothesis. Do not copy the counter program&#x27;s breakpoint location.</p>
<h2>Worked procedure</h2>
<p>Use <code>node examples.mjs 02</code>. Its loop visits the same store with different d values. At a boundary, first check halted, then the breakpoint&#x27;s pc, then its condition. Only if execution continues should the per-call executed count increase. The example&#x27;s stop state is the input to the pending store. Completion: from that stop, choose whether inspect, run or step will execute an instruction and explain why. Case 02b changes the program and asks about output after bypassing a breakpoint.</p>

Use <code>node lab.mjs check unit02 02 --help-used supplied-prior</code> for that assisted route. Write what help you used. The capstone investigation has a rubric rather than a worked answer. These short project chapters target roughly 2–3 minutes of prose and 30–60 minutes of building per unit; those are design estimates, not learner timing evidence.</p></article><article id="lesson-03"><h1>03. Watchpoints</h1>
<p>You know which memory cell becomes wrong, but you do not know which instruction writes it. Add a watchpoint that runs until that cell changes and reports the change.</p>
<h2>Before the worked result</h2>
<p>This case uses the terms and interface in contracts.md. Read the input in <code>node lab.mjs question 03a</code>, then save your answer with <code>node lab.mjs predict project 03a YOUR_ANSWER --help-used none</code> before reading the worked result below. This is practice, not a mastery claim. If you need the unit&#x27;s terms first, study them and label the answer assisted rather than an unaided prediction.</p>
<p>A watchpoint observes a data location rather than an instruction location. Here it pauses after a store changes a watched cell. The resulting state includes the store&#x27;s effect. A breakpoint pauses before an instruction; keeping these two boundaries distinct is essential when you compare snapshots.</p>
<p>A store can write the value that is already present. That is an executed write, so it belongs in the trace, but it is not a value change and does not trigger a watchpoint in this contract. A sibling demonstration first writes the existing value, then changes it, then repeats the new value. Predict whether the second store should stop before revealing its event sequence.</p>
<p>Implement watch(address) and extend run. After a step, inspect that event&#x27;s writes. Test both address and before-versus-after value. Do not stop just because any memory cell changed, and do not compare the wrong states after another instruction has already run. A stop contains the write that caused it, plus the post-store tick and next pc.</p>
<p>The public cases distinguish a watched change, an unwatched change and a same-value write. On a failure, compare the event&#x27;s executed pc with the stop&#x27;s next pc. They describe different boundaries. Explain the discrepancy in report.md before changing code; that note will be saved with the next check.</p>
<p>Your build can now investigate a symptom without prior knowledge of the program&#x27;s control flow. Run with watch ADDRESS, record the first changed value and inspect the registers that supplied the store operand. Continue by stepping once if another stopping rule applies at the new position.</p>
<p>For a second practice case, watch two addresses in your own program. Arrange for a store to an unwatched address before either watched address changes. The tool must continue through that unrelated write. Then make a watched store write its existing value. If it pauses, state which part of your implementation confused a write with a change.</p>
<p>For transfer, use dispatch.json without reading its instruction list first. Watch cell 1, collect a stop, then inspect only the nearby instructions. Form a hypothesis about how the written value was computed. This is practice in choosing evidence, not a hidden assessment or a guarantee that the program has a bug.</p>
<h2>Worked procedure</h2>
<p>Use <code>node examples.mjs 03</code>. Draw three rows for the initial same-value write, changed write and repeated new value. For each row compare the event address with the watched address, then compare before and after. Those are two separate filters. Completion: replace the watched address with a different cell and predict whether the same trace would stop. Your own run method must implement the chosen policy; the VM only supplies the event.</p>
<h2>Complete a changed case</h2>
<p>Run <code>node lab.mjs question 03b</code> and commit the answer with <code>node lab.mjs predict project 03b YOUR_ANSWER --help-used none</code>. These are applications after instruction; they are not counted as predictions before explanation or as mastery evidence.</p>
<h2>Commit, build, check</h2>
<p>For the cumulative build, create <code>project</code> once with <code>node lab.mjs start project</code>. Edit project/solution.mjs and run <code>node lab.mjs check project 03 --help-used none</code>. The check saves your code, report, original question and help before execution.</p>
<p>If an earlier layer blocks this unit, use a NEW directory: <code>node lab.mjs start-for unit03 03 --use-prior</code>. This explicitly supplies earlier layers, leaves this unit&#x27;s target unfinished and records the assistance in PROJECT.json and every receipt. It never replaces your existing project. Use <code>node lab.mjs check unit03 03 --help-used supplied-prior</code> for that assisted route. A supplied earlier layer is not your own implementation; keep your cumulative project to build the full tool yourself.</p>
<h2>Help and limits</h2>
<p>When a case fails, locate its named boundary, reduce the actual input to a minimal failing program or byte prefix, then compare one intermediate state with the sibling example from <code>node examples.mjs 03</code>. Write what help you used. The capstone investigation has a rubric rather than a worked answer. These short project chapters target roughly 2–3 minutes of prose and 30–60 minutes of building per unit; those are design estimates, not learner timing evidence.</p></article><article id="lesson-04"><h1>04. Instruction traces</h1>
<p>A stop tells you where you are. A trace tells you how you arrived. Add a record of executed instructions so you can compare causes across a loop rather than relying on memory.</p>
<h2>Before the worked result</h2>
<p>This case uses the terms and interface in contracts.md. Read the input in <code>node lab.mjs question 04a</code>, then save your answer with <code>node lab.mjs predict project 04a YOUR_ANSWER --help-used none</code> before reading the worked result below. This is practice, not a mastery claim. If you need the unit&#x27;s terms first, study them and label the answer assisted rather than an unaided prediction.</p>
<p>Each event has a post-instruction tick and the pre-instruction pc. It names the instruction, its memory writes and any emitted values. An event is not a full state snapshot. The state can be reconstructed later by replaying the deterministic VM, while events provide an inexpensive index of interesting actions.</p>
<p>In the separate counter.json loop, the store at pc 2 executes more than once. The stage04 sibling is a straight-line sequence with event PCs 0,1,2. The counter&#x27;s pc repeats while its event ticks increase. A repeated pc is not evidence that the trace duplicated an event. Conversely, two events with the same tick would violate the one-event-per-executed-instruction contract.</p>
<p>Extend step so it records a detached event. Implement trace so a caller cannot edit stored events through a returned array or a nested write object. Keep output emission in the event as well as in state output. Inspection, setting a breakpoint and adding a watchpoint do not execute instructions and must not create events.</p>
<p>Run stage 04. If the event count is correct but a write is wrong, inspect which state you used for before and after. Recording a reference to a mutable state can make every old event appear to contain the newest value. The mutation control helps expose this aliasing mistake.</p>
<p>The intermediate build is a trace recorder you can use on a program you did not write. Run a bounded session, save the terminal output in your evidence folder, and locate stores to the same address at different ticks. State which write changed the value and which merely wrote it again. These are different claims supported by different event fields.</p>
<p>For repair practice, create a program with two emits and a same-value store between them. Predict the number of events and emitted values separately, run it, and explain the difference. A trace includes instructions that produce no output.</p>
<p>For transfer, compare two runs from new debugger instances over the same immutable program. Their complete traces should agree. Change one original program operand in a new instance and identify the earliest event that differs. Do not mutate an existing instance&#x27;s program to simulate a branch; source replacement is outside this model.</p>
<h2>Representation</h2>

Checkpoints and replay</h1>
<p>You have found a late symptom and want to inspect an earlier state. Implement seek by executing forward from genesis or an earlier checkpoint.</p>
<h2>Before the worked result</h2>
<p>This case uses the terms and interface in contracts.md. Read the input in <code>node lab.mjs question 05a</code>, then save your answer with <code>node lab.mjs predict project 05a YOUR_ANSWER --help-used none</code> before reading the worked result below. This is practice, not a mastery claim. If you need the unit&#x27;s terms first, study them and label the answer assisted rather than an unaided prediction.</p>
<p>A checkpoint is a saved full VM state at a tick. Replay starts from a checkpoint at or before the target tick and executes the same instructions forward. This works here because the VM has no external input, random values or clock. A real process would require a much larger recording contract.</p>
<p>A sibling example records a checkpoint partway through a loop, runs farther, seeks to genesis and then seeks to a later recorded tick. The example runner checks both the immediate rewind state and the reconstructed state. Looking only at the final state could miss an implementation that ignored rewind altogether.</p>
<p>Implement checkpoint and seek. Store an internal deep copy. The returned checkpoint object is an observation, not a portable restore token; editing it must not change replay. Seek may use the nearest earlier checkpoint or recompute from genesis. Both strategies satisfy the behavior. Explain the cost difference in your report rather than treating one strategy as the only correct answer.</p>
<p>Keep the recorded frontier separate from the current tick. Seeking backwards changes the current state but does not erase the known trace. Re-executing a recorded tick must not append a duplicate event. Seek can only address 0 through the farthest recorded tick; it must reject requests for an unrecorded future.</p>
<p>Run stage 05. A replay failure may come from checkpoint mutation, incomplete state capture, starting after the target or duplicate trace events. Use the checker input and intermediate state to narrow the cause. Do not fix an event-count failure by silently deleting historical events.</p>
