Reverse state search</h1>
<p>Rewinding one tick at a time is still slow when a symptom has a precise condition. Add a search for the nearest earlier state that matches a register or memory value.</p>
<h2>Before the worked result</h2>
<p>This case uses the terms and interface in contracts.md. Read the input in <code>node lab.mjs question 06a</code>, then save your answer with <code>node lab.mjs predict project 06a YOUR_ANSWER --help-used none</code> before reading the worked result below. This is practice, not a mastery claim. If you need the unit&#x27;s terms first, study them and label the answer assisted rather than an unaided prediction.</p>
<p>reverseFind searches states, not instructions or write events. Its bound is exclusive: from current tick t, it begins with t−1 and moves towards tick 0. A match returns that tick and leaves the debugger positioned there. A missing match returns null and restores the state from before the search.</p>
<p>A sibling example reaches the same register value on several adjacent ticks. The correct match is the nearest earlier state, even if the instruction at that tick did not write the register. This distinguishes state search from last-write search. To investigate the last write to an address, inspect trace events backwards and seek to that event&#x27;s tick minus one instead.</p>
<p>Implement reverseFind using your existing replay operation. Validate the condition and bound before changing the current state. Store the original state so a failed search has no visible effect. Include genesis in the search. If the bound is zero, there are no earlier states to examine.</p>
<p>Run stage 06. After it passes, run <code>node debug.mjs project/solution.mjs programs/counter.json programs/replay-session.json</code>. Its final <code>find reg b 0</code> command now exercises your reverse search after the lesson-05 replay steps. If the tool returns the current tick, check whether you accidentally made the bound inclusive. If a no-match search moves the debugger to genesis, the search has leaked its exploratory state. Compare inspect before and after a deliberately absent value and keep that experiment in the report.</p>
<p>Use the matching state and nearby trace events to decide which earlier instruction to inspect. Search for a value that preceded the symptom, inspect the nearby trace and formulate a smaller question. The returned tick alone does not prove which instruction caused a bug. Distinguish the observation from the explanation.</p>
<p>For practice, use a program that holds a value unchanged for several instructions. Predict the nearest matching tick, then contrast that result with the tick of the last write. State which question each operation answers.</p>
<p>For a return to the familiar rehearsal, run dispatch.json to completion and find an earlier matching memory value. Use a new debugger instance to confirm the same state by forward execution. Then try a value that never occurs and verify state preservation. Your report should include a refutable causal hypothesis rather than just a screenshot of a matching number.</p>
<h2>Worked procedure</h2>

Save the caller&#x27;s state before exploring and restore it when no candidate matches. Completion: explain why a matching state may occur after an unrelated emit rather than at the last write. <p>Learner contract v1, adopted 2026-10-27. Implement the debugger behavior defined here over the supplied original VM. This course does not access native processes.</p>
<h2>VM</h2>
<p>State is <code>{pc,tick,regs:{a,b,c,d},mem,output,halted}</code>. Initially pc=0, tick=0, all four registers and all eight memory cells are 0, output=[], halted=false. Registers hold JavaScript safe integers; overflow raises an execution error before state changes. Memory addresses are integer 0–7. Programs have 1–256 instructions. No clock, randomness, I/O inputs or external side effects.</p>
<p>Operands called <code>value</code> are a safe integer literal or one of the register names. Instructions:</p>
<ul>
<li><code>{op:&quot;set&quot;,reg:&quot;a&quot;,value:3}</code> assigns an operand.</li>
<li><code>{op:&quot;add&quot;,reg:&quot;a&quot;,value:-1}</code> adds an operand.</li>
<li><code>{op:&quot;load&quot;,reg:&quot;b&quot;,address:0}</code> copies a memory cell into a register.</li>
<li><code>{op:&quot;store&quot;,address:0,value:&quot;a&quot;}</code> writes an operand to a memory cell.</li>
<li><code>{op:&quot;jnz&quot;,value:&quot;a&quot;,target:2}</code> jumps if the operand is nonzero; target is an in-program instruction index.</li>
<li><code>{op:&quot;emit&quot;,value:&quot;a&quot;}</code> appends the operand to output.</li>
<li><code>{op:&quot;halt&quot;}</code> sets halted=true.</li>
</ul>
<p>Every executed instruction increments tick once. Normally pc advances by one; taken jnz replaces that next pc. Halt also advances pc and tick. Falling off a program without halt raises an error. A halted step is a no-op returning null.</p>
<h2>Debugger interface and boundaries</h2>
<p>Construct <code>new Debugger(program)</code>. The program and returned observations are deep copies. <code>inspect()</code> returns the detached current state. <code>step()</code> bypasses breakpoints, executes one instruction and returns its event, or null if already halted.</p>
<p><code>addBreakpoint({pc,condition?})</code> adds a breakpoint. Conditions are <code>{kind:&quot;reg&quot;,name:&quot;a&quot;,equals:2}</code> or <code>{kind:&quot;mem&quot;,address:0,equals:2}</code>. <code>run(limit=1000)</code> checks breakpoints <strong>before</strong> execution, including at the current pc. A false condition does not stop. An immediate rerun at the same breakpoint stops again; step bypasses it. Explicit run limit is integer 1–10000 and counts only instructions executed by that call.</p>
<p><code>watch(address)</code> stops <strong>after</strong> a store changes that watched cell. Same-value stores are events but do not stop. Stops are <code>{reason,tick,pc}</code> where reason is breakpoint, watchpoint, halt or limit. A watchpoint additionally has <code>write:{address,before,after}</code>. A run executing halt reports halt even if halt was the last budgeted instruction. Already halted run reports halt without execution. Watchpoint pc is the next instruction, and tick includes the store.</p>
<p>Events are <code>{tick,pc,op,writes,emitted}</code>. Event tick is the post-instruction tick; event pc is the executed instruction&#x27;s pre-state pc. A store includes one <code>{address,before,after}</code> even for a same-value store. Only emit populates emitted. <code>trace()</code> returns detached events from the farthest recorded frontier in tick order. Seeking does not shrink that frontier; re-executing known ticks does not duplicate events.</p>
<h2>Replay, checkpoints and sessions</h2>
<p><code>checkpoint(nonemptyLabel)</code> stores an internal deep snapshot and returns <code>{label,tick,state}</code> detached from it. <code>seek(tick)</code> accepts integer 0 through recorded frontier inclusive, replays from an internal checkpoint or genesis, replaces current state and returns detached state. Seeking beyond recorded history is an error. A checkpoint is an observation, not a portable restore token. No external checkpoint/session import API exists.</p>
<p><code>reverseFind(condition,beforeTick=currentTick)</code> searches strictly <strong>earlier</strong> ticks in descending order, including tick0. Valid explicit bound is 0 through frontier+1. It returns the nearest matching tick and positions the debugger there. With no match it returns null and preserves the state before the call. It uses the same condition forms as breakpoints.</p>
<p>Each debugger instance owns its program, trace and checkpoints. A new instance starts at genesis and cannot consume another instance&#x27;s session. No persisted execution sessions, source replacement or branching external input are supported in v1. The supported interface cannot import an external session. Learner check receipts separately bind exact solution and assessment hashes and label changed source historical.</p>
<p>There is no dedicated reverse-last-write method. A debugger user can search the detached trace backwards for a write to an address and seek to the event tick minus one to inspect the cause. reverseFind is not an event/write search.</p>
<h2>Tiny supplied program for independent fixture design</h2>
<p>This is original public input, with no answer trace:</p>
<pre><code>[
  {&quot;op&quot;:&quot;set&quot;,&quot;reg&quot;:&quot;a&quot;,&quot;value&quot;:2},
  {&quot;op&quot;:&quot;store&quot;,&quot;address&quot;:3,&quot;value&quot;:&quot;a&quot;},
  {&quot;op&quot;:&quot;add&quot;,&quot;reg&quot;:&quot;a&quot;,&quot;value&quot;:-1},
  {&quot;op&quot;:&quot;jnz&quot;,&quot;value&quot;:&quot;a&quot;,&quot;target&quot;:1},
  {&quot;op&quot;:&quot;emit&quot;,&quot;value&quot;:&quot;a&quot;},
  {&quot;op&quot;:&quot;halt&quot;}
]</code></pre>
<p>Use exact command sequences and observed states in your report. These requirements define the project, not a guarantee that finite checks prove correctness or learning.</p></article><article id="capstone"><h1>Capstone: a fresh diagnosis and a familiar rehearsal</h1>

#!/usr/bin/env node
import { spawnSync } from 'node:child_process';
import { createHash, randomUUID } from 'node:crypto';
import { copyFileSync, existsSync, mkdirSync, readFileSync, readdirSync, writeFileSync, cpSync } from 'node:fs';
import { dirname, join, resolve } from 'node:path';
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
import { stages } from './public/checks.mjs';
const root = dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url));
const config = JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(root,'course.json')));
const sha = x => createHash('sha256').update(x).digest('hex');
const contractFiles = ['course.json','grade.mjs','public/checks.mjs','lab.mjs','practice.json','support.json','contracts.md','examples.json',...config.runtime.map(n=>'public/'+n)];
const contract = () => sha(contractFiles.map(n=>n+'\n'+readFileSync(join(root,n))).join('\n'));
function start(target,quiet=false) {
  mkdirSync(target); // exclusive: EEXIST refuses to overwrite a learner project
  copyFileSync(join(root,'starter/solution.mjs'),join(target,'solution.mjs'));
  for(const name of config.runtime) copyFileSync(join(root,'public',name),join(target,name));
  writeFileSync(join(target,'PROJECT.json'),JSON.stringify({course:config.id,contract:contract()},null,2));
  writeFileSync(join(target,'report.md'),'# Project report\n\n## Prediction\n\n## Evidence\n\n## Explanation\n\n## Counterexperiment\n\n## Limits and help used\n');
  if(!quiet)console.log(`Created ${target}. Implement solution.mjs. The unfinished starter is expected to fail stage 01.`);
}

function startFor(target,stage,flag) {
  if(flag!=='--use-prior')throw Error('Explicit assistance choice required: start-for NEW_DIRECTORY STAGE --use-prior');
  const support=JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(root,'support.json')))[stage];
  if(!support)throw Error('Choose an existing stage.');
  start(target,true);
  writeFileSync(join(target,'solution.mjs'),support.source);
  writeFileSync(join(target,'PROJECT.json'),JSON.stringify({course:config.id,contract:contract(),assistance:{kind:'supplied-earlier-layers',selected_stage:stage,provided_layers:support.provided_layers,target:support.target,notice:support.notice}},null,2));
  console.log(`Assisted stage ${stage}: provided earlier layers ${support.provided_layers.join(',')||'none'}. ${support.notice} Current target: ${support.target}.`);
}
function check(target,stage,help) {
  if (!stages.includes(stage)) throw Error('Choose stage '+stages.join(', ')+'.');
  if (!existsSync(join(target,'PROJECT.json'))) throw Error('Missing project: run lab.mjs start NEW_DIRECTORY first.');
  const assistance=JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(target,'PROJECT.json'))).assistance??null;
  const source = readFileSync(join(target,'solution.mjs'));
  // Snapshot and evidence directory must exist before any learner code is imported.
  const attempt = join(target,'attempts',new Date().toISOString().replaceAll(':','-')+'-'+randomUUID());
  mkdirSync(attempt,{recursive:true});
  writeFileSync(join(attempt,'solution.mjs'),source,{flag:'wx'});
  if(existsSync(join(target,'report.md'))) copyFileSync(join(target,'report.md'),join(attempt,'report.md'));
  for(const name of config.runtime) copyFileSync(join(root,'public',name),join(attempt,name));
  const question = { course:config.id, stage, requirement:config.outcomes[Number(stage)-1], contract_sha256:contract() };
  const receipt = { ...question, question, supplied_assistance:assistance, source_sha256:sha(source), help_used:help, started_at:new Date().toISOString(), verdict:'pending' };
  writeFileSync(join(attempt,'question.json'),JSON.stringify(question,null,2),{flag:'wx'});
  writeFileSync(join(attempt,'receipt.json'),JSON.stringify(receipt,null,2));
  const run = spawnSync(process.execPath,[join(root,'grade.mjs'),join(attempt,'solution.mjs'),stage],{encoding:'utf8',timeout:10000,maxBuffer:512000});
  writeFileSync(join(attempt,'stdout.txt'),run.stdout??'');writeFileSync(join(attempt,'stderr.txt'),run.stderr??'');
  const lines=(run.stdout??'').split('\n').filter(x=>x.startsWith('IVY_RESULT:'));
  let payload;
  try { payload=JSON.parse(lines.at(-1)?.slice(11)??'null'); } catch { payload=null; }
  const complete=payload?.stage===stage && Array.isArray(payload.results) && payload.results.length===config.caseCounts[Number(stage)-1] && payload.results.every(x=>typeof x.pass==='boolean');
  receipt.verdict = run.error || run.status!==0 || !complete ? 'execution_error' : payload.results.every(x=>x.pass) ? 'pass' : 'fail';
  receipt.finished_at=new Date().toISOString();receipt.results=complete?payload.results:[];
  receipt.execution={status:run.status,signal:run.signal,error:run.error?.message??null};
  writeFileSync(join(attempt,'receipt.json'),JSON.stringify(receipt,null,2));
  for(const result of receipt.results) {
    console.log(`${result.pass?'PASS':'FAIL'} ${result.id}: ${JSON.stringify(result.input)}`);
    if(!result.pass&&result.counterexample)console.log('  First counterexample: '+JSON.stringify(result.counterexample));
    if(!result.pass) console.log(`  Expected ${JSON.stringify(result.expected)}; observed ${JSON.stringify(result.actual)}. Read ${result.lesson}, section Worked procedure; repair solution.mjs and rerun.`);
  }
  if(receipt.verdict==='execution_error') console.error(`Code did not finish the public checks. ${run.error?.message??run.stderr??''} Inspect ${attempt}/stderr.txt; repair syntax, imports or nontermination and rerun.`);
  if(assistance)console.log('Provided earlier layers: '+JSON.stringify(assistance)+'. This check does not establish ownership of those layers.');
  console.log(`${receipt.verdict}; saved attempt ${attempt}. A pass covers these cases; the report is reviewed separately.`);
  process.exitCode=receipt.verdict==='pass'?0:receipt.verdict==='fail'?1:2;
}
function status(target) {
  const folder=join(target,'attempts');
  if(!existsSync(folder)) return console.log('No attempts yet.');
  const source=sha(readFileSync(join(target,'solution.mjs')));
  for(const name of readdirSync(folder).sort()) {
    const r=JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(folder,name,'receipt.json')));
    console.log(`${name} stage ${r.stage} ${r.verdict}; ${r.source_sha256===source&&r.contract_sha256===contract()?'current':'historical'}`);
  }
}

const practice=JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(root,'practice.json')));
function item(id) {const q=practice[id];if(!q)throw Error('Unknown prediction: choose '+Object.keys(practice).join(', '));return q;}
function predict(target,id,answer,help) {
  const q=item(id);
  if(typeof answer!=='string'||!answer.trim())throw Error('Provide a prediction answer before feedback. Use question ITEM to read its format.');
  if(!existsSync(join(target,'PROJECT.json')))throw Error('Missing project: run start NEW_DIRECTORY first.');
  const source=readFileSync(join(target,'solution.mjs'));
  const folder=join(target,'attempts',new Date().toISOString().replaceAll(':','-')+'-'+randomUUID());
  mkdirSync(folder,{recursive:true});
  const question={id,version:q.version,question:q.question,format:q.format,contract_sha256:contract()};
  const record={supplied_assistance:JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(target,'PROJECT.json'))).assistance??null,kind:'prediction',course:config.id,stage:id,question,answer,help_used:help,source_sha256:sha(source),contract_sha256:contract(),started_at:new Date().toISOString(),verdict:'pending'};
  writeFileSync(join(folder,'solution.mjs'),source,{flag:'wx'});
  if(existsSync(join(target,'report.md')))copyFileSync(join(target,'report.md'),join(folder,'report.md'));
  writeFileSync(join(folder,'question.json'),JSON.stringify(question,null,2),{flag:'wx'});
  writeFileSync(join(folder,'submission.json'),JSON.stringify(record,null,2),{flag:'wx'});
  const correct=answer.trim().toLowerCase()===String(q.expected).toLowerCase();
  record.verdict=correct?'pass':'revise';record.expected=q.expected;record.feedback=q.reason;record.finished_at=new Date().toISOString();
  writeFileSync(join(folder,'receipt.json'),JSON.stringify(record,null,2));
  console.log(`Your committed answer: ${answer}\n${correct?'Matches the model':'Revise this prediction'}. Expected ${q.expected}. ${q.reason}\nRead lessons/${id.slice(0,2)}.md. ${id.endsWith('a')?'Try changed case '+id.slice(0,2)+'b.':'Keep this case and your explanation in the report.'}\nSaved ${folder}. This prediction does not grade your code or certify mastery.`);
}
const [verb,targetArg,stage,...rest]=process.argv.slice(2);
try {
  if(!verb||!targetArg) throw Error('Usage: node lab.mjs start|start-for|check|status|export|predict TARGET [STAGE | NEW_EXPORT_DIRECTORY] [--help-used TEXT]');
  const target=resolve(targetArg);
  if(verb==='start-for') startFor(target,stage,rest[0]);
  else if(verb==='question') {const q=item(targetArg);console.log(q.question+'\nAnswer format: '+q.format);}
  else if(verb==='predict') predict(target,stage,rest[0],rest[1]==='--help-used'?rest.slice(2).join(' '):'not declared');
  else if(verb==='start') start(target);
  else if(verb==='check') check(target,stage,rest[0]==='--help-used'?rest.slice(1).join(' '):'not declared');
  else if(verb==='status') status(target);
  else if(verb==='export') {if(!stage)throw Error('Provide a new export directory.');mkdirSync(resolve(stage));cpSync(target,join(resolve(stage),'project'),{recursive:true});console.log('Exported code, report and all local attempts. Review contents before optional sharing.');}
  else throw Error('Unknown command. Use start, start-for, check, status, export, question or predict.');
} catch(e) {console.error(e.code==='EEXIST'?'Destination exists: choose a new directory; existing work was preserved.':e.message);process.exitCode=2;}

# 01. Control and inspect

A program emitted the wrong number. Build a tool that pauses it and shows the state that produced the number. Your first usable build is a single-step inspector for the supplied VM.

## Before the worked result

This case uses the terms and interface in contracts.md. Read the input in `node lab.mjs question 01a`, then save your answer with `node lab.mjs predict project 01a YOUR_ANSWER --help-used none` before reading the worked result below. This is practice, not a mastery claim. If you need the unit's terms first, study them and label the answer assisted rather than an unaided prediction.

A virtual machine (VM) is a program that executes a defined instruction set. This VM is a teaching model. Its four registers are named a, b, c and d; each holds one integer. Its eight memory cells are numbered 0–7. The program counter, pc, selects the next instruction. Tick counts instructions already executed. Output holds emitted integers. None of these is a native process address or a hardware register.

Read contracts.md before coding. The supplied vm.mjs validates a program, constructs the initial state and executes an instruction. You own the Debugger class that calls it. Keep that boundary: changing VM semantics to make a check pass would produce a different machine.

A reduced example is set c=5, add c=2, halt. The example runner records the before and after states using the supplied machine. First predict what a step changes, then compare your prediction with the saved output. A step changes both the register and the instruction position. Inspection changes neither. After halt, a further step returns null and does not increase tick.

Implement inspect and step in project/solution.mjs. Inspection must return a detached copy. If changing a displayed memory array changes the running VM, a debugging observation has become a program edit. The public checker deliberately mutates a returned observation to distinguish those behaviors. Returning a shallow copy is insufficient because registers and memory are nested values.

Run the first check. An unfinished-method message is an expected starting result; use its named method and lesson pointer to choose the next edit. A syntax error is an execution error, not a failed behavioral requirement. The saved attempt contains your original code, report, question identity and actual output. Repair the code and run again; keep the first attempt.

Your intermediate product is useful now: run debug.mjs with counter.json and first-session.json to inspect a state, execute one instruction and inspect again. It should be your implementation producing those observations.

For transfer, create a program that writes a register to memory and later loads it into a different register. Predict the state after each instruction without a walkthrough, then use your inspector to investigate any difference. In your report, explain why an output alone cannot identify which earlier state was wrong.

## Representation

The adjacent text and worked output state the same relation. The figure uses supplied sibling data, not the answer to your pending capstone.

## Worked procedure

Use the supplied three-instruction sibling in `node examples.mjs 01`. Follow one transition explicitly: read the instruction at the old pc; obtain a fresh next state from execute; replace the current state; return the detached event. For inspection, copy the nested register object, memory array and output array together. Completion: after the sibling's first step, decide which fields a second inspection may change. Then use case 01b on the different d-register program. This is a reduced procedure, not the implementation of your Debugger methods.

# 02. Conditional breakpoints

Single stepping a loop wastes attention on states you already understand. Extend your inspector so it runs until a selected instruction is about to execute under a condition you choose.

## Before the worked result

This case uses the terms and interface in contracts.md. Read the input in `node lab.mjs question 02a`, then save your answer with `node lab.mjs predict project 02a YOUR_ANSWER --help-used none` before reading the worked result below. This is practice, not a mastery claim. If you need the unit's terms first, study them and label the answer assisted rather than an unaided prediction.

A breakpoint is a request to pause before an instruction. Its pc refers to the next instruction, not the instruction that just finished. A conditional breakpoint additionally tests the current state. The supplied condition helper compares a named register or memory cell with an integer. A false condition means execution continues.

Consider a sibling program that decreases d through a loop and stores d on each visit. To inspect the second store's input, place a breakpoint on the store and test the register before it writes. Stopping after the store would answer a different question: what it changed. The example runner makes that boundary visible as a stop record beside a state snapshot.

Add addBreakpoint and run. Check halted state first. At every instruction boundary, test breakpoints before executing. Count only the instructions executed by this call against its limit. A tight loop must eventually return a limit stop. Reaching the limit is an ordinary result; malformed limits are invocation errors. If the last permitted instruction is halt, report halt.

An immediate rerun from a breakpoint will stop there again. This is deliberate: no instruction has run and the breakpoint still applies. An explicit step bypasses breakpoints for one instruction. That rule makes the tool predictable and avoids a hidden one-time suppression rule. Tell the user how to proceed in the command output.

Run stage 02 and read the condition case carefully if it fails. A breakpoint at the right pc but wrong loop iteration is not close enough. Check the register before the instruction rather than after executing it. Record the actual stop tick and state in your report, then revise and rerun.

The intermediate build is a loop investigator. Use break PC REG VALUE in debug.mjs to focus on one visit to a repeated instruction. Preserve the original program and enter a different condition to test whether your hypothesis depends on a particular iteration.

For transfer, write a loop with two different stores. Use the JavaScript addBreakpoint API to select one store with a memory condition; the terminal break command supports register conditions. Explain why the breakpoint belongs before that instruction and which observation would refute your hypothesis. Do not copy the counter program's breakpoint location.

Completion: from that stop, choose whether inspect, run or step will execute an instruction and explain why. Case 02b changes the program and asks about output after bypassing a breakpoint.

# 03. Watchpoints

You know which memory cell becomes wrong, but you do not know which instruction writes it. Add a watchpoint that runs until that cell changes and reports the change.

## Before the worked result

This case uses the terms and interface in contracts.md. Read the input in `node lab.mjs question 03a`, then save your answer with `node lab.mjs predict project 03a YOUR_ANSWER --help-used none` before reading the worked result below. This is practice, not a mastery claim. If you need the unit's terms first, study them and label the answer assisted rather than an unaided prediction.

A watchpoint observes a data location rather than an instruction location. Here it pauses after a store changes a watched cell. The resulting state includes the store's effect. A breakpoint pauses before an instruction; keeping these two boundaries distinct is essential when you compare snapshots.

A store can write the value that is already present. That is an executed write, so it belongs in the trace, but it is not a value change and does not trigger a watchpoint in this contract. A sibling demonstration first writes the existing value, then changes it, then repeats the new value. Predict whether the second store should stop before revealing its event sequence.

Implement watch(address) and extend run. After a step, inspect that event's writes. Test both address and before-versus-after value. Do not stop just because any memory cell changed, and do not compare the wrong states after another instruction has already run. A stop contains the write that caused it, plus the post-store tick and next pc.

The public cases distinguish a watched change, an unwatched change and a same-value write. On a failure, compare the event's executed pc with the stop's next pc. They describe different boundaries. Explain the discrepancy in report.md before changing code; that note will be saved with the next check.

Your build can now investigate a symptom without prior knowledge of the program's control flow. Run with watch ADDRESS, record the first changed value and inspect the registers that supplied the store operand. Continue by stepping once if another stopping rule applies at the new position.

For a second practice case, watch two addresses in your own program. Arrange for a store to an unwatched address before either watched address changes. The tool must continue through that unrelated write. Then make a watched store write its existing value. If it pauses, state which part of your implementation confused a write with a change.

For transfer, use dispatch.json without reading its instruction list first. Watch cell 1, collect a stop, then inspect only the nearby instructions. Form a hypothesis about how the written value was computed. This is practice in choosing evidence, not a hidden assessment or a guarantee that the program has a bug.

# 04. Instruction traces

A stop tells you where you are. A trace tells you how you arrived. Add a record of executed instructions so you can compare causes across a loop rather than relying on memory.

## Before the worked result

This case uses the terms and interface in contracts.md. Read the input in `node lab.mjs question 04a`, then save your answer with `node lab.mjs predict project 04a YOUR_ANSWER --help-used none` before reading the worked result below. This is practice, not a mastery claim. If you need the unit's terms first, study them and label the answer assisted rather than an unaided prediction.

Each event has a post-instruction tick and the pre-instruction pc. It names the instruction, its memory writes and any emitted values. An event is not a full state snapshot. The state can be reconstructed later by replaying the deterministic VM, while events provide an inexpensive index of interesting actions.

In the separate counter.json loop, the store at pc 2 executes more than once. The stage04 sibling is a straight-line sequence with event PCs 0,1,2. The counter's pc repeats while its event ticks increase. A repeated pc is not evidence that the trace duplicated an event. Conversely, two events with the same tick would violate the one-event-per-executed-instruction contract.

Extend step so it records a detached event. Implement trace so a caller cannot edit stored events through a returned array or a nested write object. Keep output emission in the event as well as in state output. Inspection, setting a breakpoint and adding a watchpoint do not execute instructions and must not create events.

Run stage 04. If the event count is correct but a write is wrong, inspect which state you used for before and after. Recording a reference to a mutable state can make every old event appear to contain the newest value. The mutation control helps expose this aliasing mistake.

The intermediate build is a trace recorder you can use on a program you did not write. Run a bounded session, save the terminal output in your evidence folder, and locate stores to the same address at different ticks. State which write changed the value and which merely wrote it again. These are different claims supported by different event fields.

For repair practice, create a program with two emits and a same-value store between them. Predict the number of events and emitted values separately, run it, and explain the difference. A trace includes instructions that produce no output.

For transfer, compare two runs from new debugger instances over the same immutable program. Their complete traces should agree. Change one original program operand in a new instance and identify the earliest event that differs. Do not mutate an existing instance's program to simulate a branch; source replacement is outside this model.

## Representation

![Explanatory boundary diagram](diagrams/state-event.svg)

The adjacent text and worked output state the same relation. The figure uses supplied sibling data, not the answer to your pending capstone.

## Worked procedure

Use `node examples.mjs 04`. Read each row as post-tick, executed-pc, operation. Copy the write record when the event is saved, then copy it again when a caller receives a trace. Those copies protect two different boundaries: the event from later internal mutation and the stored trace from caller mutation. Completion: decide which copy is missing if editing a returned nested write changes a second trace call.

## Complete a changed case

Run `node lab.mjs question 04b` and commit the answer with `node lab.mjs predict project 04b YOUR_ANSWER --help-used none`. These are applications after instruction; they are not counted as predictions before explanation or as mastery evidence.

## Commit, build, check

For the cumulative build, create `project` once with `node lab.mjs start project`. Edit project/solution.mjs and run `node lab.mjs check project 04 --help-used none`. The check saves your code, report, original question and help before execution.

# 05. Checkpoints and replay

You have found a late symptom and want to inspect an earlier state. Implement seek by executing forward from genesis or an earlier checkpoint.

## Before the worked result

This case uses the terms and interface in contracts.md. Read the input in `node lab.mjs question 05a`, then save your answer with `node lab.mjs predict project 05a YOUR_ANSWER --help-used none` before reading the worked result below. This is practice, not a mastery claim. If you need the unit's terms first, study them and label the answer assisted rather than an unaided prediction.

A checkpoint is a saved full VM state at a tick. Replay starts from a checkpoint at or before the target tick and executes the same instructions forward. This works here because the VM has no external input, random values or clock. A real process would require a much larger recording contract.

A sibling example records a checkpoint partway through a loop, runs farther, seeks to genesis and then seeks to a later recorded tick. The example runner checks both the immediate rewind state and the reconstructed state. Looking only at the final state could miss an implementation that ignored rewind altogether.

Implement checkpoint and seek. Store an internal deep copy. The returned checkpoint object is an observation, not a portable restore token; editing it must not change replay. Seek may use the nearest earlier checkpoint or recompute from genesis. Both strategies satisfy the behavior. Explain the cost difference in your report rather than treating one strategy as the only correct answer.

Keep the recorded frontier separate from the current tick. Seeking backwards changes the current state but does not erase the known trace. Re-executing a recorded tick must not append a duplicate event. Seek can only address 0 through the farthest recorded tick; it must reject requests for an unrecorded future.

Run stage 05. A replay failure may come from checkpoint mutation, incomplete state capture, starting after the target or duplicate trace events. Use the checker input and intermediate state to narrow the cause. Do not fix an event-count failure by silently deleting historical events.

Your build is now a time-travel viewer for one deterministic execution. Run `node debug.mjs project/solution.mjs programs/counter.json programs/replay-session-stage05.json`, inspect the checkpoint and then revisit the same tick. This command file uses only methods from lessons 01–05. The longer `programs/replay-session.json` also uses reverse search and is assigned after lesson 06. Include the two observed snapshots and their comparison in your report. Checkpoints are local to one debugger instance; there is no session import or source replacement API to test.

For transfer, choose a program that emits before and after the checkpoint. Seek to a tick before the first emit and then beyond the second. Verify output as well as registers and memory. Explain why saving only pc and registers would reconstruct the wrong state even if the final arithmetic looked correct.

# 06. Reverse state search

Rewinding one tick at a time is still slow when a symptom has a precise condition. Add a search for the nearest earlier state that matches a register or memory value.

## Before the worked result

This case uses the terms and interface in contracts.md. Read the input in `node lab.mjs question 06a`, then save your answer with `node lab.mjs predict project 06a YOUR_ANSWER --help-used none` before reading the worked result below. This is practice, not a mastery claim. If you need the unit's terms first, study them and label the answer assisted rather than an unaided prediction.

reverseFind searches states, not instructions or write events. Its bound is exclusive: from current tick t, it begins with t−1 and moves towards tick 0. A match returns that tick and leaves the debugger positioned there. A missing match returns null and restores the state from before the search.

A sibling example reaches the same register value on several adjacent ticks. The correct match is the nearest earlier state, even if the instruction at that tick did not write the register. This distinguishes state search from last-write search. To investigate the last write to an address, inspect trace events backwards and seek to that event's tick minus one instead.

Implement reverseFind using your existing replay operation. Validate the condition and bound before changing the current state. Store the original state so a failed search has no visible effect. Include genesis in the search. If the bound is zero, there are no earlier states to examine.

Run stage 06. After it passes, run `node debug.mjs project/solution.mjs programs/counter.json programs/replay-session.json`. Its final `find reg b 0` command now exercises your reverse search after the lesson-05 replay steps. If the tool returns the current tick, check whether you accidentally made the bound inclusive. If a no-match search moves the debugger to genesis, the search has leaked its exploratory state. Compare inspect before and after a deliberately absent value and keep that experiment in the report.

Use the matching state and nearby trace events to decide which earlier instruction to inspect. Search for a value that preceded the symptom, inspect the nearby trace and formulate a smaller question. The returned tick alone does not prove which instruction caused a bug. Distinguish the observation from the explanation.

For practice, use a program that holds a value unchanged for several instructions. Predict the nearest matching tick, then contrast that result with the tick of the last write. State which question each operation answers.

For a return to the familiar rehearsal, run dispatch.json to completion and find an earlier matching memory value. Use a new debugger instance to confirm the same state by forward execution. Then try a value that never occurs and verify state preservation. Your report should include a refutable causal hypothesis rather than just a screenshot of a matching number.

Save the caller's state before exploring and restore it when no candidate matches. Completion: explain why a matching state may occur after an unrelated emit rather than at the last write. Case 06b asks for a concrete field after a no-match search on a different program.

`courses/time-travel-debugger/public/checks.mjs`:

```mjs
// Public behavioral cases, original to this course. No learner claim decides a result.
// Compare public JSON-shaped values. Object insertion order is not a contract;
// array positions, field presence and primitive values remain significant.
export function same(a,b) {
  if(a===b)return true;
  if(a===null||b===null||typeof a!=='object'||typeof b!=='object')return false;
  if(Array.isArray(a)!==Array.isArray(b))return false;
  if(Array.isArray(a)&&a.length!==b.length)return false;
  const left=Object.keys(a).sort(),right=Object.keys(b).sort();
  if(left.length!==right.length||left.some((key,n)=>key!==right[n]))return false;
  return left.every(key=>same(a[key],b[key]));
}
export const stages = ['01','02','03','04','05','06','07'];
export const program = [{op:'set',reg:'a',value:3},{op:'set',reg:'b',value:0},{op:'store',address:0,value:'b'},{op:'add',reg:'b',value:1},{op:'add',reg:'a',value:-1},{op:'jnz',value:'a',target:2},{op:'emit',value:'b'},{op:'halt'}];
function caseFailure(counterexample){const error=Error('The first concrete boundary case differs.');error.counterexample=counterexample;throw error;}
export function suite(api, stage) {
  const results = [];
  const test = (id, input, expected, run) => {
    if(typeof input==='string')input={program:id==='01.halt'?[{op:'halt'}]:id==='02.budget'?[{op:'jnz',value:1,target:0}]:id==='07.changed-program'?[{op:'set',reg:'d',value:9},{op:'store',address:6,value:'d'},{op:'load',reg:'a',address:6},{op:'emit',value:'a'},{op:'halt'}]:program,actions:input};
    try { const actual = run(); results.push({ id, input, expected, actual, pass: same(actual,expected), lesson: `lessons/${id.slice(0,2)}.md` }); }
    catch (e) { results.push({ id, input, expected, actual: { error: e.message }, counterexample:e.counterexample??null, pass:false, lesson:`lessons/${id.slice(0,2)}.md` }); }
  };
  const newD = p => new api.Debugger(p ?? program);
  const advance = (d,n) => { for(let k=0;k<n;k++) d.step(); return d; };
  if (Number(stage)>=1) {
    test('01.initial', 'construct counter', [0,0,0,false], () => { const s=newD().inspect(); return [s.pc,s.tick,s.regs.a,s.halted]; });
    test('01.detached', 'edit returned registers and memory', [0,0], () => { const d=newD(), s=d.inspect(); s.regs.a=99;s.mem[0]=99;return [d.inspect().regs.a,d.inspect().mem[0]]; });
    test('01.step', 'step set a=3', [1,1,3,0,'set'], () => {const d=newD(),e=d.step(),s=d.inspect();return [s.pc,s.tick,s.regs.a,e.pc,e.op];});

`courses/time-travel-debugger/public/vm.mjs`:

```mjs
// Original deterministic teaching VM. No native process access or external inputs.
export const clone = value => structuredClone(value);
const registers = ['a', 'b', 'c', 'd'];
export function initial() {
  return { pc: 0, tick: 0, regs: { a: 0, b: 0, c: 0, d: 0 }, mem: Array(8).fill(0), output: [], halted: false };
}
export function validateProgram(program) {
  if (!Array.isArray(program) || !program.length || program.length > 256) throw Error('VM: program needs 1–256 instructions.');
  for (const [pc, i] of program.entries()) {
    if (!i || !['set', 'add', 'load', 'store', 'jnz', 'emit', 'halt'].includes(i.op)) throw Error(`VM: invalid instruction at pc ${pc}.`);
    if (['set', 'add', 'load'].includes(i.op) && !registers.includes(i.reg)) throw Error(`VM: invalid destination at pc ${pc}.`);
    if (['set', 'add', 'store', 'jnz', 'emit'].includes(i.op) && !(Number.isSafeInteger(i.value) || registers.includes(i.value))) throw Error(`VM: invalid operand at pc ${pc}.`);
    if (['load', 'store'].includes(i.op) && (!Number.isInteger(i.address) || i.address < 0 || i.address > 7)) throw Error(`VM: invalid address at pc ${pc}.`);
    if (i.op === 'jnz' && (!Number.isInteger(i.target) || i.target < 0 || i.target >= program.length)) throw Error(`VM: invalid jump at pc ${pc}.`);
  }
  return clone(program);
}
export function execute(program, state) {
  if (state.halted) throw Error('VM: halted; no instruction executed.');
  const i = program[state.pc];
  if (!i) throw Error(`VM: pc ${state.pc} is outside the program; use halt.`);
  const next = clone(state);
  const value = typeof i.value === 'string' ? state.regs[i.value] : i.value;
  const event = { tick: state.tick + 1, pc: state.pc, op: i.op, writes: [], emitted: [] };
  next.pc++;
  next.tick++;
  if (i.op === 'set') next.regs[i.reg] = value;
  if (i.op === 'add') next.regs[i.reg] += value;
  if (i.op === 'load') next.regs[i.reg] = state.mem[i.address];
  if (i.op === 'store') {
    event.writes.push({ address: i.address, before: state.mem[i.address], after: value });
    next.mem[i.address] = value;
  }
  if (i.op === 'jnz' && value !== 0) next.pc = i.target;
  if (i.op === 'emit') { next.output.push(value); event.emitted.push(value); }
  if (i.op === 'halt') next.halted = true;
  if (Object.values(next.regs).some(n => !Number.isSafeInteger(n))) throw Error('VM: register exceeds safe integer range.');
  return { state: next, event };
}
export function matches(state, condition) {
  if (!condition || !['reg', 'mem'].includes(condition.kind) || !Number.isSafeInteger(condition.equals)) throw Error('Condition: use {kind:"reg",name:"a",equals:2} or {kind:"mem",address:0,equals:2}.');
  if (condition.kind === 'reg' && !registers.includes(condition.name)) throw Error('Condition: unknown register.');
  if (condition.kind === 'mem' && (!Number.isInteger(condition.address) || condition.address < 0 || condition.address > 7)) throw Error('Condition: address must be 0–7.');
  return condition.kind === 'reg' ? state.regs[condition.name] === condition.equals : state.mem[condition.address] === condition.equals;
}

```

`courses/time-travel-debugger/serve.mjs`:

```mjs
// Dependency-free, read-only learner preview. No project, author, or arbitrary-directory route.
import { createServer } from 'node:http';
import { readFileSync, lstatSync, realpathSync } from 'node:fs';
import { dirname, join, sep } from 'node:path';
import { fileURLToPath, pathToFileURL } from 'node:url';

const root = realpathSync(dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)));
export const DEFAULT_PORT = 8128;
export const ASSETS = Object.freeze(["index.html", "checker.html", "diagrams/state-event.svg"]);
const types = { '.html': 'text/html; charset=utf-8', '.svg': 'image/svg+xml' };
function readAssets() {
  return new Map(ASSETS.map(name => {
    for (let n = 1; n <= name.split('/').length; n++) {
      const path = join(root, ...name.split('/').slice(0, n));
      if (lstatSync(path).isSymbolicLink()) throw Error('Learner assets must not be symlinks: ' + name);
    }
    const path = join(root, name), real = realpathSync(path);
    if (!real.startsWith(root + sep) || !lstatSync(path).isFile()) throw Error('Expected regular learner asset: ' + name);
    return ['/' + name, { bytes: readFileSync(path), type: types[name.slice(name.lastIndexOf('.'))] }];
  }));
}
function pathname(raw) {
  try {
    const value = decodeURIComponent(raw.split('?')[0]);
    if (!value.startsWith('/') || value.includes('\\') || value.includes('\0')) return null;
    if (value.split('/').some(part => part === '.' || part === '..')) return null;
    return value === '/' ? '/index.html' : value;
  } catch { return null; }
}
export async function startServer({ port = DEFAULT_PORT } = {}) {
  if (!Number.isInteger(port) || port < 0 || port > 65535) throw Error('Port must be an integer from 0 through 65535. Use --port 0 for an available local port.');
  const assets = readAssets();
  const server = createServer((request, response) => {
    const host = '127.0.0.1:' + server.address().port;
    if (request.headers.host !== host) { response.writeHead(400); response.end('Use the printed 127.0.0.1 URL.'); return; }
    if (!['GET', 'HEAD'].includes(request.method)) { response.writeHead(405, { Allow: 'GET, HEAD' }); response.end('Read-only learner preview.'); return; }
    const asset = assets.get(pathname(request.url));
    if (!asset) { response.writeHead(404); response.end('No learner asset at this path.'); return; }
    response.writeHead(200, { 'Content-Type': asset.type, 'Content-Length': asset.bytes.length, 'Cache-Control': 'no-store', 'X-Content-Type-Options': 'nosniff', 'Referrer-Policy': 'no-referrer' });
    response.end(request.method === 'HEAD' ? undefined : asset.bytes);
  });
  await new Promise((resolve, reject) => { server.once('error', reject); server.listen(port, '127.0.0.1', resolve); });
  return server;
}
async function main() {
  const args = process.argv.slice(2);
  if (args.length && (args.length !== 2 || args[0] !== '--port' || !/^\d+$/.test(args[1]))) throw Error('Usage: node serve.mjs [--port PORT]. No host or directory option is supported.');
  const server = await startServer({ port: args.length ? Number(args[1]) : DEFAULT_PORT });
  const origin = 'http://127.0.0.1:' + server.address().port;
  console.log('Offline course reader: ' + origin + '/index.html\nProject checker: ' + origin + '/checker.html\nKeep this terminal open. Press Ctrl+C to stop. No internet connection is needed.');
  const stop = () => server.close(); process.once('SIGINT', stop); process.once('SIGTERM', stop);
}
if (process.argv[1] && pathToFileURL(process.argv[1]).href === import.meta.url) {
  main().catch(error => { console.error('Preview did not start: ' + (error.code === 'EADDRINUSE' ? 'Port is already in use. Stop your earlier preview or run node serve.mjs --port 0 and open its printed URL.' : error.message)); process.exitCode = 1; });
}

```md
# Sources and boundaries

This course defines an original executable teaching model. Its primary local sources are contracts.md, the supplied runtime, the public behavioral cases and reference-produced examples.json. No purchased book source, exercise, quotation, diagram, paid service or external packet was used. The course is not an adaptation of a named book.

All numeric worked-example output in examples.json is generated by running the local author reference on original inputs. Public cases are finite requirements checks. Author verification records contain valid alternatives and deliberately broken implementations, and are excluded from the learner archive. Source-aware author testing is not an independent cold tryout or evidence of learning.

The tested environment is Node v26.5.1 on macOS. Other Node versions and operating systems remain unqualified. Minimum-runtime qualification, other operating systems, browser download identity, visual/accessibility acceptance, human duration and learning effectiveness remain unverified. No network call or inference is part of the learner's default route.

import { initial, execute, validateProgram, clone, matches } from './vm.mjs';
const unfinished = name => { throw Error(`Unfinished: implement ${name}; read the matching lesson and rerun the check.`); };
export class Debugger {
  constructor(program) { this.program = validateProgram(program); this.state = initial(); }
  inspect() { return unfinished('inspect() in lesson 01'); }
  step() { return unfinished('step() in lesson 01'); }
  addBreakpoint(spec) { return unfinished('addBreakpoint(spec) in lesson 02'); }
  watch(address) { return unfinished('watch(address) in lesson 03'); }
  run(limit = 1000) { return unfinished('run(limit) in lessons 02–03'); }
  trace() { return unfinished('trace() in lesson 04'); }
  checkpoint(label) { return unfinished('checkpoint(label) in lesson 05'); }
  seek(tick) { return unfinished('seek(tick) in lesson 05'); }
  reverseFind(condition, beforeTick = this.state.tick) { return unfinished('reverseFind(condition, beforeTick) in lesson 06'); }
}

`courses/tiny-browser-engine/README.md`:

```md
# Tiny Browser Engine — local course candidate

Build a small browser for interactive reference pages. Follow the same document through an owned DOM, cascade, layout, fixed-font text, paint commands, geometric targeting, event dispatch and incremental updates. The result is a useful constrained renderer whose decisions can be inspected and replayed.

This learner edition supports the eight-module terminal route below. Browser UI, accessibility and human learning remain separately unqualified; the terminal route needs no browser or server.

The M6 stage inspector passes the current viewport when rebuilding after dispatch. Earlier archives remain historical; use the matching current package for terminal recovery. This correction does not establish browser execution.

## Complete terminal route

See [TERMINAL.md](TERMINAL.md) for all eight lessons and conceptual practices, own packet files, cumulative stage/render work, and versioned session export/restore/resume. The browser route remains optional and unqualified here.

## GitHub source and local setup

Use this course directory from the public repository, not a private Ivy checkout
or a required ZIP download:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/itsHabib/free-to-learn.git
cd free-to-learn
git rev-parse HEAD
cd courses/tiny-browser-engine
node --version
node tools/lesson.mjs M1
```

Record the printed commit with your learner evidence. If the course page links
a pinned revision, check out that revision before starting; do not silently mix
lessons or starter files across revisions. Git and the Node version described
below are the only prerequisites for the terminal route. No `npm install` or
private author-generated files are required.

The type-along route means implementing the eight methods in your own copy of
`public/starter.body.js`, using the lesson and `public/CONTRACT.md`. The supplied
files are scaffolding, not a completed engine. If you use AI to explain or write
a method, record that assistance before checking it, predict a test result, and
explain and repair a failure yourself. Passing generated code is not proof of
independent mastery. Keep a separate copy or Git commit at each completed module
instead of replacing your only working version with a later starter.

## Start as a learner

Use an already installed recent Node with ES modules, `structuredClone` and Web Crypto. Author checks here ran on **Node v26.5.1**; other versions have not been qualified. There is no package installation step and no third-party runtime dependency.

1. Copy `public/starter.body.js` to a file such as `my-engine.body.js`. Keep the eight method names. Implement the current module and leave later methods as explicit stubs.
2. Run `node tools/check.mjs my-engine.body.js M1`. A blank starter is expected to fail. The report names each requirement, its input, expected observation and actual observation.
3. Read `node tools/lesson.mjs M1`, then M2 through M8, for the lessons, conceptual practices and cumulative project prompts. Record answers before requesting `--answers` feedback. The lesson-data source includes answer metadata, so use this CLI for a fresh attempt. The browser workbench is optional when a local server/browser session is available.
4. Run `node tools/stage.mjs my-engine.body.js M1 stage.json` to inspect your own current stage. M3 uses an empty-box fixture so text is not a hidden prerequisite.
5. Once the whole engine is implemented, run `node tools/render.mjs my-engine.body.js board board.png`, then `node tools/render.mjs my-engine.body.js board after.png click`.

These CLIs execute your local JavaScript. Use locally authored, trusted source; they are not a hostile-code sandbox. Each checking/stage job has a five-second worker deadline. Rendering is a direct trusted-source command.

## Browser workbench

`node tools/build.mjs` creates `build/` from an explicit learner allowlist. To use it later, start `node tools/serve.mjs` and open the printed **127.0.0.1** URL. An optional port may follow the command. The server serves only the build manifest's learner files and applies a worker response policy; it does not serve this directory or `private/`. Stop it with Ctrl-C.

The local server and browser **were not started during this construction pass** because a shared resource slot was not granted. The emitted worker was syntax-checked and its request protocol was exercised under Node VM. That is not browser/CSP validation. Opening `index.html` as a `file:` URL is not supported because modules, worker fetches and storage need an origin.

The workbench includes eight readable lessons, 24 short conceptual practices, explicit cumulative build tasks, a source editor, public checks, stage inspection, full page rendering, click/keyboard activation, mutation/viewport controls, per-node provenance, frame-change reports, and source/notebook/frame/PNG exports. A prerecorded author demonstration is separate and prediction-gated. It never replaces learner code.

## The eight cumulative modules

| Module | Learner-owned deliverable |
|---|---|
| M1 Own the document | Strict tree construction and atomic identity-preserving mutations |
| M2 Resolve the cascade | Selector matching, declaration priority, inheritance and provenance |
| M3 Lay out blocks | Content/border geometry and dependent sibling positioning |
| M4 Turn text into fragments | Cross-node whitespace, wrapping, line height and source-owned glyphs |
| M5 Paint what layout means | Display commands, clipping and geometric hit selection; P1 renderer |
| M6 Route input into change | Frozen-path event dispatch and controlled page updates |
| M7 Recompute only what changed | Observable stage reuse with clean-render consistency; P2 interactive engine |
| M8 Render and diagnose an unfamiliar page | General repair on a new reference system; P3 transfer evidence |

Read `public/CONTRACT.md` for exact data shapes and `public/SOURCES.md` for primary references. Data structures, parsing basics and elementary graphics are prerequisites. The supplied code handles intake, UI, fixed original glyphs, rasterization, file I/O and actions. Those are intentionally not additional learner implementation assignments.

## Evidence and recovery

Commit records preserve source bytes and SHA-256, the packet and its hash, assistance labels and separate results. Repair attempts append history. Interactions link to the exact render submission. Notebook imports validate structure and source/packet hashes before merging; imported outcomes remain unauthenticated local claims. Repeated quiz answers are labeled revisits after feedback, not fresh mastery evidence.

The notebook is limited to 160 events / approximately 4 MB, source to 128 KiB, a packet to 256 KiB and one live trace response to 16 MiB. Export before those limits. The UI falls back to memory-only use when persistent storage is unavailable or another tab changed the stored value. Unreadable stored data is preserved for export. Frame traces are exported separately from the compact notebook.

`node tools/replay.mjs notebook.json replay-report.json` validates hashes and re-executes retained source/packet/interaction attempts in a bounded worker. Replay does not authenticate a grade or establish who wrote the source.

## Practice and transfer

Instructor implementations and private transfer instruments are not included. The visible field page is transfer rehearsal. Preserve your first engine, packet, predictions and notebook before attempting a new page; retain failures and explain each general repair. Finite checks and clean-vs-incremental agreement do not establish arbitrary web compatibility or human mastery.

## Limits of this candidate

TBE-1 accepts strict `main/div/p/span/button`, quoted ID/class, printable ASCII, a declared subset of normal CSS rules, block/inline/none, integer dimensions, uniform borders, fixed 8×16 glyph cells, simple whitespace/wrapping, scoped clipping and a small supplied action vocabulary. Unsupported input receives a diagnostic. No arbitrary page JS, network content, flex/grid/tables, Unicode shaping, native forms or full browser parsing is promised.

Remaining quality work includes browser/CSP/keyboard/storage qualification, independent source and curriculum review, broader boundary controls, richer inline ancestor fragment geometry, stream/chunk handling for large traces, authentic learner transfer observation and authorized integration/release. Do not describe this local package as a completed live course.

```

`courses/tiny-browser-engine/TERMINAL.md`:

```md
# Taking Tiny Browser Engine in the terminal

No browser, server, installation or network is needed for this route. Use an already installed Node with ES modules, structuredClone and Web Crypto. This candidate is qualified on Node v26.5.1. These commands execute trusted local learner JavaScript; they are not a hostile-code sandbox.

## Each module

1. Read `node tools/lesson.mjs M1` (replace M1 with M2 through M8 as you advance). It prints the lesson, three conceptual practices and the cumulative project.
2. Record your predictions and first answers in your own file. Request feedback with `node tools/lesson.mjs M1 --answers A,B,C`, using your choices. Feedback is practice, not certification. Text diagnoses and project explanations remain self-/reviewer-graded.
3. Before M1 only, copy `public/starter.body.js` to a new `my-engine.body.js`. For M2 through M8, keep editing that same engine: do not copy the starter over completed work. Implement the current methods and retain later explicit stubs. Preserve a numbered copy or Git commit before each repair or new module.
4. Run `node tools/check.mjs my-engine.body.js M1`. The starter must fail; do not treat that expected failure as completion.
5. Run `node tools/stage.mjs my-engine.body.js M1 stage-M1.json`. M3 defaults to empty block fixtures. Other stages use the guided page. M6 invokes one action and rebuilds with the correct viewport. Later unimplemented methods are not invoked by an earlier stage.

For your own page, write a JSON packet with `html`, `css`, `viewport` and optional supplied `listeners`/`defaultActions`, following `public/CONTRACT.md`. Then use:

```
node tools/stage.mjs my-engine.body.js M8 own-stage.json own-page.json
node tools/render.mjs my-engine.body.js own-page.json own-page.png
```

The built-in names `board` and `field` still work. The render command's optional final `click` activates the first button; use sessions below for precise, repeatable input.

## Your cumulative project and recoverable session

Once the complete engine works, start a new local workspace:

```
node tools/session.mjs start my-engine.body.js own-page.json my-session
node tools/session.mjs inspect my-session
node tools/session.mjs note my-session "My prediction, assistance used, and first divergent stage."
node tools/session.mjs apply my-session '{"kind":"click","point":{"targetId":5}}'
node tools/session.mjs apply my-session '{"kind":"scroll","scrollY":12}'
node tools/session.mjs apply my-session '{"kind":"resize","width":240,"height":180}'
```

Use actual handles from `inspect`, not the example handle blindly. `apply` accepts inline JSON or an input JSON file. Inputs are click, hit, mutate, scroll and resize, matching the workbench protocol. A mutation input contains an `operation` from the DOM contract. Hit and click coordinates are viewport coordinates; the host adds scrollY.

Each saved revision creates a new `book-NNNNNN.json`, frame JSON and PNG when a frame exists. Earlier snapshots are retained. The latest numbered notebook is the active session. A rejected operation or unsupported intermediate state returns exit 1 **and retains its input/result**. Inspect the result, then submit an explicit repair. A stale frame rejects activation. New source code starts a new workspace, preserving old attempts.

```
node tools/session.mjs export my-session my-export.json
node tools/session.mjs restore my-export.json restored-session
node tools/session.mjs inspect restored-session
node tools/session.mjs apply restored-session '{"kind":"scroll","scrollY":20}'
node tools/replay.mjs my-export.json replay-report.json
```

Restore uses the retained source, packet and input history in a fresh process. It verifies notebook structure and every source/packet hash before creating the new workspace. It does not authenticate grades or authorship. Source and inputs are the recovery data; JSON frames and PNGs are diagnostics. Keep exports private if your source or notes are private. Export paths and new workspaces must not already exist. No temporary-file cleanup or deletion is performed.

For P3, freeze your first engine and notebook before receiving a reviewer-created unfamiliar packet. The visible field page and self-authored page are practice and own-project evidence, not a blind human transfer assessment. Retain the first failure, minimized case, general repair, regression results and limitations. Passing all finite checks does not establish full web compatibility or course release acceptance.

## Worked assistance in the package

`public/demo.json` (also copied to `build/demo.json`) contains precomputed outputs for the guided pages. These are worked demonstrations, not your implementation or private learner solutions. If you inspect or use those outputs while solving an exercise, record that as assistance in your work; reproducing a supplied demonstration is not independent transfer evidence.
